title: When pleasure turns perilous: a case of penile gangrene after long-term penile ring use.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Sharma B, Bajwa PS, Pawar DS.
abstract: Penile ring entrapment is an uncommon but potentially devastating urological emergency. Prolonged constriction of the penile shaft can obstruct venous and lymphatic drainage, progress to arterial compromise, and result in ischemia, gangrene and loss of distal penile tissue. We describe a 50-year-old man who presented after seven days of penile ring entrapment with progressive swelling, discoloration, necrosis and foul-smelling discharge. The distal penis was almost completely auto-amputated, with an exposed urethra, although the patient remained haemodynamically stable and was able to void. Because of extensive irreversible necrosis, distal penile amputation was performed, followed by urethral fixation to the surrounding skin. The postoperative course was uneventful and the patient was discharged the following day. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, urgent decompression and timely specialist management of penile constriction injuries, as delayed presentation may result in irreversible tissue loss and radical surgical intervention.

title: Two-Stage Flap Reconstruction for Pelvic Pressure Injuries in Spinal Cord Injury: Microbiologic Trajectory and Predictors of Complications.
authors: Lopez MP, Kozlowski KA, Griffin DB, Adam TH, Bartler AV, Chaudhry AS, Rabin DA, Ontiveros N, Kessler AB, Galiano RD.
abstract: Introduction Pelvic pressure injuries (PIs) in spinal cord injury (SCI) patients frequently become contaminated, leading to severe PIs with concomitant osteomyelitis requiring flap reconstruction. A two-stage reconstruction technique aims to address this challenge, but evidence is inconclusive regarding improved outcomes compared with a single-stage approach. We assessed interval microbiologic findings and independent predictors of complications following standardized two-stage flap reconstruction to evaluate efficacy in SCI patients. Methods We performed a retrospective study of adults with SCI who underwent two-stage flap reconstruction for stage 3/4 pelvic PIs at a tertiary center from 2018 to 2025. The primary outcome was complications by 90-days postoperatively. Multivariable logistic regressions adjusting for age, number of flaps, previous flap reconstruction, microbiology burden, and malnutrition were completed. Results Among 146 patients (mean age: 48.1±14.9 years; 81.5% male), 34.9% developed at least one complication (major:17.8% and minor:22.6%) by 90-days. After adjustment, previous flap reconstruction and malnutrition were independent predictors of overall complications (aOR=7.06, 95%CI:2.32-21.45 and aOR=2.60, 95%CI:1.13-5.98, respectively), whereas microbial burden or reconstructive complexity were not. In addition, previous flap reconstruction and malnutrition tripled the odds of major complications, (aOR=3.66 and aOR=3.09, respectively). Conclusion In a high-risk cohort undergoing standardized two-stage reconstruction, the main predictors of postoperative complications were prior flap reconstruction and malnutrition. These findings support the feasibility of a two-stage approach for managing complex PIs with varying microbiologic burden.

title: Systemic immune biomarker responses following osteopathic lymphatic pump technique in healthy adults: a prospective controlled pilot study.
authors: Patel K, Gruber M, Aymond A, Keys M, Fresina K, Michalak K, Clark C, Kang L, Morrow R, DiGiuseppe S.
abstract: Context Lymphatic pump techniques (LPT) are commonly utilized in osteopathic manipulative medicine (OMM) to enhance lymphatic circulation. Experimental studies have demonstrated that LPT increases lymph flow, leukocyte flux, and the transport of inflammatory mediators within lymphatic vessels; however, whether these effects translate to measurable acute changes in systemic immune biomarkers in humans remains unclear. Objectives The objective of this study was to evaluate acute changes in circulating immune biomarkers following osteopathic LPT in healthy adults. Methods In this prospective controlled pilot study utilizing alternating group assignment, 32 healthy adult participants (age range, 22-69 years) were included in the final analysis after receiving either osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) incorporating LPT (n=17) or a sham intervention (n=15). Peripheral blood samples were collected at baseline and approximately 30 min postintervention. Plasma cytokines and chemokines (interleukin-8 [IL-8], monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 [MCP-1], granulocyte colony-stimulating factor [G-CSF], regulated on activation, normal T cell expressed and secreted [RANTES] and immunoglobulins G and M (IgG, IgM) were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Cell-associated leukocyte markers (CD16, CD20) were measured in buffy coat lysates utilizing ELISA. Biomarker responses were calculated as percent change from baseline. Statistical analyses included within- and between-group comparisons, principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering, nonparametric effect-size estimation, and sensitivity analyses adjusting for baseline biomarker concentration and participant age. Results Biomarker responses demonstrated broad variability with overlapping distributions between groups. Across all analytes, between-group estimates were generally small relative to substantial inter-individual variability. The confidence intervals (CIs) were wide and crossed the null value for all biomarkers, indicating limited precision and absence of evidence for a consistent acute systemic response. Adjustment for participant age did not materially alter the findings. Conclusions Under the conditions tested, LPT was not associated with a consistent acute systemic biomarker signature in peripheral blood. If biological effects occur, they may be transient, compartmentalized, delayed, or smaller than the present study was designed to detect. Future studies incorporating expanded temporal sampling and assessment of tissue and lymphatic compartments, particularly in patient populations with active disease in whom these effects may be more pronounced, will be important to further define these responses.

title: Surgical hyperlactataemia during resection of an intraventricular meningioma.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: O'Keeffe A, Noureldin F, Awan M, Price S, Reisz Z, Jones H, Lavrador J.
abstract: We present the first documented case of intraoperative hyperlactataemia during a minimally invasive resection of an intraventricular meningioma. The phenomenon remains unstudied, which creates a significant gap in both neurosurgical knowledge and patient management during perioperative periods. This will therefore help neurosurgeons and anaesthesiologists to recognise intraoperative metabolic problems, which will lead to further research and the development of better methods to handle such situations.

title: Surgical Intervention for Massive Lesions (>3cm<sup>2</sup>): Proceedings of the International Congress on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
authors: Rubin J, Tham A, Butler JJ, Gauthier P, Kennedy JG, Smyth NA, Murawski CD, Adams SB, Berlet GC, Buda R, Labib SA, Nunley JA, Raikin SM, Andrews CL, Angthong C, Batista JP, Bayer S, Becher C, Boakye LAT, Brown A, Calder JDF, Canata GL, Carreira D, Clanton TO, Dahmen J, D'Hooghe P, DiGiovanni CW, Dombrowski ME, Ehlers M, Ferkel EI, Ferkel RD, Ferrao PNF, Glazebrook M, Gianakos AL, Giza E, Gomaa M, Görtz S, Haleem AM, Hamid KS, Hangody L, Hannon CP, Haverkamp D, Hertel J, Hintermann B, Hogan MV, Hunt KJ, Hurley ET, Karlsson J, Kearns SR, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, Kim HJ, Kong SW, Krebsbach S, Lambers KTA, Woo Lee J, Lee KB, Ling JS, Longo UG, Marangon A, McCollum G, McCullough K, Mitchell AW, Mittwede PN, Nehrer S, Nicolescu R, Niemeyer P, O'Malley M, Ortiz C, Osei-Hwedieh D, Paul J, Pearce C, Pereira H, Phadke R, Popchak A, Prado MP, Reilingh ML, Robert G, Rothrauff BB, Schon LC, Simpson H, Sofka CM, Spennacchio P, Stone JW, Sullivan M, Takao M, Tanaka Y, Thermann H, Thordarson DB, Tuan R, Valderrabano V, van Bergen CJA, van Dijk CN, van Dijk PAD, Vannini F, Vaseenon T, Volesky M, Walls C, Walther M, Wiewiorski M, Xu X, Yasui Y, Hua Y, Yoshimura I, Younger ASE, Zdanowicz U, Zhang Z.
abstract: BackgroundManagement of massive (>3 cm 2 ) osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT) remains challenging due to extensive subchondral bone loss, uncontained lesion morphology, and limited high-quality evidence guiding treatment strategies. To address these gaps, an international group of experts convened to establish consensus-based recommendations for surgical management of massive OLT.MethodsExperts from multiple countries participated in a structured Delphi consensus during the International Congress on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle (ICCRA) meetings held in 2017 and 2025. Blinded surveys, structured questionnaires, and in-person discussions were used to develop and refine statements supported by literature review and graded evidence. Consensus strength was defined as consensus (51%-74%), strong consensus (75%-99%), or unanimous (100%). Grade of evidence was determined by previously established guidelines.ResultsA total of 8 consensus statements were developed addressing the surgical management of massive OLT (> 3 cm 2 ), all of which achieved strong consensus (≥86%), including 1 statement with unanimous agreement. Bulk allograft transplantation was identified as a primary joint-preserving strategy for large, uncontained, or previously treated lesions. Key technical considerations included complete lesion excision, adequate graft depth, precise graft matching, and stable fixation. Experts emphasized the importance of patient selection, surgical technique, and postoperative activity modification to optimize outcomes.ConclusionThe ICCRA statements provide structured, evidence-informed guidance for the operative management of massive OLT. By defining indications, technical considerations, and expected outcomes for bulk allograft transplantation and alternative reconstructive strategies, this framework aims to support clinical decision-making and promote consistency in the management of this complex and challenging condition.Level of Evidence:V, expert opinion.

title: Supercritical CO2-Processed Micronized Acellular Dermal Matrix Enhances Soft-Tissue Regeneration: A Preclinical and Clinical Study.
authors: Yang H, Ha EH, Yoon S, Lew H, Zhu Y, Lee D, Bae JW, Shin Y, Chang H, Hong KY.
abstract: Background Micronized acellular dermal matrix (mADM) derived from decellularized human dermis is used in breast reconstruction to address soft-tissue deficiencies and peri-implant deformities. Although mADM processed using supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-mADM) has previously been evaluated with respect to its fabrication and biocompatibility, its clinical application has not yet been investigated. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the biological responses to SC-mADM and its preliminary clinical applicability as an injectable scaffold. Methods In a rabbit model, 3 mL of either low-concentration (7.5%) or high-concentration (25%) SC-mADM was injected and assessed at 3 and 6 months. Volume retention was quantified using micro-computed tomography. Histologic analyses and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction analyses of genes associated with angiogenesis and tissue remodeling were performed. Based on these findings, a prospective clinical study involving four patients and five breasts was conducted to assess the correction of post-reconstruction rippling. Results High-concentration SC-mADM demonstrated greater volume retention than low-concentration SC-mADM at both 3 and 6 months. At 6 months, CD31-positive vascular density was higher in the high-concentration group, accompanied by increased expression of angiogenesis- and remodeling-related genes. Clinically, injections of high-concentration mADM resulted in improvement in rippling and peri-implant depressions. Magnetic resonance imaging at 4 months demonstrated an early mean region-level volume retention rate of 57.6%. Conclusions Injected mADM exhibited concentration-dependent tissue integration. These preliminary findings suggest that SC-mADM may serve as a biologically active injectable scaffold for minimally invasive contour correction in breast reconstruction. Further validation in larger studies with longer follow-up periods is warranted.Clinical Relevance Statement: mADM is a promising advanced soft-tissue filler that supports volume retention and host-tissue integration. The biological responses observed in the rabbit model provide preclinical evidence supporting its potential use in soft-tissue augmentation and repair.

title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional neck dissection for oral cavity cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Ruan C, Wang L.
abstract: To compare robot-assisted remote-access neck dissection with conventional transcervical neck dissection for oral cavity cancer, focusing on oncologic adequacy, perioperative burden, complications, function, and cosmesis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception through 24 September 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and verified eligibility. Comparative studies informed quantitative synthesis; clinically informative single-arm reports characterized technical evolution. Random-effects meta-analysis used mean differences and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I-informed domains. Fifteen reports representing 14 independent cohorts were included. Five oral-cavity comparisons involved 222 patients (99 robotic, 123 conventional). Three studies involving 124 patients contributed to meta-analysis. Robotic dissection prolonged neck-dissection time by 83.9 minutes (95% CI 59.7 to 108.1; I 2 ​=22%) but did not materially change lymph-node yield (mean difference 0.8 nodes, 95% CI -4.2 to 5.8; I 2 ​=0%). Median-based comparisons likewise showed longer or similar perioperative courses without a consistent nodal-yield disadvantage. Five-year disease-free survival was reported by one direct tongue-cancer cohort and 2-year disease-free survival by one propensity-matched oral-cavity cohort; neither demonstrated a statistically detectable difference, but events were sparse. Scar satisfaction favored robotic access. All comparisons were nonrandomized and at serious risk of confounding bias; selection bias was serious in four cohorts and moderate in the propensity-matched cohort. Robot-assisted neck dissection consistently concealed the cervical scar and achieved similar average nodal counts in selected oral-cavity cancer cohorts, at the cost of substantially longer operating time. These findings support technical feasibility and informed patient choice, but nodal yield is a surrogate outcome and the current evidence does not establish equivalent regional control, survival, or overall morbidity.

title: Preparedness of osteopathic medical students to address vaccine hesitancy: training and confidence.
authors: Rifkin AS, Wicker M, Malhotra S, Imokhai PO, Corallo S, Rawson CD, Harris E, Hurley DP, Reese H, Grinis D, Selan J, Jeng M, Martin P, Roberts S, Hota S, Mirza A, Sweeney J, Madrid K, Henderson KK.
abstract: Context Vaccine hesitancy poses a growing threat to public health, contributing to measles resurgences and declining childhood vaccination coverage in the United States. Although physicians remain among the most trusted sources of vaccine information, formal training in vaccine communication is not consistently integrated into medical curricula. Osteopathic medical education emphasizes whole-person, patient-centered care, which closely aligns with the skills required for effective vaccine counseling. However, the preparedness of osteopathic medical students for vaccine-related communication has not been well characterized. Objectives This study aimed to assess osteopathic medical students' perceptions of their curricular preparation for vaccine-related communication, as well as clinical-year students' real-world experiences and confidence in addressing vaccine hesitancy during rotations. Methods A prospective cross-sectional anonymous online survey was administered via Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) to medical students enrolled in Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) programs across the United States. Participants were recruited through Student Osteopathic Medical Association (SOMA) communication channels and institutional listservs. The survey assessed demographics, clinical exposure to vaccine discussions, confidence in addressing vaccine hesitancy, curricular preparation, and perceived training needs utilizing 5-point Likert-scale items. Ordinal logistic regression and Welch's t tests compared preclinical (Osteopathic Medical Student [OMS]-1/2) vs. clinical (OMS-3/4) students, OMS-3 vs. OMS-4 students, and clinical vaccine discussion groups. Odds ratios (ORs) and p values were calculated on 95 % confidence intervals (CIs) between groups. Results A total of 1,415 osteopathic medical students completed the survey. Overall, 87.1 % reported no formal vaccine communication training, with 88.6 % of OMS1/2 students and 85.3 % of OMS3/4 students agreeing or strongly agreeing that vaccine communication should be formally included in their curriculum. Compared with preclinical students, clinical students were less likely to report adequate curricular preparation for addressing vaccine hesitancy (OR=0.67, 95 % CI [0.55, 0.81;] p Conclusions Osteopathic medical students recognize vaccine hesitancy as a routine clinical challenge, agree that additional training in counseling would be helpful, and although clinical exposure builds confidence, this may occur unevenly and without structured design; formal training would help build this competence earlier and more equitably. Evidence-based tools, including motivational interviewing, simulation, and standardized patient encounters, align closely with osteopathic principles of whole-person care. Integrating these approaches into required curricula represents a practical and necessary step toward preparing future physicians to navigate both vaccine-related conversations and difficult conversations effectively.

title: Open reduction of the femoral butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures is associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union: a retrospective clinical cohort.
authors: Schlauch AM, Zakusylo A, Ball G, Biedermann B, Onafowokan O, Kennerly V, Domashevich T, Hellwinkel JE, Mauffrey C, Schaffer NE.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether the presence of and/or open reduction of a butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures was associated with reoperation to promote union. Methods Design: Retrospective cohort. Setting Single Level I Trauma Center. Patient selection criteria Included were patients who underwent surgical fixation of an acute OTA/AO 32A-C femoral shaft fracture between January 2017 and January 2024. Patients younger than 18 years, nonunion surgeries, Outcome measures and comparisons Patient demographics were retrospectively collected. A butterfly fragment was defined as a singular, wedge-shaped segment of comminution from the diaphysis of the femur. Groups were stratified based on the presence or absence of a butterfly fragment. The primary outcome was reoperation to promote union. Secondary outcomes included fracture-related infection (FRI) and presence of post-operative cortical step sign (CSS). Comparisons of primary and secondary outcomes were made between patients with and without a femoral butterfly fragment. A subgroup analysis was performed within the butterfly fragment group comparing open versus closed reduction of the butterfly fragment. Results 139 patients were included: 99 (71.2%) without a butterfly fragment (mean age 38.5years, range 18-92years; 62.6% male) and 40 (28.8%) with a butterfly fragment (mean age 35.5years, range 18-96years; 75.0% male). 10 (10.1%) patients without a butterfly fragment and 8 (20.0%) patients with a butterfly fragment underwent reoperation to promote union (p=0.2). Of the 40 patients with a butterfly fragment, 9 (22.5%) had open reduction of the butterfly fragment with cable fixation and 31 (77.5%) did not. The mean proximal and distal displacement of the butterfly fragment did not differ significantly between those managed with open versus closed reduction (38.8mm vs 35.4mm and 20.3mm vs 18.9mm, respectively, p>0.05). Open reduction to the butterfly fragment compared to closed reduction was associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union (66.7% vs 6.5%, p Conclusions Open reduction of the butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures was associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union compared to closed reduction. These findings emphasize biologic preservation. Level of evidence III.

title: Hugo RAS versus da Vinci Xi for robot-assisted simple hysterectomy in endometrial cancer: a concurrent-period comparison of operative efficiency, cost structure, and the cost of early adoption.
authors: Sakamoto I, Nozaki T, Fukada N, Ito Y, Kagami K.
abstract: Assessing a newly introduced robotic platform is complicated by calendar-time confounding and early institutional experience. We compared Hugo robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with da Vinci Xi for robot-assisted simple hysterectomy in endometrial cancer, restricting the primary analysis to their concurrent-use period. This single-centre retrospective cohort comprised 219 patients with clinical stage I disease operated between May 2018 and November 2025; procedures with lymphadenectomy or sentinel lymph node biopsy were excluded to standardise surgical content. The primary concurrent-period analysis included 67 procedures (da Vinci Xi 37, Hugo RAS 30), and cost data were analysable for 61. The adjusted mean difference in total operative time was 16.3 min (95% confidence interval [CI] 6.0-26.6), decreasing to 6.1 min (95% CI - 0.7 to 13.0) in an exploratory analysis excluding the first ten Hugo RAS procedures. Adjusted ratios for recorded consumable and operative costs were 0.808 and 0.923, respectively. These estimates compare early Hugo RAS use with established da Vinci Xi use; the exploratory exclusion cannot isolate learning from platform effects or predict steady-state performance. The findings apply to simple hysterectomy without nodal assessment and do not establish comparative safety, oncologic equivalence, or overall economic superiority.

title: Evolving Management of Hip Fracture Patients on Anticoagulant and Antiplatelet Medications: A 22-Year Cohort Study.
authors: House HE, Schwartz A, Shimizu M, Hong I, Cohen JB, Summers HD, Levack AE.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate temporal trends in anticoagulant (AC) and antiplatelet (AP) use among patients undergoing operative treatment of hip fractures and to assess the association of antithrombotic regimen with time to surgery and postoperative outcomes. Methods Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single North American Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria Patients aged 55 years or older who underwent operative treatment for a hip fracture (AO/OTA types 31-A, 31-B, and 31-C) between 2000 and 2022 while receiving anticoagulant and/or antiplatelet therapy at admission were included. Outcome measures and comparisons Temporal trends in antithrombotic prescribing, time to surgery, perioperative transfusion, readmission, 90-day medical and surgical postoperative complications, and 90-day mortality were assessed. The odds of warfarin versus direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) prescription were compared across study years, and time to surgery from admission and each outcome were compared across study years and across antithrombotic regimens (warfarin, DOAC, DOAC or warfarin plus antiplatelet, and antiplatelet alone). Results 476 patients were included (mean age 81.2 years [range, 60-103]; 288 [60.4%] female). Anticoagulant therapy was used by 155 (32.7%) and antiplatelet therapy by 385 (80.7%); 64 (13.4%) received both. The odds of warfarin prescription relative to a DOAC decreased by an estimated 37% per year (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% CI 0.53-0.74; P Conclusions In this 22-year single-center cohort of hip-fracture patients receiving anticoagulant (AC) or antiplatelet (AP) therapy, antithrombotic regimen was not associated with time to surgery, 90-day complications, or mortality. Perioperative transfusion and 1-year readmission rates declined over the study period independent of medication class. These findings supported expedited operative management of hip fractures in patients receiving AC or AP therapy. Level of evidence III.

title: Audit of ASA status reporting in emergency laparotomy studies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Khan A, Hajibandeh S, Hajibandeh S.
abstract: Introduction The aim of this study was to evaluate the compliance with reporting of American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status of patients in studies investigating postoperative mortality after emergency laparotomy. Methods A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. All studies investigating postoperative mortality as the primary outcome in patients undergoing non-trauma emergency laparotomy were included and analysed. Compliance with ASA status reporting was assessed and the potential predictors of poor compliance were evaluated using a multivariable binary logistic regression model. Results In total, 81 studies were included. Compliance with ASA status reporting was 77.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 67.5-86.2). Multivariable binary logistic regression showed that compliance with ASA status reporting was not affected by year of publication (coefficient: -0.0199, p = 0.767), sample size of the study (coefficient: 0.0001, p = 0.995), the impact factor of the journal in which the study is published (coefficient: 0.1389, p = 0.334), the level of evidence provided by the study (coefficient: 0.3405, p = 0.594) or the risk of mortality reported by the study (coefficient: -1.6150, p = 0.656). There was no difference in the reported risk of postoperative mortality between studies that reported ASA status (13.1%, 95% CI 12.0-14.2%) and those that did not (13.1%, 95% CI 11.9-14.3%). Conclusions Reporting of the ASA status of patients in studies investigating postoperative mortality after emergency laparotomy is suboptimal. Authors, reviewers and editors should proactively ensure compliance with ASA status reporting in this setting.

title: Association Between Baseline Anemia and Nonunion After Proximal Humerus Fracture Across the Adult Lifespan.
authors: Nakken ER, Mamonov A, Garcia-Canga B, Whitney DG, Lang A, Aibinder WR.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the association between preexisting anemia and proximal humerus fracture (PHF) nonunion and to determine whether risk varies by anemia type and associated co-occurring conditions. Methods Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting Administrative claims database study using commercial and Medicare fee-for-service data from 2016 to 2023. Patient selection criteria Adults aged ≥19 years who sustained a PHF (OTA/AO 11) and had continuous insurance enrollment for ≥6 months after PHF were included, allowing entry into the at-risk period for nonunion. Anemia diagnosed during the 1-year period before the fracture was the primary exposure and was evaluated in three ways: (1) presence or absence of any anemia, (2) number of different co-occurring anemia conditions (range, 0-14), and (3) clinically relevant anemia categories, including nutritional, hemolytic, and aplastic/other anemias. Outcome measures The incidence rate (IR), IR ratio (IRR), and hazard ratio (HR) was estimated for the primary outcome of nonunion of the PHF from 6 to 18 months post-fracture, before and after accounting for potential confounders. Additionally, sub-group estimates were generated for patients 40, 50, 60, 70, and 80 years of age. Results There were 25,109 adults with a PHF and any type of anemia (mean [SD] age=76.0 [12.8] years; 78.2% women; 6.8% commercially-insured) and 64,389 with a PHF without anemia (68.3 [17.0] years; 74.6% women; 26.7% commercially-insured). The crude IR and IRR of PHF nonunion was significantly higher for the full anemia cohort (IR=6.0 [95%CI=5.1-6.8]; IRR=1.37 [95%CI=1.15-1.62) and for each anemia sub-cohort (IR [IRR] for 1, 2, and ≥3 co-occurring anemic conditions was 5.5 [1.25], 6.2 [1.42], and 8.1 [1.85], respectively) than the non-anemia cohort. Compared to the non-anemia cohort, the adjusted HR was not significantly different for the full anemia cohort (HR=0.97; 95%CI=0.80-1.17) or anemia sub-cohorts (HR range, 0.85-1.00). However, age strongly modified all associations (P for interaction, all ≤0.001). For all three types of anemia exposure (yes/no, count of co-occurring, clinically distinct groups), the HR of nonunion was elevated at the younger ages (age 40: HR=2.06 [95% CI=1.33-3.18]; age 50: HR=1.63 [95% CI=1.18-2.27]; age 60: HR=1.30 [95% CI=1.02-1.65]) and declined with older age, close to 1.00 by 70 years old and below 1.00 by 80 years old. Conclusions Anemia was associated with a higher rate of nonunion of the proximal humerus fracture among younger and middle-aged adults (HR=2.06, 1.63, and 1.30 for 40, 50, and 60 year old patients, respectively), but not for older adults. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III.

title: Agreement between and test-retest reliability within Theia3D markerless and Vicon marker-based three-dimensional motion capture systems during barbell back squats in trained lifters.
authors: Amdi CH, Zoellner A, Yang D, Whatman C, Helms ER, Spence AJ.
abstract: This study compared data loss, within-system reliability, and between-system agreement of marker-based (Vicon) and markerless (Theia3D) motion capture during back squats. Twenty-nine powerlifters (10 female, 19 male) performed barbell back squats at 70% 1RM with simultaneous motion capture. Data loss, reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient, standard error of measurement, coefficient of variation and minimal detectable change [MDC]) and agreement (concordance correlation coefficient [CCC], Bland-Altman, statistical parametric mapping) were assessed for hip, knee, ankle, trunk and stance parameters. Theia3D demonstrated substantially less data loss than Vicon (0.7% vs. 13.0%), with ankle dorsiflexion and trunk inclination particularly problematic for marker-based tracking. Within-system reliability was similar or superior for Theia3D compared to Vicon (MDC = 3.32-5.97° vs. 4.11-13.60°). However, between-system agreement was generally poor (CCC < 0.900 for most variables), with Vicon estimating larger lower-limb flexion angles and exhibiting largest disagreement at the hip joint. While Theia3D offers practical advantages (superior data completeness and measurement precision, portability, lower cost) for deep squat assessment, poor between-system agreement indicates these systems should not be used interchangeably. However, results may not transfer across movement tasks, study populations, practical setups and system selection should therefore align with study-specific priorities, available resources and expertise.

title: After-hours hip fracture surgery-influence on reoperation risk, mortality, and surgical complications: a cohort study of 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register.
authors: Boutera AT, Dybvik E, Engesæter LB, Guy P, Kristensen TB, Leer-Salvesen S, Hallan G, Sundet M, Gjertsen JE.
abstract: Background and purpose Previous studies have shown that timing of hip fracture surgery is important for outcomes. We aimed to determine whether hip fracture surgeries performed after regular working hours were associated with increased 1-year reoperation risk, 30-day mortality, or intraoperative complications. Methods Data from 98,607 patients ≥ 65 years with hip fracture reported to the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Absolute risk estimates were calculated with Kaplan-Meier, and Cox regression models were used to estimate hazard rate rations (HRRs) for 1-year reoperation risk and 30-day mortality for surgeries performed in the evening (16:00-22:00) and nighttime (22:00-08:00) compared with daytime surgery (08:00-16:00). Analyses were adjusted for age groups, sex, the American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) physical status class, cognitive impairment, type of fracture, type of surgery, waiting time to surgery, and duration of surgery. Surgeons self-reported intraoperative complications to the registry. Results 46,655 patients (47%) underwent daytime surgery, 40,916 (42%) evening surgery, and 11,036 (11%) nighttime surgery. The mean age was 83 years, 69% were females. Patients operated on during nighttime had overall shorter waiting time to surgery than the other groups. 1-year reoperation risk was 4.9% (n = 2,290) for daytime surgery, 5.2% (n = 2,151) for evening, and 6.0% (n = 673) for nighttime, with no statistically significant differences between the groups. Nighttime surgery was associated with a slightly lower 30-day mortality (7.8%, n = 870) compared with daytime surgery (9.6%, n = 4,494), HRR 0.91 (95% confidence interval 0.84-0.98). No statistically significant differences in intraoperative complications were observed across the 3 surgical time periods: daytime (2.9%), evening (2.9%), and nighttime (2.9%). Conclusion Evening and nighttime hip fracture surgery were not associated with increased risk for 1-year reoperation, 30-day mortality, or intraoperative complications compared with daytime surgery.

title: Regional Variations in Epidemiology, Diagnosis, and Surgical Management of Discoid Meniscus in Pediatric Populations Across Asia-Pacific and North American Regions: A Systematic Review.
authors: Chua CXK, Wang E, Tan CQ, Lim AKS, Hui JHP, Tan SHS.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate regional variations in clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, and treatment algorithms for pediatric discoid meniscus between Asia-Pacific and North American regions. Methods A systematic review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, searching PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure databases from inception to August 2025. Study characteristics, population details, imaging modality (sensitivity and specificity), study objective, incidence of bilateral involvement, surgical technique, and complications were recorded. Because of heterogeneity and predominantly low-level evidence, a qualitative synthesis was performed. Results Thirty-nine studies were included in the systematic review, predominantly Level III evidence. Epidemiological data suggested a higher reported incidence of bilateral discoid meniscus in Asia-Pacific (7%-33%) compared with North America (2%-21%), although findings were heterogeneous. Twelve radiological studies were evaluated and found Asia-Pacific studies reporting the use of alternative diagnostic technique (radiography and ultrasound), whereas North America relied exclusively on magnetic resonance imaging. Twenty-four surgical studies were included (13 Asia-Pacific, 11 North America), comprising 671 and 1442 knees, respectively. Partial meniscectomy/saucerization was the predominant surgical approach in both regions (89.7% vs 94.5%, P = .08), with low rates of subtotal or total meniscectomy. However, adjunctive procedures differed significantly; Asia-Pacific studies more commonly reported concurrent repair or stabilization procedures (47.7% vs 26.6%, P = .0001), whereas North American studies more frequently performed partial meniscectomy alone. Conclusions This systematic review suggests a higher incidence of bilateral discoid meniscus in Asia-Pacific, but findings were limited by heterogeneity. Although demographics and clinical presentation were similar between regions, imaging approaches differed, with radiographic and ultrasound studies reported exclusively in Asia-Pacific and North American studies relying solely on magnetic resonance imaging. Surgically, both regions primarily performed partial meniscectomy; however, adjunct procedures (stabilization and/or repair) were more common in Asia-Pacific. These findings underscore distinct regional treatment strategies and the need for standardized diagnostic and treatment frameworks. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level II to IV studies.

title: Osteomyelitis after open supracondylar fracture in a child: a case report and review of the literature.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Stubenböck E, Mindler G, Öhner T, Moser V, Beer T, Quadlbauer S.
abstract: The management of open fractures in children relies on several critical strategies to minimize the risk of infection, including the timing of surgical debridement, appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis, and the choice of osteosynthesis technique. Despite these considerations, the overall rate of postoperative infection in children remains relatively low. Consequently, clinical experience with deep postoperative infections in pediatric patients is limited. Furthermore, the highly variable and often subtle clinical presentation can make early diagnosis challenging. We present the case of an 8-year-old child who developed osteomyelitis following a Gustilo-Anderson grade III open supracondylar humerus fracture.

title: Ninja Warrior Athletes Have Diverse Athletic Backgrounds, High Fitness Levels, and Are Prone to Upper Extremity and Ankle Injuries.
authors: Gardner CH, DiStefano JG.
abstract: Purpose To characterize Ninja Warrior athletes' level and frequency of participation, exercise habits and capabilities, prior sports participation, injuries frequently sustained, and management of those injuries. Methods A survey was available to Ninja athletes at 5 gyms and competitions between July 2023 and February 2026. Athletes were included if they were over 18 years old and competed or trained on Ninja obstacles. The survey evaluated athletic background, injury data, and injury management data. Statistical significance was determined between men and women, and a regression analysis was performed. Results A total of 101 surveys were completed (64 men, 37 women). The mean age of respondents was 33.8 years (range 18-57 years). Men were more likely to sustain injuries than women (incidence rate ratio 2.5). Athletes had an average body mass index of 23.2 and averaged 20.9 pull-ups, a 195.5-s dead hang, and an 11.0-ft lache. The most common traumatic injury sites were hand (skin tears, 67.3%), ankle (48.5%), and shoulder (40.6%). The shoulder and elbow were the most common sites of overuse injuries. The rate of return to full preinjury level of participation was 70.7% in this study. Conclusions Ninja Warrior athletes have broad athletic backgrounds and display high reported levels of physical fitness. Unique traumatic injury mechanisms include static and dynamic stress on the fingertips as well as eccentric loading of joints. Men, on average, sustained more injuries than women. Overuse injuries most commonly occur in the shoulder and elbow regions. Clinical relevance This study provides useful data about the common phenotype of Ninja Warrior athletes and the injuries they sustain, which helps to guide diagnosis and treatment of these athletes.

title: Influence of ballistic and conventional resistance training on bone properties in postmenopausal women: A randomised controlled trial.
authors: Caliskan O, Marques EA, Breasail MÓ, Duckham RL, Folland JP, Brooke-Wavell K.
abstract: High-load conventional resistance training (CRT) is recommended for osteoporosis prevention. Ballistic resistance training (BRT) involves high velocity and impact forces with lower loads. The Resistance Exercise Programme on Risk of Osteoporosis and Osteoarthritis in Females (REPROOF) study examined effects of BRT and CRT, relative to control (CON) on proximal femur BMD. Healthy postmenopausal women aged 50-70 years were randomised into BRT, CRT or CON groups. BRT and CRT conducted supervised resistance training twice weekly for eight months. In CRT, concentric and eccentric phases each lasted ~2 s at 55-80% of one-repetition maximum (1RM). BRT involved explosive (maximum velocity) concentric movements at 20-50% of 1RM. Proximal femur and lumbar spine BMD were measured by DXA; tibia structure by peripheral QCT. Groups were compared using ANCOVA, adjusting for baseline values. Of 109 women randomised, 82 (63.1 ± 3.7 years; 24.5 ± 3.5 kgm -2 ; femoral neck T-score -1.1 ± 0.8) completed the study, with 98% adherence. BRT improved total hip BMD (+0.008 [0.001, 0.014] g/cm 2 ; P = 0.02) versus CON. CRT did not affect hip BMD but tibial shaft cortical BMD increased (+4.141 [1.007, 7.274] g/cm 2 ; P = 0.01) and cortical thickness declined relative to CON (-0.07 [-0.13, -0.01] mm; P = 0.03), accompanied by tibial shaft widening. BRT increased total hip and trochanter BMD (P ≤ 0.03) in the subgroup with low BMD. BRT benefitted proximal femur BMD relative to CON, including in the subgroup with low BMD. CRT did not affect hip BMD but caused tibial shaft structural adaptation that may affect strength in bending. BRT based interventions should be further developed and evaluated for osteoporosis prevention.

title: Five-year outcomes after brace-free versus brace-based rehabilitation following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Schoepp C, Praetorius A, Tennler J, Raeder C, Schroeder M, Hax J, Seelmann C, Ohmann T, Efe T, Dudda M, Neidlein C.
abstract: Introduction Postoperative knee bracing following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains common practice despite growing evidence questioning its clinical benefit. Previous studies demonstrated that brace-free rehabilitation was noninferior to brace-based rehabilitation one year after isolated ACLR using hamstring tendon autograft; however, its long-term effects remain unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term effects five years after surgery. Materials and methods Patients enrolled in a prospective randomized controlled trial conducted between 2016 and 2019 were recontacted approximately five years after isolated primary ACLR with hamstring tendon autograft for a long-term follow-up. In the original trial, 139 patients had been randomized to postoperative rehabilitation without a brace (n = 71) or with a functional knee brace (n = 68). Participants completed several patient-reported outcome measures. Furthermore, a standardized telephone interview was performed. Changes between the one-year and five-year follow-up were analyzed. Results Ninety-seven patients participated in the long-term follow-up (n = 45 brace-free group, n = 52 brace group). Mean follow-up was 5.2 ± 1.0 years. No significant differences were observed between groups regarding subjective knee function, activity level, quality of life, rerupture rate, revision surgery, or persistent knee-related complaints at final follow-up. However, there was a significant interaction between treatment group and time for the subjective IKDC score. Patients treated without postoperative bracing showed stable or slightly improved subjective knee function, whereas patients treated with a brace demonstrated a significant decline between one and five years. Discussion Brace-free rehabilitation after isolated ACL reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft remains safe and effective more than five years after surgery. Postoperative bracing did not reduce rerupture rates, revision surgery, or long-term functional impairment. Instead, brace-free rehabilitation demonstrated a more favorable longitudinal development of subjective knee function. These findings further question the routine postoperative prescription of rehabilitative knee braces following isolated ACL reconstruction.

title: Development and external validation of an explainable machine-learning model for the prediction of unfavourable clinical-radiological outcome at three months in thoracolumbar osteoporotic vertebral fractures.
authors: Gutiérrez-González R, Martínez-Núñez P.
abstract: No externally validated tools stratify three-month prognosis after thoracolumbar osteoporotic vertebral fracture. An explainable logistic-regression model with nine predictors achieved an external AUC-ROC of 0.744 (sensitivity 90.7%). The counterfactual analysis of vertebral augmentation, the only modifiable predictor, is hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as a treatment recommendation. Purpose Thoracolumbar osteoporotic vertebral fractures (OVF) carry substantial morbidity and mortality, yet no externally validated tool stratifies three-month prognosis. We developed and externally validated an explainable machine-learning model for the three-month unfavourable clinical-radiological outcome. Methods Retrospective observational study reported according to TRIPOD. Unfavourable outcome was defined as persistent pain, progression of vertebral height loss and/or worsening of independence in daily activities. A derivation cohort of 482 patients aged ≥50 years with acute thoracolumbar OVF treated at a tertiary centre (2017-2021) was used to train and internally validate seven algorithms with hyperparameter optimisation and stratified fivefold cross-validation. An independent two-centre cohort (n = 74) was used for external validation without retraining. Interpretability was based on SHAP values. Results The unfavourable outcome occurred in 53.9% of the derivation cohort and 58.1% of the external cohort. A nine-variable logistic-regression model with Platt calibration was selected (cross-validated AUC-ROC 0.675, 95% CI 0.622-0.728; external AUC-ROC 0.744, 95% CI 0.628-0.844). At the pre-specified internal Youden threshold (0.556), external sensitivity was 60.5% and specificity 71.0%; at a post-hoc external threshold (0.432), 90.7% and 54.8% (Brier 0.211, expected calibration error 0.096). Vertebral augmentation was the strongest and only modifiable predictor (mean |SHAP | = 0.278); counterfactual analysis showed an absolute risk reduction of 17.1-26.6 percentage points (median 25.3). Conclusion The model predicts the three-month outcome of thoracolumbar OVF with an external AUC-ROC of 0.744 and preserved calibration. The counterfactual analysis of vertebral augmentation is hypothesis-generating and not a treatment recommendation; larger external validation, long-term outcomes and harm assessment are required before clinical use.

title: Arthroscopic Double EndoButton Adjustable-Loop Plate Fixation for Acute Acromioclavicular Joint Dislocation.
authors: Huang S, Zheng Z, Qian C, Yuan H, Bao H.
abstract: Acute acromioclavicular joint dislocation is a shoulder injury. Surgical intervention is typically recommended for Rockwood type IV to VI injuries with significant displacement. Both traditional open surgery and existing arthroscopic techniques have limitations in terms of trauma, stability, and procedural complexity. This article introduces an arthroscopic fixation technique using a double EndoButton adjustable-loop plate. It aims to achieve anatomical reduction and sustained compressive fixation of the acromioclavicular joint through a dual-EndoButton structure and an adjustable-loop design. This method is relatively straightforward to perform, minimally invasive, and biomechanically sound, offering a reliable new option for the minimally invasive treatment of acute acromioclavicular joint dislocations. Preliminary clinical practice has shown favorable reduction outcomes, stable fixation performance, and potential for early rehabilitation.

title: Application of Extraperitoneal Laparo-Endoscopic Single-Site Surgery in the Treatment of Lumbosacral Trunk Entrapment: A Cadaveric Study and Clinical Case Series.
authors: Chen S, Miao J, Ma G, Wang Y, Zhang Z, Yang X, Fan S.
abstract: Objective Management of pelvic fracture with lumbosacral trunk entrapment remains controversial. Open surgery (OS) carries significant technical challenges and risks. Our team innovatively proposed extraperitoneal laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery (ELESS) to explore and release the lumbosacral trunk. This study aimed to identify the key anatomical parameters of the lumbosacral trunk, to introduce ELESS techniques for exploration and release of lumbosacral trunk entrapment, and to evaluate its safety, feasibility, and clinical efficacy compared to OS. Methods This study measured lumbosacral trunk parameters in 12 cadavers, and retrospectively analyzed clinical data of 36 patients with lumbosacral trunk entrapment from May 2022 to September 2024. Combined with anatomical data, preoperative enhanced CT and MRN tests, the lumbosacral trunk decompression surgery was performed precisely via ELESS (n = 16) and OS (n = 20). Demographic, surgical technique details, and clinical outcomes were obtained from patient records. Independent samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U test, or the Chi-square test were used to perform comparisons. Results The distance from the start of lumbosacral trunk to the sacroiliac joint was 14.85 ± 1.43 mm. The total length of the lumbosacral trunk was 34.95 ± 2.13 mm, and its width was 7.92 ± 1.11 mm. The patients were followed up for at least 16 months. The ELESS group demonstrated a significantly shorter operative time (131.5 ± 13.6 min) and reduced intraoperative blood loss (119.1 ± 28.1 mL) compared to the OS group (151.7 ± 27.9 min and 1010.5 ± 118.6 mL, p Conclusions Anatomical data is essential to identify and locate the lumbosacral trunk during surgery. The ELESS for lumbosacral trunk decompression offers the advantages of precision, minimal invasiveness, and safety. Compared to traditional OS, the ELESS is associated with less bleeding and shorter operative time, representing a reliable option for managing pelvic fractures with lumbosacral trunk entrapment.

title: Anatomical Risk Factors for Patellofemoral Instability Vary by Dejour Type of Trochlear Dysplasia.
authors: Hartmann M, Caliskan B, Vlachopoulos L, Ackermann J, Fucentese SF.
abstract: Purpose To assess whether Dejour trochlear dysplasia (TD) types differ in their association with other patellofemoral anatomical variables in patients with patellar instability. Methods All patients with TD undergoing evaluation for patellar instability between January 2010 and December 2020 were included if a true lateral radiograph and a preoperative magnetic resonance imaging were available. Two reviewers independently assessed TD type (Dejour classification), femorotibial rotation, tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TTTG) distance, sagittal TTTG, tibial tubercle-to-posterior cruciate ligament distance, supratrochlear spur height, sulcus depth, Merchant's congruence angle, trochlear sulcus angle, Caton-Deschamps index, patellotrochlear index, patellar tilt, angle, thickness, and width. Results The study included 330 patients (363 knees, 66.7% women, mean age 22.5 ± 7.9 years, body mass index 24.9 ± 5.4). TD distribution was type A (17.1%), B (33.6%), C (25.9%), and D (23.4%). Types B and D showed significantly increased Merchant's congruence angle ( P = .019), patellar tilt ( P P = .035), TTTG ( P P P Conclusions Patients with Dejour type B and D TD had significantly increased values in other patellofemoral instability risk factors compared with those presenting with type A and C dysplasia. Level of evidence Level IV, diagnostic retrospective case series.

title: The sustainability of quality improvement projects within Zambia healthcare: A case study of Chilenje First Level Hospital.
authors: Milimo P, Siaminwe L.
abstract: Introduction Quality improvement (QI) interventions are widely used to strengthen healthcare delivery and improve patient outcomes, particularly in HIV programs in low- and middle-income countries. However, sustaining improvements after project close-out remains a significant challenge in many resource-limited healthcare settings. This study assessed the sustainability of a quality improvement project implemented to improve timely initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) among HIV-positive infants identified through early infant diagnosis (EID) testing. Methods A qualitative case study design was employed using focus group discussion with 15 healthcare workers involved in the implementation of the QI project. Participants were purposely selected based on their involvement in the intervention. Data was collected using a structured interview guide informed by the Model for Improvement and Batalden and Davidoff's Quality Improvement framework. Results Quality improvement tools, including Fishbone Diagrams, the Five Whys technique, run charts, and Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles were used to identify system gaps and guide implementation of targeted interventions. Participants identified strong leadership, integration of QI practices into routine service delivery, and staff ownership as key facilitators, while reduced external supporting and limited resources for orienting new staff were identified as challenges to sustaining the intervention. Conclusion Integrating quality improvement interventions into routine healthcare practices, supported by leadership, continuous monitoring, and staff engagement, can promote sustainable improvements in HIV service delivery. This study contributes to the limited evidence on the sustainability of quality improvement interventions in resource-limited settings and highlights key organizational and system-level factors that support long-term continuation of healthcare improvements after project close-out.

title: The incremental value of cortical renorrhaphy after base-layer closure in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: an anatomy-defined systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Chai Y, Zhang L, Zhong B, Xue P, Li X, Dai J, Liu J.
abstract: Renorrhaphy labels can obscure whether an outer cortical layer is added after substantive base-layer repair. We assessed this incremental step during robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN). MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched through 28 September 2026. Eligible comparisons retained base-layer repair in both arms but differed by cortical closure. Randomized and observational evidence were separated. Sparse binary outcomes underwent generalized linear mixed modeling, exact-inference sensitivity analysis, and descriptive absolute-risk estimation. Unpoolable outcomes were synthesized narratively. A second reviewer independently verified final screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias judgments. Among 23 reports assessed, nine studies were included (seven strict and two conditional). Neither protocol-defined critical outcome could be meta-analyzed. One cohort (n=146) provided three-month estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) change: mean decline was 8 mL/min/1.73 m² with omission versus 1 with double-layer closure (unadjusted mean difference -7.00; 95% confidence interval -13.03 to -0.97), although the source reported P=0.06. No study reported a comparable deduplicated 90-day reconstruction-related major-intervention composite. Four observational cohorts (n=575; 22 events) yielded an all-cause grade ≥III complication odds ratio of 0.70 (95% confidence interval 0.28-1.71); crude risks were 36 versus 41 per 1,000. Exact inference remained inconclusive. Available anatomy-defined evidence cannot establish the incremental safety benefit of cortical closure or renal-functional superiority of omission. Standardized trials with explicit layer definitions, fixed renal follow-up, and patient-level safety adjudication are needed.Registration: PROSPERO: CRD420261529497; version 1.0 published 4 October 2026.

title: The impaired white matter integrity and altered functional connectivity in Parkinson's disease.
authors: Ding M, Hua B, Wang S, Liu Y, Ding X, Ding J.
abstract: Purpose Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by structural abnormalities in the cerebral cortex and subcortical regions. Nevertheless, functional connectivity (FC) alterations within these affected white matter (WM) regions have not been fully clarified. Methods We combine diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) to explore abnormalities in WM structure and FC in 20 PD patients and 22 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (HCs). Results Compared with the HCs, PD patients showed lower fractional anisotropy (FA) values in multiple widespread WM tracts, including the the forceps minor, the bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculus, the right inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus, corticospinal tract (CST) and superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), the left anterior thalamic radiation (ATR), uncinate fasciculus and cingulum. Seed-based FC analysis revealed that: for the CST seed, PD patients exhibited reduced FC with the bilateral postcentral gyrus and precentral gyrus, the right superior occipital gyrus and left inferior parietal lobule. For the SLF seed, PD patients exhibited reduced FC with the bilateral anterior cingulate cortex. For the ATR seed, hypoconnectivity was found in multiple cerebellar subregions, including the bilateral cerebellum VIII and cerebellum IX, the right cerebellum VI and cerebellar crus I, and the left middle temporal gyrus. Conclusion Our findings indicate that PD patients exhibit widespread WM microstructural damage and some of these damaged fibers show abnormal FC, which may account for motor deficits and cognitive decline observed in PD. The combined use of DTI and rs-fMRI provides novel perspectives on the neural mechanisms underlying PD.

title: Tensor-based dynamic MRI reconstruction with non-convex ℓ<sub>r</sub><sup>p</sup> pseudo-norm and adaptive weighting.
authors: Zhao Y, Liu S, Cao J, Yang T.
abstract: Compressed sensing significantly accelerates dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by undersampling (k, t)-space, thereby formulating an ill-posed inverse problem that heavily depends on reconstruction algorithms. Dynamic MRI data exhibit low-rank property due to strong correlations in both spatial and temporal dimensions. In this paper, we propose a tensor-based ℓ r p pseudo-norm regularization for low-rank dynamic MRI reconstruction model, and introduce the weighting mechanism to adaptively distinguish between signal and noise, termed as TNWLR. We take tensor as processing unit to protect the inherent structure and facilitate the exploitation of its inherent structural correlations. The utilization of tensor-based ℓ r p pseudo-norm adequately exploits the spatial and temporal redundancies, and provides a flexible non-convex approximation to the rank function. In addition, using the weighting mechanism enables the suppression of noise and artifacts while better preserving the low-rank structure. The alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) provides an efficient solution framework for the proposed model due to its ability to decouple complex constraints. Compared with representative reconstruction methods, extensive experiments on multi-coil brain and liver DCE-MRI datasets demonstrate improved quantitative performance and better visual preservation of anatomical structures and fine details, and strong robustness to noise.

title: State-space dynamics of joint coordination reveal preserved directional structure across running speeds.
authors: Garofolini A, Sparrow WA, Begg R.
abstract: Understanding whether locomotor demands are accommodated by reorganising inter-joint coordination or by scaling an existing coordination pattern is a fundamental question in biomechanics and motor control. We examined whether the directional organisation of ankle-knee moment coordination is preserved across running speeds using a state-space representation of their continuous interaction. Sagittal-plane ankle and knee moments were analysed in 31 experienced runners (30 male, 1 female; 28 competitive and 3 elite) running at 2.5, 3.5, and 4.5 m·s -1 . Trajectory geometry was characterised by loop area, path length, major-axis orientation, and anisotropy, while trajectory-attached vectors quantified the magnitude and direction of progression through four intrinsically defined coordination segments: Loading, Transfer, Propulsion, and Release. Increasing speed markedly expanded the coordination trajectory, increasing loop area and path length (both p < 0.001), with smaller changes in major-axis orientation (p = 0.003) and anisotropy (p = 0.005). Progression magnitude also increased with speed (p < 0.001), with a Speed × Segment interaction showing that the magnitude of this increase differed across coordination segments (p = 0.006). In contrast, although vector direction showed a significant effect of speed (p = 0.0016), reflecting modest overall directional shifts, but no significant Speed × Segment interaction (p = 0.084): the characteristic directional sequence through Loading, Transfer, Propulsion, and Release was preserved. Thus, running faster scales ankle-knee mechanical coordination while the segment-dependent directional structure was largely preserved. These findings distinguish increased mechanical demand from a clear reorganisation of inter-joint mechanical coordination across running speeds.

title: Serum P1NP is associated with hip bone mineral density gains after romosozumab readministration following bisphosphonate therapy in women with osteoporosis.
authors: Kobayashi T, Kobayakawa T, Morimoto T, Nakamura Y.
abstract: The association between baseline total P1NP and BMD response to romosozumab readministration following bisphosphonate therapy in women with osteoporosis remains unclear. This multicenter study found that higher baseline total P1NP was independently associated with greater 12-month hip BMD gains, although these findings require further validation. Purpose To investigate the association between baseline serum total procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide (P1NP) levels and subsequent changes in bone mineral density (BMD) after romosozumab readministration following bisphosphonate therapy in women with osteoporosis. Methods This multicenter study included 22 women (mean age, 76.7 years) with osteoporosis who received a second 12-month course of romosozumab following bisphosphonate therapy. Total P1NP was assessed (mean, 18.6 μg/L) at baseline. Lumbar spine (LS), total hip (TH), and femoral neck (FN) BMD were assessed at baseline and 12 months, and percent changes were calculated. Multivariable linear regression analyses evaluated associations between baseline total P1NP and BMD changes, adjusting for potential confounders. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated the ability of baseline total P1NP to identify patients achieving a ≥ 3% increase in BMD at 12 months. Results BMD increased by ≥3% in 68.2%, 27.3%, and 36.4% of patients at the LS, TH, and FN, respectively. Higher baseline total P1NP levels were independently associated with greater 12-month increases in TH BMD (adjusted β, 0.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.03-0.59) and FN BMD (adjusted β, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.12-0.72), but not LS BMD (adjusted β, 0.18; 95% CI, -0.28 to 0.64). The optimal baseline total P1NP cutoff for identifying hip BMD responders was 14.8 μg/L, with an area under the curve of 0.714. Conclusion Higher baseline total P1NP levels were independently associated with greater 12-month hip BMD gains. Baseline total P1NP may help identify potential hip BMD responders, but these exploratory findings require validation.

title: Reply to: Accounting for pubertal maturation in the vitamin D-bone mineral density association in youth with type 1 diabetes.
authors: Tantivit N, Volkening LK, Renthal NE, Jacobsen CM, Laffel LM.

title: Occipital pressure injury in the beach-chair position: a report of two cases and a review of the literature.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Alshanqiti B, Imam M, Gokaraju K, Gulihar A.
abstract: Pressure-related occipital complications of the beach-chair position have been attributed to headrest compression, prolonged immobilisation or systemic hypoperfusion. We present two patients who developed postoperative pressure alopecia and lesser occipital neuropraxia after shoulder arthroscopy on a T-MAX (Smith & Nephew, Andover, MA) beach-chair, used in its standard articulating-cradle and foam-mask configuration. Both remained normotensive throughout, with continuous cerebral oximetry showing no desaturation, and both were positioned in neutral alignment without rotation. One developed a well-demarcated patch of occipital alopecia after 92 min; the other developed lesser occipital neuropraxia after a 180-minute procedure. Both recovered fully, at four and five months respectively. Building on earlier reports implicating the retention straps alongside rotation and duration, we propose that in the near-upright position used here, at a trunk inclination of approximately 80 degrees, the load pressing on the occiput is supplied in part by the straps rather than by gravity alone. Because interface pressures were not measured, this remains a hypothesis requiring direct testing. We describe the layered padding and repositioning protocol subsequently adopted in our unit, emphasising pressure redistribution and repeated intraoperative checks of head position. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level V, Case Report.

title: Multidisciplinary Learning Profiles in Surgical Services: A VARK and Experiential Learning Theory Analysis.
authors: Ullrich LA, Obisesan O.
abstract: Background Surgical services engage multidisciplinary residents from various specialties; however, the educational delivery frequently adopts a "one-size-fits-all" model. This reliance on passive, aural-visual instruction may not adequately address residents' diverse cognitive preferences, leading to a misalignment between instructional design and residents' specific needs. Objective To identify Visual, Aural, Read/Write, and Kinesthetic (VARK) learning preferences among surgical and nonsurgical residents who rotate through surgery services and examine associations with specialty, gender, and postgraduate year (PGY). Design This is a single-institution, retrospective, cross-sectional study that assessed VARK learning style profiles in general surgery, emergency medicine (EM), obstetrics and gynecology (OB-GYN), and orthopedics residents through the lens of Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory, using descriptive statistics and Chi-square analyses. Setting St. Luke's University Health Network, at the level I and level II academic trauma centers located in Bethlehem and Easton, Pennsylvania. Participants A total of 123 residents in general surgery, EM, OB-GYN, and orthopedics who rotated through Trauma and Surgical Critical Care from 2023 to 2025. Results This study included 78 male and 45 female residents. Multimodal was the most common preference (N = 60; 48.8%), followed by Kinesthetic (N = 40; 32.5%). OB-GYN uniquely favored Aural as a secondary preference, while EM and Orthopedics demonstrated the strongest Kinesthetic profiles. Gender was statistically significantly associated with VARK preferences (p = 0.037). Females predominantly preferred Multimodal (28; 62.2%) compared to males (28; 41%). In contrast, males showed higher Kinesthetic preferences (27; 34.6%) than females (13; 28.9%). Learning profiles remained stable across PGY levels. Conclusions These findings indicate that a uniform instructional approach is suboptimal. Educators should move away from passive observation to active, multimodal engagement, incorporating kinesthetic and specialty-aligned strategies to better support the diverse educational needs of residents in high-acuity surgical services.

title: Modified Autologous Biceps Acromioclavicular and Horizontal Neutralization (AutoBAHN) Technique Using a Free Biceps Tendon Autograft for Acromioclavicular Joint Stabilization.
authors: Gruber T, Van Eecke E, Lance L, Leschinger T, Scheibel M.
abstract: We present a modification to the autologous biceps acromioclavicular stabilization and horizontal neutralization technique. In contrast to the original technique, we propose releasing the long head of the biceps tendon (LHB) at the origin and securing the proximal portion to the scapular neck in either an inlay or onlay fashion. Similar to the original technique, the distal portion of the LHB is routed through the clavicle and secured with an interference screw. Next, the LHB is passed over the acromioclavicular joint and anchored in the lateral acromion, providing vertical and horizontal stabilization. This modification aims to preserve the fundamental biomechanical principles and advantages of the original technique, using a local, strong, and autologous graft that avoids donor site morbidity and allograft-related concerns. This technique expands the indication, offering a practical and versatile alternative for acromioclavicular joint reconstruction when preservation of the native LHB insertion is not feasible or desirable.

title: MYCN-amplified spinal ependymoma: a three-patient case series and focussed literature review.
authors: Bettsworth FAJ, Hall HM, Griffiths S, Ganau M.
abstract: MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas are a rare, recently described aggressive subtype of ependymoma defined by molecular profiling. We present three cases: a 52-year-old man, a 37-year-old woman, and a 28-year-old man presented with progressive neurological symptoms and spinal cord lesions identified on magnetic resonance imaging. These cases demonstrate the challenges in radiological identification and the importance of histological and molecular profiling to guide aggressive treatment of MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Outcomes varied across cases from clinical stability to death, reflecting the heterogeneity of the clinical course. We offer a short literature review to contextualise the cases.

title: Longitudinal Progression of 6-Minute Walk Test-Derived Fatigability in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy: A Retrospective Study.
authors: Zanovello M, Sabbatini D, Paredi F, Romito A, Blasi L, Musso G, Pennuto M, Minicuci GM, Pegoraro E, Bello L, Sorarù G.
abstract: Introduction Fatigue is a major disabling symptom in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA), yet objective fatigability, the decline in physical performance during sustained activity, has not been characterized longitudinally. We aimed to characterize the progression of 6-min walk test (6MWT)-derived fatigability and its associations with disease severity. Methods In this retrospective longitudinal study of genetically confirmed SBMA patients able to walk, disease severity was assessed with 6MWT distance, the SBMA Functional Rating Scale (SBMA-FRS), its modified version (m-SBMA-FRS, the sum of trunk and lower-limb subscores), the Adult Myopathy Assessment Tool, and forced vital capacity. Fatigability was the percentage decline in distance walked between the first and sixth 6MWT minutes; values ≥ 10% indicated fatigability. Cross-sectional associations were assessed using logistic regression and Spearman correlations. Longitudinal trajectories were analyzed with generalized estimating equations. Results A total of 168 patients contributed 703 visits. Among 141 patients with baseline 6MWT total distance and distance per minute data, 65 (46.1%) were fatigable (median fatigability index 8.5%, IQR 16.8%). Fatigability was associated with the m-SBMA-FRS (OR 0.619, 95% CI 0.523-0.717) and 6MWT distance (OR 0.988, 95% CI 0.983-0.991; 0.53 per 50 m). Fatigability index correlated negatively with m-SBMA-FRS (ρ = -0.596) and 6MWT distance (ρ = -0.617). Fatigability increased over time (+1.61%/year, 95% CI +0.71 to +2.51), in parallel with 6MWT decline (-16.84 m/year, 95% CI -20.20 to -13.48). Discussion Fatigability is common in ambulant SBMA patients, worsens progressively over time, and is associated with lower-limb and trunk impairment, supporting its use in clinical assessment and natural history studies.

title: Image-guided decision-making in complex robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: vascular control, resection precision, and functional outcomes.
authors: Zhang C, Wu H, Yang Z, Wang Y, Gao B.
abstract: During robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), image-guided techniques provide increasingly detailed patient-specific information; however, their incremental clinical value for complex renal tumours remains unclear. This narrative review examines how 3D reconstruction, virtual reality or augmented reality, intraoperative ultrasound, indocyanine green fluorescence, and computational perfusion modelling influence vascular control and tumour resection. The review focuses specifically on patients with high nephrometry scores (R.E.N.A.L. or PADUA ≥ 10), completely endophytic or hilar lesions, and limited renal reserve. The evidence was synthesised using a RAPN-specific decision-to-outcome framework that distinguishes between anatomical information, documented changes in surgical planning, actual operative actions, preservation of viable and perfused renal parenchyma, and patient-level outcomes. Observational comparative studies suggest that image guidance may facilitate selective vascular management, adjust resection strategies, and reduce excessive parenchymal resection as reflected by certain metrics. Multiple cohort studies have reported positive associations with renal function, including postoperative renal parameters based on radionuclide imaging. However, randomised imaging trials have not yet demonstrated consistent or sustained functional benefits, particularly in highly complex tumours. Interpretation of study results is limited by the following factors: heterogeneity of the control groups, historical and surgeon-related confounders, potential cohort overlap, and the non-interchangeability of functional or surrogate endpoints. Future studies should quantify the incremental value of imaging techniques beyond standard of care, document planned versus actual decisions, and independently assess ipsilateral renal function while evaluating oncological safety, workflow requirements, and costs. Currently, image guidance is best viewed as an optional decision-support tool, based on actionable anatomical uncertainty rather than hypothesised long-term functional benefits.

title: Image-guided ablation treatment of Desmoid tumors: an approach for management and integration into the national comprehensive cancer network ® guidelines.
authors: Burke CJ, Block JJ, Ingham M, Samim M.
abstract: Desmoid tumors are proliferative mesenchymal tumors arising from musculoaponeurotic structures. Although lacking the ability to metastasize, these neoplasms have a propensity to locally invade and recur, resulting in significant morbidity and reduced quality of life. This variable natural history and unpredictable biologic behavior can complicate clinical management. Active surveillance may be appropriate as initial management, with systemic, surgical and other local treatment options considered depending on the extent of disease progression, in accordance with the current National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines. Notably, image-guided percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as an effective treatment option for rapid local control and sustained lesion regression. The efficacy of cryoablation in the management of these tumors is now supported by an increasing body of literature. This article will review the pathophysiology and natural history of desmoid tumors, together with treatment indications and national cancer guidelines. Image-guided ablation techniques will be described as well as how these options can fit into clinical paradigms and management pathways.

title: Dimensionality reduction of space-related metrics in elite football using factor analysis.
authors: Krampe L, Memmert D, Klemp-Weins M.
abstract: Spatial organisation is fundamental to understanding football tactics and phase-dependent coordination. However, the high intercorrelation between existing spatial metrics suggests significant redundancy. This study aims to identify the latent dimensions of spatial positioning in- and out-of-possession to refine the theoretical framework of space in professional football. An open-source dataset comprising seven male German Bundesliga matches was utilised to analyse team length, width, height, surface area, convex hull, team centroid, team spread, stretch index, Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagram. Ball possession status served as the independent variable. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients were calculated, while data suitability was examined using the KMO statistic and Bartlett's test of sphericity. An exploratory factor analysis was performed to identify underlying latent constructs. High intercorrelation among spatial metrics justified factor analysis to reduce redundancy. The analysis reveals three consistent spatial dimensions that explain team organisation, regardless of possession status. These dimensions account for 77.1% and 75.5% of the variance, respectively, with the first dimension representing almost half of the variance in each case. Factor analysis reduces complex spatial data into three functional dimensions: 'team dispersion', 'longitudinal dispersion', and 'longitudinal positioning'. This facilitates a concise yet comprehensive interpretation of tactical structures and performance analysis.

title: Delayed Implantation of a Maxillary Central Incisor Using a Modified Anatomic Healing Abutment and Transmembrane-Fixation Guided Bone Regeneration: A Case Report.
authors: Ma J, Li W.
abstract: Maxillary anterior bone loss complicates implant surgery. We adopted a modified abutment plus transmembrane-fixed GBR for delayed implantation in a 21-year-old patient. In this single case, the combined protocol was clinically feasible and associated with favorable short-term esthetic and functional outcomes.

title: Connecting Ligament Tears of the Lateral Meniscus in the Popliteal Hiatus Region: An Arthroscopic Classification Including 4 Types.
authors: Sun LN, Yan S, Shu H, Wei W.
abstract: Purpose To describe an arthroscopic classification system for connecting ligament tears in the popliteal hiatus of the lateral meniscus and describe their repair technique. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the data of patients who underwent lateral meniscus repair between 2019 and 2023. Inclusion criteria included isolated or combined tears of the connecting ligaments in the popliteal hiatus. All patients underwent arthroscopic examination and/or repair and were followed up for a minimum of 1 year. Tears were classified arthroscopically into 4 types: type 1, isolated radial tear of the meniscofibular ligament; type 2, isolated longitudinal tear of the meniscofibular ligament; type 3, isolated longitudinal tear of the posterior popliteomeniscal fascicle; and type 4, combined longitudinal tear of meniscofibular ligament and posterior popliteomeniscal fascicle. Clinical outcomes were assessed using Lysholm, Tegner, and International Knee Documentation Committee scores. Knee magnetic resonance imaging was performed at 1 year postoperatively.
