Results Among 188 patients with lateral meniscus tears, 24 (12.8%) had connecting ligament tears in the popliteal hiatus. These included 3 type 1 (12.5%), 4 type 2 (16.7%), 8 type 3 (33.3%), and 9 type 4 (37.5%) lesions. Mean postoperative Lysholm, Tegner, and International Knee Documentation Committee scores significantly improved compared with preoperative values (all P Conclusions This study describes an arthroscopic classification of popliteal hiatus-lateral meniscus tears. Additionally, all-inside suture arthroscopic repair of the popliteal hiatus ligament-lateral meniscus complex led to favorable patient-reported outcomes at short-term follow-up. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

title: Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes of Arthroscopic Free Bone Grafts Versus Latarjet Procedures for Anterior Shoulder Instability with Glenoid Bone Loss: A Systematic Review.
authors: Nguyen CD, Farquharson R, Wang E, Romero MR, Marks LA, Marigi EM, Tokish JM, Hassebrock JD.
abstract: Purpose of review Arthroscopic free bone grafts have emerged as an alternative bone augmentation technique for the management of anterior shoulder instability with glenoid bone loss. While coracoid transfer procedures remain widely used, free bone graft techniques have gained interest because of their anatomic restoration and avoidance of coracoid-related morbidity. The purpose of this systematic review is to synthesize the current available literature on arthroscopic reconstruction of the glenoid arc, evaluating its efficacy, safety, and clinical outcomes relative to arthroscopic and open Latarjet procedures. Recent findings A total of 37 studies (43 cohorts; 2,073 patients) met inclusion criteria: 18 arthroscopic free bone graft, 15 arthroscopic Latarjet, and 10 open Latarjet cohorts. Most of the studies were Level IV evidence, and consisted primarily of small, retrospective case series. Across all three procedures, postoperative pain improved to 1.1-1.2 on the VAS, and more than 90% of patients returned to sport. Recurrence or instability rates were 2.3%, 2.8%, and 2.2%, respectively (p = 0.791), and graft nonunion 3.0%, 6.0%, and 3.7% (p = 0.051). Within arthroscopic free bone graft cohorts, nonunion was 1.2% for iliac crest autograft, 22.5% for iliac crest allograft, and none for distal tibial allograft or scapular spine autograft (p < 0.001). Graft resorption was 6.7%, 3.4%, and 4.1% (p = 0.259), reaching 13.7% with distal tibial allograft. Other complications were more frequent after arthroscopic free bone graft (8.4%) than arthroscopic (4.7%) or open Latarjet (5.0%; p = 0.017). Arthroscopic free bone graft demonstrates favorable short- to mid-term clinical outcomes, with improvements in pain, return to sport, and recurrence rates that fall within the range reported for coracoid transfer procedures. Graft nonunion and resorption were low overall, although nonunion clustered in iliac crest allograft cohorts and other complications were more frequent after arthroscopic free bone graft. Interpretation is limited by the predominance of small, retrospective case series and heterogeneous outcome reporting. Higher-level prospective and comparative studies are warranted to better define the indications, radiographic healing characteristics, and long-term durability of arthroscopic free bone graft in the management of anterior shoulder instability.

title: Arthroscopic Targeted Anchor Placement During Broström Repair: A Minimally Invasive Technique Guide.
authors: Halpern R, Spadafora P, Martin KD, Efremov K.
abstract: Ankle sprains are among the most common orthopaedic injuries, with 20% to 30% of patients progressing to chronic lateral ankle instability despite conservative management. Arthroscopic lateral ankle ligament repair has shown outcomes comparable with open Broström repair while allowing treatment of concomitant intra-articular pathology. However, standard arthroscopic techniques may limit accurate anchor placement on the fibular footprint or require an accessory anterolateral portal, increasing incision burden, technical complexity, and risk to the superficial peroneal nerve. We describe an easily reproducible, arthroscopic targeted anchor placement technique for Broström repair using a 1.9-mm needlescope without the need for an accessory viewing portal. The procedure uses standard anteromedial and anterolateral portals, with the needlescope advanced directly to the anterior talofibular ligament fibular footprint for visualization. Knotless suture anchors are placed through the needlescope cannula, eliminating the need for an accessory anterolateral portal and the need for multiple assistants. This minimally invasive technique reduces incision burden while maintaining precise anchor placement. By avoiding an accessory lateral portal, it may decrease the risk of superficial peroneal nerve injury while preserving the benefits of arthroscopic lateral ankle ligament repair.

title: Arthroscopic Stabilization Reduces Recurrence but May Delay Return to Sport After First-Time Traumatic Anterior Shoulder Dislocation in Elite Male Athletes: A Systematic Review.
authors: Fraser C, Sedlacek D, Letts J, Brown D, Talbot W, Ralph-Wilkie J, Sattler L.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate arthroscopic stabilization versus nonoperative management for first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation in adult athletes, with a focus on recurrent instability, return-to-play rates, and time to return to play. Methods Five databases were searched from inception to July 2025. Studies comparing arthroscopic stabilization versus nonoperative management in adult athletes (≥18 years) with first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation were included. The primary outcome was recurrent instability. Secondary outcomes included return-to-play rates and time to return to play. A narrative synthesis was performed given the nonrandomized and heterogeneous nature of included studies. Evidence certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Results Five studies (232 participants: 111 operative, 121 nonoperative) were included. Recurrent instability rates ranged from 3% to 14% in the operative group and 24% to 80% in the nonoperative group. Return-to-play rates were high for both approaches (operative: 93%-100%; nonoperative: 97%-100%). Nonoperative management was associated with earlier return to sport (2.3-5.7 weeks vs 18.7-39.3 weeks for operative management in studies reporting this outcome). All studies involved elite athletes, with female athletes substantially under-represented. Conclusions Arthroscopic stabilization was consistently associated with lower rates of recurrent instability than nonoperative management after first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation but required a longer time to return to play. Nonoperative management enabled an earlier return to play but was associated with higher recurrence. The evidence is limited primarily to male military, collegiate, and professional athletes, restricting generalizability to female, recreational, and broader adult athletic populations. Level of evidence Level III, systematic review of Level II and III studies.

title: Arthroscopic Physeal-Sparing Suture-Anchor Fixation for Pediatric Femoral-Side Posterior Cruciate Ligament Avulsion.
authors: Li Q, Yu R, Zhang Y, Jiang Q, Chen D.
abstract: Femoral-side posterior cruciate ligament injuries are rare in skeletally immature patients, and reconstruction using transphyseal tunnels carries the risk of growth disturbance. Primary repair, when feasible, provides a physeal-sparing and tissue-preserving alternative. Arthroscopic suture-anchor repair offers a safe and effective treatment option for pediatric femoral-side posterior cruciate ligament avulsions, preserving the native ligament and avoiding the potential complications associated with tunnel-based reconstruction.

title: All-Inside Double-Bundle Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction With Hamstring Autograft.
authors: Yang Z, Liu Y, Lin Y, Ji M, Lu J.
abstract: This technical report describes a reproducible all-inside double-bundle anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction technique performed through standard arthroscopic portals. The technique integrates the anatomical rationale of double-bundle reconstruction with the bone-preserving advantages of the all-inside approach. Independent preparation of the anteromedial and posterolateral grafts allows bundle-specific sizing and tensioning. Femoral and tibial closed-socket tunnels are created with preservation of adequate bone bridges to minimize the risk of tunnel convergence. Adjustable-loop cortical suspension devices are used on both the femoral and tibial sides, enabling independent bundle fixation at different knee flexion angles to better approximate native anterior cruciate ligament biomechanics. This technique aims to enhance anatomical restoration and rotational stability while reducing bone loss and graft length requirements. Technical pearls, potential pitfalls, and patient selection considerations are discussed. Although the technique is anatomically oriented and technically feasible, its clinical advantages over established reconstruction methods remain to be determined and warrant further investigation.

title: All-Arthroscopic Repair of Partial-Thickness Upper Border Subscapularis Tear With a Resorbable Bioinductive Bovine Collagen Implant.
authors: Winzenried AE, Allahabadi S.
abstract: Partial-thickness subscapularis tears are frequently underdiagnosed, and optimal management remains controversial. Bioinductive collagen implants have shown promising results in partial-thickness superior rotator cuff tears but have not been described for partial subscapularis pathology. This Technical Note describes a simple arthroscopic technique for bioinductive collagen implant repair or augmentation of partial-thickness subscapularis tears. This approach provides a reproducible biologic option for managing partial-thickness subscapularis tears while minimizing technical complexity.

title: Accuracy of different methods for predicting proximity to failure during resistance training.
authors: Holmes G, Jones MD, Cross R, Engel A, Walker ED, Hagstrom AD, Helms ER, Gibbs MT.
abstract: Proximity to failure (PTF) is increasingly considered in resistance training (RT). Two common methods used to prescribe PTF are rating of perceived exertion (RPE) and repetitions in reserve (RIR). This study compared the accuracy of RIR and RPE for predicting PTF. In a randomised crossover design, 32 participants (19 trained, 13 untrained) completed machine chest press and leg extension exercises at 75% of one-repetition maximum. Participants completed two experimental sessions, one using RIR and one using Borg-RPE. Experimental session (RIR/RPE) and exercise order were randomised. During each set, participants indicated when they believed they had reached 2 RIR or 8 RPE and then continued to momentary failure. Accuracy was calculated as the difference between actual repetitions remaining to failure and the number predicted at the verbal call. No significant differences in accuracy were observed between RIR and Borg-RPE for either exercise (chest press: mean difference -0.03 repetitions, 95% CI - 0.50 to 0.44, p = 0.893; leg extension: mean difference 0.16 repetitions, 95% CI - 0.39 to 0.71, p = 0.556). Training status did not influence the difference in accuracy between methods. These findings indicate that Borg-RPE and RIR produce similar accuracy when estimating PTF during machine-based RT under the conditions tested.

title: ASO Visual Abstract: Primum Non Nocere: Ethical Considerations of Cytoreductive Surgery and Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) in Peritoneal Malignancies.
authors: Williams JK, Wong W, Viana SW, Putman M, Applewhite M, Angelos P, Ong C, Merkow R, Polite B, Shergill A, Amin M, Posner MC, Möller MG.

title: Within-player load-wellness monitoring and lower-limb pain in elite female football: A reproducible secondary analysis of the SoccerMon dataset.
authors: Liu Y, Li H.
abstract: Routine athlete-monitoring data can test whether within-player changes in training load and wellness precede health problems, but sparse outcomes and incomplete reporting complicate inference. We conducted a reproducible secondary longitudinal analysis of the public SoccerMon dataset, comprising 50 players from two Norwegian elite women's football teams monitored in 2020-2021. The outcome was onset on day t (the index player-day) of a self-reported lower-limb pain/injury episode after a 7-day episode washout. The primary risk set contained 42 onset-days from 15 players; the complete-case soreness interaction analysis contained 28 onset-days from nine event players. Under retrospective full-period within-player standardization, the focal acute-load x soreness interaction was estimated below 1.0 by Firth logistic regression (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.45-0.97), but uncertainty remained substantial. When within-player standardization was recalculated using only observations available before each day, the interaction attenuated to OR 0.97 (0.73-1.25). These data therefore do not provide stable evidence that within-player load deviations or load x wellness interactions are associated with next-day self-reported lower-limb pain onset. Sparse events, event concentration, missing monitoring data, and team/season imbalance further limit precision. In practice, daily load and wellness signals should be interpreted as contextual longitudinal information rather than as stand-alone next-day risk thresholds.

title: Weight loss at a cost: Semaglutide and PYY3-36 aggravate pre-existing metabolic osteoporosis in female Wistar rats.
authors: Kloock S, Zytner P, Geiger N, Sequeira V, Schmitt-Böhrer A, Felker J, Sarwar H, Weich A, Ignatius A, Fassnacht M, Haffner-Luntzer M, Dischinger U.
abstract: Incretin mimetics like semaglutide and peptide YY3-36 (PYY3-36) reduce appetite and body weight, however their individual and combined effects on bone in the setting of metabolic disease and associated osteoporosis (MetOP) lack mechanistic insights. Here, female Wistar rats were randomized to: [1] Healthy control, [2] MetOP-Saline, [3] MetOP-Sema, [4] MetOP-PYY, [5] MetOP-Sema+PYY. Animals in group 2-5 received a "Western diet" in combination with nitric oxide synthase inhibitor L-NAME to induce MetOP as previously described. Randomization to treatments occurred in week 9. After 16 weeks, femora were collected for micro-computed-tomography, histological analysis, RNA-seq, and qPCR. Serum was analyzed for bone turnover markers and steroid profiles (LC-MS/MS). Semaglutide alone and in combination with PYY3-36 significantly reduced body weight. Semaglutide induced a modest reduction in trabecular bone volume fraction (BV/TV), whereas PYY3-36 alone and in combination with semaglutide caused more pronounced trabecular deterioration, with the combination group exhibiting increased trabecular separation. Cortical bone parameters were unaffected. Osteoclast numbers were increased in the semaglutide and PYY3-36 groups. Gene expression analysis demonstrated only mild changes in femora of semaglutide-treated rats, while PYY3-36 treatment significantly upregulated angiogenesis- and extracellular matrix-associated genes. Collectively, these findings suggest that semaglutide modestly impairs bone health. PYY3-36 treatment led to deteriorated bone markers and increased resorption, potentially limiting its clinical application. Semaglutide and PYY3-36 in combination further aggravate bone loss in MetOP. These findings highlight the need to evaluate gut hormone-based weight loss strategies for long-term skeletal safety, especially in the vulnerable setting of pre-existing osteoporosis.

title: Two-year functional outcomes of kinematic versus mechanical alignment in primary total knee arthroplasty: a single-surgeon propensity-matched study in an Asian population.
authors: Neo BXB, Patil VV, Tay KD, Pang HN, Yeo SJ, Liow MHL.
abstract: Background Optimal coronal alignment in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains controversial, with kinematic alignment (KA) emerging as a patient-specific alternative to conventional mechanical alignment (MA). This study compared 2-year functional outcomes, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and complication rates between KA-TKA and MA-TKA in a propensity score-matched cohort. Methods This retrospective single-surgeon study included 1978 consecutive primary TKAs (KA: n = 921, 2018-2023; MA: n = 1057, 2010-2014). After excluding 76 revision TKAs, 1902 primary TKAs were eligible. A further 441 patients with incomplete follow-up were excluded (KA: n = 293, 33.1%; MA: n = 148, 14.6%), leaving 1461 patients who underwent propensity score matching. Following 1:1 nearest-neighbour propensity score matching for age, sex, body mass index (BMI) and baseline PROMs, 536 matched pairs (n = 1,072) were analysed. Outcomes included range of motion, Knee Society Knee and Function Scores (KSKS, KSFS), Oxford Knee Score (OKS), SF-36, MCID attainment, satisfaction, complications and revision rates at 6 months and 2 years. Results Both groups showed substantial postoperative improvement across all outcomes. At 6 months, KA achieved higher postoperative KSKS (86.7 versus 85.3, p Conclusions KA-TKA was associated with statistically higher scores in selected functional domains and comparable MCID attainment, patient satisfaction and revision-free survival at 2 years. These findings suggest KA is a feasible alignment strategy for primary TKA in the short term, although longer-term prospective data are required to confirm these associations.

title: The perfect injection, six weeks too late? Rethinking ultrasound guidance in musculoskeletal care.
authors: Joseph SS, Hussain A, Tay A.

title: The Clinical Outcome of a Fluoroscopy-Free "4-Step Cam Resection" Technique Compared With the Traditional Technique for Arthroscopic Treatment of Cam-Type Femoroacetabular Impingement.
authors: Li Y, Feng Z, Wang X.
abstract: Purpose To compare the clinical outcomes of the novel fluoroscopy-free "4-step cam resection" technique with the traditional cam resection method for treating cam-type FAI during hip arthroscopy. No established consensus exists on a standardized, reproducible technique that ensures complete cam resection without intraoperative fluoroscopy, and residual anterolateral cam deformity remains a leading cause of persistent impingement and revision surgery. The present study was therefore performed to determine whether the 4-step technique improves the completeness of cam resection compared with the conventional single-position technique. Methods Patients with symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) who underwent the "4-step cam resection" technique between January 2021 and January 2022 were included. The 4-step intervention consisted of femoral head-neck osteoplasty performed sequentially with the hip placed in four positions: (i) 10° of flexion in maximal internal rotation; (ii) 10° of flexion in neutral rotation; (iii) 30° of flexion with rotation from internal to external; and (iv) 45° of flexion with rotation from internal to external. In the traditional technique, the cam lesion was resected with the hip in a single position of approximately 45° of flexion. No intraoperative fluoroscopy was used in either group. A historical control group extracted from our database was matched in a 1:1 ratio based on demographic and preoperative clinical variables. Outcomes were assessed using the Harris Hip Score (HHS), Hip Outcome Score (HOS), and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain. Radiographic measurements, including the lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) and alpha angle and gamma angle, were evaluated pre- and postoperatively. Results A total of 36 patients (36/40, 90.0%) in the study group (Group A, "4-step cam resection" technique) completed the final follow-up and 36 patients were matched as the control group (Group B, traditional technique). At a mean follow-up of 29 months, both groups demonstrated significant improvements in HOS, HHS, and VAS scores postoperatively (p Conclusion The "4-step cam resection" technique achieves comparable subjective outcomes compared with the traditional technique and is associated with a greater decrease of gamma angle, lower VAS score, and better HOS-Sports outcome.

title: Spatial patterns of plant life-forms along elevation and aridity gradients in temperate deserts of northern Xinjiang, China.
authors: Fei C, Dong YQ, An S.
abstract: Located in the arid hinterland of Central Asia, the mountain temperate deserts in Xinjiang are jointly shaped by elevational geographic constraints and the east-west-oriented drought stress gradient. Nevertheless, the joint coupling relationships between these two gradient factors and community-level vegetation structural attributes across woody and herbaceous plant functional groups remain unclarified quantitatively at present. In this study, we investigated four community structural attributes (plant height, vegetation coverage, population density, and aboveground biomass) across four plant life forms, namely shrubs, semi-shrubs, perennial herbs, and annual herbs, along elevational, latitudinal, and longitudinal gradients in five major desert sub-regions of northern Xinjiang: Altay (n = 159), Tacheng-Yili (n = 164), Bortala and Changji-Urumqi(n = 110) and Eastern Tianshan (n = 94).In total, 527 sampling plots were surveyed during the plant growing season from May to mid-September(Desert field surveys conducted each year from May to September for a total of 3 years); plot numbers were unevenly distributed across subregions according to landscape accessibility and habitat representativeness. No temporal repeated measurements on identical permanent plots were conducted, and all analyses were based on one-off spatial snapshot observations from each plot. Trend-fitting, Single-gradient pattern analysis were applied to examine the correlational relationships between geographic gradients and community structural attributes. The results of this study are as follows: (1) Community structural attributes exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity and mostly showed unimodal or parabolic trends along the elevational gradient, with relatively high community performance concentrated in the mid-elevation range of 700-1100 m. This observed elevational unimodal pattern is consistent with the expectation of the mid-domain effect, yet such hump-shaped distributions can also arise from climatic, edaphic or topographic filtering and cannot serve as definitive direct empirical evidence for geometric mid-domain constraints. (2) Community-level vegetation performance tended to decline from the relatively humid western subregions (Tacheng-Yili-Bortala) toward the hyper-arid eastern subregions (Changji-Urumqi, Eastern Tianshan), corresponding to the west-to-east decreasing precipitation gradient driven by westerly circulation. (3) Different plant life-forms displayed distinct correlational adaptive patterns along these combined geographic gradients: shrubs and semi-shrubs maintained relatively stable community dominance under drought and low-temperature conditions; perennial herbs tended to occur in relatively mesic mid-elevation habitats; annual herbs showed high responsiveness to water-related environmental variation. (4) Among surveyed subregions, Eastern Tianshan presented the lowest observed community-attribute values, while the Tacheng-Yili subregion exhibited the highest and most stable community structural status. Collectively, our findings demonstrate correlational associations of elevational constraints and the west-east drought gradient with community structural variation in mountain temperate desert plant assemblages. These observational results provide observational reference for developing region-targeted conservation, grazing management and ecological restoration strategies for Xinjiang's desert grassland ecosystems.

title: Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease: A NHIS-NDI linkage cohort study.
authors: Adebile TV, Oloyede T, Azu E, Olagunju M, Asifat O, Paul TM, Ipede O, Abwa W, Biswas P, Yu L.
abstract: Background Sleep duration is increasingly recognized as a component of cardiovascular health, yet its prognostic significance among adults with established heart disease remains unclear. We examined associations between sleep duration and mortality among US adults with heart disease. Methods We analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease participating in the 2004 National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Sleep duration was categorized as ≤6 hours, 7-8 hours, and ≥9 hours. Cox proportional hazards models stratified by variables violating the proportional hazards assumption estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Restricted cubic splines evaluated nonlinear dose-response relationships. Results During 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died, including 16.7% from heart-related causes and 32.6% from non-heart-related causes. Compared with 7-8 hours of sleep, long sleep duration (≥9 hours) was associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality (HR:1.51 [95% CI:1.32-1.73]), heart-related mortality (HR:1.53 [95% CI:1.22-1.92]), and non-heart-related mortality (HR:1.50 [95% CI:1.27-1.77]). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated nonlinear associations, with the lowest predicted mortality risk occurring at 6-7 hours. Findings remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses and age and sex subgroups. Conclusions Among US adults with heart disease, long sleep duration was consistently associated with higher risks of all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Sleep duration may represent a simple marker of residual risk that could enhance risk stratification among adults living with heart disease.

title: Selective lung isolation in thoracic spine tumour resection: an integrated anaesthetic approach.
authors: Chua C, Monteblanco CP, Sy Su KMC, Jose GRB.

title: Risk Factors for Diabetic Foot-Related Lower Extremity Amputation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
authors: Eteuati J, Ntiamoah ME, Pitesa R, Mahadevan G, Hill AG.
abstract: Background Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs. Methods Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS. Results Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). Ulcer severity was associated with amputation in every study assessing it, using five different classification systems. Prolonged ulcer duration carried an adjusted odds ratio of 10.3 (95% CI 4.06-26.13), and each additional preoperative day was associated with a 9.3% increase in the odds of major amputation. Neuropathy showed no independent association of meaningful size in any adjusted analysis, and HbA1c was not associated in the largest adjusted DFU cohort analysis, although a smaller study with 10 outcome events reported a positive association. Conclusion Peripheral arterial disease, ulcer severity, osteomyelitis, prior amputation, and delayed access to care were associated with LLA in LMIC settings. Neither neuropathy nor HbA1c showed an independent association of meaningful size in adjusted analyses of established DFU cohorts. Prospective LMIC cohorts using standardized definitions are needed.

title: Reading Korean historical trauma in China: A qualitative content analysis of Douban reviews of Han Kang's Human Acts and We Do Not Part.
authors: Geng J, Kong D, Li B.
abstract: Using 1,704 public Douban reviews, this study examines how Chinese readers respond to Korean historical trauma represented in Han Kang's Human Acts and We Do Not Part. We developed a 39-code binary coding frame from a 200-review development subset and froze it before formal corpus-wide coding. Two researchers independently coded a separate 400-review validation set, and a third adjudicated 893 disagreement code-cells to create the Human Reference. DeepSeek-V4-Pro then provided preliminary codes for the remaining 1,304 reviews. One researcher verified all 1,304 reviews, a different researcher independently audited 261 reviews under a prespecified blinded audit, and the third adjudicated 534 audit disagreement code-cells. The final 1,704 × 39 matrix shows that readers most often discuss literary form and aesthetics, ethical and memory-oriented reflection, overall evaluation and reading behavior, and affective or embodied response. Reviews of We Do Not Part discuss translation, editions, and reading difficulty more often, whereas reviews of Human Acts more often mention sadness, memory and witnessing, state violence, and broader ethical or political concerns. The strongest co-occurrence relationships included translation evaluation with translation-induced reading/comprehension difficulty, memory-oriented ethical reflection with literary witnessing, and language of heaviness or despair with embodied response. These pairwise results show that mediation-related, mnemonic, and affective responses each co-occur with closely related reception patterns within individual reviews. The findings show that Chinese reception of Korean historical-trauma fiction cannot be reduced to overall approval or disapproval. It also varies by work and by the ways readers connect literary form, translation, memory ethics, and affect in their responses.

title: Radiographic Accuracy of Identifying Anterolateral Tibial Plafond Involvement in Pronation External Rotation Ankle Fractures.
authors: Lee CM, Oosten J, Allahverdian A, O'Hara S, Rockov ZA, Audet M, Earhart JS, Ewing BA, Weatherford BM, Garlich JM, Marecek GS.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the rate of anterolateral tibial plafond involvement in pronation-external rotation (PER) ankle fractures and analyze the accuracy of radiographs, using CT as the reference standard among fractures with paired imaging, in detecting anterolateral tibial plafond involvement, impaction, and predicting surgeons' stated intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction, as determined by surgeon assessment of the imaging findings. Methods Design: Multi-institutional retrospective chart review. Setting Two level 1 trauma centers in the United States. Patient selection criteria Adult patients operative treated PER ankle fractures (AO/OTA 44C) from 2020-2022 and adequate preoperative radiographs, defined as an AP, mortise and lateral view of the injured ankle were included. A subset of these patients also had preoperative CT imaging of the injured ankle and were therefore evaluated with both imaging modalities. Outcome measurements and comparisons All images were reviewed by 4 fellowship-trained orthopaedic trauma surgeons. For this study, anterolateral tibial plafond involvement was defined as the presence of any fracture line or impaction involving the anterolateral plafond, and impaction (a subset of involvement) as where the anterolateral plafond was crushed and depressed. A finding was considered present if at least 3 of the 4 reviewers indicated its presents on first-round responses. The rates of involvement and impaction were determined among all fractures based on radiographs alone, and separately among the subset of patients with paired radiographs and CT. Using CT as the gold standard, we determined the accuracy of radiographs and compared surgeons' stated intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction of the anterolateral plafond fracture before versus after review of CT imaging. Results Eighty-three PER ankle fractures were included (mean age 43.3 years [range, 17-89]; 63.9% male), of which 37 also had CT scans (mean age 39.2 years [range, 17-83]; 73.0% male). Among all 83 fractures, anterolateral tibial plafond involvement and impaction were identified on radiographs in 14.5% and 4.8% of cases, respectively. Among the 37 PER ankle fractures with both plain radiographs and CT scans, anterolateral plafond involvement was identified in 13.5% of radiographs versus 37.8% of CT scans (p=0.346) and impaction in 5.4% of radiographs versus 8.1% of CT scans (p=0.005). The diagnosis of impaction using plain radiographs was correct in 66.7% of fractures compared with CT, resulting in a sensitivity of 67%, specificity of 100%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 100%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97%. The diagnosis of anterolateral plafond involvement using plain radiographs had a sensitivity of 21%, specificity of 91%, PPV of 60%, and NPV of 66% compared with CT. Plain radiographs predicted surgeons' stated intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction in 66.7% of cases and had a PPV of 100% and NPV of 97%. Conclusions In PER ankle fractures, the rates of anterolateral tibial plafond involvement and impaction were 37.8% and 8.1% on CT, respectively. Plain radiographs demonstrated high specificity but limited sensitivity for identifying both impaction (67%) and involvement (21%). Because anterolateral plafond impaction was relatively uncommon in PER fractures, a CT obtained for this purpose alone would yield a positive finding in only a minority of cases; nonetheless, CT should be considered for PER ankle fractures more broadly, given that plain radiographs miss a meaningful proportion of both involvement and impaction and interobserver reliability of radiograph-based assessment was poor. Level of evidence Prognostic level III.

title: Pyramid-level training with stain normalization for breast cancer lymph-node metastasis segmentation in whole-slide images.
authors: Almobayed H, Yilmaz A, Senturk U, Erdogan Duzcu S, Akgül A.
abstract: Whole-slide histopathology images encode metastatic tissue information simultaneously at multiple spatial scales, from fine cellular morphology at high magnification to broad tissue architecture at low magnification. Existing segmentation models commonly operate at a single fixed resolution, leaving complementary information distributed across the whole-slide image pyramid underused. We present a multilevel segmentation framework with stain-normalization preprocessing that trains a unified model jointly across four study-defined WSI pyramid views (5×-40×), integrating Vahadane stain normalization and structured class-balanced sampling stratified by pyramid level, dataset, and tissue class. Applied to a 280-slide CAMELYON16/CAMELYON17 study cohort under strict slide-level data separation (196 training, 42 validation, 42 held-out test slides), the framework achieves a Dice coefficient of 92.39% on the held-out test set. Relative to the single-scale U-Net baseline (89.00%), the paired slide-level improvement is 3.39 percentage points (95% bootstrap CI: 3.19-3.60 pp; Cohen's dz=4.98; two-sided permutation p < 0.00001). Per-level evaluation confirms that full pyramid fusion outperforms each individual scale, while a boundary-focused L1 audit yields a mean HD95 of 53.88 pixels (95% CI: 50.28-57.64). The contribution is therefore a training-sampling and evaluation pipeline rather than a new network layer or architecture. These results show that multiresolution training, stain normalization, structured sampling, and leakage-controlled evaluation can materially improve breast lymph-node metastasis segmentation on established WSI benchmarks. A supplementary external cross-dataset evaluation on 103 paired BCSS breast-histopathology ROIs, performed without retraining or fine-tuning, yielded a pooled Dice of 70.58%, IoU of 54.54%, precision of 55.95%, and recall of 95.57%; the mean per-ROI Dice was 67.89% (95% bootstrap CI: 65.00-70.76%). These external results demonstrate substantial sensitivity to tumor-like tissue under a different image source and semantic annotation scheme, while also exposing the expected effect of annotation granularity and class-definition mismatch on overlap and boundary metrics.

title: Psychological resilience among informal care partners of individuals with mild cognitive impairment.
authors: Villarejo-Galende A, García-Arcelay E, Almagro M, Balasa M, Piñol-Ripoll G, Landete L, Abellan I, Berbel A, Espejo B, Baquero M, Marin J, Franco-Macias E, Viñuela Fernández F, Feria-Vilar I, Perez-Vieitez C, Rodríguez-Espinosa N, Puig-Pijoan A, Bargay Pizarro E, Rodríguez-Rodríguez E, Rodrigo J, Boada M, Sánchez-Juan P, Manzano S, Maurino J.
abstract: Background Care partners of individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) encounter unique psychosocial and operational challenges. While dementia research traditionally focuses on advanced cognitive decline, the factors underlying positive psychological adaptation during the early MCI window remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of psychological resilience among informal care partners of individuals with MCI and identify independent multivariable correlates of high adaptive capacity. Methods We conducted a multicenter, cross-sectional study across 19 specialized memory clinics in Spain in collaboration with the Spanish Confederation of Alzheimer's Disease and Other Dementias (CEAFA). Psychological resilience was quantified using the 14-Item Resilience Scale (RS-14). Secondary outcomes included health-related quality of life, caregiver strain, psychological distress, dyadic relationship quality, and perceived affiliate stigma. Multivariable logistic regression was employed to identify independent predictors of moderate-to-high resilience (RS-14 score >81). Results We analyzed 196 care partners (mean age: 63.5 [SD 13.1] years, 62.8% women). Overall, 63.3% (n = 124) demonstrated moderate-to-high resilience. In bivariate analyses, higher resilience correlated with superior quality of life, greater sense of competence, and enhanced relationship quality between care partners and care recipients. In multivariable logistic regression, only robust perceived social support (OR=2.37, 95% CI 1.78-3.14, p Conclusions Psychological resilience strongly aligns with care partner well-being prior to the onset of overt care-recipient dependency. Early psychosocial interventions designed to reinforce functional social support networks and mitigate internalized stigma may offer a valuable framework for supporting care partner well-being.

title: Prevalence, patterns of cytopenia, and its associated risk factors among HIV-positive adults on HAART at ART follow-up clinics in Dawuro Zone public hospitals, Dawuro, Ethiopia, 2025. Multi-center-based cross-sectional study.
authors: Abate A, Hurisa SG, Ibrahim M, Mitiku S.
abstract: Background Cytopenia, defined as a critical reduction in one or more hematopoietic lineages, remains the most prevalent immuno-hematological complication among HIV-infected individuals. Its multifactorial etiology involves direct viral suppression of the bone marrow, secondary opportunistic infections, and the adverse effects of Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy (HAART). Clinically, cytopenias are associated with accelerated disease progression, suboptimal therapeutic response, and increased morbidity. Despite these significant health implications, there is a paucity of data regarding the prevalence, patterns, and associated risk factors of cytopenia among HIV-positive adults on HAART in the Dawuro Zone of Ethiopia. Objective To assess the prevalence, patterns, and associated risk factors of cytopenia among HIV-positive adults on HAART in ART follow-up clinics in the Dawuro Zone public hospitals. Method A multi-center, cross-sectional study was conducted from March 1 to April 30, 2025, across three public hospitals in the Dawuro Zone [i.e., Tercha General Hospital, Tocha Primary Hospital, and Gessa Primary Hospital], Ethiopia. Eligible participants were recruited from HIV patients on HAART at the follow-up clinics who were randomly selected until the target sample size of 231 was achieved. The study aimed to determine the prevalence and pattern of cytopenia using plain and ethylene diamine tetra-acetic acid (EDTA) for CBC analysis as per the WHO definition of hematologic abnormalities. In addition, cytopenia-associated risk factors like sociodemographic, clinical, nutritional, medication, behavioral factors, comorbidities, and the presence of opportunistic infections were assessed via interviewer-administered structured questionnaires. Univariate analyses were performed to establish the prevalence of cytopenia. Potential risk factors were examined using bivariate logistic regression at a 95% confidence interval (p Result The study included 231 participants with response rates of 230 (99.6%). The prevalence of cytopenia was 64 (27.8%), of which 34 (14.8%) were unicytopenia, 23 (10%) had bi-cytopenia, and only 7 (3%) had pancytopenia. In multivariate analysis, cytopenia was significantly associated with age > 50 years (AOR = 5.1, 95% CI: 1.3-2.1, P = .023), male gender (AOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2-6.5, P = .014), bedridden patients (AOR = 6.0, 95% CI: 1.31-27.2, P = .02), having opportunistic infection (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 1.1-18.4, P = .032), LPV/r-based ART regimen (AOR = 6.06, 95% CI: 1.1-26.6, P = 0.02), poor drug adherence (AOR = 6.97, 95% CI: 2.9-16.6, P = 0.0), and participants with a CD4 count Conclusion and recommendation In this study, the prevalence of cytopenia among adult HIV-positive adults was 27.8%, indicating a moderate burden. Male gender, older age, bedridden patients, opportunistic infections, LPV/r-based regimens, poor drug adherence, and CD4 counts below 499 cells/mm3 were significant associations with cytopenia. The routine and frequent CBC tests, and adequate adherence counseling before HAART and during follow-up time, may improve cytopenia among HIV-positive adults.

title: Preserved tendon reflexes in a clinically suspected sensory-predominant GBS-spectrum disorder: a case report.
authors: Min X, Liu W, Wang R, Yang X, Ke T, Zhang W, Zhang G, Guo X, Xiao Y.
abstract: Background Guillain-Barré syndrome usually comes to clinical attention because of progressive weakness and reduced or absent tendon reflexes. Some patients, however, present mainly with sensory symptoms and still have preserved reflexes, making early diagnosis more difficult. Case presentation A 71-year-old Han Chinese man presented with distal paresthesia after an episode of diarrhea, and the symptoms became noticeably worse over the next 2 days. The sensory disturbance spread in a glove-and-sock pattern and was accompanied by heaviness in the legs, difficulty walking, and mild distal weakness. Neurological examination showed reduced distal superficial sensation, preserved tendon reflexes, and no pathological reflexes. Brain MRI showed no clinically relevant abnormality, and spinal MRI showed degenerative changes without a definite central lesion explaining the symptoms. Cerebrospinal fluid showed protein of 590 mg/L with a reported white blood cell count of 0.001 × 10 6 /L, a pattern compatible with albuminocytologic dissociation. Because nerve conduction studies and electromyography were not completed during hospitalization, the diagnosis remained a clinically suspected sensory-predominant disorder within the GBS spectrum rather than electrophysiologically confirmed classic GBS. Clinical notes recorded improvement during hospitalization, and the patient regained independent ambulation after receiving intravenous immunoglobulin alongside supportive and adjunctive therapies. At a telephone follow-up approximately 12 months later, he reported no recurrence; no objective follow-up examination was available. Conclusions In patients with acute symmetric distal sensory symptoms after a gastrointestinal illness, preserved tendon reflexes do not by themselves exclude a GBS-spectrum disorder. In this patient, the clinical course and cerebrospinal fluid findings supported consideration of that diagnosis, but the absence of electrophysiological testing precluded confirmation. This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge posed by atypical sensory-predominant presentations and also highlights that, without electrophysiological confirmation, both subtype assignment and overall diagnostic certainty remain constrained.

title: Predicting Blood Flow in Reconstructed Intestines Based on Abdominal Aortic Calcification and Clinical Effects of Left Colic Artery Preservation in Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Subanalysis of the HiSCO-09 Study.
authors: Ishikawa S, Shimomura M, Shimizu W, Miguchi M, Ikeda S, Nakahara M, Mukai S, Yoshimitsu M, Kochi M, Ohdan H.
abstract: Aim To clarify the relationship between the abdominal aortic calcification score on preoperative computed tomography and intraoperative regional tissue oxygen saturation (rSO 2 ), assess the feasibility of predicting perfusion impairment through imaging, and evaluate whether left colic artery preservation improves blood flow and reduces the risk of anastomotic leakage in patients with impaired perfusion. Methods In this subanalysis of the HiSCO-09 trial, rSO 2 was measured using INVOS in the intestinal segment at the intended intestinal anastomosis site following mesenteric preparation as a blood flow indicator. Patients were categorized according to the abdominal aortic calcification score based on preoperative computed tomography findings into low (≤ 2.13 mL) and high (> 2.13 mL) groups. Results Of the 282 patients, the high abdominal aortic calcification group included 135 patients. Compared with the low group, the high group showed significantly higher incidence of anastomotic leakage (4.8% vs. 12.6%, p = 0.019) and consistently lower rSO 2 values. Abdominal aortic calcification score correlated negatively with rSO 2 at the anastomosis site (p = 0.011). Within the high group, left colic artery preservation was associated with higher rSO 2 and a lower incidence of anastomotic leakage (p = 0.032). Conclusions Preoperative abdominal aortic calcification assessment was weakly associated with reduced intraoperative rSO 2 . Exploratory subgroup analysis indicated that left colic artery preservation was associated with better perfusion and fewer anastomotic leakages in patients with high calcification. Although insufficient as a stand-alone predictor, abdominal aortic calcification may serve as a complementary factor in multifactorial preoperative risk assessments for future prospective evaluation.

title: Paired DXA and pQCT of bone parameters in a clinical paediatric population: A cluster analysis.
authors: Tan J, Hart NH, Chivers P, Rantalainen T, Barrat N, Beeson B, Siafarikas A.
abstract: Accurate assessment of bone health in paediatric clinical populations is needed for the prevention of both non-specific and condition-specific bone deficits. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), particularly "total body less head" (TBLH), is the preferred clinical measurement. However, peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) provides additional structural insights of value to a paediatric population. Criteria are needed to establish the value of pQCT beyond use in research settings. To determine the contributions of pQCT and DXA, we analysed data from 457 individuals from a Western Australian paediatric centre routinely employing joint DXA-pQCT imaging. Sex-specific cluster analysis was performed utilising DXA-TBLH BMD, pQCT (4% and 66% arm and leg volumetric density), age and height to define clinical phenotypes and guide decision making on adding pQCT to BMD analyses. Results showed DXA and pQCT measurements were positively correlated, particularly at the 4% site. Cluster analysis showed two clusters with lower bone density and higher fracture frequency characterised by malabsorption and bone mineral metabolism conditions in females, and bone mineral metabolism and neuromuscular conditions in males. DXA and pQCT variation was greatest in these clusters, with DXA being lower. Females showed greater variability between DXA and pQCT, with height as an influencing factor. These findings reinforce the utility of combined DXA and pQCT in paediatric bone health assessment particularly in high-risk groups.

title: Online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for people with multiple sclerosis with mild-to-moderate depression- protocol for a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study.
authors: Simpson R, Scandiffio J, Langer L, Munce S, Sureshkumar A, Feinstein A, Bayley M, Bowman C, Bruno TR, Ehde D, Knox K, Lai N, Smyth P, Sud A, Donkers SJ.
abstract: Background Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) is an effective treatment for recurrent depression in the general population and is recommended in clinical guidelines for those with mild-moderate depression. However, the effectiveness of MBCT in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) with mild to moderate depression is unknown. Further, how best to tailor and implement MBCT for PwMS is largely unstudied. This manuscript describes the study protocol for a hybrid-effectiveness study to evaluate online MBCT tailored for PwMS. Methods This type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study will employ an embedded mixed methods experimental design. Quantitative findings will be collected through a powered waitlist randomized controlled trial examining online MBCT in a minimum of 152 PwMS with case-ness of mild-moderate depression (Clinical Trials Gov #NCT07742579). The intervention will consist of an online 8-week MBCT course with weekly sessions conducted by qualified mindfulness instructors experienced int the care of PwMS. Questionnaires will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and 3 months later. The primary outcome will be depression, measured using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Score - Depression (HADS-D). An intention-to-treat analysis will be conducted. Qualitative findings will be collected through semi-structured interviews with 30-40 MBCT participants, HCPs, MBCT instructors, and MS decision makers. Thematic analyses will be used to analyze interview data. The RE-AIM PRISM tool will be used to evaluate implementation and mixed data assessed in a joint display. Conclusion The results from this study will provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of online MBCT in PwMS with mild to moderate depression, recommendations for intervention tailoring and implementation. Findings will be disseminated through traditional and novel, creative knowledge mobilization methods.

title: One-Stage Posterior-to-Anterior Ankle Arthroscopy Using a Single Operative Setup and Patient Repositioning Technique: A Technical Note.
authors: Paquot J, Roche D, Lopes R.
abstract: This technical note describes a 1-stage arthroscopic technique for the management of combined posterior and anterior ankle pathology that preserves standard patient positioning while reducing operative time and material costs. The procedure begins with posterior ankle arthroscopy performed in the prone position using standard posterior portals. After treatment of the posterior lesions, the patient is carefully repositioned to the supine position without redraping or changing instrumentation. The same sterile surgical field, operating table, and arthroscopic instruments are maintained throughout the procedure. Anterior ankle arthroscopy is then performed using standard anterior portals. Strict coordination between the surgical and anesthesia teams ensures safe patient repositioning while preserving sterility. This 1-stage technique allows arthroscopic treatment of combined anterior and posterior ankle pathology using familiar prone and supine positioning. By avoiding redraping and the use of duplicate sterile instrumentation, it optimizes surgical workflow, reduces operative time, and decreases material costs while providing a reproducible approach.

title: Multiorgan failure in a young patient with necrotizing fasciitis: a case report of septic shock progressing to mixed shock with fatal cardiac outcome.
authors: Kraus RF, Kaufmann C, Alt V, Kees MG.
abstract: Background Necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rare, life-threatening conditions requiring immediate and aggressive treatment. Despite advances in medical care, mortality remains high, largely due to septic shock and severe complications. Case representation We report the case of a young adult with necrotizing fasciitis (NF) of the left leg complicated by recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding and infective endocarditis, resulting in severe heart failure and ultimately leading to death. The fatal outcome was most likely attributable to prolonged sepsis with multiorgan involve- and impairment and a 1.5-cm paravalvular abscess caused by vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium. Conclusion The treatment of a septic patient with progressive heart failure highlights the value of an integrative, multidisciplinary approach to complex clinical decision-making and the real-world challenges that may require patient-tailored, nonstandard therapeutic strategies. Prompt diagnosis, aggressive surgical debridement, and rigorous management of complications are essential. In cases of aortic valve regurgitation causing heart failure, TAVI implantation might serve as a temporary bridge until definitive open valve replacement becomes feasible.

title: Modeling bone abnormalities in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Skeletal phenotypes, glucocorticoid responses, and translational considerations.
authors: Barroso E, Wang L, Li H.
abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is increasingly recognized as a multisystem disorder in which skeletal fragility is one of the major sources of morbidity. Bone deficits arise before loss of ambulation and in glucocorticoid-naïve patients, indicating that reduced mechanical loading and steroid toxicity are important but incomplete explanations. Animal models provide an opportunity to study the skeletal consequences of dystrophin deficiency, muscle degeneration, altered muscle-bone signaling, impaired growth, and glucocorticoid exposure. However, the bone phenotype varies markedly among models. The widely used C57BL/10-mdx mouse has a mild muscle phenotype and may exhibit preserved or increased cortical indices during growth, whereas DBA/2 J-mdx mice show more consistent growth and skeletal impairment. Compound murine models can intensify muscle disease but do not necessarily recapitulate human skeletal development. Dystrophin-deficient rats develop age-related trabecular deterioration, and golden retriever muscular dystrophy dogs show bone changes that track muscle structure and function, although skeletal characterization in large-animal models remains sparse. Glucocorticoid-treated mdx mice reproduce clinically relevant growth suppression, cortical thinning, suppressed bone formation, and reduced mechanical quality while retaining treatment-related gains in muscle performance. These models have supported proof-of-concept studies of bisphosphonates, intermittent parathyroid hormone, growth hormone, and mitochondrial peptides. This review summarizes and compares skeletal phenotypes across DMD models, evaluates responses to glucocorticoids, identifies methodological factors that explain discordant findings, and proposes a translational framework for incorporating bone outcomes into DMD therapeutic development.

title: Mobile radiation shielding device for scatter dose reduction during portable radiography in an orthopedic ward.
authors: Cheewakul J, Ina N, Marshall SK, Chaichulee S.
abstract: Portable radiography in orthopedic wards exposes healthcare professionals and adjacent patients to scatter radiation in open, shared clinical environments. In crowded wards, maintaining an optimal distance or clearing the area during exposure is often impractical. This study designed, constructed, and evaluated a foldable mobile radiation shielding system comprising two three-panel units, each with a chromed steel frame (210 × 180 cm) with 0.6-mm nominal lead sheets covered by a vinyl outer layer (66 × 100 cm) per panel, mounted on wheeled castors for bedside deployment. The two units were deployed together, one along each lateral side of the bed. Scatter dose rates were measured using an radiation survey meter and a portable X-ray unit during phantom radiography across common orthopedic projections at eight angular positions (0°-315° in 45° increments) and five distances (50-250 cm). The two-unit configuration achieved a median scatter dose reduction of 94.1% (IQR: 88.0%-97.7%; Wilcoxon W = 51,360, N = 320, p < 0.001). Reductions were broadly consistent across tube voltages (65-85 kVp) and remained substantial across all measurement distances (84.3%-89.6% across 50-250 cm), but varied significantly by angular position, with the highest reduction at 90° (mean 96.91%) and the lowest reductions recorded at 0° (mean 54.02%) and 180° (mean 75.69%). These two directions represented the open axial ends of the setup and were not directly covered by the side-mounted shielding panels. Under a representative high-workload scenario, the two-unit configuration reduced estimated annual occupational doses across all projections, with all post-shielding means remaining well below the average annual occupational dose limit of 20 mSv/year. User feedback was more favorable among radiologic technologists (mean 4.80/5) than among orthopedic ward nurses (mean 3.67/5). The two-unit configuration showed substantial scatter reduction and may serve as an additional protective measure during portable radiography in orthopedic ward settings, with positioning guidance required to maximize protection at clinically relevant angular locations.

title: Lower symptom burden strengthens the association between DTI-ALPS index and brain aging in head and neck cancer survivors.
authors: Bajaj S, Quarles CC, Gilmore K, Qiao Y, Wintermark M, Wefel JS, Noll KR, Mokashi C, Zalles M, Roth M.
abstract: Background Head and neck (HN) cancer survivorship is associated with persistent symptom burden and long-term brain-behavioral health alterations, yet mechanisms underlying brain aging remain poorly understood. We investigated whether HN cancer survivors exhibit accelerated brain aging, whether limbic white matter (WM) pathways contribute to these changes, and whether measures associated with glymphatic function are associated with reduced brain aging. Methods Diffusion MRI and symptom burden data were analyzed in 135 HN cancer survivors and compared with a normative cohort from the Human Connectome Project (n = 1,228). Two machine learning models (elastic net [ENET] and random forest [RF]) using fractional anisotropy (FA) and quantitative anisotropy (QA) from 45 WM tracts were trained to estimate brain age and compute brain age gap (BAG). Glymphatic-related processes were indirectly assessed using diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular spaces (DTI-ALPS). Moderation analyses examined whether symptom burden influenced associations among DTI-ALPS, BAG, and WM integrity. Results Survivors showed a negative mean BAG of -1.64 years in the ENET model, indicating a nonsignificant tendency toward delayed brain aging, whereas the RF model showed a positive mean BAG of 3.59 years, indicating accelerated brain aging. The RF model demonstrated stronger external generalizability and greater biological coherence, including associations with ALPS and symptom-related measures. The bilateral fornix and right U-fibers were among the strongest contributors to RF-based brain age prediction. Higher DTI-ALPS index values were associated with lower BAG and greater fornix integrity, particularly in survivors with lower symptom burden and reduced activity-related interference. Conclusions HN cancer survivorship was associated with accelerated brain aging in the model demonstrating greater external generalizability and biological relevance, alongside alterations in limbic WM pathways. Higher DTI-ALPS was associated with reduced brain aging, with symptom burden modifying this relationship. These findings highlight brain health as an important component of cancer survivorship.

title: Longitudinal changes in infrapatellar fat pad fibrosis following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Takei S, Imoo Y, Onuma H, Mammoto T, Kobayashi H.
abstract: Background Infrapatellar fat pad (IFP) fibrosis is implicated in anterior knee pain, limited range of motion (ROM), and posttraumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). However, its precise longitudinal progression remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the dynamic changes in IFP fibrosis from preoperative to 12 months post-ACLR using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients who underwent anatomic double-bundle ACLR using autologous hamstring tendon grafts. IFP fibrosis was semiquantitatively graded (grades 0-5) using proton density-weighted (PDW) sagittal MR images obtained preoperatively and at 6 and 12 months postoperatively. Patients were categorized into mild (grades 0-3) and severe (grades 4-5) IFP fibrosis groups. Temporal changes in the proportion of the severe group across the three time points were evaluated using Cochran's Q test, followed by the Bonferroni-corrected McNemar test for pairwise comparisons. Results Of 558 consecutive cases screened, 169 patients (mean age, 23.9 years) were included in the final analysis. The proportion of patients classified into the severe fibrosis group significantly changed over time (Cochran's Q test, χ 2 (2) = 24.0, p Conclusions IFP fibrosis is an early and persistent pathological event following ACLR and is established primarily within the first 6 postoperative months. This early onset suggests a critical time window for targeted interventions to mitigate inflammation and prevent the irreversible establishment of IFP fibrosis, providing a basis to investigate the long-term PTOA risk.

title: Knowledge, attitude, and behaviours concerning mpox from an online survey among MSM in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR).
authors: McCall SJ, Shamas H, Bou Hamdan M, Najem M, Alaama AS, Jamil MS, DeJong J, Hermez J, Melhem NM.
abstract: Background Human monkeypox (mpox), a viral zoonotic infectious disease, was declared a public health emergency of international concern. Men who have sex with men (MSM) were most affected by mpox during the global outbreak. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and behaviours concerning mpox among the MSM population in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR). Methods This was a cross-sectional study of MSM residing in countries of the EMR. Participants were recruited through non-governmental organisations, dating applications, and LGBTQ+ websites between July and October 2023. Data on behaviours, perceptions, access to healthcare, socio-demographics, and medical characteristics related to mpox were collected online via LimeSurvey. The outcome was high mpox knowledge whereby a score greater than 12 of 17 was considered as high mpox knowledge score. Adaptive Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator logistic regression was used to predict participants' knowledge about mpox. Model discrimination and calibration were assessed. Results A total of 643 MSM participants of median age 31 (IQR:26-37) were included in the study. Among study participants, 131 (20.4%) had high mpox knowledge. Key predictors of high mpox knowledge score were being 31-40 years old, employed, in a relationship, thinking mpox vaccine is safe, and knowing someone infected with mpox. The model had good discrimination AUC = 0.812 (95%CI:0.77-0.85) and calibration C-slope = 1.073 (95%CI:0.87-1.27). Conclusion This study identified gaps and predictors of high mpox knowledge score among MSM in the EMR. These findings provide new insights needed to raise awareness and inform targeted public health interventions to reduce the spread of mpox.

title: Juvenile Paget disease due to osteoprotegerin deficiency: clinical, biochemical, and radiographic findings during zoledronate therapy in four children.
authors: Canoruc Emet D, Celık NB, Oguz B, Unsal Y, Simsek Kiper PO, Ozon A, Gonc N.
abstract: We report extended pediatric follow-up outcomes of zoledronic acid therapy in four children with TNFRSF11B related juvenile Paget disease. In the context of limited pediatric long-term data, our observations indicate favorable growth, mobility, and skeletal outcomes when therapy is initiated early and adjusted according to clinical course. Background Juvenile Paget's Disease (JPD) is an ultra-rare metabolic bone disorder associated with accelerated bone turnover, skeletal deformities, fractures, bone pain, sensorineural hearing loss and growth impairment. Although bisphosphonates are the main therapeutic option, there are no established guidelines regarding drug choice, dosage, and dosing frequency. Objective To describe the clinical, biochemical, and radiological findings observed during extended pediatric follow-up of children with TNFRSF11B related JPD treated with zoledronate (ZOL), and to provide observational evidence that may contribute to treatment strategies. Methods The study included four children: three siblings with severe JPD, carrying homozygous exon 2-5 TNFRSF11B deletion; and one child with intermediate JPD, carrying homozygous frameshift variant. All received bisphosphonates from diagnosis, initially Pamidronate (PMD) with a switch to ZOL when response was inadequate. Follow-up durations ranged from 6 to 14 years. Clinical findings, bone pain, growth and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity were evaluated every three months, and imaging was performed annually. Results Following PMD treatment, bone pain and ALP activity improved partially, however ALP normalized only after ZOL treatment. Despite normal ALP activity, some patients had recurrent bone pain and fractures during ZOL treatment, leading to treatment intensification. Early initiation of ZOL, with increased dose and frequency, especially during rapid growth, resulted in marked clinical improvement and improvement in growth parameters. Nevertheless, definitive adult height outcomes remain unavailable and profound sensorineural hearing loss was not prevented. ZOL also produced significant radiological improvements, including better trabecular structure, corticomedullary differentiation, diaphyseal modeling, and reduced femoral bowing. In contrast, delayed treatment and poor adherence were associated with worse skeletal outcomes. Conclusion Children with JPD experienced marked clinical, skeletal and linear growth improvement with early and adequate ZOL therapy. ZOL dosing should be guided not only by ALP activity but also by growth monitoring, skeletal findings, bone pain, fracture occurrence, and mobility.

title: Interleukin-33 as a potential indicator of disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis: a case-control study.
authors: Raouf MR, Abdelaziz YA, Raouf NR, Khaled M, Zaki SH.
abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease marked by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. Interleukin-33 (IL-33) has been proposed as an indicator of disease activity; however, its clinical relevance remains controversial, as studies report both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects. Methods This case-control study included 44 patients with RA and 44 age- and sex-matched healthy controls recruited from Minia University Hospital, Egypt. Serum IL-33 levels, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), rheumatoid factor (RF) and Disease Activity Score - 28-ESR (DAS28- ESR) were obtained. Medications, specifically disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), were recorded. Associations between IL-33 levels and clinical and laboratory parameters were evaluated. Multivariate regression analysis and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed. Results Serum IL-33 levels were significantly elevated in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, with a median of 145 (interquartile range 41.75-193.75), compared to 7 (4.25-11.0) in controls (p 2 = 0.83). ROC curve analysis also showed good discrimination for high disease activity (n = 8)(AUC = 0.918, 95% CI: 0.807-0.986). At the selected IL-33 cut-off of 300 pg/mL, sensitivity was 66.7% and specificity was 100%. Conclusions Serum IL-33 levels are strongly associated with disease activity in RA and may be an indicator of inflammatory burden.

title: Hydrographic and sea ice gradients shape benthic ecosystem functioning through sediment characteristics and benthic functional structure in Nares Strait, Canadian Arctic.
authors: Combaz T, Bluhm BA, Witte U, Archambault P.
abstract: Rapid changes in Arctic sea ice conditions are altering the quantity, quality, and timing of organic matter reaching the seafloor, thereby reshaping benthic ecosystem functioning. However, the exact mechanisms linking sea ice variability, benthic community structure, and sediment biogeochemical processes remain poorly understood. With its multiple forms and ages of sea ice, Nares Strait in the Canadian Arctic offers a unique natural laboratory for investigating how environmental gradients and benthic community structure jointly regulate benthic ecosystem functioning. Here, we incubated sediment cores from several locations in Nares Strait characterised by different sea ice conditions, ranging from first-year ice to multi-year ice, and measured oxygen and nutrient fluxes as proxies for ecosystem functioning. To investigate the relative importance of potential drivers, we also measured environmental variables, identified macrofauna and calculated a suite of taxonomic and functional diversity indices. Our analyses show that fluxes across the sediment-water interface varied significantly between the northern and southern regions of Nares Strait. Among individual predictors, the average proportion of deposit feeders and sea ice cover (days since ice-free) explained the largest proportions of flux variability (23% and 14%, respectively). Overall, benthic functional structure explained more variation in fluxes than taxonomic diversity. Environmental variables explained little additional variation once functional descriptors were included, while variance partitioning revealed that the shared environmental-functional component accounted for 25% of the total variation, representing more than half of the variation explained by out models (45%) and exceeding the unique contributions of either environmental or functional variables. This strong overlap indicates that benthic functional structure integrates the cumulative effects of environmental forcing on sediment biogeochemical functioning. Collectively, our findings suggest that hydrographic and sea ice gradients regulate benthic ecosystem functioning largely through their influence on sediment characteristics and benthic functional structure. Because Nares Strait encompasses environmental conditions representative of many Arctic marine systems, the mechanisms identified here provide a framework for predicting how continued sea ice decline may reshape benthic ecosystem functioning across the Arctic Ocean.

title: Healthcare-delivered lifestyle recommendations and their association with health behaviors in Iran.
authors: Sohrabi H, Mirzad M, Golestani A, Azadnajafabad S, Ahmadi N, Afzalian A, Rezaei N, Rashidi MM, Ghasemi E, Rezaei N, Yoosefi M, Kazemi A, Djalalinia S, Farzi Y, Haghshenas R, Nasserinejad M, Mehr EF, Fateh SM, Farzadfar F.
abstract: Background Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the leading cause of mortality in Iran, driven largely by modifiable lifestyle risk factors. Healthcare providers play a pivotal role in delivering preventive lifestyle recommendations, yet the extent and effectiveness of these efforts remain unclear. This study aimed to assess the distribution of lifestyle counseling across sociodemographic and clinical subgroups and its association with health behavior status in Iran using data from the 2021 WHO STEPS survey. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 27,704 included adults participating in the nationally representative 2021 STEPS survey in Iran. Data on delivery of ten specific lifestyle recommendations within the past 12 months, covering diet, physical activity, weight management, and tobacco non-initiation/cessation, were collected. Associations between recommendation delivery and health behaviors were analyzed using logistic regression models. Results Only 33.4% (95% Confidence Interval (CI): 32.8-34.0) of participants received all ten lifestyle recommendations, while 10.7% (10.2-11.1) received no recommendations. Recommendations were more frequently delivered to females, rural residents, and individuals with multiple comorbidities, indicating a risk-based response by healthcare providers. Notably, tobacco non-initiation/cessation advice was not more commonly offered to patients with multiple chronic conditions. Delivery of lifestyle counseling was associated with positive behavior status: individuals who received weight loss/ maintaining normal weight and physical activity advice were more likely to engage in sufficient physical activity (adjusted odds ratio 1.21(1.13-1.29)), and among current smokers, receiving tobacco cessation recommendation was associated with a higher likelihood of attempting tobacco cessation (aOR: 1.83(1.49-2.24)). A dose-response relationship was observed between the number of nutritional recommendations received and better diet quality (aOR for 6 vs. ≤ 2 recommendations: 1.32 (1.24-1.41)). Geographical disparities were evident, with eastern provinces receiving the least comprehensive counseling. Conclusion Delivery of lifestyle recommendations by healthcare providers in Iran shows variation by sociodemographic and clinical factors and is positively associated with behavior status. Given the cross-sectional design, causal or temporal relationships cannot be inferred. These findings suggest opportunities for more equitable and consistent delivery of preventive counseling within national NCD prevention efforts.

title: GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence: Antecedents, perceived usefulness, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness outcomes.
authors: Nguyen TKQ, Nguyen KP.
abstract: This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a common latent factor diagnostic and Gaussian copula endogeneity assessment. The baseline PLS-SEM model showed statistically significant positive associations for all nine hypothesized relationships and explained 53.1% of the variance in GAISC, 45.6% in AIEA, and 52.9% in CR. Substantively, PU was the strongest baseline antecedent of GAISC (β = .427, f2 = .244), while GAISC showed a particularly strong association with AIEA (β = .675, f2 = .838). Endogeneity adjustment indicated that seven relationships remained robust; however, the relationships between FC and GAISC and between AIEA and CR became non-significant. Accordingly, these two paths are interpreted as baseline-supported but not robust after adjustment. The findings move beyond generic GenAI acceptance by positioning GAISC as an accounting-specific competence construct linked to ethical awareness and career readiness. Because GAISC and CR were measured through student self-reports and the evidence is cross-sectional, the results are interpreted as association-based rather than as demonstrations of objectively verified competence, employability, or causal effects.

title: GB-algebraic class.
authors: Liu M, Maihemuti N, Peng J, Tang J.
abstract: The purpose of this article is to study the relationships among the BCI-algebraic class, the GB-algebraic class, and the class of algebras of type (2,0). The results indicate that: (1) The BCH-algebraic class and the GB-algebraic class are two distinct algebraic classes, both of which contain the BCI-algebraic class. (2) There exist a proper BCH-algebra and a proper GB-algebra, and necessary and sufficient conditions are provided for BCH-algebras and GB-algebras to be proper BCH-algebras and proper GB-algebras, respectively. (3) All (2,0)-type algebras form a proper class, and the GB-algebraic class is a proper subclass of the class of algebras of type (2,0). Several conditions for (2,0)-type algebras to be GB-algebras are given.

title: Feasibility of patient-reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) computerized adaptive tests in patients receiving physical therapy: A mixed-methods study.
authors: Haan EA, Doomen A, Wittink H, Kiers H, Arensman RM, Terwee CB.
abstract: Introduction Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) are widely used in physical therapy, but both clinicians and patients report respondent burden due to the number and the length of existing instruments. PROMIS® Computerized Adaptive Tests (CATs) may reduce this burden, yet their feasibility in primary care physical therapy is unknown. This study examined the feasibility of Dutch-Flemish PROMIS CATs in patients with musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders of the spine and upper extremity. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods concurrent triangulation study in 14 physical therapy practices where PROMIS CATs were integrated into the electronic health record system and administered during routine care. A survey assessed physical therapists' experiences and opinions regarding acceptability, demand, practicality, and implementation. Semi-structured interviews with physical therapists and patients further explored these domains. Survey data were analyzed descriptively, and interview transcripts were thematically analyzed by two independent researchers. Results Twenty-five physical therapists completed the survey. Ten physical therapists and nine patients participated in interviews.
