Most physical therapists reported that PROMIS CATs were easy to use and facilitated focused discussions about symptoms and functioning. Patients described CATs as quick to complete and relevant to their condition and were willing to complete PROMs if results were used in consultations. Reported barriers included the simultaneous use of legacy PROMs (patients), difficulties using the online portal, and uncertainty about interpreting CAT scores (therapists). Some participants reported that certain CAT items felt less relevant and expressed a desire to view individual item responses. Conclusions PROMIS CATs are considered feasible to implement in physical therapy practice and are generally experienced as acceptable, efficient, and clinically useful. Future implementation should focus on phasing out legacy PROMs to reduce respondent burden, improving skills in score interpretation, ensuring financial reimbursement for use, incorporating PROMIS into clinical guidelines, and evaluating additional PROMIS domains relevant to primary care physical therapy.

title: Expression of Concern: Multiple attribute group decision-making based on interval-valued q-rung orthopair uncertain linguistic power Muirhead mean operators and linguistic scale functions.

title: Explainable deep learning localizes age-discriminative candidate regions on hand radiographs of adult women.
authors: Jang HS, Cho J, Kim DH, Kim MG, Choi D, Lee SH, Park C, Kim YK, Kang HJ, Ye JC.
abstract: Objective To determine whether deep learning can distinguish younger from older adult women on hand radiographs and to identify candidate anatomical regions for age-group discrimination using explainable artificial intelligence and quantitative cortical measurements. Materials and methods This retrospective, single-center, exploratory study included 2,221 women sampled consecutively within each age group during 2020-2023 (1,134 aged 20-45 and 1,087 aged 55-80 years at radiography). Patients contributed one posteroanterior radiograph and were assigned to mutually exclusive training, validation, or test sets. Five architectures were evaluated on the same 334 held-out test radiographs (171 younger; 163 older), with performance averaged across five random-seed runs. DenseNet121 was selected by descriptive comparison for gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) and ray-based analyses with retraining. Manual cortical measurements of test radiographs yielded metacarpal and proximal phalangeal indices for candidate rays identified by Grad-CAM. Results DenseNet121 achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, 0.996; 95% CI, 0.992-0.999). Grad-CAM showed prominent activation around the third proximal phalanx, with additional activation in the second and fourth rays. Performance remained high after ray masking; the third-ray-only model achieved the highest mean accuracy among single-ray models. The third proximal phalangeal index had the highest AUC among the six indices (0.956; 95% CI, 0.937-0.976). Conclusion Grad-CAM, ray-based analyses, and quantitative cortical measurements support the third proximal phalanx as an anatomically interpretable candidate region for age-group discrimination in adult women. Integrating explainable artificial intelligence with quantitative radiographic assessment provides an exploratory workflow for investigating hand skeletal aging, with potential relevance to broader musculoskeletal imaging research.

title: Experimental and numerical assessment of calcium hydroxide dosage on the seepage performance of Yellow River sediment-based alkali-activated materials for embankment seepage control.
authors: Han L, Li J, Liu M, Yao X, Wang T.
abstract: To investigate the effect of calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) dosage on the seepage performance of Yellow River sediment-based alkali-activated materials, Yellow River sediment from the Huayuankou reach was used as the main precursor in a composite NaOH-Ca(OH)2 activation system. The permeability coefficient was systematically examined at Ca(OH)2 dosages of 2.5%-15.0% (by mass of dry sediment) and curing ages of 3, 7, and 28 days, and low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) was used to characterize the pore structure and its relationship with permeability. The permeability coefficient exhibited a pronounced nonlinear response to Ca(OH)2 dosage. Increasing the dosage from 2.5% to 10.0% reduced the permeability coefficient by 82.58%, 82.45%, and 69.07% at 3, 7, and 28 days, respectively, whereas a further increase to 12.5% caused a rebound of 43.48%, 48.70%, and 13.80%; beyond 12.5%, the permeability decreased again. The small-pore fractal dimension correlated negatively and significantly with the permeability coefficient (R² = 0.92, 0.96, and 0.92 at 3, 7, and 28 days), and a multivariate model linking permeability coefficient, Ca(OH)2 dosage, and curing age was established with R² = 0.97. Two-dimensional seepage analyses of a typical Yellow River embankment (7.02 m high) using GEO-Studio show that, relative to the unreinforced embankment, reinforcement layers prepared with 10.0% and 12.5% Ca(OH)2 lowered the elevation of the seepage exit point from 33.45 m to 33.30 m and 33.27 m (i.e., by 0.15 m and 0.18 m), while the unit-width seepage discharge remained almost unchanged (from 6.14 × 10 ⁻ ⁷ to 6.89 × 10 ⁻ ⁷ and 6.95 × 10 ⁻ ⁷ m³/(s·m)). This indicates a redistribution of the seepage field and a lower phreatic surface, rather than a deterioration in impermeability. The results provide a reference for the resource utilization of Yellow River sediment in embankment seepage control.

title: Evaluating toric intraocular lens outcomes: A comparison between asymmetric and symmetric bowtie astigmatism.
authors: Emmaneerat N, Uthaithammarat L, Somkijrungroj T, Satitpitakul V.
abstract: Objectives To compare outcomes of toric intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in patients with asymmetric versus symmetric bowtie astigmatism. Methods This retrospective chart review included 76 eyes from 60 patients: 24 eyes (20 patients) with asymmetric bowtie astigmatism (Group 1) and 52 eyes (43 patients) with symmetric bowtie astigmatism (Group 2). All patients underwent uneventful phacoemulsification with toric IOL implantation. Uncorrected distance visual acuity (UCVA), residual astigmatism, and spectacle independence at three months postoperatively were evaluated. Results The median UCVA was 0.10 logMAR in Group 1 and 0.00 in Group 2 (P = 0.045). UCVA of 20/20 or better was achieved in 29% of Group 1 and 52% of Group 2. The median residual astigmatism was significantly higher in Group 1 (-1.39 D, IQR 1.23) than in Group 2 (-0.70 D, IQR 0.35; P Conclusion At three months postoperatively, toric IOL implantation provided comparable UCVA and spectacle independence in both groups, though residual astigmatism was significantly higher in the asymmetric group.

title: Establishing paediatric robotic surgery in lower-volume centres: an eight-phase implementation roadmap and initial case outcomes.
authors: Lee YY, Nor NHM, Mali VP, Koh ZJ, Nyo YL, Gundeti MS.
abstract: Robotic surgery in children continues to expand, but the evidence guiding it is generated almost exclusively in high-volume institutions. Learning curves for paediatric robot-assisted pyeloplasty indicate competence at 13-30 cases and consolidation at 40-100. It is challenging for a unit undertaking eight to 15 index operations a year to accumulate that experience at an acceptable rate, and deferring adoption until caseload rises merely lengthens the intervals across which skill decays. We propose that such units uncouple skill acquisition from clinical caseload and import operative experience instead, and we set out an eight-phase roadmap anchored to the first proctored case. We illustrate each phase with the first 12 consecutive robotic operations of a restarted paediatric programme in an adult-paediatric tertiary hospital, performed across five proctor visits over 15 months, with no conversions and one complication. We report the performance data monitored against published benchmarks, the time and resources the approach required, and lower-cost alternatives, including proctorship by adult robotic surgeons within the same institution. The roadmap presupposes access to an established robotic platform and a caseload sufficient to maintain two console surgeons; units below that threshold may be better served by regional collaboration than by an independent programme.

title: Empathy with nature and pro-environmental behavior among Generation Z tourists in Yunnan Province, China.
authors: Long H, Shi J, Zhang Q, Zhao D, Li Z.
abstract: Using a cultural landscape World Heritage destination as the research setting, this study examines the association between empathy with nature and self-reported pro-environmental behavior among Generation Z tourists. Although empathy with nature, connectedness to nature, and place identity have been linked to pro-environmental behavior, few studies have examined these constructs jointly in cultural landscape tourism. Drawing on an emotion-cognition-identity-morality perspective, the proposed framework specifies connectedness to nature and place identity as parallel and sequential mediators and environmental responsibility as a moderator. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to analyze cross-sectional questionnaire data from 519 Chinese Generation Z tourists who had visited Jingmai Mountain in Yunnan Province. Empathy with nature was positively associated with self-reported pro-environmental behavior. Significant indirect effects were found via connectedness to nature and place identity, both independently and sequentially. The positive relationship between empathy with nature and pro-environmental behavior was also amplified among individuals with higher environmental responsibility. These findings are consistent with the proposed framework but do not establish causal relationships or temporal ordering. The study extends the empirical examination of empathy with nature to cultural landscape heritage tourism within a Generation Z sample, without establishing that the observed relationships are distinctive to this cohort. These findings identify psychological correlates of self-reported pro-environmental behavior and provide implications for visitor engagement and heritage conservation research, with practical applications requiring further intervention testing.

title: Embedding behavioural and implementation science in a whole school approach to promote physical activity among children and young people with disabilities.
authors: Byrd E, Wilson JJ, McFlynn P, Simms V, Taggart L, Boner Á, Murphy MH.
abstract: Background A whole school approach (WSA) to physical activity is a comprehensive strategy encouraging children's physical activity throughout the school day. However, research on implementing this approach in special educational needs (SEN) school settings is limited. A strategic approach that considers the school context, behaviour change mechanisms and implementation strategies can improve the effectiveness and sustainability of physical activity in a WSA. This study aimed to embed implementation and behavioural science principles to co-develop an implementation research logic model (IRLM) to guide implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Methods A collaborative co-development approach was used in this study exploring the WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Teachers, school leadership, parents, the education authority and professionals from community sports clubs in one UK region participated in a series of workshops. The workshops and analyses were guided by behavioural and implementation theories, models, and frameworks. Results Workshop discussions revealed 31 determinants of implementation, comprising 18 facilitators, 12 barriers and one item identified as both barrier and facilitator. These determinants informed the development of eight implementation strategies to promote physical activity through a WSA in SEN settings (e.g., staff training, building collaborative networks and engaging families). Eleven implementation, seven school-level and six pupil-level outcomes, were identified to assess effectiveness and implementation. Eight causal mechanisms explained the pathway from strategies to outcomes. Finally, these determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes were mapped onto an IRLM to guide the implementation of a WSA to physical activity for children and young people with SENs across settings. Conclusions We have co-developed an IRLM embedded in implementation and behavioural science to support the implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. The model illustrates causal mechanisms between implementation determinants and implementation strategies to achieve intended outcomes. This IRLM has informed a guidance document for implementing WSA to physical activity within SEN settings, addressing real-world challenges faced in promoting physical activity among pupils with SEN.

title: Does Perineural Dexamethasone Prolong the Time to First Rescue Opioid Analgesia Compared With Intravenous Dexamethasone in Pediatric Hip Surgery? A Randomized Blinded Trial.
authors: Reysner T, Shadi M, Janusz P, Musielak B, Idzior M, Wieczorowska-Tobis K, Reysner M.
abstract: Background The pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block is an increasingly utilized regional anesthesia technique for pediatric hip surgery. Dexamethasone prolongs the duration of peripheral nerve blocks and can be administered either intravenously or perineurally; however, the comparative pediatric evidence on postoperative analgesia and metabolic effects with these two routes is limited. Questions/purposes (1) Does perineural dexamethasone prolong the time to first rescue opioid analgesia compared with intravenous dexamethasone when used as an adjunct to PENG block in pediatric hip surgery? (2) Does perineural dexamethasone reduce postoperative opioid consumption and pain intensity? (3) Does the route of dexamethasone administration influence postoperative inflammatory markers and blood glucose levels? (4) Is perineural dexamethasone associated with an increased risk of neurologic complications? Methods This randomized, blinded trial was conducted at a single urban tertiary university referral center in Poznań, Poland, providing subspecialty pediatric orthopaedic care. Parents and caregivers, treating anesthesiologists, surgeons, and outcome assessors were unaware of group allocation. Between February 2025 and March 2026, we assessed 72 children scheduled for elective reconstructive hip surgery. Children age 3 months to 6 years with developmental dysplasia of the hip or neurogenic hip displacement associated with cerebral palsy were considered potentially eligible. Of the 72 children assessed, 92% (66) met the eligibility criteria. Nine percent (6 of 66) of these children were not enrolled because four families declined participation and two declined regional anesthesia. The remaining 83% (60 of 72) were randomized. No participants were lost during the 48-hour in-hospital follow-up or had incomplete outcome data, and all 60 were included in the analysis. The perineural and intravenous groups had mean ± SD ages of 4.8 ± 1.2 and 5.2 ± 1.1 years, respectively; 47% (14 of 30) and 50% (15 of 30) were boys, and 70% (21 of 30) and 73% (22 of 30) had developmental dysplasia of the hip. The remaining children had neurogenic hip displacement associated with cerebral palsy. There were no clinically important between-group differences in these baseline characteristics. All patients received standardized spinal anesthesia and multimodal postoperative analgesia consisting of paracetamol 15 mg/kg and metamizole 15 mg/kg every 6 hours, ibuprofen 10 mg/kg every 8 hours, and rescue nalbuphine 0.1 mg/kg for Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) scores of ≥ 4. The primary endpoint was time to first rescue opioid analgesia within 48 hours. Secondary endpoints included total opioid consumption, postoperative pain scores, inflammatory markers (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR] and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR]), blood glucose levels, and peripheral nerve injury assessed at 12, 24, and 48 hours. Results We found no difference between the perineural and intravenous dexamethasone groups in time to first rescue opioid analgesia after adjustment for age, body weight, and duration of surgery (HR 0.56 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.28 to 1.08]; p = 0.08). Perineural dexamethasone reduced total opioid consumption during the first 48 postoperative hours (mean ± SD 0.131 ± 0.048 versus 0.225 ± 0.053 mg/kg morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs), mean difference -0.095 mg/kg [95% CI -0.121 to -0.068]; p Conclusion After adjustment for age, body weight, and duration of surgery, we found no difference between perineural and intravenous dexamethasone in time to first rescue opioid analgesia. Perineural dexamethasone was associated with lower opioid consumption and lower early postoperative blood glucose levels. Larger multicenter studies are needed to evaluate these findings in pediatric regional anesthesia. Level of evidence Level I, therapeutic study.

title: Developing a manager-informed indicator framework for public sport facility performance measurement: Evidence from perceived indicator importance.
authors: Pan X, Chen C, Zainal Abidin NE, Aman MS.
abstract: Public sport facility performance measurement draws on provision, user-experience, and distributive indicators, yet these indicators are often considered separately and their roles within a common framework remain unclear. This study developed a manager-informed input-output indicator framework for organising candidate indicators before operational performance measurement. A cross-sectional survey of 228 personnel with management-related responsibilities for public sport facilities in Fujian Province, China, asked participants to rate the importance of five provision-side and eight outcome-side indicators on a five-point scale. The main model retained all 13 indicators and specified both blocks as composites; two reduced-indicator models served as sensitivity analyses. Mean importance ratings ranged from 3.68 to 3.87, and between 62.7% and 70.6% of respondents rated each candidate indicator as important or very important. The Input Importance Composite was positively associated with the Output Importance Composite (β = 0.601, t = 11.879, p < 0.001, 95% confidence interval [0.488, 0.690]). The main model explained 36.2% of the variance in output-side importance ratings, with an effect size of f² = 0.566, and similar associations were observed in the reduced formative-reflective and reduced composite models. Together, the descriptive and structural findings indicate that provision-side and outcome-side importance ratings were positively aligned within participants' judgments. Supplementary analyses showed no predictive-loss advantage over a linear-model benchmark, and the same-source design left common method concerns unresolved. The observed association is confined to perceived indicator importance; relationships between facility provision and outcomes require separate operational validation. The framework provides a preparatory structure for future validation using administrative, financial, facility, spatial, policy, user, and community data.

title: Current Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Surgical Planning for Craniosynostosis: A Scoping Review.
authors: Crouch L, Fleming K.
abstract: Importance Craniosynostosis, the premature fusion of cranial sutures, can cause abnormal skull shapes, neurological issues and aesthetic concerns. Surgical correction is standard, but planning is complex and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers the potential to enhance diagnosis, optimise planning and predict postoperative outcomes. Observations A scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines identified 11 studies involving paediatric patients with craniosynostosis. AI methods included unsupervised machine learning, convolutional neural networks, finite element models and variational autoencoders. Applications encompassed cranial severity scoring, phenotype classification, preoperative surgical simulation, intraoperative guidance and outcome prediction. AI-derived metrics correlated strongly with expert assessments, facilitated patient-specific planning and predicted postoperative aesthetics. Conclusions and relevance AI is a transformative adjunct in craniosynostosis surgery. Clinically, it improves diagnostic accuracy, supports personalised surgical planning and guides intraoperative decision-making. Some studies show AI can contribute to better functional and aesthetic outcomes, showing great promise in the paediatric surgical field. Although AI does not replace clinical expertise, it enhances precision and reproducibility. Future research should prioritise prospective validation, integration into surgical workflows and development of interpretable, surgeon-friendly AI tools to maximise clinical benefit.

title: Association between physical activity intensity and self-reported emphysema: A cross-sectional study using NHANES.
authors: Wei Q, Song H, Jiang L, Li X, Zhu J.
abstract: Background Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized. Methods This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Results Higher levels of physical activity, particularly ≥3000 MET-minutes per week, were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema. A dose-response relationship was observed, with increasing PA levels associated with progressively lower odds of self-reported emphysema. Conclusions Higher physical activity levels were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema in this cross-sectional analysis. These findings highlight a potential association between PA and self-reported emphysema; however, causal inference cannot be established. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate this relationship and explore underlying mechanisms.

title: Arthroscopic Double-Bundle Posterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Superficial Quadriceps and Hamstring Autografts With All-Suspensory Fixation.
authors: Chou HI, Wu SC, Liu LL, Lee KT.
abstract: Double-bundle posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction provides superior posterior stability and knee kinematics compared with single-bundle techniques but remains technically challenging regarding graft management and fixation. Several strategies can be implemented to obtain improved outcomes while mitigating complications, including techniques for optimizing arthroscopic visualization, graft preparation, fixation methods, tensioning, and tunnel positioning. In this technical note, we present a double-bundle posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction technique using a 4-stranded superficial quadriceps tendon autograft for the anterolateral bundle and a 4-stranded hamstring tendon autograft for the posteromedial bundle with all-suspensory fixation and internal brace augmentation. The objective of this technique is to provide robust biomechanical stability to accurately restore native knee kinematics.

title: Arthroscopic Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Iliotibial Band Autograft With Bone Block.
authors: Huang D, Weng W, Wang J, Ye Z, Wang G, Chen X, Huang J.
abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction is the first-line treatment for ACL injury, whereas existing autologous grafts each have inherent limitations. This study describes the use of an iliotibial band (ITB) graft with a bone block for ACL reconstruction, designed as a femoral bone block combined with tibial tendon configuration, which precisely matches the anatomical attachment and biomechanical loading characteristics of the native ACL. The surgery is performed through arthroscopic evaluation, harvesting and weaving of the ITB with a bone block, creation of femoral and tibial bone tunnels, and graft introduction and fixation. This graft features the advantage of easy harvesting of the ITB, whereas the femoral bone column allows for rapid bone-to-bone healing, enhances stability within the femoral tunnel, and reduces the risk of tunnel widening and femoral-sided rerupture. Tibial-sided tendon fixation avoids excessive tibial tunnel enlargement and simplifies surgical steps. Arthroscopic ACL reconstruction using the ITB with bone block is technically straightforward and provides high initial stability. It offers another graft option for both primary treatment of ACL injury and revision surgery after failed reconstructions and is particularly suitable for patients with multiple previous tendon harvests from the same knee or those requiring large-diameter grafts because of bone tunnel enlargement.

title: Antibiotic use and gastrointestinal symptoms among adults in the West Bank, Palestine: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Abu Zahra J, Joma H, Awwad A, Radwan R, Khalili H, Omran Y, Ihmoud F.
abstract: Background Antibiotics are extensively used to treat infections caused by bacteria and have had a substantial impact on improving public health. However, they can change the composition of the gut microbiota and induce gastrointestinal symptoms including diarrhea, constipation, bloating, abdominal pain and reflux. Although these effects have been described in different populations, evidence from the West Bank remains limited. Materials and methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among adults aged 18 years and older in the West Bank. Participants were recruited using non-probability convenience sampling, and data were collected through an online questionnaire disseminated through social media platforms. The questionnaire evaluated demographic characteristics, antibiotic use patterns over the previous three months, self-medication habits, lifestyle factors, and gastrointestinal symptoms. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and binary logistic and linear regression, with a negative binomial model as a sensitivity analysis. Results This study comprised 403 participants from the West Bank (mean age: 34.16 years, 55.3% men). Overall, 47.4% of participants reported antibiotic use over the last three months, and 56.8% reported having clinically relevant GI symptoms. In unadjusted analysis, antibiotic users had significantly higher GI symptom scores than non-users (p = 0.003), and A positive trend in GI symptom prevalence was observed across antibiotic-course categories (p for trend = 0.027). However, after adjustment for demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors, antibiotic use was not independently associated with clinically relevant GI symptoms (adjusted OR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.69-1.65, p = 0.788) or GI symptom score. Conclusions In this West Bank sample, recent antibiotic use was not independently associated with gastrointestinal symptoms after adjustment for potential confounders. Greater symptom burden was associated mainly with pre-existing gastrointestinal conditions, psychological stress, and recent infection, suggesting that the crude association may reflect underlying clinical factors rather than antibiotic exposure itself. Prospective studies with detailed antibiotic exposure and temporal data are needed to clarify these relationships.

title: What Are the Oncologic Outcomes of Patients With Osteosarcoma and Venous Tumor Thrombi Managed by an Aggressive Multidisciplinary Approach of Chemotherapy and Surgical Resection?
authors: Liang H, Qi F, Liu K, Du Z, Sun X, Guo W, Wang J, Yang Y.
abstract: Background Macroscopic venous tumor thrombus (VTT) is a rare but aggressive manifestation of osteosarcoma that poses substantial challenges for both surgical management and systemic disease control. Our previous work characterized its frequency, radiographic features, and adverse prognostic association, particularly in pelvic osteosarcoma; however, surgical management was heterogeneous. The patient-level outcomes achieved after a standardized multidisciplinary treatment approach and the association between VTT resection strategy and postoperative oncologic outcomes remain unclear. Questions/purposes (1) What were the oncologic outcomes of patients with osteosarcoma with macroscopic VTT treated under a standardized treatment algorithm incorporating aggressive surgical resection? (2) Did the choice of VTT resection strategy affect oncologic outcomes? Methods We screened the records of 39 patients with treatment-naive osteosarcoma and macroscopic VTT identified on imaging who were treated according to a standardized multimodal treatment algorithm between 2019 and 2024. This algorithm consisted of standardized multimodal imaging at diagnosis to detect and characterize VTT. After biopsy confirmation, patients received four-agent neoadjuvant chemotherapy, preoperative inferior vena cava filter placement when technically feasible, and repeat imaging to reassess the resectability of both the primary tumor and VTT. Surgery was undertaken only when both lesions were considered resectable. VTT involving peripheral venous branches or completely occluded and enlarged major veins was managed with en bloc venous resection, whereas thrombectomy was performed for VTT involving patent or partially patent major veins. Postoperative chemotherapy was initiated 2 to 3 weeks after surgery. After excluding one patient without pathologic confirmation of the macroscopic VTT, two patients in whom en bloc resection of the primary tumor was not achieved, and seven patients who did not receive postoperative chemotherapy, 29 patients were included in this retrospective analysis. The study population was young (mean ± SD age 16 ± 7 years), with a slight male predominance (17 of 29 patients), and primary tumors were distributed between the extremities (16 of 29) and pelvis (13 of 29). More than half of the patients presented with metastatic disease (16 of 29), most VTTs involved major venous trunks (22 of 29), and 20 of 29 patients had Results Patients treated under the standardized algorithm had limited durable disease control, with disease progression in 26 of 29 patients, a median PFS of 7 months (95% confidence interval [CI] 0 to 16), and an estimated 2-year OS of 60%. Patients with localized disease had longer PFS (median 13 months [95% CI 8 to 19] versus 5 months [95% CI 4 to 5]; p = 0.046) and MPFS (median 13 months [95% CI 8 to 19] versus 4.6 months [95% CI 4 to 5]; p = 0.04) than those with metastatic disease. There were no differences in OS (not reached versus median 32 months [95% CI 10 to 54]; p = 0.52), PFS (median 11 months [95% CI 0 to 31] versus 6 months [95% CI 3 to 9]; p = 0.62), LRFS (median 21 months [95% CI 9 to 34] versus 61 months [95% CI 2 to 120]; p = 0.54), and MPFS (median 13 months [95% CI 0.3 to 25] versus 8 months [95% CI 3 to 13]; p = 0.24) between patients who had thrombectomy versus en bloc venous resection. Conclusion Despite a standardized multidisciplinary approach incorporating perioperative chemotherapy and aggressive resection of both the primary tumor and macroscopic VTT, progression remained frequent, and durable disease control was uncommon. Among these 29 selected patients, VTT resection strategy-thrombectomy versus en bloc venous resection-was not detectably associated with oncologic outcomes, although the two groups were not directly comparable. Surgeons should recognize that osteosarcoma with macroscopic VTT is a rare, highly aggressive condition for which current treatment modalities seldom achieve a cure and should carefully balance the potential oncologic benefit of aggressive surgery against its morbidity. Future prospective multicenter studies should refine patient-level selection criteria and directly evaluate the incorporation of adjuvant radiotherapy into this standardized treatment algorithm. Novel systemic therapies should also be investigated to improve control of metastatic and rapidly progressive disease. Level of evidence Level III, therapeutic study.

title: Virtual reality exercise before bariatric surgery: a feasibility randomised controlled trial.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Gendia A, Aburrous M, Adwan H, Gilbert J, Tam A, Cota A, Clarke M, Finlay I, Clark J.
abstract: Introduction Preoperative physical activity remains a challenge in bariatric patients. This pilot randomised controlled trial assessed the feasibility, adherence and clinical impact of virtual reality (VR)-based exercise in preparation for bariatric surgery. Methods A single bariatric centre randomised patients from January 2020 to May 2023 to a 6-week home-based exercise programme: either VR-based exercise or standard walking exercise. Physical activity levels were assessed using the New Zealand Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form pre- and post-intervention. Secondary outcomes included adherence, patient satisfaction, weight loss and 30-day postoperative outcomes. Results A total of 43 patients were enrolled (mean age 46.3 ± 11.2 years, mean body mass index [BMI] 46.4 ± 6.37kg/m 2 , 83.7% female). Of these, 25 (58.1%) completed the intervention (VR: 13, control: 12). Enjoyment scores were significantly higher in the VR group (4.3 ± 0.85 vs 3 ± 0.95; p = 0.001). Post-intervention increases in physical activity were observed in both groups, with modest improvements in brisk and vigorous activity levels. Total weight loss percentage (TWL%) at 6 weeks and BMI at 12 months were comparable between groups. Dropout rates were similar (VR: 43.5%, control: 40%; p = 1). No statistically significant differences were observed in postoperative complications or readmissions. Conclusions VR-based exercise was deliverable and acceptable as a preoperative exercise intervention in bariatric surgery, with significantly higher enjoyment compared with standard walking exercise. However, adherence remained challenging, with similar dropout rates between groups and no significant between-group differences in clinical outcomes. These findings may support further development of tailored VR-based prehabilitation programmes, with future adequately powered trials. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04297306.

title: Updates on Low Energy Availability in Athletes: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport and the Female or Male Athlete Triad.
authors: Kussman A, Leonard N, Fahy K.
abstract: Purpose of review This paper evaluates the latest literature on low energy availability (LEA) in athletes, which is the basis for the clinical conditions known as the Female Athlete Triad, Male Athlete Triad, and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs). It explores how these different conditions are related, and how the clinician can approach screening, diagnosis, and management of LEA in athletes. Recent findings Within the past five years the Male Athlete Triad Consensus Statements were published in 2021, expanding upon knowledge regarding LEA in the Female Athlete Triad and applying this to the male population. Additionally, there has been an important update to the REDs model and a new clinical assessment tool (CAT2) published in 2023. This is based on new research into the different physiologic and psychologic sequelae of LEA. This has sparked additional discussion regarding the diagnosis, management, and prevention of LEA. The consequences of LEA can be severe, and can affect multiple different organ systems. Treatment should ideally involve a multidisciplinary team consisting of a physician, dietitian, and mental health provider, but may also include additional professionals such as athletic trainers, physical therapists, physiologists, other medical specialists, or other members of the athlete support system (including family and coaches). The mainstay of management remains optimizing energy availability (EA) through improving macro and micronutrient intake, and also requires addressing some of the more common sequelae of LEA. Prevention largely focuses on educational efforts and fostering healthy environments, particularly when discussing weight, body composition, and performance.

title: Transoral robotic surgery for head and neck tumours: a critical systematic review of patient selection and outcome reporting.
authors: Clay B, Crabtree P, Banham E, Jayaram R.
abstract: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) is an emerging modality for the minimally invasive resection of head and neck tumours. Despite its introduction approximately 15 years ago, its use has not become widespread in clinical practice. It is hypothesised that both heterogenous patient selection and heterogenous reporting of safety, procedural efficiency,​oncological efficacy, and functional outcomes of TORS compared to alternative treatments has limited effective evidence synthesis and contributed to limited clinical adoption. This review aims to systematically assess patient selection and outcome reporting in the literature and identify areas for improvement. The Medline, Embase and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to June 2025. Articles were included if they reported TORS without neoadjuvant therapy for the management of any tumour in the head and neck, without restriction by subsite, stage, histological type, adjuvant therapy, or reported outcome(s). 1471 studies were identified from searches. After deduplication and screening, 70 studies were included, comprising one randomised controlled trial, 22 non-randomised comparative studies and 47 non-comparative studies. Participant inclusion criteria were generally well-defined according to tumour site and histopathological characteristics. Reporting of all outcomes across safety, oncological, functional and procedural domains was grossly heterogenous. Only six specific outcomes were reported by multiple comparative studies, four of which by the same two studies, which differed in fundamental disease characteristics. This study highlights the need for consistent reporting in TORS-based studies, possibly via a core outcome set, to facilitate robust evidence synthesis of the safety and efficacy of TORS.

title: Translation and cultural adaptation of the Oxford Shoulder Score to Swedish and validation of a new 7-day recall version in patients with a proximal humerus fracture.
authors: Lundin PC, Sundh TFD, Adolfsson LE, Björnsson Hallgren HC.
abstract: Background and purpose The Oxford Shoulder Score (OSS) is a widely applied patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) designed to assess function and pain in individuals with shoulder disorders. We primarily aimed to evaluate a translated and culturally adapted Swedish version of the original OSS and secondarily to evaluate a version with a 7-day recall period, intended for rapidly changing conditions such as the early phase following fractures and surgeries. Methods The OSS was translated according to Beaton's guidelines for cross-cultural adaptation. 246 patients with a nonoperatively treated proximal humerus fracture completed the Swedish OSS and the QuickDASH at 1 week (T1, 7-day recall period), 3 months (T2, 7-day recall period), and 12 months (T3, 4-week recall period). Results Convergent validity between OSS and QuickDASH (Spearmans's rho) was rs -0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] -0.80 to -0.68) at T1, -0.88 (CI -0.91 to -0.84) at T2, and -0.86 (CI -0.90 to -0.81) at T3. Responsiveness for change scores (T2-T1) was -0.77 (CI -0.82 to -0.70) and (T3-T2) -0.80 (CI -0.85 to -0.74). Internal consistency for the respective domains was for pain at T1 0.73 (CI 0.68-0.78), at T2 0.84 (CI 0.80-0.87), at T3 0.87 (CI 0.84-0.89), and for function at T1 0.74 (CI 0.68-0.78), at T2 0.88 (CI 0.86-0.90), at T3 0.91 (CI 0.89-0.92). Intra-rater reliability was ICC = 0.94 (CI 0.90-0.96) between T3 and 2 weeks later. Conclusion The Swedish translation of the OSS demonstrated excellent measurement properties. The 7-day recall version demonstrated equivalent good validity, responsiveness, and reliability and seems valuable for monitoring fresh injuries such as proximal humerus fractures.

title: The relationship between ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and reactive postural control mechanisms in response to anterior perturbations.
authors: Pashaei M, Ramezanloo H, Hatefi M.
abstract: Adequate ankle dorsiflexion range of motion (DF-ROM) is essential for generating sufficient corrective torque during an ankle strategy; however, limitations in dorsiflexion may mechanically constrain this response, potentially leading to earlier reliance on hip or stepping strategies. Although indirect evidence links dorsiflexion capacity to dynamic balance performance, it remains unclear whether restricted dorsiflexion influences the selection of reactive postural control strategies in healthy young adults. Twenty active male participants were recruited for this study. Ankle DF-ROM was measured via the weight-bearing lunge test and categorized as either normal (≥20°) or restricted (<20°). Reactive postural control was assessed in response to a single unexpected anterior perturbation administered by a custom-engineered movable platform, with the perturbation load normalized to participants' body mass. Sagittal-plane kinematics were recorded at 60 Hz and independently evaluated by two blinded raters to classify the initial balance recovery response into ankle, hip, or stepping strategies based on established criteria. Statistical analysis revealed no significant association between ankle DF-ROM category and the type of reactive postural control strategy employed following anterior perturbations. Pearson's chi-square test indicated no significant relationship between dorsiflexion status and balance strategy selection (χ2(2) = 0.826, p = 0.662). Due to low expected cell counts, Fisher's exact test was also conducted, corroborating the absence of a significant association (two-sided p = 0.835). The distribution of postural strategies did not differ substantially between participants with normal and restricted dorsiflexion. In healthy young adults exposed to a standardized anterior perturbation, ankle DF-ROM was not independently associated with reactive postural strategy selection. These findings suggest that the postural demands imposed by the perturbation may have contributed to the predominance of stepping responses and may have reduced the sensitivity to detect an influence of ankle mobility on strategy selection.

title: The impact of functional sagittal pelvic tilt on CT-based hip dysplasia diagnostics in adults: a cross-sectional 3D simulation study.
authors: Hüsken MFT, Lissendorp F, Magré J, Willemsen K, Weinans H, Sakkers R, Nasrabadi J, Arbabi V, Bekkers J, Ten Ham AM, Schlösser TPC, Van der Wal BCH.
abstract: Background and purpose Accurate acetabular coverage assessment is essential for diagnosing adult hip dysplasia. Computed tomography (CT) best evaluates 3-dimensional acetabular morphology but is typically acquired supine, while symptoms arise during weightbearing. This study evaluates how sagittal pelvic tilt affects CT-based acetabular parameters in adults with hip dysplasia and whether pelvic tilt causes clinically relevant measurement changes. Methods 3D-models from supine CT of 29 adults with hip dysplasia (lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) ≤ 25°) yielded 39 affected hips. LCEA, inclination (AI), anterior/posterior/horizontal acetabular sector angles (AASA, PASA, HASA), acetabular version (AV), extrusion index (EI), and total and loadbearing coverage were measured. Pelvic tilt was simulated in 5° increments from 30° anterior to 30° posterior around the hip centers and parameters were remeasured in each position. Differences Results Median supine LCEA was 21°, AI 50°, AASA 43°. Across -30° to +30° tilt, AASA/loadbearing coverage decreased, PASA/AV increased, LCEA/EI showed parabolic patterns, and HASA/total coverage remained stable. From supine to simulated upright, paired mean differences were: LCEA -1° (95% confidence interval [CI] -2 to 0), AASA -4° (CI -5 to -3), PASA +4° (CI 4 to 5), HASA 0° (CI -1 to 1), AV +4° (CI 3 to 4), AI +1° (CI -1 to 3), EI +2% (CI 0 to 4), total coverage 0% (CI 0 to 0), and loadbearing coverage -2% (CI -2 to -2). Conclusion Functional sagittal pelvic tilt resulted in generally small changes in CT-based acetabular measurements in dysplastic hips, which may be clinically relevant in borderline cases, particularly for AASA, PASA, acetabular version, and EI, whereas LCEA and AI were not significantly affected.

title: Technology-enhanced training for prehospital mass-casualty incident preparedness: A scoping review.
authors: Saouli A, AlRahma A, Farhan H, Omayer A, Nour R, Yousif A, Hubloue I, Zary N.
abstract: Background The use of technology-enhanced training for prehospital mass-casualty incident (MCI) preparedness has expanded rapidly, yet how these technologies function throughout the educational process and how competencies are evaluated remain systematically under-examined. This scoping review, conducted as part of the MCIPHER (Mass-Casualty Incident Prehospital Emergency Response) project, mapped the technological modalities, educational functions, and assessment frameworks used in prehospital disaster training. Methods Following Arksey and O'Malley's framework with Levac refinements and PRISMA-ScR reporting, we searched seven databases and supplementary sources for English-language studies and protocols (2015-2025) on technology-enhanced prehospital MCI training for healthcare learners and professionals. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Descriptive and narrative synthesis included modified Kirkpatrick outcome mapping for completed studies, incorporating L2+ (Applied Learning). Results Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Virtual reality was the most common modality (43%, n = 12), followed by hybrid approaches (29%, n = 8) and screen-based simulations (21%, n = 6). Synthesis of the interventions revealed three consistent operational patterns: half of the studies (50%, n = 14) utilized dual-purpose platforms for both training delivery and automated assessment; embedded data collection was directly linked to achieving applied learning outcomes; and 75% (n = 21) lacked an explicit training design framework. Two additional patterns-a disconnect between immersion level and evaluation depth, and a tension between technological sophistication and scalability-emerged as areas needing future research. Furthermore, no studies originated from low- or lower-middle-income countries. Using the modified Kirkpatrick framework, 56% (n = 14 of 25 completed studies) demonstrated applied learning through embedded performance metrics. Only one study (4%) evaluated workplace behavior change (L3), and none (0%) assessed organizational impact (L4). Conclusions The educational value of technology in prehospital MCI training depends more on integrated performance measurement than on visual fidelity or surface immersion. Future investments should prioritize dual-use platforms with embedded assessment, improve pedagogical reporting transparency, and address geographic disparities in training access.

title: Task-specific gait biomechanics following unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury.
authors: Jäckle K, Kramer M, Meier MP, Hawellek T, Roch PJ, Homann C, Castro WHM, Wagner H, Boström K, Lehmann W, Weiser L.
abstract: Background Patients treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury may experience residual functional limitations. It remains unclear how these limitations manifest during tasks with different biomechanical demands. This exploratory study compared task-specific gait biomechanics between patients after fixation and healthy controls. Methods In this prospective cross-sectional observational study, 11 patients after unilateral iliosacral screw fixation (mean age 68.73 ± 9.89 years; 10 women) were compared with 21 healthy controls (52.48 ± 20.36 years; 11 women). Participants performed level walking, stair climbing, and step crossing using an Xsens MVN inertial motion capture system. Pelvic kinematics and model-estimated muscle activation and joint contact forces were evaluated using Computed MyoGraphy. Repeated trials were analyzed using participant-level random-intercept mixed models adjusted for age and sex. Pelvic rotation during stair climbing was the primary outcome; other outcomes were secondary or exploratory. Results Pelvic rotation during stair climbing was lower in patients (adjusted difference -5.45°, 95% CI -7.98 to -2.92°; within-family FDR-adjusted q = 0.0003). Contralateral pelvic tilt during step crossing was greater (adjusted difference 1.44°, 95% CI 0.46-2.41°; q = 0.011). No statistically significant group differences were detected in the analyzed level-walking parameters, thoracic counter-rotation, lower-limb muscle activation, or hip joint contact-force asymmetry. Model-estimated peak L5-S1 joint contact force during stair climbing was lower in patients (adjusted difference -0.70 × body weight; q = 0.001). Conclusions Patients after posterior pelvic ring injury treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation showed task-specific differences in pelvic movement during demanding locomotor activities. The findings support including stair and step tasks in functional assessment, but do not establish that fixation caused the observed differences. Small sample size, demographic imbalance, and the absence of patient-reported outcomes limit clinical interpretation.

title: Task-specific effects of noisy galvanic vestibular stimulation on gait symmetry in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
authors: Li Y, Zhang Z, Yasen A, Peng X, Miao Y, Qian S, Xie H.
abstract: Background Vestibular dysfunction has been identified as a potential contributor to postural instability and gait asymmetry in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Noisy galvanic vestibular stimulation (nGVS) enhances gait performance by optimizing vestibular signal processing via stochastic resonance. However, how nGVS modulates gait symmetry in AIS and whether its efficacy depends on locomotor tasks or spinal deformity severity remain to be elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the effects of nGVS on medial-lateral gait symmetry in patients with AIS during level walking and single-step stair negotiation. Methods This single-group crossover study recruited 30 patients with AIS to perform level walking, stair ascent, and stair descent under nGVS, sham-stimulation, and no-stimulation conditions. Primary dependent measures included medial-lateral gait symmetry across kinematic (lateral trunk displacement (T), lateral trunk lean (α), lateral pelvic displacement (P), pelvic obliquity (β), and hip adduction (θ)) and kinetic domains (first (ML1) and second (ML2) medial-lateral ground reaction force peaks), quantified by the symmetry index (SI) and normalized cross-correlation coefficient (Xcorr). Post-hoc comparisons prioritized the (nGVS vs. sham) contrast to isolate true nGVS efficacy. Correlations between the sham-controlled net efficacy (Δ) and Cobb angle were also examined. Results Compared to sham stimulation, nGVS significantly increased Xcorr_α (descent: p = 0.017; ascent: p = 0.033), Xcorr_β (descent: p = 0.006), Xcorr_θ (ascent: p = 0.008), and Xcorr_ML (descent: p p = 0.015; ascent: p = 0.022) during single-step stair negotiation. Correlation analyses revealed that greater Cobb angle was significantly correlated with Δ Xcorr_ML (descent: ρ = 0.583, p = 0.001; ascent: r = 0.575, p = 0.001), Δ Xcorr_α (descent: r = 0.539, p = 0.002; ascent: ρ = 0.427, p = 0.019), Δ Xcorr_β (descent: ρ = 0.394, p = 0.031), Δ Xcorr_θ (ascent: r = 0.398, p = 0.030), and Δ SI_ML1 (descent: ρ = - 0.444, p = 0.014). However, this state-dependent relationship did not reach statistical significance across Δ SI_α ( r = - 0.394, p = 0.137) and Δ SI_β ( r = - 0.423, p = 0.108). Conclusions These findings demonstrated that nGVS ameliorated medial-lateral gait symmetry in AIS by refining multi-segmental control under heightened biomechanical demands, indicating a task-specific pattern. Furthermore, nGVS-induced enhancements in medial-lateral gait symmetry were state-dependent, wherein patients exhibiting larger Cobb angles within the mild-to-moderate range (10°-30°) derived greater biomechanical gains.

title: Spatial Niches Shape Function in the Intratumoral Microbiome: From Multiscale Mapping to Niche-Informed Therapy.
authors: Dong L, Song Y, Li X, Wu J, Luo X, Du Y, Xu T.
abstract: Most studies of the intratumoral microbiome describe microbial composition and abundance but do not reveal where bacteria are located within the tumor microenvironment. Evidence that microbial signals vary across tumor regions and host-cell compartments makes spatial context essential to biological interpretation. In this review, we organize evidence at three levels: tissue niches reflect oxygenation, perfusion, pH, necrosis, and anatomy, cellular niches involve malignant, immune, and stromal cells, and physical interfaces include intracellular residence, extracellular association, biofilms, and diffusible products. We examine how contamination-aware sequencing, single-cell host-microbe profiling, spatial transcriptomics, and imaging distinguish detection from localization and relate microbial geography to host-cell states. Spatial organization may affect oncogenic signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, DNA damage, immune regulation, metastatic fitness, and treatment response. The same bacterial strain may exert opposing immune effects inside and outside host cells. This framework clarifies therapeutic implications. Engineered bacteria can deliver payloads to hypoxic, poorly perfused regions, whereas intracellular nanocarriers, species-selective phages, and biofilm-disrupting platforms address different microbial reservoirs. Major limitations include low-biomass contamination, uncertain viability, incomplete localization, limited causal evidence, and poorly resolved temporal dynamics. Integrating microbial identity with location and physical state should yield more mechanistic models of the intratumoral microbiome and better-defined therapeutic strategies.

title: Resilience and its mediating role in the association between family functioning and symptom experience in kidney transplant recipients: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Tang Y, Zhu J, Li J, Zhou J, Wang R, Qiu T.
abstract: Objective To investigate the levels of family functioning, resilience, and symptom experience in kidney transplant recipients, and to examine the mediating role of resilience in the relationship between family functioning and symptom experience. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to February 2025. A convenience sample of 333 kidney transplant recipients was recruited from a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China. Participants completed the Chinese Version of the Resilience Scale for Kidney Transplantation, the Organ Transplant Symptom and Well-being Inventory, and the Family APGAR Index. Data were analyzed using correlation, hierarchical regression, and bootstrap mediation tests. Results Participants reported a moderate level of symptom burden (OTSWI total score: 46.56 ± 23.86). Both resilience (r = -0.222, p Conclusion The findings are consistent with resilience partially mediating the association between family functioning and symptom experience in kidney transplant recipients. Assessing both family support and psychological resilience may help identify high-risk patients and inform integrated interventions aimed at alleviating symptom burden.Given the cross-sectional design, causal inference cannot be established.

title: Relaxin-2 reverses diastolic dysfunction and suppresses sustained arrhythmias in a rat model of Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF).
authors: Palma JB, Gabris-Weber B, McMahon B, Mauro AJ, St Hilaire C, Cuevas RA, Dschietzig TB, Romero G, Salama G.
abstract: Aims Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) afflicts millions annually and current treatments provide symptomatic relief. The goal is to test the effects of synthetic human Relaxin-2 (RLX) on diastolic dysfunction (DD) and arrhythmia vulnerability. Methods and results Male ZSF1 rats were placed on a normal diet (ND, N = 8 controls) or a high-fat diet (HFD, N = 11), resulting in the development of DD in 11-weeks, based on serial echocardiograms (enlarged left atrium (LA), wall thickness, doppler flow: E/e'). Once HFpEF was confirmed, ND and HFpEF rats were randomly treated with Relaxin (400 µg/kg/day RLX, N = 6) or the vehicle (N = 5) for 2-weeks using implanted minipumps. Echocardiograms were repeated for 2 more weeks, then hearts were isolated, optically mapped, subjected to programmed electrical stimulation (PES) and tissues dissected for immuno-fluorescence (IF), and qPCR analysis. Circulating levels of glucose, RLX and NT-pro-ANP were measured, pre- and post-treatment. Echocardiograms indicated that RLX reversed DD by reducing LA dimensions and E/e'. Optical mapping showed that vehicle-treated, ND rats (N = 3) had non-sustained atrial (1/3), and ventricular (3/3) arrhythmias and RLX-treatment reduced them to 0/3 and 1/3, respectively. Vehicle-treated, HFD rats had non-sustained (2/5) and sustained (2/5) atrial and ventricular arrhythmias (N = 5). RLX-treatment (N = 6) suppressed sustained atrial and ventricular arrhythmias (0/6) but not non-sustained atrial (2/6) and ventricular (3/6) arrhythmias. RLX tended to increase conduction velocity (CV), particularly at short cycle lengths consistent with increased Nav1.5, Connexin-43, β-catenin and Wnt1 expression, based on IF. There were no significant changes in fibrosis in this HFpEF model. NT-pro-ANP was elevated in HFpEF and reduced towards control values by RLX. qPCR analysis showed that RLX decreased Dickkopf (DKK1) and Matrix Metallopeptidase 1a (MMP1A) genes and increased SCN5A expression compared to vehicle (N = 6 and 5, respectively). Conclusions The ZSF1 model showed indications of HFpEF, including DD, enlargement of the LA, hemodynamic stress, increased vulnerability to sustained AF and VF, and elevated glucose and blood pressure. RLX treatment largely reversed DD, hemodynamic stress, and suppressed sustained arrhythmias. RLX elicited cardiac genomic changes, most likely through Wnt/canonical signaling, demonstrating RLX's potential as a therapy for HFpEF.

title: Real-world treatment patterns following denosumab discontinuation: a descriptive epidemiological study.
authors: Yoshiyama T, Fukasawa T, Masuda S, Matsuda S, Kawakami K.
abstract: This descriptive epidemiological study suggests that sequential osteoporosis therapy after denosumab discontinuation is underutilized in real-world practice. Within 1 year after discontinuation, approximately 30% of patients restarted denosumab, approximately half had no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and only 16% initiated sequential osteoporosis therapy. Purpose To describe real-world treatment patterns following denosumab discontinuation, including delayed reinitiation, no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and sequential osteoporosis therapy. Methods This descriptive epidemiological study used a Japanese claims database (April 2014-March 2024). We included adults aged ≥40 years who newly initiated denosumab and discontinued it after ≥2 doses. Discontinuation was defined as the last administration before a gap of >240 days or final observed administration followed by ≥240 days without another administration. The primary outcomes within 1 year after discontinuation were delayed denosumab reinitiation, no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and sequential osteoporosis therapy. We also described the type and timing of sequential therapy and estimated the 1-year cumulative incidence of fragility fractures. Results Among 37,526 eligible patients, the 1-year cumulative incidence of delayed denosumab reinitiation was 29.6%, the probability of no subsequent osteoporosis treatment was 50.9%, and the cumulative incidence of sequential osteoporosis therapy was 16.3%. Oral bisphosphonates were the most frequently used sequential therapy (26.7%), followed by romosozumab (22.2%), selective estrogen receptor modulators (21.3%), intravenous bisphosphonates (15.1%), teriparatide (14.6%), and abaloparatide (0.1%). Sequential therapy was most often initiated 180-209 days after discontinuation, particularly for romosozumab (45.7%), whereas selective estrogen receptor modulators were frequently initiated 0-29 days after discontinuation (39.8%). The 1-year cumulative incidence of fragility fractures was 5.4%. Conclusions Within 1 year after discontinuation, approximately 30% of patients restarted denosumab, half received no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and one in six initiated sequential therapy. These findings suggest a substantial gap in the continuity of osteoporosis care.

title: Re: Initial experience of benign upper gastrointestinal robotic-assisted surgery: first 200 cases and early postoperative outcomes.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Al-Qasem M, Greene K, Akharaekpanya I, Bawa S, Horgan L, Nevins EJ.

title: RPDL-YOLO: An efficient YOLOv8 framework for small bird detection in airport airside environments.
authors: Wen X, Liu L, Chen Y, Liu Z, Ma Z, Wu Y, Liang K, Jiang T, Yang H.
abstract: Bird intrusions into airport security zones pose significant threats to aviation safety. However, the small size, rapid movement, and irregular flight patterns of birds often result in missed detections and false alarms in vision-based surveillance systems, especially in complex open-sky environments with low contrast and significant background interference. Although YOLOv8s achieves strong real-time performance, it remains limited in fine-grained feature representation and small-object detection capability. To address these challenges, we propose an improved detection model termed RPDL-YOLO (Refined Perception with Dual-branch Detection and Localization YOLO). The proposed model introduces three key enhancements: (1) integrating RepViTBlock into the backbone to improve spatial feature representation; (2) removing the redundant P5 detection head and constructing a dual-branch high-resolution P2 detection structure to strengthen small-object perception; and (3) designing a Mix_IoU loss function that combines EIoU and GIoU to improve localization accuracy and training stability. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the YOLOv8s baseline, the proposed method achieves improvements of 7.6% in Precision, 5.4% in Recall, and 4.6% in mAP@50, while maintaining a real-time inference speed of 93.1 FPS. These results demonstrate that RPDL-YOLO significantly enhances detection performance for small and fast-moving bird targets while maintaining computational efficiency, making it suitable for practical airport bird-strike prevention.

title: Quality-of-life following emergency laparotomy: is frailty a factor?
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: McKeever C, Curl-Roper T.
abstract: Introduction More than half of patients undergoing emergency laparotomy (EL) are over 65 years of age, and frailty doubles the inpatient mortality for these patients. This study aims to measure quality-of-life (QoL) following EL, and determine whether outcomes are impacted by preoperative frailty. Methods We present four years of follow-up data (7 February 2020 to 5 February 2024) for patients who underwent EL at our single centre. Patients completed the 5-Level EQ-5D and 12-Item Short Form questionnaires at follow-up, the outcomes of which are presented. The responses of patients in low-risk (Clinical Frailty Score [CFS] 1-3, American Society of Anesthesiologists [ASA] grade 1-2) and high-risk (CFS 4-8, ASA 3-5) groups were compared. Results Some 988 patients were prospectively entered into the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit database during the study period. Of these, 590 patients (60%) were followed up, 40% were frail (CFS 4-8) and 57% had a high ASA grade (3-5). Overall, our cohort of patients had QoL outcomes that were between 4.6% (mental component) and 17.4% (physical component) lower than would be expected for the baseline population. Frail (CFS 4-8) and physiologically less fit (ASA 3-5) patients had significantly worse QoL outcomes ( p Conclusion Our cohort of patients had a lower QoL following EL than the baseline population. High preoperative CFS or ASA grade was associated with lower QoL. Where appropriate during the consent process, surgeons should consider counselling frail and unfit patients regarding the potential for low QoL postoperatively.

title: Psychometric validation of the European Portuguese version of Quality of Life Questionnaire of the European Foundation for Osteoporosis (QUALEFFO-41) in the Portuguese population.
authors: Azevedo SF, Barbosa AP, Cunha A, Melim D, Augusto D, Pimentel G, Oliveira M, Vieira R, Barcelos A.
abstract: The European Portuguese version of the QUALEFFO-41 showed good reliability, validity, and excellent discriminatory ability between patients with vertebral fragility fractures and controls. These findings support its use as a disease-specific quality-of-life instrument in Portuguese clinical practice and research. Purpose Vertebral fragility fractures substantially impair quality of life (QoL). The Quality of Life Questionnaire of the European Foundation for Osteoporosis (QUALEFFO-41) is a disease-specific instrument widely used to assess QoL in patients with vertebral fractures; however, its psychometric properties have not yet been validated for use in Portugal. This study aimed to perform the psychometric validation of the European Portuguese version of the QUALEFFO-41. Materials and methods A multicentric prospective validation study was conducted in Portuguese patients with vertebral fragility fractures and age- and sex-matched controls. Following cognitive debriefing and cultural adaptation, participants completed the QUALEFFO-41 and the SF-36, with a 2-week retest interval. Internal consistency (Cronbach's α), test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC), construct validity (convergent and discriminant validity), criterion validity (correlations with SF-36), and discriminatory ability were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to determine optimal cut-off points. Results Seventy-five participants were included (55 patients with vertebral fragility fractures and 20 controls). Internal consistency was adequate across domains (Cronbach's α 0.70-0.98) and excellent for the total score (α = 0.90). Test-retest reliability was high, with ICCs ranging from 0.75 to 0.98. Multitrait analysis demonstrated satisfactory convergent (71.4-100%) and discriminant validity (70.6-100%). Significant correlations were observed between QUALEFFO-41 domains and corresponding SF-36 domains, particularly for general health perception (r = -0.85). Patients with vertebral fragility fractures reported significantly worse QoL than controls across all domains and the total score (p Conclusions The European Portuguese version of the QUALEFFO-41 demonstrates robust reliability, validity, and strong discriminatory capacity. It is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing quality of life in Portuguese patients with vertebral fragility fractures in both clinical practice and research settings.

title: Problem-solving and social support appraisals in the cross-sectional association between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity.
authors: Pretorius TB, Padmanabhanunni A.
abstract: The present study investigated the relationship between social media integration and PTSD-consistent symptomatology among South African university students, with a specific focus on the roles of problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support. Participants were 491 students who completed the Social Media Use Integration Scale, the Problem-Solving Inventory-20, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses with PROCESS. Social media integration was positively associated with overall PTSD-consistent symptomatology and all symptom clusters measured by the PCL-5. Problem-solving appraisal was negatively associated with PCL-5 symptom severity. It partially mediated the relationship between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity. Perceived social support showed a more selective pattern of association, with higher support linked to lower negative alterations in cognition and mood, as well as hyperarousal. In addition, social support moderated the relationship between social media use and PCL-5 symptom severity, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and hyperarousal. These findings suggest that greater social media integration is associated with higher PCL-5 symptom severity, whereas problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support serve as important protective factors. Interventions aimed at strengthening coping appraisals and supportive social networks may help reduce trauma-related distress among young adults in the context of frequent social media use.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with irregular red blood cell antibodies among blood donors in Eastern Tanzania.
authors: Monah MC, Shedura VJ, Torokaa PR, Urio L, Abdul S, Bulemo R, Mbwana MR, Ntibabara SS, Mwashiuya O, Tingo B, Mahiti M, Kibwana U, Masoud S, Manyahi J, Majigo M, Joachim A, Kamori D.
abstract: Background Irregular red blood cell (RBC) antibodies are antibodies other than naturally occurring anti-A and anti-B. Although the global prevalence of these antibodies is relatively low, ranging from 0.2% to 2%, donors who have irregular RBC antibodies can present immunological risk for patients due to hemolytic transfusion reactions. Hence, it is imperative to determine the prevalence of these antibodies in resource-limited settings where laboratory infrastructure for screening is limited. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence and factors associated with irregular RBC antibodies among blood donors in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted from 01st April to 31st May 2024. Random sampling was used to select participants. The data were summarized by using frequency and percentage for categorical variables and mean and standard deviation for continuous variables. The logistic regression model was used to assess the relationship between the presence of irregular RBC antibodies and the independent variables. A p-value of Results A total of 501 blood donors were enrolled in the study. The participants had a mean age of 32 years and a standard deviation (SD) of 9.48. The majority, 65.3% of participants, were male, and 83.6% had no history of blood transfusion. The overall prevalence of irregular RBC antibodies was 7.6% (95% CI 5.5%-10.3%). Being female (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.4, 95% CI 1.72-6.85), age over 40 years (aOR 4.4, 95% CI 1.29-15.00), and having a history of blood transfusion (aOR 3.1, 95% CI 1.53-6.42) were significantly associated with irregular RBC antibodies. Conclusion The present study revealed a relatively high prevalence of irregular RBC antibodies among eligible blood donors in Tanzania. Therefore, these findings highlight the need for enhanced practices in screening and the prudent use of blood and blood products in Tanzania.

title: Posterior Tibial Slope Is Not Associated With Failure After Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Tear Repair at a Minimum 2-Year Follow-Up.
authors: Rock C, Myers RJ, Agner KE, Al Janabi H, Abdelshahid M, Nowell J, Barker T, Kaeding CC, Magnussen RA, Flanigan DC, Apseloff NA.
abstract: Purpose To examine the relation between posterior tibial slope (PTS) and failure after medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT) repair. Methods Patients who underwent isolated primary arthroscopic transtibial pullout MMPRT repair between 2012 and 2022 at a single institution and with a minimum 2-year follow-up were retrospectively identified. Patients were grouped into high (PTS ≥ 12°), intermediate (PTS 8°-11°), and low (PTS ≤ 7°) categories. Failure was defined as repeat ipsilateral knee arthroscopy or conversion to knee arthroplasty. A Kaplan-Meier curve and log-rank test were employed to analyze the relation between PTS and MMPRT repair failure. Results A total of 74 patients (77% women) with a mean age of 52.3 ± 9.3 years (range 23.5-73.3 years) with a minimum 2-year follow-up were identified. The mean follow-up time was 4.8 years (range 2.4-7.8 years) in the failure group and 6.2 years (range 3.4-9.2 years) in the nonfailure group ( P = .004). The mean follow-up was 6.21 ± 1.74 years in the high PTS group, 5.91 ± 1.64 years in the intermediate group, and 5.50 ± 1.81 years in the low group ( P = .478). The overall failure rate was 15/74 (20.3%) at a median (interquartile range) of 2.70 (0.80-5.19) years. No significant differences in time to failure were observed among PTS groups. The median (interquartile range) surgery-free survival time was 6.2 (4.6-7.8) years in the high PTS group (n = 22; 5 failures), 6.2 (4.7-7.8) years in the intermediate PTS group (n = 38; 8 failures), and 5.5 (3.9-7.2) years in the low PTS group (n = 14; 2 failures) ( P = .91). There were also no significant differences in coronal alignment among PTS groups. Conclusions In this study, PTS was not significantly associated with failure rates or time to failure after isolated MMPRT repair. Level of evidence Level III, therapeutic retrospective comparative study.

title: Patient complaints in dentistry: A qualitative meta-synthesis.
authors: Snyman L, Postma TC, Van Staden W.
abstract: Introduction Patient complaints in dentistry concern their dissatisfaction, safety concerns, quality of care, and challenges within the patient-practitioner relationship. Whilst existing research of these complaints has largely focused on quantitative analysis of regulatory complaints and malpractice, these studies capture little of the meaning that patients express in their complaints. This study synthesized a qualitative understanding of patient complaints across various dentistry settings. Method This qualitative meta-synthesis followed the six-step approach of Sandelowski and Barroso, drawing on previously published qualitative findings from various studies that constituted a higher-order case as suggested by Hoon's design framework. Data was sourced through a comprehensive search of health databases (MEDLINE, PsycINFO, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL). From studies found suitable upon appraisal, findings were subjected to reflexive thematic analysis. The resulting synthesis is reported according to the PRISMA guidelines extended for qualitative evidence synthesis. Results From an initial 857 studies, 19 met criteria for inclusion. Complaints reflected patient experiences in four inter-related domains of concern, namely, 1) impeded access to dental care, 2) unsatisfactory communication, interactions and attitudes, 3) deficient clinical treatment, and 4) unethical and unprofessional conduct. These domains may be understood as underlying processes in which patients experienced threats to trust, patient agency and autonomy, relational security, and that professional and ethical obligations have been breached. They may also be understood as signals of broader systemic and relational functioning. Conclusion Our findings suggest that complaints may reflect breakdowns in the fiduciary patient-practitioner relationship and constitute an important source of insight into the relational and systemic conditions necessary for trustworthy, person-centered dental care. Clinical relevance The four domains yielded in this synthesis may inform dentists and health systems on the scope of compromised relationships and systemic deficiencies as well as efforts to improve the quality of dental care and reduce patient complaints.

title: Pathogen-specific salvage of totally implantable ports and the role of antibiotic lock therapy.
authors: Rothe K, Feder V, Corredor NC, Querbach C, Bogner C, Herhaus P, Erber J, Schneider J, Feihl S, Bassermann F, Spinner CD, Braitsch K.
abstract: Purpose Totally implantable venous-access ports (TIPs) are central to cancer therapy, but bloodstream infection (BSI) frequently ends in device loss. Device retention rests on systemic antibiotic therapy, to which antibiotic lock therapy (ALT) can be added, yet the determinants of successful salvage in adults are poorly defined. This study examined which TIP infections can be salvaged. Methods 233 consecutive episodes of TIP-related BSI at a tertiary cancer centre (2017-2020) were analysed retrospectively. The primary outcome was successful TIP salvage: retention of a functioning device with clinical cure. Determinants were assessed by logistic regression and salvage across protocol-defined pathogen categories was tested for trend. Results Isolates were Gram-positive in 58%, Gram-negative in 38% and fungal in 4%; 19% polymicrobial. The TIP was salvaged in 68/225 episodes (30%); primary explantation commonest (53%). Salvage fell across the protocol categories: coagulase-negative staphylococci 41%, Gram-negative bacilli/enterococci/other Gram-positives 35%, S. aureus/P. aeruginosa/Candida 2% (P for trend Conclusion TIP salvage was associated with the infecting organism. The pathogen gradient mirrored guideline-based removal recommendations. About 60% of attempted retentions succeeded, without detectable benefit of ALT. With a pathogen-stratified protocol, salvage can be attempted in selected patients.

title: Pain severity and quality of life among patients undergoing hemodialysis.
authors: Abudawood KA, Albeladi R, Alhindi R, Alqarni E, Aljelaidy N, Alghamdi R, Alfahmi M, Alkathiri R, Almasri N, Alotaibi R, Alamoudi FA.
abstract: Objectives Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive condition that imposes physical and psychological burdens, negatively affecting the quality of life (QOL) of patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD). Pain is a prevalent symptom linked to HD treatment. Multiple sociodemographic and clinical factors affect the QOL of people with CKD; therefore, healthcare providers must understand the relationship between these variables. This study aimed to examine the relationship between pain severity and QOL among adult patients undergoing hemodialysis. Methods An observational correlational cross-sectional study was conducted at inpatient and outpatient HD units. A convenience sample of 157 adult patients participated. They completed a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Arabic Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire (SF-MPQ), and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF).
