Results Participants reported a low-to-moderate QOL across domains, with the psychological domain having the lowest mean (55.04 ± 17.84). The mean pain severity was 3.94 ± 3.34, with 15% of the sample experiencing severe pain. Significant negative correlations were found between pain severity and physical (r = -0.444, p p p = 0.006) QOL domains. Regression analysis identified monthly income and age as significant predictors of psychological, social, and environmental QOL. Additionally, hemodialysis-specific factors showed limited predictive power, though longer dialysis sessions predicted better psychological QOL ( p = 0.005) and higher weekly dialysis frequency predicted better overall QOL ( p = 0.007). Conclusions Pain adversely affects multiple aspects of QOL in HD patients. Comprehensive interventions focusing on pain management and socioeconomic support are essential to improve QOL outcomes in this adult population.

title: Nipple reconstruction using banked autologous costal cartilage with modified Hammond flap technique.
authors: Park SK, Bernal IC, Brito EM, Daza S, Weiss ES.

title: Network analysis of physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress among Chinese university students.
authors: Wang J, Ma Y, Han T, Wang J.
abstract: Objective Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress may be interconnected among university students, but their dimension-specific associations remain unclear. This study examined their network structure and compared male and female networks. Methods A convenience sample of 1,600 university students from two higher-education institutions in central China was surveyed from 16 March to 29 May 2026. Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales. A 12-node regularized partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence, bridge expected influence, bootstrap procedures, and network comparison tests were used. Results The network retained 27 non-zero edges, with stronger connections mainly within domains. Daytime dysfunction-stress had the largest positive cross-domain edge-weight point estimate, whereas exercise frequency-stress and exercise duration-subjective sleep quality were prominent negative connections. Stress showed relatively high expected influence and positive bridge expected influence point estimates, although bootstrap difference tests did not clearly distinguish these estimates from those of several other nodes. No gender-related differences were detected in global strength, network structure, or individual edges after multiple-comparison correction, while supplementary analyses indicated limited detection capability. Conclusions Cross-domain associations among physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were concentrated in a limited number of dimensions, particularly stress, daytime dysfunction, exercise frequency, and exercise duration. Stress and daytime dysfunction showed relatively prominent sleep-psychological distress associations, whereas higher exercise frequency and longer exercise duration were associated with lower stress and fewer subjective sleep problems, respectively. No gender-related network differences were detected, but this does not establish network equivalence. These cross-sectional findings identify dimension-specific associations but cannot establish causal relationships or intervention targets.

title: Navigated robotic guidance for minimally invasive bertolotti resection technical feasibility and workflow evaluation.
authors: Good ZR, Good CR.
abstract: Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This original article evaluates the technical feasibility and workflow of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow to perform minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A technical framework is presented for preoperative computerized computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, and navigated robotic trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of the planned navigated robotic steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but they should not be interpreted as proof of superior outcomes. This initial paper outlines a novel technique, however; further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance can be established.

title: Musical Feedback to Reduce the Knee Adduction Moment Via Center of Pressure Medialization: A Proof-of-Concept Study in Healthy Adults for Knee Osteoarthritis Gait Retraining.
authors: Cedin L, Antognini C, Knowlton C, Ferrigno C, Wimmer MA.
abstract: Elevated knee adduction moment (KAM) is a primary contributor to medial knee osteoarthritis (OA) progression. Medialization of center of pressure (CoP) can reduce KAM, but sustaining engagement and a consistent walking pattern remains a challenge. We investigated whether concurrent plantar pressure-modulated musical feedback would cue a medial CoP shift to reduce KAM without producing detrimental lower limb compensations in healthy adults. Twelve participants (6F/6M; age: 31.5 ± 5.3 years) walked while a marker-based motion analysis system (Qualisys) and wireless pressure-sensing insoles (Moticon) recorded gait. Real-time insole data drove auditory feedback: self-selected music was progressively muffled whenever the participant failed to shift their CoP medially beyond their threshold (25 % reduction in peak lateral CoP from baseline). Gait was assessed at baseline, post-instructions, and post-training. Repeated-measures ANOVA was used for kinetics and spatiotemporal outcomes, and statistical parametric mapping, as a secondary analysis, for kinematic waveforms. All participants medialized their CoP based on instructions and musical feedback. Musical feedback significantly reduced the second KAM peak (post-training: -13.7 %; p = 0.002) and the knee adduction angular impulse (post-training: -9.4 %; p < 0.001), but with a borderline increase in peak knee flexion moment (p = 0.050) that may reflect compensation. Gait adaptations were executed without a change in walking speed. Also, foot progression angle and stride width remained unchanged. CoP medialization was achieved mainly through ankle inversion, ankle external rotation, and hip internal rotation. These preliminary findings support concurrent sonified biofeedback for gait retraining, warranting evaluation in medial knee OA patients.

title: Minimally Invasive Biological Gracilis Augmentation of Fascia Lata for Intra- and Extra-articular Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: XO FAST Technique.
authors: Denis-Aubrée P, Herman S, Hardy A, Bohu Y.
abstract: The fascia lata (FL) is a long-established and proven graft for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, allowing intra- and extra-articular reconstruction to be combined with a single graft and a single femoral tunnel, without femoral fixation. Despite its biomechanical and clinical advantages, its use has been limited by the morbidity of the donor site and the size of the incision. We describe a minimally invasive technique for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using a pedicled FL strip reinforced with the gracilis tendon, which reduces donor-site morbidity while maintaining the benefits of combined reconstruction. This technique is based on reproducible anatomical landmarks for harvesting the FL, a limited lateral, and simplified graft preparation. The graft allows optimal control of anterior and rotational stability of the knee while preserving the extensor apparatus and the semitendinosus tendon. The absence of femoral fixation, the use of a single femoral tunnel, and a single tibial interference screw make this technique particularly suitable for pediatric surgery, revision surgery, and situations with a high risk of rerupture. This technical note presents a reliable and reproducible alternative to conventional techniques for reconstructing the anterior cruciate ligament using the FL, limiting morbidity while optimizing stability and functional outcomes.

title: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma presenting with chest wall and skeletal disease mimicking plasmacytoma.
authors: Hassan SA, Kamalasanan K, Pincha R, Khanikar D.

title: Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Reconstruction With Transverse Reefing (Tubing) of Medial Patellar Retinaculum and Biological Fixation.
authors: Makhmalbaf H, Hoseinzadeh Moghaddam S, Vatankhah A, Ebrahimzadeh MH, Samei M, Ganji R.
abstract: The medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) is regarded as one of the main stabilizers of the knee. Its importance is underscored by the fact that in most cases of acute lateral patellar dislocation, rupture of the MPFL occurs. It is also a key factor in recurrent patellar dislocations. Therefore, MPFL reconstruction surgery is the current approach to managing such cases. Numerous techniques have been practiced by surgeons, with some being more prevalent than others. Although there is extensive literature comparing the efficacy and safety of different techniques, no clear consensus has been reached. Furthermore, recurrent postoperative complications, such as knee pain, have prompted surgeons to seek new and less invasive techniques. In this technical note, we describe an implant-free MPFL reconstruction method leveraging the medial patellar retinaculum. Through horizontal suturing, a reinforced tubular reef is created to mimic the native MPFL and is secured via a subperiosteal femoral pouch with minimal invasiveness. This approach avoids bone tunnels, and it is expected to reduce fracture risk, eliminate donor-site morbidity, and enhance reproducibility for surgeons.

title: Maintenance of periarticular joint angles after varization double-level osteotomy for severe valgus deformity: a technical and radiographic mid-term case series.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Herbst M, Schröter S, Ateschrang A, Histing T, Ahrend MD.
abstract: Purpose To assess the restoration and mid-term course of mechanical alignment and periarticular femoral and tibial joint angles after varization double-level osteotomy (DLO) in patients with severe valgus malalignment. Methods This retrospective case series included 13 knees treated with medial closing-wedge distal femoral and high tibial osteotomy between 2011 and 2015. Eight knees were available at a minimum follow-up of five years. Mechanical alignment and periarticular joint angles were assessed preoperatively, six weeks postoperatively, and at final follow-up. Individual radiographic trajectories, conversion to total knee arthroplasty, complications, and postoperative patient-reported outcomes were evaluated descriptively. Results Seven patients with eight knees were assessed after a mean follow-up of 7.5 ± 1.2 years. Mean mTFA changed from 9.6 ± 2.6° valgus preoperatively to - 1.4 ± 1.5° six weeks postoperatively and 0.1 ± 4.7° at final follow-up. Mean mLDFA changed from 86.1 ± 2.2° to 90.5 ± 2.5° postoperatively and 90.2 ± 2.4° at final follow-up; mean mMPTA changed from 92.4 ± 1.6° to 86.4 ± 1.5° and 87.3 ± 2.1°, respectively. Individual trajectories were heterogeneous; one knee developed recurrent valgus alignment with a marked increase in JLCA. None of the eight knees underwent conversion to total knee arthroplasty. Three complications occurred, and implant removal was performed in all knees. Conclusion Within the limitations of this small retrospective case series, varization DLO restored mechanical alignment and periarticular femoral and tibial joint angles in selected patients with severe valgus malalignment. Group-level periarticular bony angles remained close to the early postoperative values at mid-term follow-up, although individual radiographic trajectories were heterogeneous. Larger prospective comparative studies are required to determine clinical effectiveness, complication rates, survivorship, and valgus-specific indication criteria.

title: Life satisfaction and motives for postponing parenthood among Polish women: A sequential indirect association model of depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination.
authors: Szcześniak M, Świątek AH, Ivanytska M, Falewicz A, Rybarski R, Pracka J, Pietruszka R.
abstract: Postponed parenthood is an increasingly common feature of reproductive patterns in high- and middle-income societies. Although previous research has examined factors associated with delayed parenthood, less is known about the psychological characteristics linked to self-reported motives for postponement. The present study examined the relationship between life satisfaction and motives for postponing parenthood and tested a theoretically ordered cross-sectional model involving depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination. Participants were 201 childless Polish women aged 20-44 years (M = 32.75, SD = 6.91). They completed the Satisfaction with Life Scale, the Multidimensional Scale of Motives for Postponing Parenthood, the Brief Screen for Depression, the Dark Future Scale, and the Pure Procrastination Scale. Higher life satisfaction was negatively related to some, but not all, motive-specific outcomes and to depressive symptoms. Depressive symptoms were positively associated with future anxiety, which was, in turn, positively related to procrastination. Higher procrastination was linked to higher motive-specific and overall postponement scores. The hypothesized specific sequential indirect association of life satisfaction with motives through depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination was statistically supported for uncertainty and incompetence (B = -.0083, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0214, - .0007]), fear of change (B = -.0054, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0148, - .0003]), financial security concern (B = -.0095, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0229, - .0012]), and the overall motives score (B = -.0324, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0818, - .0027]). The corresponding sequential indirect associations were not supported for self-focus, parenthood as a burden, or worry about a child's future, indicating that the pattern differed across motives. Sensitivity analyses indicated that some outcome-specific sequential associations were not robust to the exclusion of potential multivariate outliers. Overall, the findings suggest that life satisfaction, depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination show distinct associations with self-reported reasons for postponing parenthood. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed sequential indirect associations should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal psychological mechanisms.

title: Knowledge-guided multi-task learning with cascade out-of-distribution rejection for rice leaf disease diagnosis.
authors: Lyu X, Bai L, Yu Y, Liu L.
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of rice leaf diseases is essential for timely crop protection, but most deep learning classifiers offer little insight into the visual evidence behind their predictions and assign a disease label even to non-target images. This study aimed to develop a diagnostic framework that integrates phytopathological knowledge into deep learning and rejects out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We propose the Knowledge-Guided Multi-Task Rice Network (MTRNet), which attaches a disease-diagnosis head and three auxiliary heads for lesion shape, color, and location to a shared ResNet-50 backbone. An expert knowledge matrix automatically generates the attribute labels, providing knowledge-guided supervision without pixel-level annotation. At inference, a two-stage Cascade Inference System (CIS) combines a color-based biological plausibility filter with a consistency check between the predicted disease and its predicted attributes. MTRNet was evaluated on a public dataset of 5,932 images of four rice diseases (Leaf Blast, Brown Spot, Bacterial Leaf Blight, and Tungro) and on 1,000 OOD images, using source-aware five-fold cross-validation that keeps all copies of each source photograph within a single partition. MTRNet achieved an accuracy of 96.32% ± 1.45% and a macro-F1 score of 96.43% ± 1.34%, while providing attribute-level predictions for every diagnosis. The CIS rejected 77.78% ± 0.63% of OOD images while retaining 91.71% of genuine diseased leaves, and a split-sample analysis showed that threshold selection introduced negligible optimism (about 0.2 percentage points). The framework adds only 0.027 M parameters to the backbone, and the plausibility filter requires 0.34 ms per image. These results indicate that combining knowledge-guided multi-task learning with cascade rejection enables accurate, attribute-informed, and computationally efficient rice disease diagnosis with a built-in safeguard against non-target inputs, providing a practical basis for reliable image-based disease screening in agriculture.

title: Graft selection in combined PCL and PLC reconstruction: a scoping review of current evidence and knowledge gaps.
authors: Rinaldi VG, Fogacci A, Sassoli I, Morri M, Cimatti P, Dallari D, Zaffagnini S, Marcheggiani Muccioli GM.
abstract: Graft selection is a key component of combined posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) and posterolateral corner (PLC) reconstruction, yet the factors guiding graft choice remain poorly defined. The purpose of this scoping review was to map current graft utilization patterns, examine how graft selection is reported in relation to injury characteristics and reconstructive strategy, summarize the available graft-related clinical evidence, and identify methodological and reporting gaps that currently preclude evidence-based recommendations. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Studies published between January 2005 and January 2025 reporting graft selection in adult patients undergoing combined PCL and PLC reconstruction were included. Data regarding study characteristics, graft utilization, surgical techniques, clinical and radiological outcomes, and factors influencing graft selection were extracted and descriptively synthesized. Fourteen studies involving 365 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most studies were retrospective case series with moderate methodological quality. Allografts, particularly Achilles and tibialis tendon allografts, were more frequently used for PCL reconstruction, whereas hamstring autografts predominated in PLC reconstruction. However, no single graft strategy emerged as standard practice. The rationale underlying graft selection was explicitly reported in only 3 of 14 studies (21.4%), while fixed institutional protocols predominated and no study described a patient-specific graft selection algorithm. Furthermore, no study directly compared alternative graft sources or reported graft-specific clinical outcomes. Despite substantial heterogeneity in graft utilization, reconstruction techniques, and outcome assessment, satisfactory clinical and radiological outcomes were consistently reported. Current literature describes which grafts are used for combined PCL and PLC reconstruction but provides limited information on how or why graft selection is performed. The absence of standardized reporting, comparative studies, and graft-specific outcome analyses currently prevents evidence-based recommendations. Future prospective studies should evaluate graft selection as a dedicated research question and incorporate standardized reporting of decision-making criteria and graft-specific outcomes.

title: Frequency of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis and associated factors at b/tsDMARD initiation in a tertiary referral center: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Eken A, Ayan G, Yazgan BF, Kart Bayram GS, Ekici M, Kiraz S, Ertenli İ, Kalyoncu U, Kılıç L.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease in which adequate disease control remains challenging in a subset of patients despite the availability of numerous therapeutic agents. In 2021, the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) established the definition of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T-RA). To determine the frequency of D2T-RA among RA patients treated with biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs) and to examine factors recorded at b/tsDMARD initiation that were associated with subsequent D2T-RA classification. In this single-center cross-sectional study, D2T-RA status was assessed at an index visit conducted between April and November 2023. D2T-RA status was determined at the index visit using a study-specific operationalization of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) definition. Treatment-initiation data were collected retrospectively. Clinically selected multivariable models were adjusted for the interval from b/tsDMARD initiation to the index visit. Analyses were repeated after removing the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ) item from the definition. Of the 487 patients included, 181 (37.1%) met the operationalized D2T-RA criteria. None of the factors in the primary model was independently associated with D2T-RA classification. In the model without the 28-joint Disease Activity Score based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR), higher HAQ was associated with D2T-RA (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.03-2.36; p = 0.036). Removing the HAQ-based item reclassified 23 patients and reduced the frequency to 32.4%. With this outcome, younger age at diagnosis (OR 0.972, 95% CI 0.949-0.996; p = 0.023) and higher body mass index (OR 1.055, 95% CI 1.008-1.103; p = 0.020) were associated with D2T-RA in the primary model. D2T-RA was common in this tertiary cohort of patients receiving b/tsDMARDs. The primary model did not identify an independently associated baseline factor, whereas higher HAQ, younger age at diagnosis, and higher BMI were associated with D2T-RA in additional models. As these associations were not consistent across models, they should be interpreted cautiously..

title: Fracture risk in 85-year-old women: associations with volumetric bone mineral density, physical performance and falls.
authors: Wihlborg A, Åkesson KE, Gerdhem P.
abstract: This prospective study demonstrates associations of volumetric BMD (vBMD) by pQCT, areal BMD (aBMD) by DXA, physical performance (one-leg balance, gait speed, and knee extension force), and fall history with fracture risk in 85-year-old women. A failed one-leg balance test was associated with both hip and any fracture independent of femoral neck aBMD. Total radial vBMD was associated with any fracture. Gait speed and previous falls showed associations with fracture risk of similar magnitude as femoral neck aBMD. These findings suggest that functional performance measures may enhance fracture risk assessment in older women. Purpose This prospective study evaluates associations between fracture risk and volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), physical performance tests, and fall history, in comparison with femoral neck areal BMD (aBMD) by DXA, in 85-year-old women. Methods In the Osteoporosis Prospective Risk Assessment (OPRA) study, 382 women aged 85 years were followed for a mean of 4.3 years. Participants underwent pQCT of the radius and tibia and DXA of the hip and lumbar spine, performed physical performance tests (one-leg standing balance, considered failed if balance could not be maintained for 5 s; gait speed, analyzed continuously; and knee extension force, measured by isometric dynamometry), and reported fall history. Cox proportional hazards models estimated fracture risk, adjusting for BMI, previous fracture, smoking, and use of vitamin D, glucocorticoids, and bisphosphonates. Results During a mean follow-up of 4.3 years, 116 women (30%) sustained a fracture. Trabecular vBMD at the radius and tibia was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.85 and HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.86, respectively). Radial trabecular vBMD was also associated with lower hip fracture risk (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.42-0.98). Femoral neck aBMD was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.90), but not hip fracture (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50-1.00). A failed balance test and low gait speed was associated with higher risk of any fracture (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.04-2.29 and HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.48, respectively). In multivariate analyses, a failed balance test remained associated with any fracture (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.12-2.56) and hip fracture (HR 2.30, 95% CI 1.05-5.02). Total radial vBMD remained associated with any fracture (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.996). Conclusion Volumetric BMD by pQCT was associated with fracture risk independent of commonly recognized clinical risk factors in 85-year-old women. Physical performance tests were associated with fracture risk in unadjusted analyses, and the one-leg balance test additionally remained associated after adjustment for clinical risk factors and femoral neck aBMD.

title: Evidence for an upper cretaceous strandline deposit in the Lance Formation, Wyoming, USA.
authors: Snyder K, Llempen N, Darling C, Franchini A, McLain M, Chadwick A.
abstract: A series of apparently related quarries in the Maastrichtian (uppermost Cretaceous) Lance Formation of Wyoming provided the opportunity to evaluate the taphonomic mode for a suite of vertebrate fossils. Extensive work on the Hanson Ranch over the past three decades has exposed tens of thousands of fossils from dinosaur-bearing bonebeds. All of these bonebeds consist of disarticulated and disassociated remains. However, seven recently discovered quarries have yielded the remains of one or more dinosaur taxa (e.g., Triceratops, Edmontosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Anzu) in a state of association that was hitherto unknown on the ranch. These seven quarries were found along a line heading approximately 140 degrees, a heading reflected in the long axes of many of the elongate bones in the quarries. The preservation of associated remains suggests that soft-tissue connections or integumentary containment persisted during the transport and burial. We conclude that the floating, encapsulated carcasses of these animals were stranded along a southeasterly trending shoreline of the Western Interior Seaway.

title: Digital interaction design promotes cultural identification and heritage-related participation intention: Evidence from the Wangchuan ceremony.
authors: Liu Y, Duan K.
abstract: The sustainable protection of intangible cultural heritage faces unprecedented challenges due to the process of urbanization and the decline in the participation of the younger generation. Digital reconstruction offers a transformative way for heritage transmission, but its long-term contribution to cultural sustainability remains under-explored. This study examines the relationships among users' perceptions of digital heritage experiences, cultural identification, and heritage-related behavioural intention. On the basis of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the study introduces emotional design and cultural identification into the model and analyzes data from 220 valid questionnaires using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show significant positive associations between emotional design and perceived enjoyment, between perceived enjoyment and cultural identification, and between cultural identification and heritage-related behavioural intention. Cultural identification shows the strongest association with behavioural intention, suggesting its important role in linking users experiential responses with subsequent heritage-related behavioural intentions.These findings suggest that, if intangible cultural heritage wants to genuinely serve the sustainable development of culture, it should not remain at the level of static documentation, but should strive to create an interactive experience that can trigger emotional resonance, so as to drive the public's cultural identification. The evaluation framework provided by this study may provide reference for the design and evaluation of similar digital heritage projects.

title: Digital food delivery services in an emerging market: socioeconomic determinants and implications for service adoption in Türkiye.
authors: Ünver Ş, Kabakuş AK, Alkan Ö.
abstract: This study aims to identify the demographic, economic, and technological factors associated with individuals' likelihood of ordering food online in Türkiye. Understanding these determinants is essential for enhancing digital food service accessibility and consumer satisfaction in emerging economies. Using nationally representative microdata from the 2023 Turkish Statistical Institute's Household Information Technologies Survey, a binary logistic regression model was employed to estimate the probability of online food ordering. The model incorporated demographic variables (age, gender, education), economic factors (income and occupation), digital access indicators (computer ownership, social media use, and online information search), and regional classifications. Survey weights were applied to ensure representativeness. Results reveal that income level, age, gender, education, occupation, ownership of digital devices, social media use, and region were significantly associated with online food ordering behaviour. Women and younger, higher-income, and better-educated individuals are more likely to order food online. Regional disparities persist, with western Türkiye showing higher adoption rates than central and eastern regions, reflecting a digital divide in food delivery engagement. The findings suggest that improving technological infrastructure, digital literacy, and service quality in less developed regions could enhance inclusivity in online food delivery markets. Businesses can tailor digital marketing strategies toward younger and higher-income consumers. This study addresses an important gap in the literature by providing nationally representative evidence on the demographic, economic, and technological determinants of online food ordering behaviour in Türkiye.

title: Correction: Ultrasonography allows for a safe and early diagnosis of patellofemoral dysplasia in newborns: a prospective study.
authors: Moya-Angeler J, De la Torre-Conde C, Maestre-Cano D, Sanchez-Jimenez R, Jimenez-Soto C, Serrano-García C, Forriol F, León-Muñoz V.

title: Controlled Tensioning Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Augmentation Using Double-Tape Suture and Arthroscopic Lateral Soft-Tissue Release for Patellar Instability.
authors: Tan HY, Luo YF, Zeng JH, Huang P, Jin S, Deng XH, Zhang ZZ, Lin NH, Zhou AY, Chen Z.
abstract: Overtensioning the medial patellofemoral ligament during reconstruction is a key cause of patellofemoral overload, anterior knee pain, and limited flexion. We present a reproducible, tension-calibrated augmentation technique using a single 4.75-mm SwiveLock anchor preloaded with double FiberTape and sutures-eliminating graft harvest. This technique is intended as an augmentation rather than a full ligament substitution. The staged fixation strategy, combined with arthroscopic evaluation and selective lateral release, serves to minimize the risk of medial overconstraint. The anchor is placed at the Schöttle point, and sutures are passed subcapsularly to the medial patella, exiting through two 2.5-mm transverse bone tunnels. Initial lateral knot fixation is performed, followed by stepwise lateral release and vastus lateralis detachment to relieve residual lateral tension. Final FiberTape fixation is completed under arthroscopic visualization, allowing real-time adjustment to avoid overtightening. Final fixation was performed at approximately 30° of knee flexion, with the patella centered within the trochlear groove. This technique restores patellar tracking, permits full flexion, and may help reduce the risk of recurrence in recurrent patellar instability.

title: Control of invasive alien plants on an oceanic island modifies invertebrate folivory to the benefit of native biodiversity.
authors: Baguette FMMP, Seeburrun G, Baider C, Florens FBV.
abstract: Herbivory is one of the most important ecological interactions globally. Herbivores, among which arthropods predominate, play key roles in fundamental ecological processes, and may profoundly affect plants. Invasive alien plants (IAP) may influence herbivory in varied ways, including by supplying additional resources, yet, few comparative studies have assessed how IAP impact herbivory, particularly on heavily invaded oceanic islands. Here, we assess how IAP influences folivory, the prominent form of herbivory, to explore the ecological and conservation implications in a habitat restoration context. We studied a protected native forest on the oceanic island of Mauritius, comprising an area invaded by IAP and an adjacent area weeded of IAP used for comparison. We first quantified IAP impacts on folivory by comparing arthropod communities between invaded and weeded areas using yellow sticky traps set along 100 m transects. We then compared the incidence and severity of folivory (including chewing, galling, and mining) across habitat types on four shared native species between habitats, along with Psidium cattleyanum , the dominant IAP in invaded forest, and Harungana madagascariensis , the dominant native pioneer tree naturally regenerating in weeded forest. Finally, we compared the specific leaf area (SLA), folivory rate, and consumed leaf area on the selected species between habitats. Arthropod species richness and abundance were comparable between habitats but community structure differed. Overall, herbivory incidence on natives was higher in invaded than weeded area, with Antirhea borbonica and Labourdonnaisia calophylloides showing higher odds of folivory in invaded forest. Herbivory severity was also higher in the invaded area, with A. borbonica showing higher herbivory severity damage, although the opposite was found for Aphloia theiformis . There was no significant difference of folivory rate between habitat type, except for H. madagascariensis that sustained a significantly higher rate than P. cattleyanum . Overall, mean consumed leaf area was higher on H. madagascariensis in the weeded area, and A. borbonica in the invaded one. Finally, SLA was significantly higher on H. madagascariensis compared with P. cattleyanum , like on L. calophylloides in weeded area. Our study shows that IAP control represents limited loss for folivores. By allowing native pioneer regeneration, IAP control indirectly increases leaf resource availability, and decreases the risk of folivory damage on native species. Conservation strategies should therefore focus more strongly on in situ control of IAP, and keep native pioneer species, instead of removing them, as often done on the island. This would strengthen plant-herbivore interactions and enhance benefits for biodiversity. Ultimately, not cutting back pioneer native trees would free conservation resources, allowing the restoration of larger areas, and further improve the effectiveness of conservation measures.

title: Clinical outcomes and safety reporting after image-guided and non-image-guided subtalar joint injections: a systematic review.
authors: Gibson J, Agrawal N, Maleyko I, Thompson B, Saran S, Labidi M, Botchu R.
abstract: Background Subtalar joint (STJ) injections are used for chronic hindfoot pain but evidence comparing guidance methods remains limited. Methods This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase (via Ovid), Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to December 2025, and the searches were re-run in a broadened form in July 2026. Eligible studies included comparative studies, single-arm cohort or case-series studies with 10 or more procedures and technical/cadaveric accuracy studies reporting subtalar-specific outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Heterogeneity and scarce direct comparison precluded meta-analysis. Results Seventeen studies were eligible: 12 reported clinical data and five reported cadaveric technical accuracy data only (one clinical study also contributed a cadaveric control arm). Denominators are reported in their own units and are not combined: the clinical studies contributed 129 patients (six studies), 100 injected joints (four studies) and 779 injections (two studies). Ultrasound, fluoroscopy and landmark-guided injection were each reported in five studies. No study of CT or SPECT-CT guidance provided a subtalar-specific outcome. Needle placement accuracy ranged from 68 to 100%, but difference in design, populations and confirmation methods prevented comparison between modalities. Conclusion STJ injections are associated with clinical improvement but evidence is predominantly observational and heterogeneous. Differences in reporting technical accuracy, injectate, clinical response and adverse events prevent comparison of guidance methods. No modality's superiority is established. Prospective comparative studies using standardised outcomes and consistent safety reporting are needed.

title: Causal effects of connective tissue diseases on sarcopenia-related traits and the mediating role of immune cell phenotypes: a mediation Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Kang H, Wang Q, Zhou Y, Huang Y, Su D.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a common comorbidity of connective tissue diseases (CTDs). However, the causal relationships between CTDs and sarcopenia-related traits, and whether immune cells mediate these effects, remain unclear. Methods We performed a three-step Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using genome-wide association study summary data of European ancestry. Step 1 evaluated the causal effects of seven CTDs on five sarcopenia-related traits. Step 2 screened 731 immune cell phenotypes for associations with these traits. Step 3 assessed the causal effects of the selected CTDs on the selected immune cell phenotypes. For each exposure-mediator-outcome triplet, the indirect effect and the mediation proportion were estimated using a two-step MR approach. Results Dermatomyositis (DM), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), polymyositis (PM), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) were causally associated with at least one sarcopenia-related trait. Among 731 immune traits, 15 were significantly associated with at least three traits after FDR correction. In patients with RA, mediation analysis indicated that HLA-DR expression on CD14 - CD16 - cells partially mediated the effect on appendicular lean mass (mediation proportion = 9.76%, P = 0.040, q = 0.099) and whole-body-fat-free mass (mediation proportion = 5.76%, P = 0.039, q = 0.099), though these mediation findings did not survive FDR correction and should therefore be considered exploratory. Conclusions This mediation MR study provides genetic evidence that DM, MCTD, PM and RA are causally associated with specific sarcopenia-related traits. The partial mediation of RA's effects through HLA-DR up-regulation on CD14⁻CD16⁻ cells suggests a potential immune pathway linking RA to muscle loss, though these findings require confirmation in independent cohorts. Key Points • The first mediation MR study to quantifies the mediating role of a specific immune cell phenotype in the causal pathway from CTDs to sarcopenia-related traits. • DM, MCTD, PM, and RA were causally associated with sarcopenia-related traits, with PM and RA showing the most consistent detrimental effects. • HLA-DR expression on CD14-CD16- cells may partially mediate the effect 3 of RA on appendicular lean mass and whole body fat free mass.

title: Bridging the Robotic Training Gap: Results of the Inaugural ASTS Robotic Kidney Donor and Transplant Masterclass.
authors: Rice TC, Kadri H, Nguyen M, Yoshida A, Godfrey C, Spaggiari M, Bababekov YJ, Khan AS, Abreu P.
abstract: Introduction Robotic surgery is increasingly utilized in living donor nephrectomy and kidney transplantation, yet structured training opportunities remain scarce. The American Society of Transplant Surgeons organized a dedicated Robotic Kidney Donor and Transplant Masterclass in December 2025 to address this gap. Methods A 2-day masterclass was held, featuring comprehensive didactic sessions and a robotic simulation wet lab. A precourse survey was distributed to all 13 attendees prior to the event, and a postcourse survey was distributed approximately 2 months afterward. Confidence in the procedure was gauged using Likert scales. Results All 13 attendees completed the presurvey (100% response rate), and 11 of 13 (84.6%) completed the postsurvey. Most respondents (76.9%) were already performing robotic donor nephrectomy at their centers, while 76.9% reported that no kidney transplants at their institution were performed robotically. Precourse confidence in robotic kidney transplantation was low (mean 2.15/5), significantly improving to a mean of 3.27/5 postcourse (p = 0.017). Confidence in robotic donor nephrectomy was already high precourse (mean 4.23/5) and remained so postcourse (mean 4.45/5, p = 0.578). All 11 postsurvey respondents (100%) would recommend the masterclass and endorsed annual delivery. Discussion This masterclass demonstrates a clear unmet need for structured robotic transplant training and shows meaningful improvement in self-reported confidence, particularly for robotic kidney transplantation. Society-led masterclasses represent a practical and scalable mechanism for disseminating robotic techniques across transplant programs.

title: Blood lipoprotein remodelling after non-severe paediatric burns: A longitudinal analysis beyond the acute phase.
authors: Ryan MJ, Scott C, Lawler NG, Masuda R, Davis JA, D'Vaz N, Yonker LM, Leonard MM, Fasano A, Whiley L, Nicholson JK, Holmes E, Wood FM, Lodge S.
abstract: Paediatric burn traumas are a global health concern shown to have long-term health consequences leading to increased morbidity and mortality. However, the underlying mechanisms contributing to these long-term health risks remain poorly understood. This study utilised 1H Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy to comprehensively determine the lipoproteomic changes in the acute injury phase and long-term perturbations in blood samples longitudinally collected from 142 patients. In the acute phase of burn injury 55% of the lipoprotein main fractions and subfractions were significantly altered compared to non-burn controls. The plasma profiles from the burn injury group demonstrated increased LDL (low density lipoprotein) triglyceride concentrations (adjusted p-value = 2.12x10-9), an increased Apolipoprotein B100/Apolipoprotein A1 ratio (adjusted p-value = 4.29x10-5) and decreased HDL (High Density Lipoprotein, adjusted p-value = 1.16x10-11). At 1-year post-burn injury, it was found that 53% of the lipoprotein fraction and subfractions were altered compared to non-burn controls. The lipoproteomic profile showed a shift in LDL subfraction distribution, with a decrease in larger LDL subfractions (LDL subfraction 2 particle number, adjusted p-value = 2.52 × 10-4) and an increase in smaller LDL subfractions (LDL subfraction 6 particle number, adjusted p-value = 6.47 × 10-5), a pattern previously associated with cardiometabolic and cardiovascular risk. Significant lipid compositional changes of VLDL (very-low density lipoprotein), IDL (intermediate density lipoprotein), LDL and HDL were also observed at 1-year post-burn injury, notably the largest shifts were observed in IDL compared with non-burn controls. The proportion of cholesterol esters were markedly increased from 31.3% to 40.6%, free cholesterol increased from 12.8% to 15.1%, while phospholipids reduced from 29.5% to 23.3% and triglycerides reduced from 26.3% to 21.1%. Overall, this study demonstrates persistent lipoproteomic alterations following paediatric burn injury. These findings identify persistent metabolic perturbations that are not captured by conventional lipid measures, but further longitudinal studies incorporating inflammatory biomarkers and clinical cardiovascular outcomes are required to determine their clinical significance and relationship to future cardiovascular health.

title: Assessing the inclusion of frailty scores in either the methodology or results of clinical intervention trials of heart failure: A scoping review.
authors: Al-Shalabi M, Nazar NA, Patel M.
abstract: Chronic heart failure is highly prevalent in older adults, in whom frailty is common and associated with poorer outcomes. Despite advances in guideline-directed medical therapy, concerns regarding tolerability and polypharmacy contribute to under-utilization in frail patients. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on how clinical interventional trials of heart failure management have incorporated frailty, specifically, whether trials have (i) stratified outcomes according to frailty status and/or (ii) adjusted treatment strategies based on frailty. We searched MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov for interventional trials of heart failure published up to August 2025 that incorporated frailty using validated assessment tools. Eligible studies stratified outcomes by frailty status and/or adjusted interventions based on frailty. Data were extracted and a narrative synthesis was conducted. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria. Seven were post-hoc analyses of randomized controlled trials, two were prespecified analyses, and one was a randomized controlled trial. Two studies evaluated exercise-based interventions, one on implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and the remainder on pharmacological-based therapies. Nine studies used the Rockwood cumulative deficit approach to measure frailty, although the parameters used varied between studies. Available secondary analyses suggest preserved efficacy across frailty groups for most pharmacological interventions, whereas other modalities did not show convincing improvements in heart failure-specific outcomes among frail patients. Primary evidence of heart failure interventions incorporating frailty remains limited, with a large bulk of the evidence available being retrospective. Although several reported pharmacological interventions appear to have preserved efficacy across frailty levels, some of these therapies were not recommended in current guidelines, and heterogeneity in frailty measurement reduced the confidence of conclusions drawn. The gaps identified in this review highlight the need for further primary evidence that incorporates frailty, plus a standardized holistic method of measuring frailty in heart failure patients.

title: Arthroscopic Anatomic Rotator Cable Reconstruction Using Palmaris Longus Autograft: Surgical Technique.
authors: Lim TK, Park HS.
abstract: This technical note describes an arthroscopic anatomic rotator cable reconstruction technique using a palmaris longus tendon autograft for selected large U-shaped posterosuperior rotator cuff tears with limited tendon mobility. After thorough stepwise release and mobilization, the graft is introduced into the subacromial space and fixed to the anatomic anterior and posterior cable insertion sites and woven through the residual rotator cuff near the musculotendinous junction. The graft is tensioned to recreate the native semilunar cable arc, whereas the rotator cuff is simultaneously reduced to the medial footprint, followed by combined cuff-to-bone repair over the reconstructed cable. By recreating the native anterior-posterior cable architecture and integrating the autologous graft with the repaired cuff, this technique aims to restore biomechanical load-sharing and force coupling while permitting long-term biologic incorporation. As such, arthroscopic rotator cable reconstruction using a palmaris longus autograft may provide a valuable anatomic surgical option for rotator cable-deficient shoulders in which anatomic tendon repair alone is not feasible.

title: An invariant-guided model for automated detection of anomalous execution regimes from production telemetry.
authors: Kovtun V, Huralnyk F, Huralnyk A, Yankiv M, Alsayaydeh JAJ.
abstract: Modern cloud-based distributed software systems increasingly exhibit persistent changes in execution behaviour that cannot be adequately characterised by isolated events or threshold violations alone. Although contemporary production environments already provide mature observability infrastructures for collecting logs, metrics, and traces, the formal representation of execution regimes derived from such telemetry remains insufficiently developed. This paper proposes an invariant-guided geometric framework for modelling execution regimes and detecting anomalous regime transitions under weak supervision. The framework applies common principles of invariant-based feature mapping, weighted pseudometrics, and geometric regularisation to log-derived and KPI-derived regime representations. Separate evaluations of these modality-specific implementations on HDFS logs and operational KPI telemetry demonstrate consistent improvements over representative baseline methods under limited supervision while preserving an explicit and interpretable execution-regime representation. Joint evaluation using synchronized logs and metrics remains future work. The results support the framework as a mathematical analytical layer for execution-regime analysis that complements existing production observability infrastructures.

title: Alveolar soft part sarcoma of the thigh: wide excision and adjuvant radiotherapy with three years of disease-free follow-up.
authors: Ambesh A, Khurana R, Rastogi M.

title: ACOEM Guidelines: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS).
journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
authors: Feinberg SD, Aronoff GM, Ausfahl J, Bruns D, Darnall BD, Goldberg RL, Haldeman S, Lessenger JE, Mandel S, Mayer TG, Navani AH, Osbahr AJ, Warren PA, Winters TH, Harris JS, Hegmann KT.
abstract: Objective This summary of findings related to Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) as part of the American College of Occupational and Environmental Medicine's (ACOEM) updated Chronic Pain guideline seeks to provide clinicians with evidence-based guidance for diagnosing and treating this disorder. Methods Comprehensive systematic literature reviews were conducted in accordance with the ACOEM Guidelines methodology. Results Guidance was developed regarding 12 diagnostic methods and 79 treatment methods. Conclusions First-line treatments for CRPS are education, strengthening exercises, aerobic exercise, fear avoidance belief/kinesiophobia training, NSAIDs, oral glucocorticosteroids, and bisphosphonates. Second-line treatments are mirror therapy, pain exposure therapy, virtual reality (VR), desensitization, antidepressants (TCA, SNRI), gabapentin, and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). Third-line treatments are stellate ganglion blocks and bretylium blocks. Spinal cord stimulator (SCS) implantation is a fourth-line treatment.

title: A randomized study on migration of the Spectron EF and the Charnley flanged 40 cemented femoral stems: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis (RSA) with 10 years' follow-up.
authors: Johannessen HG, Hallan G, Furnes O, Fenstad AM, Lygre SH, Haugan K, Kadar T, Badawy M, Indrekvam K, Aamodt A, Høl PJ.
abstract: Background and purpose Our primary aim was to compare the 10-year migration of the proximally roughened Spectron EF stem with the Charnley flanged 40 stems in cemented THA. Secondary aims were to assess the influence of polyethylene type on Spectron EF migration, and clinical outcomes. Methods In this randomized trial (NCT00698672), 150 patients (70% women; mean age 70 years) underwent cemented THA with either a Charnley stem (n = 30) or a Spectron EF stem (n = 120, 4 groups with different articulating surfaces). The articulations utilized conventional polyethylene (CPE) or highly crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) cup liners combined with either cobalt-chromium (CoCr) or Oxinium (OxZr) femoral heads. RSA was performed postoperatively and up to 10 years. Migration was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Clinical outcome was assessed with the Harris Hip Score (HHS). Results After 10 years, 48 patients (14 Charnley, 34 Spectron EF) had evaluable RSA data. Both stems showed posterior translation, subsidence, and retroversion. Retroversion was greater for the Charnley stem than the Spectron EF stem at 3.2° (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.7-3.8) and 1.5° (CI 1.2-1.8), respectively, with a mean difference of 1.7° (CI 1.1- 2.4). The Spectron EF stem had more subsidence at 0.72 mm (CI 0.56-0.88) vs 0.32 mm (CI 0.06-0.57) for the Charnley stem, with a difference of 0.41 mm (CI 0.11-0.71). Spectron EF stems articulating with XLPE had 0.44 mm (CI 0.12-0.76) more subsidence than stems articulating with CPE. HHS improved from 41 (SD 15) to 86 (SD 19) for the Charnley stem and 45 (SD 13) to 86 (SD 15) for the Spectron EF stem with no statistically significant difference between the groups. Conclusion After 10 years, the Spectron EF stem showed less retroversion, but more subsidence than the Charnley stem, with otherwise similar migration and clinical outcomes. XLPE articulating stems had more subsidence than CPE with the Spectron EF stem.

title: A prognostic model based on platelet-related genes accurately predicts survival in patients with gastric cancer.
authors: Zheng C, Yang W, Lu Q, Zhou Y.
abstract: Background Platelets contribute to gastric cancer (GC) progression and metastasis. In this study, we aimed to construct a prognostic model based on platelet-related genes (PRGs) to predict outcomes in GC. Methods RNA sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes, from which PRGs were selected as candidates. A prognostic model was built using machine learning. Immune infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT, and Spearman correlation was used to assess the relationships between prognostic PRGs and immune cells. Single-cell transcriptomics was used to explore cellular expression patterns, and molecular regulatory networks were constructed. The expression of candidate genes was validated in cell lines by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Results A total of 8,387 differentially expressed genes, including 123 PRGs, were identified. An eight-gene prognostic model (THPO, MMRN1, EGF, SPARC, GNAI1, CD36, SERPINE1, and ADAMTS18) was established. Distinct immune infiltration patterns were observed between risk groups, with differences in M2 macrophages, monocytes, neutrophils, activated memory CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, and follicular helper T cells. MMRN1 expression correlated positively with monocytes ( r = 0.37), whereas GNAI1 expression was negatively associated with activated memory CD4+ T cells ( r = - 0.30). Single-cell analysis showed that prognostic genes were mainly expressed in epithelial cells and fibroblasts. Two regulatory axes, SPARC-hsa-miR-494-3p-NEAT1 and GNAI1-hsa-miR-4262-NEAT1, were implicated in GC progression. RT-qPCR confirmed downregulation of CD36 and upregulation of SERPINE1 in GC tissues. Conclusion This platelet-related gene model predicts survival and immune infiltration in GC and may support the development of personalized therapies.

title: A primary study of inverted right-angle configuration cannulated screws fixation of femoral neck fracture based on elaborated 3-dimensional features of the femoral head and neck region.
authors: Liu C, Zhang H, Liu Y, Liu P, Hou Y.
abstract: Background CT-based three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction was used to analyze the detailed anatomical morphology of the femoral head-neck region, and a modified inverted right-angle cannulated screw configuration was proposed to reduce the risk of posterosuperior screw in-out-in (IOI) placement during femoral neck fracture fixation. Methods Imaging data from 22 patients (12 males and 10 females; mean age, 52.5 ± 16.8 years) were retrospectively analyzed. CT data of both hips were imported into Mimics to construct 3D digital femoral models for morphologic analysis and screw trajectory simulation. Based on the observed anterior offset of the femoral head-neck canal and the sloped posterosuperior cortex of the femoral neck, a modified inverted right-angle screw configuration and a negative anteversion fluoroscopic view were proposed. Technical feasibility was preliminarily illustrated in two patients with femoral neck fractures. Results The femoral head-neck axis showed an anterior offset relative to the proximal femoral axis, which may increase the risk of posterosuperior IOI screw trajectory with the traditional inverted triangle configuration. In the 3D simulation, the modified inverted right-angle configuration placed the posterosuperior screw within the proposed safety zone. The negative anteversion fluoroscopic view appeared useful for identifying potential IOI screw trajectory. Technical feasibility of the proposed configuration was illustrated in two patients with femoral neck fractures, in whom no postoperative IOI screw displacement was observed on CT. Conclusion The anatomical features of the femoral head-neck region may contribute to the risk of posterosuperior IOI screw trajectory with the traditional inverted triangle configuration. In this CT-based morphologic and simulation study, the modified inverted right-angle configuration showed a more favorable simulated position of the posterosuperior screw within the proposed safety zone, while negative anteversion fluoroscopy may help identify potential IOI screw trajectory. These preliminary findings require further validation through biomechanical studies and larger comparative clinical investigations.

title: A cell line model for the study of CD4-negative HIV-1 infection and latent virus reservoirs.
authors: Lionel GJ, Binnington B, Wong RW, Jin J, Cochrane A, Branch DR.
abstract: Although controversial, limited publications support the notion that HIV-1 can infect CD4-negative cells. The objective of this study was to provide a comprehensive investigation of a universally available CD4-negative cell line model system that can be infected with X4 and R5 HIV-1 to generate integrated proviral DNA and serve to study latent viral reservoirs. There is a lack of a fully characterized model for the study of HIV-1 infection of CD4-negative cells and this creates a gap in the study of this unusual pathway. To address this critical need, human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, engineered to express either CD4, CCR5 or CXCR4, and easily available from a commercial source were used. CD4 expression was examined using western immunoblot, flow cytometry, anti-CD4 blocking antibody and mRNA expression. Cells were infected with HIV-1 pseudo-enveloped viruses bearing either JR-FL (R5-tropic) or HXB2 (X4-tropic) envelopes, constructed on NL4-3 luciferase/GFP backbone. Infection was monitored by luciferase readout and visualized by GFP immunofluorescence. Raltegravir was used to inhibit integration, and AMD3100 and maraviroc used to block chemokine coreceptors, CXCR4 and CCR5, respectively. Productive versus latent infection was quantified by dual-fluorescence readouts using HI.fate.E. We confirmed that HOS cells lack CD4. HOS cells expressing only CCR5 or CXCR4 supported HIV-1 infection, although infection was significantly lower than in matched CD4-positive controls. Raltegravir treatment blocked proviral integration in all instances. Coreceptor antagonism and envelope-deficient viruses revealed that infection of CD4-negative CXCR4+ cells remained CXCR4-dependent, whereas CD4-negative CCR5+ cells showed evidence of CCR5-independent infection. Dual-reporter HI.fate.E assays indicated that CD4-negative cells could support both productive and latent infection. These studies establish a universally available cell line model for the study of CD4-negative HIV-1 infection. This cell line model will provide insight into the question of how CD4-negative cells can be infected with HIV-1 and whether CD4-negative cells can provide latent viral reservoirs in HIV/AIDS.

title: Vaccination status and its association with complications among the patients admitted with measles in the dedicated measles hospitals, Dhaka, Bangladesh.
authors: Goutam A, Hasan A, Khan MAS, Mahid MAH, Masud SB, Babul H, Rahman L, Siddiqui A, Luthfa ST, Tuli SN, Paul I, Bari MR, Saleh ASM, Hawlader MDH.
abstract: Bangladesh is facing a major resurgence of measles, with more than 60,000 suspected cases and over 600 deaths reported between March and May 2026. Despite the growing outbreak, hospital-based evidence in Bangladesh remains limited regarding measles vaccination status and its association with clinical complications. To address this critical gap, our study aimed to assess the vaccination status and its relationship with the development of clinical complications. This cross-sectional study enrolled 260 children aged 2-72 months with clinically confirmed measles who were admitted to four dedicated measles treatment hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh, between 15 and 25 April 2026. Data on vaccination status, sociodemographic characteristics, feeding practices, nutritional status, clinical symptoms, and complications were collected through caregiver interviews and hospital records. Adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated; p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Among enrolled children, 74.6% were unvaccinated, 18.8% were partially vaccinated, and only 6.5% were fully vaccinated. In the multivariable model, age below 9 months (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.03-0.268, p < 0.001) was independently associated with lower odds of vaccination, while household income at or above the median (aOR 3.983, 95% CI 1.8-8.813, p = 0.004) was associated with higher odds. Complications developed in 31.1% of cases, with respiratory involvement being most common. Absence of exclusive breastfeeding (aOR 2.336, 95% CI 1.027-5.313, p = 0.043) and presenting with exactly three symptoms at admission (aOR 3.106, 95% CI 1.274-7.572, p = 0.013) were independently associated with complications. Unvaccinated children had markedly higher odds of complications than vaccinated children (aOR 5.729, 95% CI: 2.363-13.889, p < 0.001). The heavy burden of measles among unvaccinated children, shaped by socioeconomic disadvantage and suboptimal feeding practices, underscores the urgent need to restore immunization coverage and strengthen equitable health services in Bangladesh.

title: Unveiling the role of virtual streamer's interaction attributes in shaping consumer-generated value behaviors.
authors: Li W, Cheng G, He Y.
abstract: The interaction attributes of virtual streamers are crucial to their success. This study deconstructs virtual streamers' interaction into two dimensions: interaction intelligence and interaction humanness. Drawing on immersion theory and parasocial relationship theory, the study examines how these interaction attributes are associated with consumer-generated value behaviors, including social media engagement, donation, and purchase intention. Using data from a survey of 479 respondents and structural equation modeling, the results reveal that both the interaction intelligence and interaction humanness of virtual streamers are positively associated with consumer immersion, which, in turn, is positively related to parasocial relationships with virtual streamers. Immersion and parasocial relationships are further associated with social media engagement, donation, and purchase intention. This study advances the theoretical understanding of virtual streamer interaction and provides practical insights for content creators and platforms aiming to foster consumer-generated value behaviors in virtual streaming.

title: Ultrasound-Assisted Endoscopic Lesser Trochanter Resection for Ischiofemoral Impingement.
authors: Mitsuya Y, Miyatake K, Kusaba Y, Arakawa H, Tsujiku S, Inaba Y.
abstract: Ischiofemoral impingement is a rare cause of buttock pain resulting from narrowing of the space between the ischial tuberosity and the femoral lesser trochanter. Although most cases improve with conservative treatment, refractory cases may require surgical treatment. One such treatment option includes endoscopic resection of the lesser trochanter, which is an uncommon, extra-articular, endoscopic surgery that carries several complication risks, such as injury of important neurovascular structures. By marking the sciatic nerve preoperatively and making a portal under ultrasound guidance, this surgery can be performed safely and easily.

title: Tuberculous Salpingo-Oophoritis Mimicking Ovarian Malignancy: A Case Report of a Diagnostic Dilemma.
authors: Habte YM, Kebede HD, Tachibel KG, Nida HW, Ashenafi MM, Chane LG, Elihu ST, Chanie KY, Habte BM.
abstract: Female genital tuberculosis (FGTB) is an uncommon form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis that poses a significant diagnostic challenge because it frequently mimics ovarian malignancy clinically, radiologically, and biochemically. We report the case of a 34-year-old multiparous woman who presented 66 days after cesarean delivery with progressive lower abdominal pain and a tender pelvic mass. Pelvic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a complex left adnexal mass suspicious for ovarian malignancy, while serum CA-125 was elevated, further reinforcing the presumptive diagnosis. The patient subsequently underwent exploratory laparotomy with left salpingo-oophorectomy. Histopathological examination revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid granulomas, Langhans giant cells, and caseous necrosis, confirming tuberculous salpingo-oophoritis without evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient completed a standard 6-month anti-tuberculosis regimen with complete clinical recovery and progressive normalization of CA-125 levels during follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic dilemma posed by FGTB, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic regions where the disease may closely resemble ovarian cancer. Elevated CA-125 should therefore be interpreted cautiously in premenopausal women, as it is a nonspecific marker that may also reflect benign inflammatory conditions. A high index of suspicion for FGTB, coupled with careful integration of clinical, radiological, and epidemiological findings into preoperative decision-making, is essential to facilitate timely diagnosis, appropriate management, prompt initiation of anti-tuberculosis therapy, and avoidance of unnecessary extensive surgical intervention while minimizing long-term reproductive morbidity.

title: The "osteostat": A theory of bone mechanosensing and setpoint adaptation based on osteocytes.
authors: Pauchard Y, Buenzli PR.
abstract: The osteocyte network in bone is believed to play an important role for how bone tissues sense and respond to mechanical stimulation. Yet, bone adaptation to mechanical loads is often conceptualised as a simple response to mechanical stimuli, such as Wolff's law, which is based on mechanical variables only and takes no account of the cellular basis of mechanosensation. Wolff's law presumes the existence of a reference mechanical stimulus, the mechanical setpoint, above which bone is added , and under which bone is removed. In this paper, we develop a theory of bone tissue sensing and adaptation based on osteocytes to provide new understanding of the role played by osteocyte signals in mechanical adaptation. In this theory, the mechanical setpoint of Frost's mechanostat is explicitly embodied as osteocyte properties involved in mechanotransduction. The mechanical setpoint is allowed to adapt due to the replacement of osteocytes during remodelling, making the setpoint space and time dependent. We propose a mathematical model to implement this new theory of bone adapation and present numerical simulations of this model to explore how mechanobiological response curves (effective Wolff's laws) are modulated by setpoint adaptation during remodelling. By accounting for varying osteocyte populations within bone tissue, we explore bone adaptation under osteocyte disruptions, which is particularly relevant to age-related bone loss. Our model suggests that biological disruptions of remodelling balance cannot always be compensated by mechanical feedback, and that setpoint adaptation during remodelling may have significant observable consequences, such as hysteresis in bone response signatures that resemble lazy zones.

title: Taxon-related variation in palmar and plantar friction ridge patterns among Aotus infulatus, Saimiri collinsi and Sapajus spp.: Individual-level variation and implications for identification.
authors: Sales JVF, de Barros RM, de Castro PHG, Souza AR, Hirano LQL.
abstract: Friction ridges play important biomechanical roles in primates, contributing to the regulation of skin moisture and increasing friction with substrates and objects during locomotion and manipulation. In this context, the present study aimed to characterize and compare level I and II dermatoglyphic patterns of the palmar and plantar surfaces of Aotus infulatus (owl monkey), Saimiri collinsi (squirrel monkey), and Sapajus spp. (capuchin monkey). Following chemical restraint, skin impressions of the hands and feet were obtained by applying a thin layer of commercial ink used for human fingerprinting. The analyses revealed a consistent pattern of differentiation among taxa. A. infulatus exhibited greater dermatoglyphic homogeneity, with a higher frequency of deltas and whorls, as well as a greater occurrence of the dot on the ridge (P-IN) minutia compared to the other groups. Additionally, no identical palmar or plantar epidermal impressions were observed among individuals within the same taxon, indicating individual-level variability in these structures. Thus, palmar and plantar friction ridge patterns may provide useful morphological markers for comparative studies of taxon-related variation in non-human primates, with potential applications in biological research, population management, and conservation strategies.

title: Structural distance to the tRNA-synthetase binding interface predicts pathogenicity but is captured by AlphaMissense and EVE.
authors: Liebeskind K, Francklyn C, Barrantes-Reynolds R.
abstract: Variants of uncertain significance have accumulated as genomic sequencing has become more widespread, which complicates rare disease diagnosis and requires substantial resources for re-evaluation. Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARSs) are a protein family with extensive variant data and well-characterized disease associations, making them an ideal system for investigating the relationship between variant location and pathogenicity. Using structural distance measurements to the ARS-tRNA binding interface combined with existing pathogenicity predictors, AlphaMissense and EVE, we investigated whether explicit structural binding information could improve missense variant pathogenicity prediction. Pathogenic variants were found to cluster significantly closer to the tRNA-binding interface than benign variants (p = 1.3e-09). Incorporating explicit distance information into a Bayesian mixture model did not substantially improve predictive performance over AlphaMissense and EVE alone. This suggests that these models already implicitly capture relevant structural binding context. However, a clinically important subset of interface variants classified as ambiguous by both existing models identifies a specific gap where explicit structural distance information may provide added discriminative value. However our analysis revealed that structural distance alone does not meaningfully contribute in prediction of pathogenicity for these variants. Incorporating additional biologically relevant features not captured by existing models, such as protein stability or conformational dynamics, as well as refining structural distance calculations, may further improve classification of this subset. These findings highlight both the power and the limitations of existing pathogenicity predictors and suggest that structurally informed approaches targeting the binding interface in addiition to other features represent a promising direction for improving classification of these ambiguous variants that have great clinical significance.

title: Statistically Fragile Evidence Underlies Comparative Trials of Arthroscopic Meniscectomy Versus Nonoperative Management for Degenerative Meniscus Tears.
authors: Bosco AP, Rasquinha RD, Voyer E, Rosenberg AE, Quinn M, Marcaccio S.
abstract: Purpose To assess the statistical robustness of comparative studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing arthroscopic meniscal debridement or meniscectomy with nonoperative or sham interventions. Methods Comparative studies and RCTs of meniscus debridement or meniscectomy versus nonoperative or sham interventions were identified through a comprehensive literature search in June 2025 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Study characteristics, dichotomous outcomes, and continuous outcomes were extracted. The fragility index and continuous fragility index were calculated as the number of event reversals required to change significance; these metrics were normalized by sample size to calculate the fragility quotient (FQ) and continuous FQ. Results Of 429 studies screened, 10 were included (5 RCTs, 5 comparative), yielding 50 dichotomous (e.g., progression to arthroplasty or adverse events) and 83 continuous (e.g., Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score subscales, International Knee Documentation committee scores, pain visual analog scale scores, etc.) outcomes. The median fragility index was 6 (interquartile range [IQR] 4-12.75) with median FQ of 0.031 (IQR 0.014-0.049). The median continuous fragility index was 18 (IQR 6.8-41.5) with median continuous FQ of 0.13 (IQR 0.084-0.16). Dichotomous outcomes from RCTs were significantly more fragile than those from comparative studies (RCT FQ = 0.021 vs 0.049; P = .010), whereas continuous outcome fragility did not differ significantly. Conclusions Studies comparing meniscal debridement with nonoperative management are statistically fragile, meaning that statistical significance could be reversed with only a small number of outcome changes, particularly for dichotomous outcomes. Continuous outcomes showed greater robustness but remained limited by loss to follow-up and study design. Level of evidence Level III, systematic review of Level I to III studies.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and county-level coordination between sports-related intangible cultural heritage and tourism development in the Wuling Mountain Area, China.
authors: Zhang J, Zhang S, Lei J.
abstract: Sports-related intangible cultural heritage (SRICH) can support culturally grounded tourism, but its county-level alignment with tourism development remains unclear in ethnically diverse mountain regions. This study examined 71 county-level units in China's Wuling Mountain Area in 2010, 2015, 2019, and 2024. Geographical concentration, kernel density estimation, and standard deviational ellipses traced the administrative distribution of officially recognized SRICH records. Entropy weighting, coupling coordination, relative-balance diagnosis, and Moran's I assessed their county-level relationship with tourism development. SRICH coverage expanded and geographical concentration declined, while county-represented density peaks increased within a broadly stable regional configuration. Tourism development rose rapidly before 2019 and more slowly thereafter, retaining a marked core-periphery structure. Mean D increased from 0.192 to 0.403; 62.2% of this change was associated with counties entering the official inventory after 2010. Within the baseline-covered cohort, the joint levels of the two subsystems increased, whereas relative balance changed little, and SRICH-lagging counties remained predominant. All three indices showed significant positive global spatial autocorrelation, while FDR-adjusted local clusters were sparse and none remained significant in 2024. The results inform differentiated cross-provincial safeguarding and tourism planning, with greater attention to counties where the two subsystems follow different trajectories. The coupling coordination degree D is interpreted as a comparative measure of the recorded joint levels of SRICH and tourism development.

title: Seasonal and spatial dynamics of in-channel water bodies on a river sandbar and associated macroinvertebrate communities.
authors: Nakamura M, Hara N, Yamanaka C, Oh HJ, Doi H, Tanaka A, Ishida Y, Takemon Y, Katano I.
abstract: In-channel water bodies (ICWBs) on river sandbars, including backwaters and riverine ponds shaped by hydrological disturbance, remain poorly understood with respect to their seasonal and fine-scale spatial dynamics. We investigated the environmental conditions and benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages in ICWBs formed around traditional wood-based river training structures ("Seigyu") within a single sandbar in a regulated river in central Japan. Environmental conditions showed marked seasonal variation and fine-scale spatial gradients across habitat types over distances of tens of meters. Water temperature emerged as one of the strongest environmental gradients, exhibiting seasonal variation and longitudinal spatial structure within the sandbar. Macroinvertebrate communities in ICWBs were distinct from those in the adjacent main channel, and many taxa were restricted to ICWBs. Community composition varied among habitat types and across seasons, indicating that temporal processes interact with fine-scale spatial heterogeneity to structure assemblages. These results suggest that ICWBs on sandbars function as dynamic habitat patches whose ecological roles are shaped by the interaction between seasonal hydrological dynamics and fine-scale spatial heterogeneity.

title: Robotic total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer: oncological outcomes in a retrospective single-center cohort study.
