authors: Passagnoli F, Martinelli S, Loi M, Coratti F, Fortuna L, Staderini F, Cricchio M, Cianchi F.
abstract: Robotic surgery is increasingly used in rectal cancer treatment, potentially improving precision in the narrow pelvic space. However, evidence on its oncological advantages remains limited. This study evaluated short- and long-term oncological outcomes of robotic total mesorectal excision (TME) in a tertiary referral center, focusing on the prognostic value of circumferential resection margin (CRM), including evaluation of a 5 mm threshold. A retrospective analysis included 135 consecutive patients undergoing robotic TME for rectal cancer between January 2018 and June 2024. Clinic-pathological, perioperative, and oncological data were collected. Short-term oncological outcomes included distal margin, CRM status, and TME quality (Quirke classification). Long-term outcomes were overall survival (OS), local recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival (LRFS, DMFS). Survival analyses identified prognostic factors. No positive distal margins were observed. CRM negativity was achieved in 94.8% of patients, while complete or near-complete TME was obtained in 96.3%. Reoperation rate was 4.4%, with no 30-day mortality. After a median follow-up of 38 months (mean 44 months), local recurrence occurred in 6% and distant metastases in 21% of patients. CRM positivity and incomplete TME were significantly associated with worse OS and higher metastatic risk. No prognostic benefit has been demonstrated for a CRM ≥5 mm compared to the traditional cutoff. In our case series, robotic total mesorectal excision (TME) ensures high-quality oncological dissection and favorable perioperative and survival outcomes. The predictive value of the CRM and Quirke's mesorectal dissection quality index is confirmed, whereas a favorable prognostic role of a CRM ≥5 mm could not be demonstrated.

title: Reproductive Implications of a Rare Paternal Dicentric Rearrangement 45,XY,dic(5;13)(p15;p12) in an IVF Cycle With Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Structural Rearrangements: A Case Report.
authors: Do VN, Tran HP, Van Nguyen T, Tang VK.
abstract: This case highlights the counseling challenges associated with a rare paternal dicentric rearrangement. PGT-SR identified only one transferable balanced/normal copy-number profile among four biopsied blastocysts, underscoring the need to discuss the possibility of few or no transferable embryos and the limitations of PGT-SR.

title: Reply to the Letter to the Editor: Do Personalized Recovery Trajectories Enhance the Utility of Patient-reported Outcome Measures After Orthopaedic Surgery?
authors: Graber J, Jin X, Juarez-Colunga E, Dibblee P, Woodfield D, Minick KI, Chamberlain AM, Bade M, Stevens-Lapsley J.

title: Quantitative evaluation of cervical foraminal stenosis and nerve root diameter using MRI-based multiplanar reconstruction: a prospective study.
authors: Shibata T, Morishita Y, Tanaka J, Sakai T, Shiokawa T, Kaneyama H, Sanada K, Hagihara S, Yoshimura A, Mio R, Koga D, Yamamoto T.
abstract: Objective Accurate evaluation of cervical foraminal stenosis using conventional MRI is challenging. We quantitatively evaluated cervical foraminal and nerve root diameters using MRI-based multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) and compared measurements between the proximal-type cervical spondylotic amyotrophy (CSA) and cervical spondylotic radiculopathy (CSR) groups. Materials and methods Twenty-eight consecutive patients were prospectively enrolled: 16 with CSA and C4/5 foraminal stenosis; 12 with CSR without symptomatic C4/5 involvement. T2-weighted coronal MRI was obtained, and images perpendicular to the C4/5 foramen were reconstructed. Foraminal height and anteroposterior diameter, as well as the craniocaudal and anteroposterior diameters of the C5 nerve root, were measured. Side-to-side comparisons were performed in CSA, and measurements were also compared with those in CSR. Results In CSA, foraminal height was significantly smaller on the symptomatic side than on the asymptomatic side (p = 0.042). The anteroposterior diameters of the C4/5 foramen and C5 nerve root were significantly smaller on the symptomatic side (2.4 ± 0.4 mm vs. 3.1 ± 0.5 mm and 1.9 ± 0.4 mm vs. 2.7 ± 0.5 mm, respectively, p Conclusion MRI-based MPR allows quantitative evaluation of cervical foraminal narrowing and nerve root diameter. Focal anteroposterior narrowing of the C4/5 foramen with reduced diameter of the C5 nerve root was associated with the symptomatic side in CSA.

title: Pudexacianinium chloride (ASP5354) for ureter visualization in patients undergoing abdominopelvic surgery: a phase III, multicenter, open-label, randomized study.
authors: Albert M, Lautz TB, Allawi A, Cobb L, Goldstein SD, Khaitov S, Tabash R, Kishimoto T, Takusagawa S, Liu L, Haas GP, Sylla P.
abstract: Background This phase III, multicenter, randomized, open-label study (NCT05754333) evaluated pudexacianinium chloride (ASP5354), a novel near-infrared fluorescence (NIR-F) imaging agent, for intraoperative ureter identification in minimally invasive and open abdominopelvic surgeries. Methods Patients with normal renal function, mild renal impairment, or patients with moderately impaired renal function received one intravenous dose of pudexacianinium 3 mg intraoperatively. Investigators scored ureter conspicuity under white light (WL) or (WL+)NIR-F using a validated 5-point Likert scale. Primary and key secondary endpoints included intra-participant differences in conspicuity scores for WL versus (WL+)NIR-F, supported by blinded central image review and quantitative contrast enhancement factor (CEF) analysis. Results Adults with normal renal function or mild renal impairment were randomly assigned in a 5:1 ratio to WL+NIR-F arm (intent-to-treat population, n = 72 [median age 55.0 years; 68.1% female]) or to WL-only arm (n = 13 [median age 64.0 years; 76.9% female]). Eight adults with moderate renal impairment (median age 70.0 years; 75.0% female) and 14 adolescents with normal renal function or mild renal impairment (median age 14.5 years; 57.1% female) were imaged under WL+NIR-F (no randomization). In the same participants of intent-to-treat population, (WL+)NIR-F yielded significantly higher conspicuity scores than WL, both 30 min (± 15) postdose and at end of surgery, confirmed by central review and CEF analysis. Benefits persisted to 210 min post-injection (timepoints with ≥ 5 evaluable patients). No drug-related serious adverse events occurred, and most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild- or moderate-grade. Adults with moderate renal impairment had higher mean plasma pudexacianinium concentrations and slower urinary excretion than adults with normal renal function or mild renal impairment. Adolescents had numerically lower mean urine production rates and higher mean urine pudexacianinium concentrations than adults. Conclusions Pudexacianinium is an effective visualization agent without invasive instrumentation. NIR-F imaging with pudexacianinium enhances ureter identification compared with WL-only, which may reduce risk of intraoperative ureter injury.

title: Prolonged length of stay in the Italian emergency departments: A competing risks frailty model.
authors: Battaglia S, Attanasio M, Arnone S, Geraci A, Murolo G, Favitta S, Enea M.
abstract: Background Emergency department (ED) overcrowding has increased worldwide in recent years. This paper provides quantitative information based on data collected immediately before the COVID-19 outbreak, which can serve as a baseline for developing systematic approaches to prolonged length of stay (LoS) in EDs. Materials and methods We analysed a random sample of 10,077 ED accesses drawn from the 503,797 eligible accesses recorded in 2019 in the 16 largest hospitals of Sicily, Italy. LoS was modelled using a cause-specific competing-risks Cox frailty model with Discharge and Hospitalization as competing endpoints. Two log-normal frailty components were included to account for unobserved heterogeneity between EDs and between patients. Non-proportionality was addressed by stratifying on pathology and by including time-varying effects for triage. Cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) were computed to estimate the probability of each endpoint and strata over time. Results Median LoS was 1.70 hours for Discharge and 3.77 hours for Hospitalization, and the gap widened markedly in the upper tail (90th percentile: 7.10 vs 34.95 hours). Discharge was associated with pathology, age, triage, sex and season; Hospitalization with pathology, age, triage and season. The hazard of Discharge decreased by 2% per additional year of age (HR = 0.98, 95% CI 0.977-0.983) and was 10% higher for accesses in summer (HR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.16). The hazard of Hospitalization increased by 0.4% per year of age (HR = 1.004, 95% CI 1.001-1.007). The effect of triage was time-dependent: at 10 hours of LoS, red-coded accesses had a 69% lower hazard of Discharge (HR = 0.31) and a 53% higher hazard of Hospitalization (HR = 1.53) than other codes. Circulatory and respiratory diseases and blood diseases showed the highest CIFs for Hospitalization and prolonged LoS for both endpoints, whereas skin and musculoskeletal diseases, injuries and poisoning, and nervous system diseases showed the highest CIFs for Discharge. Conclusions Prolonged LoS in Sicilian EDs was driven mainly by pathology, and the exit process differed systematically across disease groups: patients with circulatory and respiratory diseases and with blood diseases waited longest before both Discharge and Hospitalization.The large between-ED heterogeneity in the hazard of Hospitalization, indicates that admission delays reflect organisational as well as structural constraints. Interventions to reduce overcrowding - in particular any expansion of inpatient capacity - should therefore be targeted at the specific wards receiving these patients, rather than applied uniformly across the hospital.

title: Perioperative neurocognitive outcomes after robot-assisted pelvic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported proportions, comparative risk and prognostic factors.
authors: Drobot RB, Skorupka JJ, Lipa M.
abstract: Delirium and cognitive decline may complicate recovery after robot-assisted pelvic surgery, but their frequency and relationship to positioning remain uncertain. We assessed reported proportions, comparative surgical risk and prognostic factors. PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched through 4 August 2026. Eligible adult robotic pelvic studies reported objective cognitive testing or delirium. Two reviewers performed original screening, extraction and question-specific bias appraisal. Post hoc logit random-effects meta-analyses summarized prospective cohorts using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals in R. Twenty-six reports represented 25 studies. Five cognitive cohorts (356 participants) yielded 29.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 20.2-39.8%); excluding Beck yielded 31.8% (20.7-45.4%). Three delirium cohorts (245 participants) yielded a descriptive model summary of 10.3% (2.2-37.0%). Individual delirium proportions were 8/82 (9.8%; exact 95% CI 4.3-18.3%), 4/80 (5.0%; 1.4-12.3%) and 14/83 (16.9%; 9.5-26.7%). The approximate 95% prediction interval from the delirium meta-analysis was very wide (<0.1-99.8%). The same-procedure prostatectomy comparison yielded an unadjusted risk ratio of 1.06 (0.73-1.55) for early cognitive decline. Comparative evidence was of low or very low certainty. Definitions, surveillance and selection limited interpretation; Trendelenburg-duration findings were inconsistent. These proportions describe selected study-defined outcomes. They do not establish attributable robotic or positioning risk, a safe exposure threshold, or benefit from horizontal breaks. Standardized prospective measurement is needed.

title: Perceptual, affective and motivational responses during a last man standing ultra-trail race.
authors: Lesport A, Grappe F, Groslambert A, Baron B.
abstract: The aim of this study was to monitor the psychological responses (individual perceptual, affective, and motivational) of trail runners during an ultra-endurance elimination race. Twenty-one participants (3 women, 18 men; 35.80 ± 8.95 years) were familiarized with perceptual (RPE, fatigue), affective (pleasure, feelings), and motivational scales one week before the event. The race required runners to complete a 6-km loop with 165 meters of elevation gain every hour for up to 33 hours. Runners completed the scales immediately after each loop. Participants finished on average 12.7 ± 6.11 loops (76.29 ± 36.65 km). Results showed that RPE and fatigue increased, while pleasure and feelings diminished as the race progressed. Motivation decreased over time specifically driven by autonomous forms of regulation. Notably, these parameters did not reach absolute extreme values by the end of the exercise. Three motivational pillars predominate - intrinsic motivation, identified and integrated regulations - and correlated significantly with the number of loops remaining. These findings suggest that runners rely on self-regulatory strategies to maintain effort within a subjectively sustainable zone. The observed decline in psychological parameters preceding withdrawal highlights the importance of integrating psychological monitoring into training programs, with practical implications for athletes and coaches.

title: Optimizing rheumatology referral in patients with psoriasis: a community-based pilot study of four screening questionnaires within a collaborative dermatology-rheumatology pathway.
authors: Arendse G, Al Horoub Y, Walker K, Gardner K, Odeshi O, Awan S, Arendse R.
abstract: Background Musculoskeletal symptoms in patients with psoriasis may indicate psoriatic arthritis (PsA) or other rheumatic diseases requiring specialist assessment. Screening questionnaires may facilitate referral from dermatology to rheumatology, but their performance within collaborative community pathways remains uncertain. Objectives To compare four psoriasis screening questionnaires for PsA and inflammatory arthritis (IA) within a community dermatology-rheumatology referral pathway and assess operational feasibility. Methods Fifty adults with dermatologist-confirmed psoriasis, no prior PsA, and no systemic psoriasis therapy were prospectively recruited to a cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy pilot study. PEST, EARP, PASE, and ToPAS II were completed before blinded rheumatological assessment. Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, 95% confidence intervals, and Youden index were calculated for PsA and IA using complete-case denominators. Results IA was identified in 13/50 participants (26.0%), including 10 with PsA (20.0%); OA and FMS occurred in 56.0% and 8.0%. Screen-positive rates ranged from 36.0% (PASE) to 64.0% (EARP). ToPAS II had the highest observed Youden index for IA (0.408; sensitivity 76.9%, specificity 63.9%) and PsA (0.290; 70.0%, 59.0%). Alternative or coexisting diagnoses were common among screen-positive participants. Conclusions The pathway was operationally feasible within the two participating practices and identified previously unrecognized inflammatory rheumatic disease. ToPAS II showed the highest observed sensitivity-specificity balance, but small case numbers preclude definitive ranking. Alternative diagnoses among screen-positive participants support use of these questionnaires as triage instruments rather than diagnostic tests for PsA. Key Points • A community dermatology-rheumatology referral pathway was feasible in routine practice. • Rheumatological assessment identified inflammatory arthritis in 26% of participants. • In this pilot cohort, ToPAS II showed the highest observed sensitivity-specificity balance for inflammatoryarthritis and PsA, although definitive ranking was not possible. • Screening questionnaires should guide rheumatology referral rather than diagnose PsA alone.

title: Massive Pleural Synovial Sarcoma Presenting With Obstructive Shock.
authors: Hou S, Ali MB, Ali M, Abdelwahed A, Jilani D.
abstract: Primary pleural synovial sarcoma (PPSS) is an exceptionally rare and aggressive malignancy. We report a massive PPSS characterized by positive TLE1 immunostaining but negative SS18-SSX Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). This case highlights the importance of integrating morphology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical context when molecular testing is inconclusive.

title: Mandibular reconstruction with vascularised fibula free flap transfer in a patient with congenital protein C deficiency.
authors: Nukami M, Ishida K, Inomata T, Orgun D, Fujita S, Hirayama H, Miyawaki T.

title: Long-term periprosthetic femoral bone loss after cementless total hip arthroplasty: natural history and response to late osteoporosis treatment.
authors: Ando W, Takao M, Hamada H, Uemura K, Takashima K, Sugano N.
abstract: Purpose The long-term course of periprosthetic bone mineral density (BMD) after cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) and BMD changes during late osteoporosis treatment remain unclear. Methods Fifty-eight hips in 44 patients underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) > 15 years after cementless THA using a proximally coated tapered stem. Longitudinal changes were assessed in 18 hips (12 patients) with serial DXA obtained within three months, at one year, and at a mean of 17.2 years postoperatively. For therapeutic analysis, ten hips (7 patients) with osteoporosis received zoledronic acid annually, together with daily eldecalcitol and calcium, for two years with serial DXA before treatment and during follow-up. Results At a mean of 17.2 years, lumbar spine BMD declined to 74.9% of baseline (P 0.05, vs lumbar spine). In contrast, proximal zones 1, 2, 6, and 7 showed significantly greater reductions (60.0%, 61.8%, 54.0%, and 30.8%, respectively; all P Conclusions Proximal periprosthetic bone loss was evident beyond 15 years after cementless THA, with the greatest reduction in Zone 7. Late osteoporosis treatment was associated with no significant further decline in periprosthetic BMD but did not reverse severe proximal bone loss.

title: Letter to Editor-Acetabular superior wall fractures: a distinct acetabular fracture entity.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Salášek M, Džupa V.
abstract: A short comment to the original paper Acetabular superior wall fractures: a distinct acetabular fracture entity (doi: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00402-026-06407-z ) is included in our Letter to Editor. This comment focused on potential pediatric equivalent of acetabular superior wall fracture. Diagnostics and treatment management of these pediatric fractures were discussed.

title: Krackow Stitch Augmentation for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: Surgical Technique.
authors: Nakamura H, Mitsui Y, Abe R, Sakai S, Higuchi K, Yoshida T, Gotoh M.
abstract: Despite the advances in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, postoperative structural failure remains a persistent problem. Retear patterns are commonly classified as type 1 failure, which is associated with the poor quality of the torn tendon edge, and type 2 failure, which occurs at the medial suture site owing to stress concentration within the repaired tendon. Consequently, we propose an arthroscopic medial augmentation technique using a suture tape-based Krackow construct placed medial to the footprint as an adjunct to conventional rotator cuff repair. By obtaining additional fixation in more medial tendon tissue, this technique may reduce dependence on a compromised tendon stump and may also help distribute the load away from the medial suture site. This Technical Note describes the surgical details of this augmentation method that is intended to provide additional tendon reinforcement and load sharing without altering the surgeon's preferred primary repair configuration.

title: Intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
authors: Haile TG, Asres N, Gebregziabher D, Fissahaye B, Leake Y, Teklay G, Gebru HB.
abstract: Introduction Intimate partner violence is a major global public health concern and a serious human rights violation, involving physical, sexual, and psychological abuse within intimate relationships. Worldwide, about one in three women experiences intimate partner violence during their lifetime. Accordingly, this study aims to estimate the overall prevalence and identify the key predictors of intimate partner violence in Ethiopia. Methods A comprehensive systematic search was carried out in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the AMSTAR-2. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted using STATA version 18 to generate pooled estimates. Results This umbrella review synthesized evidence from six systematic reviews and meta-analyses comprising 80 primary studies involving 43,785 women. The overall prevalence of intimate partner violence was 35% (95% CI: 28-42%), with substantial heterogeneity across reviews (I2 = 83.48%). It also revealed a prevalence of 32% (95% CI: 26-37%) among pregnant women and 33% (95% CI: 25-40%) during the COVID-19 pandemic. The prevalence of specific forms of violence was estimated at 18% (95% CI: 14-22%) for sexual violence, 19% (95% CI: 15-23%) for physical violence, and 27% (95% CI: 23-31%) for psychological violence. Key predictors of IPV included both partners' and women's educational status, partner alcohol consumption, women's decision-making power, substance use, and income loss during the COVID-19 pandemic, with all associations found to be statistically significant. Conclusion This umbrella review shows that intimate partner violence remains a major public health issue in Ethiopia, affecting over one-third of women. Strengthening policy implementation and expanding survivor-centered services are essential to reduce IPV and advance Sustainable Development Goal 5.

title: High-Pressure/High-Dose Versus Standard PIPAC in Epithelioid Peritoneal Mesothelioma: Safety, Feasibility, and Outcomes From a Bicentric Comparative Cohort Study.
authors: Kockelmann F, Michot N, Demtröder CRD, Schmeding M, Ouaissi M, Zieren J, Giger-Pabst U.
abstract: Background Pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) is a minimally invasive option for peritoneal mesothelioma (PeM) in patients not eligible for cytoreductive surgery (CRS) and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). This bicentric study compared the safety, feasibility, and sex-specific outcomes of standard versus high-pressure/high-dose PIPAC (HP/HD-PIPAC). Methods Patients who had non-resectable epithelioid PeM (ePeM) treated with PIPAC at two German centers were retrospectively analyzed. Group 1 received standard PIPAC (cisplatin 7.5 mg/m 2 + doxorubicin 1.5 mg/m 2 , 12 mmHg), and group 2 received HP/HD-PIPAC (cisplatin 20 mg/m 2 + doxorubicin 4 mg/m 2 , 20 mmHg). Procedural outcomes, postoperative complications, interval from diagnosis to first PIPAC, and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Uni- and multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with OS. Results The 46 patients in the study (group 1: 25 patients; group 2: 21 patients) underwent 120 of 132 scheduled PIPAC procedures. The median OS from diagnosis was 48 months overall: 48 months in group 1, and 36 months in group 2. The interval from diagnosis to first PIPAC was shorter in group 2 (2 vs. 20 months; p = 0.009). Severe complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥III) occurred in 6.2 % of group 1 versus 2.9 % of group 2. The median OS was 106 months for the females versus 35 months for the males (p = 0.064). Multivariable analysis identified female sex, bidirectional treatment, and a longer interval between diagnosis and first PIPAC as independent factors associated with improved OS. Conclusions The HP/HD-PIPAC regimen is feasible and safe. Although no significant survival differences were observed between treatment groups, prospective studies are required to define the optimal timing and integration of PIPAC within multimodal treatment strategies. Findings should be interpreted in the context of the retrospective study design.

title: HeteroGrad-DT: Gradient Flow Transformer for heterogeneous multi-task offline reinforcement learning.
authors: Wang Y, Ma D, Li J, Guo L.
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning enables policy learning from static datasets without online exploration, making it particularly suitable for robotic control under safety and data constraints. Decision Transformer recasts offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling. Extending it to heterogeneous multi-task settings is challenging because task representations and dynamics differ, while joint training can suffer from destructive gradient interference. To address these challenges, we present HeteroGrad-DT, an integrated framework that employs task-specific tokenizers and decoupled prediction heads to retain task-native input and output dimensionality at the model interfaces while learning a shared sequence backbone. It further introduces a Gradient Flow Transformer that periodically coordinates cross-task updates using fixed-dimensional task statistics, compact summaries of shared-backbone gradients accumulated within the current synchronization interval, and an alignment-based coordination objective, rather than relying only on stepwise projection or static regularization. Experiments on the DeepMind Control Suite with up to 30 tasks show that HeteroGrad-DT improves average normalized return over representative multi-task methods. In the 30-task setting, it achieves a 32.3% relative improvement over standard training with a shared backbone and an 8.6% gain over a representative gradient-conflict mitigation baseline using the same task-aware interfaces. Ablation, mechanism, and sensitivity analyses further support complementary benefits from task-aware interfaces and gradient coordination in the evaluated settings.

title: Genome skimming of Poecilosclerida (Porifera) reveals conserved and hyperrearranged mitochondrial genomes.
authors: de Paula TS, Leite DMB, Thompson F, Hajdu E.
abstract: Genome skimming is a cost-effective approach that efficiently recovers multi-copy genomic regions, making it particularly valuable for phylogenetic research and biodiversity assessments. In this study, we applied shallow shotgun metagenome sequencing to 15 poecilosclerid sponges, successfully assembling complete mitochondrial genomes for four species and full rDNA clusters for the majority of samples, despite considerable variation in the retrieval of genomic regions and exogenous, non-poriferan sequences. Phylogenetic reconstructions using both rDNA and mtDNA sequences uncovered extensive polyphyly within several key families, such as Coelosphaeridae and Mycalidae, underscoring significant systematic inconsistencies at generic, familial, and ordinal levels, and emphasizing the need for comprehensive taxonomic revision throughout Poecilosclerida to reflect natural groups. The mitogenomes obtained from Clathria ( Microciona ) sp. (18,725 bp), Desmapsamma anchorata (19,099 bp), Latrunculia biformis (19,630 bp), and Neopodospongia tupecomareni (19,983 bp) exhibited conserved architectural features typical of the order, alongside notable variations such as gene overlaps, non-canonical start codons, and an unusual fused nd3 :: nd4L gene. Our findings highlight the applicability of genome skimming for phylogenetics and metagenomic insights, though success can vary due to biological and methodological factors. This approach has proven to be a cost-effective and powerful tool for advancing sponge systematics, despite challenges in assembling hyperrearranged mitogenomes in certain lineages, paving the way for broader genomic surveys in non-model organisms.

title: General practitioners' perspectives on treatment decisions and interprofessional care for women with uncomplicated urinary tract infections: An exploratory qualitative study.
authors: Plate A, Heinz N, Thiruchelvam T, Meyer-Massetti C, Jenkinson SP, Steinbrüchel C, Drewniak D, Neuner-Jehle S, Senn O.
abstract: Background Antibiotic-sparing strategies, such as delayed prescribing or symptomatic therapy, can reduce antibiotic use in uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs), yet their implementation in primary care remains inconsistent. Within this context, non-physician medical staff within general practices and community pharmacies play increasingly important roles in patient counselling and care coordination, potentially shaping treatment expectations and treatment decisions. This study investigated how general practitioners (GPs) make treatment decisions in the management of uncomplicated UTIs in women and examined their views on the roles of non-physician medical staff and community pharmacies in supporting antibiotic-sparing management. Methods We conducted an exploratory qualitative interview study with GPs who regularly manage women with uncomplicated UTIs. Virtual, semi-structured interviews were conducted. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed thematically. Results Fifteen GPs participated; their mean age was 46.6 years, 53.3% were female, and their experience in general practice ranged from 5 to 25 years. The thematic analysis generated six themes capturing clinical, relational, practical, and interprofessional influences on UTI management. Most GPs reported prior experience with antibiotic-sparing strategies, but thresholds for antibiotic prescribing varied and were shaped by clinical factors, patient expectations, trust, and practical constraints. Practice staff already influenced UTI management, both directly through triage, testing, and counselling and indirectly through practice routines and care pathways, while GPs differed in the degree of professional autonomy they considered appropriate. Pharmacy-based care was often only partly visible to GPs, with experiences varying according to local relationships and professional roles. Discussion The findings suggest that antibiotic-sparing UTI management extends beyond the GP prescribing decision and is shaped across the broader care pathway. Clearer professional roles, appropriate training, and feasible communication structures may support more coordinated care and antimicrobial stewardship in primary care.

title: Food sharing networks in a multi-ethnic, predominantly indigenous peri-urban community in the Brazilian Amazon.
authors: Wright Iii HM, Piperata BA, Downey SS, Scaggs SA, Pinto Fraxe TJ.
abstract: Social networks have long supported access to food among rural Indigenous and non‑Indigenous agrarian populations. As increasing numbers of rural Indigenous and agrarian households migrate to urban areas, questions arise about how these social networks shape food access in peri‑urban and urban settings where cash‑based markets predominate. Some researchers argue that, as Indigenous and agrarian households migrate to peri‑urban and urban settings, economic capital ("buying power") becomes the primary means of accessing food, reducing reliance on social capital and food‑sharing networks. Others find that migrants develop new affinity‑based support networks, often with individuals of similar regional or cultural backgrounds, which continue to play an important role in securing food in urban contexts. To better understand peri-urban food sharing, we examine the properties of the food-sharing networks of 106 households in Parque das Tribos, a primarily Indigenous, multiethnic community located in Manaus, Brazil. We utilize regressions to test the predictive relationship between residents' perceptions of household food security using a locally adapted version of the Brazilian Food Insecurity Survey (EBIA) instrument and social network properties, as well as the role of household socioeconomic factors in predicting their levels of engagement in food-sharing relationships. We find a positive relationship between perception of household food security and participation in larger, higher quality, relatively dense networks based on reciprocal relationships, even after accounting for economic factors such as income and conditional cash transfer programs. Overall, the results indicate that social capital is more strongly associated with household food security than economic capital.

title: Feasibility of the Resistance Training for Teens StrongHER program for Muslim adolescent girls.
authors: O' Loughlin NM, Lubans DR, Mazzoli E, Brown TD, Duncan MJ, Barnett LM.
abstract: Muslim adolescent girls can face intersecting barriers to physical activity. This study examined the feasibility of implementing Resistance Training for Teens StrongHER ( RT4T StrongHER) , a tailored program, in Islamic school settings. A wait-list control feasibility study was conducted with 56 female students (mean age = 14.6 ± 0.7) from two Islamic secondary schools in Victoria, Australia: one intervention school (n = 27) and one wait-list control school (n = 29), each contributing one class. The eight-week program was delivered during Health and Physical Education (HPE) lessons by the class teacher. Feasibility was assessed in the intervention group using teacher fidelity logs and teacher- and student-reported post-intervention process evaluation surveys. Resistance training knowledge, confidence, and motivation were assessed pre- and post-intervention in both groups and analysed using linear mixed models. All intended lessons were delivered, with moderate-to-high acceptability and compatibility with Islamic school settings. Exploratory analyses indicated significant Group × Time interactions for resistance training knowledge (B = 2.39, 95% CI [0.87, 3.90]) and confidence (B = 0.53, 95% CI [0.23, 0.82]). The interaction for motivation was not statistically significant (B = 0.22, 95% CI [-0.10 to 0.54]). Findings suggest RT4T StrongHER appears feasible within Islamic school HPE contexts.

title: Favorable Short-Term Outcomes for Minced Cartilage Implantation in Cartilage Defects of the Knee: A Systematic Review.
authors: Tham A, Alzobi O, Rubin J, AlSaadi A, Al-Shammari F, Emanuel KS, Kekhoffs GMMJ, Kennedy JG.
abstract: Purpose To systematically review available data on clinical, structural, and safety outcomes after minced cartilage implantation (MCI) in knee cartilage defects and to descriptively compare outcomes with microfracture and other treatment modalities. Methods A systematic search following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines was performed in 3 databases evaluating MCI for knee cartilage defects. Extracted variables included patient characteristics, patient-reported outcomes, structural outcomes, and complications at 12 and ≥24 months. Outcomes were summarized descriptively using study-level data without pooled estimates. Results Seventeen studies comprising 493 patients treated with MCI were included, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months and a maximum of 60 months and mean defect sizes ranging from 2.53 to 4.5 cm 2 (International Cartilage Repair Society grade III-IV). Improvement in International Knee Documentation Committee scores ranged from 21.6 to 40.8 points at 12 months and 19.7 to 43.9 points at ≥24 months. Visual analog scale pain scores improved from a range of 3.5 to 7.2 preoperatively to a range of 0.6 to 2.5 points at both timepoints. Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score total and subscale scores showed improvement across all reporting studies. Magnetic Resonance Observation of Cartilage Repair Tissue scores ranged from the low 50s to mid-80s at both timepoints. Comparative studies with microfracture displayed mixed findings of functional scores at 12 months and numerically higher International Knee Documentation Committee scores at ≥24 months. Complication rates ranged from 0% to 14% at 12 months and 0% to 8% at 24 months. Conclusions In this study, MCI is associated with improvements in pain and knee function, favorable structural repair, and low reported complication rates at short- to midterm follow-up. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level I to IV studies.

title: Explainable radiomics and clinical models for prediction of total knee arthroplasty in knee osteoarthritis: data from Osteoarthritis Initiative.
authors: Pooyan A, Alipour E, Eshraghi N, Mirghaderi P, Pishgar F, Nyflot MJ, Park C, Kim HS, Thurlow PC, Link TM, Chalian M.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate MRI radiomics models, with and without clinical variables, for predicting total knee arthroplasty (TKA) within 9 years in patients with knee osteoarthritis. Materials and methods This retrospective exploratory study included 507 participants from the Osteoarthritis Initiative-Zuse Institute Berlin dataset with manually segmented knee MRIs; 66 underwent TKA. Four hundred radiomics features from bone and cartilage were combined with 13 clinical variables. Logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated using radiomics-only, clinical-only, and combined feature sets in an 80/20 development-holdout analysis and stratified nested cross-validation. Preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning were restricted to training folds. Results On the held-out test set, radiomics-only LASSO had the highest observed AUC-ROC of 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.88), followed closely by combined LASSO at 0.75 (0.61-0.87). Combined logistic regression and XGBoost achieved AUC-ROC values of 0.73 (0.60-0.86) and 0.72 (0.57-0.84), respectively. Differences among the leading models were modest. In nested cross-validation, combined LASSO showed the highest discrimination (AUC-ROC, 0.786 [0.722-0.841]; AUC-PR, 0.343 [0.239-0.451]; F1 score, 0.405 [0.321-0.481]), with modest improvement over radiomics-only LASSO (AUC-ROC, 0.781 [0.717-0.834]). Consistently retained predictors included femoral bone sphericity, femoral cartilage first-order skewness, and WOMAC disability. Conclusion MRI radiomics features, alone or combined with clinical variables, showed potential for predicting TKA risk. Performance differences among leading models were modest, and these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical application.

title: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA)-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in a subset of professional soccer players.
authors: Tan E, Botchu R, James SL.
abstract: Objective Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA) is a relatively new MRI entity described in professional soccer players. We report a subset of players who sustained acute muscle injuries and ERSA lesions in the same muscle. Materials and methods A retrospective review was conducted from July 2024 to July 2026 to identify all MRI studies of professional soccer players with an acute thigh muscle injury and ERSA lesion in the same muscle. Anatomical site, laterality, ERSA lesion subtype and length, and acute muscle injury grade as per the British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification (BAMIC) were recorded. Results There were 18 ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in 16 soccer players (12 males, 4 females; median age 20.5 years). Affected muscles were the rectus femoris (n = 12), adductor longus (n = 5), and semitendinosus (n = 1). Type C ERSA lesions (n = 13) and BAMIC grade 2b (n = 8) muscle injuries were the most common. All acute muscle injuries were located within the ERSA lesions. No intratendinous extension was observed. Median ERSA lesion length was 21.5 cm and median acute muscle injury length was 7.0 cm. The main ERSA-associated muscle injury patterns were pre-degloving (n = 6) and myofascial (n = 6) injuries of the rectus femoris and distal myotendinous junction injuries of the adductor longus (n = 4). Conclusion We describe a new muscle injury pattern, termed ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries, in a cohort of professional soccer players. Distinct injury patterns were observed in the rectus femoris and adductor longus.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of chromosomal races in the Japanese allotetraploid spined loach, Cobitis sp. 'yamato' species complex.
authors: Oka H, Yashima Y, Uechi T, Fujimoto T, Kitagawa T.
abstract: The Japanese spined loach, Cobitis sp. 'yamato' species complex (hereafter Yamato spined loach), is an allotetraploid group originating from two diploid Cobitis species hybridization. Although specific regional populations have ancestral 2n = 98, decreases in 2n have been reported, indicating ongoing rediploidization. However, distribution patterns and phylogenetic relationships of each chromosomal race remain unknown. Using conventional cytogenetics, we identified seven 2n values across 45 populations (2n = 80, 82, 86, 90, 92, 94, and 98), including two newly reported karyotypes (2n = 80 and 92). Five races clustered in specific geographical areas, whereas two races (2n = 80 and 90) formed discontinuous distribution ranges. Mitochondrial phylogenies (cytb + ND2) revealed three major clusters with shallow differentiation and ancestral polymorphism retention across races, indicating rapid rediploidization. Races with few chromosomes belonged to derivative clusters, which reflect a gradual chromosome number reduction during Yamato spined loach evolution. Polyphyly within races indicates parallel and independent chromosomal reductions. Flow cytometry showed no positive correlation between chromosome number and relative DNA content, suggesting that karyotype rearrangements, rather than the loss of specific chromosomes, contributed to the decrease in chromosome or fundamental numbers.

title: Effects of hyponatremia on bone repair in mice.
authors: Yamao H, Mizukami Y, Kishigami R, Kawao N, Okumoto K, Kaji H.
abstract: Hyponatremia, a common electrolyte abnormality in older patients, is associated with osteopenia and an increased risk of fracture. However, the effects of hyponatremia on bone repair remain unclear. In the present study, we investigated the effects of 1-desamino-8-D-arginine vasopressin (dDAVP)-induced chronic hyponatremia on bone repair after creation of a femoral bone defect. A total of 54 nine-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to the control group (n = 24) or the dDAVP-treated group (n = 30), and dDAVP was administered for 6 weeks before bone defect creation. Serum sodium levels were 120.2 ± 1.2 mEq/L in dDAVP-treated mice. dDAVP administration significantly suppressed bone volume fraction (BV/TV) in the bone defect region 10 days after femoral bone injury creation in mice, compared to control (23.7 ± 3.4 vs. 39.0 ± 4.1%, p = 0.021). Histological analyses showed that dDAVP significantly reduced the numbers of alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-positive osteoblastic cells and both CD31- and endomucin-positive blood vessels in the bone injury region 10 days after femoral bone defect creation (ALP: 24.7 ± 2.0 vs. 30.0 ± 2.0 cells/mm, p = 0.043; CD31/endomucin: 107 ± 15 vs. 151 ± 9 vessels/mm 2 , p = 0.016). Moreover, dDAVP significantly suppressed the mRNA expression of osteogenic genes, such as Runx2, Osterix, ALP, osteocalcin, and type 1 collagen in the bone injury region. In in vitro studies, low sodium concentrations (125 mEq/L), but not dDAVP treatment, significantly suppressed ALP activity as well as the mRNA levels of Osterix and ALP enhanced by bone morphogenetic protein-2 in ST-2 cells (p = 0.029). Moreover, low sodium concentrations, but not dDAVP treatment, significantly suppressed mineralization in mouse primary osteoblasts (p = 0.007). In conclusion, we demonstrated for the first time that dDAVP-induced chronic hyponatremia delays bone repair after a femoral bone defect in mice, at least partly through impaired osteoblast differentiation and angiogenesis.

title: Dual-task interference in the drop jump: Frequentist, Bayesian, and waveform analysis of vertical ground reaction force.
authors: Celik H, Arpinar-Avsar P.
abstract: To ensure standardization, reliability, and maximal performance, physical performance tests are usually performed with little to no cognitive load. However, during training and competition, athletes usually perform physical actions while under the demands of a concurrent cognitive task (CT). This study examined the effect of a concurrent CT on the force-time metrics of the drop jump (DJ) and their reliability under single-task (DJ without a CT) and dual-task conditions (DJ with a CT based on simple arithmetic calculations). Thirty-five healthy young participants performed single-task and dual-task DJ trials in a randomized order. Nineteen force-time metrics covering the braking, propulsion, and landing phases of the DJ were compared between conditions using paired t-tests with Holm adjustment and Hedges' gz, Bayesian paired t-tests, and statistical parametric mapping (SPM) of vertical ground reaction force (VGRF) waveforms. For three-trial mean scores, 17 of the 19 metrics had within-session intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.812-0.930 across both conditions. Under the dual-task condition, jump height (p < 0.001, gz=1.40, Bayes factor BF10 = 1.76×107) and reactive strength index (p < 0.001, gz=1.04, BF10 = 45,943) were lower, while ground contact time was longer (p = 0.025, gz=-0.57, BF10 = 20.57). SPM showed that VGRF was significantly lower under the dual-task condition during 29.2-34.3% (within braking) and 52.0-79.1% (within propulsion) of ground contact. In the landing phase, VGRF was significantly lower under the dual-task condition during 1.3-6.3% (initial force rise) and significantly higher during 15.5-19.6% (attenuation of the impact force). The spring-like correlation (p = 0.462, gz=0.20, BF01 = 2.79) and the vertical time to stabilization (p = 0.462, gz=0.15, BF01 = 3.74) showed no significant difference between conditions, with weak and moderate evidence for the absence of an effect. These findings suggest that a concurrent CT reduces force production within both the braking and propulsion phases of the DJ and alters the VGRF waveform during the subsequent landing phase in healthy young participants.

title: Differences in Imaging and Surgical Management of Patellar Instability in Children and Adolescents Between Asia-Pacific and North America: A Systematic Review.
authors: Heng WT, Zhang S, Tan SHS, Hui JHP.
abstract: Purpose To compare diagnostic imaging practices and surgical interventions for patellofemoral instability in children and adolescents between Asia-Pacific and North America. Methods A systematic review was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guideline. Inclusion criteria were original surgical studies of patellofemoral instability in children or adolescent patients, with a sample size of more than 5, from either Asia-Pacific or North America. Exclusion criteria included nonoriginal research, cadaveric/biomechanical studies, imaging-only reports, unrelated diagnoses, and adult-only cohorts. Data were synthesized descriptively by region. Results Sixty-eight studies were included, with 15 from Asia-Pacific and 53 from North America. The total sample size was 397 patients in Asia-Pacific and 10,376 in North America. Magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and radiographs were reported more consistently in Asia-Pacific studies, whereas North American studies more frequently reported medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction and tibial tubercle osteotomy. Asia-Pacific studies more commonly reported medial soft-tissue tightening, lateral retinacular release, trochleoplasty, and medial hemiepiphysiodesis. The included literature was predominantly Level III to IV evidence, with marked heterogeneity in study design, populations, and procedures. Conclusions This systematic review identified reported regional variation in the imaging and surgical management of patellofemoral instability in children and adolescents between Asia-Pacific and North America. Asia-Pacific studies more frequently described computed tomography use and soft-tissue procedures, whereas North American studies more frequently reported medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction and tibial tubercle osteotomy. These findings should be interpreted with caution because of heterogeneity in study design and a marked imbalance in sample size between regions. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level I to IV studies.

title: Design, modeling, and performance analysis of a 2-DOF pneumatic flexible wrist with controllable braking torque.
authors: Liu H, Wang S, Xu W.
abstract: To address the structural complexity and limited compliance of traditional rigid robotic wrists, as well as the absence of adjustable stiffness in soft wrists designed primarily for flexibility, a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) pneumatic flexible wrist with controllable braking torque was developed. The wrist comprises three circumferentially arranged pneumatic actuators connected in parallel around a central pneumatic cross-hinge brake, enabling multidirectional pivoting, while the braking torque can be adjusted according to task requirements for pose stabilization. This configuration combines the high stiffness required for posture maintenance during braking with compliant actuation during motion. Theoretical models of the wrist pivot angle, pivoting direction, and braking torque were established. The pivot-angle model was empirically calibrated using the measured pivot-angle data, while the pivoting-direction and braking-torque models were validated experimentally. Mechanical performance was evaluated under constant-friction-torque and constant-pivot-angle conditions, and empirical relations were obtained by fitting the experimental data. A three-dimensional motion-capture system was also used to characterize the dynamic response under different braking conditions and excitation signals. Under the present experimental conditions, the results show that the wrist exhibits high compliance and enables continuous omnidirectional pivoting with a maximum single-axis pivot angle of 45.2°. The pneumatic cross‑hinge brake achieves multidirectional braking with continuously adjustable torque, reaching a maximum braking torque of 0.842 N·m under brake-only actuation at 0.35 MPa. During coordinated actuation-braking operation, the wrist's overall resistance to external loads increased by a factor of 4.98 compared with its unpressurized initial state. This composite load-resisting capacity originates from the combined effects of the pneumatic actuators and the central brake.

title: Cooperative R&D contracts for power batteries under R&D outcome uncertainty and subsidies.
authors: Liu J, Chen H, Cao Y.
abstract: This paper examines a supply chain comprising a single new energy vehicle manufacturer (NEVM) and a single power battery supplier (PBS), considering government subsidies and R&D outcome uncertainty. An exponential function is employed to characterize R&D outcome uncertainty. The impacts of R&D subsidies and R&D capability on R&D investment, supply chain members, and their expected profits are examined. A comparative analysis of cost-sharing (CS) and revenue-sharing (RS) contracts is conducted. The findings reveal that: (1) R&D investment exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with R&D capability and a positive relationship with R&D subsidies. (2) Under an RS contract, the expected profits of the supply chain and its members increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability. Under a CS contract, the expected profits of the PBS and the supply chain increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability; however, the NEVM's expected profit exhibits a U-shaped relationship with R&D subsidies and R&D capability. (3) Compared with centralized decision-making, neither contract achieves the centralized benchmark for the supply chain's expected profit. However, compared with decentralized decision-making, the CS contract increases the PBS's R&D investment and expected profit; the RS contract increases the PBS's R&D investment and expected profit as well as the supply chain's expected profit. Both contracts can only improve the NEVM's expected profit under certain conditions. These findings provide valuable theoretical insights and practical implications for decision-making by NEVMs, PBSs, and government agencies.

title: Comparison of Wiltse Approach-Based Invasion-Controlled Surgery With Traditional Open Surgery for Thoracolumbar Spinal Metastases Within the NOMS Framework.
authors: Wang P, Shen Z, Zhou J, Xu G, Yuan H, Xu M, Xiao J, Xu W.
abstract: Objectives To compare Wiltse approach-based invasion-controlled surgery (ICS) with traditional open surgery (TOS) for symptomatic thoracolumbar spinal metastases within the Neurologic, Oncologic, Mechanical, and Systemic (NOMS) framework, focusing on perioperative burden, postoperative recovery, neurological outcomes, pain, and QLQ-BM22 domains. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 30 patients undergoing ICS and 60 patients undergoing TOS from January 25, 2019, to January 25, 2022. Perioperative, neurological, and patient-reported outcomes were compared, including operative burden, postoperative recovery, complications, ASIA grade, VAS score, and QLQ-BM22 domains. Continuous variables were assessed with Shapiro-Wilk tests and compared using two-sided Welch independent-samples t-tests; categorical variables were analyzed using Pearson's χ 2 or exact tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for sensitivity analyses when patient-level data were available. Results The groups differed in preoperative ASIA distribution (p = 0.036). Compared with TOS, ICS was associated with shorter operative time (p Conclusions Wiltse approach-based ICS was associated with reduced operative burden and faster postoperative recovery, without evidence of a worse postoperative neurological distribution in the unadjusted comparison. ICS may be considered a complementary muscle-sparing option within NOMS-guided management for appropriately selected patients who require posterior stabilization with decompression or separation. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: ChiCTR1800016921.

title: Clinical outcomes and influencing factors of breast reconstruction after mastectomy in breast cancer patients: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Zhang F, Guo H, Ma J, Bo H, Li Z, Zhou Y.
abstract: To systematically analyze postoperative complications, cosmetic satisfaction, and long‑term oncologic outcomes of different post‑mastectomy breast reconstruction modalities and identify associated risk factors. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 327 breast‑cancer patients (autologous flap = 182, implant‑based = 145) undergoing immediate or delayed breast reconstruction between October 2018 and November 2024. Eligible patients had a minimum of 12‑month complete oncologic follow‑up. Baseline clinicopathological features, 3‑month perioperative complications, 12‑month composite cosmetic‑satisfaction scores, disease‑free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) were compared between groups. Subgroup analyses were performed stratified by reconstruction timing (immediate versus delayed). Multivariate Cox proportional‑hazards regression was applied for exploratory identification of factors associated with reconstruction‑related complications. Given that adverse events were captured within a fixed 3‑month postoperative window, the Cox model violates some time‑to‑event assumptions; results should be interpreted only as observational associations rather than definitive causal risk estimates. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. The median follow‑up duration was 61.3 months. The overall 3‑month complication rate was 14.37% (47/327). The autologous‑flap group exhibited a higher rate of reconstructive‑flap partial necrosis (8.24% vs. 0.00%, P 0.05). Within this single‑center retrospective cohort, autologous‑flap and implant‑based breast reconstruction demonstrated comparable long‑term oncologic survival. Reconstructive surgery does not alter oncologic mastectomy resection margins; survival comparisons reflect real‑world observational associations and cannot prove causal oncologic equivalence. Autologous‑flap reconstruction was associated with superior composite cosmetic scores at the expense of higher partial reconstructive‑flap necrosis risk. Implant‑based reconstruction carried higher capsular‑contracture risk, particularly in patients receiving chest‑wall radiotherapy. The apparent protective effect of immediate reconstruction on crude complication rates is heavily confounded by baseline patient‑tumor‑treatment characteristics. Individualized reconstructive planning should integrate oncologic features, adjuvant‑therapy schedules, donor‑site conditions, device‑related considerations, and patient preferences. Important inherent limitations of retrospective observational design preclude causal inference from these findings.EBM level: III.

authors: Yılmaz E, Yılmaz ZY.
abstract: Pubertal activation in Williams syndrome may progress rapidly, but classification as central precocious puberty depends on documented age at onset. We discuss the distinction between chronological diagnostic criteria and syndrome-specific growth patterns, the specific indication for adding growth hormone to GnRH agonist therapy, and the importance of reporting bone-age and predicted adult height methods when interpreting treatment response.

title: BoneNet: a framework for predicting MSK-FE-estimated femoral neck strain patterns from exercise IMU data.
authors: Altai Z, Hollinger D, Phillips ATM, Moran J, Zhai X, Mei Q, Liew BXW.
abstract: Femoral neck fractures pose serious risks, particularly in osteoporosis, highlighting the need for effective bone-strengthening exercises and practical, non-invasive assessment of femoral loading. This study quantifies exercise-induced strains and presents BoneNet, an explainable convolutional neural network that predicts femoral neck strains from inertial measurement unit (IMU) data, offering a potential approach for estimating musculoskeletal-finite element (MSK-FE)-derived femoral neck strain patterns. Data were collected from 40 healthy participants (40.3 ± 13.1 years), with 37 included in the FE and BoneNet analyses. MSK-FE models estimated femoral neck strains during walking, running, jumping and hopping at varying intensities. BoneNet used IMU accelerometer and gyroscope signals from seven- and three-sensor configurations with participant-grouped cross-validation. Fast running yielded 3731 ± 1472 µε (tensile) and - 9541 ± 3610 µε (compressive), with walking strain magnitudes 47% lower for both tensile and compressive strains. Unilateral hopping with longer ground contact yielded 3003 ± 1189 µε and - 7755 ± 3040 µε, with walking strain magnitudes 34% and 35% lower, respectively. Walking generally produced higher strains than all other exercises. Using seven IMUs, BoneNet achieved correlations of r = 0.75-0.94 for five exercises, while squat jumps showed weak correlations (r = 0.27-0.36) and high relative RMSE (54.9-59.4%). Three IMUs showed comparable correlations, but squat-jump errors remained high (relative RMSE 56.0-61.2%). Running at all intensities and unilateral hopping with longer ground contact may have implications for bone adaptation, while BoneNet shows potential for estimating strain patterns rather than validated absolute values.

title: Barriers to Radiation Protection Among Female Orthopedic Trainees: A Survey of Current Residents.
authors: Orringer M, Ramos V, Blumenthal S.
abstract: Objective Higher rates of breast cancer have been linked previously to occupational radiation hazards in the orthopaedic operating room. However, increased awareness regarding the elevated risk of cancer among female orthopaedic surgeons has not necessarily resulted in improved access to appropriately fitting protective lead garments. The primary objective of this study was to survey female residents on their access to one-piece versus two-piece lead garments. Secondary objectives included identifying descriptive barriers and regional differences in access. Design An anonymous survey was distributed via email, word of mouth, and orthopaedic surgery social media groups to trainees around the United States. Statistical analysis was performed using SAS Enterprise 8.3, with descriptive analysis conducted for reported barriers to access. Setting Electronic RedCap-based survey study. Participants Eighty-nine female resident trainees completed the survey, including 58 junior (PGY1-3) and 31 senior residents (PGY4-5). Results 98% of surveyed residents endorsed awareness of the increased breast cancer risk among female orthopaedic surgeons, and 63% of residents reported concerns regarding elevated risk due to inadequate radiation protection. 39% of participants reported anxiety related to lead accessibility. Only 46% of surveyed residents were provided custom garments from their institution, and 51% of respondents reported financial barriers to obtaining appropriately fitting lead. Common barriers included inadequate financial resources, storage or ability to transport between sites, and lack of awareness among program leadership. Conclusions Access to lead protective garments varies between institutions, inducing significant financial and psychological stress among female trainees. Provision of protective garments ranges widely, with less than half of surveyed residents receiving appropriately fitted lead. Cost remains the most frequently cited barrier to adequate radiation protection.

title: Arthroscopic Flipped Coracoid Transfer (Laterjet Procedure) With Endobutton Fixation for Anterior Shoulder Instability.
authors: Patzer T, Zolle M, Hofmaier A.
abstract: Glenoid bone loss is one of the most important risk factors for recurrent anterior shoulder instability. Transfer of the coracoid process is a well-established procedure for this. In the classic Latarjet procedure, the subscapularis tendon is split and the graft is fixed with screws. The subscapularis split may weaken the tendon, and screws may contact the humeral head after partial graft osteolysis, leading to cartilage damage. To avoid splitting the subscapularis, the "flipped" coracoid transfer technique has been described, in which the coracoid process is passed above the subscapularis and the superior instead of the inferior surface of the graft is fixed to the anterior glenoid. The origin of the conjoint tendon is located superiorly. The "flipped" technique uses a U-tape cerclage with 2 glenoid tunnels drilled posteriorly, thereby reducing the risk of axillary nerve injury anteroinferiorly. The tape obtains the risk of suture cutout with insufficient primary stability. Therefore, the present "flipped" technique uses 2 double Endobuttons with a sliding, self-locking Nice knot posteriorly. This fixation has been shown to provide sufficient stability. The technique is performed fully arthroscopically except for coracoid osteotomy which is performed through a 4-cm miniopen incision.

title: An ultrasonic sensing system for colonic content discrimination in ostomy patients: Development and experimental validation.
authors: Tang Y, Pan Y, Huang T, Li Y, Zhong S, An H, Deng G, Guo X.
abstract: Background Enterostomy leads to excretion incontinence, complications, and impaired quality of life, while existing interventions lack colonic content sensing capabilities. Objective The aim of this validation-based study was to develop and evaluate the technical performance of a smart ultrasonic sensing system for discriminating colonic content states to improve ostomy management. Method A modified 2 MHz reflective ultrasonic sensing system was developed, integrating an ultrasonic probe, transceiver circuit, signal amplification module, single-chip microcomputer, RGBW LEDs, and a buzzer alarm. Functional testing was performed under three immersion conditions (non-immersed, semi-immersed, and fully immersed) in normal saline. Voltage thresholds were established in vitro using excised colonic segments from 20 Oryctolagus cuniculus (O. cuniculus), with voltage signals measured under four colonic content states (gaseous, solid, fluid, and empty). In vivo validation was then conducted in 20 O. cuniculus and 12 Canis lupus familiaris (C. lupus familiaris). Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA with LSD post-hoc tests (SPSS 27.0, p Results Voltage output increased progressively with immersion depth in normal saline: 343.85 ± 2.11 mV (non-immersed), 637.60 ± 8.01 mV (semi-immersed), and 943.35 ± 3.86 mV (full- immersed) (p Conclusion This study developed an integrated ultrasonic sensing system for artificial anal plugs, which achieved high classification accuracy and can provide reliable real-time feedback on colonic content, demonstrating strong potential for artificial anal plugs.

title: An exploratory study on the influence of CT slice spacing on the positioning accuracy of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments designed for a distal radius osteotomy.
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Gryska E, Axelsson P, Libberecht K, Stor Swinkels C, Björkman A.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT) images with slice spacing up to 3 mm are generally sufficient for accurate 3D reconstructions of patient anatomy. For designing patient-specific instruments, particularly for forearm and wrist osteotomies, higher-resolution imaging (slice spacing of 0.4-1.25 mm) is commonly used. However, it remains unclear whether CT slice spacing meaningfully affects the surface fit of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments. This in-vitro study quantified the impact of CT slice spacing on the positional accuracy of instruments for the distal radius. Methods Data from 12 patients were analysed. Each had a high-resolution CT image (0.625 mm slice spacing), from which a reference 3D radius model and a patient-specific instrument were designed. The original images were downsampled to slice spacings of 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.875, and 2.5 mm to generate corresponding radius models and instrument bases. An experienced hand surgeon, blinded to slice spacing, fixated each 3D-printed instrument base onto its reference 3D-printed radius model in a simulated surgery. The assembled constructs were scanned, and the translation and rotation deviations of each lower-resolution instrument position were measured relative to the gold-standard instrument from the original scan. Results Mean rotational deviations across all slice spacings remained consistently low ( Conclusion CT slice spacing had a generally small effect on the positional accuracy of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments for the distal radius in vitro. These results indicate that clinically acceptable instrument accuracy may be achieved across a broad range of CT slice spacing commonly used in musculoskeletal imaging, potentially reducing the need for high-resolution protocols in selected clinical scenarios.

title: Age-related slowing of sensorimotor reaction time in masters track and field athletes.
authors: Zhou Y, McLaurin NN, Böcker J, Chilibeck PD, Taivassalo T, Forbes SC, Pesta D, Rittweger J, Tanaka H.
abstract: Introduction Masters athletes offer a powerful model for understanding how lifelong training shapes age‑related changes in reaction time (RT), a key indicator of sensorimotor performance. Purpose This cross-sectional study examined RT in masters track and field athletes across age, sex, RT tasks of varying complexity, and event disciplines (endurance, power, sprint). Methods A total of 182 competitors (82 females) from the 2025 World Masters Athletics Championships completed four RT tasks using a wireless light-based testing system. Results RT increased progressively with age across all tasks, with the slowest responses consistently observed in athletes ≥80 years old. Female athletes demonstrated slower RT than males, and RT increased systematically with task complexity. Sprint athletes showed faster RT than endurance athletes overall, although event‑specific differences did not persist within age groups. Age was positively associated with RT in all tasks (r = 0.41-0.53), with similar correlation strengths between sexes. Quadratic age effects emerged selectively in male athletes for two-hand simple and step-choice tasks, suggesting accelerated slowing at older ages in tasks requiring greater motor coordination. Linear regression models indicated that RT increased by approximately 3.3-3.6 ms per year of age after adjusting for sex, task, and event discipline, while body composition variables were not significant predictors. Conclusions Although lifelong training is associated with better sensorimotor performance, slower RT remains evident in masters athletes, with consistent sex differences and minimal influence of event discipline.

title: Validity and reliability of the short form-late life function and disability instrument Turkish version.
authors: Ataş M, Ceyhan Doğan S.
abstract: The growing aging population worldwide has increased the need for valid, culturally adapted tools to assess function and disability in older adults. The Short Form-Late Life Function and Disability Instrument (SF-LLFDI) is a brief, psychometrically sound tool originally developed to evaluate physical functioning and disability in community-dwelling older adults; however, no Turkish-validated version existed prior to this study. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Turkish SF-LLFDI. Cross-cultural adaptation followed Beaton et al.'s internationally recognized guidelines, involving forward translation, back-translation, expert committee review, and pilot testing with 25 participants. A total of 230 community-dwelling adults aged ≥70 years were recruited. Reliability was assessed via internal consistency (Cronbach's α) and test-retest stability using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) in a subsample of 77 participants over a 15-day interval. Construct validity was examined through exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory factor analyses (CFA), and criterion validity was evaluated by correlating SF-LLFDI scores with the Barthel Index, Lawton-Brody IADL, Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), Timed Up and Go Test (TUG), SF-36, Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE), and Charlson Comorbidity Index. The Turkish SF-LLFDI demonstrated excellent internal consistency (α = 0.987) and outstanding test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.997-0.999). EFA confirmed the original factor structure, accounting for 83.13% of the variance in the Function subscale and 79.83-85.00% in the Disability subscales. CFA indicated adequate model fit (χ2/df = 2.76-4.71, RMSEA = 0.069-0.078, CFI = 0.960-0.984, GFI = 0.900-0.947). Strong concurrent validity was evidenced by significant correlations with the Barthel Index (r = 0.960), Lawton-Brody IADL (r = 0.937), SPPB (r = 0.986), TUG (r = -0.975), MMSE (r = 0.848), SF-36 (r = 0.664-0.938), and Charlson Comorbidity Index (r = -0.897) (all p < 0.001). The Turkish SF-LLFDI is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing function and disability in Turkish-speaking older adults, suitable for use in both clinical and research settings.

title: The competency trap: how work hour restrictions and low operative volume may produce persistent suboptimal proficiency in surgeons - a comparative analysis of Italy, Germany, The United States, and The United Kingdom.
authors: Papadia FS, Karcz KW, Ziółko B, Di Lorenzo N, De Cian F.
abstract: Work hour restrictions for surgical trainees reduce fatigue-related errors but may inadvertently limit operative volume. This paper introduces the concept of a "competency trap": a theoretical risk, supported by indirect evidence, whereby the interaction between work hour limits and low case volume may produce a surgeon who is well-rested but at risk of persistent suboptimal proficiency for complex procedures. We conducted a conceptual synthesis of literature on surgical learning curves, skill decay, volume-outcome relationships, and work hour regulations. We analyzed training requirements in Italy (DM 68/2015), Germany (Arbeitszeitgesetz, Logbuch), the United States (ACGME), and the United Kingdom (NHS, ePortfolio). Illustrative volume data from the Piemonte region (PNE 2022) are presented as a lower-bound case study. A mathematical model with sensitivity analysis was constructed across multiple procedure types. Learning curves vary by procedure: short (C = 60, cholecystectomy), medium (C = 75, colectomy), long (C = 90, bariatric surgery), very long tier 1 (C = 100, pancreatectomy, hepatectomy), and very long tier 2 (C = 120, esophagectomy). Italy faces structural vulnerabilities: low first-operator percentage (10% for high-complexity cases, effectively 3 independent cases), no mandatory electronic logbook, and ongoing EU infringement proceedings for work hour non-enforcement. Germany permits Opt-Out to 58-hour weeks with eLogbuch transparency. The United States mandates 850 major cases (200 as chief resident) with electronic verification. The United Kingdom has fully enforced 48-hour EWTD limits without opt-out and a mandatory ePortfolio, but has lost over 3 million training opportunities since 2020 (organizational estimate). Using Piemonte as a lower-bound case study (V_p = 5 cases/year), the trap is present across all procedures. Under optimistic assumptions (K₀=20, V_p = 12), the trap resolves for colectomy (V_m = 10) but persists for bariatric surgery (V_m = 12.5). Under lower-bound volume assumptions derived from the Piemonte case study, Italy and the United Kingdom face theoretical competency trap risk across a wide range of procedures. Solutions require reformed minimums with higher first-operator percentages, mandatory electronic logbooks, hub-and-spoke centralization, simulation-based maintenance, and resolution of work hour implementation gaps with adequate staffing.

title: Systemic Physiological Impact on Cervical Bone Quality Measurements: A Comparative Analysis of Cervical Vertebral Bone Quality Scores and Hounsfield Units.
authors: Qi F, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Feng T, Wang L, Liu X.
abstract: Objectives Cervical vertebral bone quality (C-VBQ) scores and cervical Hounsfield units (C-HU) demonstrate significant potential for bone quality assessment. However, research on the influence of physiological factors on these metrics remains limited. This study aims to: quantify segment- and gender-specific associations between various physiological factors and both measures. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 512 patients with cervical spondylotic myelopathy from January 2023 to January 2024, with a mean age of 63.04 ± 8.86 years. Differences between male and female groups were compared using independent sample t-tests, Welch's corrected t-test, Mann-Whitney U tests, and chi-square tests, as appropriate for variable type and distribution. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses, as well as multiple linear regression, were performed to clarify the associations between physiological factors and these two measurement methods across different cervical segments and genders. Results At the C4/5 segment, the C-VBQ score showed the strongest correlations with age, fasting blood glucose (FBG), glycated albumin (GA), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), conjugated bilirubin (CB), unconjugated bilirubin, total bilirubin, and serum calcium, while C-HU correlated most strongly with age, serum phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), CB, GA, and APTT (all p Conclusions The associations of bilirubin metabolism and glucose metabolism indicators with both methods were more pronounced at the C4/5 segment and among female populations, and the C-VBQ score appeared to be more sensitive.

title: Successful limb salvage and favorable functional outcome after subtotal scapulectomy and custom 3D-printed reconstruction in a 14-year-old with high-grade osteosarcoma.
authors: Blecha O, Belzarena AC, Lesensky J.
abstract: Scapular reconstruction following tumor resection remains a surgical challenge because of the scapula's essential role in upper extremity biomechanics. Although patient-specific implants have expanded reconstructive options, achieving durable fixation and functional restoration remains difficult. A 14-year-old male with high-grade osteosarcoma of the scapular wing underwent limb-salvage surgery using a custom 3D-printed endoprosthesis. Preoperative planning incorporated dedicated software and patient-specific cutting guides. Wide resection preserved a small portion of the glenoid and the native glenohumeral joint to maximize postoperative function. At 3 months, radiographs demonstrated early osseointegration. The patient achieved 100° of active shoulder abduction without scapular winging or instability. At 2 years, he maintained near-full motion, demonstrated stable implant integration without loosening or recurrence, and returned to sports and daily activities with minimal limitations. Patient-specific scapular endoprosthetic reconstruction can achieve excellent oncologic and functional outcomes after subtotal scapulectomy, even in very young patients with high-grade malignancy.

title: Stabilization of canine ilial body fractures using an anatomically contoured locking iliac plate: A short retrospective case series.
authors: Ferrigno CRA, de Magalhaes Ferraz VC, Chiaramonte A, Woo G, Boone A, Bevelock T, Weaver C, Kasmark L, Ferreira MP.
abstract: Objective To report the clinical outcomes of canine ilial body fractures stabilized with a newly designed, anatomically 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate. Study design Retrospective case series. Animals Ten client-owned dogs treated between 2023 and 2024. Methods Medical records and orthogonal pelvic radiographs were reviewed for signalment, fracture configuration, surgical findings, time to radiographic union, postoperative sacral index (SI), complications, and limb function. Continuous variables were summarized as median (interquartile range, IQR), mean ± standard deviation (SD), and range; categorical variables as counts and proportions with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Median age was 3.5 years (IQR 2.25-5.75; range 0.75-10) and median body weight 32.0 kg (IQR 28.3-38.5; range 21-52). Median time to radiographic union was 60 days (IQR 60-62.5; range 60-97). Six of ten dogs (60%; 95% CI 31.3-83.2%) achieved union by 60 days. One dog (10%; 95% CI 1.8-40.4%) developed a cutaneous fistula that resolved within seven days of plate removal after fracture healing. The SI was within normal limits in all dogs at final follow-up, and limb function was normal in 10/10 dogs. Conclusions In this small case series, stabilization of canine ilial body fractures with the dedicated 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate was associated with reliable bone healing, a low complication rate, and preserved pelvic canal dimensions. Clinical significance: A dedicated, anatomically contoured locking plate is a feasible option for fixation of canine ilial body fractures, conforming to the iliac surface with no or minimal intraoperative contouring and allowing straightforward application. Larger comparative studies are warranted.
