abstract: Suspect rupture of a previously documented pelvic mesenteric cyst when acute abdominal pain and new free fluid develop, even if CT no longer clearly shows the cyst. Prompt surgical source control is essential; residual cyst wall warrants clinical and radiological surveillance.

title: Robotics in endoscopic spine surgery: a scoping review of clinical applications, workflow integration, and patient outcomes.
authors: Serdoura F, Gonçalves Dos Santos D, Correia MC, Silva JD, Nunes B.
abstract: Robotic and endoscopic technologies are increasingly being combined in spine surgery, yet the clinical literature remains fragmented across procedures, platforms, and robotic functions. We conducted a scoping review to map clinical applications of robot-assisted endoscopic spine surgery, describe how robotic systems are incorporated into endoscopic workflows, and summarize the technical, perioperative, and patient-centered outcomes reported to date. PubMed and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Human clinical reports were eligible when endoscopy constituted part of the operative visualization or working approach and a robotic system directly assisted the same spinal procedure. Study selection was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Of 374 records identified, 122 duplicates were removed and 252 records were screened. Sixty-six reports were sought, 13 were not retrieved, 53 full texts were assessed, and 24 studies were included. The evidence comprised 11 comparative studies, four uncontrolled clinical series, and nine case-based or technical clinical reports. Applications ranged from discectomy and decompression to interbody fusion, pars repair, infection, trauma, and thoracic or craniovertebral procedures. Robots were used for trajectory planning, localization, percutaneous access, guidewire or pedicle screw placement, drilling, endoscope stabilization, and interbody instrumentation. Comparative studies most often showed gains in fluoroscopy use, access efficiency, or instrumentation accuracy; patient-reported outcomes were usually similar between groups. Robotic-endoscopic integration is clinically feasible across an expanding range of spinal procedures, but its patient-level value remains incompletely defined.

title: Robotic pancreatic enucleation versus laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation: a meta-analysis.
authors: Shi J, Zhu C, Zhou Y.
abstract: Pancreatic enucleation (PE) is an operation that spares pancreatic parenchyma and thereby preserves glandular function, and it is now widely favoured for benign and low-grade malignant pancreatic neoplasms. Whether adding robotic assistance brings benefit beyond the standard laparoscopic route, however, remains an open question. This meta-analysis therefore contrasted robotic pancreatic enucleation (RPE) with laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation (LPE) with respect to perioperative efficacy and safety. Records of cohort studies that contrasted RPE with LPE were retrieved from the Cochrane Library, PubMed, the Wanfang, Embase and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, covering each database from inception to 1 September 2026. Two investigators working in duplicate screened the records, extracted the data and rated methodological quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). R 4.5.3 with the meta package was used for pooling; mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) were presented with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Publication-bias and sensitivity analyses were omitted because fewer than 10 eligible studies were available. Five studies met the eligibility criteria (each scoring NOS ≥ 7) and together enrolled 272 patients, 144 in the LPE arm and 128 in the RPE arm. Operation time (MD 0.20, 95% CI - 38.98 to 39.39, P = 0.99), intraoperative blood loss (MD 14.60, 95% CI - 3.39 to 32.58, P = 0.11), postoperative pancreatic fistula (risk ratio [RR] 1.21, 95% CI 0.89-1.64, P = 0.23), postoperative bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.06-2.97, P = 0.39), and major complications (RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.54-3.00, P = 0.58) did not differ significantly between groups. Postoperative hospital stay was statistically shorter in the RPE group (MD 1.22, 95% CI 0.29-2.16, P = 0.01); however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously and does not, by itself, establish a clinically meaningful recovery advantage. The available evidence is insufficient to demonstrate a clear overall difference between robotic and laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation in perioperative efficacy or safety. Although postoperative hospital stay was shorter in the RPE group in the pooled analysis, the small observational evidence base and potential residual confounding preclude a firm conclusion that robotic surgery provides a recovery advantage. Larger, well-designed prospective multicentre studies are needed.

title: Robot-Assisted Low Anterior Resection Using the hinotori™ Surgical Robot System in a Patient with Situs Inversus Totalis: A Case Report.
authors: Asai R, Tajima JY, Terasaki K, Yokoi R, Matsumoto K, Fukada M, Sato Y, Yasufuku I, Tanaka Y, Matsuhashi N.
abstract: Introduction Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital anomaly characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of organs. Especially in a minimally invasive surgery, care must be taken to avoid misidentification because of reversed anatomical landmarks. Robot-assisted surgery (RAS) may be a feasible surgical option and may facilitate precise surgical manipulation in anatomically challenging situations. Although there are several reports of RAS using the da Vinci surgical robot system (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA, USA) for colorectal cancer (CRC) in patients with SIT, the optimal robot platform, port settings, and procedures have not been determined. Case presentation In a 74-year-old woman with SIT referred to our department for treatment of advanced rectal cancer, preoperative examinations showed cancer invasion beyond the intestinal walls and multiple lymph node swelling within the mesentery. After completing 4 cycles of preoperative chemotherapy, robot-assisted low anterior resection using the hinotori™ surgical robot system (hinotori; Medicaroid, Kobe, Hyogo, Japan) was planned. Prior to the surgery, we conducted meticulous simulation with other medical staff using the hinotori, instruments, monitors, and a dry box. During the operation, port placements and instruments were set in a completely left-right reversed position from the standard configuration. From the medial approach through mesenteric vessel division and dissection of the left-sided colon and rectosigmoid junction, the cockpit surgeon smoothly operated monopolar curved scissors with the non-dominant left hand with reversed procedures. In the operating room, a monitor displaying a left-right flipped image was placed alongside the original-image monitor, and surgery proceeded while the patient-side surgeons confirmed anatomical accuracy. As the hinotori has no sealing devices or linear staplers, vessel ligation, division of the mesorectum, and rectal transection were performed by the patient-side surgeons. The patient was discharged without major complications. Conclusions To our knowledge, this is the first report of a surgical robot system other than the da Vinci system used to perform surgery for CRC in a patient with SIT. Sufficient preoperative simulation and display of flipped images contributed to the safe operation of robot-assisted low anterior resection in the patient. It is necessary to understand the characteristics of each surgical robot platform and perform surgery by leveraging the system's individual features.

title: Right- and left-handed pitch-type recognition among skilled pitchers and hitters in baseball: Implications for processes of action prediction.
authors: Besler Z, Müller S, Chua R, Hodges NJ.
abstract: Both visual and motor experiences impact action prediction, yet potentially through different mechanisms. Here we tested for differences in action prediction among baseball athletes with primarily motor- (pitchers) and visual- (batters) experience and determined effector congruency effects by comparing videos of pitches that appeared right- or left-handed, to give evidence for motor simulative processes. Highly experienced hitters (n = 41; 34 = right-handed/RH) and pitchers (n = 42; 33 = RH) were compared watching temporally occluded RH and left‑handed pitches. Pitchers and hitters had reliable responses, with high accuracy (~70%) and discriminability, but they did not differ in overall accuracy. Neither hitters nor pitchers showed an overall RH pitch advantage, failing to support a visual-frequency effect or motor-simulation effect. However, pitchers were more accurate at the early occlusion points for changeups, especially for right-hand pitches and a pitcher advantage was seen for discrimination between pitches with different postural cues (curveballs & changeups). In conclusion, motor experience pitching afforded high accuracy and increased discriminability of off-speed pitches. The general absence of effector congruency effects does not, however, support a strong motor simulation account of action prediction in baseball. Future work should include veridical left-handed pitches and, where possible, more left-handed athletes.

title: Rethinking gait analysis in osteoarthritis: Emerging technologies.

title: Recent advances in photoacoustic imaging for breast reconstruction using the abdominal flap.
authors: Tsuge I, Takaya A, Morimoto N.
abstract: Recent advances in diagnostic imaging have significantly impacted surgical planning and options. In breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps, a method employing flaps from the lower abdomen allows for a high-quality reconstruction with a morphology and texture resembling those of the contralateral breast. Understanding microvascular patterns is crucial in this surgery to prevent volume deficiencies and contribute to successful tissue transplantation while maintaining the softness of the tissue. While the location and number of "perforators"-arteriovenous bundles penetrating the anterior sheath of the rectus abdominis-have traditionally been the focus, recent studies have further emphasized the importance of selecting appropriate perforating vessels to maintain the vascular network within the superficial adipose tissue and subcutaneous tissue and to elevate a high-quality flap with extensive and stable blood flow. Clinical studies using contrast-enhanced CT have drawn attention to the midline-crossing arterial network, demonstrating its relationship with a wide range of hemodynamic areas. Preoperatively, clearly identifying the blood vessels linking the left and right sides of the abdominal midline provides valuable information for planning free DIEP flaps for breast reconstruction, ensuring stable blood flow to the flap. However, clear visualization with contrast-enhanced CT requires high volumes of contrast agents, and color Doppler ultrasound has difficulty visualizing horizontally; therefore, a non-invasive and superior imaging method is required. Photoacoustic imaging can comprehensively and noninvasively visualize the subcutaneous vascular network and is attracting attention as a new preoperative examination technique. We conducted clinical research using newly developed medical photoacoustic imaging and reported the results and future challenges in several publications. We have also recently reported the impact of abdominal surgical scars on the midline-crossing artery. This review summarizes the current trends in preoperative vascular studies for breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps and discusses the current state of evolving photoacoustic imaging technology.

title: Radiation-Associated Angiosarcoma Among Breast Cancer Survivors: Clinicopathologic Features and Oncologic Outcomes.
authors: Perrier AD, Vavolizza RD, Wingate H, Keung EZ, Roland CL, Torres KE, Scally CP, Lyu HG, Guadagnolo BA, Ravi V, Hunt KK, Lillemoe HA.
abstract: Background Data is limited for radiation-associated angiosarcoma (RAAS) given its rarity and the tendency for investigators to combine primary and secondary breast angiosarcomas together. Methods This retrospective study included patients with RAAS of the breast/chest wall who received treatment at a comprehensive cancer center from 2011-2025. All patients had prior breast cancer treated with surgery and radiation therapy (RT). Clinicopathologic features, treatment patterns, and survival outcomes were collected and analyzed. Results Among 135 patients, median age at RAAS diagnosis was 68 years with median latency period of 7.5 years. Skin changes were the most common clinical presentation (90%). Multimodal treatment with chemotherapy and surgery was most common (69%); only 5 patients received re-irradiation. Among 125 patients who underwent surgery, 75 (60%) had total mastectomy and 35 (28%) had mastectomy (or completion mastectomy) with extended resection of irradiated skin. Among 78 patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, 56% demonstrated complete/near-complete pathologic response (residual viable tumor Conclusions In patients with RAAS after breast cancer treatment, improved local control was seen with more aggressive treatments, including chemotherapy (particularly in those who had robust response) and extended surgical resection. These findings may help refine current clinical algorithms for the management of RAAS.

title: Psychosocial influences on hypertension in Southeastern Nigeria: A mixed-methods study protocol.
authors: Ebigwei Omeda AR, Chilaka M, Mohammadnezhad M, Vaportzis E.
abstract: Introduction The Southeastern region of Nigeria faces a severe public health challenge from hypertension due to its high prevalence. Psychosocial factors including perceived stress, anxiety, depression, coping mechanisms, and social support play essential roles in hypertension development and health behaviour, yet there has been limited scholarly attention to these determinants in Nigerian and international qualitative research. This study addresses this evidence gap by investigating the psychosocial determinants of hypertension-related health behaviour outcomes in adults living in Southeastern Nigeria. Materials and methods The sequential explanatory mixed methods study includes validated psychometric instruments assessing perceived stress, anxiety, depression, coping mechanisms, and social support. The primary quantitative outcome is the Health Behaviour Index, a composite measure of hypertension-related health behaviours. Regression analyses, correlation tests, and mediation/moderation models will be used to examine relationships among these variables. The research team will collect qualitative data through semi-structured interviews accessible to participants either online or in person. Thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework will be employed to explore participants' lived experiences of stress, coping, and hypertension management. Findings will be disseminated at academic conferences and published in peer-reviewed journals and stakeholder meetings held in both the UK and Nigeria. The research aims to generate evidence to support the development of comprehensive psychosocial care plans that address both physical and mental aspects of hypertension treatment in areas with limited resources.

title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among cisgender bisexual women: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Lawley KA, Kusuma K, Farquhar SA, Goodreau SM, Winer RL.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection in the United States, and a primary cause of cervical cancer. Although cervical cancer is largely preventable through HPV vaccination, vaccine coverage remains suboptimal. Research on HPV prevalence and vaccination among cisgender bisexual women is limited and inconsistent. This may be partly due to variation in how bisexuality is defined. Bisexuality may be operationalized based on sexual identity (e.g., self-identification as bisexual) or sexual behavior (e.g., sexual contact with more than one sex or gender), and these differing definitions may capture distinct populations and yield divergent health findings. This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type. Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women.

title: Prevalence and distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes among women living with HIV in Nigeria.
authors: Ifeorah IM, Chinwendu J, Eneh SC, Olakunde BO, Akpan U, Awolola NA, George UE, Faleye TOC, Bolutife P, Omoruyi CE, Iyi CC, Tishiya C, Ivo EA, Banjo AAF, Chigbu CO, Hou L, Ezeanolue EE, Adewumi OM.
abstract: Women living with HIV (WLHIV) are at significantly higher risk of persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV), and consequently, cervical cancer. However, large scale data on the epidemiology of hrHPV genotypes among WLHIV are limited in Nigeria. The study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of hrHPV among WLHIV in Nigeria. We conducted a cross-sectional study among 1327 WLHIV aged 25-60 years receiving HIV care from six selected Nigeria Implementation Science Alliance-Model Innovation and Research Centers (NISA-MIRCs) across Nigeria. Cervical swabs were obtained, and HPV DNA genotype was determined using the Hybribio Genoarray assay that detects 37 HPV genotypes including 14 high-risk HPVs. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected using interviewer-administered structured questionnaire. Factors independently associated with hrHPV infection were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical analysis was performed using R statistical software (version 4.4.1) with significance set at p < 0.05. Among the 1105 participants with analyzable samples, the overall HPV and hrHPV prevalence were 30.9% and 22.1%, respectively, with regional differences. Non-HPV 16 and 18 accounted for nearly two-thirds (67.6%) of hrHPV infections. The top five most often detected hrHPVs were HPV-58 (14.2%), HPV-16 (12.7%), HPV-52 (12.4%), HPV-31 (10.6%), and HPV-18 (10.3%). In a multivariate analysis, ART usage for one year or less was associated with hrHPV infection (aOR = 8.2, 95% CI 4.3-16.0). This multi-site study showed a significant and genotype-diverse burden of hrHPV among HIV-positive women in Nigeria, with most infections caused by non-HPV16/18 variants. These findings emphasize the need for increased integration of cervical cancer screening within HIV care and support the call for HPV vaccines with broader genotype coverage beyond HPV 16 and 18 to address the prevailing genotype distribution in this population.

title: Predictors of post-retirement mortality in athletes required to maintain very high body mass: a retrospective cohort study using AI-driven three-dimensional body reconstruction, 1865-1990.
authors: Kimura A.
abstract: Background Elite athletes in weight-uncapped disciplines sustain very high body mass throughout their careers (body mass index (BMI) 35-50 kg/m 2 ) and show a two- to three-fold mortality excess, yet no post-retirement care framework exists. Prior sumo mortality analyses used career-entry as follow-up origin, introducing immortal time bias. We generated virtual three-dimensional body reconstructions from historical photographs using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven landmark extraction to examine whether a reconstructed waist circumference adds prognostic information on post-retirement mortality beyond BMI. Methods All wrestlers reaching the makuuchi division (1865-1990 birth cohort; source N = 978) were assembled from published compendia. Transverse abdominal diameter was measured on career-peak photographs calibrated against recorded height; sagittal diameter was recovered by a volume-conserving solver; virtual waist circumference (C3) was the perimeter of the resulting ellipse. Retirement-anchored Cox models adjusted for birth year, retirement age and rank entered one body-size measure at a time; cause-specific models used follow-up from 1990 with multiple imputation of undocumented causes. Standardised mortality ratios (SMRs) used age × calendar-year-specific Japanese male rates. Primary cohort: birth n = 604; 587 with a calibrated photograph). Results The primary cohort had 467 deaths over median 31.1 years follow-up; median BMI 36.2 kg/m 2 , median C3 136 cm. C3 rose with rank and correlated with BMI ( r = 0.95). C3 per standard deviation (SD) (hazard ratio (HR) 1.47, 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.29-1.69]; Harrell's C 0.675) and BMI per SD (HR 1.38, 1.22-1.55; C 0.672) showed similar prognostic performance and could not be separated. The photographic diameter alone did not predict mortality (HR 1.08, 0.95-1.22) and added nothing to BMI (HR 1.03). Elite rank (HR 1.08) and career length (HR 0.98) showed no association. From 1990, with imputation, BMI predicted cardiometabolic death (HR 1.42, 1.08-1.87) but not neoplastic death (HR 1.07, 0.73-1.56), and C3 showed the same pattern (cardiometabolic HR 1.50, 1.08-2.07; neoplastic HR 1.20, 0.77-1.86); elite rank predicted neither. SMRs were 1.89 (1.72-2.07) overall, 1.84 for pre-1950 births and 2.57 for post-1950 births. Discussion Sumo wrestlers experienced about twofold all-cause mortality versus matched Japanese males across all historical strata. A waist circumference reconstructed from photographs, height and weight predicted mortality-specifically cardiometabolic mortality-as well as BMI, but its prognostic information derived from recorded body mass: the photographic component added none. Because obesity onset was unrecorded, the reconstruction is unvalidated, and no post-retirement data exist, the null findings for career length and photographic shape are not evidence that obesity duration or abdominal fat distribution is unrelated to mortality.

title: Perceived occupational physical fitness priorities and a preliminary conceptual framework for information technology students at selected vocational colleges in Shanxi Province, China: An exploratory cross-sectional mixed-methods study.
authors: Jin X, Cui X, Zhao Y, Hou Y.
abstract: Students majoring in information technology are frequently exposed to prolonged sitting, continuous screen use, sustained static postures, repetitive fine motor operations, and high cognitive load during their academic training and future work. These conditions may increase the risk of visual fatigue, neck and lower-back discomfort, physical fatigue, and psychological stress. This study adopted an exploratory cross-sectional mixed-methods design, using questionnaire surveys as the primary method and semi-structured interviews as a supplementary method. Participants included information technology students from selected vocational colleges, teachers whose teaching or research activities were related to vocational education or information technology student training, and personnel from information technology-related enterprises in Shanxi Province, China. The final analytical sample comprised 1,924 questionnaires: 1,863 from students, 37 from teachers, and 24 from enterprise personnel. The results showed that 68.71% of students selected "Frequently" or "Occasionally" when asked about physical discomfort following professional practical operations such as prolonged computer use or equipment debugging. The most frequently selected physical-discomfort categories included dry eyes or blurred vision, cervical or lumbar soreness, physical fatigue, and insufficient endurance. Weekly exercise duration was most commonly reported as 1-3 h/week (52.01%), whereas 14.76% of students selected "Almost no exercise." Qualitative interviews with students and teachers further suggested limited incorporation of occupation-specific training-such as visual relaxation and protection, musculoskeletal relaxation, postural adjustment, and sedentary behavior interruption-into current educational practice. The teacher sample indicated perceived constraints related to limited access to job-demand information, the availability of occupation-specific training methods and teaching resources, and student engagement. The enterprise sample suggested that some enterprise personnel recognized the potential role of occupational physical fitness in job adaptation and work efficiency; however, their actual involvement in curriculum development and the provision of job-related standards remained limited. Based on literature analysis, expert content validity evaluation, questionnaire survey data, and interview data, this study proposed a preliminary conceptual framework for occupational physical fitness in information technology programs, consisting of general physical fitness, occupation-specific physical fitness, and psychological fitness. These findings provide preliminary contextual evidence that occupation-related curriculum content and school-enterprise collaboration may warrant further investigation in vocational-education contexts similar to those examined in this study. Because this study used convenience sampling, included relatively small teacher and enterprise samples, and has not yet verified the proposed framework through structural validity testing or objective measurements, the framework requires further examination in larger and more balanced samples.

title: Osteogenesis imperfecta caused by ultra-rare variants in IFITM5: New cases and molecular studies on missense variants.
authors: Ordaz-Robles T, Tiranardi M, Ríos-Ruíz JG, Bardai G, Rauch F, Moffatt P.
abstract: Variants in IFITM5 are a unique cause of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI). The recurrent c.-14C > T leads to classical OI type V, whereas missense variants are considerably rarer and associated with a distinct phenotype. Here we present 3 Mexican boys with IFITM5 missense variants and investigated their cellular and molecular consequences in vitro. Individual 1 (p.Ser40Trp) had a history of 30 fractures, primarily involving both femurs, leading to bone deformities and short stature (height z-score - 3.1). Individual 2 (p.Ser40Leu) had bilateral lower extremity deformities at birth and sustained 15 fractures postnatally. Individual 3 (p.Asn48Ser) experienced 6 fractures, all involving the left femur. None exhibited the hallmark features of OI type V, including hyperplastic callus formation or interosseous membrane calcification. Transient transfection in MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts showed that all 3 IFITM5 variants were aberrantly retained intracellularly, although total protein levels remained normal. In a surrogate MEF2-based luciferase assay in MLO-A5 osteocytic cells, the variants failed to elicit a signaling response and appear to exert a dominant negative effects on wild type IFITM5 when co-expressed. Consistently, plasma membrane localization of the wild type protein was reduced in the presence of the mutants. Additional variants identified in ClinVar and gnomAD (p.Ser40Pro, p.Asn48Asp, and p.Asn48His) showed similar intracellular retention and loss of activity. Biochemical analyses indicated loss of palmitoylation of the adjacent cysteine residues. These findings expand the clinical spectrum of IFITM5 missense variants and support a dominant negative-like disease mechanism distinct from the classical IFITM5 c.-14C > T variant.

title: Opportunistic abdominal aortic calcification assessment on spine radiographs in women with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis: linking cardiovascular burden and femoral neck bone loss.
authors: Pinheiro MMC, Ramos FP, Silva LVA, Szejnfeld VL, Castro CHM.
abstract: Introduction/objectives Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and osteoporosis are major comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We assessed abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) opportunistically on spine radiographs and examined its associations with CVD, estimated cardiovascular risk, bone mineral density (BMD), and fragility fractures in women with longstanding RA. Method This cross-sectional study included 196 consecutive women with longstanding RA followed at a tertiary hospital. All underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and conventional spine radiography. AAC was graded using the Kauppila score (KS) and categorized as absent, mild-to-moderate (KS 1-6), or extended (KS > 6). Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with AAC and overt CVD. Results Participants had a mean age of 62.8 ± 9.6 years and median RA duration of 21 years. AAC was present in 48 women (24.5%), including extended AAC in 25 (12.7%). Overt CVD was documented in 32 participants (16.3%). Extended AAC was independently associated with hypertension (OR 8.57, 95% CI 1.10-67.02), longer RA duration (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.004-1.09), and lower femoral neck T-score (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.95). AAC of any severity was associated with overt CVD (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.26-6.63). Conclusions AAC detected on routine spine radiographs was common among women with longstanding RA and was associated with cardiovascular burden and lower femoral neck BMD. Opportunistic AAC assessment may complement cardiovascular and skeletal risk evaluation in RA. Larger cohorts are needed to confirm these exploratory associations, and prospective studies are needed to establish predictive value.

title: No Differences in Patient-reported Outcomes Between the Direct Anterior and Posterolateral Approach for THA: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Rykov K, de Vries AJ, Reininga IHF, Sietsma MS, Ten Have BLEF.
abstract: Background The direct anterior approach (DAA) for THA is seeing wider use because it is purported to deliver a faster postoperative recovery. However, most previous studies comparing the DAA with the posterolateral approach (PLA) were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous patient populations, and the use of outcome measures with ceiling effects. Questions/purposes (1) Does the DAA result in a higher proportion of patients achieving the patient acceptable symptom state (PASS) on the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) after THA compared with the PLA? (2) Are there differences in symptoms, physical function, life activities and participation, health-related quality of life (QoL), or complications between the DAA and PLA in the first postoperative year? Methods A prospective, parallel-group, nonblinded, randomized controlled trial comparing the DAA and PLA for THA was conducted. Patients with primary or secondary osteoarthritis with an indication for THA with an uncemented femoral stem and cemented acetabular component were eligible. Of the 241 patients assessed for eligibility, 53% (128) were included in the study. Fifty-one percent (65 of 128) were randomized to the DAA group, and 49% (63 of 128) were randomized to the PLA group. One patient in each group was lost to follow-up, leaving 98% (64 of 65) and 98% (62 of 63) of patients available for analysis, respectively. There were no between-group differences in baseline or perioperative measurements. The primary outcome was achievement of the PASS on the HOOS at 3 months postoperatively. An a priori sample-size calculation indicated that 60 patients per group were required to detect a 20% difference in PASS achievement between groups (80% power; α = 0.05). With an expected loss to follow-up of 10%, the sample size was set to 65 patients per group. Secondary outcomes included symptoms, physical functioning, participation, and health-related QoL, assessed using patient-reported outcome measures and physical performance tests. Complications were assessed using the Clavien-Dindo classification. Outcomes were assessed preoperatively as well as at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Results At 3 months, the proportion of patients achieving the PASS did not differ between the DAA and PLA for any HOOS subscales, including symptoms (65% [41 of 63] versus 63% [39 of 62], OR 1.03 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.80 to 1.35]; p = 0.80), pain (48% [30 of 63] versus 53% [33 of 62], OR 0.90 [95% CI 0.63 to 1.27]; p = 0.53), activities of daily living (68% [43 of 63] versus 65% [40 of 62], OR 1.06 [95% CI 0.82 to 1.36]; p = 0.66), sports and recreation (55% [34 of 62] versus 58% [36 of 62], OR 0.94 [95% CI 0.69 to 1.29]; p = 0.72), and QoL (73% [46 of 63] versus 71% [44 of 62], OR 1.03 [95% CI 0.83 to 1.28]; p = 0.80). There were no between-group differences in symptoms, physical function, life activities and participation, and health-related QoL at any time point. Complications occurred in 8% (5 of 65) of patients in the DAA group and 2% (1 of 63) of patients in the PLA group (OR 3.05 [95% CI 0.51 to 18.40]; p = 0.21). Conclusion In this randomized controlled trial, the DAA did not improve patient-reported or functional outcomes compared with the PLA during the first postoperative year. In the absence of demonstrated patient-reported or functional benefits of the DAA, surgeons should not represent to patients that the DAA provides advantages in terms of the pace or magnitude of recovery. Future studies powered to detect differences in the risk of complications should be performed to see whether harms are more likely with the DAA than with other surgical approaches. Level of evidence Level I, therapeutic study.

title: No Difference in Revision Risk for Uncemented Humeral Stems Compared to Cemented Humeral Stems in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for Proximal Humerus Fracture: A Registry-Based Cohort Study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Chauhan A, Chang RN, Prentice HA, Cruz JR, McQueen PD, Paxton EW, Navarro RA, Koyonos LD.
abstract: Background Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is an effective treatment option for complex proximal humerus fractures (PHF). Humeral stems are commonly cemented in patients with poor bone quality, increased comminution and/or older age to provide rotational stability for stem fixation. Recently, the use of uncemented stems has gained popularity due to newer, more stable designs. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to evaluate whether there were any differences in uncemented versus cemented stems with respect to revision risk. Methods Data from a US-based integrated healthcare system's Shoulder Arthroplasty Registry was utilized to conduct a cohort study. Adult patients with primary rTSA for PHF from 2011-2024 were included. The exposure of interest was humeral stem fixation, classified as uncemented versus cemented. Crude cumulative revision incidence was calculated as one minus the Kaplan-Meier estimate at 5-years follow-up. Propensity score-weighted Cox proportional hazard regression was used to evaluate the risk for all-cause revision. Propensity score weights were calculated prior to outcome evaluation using multivariable logistic regression and included age, sex, body mass index, race/ethnicity, diabetes status, smoking status, American Society of Anesthesiologist's classification, operative year, and operative time. Results The cohort comprised 1,415 rTSA; 450 with uncemented stems and 965 with cemented stems. At 5-years follow-up, the crude revision probability was 3.9% for uncemented stems and 3.2% for cemented stems. After propensity score weighting, no difference was observed in all-cause revision for uncemented versus cemented stems (hazard ratio [HR]=1.20, 95% confidence interval [CI]=0.61-2.37, p=0.60). Further, no differences were observed in risk for revision for dislocation (HR=1.06, 95% CI=0.38-2.98, p=0.91) or infection (HR=1.52, 95% CI=0.48-4.82, p=0.48). Conclusions Overall, our observational registry-based cohort study found no difference in revision risk when comparing uncemented to cemented stems for the use of rTSA in PHF. However, we still recommend surgeons consider cemented stem fixation on a case-by-case basis in patients with complex fractures, poor bone quality, and metabolic conditions affecting bone density. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison using Large Database, Treatment Study.

title: Newer Generation DePuy INHANCE™ Modular Anatomic Convertible Polyethylene Glenoid and Platform Baseplate have Improved Resistance to Micromotion and Dissociation at the Polyethylene-Metal Junction.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Kane LT, Myers C, Smith M, Cuff D, Jawa A, Wiater JM, Austin L.
abstract: Introduction Metal-backed glenoid (MBG) designs in anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA) were introduced in the 1980s to address concerns with the high rate of loosening of all-polyethylene glenoid components, offering potential advantages of durable glenoid fixation and easy revisability, but have historically demonstrated concerning rates of mechanical failure including polyethylene (PE) liner dissociation. Recently, platform baseplates have been introduced which can be used in anatomic or reverse TSA configurations. Platform baseplates may improve clinical performance, but more biomechanical analysis is needed to support their implant design improvements over the failed MBG designs of the past. The purpose of this study was to biomechanically evaluate a newer generation DePuy INHANCE™ modular anatomic convertible glenoid PE liner and platform baseplate and its ability to withstand mechanical forces and resist polyethylene dissociation when subjected to worst-case loading conditions. Methods The DePuy INHANCE™ convertible glenoid + platform baseplate were tested for resistance to micromotion from repetitive loading and compared to an all-polyethylene glenoid component. The study implant was also evaluated for its ability to withstand tensile displacement and polyethylene dissociation from shear and axial forces and compared against another commonly used modular anatomic glenoid PE liner and platform baseplate implant. Micromotion testing was performed in accordance with the standardized modular dissociation test method (ASTM F028-17) that was developed specifically for modular anatomic glenoid systems. Results The average tensile displacement of the INHANCE™ study implant after cyclic rocking was significantly less than the all-polyethylene glenoid component (0.1 mm vs. 0.4 mm; p=0.03). The INHANCE™ polyethylene-metal junction had a significantly greater resistance to modular dissociation under shear loading (1104N, 95% CI [1068, 1140] vs. 713N, 95% CI [687, 739]; p Conclusion Our investigation shows that the DePuy INHANCE™ modular anatomic convertible glenoid PE liner and platform baseplate demonstrates favorable biomechanical performance against micromotion and polyethylene dissociation. These results should be considered when evaluating the current and future role of platform baseplates in aTSA.

title: Network meta-analysis of the efficacy of different exercise therapies in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
authors: Diao K, Zhang T, Wang H, Wang Y, Pan Y.
abstract: Background Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a leading cause of disability in the elderly and a growing social burden due to aging and increasing obesity rates. This study aims to investigate the effects of different exercise modalities on pain, physical function, stiffness, and muscle strength in patients with KOA. Methods A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and EBSCO databases for randomized controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of exercise therapy for KOA from January 2000 to 16 August 2025, followed by an updated search through 28 March 2026. No additional eligible studies were identified in the updated search. In total, 51 studies involving 3,045 participants (71.7% female; study-group mean ages ranged from 50.3 to 74.4 years) were included. The studies were conducted in 14 countries across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and Oceania. A network meta-analysis was performed using Stata 16.0. This systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251177632). Results The results showed that mind-body exercise was the most effective in reducing pain (standardized mean differences (SMD) = -1.13, 95% confidence interval (CI) [-1.47 to -0.79], P P P P P Conclusion Mind-body exercise appeared to be the most favorable option for reducing pain and stiffness in patients with knee osteoarthritis, whereas strength training appeared to be the most beneficial for improving muscle strength. These findings may help inform individualized exercise prescription, but should be interpreted cautiously given the uncertainty and limitations of the available evidence.

title: Multimodal Imaging for Cervical Aggressive Fibromatosis: Diagnosis and Individualized Interventional Therapy.
authors: Wang Y, Hu Y, Han M, Yang S.
abstract: Multimodal imaging, including contrast-enhanced ultrasound, is crucial for characterizing cervical aggressive fibromatosis. When surgery poses a high risk, imaging findings can support alternative strategies like CT-guided brachytherapy, offering a safe and effective treatment option for this locally invasive tumor.

title: Multifocal isolated bone involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis in a 6-week-old infant.
authors: Ploeger C, Firouzabadi FD, Frank M, Chorney M, Contractor S, Ohene-Baah NY.
abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare clonal disorder of dendritic cells with a wide spectrum of clinical and radiologic manifestations. LCH occurs most frequently in infants often manifesting in multisystem or cutaneous disease. Consequently, the isolated multifocal bone involvement seen in this case is an unusual presentation for early infancy. We report a case of a 6-week-old female infant presenting with feeding intolerance and decreased use of the right upper extremity, found to have multifocal lytic skeletal lesions involving the humerus, ribs, calvarium, spine, pelvis, and long bones without clinical or imaging evidence of skin, hepatic, splenic, pulmonary, thymic, gastrointestinal, or central nervous system involvement. Diagnosis was established via CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of a proximal humeral lesion, which confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis. This case highlights the imaging features of multifocal osseous LCH in early infancy and demonstrates the safety and diagnostic utility of image-guided long bone biopsy in this vulnerable population. Early recognition and tissue confirmation are essential to avoid misdiagnosis and guide appropriate patient management.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals new mechanistic insights underlying the osteoanabolic effects of short chain fructooligosaccharide.
authors: Adedigba P, Grez-Capdeville M, Knotts TA, Peng G, Cooper B, O'Connell TM, Prideaux M, Lucas EA, Smith BJ.
abstract: Despite evidence that short chain fructooligosaccharide (FOS) improves bone mass and intestinal mineral absorption, the mechanism driving these effects remains uncertain. This study investigated how FOS modulates molecular and cellular pathways in bone through alterations in the gut microbiota and metabolome. Eight-week-old C57BL/6 female mice were fed a control or FOS-supplemented diet (10%) for 4 weeks. Bone histomorphometry, femur and bone marrow transcriptomics, cecal content 16S rRNA sequencing, and serum untargeted metabolomics were performed. Mice fed the FOS diet exhibited greater femoral trabecular bone volume and cortical bone thickness and area. FOS increased trabecular and cortical bone formation (i.e., periosteal and endocortical surface), and enhanced mineralization on the trabecular and endocortical surfaces. These changes coincided with increased osteoblasts and osteocytes, while osteoclasts were unchanged. Transcriptomics on the flushed femur revealed enrichment of pathways involving calcium ion homeostasis, PPAR signaling and adipogenesis, while in the bone marrow pathways associated with T-cell modulation and extracellular matrix organization were enriched. FOS altered the gut microbiota, increasing the abundance of taxa associated with fermentation and aromatic compound degradation, and increased serum metabolites (e.g., indole, mevalonate, polyphenol, and fatty acid intermediates). These findings reveal new insights into gut microbial and serum metabolite shifts induced with short-term FOS supplementation accompanying a rapid increase in osteocytes as well as bone formation and mineralization.

title: Multi-modal multi-task internet sentiment recognition model based on mid-to-back fusion strategy.
authors: Wu S, Lin R.
abstract: Previous studies of multimodal sentiment recognition have paid limited attention to the discrepancy between unimodal expression and multimodal perception in sentiment labeling, and to the question of where in the network the modalities should be fused. This paper proposes a multimodal multi-task sentiment recognition model based on a mid-to-back fusion strategy. Text, audio and visual inputs are encoded with the pre-trained BERT, Wav2Vec 2.0 and CLIP models, respectively, and refined by convolutional, recurrent and self-attention layers. Each unimodal branch is trained with its own unimodal sentiment label, so that modality-specific representations are optimized before fusion; the three high-level unimodal representations are then integrated by a residual multi-head self-attention module supervised by the multimodal label, and the four tasks are optimized jointly. On the Chinese CH-SIMS dataset the proposed model achieves a three-class accuracy of 70.14% and a binary accuracy of 75.09%, improving on the strongest published multi-task baseline by 1.1 and 3.4 percentage points, respectively; the binary-accuracy gain is statistically significant, with p < 0.01 in Welch's t-test. Fusion-position ablations show that delaying fusion raises neutral-class accuracy from 28.87% with early fusion to 43.82% with mid-to-back fusion, and the model transfers to the English CMU-MOSI benchmark, on which it reaches a binary accuracy of 86.53%. The model still has room for improvement with respect to dataset diversity, the complexity of real-world applications, non-standard language and cross-cultural sentiment understanding. Overall, the proposed approach improves the effectiveness of multimodal fusion and offers a new perspective for multimodal sentiment recognition.

title: MFMNet: Adaptive tri-layer graph pyramid with cross-scale attention router for synergistic drug prediction.
authors: Wang L, Sun L, Pan J, Shao G, Shi G, Zhang G, Shi Y, Jin L.
abstract: Background and objective Experimental screening of synergistic anticancer drug pairs is time-consuming, while effectively integrating complementary molecular graph representations with cell-line-specific information remains challenging for computational drug-synergy prediction. Methods We developed MFMNet with a Tri-Layer Graph Pyramid (TGP) comprising GCN, GIN, and GAT branches for extracting complementary molecular graph representations. A Cross-Scale Attention Router (CSAR), implemented as an adaptive feature-wise gating mechanism, integrates the graph representations before they are combined with drug embeddings and cell-line transcriptomic features for synergistic drug-pair prediction. Results In the initial five-fold cross-validation analysis, MFMNet achieved a mean five-fold AUROC of 0.9301 ± 0.0036. Under the stricter fold-matched evaluation protocol, the full MFMNet backbone achieved an AUROC of 0.9227 ± 0.0055 and a PR-AUC of 0.9127 ± 0.0084, with statistically significant improvements over XGBoost, DeepDDS-GCN, and DeepDDS-GAT after Holm correction. Conclusions MFMNet provides a computational framework for synergistic drug-pair prediction by integrating complementary molecular graph representations with drug and cell-line features. The results support its use for computational prioritization of candidate synergistic drug combinations. All reported performance estimates refer to record-level five-fold cross-validation within the O'Neil dataset; generalization to entirely unseen drugs and cell lines requires further study.

title: Lipoma of the floor of the mouth: a case report.
authors: Dani B, Jennani El Boufrahi Z, Boulaadas M.
abstract: Lipoma is a common benign mesenchymal tumor, but its intraoral occurrence is rare, accounting for only 1%-4% of benign oral cavity tumors, with the floor of the mouth being an especially uncommon site. We report the case of a 47-year-old woman presenting with a progressively enlarging swelling of the right floor of the mouth over 6 months, causing functional tongue compression. Cervicofacial computed tomography revealed a well-circumscribed fatty-density lesion measuring 27 × 58 × 48 mm without signs of local aggressiveness. Complete surgical excision was performed under general anesthesia, with an uneventful postoperative course. Histopathological examination confirmed a lipocytic lipoma. This rare entity may pose a diagnostic challenge, especially in large symptomatic lesions. Imaging is essential for preoperative planning, and complete excision remains the treatment of choice. Histopathological confirmation is mandatory to exclude well-differentiated liposarcoma.

title: Intraoperative communication and team coordination during early open-console robotic surgical system implementation: a prospective mixed-methods observational study.
authors: Sadri H, Pezeshki P, Stott B, Huynh H, Zanaty M, Di Palma A, Meskawi M.
abstract: Background Robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) separates the console surgeon from the bedside team, increasing reliance on explicit communication and shared awareness. Open-console platforms may alter this dynamic, but prospective evidence during early implementation is limited. This study examined intraoperative communication, coordination, and contextual barriers and facilitators with a newly implemented open-console robotic system. Methods We conducted a prospective, single-center, convergent mixed-methods observational study of the Hugo RAS at a Canadian hospital from February to March 2026. A surgical robotics implementation specialist observed 20 procedures using a structured checklist covering eight domains. Surgeons, bedside assistants, circulating nurses, and scrub nurses completed 62 post-procedure, case-linked survey forms. Survey responses were summarized descriptively. Field notes were analyzed using framework-based thematic synthesis, and findings from the data sources were integrated. Results Across 62 case-linked survey forms, participants reported high levels of verbal communication effectiveness (mean 4.60/5), instruction clarity (mean 4.55/5), and perceived communication support provided by the open-console configuration (mean 4.81/5). Perceived procedural difficulty (mean 2.06/5) and communication-related stress (mean 1.32/5) were low. Field observations indicated that communication was generally concise and role-specific, with greater communicative demands during high-coordination transitions, teaching, and in unfamiliar room configurations. Ambient noise and overlapping conversations occasionally diminished message clarity. Conclusions Open-console RAS was associated with effective perceived communication between surgeons and bedside staff and low communication-related stress, alongside localized increases in communication demands during non-routine or transition-intensive periods. These findings identify practical targets for staff onboarding and closed-loop communication that merit evaluation in multicenter comparative studies.

title: Intelligent rendering optimization for animated scenes using reinforcement learning and computer vision.
authors: Li X, Dai Q, Jia L.
abstract: Real-time rendering of complex animated scenes is computationally intensive and often struggles to balance visual fidelity and performance in dynamic or densely populated environments, as conventional pipelines lack adaptive resource optimization, leading to reduced frame rates and degraded visual quality. This research proposes an intelligent rendering framework integrating Computer Vision (CV) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) through the Adaptive Seeker-Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (AdapS-Twin D3PG) algorithm. The ATD-12 dataset consists of 10,000 collected animation image triplets designed for video frame interpolation and motion analysis tasks, and is utilized for training and evaluation. To enhance data quality, Savitzky-Golay filtering is applied to smooth motion trajectories while preserving essential temporal patterns, and Min-Max normalization standardizes frame color and intensity values for consistent input representation. Feature extraction using Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) captures structural and shape-based information, enabling the RL agent to identify high-priority regions for selective rendering refinement. The proposed AdapS-Twin D3PG dynamically adjusts rendering parameters, refining critical regions while coarsely processing less significant areas to optimize computational efficiency. Experimental results from the Python-implemented framework demonstrate that the proposed AdapS-Twin D3PG model achieves superior quantitative performance with Accuracy (95.48), Recall (93.72), F1 Score (93.94), and AUC (96.82). The system also delivers enhanced visual reconstruction quality, evidenced by a PSNR of 39.4 dB and a low FID of 13.8, while maintaining an efficient rendering time of 4.2 seconds, thereby confirming its effectiveness in optimizing both visual fidelity and computational efficiency for real-time animated scene rendering.

title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
authors: Wang Z, Yang C, Wang W, Zhang Z, Sun Z, Diao Z.
abstract: Background Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear. Methods We integrated network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, virtual gene perturbation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, external transcriptomic validation, and qRT-PCR to investigate candidate molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid. Results A total of 127 shared candidate targets between pyrethroid insecticides and keloid were identified, mainly enriched in MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and FoxO signaling pathways. Three machine-learning algorithms prioritized VCAM1 and FGFR1. In GSE145725, both genes showed significant differential expression and high dataset-level discriminatory performance. In the integrated external validation cohort generated from GSE90051 and GSE158395, VCAM1 remained significantly upregulated and showed good discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.869), whereas FGFR1 showed weaker external support (AUC = 0.677) without significant differential expression. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported the structural plausibility of selected pyrethroid-target interactions, particularly theta-cypermethrin with VCAM1. Single-cell analysis characterized the cell-type-specific distribution of candidate genes, while virtual gene perturbation suggested a putative VCAM1-SOCS3 regulatory relationship. qRT-PCR further showed that 20 μM cypermethrin exposure for 24 h significantly increased VCAM1 mRNA expression in KEL FIB cells. Conclusion VCAM1 emerged as the most consistently supported candidate linking cypermethrin exposure with keloid-associated molecular alterations, while the predicted VCAM1-SOCS3 relationship requires further mechanistic validation.

title: Implant-Preserving Guided Bone Regeneration for Peri-Implant Bone Loss Associated With Early Peri-Implantitis: A Case Report.
authors: Samantaray RK, Sinha P, Agarwal SK, Sharan J, Devi LB, Basynat SK.
abstract: A 60-year-old man developed localized peri-implant bone loss 2.5 months after implant placement. Surgical debridement was followed by guided bone regeneration using autogenous retromolar bone and a resorbable collagen membrane. At follow-up, satisfactory hard-tissue healing and implant stability were observed, permitting successful prosthetic rehabilitation and maintenance of function.

title: Impact of early versus delayed mobilization after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair in small and medium-sized tears: a prospective randomized study.
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Abdallah MR, Hassan AS, Abdelal M.
abstract: Purpose To compare early versus delayed mobilization following arthroscopic single-row knotless rotator cuff repair for small and medium-sized tears, performed in the beach-chair position without the use of an abduction sling. Methods A prospective randomized study was conducted on 70 patients aged 20-70 years with small and medium-sized full-thickness supraspinatus tears repaired using single-row knotless suture anchors (one or two depending on tear size). Patients were assigned to early mobilization (EPM, n = 35) or delayed mobilization (DPM, n = 35). Outcomes were assessed using range of motion (ROM), pain (VAS), Constant-Murley and UCLA scores, and MRI tendon integrity at 12 months. Results EPM patients showed faster ROM recovery at 3 months (mean 130° vs. 115°; p = 0.02), but one re-tear (2.8%) occurred in this group compared to DPM, where no re-tears occurred. At 12 months, both groups achieved comparable functional and pain outcomes. Conclusion Early mobilization accelerates short-term ROM recovery, whereas both early and delayed protocols result in comparable functional and pain outcomes by 12 months. Given the limited number of retear events and the absence of a prespecified tear size subgroup analysis, no definitive recommendation can be made regarding a differential mobilization strategy according to tear size.

title: Illness perceptions among adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis: A qualitative study informed by the common-sense model of self-regulation.
authors: Zhu D, Wang B, Li Y, Nie X, Yin H, Huang S, Wang Q, Xu R.
abstract: Background Ankylosing spondylitis mainly affects people in early and middle adulthood. This period involves important transitions in education, career, relationships, and family. Illness perceptions play an important role in treatment adherence and disease management. Few qualitative studies have examined how Chinese adults perceive and cope with the disease using a clear theoretical framework. Objective This study aimed to explore illness perceptions among adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis, informed by the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation. Methods This was a qualitative descriptive study conducted in a tertiary hospital in Nanjing, China. Sixteen adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis were recruited through maximum variation purposive sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Results Three themes were identified: fragmentation and biases in illness perceptions; disrupted daily life and recurring emotional burden; and negotiating control between professional support and experiential self-management. Conclusions Illness perceptions among adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis were dynamic and context-dependent, influenced by symptom experiences, causal interpretations, perceived consequences, and ongoing negotiation between professional guidance and experiential self-management. Illness coherence did not necessarily increase with longer disease duration, and no consistent age-related pattern emerged. These findings offer insight into how adults with AS construct and adapt their illness perceptions, which may guide future patient-centered support.

title: Highlights of the Annual Scientific Meeting of the Australasian Musculoskeletal Imaging Group (AMSIG) 2026, Sydney, Australia.
Heterotopic ossification in the abdominal wall after midline incision: a case report.
authors: Han JH, Kang SI, Kim S.
abstract: Heterotopic ossification (HO) of the abdominal wall following a midline incision is a rare postoperative complication characterized by mature bone formation in soft tissue. We report a 70-year-old woman who underwent emergency Hartmann procedure for perforated sigmoid diverticulitis. Four months later, preoperative computed tomography for colostomy reversal incidentally revealed two ossified lesions along the previous surgical wound: a 21-mm inverted V-shaped lesion and a 70-mm inverted J-shaped lesion. Both lesions were completely resected during open stoma reversal, and histopathological examination confirmed mature heterotopic bone. Unlike the reported male predominance, this patient was female. Although the pathogenesis remains uncertain, proposed mechanisms include periosteal implantation, mesenchymal cell differentiation induced by inflammation, and excessive suture-line tension. This case demonstrates that abdominal wall HO can develop rapidly, attain considerable size despite the absence of symptoms, and should be considered in the differential diagnosis of postoperative abdominal wall masses.

title: Hearing assistance technologies and social health among individuals with care and support needs: a scoping review.
authors: Yüceer B, Janning C, Güney S, Wolf-Ostermann K.
abstract: Background Hearing loss can affect communication, social interaction, participation, and the maintenance of social relationships, particularly among individuals who require care or support in everyday life. Hearing assistance technologies (HATs) may facilitate communication, but their relationship with the multiple dimensions of social health remains insufficiently understood. A multidimensional social-health framework encompassing Capacity, Independence, Social Participation, Structure, Function, and Appraisal provides a basis for examining these relationships beyond individual hearing outcomes. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on HATs in relation to social health among individuals with care and support needs. Methods This scoping review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley and further refined by Levac. PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Ovid MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched. Studies were eligible if they included individuals aged ≥ 18 years with care and support needs and examined HATs in relation to findings relevant to social health. Data were charted and synthesised descriptively, and findings were organised according to the six domains of the multidimensional social-health framework, comprising Capacity, Independence, Social Participation, Structure, Function, and Appraisal. Results The searches identified 1,145 records, of which 21 studies met the inclusion criteria. The included samples were predominantly older. Findings were most frequently mapped to the Appraisal and Social Participation domains, whereas Structure and Function were comparatively underrepresented. Intervention findings included improvements in communication-related outcomes and reductions in hearing-related participation restrictions, whereas findings for loneliness, relationship satisfaction, social-network characteristics, and broader social engagement were less consistent. Qualitative findings highlighted stigma and perceived social judgement, with the social acceptability of hearing technologies also described in relation to everyday interaction and technology use. Conclusions Evidence on HATs in relation to social health among individuals with care and support needs remains heterogeneous and uneven across social-health domains. Limited attention to the structural and functional dimensions of social relationships highlights the need for more comprehensive assessment of social health in hearing-care research. Future studies should adopt longitudinal, network-sensitive, and culturally responsive approaches and consider the interpersonal, environmental, and care contexts in which HATs are used.

title: HIF-1α expression is associated to cell proliferation and ECM production in temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis.
authors: Liu L, Shi X, Li X, Lin Y, Yang H, Zhang J, Yang C.
abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJOA) is a complex joint disorder characterized by progressive degradation of the cartilage matrix and apoptosis of chondrocytes; however, hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) serves a positive role in maintaining the stability of the articular cartilage matrix. Therefore, the present study aimed to determine the expression levels of HIF-1α in the cartilage tissue of rats with TMJOA, and to explore its association with the proliferation of chondrocytes and the formation of cartilage matrix. Experimental animals were subjected to occlusal interference treatment for periods ranging from 2 to 10 weeks to induce osteoarthritis (OA)-like pathological changes. Subsequently, various histochemical methods were employed to systematically evaluate the degree of articular cartilage damage in the TMJOA rat model. The expression levels of HIF-1α, proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), collagen type II (COLII) and aggrecan in cartilage tissues of rats with OA were analyzed using immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence techniques. Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to quantify the expression levels of HIF-1α, PCNA, Aggrecan and COLII in primary chondrocytes under hypoxic conditions (1% O2). EdU was used to assess the chondrocyte proliferation. From week 4 onward, a reduction in HIF-1α expression levels were detected in the lesioned cartilage of the TMJOA rats. Furthermore, the percentage of HIF-1α-positive chondrocytes was found to be significantly negatively associated with the OA score. This study demonstrated that the expression pattern of HIF-1α was consistent with cell proliferation and extracellular matrix production, and was negatively correlated with the severity of condylar cartilage degeneration.

title: Glenohumeral radial mismatch and revision for aseptic loosening after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty: a Dutch Arthroplasty Register study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Boulidam D, Macken AA, Buijze GA, Spekenbrink-Spooren A, Sierevelt IS, Eygendaal D, van Noort A, van den Bekerom MPJ.
abstract: Background Aseptic glenoid loosening remains a leading cause of revision after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA). Glenohumeral radial mismatch is considered an important biomechanical factor influencing glenoid component survival, with smaller mismatches associated with radiolucent lines, an early sign of implant loosening. However, its effect on implant survival remains unclear. Therefore, the aim of this study is to evaluate the association between glenohumeral radial mismatch and revision for aseptic glenoid loosening in patients undergoing aTSA. Methods All primary aTSAs performed between 2014 and 2024 and registered in the Dutch Arthroplasty Register were included. Patients were eligible if they had a Walch A glenoid (A1 or A2) and received a fully cemented all-polyethylene glenoid component. Cases with components for which the radius could not be identified were excluded. Patients were divided into a low radial mismatch group ( Results A total of 1,683 shoulders were included (909 low mismatch, 774 high mismatch). Median follow-up was 5.3 years (IQR 2.8-7.7), and median radial mismatch was 4.8 mm (IQR 3.0-6.2). Overall, 88 (5%) revisions were recorded, including 26 (1.5%) for aseptic glenoid loosening and 17 (1%) for instability. At 6 years, estimated revision-free survival in the low and high radial mismatch groups was 98.5% and 98.2% for aseptic loosening. Univariable Cox regression showed no statistically significant association between radial mismatch and aseptic loosening or overall revision, whereas high mismatch was associated with a higher hazard of revision for instability (HR 3.86, 95% CI 1.26- 11.83; p = 0.037). Conclusion In this registry-based cohort of patients with Walch A glenoids treated with fully cemented all-polyethylene glenoid components, glenohumeral radial mismatch was not associated with revision for aseptic glenoid loosening or overall revision. An association between higher radial mismatch and revision for instability was observed; however, given the low number of events, this finding should be interpreted with caution. Future studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Functional outcomes over 24 months after arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tendon tears in a multicentre study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Audigé L, Croci E, Trong MLD, Flury M, Jost B, Cunningham G, Benninger E, Baum C, Müller AM.
abstract: Background Isolated subscapularis tears are rare, and it is currently unclear how the tear size relates to the postoperative outcomes after arthroscopic repair. This study aimed to evaluate clinical- and patient-reported outcomes, as well as adverse events of arthroscopically treated isolated subscapularis tears based on the tear extent over 24 months. Methods Across 19 orthopaedic centres, 69 patients undergoing primary arthroscopic repair for isolated subscapularis tears were prospectively recruited between June 2020 and November 2021. Medical imaging examinations were conducted at baseline and at 12 months. Clinical- and patient-reported outcomes were obtained at baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months. Adverse events within 24 months were documented. Patients were grouped into partial tears (n = 14), full-thickness tears of the superior half (n = 35) or complete full-thickness tears (n = 20) of the subscapularis. All outcomes were compared using generalised linear mixed models adjusted for baseline values, age, sex, American Society of Anaesthesiologists classification, tear aetiology, and steroid infiltrations. Results Improvements in all outcome scores were observed after surgery. No group differences were observed in the ranges of motion in flexion, abduction and external rotation (P≥0.634). The partial tear group had a higher pain level than both full-thickness groups at 12 months (P≤0.005). Abduction strength, Constant Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, Subjective Shoulder Value and EQ-5D-5L showed positive changes within 12- or 24-month follow-ups, with no group differences (P≥0.089). The risk of at least a symptomatic adverse event of any severity level affecting the operated shoulder and arm was highest for patients with partial tears (50%) and lowest for patients with complete full-thickness tears (25%). The most frequent occurrences were persistent or worsening pain, stiffness, and recurrent defects. Overall, 62% of patients with partial tears, 97% of patients with superior full-thickness tears and 77% of patients with complete full-thickness tears were satisfied at 24 months. Conclusion Arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tears leads to significant and sustained improvements in clinical and patient-reported outcomes over 24 months, regardless of tear extent. However, patients with partial tears demonstrated greater residual pain and fewer patients reported satisfaction compared with those with full-thickness tears. These findings may reflect differences in patient characteristics and surgical treatment choices. Further studies are needed to determine the suitability and efficacy of surgical treatments for isolated subscapularis partial tears. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison, Prognosis Study.

title: Fragility fractures: An increasing issue in the ageing population worldwide.
authors: Ruggieri P, Pala E, Giannini S, Sergi G, Arcidiacono GP, Angelini A, Trovarelli G.

title: Finger Lacerations Are Highly Prevalent Among Shoulder Surgeons, and No Widely Effective Preventive Measures Are Available.
authors: Do A, Lazaridou A, Scheibel M.
abstract: Purpose To explore factors associated with the occurrence of finger lacerations during arthroscopic and open knot-tying techniques in shoulder surgery. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted at an international shoulder surgery course in March 2024. Attending shoulder surgeons performing arthroscopic and open shoulder surgeries were asked to participate in a survey on site using a structured questionnaire to explore factors associated with the occurrence and anatomical distribution of skin lacerations during arthroscopic and open knot-tying techniques. Demographic, procedural, and intraoperative variables were collected and compared between techniques. Linear and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of laceration occurrence and severity. Results A total of 100 surgeons were invited to participate, all of whom completed the survey (response rate: 100%). Eighty-nine percent of respondents reported having experienced finger lacerations either currently or in the past, with 79% still affected at the time of the survey. The remaining 10% had adopted effective preventive measures: 3% modified their knot-tying technique, 2% wrapped tape around the affected fingers, and 5% developed hyperkeratosis as a protective adaptation. Among those affected, lacerations were reported to occur always in 20%, often in 42%, sometimes in 22%, and rarely in 16% of arthroscopic cases. The distal interphalangeal joints of the index and little fingers were most commonly involved, with the index finger affected in 71%, the little finger in 30%, and 18% reporting lesions on both fingers. Rotator cuff reconstruction was the procedure most frequently associated with laceration occurrence; however, no significant correlation was found between laceration frequency and the number of reconstructions performed per year ( r = 0.091, P = .371). Similarly, no association was observed between handedness and the affected side, with 43% reporting bilateral involvement ( χ 2 = 2.464, P = .292). Hyperkeratosis was observed in 54.4% of affected surgeons, suggesting a potential adaptive response to repetitive skin trauma. Conclusions Finger lacerations are a common problem among shoulder surgeons. Seventy-nine percent of respondents reported being regularly affected, particularly at the distal interphalangeal joint of the index and little fingers. Surgeons performing rotator cuff repairs showed a significantly higher incidence of finger lacerations at present. Clinical relevance Finger lacerations and glove microlesions during knot tying are common among shoulder surgeons and may compromise barrier integrity. The lack of widely effective preventive measures underscores the need for improved strategies to protect both surgeons and patients.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
authors: Zhong YL, Li SG, Yue ZJ, He ZT, Tan Q, Chen JQ, Zheng JH.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo = 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority.
