Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

title: Evaluation of articular cartilage of the glenohumeral joint in patients with labral tears using T2 mapping technique on MRI: Is there a correlation between cartilage T2 values and labral tear location or frequency of shoulder dislocation?
authors: Kim AY, Antony CD, Choi JA, Lee SA.
abstract: Objectives The purpose of this study was to evaluate glenohumeral cartilage using T2 mapping and to investigate whether cartilage T2 values were associated with labral tear location and frequency of shoulder dislocation. Methods In this prospective study, 30 shoulder MRIs with T2 mapping were performed at a 3.0 T scanner. T2 values of cartilage were measured twice by two radiologists after dividing the glenoid and humeral side into 9 areas as: anterosuperior, anterior_middle, anteroinferior, central_superior, central_middle, central_inferior, posterosuperior, posterior_middle, posteroinferior. Intra- and interobserver agreements were calculated using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Labral tears were classified according to location into following groups: superior labral tear group (10-2 o'clock), anterior labral tear group (2-6 o'clock), posterior labral tear group (6-10 o'clock), inferior labral tear group (5-7 o'clock), MDI group (multidirectional instability, involving 3 quadrants or more). Correlations were analyzed using independent student T and ANOVA tests. Results Overall interobserver agreement was moderate (glenoid, 0.612; humeral head, 0.530), whereas intraobserver agreement was good (glenoid, 0.763; humeral head, 0.866). Glenoid cartilage T2 values differed significantly between tear-location groups in the anterosuperior and posteroinferior regions. Cartilage T2 values were not significantly associated with the frequency of shoulder dislocation. Conclusion Interobserver agreement was moderate overall but varied by region, whereas intraobserver agreement was good. Labral tear location was associated with significant differences in T2 values in the anterosuperior and posteroinferior glenoid cartilage regions. No significant association was observed between cartilage T2 values and the frequency of shoulder dislocation.

title: Evaluating the Quality and Accessibility of Integrated Vascular Surgery Residency Program Websites for Prospective Applicants.
authors: Yu J, Cui CL, Gilmore BF, Heidt NA, Kim Y.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic prompted a shift to virtual residency interviews, although approximately half of integrated vascular surgery residency (VSR) programs have since returned to an in-person format. Amidst this evolving landscape, program websites have remained an invaluable resource for candidates to learn about VSR programs. In this study, we examined whether VSR program websites provide adequate and current information for residency candidates. Methods A list of all active VSR programs was obtained from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) website. Each program's website was reviewed in November 2025, and data were collected regarding program structure, faculty and current resident rosters, application requirements, and publicly available formal policies. Results Of the 81 active programs, 80 (98.8%) had a formal residency program website. Information on residency program structure was reported in the majority of websites, including mission statement (91.4%), rotation and curriculum data (65.4%), rotating sites (61.7%), educational conferences (64.2%), and resident research experience (56.8%). Only ten programs (12.3%) reported resident operative volumes. Information regarding the residency program director (PD; 91.4%), program coordinator (PC; 92.6%), teaching faculty (92.6%), and current residents (81.5%) was available in most websites. However, with the exception of the PC (91.4%), contact information for the PD (40.7%), faculty (29.6%), and residents (13.6%) was not easily accessible. The majority of websites had a "how to apply" section (86.4%), but relatively few reported their interview dates (30.9%). Resident experience videos were available in less than half of websites (39.5%). Data on salary (53.1%), resident benefits (53.1%), vacation policies (27.2%), and academic conference policies (28.4%) were also inconsistently reported. Conclusions Residency program websites remain a central resource for applicants, particularly in the current era of virtual and hybrid interview formats. In this study, we found substantial variability in the information presented across VSR program websites, with a notable lack of accessible contact information for program leadership, faculty, and residents. Enhancing website content and transparency may better support applicants as they evaluate programs and prepare for the residency application process.

title: Endoscopic orbital transposition with three-dimensional flap reconstruction for a laterally located frontal sinus cyst: how I do it.
authors: Kano K, Yamada S, Mori T, Masuda M, Sugawara K, Misawa K.
abstract: Access to far-lateral frontal sinus lesions remains challenging, even after a Draf III procedure. We describe an endoscopic orbital transposition approach combined with 3D vascularized flap reconstruction for a laterally located frontal sinus cyst. After completion of the Draf III procedure, the orbit was mobilized laterally to access the cyst. Exposed bone surfaces were reconstructed using three vascularized flaps: a posterior pedicled lamina papyracea flap, a Superior Lateral Anterior Pedicled flap, and bilateral septoturbinal flaps. This technique provides direct access to far-lateral frontal sinus lesions while enabling broad vascularized coverage of exposed bone surfaces and may help reduce postoperative restenosis.

title: En Bloc Sutureless Patch Repair of the Inferior Vena Cava and Right Hepatic Vein in a Patient with Invasive Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report.
authors: Amakura K, Yajima S, Yoshioka D, Kawashima A, Hasegawa S, Kawamura T, Kawamura A, Misumi Y, Miyagawa S.
abstract: Introduction In patients with invasive renal cell carcinoma, extensive involvement of the inferior vena cava (IVC) and right hepatic vein presents a unique surgical challenge. We report a case of a man with invasive renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney who developed massive hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock due to right hepatic vein laceration during surgery, which necessitated an emergency repair procedure. This procedure was effective and might be useful in other patients with invasive renal cell carcinoma with IVC and hepatic vein involvement. Case presentation A 72-year-old man presented with severe acute left-sided epigastric pain. Plain abdominal CT and MRI revealed an enlarged left kidney with a low-density mass extending from the left renal vein to the IVC. Renal biopsy revealed renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney. The patient was treated with neoadjuvant therapy and underwent surgery. A median laparotomy was performed to expose and dissect the IVC. During the Kocher maneuver to mobilize the liver, the right hepatic vein was lacerated because the venous wall had been weakened by tumor thrombus. This led to massive hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock, necessitating an emergency repair procedure. The IVC defect and transected right hepatic vein were reconstructed en bloc using an autologous pericardial patch. The upper half of the patch was sutured directly to the liver parenchyma (not to the right hepatic vein), whereas the lower half was attached to the residual IVC wall. After vascular reconstruction, the left kidney and associated renal veins were excised. Postoperative contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed patent blood flow from the right hepatic vein through the patch to the IVC. Pre-existing small pulmonary nodules subsequently increased in size and were considered likely metastatic lesions. The patient died of respiratory failure on POD 120. Conclusions Sutureless patch repair offers an alternative to conventional grafting methods and may be useful in cases of invasive carcinoma that require combined reconstruction of the hepatic veins and IVC.

title: Effects of crude oil on the somatic and immune development of juvenile threespine stickleback.
authors: Ireland KS, Milligan-McClellan KC.
abstract: Aquatic oil spills have profound effects on surrounding ecosystems, prompting significant investments in oil spill response efforts to remove oil from the environment as quickly as possible. Oil has immunotoxic effects and may be particularly harmful to larval and juvenile fish as it can cause a number of developmental defects and stunted growth. In spite of significant efforts to clean up oil, it is unclear whether larval and juvenile fish can recover from the effects of oil, and no work has been published on the effect crude oil has on developing threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) fish. Threespine stickleback are a ubiquitous sentinel species in the Northern Hemisphere and an important food source for many larger, economically valuable fish. As fish with fully marine, anadromous, and freshwater populations, stickleback are exposed to oil in a variety of aquatic environments. We aimed to understand fish recovery following removal of crude oil. Stickleback were exposed to Alaska North Slope crude oil and then were moved to water without crude oil for two weeks of recovery. Measurements of growth and immunity were taken before and after the recovery period. We found that crude oil effected different developmental pathways independently. Crude oil significantly impacted snout-vent length and eye diameter, but not swim bladder length or area, nor expression of IL1B and TNF genes. Stickleback fish were unable to recover from exposure after being transferred to clean water for two-weeks. This is the first study to examine the effect crude oil has on early stages of stickleback development and potential recovery. The results suggest larval and juvenile stickleback exposed to crude oil need longer than two-weeks to recover if they are able to recover at all.

title: Effect of pelvic floor reconstruction on postoperative urinary continence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a meta-analysis.
authors: Wu X, Lu H, Huang W, Shao Z.
abstract: Urinary incontinence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) remains a common and burdensome complication. Whether pelvic floor reconstruction (PR) helps restore continence is still debated. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to October 8, 2026, for controlled studies comparing PR with no reconstruction (nPR) during RARP. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Begg's, and Egger's tests. The certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. Twenty-two studies (5 RCTs and 17 non-RCTs) with 6425 patients (4134 PR and 2291 nPR) were included. At postoperative weeks 1, 2, 4, 12, 24, and 52, continence rates were significantly higher in the PR group than in the nPR group (pooled ORs ranged from 2.58 at 24 weeks to 2.82 at 12 weeks; all 95% CIs excluded 1). Significant heterogeneity was found at all time points except week 2 (I² = 74.3%-87.5%); the 2-week analysis showed minimal heterogeneity (I² = 0.0%). No obvious publication bias was detected. The GRADE assessment indicated that the certainty of evidence was moderate at 2 weeks and low at all other time points, primarily due to the predominance of observational studies and high heterogeneity. Pelvic floor reconstruction during RARP may improve early urinary continence recovery. However, given the low certainty of evidence, considerable heterogeneity, and the predominance of observational data, the magnitude and durability of this benefit remain uncertain. PR should be considered a reasonable option rather than a standardized intraoperative adjunct. Further high-quality, multicenter RCTs with uniform endpoints are warranted.

title: Ecological insights and societal impacts: Unveiling the relationship between outdoor sports and mental well-being among college students.
authors: Chen S.
abstract: This study develops and empirically validates a College Sports Ecological Risk Assessment (CSERA) model grounded in Bronfenbrenner's multi-level social ecosystem theory to address the prevalent unidimensional limitations of conventional sports risk evaluation instruments. The proposed CSERA model encompasses four standardized risk domains-teaching risk, student personal risk, competition risk, and sports equipment risk-systematically mapped onto the micro-, meso-, and macro-system nested ecological layers of campus sports systems. Drawing on stratified probability-proportional-to-size (PPS) cluster survey data from 330 full-time undergraduates across 10 universities in Shanghai, this study adopts confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), kernel density estimation, and the Ti algorithm to test three predefined hypotheses concerning risk perception heterogeneity, the mediating role of mental well-being, and model predictive efficacy. Consistent with the results of multi-group ANOVA and bootstrap mediation analyses, teaching risk (42%) and student personal risk (35%) serve as dominant negative correlates of college outdoor sports participation. Distinct grade-based heterogeneity is identified in risk perception: freshmen demonstrate greater susceptibility to micro-system personal sports risk, whereas upper-grade students prioritize meso-system teaching risk concerns. Mental well-being exerts a statistically robust partial mediating effect on the focal association (indirect effect = 0.23, 95% CI [0.15, 0.31], 5000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples). Cross-model MSE comparison results suggest that the CSERA model (MSE = 0.02) achieves substantially better predictive performance than hierarchical regression, risk matrix, and BP neural network models (MSE = 0.08), with its empirical stability validated via three complementary robustness tests. All observed associations are correlational given the cross-sectional self-reported design. These findings are based on undergraduates from resource-sufficient universities in Shanghai and may not be directly generalizable to institutions with limited sports infrastructure or other geographic regions. This study offers a replicable quantitative assessment tool for campus sports risk governance and provides tentative directional references for grade-differentiated physical education design that may inform campus sports safety management considerations.

title: Does the Timing of Surgical Debridement Affect Outcomes in Septic Arthritis of the Native Hip and Knee? A Propensity-weighted Analysis.
authors: Randall ZD, Barber HF, McAndrew CM, Berkes MB.
abstract: Background Septic arthritis of the native hip and knee can cause irreversible cartilage damage and systemic illness. Because operative debridement provides source control, delaying it may permit infection to progress, potentially increasing the need for repeat surgery and the risk of death; however, evidence examining these associations remains limited. Questions/purposes Is delayed debridement associated with increased risk of (1) repeat debridement or (2) 1-year mortality in septic arthritis of the native hip and/or knee? Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Florida State Inpatient Database, a statewide, all-payer database that records procedures by hospital day and includes longitudinal patient identifiers. Between October 2015 and December 2022, we identified 3587 adult admissions involving septic arthritis of the native hip (n = 1014) or knee (n = 2573) treated with surgical debridement. We excluded 1% (42 of 3587) of admitted patients in whom the first debridement occurred after hospital day 10, leaving 99% (3545 of 3587) for analysis (hip n = 1001; knee n = 2544). No included outcome or covariate data were missing. In the screened hip and knee cohorts, the mean ± SD ages were 55 ± 17 years and 60 ± 16 years, respectively, and 46% (462 of 1014) and 34% (879 of 2573) were female. Debridement occurred on hospital days 0 to 1 in 51% (506 of 1001) of hip admissions and 59% (1510 of 2544) of knee admissions; the remaining 49% (495 of 1001) and 41% (1034 of 2544), respectively, underwent debridement on day 2 or later. Stabilized inverse probability-of-treatment weighting was used to balance measured baseline covariates. Weighted log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Among patients with septic knee arthritis, debridement on day 2 or later was associated with a higher risk of repeat debridement than debridement on days 0 to 1 (13% [133 of 1034] versus 5% [72 of 1510], adjusted RR 2.40 [95% CI 1.81 to 3.19]; p Conclusion Surgeons should prioritize prompt debridement of septic knee arthritis, and hospitals should implement coordinated pathways to avoid preventable delays. No timing-specific recommendation can be made for septic hip arthritis based on our findings. Larger multicenter studies with granular data on presentation, diagnostic aspiration, antibiotic administration, and debridement are needed to clarify whether debridement timing influences outcomes in septic hip arthritis and to distinguish preventable delays from those related to diagnostic uncertainty or the management of medical comorbidities. Level of evidence Level III, therapeutic study.

title: Distal Humerus Nonunion Following Failed Internal Fixation: How do the Outcomes of Internal Fixation and Total Elbow Arthroplasty Compare?
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Nieboer M, Yu K, Tangtiphaiboontana J, Barlow J, Morrey M, Sanchez-Sotelo J, O'Driscoll S.
abstract: Background Distal humerus nonunions are difficult to treat. The supracondylar ostectomy and shortening (S.O.S.) technique, which combines humeral shortening, parallel plating, and bone grafting, maximizes the success of internal fixation. The purpose of this study was to compare the outcomes of the S.O.S. technique with the outcomes of total elbow arthroplasty (TEA) for distal humerus nonunions. Materials and methods This retrospective review identified 25 distal humerus nonunions treated with the S.O.S. procedure and 45 TEA's performed specifically for distal humerus nonunion at a single institution between 1995 and 2019. All elbows had undergone at least 1 prior fixation attempt. The S.O.S. cohort had a younger mean age and less common intra-articular nonunion compared to the TEA cohort. Sex, mean number of prior surgeries, history of open fracture, and history of infection were similar between groups. Outcomes included complications, reoperations, range of motion, and Mayo Elbow Performance Scores (MEPS). Results In the SOS cohort, 2 elbows were lost to follow-up, 21 elbows achieved union, and 2 elbows failed to heal and subsequently underwent conversion to a TEA. Complications occurred in 9 elbows (36%) following S.O.S. compared to 18 elbows (40%) following TEA (OR 0.8, p=0.7). The rates of all-cause reoperation were 48% (12 elbows) after S.O.S vs 27% (12) after TEA (OR 2.5, p=0.08). The S.O.S. cohort had a 100° mean flexion-extension arc compared to 115° for TEA (p=0.06) with similar mean pronation-supination arcs (S.O.S. 155° vs TEA 145°, p=0.2). MEPS scores were similar between groups (S.O.S 79 points, TEA 82 points, p=0.6). When stratifying by location of nonunion, elbows with intra-articular nonunion undergoing S.O.S had a 75% reoperation rate compared to 35% for extra-articular nonunions (OR 5.5, p=0.08). Intra-articular nonunions achieved higher MEPS with TEA compared to S.O.S. (85 vs. 51 points, p Conclusion Despite achieving a high union rate, the S.O.S. procedure presented similar results compared to TEA in terms of MEPS, motion, complications, and reoperations. Elbows with an intra-articular nonunion had better outcomes with TEA while elbows with an extra-articular nonunion fared better with the S.O.S. Procedure

title: Diagnostic Laparoscopy Revealed an Occult Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm Presenting as Pseudomyxoma Peritonei.
authors: Iijima M, Nishikawa S, Suzuki T, Shiraishi K, Kashiwazaki K, Sasaki A, Uchida H.
abstract: Introduction Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) is a rare clinical condition that most commonly arises from low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (LAMNs). However, preoperative identification of the appendiceal primary lesion may be challenging when characteristic appendiceal abnormalities are absent on imaging studies. We report a rare case of PMP caused by a radiologically occult LAMN that was initially suspected to represent peritoneal carcinomatosis. Case presentation A 74-year-old woman with no abdominal symptoms was referred to our hospital after a pelvic mass in the pouch of Douglas was incidentally detected during a preoperative evaluation for orthopedic surgery. Serum cancer antigen 125 was mildly elevated (37.2 U/mL), whereas carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels were within normal limits. CT and MRI demonstrated peritoneal lesions suggestive of peritoneal dissemination; however, no appendiceal abnormality was identified. Diagnostic laparoscopy was performed to obtain a definitive diagnosis. Intraoperatively, mucinous deposits were observed within the peritoneal cavity, and an appendiceal fistulous opening was identified, suggesting an appendiceal origin. The patient subsequently underwent an appendectomy, and histopathological examination revealed a LAMN. Conclusions This case highlights the diagnostic limitations of preoperative imaging in patients with occult appendiceal neoplasms and demonstrates the value of diagnostic laparoscopy in establishing an accurate diagnosis and guiding appropriate management.

title: Comparative Study of Myocutaneous Latissimus Dorsi Flap Breast Reconstruction With Implant Versus Lipofilling: Complication Rates and Risk Factors.
authors: Almeida AP, Oliveira VM, Paulinelli RR, Bagnoli F, Rinaldi JF, Brenelli FP, Filho IC, Miranda TR.

title: Combined Arthroscopic Anterior Cruciate Ligament and Oblique Popliteal Ligament Reconstruction of the Knee.
authors: Amouzadeh Omrani F, Sarzaeem MM, Manafi Rasi A, Omidian MM, Alahgholiei A, Dolikhani M, Pourmojarab A.
abstract: The oblique popliteal ligament is the largest ligamentous structure of the posterior knee capsule and serves as a primary restraint to genu recurvatum and a contributor to rotatory stability. This technical note describes an arthroscopic-assisted method for oblique popliteal ligament reconstruction, performed as an isolated procedure or in combination with anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, or multiligament knee reconstructions. Indications include symptomatic post-traumatic genu recurvatum, posterior capsular laxity, recurrent or high-risk anterior cruciate ligament failure associated with hyperextension, persistent posterior or rotational instability, and complex multiligament injuries. The technique uses standardized femoral and tibial tunnels; controlled posterior graft passage through posteromedial, trans-septal, and posterolateral portals; and fixation in slight knee flexion to optimize posterior capsular tension in full extension. The procedure is designed to restore native posterior knee biomechanics while minimizing neurovascular risk. Oblique popliteal ligament reconstruction may represent a valuable adjunct in managing selected cases of knee instability characterized by hyperextension and posterior capsular deficiency.

title: Co-designing a post-discharge intervention to improve mobility recovery among patients with lower limb fractures using human-centered design in greater Kampala, Uganda.
authors: Zziwa S, Mwaka ES, Zia N, Buregyeya E, Kobusingye O, Nuwaha F.
abstract: Introduction Lower limb fractures are a major cause of functional limitation and require coordinated post-discharge care to support recovery and prevent complications. In low- and middle-income countries, including Uganda, continuity of care after discharge is often limited by health system constraints, socioeconomic barriers, and community barriers. This study aimed to co-design a post-discharge intervention to improve recovery among patients with lower limb fractures in Greater Kampala, Uganda, using a Human-Centered Design (HCD) approach. Methods A qualitative exploratory study guided by the HCD participatory and iterative framework was conducted between July and December 2025. Stakeholders including healthcare providers, community health workers, patients, and caregivers participated in focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and in-depth interviews to explore their experiences, needs, and challenges related to post-discharge care. Stakeholders subsequently participated in an iterative co-design process to prioritize and refine intervention components. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically using NVivo version 15. Results Several interconnected barriers to post-discharge care were identified, including discontinuity of care after hospital discharge, inadequate discharge information, transportation challenges, community and family influences on treatment decisions, use of traditional bone setters, and health-system limitations. Through the co-design process, stakeholders proposed intervention strategies comprising structured discharge preparation, improved documentation of patient and caregiver contact information, strengthened linkages between health facilities and community health workers, community-based follow-up, and decentralized follow-up services at lower-level health facilities. Conclusions Health-system and community-level factors influenced post-discharge care among patients with lower limb fractures. The study co-designed an integrated facility-community intervention comprising structured discharge processes, strengthened community health worker linkages, and community-based follow-up. Further studies should evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of the intervention in improving post-discharge care and recovery outcomes.

title: CORR Insights®: How Does the Achievement of Minimum Clinically Important Difference, Substantial Clinical Benefit, and Patient Acceptable Symptom State Change Over Time After Periacetabular Osteotomy?
authors: Allen M.

title: Beyond accuracy: is reproducibility the case for robotics in spinal trauma surgery?
authors: Soni A, Vidyadhara S, Iyer RD, Thirugnanam B, Rao SK.
abstract: The accuracy of robot-assisted pedicle screw placement is well established, largely from elective surgery for degenerative disease. Spinal trauma presents a different problem: surface landmarks are distorted, patients are often multiply injured or frail, bone quality is poor, and surgery is frequently performed out of hours by whoever is available. This narrative review proposes that the main potential contribution of robotics in spinal trauma is reproducibility, defined as low variation in the technical result across operators, cases and operating conditions, and examines how far the evidence supports this. Available data suggest that robotic accuracy depends less on surgeon experience and case difficulty than conventional techniques do, but experience still matters, and no study has tested equivalence across surgeons or conditions. Evidence for consistent performance at night or in emergencies is limited. Most of the data come from elective or mixed cohorts with technical endpoints, and reported reductions in blood loss and hospital stay often reflect percutaneous surgery rather than robotic guidance alone. We describe 202 consecutive operations for traumatic, osteoporotic and pathological spinal fractures from a single centre; these data illustrate the range of cases managed within one robotic workflow and do not test the proposal. Registration drift in unstable segments, device failure, radiation, set-up time and cost remain important limitations. The robot does not replace expertise in trauma surgery. It may move part of the expertise that governs screw placement from the individual surgeon to a trained team, but this remains to be demonstrated.

title: Augmented reality for robotic surgery: a feasibility study and comparison of registration algorithms for robot-assisted minimally invasive esophagectomy (RAMIE).
authors: Kuiper GM, van der Duin J, de Jong RLPD, Li Y, van Jaarsveld RC, Badaloni F, Gogoladze K, van Hillegersberg R, Al Khalil Y, Alechina NA, Pluim JPW, Ruurda JP.
abstract: Background Intraoperative augmented reality (AR) guidance could improve surgical orientation in robot-assisted minimally invasive esophagectomy (RAMIE), but reliable image-to-patient registration between preoperative imaging and the intraoperative scene remains a key technical barrier. This feasibility study aimed to explore the potential of AR for RAMIE and to establish a foundation for intraoperative AR guidance by systematically comparing image-to-patient registration methods using real-world clinical data. Methods In this feasibility study, ten consecutive patients undergoing RAMIE were included. Preoperative 3D anatomical models were generated from CT scans using semi-automated segmentation. Intraoperative 3D point clouds were reconstructed from stereoscopic robotic surgical video using stereo-based depth estimation. One manual and six fully automated image-to-patient registration methods were evaluated: Go-ICP, AFWA, CPD, RANSAC, Super4PCS, and FMR. The azygos vein was used as the registration landmark, and registration performance was assessed by qualitative acceptance rate and surface-to-surface distance using the trachea as an independent evaluation structure. Results Manual registration achieved a success rate of 0.80, with a mean surface distance (MSD) of 11.46 mm, Hausdorff distance (HD) of 15.20 mm, and a mean computation time of 22.73 s. Among automated methods, success rates ranged from 0.10 (AFWA, FMR) to 0.40 (Super4PCS). All automated methods completed registration in under 3 s. Surface distances were based on one to eight accepted registrations per method and did not reliably distinguish accepted from rejected registrations. Conclusion This feasibility study shows that image-to-patient registration for augmented reality in RAMIE is technically achievable using real clinical data. Manual registration provides the highest robustness, while fully automated global methods remain limited under intraoperative conditions. Achieved registration accuracies in accepted cases may support basic anatomical orientation but require further development, particularly in deformable registration and intraoperative reconstruction, before reliable intraoperative AR guidance becomes feasible.

title: Associations of plasma biomarkers and amyloid positron emission tomography with regional tau burden in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Sakurai R, Iwabuchi Y, Shimizu A, Bun S, Kubota M, Shimohama S, Tezuka T, Takahata K, Tabuchi H, Seki M, Momota Y, Yamamoto Y, Shikimoto R, Mimura Y, Kurose S, Watanabe M, Takayama T, Hoshino Y, Hoshino T, Suzuki N, Morimoto A, Osumi A, Mimura M, Ito D, Jinzaki M.
abstract: Purpose Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) and plasma biomarkers are clinically established; however, their topographical relationship with regional tau burden remains unclear. We investigated whether amyloid PET and plasma biomarkers are associated with regional tau pathology, measured using second-generation tracer florzolotau ( 18 F) PET, across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study enrolled participants who underwent biomarker assessment between September 2018 and May 2022. The primary outcome was the voxel-wise spatial correlation of florzolotau ( 18 F) standardised uptake value ratio with amyloid PET centiloid and plasma biomarkers, assessed using age- and sex-adjusted whole-brain and region-of-interest (ROI) linear regression analyses, including multivariate models adjusted for amyloid PET centiloid. Results The study included 92 individuals (mean age, 71 [standard deviation, 8.8] years; 46 men), comprising 40 amyloid-negative healthy controls, 10 patients with preclinical AD, 21 with mild cognitive impairment due to AD, and 21 with AD dementia. In initial analyses, regional tau uptake correlated widely with plasma amyloid-beta 42/40 (Aβ42/40) ratio, p-tau, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). However, following multivariate adjustment for global amyloid burden, correlations for Aβ42/40 and GFAP were completely abolished. In contrast, plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, and neurofilament light chain (NfL) maintained significant amyloid-independent correlations with temporoparietal tau uptake, with p-tau217 uniquely retaining robust and extensive associations across the cortex. Conclusion Plasma p-tau217 is strongly associated with the spatial distribution and severity of tau burden independent of global amyloid burden. Measuring plasma p-tau217 holds significant potential for patient stratification and monitoring in the era of disease-modifying therapies. Trial registration UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000032027), registered 31 March 2018, prospectively registered (URL https//center6.umin.ac.jp/cgiopenbin/ctr_e/ctr_view.cgi? recptno=UMIN000032027). Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCTs031180225), prospectively registered (URL https//jrct.niph.go.jp/enlatestdetail/jRCTs031180225).

title: Associations of palmar surface lactic acid with hand scaling and in vitro pathogen inactivation: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Nagano K, Manabe K, Mori I, Okada Y, Shimizu E, Naito S.
abstract: The relationship between palmar surface lactic acid and hand scaling is not well understood. This cross-sectional study examined associations between palmar surface lactic acid, hand scaling, and in vitro anti-pathogenic activity, to generate hypotheses relevant to hand skin condition and pathogen inactivation. In 49 healthy adults, after standardized hand washing and acclimation (20°C, 40% RH), we assessed scaling (visual score), surface lactic acid and stratum corneum ceramides (LC-MS), stratum corneum amino acids (ion-exchange chromatography), skin pH and temperature, and sweat rate. Anti-pathogenic activity of palmar extracts was quantified as log10 reduction against influenza A/H3N2, Escherichia coli NBRC3301, and Staphylococcus aureus NBRC13276. Associations were evaluated using Spearman and partial correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for false discovery rate. Higher lactic acid content was associated with less scaling. Stronger anti-pathogenic activity was also associated with less scaling. Total ceramides and total amino acids were not significantly associated with scaling, whereas several ceramide classes showed negative associations with scaling. In partial correlation models, lactic acid remained independently associated with greater anti-pathogenic activity and with lower scaling (significant in two models and trend-level in one model), and the simple correlation between anti-pathogenic activity and scaling was attenuated after accounting for lactic acid. Lactic acid was also associated with sweat rate across these models (significant in two and trend-level in one). These findings are hypothesis-generating and may inform future mechanistic or interventional studies on lactic acid and palmar skin. Given the cross-sectional design, causality cannot be inferred.

title: Assessment of Interprofessional Trauma Team Performance and Cohesion During a Civil-Military Large-Scale Live Simulation Exercise-A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Sonesson LT, Boffard KD, Bricknell MCM, Mitchell A, Reedy G.
abstract: Background Large-scale civil-military simulation exercises allow interprofessional trauma teams practice leadership, communication, and decision-making under high stress; however, evidence on their contribution to multinational interoperability is limited. We assessed trauma-team performance and cohesion during a multinational live simulation and identified barriers and enablers of interoperability. Materials and methods This prospective cross-sectional observational study was conducted during NATO Vigorous Warrior 2024 across eight Role 2 hospitals in Hungary. Trauma teams (n = 75) from nine nations managed simulated major trauma casualties. Performance was evaluated using the Non-Technical Skills for Surgeons (NOTSS) and Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) frameworks. Four expert assessors made structured observations, and members completed post-scenario self-assessments; team and assessor ratings were compared descriptively. Results Teams rated their overall performance more favorably than assessors across all domains: overall performance was rated excellent by 57% of members versus 25% of assessors, who rated 25% of teams poor or below average. Discrepancies were greatest for leadership clarity, structured communication, and role allocation. Designated leadership, clear chains of command, and organized equipment were associated with better decision-making and task completion. Multinational composition enriched problem-solving but created communication barriers, tensions, and documentation inconsistencies; absent standardized debriefing further limited structured learning. Conclusions Leadership clarity, structured communication, and psychological safety underpin effective multinational trauma teamwork. The perceived-observed performance gap, which may reflect self-assessment leniency and assessor stringency ("hawk-dove" effect), indicates scope for calibration through structured feedback. Standardized training frameworks, harmonized resuscitation protocols, and structured debriefing are needed to improve interoperability and readiness across civil-military trauma systems.

title: Assessing the Impact of Robotic Surgery on General Surgical Resident Training.
authors: Mann DR, Kim S, Willis RE, Donahue CA.
abstract: Objective The prevalence of robotic surgery has grown exponentially since its U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval in 2000. This shift in technology has raised questions about the impact on surgery resident training. There is concern that increased utilization of robotic surgery may result in deficiency in laparoscopic training. The aim of this study was to assess the recent impact of robotic surgery on general surgery resident training. Design We performed a 2-phase study consisting of a retrospective review of institutional operative volume and a cross-sectional survey of current residents and alumni. A retrospective review of operative cases using the electronic medical record from 2015 to 2021 was performed to assess trends in common core minimally invasive surgical procedures. Following this, a quantitative, anonymous survey was sent to former and current general surgery residents who graduated after 2015. Setting A mid-sized, university-affiliated academic general surgery residency program with 6 to 8 categorical residents per year. Participants Operative case data from all minimally invasive general surgery procedures performed at the institution between 2015 and 2021 were analyzed. An anonymous electronic survey was distributed to general surgery alumni (graduation years 2015-2022) and current residents (clinical years 2023-2028 cohort). A total of 75 residents were invited to participate. Results From 2015 to 2021, 1436 robotic and 5504 laparoscopic surgeries were performed. There was a nearly 6-fold increase in robotic surgery over the study period. By 2021, both robotic ventral hernia repair and inguinal hernia repair volumes exceeded laparoscopic equivalents. Survey response rates were completed by 28/33 (85%) former alumni and 23/42 (55%) current residents. Majority of alumni (89.3%) reported good or excellent laparoscopic training experience compared with 39.1% of current residents. Most alumni and current residents reported good or excellent robotic training experience (67.9% and 82.6%, respectively). While nearly all alumni felt robotic surgery did not negatively impact laparoscopic training, 59.1% of current residents reported that robotic surgery has impeded their laparoscopic skill development. Conclusions Robotic surgery is increasing exponentially while laparoscopic surgical procedures have begun to decline. Residents may continue to perceive their laparoscopic experience as less robust than their robotic experience. Given the prolonged learning curve in laparoscopic surgery, it may be necessary to establish specific, defined minimum case requirements for laparoscopic surgery that are independent of robotic surgery.

title: Age-associated alterations in morphometry, intra-cortical canals, lacunar architecture, and mineral density in Type 2 diabetes: Implications for vertebral bone fragility in ZDF rats.
authors: Ali W, Monahan G, McNamara L, Vaughan T.
abstract: Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) is associated with elevated bone fracture risk despite normal or higher bone mineral density (BMD), yet the mechanisms underlying vertebral fragility remain poorly understood. We investigated age-related changes in (1) growth, (2) microarchitecture, (3) microporosity (4) mineralization and (5) mechanical properties of vertebral bone from control and diabetic male ZDF rats at 12-weeks and 46 weeks of age. We report that vertebral growth and microarchitecture were compromised in diabetic rats at late-stage diabetes (46-weeks), as compared to control rats, evident from lower vertebral height and depth, thin cortical bone, and deteriorated trabecular architecture. While control rats maintained stable mineral density distribution with ageing, diabetic rats exhibited increased heterogeneity in cortical and trabecular bone in late-stage diabetes, despite unaffected mean BMD. In central cortical bone, diabetic rats had accelerated loss of intra-cortical canals as compared to controls with an unaffected age-driven lacunae density. In the central trabecular bone, T2D induced enlarged lacunae and altered mineral density distribution at early-stage diabetes (12 weeks), while as disease progressed, lacunae became rounder whilst maintaining lacunar density. Furthermore, age-matched differences in peri-lacunar mineralization were not found between control and diabetic rats. These multifactorial changes may contribute to the reduced failure load of vertebral body in diabetic rats (35% lower than age-matched control rats) at 46-weeks of age. Our findings underscore that fracture risk assessment and therapeutic strategies must look beyond BMD in T2D patients.

title: Adjuvant Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy Without Systemic Therapy After Repeat Local Treatment for Patients With Liver-only Recurrence of Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Outmani L, Filipe WF, Buisman FE, Koerkamp BG, Bolhuis K, van Doorn L, Doornebosch PG, Homs MYV, Kok NF, Kuhlmann KFD, Mostert B, Vermaas M, Verhoef C, Grünhagen DJ.
abstract: Background Approximately 30% of patients develop liver-confined recurrences after local treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), which may be reduced by adjuvant therapy. Hepatic arterial infusion pump (HAIP) chemotherapy delivers high-dose liver-directed chemotherapy. Objective To investigate adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy in patients with resectable liver-confined recurrence after prior local treatment of CRLM. Methods This multicenter, single-arm phase II trial enrolled patients with resectable recurrent CRLM across 3 centers in the Netherlands. Patients with prior or present extrahepatic disease were excluded. Adjuvant HAIP with floxuridine was administered up to 6 cycles. The primary endpoint was hepatic disease-free survival (hDFS) estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with a prespecified efficacy boundary of 36 months. Results Forty-five patients underwent local treatment followed by adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy. Twenty-eight patients(62%) were treated for a first recurrent CRLM, and 17 patients for a second or higher. Twenty-five patients (56%) had ≥3 CRLM. All patients started HAIP chemotherapy, with a median of 6 cycles (interquartile range: 4 to 6). After a median follow-up of 38.7 months (95% CI: 33.0-42.3), the median hDFS was 16.5 months (95% CI: 9.1-25.8). The median progression-free survival was 14.0 months (95% CI: 7.7-23.0), and the 3-year overall survival was 71% (95% CI: 58%-87%). Initial recurrence included the liver in 23 patients (51%). HAIP implantation-related complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3) occurred in 4 patients (9%), and HAIP chemotherapy-related complications (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade ≥3) occurred in 6 patients (13%). Biliary sclerosis occurred in 4 patients; 3 required stent placement. Conclusion Adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy did not achieve the hypothesized hDFS in patients undergoing repeat local treatment for recurrent CRLM.

title: Adalimumab Does Not Improve Clinical Outcomes After Needle Fasciotomy for Dupuytren Contracture: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
authors: Brouwers J, Claessens F, Mergaerts L, Vandezande L, Degreef I.
abstract: Background Dupuytren disease is a fibroproliferative disorder in which tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-driven myofibroblast activity contributes to progressive digital flexion contractures by causing collagen deposition. Needle fasciotomy mechanically releases established collagen cords but does not target the underlying fibroproliferative process. Adalimumab, an anti-TNF agent, has been shown to reduce nodule hardness in early-stage Dupuytren disease, but it remains unknown whether it has additional impact combined with needle fasciotomy in more established contractures. Questions/purposes (1) Does a single perioperative intralesional injection of adalimumab immediately after needle fasciotomy increase the proportion of patients achieving at least 10° improvement in total passive extension deficit (TPED)? (2) Does adalimumab improve the change in TPED at 3 and 12 months? (3) Does adalimumab improve VAS pain and QuickDASH scores at 3 and 12 months? (4) What complications occurred in the adalimumab and placebo groups? Methods We conducted a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled pilot trial at a hand surgery department in a single academic center in adults with Dupuytren disease and an indication for needle fasciotomy. Eligible patients had a Dupuytren diathesis score greater than 4 and a nonfixed compound metacarpophalangeal and/or proximal interphalangeal contracture. Thirty patients were randomized 1:1 to receive a single 40-mg intralesional injection of adalimumab or matching saline placebo immediately after needle fasciotomy. One patient was excluded after randomization, leaving 29 patients for analysis (14 in the adalimumab group and 15 in the placebo). Fisher exact and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for categorical and continuous outcomes, respectively. Results Adalimumab did not improve the proportion of patients achieving at least a 10° improvement in TPED. At 3 months, 86% (12 of 14) of patients in the adalimumab group and 87% (13 of 15) in the placebo group achieved this improvement level, with a between-group difference in proportions of -1% (95% confidence interval [CI] -31% to 29%; p > 0.99). At 12 months, 71% (10 of 14) and 80% (12 of 15) of patients, respectively, achieved the endpoint, with a between-group difference of -9% (95% CI -41% to 24%; p = 0.68). Both groups showed no difference in change in TPED at 3 months; the median (IQR) change was -30° (-60° to -10°) versus -26° (-86° to -14°) at 3 months (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of between-group difference -4°; p = 0.76) and -32° (-60° to -5°) versus -24° (-80° to 5°) at 12 months (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of between-group difference 7°; p = 0.75). Pain and QuickDASH scores improved over time in both groups, with no between-group difference at 3 or 12 months (p > 0.05 for all). One procedure-related complication occurred; no adverse events related to either study injection were reported or observed. Conclusion A single 40-mg intralesional injection of adalimumab added to needle fasciotomy did not improve extension, TPED, pain, or QuickDASH outcomes compared with placebo at 3 or 12 months. Given the absence of detected benefit in this pilot trial, adalimumab should not be used routinely as an adjunct to needle fasciotomy outside a clinical trial. Further studies investigating repeated or higher-dose regimens, treatment at earlier disease stages, and potential combination approaches are needed to better define the therapeutic role of anti-TNF treatment and determine whether it may have a clinical application before its use in routine practice can be considered. Level of evidence Level II, therapeutic study.

title: Acute Hematemesis Leading to the Incidental Diagnosis of Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in an Adolescent: First Case Report From Pakistan.
authors: Hameed M, Mazhar Z, Abedeen ZU, Sohaib HU, Bashir H, Zainab HH, Ghani MZ, Rehman AU.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is exceptionally rare in children and adolescents and typically presents with progressive dysphagia and weight loss. Its occurrence without conventional risk factors may pose a diagnostic challenge. A 16-year-old boy presented with acute hematemesis and no history of dysphagia, odynophagia, or recognized esophageal cancer risk factors. He was undernourished, with a BMI of 17 kg/m 2 and progressive unquantified weight loss. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a deep proximal esophageal ulcer, distal esophageal ulcers, a Mallory-Weiss tear, and gastritis. The latter lesions offered potential explanations for the bleeding, but the atypical proximal ulcer raised suspicion for malignancy, prompting biopsy. Histopathology confirmed moderately differentiated ESCC with high-grade dysplasia. Contrast-enhanced CT showed localized upper thoracic esophageal wall thickening without regional lymphadenopathy or distant metastases, and the disease was staged as T2N0M0. The patient completed three cycles of neoadjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel-based chemotherapy followed by radiotherapy. A repeat endoscopy showed a circumferential raw mucosal area with a superficial erosion in the distal esophagus, while the upper and middle thirds of the esophagus appeared normal; however, esophagectomy was recommended as part of the planned definitive management. This case highlights the incidental discovery of ESCC during evaluation of acute hematemesis in an adolescent without conventional risk factors. Hematemesis with low BMI or unexplained weight loss should prompt careful evaluation for underlying esophageal pathology, even when an apparent benign bleeding source is identified. Early biopsy, appropriate staging, and multidisciplinary management are essential for timely diagnosis and treatment.

title: A unified progressive fusion network with adaptive degradation prompts for multi-weather thermal infrared image restoration.
authors: Xia Y, Mu S.
abstract: Thermal infrared (TIR) image restoration aims to recover clearer and more informative images from inputs degraded by unfavorable weather conditions. Current TIR restoration approaches, however, mainly focus on individual degradation categories, such as rain, snow, or haze, which limits their ability to address different weather degradation categories within a unified framework. To address this challenge, we introduce a TIR unified prompt-guided fusion network, an adaptive degradation-prompting framework designed for unified TIR image restoration under individually occurring rain, snow, or haze degradations. A weather-adaptive dynamic prompt module is first constructed, where a lightweight degradation predictor estimates the probability distribution over predefined degradation categories in TIR images and produces dynamic degradation prompts from a learnable prompt bank. The generated degradation prompts are then provided to the progressive fusion enhancement module and integrated through a prompt fusion strategy to guide feature enhancement and restoration, allowing the network to restore TIR images effectively under diverse weather conditions. To improve restoration quality across the evaluated degradation categories, we further design a joint loss function that combines Charbonnier reconstruction loss, Laplacian edge loss, and degradation-aware auxiliary constraints. Experimental results on the M3FD-based synthetic benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the best overall performance and competitive or superior performance across most evaluated degradation conditions, while effectively suppressing degradations caused by rain, snow, and haze. Moreover, the restored images achieve competitive performance in downstream object detection, further demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework for adverse-weather TIR perception. The source code is available at https://github.com/xia11998/TIR-UPF.

title: A new species of Epicrionops (Amphibia: Gymnophiona: Rhinatrematidae) from Ecuador, with integrative morphological and phylogenetic insights into Ecuadorian Epicrionops Boulenger, 1883 and Amazops Wilkinson, Reynolds & Jacobs, 2021.
authors: Sánchez-Nivicela JC, Cisneros-Heredia DF, Yánez-Muñoz MH, Koch C, Ron SR.
abstract: The Neotropical tailed caecilians of the genera Epicrionops and Amazops (Rhinatrematidae) remain poorly known. Here, we examined their morphology, distribution, and molecular phylogenetic relationships using specimens from Ecuador. Our review of museum collections expands the empirical basis for understanding variation in these genera and reveals broader geographic and morphological diversity than previously recognised. Morphological and µCT-based analyses identified consistent diagnostic differences between Amazops and Epicrionops , particularly in annular counts and cranial bone configurations. We describe a new species of Epicrionops from the montane forests of southeastern Ecuador, characterized by a relatively small body size in fully metamorphosed individuals (174-317 mm); a maxillopalatine enclosing the orbit; a long spatulate posterodorsal process of the squamosal; an articular facet of the quadrate contacting the posterior end of the maxillopalatine but not the squamosal; a retroarticular process of the pseudoangular that is dorsally concave and ventrally convex; frontals with slightly notched anterior and posterior margins and curved lateral edges; and an os basale with a narrowing cultriform process and wavy, rounded margins. The pterygoid is large, attached to the maxillopalatine, and barely contacts the quadrate. Phylogenetic analyses of mitochondrial genes (12S, 16S, ND1) recovered the new species in a clade with E. marmoratus - bicolor , the only congeners for which molecular data are currently available. We report, for the first time, the phylogenetic position of the genus Amazops and also expand the known distribution of Amazops amazops . Our molecular data suggest that the genus is more diverse than currently recognized, identifying additional potentially undescribed species. These findings provide new integrative evidence on the morphological and phylogenetic diversity of Rhinatrematidae and highlight the need for broader sampling and integrative analyses in the tropical Andes.

title: A large orca from the Lower Pleistocene of the Southern North Sea Basin pushes back the origin of macropredatory behavior in the oceanic dolphins (Odontoceti, Delphinidae).
authors: Bakker H, Post K, Munsterman DK, Hoekendijk JPA, Bianucci G.
abstract: The evolutionary history of the biggest extant top predator of our planet, the killer whale Orcinus orca , remains poorly understood. Currently, the fossil record of the genus Orcinus includes only a single formally recognized extinct species, the small-bodied (3.5 meters) piscivorous Orcinus citoniensis from the Pliocene of Cetona, Italy. Here we describe and refer to Orcinus sp., five delphinid fossil remains from the Pleistocene of the southern North Sea, consisting of two fragmentary crania, an incomplete mandible and two atlas-axis cervical complexes. Regression analyses based on extant Orcinus orca measurements and 3D model comparisons indicate an estimated body length between 7.2 and 7.7 m, comparable to that of the largest living male killer whales. Palynological dating of the sediment of one cranial specimen supports a Gelasian (2.6-2.1 Ma) age. This large representative of the genus Orcinus displays morphological features - including large, deep, and widely separated alveoli and deeply excavated condylar fossae - indicating macroraptorial feeding abilities. Orcinus sp. represents the largest Pleistocene delphinid yet documented and provides the earliest known evidence for the emergence of macroraptorial predation within Delphinidae, substantially predating the Middle Pleistocene divergence of modern killer whale ecotypes inferred from genomic data. By demonstrating that this feeding strategy was established more than two million years ago, our results underscore both the long-term stability of apex predation in marine ecosystems and its potential vulnerability to rapid human-induced environmental change.

title: 18-years Follow-up after Mosaicplasty in Adolescent Athletes with Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Elbow.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Toftdahl L, Ovesen J, Thillemann TM.
abstract: Background Autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty is an established surgical treatment of unstable osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) lesions of the elbow. However, the information on the long-term outcomes is lacking. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the long-term clinical and radiographic results after autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty in the treatment of OCD of the elbow. Methods This prospective long-term follow-up study is an extension of previously published data on 10 patients treated with autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty due to advanced, unstable OCD at the capitellum from 2003-2007. Objective and patient-reported outcomes were evaluated including Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), Oxford Elbow Score, Quick-Disability of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (Quick-DASH), Timmerman-Andrews Score, a Subjective Elbow Value, and Range of Motion (ROM). Radiographic signs of osteoarthritis were graded according to the Kellgren-Lawrence classification. Results At mean 18 years (range 16.0-19.7) five patients were available for follow-up. Mean age at follow-up was 34.4, and all five patients were women. MEPS was a median 100 (range 85-100). Activities of daily life were mildly affected in two patients. Two patients had non-symptomatic osteoarthritis grade 1 and 2. Patients experienced a functioning and near-normal elbow. Conclusion The long-term results after mosaicplasty are encouraging, and we find it reasonable to recommend mosaicplasty as the surgical treatment in this group of female patients with advanced, unstable OCD lesions of the elbow. However, it is of concern that two out of five patients had non-symptomatic early radiographic signs of osteoarthritis at an early age. As this study has an inclusion rate of 50 % of the original cohort, attrition bias must be taken into consideration. Level of evidence Level IV, case series, treatment study.

title: Web Alert.
authors: Dexter WW, Strosahl C.

title: Vitamin D status and COVID-19 severity and outcomes: an observational cohort study.
authors: Tariq M, Kim CM, Seo JW, Kim DY, Yun NR, Olaniyan MA, Kim DM.
abstract: Background Vitamin D has been proposed as a modulator of immune responses in COVID-19, but its association with disease severity remains uncertain. The relationship between circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and its active metabolite, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25(OH)₂D], and clinical outcomes in patients with COVID-19 was evaluated. Methods Serum vitamin D metabolites were measured in 95 RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 patients and 64 healthy controls recruited between June 2020 and January 2022. Vitamin D deficiency was defined as 25(OH)D Results Vitamin D deficiency [25(OH)D Conclusions In this observational cohort, circulating vitamin D metabolites were not significantly associated with COVID-19 severity or short-term mortality. Established clinical factors, including older age, systemic inflammation, and comorbidity burden, showed stronger associations with adverse outcomes than vitamin D metabolite concentrations. Limited statistical power warrants cautious interpretation, and larger, adequately powered studies are needed to validate these findings.

title: Upper body posture affects three-dimensional scapula orientation: Clinically applicable models may quantify patient-specific scapula orientation in an upright standing patient.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Ritter D, Dampier K, Olmsted AD, Poltaretskyi S, Raiss P, Bachmaier S, Moroder P.
abstract: Background Scapulothoracic orientation is a key determinant of shoulder function and influences implant positioning and clinical outcomes in shoulder arthroplasty. However, current preoperative planning relies on supine CT scans, which does not represent the patient's upright scapular orientation. Clinically viable methods to quantify upright scapula orientation are lacking. The aim of this study was to quantify upper-body posture obtained from simple lateral photographs. We hypothesized that these photographs can be used to predict three-dimensional (3D) scapular orientation in an upright position. Methods A database of 123 lateral photographs was used in this study to extract clinical assessment parameters (CAPs): forward head posture (FHP), forward shoulder posture (FSP), thoracic kyphosis index (TKI), and forward elbow-humerus ratio (EHF). A validated 3D skeletal upper-body model was used to simulate nine sagittal posture variations, generating corresponding scapular orientations: internal rotation (SIR), anterior tilt (SAT), and upward rotation (SUR). Each CAP was correlated with the 3D model outputs. Weighted correlation models were developed to predict continuous upright scapular orientations for each patient photograph. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering (Ward's method) identified objective upper body posture subgroups. Results All CAPs demonstrated normal distributions. Clustering revealed three distinct sagittal posture groups. Strong correlations were found between CAPs and scapular orientation in the 3D model, particularly between TKI and all scapular angles (R 2 ≥ 0.94). Applying these correlations enabled continuous prediction of upright scapular orientation in all subjects. Predicted SIR, SAT, and SUR differed significantly between posture clusters (P Conclusion Upper body posture in the standing position correlates with upright scapular orientation. Quantifying posture through simple lateral photographs and applying prediction models provides a clinically feasible method to estimate patient-specific upright scapula orientation. This posture-informed approach offers a practical adjunct to supine CT-based preoperative planning and may improve accuracy in implant positioning and range-of-motion simulation. Level of evidence Basic Science Study, Computational Modeling.

title: Triple hernia: coexisting spigelian, femoral and indirect inguinal hernias.
authors: Sure SS, Alexander N, Kumar A, Harikrishnan B.

title: The Growing Popularity of Youth Hockey: A Review of Injury Patterns and Prevention Techniques.
authors: Sheffield D, Riederer MF.
abstract: Ice hockey is growing in popularity not only in the United States and Canada, but also throughout the world with today's youth. Due to the nature of the sport, there are common and unique injuries that occur in young athletes which differ from adult counterparts. Injuries occur more frequently with age. With the introduction of body checking, there is a considerable increase in injuries, especially concussions. Concussions are the most common youth hockey injury with the greatest number of publications in the past several years. Acromioclavicular joint sprains and clavicle fractures are common upper body injuries, whereas hip muscle strains, knee sprains, and contusions are common lower body injuries. Most injuries occur during competition and result in at least a week off from sports participation. Protective gear, such as properly fitting helmets, full-face protection, and mouthguards, along with rule changes such as restrictions on body checking and avoidance of direct head contact, have been shown to lower the risk of injuries. This paper reviews the most recent literature on youth hockey injuries and how these injuries can ultimately be prevented.

title: Subtotal cricoid cartilage resection and crico-tracheal reconstruction for papillary thyroid carcinoma involving cricoid.
authors: Pang F, Ma G, Shi Z, Liu D, Guo Y, Xie L, Zhuang S, Xie M, Wu L, Liu T.
abstract: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) invading laryngotracheal structures is challenging. When most of the cricoid is involved, total laryngectomy is often recommended. We describe a function-preserving alternative using subtotal cricoid resection and crico-tracheal reconstruction. A 51-year-old man with recurrent PTC after thyroidectomy, neck dissections, and radioactive iodine presented with dyspnea. The tumor involved ~75% of the cricoid cartilage and the first to fourth tracheal rings. Subtotal cricoid excision preserved the left one-quarter, followed by tracheal rotation and anastomosis to the residual cricoid. Recovery was uneventful. Oral feeding began on day 15 and decannulation occurred on day 21. Bronchoscopy on day 25 showed a patent airway and a well-healed anastomosis. Margins were negative. At 1.5 years, voice was satisfactory without dyspnea or recurrence. In selected PTC with major cricoid involvement, subtotal cricoid resection with crico-tracheal reconstruction can preserve laryngeal function.

title: Stemless Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty is Associated with Less Opioid Use at Initial Follow-up.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Krumm ZR, Denard PJ, Brockmeier SF, Petre D, Kissenberth M, Shah A, Lederman E, Werner BC.
abstract: Background As the rates of total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) rise, surgeons are tasked with the need to manage initial postoperative pain to facilitate outpatient surgeries and increase functional and patient reported outcomes while minimizing avoidable complications and revision. Of particular interest is the effect of anatomic TSA (aTSA) design on postoperative pain and opioid use, especially in light of the national effort to reduce opioid prescriptions following orthopedic surgery. Methods A multi-center retrospective cohort study was performed on patients who underwent either short-stem or stemless aTSA between 2013 and 2023. Two cohorts were established and baseline data on demographics, preoperative Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain, and preoperative opioid use were obtained. The primary endpoint of this study was the postoperative VAS pain at the initial (10-14 day) postoperative follow-up, with the reported opioid use and the need for opioid medication refill as secondary endpoints. Student's t-test was performed on continuous variables, and chi-square or Fisher's exact test was performed on categorical variables as appropriate. Multivariable linear regression was performed to determine predictors of postoperative VAS. Results 817 patients were included in this study; 366 patients in the short-stem cohort and 451 in the stemless cohort. No difference was observed between groups for the preoperative VAS pain (p=0.102), postoperative VAS pain (p=0.838), and change in VAS pain (p=0.117). The prevalence of opioid use was lower at the initial follow-up visit in the stemless cohort (35.4% vs 48.9% in short-stem, p Conclusion Patients undergoing stemless aTSA may not demonstrate different postoperative pain scores at initial follow-up than patients undergoing short-stem aTSA; however, use of a stemless aTSA has a weak to moderate association with less opioid medication use at initial follow-up. Although there was no statistically significant difference in postoperative VAS pain scores, patients who underwent stemless aTSA used less opioid medication by their initial 10-14 day postoperative visit than their short-stemmed aTSA comparison cohort. Level of evidence Level III; Retrospective Cohort Comparison; Treatment Study.

title: Sociobehavioral Comorbidities and Outcomes After Colectomy in a National United States Veteran Cohort.
authors: D'Aquila ML, Schultz KS, Schneider EB, Hall DE, O'Leary JR, Richburg CE, Shah T, Trope WL, King JT, Golshan M, Justice AC, Leeds IL.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the independent association between sociobehavioral comorbidities (SBCs) and complications after colectomies in a national Veteran cohort. Background SBCs are determinants of health outcomes, and Veterans represent a high-vulnerability population. However, the relationship of SBCs with postoperative complications remains understudied, and current surgical risk models underestimate risk among patients with significant SBC burden. Methods We conducted an observational study of Veterans undergoing elective colectomy included in the Veterans Affairs Surgical Quality Improvement Program (VASQIP). Structured data from the Veteran Health Administration Corporate Data Warehouse were used to identify 6 SBC phenotypes (mental health disorder, suicide risk, substance use, social isolation, housing instability, and food insecurity) across 3 preoperative ascertainment windows: ≤90 days, ≤365 days, and lifetime. The outcome was any 30-day VASQIP-defined postoperative complication. Multilevel logistic regression estimated associations between SBCs and complications. Results Among 38,188 Veterans undergoing colectomy between 2009 and 2025, the median age was 66 years; 5% were female; 30% were non-white; and 48% had cancer. Mental health disorder, social isolation, or substance use were each associated with an 8%-40% increase in the odds of a complication across all ascertainment windows. Within the most proximal window, risk of complication increased as SBC burden increased: 16% increased odds with 1 SBC (aOR 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.23) and 80% increased odds with 4-6 SBCs (aOR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.32-2.36). Conclusions In a national Veteran cohort, SBCs were associated with postoperative colectomy complications. The strongest associations were observed with SBCs ascertained within the 90-day window, and the odds increased in a dose-response relationship with increasing SBC burden.

title: Single-port robotic thoracic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative outcomes versus multiport robotic surgery and uniportal VATS.
authors: Gritsiuta AI, Yazditabar J, Radfar P, Ross P, Zervos MD, Petrov RV.
abstract: Single-port robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (SP-RATS) has expanded rapidly, but its comparative effectiveness remains uncertain across platforms and access strategies. We systematically evaluated SP-RATS against multiport robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (MP-RATS) and uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS). PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and supplementary sources were searched through October 5, 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses with modified Knapp-Hartung inference were used for continuous and common binary outcomes, whereas rare events were analyzed using fixed-effect Peto odds ratios. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and certainty using GRADE. Sixty reports were included; 23 provided Group A or B comparative data, with one study at critical risk of bias excluded from the primary quantitative synthesis. Compared with MP-RATS, SP-RATS demonstrated broadly similar perioperative outcomes without a consistent disadvantage. Lymph-node yield was nominally lower (MD, - 1.18 nodes; 95% CI, - 2.31 to - 0.05; P = 0.043), but this finding did not persist across sensitivity analyses. Compared with uVATS, SP-RATS was associated with shorter chest-tube duration (MD, - 0.49 days; 95% CI, - 0.85 to - 0.13; P = 0.013), with additional favorable signals in lymph-node yield, chest drainage, and conversion, although these were less consistent across sensitivity analyses. Complications, R0 resection, and mortality did not differ significantly between approaches. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all pooled outcomes. SP-RATS appears to be a viable minimally invasive alternative, achieving reduced robotic access without an evident trade-off in perioperative safety or immediate oncologic outcomes. Prospective comparative studies are needed to determine whether reduced robotic access provides reproducible clinical benefit.

title: Single-port robotic surgery versus laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery for the surgical staging of early-stage endometrial cancer: a sequential-period propensity-score analysis.
authors: Kim JH, Kim Y, Jo D, Seo H, Shin S, Kim S, Choi MC, Lee SW, Kim DY, Kim JH, Park JY.
abstract: We compared perioperative outcomes of da Vinci SP robotic surgery and laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery (LESS) for staging early-stage endometrial cancer in a sequential-period cohort. Between 2010 and 2025, 178 women with presumed and final FIGO stage I or II endometrial carcinoma underwent single-port staging with lymph node assessment; LESS was used through 2021 (n = 95), and SP surgery was introduced in 2021 (n = 83). Patients were analyzed by planned approach, including procedures requiring an additional port. The primary outcome was the hemoglobin decline from the preoperative value to the value measured on the day of surgery. The hemoglobin decline was 1.92 ± 1.14 g/dL after LESS and 0.92 ± 0.88 g/dL after SP surgery (p < .001), and estimated blood loss was 205.4 ± 192.4 and 68.5 ± 79.3 mL (p < .001). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, the between-group difference in hemoglobin decline (SP minus LESS) was - 1.06 g/dL (95% CI - 1.42 to - 0.70). This estimate was not materially changed by further adjustment for perioperative fluid volume and sampling time. In a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with pelvic lymphadenectomy, the difference was attenuated to - 0.72 g/dL (95% CI - 1.21 to - 0.22), and operative time was 25.5 min longer with the SP robot. Overall operative time, hospital stay, conversions, and complications did not differ significantly. SP staging was associated with a smaller hemoglobin decline. Because the 2 approaches were used in largely different calendar periods, these findings do not establish an independent effect of the platform.

title: Short-term outcomes of the hinotori versus da Vinci robotic surgical systems in colorectal cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Huang J, Du P.
abstract: Direct comparative evidence on the hinotori and da Vinci robotic systems in colorectal cancer surgery remains limited. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare their short-term perioperative outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies directly comparing hinotori with da Vinci robotic surgery in patients with colorectal cancer. Study-level data were pooled using random-effects models, with mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes, each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Five retrospective propensity-score-matched studies involving 462 patients (hinotori, n = 204; da Vinci, n = 258) were included. Operative time (MD 30.57 min, 95% CI 17.51-43.64; I² = 0%) and console time (MD 30.72 min, 95% CI 17.29-44.16; I² = 42%) were significantly longer with hinotori, whereas length of hospital stay was significantly shorter (MD - 1.58 days, 95% CI - 2.92 to - 0.24; I² = 63%). No statistically significant differences were detected for estimated blood loss (MD 3.42 mL, 95% CI - 6.98 to 13.82; I² = 66%) or for postoperative complications (grade I-II: OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.36-1.69; grade III-IV: OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.16-1.76; overall: OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.37-1.46). In this meta-analysis of propensity-score-matched studies, hinotori was associated with longer operative and console times and a shorter hospital stay than da Vinci, whereas no statistically significant difference was detected in blood loss or postoperative complications. Because clinically important differences in safety could not be excluded and residual confounding could not be ruled out, these findings should be regarded as preliminary; larger prospective comparative studies are warranted.

title: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a narrative review of resection accuracy and individualized soft-tissue balance.
authors: Shen L, Zhai C, Jiang T, Wang Y.
abstract: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA) was introduced to reduce variability in bone resection and component positioning. Contemporary platforms do much more than that: they combine three-dimensional planning, intraoperative registration, objective gap assessment and virtual component adjustment. As a result, the question has shifted from whether a robot can reproduce a planned resection to whether robotic data can be used to individualize alignment and soft-tissue balance. This review follows that shift and examines the clinical evidence behind it. This narrative review examined the relationship between robotic resection accuracy, individualized soft-tissue balancing, and clinical outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English-language peer-reviewed studies published between January 2010 and September 2026, using combinations of the terms ("robotics" OR "robotic" OR "robot-assisted" OR "robotic-assisted" OR "robot arm" OR "robotic arm") AND ("arthroplasty, replacement, knee" OR "total knee arthroplasty" OR "total knee replacement" OR "knee arthroplasty" OR "knee replacement"). Reference lists of key reviews and primary studies were hand-searched. Priority was given to randomized trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, large comparative cohorts, long-term studies, and studies that quantified intraoperative gap or laxity behavior. The most reproducible advantage of RA-TKA is still execution accuracy, with fewer limb- and component-alignment outliers than conventional instrumentation. The newer value proposition is more complex. Depending on the platform and workflow, robotic systems can quantify compartment gaps and support virtual component adjustments, while force-controlled assessment is available in selected systems. These capabilities may reduce soft-tissue releases, but their clinical value depends on the balancing strategy and target definitions.
