Contemporary functional and patient-specific workflows often achieve high rates of predefined gap balance while keeping joint-line orientation within guardrails. Clinical superiority, however, is inconsistent. In recent randomized trials, functional alignment markedly reduced soft-tissue release, but patient-reported outcomes were not consistently superior to mechanical alignment at 2 years. Long-term survivorship data remain limited and conflicting, and economic value depends heavily on procedural volume, platform costs and downstream resource use. RA-TKA improves execution accuracy and can facilitate quantitative soft-tissue assessment and individualized planning. These capabilities have not established consistent superiority in patient-reported outcomes or survivorship. Further evidence is needed to validate alignment and laxity targets and determine the long-term clinical and economic value of specific workflows.

title: Relative Real-time Arthroscopic Evaluation of Glenohumeral Structural Failure during Manipulation under Anesthesia for Primary Frozen Shoulder.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Abdel-Mordy Kandeel A, Lasheen MM, Ali Elsayed AF, Morsi E.
abstract: Background Patterns of glenohumeral structural failure during manipulation under anesthesia (MUA) for management of frozen shoulder (FS) have not yet been thoroughly examined. This study investigated the necessity of macroscopic glenohumeral capsular failure/tearing during MUA for motion restoration in patients with primary FS. Methods This prospective case-series study (conducted between November 2023 and May 2025) included 31 patients with primary FS. Patients were managed with 1 st -look arthroscopy (evaluating the integrity of the different glenohumeral structures) followed by MUA, 2 nd -look arthroscopy (documenting the primary outcome of the study; i.e., post-manipulation glenohumeral structural disruptions/failure, especially the capsular tears), and then combined anterior and posterior arthroscopic glenohumeral release. Secondary outcome measurements included immediate post-MUA passive range of motion (ROM), as well as 6-month postoperative (post-MUA and arthroscopic release) ROM and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) scores. Results The mean age of included patients was (52.41±11.31) years. 2 nd -look arthroscopy revealed post-manipulation disruption of the intra-articular adhesions and the superior glenohumeral ligament in all (100%) patients; however, no capsular tear was detected in any patient. Otherwise, different glenohumeral structures showed post-manipulation minor failure (not necessitating repair), including superior labrum from anterior to posterior (SLAP) lesion in 4 (12.8%), antero-inferior labral detachment in 4 (12.8%), middle gleno-humeral tear in 3 (9.7%), inferior glenohumeral ligament tear in 1 (3.2%), partial articular-sided supraspinatus tendon avulsion (PASTA) lesion in 4 (12. 8%), and partial subscapularis tear in 3 (9.7%) patients. Major structural failure (necessitating repair) was encountered in 6.4% of the study group, including a full-thickness rotator cuff tear in 1 (3.2%) patient and an avulsion fracture of the greater tuberosity in another (3.2%) patient. There was an immediate post-manipulation significant improvement in passive ROM with further significant improvement on 6-month postoperative evaluation (P-value ˂0.05). In addition, the final postoperative evaluation revealed significant improvement in VAS and ASES scores (P-value ˂0.05). Conclusion Immediate post-MUA motion restoration in middle-aged patients with primary FS might be attributed to the MUA-induced disruption of the intra-articular adhesions (a consistently encountered finding in this study) and/or capsular stretching out/micro-tears (rather than capsular macro-tears). However, currently reported conclusions should be validated via further larger-volume cohort clinical studies.

title: Relationship Between Post-Operative Complications and Length of Stay in Patients Requiring Free Flap Reconstruction of the Head and Neck.
authors: Lee L, Dunn M, Wykes J, Low TH, Palme C, Clark J, Manzie T.
abstract: Background Reconstructive with free flap procedures are often required following ablative removal of pathologies from the head and neck. The Clavien-Dindo Classification (CDC) system is widely used to grade complication severity; however, there are limited studies examining the relationship between complications and length of stay (LOS) in this cohort. Purpose To evaluate the association between complication severity and both hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) LOS in patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 994 patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Complications were graded using the CDC system. LOS was analysed using generalised linear models with a Gamma distribution and log-link. Kruskal-Wallis tests were used for supplementary analysis. Results Complications occurred in 54.5% of patients. Higher CDC grades were significantly associated with longer ICU (p Conclusion This study provides outcome data linking complication severity to ICU and hospital LOS. The CDC, while advantageous, fails to separate significant negative outcomes, such as free flap failure from a more simple return to theatre. Modifications may further improve distinction in complications and effect on overall hospital stay.

title: Recurrence After Primary Lumbar Discectomy: Rate, Reoperation, and Risk Factors in A Single-Center Cohort Over A 10-Year Study Period.
authors: Yıldızhan S, Rakip U, Canbek İ, Gazi Boyacı M, Korkmaz S, Aslan A.
abstract: Objective Recurrent lumbar disc herniation after primary discectomy is a clinically important complication whose temporal pattern, revision surgical profile, and associated comorbidities remain incompletely characterized in long-term cohorts. We aimed to define the rate and timing of reoperation-confirmed recurrence, characterize the revision profile, and examine associated risk factors. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 432 consecutive patients who underwent primary lumbar discectomy between January 2015 and December 2024, with a median follow-up of 85 months (interquartile range 50-103). Recurrence was defined as reoperation-confirmed, same-level ipsilateral reherniation after an initial pain-free interval. Follow-up status and external reoperations were verified through the national electronic health record system up to the study end date (6 March 2026), with no loss to follow-up. Associations were examined using multivariable logistic regression (with Firth penalization) and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results Reoperation-confirmed recurrence occurred in 28 patients (6.5%); this represents the reoperation-confirmed recurrence rate rather than the overall incidence of recurrent herniation, since conservatively managed recurrences were not counted. Recurrence was predominantly late, with 68% of events beyond the first postoperative year (median 18.5 months). At reoperation, 21 patients (75%) required instrumented posterolateral fusion for objective segmental instability, with a mean segmental translation of 4.2 ± 1.1 mm and a mean angulation of 12.2° ± 2.1° on dynamic flexion-extension radiographs, both exceeding the predefined instability thresholds. The remaining 7 patients (25%) underwent revision discectomy alone. No second recurrence occurred over a median post-revision follow-up of 61.5 months. In the primary logistic model, hypertension was associated with recurrence (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.42, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04-11.21; p = 0.043), whereas the association of diabetes mellitus was of similar magnitude but did not reach statistical significance (OR 3.17, 95% CI 0.97-10.35; p = 0.056). Diabetes mellitus reached significance only in the secondary Firth penalized and time-to-event analyses. Active smoking was not associated with recurrence (OR 0.64; p = 0.321). Given the limited number of events (n = 28), these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory; in particular, the study was not powered to overturn existing evidence linking smoking with recurrence, and the 10-year survival estimate is exploratory given few patients at risk beyond 5 years. Conclusion In this 10-year single-center cohort, reoperation-confirmed recurrence occurred in 6.5% of patients and was predominantly late (median 18.5 months), indicating that postoperative surveillance should extend beyond the first year. Three quarters of revisions required instrumented fusion for objective instability. No second recurrence was observed. Hypertension was associated with recurrence in the primary analysis, whereas the association of diabetes mellitus did not reach significance in the primary model and was supported only by secondary analyses. Both comorbidities should be investigated further in adequately powered multicenter studies.

title: Precision in achieving planned HKA alignment using a hybrid method of resection in imageless robot assisted total knee arthroplasty: a retroprospective study of 103 knees.
authors: Rathod PM, Raju S, Nehru AP, Vasudevan V, Naik R, Singhi PK, Chandrasekaran N.
abstract: Evidence on hybrid robotic-resection workflows in robotic-assisted TKA is limited. This study quantified agreement between planned, intraoperatively achieved, and early postoperative standing hip-knee-ankle (HKA) alignment using a hybrid resection workflow with the CORI system. We retrospectively reviewed 85 patients (103 knees) from 264 consecutive primary TKAs performed with the imageless hand-held robot (CORI) system at a single center between September 2024 and August 2025. The distal femur was resected and the proximal tibia refined with the burr, and the remaining femoral cuts were made with a conventional 4-in-1 jig. HKA was measured preoperatively, as planned, and as achieved intraoperatively after resections with trials and on full-length weight-bearing radiographs at 3 weeks. Forgotten joint score (FJS 12) was recorded at 6 months. Agreement was assessed using mean signed error, RMSE, and 95% confidence intervals, and measurement reliability using ICC for inter and intra-observer variations. The cohort comprised 85 patients (103 knees; 67 unilateral, 18 bilateral). Mean preoperative HKA was 166.1° ± 6.7° and improved to 177.8° ± 1.9° on early postoperative standing radiographs. Planned HKA was 178.8° ± 0.8° and intraoperatively achieved HKA was 178.0° ± 1.6°, a mean signed error of - 0.8° ± 1.3° (95% CI), indicating slight under-correction relative to plan. RMSE was 1.50° (planned vs achieved), 2.17° (planned vs postoperative), and 1.98° (achieved vs postoperative). Mean FJS 12 at 6 months was 76.0 ± 11.8 (range 54-95) Measurement reliability (inter and intra observer) was good to excellent (ICC 0.89-0.98).In this retrospective series, the hybrid CORI workflow showed close agreement between planned, intraoperatively achieved, and early postoperative standing HKA, with a small mean under-correction of 0.8° relative to plan. These findings are descriptive; without a comparator or long-term clinical outcomes, they cannot establish equivalence to fully robotic or conventional TKA. Prospective comparative studies are needed to evaluate the comparisons.

title: Postoperative prophylactic and delayed oral antibiotics after total shoulder arthroplasty: a multi-institutional database analysis.
authors: Shehadeh TH, Singh A, Chaudhry J, Lanham N.
abstract: Background To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic and delayed postoperative oral antibiotics following total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA). Methods The TriNetX database was queried for primary TSA patients. Those with prior pathologic fracture, upper extremity malignancy, infection, prosthetic joint infection (PJI), or revision surgery within 6 months were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, two comparisons were performed: (1) prophylactic oral antibiotics within 1 postoperative day versus controls (n=5,891 per cohort) and (2) delayed oral antibiotics on postoperative days 7-30 versus controls (n=3,087 per cohort). Outcomes at 30 and 90 days included acute kidney injury (AKI), emergency department (ED) visits, readmission, PJI, and revision surgery. Results At 30 days, prophylactic antibiotics were associated with fewer readmissions (2.78% vs. 3.73%; P=0.004), with no differences in AKI, ED visits, PJI, or revision surgery. At 90 days, they were associated with higher PJI (0.92% vs. 0.48%; P=0.004) and a trend toward lower ED visits (5.25% vs. 6.16%; P=0.032) and readmissions (3.70% vs. 4.67%; P=0.009), but higher revision surgery (1.17% vs. 0.73%; P=0.014). Delayed antibiotics were associated with higher rates of AKI, ED visits, readmissions, and revision surgery at both 30 and 90 days (all P Conclusions Although residual confounding cannot be excluded, postoperative prophylactic or delayed oral antibiotics were not associated with reduced PJI or revision surgery and may be associated with antibiotic-related adverse effects. Level of evidence: III.

title: Pickleball Pain: Point of Care Ultrasound Used to Diagnose Midfoot Pain: Erratum.
authors: Bentz GD, Bentz G, Sealy E.

title: Pickleball Injuries in Adults: A Narrative Review.
authors: Witt D, Ervin W, Riederer M.
abstract: Pickleball has emerged as the fastest-growing sport in the United States, with an estimated annual health care burden of $250 to $500 million. Emergency department visits for pickleball-related injuries increased 18-fold between 2014 and 2023, with a diverse and expanding range of injuries documented. Women are disproportionately affected by pickleball-related fractures, particularly distal radius fractures, reflecting postmenopausal bone loss combined with fall-dominant injury mechanisms. A striking finding among Achilles tendon injuries is the "first-month phenomenon," with most ruptures occurring within the first month of play and nearly one-third on the player's very first day, challenging the perception of pickleball as a low-impact sport. Ocular injuries represent an emerging concern, as nearly 88% of injuries documented over a 20-year surveillance period occurred within the last three years; however, no governing body currently mandates protective eyewear. Targeted prevention strategies addressing the distinct vulnerabilities associated with age, sex, and experience level are warranted.

title: Patients Use Google to Ask Questions About the Structure, Function, and Risks of Peptide Use in Orthopaedic Surgery.
authors: Obana KK, Weiss DL, Chen JY, Levine SB, Chen AZ, Luzzi AJ, Trofa DP.
abstract: Purpose To identify the common patient questions and to evaluate the quality of online resources regarding peptide therapy, namely, body protection compound-157, in orthopaedic surgery. Methods Three orthopaedic peptide searches were entered into a clean Google Web Search on June 30, 2025. Questions under the "People also ask" tab were expanded sequentially. The first 100 consecutive results meeting inclusion criteria for each query were included (300 total). Questions or websites unrelated to orthopaedic peptides and repeat verbatim questions within each query were excluded. Questions were categorized into 1 of 3 Rothwell Classifications and subcategorized by topic. Websites were categorized based on source. The Journal of the American Medical Association Benchmark Criteria was used to evaluate the quality of each website. Results Most questions fell into the Rothwell Fact category (61.0%). Most common question topics were Structure/Function (31.7%), Risks/Complications (20.7%), and Treatment Comparisons (9.7%). The least common question topics were Specific Activities (0%), Pain (0.3%), Longevity of Treatment (0.7%), and Management (0.7%). The most common websites were Commercial (28.0%), Academic (18.0%), and Government (18.0%). PubMed articles consisted of 98.1% of Government websites. The overall average Journal of the American Medical Association score was 2.0 ± 1.5. Government websites had the highest score (3.6 ± 0.7) and constituted 48.6% of websites with a score of 4/4. Medical Practice and Single Surgeon websites had the lowest Journal of the American Medical Association score of 0.7 ± 1.0 and 0.7 ± 0.9, respectively. Conclusions The most common online patient questions pertain to the structure, function, and risks associated with peptide therapy. The quality of the information is heterogeneous. Clinical relevance Because of the increasing popularity and accessibility, improved technology, and limited research, physicians should be aware of the most common online patient questions pertaining to peptide therapy in orthopaedics. Care should be taken when presenting the impact of peptides without discussing the quality to avoid overvaluing its impact.

authors: Eichner ER.

title: Operative versus nonoperative management of olecranon fractures in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Lima JPC, Morales Ribeiro V, Segatti R, Butturi Varone B, Dos Santos Cardoso F, Giordano V.
abstract: Introduction Displaced olecranon fractures in the frail geriatric patient represent a therapeutic challenge, involving the decision between operating to achieve anatomical reduction of the articular surface or not operating due to the high risks associated with poor bone quality and failure of mechanical fixation. Materials and methods PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were systematically searched for studies published from inception through February 2026 comparing tension band wiring, plate fixation, or cerclage wiring with nonoperative treatment for displaced olecranon fractures in geriatric patients. Risk ratio (RR) was used to evaluate binary outcomes, and standard mean difference (SMD) for continuous outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Of 459 articles, eight studies were included. A total of 723 older adults were included. Most patients had Mayo type IIA or IIB fractures. Tension band wiring was the most frequently performed surgical technique, followed by plate fixation and cerclage wiring. Operative treatment was associated with a lower risk of radiographic nonunion (RR 0.19; 95% CI 0.04, 0.8) but increased the risk of overall complications (RR 3.21; 95% CI 1.63, 6.35) and reoperation (RR 4.85; 95% CI 1.72, 13.65) compared to nonoperative treatment. Physical function showed a non-significant trend toward improvement with operative treatment (SMD -0.29; 95% CI -0.72, 0.14). At final follow-up, pain intensity was low and comparable between the two treatment groups across the majority of studies. Approximately half of the reoperation excess comprised elective or symptomatic implant removal, and the overall certainty of the evidence is low. Conclusion In older adults with displaced olecranon fractures, operative management was associated with a reduced risk of radiographic nonunion and with a higher risk of complications and reoperation compared to nonoperative management. Level of evidence Level III Systematic Review/MetaAnalysis Treatment Study.

title: Myelin water fraction mapping with voxelwise appraisal of solution ambiguity by globally optimized single and joint inversion of spin- and gradient-echo data.
authors: Kobe M, Laufenberg M, Stöcker T, Paasche H.
abstract: Quantitative mapping of the myelin water fraction (MWF) is a key objective in neuroimaging, yet the ambiguity of MWF estimates arising from ill-posed inversion problems is rarely assessed at the voxel level. We propose a global-search inversion framework based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) for single and joint inversion of multi-echo MRI data (T 2 and T 2 *) without additional regularization of the individual inverse problems. Repeated PSO runs per voxel yield ensembles of solutions that enable an empirical appraisal of near-optimal solution variability under the chosen model assumptions and misfit criterion. Simulation results show accurate recovery of MWF under the investigated conditions and demonstrate how joint inversion can constrain the solution space. In vivo experiments reveal differences between T 2 - and T 2 *-based MWF estimates, with variations across subjects. Joint inversion yields compromise solutions, while preserving sensitivity to inter-contrast discrepancies. The proposed framework complements conventional MWF imaging by providing voxelwise information on the variability of near-optimal solutions, offering a basis for evaluating inversion stability and solution ambiguity.

title: Lower Extremity Neuropathies in Athletes.
authors: Stokes DC, Cushman DM.
abstract: Lower extremity neuropathies are an important and often underrecognized cause of pain and dysfunction in athletes. While classic neuropathic symptoms such as numbness, paresthesias, and weakness in the distribution of the affected peripheral nerve may be present, clinical presentations are frequently subtle and nonspecific. On physical examination, clinicians may identify focal neurological deficits, a positive Tinel sign at the site of suspected compression, and symptom reproduction with provocative maneuvers. Diagnostic evaluation may include electromyography/nerve conduction studies, as well as imaging modalities such as radiographs, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, to support the diagnosis. Initial management is typically nonoperative, although surgical intervention may be considered for persistent or progressive symptoms. This article provides an updated review of the evaluation and management of common lower extremity neuropathies in athletes.

title: Long-term clinical outcomes of distal biceps tendon reconstruction using fascia lata allograft.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Fawzy H, Hilgersom NFJ, Nijs A, Oost IK, Eygendaal D, The B.
abstract: Background Distal biceps tendon reconstruction using graft augmentation is indicated when primary repair is not feasible. Long-term outcome data on fascia lata allograft reconstruction remain limited. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term functional outcomes, complications, and patient satisfaction following distal biceps tendon reconstruction using fascia lata allograft. Methods This retrospective case series included adult patients who underwent distal biceps tendon reconstruction using fascia lata allograft between June 2008 and June 2023. Thirty-nine eligible patients were identified, of whom 27 were included in the final analysis after providing informed consent. Baseline characteristics, surgical details, and complications were obtained from medical records. Long-term outcomes were assessed at a single follow-up time point using patient-reported outcome measures, including the Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (QuickDASH) and the Oxford Elbow Score (OES), as well as additional questions regarding satisfaction and return to work and sports participation. Results Twenty-seven male patients were included with a median age of 49 years (range, 36-64) and a median follow-up of 78 months (range, 15-190). Sixteen complications occurred in 12 patients (44%), of which 11 (69%) were minor. The most common complication was lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve neuropraxia (56%), which resolved in most cases. The mean QuickDASH score was 10 and the mean OES was 88. Among patients employed prior to injury, 77% returned to work. Among those participating in sports before injury, 52% resumed their previous sport level and frequency. Overall satisfaction and satisfaction with arm function were high (mean, 4.3/5), whereas satisfaction with arm appearance was lower (mean, 3.1/5). Conclusion Fascia lata allograft reconstruction for chronic distal biceps tendon ruptures provides good long-term functional outcomes and high overall patient satisfaction. Although complication rates were notable, most events were minor and transient. Occupational demands and cosmetic expectations should be considered during preoperative counseling.

title: Letter to the Editor: Cigarette Smoking Was Not Associated With Lower Odds of Radiographic Fusion After Combined TLIF and Posterolateral Lumbar (270°) Arthrodesis: A CT-based Retrospective Cohort Evaluation.
authors: Blanco RL, Bustos JG, Olmos-García MA.

title: Leadless Pacemaker Implantation in Fabry Disease With Permanent Atrial Fibrillation and Bradycardia: Diagnostic and Implantation Guidance by Preprocedural Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
authors: Saito H, Suzuki Y, Yamada S, Fujii H, Takami K, Takahashi Y, Nishijyo K, Yoshida A.
abstract: In advanced Fabry cardiomyopathy, preprocedural cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may reveal a lower septal region spared from otherwise extensive septal late gadolinium enhancement. This information, combined with pre-fixation electrical mapping, may help identify an optimal site for leadless pacemaker implantation and minimize repeated fixation attempts.

title: Late leptomeningeal dissemination of a primary intramedullary spinal cord melanoma after three years of control on pembrolizumab.
authors: Rahamimov O, Livoff A, Frommer-Shapira R, Rahamimov N.

title: Large Language Models Aligned With Medical Experts on Established Topics but Were Less Aligned on Emerging or Debated Topics in Posterolateral Corner Treatment: An Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Delphi Study.
authors: Yu Y, Tollefson LV, LaPrade RF, Chahla J, Oettl FC, Samuelsson K, Feldt R.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate how Large Language Models (LLMs) align with a concurrently performed human medical expert-modified Delphi study on the posterolateral corner and to qualitatively analyze LLM behavior. Methods Four commercially available and current LLMs (Gemini-2.5-Pro. GPT-4o, o4-mini, and o3) were tasked with rating posterolateral corner consensus statements on a 5-point Likert scale and estimating the level of expert consensus for each statement, mirroring a human expert Delphi process. LLM performance was evaluated based on alignment with expert majority opinion, accuracy in predicting expert consensus, and self-consistency across multiple LLM invocations. Deep research to improve LLM performance was also explored. Results LLM-generated ratings showed moderate correlation with average expert ratings, with some models exhibiting tendencies toward overly positive ratings. Consensus derived from LLM self-consistency did not reliably approximate expert consensus. LLM estimates of consensus were informative, with some models showing improved alignment with actual expert consensus. Qualitative analysis revealed distinct behavioral patterns across different LLMs regarding justification generation, certainty expression, and handling of conflicting evidence. Preliminary findings suggest that deep research capabilities can enhance rating accuracy as well as consensus prediction. Evidence of hallucination in LLM reasoning is observed and requires further verification. Conclusions Although LLMs show potential in reflecting expert medical knowledge and estimating consensus, their direct ratings and self-consistency may not perfectly align with expert panels. Different LLMs display unique strengths and weaknesses, suggesting that model selection or a combination can be beneficial for applications like modified Delphi studies. Improved consensus estimation was seen by providing the models access to web search, enabling them to find recent, relevant research articles. Level of evidence Level V, expert opinion.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of Chinese operating room nurses toward isolation in oncologic surgery: a cross-sectional survey.
authors: Zhang M, Liao X, Xie L, Yuan Q.
abstract: Background Surgical isolation techniques are a critical fundamental skill in oncological surgery, essential for preventing the dissemination and implantation of tumor cells. However, research on the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of surgical isolation techniques among operating room nurses remains limited. This study aims to assess the KAP levels of isolation techniques among Chinese operating room nurses during oncological surgeries. Method This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted between October and December 2024. Operating room nurses from a tertiary hospital were recruited via non-probabilistic convenience sampling, yielding 121 valid responses through the Wenjuanxing online platform. A validated KAP questionnaire based on relevant guidelines was developed to assess participants' KAP regarding surgical isolation techniques. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics to evaluate overall KAP levels and distribution. Result A total of 121 operating room nurses were included, comprising 18 males (14.88%) and 103 females (85.12%). Among them, 84.30% were under 40 years old, and 92.56% held a bachelor's degree or higher. The assessment revealed that the scores for operating room nurses' KAP (correct rate) were 69.94 ± 10.15 (69.94%), 40.95 ± 3.99, and 45.10 ± 4.46, respectively. The three lowest-scoring knowledge items were related to the principles of tumor resection, surgical incision protection, and pneumoperitoneum management during laparoscopic tumor surgery. The three lowest-scoring attitude items were: "using surgical isolation techniques to facilitate surgical progress," "using surgical isolation techniques does not increase workload," and "feeling satisfied with one's own mastery of isolation techniques." The three lowest-scoring practice items involved handling instruments that contact the tumor, handling dressings that contact the tumor, and changing gloves before closing the abdomen. Conclusion While operating room nurses maintain positive attitudes toward isolation techniques, gaps remain in their knowledge of tumor-free manipulation, instrument handling, and zone demarcation. To standardize clinical practices during tumor surgeries, regular performance audits and targeted training programs are strongly recommended.

title: Knotless Suture Anchors Reduce Repair Time in Arthroscopic Hip Labral Repair Compared With Knotted Anchors.
authors: Kahana-Rojkind AH, McCarroll T, Quesada-Jimenez R, Reyes-Cordova A, Sandler D, Sugarman EP, Domb BG.
abstract: Purpose To compare procedure time between knotless and knotted all-suture anchors during arthroscopic acetabular labral repair in a cadaveric model and to evaluate implications for surgical training and workflow efficiency. Methods Ten fresh-frozen cadaveric hemipelvis specimens underwent arthroscopic labral repair. Five specimens (20 anchors) were repaired using knotted all-suture anchors, and 5 specimens (20 anchors) were repaired using tensionable knotless all-suture anchors. A standardized simple-loop suture configuration was used in all repairs. Repair time per anchor was recorded and subdivided into "Pass," "Tie/Convert," and "Cut" phases. Comparisons between groups were performed using independent t tests or Mann-Whitney U tests, with α = 0.05. Results Mean total repair time per anchor was significantly shorter in the knotless group (79.36 ± 18.07 seconds) compared with the knotted group (142.48 ± 27.96 seconds; P = .007). Tie/Convert phase was also significantly shorter in the knotless group (15.92 ± 4.50 seconds vs 73.11 ± 18.44 seconds; P P = .050). Cut phase was shorter with knotless anchors (11.35 ± 4.93 seconds vs 25.70 ± 27.06 seconds; P = .191) although not statistically significant. Conclusions Knotless suture anchors significantly reduced acetabular labral repair time compared with knotted anchors in this cadaveric model, primarily because of a shorter Tie/Convert phase required for suture fixation. Clinical relevance Knotless suture anchors may streamline labral repair by eliminating arthroscopic knot tying. Their technical simplicity and efficiency may benefit surgical training and enhance consistency among less experienced surgeons.

title: Infliximab for Refractory Diffuse Sclerosing Osteomyelitis of the Mandible Associated With Ulcerative Colitis: A Case Report.
authors: Yao M, Obata K, Takei K, Miyake Y, Fujishima M, Kishimoto K.
abstract: Diffuse sclerosing osteomyelitis (DSO) of the mandible is a chronic nonbacterial inflammatory bone disease. We report a 65-year-old woman with ulcerative colitis who presented with swelling and pain of the left mandible. The lesion was refractory to tooth extraction, prolonged antibiotics, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. CT showed widespread loss of trabecular structure and osteosclerosis, and bone scintigraphy demonstrated abnormal uptake confined to the mandible, without findings suggestive of synovitis, acne, pustulosis, hyperostosis, and osteitis syndrome. DSO was diagnosed based on the overall clinical course, progressive radiological findings, persistence despite treatment of the suspected odontogenic foci and repeated antibiotic therapy, and supportive histopathological findings. Anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) therapy was considered for the refractory DSO, and infliximab was selected because it is also effective for ulcerative colitis; her symptoms resolved promptly, and imaging showed marked improvement with restoration of trabecular bone. No relapse or treatment-related adverse events occurred during 3 years of follow-up. The clinical and radiographic improvement observed following infliximab treatment in this older adult raises the possibility that TNF-α-mediated inflammatory pathways may be involved in refractory DSO associated with ulcerative colitis and supports further investigation of anti-TNF-α therapy in this setting.

title: Impact of multiplex PCR respiratory panels on antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in hospitalized adults with pneumonia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Ahn C, Chanliongco AN, Smith AJ, Steuber TD, Sperry M.
abstract: Background Inadequate empiric antimicrobial therapy increases mortality and healthcare costs. Rapid multiplex PCR respiratory panels can provide faster and more sensitive pathogen detection than conventional culture-based methods; however, interpretation may be limited by detection of colonizing organisms and resistance genes that do not always correspond to phenotypic resistance. Their impact on clinical outcomes and antimicrobial stewardship remains uncertain due to heterogeneous studies and clinical implementation strategies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the clinical value of these panels in hospitalized adults with pneumonia. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library through October 15, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing multiplex PCR-guided therapy with standard microbiological testing. The primary outcome was total antibiotic duration. Secondary outcomes included incidence of targeted/appropriate antimicrobial therapy, length of hospitalization, 1-month mortality, 1-month hospital readmission, and antibiotic-related adverse events. Findings The analysis included six RCTs involving 2,087 patients. Multiplex PCR-guided therapy showed a modest but non-significant reduction in antibiotic duration (MD -0.74 days; 95% CI: -2.28 to 0.79; p = 0.22). No statistically significant differences were found for secondary outcomes, including targeted or appropriate antimicrobial therapy, length of hospitalization, antibiotic-related adverse events, 1-month mortality, or 1-month hospital readmissions. Conclusions Multiplex PCR panels provide rapid diagnostic data, but the available randomized evidence provides insufficient evidence that their implementation reduces total antibiotic duration or downstream clinical outcomes in patients with pneumonia. These findings do not exclude potential benefits in earlier antimicrobial optimization, which appear to depend on clinical context and implementation strategy.

title: Glycerin suppositories as inexpensive multi-sequence MRI skin markers.
authors: Blum A, Clara M, Taihi A, Noureddine R, Teixeira PG, Boubaker F, Gillet R.
abstract: Objective To assess MRI conspicuity and clinical usability of a commercially available glycerin suppository as a low-cost skin marker for musculoskeletal MRI across routine sequences. Materials and methods A glycerin suppository was compared in vivo with vitamin E, water, olive oil, and diluted gadoteric acid solution across routine musculoskeletal MRI sequences. Conspicuity was scored independently by two musculoskeletal radiologists on a 4-point ordinal scale. Clinical usability was retrospectively assessed in 130 examinations at 1.5 and 3 T. One fat-sensitive image set (conventional T1-weighted or Dixon fat-only) and one fluid-sensitive set were scored independently by two readers. Scores of 2 or higher defined usability. Inter-reader agreement was assessed with Cohen kappa. Results Experimentally, the glycerin suppository showed the most consistent multi-sequence visibility among the tested markers. Unlike vitamin E markers, it remained highly conspicuous on fat-suppressed T1-weighted, fat-suppressed T2-weighted, and Dixon water-only images; it remained visible on STIR but showed lower conspicuity on Dixon fat-only images. Packaging did not affect visibility. Clinically, the marker was usable on both image sets in 123/130 examinations (94.6%) for reader 1 and 120/130 (92.3%) for reader 2. Usability on conventional T1-weighted images was 100% for both readers but decreased on Dixon fat-only reconstructions to 80.0% and 66.7%, respectively. Weighted kappa was 0.90 for fat-sensitive and 0.88 for fluid-sensitive scores. No marker-related image-quality degradation occurred. Conclusion Glycerin suppositories are inexpensive, disposable MRI skin markers with broad sequence visibility. Their limitation is reduced conspicuity on Dixon fat-only reconstructions.

title: Functional Outcomes After Total Ankle Replacement: A Forgotten Joint Score-12 Analysis With Up to 10-Year Follow-up.
authors: Shetty CB, Wales K, Shah K, Ramanathan AK.
abstract: BackgroundTotal ankle replacement (TAR) offers pain relief and preservation of motion in patients with end-stage ankle arthritis. The Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12) is a validated patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) designed to assess joint awareness, but data in TAR remain limited.MethodsA retrospective study of all TARs performed at our institution between 2014 and 2023 was conducted. Patients with a minimum of 2 years of follow-up were contacted by telephone, and the FJS-12 was administered. Mean follow-up was 4.83 ± 2.48 years (range 2-10). Demographics, surgical details, and complications were recorded. Statistical analyses explored factors associated with FJS-12 scores. At the end of FJS-12 administration, patients graded their satisfaction on a 4-point Likert scale.ResultsOf 102 ankles screened, 81 patients were eligible (mean age 69.7 years; mean body mass index [BMI] 31.3). Female sex (P = .008), right-sided TAR (P = .004), and additional tendo-Achilles lengthening (P = .004) were associated with lower FJS-12 scores. Scores declined at 3 years post-surgery (P = .011). Other factors, including BMI, smoking, and hypertension, had no significant impact. Based on the score distribution and satisfaction analysis, the Patient Acceptable Symptom State (PASS) threshold corresponded to an FJS-12 of 43, and the forgotten-joint threshold to 85.ConclusionTotal ankle replacement provided favorable short- to mid-term functional outcomes, as measured by the FJS-12. The FJS-12 is a sensitive PROM that detects subtle differences in patient-reported outcomes and may be a useful adjunct in routine TAR follow-up. We propose preliminary TAR-specific PASS and forgotten-joint thresholds that closely match those reported for knee replacement and are lower than those for hip replacement. These thresholds provide clinically meaningful benchmarks for patient satisfaction and should be validated in larger, prospective, multicentre cohorts.Level of Evidence:Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Female Sex Is Independently Associated With Greater Sagittal Tibial Tubercle-Trochlear Groove Distance and Patellar Tilt in High-Grade Trochlear Dysplasia.
authors: Hartmann M, Caliskan B, Ackermann J, Fucentese SF.
abstract: Purpose To assess sex-related differences in patellofemoral (PF) anatomy among patients with PF instability and high-grade trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types B-D). Methods Consecutive patients with symptomatic PF instability and high-grade trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types B-D) who were scheduled for surgical treatment between January 2010 and December 2020 and had available preoperative radiographs and magnetic resonance imaging were retrospectively identified at a single center. Patients with normal trochlear morphology, type A dysplasia, missing preoperative magnetic resonance imaging, or prior osseous procedures were excluded. Standardized magnetic resonance imaging-based measurements were obtained for trochlear morphology, tibial tubercle position, and patellar geometry. Depending on data distribution, parametric or nonparametric tests were used to compare sexes. Multivariate linear mixed-effects models were performed to calculate regression coefficients ( B ) with 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for patient clustering, age, body height, supratrochlear spur height, Caton-Deschamps index, sulcus depth, and tibiofemoral rotation. Results A total of 301 knees from 278 patients were analyzed; 192 knees (63.8%) were from female patients. The mean age was 22.6 ± 8.1 years (range, 11-50 years), and the mean body mass index was 24.9 ± 5.5 (range, 16.4-48.1). Distribution according to the Dejour classification was 40.5% type B, 31.2% type C, and 28.2% type D. Female patients showed smaller patellar width (37.9 ± 3.4 mm vs 41.3 ± 4.1 mm; P P P = .001) and sagittal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (sTTTG) distance (9.9 ± 5.2 mm vs 8.4 ± 6.0 mm; P = .005). After adjustment for age and body height, differences in patellar width, patellar thickness, patellar tilt, and sTTTG remained significant. After additional adjustment for supratrochlear spur height, Caton-Deschamps index, sulcus depth, and tibiofemoral rotation, patellar tilt ( B = 3.51°, P = .021) and sTTTG distance ( B = 2.36 mm, P = .004) remained greater in female patients. Conclusions Among patients with PF instability and high-grade trochlear dysplasia, female sex was associated with greater patellar tilt and sTTTG distance after adjustment for age, body height, and relevant anatomical covariates. Level of evidence Level III, prognostic retrospective comparative study.

title: Evolution from Platysma Myectomy to Myotomy: Preserving Lower Lip Function in Facial Synkinesis.
authors: Johansen CF, Bhatia SS, Har-Shai L, Rozen SM.
abstract: Background Platysma hypertonicity, a sequela of facial synkinesis (FS), is treated with platysma myectomy. However, its close relationship to the facial nerve's cervical branch raises concern for postoperative lower lip dysfunction. This study compares lower lip outcomes following platysma myectomy, platysma myotomy at the thyroid cartilage level, and no platysma intervention. Methods Included were FS patients who underwent selective neurectomies and ipsilateral depressor anguli oris myectomy (NDAO) between 2019 and 2025. Mean follow-up was 12 months. Patient groups included NDAO (n=27), NDAO with platysma myectomy (n=19), and NDAO with platysma myotomy (n=10). Pre and postoperative commissure position, lower lip height, lower lip inclination angle, and lower quadrant dental show were measured using Emotrics and ImageJ. Results Patients were on average 52 years old. The NDAO group improved significantly across all outcomes (p ≤ 0.004); the myotomy group improved in inclination and dental show (p ≤ 0.014); the myectomy group showed no significant improvement. The myotomy group outperformed the myectomy group across all measures (p ≤ 0.006) and had better commissure position and dental show than the NDAO group (p ≤ 0.045). The NDAO group had significantly better lower lip height, inclination, and dental show than the myectomy group (p ≤ 0.018). Conclusions Selective neurectomies with DAO myectomy alone and with platysma myotomy were associated with improved lower lip outcomes. Platysma myectomy was associated with postoperative lower lip elevation, consistent with possible cervical branch injury. Both platysmal approaches target cervical symptoms while the platysma myotomy also preserves lower lip position.

title: Endoscopically Assisted Periacetabular Osteotomy for Treatment of Hip Dysplasia: The Orthopaedic Total Extraperitoneal Approach.
authors: Öztürk V, Çelik M, Çağdaşer S, Hürmeydan ÖM, Aslantaş FÇ, Kural C, Bilgili MG.
abstract: The orthopaedic total extraperitoneal (O-TEP) approach is an endoscopic technique that has recently emerged as an option, particularly for the surgical management of pelvic and acetabular fractures. Unlike conventional orthopaedic endoscopic procedures, O-TEP was developed by adapting the laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal approach, commonly used for inguinal hernia repair, to orthopaedic surgery. In technically demanding procedures such as periacetabular osteotomy (PAO), minimizing soft-tissue dissection and directly visualizing critical neurovascular structures are essential. Owing to its minimally invasive design, the O-TEP PAO technique is intended to limit soft-tissue dissection while enabling direct visualization of key vascular and neural structures at risk. This Technical Note provides a step-by-step description of O-TEP PAO technique for acetabular dysplasia and discusses its feasibility, potential advantages, and key limitations in the context of the current literature on endoscopy-assisted PAO techniques.

title: Employers' Perceptions of Costs & Benefits to Mitigate Against Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) in the Workplace: A Qualitative Study.
journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
authors: Huỳnh TB, Moore KG, Sembajwe G, Dale AM, Ball C, Dinehart T, Zalizniak J, Parvanta C.
abstract: Objective To explore employers' mitigation strategies against Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 28 US employers to understand how the pandemic impacted their business operations, mitigation strategies implemented, and the utility of their emergency preparedness plans. Results Employers reported significant operational and financial challenges implementing COVID-19 mitigations including engineering and administrative controls, particularly policies around social distance, remote work, use of personal protective equipment (PPE), and vaccinations. Except for healthcare organizations, most large-sized firms had emergency preparedness plans, but these lacked infectious diseases components. Many small businesses had neither emergency nor infectious disease plans. Conclusions Our study highlighted gaps in emergency preparedness among employers, particularly small businesses. Employee resistance to new policies in future epidemics may be mitigated by ongoing employee engagement and leadership support within a company's existing safety culture.

title: Effect of Skin Pigmentation and Implantation Depth on Fluorescence-Based Oxygen Sensing in Ex Vivo Human Skin.
authors: Ibrahim MM, Kareem S, Elhessy A, Rasko YM, Mureau MAM.
abstract: Background Tissue oxygenation is crucial in reconstructive surgery, particularly when assessing flap viability. Current optical monitoring technologies, such as near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and indocyanine green (ICG) dyes, encounter challenges due to variable signal strength influenced by skin pigmentation and tissue depth. Oxygen monitoring methods based on fluorescence lifetime could provide a more reliable and consistent alternative. Methods Benzoporphyrin-based oxygen sensors incorporated into polyHEMA hydrogel were assessed in ex vivo human skin representing all six Fitzpatrick skin types. We measured fluorescence intensity and lifetime at both intradermal and subcutaneous depths with controlled oxygen concentrations (100% and 12%). Additionally, sensor performance was tested across physiological ranges of temperature and pH to evaluate environmental robustness. Results We demonstrated that fluorescence lifetime measurements were consistent throughout all Fitzpatrick skin types at both intradermal and subcutaneous depths, while showing minimal sensitivity to pigmentation or implantation depth. In contrast, the absolute fluorescence intensity decreased with more skin pigmentation and demonstrated variability. Tissue oxygen tension (TOT) derived from lifetime measurements has significantly decreased under hypoxic conditions (12% oxygen) for all Fitzpatrick skin types, which confirms dependable oxygen responsiveness. Additionally, sensor performance remained consistent and stable within physiological temperature and pH ranges. Conclusions Fluorescence lifetime sensing demonstrated stable and consistent performance across varying skin pigmentation and implantation depths under controlled ex vivo conditions. These findings support its potential as a pigmentation-independent sensing approach and provide a foundation for further in vivo validation. Future research in physiological and clinical models is needed to confirm performance under dynamic conditions.

title: Distal Pancreatectomy in Octogenarians and the Role of Robotic Surgery.
authors: Vallorani A, Hays SB, Kuchta KM, Ganguli S, Johnson C, Rojas A, Mehdi SA, Grandhi MS, Rieser CJ, Boone BA, Paniccia A, Polanco PM, Schmidt CR, Zeh HJ, Zureikat AH, Hogg ME.
abstract: Background A minimally invasive approach currently is the gold standard for distal pancreatectomy (DP). Robotic distal pancreatectomy (RDP) is increasingly adopted and offers technical advantages. As life expectancy rises, more octogenarians undergo pancreatic resection, and emerging evidence suggests minimally invasive approaches may benefit older adults. However, the role of RDP in this population remains underexplored. Methods A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study from four high-volume North American hepato-pancreatobiliary centers was conducted. Adults undergoing elective open distal pancreatectomy (ODP) or RDP between 2007 and 2023 were stratified as Results Of 797 patients undergoing DP, 62 were aged ≥ 80 years. Despite more comorbidities and higher PDAC rates, older patients had comparable perioperative outcomes. Blood loss, conversion, complications, length of stay, readmissions, and 90-day mortality were similar between age groups. On adjusted analysis, age ≥ 80 years was not associated with major complications or 90-day mortality in the overall cohort or PDAC subgroup. Whereas RDP was independently associated with fewer major complications, longer operative time and greater blood loss increased adverse outcomes. Among PDAC patients, perioperative and oncologic outcomes, including survival, were comparable across age groups. Conclusion Octogenarians achieve perioperative and oncologic outcomes comparable with those of younger patients when treated in high-volume centers, including survival. A robotic approach proved advantageous in reducing complications. The current findings reinforce the role of resection when indicated.

title: Diagnosis and Management of Quadrilateral Space Syndrome Using Arthroscopic, Extra-Capsular Axillary Nerve Release.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Whitelaw K, Vasquez D, Wiley N, Macksood J, Elhassan B, Lohre R.
abstract: Introduction Quadrilateral space syndrome (QSS) is an uncommon condition that can produce debilitating shoulder pain and dysfunction. Management has been mediated through various open and arthroscopic techniques, though cohort studies remain limited. Given the lack of literature covering QSS, the objective of this study is to characterize patient outcomes of arthroscopic axillary nerve release within the quadrilateral space. Our hypothesis is that quadrilateral space syndrome can be treated with an arthroscopic, all extra-capsular release to improve pain and measured patient reported outcome measures (PROMs). Materials & methods A retrospective chart review was performed of all patients diagnosed with quadrilateral space syndrome and receiving arthroscopic quadrilateral space release at a single institution performed by two surgeons between 2021 and 2024. Patient demographics, pre-and post-injection patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) and pre-and post-operative PROMs were collected. Results Sixty patients, each with one unique treated shoulder and no bilateral cases, were identified as receiving treatment for QSS. Of these, 40 (66.7%) underwent arthroscopic quadrilateral space release, while 20 (33.3%) received image-guided injection alone. The average follow-up of surgical patients was 29.5 +/- 15.6 months, with 17 patients completing greater than two-year follow-up. Forty patients (n=40/60; 66.7%) had prior ipsilateral shoulder surgery with an average of 2 +/- 3.5; range: 1-20) prior surgeries. Following arthroscopic release, VAS pain scores (7.0 +/- 2.1 vs 3.3 +/- 2.4; p Conclusion Arthroscopic, extracapsular axillary nerve release is effective at improving measurable pain and PROM measures with a low complication profile in short-term follow-up. Surgical pain relief was comparable to diagnostic injection.

title: Cryptotia Correction via V-Y Advancement Flap, Cartilage Z-Plasty, and Conchal Graft: A 20-Case Retrospective Study.
authors: Feng J, Jiang M, Zhi J, Zhang Y, Liu T, Wang B.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Open Reduction Internal Fixation Versus Radial Head Arthroplasty for Mason III/IV Radial Head Fractures: A Decision Analytic Markov Model.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Kumar R, Salman SG, Bouras A, Rice SW, Shen O, Cheng C, Bhashyam AR.
abstract: Background Mason type III and IV comminuted radial head fractures present a treatment dilemma between open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) and radial head arthroplasty (RHA). Functional outcomes, implant complications, and later treatment options vary across patients. We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of these strategies under explicit clinical and economic assumptions. Methods We constructed a 5-state Markov cost-utility model for a Mason III/IV fracture, using a 10-year horizon, 3% annual discounting, and US Medicare payment benchmarks. An illustrative base case used good outcome probabilities of 15/23 for ORIF and 20/22 for RHA. Time-zero allocation of follow-up outcomes, state utilities, and later transitions were assumptions. Index costs used verified 2025 Physician Fee Schedule and Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System rates. We performed one-way, probabilistic (10,000 iterations), breakeven, and structural sensitivity analyses. Results ORIF accrued $16,795 and 7.045 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs); RHA accrued $19,242 and 7.299 QALYs. RHA's incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was $9,627/QALY, with incremental net monetary benefit of $22,970 at $100,000/QALY. Allocating outcomes at year 2 yielded $14,880/QALY, assuming zero unmeasured early differential secondary-care costs. RHA was cost-effective in 94.6% of probabilistic iterations at $100,000/QALY. The breakeven ORIF good outcome probability was 85.7%. When initial clinical outcomes were equal, ORIF was less costly with equal QALYs. Conclusion The illustrative base case favored RHA under the assumed functional difference and utilities. Higher ORIF success, early convergence, or a treatment-specific utility burden could remove that preference. These conditional findings require validation with contemporary fracture-specific utility and treatment-pathway data. Level of evidence Level III; Economic and Decision Analysis.

title: Continuation of Clopidogrel in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Perioperative Bleeding and Cardiovascular Outcomes in a Consecutive Case Series.
authors: Abbaszadeh A, Mortazavi SMJ, Sahebi M, Ayati Firoozabadi M.
abstract: Background Perioperative clopidogrel management in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is challenging because interruption may increase thrombotic risk, whereas continuation may increase bleeding. Evidence remains limited. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 31 consecutive patients (35 knees) undergoing primary TKA while continuing clopidogrel 75 mg daily (April 2018-September 2019). A multidisciplinary team involving orthopaedic surgery, cardiology, and anesthesiology determined continuation. One senior surgeon performed all procedures using a tourniquet-free technique with intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid. All patients also received low-dose aspirin for at least 2 weeks postoperatively as venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Outcomes through 90 days included bleeding, transfusion, wound complications, infection, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events, symptomatic venous thromboembolism, and anesthesia-related complications. Results Mean age was 69 ± 6.4 years; mean estimated blood loss was 285 ± 95 mL, and mean hemoglobin decrease was 1.8 ± 0.6 g/dL. No transfusions or major bleeding occurred. Minor wound drainage followed 3 procedures (8.6%), and superficial cellulitis occurred in 1 knee (2.9%); no deep infections occurred. Four patients (12.9%) reported mild, nonspecific headaches; none met criteria for post-dural puncture headache. No clinical signs or symptoms suggestive of spinal hematoma or persistent neurologic deficit, and no myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death, were observed. Conclusions Clopidogrel continuation during primary TKA may be feasible in carefully selected patients receiving multidisciplinary assessment and multimodal blood management. The small sample, retrospective design, and absence of a control group preclude conclusions about comparative safety.

title: Component-specific institutional learning curve of intracorporeal urinary diversion during robot-assisted radical cystectomy: a risk-adjusted cumulative sum analysis.
authors: Fukata S, Ichimura N, Suzuki Y, Kohno S, Yoshimura R, Kurano Y, Shigehisa R, Atagi K, Takemori D, Shiba Y, Yamamoto S, Osakabe H, Nao T, Shimamoto T, Fukuhara H, Shimizu N, Ashida S, Karashima T, Inoue K.
abstract: The learning curve for intracorporeal urinary diversion (ICUD) during robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC) remains insufficiently defined. This study evaluated component-specific learning curves using risk-adjusted cumulative sum (RA-CUSUM) analysis. We retrospectively analyzed 137 consecutive RARC cases, including 80 ICUD cases and 57 extracorporeal ileal conduit diversion cases. Total operative, robotic console, cystectomy plus pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND), and ICUD times were evaluated using RA-CUSUM analysis. The ICUD cases were divided into learning and stabilization phases according to the transition point identified by RA-CUSUM analysis of ICUD time. Perioperative outcomes and factors associated with ICUD time were evaluated. The RA-CUSUM analysis identified transition points at the 38th ICUD case for ICUD time and at the 62nd, 64th, and 75th RARC cases for robotic console, cystectomy plus PLND, and total operative times, respectively. Conventional CUSUM analysis also identified case 38 as the transition point. Total operative, robotic console, and ICUD times were significantly shorter in the stabilization phase than in the learning phase (all P < 0.001), as was hospital stay (P = 0.002). Complication rates did not differ significantly between the phases. None of the six covariates included in the multivariable regression model were significantly associated with ICUD time. Recurrence-free and overall survival also did not differ between phases. ICUD time reached a transition point at the 38th case, whereas cystectomy plus PLND reached a transition point at the 64th RARC case. RA-CUSUM analysis may be useful for evaluating procedural maturation and guiding component-specific training during RARC.

title: Clinical Outcomes, Implant Survival, and Complications of Expandable Endoprostheses for Lower Limb Reconstruction in Skeletally Immature Patients with Bone Sarcoma: A Systematic Review and Single-Cohort Meta-Analysis.
authors: Piezzo M, Tinelli O, Malfi P, Garofalo R, Fazioli F, Pezzella R.
abstract: Background The management of malignant bone sarcomas in the lower extremities of skeletally immature children and adolescents remains a major challenge in orthopedic oncology. Expandable endoprostheses have become more popular over the last decades, but scientific data are limited. Methods To provide reliable data on functional outcomes, complications, and survival rates after this procedure, we conducted a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of prospective and retrospective studies. The primary objective was Musculoskeletal Tumor Society functional score. Secondary objectives included complications and survival rates. Risk of bias was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) tool. Results A total of 1055 patients from 27 studies met the eligibility criteria. Overall methodological quality was moderate, with a mean MINORS score of 10.44. The mean age at surgery was 10.0 years (range 2.0-16.0), and the median follow-up was 5.44 years (range 1.7-24.0). Osteosarcoma accounted for 88.0% of cases and Ewing sarcoma for 10.4%. The pooled estimate of Musculoskeletal Tumor Society score was 82.9 (95% confidence interval [CI] 80.5-85.3). The pooled complication rate was 58.0% (95% CI 48.0-67.0), with no significant difference between minimally invasive and non-invasive expansion mechanisms. According to the Henderson/International Society of Limb Salvage classification, type III structural failures were the most frequent failure mode in both minimally invasive and non-invasive cohorts. The pooled 5-year overall survival rate was 76.0% (95% CI 54.7-89.2). Conclusions This meta-analysis supports expandable endoprostheses as an effective limb-salvage option for skeletally immature patients with bone sarcoma, providing good functional outcomes and acceptable 5-year survival despite a high complication burden.

title: CORR Insights®: Disruption of Intrinsic Healing Elements Does Not Alter Early Functional or Mechanical Outcomes After Zone II Flexor Tendon Repair in a Large-animal Model.
authors: Beredjiklian PK.

title: Butterfly vertebral body with spinal epidermoid cyst: a rare case report and review of the literature.
authors: Ren S, Shao L, Cai Y, Zhang X, Gao X, Sun Y.
abstract: Butterfly vertebrae and congenital spinal epidermoid cysts are embryonic spinal disorders, and their occurrence is closely related to tissue remnants during embryonic development. Notably, although both conditions are extremely rare, they may occur simultaneously in clinical practice, suggesting a possible, albeit hypothetical, spatiotemporal correlation in their embryonic origin-that is, developmental abnormalities during the somite differentiation and process of neural tube closure in the 3rd to 5th gestational weeks may simultaneously affect the formation of mesodermal vertebrae and the separation of ectodermal tissues. We report a rare case of concurrent T12 butterfly vertebra deformity and intradural extramedullary epidermoid cyst at the same spinal level, and explore their potential embryological correlation. A 43-year-old female with progressive lower extremity weakness and low back pain underwent imaging (X-ray, CT, MRI) confirming T12 butterfly vertebra and a spinal canal mass. Surgical intervention included posterior laminectomy, cyst resection, and spinal fixation. Histopathology confirmed epidermoid cyst diagnosis. To the best of our knowledge, this study reports the first case of concurrent butterfly vertebra (mesodermal origin) and spinal epidermoid cyst (ectodermal origin) at the same vertebral level. This unique coexistence provides a distinctive paradigm for investigating mesodermal-ectodermal interactions during spinal development. Identifying butterfly vertebrae warrants intraspinal screening for coexisting developmental anomalies to prevent potential irreversible neurological deficits.

title: Boxing Medicine Beyond the Ringside.
authors: Houser A, Pate C, Jovan J, Park S.
abstract: Boxing is widely regarded as one of the oldest and most physically demanding sports, dating back to 3000 BC, and it first appeared at the modern Olympics in 1904. Boxers require a multidisciplinary approach to healthcare, and this review focuses on care beyond the ringside. Chronic injuries, particularly involving the upper extremity, require individualized management plans to get the athlete back into the ring on fight night. Team physician-guided return to play for boxers with concussions is another evolving pillar of boxing medicine. Weight management and nutrition are critical yet often underappreciated aspects of performance and safety, with attention to safe weight-cutting practices and hydration. Finally, the psychological toll of training, competition, and postcareer transition underscores the need for integrated mental health support. This review aims to synthesize current evidence and best practices in boxing medicine and to advocate for a comprehensive, athlete-centered approach that extends well beyond the ring.

title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and pain prognosis after interventional treatment for herpes zoster-associated neuralgia.
authors: Liu Z, Mao J, Xv H, Wang P, Gong D.
abstract: Background Pain outcomes after interventional treatment for herpes zoster-associated neuralgia (HZAN) vary substantially, and reliable prognostic markers remain limited. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance, but its association with pain prognosis after interventional procedures for HZAN is unknown. Methods In this retrospective study, patients with HZAN who underwent interventional pain procedures were included. The TyG index was calculated from fasting triglyceride and glucose levels and analyzed as both a continuous variable and by quartiles. Poor pain prognosis at 3 months after discharge was defined using a composite outcome reflecting clinically meaningful pain persistence and impact. Multivariable logistic regression models with incremental adjustment were constructed. To explore potential dose-response associations, restricted cubic spline models were constructed. In addition, prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted to explore potential effect modification across clinical subgroups. Results Among 345 patients, 86 (24.9%) met the composite endpoint for poor pain prognosis. After adjustment for clinically relevant covariates, each one-unit increase in TyG was associated with greater odds of poor pain prognosis (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 1.99, 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.25-3.18]). The adjusted OR for the highest versus lowest TyG quartile was 2.62 (95% CI [1.19-5.77]). The sensitivity analysis using a numeric rating scale (NRS) ≥4 at 3 months as the sole outcome yielded a similar association (adjusted OR 1.87, 95% CI [1.15-3.05]). Restricted cubic spline analysis found no evidence of nonlinearity, and subgroup analyses provided no statistically significant evidence of effect modification. Conclusions The TyG index demonstrates an independent association with pain prognosis after interventional treatment for HZAN, with a linear dose-response relationship. These findings support further investigation of TyG as a metabolic marker associated with pain prognosis, but do not establish its value for individual risk prediction.

title: Anticipating the future robotic surgeon: rethinking surgical expertise and education in an era of automation.
authors: Schouten AM, Arns KHHM, Boon WPC, van der Steeg AFW, Piscicelli L, Ivory C, Brinkman WM.
abstract: Increasing automation and artificial intelligence (AI) integration in robot-assisted surgery may reshape surgical expertise, professional responsibility, and education. This study explored how surgical expertise might evolve over the next ten years and identified educational priorities robust across multiple plausible futures. A qualitative Technology Foresight approach combined (1) 24 semi-structured interviews with surgeons and experts in robotics, AI, augmented reality, law, and medical technology; (2) observations of 18 surgical procedures (approximately 85 h); and (3) a six-participant expert workshop. Thematic analysis identified drivers, barriers, anticipated changes in surgical work, and critical uncertainties. These findings informed a scenario framework appraised and refined during the workshop. Technological autonomy and societal acceptance emerged as the two critical uncertainties, producing four scenarios: Augmented Surgery, Autonomous Surgery, Selective Adoption, and Capability Without Trust. In most scenarios, participants anticipated a shift in surgeons' roles from direct operators towards supervisors and coordinators of complex sociotechnical systems, while expecting responsibility for patient care to remain human. Four proposed educational priorities remained relevant across futures: maintaining low-frequency, safety-critical operative competencies; learning when to trust, challenge, or override intelligent systems; managing technological dependencies and multidisciplinary interactions; and developing adaptive expertise to evaluate and integrate emerging technologies throughout surgical careers. Automation may redefine rather than simply expand surgical expertise by separating direct action from professional responsibility. Surgical education should therefore extend beyond technical robotic proficiency to cultivate judgement, oversight, systems thinking, and adaptability. Professional societies, regulators, educators, and technology developers must align curricula, governance, and standards with these changing responsibilities.

title: An integrated thin-film microfluidic point-of-care testing system for rapid detection of Ureaplasma urealyticum in cervical swabs.
authors: Wang J, Zhu K, Xue M, Su F, Yang H, Liu X.
abstract: Objective Ureaplasma urealyticum (UU) is a common urogenital microorganism associated with a range of genitourinary and perinatal conditions; rapid and reliable detection is valuable in selected clinical contexts. However, traditional bacterial culture and PCR methods are limited by their speed and involve complex operating procedures. Methods We evaluated an integrated thin-film microfluidic sample-to-answer system (ingeDx) for nucleic acid-based detection of UU in cervical swab samples. The system integrates cell lysis, nucleic acid purification, amplification and detection, enabling rapid (~ 45 min for the entire process) analysis with Ct values consistent with standard quantitative PCR. Results The lowest concentration evaluated (200 copies/mL) was detected in 10 of 10 replicates, although a formal limit-of-detection determination was not performed. No cross-reactivity was observed with the 16 other common pathogens tested; the coefficient of variation of Ct values at the evaluated concentration was below 3%, and the cost per test remained below $1. Clinical validation on 113 cervical swab samples demonstrated strong agreement with a reference NMPA-registered real-time PCR kit: positive agreement 98.08% (95% CI: 89.88%-99.66%), negative agreement 95.08% (95% CI: 86.51%-98.31%), overall agreement 96.46% (95% CI: 91.25%-98.61%), and Kappa 0.929 (95% CI: 0.861-0.997); the AUC for UU was above 0.98. Conclusions This system may be well suited for primary healthcare, epidemic response, and resource-limited settings, offering an efficient solution to enhance diagnostics and reduce patient waiting time and supporting timely responses to public health needs.

title: Altered mechanical and vascular responses of the Achilles tendon to acute loading in Kendo athletes.
authors: Iwamoto N, Nakamura C, Takahashi H.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to elucidate acute, bilateral Achilles tendon (AT) responses to high-intensity single-leg hopping in Kendo athletes and healthy controls. Materials and methods Twenty Kendo athletes and 20 sedentary controls performed a single-leg hopping task. Ultrasound imaging assessed AT anteroposterior diameter (APD), shear wave velocity (SWV), and intratendinous vessel count before (PRE), immediately after (POST), and 5-min post-exercise (POST5). Results Following exercise, Kendo athletes exhibited a significant main effect of time for both APD (P = 0.012) and SWV (P = 0.012), regardless of side. No significant acute changes in APD or SWV were observed in the control group. For intratendinous vascularity, a significant side-by-time interaction was observed in Kendo athletes (P = 0.026): the right leg showed no significant change, whereas the left leg exhibited a progressive increase from PRE to POST (P Conclusion Within Kendo athletes, morphological and mechanical responses occurred bilaterally, whereas the temporal vascular response differed between the left and right Achilles tendons. However, this side-specific vascular pattern was not shown to differ significantly from that observed in sedentary controls.

title: Aggressive distal tibial giant cell tumour with early recurrence, adjacent bone involvement and limb length restoration using distraction osteogenesis.
authors: M P, Siddartha S A, B G, N P, J S R G S, Gupta V.

title: A Review of Platelet-Rich Plasma as Treatment for Partial Elbow Ulnar Collateral Ligament Tears.
authors: Fogel AJ, Goli P, Yaeger LH, Baker M, Hartman JA, Smith MV, Hollabaugh WL.
abstract: Platelet-rich plasma injections are increasingly utilized for partial-thickness ulnar collateral ligament tears in throwing athletes. This narrative review evaluates platelet-rich plasma's efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness for partial ulnar collateral ligament tears using literature from 2020 to 2026. A systematic search identified four studies, including cohorts and an economic simulation model. The largest cohort demonstrated that 60% of athletes with partial tears returned to play when platelet-rich plasma was combined with rehabilitation. Smaller case series reported successful return to play with similar treatment, though limited by a lack of comparison groups and small sample sizes. Complications included ulnar nerve dysfunction, particularly in athletes with preexisting nerve instability. Early surgery was often more cost-effective for long-term career durability. Current evidence suggests platelet-rich plasma alongside rehabilitation may benefit select athletes with partial ulnar collateral ligament injuries but is limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous protocols, and inconsistent outcome measures. Future research is needed regarding patient selection and standardized treatment protocols.

title: Tibial Condylar Valgus Osteotomy Combined With Inverted V-Shaped High Tibial Osteotomy.
authors: Nakayama H, Yasuda K, Kondo E, Yonekura A, Tachibana T, Yoshiya S, Iseki T.
abstract: In constructing surgical strategies for correction of varus deformity in osteoarthritic knees, both bony and intra-articular deformities should be taken into consideration. Bony deformity is corrected by high tibial osteotomy (HTO), whereas intra-articular deformity associated with increased joint line convergence angle can be addressed by tibial condylar valgus osteotomy (TCVO). In the TCVO procedure, the medial tibial joint line is elevated by an L-shaped osteotomy. A surgical procedure combining open-wedge HTO and TCVO has been reported before. Although this combined procedure can address both bony and articular deformities, correction of severe bony deformity by open-wedge HTO with large wedge opening may induce problems of unacceptable joint line obliquity and increase in leg length. In this situation, inverted V-shaped HTO reported by Aoki and Kondo can be an alternative option. The inverted V-shaped HTO procedure is designed to combine hemiclosed and hemiopen osteotomies. However, the correction is made near the center of rotation of tibial angulation, and wedge width can be reduced compared with other HTO procedures; potential problems associated with conventional HTO can be avoided. In this paper, the surgical rationale and sequence of combined TCVO and inverted V-shaped HTO for correction of severe varus deformity are described.

title: The Impact of Rurality on the Standard of Care for Hip Fracture Patients: An ANZHFR Study.
authors: Hurst KP, Fielding K, Hoque S, Wall C, Maguire R, Seal A.
abstract: Background Hip fracture care requires timely, multi-disciplinary management. This study examined whether rural hospital location was associated with adherence to the Australian Hip Fracture Clinical Care Standard (HFCCS). Methods Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry data from 2018 to 2023 were analysed for patients aged ≥ 50 years. Hospitals were classified using the Modified Monash Model as metropolitan (MM1-2) or rural (MM3-7). Patients transferred before surgery were excluded from the primary analysis and examined separately. Missing data were addressed using multiple imputation. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex and ASA classification. Results The primary analysis included 58 757 patients (50 727 metropolitan; 8030 rural). Metropolitan hospitals had higher adherence to cognitive assessment (72.8% vs. 68.1%), nerve block administration (94.0% vs. 91.2%), delirium assessment (76.2% vs. 70.1%), surgery within 48 h (80.3% vs. 78.7%), mobilisation within 24 h (92.9% vs. 90.9%) and secondary fracture prevention (81.3% vs. 69.8%) (all p Conclusion Rural hospital location was associated with lower adherence to several HFCCS indicators, particularly cognitive and delirium assessment, early mobilisation and secondary fracture prevention, while timely analgesia was more frequent in rural hospitals. Geographical variation in guideline-based hip fracture care persists in Australia and warrants further investigation.

title: Safety and Operative Burden of Immediate Lymphatic Reconstruction During Breast Cancer Surgery With Concurrent Breast Reconstruction: A 13‐Year ACS‐NSQIP Analysis
authors: Karamitros G, Bouloukakis G, Perdikis G, Rasko Y, Kokosis G, Skoracki R, Lamaris G.

title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy Decreases the Odds of Developing Soft-Tissue Disorders of the Shoulder in Perimenopausal Women.
authors: Shah IK, Shah AK, Burkhart RJ, Dannacher CA, Desai NN, Calcei JG, Campbell AL.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether perimenopausal women receiving menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) have decreased odds of developing soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with women without an active MHT prescription, specifically adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, bicipital tendinitis, calcific tendinitis, atraumatic rotator cuff tear/rupture, and shoulder impingement syndrome and to quantify the impact of differing formulations and administration route. Methods The TriNetX US Collaborative Research Network, a deidentified database of over 180 million patients, was queried on June 11, 2026. Women aged 40 to 60 years in a menopausal state were identified by International Classification of Diseases code N95.1 and primary ovarian insufficiency by International Classification of Diseases code E28.3. Patients were grouped by MHT prescription status. Patients were one-to-one propensity-matched on age, race, ethnicity, and metabolic disease status, with standardized mean difference less than 0.1.
