The odds of developing soft-tissue shoulder disorders were studied, with P values less than .05 considered statistically significant. Results A total of 296,992 patients were included. The index the mean age was 49.1 years, 74.5% to 74.6% were White, 6% were Hispanic/Latino, 9% were African American, and 4.1% were Asian. Women prescribed any form of systemic MHT showed significantly lower odds of developing adhesive capsulitis (odds ratio [OR] 0.875, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.786-0.973; P = .014), bicipital tendinitis (OR 0.775, 95% CI 0.669-0.898; P = .001), calcific tendinitis (OR 0.829, 95% CI 0.706-0.974; P = .023), shoulder impingement syndrome (OR 0.873, 95% CI 0.792-0.962; P = .006), and rotator cuff tear/rupture (OR 0.892, 95% CI 0.804-0.991; P = .032). Topical estrogen specifically was associated with decreased odds of developing adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, bicipital tendinitis, shoulder impingement syndrome, and rotator cuff tear/rupture. Conclusions In peri- and postmenopausal women, MHT use was associated with decreased odds of soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with individuals not using MHT. Topical estrogen was more closely associated with reduced odds of soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with oral estrogen and oral combined formulations. Level of evidence Level III, therapeutic retrospective comparative study.

title: Evaluation of a Fascial Sling Technique for Primary Modiolus Reconstruction to Preserve Lip Symmetry Following Head and Neck Free Flap Surgery: A Preliminary Report
authors: Omine F, Sasaki K, Oshima J, Hanihara H, Aihara Y, Shibuya Y, Sekido M.

title: Diamond-Unit Crisscross Mattress Suture for Double-Row Rotator Cuff Repair: An All-Arthroscopic Technique.
authors: Wang XH, Fang C, Yu G, Wang YM, Zhao QC.
abstract: This article describes the diamond-unit crisscross mattress suture technique for double-row rotator cuff repair using an all-arthroscopic approach. This method combines knotted fixation at the medial row and knotless fixation, offering uniform tendon footprint coverage while reducing anchor usage. The technique is straightforward to perform and does not require additional sutures. By using a single lateral-row anchor, it improves the contact and stability between the tendon and bone. This technique is intended for selected small- to medium-sized tears, particularly those with irregular or degenerative margins.

title: Association of Subscapularis Tear Severity With Posterosuperior Cuff Tear Morphology in a Combined‐Tear Surgical Cohort: A Retrospective Cross‐Sectional Study
authors: Bircan R, Kaya İ, Yaş S, Çalta M, Eren T, Kanatlı U.

title: Association of Subscapularis Tear Severity With Posterosuperior Cuff Tear Morphology in a Combined-Tear Surgical Cohort: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Bircan R, Kaya İ, Yaş S, Çalta MŞ, Eren TK, Kanatlı U.
abstract: Objectives In combined tears, the relationship between posterosuperior cuff tear (PSCT) morphology and subscapularis (SSC) tear severity is unknown. This study aimed to determine whether PSCT morphology is associated with SSC tear severity, which morphologies are associated with complete SSC rupture, and whether any association is confined to a particular severity threshold and persists after accounting for classification uncertainty and overall cuff extent. Methods A retrospective review of 368 patients who underwent arthroscopic surgery for combined, chronic, full-thickness PSCTs with concomitant SSC tears between 2016 and 2023 was conducted. High-resolution preoperative MRI and high-definition intraoperative video recordings were used to classify PSCT morphology (crescent, U-shaped, anterior L-shaped, posterior L-shaped, massive-retracted) and SSC tears (Lafosse Types I-V). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for both classifications. Binary logistic regression (adjusted for age, sex, side, and BMI) was used to evaluate associations with complete subscapularis rupture (Lafosse IV/V). Results The mean patient age was 60.3 ± 9.2 years. PSCT morphology was significantly associated with SSC tear severity (Monte Carlo P less than 0.001; Cramer's V 0.234). The proportion with complete SSC rupture rose from 23.8% in posterior L-shaped and 25.6% in crescent tears to 39.6% in U-shaped, 60.9% in anterior L-shaped, and 71.4% in massive-retracted tears. Complete subscapularis rupture was significantly more likely in anterior L-shaped (adjusted OR 4.50, 95% CI 1.86 to 11.41) and massive-retracted morphologies (adjusted OR 7.12, 95% CI 2.24 to 27.17), both surviving correction (adjusted p = 0.003). Posterior L-shaped and U-shaped morphologies showed no significant difference from crescent tears. Conclusion In surgically treated combined tears, PSCT morphology shows a graded association with SSC tear severity that is concentrated in the anterior L-shaped and massive-retracted morphology patterns. However, because most complete ruptures overall occurred within crescent tears due to their high prevalence, morphology alone cannot serve as a definitive diagnostic rule-out tool. Nevertheless, anterior L-shaped or massive-retracted PSCT patterns warrant systematic inspection of the SSC.

title: Arthroscopic Supraspinatus Repair With Bioinductive and Mechanical Reinforcement Using a Biocomposite Scaffold.
authors: Gomez G, Capasso M, Gomez GM, Bourlot D, Colombo P, Aguirre Trujillo KF.
abstract: Rotator cuff repair failure remains a major challenge, particularly in large, chronic, and revision supraspinatus tears. Structural failure is multifactorial and involves both mechanical insufficiency and compromised biologic healing capacity. Retear rates in large and massive tears have been reported between 20% and 70%. Biocomposite-reinforced scaffolds have been introduced to address both mechanical and biologic limitations. BioBrace (CONMED, Largo, FL) consists of a porous type I collagen matrix reinforced with resorbable poly-L-lactic acid microfilaments, designed to provide load-sharing support while promoting tissue ingrowth. This technical note describes a stepwise arthroscopic double-row supraspinatus repair incorporating a bioinductive and mechanically reinforced scaffold.

title: Arthroscopic Bone Xenograft Augmentation for Glenoid Bone Deficiency and Recurrent Anterior Shoulder Instability Improves Functional Outcomes Despite Graft Nonunion.
authors: Russo R, Fedele A, Rossi V, Russo F, Russo C, Francesco DP, Gigante AP, Guastafierro A.
abstract: Purpose To analyze the healing of equine-derived xenograft bone blocks with the native glenoid using computed tomography (CT) and to evaluate clinical outcomes in patients undergoing arthroscopic bone block stabilization with xenograft, Bankart repair, and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis for recurrent anterior shoulder instability with glenoid bone loss. Methods Patients with recurrent anterior shoulder instability and glenoid bone loss between 12.5% and 25% who underwent arthroscopic equine-derived xenograft bone block augmentation combined with Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis between 2019 and 2023 were identified. Minimum clinical and radiological follow-up was 24 months. Xenograft healing was evaluated on serial CT scans, and clinical outcomes were assessed using Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index, Rowe, quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand, and visual analog scale scores. Results A total of 76 patients (72 men, 4 women) met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed, with a mean clinical follow-up of 50.7 months (range, 24-75 months). Radiological follow-up on CT averaged 46.1 months (range, 24-72 months). All patients underwent CT imaging according to the study protocol. Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index improved from 1335.7 ± 136.8 to 134.6 ± 138.2 ( P P P P Conclusions Despite the lack of radiographic union, most patients treated with arthroscopic bone xenograft plus Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis showed functional improvements surpassing the MCID threshold at a minimum 2-year follow-up. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

title: Arthroscopic Anatomic Glenoid Reconstruction With Distal Tibial Allograft and Remplissage Suture Staple Procedure in the Beach-Chair Position.
authors: Wagala NN, Lurie B, Sliepka JM, Zhang AL.
abstract: Critical bone loss in patients with recurrent shoulder instability is often addressed with bone block procedures such as glenoid reconstruction. Various bone block procedures and techniques currently exist to address glenoid bone loss; however, the addition of remplissage may be frequently overlooked despite concomitant engaging or off-track Hill-Sachs defects. Recent biomechanical studies suggest that the addition of remplissage may improve shoulder stability after glenoid reconstruction. This technique highlights an efficient method for addressing glenoid bone loss with arthroscopic anatomic glenoid reconstruction using distal tibia allograft as well as Hill-Sachs lesions with knotless remplissage suture staple procedure in the beach-chair position.

title: Anatomic Triple-Bundle Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Technique With Three Femoral Tunnels and Three Tibial Tunnels Using Hamstring Tendon.
authors: Shammas BM, Jasim A M.
abstract: Reconstruction of the anterior cruciate ligament is a common procedure for athletes with the aim of returning to sports activities. Despite improved surgical techniques and rehabilitation, the return-to-sport rate and retear rates remain unsatisfactory. Some centers in Japan and India nowadays have resorted to triple-bundle anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction to solve these issues. We described a technique for triple-bundle anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with three femur tunnels and three tibial tunnels using hamstring tendon.

title: An Adaptive Knee Brace Is Associated With Improved Dynamic Stabilization Compared With a Standard Passive Brace in Anterior Cruciate Ligament-Deficient Men During a Functional Hop Task.
authors: Greenberg S, Gottlieb R.
abstract: Purpose To compare the dynamic knee stabilization effects of an adaptive dynamic brace (ADB) with those of a standard passive brace in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)-deficient men. Methods ACL-deficient participants were included. The subjects performed 3 single-leg functional hop tests: drop jump, crossover hop, and 90° rotational hop. Each task was performed once while wearing the ADB and once while wearing a traditional passive brace. Three-dimensional kinematic data were collected using an 8-camera optoelectronic motion-capture system. Repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to evaluate the effects of brace condition and time. An a priori power analysis indicated that a minimum of 12 participants were required. Results Twelve ACL-deficient participants were included (age: 30.2 ± 3.4 years; time since injury: 32 ± 6 months; ACL-Return to Sport after Injury score: 70 ± 3). No significant differences in knee flexion angles were observed between braces. Knee flexion during landing was significantly lower in the crossover hop compared with the drop jump and rotational hop tasks ( P P P P P Conclusions The ADB showed improved dynamic stabilization particularly during high-risk landing and rotational movement compared with a standard passive brace. Clinical relevance The ADB may enhance the effectiveness of rehabilitation strategies in ACL-deficient individuals by improving dynamic knee stability during functional activities.

title: When does robotics add value in splenic surgery? From total splenectomy to precision and function-oriented spleen preservation.
authors: Gao T, Zhang S, Yin Y, Luo Z, Zhao Y.
abstract: Robotic platforms are increasingly used for technically demanding splenic dissection and spleen-preserving procedures, yet their incremental clinical value over conventional laparoscopy remains uncertain. The clinical rationale for preserving splenic tissue is distinct from the question of whether robotic assistance improves outcomes; evidence supporting spleen preservation should not itself be interpreted as evidence of robotic superiority. This structured narrative review, informed by a PRISMA 2020-reported search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science Core Collection, examines the settings in which robotics may offer additional value across routine and complex total splenectomy, precise hilar dissection, and partial splenectomy. Potential technical advantages are considered against implementation burden, including operative time, platform cost, team training, and emergency-conversion requirements. Three-dimensional vascular reconstruction, intraoperative ultrasonography, and indocyanine green fluorescence imaging are discussed as enabling technologies within an Anatomy-Perfusion-Function framework that distinguishes anatomical preservation, perfusion preservation, and functional preservation. Direct evidence remains dominated by retrospective cohorts, small series, and technical reports; data from pancreatic and gastric surgery provide only indirect support for precise splenic hilar manipulation. Given the heterogeneity and predominantly non-randomized nature of the available evidence, current findings support selective, scenario-specific use rather than claims of general robotic superiority. Future studies should compare platforms within the same clinical indication and complexity stratum while assessing perioperative outcomes, functional endpoints, and resource use together.

title: Understanding acceptance before intervention: patient perspectives on robotic-assisted femoral neck fracture fixation.
authors: Al-Smadi F, Abudourusuli X, Yang H, Al-Smadi S, Liao J, Ouyang L, Zhang Z, Zeng R, Mi B, Xie X, Liu M, Liu G.
abstract: Patient acceptance is important for surgical robotics implementation, but evidence in acute orthopaedic trauma is limited. We examined preoperative acceptance of robotic-assisted femoral neck fracture fixation and factors associated with behavioral intention. This prospective multicenter observational study included 378 adults with femoral neck fractures assessed before definitive fixation technique selection. A Chinese-adapted questionnaire assessed six acceptance constructs and behavioral intention. Multivariable linear regression with heteroskedasticity-consistent type 3 (HC3) robust standard errors examined associations with intention, while logistic regression assessed factors associated with post-introduction self-reported understanding of the robot's role. Performance expectancy (B = 0.524; 95% CI, 0.391-0.657; P < 0.001), social influence (B = 0.262; 95% CI, 0.151-0.373; P < 0.001), and pleasure (B = 0.159; 95% CI, 0.038-0.281; P = 0.010) were associated with greater intention. In a separate contextual model, prior knowledge of femoral neck fracture surgical techniques (B = 0.905), self-reported understanding (B = 0.540), and robotic-option offering (B = 0.545) were positively associated with intention, whereas additional-cost concern was inversely associated (B = - 0.242). The association with robotic-option offering was not significant in a restricted-center analysis (B = 0.447; P = 0.125). Prior knowledge (aOR = 7.46; 95% CI, 4.01-13.89) and robotic-option offering (aOR = 2.54; 95% CI, 1.15-5.61) were associated with self-reported understanding. Acceptance of robotic-assisted femoral neck fixation reflects perceived technological value and the clinical decision context. Implementation should emphasize realistic expectations, clear explanations of the robot's role, cost transparency, and informed patient choice.

title: The influence of music on technical skill in robotic surgery among general surgery residents: a simulation-based experimental study.
authors: Dias GC, Guiu RJ, Silva PHA, de Andrade HZ, Strasser RT, da Silva Costa CD, Filho MAR, Silva GG.
abstract: Music is commonly played in operating rooms, but its effect on the acquisition of robotic surgical skills is unclear, particularly when the music is chosen by the trainee. This study evaluated whether a personalized musical intervention influences the technical performance of general surgery residents on a robotic surgery simulator. Thirty-two residents with no previous robotic experience performed three exercises (Pick and Place, Ring and Rail 1 and Energy Dissection 1) on the RobotiX Mentor simulator in three consecutive runs: run 1 without music, run 2 with self-selected preferred music and run 3 under a condition allocated by sealed envelope for each exercise (no music, preferred music or random music). The effect of music was assessed only in run 3, using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Bonferroni correction for 26 comparisons and epsilon-squared effect sizes. No comparison reached statistical significance after correction; the lowest unadjusted p values were observed for instrument collisions in Pick and Place (p = 0.045) and inappropriately applied energy in Energy Dissection 1 (p = 0.029). Effect sizes were mostly small, although some were moderate. Execution time decreased from run 1 to run 2 in all exercises (p ≤ 0.003), with larger reductions in more complex tasks, a pattern attributable to task repetition; because these runs were not randomized, they cannot support causal inferences about music. Under the conditions evaluated, personalized music was not associated with a significant improvement in technical performance during early robotic simulator training. Larger, fully randomized studies are warranted.

title: The impact of arthroscopic repair of the tibionavicular bundle of the deltoid ligament on ankle fractures.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Kürüm H, Akcan A, Çakır M, İpekten F.
abstract: Background Notwithstanding well-established ligament repair with ankle arthroscopy and a thorough understanding of deltoid ligament anatomy, evidence supporting early arthroscopic repair of the deltoid ligament (EAR-DL) remains limited. The purpose of this study was to compare EAR-DL with conservative treatment following ankle fracture. Methods This retrospective study evaluated 45 patients with deltoid ligament tears among 1165 ankle fractures. Patients were grouped based on the EAR-DL decision or conservative treatment. The EAR-DL decision is based on evidence gathered from clinical, radiological, and surgical findings. Patients with imaging-confirmed deltoid ligament injury and ≥ 12 months of follow-up were included; those with major concomitant injuries were excluded. Clinical and radiological outcomes, including instability, functional scores, return to sport, and medial clear space (MCS), were compared. The concomitant injury count (CIC) was developed to measure injury complexity; yet this exploratory score has not yet been validated or assessed for reliability. Final outcomes were evaluated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for baseline values. MCS ≤ 4 mm was considered normal, and ankle stability was assessed using anteromedial drawer and valgus stress tests. Results C3 was the most common fracture pattern in 14 patients (31.1%), followed by B3 in 9 patients (20.0%). The most common CIC level was 3, observed in 28 patients (62.2%). No recurrent instability occurred following EAR-DL, compared with 4 (15.4%) cases in the conservative group (p = 0.126). The return to sports was observed at an average of 33.04 ± 3.18 weeks in the conservative group and at 29.32 ± 1.60 weeks in the EAR-DL group (p Conclusions In this retrospective cohort study, no statistically significant difference was found between the groups in recurrent instability. EAR-DL was associated with a smaller MCS and exploratory, unadjusted clinical outcomes compared with conservative management. Prospective, adequately powered studies are required to determine whether EAR-DL provides clinically meaningful benefits. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Retraction notice to "c-Src-dependent transactivation of PDGFR contributes to TNF-α-induced MMP-9 expression and functional impairment in osteoblasts" [Bone 60 (2014) 186-197].
authors: Tsai CL, Chen WC, Lee IT, Chi PL, Cheng SE, Yang CM.

title: Preoperative CT-derived psoas attenuation and correction loss after traumatic thoracolumbar fracture fixation: A construct-dependent association.
authors: Özdemir M, Latifoğlu F, Uğur OT, Peksoy F, Kamaşak K.
abstract: Background Postoperative correction loss remains a concern after posterior fixation of traumatic thoracolumbar fractures. Although bone quality and construct characteristics influence mechanical stability, the role of preoperative muscle quality remains poorly defined. We examined whether CT-derived psoas attenuation was associated with correction loss and whether fracture-level screw placement modified this association. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included 78 adults who underwent posterior pedicle screw fixation for traumatic AO Spine A3 thoracolumbar fractures. Preoperative psoas and paravertebral attenuation and cross-sectional area were measured at L3. Correction loss was defined as the difference between final-follow-up and immediate postoperative Cobb angles measured on supine sagittal CT reconstructions. Multivariable linear regression tested the interaction between centered psoas attenuation and fracture-level screw placement, adjusting for age, sex, vertebral attenuation, instrumented levels, and follow-up duration. An extended model added vertebral height loss and canal compromise. HC3 robust variance estimation and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Mean correction loss was 4.1 ± 5.4°, and 23 patients (29.5%) experienced loss greater than 5°. The psoas attenuation-by-fracture-level screw interaction was significant (B=0.311°/HU; 95% CI, 0.091-0.530; p = .006; HC3 p = .037). Without fracture-level screws, each 10-HU increase in psoas attenuation corresponded to approximately 2.6° less correction loss (B=-0.255°/HU; 95% CI, -0.440 to -0.071; p = .007), although HC3 inference crossed the null (p = .068). No clear association was observed with fracture-level screws. The interaction persisted after adjustment for vertebral height loss and canal compromise (B=0.342°/HU; 95% CI, 0.127-0.556; p = .002; HC3 p = .016), when short- versus long-segment fixation replaced instrumented-level count, and in patients with at least 12 months of follow-up. Paravertebral attenuation showed a similar pattern, whereas muscle cross-sectional area did not. Conclusions Preoperative psoas attenuation showed a construct-dependent association with correction loss after fixation of traumatic AO Spine A3 fractures. Lower attenuation may identify mechanical vulnerability when the fractured vertebra is not incorporated into the construct. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before CT-based muscle assessment can guide construct selection.

title: Patellofemoral joint cartilage status was not deteriorated after inverted V-shaped high tibial osteotomy.
authors: Hayashi S, Kato K.
abstract: Background Inverted V-shaped high tibial osteotomy (iVHTO), combining hemi-open-wedge (OW) and hemi-closed-wedge (CW) techniques, was developed to overcome the limitations of conventional high tibial osteotomy. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative changes in patellofemoral (PF) joint alignment, cartilage status, and clinical outcomes following iVHTO. Methods Thirty-seven knees in 27 patients underwent iVHTO for medial compartment osteoarthritis requiring a correction angle of >15°, or Results The mean follow up period was 25.1 months. PTA and LSR decreased significantly postoperatively (both P Conclusion iVHTO achieved satisfactory correction of lower limb alignment while preserving PF joint alignment and cartilage status. Significant improvements in patient-reported outcomes were observed, and preoperative AKP resolved in all affected patients.

title: Outside-In Inverted L-Shaped Capsulotomy in Hip Arthroscopy.
authors: Feng Y, Ni J, Tian Z, Chen Z, Wei W, Wang D, Shi Z.
abstract: Hip arthroscopy has become the mainstream surgical treatment for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, with approximately 88.75% of patients returning to sports postoperatively. Capsulotomy is a critical step in arthroscopic labral repair; however, various reported techniques possess inherent limitations. This technique employs an outside-in longitudinal capsulotomy along the femoral neck, followed by a transverse capsular release from its acetabular attachment along the path of the labral tear, creating an inverted "L"-shaped opening. On completion of the repair, the hip capsule is closed and retensioned using the remaining sutures from the labral repair anchors. This article summarizes the advantages, disadvantages, pearls, and pitfalls of this technique.

title: Outcomes associated with suprapectoral versus subpectoral biceps tenodesis site after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a retrospective comparative cohort analysis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Rosso C, Loske S, Audigé L, Dao Trong ML, Weiss I, Mueller A, Selman F, Cunningham G.
abstract: Objectives To investigate functional outcomes, groove pain, presence of Popeye sign and complications associated with suprapectoral and subpectoral biceps tenodesis site in rotator cuff (RC) surgery. Methods Within the ARCR_Pred multicenter cohort study, patients from 19 centers undergoing primary arthroscopic RC repair between June 2020 and November 2021 were prospectively enrolled. Patients undergoing biceps tenodesis without preoperative Popeye sign were allocated to suprapectoral or subpectoral groups, respectively. Outcomes (range of motion, pain, strength, Subjective Shoulder Value, Constant-Murley Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), groove pain, Popeye sign, Speed's test, and postoperative adverse events) were compared using adjusted mixed models. Propensity-score matching was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results Among 445 eligible patients (242 suprapectoral, 203 subpectoral), biceps-specific outcomes were not significantly different for all parameters except for postoperative Popeye sign, being more frequent in the suprapectoral group (36 (15%) vs. 10 (5%); Odds ratio [OR] 0.20; P = 0.009). Shoulder abduction strength at 90° was higher in the suprapectoral cohort at 12 months postoperatively (7.1 vs. 6.3 kg; adjusted difference 0.8; P = 0.024), not reaching minimal clinical important difference. All other functional outcome parameters demonstrated no clinically significant differences. Biceps specific complications were not significantly different between groups. The propensity-score matching sensitivity analysis supported these findings except for the shoulder abduction strength. Conclusion Suprapectoral tenodesis was associated with a higher prevalence of postoperative Popeye sign. No significant differences were detected in postoperative groove pain. The observed strength advantage after suprapectoral tenodesis was not clinically meaningful. Procedure-specific complication rates were low in both groups.

title: Malignant Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Breast: A Case Report and Selected Review of the Literature.
authors: Tachibana K, Kiko Y, Ozaki A, Okano M, Noda M, Hoshi N, Abe S, Minami K, Hashimoto M, Terui T, Hashimoto Y, Ohtake T.
abstract: Introduction Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is a rare mesenchymal neoplasm that may arise at various anatomical sites. Breast SFT is uncommon, and malignant SFT of the breast is exceptionally rare and can be difficult to distinguish from other spindle cell tumors. Case presentation A 67-year-old woman presented with a rapidly enlarging mass in the right breast. Imaging demonstrated a well-circumscribed, hypervascular tumor that increased from approximately 10 to 16 cm within 1 month. Core needle biopsy suggested a stromal sarcoma or a malignant phyllodes tumor, and a total mastectomy was performed. Histopathological examination showed a patternless spindle cell proliferation with staghorn-like vessels, frequent mitoses, and necrosis. The tumor cells showed diffuse nuclear signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) positivity and were positive for cluster of differentiation (CD) 34, CD99, β-catenin, B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL2), and smooth muscle actin. Malignant SFT was diagnosed. The patient remains disease-free 5 years after surgery without adjuvant therapy. Conclusions A malignant SFT should be considered in the differential diagnosis of rapidly growing breast spindle cell tumors. Complete surgical excision with negative margins and STAT6-based histopathological confirmation can support an accurate diagnosis and favorable long-term outcomes.

title: Long-Term Survival After CRS-HIPEC for colorectal Cancer Peritoneal Metastases.
authors: van Kesteren LJ, Aalbers AGJ, Chakroun A, van der Snee L, Hompes R, Lameris W, Bolhuis K, Grotenhuis BA, van Dieren S, Buffart TE, Kok NFM, Tuynman JB.
abstract: Background Most patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and peritoneal metastases (PM) face a dismal prognosis. Cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC) is a curative-intent treatment for patients with limited disease. This study assessed long-term survival and recurrence patterns. Methods A consecutive cohort of patients with CRC-PM treated with CRS-HIPEC. Patients with complete macroscopic cytoreduction were eligible. Main outcomes were overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), peritoneal recurrence-free survival (PRFS) and recurrence patterns. Results In total, 440 patients were evaluated over a median follow-up of 35.2 months (IQR 25.3-68.7). Induction systemic therapy was administered to 43.1% of patients. Median DFS was 9.7 months (95% CI 8.3-11.1), and median OS was 50.2 months (95% CI 44.3-56.2). Independent prognostic factors for decreased OS were Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) > 10, positive lymph node status (N-stage), ASA score > 2, and right-sided primary tumors. During follow-up, 71.4% of patients developed recurrent disease in the peritoneum (54.8%), lungs (22.9%), and liver (19.1%). Independent prognostic factors for decreased PRFS were lymph node metastases and higher PCI scores. Neither induction therapy nor HIPEC regimen was correlated with PRFS. Early metachronous presentation of peritoneal metastasis, also emerged as a significant adverse factor for OS, DFS and PRFS. Conclusions Patients undergoing complete CRS-HIPEC achieved a favorable median OS exceeding 50 months, with approximately 30% of individuals exhibiting long-term survival indicative of cure. However, early recurrence remains a major problem and is in need for further research to improve CRS-HIPEC regimens.

title: Integrated deep learning reconstruction combining phase correction, denoising, and super-resolution for prostate diffusion-weighted imaging.
authors: Nishioka N, Onodera M, Kato D, Tsuneta S, Fujima N, Matsumoto R, Abe T, Kwon J, Yoneyama M, Kudo K.
abstract: Objective To evaluate integrated deep learning reconstruction (Integrated DLR), which combines phase correction, denoising, and super-resolution, for prostate diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) by comparing it with compressed sensing (CS) and deep learning-based denoising reconstruction (Denoising DLR). Methods This single-center, retrospective study included 47 patients scanned on a single-vendor 3-T system. Three DWI datasets were reconstructed from identical raw data using CS, Denoising DLR, and Integrated DLR. Two radiologists rated overall image quality, noise, artifact, and prostate delineation. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was assessed in all patients. In 21 patients with pathologically confirmed prostate cancer, we assessed lesion conspicuity, lesion localization/anatomical relationship, Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version 2.1 DWI scores, apparent lesion contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Comparisons were performed using Friedman tests followed by Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results Scores for overall image quality, noise, and prostate delineation were highest with Integrated DLR, followed by Denoising DLR and CS, for both readers (all p Conclusion Integrated DLR improved prostate DWI image quality and lesion visibility compared with CS and Denoising DLR, potentially facilitating visual assessment of prostate DWI.

title: Injury labels and patient-problem codes in FDA adverse event reports for robotic arthroplasty platforms: a cross-sectional analysis of 12,175 MAUDE reports.
authors: Abushal MH.
abstract: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) device reports carry two structured fields used to describe patient harm: the event-type label and patient-problem codes. I quantified how often prespecified contrasting categories of these fields co-occur in reports for robotic arthroplasty platforms. Cross-sectional analysis of reports in the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database, accessed through openFDA (product code OLO, received to 30 September 2026) matching search definitions for Mako and NAVIO/CORI (manufacturer field) and VELYS and ROSA Knee/Recon (brand field); procedures were not confirmed. The primary outcome was co-occurrence of an injury label with a no-consequence code, or of a non-injury label with a harm-related code, counted exactly from archived report-level records. Sensitivity analyses included harmonised definitions and duplicate screening. Of 12,175 reports, 2,106 (17.3%) were labelled injury, from 0.6% (VELYS) to 44.2% (ROSA). A no-consequence code appeared in 46.0% (Mako), 71.3% (NAVIO/CORI) and 59.5% (ROSA) of injury-labelled reports; a harm-related code appeared in 12.8% of non-injury VELYS reports. Overall, 1,785 reports (14.7%; 95% confidence interval 14.0-15.3) showed co-occurrence. The injury-label share exceeded the harm-related code share for Mako, NAVIO/CORI and ROSA; for VELYS, the reverse held. These directions persisted with clinical code categories, harmonised definitions and duplicate removal. Contrasting label and patient-code categories frequently co-occurred, in platform-specific directions. This reflects the fields' different purposes, not demonstrated coding disagreement, patient harm or device safety. Because reporting practices and search-field composition may contribute, harm proportions from either field alone should not be used to rank platforms.

title: Hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement in American football athletes: examining factors associated with outcomes at a mean follow-up time of 6.3 years.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Atkinson A, Crick M, Froom R, Westbrooks B, King E, Mussell E, Crawford A, Aiken C, Ithurburn M, Ryan M, Emblom B.
abstract: Introduction Femoroacetabular impingement (FAIS) is a common cause of hip pain and performance limitation in athletes. Hip arthroscopy is the gold standard of treatment in professional American football athletes, with numerous studies demonstrating favorable outcomes and high return-to-sport (RTS) rates. However, limited outcomes data exists in collegiate athletes and fewer still in high school athletes. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term patient-reported outcomes (PROs), RTS rates, and predictors of outcomes following hip arthroscopy for symptomatic FAIS in high school and collegiate football athletes. Materials and methods A retrospective cohort study was performed which included high-school and collegiate football athletes who underwent hip arthroscopy for symptomatic FAIS. Outcomes were assessed using the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), International Hip Outcome Tool-12 (IHOT-12), and Hip Outcomes Score-Sport Specific Subscale (HOS-Sport). Data regarding return to preinjury sport were also collected. Pre-operative radiographic data, including alpha angle, lateral center edge angle, and Tönnis grade, were collected. Results This cohort had a mean post-operative follow up of 6.3 years, with mean PRO scores of 82.2 on the mHHS, 84.6 on the iHOT-12, and 88.3 on the HOS-Sport. PASS thresholds were achieved by 69%, 77% and 80% of athletes for the same outcomes, respectively. 60% of the cohort attempted to return to sport, and 91% of the athletes who attempted to return to preinjury level of sport were successful. Increased age at time of surgery and larger pre-operative alpha angles were associated with worse PRO scores at follow-up. Conclusions Hip arthroscopy for FAIS in high school and collegiate football players yielded favorable long-term outcomes and RTS rates. This is similar to current outcomes data in professional athletes. Increased alpha angle and age at surgery were associated with worse outcomes, emphasizing the importance of early recognition and appropriate surgical treatment. Comparisons of outcomes between blocking and nonblocking positions may warrant further investigation in larger cohorts.

title: HSMD: A Hilbert-scanning mamba dense network for 3D MRI reconstruction.
authors: Liu Z, Chi J, Yang J, Liu B, Liu F.
abstract: Long MRI acquisition times motivate the use of k-space undersampling for accelerated imaging, but undersampling often introduces aliasing artifacts and structural detail loss. Existing 2D slice-wise reconstruction methods fail to fully exploit inter-slice anatomical correlations. This study develops a Hilbert-Scanning Mamba Dense Network (HSMD) for high-quality 3D MRI reconstruction, which leverages inter-slice contextual information to improve reconstruction fidelity. The proposed HSMD consists of a Shallow Feature Extraction Module (SFEM) and five cascaded Multi-Directional Spatial Attention (MDSA) modules. The SFEM is responsible for extracting local detailed features and coarse-scale structural context from undersampled MRI inputs. The MDSA modules extract and fuse multi-directional spatial information along the depth, height, and width dimensions to enhance the representation of 3D structural features. Furthermore, a multi-directional Hilbert selective state-space scanning strategy is introduced into MDSA to capture long-range spatial dependencies within 3D volumetric data, thereby improving structural representation while preserving spatial locality. Experimental results on the BraTS and UCSF-PDGM datasets under diverse acceleration factors validate that the proposed HSMD achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The HSMD exhibits excellent capability in 3D undersampled MRI reconstruction, holding promising prospects for efficient and reliable clinical MRI applications.

title: Exposure to Plastic Surgery During General Surgery Training and Production of Independent Plastic Surgery Residents: A National Query of 341 Programs.
authors: James T, De Brito KCW, Streetman DR, Khan F, Dembinski D, Gobble R.
abstract: Objective Exposure to plastic and reconstructive surgery is critical for general surgery residents to develop interest in pursuing plastic surgery as a career. This study aims to quantify trends in exposure to plastic surgery among general surgery residents and exposures relationship to pursuing independent plastic and reconstructive surgery match. Design This was a retrospective cross sectional observational study using publicly available data and program correspondence. Setting Data on program curriculum and rotation schedules were collected from general surgery program websites and communication with general surgery program coordinators (maximum 3 attempts). Participants In total, 416 general surgery graduates from 341 programs from 2016 to 2024 were included in this study. Results General surgery programs with more exposure to plastic surgery through dedicated rotations produced more independent plastic surgery residents, with programs producing only 1 matched applicant found to have 1.84 months of exposure, compared to programs with 4+ matched applicants averaging 2.48 months of exposure (p-value = Conclusions GS residencies with an affiliated independent PRS program are more likely to match interested residents into PRS than those without. There is not a similar benefit for GS programs affiliated with integrated programs alone. Exposure to PRS through dedicated rotations is positively associated with increasing matched applicants following GS residency.

title: Diagnostic Pitfall: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension Presenting With Postpartum Right-Sided Heart Failure in a 21-Year-Old-Case Report.
authors: Alla SSM, Khetan MS, Alla D, Ganguru SL, Appala S, Sree K, Shah RJ, Seth A, Rawtani NA, Aamir MR, Emmanuel NW.
abstract: Mixed connective tissue disease is a multisystem autoimmune condition characterized by overlapping clinical and serological features related to anti-U1-RNP antibodies of at least two connective tissue diseases. It may present with myocarditis, pericarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and, less commonly, heart failure. We present a 21-year-old female with bilateral foot swelling, cough, and shortness of breath 3 months after a vaginal delivery. On examination, she was hypotensive (90/70 mmHg), with an elevated jugular venous pressure, a pulmonary systolic murmur with loud P2, and a tricuspid regurgitation murmur. Bronchial breath sounds and fine crepitations were present in both lower lung fields. She was evaluated initially for suspected postpartum cardiomyopathy. Transthoracic echocardiography was suggestive of a probable moderate to severe PAH. High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral moderate pleural effusions, honeycombing with partial atelectasis of the underlying lung, and cardiomegaly. Computed Tomography Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA) showed findings likely consistent with probable mild pulmonary hypertension. An antinuclear antibody panel was performed and was positive for anti-U1-RNP, SS-A, SS-B, and Jo-1 antibodies. She was started on Lasix 40 mg, Aldactone 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, and heparin. Treatment with 20 mg of prednisolone was started and gradually tapered. Her anasarca and dyspnea improved, and she was discharged with follow-up arranged with cardiology and rheumatology. Timely identification of MCTD-associated pulmonary hypertension and its cardiovascular complications is essential and allows early commencement of treatment, which further prevents the patients from developing heart failure.

title: Determinants of fluoroscopy frequency and effect of standardized workflow optimization in robot-assisted pelvic channel screw placement: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
authors: Li J, Zhang W, Gong T, Li X, Yin K, Zhang X, Tai H.
abstract: Robot-assisted percutaneous pelvic channel screw placement has been shown to significantly reduce intraoperative radiation exposure. However, even within the robot-assisted framework, fluoroscopy frequency still shows substantial within-group variation. Existing studies lack a systematic analysis of the determinants of fluoroscopy frequency and lack targeted workflow optimization strategies. To identify the independent determinants of fluoroscopy frequency in robot-assisted pelvic channel screw placement and to evaluate whether a standardized optimization protocol based on these factors can further reduce residual fluoroscopy exposure. We retrospectively enrolled patients with pelvic fractures who underwent robot-assisted percutaneous pelvic channel screw placement at Gansu Provincial Hospital between January 2020 and May 2025. Part A: The number of fluoroscopy sessions per case was the dependent variable. Multivariable negative binomial regression was used to analyze potential determinants, including surgeon experience stage, screw type, oblique bone surface at the entry point, BMI, and bone mineral density. Part B: Based on Part A results, we developed and implemented a standardized optimization protocol targeting modifiable factors, with December 2023 as the cutoff. We compared fluoroscopy frequency, fluoroscopy time, and screw accuracy between the pre-optimization group (n = 312) and the post-optimization group (n = 289). To address methodological time-trend confounding, we added interrupted time series analysis, propensity score matching, and a negative control subgroup analysis. This was a non-randomized, single-center, before-after design, and residual confounding cannot be completely excluded. Part A (n = 601): Multivariable negative binomial regression showed that oblique bone surface at the entry point (IRR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.31-1.77, P 30 cases, IRR = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.25-1.75, P < 0.001), S2 screws (IRR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.10-1.44, P = 0.001), and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² (IRR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.02-1.39, P = 0.026) were independent determinants of fluoroscopy frequency. Part B: The post-optimization group showed a significant reduction in fluoroscopy frequency compared with the pre-optimization group (9.8 ± 2.9 vs. 13.5 ± 3.7, P < 0.001). Fluoroscopy time also decreased (16.2 ± 5.4 s vs. 21.8 ± 6.9 s, P < 0.001). Screw accuracy showed no significant difference (98.7% vs. 98.1%, P = 0.52). The optimization effect was most pronounced in the oblique bone surface subgroup (31.5% reduction) and was 14.2% in the non-oblique subgroup. In the negative control subgroup (experienced surgeons, non-oblique, non-obese, S1 screws), fluoroscopy frequency did not change significantly before and after optimization (10.2 ± 2.6 vs. 10.5 ± 2.8, P = 0.41); however, post-hoc power for this subgroup was extremely low (approximately 0.10), so this null result should be regarded as inconclusive rather than as evidence of no effect. These findings suggest a possible risk-stratified specific effect of the optimization protocol, but time trends, the Hawthorne effect, and the unseparated multicomponent bundle cannot be excluded. In robot-assisted pelvic channel screw placement, oblique bone surface at the entry point, early surgeon experience stage, S2 screws, and obesity are independent determinants of fluoroscopy frequency. A standardized multicomponent optimization protocol targeting modifiable factors can safely reduce fluoroscopy frequency by approximately 27% without compromising screw accuracy. Optimization of fluoroscopy frequency should become a core indicator in robot-assisted surgical training and quality control. However, this was a non-randomized, single-center, before-after study; the optimization protocol was a multicomponent bundle whose individual contributions cannot be separated; and the oblique bone surface and negative control subgroups were underpowered. These findings require prospective validation.

title: Defining the musculoskeletal ultrasound phenotype of ochronotic arthropathy: a systematic study of 34 patients with alkaptonuria.
authors: Bianchi E, Conticini E, Bardelli M, Baldi C, Selvi E, Mazzon A, Peruzzi L, Santucci A, Cantarini L, Frediani B, Falsetti P.
abstract: Objectives Ochronotic arthropathy is the leading cause of disability in patients with alkaptonuria (AKU), yet its musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSUS) phenotype has not been systematically characterized. This study aimed to define the ultrasound features of ochronotic arthropathy and identify recurring imaging patterns that may facilitate its recognition in clinical practice. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study including consecutive patients with genetically confirmed AKU evaluated at a tertiary referral centre between 2017 and 2025. Patients receiving nitisinone therapy and prosthetic joints were excluded from the ultrasound assessment. Bilateral standardized MSUS examinations of the shoulders, hips, knees and Achilles tendons were performed by experienced rheumatologists according to OMERACT definitions. The frequency and distribution of structural and inflammatory abnormalities were recorded, and their associations with clinical variables were explored. Results Thirty-four patients (17 females; mean age 52.1 ± 18.9 years) were included. Diagnostic delay positively correlated with the cumulative number of joint prostheses (ρ = 0.46, p = 0.006). The shoulder was the most frequently involved site (85.3%), showing bilateral hyperechoic rotator cuff deposits (66.7%), tendon tears (29.0%) and long head of the biceps tenosynovitis (30.0%). Knee abnormalities were identified in 61.8% of patients and included extensor tendon hyperechoic deposits (65.4%), meniscal involvement (50.0%), osteoarthritic changes (44.4%) and synovitis (29.4%). Achilles tendon involvement was observed in 48.4% of patients and was characterized by insertional and mid-portion linear hyperechoic deposits associated with tendinosis, entheseal thickening, erosive changes and only limited Power Doppler activity. Hip involvement was less common (20.0%). Significant associations were found between knee involvement and extensor mechanism abnormalities (p = 0.005) and between hip involvement and Achilles tendon enthesopathy (p = 0.038). Conclusions Ochronotic arthropathy demonstrates a distinctive musculoskeletal ultrasound phenotype characterized by bilateral tendon and entheseal involvement, linear hyperechoic deposits, advanced tendinosis and limited inflammatory activity. These findings provide the first systematic description of the ultrasound phenotype of AKU and suggest that MSUS may represent a valuable adjunctive tool for raising clinical suspicion of ochronotic arthropathy in patients with otherwise unexplained early degenerative musculoskeletal disease. Key Points • Ochronotic arthropathy shows a distinctive musculoskeletal ultrasound pattern. • Bilateral tendon and entheseal abnormalities are highly prevalent in AKU. • Linear hyperchoic deposits frequently accompany advanced tendinosis.

title: Deep learning-derived functional MRI connectivity maps of cervical spinal cord segments during hand grasping.
authors: Khan D, Rehman HZU, Jadoon K.
abstract: Task-based fMRI of the cervical spinal cord is limited by physiological noise and small sample sizes. The primary objective of this study was to examine whether a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based denoising framework can improve the detection of task-dependent functional connectivity between cervical spinal segments using generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analysis. An open dataset of 26 healthy adults performing a hand-grasp task with alternating right- and left-hand blocks during 3 T fMRI was analyzed. A CNN with Inception V3 transfer learning (91.0% slice-level and 89.2% block-level accuracy) was trained to classify grasp versus rest, and the trained model was then utilized to derive denoised time series from masks of the spinal segments C5-C8. A gPPI model with a C6 ventral horn seed was evaluated using FDR correction and permutation testing (n = 1000). C6 showed positive task-dependent connectivity with C7 (β = 0.72, p = 0.003) and C8 (β = 0.58, p = 0.018), and negative connectivity with C5 (β = -0.31, p = 0.041), which is broadly consistent with the organization of the cervical myotomes. The C6-C5 effect was marginal and was not detected when conventional time series were used (p = 0.21), and therefore it requires replication. Grad-CAM maps aligned with ventral horn motor pools (Dice = 0.89 at C7). These results suggest that deep learning-based denoising may increase the sensitivity of spinal cord fMRI to segmental connectivity, although validation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: Cervical biomechanical responses to parachute opening shock: effects of shock magnitude and initial body orientation.
authors: Cao S, Deng S, Dou Q, Suo T.
abstract: Injuries associated with parachute opening shock (POS) are a major form of trauma related to parachuting and remain an important concern in aerospace medicine. A full human body finite element model of POS incorporating a three-point harness system was developed, and its global dynamic response was evaluated using data from a physical POS test conducted with a Hybrid Ⅲ dummy. The first head acceleration peaks of the simulated and experimental responses were similar in magnitude and time to peak. The effects of POS magnitude and initial body orientation on cervical kinematics, regional loading, and local tissue biomechanical responses were subsequently investigated. The results indicated that POS induced nonuniform segmental cervical flexion and distinct loading patterns across different cervical regions. Increasing the POS magnitude generally increased cervical loads, intervertebral differential flexion, and tensile strains in the posterior cervical ligaments, whereas peak stress in individual vertebrae showed segmental variations. Changes in initial body orientation substantially altered the loading patterns of the middle and lower cervical spine by modifying harness load distribution and trunk motion. This study establishes a human body finite element framework that incorporates harness load transfer to reveal how POS magnitude and initial body orientation redistribute cervical loading from global trunk motion to segmental deformation and local tissue responses.

title: Whose morning, whose evening? Temporal asymmetries in intermedia agenda-setting between X and online news in Türkiye.
authors: Ceylan M, Yılmaz R, Erdoğan Bodur R.
abstract: This study examines whether temporal ordering between X and online news varies across first-level issue and second-level attribute agendas in Türkiye's polarized media environment. The analysis draws on 448,664 X posts and 10,357 articles from 19 mainstream online news outlets collected during the 31-day period preceding and including the 31 March 2024 Istanbul local election. Using 12-hour AM/PM windows, we conducted 122 cross-lagged panel analyses-62 same-day AM → PM and 60 overnight PM→next-day AM panels across the two agenda levels-comparing issue- and attribute-indicator frequency profiles. First-level issue agendas were strongly synchronized, with correlations often approaching or exceeding r = .90, whereas second-level attribute relationships were weaker and less consistent. At the first level, morning online news issue salience more often preceded later X issue salience within same-day transitions, whereas evening X issue salience more often preceded the following morning's online news issue salience across overnight transitions. Most first-level cross-lagged correlations exceeded their Rozelle-Campbell (RCb) baselines, while second-level coefficients did so less consistently. These findings indicate that agenda leadership in a hybrid media system is temporally contingent and level-specific rather than static. The observed patterns represent temporally ordered associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of direct causal influence.

title: Various aspects of upper-limb muscle strength and tennis performance: A comparative study of U12 and U14 female tennis players.
authors: Waldziński T, Durzyńska A, Niespodziński B, Mieszkowski J, Waldzińska E, Kochanowicz A.
abstract: This study investigated the relationship between muscle strength and tennis performance, assessed using the International Tennis Number (ITN) on-court test, operationalized as point-based outcomes (total points and subcomponent points), in young female tennis players aged under 12 (U12) and under 14 (U14). Thirty-three players underwent a comprehensive evaluation including ITN testing, general strength tests (handgrip strength, flexed arm hang, and tennis-ball throw), isometric upper-limb muscle strength, and sense of force assessment. Results demonstrated significantly higher ITN scores and muscle strength in the U14 group, with differences largely attributable to body size and training experience. Correlation analyses revealed age-specific patterns: in U12 players, ITN scores were associated primarily with general strength measures, whereas in U14 players, they were more strongly linked to joint-specific upper-limb strength and neuromuscular characteristics. Sense of force did not differ between groups, though correlations with ITN varied depending on age and joint function. These findings suggest that, in this sample, performance in younger players was more closely associated with general strength measures, whereas in older players it was more closely associated with joint-specific upper-limb strength.

title: Trochleoplasty combined with MPFL reconstruction is associated with a postoperative reduction in the measured Caton-Deschamps index.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Coppola C, Nardelli P, Liebensteiner M, Lindtner RA, Khosravi I, Mayr R.
abstract: Introduction To investigate changes in MRI-measured Caton-Deschamps index (CDI) at mid- to long-term follow-up following groove-deepening trochleoplasty (TP) combined with medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction (MPFLR) and to compare these changes between single-bundle quadriceps tendon graft (QTG) and double-bundle hamstring tendon graft (HTG) reconstruction. Materials and methods Seventeen patients who had undergone TP with concomitant MPFLR were analyzed retrospectively. Patellar height was assessed preoperatively and postoperatively on sagittal magnetic resonance images by three independent observers using the CDI. Preoperative and postoperative CDI values were compared using a paired t-test. CDI changes were compared between single-bundle QTG (n = 9) and double-bundle HTG (n = 8) reconstruction using an independent-samples t-test. Interobserver reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results The mean CDI decreased significantly from 1.06 ± 0.13 preoperatively to 0.95 ± 0.15 postoperatively (Δ = -0.10 ± 0.07; P Conclusions Combined trochleoplasty and MPFL reconstruction was associated with a significant postoperative reduction in MRI-measured CDI at mid- to long-term follow-up, with an average decrease of - 0.10. Whether this finding reflects true anatomical patellar distalization cannot be determined from the present study.

title: The surgeon in the loop: automation bias and human-AI interaction in robotic surgery.
authors: Morais MC, Godbole AA, Iqbal E, Nussbaum J, Khare HP, Ballo M, Filicori F.
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence systems for intraoperative surgical guidance are approaching clinical deployment, yet no study has quantified automation bias (defined as the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations) in the context of surgical decision-making. As these systems enter operative workflows, the surgeon's ability to recognize and override incorrect AI guidance becomes a critical safety requirement. Aim To measure the extent to which surgeons modify incision plans after exposure to AI-labeled visual guidance and to determine the rate at which incorrect AI suggestions are accepted. Methods A two-phase controlled experiment was conducted among 19 surgeons (10 residents, 2 fellows, 7 attendings). Participants drew incision lines on 20 static frames from robotic cholecystectomy videos, first without guidance (Phase 01) and then with a mock AI overlay (Phase 02). Overlays were either correct (derived from expert consensus) or deliberately incorrect (shifted toward unsafe anatomy) at an approximately 70:30 ratio. No actual AI model was used. The primary outcome was mean perpendicular distance (MPD) between Phase 01 and Phase 02 lines. Secondary outcomes included AI-corridor adherence, over-reliance and under-reliance rates, behavioral accuracy, and confidence shift. Results Across 231 paired observations, MPD did not differ significantly between correct (75.5 pixels; SD, 33.4) and incorrect (71.1 pixels; SD, 31.7) overlay conditions (P = .35). Directional analysis revealed that surgeons accepted incorrect AI suggestions in 60.6% of incorrect-overlay frames (43/71), with a specificity for rejecting incorrect guidance of only 39.4% (28/71). Correct suggestions were accepted 76.9% of the time (123/160). Overall behavioral accuracy was 65.4%. Self-reported confidence increased significantly after AI exposure (Δ = + 0.65; P Conclusion Surgeons accepted approximately 3 of every 5 incorrect AI recommendations. As intraoperative AI systems approach deployment, surgeon oversight cannot be assumed to neutralize algorithmic error; it must be empirically measured, deliberately designed for, and prospectively validated.

title: The mediating role of empathy in the association between interpersonal communication competence and attitudes toward disability in higher education.
authors: Delimehmet Dada Ş, Sardohan Yıldırım AE.
abstract: Developing positive attitudes toward people with disabilities is crucial for social equality and integration. This study examines the relationship between university students' attitudes toward people with disabilities, their empathy levels, and their interpersonal communication competence, with a focus on the mediating role of empathy. Data from 587 students were collected using a cross-sectional survey design and analyzed using correlation analysis and path analysis-based mediation modeling. The findings indicate that higher empathy and communication competence are associated with more positive attitudes and lower levels of prejudice. Empathy partially mediated the association between communication competence and egalitarian attitudes, whereas the indirect association between communication competence and prejudiced attitudes was not statistically significant. In addition, demographic factors such as gender and age were associated with attitudes, with female students reporting more positive views. These results underline the relevance of empathy and communication skills for inclusive attitudes and suggest that higher education institutions may consider policies that strengthen these competencies. Overall, this study contributes to understanding how empathy and communication are associated with disability-related attitudes in higher education.

title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
authors: Giorgi PD, Ramponi A, Legrenzi S, Bove F, Mezzadri U, Addevico F, Prina A, Schirò GR.
abstract: Introduction Sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation (SPD) is a rare, high-energy injury associated with substantial mortality and morbidity. Surgical stabilization is technically challenging and has historically been associated with relatively high rates of construct failure. The present study describes and evaluates a novel minimally invasive spinopelvic diamond-shaped construct (The MIS-Diamond fixation), designed to improve rigid triangular stabilization while minimizing soft-tissue morbidity and facilitate the fracture reduction. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted including patients who underwent MIS-Diamond fixation for AO Type C3 sacral fractures at a single Level-I Trauma Center between January 2014 and December 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, and radiological outcomes were systematically assessed. Fractures were classified according to the AO Spine Sacral Injury Classification System. Results Thirty-two patients (mean age 39 years) were included. Surgery was performed at a median of 5 days post-injury, with a mean operative time of 115.8 min and mean estimated blood loss of 82.7 mL. No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a postoperative S1 motor impairment attributed to indirect radicular injury during reduction. Implant-related complications were recorded in 4 patients (12.5%), including one late-onset surgical site infection and three cases of asymptomatic iliac screw loosening. No soft tissue or wound healing complications were observed. Implant removal was successfully completed in 28 patients (87.5%) at 12 months postoperatively. Discussion MIS-Diamond fixation demonstrated a favourable safety profile while enabling early postoperative mobilization. The incorporation of a 5.5 mm transverse iliac rod converts the classical triangular construct into a rigid box-like configuration, enhancing rotational stability and preventing coronal diastasis during vertical distraction. Limiting instrumentation to L4-L5 reduces the number of immobilized motion segments compared to previously described longer constructs, potentially mitigating long-term degenerative sequelae. Conclusions The MIS-Diamond fixation represents a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical option for SPD, providing reliable multiplanar stabilization with a low complication profile. Routine implant removal at 12 months is feasible and recommended to preserve motion segment function. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

title: The Influence of Height-Adjusted Nutritional Status Assessment on Complications Following Growing-Rod Surgery for Early-Onset Scoliosis.
authors: Zhang Y, Geng H, Wang J, Hai Y.
abstract: Objectives Accurate nutritional assessment in children with early-onset scoliosis (EOS) is challenging because spinal deformity reduces measured standing height and may distort BMI-for-age classification. This study aimed to evaluate, using a longitudinal design, height-adjusted nutritional status before each growing-rod procedure throughout the treatment course and to investigate its association with postoperative complications in patients with EOS. Methods A retrospective cohort study included 53 patients with EOS who underwent 86 growing-rod procedures between January 2016 and January 2023, with each procedure serving as the unit of analysis. Nutritional status was reassessed before each analyzed procedure using BMI calculated from height corrected by the Ylikoski formula and was linked to the postoperative outcome of the corresponding procedure. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to evaluate factors associated with postoperative complications while accounting for within-patient clustering. Results A total of 14 procedures resulted in postoperative complications, yielding an overall complication rate of 16.3% (14/86), with 15 specific complication events recorded. After height-adjusted BMI correction, 46 procedures were classified into the malnourished group and 40 into the normal nutrition group. The complication rate was significantly higher in the postadjusted malnourished group than in the normal nutrition group (23.9% vs. 7.5%, p = 0.042). Multivariable analysis using GEE revealed that undergoing ≥ 3 surgeries (OR = 4.614, 95% CI: 1.133-18.786, p = 0.033), and postadjusted malnutrition (OR = 3.701, 95% CI: 1.006-13.613, p = 0.049) were associated with increased risk of postoperative complications. However, after the Mancl-DeRouen small-sample correction, the association between height-adjusted malnutrition and complications was no longer statistically significant (OR = 4.21, 95% CI: 0.38-46.12, p = 0.239). Conclusions Height-adjusted malnutrition and repeated surgeries (≥ 3) were associated with increased postoperative complications after growing-rod surgery in EOS patients. However, larger cohorts are needed to confirm these findings. The procedure-specific application of height-adjusted BMI provides an alternative approach to longitudinal nutritional assessment during repeated growing-rod treatment. Timely intervention should be implemented for patients with poorer nutritional status.

title: The Effect of Cementless Stem Design on Late Periprosthetic Fractures After Total Hip Arthroplasty. Does the Design of Cementless Stems Affects the Rate of Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures?
authors: Koutalos AA, Akrivos V, Gkekas N, Karachalios T.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are a leading cause of revision after total hip arthroplasty (THA). Cementless stems have been associated with higher rates of early and late PFFs than cemented fixation. This study evaluated whether cementless stem design is associated with the risk of late PFF following primary THA. Methods We performed a retrospective review of all primary cementless THAs implanted at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2000 and December 2023 (n = 3772). Early fractures ( Results At a mean follow-up of 14.5 years, the incidence of late PFF was 1.4% (53 of 3772). No difference in overall survival was observed among stem designs ( P = .108). Exploratory pairwise comparisons showed higher PFF-free survival for 1 type 2 stem design than for two other type 2 designs ( P = .002 and P = .003, respectively). No differences were found between type 2 (double wedge) and type 3 (tapered) stems ( P = .510). Increased age was independently associated with PFF ( P = .02). Conclusions Late PFF after cementless THA was uncommon. Although survivorship did not differ between broad stem categories, variability among individual designs warrants further evaluation in larger multicenter or registry-based studies.

title: Tailored Approach for Portal Vein Involvement with a Replaced Right Hepatic Artery during Robotic Pancreatoduodenectomy.
authors: Tomita K, Gamboa A, Maxwell JE, Snyder RA, Kim MP, Tzeng CD, Katz MHG, Ikoma N.
abstract: In robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) for tumors with portal vein (PV) involvement and a replaced right hepatic artery (rRHA), precise dissection from the posterior aspect of the pancreatic head is not always straightforward. Therefore, an anterior and inferior approach may be more appropriate in the robotic setting. The rRHA should be identified at both its proximal and distal ends (at its origin from the superior mesenteric artery [SMA] and along the right side of the bile duct within the hepatoduodenal ligament, respectively) and dissected from both sides to the greatest extent feasible. 1 The key principle is to obtain proximal and distal control of the rRHA before approaching the most adherent portion of the tumor. Unlike standard RPD, the presence of an rRHA requires early identification and vascular control from both its proximal and distal sides before PV/superior mesenteric vein (SMV) dissection because the artery may limit posterior exposure and is at risk during dissection of the tumor from the portomesenteric vein.

title: Survival benefit of prophylactic central neck dissection in T3b differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
authors: Zhao Y, Long C, Xiao L.
abstract: Objective To assess whether prophylactic central neck dissection (pCND) is associated with disease-specific survival (DSS) in clinically node-negative patients with T3b differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC). Design A population-based retrospective study. Methods We analyzed 3274 clinically node-negative T3b DTC patients from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (2004-2022) who underwent surgery with pCND (n = 1511) or without pCND (n = 1763). Random Survival Forest (RSF) models with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified variable importance and effects. Dependence and partial dependence plots derived from the RSF model were used to reveal the relationships between the variables and predicted survival probability. Traditional Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models provided complementary validation. Results Central neck dissection emerged as the third most important prognostic factor (17% relative importance), followed by age (30%) and tumor size (27%). In partial dependence analysis, the adjusted 10-year DSS was 1.2 percentage points higher with pCND (98.4% versus 97.2%, p Conclusions pCND was independently associated with better DSS in clinically node-negative T3b DTC, most of which was papillary thyroid carcinoma. Because node negativity was confirmed pathologically only in the pCND group, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation before they inform guideline recommendations.

title: Successful Transplantation of a Split Horseshoe Kidney From a Deceased Donor Into 2 Recipients: Technical Considerations and Mid-Term Outcomes.
authors: Majerson A, Rojas A, Sarras MA, Villagran F, Huidobro JP, Roessler E.
abstract: Horseshoe kidney is the most common renal fusion anomaly and remains an infrequent source of transplantable organs due to its complex vascular and urologic anatomy. We report 2 successful kidney transplants derived from a single horseshoe kidney procured from a deceased donor, emphasizing preoperative imaging, bench reconstruction, and postoperative outcomes. During bench surgery horseshoe kidney was splited and arterial reconstruction was performed prior to implantation. Renal units were transplanted into 2 recipients, with immediate renal function and no intraoperative or postoperative complications reported. At 6 months follow-up, both recipients presented with stable graft function. This case demonstrates that, with meticulous preparation, horseshoe kidneys can expand the donor pool safely and effectively.

title: Stroke disability burden and rehabilitation service-capacity proxies in China, 1990-2023: A population-based analysis using GBD 2023 and national service statistics.
authors: Zhou Y, Fan W, Lv D, Li Q, Cao Y, Tian H, Guo W, Bi X.
abstract: China's stroke burden is increasingly shaped by survival with disability, population ageing, and demand for rehabilitation and long-term support. Yet the extent to which stroke disability burden has shifted towards older-old and oldest-old adults, and how this burden relates to community and elder-care service capacity, remains insufficiently quantified. We conducted a population-based secondary analysis of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for China from 1990 to 2023, focusing on ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage. We examined disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), YLD share of DALYs, age-specific patterns among adults aged 50 years or older, estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs), and three-factor decomposition of absolute DALY changes. We also linked 2023 stroke YLDs with national community health and elder-care service indicators as descriptive capacity proxies. From 1990 to 2023, the YLD share of DALYs increased from 10.5% to 22.3% for ischaemic stroke and from 1.8% to 3.3% for intracerebral haemorrhage. The crude all-age ischaemic stroke YLD rate increased by 2.75% per year (95% CI 2.68 to 2.82), while the crude all-age intracerebral haemorrhage DALY rate declined but its YLD rate and YLD share increased. Crude all-age rates were interpreted as population-level burden indicators influenced by population age structure, alongside age-stratified and decomposition analyses. Among adults aged 50 years or older, disability burden shifted towards older-old and oldest-old groups, particularly for ischaemic stroke. In 2023, combined all-age YLDs from ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage were approximately 4.77 million, corresponding descriptively to 128.2 YLDs per community health service centre/station and 16.7 YLDs per community health bed. Stroke in China is increasingly a survivorship and disability challenge. The burden-to-capacity proxy indicators provide planning context but do not directly measure rehabilitation access, adequacy, quality, or unmet need.

title: Staged Endodontic Management and Esthetic Rehabilitation of a Fractured Immature Incisor With Failed Endodontic Treatment and Iatrogenic Complications: A Case Report.
authors: Priya P, Basnet A.
abstract: Managing a previously treated immature incisor with multiple concurrent structural, endodontic, and periapical complications is clinically challenging. This report describes staged surgical, nonsurgical endodontic, and restorative management of a fractured, discolored tooth with a blunderbuss canal, overextended gutta-percha, apicomarginal defect, cervical perforation, and periapical cyst.

title: Sports-related peripheral neuropathies in athletes: mechanisms, imaging evaluation, and sport-specific patterns.
authors: Gulde MLS, Helito PV, Hagert E, Vidal Leao R, Mágero N, Bordalo M.
abstract: Peripheral neuropathy in athletes is increasingly recognized as a significant source of morbidity, with injury patterns varying according to the biomechanical demands of specific sports. Although peripheral nerve disorders in athletes may result from acute trauma, they more commonly arise from chronic, repetitive mechanical stress inherent to athletic activity. Despite their frequency, they frequently remain underdiagnosed, as clinical manifestations often overlap with other musculoskeletal disorders. Mechanisms of injury include compression, traction, laceration, ischemia, and repetitive microtrauma. Distinct athletic modalities are associated with characteristic neuropathies reflecting sport-specific kinematics and loading patterns. Awareness of these biomechanical factors and recognition of typical clinical presentations are essential for accurate assessment of athletes with suspected nerve injury. Diagnostic evaluation frequently requires advanced imaging modalities, particularly magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) and high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS), which enable detailed structural assessment of peripheral nerves and detection of secondary imaging findings. Electrodiagnostic studies may provide complementary functional information in selected cases. Early and precise diagnosis is critical to guide management, facilitate safe return to sport, and prevent long-term functional deficits. While most nerve disorders respond to conservative treatment, severe, progressive, or refractory cases may warrant surgical intervention to restore function and enable return to play (RTP). This review examines mechanisms of injury, clinical evaluation, classification systems, imaging findings, and sport-specific patterns of peripheral nerve injury across diverse athletic disciplines.

title: Spatial metabolic heterogeneity and immunometabolic plasticity in bone metastasis and therapeutic resistance.
authors: Zhang S, Yang B, Xiao G.
abstract: Bone metastases contain spatially distinct tumour, bone, stromal and immune compartments whose interactions evolve during treatment. These interactions can sustain resistant disease, but pathway presence alone does not establish a therapeutic dependency. This critical narrative review organises evidence around four dimensions of lesion state: resource availability, directional metabolic exchange, cellular state and treatment-induced selection. We focus on solid tumours, particularly breast, prostate and lung cancers, and distinguish human lesion observations from experimental causality. Osteoclast-derived glutamine, macrophage iron supply and collagen-derived hydroxyproline illustrate experimentally supported survival circuits whose quantitative contribution in patients remains unresolved. Direct human metabolic measurements are limited, although hyperpolarised carbon-13 imaging has demonstrated feasibility in selected prostate cancer bone metastases. Lesion-level pharmacodynamics is defined by an identified lesion, sampling interval, assay and expected proximal response, with drug exposure, target engagement and clinical benefit assessed separately. Tissue assays, tracer imaging and structural or diffusion imaging provide complementary information; none currently resolves all proposed intercellular exchanges in deep skeletal lesions. A four-item translational checklist requires candidate dependencies to be present in progressing disease, necessary under the relevant treatment pressure, inadequately compensated and measurable within the lesion.
