Progress requires assay-specific control of ischaemia and decalcification, functional testing in models relevant to human disease and prospective evaluation of mechanism-matched combinations.

title: Self-inflicted Methotrexate poisoning mimicking auto-inflammatory disease.
authors: Marteau P, Quéméneur-Wettling AS.

title: Robotic transabdominal specimen extraction vs. transanal specimen extraction for sigmoid and upper rectal cancer: a comparative analysis of short-term outcomes.
authors: Li TY, Luo AL, Min FZ, Yu T, Zou Y, Zuo JY, Ye SP.
abstract: Robotic surgery has become an established approach for the management of patients with sigmoid colon and upper rectal cancer (SURC). Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES), which avoids an additional abdominal wall incision, is a widely used minimally invasive approach in colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. It remains uncertain whether transanal specimen extraction, classified as type IV natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES-IV), offers advantages over conventional transabdominal specimen extraction (TASE) during robot-assisted surgery for SURC. We retrospectively compared the perioperative outcomes of the two extraction strategies. We retrospectively reviewed 254 patients who underwent robot-assisted surgery for SURC at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University, between January 2019 and January 2026. Ninety-one patients received NOSES-IV, and 163 received TASE. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 83 patients per group were included, and their short-term perioperative outcomes were compared. After matching, the baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups. Compared with the TASE group, the NOSES-IV group had a shorter gastrointestinal reconstruction time (P < 0.001) and less intraoperative blood loss (P = 0.022). Patients in the NOSES-IV group also ambulated (P = 0.029), passed flatus (P = 0.018), and resumed semiliquid diet earlier (P = 0.038). On postoperative days 1, 3 and 5, their C-reactive protein levels were lower (P = 0.017). They also had fewer incision-related complications (P = 0.014), a shorter postoperative hospital stay (P = 0.034), and lower visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores (P = 0.008). In this retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort, compared with TASE, robot-assisted NOSES-IV for SURC was associated with fewer incision-related complications, less postoperative pain, and earlier recovery. The total operative time, lymph node yield, resection margin status, and anorectal function at 3 months did not differ between the groups. These findings suggest that NOSES-IV is a feasible option for appropriately selected patients, but confirmation in larger, multicentre, prospective studies with longer follow-up is needed.

title: Robotic arthroplasty and the gap between technical precision and clinical benefit.
authors: Xu Z, Fan W, Kong K, Jin M, Li Z, Li D, He C, Mamuladze T, Korytkin AA, Li H, Zhai Z.
abstract: Robotic-assisted arthroplasty improves resection accuracy, component positioning, and reproducibility. Whether these technical gains produce clinically meaningful benefits remains uncertain. This expert narrative review drew on PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science searches performed on April 28, 2026. Systematic reviews and randomized trials were prioritized, supplemented by observational, registry, economic, and technical studies. Evidence was appraised qualitatively by design, follow-up, bias, and platform differences; technical endpoints were assessed separately from patient-important outcomes. Evidence most consistently supports fewer alignment and component-positioning outliers. Functional and perioperative benefits vary by procedure, platform, outcome, and follow-up; evidence for generalizable long-term benefit remains inconsistent. The precision-target gap is proposed as one explanation: more accurate execution may yield limited benefit when the surgical target is insufficiently validated for the patient. Small differences from conventional care, confounding, and outcome measurement provide alternative explanations. Clinical value requires evidence that a surgical target improves outcomes and that robotic delivery adds benefit. Patient-specific models, intraoperative sensing, and decision support require external validation and prospective comparison with optimized conventional care. Adoption should reflect patient-important outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and local practice.

title: Reliability and feasibility of the ankylosing spondylitis performance index (ASPI) in routine clinical care for patients with axial spondyloarthritis.
authors: Hellamand P, van de Sande MGH, van der Horst Bruinsma IE, van Weely SFE.
abstract: Objective Patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) frequently experience limitations in physical function. The performance-based ankylosing spondylitis performance index (ASPI), developed from BASFI items, has demonstrated validity, reliability, and responsiveness in research settings for evaluating physical function. We aimed to assess its reliability and feasibility in routine care. Methods In this prospective observational cohort study, patients with axSpA aged 18-70 years were included if they had a clinical diagnosis of axSpA and were either on a stable NSAID dose for >6 weeks, a stable tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) dose for >3 months, or had axSpA without sacroiliitis on X-ray initiating TNFi. ASPI was performed at baseline and 3 months. Test-retest reliability at baseline and 3 months was assessed in the stable treatment group. Feasibility was assessed in all patients using patient-reported outcomes. Results A total of 39 patients (32 on stable treatment) were included, with a mean age of 44 years, and ~50% women. Bland-Altman analysis revealed low systematic bias (0.1 s), with limits of agreement from -4.4 to 4.6 s. The ASPI composite score showed excellent reliability (ICCs 0.90-0.91). Feasibility was high with a 92% completion rate at baseline; median (IQR) perceived burden score of 5 (2-7) (0 = no burden, 10 = burdensome); and a median score of 10 (1 = unfavorable, 10 = favorable) for annual administration. Conclusion This study supports the ASPI as a reliable, feasible, and acceptable instrument for evaluating physical function in patients with axSpA. Together with previous evidence on its clinimetric properties, these findings support its potential use as a complementary performance-based measure alongside patient-reported outcomes. Larger studies are needed to evaluate its broader implementation across diverse clinical settings. Key Points • Although the ASPI has demonstrated validity, reliability, and responsiveness in research settings, evidence on its feasibility and reliability in routine clinical care has been limited. • The ASPI showed excellent test-retest reliability in routine care, with intraclass correlation coefficients meeting the threshold for individual-level assessment. • The ASPI was feasible and acceptable from the patient perspective, with high completion rates, clear instructions, and favorable ratings for annual administration. • Together with previous evidence on its clinimetric properties, these findings strengthen the rationale for using the ASPI as a complementary performance-based measure of physical function in routine axSpA care, while larger studies are needed to evaluate its implementation across diverse clinical settings.

title: Projection restoration with dual-domain Swin refinement for sparse-view CT reconstruction.
journal: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
authors: Yadav B, Raghunath A, Weber F, Maier A.
abstract: Purpose We investigated whether projection restoration before reconstruction, followed by image-domain refinement, improves sparse-view computed tomography (CT) quality under aggressive undersampling. Methods A compact dual-domain Swin framework restores sparse sinograms before geometry-aware differentiable filtered back projection (FBP) and refines the resulting images. The projection branch uses gated Swin processing and angular upsampling with a bicubic bypass. Abdominal AAPM sinograms contained 2304 full views, retaining 576, 288, and 144 views at 4x, 8x, and 16x. Comparators were FBP, bilinear and bicubic interpolation, ProCT, and geometry-adapted DuDoTrans; ablations used ten epochs. Results DuDoSwin achieved PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 45.64 dB/0.981/0.011 at 4x, 44.11 dB/0.975/0.020 at 8x, and 42.02 dB/0.963/0.035 at 16x. Mean PSNR and SSIM exceeded ProCT and DuDoTrans; DuDoTrans had lower LPIPS at 4x and 8x. DuDoSwin used 1.36-1.80 million parameters but was slower than both learned comparators. Comparisons against interpolation and DuDoTrans were significant in Holm-corrected paired tests. Bypass removal improved ablation PSNR by 0.35 dB at 8x. Evaluation included the validation patient; exclusion changed mean PSNR by at most 0.1 dB and altered no ranking. Slice-wise tests ignore within-patient dependence. Conclusion Explicit projection restoration followed by image-domain refinement yielded favorable PSNR and SSIM, with perceptual metric and computational trade-offs. Neither residual shortcut improved the 8x ablation results. Independent patient evaluation remains necessary.

title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Prevention of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Fiandeiro M, Gupta S, Nicholson T, ICM Shoulder Group.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is an uncommon but serious complication of shoulder arthroplasty. Many preventive practices are also extrapolated from hip and knee arthroplasty despite important differences in microbiology and surgical procedures. Furthermore, prevention is complicated by the importance of Cutibacterium acnes, which resides within the dermis and sebaceous structures and may not be reliably eliminated by conventional skin preparation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) aimed to develop evidence-based consensus recommendations for prevention of shoulder PJI. Methods The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts. More than 100 proposed questions were refined to 86, of which 25 addressed prevention. For each question, delegates performed a systematic literature review and developed a proposed recommendation. Evidence and recommendations were presented to the full group, discussed, revised, and voted upon using a modified Delphi process. Delegates voted agree, disagree, or abstain. Degree of consensus and strength of recommendation were assessed separately. Results Consensus was achieved for all 25 questions, with 65%-100% agreement. Male sex and clinical or physical evidence of malnutrition were identified as PJI risk factors. Moderate-strength evidence supported avoiding corticosteroid injection within 3 months of shoulder arthroplasty, while evidence regarding hemoglobin A1c >8% was conflicting. Consensus supported individualized perioperative management of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis, alcohol-based skin preparation, and avoidance of razor shaving. Evidence was insufficient to determine the effects of testosterone supplementation, diagnostic indication, continuation of antiplatelet therapy before revision, extended oral antibiotic prophylaxis, or antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and other invasive procedures. Evidence was also insufficient to support specific intraoperative interventions for reducing PJI, including intrawound antibiotics, antiseptic irrigation, iodine-impregnated drapes, electrocautery, tranexamic acid, or selection of a particular arthroplasty type. Conclusion The 2025 ICM identified several strategies applicable to current practice while highlighting substantial gaps in shoulder-specific evidence. Many recommendations remain based on limited or extrapolated evidence. Prospective shoulder-specific studies using clinical PJI as the primary outcome are needed to determine which prevention strategies provide meaningful benefit.

title: President and Program Chairs' Introduction.
authors: Lin SS, Easley ME, Cooper MT, Park JS.

title: Predictors and clinical outcomes of extubation failure in patients with cervical spinal cord injury.
authors: Yeremian S, Wilensky AH, Kuhls DA, McNickle AG.
abstract: Introduction Respiratory compromise is common in cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) and poses a challenge in deciding whether to extubate or perform a tracheostomy. This study evaluated the characteristics of failed extubations and hypothesized that those with unsuccessful extubation attempts would have a higher trauma burden and worse weaning parameters. Methods This was a retrospective review of intubated cervical SCI at a Level 1 trauma center from 2018 to 2024. Demographics, injury, surgical and airway management data were collected. Location of intubation and extubation, weaning parameters, and time to airway event or failure were tabulated. Statistical analysis was completed using Stata with p Results Seventy patients with SCI were analyzed with a mean age of 54 years (range 18-89) and 62 (89%) males. Twenty successful extubations (SE) were compared to 36 failed extubations (FE), excluding the direct to tracheostomy (10) or terminally extubated (4) patients. Frequency of TBI (5% FE vs 14% SE, p = 0.3), blunt cerebrovascular injury (25% vs. 32%, p = 0.63) and ISS (30 vs 23, p = 0.13) were not statistically different. Documented weaning parameters - rapid shallow breathing index and negative inspiratory force were similar, although more FE patients were extubated in the OR/PACU. FE patients had significantly fewer hospital and ICU-free days; however, mortality differences did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions Failed extubation in SCI is associated with longer length of stay. Trauma burden and weaning parameters were not correlated with FE; however, extubation outside of the ICU may increase the risk of failure.

title: Post-Treatment Follow-up, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport: Proceedings of the International Consensus Meetings on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
authors: Rubin J, Tham A, Butler JJ, Gauthier P, Hedbany D, Kennedy JG, Smyth NA, Murawski CD, Adams SB, Berlet GC, Buda R, Labib SA, Nunley JA, Raikin SM, Andrews CL, Angthong C, Batista JP, Bayer S, Becher C, Boakye LAT, Brown AJ, Calder JDF, Canata GL, Carreira DS, Clanton TO, Dahmen J, D'Hooghe P, DiGiovanni CW, Dombrowski ME, Ferkel RD, Ferrao PNF, Glazebrook M, Giza E, Gomaa M, Görtz S, Haleem AM, Hamid KS, Hangody L, Hannon CP, Haverkamp D, Hertel J, Hintermann B, Hogan MV, Hunt KJ, Hurley ET, Karlsson J, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, Kim HJ, Kong SW, Lambers KTA, Woo Lee J, Lee KB, Ling JS, Longo UG, Marangon A, McCollum G, Mitchell AW, Mittwede PN, Nehrer S, Niemeyer P, O'Malley MJ, Osei-Hwedieh D, Paul J, Pearce CJ, Pereira H, Popchak A, Prado MP, Reilingh ML, Rothrauff BB, Schon LC, Simpson H, Sofka CM, Spennacchio P, Stone JW, Sullivan M, Takao M, Tanaka Y, Thordarson DB, Tuan R, Valderrabano V, van Bergen CJA, van Dijk CN, van Dijk PAD, Vannini F, Vaseenon T, Walther M, Wiewiorski M, Xu X, Yasui Y, Hua Y, Yoshimura I, Younger ASE, Zhang Z.
abstract: BackgroundPostoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and return to sport (RTS) are key components of recovery following surgical management of osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT). However, substantial variability exists in postoperative protocols, with limited high-quality evidence guiding clinical practicesMethodsInternational experts convened during the International Congress on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle (ICCRA) in Pittsburgh, USA (2017), with subsequent ratification of recommendations in New York, USA (2025). The original consensus statements were developed using a modified Delphi process involving electronic surveys, structured questionnaires, and expert discussion. Consensus strength was defined as consensus (51%-74%), strong consensus (75%-99%), or unanimous (100%). The recommendations addressed postoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and RTS following OLT management.ResultsA total of 16 consensus statements were developed and subsequently ratified, comprising 7 statements addressing post-treatment follow-up and 9 addressing rehabilitation and RTS. All statements achieved strong consensus, with agreement ranging from 75% to 98%. Follow-up recommendations emphasized standardized clinical assessment and patient-reported outcomes, with extended monitoring in select patients. Rehabilitation recommendations supported early controlled motion and progressive weightbearing, with individualized progression according to procedure and clinical performance. Return to sport recommendations emphasized functional recovery and individualized decision-making. Ten statements (63%) were classified exclusively as Grade E, highlighting the limited evidence supporting several recommendations.ConclusionThe ICCRA consensus statements establish a structured framework for postoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and RTS following surgical management of OLT. Despite strong expert agreement, several recommendations remain supported by limited evidence, underlining the need for prospective studies to establish validated, procedure-specific rehabilitation protocols and objective RTS criteria.Level of Evidence: V, expert consensus .

title: Pin-related complications in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 15,874 knees.
authors: Ade-Conde M, Dhanoa D, Wolfstadt JI, Lanting BA, Abdel Khalik H.
abstract: This review evaluated the incidence, characteristics, and management of pin-related complications following robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA). MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from January 1, 2010, to April 15, 2026 for studies evaluating pin-related complications following primary RA-TKA. Pooled complication rates were estimated using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model, and a random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analysis compared complication rates between intra-incisional and extra-incisional tracker pin placement. Descriptive analyses summarized pin techniques, complications, and management. Thirty-seven studies comprising 15,874 RA-TKAs were included with a mean age of 65.5 years, body mass index of 30.5 kg/m², and follow-up of 10.7 months. Femoral pins were most commonly placed intra-incisionally (54.9%), whereas tibial pins were most commonly placed extra-incisionally (52.5%). The random-effects pooled pin-related complication rate was 0.47% (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.90%), compared with a crude rate of 0.89% (142/15,874). Wound complications (n = 93, 0.59%) and fractures (n = 24, 0.15%) were most common. Of the 93 wound complications, 69 (74.2%) occurred at extra-incisional tibial sites. Of 40 pin-related complications with reported management, 70% were managed nonoperatively. Meta-analysis of four studies (5,635 knees) found no significant difference between intra-incisional pin placement (risk ratio [RR] 0.25, 95% CI 0.03-2.06; P = 0.20; I² = 70%). Among RA-TKA pin-related complications with reported management, most were managed nonoperatively. Wound complications were most frequently reported at extra-incisional tibial sites, but comparative evidence did not demonstrate a significant difference between placement strategies. Further comparative studies and standardized reporting are needed to optimize pin safety. PROSPERO ID: CRD420261371245. LOE: IV.

title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
authors: Marié-Bailly I, Guillard R, Wanneveich M, De Dieuleveult B, Hassan M, Vérin M.
abstract: Tinnitus affects 14% of the global population, with 2% experiencing a severe form of the condition. Sound therapy using white noise emitted by hearing aids is a common intervention, supported by the phenomenon of residual inhibition observed during tinnitus assessment. This study aims to investigate whether audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training can improve the quality of life of patients with chronic subjective tinnitus by enabling them to listen to their own phonation, which may mask the tinnitus or induce residual inhibition. We will conduct a prospective, controlled, monocentric, 2-arm block-randomized study, stratified by the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) score, involving two groups for two sequential phases (Phase 1 and Phase 2). Fifty-six patients with tinnitus, recruited from the Ear Nose Throat (ENT) Department of Orléans University Hospital, will undergo a five-week training program, randomized into weekly remote group workshops, and daily individual sessions using specially developed videos. Training efficacy will be assessed through self-report questionnaires. The primary endpoint, the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, will be assessed at three ENT medical visits: at inclusion, end of phase 1 and end of phase 2. Additionally, patients in both groups will regularly complete Visual Analog Scales for Tinnitus and five related questions (noise, cervical, jaw, sleep, stress-anxiety) via a secure digital platform throughout the study. High-density electroencephalograms (HD-EEG) will be performed in a blinded manner before and after Phase 1 at the Neurology Department of Orléans University Hospital. This pilot study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of audio-proprio-phonatory training in patients with chronic subjective tinnitus and to objectively measure its effects using HD-EEG. We will explore potential correlations between changes brain activity (such as functional brain connectivity) and clinical responses to the intervention.

title: Multi-feature fusion for grassland information extraction and temporal change monitoring.
authors: Liu X, Chen J, Liu Z, Zhu X, Jiang S, Kang W.
abstract: Grasslands play a vital role in maintaining ecological security and supporting sustainable development, yet accurate extraction and dynamic monitoring remain challenging in complex mountainous regions. This study takes Chengbu Miao Autonomous County, Hunan Province, as the study area and develops a multi-feature fusion framework on the Google Earth Engine platform by integrating optical imagery, Sentinel-1 SAR data, vegetation indices, texture features, topographic factors, and time-series characteristics. A Random Forest model was employed for high-accuracy grassland extraction, while multi-temporal remote sensing observations from selected cloud-free years between 2000 and 2025 were used to analyze long-term spatial distribution and temporal dynamics. Fractional vegetation cover (FVC) was introduced to assess grassland ecological conditions, and Nanshan Pasture was selected to investigate the impacts of topography, human activities, and climatic factors on grassland variation. The results show that multi-feature fusion significantly improves classification accuracy, achieving an overall accuracy (OA) of 93.79% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.7165 in the optimal feature combination scheme, with optical and SAR data exhibiting strong complementarity under complex terrain conditions. Grassland area in Chengbu County remained relatively stable from 2000 to 2025, with annual variations ranging from 47.32 to 52.15 km² and no significant long-term change trend. The mean FVC exhibited relatively stable interannual fluctuations, with values generally ranging from 0.59 to 0.72 during most years. However, spatial analysis of FVC trends revealed considerable heterogeneity, with significant decreasing trends observed in localized areas, particularly in the southwestern part of Nanshan Pasture, indicating potential vegetation degradation risks. In Nanshan Pasture, FVC showed a significant negative correlation with DEM (r = -0.2839) and precipitation (r = -0.589), while correlations with human activities and land surface temperature were relatively weak. Overall, grassland dynamics in the study area may reflect the combined effects of environmental conditions and human activities, although the relationships identified in this study mainly represent statistical associations rather than causal mechanisms. The proposed framework provides an effective methodological reference for grassland monitoring, ecological assessment, and sustainable management in subtropical mountainous grassland environments.

title: Mixed acinar adenocarcinoma and small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the prostate with extensive skeletal and nodal metastases and preserved prostate-specific membrane antigen avidity.
authors: Sharma JO, Bathija N, Mahajan R, Soni A, Goel A, Marcus S.

title: Minor Deviations in Cup Center of Rotation Can Reduce Impingement-Free Range of Motion in Total Hip Arthroplasty.
authors: Sullivan M, Clark GW, Chartier L, Esposito CI.
abstract: Background Precise restoration of the acetabular center of rotation (COR) is important for hip biomechanics, particularly in patients with stiff spinopelvic mobility. This study quantified the effect of small COR shifts on impingement-free virtual range of motion (ROM). Methods We retrospectively reviewed the final acetabular component position achieved during robotically assisted total hip arthroplasty in 100 patients. Impingement-free ROM was measured for the final plan, then reassessed after translating the COR 2 mm anteriorly, superiorly, or medially. Patients were stratified by spinopelvic flexibility. Results A 2 mm COR shift altered virtual ROM in 93% of patients. Medial translation increased failure to meet any functional ROM threshold from 16% to 30% ( P P Conclusions Small deviations from planned COR meaningfully reduce virtual ROM and have the greatest impact in patients with stiff spinopelvic mechanics.

title: Leuprorelin Acetate for Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy: A Systematic Review of Clinical Efficacy, Long-Term Outcomes, and Safety Considerations.
authors: Wang B, Wang I, Park C, Barkhaus PE, Shirilla D.
abstract: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA; Kennedy disease) is a rare X-linked neuromuscular disorder caused by a CAG repeat expansion in the androgen receptor gene. Leuprorelin acetate, a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonist, suppresses androgen signaling and is approved for SBMA-associated dysphagia in Japan; however, evidence regarding efficacy remains heterogeneous. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception through June 18, 2026, for studies evaluating leuprorelin in genetically confirmed SBMA. Randomized trials, observational cohorts, natural history-controlled studies, extension studies, and safety case reports were included, and findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Eleven studies met inclusion criteria, including eight efficacy studies (460 patients) and three safety-focused case reports. Leuprorelin reduced pathogenic androgen receptor accumulation and improved biochemical markers, including serum creatine kinase and creatinine decline. Although neither pivotal randomized trial demonstrated significant short-term functional improvement at 48 weeks, longer-term studies showed slower decline in Revised Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R), Limb Norris, and Norris Bulbar scores and improved event-free survival from pneumonia and death. Benefits were greatest with earlier treatment, particularly disease duration < 10 years. Leuprorelin was generally well tolerated; common adverse effects included hot flushes, sexual dysfunction, and decreased bone mineral density. Leuprorelin may slow long-term functional deterioration in SBMA, with greater benefit following early initiation and prolonged treatment.

title: Introduction of contraceptive implants as a family planning strategy in Honduras and Chiapas: Results from the Salud Mesoamerica Initiative (SMI).
authors: Santoro A, Basualdo N, Rolón F, Bartolomeu L, Volij C, Simon M, Hagedorn B, Ríos-Zertuche D, Esteban S, Rubinstein A.
abstract: Expanding access to a broad range of contraceptive methods is critical for reducing unintended pregnancies and improving reproductive health. This study evaluates the introduction of subdermal contraceptive implants in the selected areas of Honduras and Chiapas, Mexico, in the context of the Salud Mesoamérica Initiative, a results-based financing program focused on disadvantaged populations. Data were obtained from household surveys conducted between 2012 and 2022 among women aged 15-49 years in selected intervention and comparison municipalities in Chiapas, Mexico, and Honduras, using a two-stage sampling design. Indicators included contraceptive prevalence rates, reasons for method switching, and adoption by sociodemographic characteristics. Findings show a substantial increase in implant use in both settings over time. In the selected areas of Honduras, implant uptake increased gradually, reaching 7.9% in the 2022 SMI household survey, while in the selected areas of Chiapas use rose to 7.2%. Younger women aged 20-29 years and those with full literacy exhibited the highest adoption rates. In the selected areas of Chiapas and Honduras, implants most often replaced non-modern and short-acting hormonal methods, suggesting successful integration into the existing method mix. Variations in adoption across sociodemographic subgroups highlight persistent inequities. The results underscore the potential of subdermal implants to expand access to long-acting reversible contraception in resource-limited settings. To sustain and enhance this progress, strategies must address sociocultural and structural barriers, ensuring equitable access across all population groups and mitigating service disruptions. These findings may inform future strategies to expand informed contraceptive choice in similar resource-limited settings; their effects on reproductive health outcomes require further evaluation.

title: Intravenous midazolam alters short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses differently in younger and older adults.
authors: McGregor KM, Safavynia SA, Novak T, Weber AM, Wang J, Nocera JR, Woodbury A, Crosson B, García PS.
abstract: Objective Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely understood. We examined whether intravenous midazolam differentially modulates corticospinal excitability and short-interval paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) responses in younger and older adults. Methods Sixteen younger adults (18-35 years) and sixteen older adults (50-69 years) underwent single-pulse and paired-pulse (conditioning stimulus: 110% motor threshold; test stimulus: 143% motor threshold) TMS of the left primary motor cortex at baseline and during intravenous midazolam administration. Single-pulse motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude was used to assess corticospinal excitability. Short-interval paired-pulse responses were quantified as the ratio of conditioned to unconditioned MEP amplitude. Results At baseline, younger adults showed greater corticospinal excitability than older adults, reflected by larger single-pulse MEP amplitudes (adjusted p = 0.04). Younger adults demonstrated paired-pulse inhibition at baseline, reflected by a conditioned/unconditioned MEP ratio below 1.0 (ratio = 0.73; adjusted p Conclusions Younger and older adults differed in baseline corticospinal excitability and in short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses. Intravenous midazolam reduced corticospinal excitability and altered paired-pulse response patterns, eliminating baseline paired-pulse inhibition in younger adults while producing little measurable change in older adults. These findings suggest that aging may modify the net motor cortical response to benzodiazepine challenge. The results should be interpreted in relation to the paired-pulse stimulation parameters used and support further studies using complementary approaches to characterize age-related differences in inhibitory and facilitatory motor cortical circuits.

title: Injury mechanisms and imaging findings in mixed martial arts.
authors: Thompson G, McCarthy CL.
abstract: Mixed martial arts (MMA) is a rapidly growing combat sport that combines striking and grappling disciplines including boxing, Muay Thai, karate, judo, and Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ). As participation and professional competition increase, musculoskeletal radiologists become increasingly likely to encounter characteristic MMA-related injuries. Although craniofacial trauma, lacerations, and concussion remain the most common injuries in competition, several distinctive musculoskeletal injury patterns arise from grappling, takedowns, and submission techniques. Understanding the biomechanical forces generated by these manoeuvres contributes to accurate image interpretation and appropriate management. Injuries arising from submission techniques are particularly associated with recognisable imaging patterns. The arm bar most commonly results in ulnar collateral ligament injury at the elbow, whereas the Americana and Kimura shoulder locks may produce anterior and posterior capsulolabral injuries respectively. Heel hooks are associated with rotational knee trauma involving the anterior cruciate ligament and collateral ligaments, with injury patterns varying according to whether valgus-external rotation or varus-internal rotation forces are applied. Less common but highly characteristic injuries include combined lateral collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament injury with intact cruciate ligaments as a result of grappling guard positions and choke manoeuvres. This review summarises the major MMA techniques, associated mechanisms of injury, and key imaging findings relevant to musculoskeletal radiologists.

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Exposure Associated With a Migraine With Brainstem Aura-Like Presentation and Prolonged Recovery: A Case Report.
authors: Al-Dawoudi A, Varlamov D, Alhallak S, Dalain M.
abstract: Immersive virtual reality (VR) exposure can produce a range of neurological symptoms, but its possible relationship with prolonged migraine-related symptoms remains poorly characterized. We report a 32-year-old male who developed acute disorientation, vertigo, cognitive clouding, derealization, and sensory disturbances immediately following a 30-min immersive VR session. Symptoms partially improved but recurred with sensory overstimulation the following day. Despite unremarkable neuro-otological examinations, the patient experienced a markedly atypical, two-week period of persistent neurological symptoms featuring hypersomnia, cognitive fatigue, and sensory hypersensitivity. The presentation was considered a migraine with brainstem aura-like presentation, although it did not fulfill ICHD-3 criteria for definite migraine with brainstem aura. Symptoms gradually resolved completely by approximately 2 weeks, with no recurrence reported at the 3- and 6-month follow-ups. This case describes a temporal association between immersive VR exposure and a prolonged migraine-like neurological presentation, highlighting the need for clinical awareness of symptoms occurring after immersive digital exposure.

title: Hypertonic Saline-Induced Cramp-Like Muscle Contractions Occur Through Acetylcholine Receptors at the Neuromuscular Junction in Rats.
authors: Ota H, Kobayashi Y, Yamamoto R, Ueda M, Akaki J, Mizumura K, Taguchi T.
abstract: Introduction/aims Muscle cramps are characterized by sudden, involuntary, painful contractions of skeletal muscle. However, adequate treatment and prevention methods and experimental models are poorly established. In this study (Experiment I), we developed a putative model that mimics clinical muscle cramps using intramuscular hypertonic saline (HS) infusion. In Experiment II, we tested the hypothesis that HS-induced cramp-like contractions occur via nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ). Methods Under isoflurane anesthesia, electromyographic (EMG) activity was recorded using a needle-type electrode inserted into the rat tibialis anterior (TA) muscle. Through a 30-gauge needle, 5% HS was continuously administered to the TA approximately 1.5 mm distal from the recording electrode. Results In Experiment I, the number, amplitude, and root mean square values of EMG events were significantly higher in the group treated with HS than in the group treated with isotonic saline (IS). The HS-induced EMG activity increased as the volume of HS increased (10-100 μL for 1 min). In Experiment II, HS-induced EMG activity was nearly abolished following the intravenous administration of pancuronium bromide, a blocker of nAChRs, at the NMJ, but not μ-conotoxin GIIIB, a selective blocker of skeletal muscle Na v 1.4 channels. HS-treated muscle showed greater histological alterations with enlarged interstitial spaces in the cross-sectional area. Discussion HS infusion elicited robust, reproducible EMG activity, which occurred largely via nAChRs at the NMJ but not via Na v 1.4 channels on the muscle cell membrane. Thus, this model is useful for studying muscle cramps, and the NMJ could be a therapeutic target.

title: Healthcare utilization before and after a diagnosis of giant cell arteritis - a population-based cohort study in Denmark.
authors: Gaster T, Donskov AO, de Thurah A, Nørgaard M, Hauge EM, Keller KK.

title: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in patients with rheumatic diseases: clinical characteristics, associated factors, and fragility fractures.
authors: Ok NF, Duruöz MT, Gezer HH.
abstract: Background Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely used in the treatment of rheumatic diseases because of their potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. However, prolonged GC exposure is associated with glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) and an increased risk of fragility fractures. Objectives To determine the prevalence of reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and densitometric osteoporosis and to investigate factors associated with BMD and fragility fractures in patients with rheumatic diseases receiving GC therapy. Methods This cross-sectional medical records review study included 223 patients with rheumatic diseases receiving GC therapy who underwent osteoporosis screening. Clinical characteristics, GC exposure, fragility fractures, laboratory parameters and femoral neck and lumbar spine dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) results were recorded. Patients were classified by the lowest T-score using World Health Organization criteria as normal (T-score > - 1.0), osteopenia (- 2.5 Results Mean age was 59.9 ± 10.9 years; 93.3% were female. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common diagnosis (54.3%). Among 214 patients with available DXA classification, 16.4% had normal BMD, 55.6% osteopenia and 28.0% osteoporosis; thus, 83.6% had reduced BMD. Patients with reduced BMD were older, had longer disease duration, longer GC treatment duration and higher cumulative GC exposure than those with normal BMD (p Conclusion Reduced BMD was common among patients with rheumatic diseases receiving long-term GC therapy and was associated with older age, longer disease duration and greater GC exposure. Most fragility fractures occurred in patients without densitometric osteoporosis, suggesting that BMD alone may not fully reflect fracture risk in this population. Key points • Reduced BMD (T-score ≤ - 1.0) was present in 83.6% of patients with rheumatic diseases receiving long-term GC therapy, whereas densitometric osteoporosis (T-score ≤ - 2.5) was present in 28.0%. • Fragility fractures were frequent, and approximately two-thirds of patients with fractures did not have densitometric osteoporosis. • Older age, female sex and longer disease duration were independently associated with fragility fractures, highlighting the need for fracture risk assessment beyond BMD alone.

title: GT-PNID: A lightweight graph-temporal network integrating GCN and transformer for power network intrusion detection.
authors: Zhou H, Wu M, Chen W, Zhou Q.
abstract: Driven by the advancement of information technology, the transformation of traditional power grids toward intelligence has rendered power systems more vulnerable to cybersecurity risks arising from greater openness and connectivity. Smart grid communication networks exhibit high heterogeneity, diverse protocols, and strict real-time constraints. Existing intrusion detection systems suffer from two key limitations: neglect of spatiotemporal dependencies in network traffic, which hinders the modeling of complex attack evolution, and absence of a unified detection framework with cross-scenario generalization capability. To overcome these limitations, this study develops GT-PNID, a graph-temporal network-based intrusion detection model designed for grid communication networks. The model utilizes a sliding-window dynamic graph construction mechanism to transform heterogeneous traffic into spatiotemporal graph structures. Subsequently, graph convolutional layers are applied to extract local spatial features, while a multilayer Transformer is introduced to model long-range temporal dependencies, followed by graph-level feature fusion for joint spatiotemporal representation. Experiments on CICIDS2017 and NSL-KDD datasets demonstrate that accuracy and F1-scores exceed 99.98%, while the model's parameter count (424,478) and per-sample inference time (0.09 ms) are substantially lower than mainstream methods, confirming its superior detection capability, lightweight efficiency, and cross-dataset generalization potential for smart grid security.

title: Fuzzy-clustering-based multi-scale intrusion detection for the industrial internet of things.
authors: Yang Y, Zhang D, He Q, Lin M, Zhao J.
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) faces severe intrusion-detection challenges under multi-protocol, multi-device, and massive heterogeneous traffic, especially extreme class imbalance and poor minority-class detection. To address this, we propose a fuzzy-clustering-based multi-scale intrusion detection model (FPBW-IDS). At the data level, we introduce boundary-prioritized FCM-SMOTE: fuzzy memberships distinguish core vs. border samples, interpolation is prioritized in high-membership regions, and sampling weights are adjusted by membership, thereby significantly enhancing minority-class representation and suppressing noise diffusion while keeping the majority class fixed at a multiplier of 1.0. At the feature-learning level, we build three parallel branches across the spatial, temporal, and frequency domains: parallel Pyramid Depthwise Separable Convolutions (PDSC) to capture spatial (cross-feature) dependencies, BiGRU to model temporal dependencies, and wavelet transforms to extract multi-scale spectral statistics; their outputs are fused with learned weighting to form a complementary tri-domain representation. Experiments on the CICIDS2017 dataset show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance under both unsampled and sampled settings: Accuracy 99.39%, Precision 98.22%, Recall 93.69%, F1 95.56% in the comprehensive comparison; and Accuracy 98.97%, Recall 99.09%, F1 96.69% in a recall-oriented setting, markedly reducing missed detections while maintaining stable training/validation curves and a small generalization gap. These results show the effectiveness and reliability of clustering-guided oversampling combined with tri-domain multi-scale representation for IIoT intrusion detection.

title: Experimental and theoretical investigation of parameter-driven stability and chaos in a non-linear neuron circuit model.
authors: Ehsan H, Sajjad H, Jhangeer A, Říha L.
abstract: In this study, a neural-inspired electronic circuit consisting of a pressure-sensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo model with the addition of a piezoelectric bi-membrane and two capacitors is explored. The governing equations are obtained analytically from Kirchhoff's laws, which represent the nonlinear interactions, oscillatory response, and stability of the circuit. A perturbation term is added to investigate the deviations from the system potential, and the transitions in the system are studied under the assumption of the model. By applying statistical methods and eigenvalue analysis, the parameter space is systematically subdivided and examined, and the results show that the behavior of the system is dominated by divergent behavior, although some periodic oscillatory behavior is seen in certain regions. This highlights the importance of initial conditions and parameter selection on the behavior of the system, which are essential to obtaining stable behavior and developing an efficient control design. Furthermore, an ensemble-size sensitivity analysis is performed to verify the robustness and convergence of the statistical characterization across different numbers of initial conditions. Phase disturbance plots, power spectrum density plots, attractor reconstruction plots, return maps, and noise detection maps are used to analyze the system dynamics. In addition, a multi-sum (multi-parameter interaction) diagram is created to depict the interactions between circuit variables and the overall system behavior.

title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Si-based agent in Rheumatoid Arthritis with complicating vestibular impairment.
authors: Harada S, Koyama Y, Kobayashi Y, Imai T, Yoshioka Y, Kobayashi H, Inohara H, Shimada S.
abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive disability. Although current therapies have improved clinical outcomes, safer and more effective therapeutic approaches remain needed. Silicon (Si)-based agents have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and have shown beneficial effects in several inflammatory disease models. Methods We evaluated the effects of oral administration of a Si-based agent in a type II collagen-induced arthritis mouse model. Arthritis severity was assessed using an arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and the hindlimb extension reflex test. Serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels were also measured. Vestibular function was evaluated using the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), and inner-ear structural changes were assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and histological analysis. Results The Si-based agent reduced arthritis-related outcomes, including the arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and joint movement restriction, and reduced serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels. In contrast, no significant differences between the Si-based agent and control groups were detected in VOR-related outcomes, endolymphatic space measurements, or inner-ear histological findings. Conclusions These findings suggest that the Si-based agent may have beneficial effects on arthritis-related manifestations. However, its effects on the vestibular function-related outcomes examined in this study were not evident. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between RA and vestibular dysfunction and to determine the potential therapeutic effects of Si-based agent on these complications.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of open-weight LLMs for multi-domain Bengali text classification with zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
authors: Hosen MH, Nawar S, Chowdhury R, Uddin A, Rabbi RI, Othman KR, Symon NK.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced multilingual NLP significantly, yet their effectiveness for Bengali, a globally important but low-resource language, remains understudied due to limited linguistic resources and the absence of a standardized evaluation benchmark. This is due to the unavailability of large linguistic resources and the lack of a standard benchmarking framework, which has yet to be established. This study aims to address the underrepresentation of Bengali text classification by leading a systematic evaluation. It involves assessing multiple open-weight LLMs on Bengali text classification tasks and observing their limitations and regular error patterns. The procedure consists of six open-weight LLMs, which include LLaMA-3.2-3B, Mistral-V3-7B, DeepSeek-R1-8B, Phi-4-14B, Gemma-2-27B, and Qwen-2.5-72B, and are evaluated using four critical text classification tasks in Bengali, namely sentiment analysis, emotion recognition, hate-speech detection, and fake-news classification. Furthermore, two prompting methods are compared in the context of zero-shot and few-shot prompting using both the vLLM inference engine and Hugging Face Transformers pipelines to investigate the adaptability of the models in resource-limited settings. Across all four tasks, the two largest models (Qwen-2.5-72B and Gemma-2-27B) obtained the highest scores, although the ranking was not strictly monotonic in parameter count and, because each scale is represented by a single model family, the design cannot attribute these differences to model size alone. When training in zero-shot, Qwen-2.5-72B showed the best performance at 79.90% accuracy and 79.88% Macro-F1 score, showing amazing accuracy on hate-speech detection. In the case of fake news, Gemma-2-27B performed best at 84.45% accuracy and 84.33% Macro-F1 score. With a few-shot set-up, Gemma-2-27B and Qwen-2.5-72B demonstrated a high level of performance in terms of Macro-F1 score, reaching 84.17% for fake-news detection and 66.80% for emotion recognition, respectively. Paired multi-model tests (Cochran's Q with Holm-corrected McNemar post-hoc comparisons) confirmed significant differences among the six models across all tasks and prompting settings, whereas the effect of five-shot prompting, obtained with a single fixed demonstration set, was significant for only 4 of 24 model-task combinations after correction and never for the three largest models. The findings characterise benchmark classification performance under the evaluated settings rather than real-world effectiveness, and indicate that model scale, multilingual pre-training, and in-context demonstrations are jointly associated with, but cannot be causally isolated as drivers of, performance on Bengali text classification.

title: Erratum to: Can Orthopaedic Surgery Go Green? Environmental Footprint of Disposable Versus Reusable Instruments in TKA.

title: Enhanced Diagnosis and Management of Far-Out Syndrome Using 3D Visualization and Uni-Portal Non-Coaxial Spinal Endoscopic Surgery: A Case Report With Literature Review.
authors: Wu H, Chen Z, Cheng X, Dong R, Li T, Qu Y, Song E.
abstract: Background Far-out syndrome (FOS) is an uncommon cause of L5 radiculopathy that may be missed when extraforaminal compression lies beyond routine imaging planes. This report describes the added value of three-dimensional (3D) CT/magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) fusion for diagnosing persistent symptoms after lumbar endoscopic surgery and planning revision decompression. Case presentation A 55-year-old woman had persistent right L5 radiculopathy after unilateral biportal endoscopic discectomy (UBED). CT/MRI suggested L5-S1 extraforaminal stenosis. Patient-specific 3D CT/MRN fusion showed the exiting L5 root compressed by the L5 transverse process, sacral ala, posterior osteophyte, disc protrusion, and ligaments, redirecting revision planning to the extraforaminal zone. Uni-portal non-coaxial spinal endoscopic surgery (UNSES) achieved targeted bony, ligamentous, and disc decompression without vascular, neural, or dural injury. From pre-revision values of VAS 7/10 for back pain and 7/10 for leg pain, ODI 54%, and JOA 5, scores improved at postoperative Day 1 to 3/10, 2/10, 22%, and 23, respectively. At 1, 3, and 6 months, back/leg VAS was 2/1, 1/0, and 1/0; ODI was 24%, 16%, and 8%; and JOA was 23, 25, and 27, respectively. Conclusions In this patient, 3D CT/MRN fusion complemented conventional imaging by integrating bone, disc, and nerve anatomy and directly informing revision decompression. UNSES was feasible, with improvement maintained through 6 months. As a single case, these findings support clinical feasibility and educational value rather than general efficacy or safety.

title: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.
authors: Tedla JS, Lalaji SL, Midde AK, Papalkar NA, Bindhu Priya N, Sangadala DR, Reddy RS, Mukherjee D, Alamri AM, Alzahrani AS, Alhadi NA.
abstract: Background In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment. Methodology A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18-80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269. Results The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant. Conclusion Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status and physical performance in football players: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Gu J, Zhang Y, Xiao L.
abstract: Background/objectives Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players. Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026. Controlled intervention studies comparing vitamin D supplementation with control conditions were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges' g and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261430873). Results Eleven reports representing nine independent studies and 312 players were included. In RCT-only primary analyses, vitamin D supplementation was associated with higher circulating 25(OH)D concentrations (g = 1.41, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.92; I² = 58.0%). Pooled effects were not statistically significant for jump performance (g = 0.21, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.53), sprint performance (g = -0.03, 95% CI -0.40 to 0.34), aerobic capacity (g = 0.00, 95% CI -0.45 to 0.45), or muscular performance (g = 0.19, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.51). The certainty of evidence was low for circulating 25(OH)D, jump performance, and muscular performance, and very low for sprint performance and aerobic capacity. Conclusions Vitamin D supplementation was associated with increased circulating 25(OH)D concentrations, whereas current evidence is insufficient to support a consistent improvement in physical performance. Given the low to very low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials using standardized, football-relevant performance tests are warranted.

title: Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol.
authors: Asensio-Perez D, Lucena-Anton D, Moral-Munoz JA.
abstract: Background Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke. Aim To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke. Methods A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p Discussion This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Effectiveness of dose-matched rehabilitation with immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): study protocol for a single-blind, randomized crossover trial. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07529665. Date of registration: 2026-04-14. Version 1.
