title: E-Service quality and customer satisfaction in online shopping: Implications for sustainable digital commerce.
authors: Awadh MA.
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified competition among online retailers, making e-service quality increasingly important for building customer trust, satisfaction, and sustainable customer-platform relationships. This study examines the relationships among e-service quality, customer trust, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty using a second-order Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework. The five SERVQUAL dimensions such as empathy, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, and tangibles were modeled as first-order constructs reflecting the higher-order construct of service quality. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 402 respondents with prior online-shopping experience. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and SEM were employed to assess the measurement and structural models. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and overall model fit. The structural results showed that service quality significantly and positively influenced customer trust and customer satisfaction, while customer trust significantly enhanced satisfaction. Trust also partially mediated the relationship between service quality and satisfaction, indicating that e-service quality improves satisfaction both directly and through increased customer confidence. The SERVQUAL dimensions contributed positively to overall service quality, with responsiveness and assurance showing particularly strong contributions, while empathy exhibited a comparatively moderate contribution. In contrast, customer loyalty had no significant direct effect on trust or satisfaction, and its indirect effect on satisfaction through trust was also nonsignificant. These findings demonstrate that reliable, responsive, secure, and well-designed digital services are important for strengthening trust and satisfaction in competitive e-commerce environments. By identifying trust as a key mechanism linking multidimensional e-service quality with customer satisfaction, the study contributes to SERVQUAL and digital-commerce literature and provides implications for the economic and relational sustainability of e-commerce platforms through more resilient and durable customer relationships.

title: Does the number of debridement procedures impact risk of infection in open fractures?
authors: Bateman LM, Fisher LA, Diaz-Coto S, O'Hara NN, Bzovsky S, Zura RD, Miller AN, Slobogean GP, Sprauge S, Gitajn IL, PREP-IT investigators.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between the number of debridements and risk of infection, while stratifying by degree of wound contamination. It was hypothesized that patients with severe contamination, a higher number of debridements would be associated with lower risk of infection. Methods This is a retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected data in the PREP-IT trial (Program of Randomized trials to Evaluate Preoperative antiseptic skin solutions in orthopaedic Trauma). The primary outcome measure was adjudicated surgical site infection. Independent variables were number of debridement procedures and time from injury to definitive wound closure. Analysis was stratified by degree of contamination and multivariable analyses were performed to control for confounders. Results 3502 total open fractures corresponding to 3222 patients with a median (interquartile range, IQR) age of 42 (29-58) years (2199 [62.8%] men; median (IQR) body mass index 27.7 [24.3-32.6]) were included in this analysis. 2199 patients were included in the non/minimal contamination group, 970 in the surface contamination group, and 333 in the embedded contamination group. After controlling for patient-level characteristics there was a 27% increase in the risk of infection for each debridement performed in the overall patient cohort (OR 1.27 [1.12-1.43] p Conclusion The results of this study indicate that increased number of debridement procedures was not associated with lower infectious rates. Patients with the highest degree of contamination demonstrated significantly increased risk of developing an infection with each additional debridement. These findings support the importance of limiting unnecessary additional debridement procedures to reduce infection risk and optimize outcomes.

title: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Presenting as a Rapidly Enlarging Forehead Mass Initially Suggestive of a Subgaleal Hematoma: A Case Report.
authors: Yonenaga A, Isono N, Higashiyama A, Tsukada M, Hori K.
abstract: While diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) occurring in the subcutaneous soft tissue is extremely rare, we present herein a case of DLBCL occurring in the forehead. A 70-year-old woman presented to the plastic and reconstructive department with a painless forehead mass. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) initially suggested a subgaleal hematoma, subsequent computed tomography (CT) revealed bone destruction. Due to the progressive enlargement, a biopsy was performed, confirming a pathological diagnosis of DLBCL. A genetic analysis of tissue samples revealed MYC and BCL6 rearrangements consistent with double-hit lymphoma (DHL). The patient was treated with the help of R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone) followed by DA-R-EPOCH (dose-adjusted rituximab, etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and doxorubicin). Although the frontal skull mass completely resolved, residual disease persisted in the femur, ultimately leading to the patient's death. This case highlights the importance of including lymphoma in the differential diagnosis of rapidly enlarging soft tissue masses as well as the utility of early biopsy in ensuring timely intervention.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of 3D MRI rendering techniques for evaluation of hourglass-like constrictions in Parsonage-Turner syndrome.
authors: Shakoor D, McKinney EJ, Queler SC, Davis-Hayes C, Hao M, Baker A, Wang SH, Tan ET, Sneag DB.
abstract: Objective To evaluate inter-reader agreement and diagnostic accuracy of curved multiplanar reformatting (cMPR) and maximum intensity projection (MIP) techniques for detecting hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs). Materials and methods Thirty brachial plexus 3-Tesla, 3D, 1-mm isotropic MR neurography (MRN) datasets (10 patients without and 20 patients with Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS) affecting the suprascapular nerve (SSN)) were retrospectively analyzed by four musculoskeletal radiology fellows for the number and severity of HGCs using both post-processing views in a randomized, blinded fashion. An experienced, attending radiologist served as the reference standard. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC1 and intraclass correlation (ICC). Image interpretation time was compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results Inter-reader agreement for HGC presence was substantial to almost perfect among fellows (cMPR AC1 = 0.7, MIP AC1 = 0.67) and when compared to the attending (cMPR AC1 = 0.67-0.83, MIP AC1 = 0.63-0.83). Agreement for severe HGC count was substantial to almost perfect (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.65, MIP ICC = 0.79; vs. attending: ICC = 0.62-0.83, MIP ICC = 0.69-0.88), but poor to fair for mild HGCs (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.23, MIP ICC = 0.26; vs. attending: ICC = 0-0.21, MIP ICC = 0-0.09). Sensitivity to HGC presence was excellent (cMPR, 85-100%; MIP, 90-100%), though specificity (cMPR, 50-100%; MIP, 40-90%) and diagnostic accuracy (cMPR, 80-90%; MIP, 76-90%) varied. The MIP method required significantly less interpretation time than cMPR (median: 33 vs. 104 s, p Conclusion High inter-reader agreement and sensitivity but variable specificity for HGC detection suggest both techniques are viable tools for MRN, with cMPR better suited for detailed HGC evaluation and MIP for initial screening.

title: Development, validation, and testing of an agriculture support exoskeleton in adjunct to conventional physiotherapy for farm labourers with chronic low back pain: A two-phase, mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pilot study protocol.
authors: Kaur G, Qureshi I, Bagde A, Sarode B, Jolhe DA, Nistane VM.
abstract: Background Low back pain (LBP) affects 619 million people globally, with projections reaching 843 million by 2050. Farm labourers exhibit markedly higher prevalence than the general population, with lifetime (70-85%), 12-month (15-45%), and point (approximately 30%) prevalences driven by sustained trunk flexion, repetitive manual handling, and limited access to ergonomic or rehabilitative interventions. While conventional physiotherapy is the cornerstone of chronic LBP (CLBP) management, its effectiveness may be limited by ongoing mechanical loading during agricultural work. Back support exoskeletons (BSEs) have shown promise in reducing lumbar loading. However, no study has integrated exoskeleton development, validation, and clinical testing within a physiotherapy framework for farm labourers. The objective of the two-phase protocol is to design, develop, and laboratory-validate an agriculture support exoskeleton (AgSuEx), followed by examining the effects of AgSuEx-assisted physiotherapy compared with conventional physiotherapy alone on pain intensity, work productivity, disability, physical function, and quality of life (QOL) among farm labourers with CLBP. Methods The two-phase, mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pilot study will be conducted in Wardha district, Maharashtra, India. Phase I will involve participatory co-design, iterative engineering development, and laboratory validation of an AgSuEx using finite element analysis (FEA), multibody dynamics (MBD) simulation, surface electromyography (sEMG), inertial measurement units (IMUs), interface pressure mapping, and validated usability instruments, integrated with focus group discussions (FGDs) from farm labourers. Phase II will employ a quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group pretest-posttest design with repeated measures. Farm labourers aged 25-49 years with CLBP will be assigned (1:1) to AgSuEx-assisted conventional physiotherapy or conventional physiotherapy alone for 6 weeks, with follow-up at 3 and 6 months. Outcomes Phase I primary outcome: lumbar extensor sEMG activation. Phase II primary outcomes: pain intensity (Quadruple VAS) and work productivity. Secondary outcomes: functional disability (RODI), physical function (RMDQ), and QOL (SF-12). Device-specific outcomes (SUS, QUEAD and LPP) will be assessed across both phases. Outcome assessors and data analysts will be blinded to group assignment. Conclusion This protocol will generate preliminary evidence on the feasibility, usability, and preliminary clinical effects of integrating a Make in India AgSuEx with conventional physiotherapy for farm laborers with CLBP. Findings will guide future larger-scale controlled trials and inform ergonomic and rehabilitative strategies for agrarian populations. Trial registered prospectively Clinical Trial Registry- India CTRI/2025/11/097725 [Registered on: 20/11/2025]. Acknowledgement Number: REF/2025/11/116856. URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTQ1NzE3&Enc=&userName=Protocolversion4.0,4/09/2026.

title: Deep-Learning Enhanced Augmented Reality for Robotic Radical Prostatectomy on Consumer Grade Hardware.
authors: Benard V, Windisch O, Bjelogrlic M, Turbé H, Lovis C, Diana M, Valerio M.
abstract: BackgroundAugmented Reality (AR) during Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy (RARP) provides surgical guidance by overlaying patient-specific 3D Virtual Models (VM) onto the intraoperative view. A main drawback is instrument occlusion, where VM overlaps the surgical tools, disturbing the augmented view. Deep learning (DL)-based desocclusion addresses this issue, but current implementation rely on expensive, specialized hardware.MethodsWe developed an AR desocclusion pipeline running on consumer-grade hardware (∼1150 US Dollars). For model selection, we trained and benchmarked 21 encoder architectures paired with a U-Net decoder. The selected model was integrated into a macOS application using CoreML inference on the Apple Neural Engine. Memory usage, thermal state and framerate were monitored on a continuous 81-minute console session. Photon-to-photon latency (from surgical field to the surgeon eye) was measured on the DaVinci® Xi using a microcontroller-phototransistor setup.ResultsFastViT-S12/Unet offered the highest accuracy among models meeting our inference-time budget (∼2 ms inference), achieving a Dice score of 95.1% (95% CI, 94.3-95.7) internally, 91.6% (95% CI, 90.2-92.9) and 90.2% (95% CI, 84.7-94.4) on externals tests, with a mean inference time of 1.89 ± 0.36 ms. The pipeline maintained 57.98 frames per second using 1.47 GB of unified memory with a nominal thermal state. On the surgical console, photon-to-photon median latency increased from 60 ms (Q1-Q3: 57.5-62.5) to 120.5 ms (Q1-Q3: 111-131) with the AR pipeline.ConclusionsReal-time AR-RARP with DL-based desocclusion is achievable on low-cost hardware with an added latency remaining within ranges reported as technically acceptable for intraoperative use.

title: Cytokine and chemokine circuits in non-small cell lung cancer: Spatial biomarkers and an evidence-guided framework for combination immunotherapy.
authors: Xu Y, Yang M, Ma Y, Wang Y, Liu J, Liang T, Guo L.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains uneven because tumor immunity is organized by cytokine and chemokine circuits that vary across anatomic niches and treatment states. This narrative review integrates single-cell, spatial, mechanistic and clinically annotated evidence around source-ligand-receptor-target relationships to assess how cytokine and chemokine circuits relate to ICI response and resistance in NSCLC, and what these findings imply for spatial biomarkers and combination strategies. Representative activating circuits reviewed here include XCL1/2-XCR1- and CCL5-dependent cDC1 recruitment, IL-12/IL-18-supported NK-cell activation, CXCL9/10-CXCR3-guided effector trafficking and CXCL13-CXCR5-dependent tertiary lymphoid structure organization. These programs may support antitumor immunity relevant to ICI response, whereas suppressive programs involving TGF-β, IL-10, CSF1, CCL2, IL-17, together with interacting pathways such as adenosine-mediated metabolic suppression, may contribute to immune exclusion and resistance in NSCLC. Clinical translation remains uneven: spatial biomarkers and pathway-directed combinations are supported mainly by cross-sectional cohorts, mechanistic studies and early clinical trials, with several negative or context-specific results. We therefore synthesize these findings and outline a conceptual, evidence-tiered framework that considers cellular source, receptor-bearing target, spatial niche, treatment history and pharmacodynamic evidence. By linking spatial immune organization to mechanisms of response and resistance, this framework provides a foundation for biomarker-informed combinations tailored to distinct immune dysfunctions, with the potential to overcome resistance and extend durable immunotherapy benefit to more patients with NSCLC.

title: Conventional laparoscopy versus Hugo RAS in general surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis of perioperative outcomes.
authors: Vaghiri S, Pandkhahi A, Prassas D, Habib E, Schmitz-Conti N, Knoefel WT, Alexander A.
abstract: Introduction The Hugo Robotic-Assisted Surgery (RAS) system is a relatively new robotic platform increasingly used in minimally invasive surgery. However, comparative data on its clinical outcomes versus those of conventional laparoscopy in general surgery remain limited. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare perioperative and postoperative outcomes between Hugo RAS and conventional laparoscopy. Methods PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 16 July 2026. Comparative studies of adult patients undergoing minimally invasive general surgery using Hugo RAS or conventional laparoscopy were included. The primary outcomes were overall postoperative complications and major complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ III). Secondary outcomes included operative time, length of hospital stay, conversion to open surgery, postoperative ileus, anastomotic leakage, reoperation, and readmission rates. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Results The search identified 4158 records, of which three retrospective and one prospective comparative studies, involving a total of 898 patients, met the inclusion criteria. Overall, 161 patients underwent Hugo RAS procedures and 737 underwent conventional laparoscopic surgery. The rate of overall postoperative complications was similar between the two groups (OR = 0.80; 95% CI, 0.49-1.31; p = 0.38; I² = 12%). However, major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ III) were significantly less frequent in the Hugo RAS group (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.10-0.92; p = 0.04; I²=0%), although the certainty of evidence was low. No significant differences were found for other outcomes of interest. Conclusion Hugo RAS appears to be a safe and technically feasible alternative to conventional laparoscopy in minimally invasive general surgery, with similar overall postoperative outcomes. The lower rate of major postoperative complications observed with Hugo RAS is encouraging, but should be interpreted cautiously because the available evidence is based on only four non-randomized studies and is subject to methodological limitations and clinical heterogeneity. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine whether these findings are consistent across different surgical procedures.

title: Cone-Beam CT-Guided SpineJack® vertebral augmentation: A reproducible technique for accurate pedicular access and implant deployment.
authors: Dien E, Grange S, Mondon P, Peraldi L, Lavigne J, Chalamet B, Ben-Rejeb MI, Bouchet M, Gleyzolle A, Ahoury N Guessan J, Barrey C, Amoretti N, Pialat JB, Stacoffe N.
abstract: Background SpineJack® vertebral augmentation requires precise bilateral transpedicular access and accurate implant deployment. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and technical performance of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-guided SpineJack augmentation. Methods This retrospective single-institution, two-site study included consecutive CBCT-guided procedures performed between May 2021 and April 2026. Technical success required planned bilateral implantation, expansion, and cement augmentation without pedicle breach or implant malposition on final CBCT. Secondary outcomes included immediate vertebral height restoration, complications, procedure duration, radiation exposure, and treatment setting. Results The analysis included 178 procedures; median age was 45 years (interquartile range [IQR], 27-59), and 158 procedures (88.8%) involved traumatic fractures. Technical success was 100% (178/178), including 64 procedures (36.0%) with pedicle-implant clearance Conclusions CBCT-guided SpineJack augmentation achieved accurate bilateral implant deployment and substantial immediate vertebral height restoration without major procedure-related complications. These findings support CBCT as a reliable guidance strategy for vertebral augmentation, with demonstrated feasibility in outpatient practice.

title: Completing upper secondary school: Results from a ten-year longitudinal study in Norway.
authors: Sæle RG, Sørlie T, Goll CB, Friborg O.
abstract: The completion of education is important both for the individual and society. High dropout rates from upper secondary school have been a national problem in Norway, and especially in northern Norway. Academic aptitude or grades (GPA) are important, but given the multifaceted nature of dropout, we conducted a longitudinal analysis to examine predictors of school completion after ten years. The study included 1676 students in Troms County (latitude 69 degrees north) starting in upper secondary education in 2010. We included a broad set of predictors related to school performance, psychological factors such as vulnerability, resilience, personality, and mental health, alongside demographic data. The mixture modeling revealed three completion trajectories: normal progression (40.1%), delayed completion (36.6%), and non-completion (23.3%). Correlation analyses showed significant relationships between completion and several of these predictors; however, in multinomial regression analyses, no variables beyond GPA significantly predicted the normal progression trajectory, whereas delayed completion was additionally accounted for by study track choice and self-perceived health, with GPA playing an even stronger role. This underscores the importance of prior school performance, but we also discuss the implications of the findings for the delayed-completion group.

title: Comparative outcomes of Hugo RAS and Versius surgical systems versus da Vinci in four urological procedures: a systematic review.
authors: Thayalan S, Toubasey S, O'Sullivan C, Challacombe B.
abstract: Robot-assisted surgery has transformed urological surgery, with the da Vinci Surgical System dominating for over two decades. Following the expiry of key Intuitive patents in 2019, two particular platforms - Medtronic's Hugo™ RAS system and CMR Surgical's Versius ® Surgical Robotic System - have gained regulatory approval and entered urological practice. Comparative evidence between these platforms and da Vinci ® across urological procedures remains limited. This systematic review follows PRISMA guidelines and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO: CRD420261319741). MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from January 2016 to August 2026. Comparative studies of Hugo™ RAS or Versius ® versus da Vinci ® in patients undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), pyeloplasty, or radical cystectomy were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. 19 studies (21 procedural comparisons) involving 2,482 patients were included. In RARP, blood loss and length of stay showed substantially overlapping ranges between platforms, with no consistent direction of effect, though setup and docking times were consistently longer with the newer platforms. Positive surgical margin rates and early continence recovery overlapped widely in RARP. In RAPN, warm ischaemia times differed by five minutes or less across reporting studies, and trifecta rates were within 5 percentage points. The single small pyeloplasty study reported identical median operative times, but provided minimal comparative information. Early comparative evidence has not demonstrated consistent differences in peri-operative, oncological or early functional outcomes between Hugo™ RAS or Versius ® and da Vinci ® in experienced, high-volume centres. However, the included studies were small, non-randomised and not powered to detect clinically meaningful differences or to demonstrate equivalence. These findings therefore represent an absence of evidence of a difference rather than evidence of comparable effectiveness. Prospective studies including robotic-naïve centres are needed to advance our understanding.

title: Comparative mortality of pelvic ring fractures vs. hip fractures in adults ≥55 years: A propensity-matched cohort study.
authors: Sabat L, Johnson M, Pasha M, Perdue P, Zuelzer D.
abstract: Background Hip and pelvic fragility fractures are associated with substantial mortality in older adults. While standardized care pathways are established for hip fractures, management of pelvic fragility fractures remains less defined. This study compared mortality between matched hip and pelvic ring fracture patients managed operatively or nonoperatively. Hypothesis Pelvic and hip fractures would demonstrate comparable mortality within operative and nonoperative treatment groups. Patients and methods This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX network to identify adults aged ≥ 55 years with hip or pelvic ring fractures. Patients were stratified by operative or nonoperative management, and cohorts were propensity score matched 1:1 based on demographic and clinical characteristics. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were mortality at 30 days, 90 days, and 2 years. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated 1-year mortality. Results After matching, 255,202 patients per cohort were included in the nonoperative subgroup and 11,448 per cohort in the operative subgroup. Among nonoperative patients, 1-year mortality was higher after hip than pelvic fracture (11.13% vs 10.68%; HR 1.123, 95% CI 1.105-1.141). Among operative patients, 1-year mortality was also higher after hip fracture (8.84% vs 5.94%; HR 1.424, 95% CI 1.314-1.545). However, 30-day mortality was higher after operative pelvic fracture (3.11% vs 2.49%; p = 0.004). Male sex, older age, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease were associated with increased mortality. Discussion Hip fractures were associated with greater 1-year mortality across management strategies; however, operative pelvic fractures demonstrated greater early mortality. These findings highlight pelvic fragility fractures as high-risk injuries warranting further evaluation of standardized geriatric care pathways. Level of evidence III.

title: Bridging the gap: A qualitative study on veterans' experiences with systemic barriers and support during transition.
authors: Ingram P, Mele A, Lazar CM, Mattocks K, Kelly M, Edmond S, Rosen MI, Weede A, Perez J, Martino S.
abstract: Many veterans face complex challenges during the transition from military to civilian life, particularly when navigating healthcare and benefits systems. This qualitative study examines how recently separated veterans with service‑connected musculoskeletal disorders perceive and navigate systemic barriers within Department of Defense and Veterans Affairs transition and healthcare systems. Semi‑structured interviews were conducted with 20 veterans within one year of separation who had filed a musculoskeletal service‑connection claim. Using a rapid qualitative analytic approach, interviews captured experiences with the discharge process, transition programming, and efforts to access healthcare and benefits. Analysis identified four major themes: the interaction of physical, psychological, and bureaucratic stressors during discharge, particularly salient for those managing musculoskeletal conditions; varied and often critical views of transition programming, which many perceived as generic and misaligned with individual needs; systemic barriers to care and benefits, including delays, fragmented processes, and cultural norms that discourage disclosure; and recommendations emphasizing continuity of care, case management, and emotional support to address identity disruption and loss of purpose. Overall, the findings highlight persistent structural and cultural obstacles that complicate transition and hinder early engagement with services. Improved coordination, continuity‑oriented supports, and psychologically responsive programming may reduce these barriers. Further research is needed to evaluate scalable models that enhance early post‑separation outcomes.

title: Assessment of the appropriateness of stress ulcer prophylaxis practice among hospitalized patients across Lebanese hospitals: A multicenter prospective study.
authors: Housary K, Dib C, Itani R.
abstract: Background Stress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP) is recommended for critically ill patients at high risk of stress-related gastrointestinal bleeding. Despite established guideline recommendations, inappropriate use of acid suppressant medications (ASMs), particularly proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), remains common worldwide and may expose patients to unnecessary adverse effects and increased healthcare costs. This study aimed to assess the appropriateness of SUP prescribing practices among hospitalized patients across Lebanese hospitals, focusing on indication, choice of pharmacologic agent, dosing regimen, route of administration, duration of therapy, discharge prescribing, and factors associated with inappropriate SUP practice. Methods A multicenter prospective study was conducted between April 20 and May 22, 2026, across ten tertiary-care hospitals in different regions of Lebanon. Adult patients (≥18 years) admitted to Internal Medicine Unit, Intensive Care Unit (ICU), or Coronary Care Unit wards were assessed for the appropriateness of SUP, regardless of whether ASMs were prescribed. The appropriateness of SUP practice was evaluated according to the Society of Critical Care Medicine and American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (SCCM/ASHP) 2024 and ASHP 1999 guidelines. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with inappropriate SUP practice. Results A total of 552 patients were enrolled, with a mean age of 64.3 ± 18.5 years, and 58.7% were male. According to the SCCM/ASHP 2024 and ASHP 1999 guidelines, 90.8% and 77.2% of patients, respectively, were not eligible for SUP. Omeprazole was the most frequently prescribed agent (75.4%), and PPIs were used in all SUP prescriptions. Among patients admitted to ICU, 11.2% continued receiving ASMs after the SUP indication had resolved or following ICU transfer without a persisting indication. Overall, SUP practice was inappropriate in 77.9% of patients. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that anticoagulant therapy was associated with higher odds of inappropriate SUP practice (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI = 1.35-5.74, P = 0.006). Conclusions Inappropriate SUP practice is highly prevalent among hospitalized patients in Lebanon, largely due to prescribing without guideline-based indications. Inappropriate continuation after resolution of the SUP indication or ICU transfer was also observed. Strengthening adherence to evidence-based recommendations through stewardship programs, prescribing audits, standardized protocols, and updated national guidance may help optimize SUP use and improve patient care.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and Chinese art teachers' career exploration behavior: The roles of job substitution risks, job insecurity, and organizational AI readiness.
authors: Li J, Gao Y.
abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers' professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination. Organizational AI readiness positively moderated the AI adoption-career exploration relationship: the association was stronger at higher readiness. COR theory offers a resource-threat interpretation of the indirect associations, while CCT highlights that career exploration may reflect threat-related coping, growth-oriented development, or both. The data did not separately measure these motivations or establish causal ordering. The findings provide context-specific insights into career exploration among art teachers during AI-related technological change.

title: Antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar's poultry sector: informality, knowledge gaps, and market constraints.
authors: Molia S, Tsimok'Haja Ramahatafandry I, Rakotoharinome M, Lienhardt C, Figuié M, Hobeika A, Kassié D.
abstract: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is a major global public health threat, largely driven by the overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Tackling its animal health component is particularly difficult in low- and middle-income countries, where data and resources are limited. This qualitative study aims to explore antibiotic use (ABU) and its underlying drivers in poultry farms in Analamanga, Madagascar's region with the highest poultry density. In April 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 79 poultry farmers (13 backyard and 66 semi-intensive), 10 animal health professionals, and 10 agrovet shop sellers. Thematic analysis was used to examine farm characteristics, poultry health management, veterinary medicine supply and use, and interactions with poultry production stakeholders, in order to identify antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar's poultry sector. Backyard and semi-intensive farmers shared several features: informality (absence of farm registration, rare cooperative membership, limited training), irregular profitability, easy access to antibiotics, recurrent antibiotic misuse (for example use in poultry viral infection treatment, first-line fluoroquinolone treatments), and limited veterinary inspection by competent authorities. However, the two farmer groups differed, as semi-intensive farmers had slightly greater knowledge of ABU and ABR than backyard farmers; they primarily consulted chick and feed suppliers for health advice and medicine purchase; and they widely perceived antibiotics as essential to maintaining poultry health and productivity. Practical roadblocks to invest in preventive measures or adopt effective antibiotic stewardship (ABS) were their narrow profit margins, limited access to credit, and weak bargaining power towards poultry product buyers. Tailored approaches such as supporting professionalization of poultry sector, building capacity of chick and feed suppliers to provide training in appropriate ABU and management of flocks, flock vaccination, deworming schedules, treatment record keeping and ABS principles may enhance antibiotic usage in the Madagascar poultry sector. Future research should build on this exploratory study, which used a convenience sample of stakeholders, by examining ABU trends and drivers in Analamanga with representative sampling and rigorous quantitative validation across Madagascar's poultry sector.

title: Adaptive-based cascaded PI-PID controller for load frequency regulation with real time verification.
authors: Alharbi AM, Awad MA, Attia MA, Mekhamer SF, El-Ebiary AH.
abstract: In order to address Load Frequency Control (LFC) problems in single-area and interconnected two-area power systems, this work proposes a cascaded control scheme that combines PI-PID control with the Set-Membership Affine Projection Algorithm (SMAPA). The proposed approach is evaluated under various practical operating conditions, including step load disturbances, random load variations, wind power fluctuations, and parameter uncertainty. In addition, frequency-domain stability analysis is performed to further assess the robustness of the proposed controller, while real-time validation is conducted for the two-area system to demonstrate its practical effectiveness. The proposed controller is compared with conventional PI controllers tuned using five optimization methods for the single-area system. For the two-area system, its performance is benchmarked against PID controllers designed using three optimization methods and the recently reported SPPI-based approach. The simulation results show that the proposed controller achieves lower overshoot and faster settling time in both configurations. These improvements are attributed to the integration of real-time adaptive parameter updating provided by SMAPA with the favorable dynamic characteristics of the PI-PID control structure. The results demonstrate that the proposed cascaded SMAPA-based PI-PID controller provides robust frequency regulation under different operating conditions and offers promising potential for practical interconnected power system applications.

title: A stepwise fresh porcine head model for three-dimensional dissection of ventricular, limbic, and deep venous anatomy.
authors: Ganaha S, Ermolo A, Katayama Y, Kitamura Y.
abstract: Deep ventricular, limbic, cisternal, and deep venous structures form a compact three-dimensional anatomical system that is difficult to understand from two-dimensional resources alone. We evaluated the technical feasibility of organizing fresh ex vivo porcine heads into a four-module, stepwise dissection model for demonstrating these relationships. Five porcine heads obtained from a regulated food supply chain were prepared without formalin fixation, vascular injection, or specialized laboratory equipment. A neurosurgery resident performed the dissections under faculty supervision. Anatomical feasibility was assessed by the successful identification of prespecified targets within transcallosal, transchoroidal, interforniceal, posterior deep venous, and atrial-inferior horn dissections. The complete four-module sequence was achieved, and all prespecified anatomical targets were identified during dissection in all five specimens. In an independent image-based assessment of three specimens with complete unannotated photographic sets, 26 of 31 targets were identifiable in all three specimens, whereas five deep ventricular or venous targets were identifiable in two of three specimens. The dissection demonstrated the spatial continuity of the caudate nucleus, fornix, foramen of Monro, choroid plexus, thalamostriate vein, velum interpositum, internal cerebral veins, Galenic venous system, hippocampal formation, choroidal fissure, and adjacent cisternal spaces. Natural vascular coloration remained visible without injection and supported orientation during sequential dissection. This low-infrastructure preparation may serve as an accessible physical reference for understanding the three-dimensional continuity of deep ventricular, limbic, cisternal, and venous anatomy, particularly where access to human cadaveric dissection is limited.

title: A psychological perspective on peer tutoring in EFL collaborative writing in Chinese higher education contexts.
authors: Huang Z, Arumugam N.
abstract: In Chinese higher learning institutions, students learning English as a foreign language (EFL) often demonstrate low writing self-efficacy (WSE) and poor writing competence. The present study examined the associations between the integration of peer tutoring with collaborative writing and students' WSE and writing outcomes from a psychological perspective. A quasi-experiment was implemented for 11 weeks for 100 Chinese university students studying EFL. Changes in WSE were examined, and writing competence was assessed using tests. The results showed a notable rise in students' WSE after the instructional intervention. The multiple linear regression analysis indicated that gains in WSE were positively associated with the writing outcome after controlling for pretest writing competence and group membership, explaining 20.2% of the total variance. These results suggest that peer-supported collaborative writing was associated with higher EFL writing competence alongside increased WSE. These findings align with theoretical justifications based on peer scaffolding and the Zone of Proximal Development, although these processes were not directly measured in the present study. These findings imply that incorporating peer tutoring into collaborative writing might be associated with the development of WSE and improved writing competence among EFL students at Chinese universities. Increased WSE appeared to be a significant, albeit partial, predictor of writing competence, highlighting the potential relevance of WSE development in peer-supported collaborative writing contexts.

title: A pre-post single-arm pilot trial of a digital multicomponent intervention for self-efficacy enhancement among online support groups of primary caregivers of children with neuro-muscular disorders: SEE-NMD protocol.
authors: Aziz NI, Khalid W, Khan S.
abstract: Introduction Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) and Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) are progressive genetic neuromuscular disorders that impose substantial caregiving demands on families. In Pakistan, where disease-modifying therapies remain largely inaccessible, care is predominantly supportive, frequently resulting in psychological distress and diminished caregiver confidence. An individual's belief in their capacity to execute required behaviours, self-efficacy, is a recognised determinant of caregiving quality, yet evidence on caregiver self-efficacy in SMA and DMD within low-resource settings remains sparse. This protocol describes the methods for an exploratory, single-arm, pre-post trial. The trial aims to generate preliminary evidence on changes in self-efficacy following a multicomponent, digitally delivered intervention and its implementation feasibility among primary caregivers of children with SMA and DMD in Pakistan. Methods and analysis A single-arm, pre-post study design will recruit primary caregivers of children with SMA and DMD enrolled in the Treat-NMD Registry of Pakistan, with 40 caregivers per condition (80 total) analyzed as separate disease-specific cohorts. An eight-week intervention will be delivered via online support groups, comprising educational video clips, expert-led live sessions, pictorial guides, and progressively tapering audio reminders. The primary outcome, self-efficacy, will be measured using a culturally adapted, content-validated Urdu version of the DMD Caregiver Self-Efficacy Scale (DMD-CSES), assessed at baseline (T0) and eight weeks post-intervention (T1). Pre- and post-intervention scores will be compared using a paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, depending on the data distribution, with analyses conducted in STATA Version 17. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval has been granted by the Ethics Review Committee of Aga Khan University (2025-11875-37040). Verbal informed consent will be obtained from all participants, and confidentiality will be maintained throughout the trial. The findings will be disseminated via peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and shared with the Treat-NMD registry network. Trial registration name and number NCT07356063, Date of registration: 11/January/2026.

title: A bedside score using arrival data to identify major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring fracture: Development and validation.
authors: Salman SG, Phadke RA, Carlin T, Rosenfelt T, Ramirez J, Mendez-Reyes JE, Hoffman MK, Leonard J, Davis RW, Ward JL, Vera RM, Silberfein EJ, Rana A, Atassi OH, Perkins CH, Dawson JR, Wilson C, Fitzgerald CA, Seger CP, Zielinski MD, Mattox KL, Dumas RP.
abstract: Background Early recognition of major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring injury could guide mobilization of transfusion and hemorrhage-control resources. We developed an arrival-based bedside score and compared its performance with shock index. Methods We studied 239,736 adults with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures in the 2019-2024 National Trauma Data Bank. Major hemorrhage was defined as a hemorrhage-control procedure, hemorrhagic death, or transfusion of ≥ 1000 mL or ≥ 4 units of red blood cells within 4 h. Penalized logistic regression selected arrival variables for an integer score. We assessed performance in a held-out test set (n = 79,912) and at approximately matched alert volume. A model refitted on 2019-2022 admissions was evaluated in 2023-2024. Subgroup analyses were post hoc. Results Major hemorrhage occurred in 26,479 patients (11.0%); 31.0% were aged ≥ 75 years, and 45.9% had fallen. In the test set, the score achieved an AUROC of 0.882 (95% CI, 0.879-0.886), exceeding shock index by 0.060 (95% CI, 0.055-0.064; P Conclusions In patients with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures, an arrival-based score identified major hemorrhage more accurately than shock index at a similar alert burden. Reduced performance after falls and uncertain applicability to suspected fractures warrant caution. External validation and prospective impact assessment are needed before clinical use.

title: A Kampo medicine, kamishoyosan, ameliorates menstruation-associated symptoms in patients with premenstrual syndrome: An exploratory open-label, randomized controlled trial.
authors: Chikumi J, Sato E, Ikebuchi A, Tokita Y, Fukushige M, Yamamoto M, Sunada H, Endo Y, Noma H, Harada T, Taniguchi F.
abstract: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a psychological or physical symptom. We conducted an open-label, randomized, exploratory trial with the aim of evaluating the efficacy and safety of kamishoyosan (KSS) for PMS. KSS was administered orally during three menstrual cycles. The primary endpoint was the change in the premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire (MDQ) total score. The secondary endpoints included MDQ total and subscale scores, a daily symptom questionnaire, the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) Questionnaire, overall impressions, sleep status, and heart rate. A total of 50 patients were enrolled. The primary endpoint, the premenstrual MDQ total score, was significantly ameliorated after KSS treatment. Furthermore, KSS reduced MDQ scores during the menstrual cycle. Among the MDQ subscales, KSS decreased score of pain, concentration, behavioral change, and negative feelings during the premenstrual cycle. In addition, hyperthymia reduced during the menstrual cycle. The results of the daily symptom questionnaire indicated that KSS treatment alleviated irritability, easy anger, anxiety, emotional instability, abdominal distension, coldness, and stiff shoulders.The WPAI activity impairment score was lower in the KSS group, and overall impression favoured in KSS treatment.. The only adverse event related to KSS was headache in one case. These exploratory findings suggest that KSS may improve menstrual-related symptoms in PMS.

title: Tumor-mimicking lumbar intradural disc herniation managed with unilateral biportal endoscopy: a case report.
authors: He B, Huang T, Tan H, Meng Z, Sun B.
abstract: Lumbar intradural disc herniation is rare and frequently mimics intraspinal tumors. A 58-year-old man presented with bilateral L5 radiculopathy and motor weakness. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated an enhancing, cystic L4-5 intraspinal mass favoring a nerve sheath tumor. During unilateral biportal endoscopic surgery, epidural decompression revealed no extradural compression, but persistent thecal tension and absent pulsation prompted an 8-mm dorsal durotomy under reduced irrigation pressure. Sequestered disc fragments adherent to the cauda equina were resected piecemeal, while ventral defect exploration was deliberately avoided. The durotomy was closed using a sutureless inlay dural patch. Histopathology confirmed degenerative disc tissue. The patient achieved complete neurological recovery without cerebrospinal fluid leakage or pseudomeningocele on follow-up MRI. Intradural exploration is warranted when unexplained thecal tension persists, and inlay patch repair serves as an effective endoscopic alternative to primary suturing.

title: Tribute to the Editor.
authors: Al-Dadah O, Hing C.

title: Traumatic hip dislocation: Clinical and epidemiological features, management and prognostic factors in a series of 44 cases from a tertiary centre.
authors: Mencía González JP, Sánchez Cózar L, Martínez Alfaro A, Maes ASM, Eckardt Haag ME, Huguet Carmona JL, Marco Sabater A, Alcázar Pérez Á, González Rojo P.
abstract: Introduction Traumatic hip dislocation is an uncommon but potentially severe injury requiring emergency management. We aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological features and associated injuries of patients with traumatic hip dislocation treated at a tertiary centre, and to analyse the factors related to complications and to the need for salvage surgery. Patients and methods Retrospective observational study of 44 patients aged 15 years or older treated between 2010 and 2024. Demographic variables, injury mechanism, direction of the dislocation, associated fractures (Judet-Letournel and Pipkin classifications), management and complications were recorded. Bivariate analysis used Fisher's exact test for categorical variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables; a p value Results Mean age was 37.4 years (SD 19.3) and 70.5% of patients were men. The commonest mechanism was a road traffic accident (52.3%) and the posterior direction was the most frequent (72.7%). A complex dislocation (with an associated fracture) was present in 72.7% of patients, and 36.4% occurred in the context of polytrauma. Closed reduction was performed in 88.6% of cases, with a median time to reduction of 2 h. The most frequent complication was sciatic nerve injury (20.5%). Femoral head osteonecrosis occurred in 2 patients (4.5%). Male sex was associated with more late complications (p = 0.043), and a prolonged hospital stay was associated with both early (p = 0.002) and late (p = 0.017) complications. Complex dislocations showed a consistent trend towards greater morbidity. Conclusions Traumatic hip dislocation predominantly affects young men after high-energy trauma. Prompt reduction was associated with a low rate of osteonecrosis. The presence of associated fractures and a prolonged hospital stay identify patients with a worse course.

title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience.
authors: RajBhandari T, Pokharel S, Gurung YP, Bhusal R, Banskota B, Banskota AK.
abstract: Background Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children. Materials and methods This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal's only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method. Union was defined radiologically, and analyses were conducted using MS Excel and SPSS. Results This study included 70 CPT patients; 40 male (57.1%) and 30 female (42.9%). The mean age at presentation was 3.84 years, with the first surgery at 5.38 years. Most cases were Boyd type 5 (71.43%) and Crawford type 4 (71.43%). Of 35 patients who underwent surgery, the union rate was 41.93% (13/31), with a refracture rate of 23.08% among unions. Periosteal grafting had a 50% union rate, while the Masquelet technique achieved 41.67%. Conclusions This study highlights the challenges in managing Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT), emphasizing the need for personalized surgical approaches based on patient age, limb length discrepancy, and classification. Effective patient counseling on risks and benefits is crucial for informed decisions.

title: The motivational spectrum of exercise: Dissociable gradients of autonomous and controlled motivation across its amount, form, and durability.
authors: Pan X, Gao Y, Jiang L, Li M, Zhao X, Wu D, Zhao D, Zhang Y.
abstract: Sustaining physical activity, not merely starting it, is the harder half of the public health problem. Self-determination theory holds that the quality of motivation is tied to which half succeeds, yet population evidence is scarce. We designed and conducted the 2020 China National Fitness Survey and analysed 74,407 exercising adults aged 19 to 101 from every mainland province, measuring the motivational spectrum, psychological need satisfaction, and three axes of behaviour: amount, form, and durability. The autonomous-to-controlled continuum replicated across an independent adolescent sample, residence, and sex with full scalar invariance. Among exercising adults, autonomous motivation was associated with all three axes, and more strongly with a routine maintained for a year or longer than with meeting 150 min/week (OR per SD 1.47 against 1.34). Controlled motivation was associated with amount and form and showed no detectable association with durability. Amotivation showed its strongest inverse association with durability (0.78). Interaction tests confirmed the dissociation, the controlled gradient being weaker on durability than on amount within residence, chronic disease, and age strata below 80. Motivation quality is associated more with the durability of exercise than with its weekly volume.

title: Surgical anatomy of the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) approach defines safe zones for W-plate fixation of the anterior pelvic ring.
authors: Da Cunha Q, Hellwinkel JE, Mauffrey C, David G.
abstract: Objectives To define the procedure-specific surgical anatomy of the pre-symphyseal region relevant to W-plate fixation by characterizing the soft-tissue layers, identifying critical neurovascular structures, and defining quantitative safe zones for dissection and plate placement. Methods Fresh-frozen adult cadavers underwent standardized low Pfannenstiel dissections reproducing the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) exposure required for W-plate fixation. Pre-symphyseal soft-tissue layers were sequentially dissected from the skin to the anterior pubic symphysis. The locations of critical neurovascular structures relative to the pubic midline and pubic tubercles were recorded, together with anatomical layers, dimensions of the prepubic ligamentous-aponeurotic complex, soft-tissue thickness, sex-related anatomical differences, and surgical safe zones. Results Three reproducible anatomical layers were identified in ten specimens. The superficial layer contained the pre-symphyseal fat pad and superficial epigastric vessels. The intermediate layer contained the spermatic cord or round ligament, ilioinguinal and genitofemoral nerves, and suprapubic artery, with these critical structures located at a mean distance of approximately 3.2 cm from the midline. The deep layer was consistently formed by the Pyramidalis-anterior pubic Ligament-Adductor longus Complex (PLAC), which covered the anterior pubic symphysis and measured a mean of 4.6 × 3.1 cm. No critical neurovascular structure crossed the central trajectory corresponding to W-plate placement. Female specimens demonstrated greater preperitoneal soft-tissue thickness, whereas lateral surgical safe zones were narrower in male specimens. Conclusion The pre-symphyseal region demonstrated a reproducible three-layer surgical anatomy with a predictable distribution of critical neurovascular structures. Quantitative anatomic mapping defined procedure-specific safe zones for extrapelvic W-plate fixation and provided practical guidancefor surgical exposure, implant positioning, and avoidance of iatrogenic injury. Level of evidence Level IV, therapeutic study.

title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material.
authors: Li Y, Hu H, Zhang Y, Liu G.
abstract: The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure. The synergistic enhancement mechanism of PVA induced hydration cementation film coating and slurry-rock interface was revealed. The results show that: (1) High content of CG weakens the early hydration activity of cement slurry system. After PVA is added, the fluidity of slurry increases, the initial and final setting time is further prolonged, and the bleeding rate decreases, indicating that PVA can improve the flow stability and water retention performance of coal-based solid waste slurry. (2) PVA content has obvious dosage dependence on the bearing capacity of the grout rock complex. The peak stresses of the 0%, 0.3%, 0.6% and 1.0% PVA groups are 4.87 ± 0.14 MPa, 5.35 ± 0.06 MPa, 6.04 ± 0.09 MPa and 5.12 ± 0.09 MPa, respectively. The 0.6% PVA group shows relatively better mechanical properties within the test range of this paper. (3) Appropriate amount of PVA can promote the filling of C-S-H gel, AFt rod crystals and C-H flake crystals on the surface of sandstone particles and in the pores and fracture, and adsorb and coordinate through hydroxyl groups to form hydration products and flexible polymer film. The hydration products provide a rigid skeleton, and the PVA flexible film plays a buffering role in the interface bonding and deformation, and synergistically realizes the densification, continuity and toughness enhancement of the weakly cemented sandstone-grout interface. The experimental results show that 0.6% PVA content can achieve a better balance between slurry performance, water retention stability, interface hydration cementation and mechanical bearing capacity, which can provide material design basis for grouting reinforcement of weakly cemented aquifer, thickening of aquiclude and prevention and control of mining-induced water disasters.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on implementing geographic information systems for leprosy elimination in Pakistan: A qualitative study.
authors: Geskus V, Fastenau A, Brüggemann R, Schlumberger F, van Soest J, Willis M.
abstract: Introduction Leprosy remains a pressing global health concern, with Pakistan among countries still facing missed and delayed diagnosis. By highlighting elevated risk areas, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) are a cost-effective solution to improve leprosy case detection by guiding targeted interventions to high-risk areas. This study's purpose was to investigate the perceived GIS implementation facilitators and barriers, to support targeted interventions and advance the Zero Leprosy strategy. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve stakeholders, including local field staff, program managers, and international experts. Thematic analysis was guided by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Diffusion of Innovation Theory (DOI) to identify facilitators and barriers concerned with GIS implementation for leprosy. Results Key facilitators included an integrated multi-disease and pilot-based rollout approach, capacity building activities, offline-capable tools, and improved visibility to drive motivation. Barriers included the limited local capacity in complex GIS data analysis, hybrid digital-manual workflows, historical data lacking GPS, and ensuring feedback and ownership for staff members. Conclusion GIS implementation is not only dependent on individual readiness, but also on broader external and organizational facilitators and constraints. This necessitates holistic implementation strategies that recognize the interconnectedness of different parts of the system. Internal capacity building is paramount to address statistical complexity and to build trust, ownership, and independence. As the world moves closer to achieving Zero Leprosy, integrating GIS within a multi-disease approach will be critical to making sustainable progress in combatting neglected tropical diseases.

title: Software-based concordance analysis of a predictive surgical planning model for target gap achievement in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
authors: Hu M, Yu M, Meng F, Luo Z, Xia Y, Weng X, Zhai D, Feng B.
abstract: Background In robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA), achieving soft-tissue balance requires repeated intraoperative plan adjustment and remains experience-dependent. Predictive models may support planning, but their clinical value depends on whether model-generated plans approximate predefined target gaps within the robotic workflow. This study assessed the software-based concordance between model-generated plans and predefined target gaps in robotic-assisted TKA. The predefined target gaps were planning set points established within the robotic software rather than measured intraoperative gaps. Methods This retrospective software-based concordance study included 209 complete-case knees undergoing robotic-assisted TKA. A machine-learning-based predictive model generated a bone-resection plan, which was imported into the robotic planning software to calculate software-derived medial and lateral gaps in extension and flexion. These software-derived gaps were compared with predefined target gaps, which were planning set points rather than measured values and were 18 mm in 819 of 836 gap-level observations (98.0%). The primary analysis focused on target gap deviation, defined as the software-derived gap minus the predefined target gap. As a benchmark, the deviation of the preadjustment gaps from the same targets was used as a preadjustment reference. Results A total of 836 gap-level observations were analyzed. The overall mean target gap deviation was -0.142 mm (SD, 1.411 mm), with a mean absolute error of 1.016 mm. Overall, 77.6% of software-derived gaps were within ±1 mm of target, and 93.4% were within ±2 mm. Bland-Altman analysis showed a small overall bias of -0.142 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -2.91 to +2.62 mm. At the knee level, only 43.1% of knees had all software-derived gaps within ±1 mm of target. Gap-level deviations ranged from -7 mm to +5 mm, and 16.3% of knees (34/209) had at least one gap with an absolute deviation > 2 mm. Compared with the preadjustment reference (MAE 2.002 mm, 49.4% within ±1 mm), the model substantially reduced deviation (MAE 1.016 mm, 77.6% within ±1 mm, p Conclusions In this software-based concordance analysis, the predictive planning model generated surgical plans whose robotic software-derived gaps approximated predefined target gaps with a mean absolute deviation of approximately 1 mm. The model-generated plan reduced target-gap deviation relative to the initial preadjustment plan within this target-conditioned workflow. However, because the targets were near-uniform (98.0% at 18 mm) and all measurements were software-derived, compartment-specific bias, moderate whole-knee consistency (43.1%), and occasional outlier deviations indicate that the model should be used as a surgeon-supervised decision support tool rather than as an autonomous planner. Prospective validation against measured intraoperative and postoperative gaps is required before clinical effectiveness can be claimed.

title: Scanner acoustic noise in resting-state fMRI.
authors: Wang J, Zhang X.
abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) is usually acquired during rapid gradient switching that produces intense, spectrally structured sound. Scanner sound activates auditory pathways and can alter neural, vigilance, autonomic, respiratory, and movement-related states, but its sound-specific causal effect on intrinsic functional-connectivity estimates remains unresolved. Direct human comparisons are few and heterogeneous: some report stronger or more extensive network estimates under quieter acquisition, whereas others find broadly preserved topology and within-network connectivity. Near-silent Looping Star imaging can recover canonical resting-state networks with marked sound reduction, but reduced temporal signal-to-noise ratio and functional sensitivity expose a trade-off between acoustic burden and measurement performance. Most quiet-versus-standard contrasts simultaneously alter temporal sampling, gradient vibration, reconstruction, steady-state behavior, or image quality and therefore identify a total protocol effect rather than a sound-specific effect. A structured, original-scale comparison reports acoustic levels and metrics, measurement conditions, acquisition parameters, and resting-state outcomes without pooling unlike measures. Vigilance, autonomic activity, respiration, and movement are potential mediators; indiscriminate regression of these variables can remove part of the total acoustic effect. Current evidence establishes that acquisition protocols can alter rs-fMRI estimates and that scanner sound is biologically active, but it does not establish a universal, directionally uniform suppression of human resting-state connectivity by conventional echo-planar imaging. Future sound-specific attribution would require randomized within-subject manipulation, protected-ear frequency-resolved dosimetry, control of co-varying vibration and sequence properties, and synchronized state and physiological monitoring.

title: Risk factors for complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Kojima KE, Argotte PLP, Esteves DS, Guimarães MGV, Medina R, Abe Puccetti VLY, de Camargo Leonhardt M, Santos Silva JD.
abstract: Background Surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures carries a substantial risk of postoperative complications, particularly surgical site infection, yet the relative contribution of fracture pattern and associated soft tissue injury to this risk remains incompletely defined. Objective To describe the rate and spectrum of complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures and to identify factors independently associated with these complications, with particular attention to acute surgical site infection. Methods Retrospective, single-center cohort study of 126 patients who underwent surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures between December 2014 and November 2024, reported in accordance with the STROBE statement. Candidate demographic, injury-related, and treatment-related exposures were compared against a composite primary outcome (any postoperative complication) and against acute infection using Fisher's exact test, Pearson chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and multivariable logistic regression. Results Overall, 39 of 126 patients (31.0%) experienced at least one postoperative complication; chronic pain (22.2%) and acute surgical site infection (16.7%) were the most frequent individual components. In bivariate analysis, the presence of a Morel-Lavallée lesion at baseline was significantly associated with both the composite outcome (OR 12.65, 95% CI 1.42-112.27, p = 0.011) and acute infection (OR 12.12, 95% CI 2.06-71.37, p = 0.007); Young-Burgess fracture pattern was also associated with infection (p = 0.018). After multivariable adjustment for infection, a Morel-Lavallée lesion (adjusted OR 17.69, 95% CI 2.46-126.95, p = 0.004) and combined-mechanism fracture pattern (adjusted OR 8.25 versus anteroposterior compression, 95% CI 1.91-35.58, p = 0.005) remained independently associated with infection. Neither the presence, technique, nor surgical approach of posterior ring fixation was associated with any complication type, and time from injury to definitive fixation (median 13 days) showed no significant association with either outcome. Conclusion A Morel-Lavallée lesion identified at initial evaluation was associated with postoperative complications in bivariate analysis and, together with a combined-mechanism fracture pattern, remained an independent predictor of surgical site infection after multivariable adjustment. No statistically significant association was identified between posterior fixation technique and complication risk. Level of evidence III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Radiographic and inflammatory factors associated with fever-based clinical improvement in children with macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
authors: Song SH, Yun KW, Lee H, Choi EH, Kang D, Kim YK, Eun BW, Cho EY, Lee S, Kim G, Kim YJ, Kang HM, Jo KJ, Park SE.
abstract: Purpose Clinical improvement during initial macrolide-based management varies among children with macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMP) pneumonia. We evaluated the associations between inflammatory burden, chest radiographic phenotypes, and clinical improvement. Methods We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study at nine university hospitals in South Korea from 2012 to 2024. Eligible patients had PCR-confirmed M. pneumoniae infection and sequencing-confirmed macrolide resistance. Fever-based clinical improvement was defined as defervescence within 5 days of macrolide initiation before any rescue therapy. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to evaluate factors independently associated with clinical improvement. Results Among the 169 identified MRMP pneumonia cases, 130 were included, and 47 (36.2%) showed clinical improvement. The proportion of cases that showed clinical improvement decreased across radiographic phenotypes, from 60.0% with peribronchial infiltration to 10.0% with dense lobar consolidation or diffuse haziness. Peak C-reactive protein (CRP) levels of ≥ 6 mg/dL were independently associated with lower odds of improvement (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.07-0.88), as was dense lobar consolidation or diffuse haziness compared with peribronchial infiltration (aOR, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.01-0.73). When stratified jointly by CRP level and radiographic involvement, the proportion of cases with clinical improvement was 53.7% among those with CRP Conclusions In sequencing-confirmed MRMP pneumonia, fever-based clinical improvement varied with inflammatory burden and radiographic phenotype. These exploratory findings may help inform structured reassessment during macrolide-based treatment but require prospective external validation.

title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Fiandeiro M, Gupta S, Nicholson T, ICM Shoulder Group.
abstract: Background Prosthetic joint infection (PJI) following shoulder arthroplasty is difficult to diagnose because clinical findings are often nonspecific, conventional diagnostic tests have variable sensitivity, and Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes) may cause indolent infection with limited systemic inflammatory response. Diagnostic criteria have also largely been adapted from hip and knee arthroplasty with limited shoulder-specific validation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) reviewed the available evidence and developed consensus recommendations for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI. Methods The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts experienced in shoulder arthroplasty and PJI. Thirty-two diagnostic questions underwent question-specific literature review, presentation to the consensus group, discussion, and voting. A modified Delphi process was used to establish consensus. Delegates voted to agree, disagree, or abstain. Consensus was categorized by percentage agreement, while strength of recommendation was assessed separately based on evidence quality, consistency, and directness. Results Consensus was achieved for 31 analyzed questions, with agreement ranging from 72% to 100%; 29 resulted in recommendations for clinical practice and 2 were identified as requiring further research. Question 47, which addressed the definition of PJI, was reported separately. Humeral component loosening, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were supported as components of the diagnostic criteria, whereas cloudy fluid, postoperative stiffness, serum WBC count, and D-dimer were not supported as independent criteria. Arthroscopic tissue biopsy, frozen section, and selective ultrasound-guided aspiration or synovial biopsy were supported as adjuncts to diagnosis. Five intraoperative tissue specimens, prolonged aerobic and anaerobic culture incubation, and routine perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis were supported. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and synovial neutrophil testing were supported as adjuncts; alpha-defensin was considered potentially useful but insufficiently validated for formal inclusion; and leukocyte esterase inclusion was not recommended. Routine use of bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), or positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) was not supported. Evidence remained insufficient to determine the clinical significance of polymicrobial molecular results or routine negative control samples. Conclusion The 2025 ICM provides a consensus framework for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI, identifying several measures that can be incorporated into current clinical practice. However, substantial uncertainty remains because most recommendations are supported by limited evidence and several diagnostic tests lack sufficient sensitivity. Prospective, shoulder-specific studies are needed to define diagnostic thresholds and determine the role of emerging molecular, biomarker, and imaging modalities.

title: Prevalence of generalized joint hypermobility, hypermobility spectrum disorders and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome: systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Carnerup I, Bondesson E, Ahl E, Schouenborg AT, Jöud AS.
abstract: Generalized joint hypermobility, GJH is common. Hypermobility can have various negative consequences and comorbidities, especially when criterion for Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder, HSD and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, EDS are met.The prevalence of these different conditions is lacking. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of these hypermobility disorders. A systematic search was conducted January 25, 2024 and updated May 28, 2025. It included the databases Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, CINAHL, and PEDro and followed a predefined search strategy adapted for each database (PROSPERO CRD42024505862) and included the MESH terms 'Ehlers Danlos Syndrome','Prevalence', 'Epidemiology' and keywords 'Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder';'Generalized joint hypermobility' and 'Systematic review'. 3633 unique records were screened, and 17 studies were included. From the meta-analysis the pooled prevalence across included studies of GJH in females were 9.5% (95% CI: 5.5; 15.8) with an I² of 95.5 % and 5.2% (95% CI: 3.0; 9.0) in males with an I² of 94.8). The evidence base for the age group 51 and older was insufficient for a robust estimate. Only one single study assessed HSD and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, hEDS in individuals aged 18-50 years and reported a prevalence of HSD of 38% in females and 39% in males, and the prevalence of hEDS as 2% in females and 0% in males. Hence, the available evidence did not allow for robust conclusions regarding the population-level prevalence of HSD/hEDS. This study shows that GJH is common, but with considerable heterogeneity and broad prediction intervals, which makes it crucial to interpret the pooled prevalence with caution. Moreover, a significant knowledge gap in the prevalence of GJH but particularly for HSD and EDS was identified. Our findings highlight the difficulties yet the need for more prevalence data on these conditions to understand the impact on the individual patient, health care services, and society.

title: Posterior Capsular Release in Soft-Tissue Balancing to Correct Valgus Deformity and Flexion Contracture During Total Knee Arthroplasty.
authors: Sugita T, Sogi Y, Miyatake N, Sasaki A, Kodajima S, Hashimoto K, Aizawa T.
abstract: Total knee arthroplasty for valgus knee deformities presents many challenging problems, especially in soft-tissue handling, although many soft-tissue balancing techniques have been described to date. Posterior capsular release, a soft-tissue balancing technique used to correct both valgus deformity and flexion contracture during total knee arthroplasty, is described in this technical note. Because this procedure does not sacrifice important lateral stabilizers, varus instability in knee flexion can be avoided. Furthermore, the release is performed just posterior to the femoral condyle without the risk of damaging the lateral collateral ligament and peroneal nerve associated with the posterior capsular division technique. We recommend this procedure as the first-choice strategy because additional procedures are required in some cases.

title: Popliteal Venous Aneurysm with Recurrent Pulmonary Embolism Treated by Ligation without Venous Reconstruction: A Case Report.
authors: Bungo M, Watanabe KI, Teshima Y, Sakashita Y, Uemura H, Yamamura M, Sakaguchi T.
abstract: Introduction Popliteal venous aneurysm (PVA) is rare but may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE). Case presentation A 73-year-old man presented with recurrent, transient loss of consciousness. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated bilateral PE and a saccular aneurysm of the right popliteal vein. Anticoagulation therapy improved his respiratory status, but surgical treatment was performed in view of the risk of recurrent embolism. The postoperative course was uneventful. Conclusions At the 1-year follow-up, the patient remained free of clinically apparent lower-leg edema, and venous duplex ultrasonography demonstrated no deep vein thrombosis and the development of collateral venous channels. Although ligation is not a standard procedure for PVA, it may be an effective option in patients in whom reconstruction is difficult or in those at high operative risk.

title: Platelet-Rich Plasma versus Corticosteroid Injections for Subacromial Impingement Syndrome: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Liu L, Roemer J, Gerges PE, Lugo E, John DQ, Lima DJL, Routman HD.
abstract: Background Subacromial impingement syndrome (SAI) is a common cause of shoulder pain. Corticosteroid injection (CS) provides short-term relief, but concerns about tendon health and durability have increased interest in platelet-rich plasma (PRP) as an alternative. This meta-analysis compared pain and functional outcomes after PRP versus CS for SAI. Methods A systematic review was performed per PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing PRP and CS for SAI. VAS pain scores and shoulder-specific functional outcomes were extracted, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed at baseline, short-term, and mid-term follow-up. Results Eight studies (518 patients; 7 RCTs and 1 non-randomized comparative study) were included, with 259 patients per group. Baseline VAS scores were comparable (MD 0.03, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.15; I 2 = 0%).
