Short- and mid-term VAS scores showed no significant difference between groups (short-term MD 0.47, 95% CI -0.35 to 1.29; mid-term MD 0.50, 95% CI -1.80 to 2.80), though heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 = 93.6% and 98.0%), falling to 49.2% and 80.2% after excluding the non-randomized study. Functional outcomes were inconsistently reported; at 6 months, Constant score differences ranged from -13.0 to +17.2, and UCLA differences ranged from -0.6 to +0.3. Conclusion PRP and CS showed no significant difference in short- or mid-term pain relief for SAI, but heterogeneity between trials was substantial. Functional outcomes were inconsistently reported across studies. Current evidence does not show it is clinically superior to CS for pain relief, and treatment choice should still weigh cost, availability, and patient preference. Level of evidence Level II, Systematic Review.

title: Non-linear associations between parity and long-term risk of osteoporosis.
authors: Yuan W, Liao J, Tao L, Song H, Wang H, Huang J, He J, Liu H, Wu T, Zhou H, Zhang Y, Song C.
abstract: Our findings suggest that although pregnancy and lactation are periods of physiological calcium loss, higher parity is not associated with an increased risk of postmenopausal osteoporosis; rather, it appears to confer a long-term protective effect. Purpose Osteoporosis is a significant public health burden. While parity induces transient bone loss, their long-term skeletal impact remains poorly understood. This study aimed to clarify the associations between parity, defined as the number of live births, and the risk of osteoporosis, osteoporotic fractures, and bone mineral density (BMD). Methods We analyzed data from 119,969 women in the UK Biobank. Associations between parity and incident osteoporosis or fractures were evaluated using unweighted and inverse probability of treatment weighting Cox proportional hazards models. Generalized linear models assessed associations with femoral neck and lumbar spine BMD. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic, genetic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Results Compared with nulliparous women, those with a parity of 2 or 3 exhibited a significantly reduced risk of osteoporosis in the weighted fully adjusted model. In addition, parity of 3 exhibited a significantly reduced risk of osteoporotic fracture compared with the nulliparous group. This protection was evident in women ≥ 60 years and those with normal body mass index. Parity was not significantly associated with areal BMD changes after full covariate adjustment. Conclusion In women aged 40-69 years at baseline, a parity of 2 or 3 confers long-term protection against osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture (a arity of 3), occurring independently of BMD changes. These findings support the integration of parity into clinical risk assessment tools, ultimately contributing to more effective osteoporosis prevention and a reduced fracture burden across women's lifespan.

title: Morbid Obesity May be Associated With Increased Odds of Prosthetic Joint Infection After Anterior-Based Total Hip Arthroplasty.
authors: Byrne AR, Buchalter WH, Dash AS, Neuwirth AL, Geller JA, Shah RP, Cooper HJ, Herndon CL, Sarpong NO.
abstract: Background Obesity increases perioperative risk after total hip arthroplasty (THA), particularly with anterior-based approaches. However, outcomes among patients with class II versus class III obesity remain poorly defined. This study compared early complications and patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) between these obesity classes. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients with BMI ≥35 kg/m² undergoing elective anterior-based primary THA from January 2022 to January 2025. Patients were stratified into BMI 35-39.9 kg/m² (Class II) and BMI ≥40 kg/m² (Class III) cohorts. Firth penalized logistic regression evaluated the association between BMI group and prosthetic joint infection (PJI) requiring operative irrigation and debridement (I&D). Results 193 patients were included (BMI ≥40: n = 53; BMI 35-39.9: n = 140). The BMI ≥40 kg/m² cohort had a greater proportion of females (77.4% vs 57.1%; P = .015) and higher ASA classification ( P = .02). PJI occurred more frequently in the BMI ≥40 cohort (7.5% vs 1.4%; P = .049). Unadjusted odds of PJI were higher with BMI ≥40 kg/m² (OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.08-29.6), but the association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for age, sex, and surgical approach. Both cohorts demonstrated significant improvement in WOMAC and SF-12 Physical scores at 3 months without between-group differences. Conclusions Patients with BMI ≥40 kg/m² demonstrated higher observed PJI rates after anterior-based THA while achieving comparable early functional improvement. These findings suggest a clinically important risk signal warranting confirmation in larger studies rather than establishing BMI ≥40 kg/m² as an independent risk threshold.

title: Modeling and controlling a half-car model suspension system using an ANFIS controller.
authors: Fisha SE, Aga AG, Wachamo TM.
abstract: Passive suspension systems (PSS) use fixed spring and damping characteristics and cannot adapt to changing road disturbances and operating conditions. Active suspension systems (ASS) address this limitation by generating additional control forces, but controller design must balance ride comfort, road holding, model uncertainty, and control effort. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) longitudinal half-car model and evaluates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller against PSS and PID-controlled ASS under double-bump and ISO-classified random Type A and Type C Road profiles at 10 and 20 m/s. The ANFIS controller is trained using PID-generated input-output data with two inputs, five Gaussian membership functions per input, 25 Takagi-Sugeno rules, and 150 training epochs. For the double-bump case at 10 m/s, ANFIS reduces body vertical displacement from 0.0435 to 0.0084 m (80.6%), vertical acceleration from 2.40 to 0.77 m/s2 (67.9%), and front suspension travel from 0.0652 to 0.0090 m (86.2%) relative to PSS. Compared with PID, the corresponding reductions are 53.6%, 49.3%, and 43.8%, respectively. Settling time is reduced by 38.8% for body vertical displacement and 38.6% for pitch acceleration relative to PSS. The result meets all the qualifications for riding comfort of the ISO 2631 standard. The study identifies limitations related to PID-supervised training, linear modeling, and actuator-energy assessment by employing simulation. Experimental evaluation is required to establish robustness to parameter uncertainty, sensor noise, actuator delay, and implementation energy requirements.

title: Milwaukee shoulder syndrome: a neglected and underrecognized basic calcium phosphate crystal arthropathy.
authors: Kougkas N, Avgerou P, Karantanas AH.
abstract: Milwaukee Shoulder Syndrome (MSS) is a rare but extremely aggressive form of destructive arthropathy, primarily affecting elderly women. Despite its distinct clinical profile, it remains an under-recognized and frequently misdiagnosed entity. This review synthesizes current knowledge on pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and diagnostic nuances of MSS to improve clinical recognition. The condition is defined by the intra-articular deposition of basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals, such as hydroxyapatite. These crystals trigger the release of proteolytic enzymes, leading to massive rotator cuff tears, superior migration of the humeral head, and rapid joint destruction. A hallmark of MSS is the "inflammatory paradox": a striking dissociation between severe structural damage and a non-inflammatory or minimally inflammatory synovial fluid profile (typically < 2,000 cells/mm3), which often is hemorrhagic. Diagnosis is challenged by the nanocrystalline nature of BCP crystals, which are non-birefringent and invisible under standard polarized light microscopy, requiring specialized staining (Alizarin Red) or advanced analytics for confirmation. Multimodal imaging is essential, with plain radiography showing advanced degeneration and MRI or CT delineating the extent of soft tissue and bony destruction. Treatment is currently limited to supportive measures, including recurrent joint aspiration, analgesia, and physical therapy. In advanced cases, reverse total shoulder arthroplasty remains the primary surgical intervention for functional restoration. As the aging population grows, increasing clinician awareness of MSS-particularly its unique synovial fluid characteristics-is vital for reducing diagnostic delay and optimizing patient care.

title: Mechanisms and disease implications of inflammaging and potential therapeutic strategies.
authors: Song X, Li S, Jiang Z, Yang A, Lu Q, Fang M.
abstract: Inflammaging is a chronic, low-grade inflammatory state associated with aging and age-related diseases. This review examines the mechanisms underlying inflammaging, emphasizing the interplay between oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage, cellular senescence, and immune dysregulation. Persistent cellular stress promotes senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), while impaired immune clearance allows senescent cells to accumulate, sustaining a self-amplifying inflammatory cycle. We further discuss the involvement of inflammaging in neurodegenerative, infectious, autoimmune, cardiometabolic, and musculoskeletal diseases. Finally, we summarize current and emerging interventions, including lifestyle modifications, pharmacological approaches, senolytics, senomorphics, and strategies targeting mitochondrial quality control and cellular metabolism. Understanding the interconnected mechanisms and tissue-specific effects of inflammaging may facilitate the development of targeted interventions to mitigate age-related diseases and promote healthy aging.

title: Long-Term Efficacy of Restricted Quantitative Superior Placement Technique in Total Hip Arthroplasty for Severe Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: An 8- to 10-Year Follow-Up of a Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Li S, Yang Z, Jiang D, Xie Y, Lu X, Zhao X, Gu M, Li Z, Liao W, Zhang Z.
abstract: Objective Total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), particularly those with Crowe II or III dysplasia, is challenging because of abnormal acetabular morphology and deficient bone stock. This study aims to compare the long-term outcomes of true anatomic versus restricted quantitative superior placement of the acetabular component. Methods This prospective, patient- and assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted from August 1, 2013, to July 31, 2024. Forty-four hips were allocated 1:1 to true anatomic center placement or restricted quantitative superior placement. Restricted quantitative superior placement was defined as positioning the cup center no more than 15 mm superior to the true anatomic center. Harris Hip Score (HHS), 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), complications, perioperative outcomes, and radiographic parameters were assessed. The mean final follow-up was 8.94 years. Independent-samples t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, Chi-square test, and Fisher's exact test were used for statistical analysis. Results No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in prosthetic complications. No revisions were recorded among the 36 hips that completed the 8-10-year follow-up. At the 8-10-year follow-up, the restricted quantitative superior placement group had a higher HHS than the true anatomic center group (93.70 ± 5.20 vs. 86.73 ± 11.62, p = 0.024); multiple imputation analysis showed a mean difference of 5.79 points (95% CI, 0.46-11.13; p = 0.034). Significant between-group differences were also observed at 2 and 7 years. SF-36 scores did not differ significantly between groups. Morselized bone grafting was required in 45.5% of the anatomic center group and 40.9% of the restricted quantitative superior center group. Structural grafting was used in 18.2% and 9.1%, respectively. Radiographic analysis showed higher center of rotation height and less limb lengthening in the restricted quantitative superior center group. Conclusions Restricted quantitative superior placement within 15 mm above the true anatomic center was associated with higher long-term HHS, with no significant difference in prosthetic complications and no revisions recorded among the 36 hips that completed the 8-10-year follow-up. It may represent a potential reconstructive option for patients with DDH. Trial registration Chictr.org, ChiCTR-TRC-1404388; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=5182.

title: Letter to the Editor: Long-term Oncologic Outcomes After Unplanned Soft Tissue Sarcoma Surgery: Implications for Surveillance Strategies.
authors: Saygılı AT.

title: Less Can Be as Effective as More: Two WOSI Items Capture Clinical Outcomes After Surgical Stabilization for Shoulder Instability.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Sawicka-Garbarek E, Kaszyński J, Cisowski P, Kaczmarek P, Ślęzak M, Soroko E, Lubiatowski P.
abstract: Background WOSI is one of the most popular and detailed questionnaires in both rating of the current patient status as well as measuring patients' recovery after treatment of shoulder instability. It includes questions about both psychological and somatic aspects of the patient's functioning. Our aim was to test whether the psychological items of the WOSI questionnaire, regarding beliefs and emotions, can be an indicator of recovery. Methods WOSI items with the highest psychological load (PSYCHE-WOSI) were identified through expert rating and assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient and hierarchical cluster analysis (Ward's method, tree diagram). Data from 78 patients (mean follow-up, 4.3 months) after surgical stabilization for shoulder instability, including WOSI, UCLA, Constant, ASES, and SST scores, were used to assess their utility as recovery indicators. Correlation, regression, and canonical correlation analyses were performed to identify PSYCHE-WOSI items most strongly associated with pain, function, range of motion, and overall PROMs. Results The PSYCHE-WOSI factor comprised items 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, and 21. Items 15 and 17 showed the strongest associations with function, range of motion, and overall PROMs, whereas items 16 and 21 were most strongly associated with pain outcomes. Conclusion A distinct psychological factor can be identified within WOSI. PSYCHE-WOSI items are strongly associated with PROMs and may provide a simple, rapid, and cost-effective tool for assessing recovery, supporting a more holistic, patient-centered approach to postoperative rehabilitation. Level of evidence Basic Science Study, Validation of Outcome Instrument.

title: Intraosseous Angiolipoma of the Maxilla: First Reported Case With a Review of the Literature.
authors: Shafiei S, Khaleghi A, Arefifard H, Shamloo N.
abstract: Angiolipomas are benign mesenchymal neoplasms composed of mature adipocytes and vascular channels, typically occurring in subcutaneous tissue. Intraosseous is extremely rare and has been described in only 22 cases in the previous studies, affecting mainly the mandible, calvarium, ribs, and long bones. To our knowledge, there has not been one reported case in the maxilla. We report the first case of intraosseous angiolipoma of the maxilla and review the literature to emphasize its diagnostic challenge and clinical significance. A 46-year-old male patient presented for routine dental checkup with no symptoms and an uneventful clinical examination. His past medical history was extraction of maxillary molars and surgical removal of radicular cysts from the same area five years ago. Panoramic radiograph showed well-defined unilocular radiolucency in the left posterior maxilla. Cone-beam computed tomography established cortical perforation of the buccal and palatal plates and sinus floor involvement. Based on imaging and history, a preliminary diagnosis of residual cyst was rendered. Enucleation and curettage with primary closure was performed to manage the lesion. During surgery, the mass was found to be adherent to the buccal fat pad and surrounding musculature. The excised specimen was 2.5 × 1.5 × 1.1 cm and yellowish in hue. Histopathology revealed mature adipose tissue scattered with several thin-walled vessels in a lobulated pattern covered with a fibrous capsule. There was evidence of muscle fibers, hemorrhage, and nerve bundles, however no malignancy or atypia was observed. The final diagnosis was intraosseous angiolipoma. The lesion was removed by surgery, and the postoperative course was uneventful. No recurrence was observed during 1-year follow-up. This article presents the first case of intraosseous angiolipoma of the maxilla, contributing to the known anatomic distribution of this tumor.

title: Intra-articular Extender Button Deployment Without a Secondary Incision for Salvage of Compromised Femoral Cortical Fixation in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
authors: Singh P, Boyd B, Marsh D, Chan FJ.
abstract: As suspensory fixation techniques for anterior cruciate ligament grafts gain popularity, so does the need to troubleshoot when intraoperative complications arise. A compromised lateral femoral cortex that cannot support the suspensory fixation is a complex intraoperative complication that can lead to graft failure. During these situations, an extender button is often used via a secondary incision. The technique described in this article allows for intra-articular passage of the extender button without the need for a secondary incision using 2-0 Vicryl sutures to attach the extender button to the suspensory button prior to graft passage. This cost-effective method can decrease operative time and potentially decrease postoperative pain and wound complications by foregoing the need for a second incision.

title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses prioritize candidate genes associated with lysosomes and ferroptosis in rheumatoid arthritis synovium.
authors: Yan G, Yan H, Yu P, Xiang Y, Yang G, Zhang Y, Long L, Huang X.
abstract: Objectives To prioritize candidate genes associated with lysosome-related and ferroptosis-related annotations in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovium and characterize their expression across synovial cell populations. Methods Publicly available bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from patients with RA and osteoarthritis (OA) were integrated with curated lysosome-related genes (LRGs) and ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared by both gene sets were identified. Gene-set expression scoring and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) were used to characterize cellular expression patterns and prioritize candidate genes. Candidate-gene expression was assessed in external datasets and by exploratory quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Results Myeloid cells and fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) populations showed relatively high expression scores for the shared gene set. Intersection analysis of the shared DEGs and selected co-expression module genes identified four candidates: VAMP2, HRAS, GRN, and BGN. External datasets supported lower VAMP2 expression in RA than in OA. Exploratory qRT-PCR analysis of synovial samples from four patients with RA and four patients with OA showed a consistent expression difference. Conclusion Integrated transcriptomic analyses prioritized VAMP2 as a candidate gene associated with lysosome-related and ferroptosis-related annotations in RA synovium. External datasets and exploratory qRT-PCR supported its lower expression in RA. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a causal role for VAMP2 in lysosomal regulation or ferroptosis. Key Points • Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses prioritized four candidate genes associated with lysosome-related and ferroptosis-related annotations. • Myeloid cells and FLS populations showed relatively high expression scores for the shared gene set. • External datasets and exploratory qRT-PCR supported lower VAMP2 expression in RA, prioritizing it for further functional investigation.

title: Incidence, Temporal Trends, and Associated Characteristics of Hip Fracture in Long-Term Care Residents: A Population-Based Cohort Study in British Columbia.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
authors: Muhammad O, Whiting SJ, Rostami M, Feng C.
abstract: Objectives To examine temporal trends in hip fracture incidence and determine whether resident-level or facility-level characteristics were associated with hip fracture occurrence among long-term care residents in British Columbia, Canada. Design Population-based retrospective cohort study. Setting and participants A total of 33,739 adults aged ≥65 years newly admitted to 305 licensed long-term care facilities in British Columbia between 2010 and 2014. Methods Linked Canadian administrative health data integrated hospital discharge records with resident- and facility-level assessment data. Residents were followed from admission until first hip fracture, death, discharge, transfer, or administrative censoring. Hip fracture incidence rates were calculated per 100,000 person-years. Multivariable logistic regression examined resident-level and facility-level characteristics associated with hip fracture occurrence. Results Among 33,739 residents, 1914 (5.7%) sustained a first hip fracture, corresponding to an overall incidence rate of 3418 per 100,000 person-years. Annual incidence declined from 3830.5 per 100,000 person-years in 2010 to 3146.4 per 100,000 person-years in 2014, representing an 18% relative reduction. Independent characteristics associated with fracture occurrence included lower body mass index categories compared with obesity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.36-1.82), female sex (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.45-1.78), dementia (aOR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.33-1.62), age 90 years and older (aOR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.18-1.51), and recent falls (aOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.03-1.29). In contrast, facility size, rurality, and health region were not independently associated with fracture occurrence after adjustment for resident-level characteristics. Conclusions and implications Hip fracture incidence declined modestly but remained substantial. Fracture occurrence was associated primarily with resident-level clinical characteristics rather than broad facility-level structural indicators. These findings support systematic identification of high-risk residents and suggest that fracture prevention efforts may be most effective when targeted toward low body mass index, dementia, advanced age, and recent falls.

title: Implant-Associated Peripheral Giant Cell Granuloma: A Case Report and Clinical Management.
authors: Arteaga AB, Cardenas LE, Mariana Villarroel-Dorrego, Montaner RA.
abstract: A 79-year-old woman presented with a peripheral giant cell granuloma (PGCG) associated with a dental implant and bone loss. Treatment consisted of surgical laser excision, ozone therapy, and implant removal. After 6 months, there was complete healing with no recurrence. Elimination of irritants is crucial for success.

title: Immunological Tolerance after Living-Donor Liver Transplantation from the Same Donor as for a Prior Bone Marrow Transplant: A Case Report without Rejection or Graft-Versus-Host Disease.
authors: Tokoro T, Takada S, Katano K, Sugita H, Gabata R, Takei R, Okazaki M, Seki A, Nakanuma S, Makino I, Uchida K, Yamazaki H, Yagi S.
abstract: Introduction We report a unique case of successful early weaning off immunosuppression following living-donor liver transplantation from the same donor as for a prior bone marrow transplantation, without the development of rejection or graft-versus-host disease. Case presentation The patient, a 45-year-old man, underwent bone marrow transplantation at ages 12 and 14 for myelodysplastic syndrome, receiving hematopoietic stem cells from his human leukocyte antigen-identical older brother. Following the second bone marrow transplantation, the patient did not experience myelodysplastic syndrome recurrence and successfully discontinued immunosuppressive therapy. Decades later, he developed hepatitis C cirrhosis complicated by multiple hepatocellular carcinomas, necessitating living-donor liver transplantation. His brother, the original bone marrow transplantation donor, served as the liver donor; they shared an identical blood type and a full human leukocyte antigen match. Post-living-donor liver transplantation, the patient received methylprednisolone for 1 week only, after which all immunosuppression was ceased. At 30 months post-transplant, the patient remains free of rejection, graft-versus-host disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence, suggesting the establishment of long-term immunological tolerance. Conclusions This case highlights the potential for immunosuppression-free liver transplantation when the donor and recipient share a full human leukocyte antigen match and prior bone marrow engraftment, offering important insights for the field of transplant immunology.

title: Hospital incentives and implementation support for appropriate adoption of robotic surgery: a scoping review and evidence-informed framework.
authors: Esmaeilzadeh P, Hasavari S.
abstract: Hospitals that acquire robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) platforms often seek to increase utilization, yet surgeons and operating-room teams bear the learning, coordination, and early efficiency costs of adoption. This scoping review mapped evidence on hospital incentives and broader implementation support for appropriate surgeon adoption of RAS. Following JBI guidance and a registered protocol, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore to September 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation searching, and reported findings following PRISMA-ScR. Two reviewers independently screened 1,058 records and included 17 sources (12 empirical studies; five reviews or recommendation documents). No included source evaluated a hospital incentive program, so the evidence was indirect. Nine of the 12 empirical studies used US data, and none linked incentive or support exposure to the appropriateness of patient selection or to patient outcomes. Industry payments were associated with greater robotic use; one observational evaluation linked proficiency-based training with shorter operative times and lower unadjusted costs; and qualitative studies identified barriers related to training, staffing, operating access, and credentialing. Using the capability, opportunity, and motivation (COM-B) model to organize these findings, we propose a four-layer framework (clinical justification, capability, operating opportunity, and governance), map the evidence to each layer, and specify a minimum configuration for hospitals with limited resources. The framework is a set of testable proposals, not a validated intervention. Hospital support appears most defensible when it addresses a documented barrier within a clinically justified service, and robotic case volume alone does not adequately measure program success.

title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway.
authors: Lou F, Deng G, Chen J, Jing Y, Wang A, Zhang M, Zhang Y, Wang B.
abstract: Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg). Cognitive performance was assessed using behavioral assays. Brain tissue morphology and neuronal survival were evaluated through histopathological examination. Glial cell activation and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) were measured. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict binding interactions with core targets. Western blotting was performed to determine the expression levels of key proteins involved in the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway. Results Treatment with Harpagide significantly improved behavioral performance, ameliorated brain pathological changes, preserved hippocampal neurons, suppressed glial activation, and reduced the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in SAE mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted four core targets: GAPDH, CASP3, MMP9, and ICAM1. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between Harpagide and MMP9. Western blot analysis further showed that Harpagide treatment was associated with reduced expression of MMP9 and phosphorylated NF-κB p65 in both hippocampal and cortical tissues. Conclusions The present study demonstrates that Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE, which are associated with mitigated neuroinflammation and reduced MMP9/NF-κB signaling, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for this devastating condition.

title: Gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, and patient-reported outcomes in Class III orthognathic surgery patients: An item-level analysis.
authors: Altundal G, Celikel ADG, Marsan G.
abstract: Objective To evaluate gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, functional and psychosocial evaluations, and treatment process perceptions among adult patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion undergoing orthodontic preparation for orthognathic surgery. Methods In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 81 adults (37 females, 44 males) with skeletal Class III malocclusion completed a 27-item investigator-developed questionnaire during pre-surgical orthodontic preparation, covering demographics, problem awareness, functional and psychosocial evaluations, motivation and expectations, treatment process, and patient engagement. Gender differences were analyzed item by item with Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, or Fisher's exact tests. P-values for the 37 comparisons were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure within questionnaire domains, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were estimated. Because the a priori sample size calculation did not address between-gender comparisons, these were treated as exploratory. Results Seven differences met the unadjusted threshold (p Conclusions Gender differences in social self-confidence, perceived information adequacy, and pre-operative satisfaction were the strongest exploratory findings. Because the study was not powered for gender comparisons, non-significant results do not indicate that the genders are similar. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered multi-center, longitudinal studies.

title: From data neglect to data respect: A framework for institutionalising a sustainable research data management culture in Kenyan universities.
authors: Nakitare J, Mathangani S, Kamau G.
abstract: Research Data Management (RDM) is increasingly recognised as critical for enhancing research integrity, efficiency, and data reuse globally; however, in Kenya, institutionalised RDM frameworks remain underdeveloped, resulting in fragmented practices, data loss risks, and limited data sharing and reuse. This study, drawn from a PhD investigation, proposes a comprehensive RDM framework informed by empirical evidence on current practices, enablers, and challenges in selected Kenyan universities. The study is anchored on the Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC) Capability Maturity Model for RDM and the UK Data Archive Research Data Lifecycle model. The framework was developed through a multi-stage mixed-methods study comprising a systematic review, a bibliometric analysis, and surveys examining the RDM landscape in Kenyan universities. A multiple-case study design involving six public and private universities, purposively selected based on the June 2023 Webometrics rankings, was adopted. Data was collected through interviews with six head librarians and five heads of research units, as well as questionnaires administered to 306 respondents from a targeted sample of 355. Quantitative data was analysed using IBM SPSS (Version 28), while qualitative data were thematically analysed using NVivo (Version 14). Triangulation and pretesting were used to enhance validity and reliability. All necessary ethical considerations were addressed before data collection. Findings indicate a growing awareness of RDM among researchers; however, practices remain largely ad hoc, poorly coordinated, and weakly supported institutionally. Notably, none of the universities studied had dedicated RDM policies, structured RDM support services, or dedicated RDM Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure, revealing gaps across personal, institutional, and national levels. This study proposes a multi-level, stakeholder-driven RDM framework that integrates researchers, librarians, ICT personnel, research offices, and key national agencies such as the National Commission for Science, Technology and Innovation (NACOSTI), the Commission for University Education (CUE), and the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) to support coordinated, policy-driven data stewardship aligned with international best practices for sustainable RDM in Kenyan universities.

title: Fracture-related infection after operative fixation of acetabular fractures: Incidence and factors independently associated with infection.
authors: Ramesh P, Imran A, Devendra A, M S S, Mogan K, Sp S, Dheenadhayalan J, Rajasekaran S.
abstract: Background The purpose of this study was to determine the incidence of fracture-related infection following acetabular fracture fixation and to identify factors independently associated with its occurrence. Methods A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted at a Level I trauma center. Patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent operative fixation of an acetabular fracture between January 2021 and July 2025 were included. Fracture-related infection was defined according to the AO/EBJIS consensus definition. Patients were followed for a minimum of 12 months. Multivariable analysis was performed using Firth penalized logistic regression. Results Of 359 patients, 27 (7.5%) developed fracture-related infection. All 27 met at least 1 confirmatory criterion. The median time to diagnosis was 9 days (IQR, 7-14), with 20 infections (74.1%) diagnosed within 14 days of fixation. Sixteen infections (59.3%) were culture-positive, with gram-negative organisms more common than Staphylococcus aureus. Eleven infections (40.7%) were culture-negative, including 6 patients who had received empirical linezolid before tissue sampling. All infected patients underwent infection-related reoperation; 23 (85.2%) were managed with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention, and 4 (14.8%) underwent implant removal. On Firth penalized multivariable analysis, higher body mass index (adjusted OR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.15-1.55), longer operative duration (1.63; 1.11-2.36), diabetes mellitus (2.55; 1.09-6.05), and a longer admission-to-surgery interval (1.08; 1.00-1.16) were independently associated with infection. Polytrauma was not independently associated with infection (2.10; 0.89-5.09). At final follow-up, fracture union was achieved in 20 patients (74.1%). Conclusions Fracture-related infection after acetabular fracture fixation appears to reflect a combination of patient-related and operative factors. Recognizing these factors may help identify patients at higher risk and allow closer postoperative surveillance. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III.

title: Forequarter Lateral Implosion Injury: A Review of Recognition and Multidisciplinary Management.
authors: Muldiiarov V, Weatherby DJ, White TW, Ayzenberg M, Bauman ZM.
abstract: Background Forequarter lateral implosion injury (LII) is a severe combined injury of the chest wall and ipsilateral shoulder girdle after high-energy trauma. This review summarizes current evidence and provides a practical framework for recognition, multidisciplinary assessment, and management. Methods Published literature on combined ipsilateral chest wall and shoulder-girdle injuries was reviewed and synthesized by a clinical topic. This evidence was integrated with the authors' clinical perspectives on recognition, multidisciplinary assessment, treatment selection, and operative planning. Results LII is characterized by combined disruption of the chest wall and shoulder girdle, often including displaced or segmental rib fractures with clavicular and/or scapular injury. Computed tomography (CT) is central to identifying chest wall instability, shoulder-girdle displacement, and global forequarter malalignment. Available evidence supports multidisciplinary assessment but does not justify routine fixation of every injured component. Operative management should be selective and based on established chest wall and orthopedic indications, respiratory physiology, injury severity, functional demands, and surgical expertise. Conclusions LII should be recognized and assessed as an integrated chest wall-shoulder girdle injury rather than a collection of isolated fractures. Combined or staged reconstruction may be appropriate when operative indications coexist, whereas nonoperative management remains appropriate in selected patients. Further studies are needed to define treatment selection and long-term functional outcomes.

title: Foot and ankle involvement is common across the spondyloarthritis spectrum with distinct anatomical and clinical patterns: a post hoc cross-sectional analysis of the ASAS-PerSpA study.
authors: Gezer HH, Duruöz MT, Aktas I, Akar S, Sahin N, Akgul O, Hizmetli S, Melikoglu MA, Kalyoncu U, Capkin E, Nazlıkul FGU, Yilmaz F, Sezer I, Ataman S.
abstract: Foot and ankle involvement is a common but frequently overlooked manifestation of spondyloarthritis (SpA). This study aimed to evaluate the frequency, anatomical patterns, and factors associated with foot and ankle involvement in a SpA cohort. This post hoc analysis included 489 patients from the Turkish cohort of the ASAS-PerSpA study. Foot and ankle involvement was defined as the presence of arthritis, enthesitis, and/or dactylitis. Anatomical distribution of each manifestation was analyzed, and demographic and clinical characteristics were compared between patients with and without involvement. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with foot and ankle involvement. Foot and ankle involvement was identified in 229 of 489 patients (46.8%). Enthesitis was the predominant manifestation (184/489, 37.6%), followed by arthritis (122/489, 24.9%) and dactylitis (27/489, 5.5%). Overall involvement was most frequent in peripheral SpA (28/35, 80.0%) and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) (52/73, 71.2%). The ankle represented the predominant site of arthritis, whereas the plantar fascia and Achilles tendon were the most frequently involved entheses. Isolated enthesitis was the most common presentation, although arthritis and enthesitis frequently coexisted. Patients with foot and ankle involvement had significantly higher disease activity, greater peripheral structural damage, and worse health status than those without involvement (p < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, psoriasis (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.11-3.76) and higher ASAS Health Index scores (OR 1.11 per point, 95% CI 1.04-1.18) were independently associated with foot and ankle involvement, whereas axial involvement showed an inverse association (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.24-0.97). Foot and ankle involvement affects nearly half of patients with SpA and is particularly frequent in peripheral SpA and PsA. Enthesitis is the most common manifestation, and poorer overall health status is independently associated with foot and ankle involvement. These findings highlight the clinical relevance of foot and ankle manifestations across the SpA spectrum.

title: Factors Associated with Functional Improvement After Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Comprehensive Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Xiong R, Li W, Wang S, Jiang C, Zhu Y.
abstract: Background Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is now widely used across diverse indications. Existing meta-analyses usually evaluate single factors and rely solely on postoperative functional scores, without accounting for baseline status. A comprehensive quantitative synthesis of determinants of functional improvement, using change in validated scores from pre- to postoperative, is therefore needed. Objective This study aims to systematically evaluate patient- and surgery-related determinants of functional enhancement after rTSA, based on changes in ASES score and Constant-Murley score, through a systematic review and meta-analysis, and provide an evidence-based reference for clinical decision-making. Methods PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to November 2025. Randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies of reverse shoulder arthroplasty reporting relevant ASES or Constant outcomes by patient- or surgery-related exposures were included, with analyses primarily focused on preoperative-to-postoperative changes. Effect sizes were extracted and pooled using Review Manager 5.3, applying fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity, with publication bias evaluation, and study quality assessment. Results Sixty-five studies were included, with overall methodological quality judged to be high. Meta-analyses showed that prior shoulder surgery was the only consistent patient determinant of smaller gains in ASES and Constant scores, whereas age and obesity had no meaningful impact, and lower socioeconomic status predicted worse postoperative ASES. Among surgical factors, humeral cemented fixation and subscapularis repair were associated with greater functional improvement. Funnel plots supported the robustness of these findings. Conclusion This meta-analysis is the first to prioritize pre- to postoperative change in function after rTSA. Prior shoulder surgery was associated with less improvement in ASES and Constant scores, whereas cemented humeral fixation was associated with greater improvement in Constant scores and subscapularis repair with greater improvement in ASES scores. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Extensive necrotic ileal intussusception after laparoscopic adnexal surgery in a patient with Roux-en-Y reconstruction: a rare surgical emergency.
authors: Youssef H, Poirier A, Matos Santos B, Tokoto PA, Dash J, Liot E, Chevallay M, Moenig S.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Antimicrobial Stewardship Strategies in Residential Aged Care: An Umbrella Review.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
authors: Dewi S, Adhikary RK, Menikpurage T, Prastyani AW, Belachew A, Mond J, Bennett N, Lim LL, Sutarsa IN, Dykgraaf SH.
abstract: Objectives To identify, appraise, and synthesize global evidence on the effectiveness of antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) interventions in residential aged care homes (RACHs). Design An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Setting and participants Systematic review on AMS interventions for those aged 65 and above who resided in RACHs globally. Fifteen reviews (2013-2024) encompassing 66 unique primary studies were included. Six reviews featured meta-analyses. Methods Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, searches across major databases, including Scopus and PubMed, were conducted. Study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal were performed independently by 2 reviewers. AMS interventions were mapped against the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Core Elements of AMS for nursing homes. Quantitative and qualitative data were synthesized alongside available meta-analyses. Results Multifaceted AMS strategies combining education, clinical guidelines, drug expertise, and audit and feedback were associated with reductions in antimicrobial consumption, infection rates, and urine culture requests. Long-term implementation (up to 60 months) showed decreased antimicrobial resistance among uropathogens. However, interventions demonstrated little to no impact on the appropriateness of antimicrobial selection, hospital admissions, or mortality. Cost-effectiveness data remained limited. Conclusions and implications Multifaceted AMS interventions are effective in reducing antibiotic use and infection rates in RACHs. Facilities should implement multifaceted strategies, prioritizing education and clinical algorithms. In resource-limited settings, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention framework and the World Health Organization AWaRe book can be adaptively scaled using nurse-led champions to circumvent high costs. Future longitudinal studies must use standardized aged-care metrics, evaluate cost-effectiveness, and address global equity by investigating AMS models in low- and middle-income countries.

title: Enhanced visualization and quantitative evaluation of traumatic vertebral bone marrow edema using multiparameter fusion imaging with spectral CT.
authors: Zhang Y, Luo S, He A, Sun Y, Wen J, Liu H.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic performance of calcium-suppressed (CaSupp), electron density-weighted (EDW), and fused CaSupp + EDW images from dual-layer detector spectral CT for traumatic vertebral bone marrow edema (BME), with MRI as the reference standard. Methods Seventy-one patients with lumbar traumatic fractures (355 vertebral bodies) underwent spectral CT and 3.0 T MRI within 72 h. Conventional CT, CaSupp, EDW, and fused images were reconstructed. Three radiologists of different seniority assessed image quality and qualitatively diagnosed BME; one radiologist measured virtual Hounsfield units (vHU) and percentage electron density (%EDW). Friedman, Fleiss' kappa, ROC, GEE, and McNemar analyses were applied (α = 0.05). Results Fusion imaging achieved the highest accuracy (94.7 %, 95 % CI 92.1-97.1 %), sensitivity (88.7 %, 95 % CI 81.7-95.8 %) and NPV (97.0 %), outperforming conventional CT (sensitivity 63.4 %) at comparable specificity (96.3 %). Inter-reader agreement was excellent for fusion (κ = 0.810) but poor to slight for CaSupp (0.027) and EDW (0.171). vHU and %EDW were higher in BME-affected than normal vertebrae (both P Conclusion Multiparameter fusion of CaSupp and EDW enables simultaneous visualization and quantification of vertebral BME with superior diagnostic performance and inter-reader consistency. It may serve as a useful supplementary tool for patients with MRI contraindications or in the emergency setting.

title: Effective and ineffective teamwork in robotic-assisted surgery: operating room professionals' accounts.
authors: Nyein KP, Canady KM, Bingea DR, Wildman JL, McGuire BB, Condron C.
abstract: Background Robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) has transformed modern surgical practice and introduced unique challenges to teamwork and communication. While prior research has examined human factors integration, barriers, and interventions in RAS, we explore operating room (OR) professionals' experiences of teamwork across all operative phases. Objective This study aims to give voice to OR professionals actively performing RAS and to understand what they perceive as effective and ineffective teamwork in their experiences. Method Using an interpretivist paradigm, we conducted critical incident-based, semi-structured interviews with 21 OR professionals across multiple roles and specialties at two teaching hospitals using a closed-console RAS system. We analyzed the data using reflexive thematic analysis and employing an inductive, semantic coding strategy in which the content of the data was coded as explicitly described by the participants. Results We organized the results across three operative phases. In the pre-operative phase, deliberate planning, including team briefings, equipment checks, procedural steps, and patient and robot positioning, was reported as more important for teamwork in RAS. During the intraoperative phase, effective and ineffective teamwork was, respectively, described as the presence or absence of explicit verbal communication (closed-loop communication, real-time narration, anticipation in tandem with verbal prompts), team reflexivity, centralized coordination through a bedside assistant, psychological safety, and shared mental models. In the post-operative phase, participants linked teamwork quality to patient safety and operative efficiency in a cascading effect. Conclusion Teamwork in RAS requires a more deliberate, structured team approach than in open or laparoscopic surgery. We provide best practices for effective teamwork and pitfalls to avoid in RAS. Targeted training emphasizing teamwork and communication may enhance team effectiveness and patient safety in robotic surgical environments.

title: Differential changes in cervical proprioception and motor imagery following structured imagery training in chronic neck pain.
authors: Bostan A, Akan A, Ulger O.
abstract: Background Chronic neck pain (CNP) is associated with altered sensorimotor function, including impairments in cervical proprioception and changes in body-related perception. While implicit motor imagery (IMI)-based interventions have shown clinical benefits, their effects on cervical proprioceptive performance and motor imagery-related outcomes in individuals with CNP remain unclear. Objective To investigate the effects of lateralization and IMI training on cervical proprioception (CP), neck awareness (NA), IMI performance, pain, disability, kinesiophobia, and range of motion (ROM) in individuals with CNP. Methods In this clinical trial, 34 participants (17 CNP, 17 healthy controls) completed a 4-week structured imagery training (SIT) program combining lateralization and IMI training delivered via telerehabilitation. Primary outcome was cervical joint position error (JPE). Secondary outcomes included IMI performance (left/right judgment task), pain, disability, kinesiophobia, NA, ROM, and cognitive interference (Stroop). Results Following SIT, the CNP group showed statistically significant within-group reductions in pain intensity (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012, d = 0.76), kinesiophobia (Holm-adjusted p = 0.034, d = 0.50), neck-related disability (Holm-adjusted p = 0.034, d = 0.37), and FreNAQ-T scores (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012, d = 0.09). However, baseline-adjusted models revealed no statistically significant between-group post-training differences for extension JPE (p > 0.05, partial η2 = 0.009), flexion JPE (where post-training values remained persistently elevated in CNP; partial η2 = 0.310), and IMI accuracy/reaction times for neck and hand tasks (all Holm-adjusted p = 1.000, partial η2 ≤ 0.068). Conclusions A 4-week SIT program was associated with short-term improvements in subjective clinical symptoms in individuals with CNP; however, no differential group effects were observed for objective cervical proprioception or motor imagery performance.

title: Development of shelf-stable reagents and assay kits for bioluminescence applications using the capillary-assisted vitrification platform stabilization technology.
authors: Radford S, Peris-Taverner Y, Dibble M, Corn K, Zhu T, Martello S, Mayeaux M, Ladd A, Renu S, Chunduri T, Jadhav A, Dart M, Rafat M, Shank-Retzlaff M, Bronsart LL.
abstract: Luminescence is a powerful method for detecting trace analytes and monitoring biological processes. However, most bioluminescence reagents, including luciferase and its substrates, are sensitive to temperature, limiting their usable shelf lives, and resulting in inconsistent performance. Enhancing the stability of these reagents could reduce signal variability between experiments, simplify workflows, and address cold chain storage issues. In this study, we demonstrate the application of the platform stabilization technology, capillary-assisted vitrification (CAV), as a tool to stabilize different luciferases and their substrates, and the application of the stabilized reagents in both in vitro and in vivo bioluminescent assays. We demonstrate that CAV-stabilized reagents can be stored and shipped ambiently, maintain consistent performance over time, and are suitable for use in cell viability quantification, tumor monitoring, in vivo imaging, microbial detection, and immunoassays. Additionally, different reagents can be co-formulated to make ready-to-use assay kits that can also be shipped and stored ambiently. Our results demonstrate that CAV stabilization is a viable alternative to traditional storage methods, with broad potential to improve bioluminescence workflows.

title: Development of a variable ground pressure tracked chassis for soil compaction mitigation.
authors: Chu P, Ding Z, Su Z, Fang M, Tang Z.
abstract: Traditional tracked agricultural machinery with a fixed contact geometry struggles to balance high maneuverability on hard pavements and low soil compaction in soft paddies. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an active variable ground pressure tracked chassis system. The effective ground contact length of the track is adjusted by distributed electric cylinders and a multi-stage linkage mechanism. To evaluate its performance, we conducted kinematic modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and field tests. First, a planar kinematic model was established to describe the relationship between the cylinder stroke and the track geometry. Second, an internal load transfer path method was used in the FEA post-processing to reduce numerical errors from the track lugs, showing that the low-pressure mode reduces the mean compressive stress from 0.03 MPa to 0.008 MPa. Finally, soil bin tests with a physical prototype were carried out. The results indicate that the low-pressure mode decreases the peak subsoil stress from 93 kPa to 63 kPa at low speeds. In contrast, the regular mode with a shorter track length on hard surfaces reduces steering resistance. This study provides a practical design method for adaptable agricultural tracked vehicles.

title: Depressive symptoms among people living with HIV in Northern Tanzania: The role of family history, social support, and maladaptive coping.
authors: Ng'unda NA, Ghaimo FE, Kiwango F, Chacha S, Mmbaga BT, Mushi D, Mzilangwe ES.
abstract: Background Depression is a common mental disorder among people living with HIV (PLWH) and is driven by both neuroimmunological and psychosocial pathways. In turn, depressive symptoms worsen HIV outcomes through reduced adherence, risk behaviors, and impaired immune function. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms and identify associated factors among PLWH attending health facilities in northern Tanzania. Methodology We conducted a cross-sectional study (September-October 2023) in four Care and Treatment Clinics (CTCs) across three health system levels in Moshi Municipality. Study sites were selected purposively to represent tertiary, secondary, and primary care. Within each site, adult (≥18 years) clients on ART for ≥6 months were sampled using systematic random sampling. Standardized instruments included a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Duke-UNC Functional Social Support Questionnaire (FSSQ), the Brief COPE, and a 12-item HIV-related stigma scale. Data were entered and analyzed using STATA version 16. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify associations between depressive symptoms and various independent variables. Results A total of 598 clients participated, just above half (56%) from the secondary health facility level, and nearly three-quarters (70.9%) of participants were female. The prevalence of depressive symptoms was 14%. Participants reported having a family history of mental illness, good social support and predominantly use maladaptive coping strategies were more likely to report having depressive symptoms (AOR 2.15, 95%CI: 1.12-4.13; P 0.022), (AOR 8.19, 95%CI: 1.29-51.92; P 0.026), (AOR 3.98, 95%CI: 2.62-6.05; P Conclusion Depressive symptoms are common among PLWH receiving HIV care and treatment in northern Tanzania, and are associated with a reported family history of mental illness, predominant use of maladaptive coping, and even good social support. Thus, more studies need to be done on the relationship between depressive symptoms and social support among PLWH. Integrating mental health intervention into HIV services and providing personalized interventions focused on addressing maladaptive coping and social support are key to reducing depression among people living with HIV.

title: Crack identification and detection in mine boreholes using deep learning: A case study of hexi coal mine.
authors: Huang R, He W, Chen L, Xiang Y, Li W.
abstract: The internal cracks in deep rock masses are an important factor determining the safety of coal mining. The borehole peeping technology is an important method for obtaining the distribution of coal and rock fractures in deep geological engineering. However, there are often problems such as strong background interference and complex joints in real mines, which bring greater challenges to obtaining the distribution of cracks. Therefore, this study proposes a deep learning-based method for identifying internal cracks, which is used for the intelligent identification and analysis of cracks in drilled rock masses. The experimental verification was carried out based on the real borehole peeping images of the tunnels in Hexi Coal Mine as the data set. By embedding the ResCBAM attention mechanism into the YOLOv8 head network, the reliability and accuracy of identifying internal cracks in rock were further enhanced. The test results show that, the proposed Res-YOLOv8 algorithm can more accurately suppress the interference of complex backgrounds and present the morphological characteristics of rock cracks to compare with the fusion of typical attention mechanisms SE and CBAM with YOLOv8. The ResCBAM-YOLOv8 algorithm demonstrates strong performance in the evaluation indicators of confusion matrix, loss rate, precision, recall and MPA. The proposal of method has improved the efficiency of detecting and identifying cracks in coal and rock masses in real mines, and provided more reliable technical support for the stability evaluation of coal mine roof.

title: Comparative outcomes of endovascular versus synthetic bypass for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions: A 3-year single-center cohort study.
authors: Han C, Kim GM, Choi J, Tak YJ, Lee C, Lee CW, Bae M, Wang IJ, Huh U.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) ranges from intermittent claudication to critical limb‑threatening ischemia (CLTI), with <3% of intermittent claudication cases progressing to CLTI. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stenting (PTAS) and synthetic graft femoropopliteal bypass (FPB) in a homogeneous PAD cohort. A subgroup analysis of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) B and C lesions, which lack standardized treatment algorithms, was also performed. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with no prior history of vascular interventions in the same limb who were treated for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions between 2016 and 2020 (29 underwent PTAS and 59 underwent FPB). Primary outcomes were reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, and vessel patency (primary, assisted primary, and secondary) over a 3‑year follow‑up. Subgroup analysis was performed to assess differences in treatment outcomes. No statistically significant differences were detected in reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, or patency between the two treatments. For loss of primary patency, the hazard ratio (HR) for FPB versus PTAS was 1.89 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-4.69; log-rank p = 0.146) and 1.23 (95% CI, 0.45-3.38) after adjustment for lesion length and TASC grade. In the TASC B and C subgroup, no significant differences were observed in primary, assisted primary, or secondary patency (log-rank p = 0.809, 0.302, and 0.135, respectively). The study was underpowered to detect modest effects (post-hoc power for primary patency, 34.4%). In this small single-center cohort, no statistically significant difference in 3-year outcomes was detected between PTAS and FPB for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions; clinically meaningful differences cannot be excluded, and the findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

title: Comparative effects of weightlifting derivatives and traditional resistance training on force-velocity profile characteristics in mixed martial arts athletes.
authors: Yan J, Chen W, Sun Y, Zhu W, García Ramos A.
abstract: This study compared the effects of weightlifting derivatives versus traditional resistance training on optimizing force-velocity profile (FVP) characteristics in mixed martial arts (MMA) athletes exhibiting force deficits. Thirty-five male athletes exhibiting force deficits in FVP testing were randomly assigned to a weightlifting derivatives training group (n = 20) or a traditional resistance training group (n = 15). Both groups completed a 10-week intervention. Key performance metrics were assessed pre- and post-intervention. The FVP was determined from loaded squat jumps to derive theoretical maximal force (F 0 ), velocity (v 0 ), and theoretical maximal power output (P max ). Additional outcome variables included countermovement jump (CMJ) height, isometric mid-thigh pull (IMTP) for peak force and 250 ms rate of force development (RFD), and landmine punch throw (LPT) peak power. The weightlifting derivatives training group showed more favorable adaptations in P max , increased by 5.11 ± 5.65% compared with a decrease of -6.46 ± 5.86% in the traditional group (p max and selected explosive performance outcomes, whereas traditional resistance training may produce greater force-oriented adaptations.

title: Co-designing physical activity intervention in Danish kindergartens: A design-based research approach.
authors: Sederberg M, Pawlowski CS, Jeppesen LS, Bandak E, Bugge A.
abstract: Physical activity in early childhood supports health, psychosocial development, and motor competence, yet many Danish kindergarten children do not meet recommended activity levels. Early childhood settings are therefore key health promotion environments where routines, pedagogical practices, and staff competencies shape children's access to daily physical activity. This study examines how a kindergarten-based intervention can be co-designed to strengthen physical activity by equipping pedagogical staff and supporting enabling environments through participatory, practice-embedded processes using a design-based research approach. Five Danish kindergartens participated in a one-year development phase guided by a complex intervention framework. The process included four iterative domains: context analysis, laboratory work, design experiments, and reflection. Data from observations, interviews, workshops, and prototype testing were analyzed thematically. The co-design process resulted in six elements: active group time with PA prompts; a play catalog with pedagogical cues; a key ring with pedagogical prompts; structured playground activities; designated PA Agents; and a competence development program. Six themes informed the design: Physical activity as an overlooked pedagogical resource; variation in children's physical activity competences; the role of leadership in cultural change; pedagogical staff's bodily engagement; pedagogical judgment as a driving force, and; competence development as an adoption strategy. The process produced a contextually grounded and professionally owned intervention. By strengthening local capacity, ownership, and equitable access to physical activity, the co-design approach supports health promotion embedded in every day kindergarten practice and informs future feasibility testing.

title: Clinical outcome of a modern patellofemoral arthroplasty prosthesis into the second decade - a cohort study with minimum 10-year follow-up.
authors: Tsikopoulos K, White P, Musawi HA, Newman J, Porteous A, Robinson J, Murray J, Bristol Knee Group.
abstract: Background A modern patello-femoral joint arthroplasty (PFA) prosthesis featuring a sided trochlea on-lay component produced in oxinium (i.e., oxidized zirconium) has been introduced recently to reduce wear and increase wettability. Good medium-term functional outcome and survivorship have been documented as of yet. The aim of this study was to explore the long-term outcomes in a consecutive series with 10-year follow-up. Methods Data were collected between September 2005 and November 2014 and a total of 161 modern PFJ replacements with a mean follow-up of 13.8 years (range 2 to 22 years) were considered. The primary outcome was the assessment of implant survivorship and revisions 10 years post-operatively and beyond. Secondary outcomes included the assessment of the Oxford Knee Score (OKS) preoperatively, one and five years post-operatively in addition to complications and all-cause mortality. Results The revision free survival of this modern implant was 92% at 5y, 81% at 10y, 78% at 15y and 75% at 20 years, and there was no effect for sex (P = 0.371), nor age (P = 0.902),nor side (P = 0.554).The mean preoperative and five-year postoperative OKSs were 18.83 (SD 7.51) and 30.00 (SD 12.77), respectively (mean difference was 11.17 [95% CI 8.17 to 14.17]; P Conclusions This study shows satisfactory implant survivorship 20 years post-operatively and good functional outcomes up to 5 years postoperatively.

title: Caring for Our Care Force: A Pilot Intervention for Employees and Leaders in Long-Term Care.
journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
authors: Brossoit RM, Jaworski M, Calamia M, Castro DM, Yang L, Luger TM, Goodwin C.
abstract: Objective Burnout and mental health concerns are prevalent among healthcare workers, particularly in long-term care, highlighting the need for effective workplace interventions. Methods By integrating training approaches developed in clinical psychology and occupational health psychology, six workshops were designed for long-term care employees (N = 89; e.g., nurses) and leaders (N = 69; e.g., supervisors, senior leadership). The pilot intervention was implemented across seven facilities and evaluated using a single-group pre-test/post-test design, with quantitative survey data and brief open responses. Results Participants rated the quality and utility of the workshops favorably. No significant changes emerged for learning, behavioral, or well-being outcomes, and effects sizes were small. Conclusions This work advances the Total Worker Health intervention literature. We highlight lessons learned to provide practical recommendations for program design, implementation, and evaluation in future workplace intervention efforts.

title: Balancing Iliac Crest Avoidance and Neural Safety in L5/S1 TELD: Quantitative Identification of a Candidate Balanced Trajectory Window Using AI-Assisted 3D MRI Reconstruction.
authors: Wang Y, Huang C, He Q, Lu J, Li M, Liu X, Zhou J, Bian C, Zhang G, Luo H, Zhang R, Liu F, Yang X, Su Z, Lu S.
abstract: Objective Transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (TELD) at L5/S1 is challenging due to the iliac crest barrier. Conventional planning relies on CT or 2D imaging, inherently lacking soft-tissue contrast to visualize neural structures. This study aimed to define a quantitative candidate balanced trajectory zone using AI-assisted 3D MRI reconstruction to simultaneously evaluate iliac crest obstruction and neural safety constraints. Methods A deep learning model was trained on 50 thin-slice lumbar MRIs to achieve precise segmentation and 3D reconstruction of neural, dural, and osseous structures. Thirty lumbar models were selected after image- and reconstruction-quality screening for surgical puncture simulation. Using a 5° increment as the angular increment, 49 virtual working trajectories (coronal plane angles, CPA 0°-30° and cross-sectional angles, CSA 0°-30°) were established for each bilateral intervertebral foramen, yielding a total of 2940 trajectories. Intersection volumes between each trajectory and the iliac crest, L5 nerve root, dural sac, and articular processes were quantitatively analyzed. Results The model achieved an 86.4% mean Dice coefficient (73.2%-92.4%). Among 2940 trajectories, 1207 (41.1%) completely avoided the iliac crest. Spatial analysis revealed a trade-off: increasing CSA reduced iliac and S1 superior articular process obstruction but increased L5 osseous removal, whereas steeper CPAs spared the L5 nerve root but risked the L5 inferior articular process. Quantitative analysis identified a candidate balanced trajectory window (CPA 20°-25°, CSA 25°-30°) that achieved a balance between iliac crest avoidance, neuro-osseous preservation, and facet integrity. Conclusions This candidate trajectory window (CPA 20°-25°/CSA 25°-30°) may provide a useful reference for balancing iliac crest avoidance with neuro-osseous safety. These findings provide quantitative constraints for manual planning and for the future development of computer-assisted trajectory-planning systems.

title: Avascular necrosis of the femur following COVID-19: an updated systematic review.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Azadvari M, Akbari N, Hatam S, Rastkar M, Razavi SZE.
abstract: Background One of the complications of COVID-19 infection is avascular necrosis of the femoral head. To date, various studies have reported a wide range of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in patients with COVID-19. The previous systematic review included only 14 studies. So, this systematic review aims to update the findings of these studies. Methods Databases such as PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were systematically searched by two independent researchers on April 1st, 2024. Results A literature search revealed 1229 records, 161 full-texts were evaluated, and finally, 55 studies remained for systematic review. Fifty-five studies were included in this systematic review. Four studies were cross-sectional studies, six were retrospective studies, and the remaining (45studies) were case reports or case-series studies. Totally, 864 cases were included. Except for 12 studies, 43 studies reported the administration of steroid therapy in included cases. The most common underlying conditions were hypertension, followed by diabetes. In 274 (31.7%) of included cases, AVN was bilateral, and both hips were involved. In some studies, non-surgical treatments-including supplement therapy, anticoagulant therapy, physiotherapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy-were administered. Several studies reported symptomatic improvement in patients treated with the core decompression approach. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) was the most commonly used surgical treatment. Conclusions Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in cases that have survived COVID-19 should be considered carefully as early diagnosis helps to preserve the joint and its function.

title: Atraumatic Interspinous Bursitis in an Adolescent-A Case Report.
authors: McKenna DP, Davey MS, O'Toole P, Alberghina F.
abstract: Cervical interspinous bursitis is an important cause of cervical spine pain, with the diagnosis relying on both clinical findings and higher order imaging in the form of MRI. We present a rare case of exercise-associated cervical interspinous bursitis in a pediatric patient.

title: Association between clinical phenotypes and autoantibody profiles in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: a Tunisian cohort study.
authors: Chatti AB, Naceur I, Jridi M, Achour TB, Ghorbel IB, Said F, Smiti M.
abstract: Introduction/objectives Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are heterogeneous disorders characterized by variable muscular and extramuscular involvement. Myositis-specific autoantibodies (MSAs) have emerged as key tools for defining more homogeneous clinical subsets. This study aimed to investigate clinical-serological associations in a Tunisian cohort of patients with IIMs. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-center study including adult patients with MSA-positive IIMs fulfilling the 2017 ACR/EULAR classification criteria and/or anti-synthetase syndrome (ASyS) criteria. Clinical, biological, electromyographic, and histological data were analyzed according to serological subgroups: ASyS, dermatomyositis (DM)-specific antibodies, and anti-SRP immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM). Results Fifty patients were included (mean age 50.5 ± 12.9 years; 70% female). The most frequent subgroup was ASyS (n = 33), followed by DM (n = 10) and IMNM (n = 7). Interstitial lung disease (ILD) was most frequent in ASyS (85%), particularly associated with non-Jo-1 antibodies, while muscular involvement was less prominent compared to other groups. DM-specific antibodies were associated with a typical cutaneous phenotype, including heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, and skin ulcerations, as well as higher frequency of dysphagia. Anti-SRP IMNM was characterized by severe and predominant muscle involvement, frequent dysphagia, and minimal extramuscular manifestations. No statistically significant difference in cancer prevalence was observed between groups, although a numerically higher frequency was noted in DM-associated antibodies. Conclusion This Tunisian study highlights the clinical heterogeneity of IIMs and the close relationship between MSA profiles and clinical phenotypes. Although ASyS, DM-associated myositis, and anti-SRP IMNM displayed distinct clinical patterns, substantial phenotypic overlap was observed, particularly between ASyS and anti-MDA5-positive DM. These findings underscore the value of an integrated clinico-serological approach to IIM classification.

title: Arthroscopic Fixation of Ulnar Coronoid Process Fracture With Suture and Button Stabilization.
authors: Jiang Z, Wei K, Li J, Ma Y, Jiang G, Chen B, Cui Z.
abstract: Ulnar coronoid fractures often cause elbow instability, whereas conservative treatment risks stiffness. Traditional open surgical approaches are frequently associated with challenges such as inadequate exposure, risks of neurovascular injury, and heterotopic ossification. Although arthroscopic transosseous fixation offers a less invasive alternative, it may still cause fragment comminution, particularly when the bone fragments are small. This technical note describes an arthroscopic fixation technique using the capsular-fragment continuity. The procedure involves placing high-strength sutures through the anterior capsule. A bony tunnel terminating at the fracture bed (without traversing the free fragment) is then created in the ulnar shaft using a posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction guide. A suture passer is advanced from the tunnel's posterior exit, through the capsular-fragment continuity, to retrieve the high-strength sutures, which are secured over an Endobutton plate for fixation. This technique provides a safe, effective, and minimally invasive option for coronoid fractures, especially with elbow instability.

title: Arthroscopic 3-Point Suture-Bridge Fixation for Posterior Cruciate Ligament Tibial Avulsion Fractures via Triple Bone Tunnels.
authors: Yao W, Liu P, Li Z, Xin X, Li Y, Jia H, Liu Z.
abstract: Posterior cruciate ligament tibial avulsion fractures are a distinct clinical entity. Although the optimal fixation strategy for these fractures remains debated, arthroscopic fixation emerges as a preferred surgical approach owing to its minimally invasive nature, superior intra-articular visualization, and effectiveness in restoring ligamentous tension and joint stability. In this technical note, we use a 3-point fixation technique involving 3 small-diameter tibial bone tunnels for the management of a posterior cruciate ligament tibial avulsion fracture. This approach facilitates precise fracture reduction and significantly enhances postoperative knee joint stability.

title: Anatomical Conoid Ligament Reconstruction Improves Posterior Stability in Neer Type IIB Distal Clavicle Fractures: A Cadaveric Biomechanical Study.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Kurata S, Inoue K, Tsujimura K, Imanaka A, Kawamura K, Sinthubua A, Mahakkanukrauh P.
abstract: Hypothesis This biomechanical study aimed to compare suture button tape (SBT) fixation techniques using different clavicular drill-hole positions in a Neer type IIB distal clavicle fracture (DCF) model. We hypothesized that anatomical conoid ligament reconstruction would provide greater posterior stability than that provided by anterior reconstruction without compromising superior stability. Methods A Neer type IIB DCF model was created using 12 fresh-frozen cadaver shoulders and tested using the following three groups: conoid group (intact conoid ligament); anatomical group (drill hole placed at the posterior aspect of the clavicle over the conoid tubercle); and anterior group (drill hole placed at the anterior one-third of the clavicular width). Reduction accuracy was assessed by measuring displacement rates (superior, anteroposterior, and combined) at the reduced positions. Mechanical stability was evaluated by applying 70-N superior and posterior loads to the proximal clavicle and measuring displacement relative to the reduced position. A statistical analysis using Friedman tests was performed; if the results were significant, then pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were subsequently performed. Bonferroni correction was applied across all 21 pairwise comparisons. An adjusted P Results No significant pairwise differences in reduction accuracy were detected after Bonferroni correction. Under superior loading, the median displacement rates were 33.2%, 4.2%, and 12.6% in the conoid, anatomical, and anterior groups, respectively. The displacement rate in the anatomical group was lower than that in the conoid group (adjusted P = .021). No significant difference between the two reconstruction groups was detected. Under posterior loading, median displacement rates were 48.1%, 16.5%, and 23.7% in the conoid, anatomical, and anterior groups, respectively. The displacement rate in the anatomical group was lower than that in the conoid and anterior groups (adjusted P = .010 and .031, respectively). The mean within-specimen difference in posterior displacement between the anterior and anatomical groups was 1.8 mm (95% confidence interval, 0.6-2.9 mm). Conclusion Anatomical reconstruction using SBT provided greater resistance to posterior displacement than that provided by anterior reconstruction, with a mean within-specimen reduction in posterior displacement of 1.8 mm under a 70-N posterior load.
