No statistically significant difference in superior displacement was detected between the two reconstruction groups. The clinical relevance of the observed posterior displacement difference has not yet been established. Level of evidence Basic Science Study, Biomechanics.

title: All-Arthroscopic Muscle Advancement Technique for Repair of Massive Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears in the Lateral Decubitus Position.
authors: Nakazawa K, Manaka T, Hirakawa Y, Ito Y, Nishiura R, Mori S, Terai H.
abstract: Massive posterosuperior rotator cuff tears remain challenging because of the high retear rate after arthroscopic repair. Muscle advancement has been reported as an effective technique for reducing repair tension and improving healing in severely retracted supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons. Although all-arthroscopic muscle advancement has recently been reported, previously described techniques were performed in the beach-chair position. We describe an all-arthroscopic muscle advancement technique in the lateral decubitus position. This technical note describes the indications, technique, and technical aspects of this procedure. Indications include massive posterosuperior rotator cuff tears in which the supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons cannot be reduced to the greater tuberosity with conventional release alone, particularly in patients without severe fatty degeneration. The procedure is performed in the lateral decubitus position using a traction device and a 30° arthroscope. Stepwise release of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus from the scapula is performed arthroscopically, followed by rotator cuff repair after sufficient advancement to the greater tuberosity is confirmed. This technique may allow anatomic reduction and low-tension repair even in difficult-to-repair tears. The lateral decubitus position may provide a wider working space and improved visualization around the scapula; however, advanced arthroscopic skills and careful attention to the suprascapular nerve are required.

title: ASO Visual Abstract: Long-term Survival After CRS-HIPEC for Colorectal Cancer Peritoneal Metastases.
authors: van Kesteren LJ, Aalbers AGJ, Chakroun A, van der Snee L, Hompes R, Lameris W, Bolhuis K, Grotenhuis BA, van Dieren S, Buffart TE, Kok NFM, Tuynman JB.

title: A Case of Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Complicated With Compartment Syndrome Treated by Hyperbaric Oxygen.
authors: Wang H, Yao F, Zhang L, Sun Q.
abstract: In severe carbon monoxide poisoning complicated by compartment syndrome, prompt fasciotomy combined with hyperbaric oxygen and multidisciplinary supportive care was associated with full neurological recovery and limb salvage. Brain MRI abnormalities did not parallel the favorable clinical course in this patient.

title: Whole-Body Imaging Reveals Characteristic Muscle Involvement Patterns in VCP Myopathy.
authors: Yoshioka W, Noguchi S, Shimazaki R, Eguchi K, Hayashi S, Nishino I.
abstract: Introduction/aims Valosin-containing protein (VCP) myopathy is a rare multisystem disorder with variable clinical onset and progression. While region-focused imaging studies have provided partial information on muscle involvement, how involvement is distributed across body regions and whether this pattern is characteristic remain unclear. We aimed to characterize disease-specific spatial patterns of muscle involvement. Methods Twelve patients from eleven unrelated families with genetically confirmed VCP myopathy underwent CT or T1-weighted MRI. Fat replacement in 43 muscles across shoulder, trunk, pelvis, and lower limbs was graded using the modified Mercuri score (mMS). Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) dimensionality reduction and hierarchical clustering analyses identified characteristic patterns. Clinical correlations were assessed. Results UMAP visualization of 43 muscles showed that VCP myopathy cases tended to occupy a relatively distinct region compared with other myopathies. Hierarchical clustering identified Mild (n = 9) and Severe (n = 3) groups, which differed significantly in total mMS (p = 0.009). Both groups showed fatty replacement in trunk muscles (including iliocostalis lumborum, longissimus, and external abdominal oblique) and adductor magnus, with relative sparing of sternocleidomastoid, infraspinatus, subscapularis, trapezius, rhomboid, and rectus femoris. Substantial asymmetry occurred only when both sides were affected. Total mMS showed no correlation with age at imaging or disease duration. Discussion This study demonstrates that VCP myopathy exhibits a characteristic pattern of muscle involvement on whole-body multi-region assessment. Although clinical heterogeneity was observed, consistently affected trunk muscles and adductor magnus, which may be involved early after symptom onset, may provide supportive imaging clues when VCP myopathy is suspected.

title: Weekly dynamics, subtype replacement and regional heterogeneity of influenza activity in China, 2024-2026: A national sentinel surveillance analysis.
authors: Wang S, Xia Z, Shi B, Chen M, Shu X, Peng P.
abstract: Objective National influenza surveillance in China is reported weekly, but recent post-pandemic patterns integrating regional timing, subtype/lineage replacement and outbreak activity have not been quantitatively characterized in a continuous national series. We aimed to reconstruct and quantify weekly influenza dynamics in China from 2024/W01 to 2026/W21. Methods We performed a retrospective secondary time-series analysis of 125 publicly available, aggregate weekly reports from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Chinese National Influenza Center. Values were reconciled against official reports when working datasets differed or quality-control checks identified inconsistencies. Positivity was recalculated from positive and tested specimens. Regional differences were evaluated across paired weeks using heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent Newey-West standard errors and exploratory lead-lag relationships were assessed using cross-correlation of first-differenced weekly series. Results Nationally, 1,796,636 influenza-like illness specimens were tested and 253,219 were influenza-positive (weighted positivity, 14.1%); national positivity peaked in 2025/W49 at 49.8%. Overall weighted positivity was 14.6% in Southern China and 13.3% in Northern China. Across 125 paired weeks, Southern China had a mean positivity 4.41 percentage points higher than Northern China (95% CI, 2.23-6.59; P Conclusions Recent influenza activity in China was multi-wave and regionally heterogeneous, with measurable north-south temporal differences, sequential subtype replacement and a large A(H3N2)-associated outbreak surge. The analysis also demonstrates the importance of explicit source-level quality control when reusing aggregated public surveillance reports.

title: WELL-BEING IN EMOTIONALLY DEMANDING WORK CONTEXTS: THE ROLE OF RELATIONSHIPS WITH RESIDENTS FOR CAREGIVERS IN LONG-TERM HEALTHCARE.
journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
authors: Della Torre E, Giangreco A, Maes J, Sebastiano A.
abstract: Objective This study examines how relationships with residents mediate the impact of job resources (autonomy, organizational support) and job demands (workload) on caregivers' well-being in long-term healthcare (LTC), using the Job Demands-Resources and Conservation of Resources theories. Methods Repeated cross-sectional survey data from 1316 caregivers in 13 LTC facilities located in northern Italy are analysed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling. Results Relationships with residents partially mediate the link between job characteristics and caregivers' well-being, while the hypothesized interactions between workload and job resources in predicting relationship quality were not statistically significant. Conclusions Relationships with residents are crucial for caregivers' well-being in LTC, a sector suffering from skills shortage and societal issues in caring for fragile citizens. Managerial implications and generalization for other emotionally demanding sectors are debated.

title: Utilization of a Lifestyle Medicine Program for Presurgical Health Optimization: Impact on Early Postoperative Outcomes of Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
authors: Prather H, Leupold O, Carli A, Gonzalez Della Valle A, Cushner F, Cheng J.
abstract: Background Chronic systemic inflammation is associated with osteoarthritis and chronic diseases that increase surgical risk before total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA). This study compares early postoperative outcomes between patients who did and did not complete an intensive lifestyle medicine (LSM) program to reduce chronic systemic inflammation. Methods Anthropometric variables, lifestyle measures, patient-reported outcome measures, and postoperative 90-day outcomes (ie, length of stay, infection, persistent pain, opioids) were obtained from an LSM repository. Comparisons were made between patients who completed the intensive LSM track (multiple visits, interprofessional providers) and those who declined behavior change preoperatively (selective track: single provider visit). A subanalysis evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) medication users. Results Among 292 patients (72% women; 62 ± 9 years; 76% White), 154 completed the intensive track and 138 participated in the selective track. Most (91%) had ≥2 chronic diseases. Baseline characteristics were similar between tracks, except for higher anxiety/depression scores in the intensive track (3.3 ± 3.0 vs 1.8 ± 2.4[ P P P = .001]), with no differences in other outcomes. Conclusions Postoperative persistent pain rates were significantly lower in patients who completed an intensive LSM program before THA or TKA, compared to patients who did not engage in health improvement. GLP-1RA users showed no health benefits and required more opioid refills.

title: Upper airway morphometry in acute neck infections: Clinical associations and deep learning-based segmentation.
authors: Viertonen V, Sirén A, Widell A, Vierula JP, Happonen T, Nyman M, Nurminen J, Huhtanen H, Hirvonen J.
abstract: Objectives Upper airway (UA) compromise is a significant and potentially life-threatening complication of acute neck infection (ANI), but objective, quantitative imaging features are lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the association between UA morphometry in emergency neck MRI and disease severity in ANI, and to develop and evaluate a deep learning (DL)-based model for automatic UA segmentation in ANI patients. Materials and methods A total of 322 patients were included. UA lumen was manually segmented, and prespecified morphometric features were extracted. UA morphometry was correlated with clinical outcomes. Interobserver agreement for all extracted features was evaluated with the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). An nnU-Net model was trained on manually segmented data, and its performance was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and feature-specific ICCs. Results ICU admission occurred in 33/322 patients (10.2 %) and prolonged stay (>5 days) in 47/319 (14.7 %). Minimum cross-sectional area, compactness, maximum midline shift, and length of airway narrowing were associated with ICU admission (false-discovery-rate q ≤ 0.008) but not with prolonged stay, and did not significantly improve an established clinical model (AUC 0.80 to 0.84, DeLong p = 0.07 to 0.12). Interobserver agreement was moderate-to-excellent. The nnU-Net reached a median DSC of 0.920 with ICCs of 0.853 to 0.973 and reproduced the ICU associations. Conclusion Quantitative UA morphometry in ANI is reproducible. A narrow caliber, a long narrowed segment, and lateral displacement of the airway are associated with ICU admission, without demonstrated incremental value over established predictors in the prespecified comparison. nnU-Net segmentation reproduces the features and their univariable associations.

title: Triggers of Gout Flares from Local to Systemic Perspectives.
authors: Straton AR, Crisan TO, Joosten LAB.
abstract: Gout is the most common type of inflammatory arthritis, caused by MSU crystal deposition in the joint, resulting from chronic hyperuricemia. Typically, the first clinical presentation is a gout flare characterized by severe pain, redness, joint swelling, and limited mobility. Despite continuous exposure to increased serum urate concentration followed by MSU crystal formation, flares are unpredictable and intermittent when poorly managed. Acute gout flares follow a two-step model: firstly, MSU crystals build up and, secondly, an endogenous or exogenous triggering event is needed. Once both triggers are given, resident macrophages initiate an acute inflammatory response. However, these additional factors are still under debate and increased serum urate concentrations alone are insufficient to ignite gout flares. In this review, we aim to sharpen our understanding of the unique characteristics responsible for transitioning from an asymptomatic state to acute joint inflammation observed in gout patients. We focus on integrating joint mechanisms during a gout flare, such as NLRP3 inflammasome activation, macrophage heterogeneity changes, and local physicochemical conditions with systemic influences from immunometabolism and genetic variation to explain the interindividual variability in flare susceptibility.

title: Trends in psychotropic drug use in nursing home residents with dementia and their association with regulatory changes: A routine care data analysis from 2016 to 2023.
authors: Albers CAW, Wouters F, de Bruijne MC, Smalbrugge M, Joling KJ.
abstract: Introduction Non-pharmacological interventions are the first-choice treatment for managing neuropsychiatric symptoms in nursing home (NH) residents with dementia, yet psychotropic drugs (PDs) are frequently prescribed despite their limited effectiveness. In the current century, policies in various countries have increasingly emphasized the need for restraint in prescribing PDs, partly through amendments to guidelines and legislation. In the Netherlands, regulatory changes included the 2018 revision of the guideline for challenging behavior, the introduction of the Care and Coercion Act (CCA), and a new Dementia Care Standard in 2020. This study examined the prevalence of PD prescriptions (PDPs) from 2016 to 2023 among residents with dementia in Dutch NHs, and the course of the PDP trend in the context of regulatory changes, using routine care data. Methods We analyzed routine care data from 11 NH organizations. Quarterly point prevalences were calculated for any PDP and five PD categories separately (antipsychotics, anxiolytics, hypnotics, antidepressants, anti-dementia drugs). We calculated confidence intervals to indicate temporal changes in PDP prevalence and assess the relationship with different reforms. We used interrupted time series (ITS) analysis to explore the association between regulatory changes and the PDP trend. Results Data from 17,738 residents showed an overall decline in PDP prevalence from 48.3% in 2016 to 42.7% in 2023. Antidepressants and antipsychotics were the most frequently prescribed PDs. Antidepressants showed the largest absolute prevalence decline over time. Anti-dementia drugs showed the greatest relative decline. ITS showed a steeper declining trend after the combined introduction of the CCA and Dementia Care Standard in the second quarter of 2020, compared with the period after the guideline revision in 2018. Discussion The PDP rate decreased over time but was still substantial. Regulatory changes, including new legislation and (clinical) guidelines, appear to have contributed to a further decline from Q2 2020 onwards. This decline suggests that policy and guideline interventions may meaningfully influence prescribing behavior, offering a promising lever for reducing potentially inappropriate psychotropic use in dementia care. Insight into the appropriateness of prescribing practices is essential to identify areas for further improvement.

title: Transformer-aided guard: A hybrid spatio-temporal framework for confidence-aware intrusion detection in cyber-physical systems.
authors: Aljohani A.
abstract: In this age of ubiquitous networks, Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) have evolved into an essentail part of critical infrastructures like smart grids and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. The interconnectedness of cyber and physical components, however, makes CPSs more vulnerability to sophisticated and stealthy cyber intrusions which are typically untraceable by conventional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). Even though Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are adopted with the aim of strengthening the performance of IDS, there are several challenges noted with available models including limited accuracy. Also, their capacity to capture the dynamic and structured dependencies within CPS environments is insufficient. Within the background, the present study proposes the Transformer-Aided Guard (TAG) approach. This is a novel hybrid spatio-temporal framework, designed for confidence-aware and precise intrusion detection. Through the Swin Transformer and spatial relationship learning using a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (STGNN), the network leverages temporal sequence modelling. Spatial and temporal embeddings are integrated by a dual-stage infusion mechanism, making it possible to attain more complex learning. Furthermore, a post-hoc Bayesian inference layer based on Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) is incorporated to measure prediction uncertainty and enhance decision reliability. Extensive evaluations performed on the benchmark datasets revealed effectiveness of the framework as a promising average accuracy of 98% is achieved. Applicability of the framework is also validated through its detection latency across diverse CPS environments, whereas the ablation study conducted validate the contribution of each architectural component. The findings testify TAG as a secure, scalable, and reliable intrusion detection framework for the next-generation CPS applications.

title: The prevalence of mental health service use after long-term minor-to-moderate motor vehicle crash injury: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Yu S, Griffiths D, Armfield N, Gray S, Di Donato M, Collie A.
abstract: Background Minor to moderate motor vehicle crash (MVC) injuries can lead to persistent psychological distress, yet evidence regarding mental health service (MHS) use is limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and characterise the determinants of MHS use after minor to moderate MVC injury. Methods This retrospective cohort study examined Australians with work-related, MVC injuries and workers' compensation claims exceeding 24 months duration. Claims and services data were linked with healthcare records to capture MHS use before and after injury. The injured group was divided into severity sub-groups based on hospital admission status (hospitalised, non-hospitalised). A community comparator group was matched to the non-hospitalised group based on gender and injury year. The primary outcome was MHS period prevalence within 24 months. Determinants of MHS were identified through binomial logistic regression. Results There were 574 non-hospitalised, 293 hospitalised, and 8294 community comparators included in the study cohort. The prevalence of MHS use at 24 months post injury was highest for the hospitalised group (36.9%), followed by the non-hospitalised group (31.5%) and community comparators (13.5%). The non-hospitalised group had 3.14 times greater odds (95% CI 2.53, 3.88) of MHS use compared to community comparators, and had the highest prevalence of publicly-funded MHS (18.8%). Hospitalised participants (28.3%) had a higher prevalence of workers' compensation funded MHS compared to non-hospitalised participants (19.3%). The adjusted odds of MHS use were higher among females (OR 2.05 [1.42, 2.97]), and people who had used MHS in the 12 months prior to injury (OR 4.66 [2.41, 9.50]). Conclusion People with non-hospitalised MVC injuries had a significantly higher prevalence of MHS use compared with their matched community comparator group, and people with hospitalised MVC injuries had the highest prevalence at 24 months-follow up. The highest proportion of people assessing publicly funded MHS was by people in the non-hospitalised group. These findings highlight the ongoing mental health needs of people with minor to moderate MVC injury. Monitoring for the early post injury psychological signs and symptoms, and timely referral to MHS, could reduce psychological burden following MVC injury.

title: The moderator effect of the family business protocol on the financial performance of born globals firms: A trajectories analysis.
authors: Escandon-Barbosa D, Salas-Paramo J.
abstract: Born global firms (BGFs) face unique challenges in achieving financial stability due to their rapid internationalization and resource constraints. While family-owned BGFs may benefit from long-term orientation and family firm protocol structures, the impact of a family business protocol (FBP) on their firm's performance remains underexplored. This study investigates the triple moderating effect of FBP on the firm performance trajectories of BGFs, considering how market uncertainty, formal family firm protocol mechanisms shape strategic decision making (Absorptive capacity) and firm performance over time. With a longitudinal approach, we analyze a dataset of family owned BGFs across multiple industries, applying trajectory analysis to assess variations in performance under different family firm protocol structures. Our findings suggest that the presence of an FBP improve financial resilience through reducing decision making conflicts and at the same time increasing strategic consistency, particularly in firms operating in volatile environment in international markets. However, excessive formalization may also impose rigidity, potentially limiting adaptability in highly dynamic environments. In this way this study contributes to the literature on international entrepreneurship and family business by offering new insights into the role of formal family firm protocols in shaping the financial trajectories of BGFs. The findings offer valuable implications for family business owners, policymakers, and scholars seeking to optimize family firm governance structures for sustained financial growth in globally oriented firms.

title: The effect of three dimensional-printed guides on assisting rotational axis localization of hinged external fixator in the surgery for elbow terrible triad injury.
authors: Chen H, Zhao T, Gao H, Ma P.
abstract: Purpose This study evaluated the effect of 3D-printed guides on rotation-axis localization for hinged external fixation in terrible triad (TT) injury of the elbow. Methods We enrolled 55 patients with TT injuries treated with a hinged external fixator between January 2017 and January 2025, divided into a guide group (n = 29) and a freehand group (n = 26) according to the method of rotation-axis localization, with follow-up at six weeks and one year postoperatively. Pin insertion time, number of fluoroscopic exposures, elbow range of motion, functional elbow rate, Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), type and incidence of complications, and number and causes of reoperations were compared between groups. Results Compared with the freehand group, the guide group had a shorter mean pin insertion time (300.93 ± 21.97 s vs. 1392.5 ± 218.16 s) and fewer fluoroscopic exposures (2.31 ± 0.54 vs. 17.50 ± 2.93; both P 0.05). At the final follow-up, flexion-extension arc (134.36° ± 18.21° vs. 125.75° ± 26.44°), rotation arc (165.71° ± 20.34° vs. 157.04° ± 26.84°), MEPS (97.86 ± 7.26 vs. 95.21 ± 11.28), functional elbow rate (93% vs. 79%), and complication rate (11% vs. 21%) remained similar, without significant differences (P > 0.05). During follow-up, one patient in the guide group required reoperation for heterotopic ossification, whereas three patients in the freehand group required reoperation for heterotopic ossification or fixator loosening. Conclusion Compared with freehand localization of the rotation axis, guide-assisted localization reduced pin insertion time, fluoroscopic exposures, and pin adjustments. Furthermore, the guide group demonstrated non-inferiority in surgical outcomes compared to the freehand group.

title: The (Micro)surgeon's creed: Lion's heart, eagle's eye, lady's hand.
authors: Tang C.

title: Technological adoption and innovation in OECD and BRICS countries: A two‑way fixed effects difference‑in‑differences analysis.
authors: Addis AK, Chen L, Addis HK.
abstract: Understanding how technological progress unfolds across advanced and emerging economies remains central to both innovation research and development policy. This study compares the trajectories of technological adoption and innovation in OECD and BRICS countries using a two-way fixed effects difference-in-differences (DID) framework over the period 1995-2023. The analysis focuses on three core indicators: mobile cellular subscriptions, internet usage, and patent applications, and is supported by an extensive set of diagnostic checks, including partial R² contributions, residual normality and heteroskedasticity tests, and Ramsey RESET tests. Despite historically higher levels of connectivity and innovation in OECD countries, the estimated results indicate a relative slowdown in growth rates for mobile subscriptions, internet adoption, and patenting activity, with negative and statistically significant coefficients across specifications with and without control variables. On the other hand, BRICS countries show steady progress in all three outcomes, often rapid, catch‑up. These findings challenge conventional assumptions about the persistence of technological leadership in advanced economies and suggest that emerging economies are increasingly shaping global patterns of technology adoption and innovation. The results emphasize the necessity of policy frameworks that recognize heterogeneous pathways of technological progress and support both diffusion and innovation in a changing global economic landscape.

title: Synthetic CT from biplanar radiographs for patellofemoral anatomical assessment: development and validation of an adapted X2CT-GAN model.
authors: Lu Q, Pan R, Qian J, Fang F, Hu H.
abstract: Objectives Accurate assessment of osseous morphology is essential for the diagnosis and surgical management of patellofemoral instability. Methods capable of providing CT-like anatomical information while reducing radiation exposure are therefore of considerable clinical interest. This study aimed to validate the accuracy of radiography-derived synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated by a deep learning model for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability. Methods A total of 210 paired radiographs and CT scans were retrospectively collected and randomly divided into a training set (n = 170) and a validation set (n = 40). A deep learning model based on the X2CT-GAN framework was used to reconstruct sCT volumes from anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. Two blinded readers independently measured tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance, trochlear sulcus angle, and Caton-Deschamps index on both sCT and real CT images. Reliability, inter-modality agreement, and threshold-based classification agreement were evaluated. Results All intra- and inter-observer reliability values were excellent. Inter-modality agreement was excellent for TT-TG distance and good for trochlear sulcus angle. Agreement for patellar height was good. The mean absolute error for TT-TG distance ranged from 1.24 to 1.38 mm. Agreement for threshold-based classifications ranged from substantial to almost perfect, with high specificity observed across all evaluated cutoff values. Conclusions Radiography-derived sCT demonstrated good agreement with real CT for both quantitative measurements and threshold-based classifications relevant to clinical decision-making in patellofemoral instability. These findings suggest that radiography-derived synthetic CT may represent a promising lower-radiation alternative for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability in selected clinical scenarios.

title: Statistical Parametric Mapping reveals sex-specific, phase-dependent differences in bilateral three-dimensional ground reaction force during Wushu Changbing PiJi in high-level athletes.
authors: Feng J, Ma L, Shen Y, Wang S, Qiu Y, Zheng P.
abstract: PiJi is a core attacking technique in Wushu Changbing competition, but continuous waveform evidence remains limited regarding the sex-specific phase characteristics of bilateral 3D ground reaction force (GRF) during PiJi performed with maximal voluntary effort (MVE). This study aimed to compare continuous changes in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral GRF between high-level male and female athletes during PiJi performed with MVE. In this cross-sectional, laboratory-based observational study, 44 right-hand-dominant athletes, including 22 male athletes and 22 female athletes, performed PiJi with MVE, yielding 616 valid trials. Bilateral 3D GRF was recorded using two force plates. Each trial was time-normalized and linearly interpolated to 143 equally spaced nodes, and within-participant mean waveforms were calculated before between-group differences were analyzed using statistical parametric mapping. Primary analyses used random-field-theory inference, with sensitivity examined using 5,000 permutation tests. After Bonferroni correction, phase-specific sex differences were detected in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral 3D GRF. Scalar localization showed that male athletes had higher trailing-foot Fy during the middle phase (33.98%-47.04%) and higher trailing-foot Fx (62.41%-71.99%) and net bilateral Fx (54.18%-70.41%) during the middle-to-late phase; female athletes showed only a brief period of higher trailing-foot vertical Fz during the middle phase (42.11%-44.61%). Although lead-foot 3D GRF differed overall, no confirmatory difference was localized to any single scalar component. These findings indicate that sex-related GRF differences in high-level PiJi were concentrated mainly in specific horizontal-plane phases of trailing-foot and net bilateral force, whereas the lead-foot difference was identified only at the overall 3D GRF level. These results provide kinetic evidence for phase-specific assessment of PiJi technique and suggest that training monitoring and mechanistic research should consider foot, direction, and movement phase rather than relying only on peak force or discrete variables. Future studies integrating multimodal measures and sport-specific performance may further clarify the functional significance of bilateral force-generation patterns.

title: Staged Revision Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty to Functional Hemiarthroplasty With Retained Humeral Implant: A Salvage Technique.
authors: Aguirre T, DeFoor MT, Dickinson NJ, Unger FA, Vidal M, Blankenship M, Provencher MT.
abstract: With the increased incidence and indications for reverse total shoulder arthroplasty, the increased need for revision shoulder arthroplasty also continues to rise. Therefore, revision strategies and techniques are essential to optimize patient outcomes and preserve function, particularly in the challenges of glenoid failure, poor glenoid bone stock, and/or poor native bone quality. Because of the risk of intraoperative fracture, increased blood loss, prolonged operative time, excessive implant costs, and the high risk of complications of a humeral stem extraction and revision, extraction of a well-fixed humeral stem may be unnecessary and undesirable. When feasible, stem retention is preferred, which can lead to reduced surgical morbidity, cost-saving practice habits, and better patient outcomes, especially in systems lacking platform convertibility. This Technical Note expands the reconstructive salvage options in systems lacking platform convertibility through conversion of a reverse total shoulder arthroplasty to a functional hemiarthroplasty by cementing a glenosphere onto a retained, nonconvertible, stemmed humeral tray. This technique may serve as a definitive solution or, more likely, a temporary construct in select salvage and revision cases, offering joint stability and pain control while preserving articular congruency and avoiding the morbidity associated with full-component revision.

title: Significant Differences in the Presentation, Diagnosis, and Management of Juvenile Osteochondritis Dissecans Exist Among Asia-Pacific and European Surgeons.
authors: Hui SJ, Liew JJL, Chew KY, Loke RWK, Hui JHP, Malhotra R.
abstract: Purpose To compare diagnostic and treatment preferences for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans between Asia-Pacific and European surgeons. Methods Between January 2024 and July 2024, an electronic survey was distributed to orthopaedic surgeons affiliated with Pediatric Research in Sports Medicine Asia-Pacific (n = 54 invited). Responses were compared with data from the 2023 European Society of Sports Traumatology, Knee Surgery and Arthroscopy survey. Domains included clinical presentation, imaging preferences, nonoperative strategies, operative techniques, and follow-up protocols. Proportions were compared using χ 2 or Fisher's exact tests ( P Results Fifty-four surgeons (100%) responded to our survey. A total of 104 surgeons were analyzed (54 Asia-Pacific, 50 Europe). Trauma was more frequently cited as a presenting factor in Asia-Pacific (knee: 100% vs 17%; ankle: 100% vs 21%; P P P P P P P P = .002), whereas Asia-Pacific surgeons favored osteochondral autograft (68% vs 33%; P = .001) and antegrade drilling (84% vs 48%; P Conclusions Significant regional differences exist between Asia-Pacific and European surgeons in the presentation, diagnostic evaluation, and management strategies for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans. Clinical relevance Marked regional variation exits in the diagnostic and therapeutic management of juvenile osteochondritis dissecans. These differences influence imaging selection, operative thresholds, and surgical technique choice. Understanding such variability is essential for developing international consensus guidelines and ensuring consistent, evidence-based care across various health care systems.

title: SEQuential tUnneled Catheters and Infective Events in haemodiaLysis: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study (SEQUEL Study).
authors: Bay SS, Pon SX, See XY, Yew SY, Liyana Abdullah E, Poon KV, Thye CK, Cheng SF, Lee YW, Jalalonmuhali M, Wan Md Adnan WAH, Gan CC.
abstract: Background Tunnelled-cuffed catheters (TCCs) are widely used for haemodialysis access when permanent vascular access is unavailable. Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear. This study evaluated these two competing determinants of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI). Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included all TCC insertions at a tertiary nephrology unit between January 2016 and December 2021. The primary analysis examined CRBSI incidence per 1000 catheter-days stratified by catheter sequence number (first, second, third+ insertion per patient). Secondary analyses compared femoral versus internal jugular TCCs overall and within sequence strata. A registry-index cohort (patients with no documented prior TCC before January 2016, n = 135) was used to reduce, though not eliminate, sequence-related confounding in the site comparison; given only 24 CRBSI events, this analysis is exploratory and a clinically meaningful site difference cannot be excluded. Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank testing were used for time-to-event outcomes. A cluster-robust marginal Cox model was used to account for repeated catheter insertions within patients, adjusting for sequence number, insertion site, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter. Results Among 626 TCC insertions in 339 patients (389 FV, 237 IJV), contributing 98,727 catheter-days, CRBSI incidence escalated with catheter sequence: 1.17 per 1000 catheter-days for first insertions, rising to 1.98 for second and 2.49 for third-or-more insertions. Notably, by the second insertion, CRBSI rates were similar between FV and IJV access (31.7% each). In the index cohort (n = 135; FV = 95, IJV = 40), CRBSI-free survival did not differ significantly between sites (log-rank p = 0.340), nor did catheter survival (p = 0.950) or patient survival (p = 0.487). In the all-TCC cohort, after adjustment for catheter sequence number, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter using a cluster-robust marginal Cox model, femoral access remained associated with a higher, though attenuated, CRBSI hazard after adjustment for the measured covariates (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02-2.01; p = 0.039), indicating a modest residual site hazard beyond the sequence effect. Conclusions Repeated catheterization was independently associated with increasing CRBSI risk, and catheter sequence number was the strongest predictor in the fully adjusted model. The femoral site effect was substantially attenuated after adjustment for sequence and was not statistically significant in the registry-index cohort analysis, though the wide confidence intervals preclude an equivalence interpretation. IJV access remains preferred; when IJV is unavailable, femoral TCC placement may be an acceptable alternative from an infection-risk perspective, but this must be weighed against thrombotic and limb complications, including deep vein thrombosis, which were not systematically ascertained in this study. Residual confounding cannot be excluded in this single-center retrospective study.

title: Rotator Cuff Repair with Concomitant Biceps Tenodesis is Cost-Effective at Mid-Term Follow-up: A Systematic Review and Cost-Effective Analysis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Berreta RS, Badin D, Koyejo LD, Chan D, Ashkar A, Siragusa J, Harris E, Fox H, Jain A, Srikumaran U.
abstract: Background There is limited evidence describing the cost-effectiveness of isolated rotator cuff repair (RCR) compared to rotator cuff repair with biceps tenodesis (BT) in the treatment of primary rotator cuff tears at mid-term follow-up. Purpose (1) To perform a cost utility analysis comparing RCR to RCR with BT in patients with rotator cuff tears over a 5-year time horizon. Methods A decision tree economic model was constructed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of RCR vs RCR with BT across a 5-year time horizon. Model transition probabilities, costs, and health utility measures, based on EQ-5D (European Quality of Life-5 Dimension) scores, were derived from the literature. Health utility was measured in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) and cost-effectiveness was based on the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) considering a willingness to pay (WTP) threshold of $50,000/QALY. Monte Carlo probabilistic and one-way sensitivity analysis was performed to assess for parameter uncertainty. Each cycle length was defined as 1 year, and 5-year costs and utilities were calculated with 3% annual discounting. Results Over a 5-year horizon, RCR with BT yielded 3.713 QALYs at a mean cost of $34,182 compared to 3.651 QALYs and $33,372 for RCR alone. RCR with BT was found to be cost-effective with an ICER of $13,064/QALY and a positive net monetary benefit of $2,289. RCR with BT was the preferred treatment in 88.51% of 1,000 simulations on probabilistic sensitivity analysis. One-way sensitivity analyses demonstrated cost-effectiveness for performing RCR with BT was maintained with tenodesis implant costs up to $3,048, revision rates up to 6.7%, and additional operative time up to 53.7 minutes. Conclusion Despite higher upfront costs, performing biceps tenodesis at the time of index rotator cuff repair provides greater quality-adjusted life years and is cost-effective compared to isolated rotator cuff repair at mid-term follow-up. Level of evidence Level III, Economic Study.

title: Robotic navigation-assisted versus conventional freehand placement of the infra-acetabular screw in acetabular fracture surgery: A retrospective comparative study.
authors: Cao W, Chen Z, Liu H, Zhan N, He J, Qi L, Li J, Zheng Y, Tang J, Li M, Chen H.
abstract: Background The infra-acetabular screw (IAS) is an important component of fixation constructs for complex acetabular fractures, but accurate freehand placement is technically demanding, and evidence on robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement remains limited. This study compared robotic navigation-assisted (RA) and conventional fluoroscopic freehand (CF) IAS placement in acetabular fracture surgery. Methods In this retrospective study, 53 patients with acetabular fractures who underwent IAS fixation between June 2022 and July 2024 were included, 28 underwent RA placement using the HoloSight robotic navigation system and 25 underwent CF placement. The primary outcome was screw-placement accuracy, graded on postoperative CT according to the Lonstein criteria. Secondary outcomes included the number of guide-wire adjustments, fluoroscopy frequency, IAS insertion time, total operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture reduction quality, hip function, and complications. Results The grade 0 (no cortical penetration) rate was higher in the RA group than in the CF group (96.4% [27/28] vs. 60.0% [15/25], p = 0.005). RA placement was associated with fewer guide-wire adjustments (0.07 ± 0.26 vs. 3.60 ± 1.15), fewer fluoroscopies (9.32 ± 1.66 vs. 21.28 ± 3.18), shorter IAS insertion time (10.36 ± 2.50 vs. 26.68 ± 4.11 min), shorter total operative time (134.54 ± 15.46 vs. 155.80 ± 18.48 min), and less intraoperative blood loss (468.21 ± 84.68 vs. 588.40 ± 80.76 mL) (all p Conclusions Robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement was associated with significantly higher screw-placement accuracy and greater procedural efficiency than the conventional freehand technique, without compromising fracture reduction quality, hip function, or safety.

title: Relationships between cam morphology and [<sup>18</sup>F]sodium fluoride PET uptake in asymptomatic hips.
authors: Watkins L, Datta S, Goyal A, Vainberg Y, Shalit R, Stevens KJ, Gold GE, Kogan F.
abstract: Objective Bone deformities are linked to femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and increased risk of hip osteoarthritis (OA) but are also common in the general population. The purpose of this study is to examine relationships between FAI-linked morphology and resting bone metabolic activity in asymptomatic hips. Methods This exploratory secondary analysis of hip scans from a [ 18 F]NaF PET-MRI study on knee pain included 76 asymptomatic hips from 41 individuals (53 ± 13 years, body mass index 25.9 ± 5.1 kg/m2, 21 female/20 male). Hips were evaluated for cam, pincer, and additional morphology with the Hip Osteoarthritis MRI Scoring System. Mean and maximum PET standardized uptake values (SUV) were recorded for the femoral head-neck junction, center of the femoral head, and anterolateral acetabulum. The influence of morphology on SUV mean and SUV max was assessed with linear mixed effects models. Results Forty-two hips had isolated cam morphology, two had isolated pincer morphology, and four had mixed-type morphology. Cam morphology or alpha angles were not associated with increased bone metabolic activity. Hips with gluteal tendinitis/trochanteric bursitis had significantly higher SUV max in the center of the femoral head (p = 9.98e-5). No other morphological features were associated with bone metabolic activity, though the low prevalence of features such as pincer morphology limits interpretation of these findings. Conclusion In older asymptomatic hips without OA, no association was detected between cam morphology and elevated resting bone remodeling. Understanding structure-function relationships in asymptomatic hips with cam morphology may help contextualize findings associated with pain in patients with FAI or OA.

title: Psychometric evaluation of the Palliative Nursing Care Quality Scale (PNCQS) among ICU and oncology nurses in Iran.
authors: Shahmari M, Gardashkhani S, Habibpour E, Kamalifar E, Dehghan Nayeri N, Zare M.
abstract: Background Reliable and culturally adapted instruments are essential for assessing the quality of palliative nursing care. The Palliative Nursing Care Quality Scale (PNCQS) had not been psychometrically evaluated in Iran. This study aimed to translate the PNCQS into Persian and examine its validity and reliability among Iranian nurses. Methods In this methodological study, the PNCQS was translated into Persian according to the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. A total of 620 nurses from oncology and intensive care units in teaching hospitals in Tehran, Tabriz, and Ardabil were recruited using a multi stage cluster sampling strategy with convenience sampling at the final stage. Face, content, and construct validity were evaluated. Construct validity was examined by first testing the original one-factor model using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), followed by exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and cross-validation of the derived factor structure using CFA on an independent sample. CFA was conducted in AMOS using maximum likelihood estimation with bootstrapping (1,000 resamples). Reliability was assessed by internal consistency (Cronbach's α) and two-week test-retest reliability using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results The scale showed excellent content validity (S-CVI = 0.99). The initial CFA demonstrated that the original 20-item unidimensional model did not adequately fit the Iranian data. Subsequent EFA identified a four-factor structure-Family-Centered Care, Empathic and Spiritual Care, Hope and Life Review, and Physical Symptom Management-explaining 51.41% of the total variance. This structure was confirmed by CFA in an independent sample (n = 400), demonstrating good model fit (χ²/df = 2.84, CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.95, RMSEA = 0.06). Composite reliability exceeded 0.70 for all factors. Although the AVE for Family-Centered Care was slightly below the recommended threshold (0.42), its composite reliability was acceptable (0.81), and discriminant validity was established for all constructs. Cronbach's α was 0.92 for the total scale (subscales: 0.76-0.83), and the two-week test-retest ICC was 0.76. Conclusion The Persian PNCQS demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and a culturally appropriate four-factor structure for assessing the quality of palliative nursing care among Iranian nurses. It provides a reliable multidimensional instrument for clinical practice, research, and quality improvement initiatives in palliative care.

title: Procyanidin B2 ameliorates osteoporosis by modulating osteoclast precursor differentiation through activation of the PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 axis.
authors: Zou Y, Wang C, Zhang T, Huang Y, Xu H, Ma X, Li L, Lyu F, Zhang F.
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a chronic, systemic skeletal disorder characterized by excessive osteoclast activation and bone resorption, for which effective therapies with minimal adverse effects remain limited. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated during oxidative stress promote osteoclast differentiation and are considered a primary contributor to OP pathogenesis. Procyanidin B2 is a natural flavonoid with potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; however, its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms of action in OP remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of procyanidin B2 on osteoclastogenesis using tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase staining, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, and pit formation assays. Our findings indicate that procyanidin B2 inhibits RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, procyanidin B2 activates the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt) signaling pathway, thereby upregulating nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) expression. This induction of Nrf2 enhances ROS clearance in osteoclast precursors (OCPs), leading to functional modulation of their differentiation trajectory rather than mere suppression of OCP proliferation. Moreover, micro-computed tomography and histological analyses reveal that procyanidin B2 alleviates ovariectomy-induced bone loss in mice and demonstrates favorable in vivo biocompatibility. Collectively, these findings indicate that procyanidin B2 mitigates OP by modulating OCP differentiation throughout activation of the PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 axis and highlight its potential as a novel natural therapeutic agent for the prevention and treatment of OP.

title: Physiological and health-related effects of 5G-relevant radiofrequency fields: A systematic review of experimental studies in humans and mammals.
authors: Bodewein L, Dechent D, Emonds T, Graefrath D, Keller AS, Krabbe J, Morgan L, Scheelhaase PJ, Schmid G, Schneeweiss P, Driessen S.
abstract: The introduction of the latest mobile communications standard of the fifth generation (5G) is accompanied by controversial discussions about potential health risks due to radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review of experimental and epidemiological studies investigating the physiological and health-related effects of 5G-relevant radiofrequency electromagnetic fields in humans and mammals. The review protocol has been registered in PROSPERO (CRD42022374434) and the review conforms to the PRISMA guidelines. The risk of bias and the quality of included studies were assessed using the recommended approach by the Office of Health Assessment and Translation of the National Toxicology Program. A total of 100 experimental animal and seven human controlled studies were included, analyzed, and evaluated. Narrative summaries were performed for a total of 23 topics (e.g., effects on cognition, male fertility, and thermoregulation). However, investigated species and outcomes in studies were very heterogeneous. Additionally, most studies had substantial methodological weaknesses. Only 11 studies showed a low risk of bias. In summary, for most topics, the current scientific data were inadequate to draw any conclusions about the physiological and health-related effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic fields in the investigated frequency range of 3-30 GHz. However, moderate evidence below the limit values was found for cytokine secretion in mice and low evidence was found for structural changes in the hippocampus of rats above the limit values, when taking the exposure limits presently recommended by the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection as the basis. Therefore, we strongly recommend high-quality systematic research. Particular attention should be paid to reasonable hypotheses, experimental studies on effects on the skin, eyes, and temperature increase, exposures to different frequencies and field strengths, as well as epidemiological studies with separate consideration of 5G (if possible).

title: Persistent Low Uptake and Inconsistent Adoption of Same Day Hernia Repair for Privately Insured Patients in Australian Hospitals.
authors: Northcott C, Dahal P, Cameron A, Maddern GJ.
abstract: Background Hernia repair can safely be provided as a same-day procedure. However, despite advice from published guidelines, previous analyses of Australian data have shown low rates of same-day surgery in private hospitals for hernia repairs. Methods This study used aggregated administrative data for Medibank-insured patients treated in Australian hospitals between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2024 for surgical repairs of inguinal, femoral, or umbilical hernias to analyse trends in same-day services. Results The proportion of hernia procedures performed as same-day separations increased over time, rising from 22.7% in 2015 to 31.0% in 2024 (p Conclusions Despite a groundswell of evidence, changes in surgical practice to adopt same-day hernia repair for privately-insured patients are happening very slowly and are well below the recommended target of 70%-80%. The rise in same-day separations appears to reflect greater use of day-case pathways rather than shorter hospital stays among patients requiring admission overnight. Variation across locations suggests opportunities to improve consistency in care delivery through system-level changes, and for same-day hernia repair to become routine practice across all hospitals in Australia.

title: Patient safety competence in orthopaedic care: The interplay of education, orientation, and workplace learning.
journal: International Journal of Orthopaedic and Trauma Nursing
authors: Ketola S, Rauhala A, Eloranta S.
abstract: Patient safety competence is a fundamental prerequisite for safe, high-quality healthcare. However, less is known about how healthcare professionals perceive their competence and how it develops. This study examined self-assessed patient safety competence of healthcare professionals working in orthopaedic care, across the WHO patient safety competence domains, perceived sources of competence development, and views on future learning needs. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among healthcare professionals working in outpatient, ward, perioperative, anesthesia, rehabilitation, and managerial roles in a specialized orthopedic hospital in Finland. Self-assessed patient safety competence was relatively high across all domains. The highest ratings were observed in teamwork, infection prevention and control, and patient safety in invasive procedures, whereas systems thinking and understanding the impact of complexity on patient care received the lowest ratings. Significant differences were identified in patient, client, and family involvement, with the highest ratings reported by outpatient clinic nurses, and in infection prevention and control, where scrub nurses reported the highest competence. Practical clinical work and workplace orientation were perceived as the primary sources of competence, while formal continuing education played a less prominent role. Despite high competence ratings, respondents expressed substantial interest in further competence development, particularly through workplace-based learning and unit-level training. The findings suggest that patient safety competence develops primarily through experiential learning and workplace-based socialization rather than through formal education alone. Patient safety competence should therefore be understood not only as an individual capability but also as an organizational resource embedded in learning processes, knowledge sharing, and patient safety culture.

title: Pararectal Leiomyosarcoma Following Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy (TLH) for Initially Diagnosed Uterine Leiomyoma.
authors: Monjé N, Alexa M, Hasenburg A, Degirmenci Y.
abstract: This case report highlights the diagnostic challenges of clinically distinguishing leiomyomas and leiomyosarcomas and the importance of post-hysterectomy monitoring. Patients with extensive prior oncological treatments and genetic cancer predisposition require individualized surveillance strategies, as they remain at elevated risk for secondary malignancies that may present in unusual locations or timeframes.

title: Paediatric chronic Monteggia Bado III fracture: how to avoid and treat.
authors: Vaz R, Alves C, Cabral J, Carvalho M.
abstract: Paediatric Monteggia fracture is misdiagnosed in 28% of cases, with possible functional impairment in delayed diagnosis. Assessment of the radiocapitellar alignment on both anteroposterior and lateral views of the elbow is imperative, especially when an apparently isolated ulnar fracture is present. Although Bado I injuries are the most common and diagnosed on lateral radiographs, type III injuries often go unnoticed due to inadequate examination of the anteroposterior view. We present a case of a 6-year-old female patient with a neglected Monteggia fracture (Bado III). The patient underwent surgery 10 months after initial trauma, involving open reduction of the radial head, repair of the annular ligament, and proximal ulnar osteotomy. At 1 year follow-up, the patient achieved a QuickDASH of 0. This case highlights the importance of early recognition and appropriate imaging evaluation, while demonstrating that satisfactory outcomes can be achieved in chronic cases with proper surgical management.

title: Open access route and citation impact in orthopaedic research: A comparison of Gold/hybrid, Green, and Bronze open access within ten high-impact subscription-based journals.
authors: Daniels WJ, Cruickshank M, Dejong T, Ghert M.
abstract: Open access (OA) publishing has expanded access to research, but citation patterns may differ across OA routes. We examined the association between OA route and citation rate within ten high-impact, predominantly subscription-based orthopaedic journals, analysing 24,115 articles published from 2014 to 2019. Journals in which more than 95% of articles were OA were excluded by design; fully OA journals were therefore not represented, and every Gold OA article in this corpus was published as hybrid OA within a subscription journal (hereafter Gold/hybrid OA). Articles were classified as Gold/hybrid OA, Green OA, Bronze OA, or Closed Access using Web of Science OA indicators. Results are reported in three layers: unadjusted descriptive comparisons, a primary adjusted analysis, andsensitivity analyses. The primary analysis used an entropy-balanced negative binomial generalized linear mixed model adjusting for publication year, document type, author count, and journal influence, with journal-level random effects. Most articles were Closed Access (78.5%), followed by Green OA (9.1%), Bronze OA (8.7%), and Gold/hybrid OA (3.8%). In the primary analysis, Gold/hybrid OA and Green OA had higher citation rates than Closed Access (rate ratio 1.41, 95% CI 1.30-1.54; and 1.35, 95% CI 1.28-1.43), and did not differ from each other (1.04, 95% CI 0.95-1.15). Citation rates varied by publication year: Gold/hybrid OA had the highest predicted rate in recent cohorts and Green OA in older cohorts with longer follow-up. Bronze OA had the lowest unadjusted citation counts, largely because it was enriched for lower-cited document types. The higher citation rates for Gold/hybrid and Green OA persisted across all sensitivity analyses. Within subscription-based orthopaedic journals, OA routes are not interchangeable; these findings do not extend to fully OA journals.

title: One bullet, five compartments: a transregional gunshot trajectory and the limits of operative intervention.
authors: Bachelet B, Ravi B, Suh H, Roy S, Hsu J.
abstract: Gunshot wounds with transregional bullet trajectories present significant diagnostic and management challenges. We report the case of an 20-year-old male who sustained a single gunshot wound entering at the left angle of the mandible, traversing the neck with injury to the thyroid cartilage, ricocheting off the right sternoclavicular joint and tracking through the right lung causing haemopneumothorax, before lodging in the perinephric fat adjacent to the right kidney. Pan-scan computed tomography (CT) was pivotal in delineating this complex trajectory. Management required a multidisciplinary approach involving Head & Neck surgery, Trauma surgery, Cardiothoracics, and Intensive Care. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed no peritoneal breach, supporting selective non-operative management (SNOM) of the retroperitoneal bullet. This case highlights the importance of thorough CT imaging from head to pelvis, the safety of SNOM for retroperitoneal bullets in stable patients, and the necessity of coordinated multidisciplinary surgical care for managing complex transregional gunshot injuries.

title: Navigated robotic-arm-assisted hybrid multi-portal endoscopic fenestration of a thoracic intradural arachnoid cyst: a technical case report.
authors: Huo CW, Mobbs RJ, Wang YY.
abstract: Endoscopic treatment of spinal intradural lesions is technically demanding because bimanual manipulation, irrigation control, neural protection, and dural closure are constrained. A 44-year-old woman with myelopathy from a dorsal T4-T10 intradural arachnoid cyst underwent endoscopic fenestration at T4/5. The hybrid multi-portal technique combined unilateral biportal-style exposure, a uniportal working-channel endoscope, intraoperative navigation, and robotic-arm camera stabilization. An accessory portal enabled bimanual intradural manipulation. Irrigation pressure was reduced after durotomy, and the dura was closed with sutures and clips reinforced by sealants. Day 1 magnetic resonance imaging confirmed cord decompression, and lower-limb sensory and bladder symptoms had resolved at 6 weeks. To our knowledge, this is the first reported navigated robotic-arm-assisted hybrid multi-portal endoscopic fenestration of a thoracic intradural arachnoid cyst. This single case demonstrates technical feasibility but not superiority over open or microscopic surgery.

title: Nationwide trends in physical disability among rheumatoid arthritis patients in Korea (2010-2022): A retrospective cohort study based on national registry data.
authors: Kim BY, Kim JW, Lee H, Choe JY, Park SH, Kwak SG.
abstract: Background Whether the burden of legally certified disability among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has decreased in the modern treatment era is uncertain, particularly in Asia. We investigated trends in registered and physical disability among Korean patients with RA. Methods Using National Health Insurance Service data (patient-level 50% random sample), we identified patients aged ≥19 years with seropositive RA registered in the copayment assistance program for rare and intractable diseases in 2010-2022. Disability status, including physical disability (certified musculoskeletal impairment), came from the national disability registry. We estimated annual prevalence and, in newly diagnosed patients, incidence per 1,000 person-years, and compared the results with national disability statistics. Results The number of patients with seropositive RA identified in the database and included in this study was 33,992 in 2010 and 67,844 in 2022. The prevalence of registered disability declined from 20.3% to 14.6% and that of physical disability from 17.4% to 10.9% (both p for trend Conclusions Certified physical disability among Korean patients with RA declined substantially between 2010 and 2022, whereas the incidence of any registered disability remained stable. An excess burden of physical disability compared with the general population persisted.

title: Musculoskeletal Health in Elite Athletes With Bilateral Lower Limb Loss: The ADVANCE Cohort Study.
authors: Watson F, O'Sullivan O, Bull A, Bennett A, Kemp H, Fear N, Boos C, Behan FP.
abstract: Context Lower limb (LL) loss can be detrimental to bone and joint health. Exercise improves musculoskeletal outcomes in individuals without LL loss, but with limited investigation after LL loss. The aim is to assess differences in bone and joint health between elite athletes and nonathletes with bilateral LL loss to assess associations between exercise and musculoskeletal health in this population. Design ADVANCE (Armed Services Trauma Rehabilitation Outcome) is a longitudinal cohort study involving UK military personnel and veterans who served in Afghanistan. Methods Sixty-four ambulatory participants with bilateral LL loss were included. Seven participants were elite athletes (athlete group; n = 7) and were compared with the remaining participants (nonathlete group, n = 57). The Kellgren-Lawrence score for knee and hip osteoarthritis (OA), femoral neck and lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD), Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, Non-Arthritic Hip Score, International Physical Activity Questionnaire, and 6-minute walk test distance were compared. Outcomes were also compared between the Athlete group and Nonathlete group split by activity level. Results Participants were 33.1 ± 4.7 years old and 6.9 ± 1.5 years postinjury. No Athlete group participants had knee OA compared with 51.8% of Nonathlete participants. There was a weak trend for more prevalent hip OA in the Nonathlete group (P = .074); 7.1% Athlete group participants and 30.7% Nonathlete group participants had Kellgren-Lawrence score ≥ 1. Femoral neck BMD was not different between groups, but there was a trend for lower lumbar spine BMD in the Nonathlete group compared with the Athlete group (-0.41 vs 0.57; P = .06). More active nonathletes had better femoral neck t scores than less active nonathletes, P = .03. Neither Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score Pain, Symptoms, Non-Arthritic Hip Score, nor 6-minute walk test distance were different between groups. Conclusion Athletes and active nonathletes with LL loss may have favorable BMD profiles. Athletes with LL loss have lower prevalence of radiographic hip and knee OA. Although not conclusive due to our study design, this suggests that exercise may be associated with beneficial musculoskeletal health outcomes in this population.

title: Medial clavicle fracture with anterosuperior sternoclavicular joint dislocation: joint-sparing suture anchor imbrication and open reduction internal fixation.

title: Mechanisms of local regeneration and community assembly under broad-leaved Korean pine (Pinus koraiensis) forests in northeastern China.
authors: Du X, He S, Dong B, Zhang Y, Jiang H.
abstract: Aims Seedling and sapling community assembly is a key process affecting forest regeneration and succession, yet the spatial aggregation patterns and assembly mechanisms of locally regenerating communities in broad-leaved Korean pine ( Pinus koraiensis ) forests remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we identified aggregation scales and patch sizes and elucidated the assembly mechanisms of local seedling and sapling communities. Methods We conducted stand and regeneration surveys in four broad-leaved Korean pine forest plots. For each regenerating individual, we recorded its species identity, spatial position, and height. Leaf traits were measured at the species level, and local canopy environmental variables were quantified based on stand survey data. Ripley's g(r) , fitted using a Thomas process with a two-nested-scale function, was used to identify aggregation scales, and hierarchical clustering was used to delineate local communities. Abundance-based and presence-based standardized effect sizes of mean pairwise trait distance (SES.MPD), standardized effect sizes of Pielou's evenness (SES.E), and the degree of distribution tendency ( D ) were then used to characterize community structure, and redundancy analysis (RDA) was used to assess trait-environment relationships. Results Both local seedling and sapling communities exhibited two characteristic aggregation scales, at approximately 1 and 15 m. Compared with sapling communities, seedling communities showed stronger aggregation at both the small and large scales, had more patches and more individuals per patch. Across 1-15 m scales, abundance-weighted SES.MPD , presence-based SES.MPD , SES.E , and their corresponding D values indicated non-random functional structure in both communities, with stronger abundance-based patterns in seedlings but more consistent presence-based patterns in saplings, and stronger signals of competition at smaller scales in saplings. The RDA showed that environmental explanatory power was relatively weak overall, but increased with spatial scale and developmental stage. Compared with the seedling communities, the sapling communities demonstrated weaker or even opposite correlations in community-weighted mean leaf area (CWM.LA), specific leaf area (SLA), and leaf width (LW) with vertical distribution tendency degrees and local coniferous leaf area index. Conclusions Overall, stochastic processes played a major role in shaping local regeneration communities. Limited dispersal caused regenerating individuals with similar traits to cluster across spatial scales. As seedlings developed into saplings, the influence of canopy conditions progressively accumulated, and local competition apparently became stronger, especially at small spatial scales. These findings suggest that the mechanisms shaping regeneration communities change during development, and that seedlings and saplings respond differently to canopy structure.

title: Lifestyle and dietary changes among cancer patients receiving active treatment: A cross-sectional study at a tertiary care center in Lebanon.
authors: Farhat S, Hammoud Z, Zayour N, Fahs J, Freijeh T, Moussaoui N, Al Rachiini H, Matar B.
abstract: Background Cancer diagnosis is often accompanied by changes in nutritional needs and lifestyle habits, which may ultimately be associated with patients' quality of life (QOL). Despite the high burden of cancer in Lebanon, limited data exist on how dietary intake and lifestyle behaviors change following diagnosis. This study aimed to assess self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors following cancer diagnosis and examine factors associated with these changes and their relationship with QOL. Methods This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted at Al Zahraa Hospital University Medical Center in Beirut, Lebanon. Adult cancer patients receiving active treatment were assessed regarding self-reported dietary and lifestyle behaviors before and after cancer diagnosis. QOL was assessed using the validated Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General (FACT-G). Results This study included 145 participants, the majority of whom were Lebanese (93.79%) and female (69.7%). Most lacked health insurance (84.8%), and 91.0% reported a financial burden related to treatment. Compared with recalled pre-diagnosis behaviors, 47.6% of participants reported favorable changes in smoking behavior, while 34.5% reported decreased physical activity. The most frequently reported favorable dietary changes according to the prespecified framework were reduced sugar (60.0%), reduced red meat (49.6%), and reduced fast-food consumption (34.5%). Younger age and employment were associated with the favorable dietary-change score in bivariate analyses, while age and marital status were associated with tobacco-habit change in multivariable analysis; medical insurance was associated with physical-activity change in bivariate analysis. The mean FACT-G total score was 70.48 ± 20.79. Favorable dietary changes were associated with FACT-G scores, including changes in fruit, milk, and fast-food intake. Conclusions Self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors were observed among patients receiving active cancer treatment, with substantial variation across behavioral domains. The favorable dietary-change score was associated with QOL; however, the cross-sectional design and retrospective assessment preclude causal or directional interpretation. These findings may inform future longitudinal and interventional studies evaluating structured, individualized nutritional and lifestyle support during cancer treatment in Lebanon.

title: Knee flexion influences MRI-based static tibiofemoral rotation after ACL injury and reconstruction.
authors: Ackermann J, Jones M, Ball SV, Kabeer AS, Bamania P, Watura C, Lee JC, Williams A.
abstract: Purpose To determine the influence of knee flexion on MRI-based static TF rotation, and evaluate whether this relationship is modified by anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) state, posterior tibial slope asymmetry (ΔPTS), or lateral extra-articular tenodesis (LET). Methods A retrospective review was conducted of professional soccer players who underwent primary ACL reconstruction between 2012 and 2024 with available MRI. Static TF rotation, medial and lateral PTS, and knee flexion were measured on MRI. ΔPTS was defined as the difference between lateral and medial PTS. Linear mixed-effects models assessed associations, including interactions for flexion, ΔPTS, ACL state, and LET, with adjustment for meniscal status. Results A total of 310 MRI examinations from 106 professional soccer players (mean age 23.3 ± 4.2 years) with ACL injury (n = 106) and after ACL reconstruction (n = 204) were retrospectively analyzed. Greater knee flexion during MRI acquisition was associated with increased internal TF rotation (β = 0.15° per 1° flexion; 95% CI, 0.02-0.27°; p = 0.020). ΔPTS was a strong independent predictor of TF rotation (β = 1.33° per 1° ΔPTS; 95% CI, 0.72-1.95°; p Conclusion Knee flexion during MRI acquisition significantly influences axial TF rotation. PTS asymmetry remains an independent determinant of rotational alignment, although its apparent effect decreases at greater flexion angles and after ACL reconstruction. Based on model estimates, a clinically plausible 10-20° difference in knee flexion during MRI acquisition may produce approximately 1.5-3° of apparent static TF rotation. In MRI studies of static TF rotation standardizing the flexion angle of knees is critical.

title: Kin count: Social, physiological, and environmental correlates of annual survival in Belding's ground squirrels.
authors: Mateo JM, Brooks KC, Dosmann A.
abstract: Long-term studies of free‑living animals provide opportunities to identify the traits and environmental conditions that predict survival under natural selection. Using over two decades of mark-recapture demographic data, we evaluated intrinsic, social and environmental predictors of annual survival in a population of Belding's ground squirrels (Urocitellus beldingi), obligate hibernators that exhibit female philopatry and kin-structured social groups. We assessed the effects of age, sex, body mass, glucocorticoid physiology, reproductive effort, kinship and snowfall using sex-specific generalized linear mixed models and logistic regressions. Adult females had higher survival than adult males, whereas juveniles-particularly males-experienced the highest mortality. As expected, survival was strongly associated with body condition: heavier individuals and those with lower fecal glucocorticoid metabolites were more likely to survive. For the first time, we demonstrate that the number of relatives predicted survival in this species. That is, adult females' probability of surviving to the next summer increased with the specific number of living female close kin, beyond the effect of kin presence alone. Male survival was unrelated to kinship. In contrast, juvenile females with more kin had lower survival, suggesting age‑specific trade‑offs associated with kin structure. Earlier emergence from hibernation improved juvenile survival and was also associated with successful adult female reproduction. Snowfall influenced survival through phenological pathways: lower snow before the active season was associated with earlier emergence and higher survival in adult females, while post‑season snow was not related to survival. Together, these results show that social structure, physiological state, and climate‑driven seasonal timing interact to shape annual survival in an obligate hibernator, with effects that vary by sex and life stage. Understanding these interactions will be increasingly important as snowfall declines across much of U. beldingi's range.

title: Is surgeon technique a modifiable risk factor for heterotopic ossification after posterior acetabular fracture fixation? A multi-surgeon study.
authors: Kumar DS, Luther L, Schaffer NE, Litten RM, Traven SA, Moore RS, Moreno-Diaz AF, Velasco-Castro J, Maxson R, Sumpter AE, Agarwal A, Boyce RH, Collinge CA, Evans JM, Jahangir AA, Johnson JP, Mir HR, Perdue AM, Quade JH, Sethi MK, Spitler C, Stinner DJ, Tatman LM, Mitchell PM.
abstract: Introduction Heterotopic ossification (HO) is a well-recognized complication following operative fixation of acetabular fractures through a posterior approach. Established risk factors largely reflect nonmodifiable patient and injury characteristics. Whether surgeon-controlled aspects of operative technique influence HO remains poorly defined. The purpose of this study was to determine if the individual surgeon and specific technique variables are associated with HO after accounting for established patient and injury factors. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 1292 patients who underwent acetabular fracture fixation through a Kocher-Langenbeck approach at two Level 1 trauma centers between 2010 and 2025 by 14 fellowship-trained orthopaedic traumatologists. Patients receiving any form of HO prophylaxis were excluded. Four surgeon-controlled variables were examined: aggressiveness of gluteus minimus debridement, trochanteric osteotomy, thrombin gel use, and closed suction drainage. HO was graded on final radiographs by two independent reviewers using the Brooker classification, with third-reader adjudication for disagreements, and categorized as little-to-no (grade 0-I), moderate (grade II), or severe (grade III-IV). Mixed-effects logistic regression models with surgeon as a random effect were used to assess the associations between patient, injury, and surgeon-controlled technique variables, as well as the individual surgeon, with severe and moderate HO formation. Results Little-to-no HO occurred in 1132 patients (87.6%), moderate HO in 96 (7.4%), and severe HO in 64 (5.0%). Aggressive gluteus minimus debridement was not associated with HO severity. For severe HO, the surgeon did not contribute meaningfully to model performance, and no surgeon-controlled technique variables were significant; severe head injury, mechanical ventilation beyond 72 h, African-American race, and dual surgical approaches were associated with severe HO. For moderate HO, the surgeon contributed moderately, and both trochanteric osteotomy (odds ratio [OR] 3.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-12) and closed suction drainage (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.0-3.1) were associated with increased odds of moderate HO. Conclusion Severe HO following posterior acetabular fracture fixation is predominantly driven by patient and injury characteristics rather than surgeon technique. Aggressive gluteus minimus debridement does not appear to reduce HO risk, and prevention efforts should prioritize patient-level risk stratification.

title: Investigating GLP-1 sourcing preferences on social media and motivations for use: Survey with choice-based conjoint (CBC) exercise.
authors: Haupt MR, Weiss SM, Calac AJ, Salazar S, Larsen MZ, Mackey TK.
abstract: The growing use of glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) drugs such as Ozempic for weight loss interventions has led to increased concerns about inappropriate use, supply shortages, and high-risk sourcing. However, little is known about the influence of online marketing strategies on purchasing preferences for GLP-1 products. This study uses a survey with a Choice-Based Conjoint (CBC) exercise to assess features of social media posts that are most influential for intent to purchase GLP-1 products and identify motivations for use. Participants were recruited based on current use of GLP-1 drugs, previous use, or considering use (n = 242). Utility scores from the conjoint analysis quantified the influence of tested features.
