Conjoint findings showed greater preference for posts that feature branded semaglutide (e.g., Wegovy)(15.38, SD = 45.29), display products in packaging (47.49, SD = 46.72), have accredited digital pharmacies as the seller (25.16, SD = 47.31) (e.g., Amazon Pharmacy), include medical endorsements for diabetes treatment (13.16, SD = 49.04), and offer a free consultation (13.18, SD = 32.00). Analysis was conducted on survey questions measuring GLP-1 purchasing channels and motivations for use. Over half of participants (51.7%) reported that social media content influenced their perceptions of GLP-1 drugs and 45.8% (n = 65) of GLP-1 users reported purchasing product from high-risk sources (i.e., personal network or individual sellers online). Exploratory analysis shows a possible association between self-reported high-risk sourcing and reliance on GLP-1s for medical conditions. Overall, our findings identify influential attributes of GLP-1 social media ads (i.e., branding and visual display of products) and suggests greater support is needed for online moderation efforts to prevent high-risk purchasing activity and increase safe access to GLP-1s for those with medical needs.

title: Intraoperative visualization with 3D fluoroscopy for posterior pelvic fixation is associated with lower cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure.
authors: Tse S, Chinweze RO, Velasco-Castro J, Andring N, Jbeily E, Robinson C, Saade A, Simister S, Campbell ST, Fitzpatrick E, Lee MA, Saiz AM, Soles GL.
abstract: Introduction Achieving optimal screw positioning in posterior pelvic ring (PR) fracture fixation is critical for fracture stability and safety. Formerly, our institution used intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy followed by postoperative computed tomography (CT) to assess fracture reduction and screw placement. Introduction of the 3D mobile C-arm enables immediate volumetric intraoperative assessment, may improve intraoperative visualization, and may alter conventional imaging requirements. This study compared cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure between cases performed with intraoperative 3D fluoroscopy (3DF) against standard intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy (2DF), including postoperative CT utilization. Methods A retrospective review was conducted on patients treated for posterior PR fractures at a level 1 trauma center between 2014 and 2023. Utilization of 3DF or plain-film fluoroscopy, and any intraoperative screw changes were documented. Rates and details of postoperative complications and subsequent reoperations were recorded for patients with > 3 months follow-up. Radiation doses for 3DF, 2DF, and postoperative CT were extracted from radiology reports. Results Among 245 patients (mean age 47.2, 52.2% male) undergoing fixation for posterior PR fractures, 89 (36.3%) had 3DF intraoperatively, while 156 (63.7%) had 2DF. 27 patients (8 3DF, 19 2DF, p = 0.443) had screws changed intraoperatively, primarily to modify screw path (n = 16, 59.3%), to achieve better purchase/reduction (n = 5, 18.5%), to modify screw size (n = 3, 11.1%), to change screw type (n = 2, 7.4%), and failure to advance screw (n = 1, 3.7%). Mean radiation dose for the 3DF group was significantly lower (179.2 mGy vs 526.1 mGy, p 3 months follow-up, reoperation was less frequent with 3DF (9.5% vs 31.2%, p = 0.012), predominantly for symptomatic implant removal. Discussion and conclusion Intraoperative 3DF was associated with lower cumulative radiation exposure compared to traditional fluoroscopy with routine postoperative CT, and intraoperative dose alone was also lower. Reoperation was less frequent in the 3DF group, but most reoperations were implant removals for symptomatic or planned indications. These findings highlight the potential of 3DF as a practical radiation efficient quality assurance tool in posterior pelvic fixation.

title: Intraoperative demonstration of a check-valve mechanism in a spinal extradural arachnoid cyst with nerve root incarceration.
authors: Dezawa T, Fukutake K, Hasegawa K, Kamakura D, Tochigi N, Takahashi H.
abstract: Spinal extradural arachnoid cysts (SEDACs) are rare lesions thought to arise from a dural defect associated with a check-valve mechanism, although direct intraoperative evidence is limited. We report a 17-year-old female presenting with persistent low back pain and bilateral lower extremity numbness. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a cystic lesion at the Th12-L1 level displacing the dural sac, while computed tomography myelography failed to identify a communicating tract. Surgical exploration was performed due to persistent symptoms and a suspected dynamic mechanism. Intraoperatively, a dural defect at the nerve root sleeve with nerve root incarceration was identified. Cerebrospinal fluid leakage ceased after closure of the defect, confirming a check-valve mechanism. The cyst was resected and the defect repaired. The patient's symptoms resolved completely, with no recurrence at 2-year follow-up. This case provides direct intraoperative evidence of the proposed pathophysiology of SEDAC.

title: Intra-individual relationships between jump height and lower-limb joint kinetics in single-leg countermovement jumps in male athletes.
authors: Yamamoto S, Kubota H, Imai K, Miyazaki T.
abstract: Athletes show trial-to-trial intra-individual variability in performance outcomes during repeated maximal-effort motor tasks within a single competition. Although inter-individual relationships between performance outcomes and joint kinetics have been demonstrated, the trial-to-trial intra-individual relationships remain unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to clarify the intra-individual relationships between jump height and lower-limb joint kinetics during single-leg countermovement jumps (CMJs) in male athletes. Fifty-two male athletes performed 12 maximal-effort single-leg CMJs within a single session. Ground reaction forces and marker coordinates were recorded, from which jump height and lower-limb joint kinetics were calculated. Hierarchical linear modeling was used to examine the intra-individual relationships between jump height and each joint kinetic variable. Significant positive fixed effects on jump height were observed for hip (extension torque [γ 10 = 0.013], flexion-extension power [γ 10 = 0.005], and positive work [γ 10 = 0.018]) and ankle joint kinetics (plantarflexion torque [γ 10 = 0.035] and positive work [γ 10 = 0.045]), whereas no significant fixed effects were observed for knee joint kinetics (γ 10 ≤ 0.007). The inter-individual correlation analysis showed that greater values of hip and knee joint kinetics and ankle plantar-dorsiflexion power were associated with greater jump height. These results indicate that the intra- and inter-individual analyses showed different patterns of associations between jump height and lower-limb joint kinetics. Moreover, significant random effects were observed for all lower-limb joint kinetics, indicating that these intra-individual relationships differed among participants. Understanding joint kinetics associated with trial-to-trial intra-individual variability in jump height may contribute to identifying participant-specific biomechanical factors underlying jump height.

title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing.
authors: Zhao J, Chen Y, Yang F, Tian C, Luo W, Su Z, Yang B, Liu W, Yang H.
abstract: Background Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood. Methods Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis. Results WGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune-inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues. Conclusion This integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3-although identified by machine learning-requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

title: Influencing factors of the long-term predictive accuracy of the ocular trauma score.
authors: Li W, Fan N, Mei Z, Liu R, Peng Q.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the performance of the Ocular Trauma Score (OTS) in predicting long-term visual outcomes after mechanical ocular trauma and to identify the key factors influencing its accuracy. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 106 patients with mechanical ocular trauma, with a median follow-up of 14 months. Retrieved variables included demographic characteristics and clinical data after the injury. The distribution of final best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was compared between the actual outcomes and the OTS-predicted outcomes. A weighted average predicted BCVA was calculated based on the BCVA probability distribution for each OTS category to classify patients into Better (actual BCVA better than OTS predicted) and Non-Better groups. Factors associated with OTS prediction discrepancies were identified using univariate analyses. Multivariable Firth logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation was performed to identify factors independently associated with better-than-predicted outcomes. Results The OTS demonstrated a clear severity-dependent predictive pattern. Predictive accuracy was highest for mild injuries (OTS category 5) but showed a systematic pessimistic bias in severe injuries (OTS category 1), overestimating poor outcomes (NLP) and underestimating recovery potential (BCVA grades 3-5). For intermediate injuries (OTS categories 2-3), the likelihood of achieving moderate vision (20/200-20/50) was underestimated. Multiple surgeries were associated with better-than-predicted outcomes in the univariate analysis (p = 0.021). In the multivariable analysis, endophthalmitis (odds ratio [OR] = 2.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08-8.29, p = 0.034) and penetrating injury (OR = 3.71, 95% CI: 1.17-12.94, p = 0.026) were independently associated with better-than-predicted outcomes, whereas initial BCVA grade 2, despite a significant univariate association, did not retain statistical significance after adjustment (OR = 2.01, 95% CI: 0.79-5.10, p = 0.144). Conclusion The OTS remains a useful prognostic tool but demonstrates limited accuracy in severe mechanical ocular trauma. Endophthalmitis and penetrating injury were identified as independent modifiers, while initial BCVA grade 2 and multiple surgeries were associated with better-than-predicted outcomes in the univariate analysis. Contextualising its predictions with contemporary surgical factors and clinical modifiers may improve the individualised application of the OTS.

title: Impact of radiographic damage on health-related outcomes across rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and hand osteoarthritis: a comparative analysis of disease burden.
authors: Kökoğlu EO, Cengiz G, Kaplan H, Denizhan TK, Beke SK, Çalış M, Sofu N, Zararsız GE.
abstract: Introduction/objectives To evaluate the comparative impact of radiographic joint damage on hand functions, objective grip strength, and quality of life across patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis (PsA), and hand osteoarthritis (OA). Method This cross-sectional study included patients with RA (n = 50), PsA (n = 40), and hand OA (n = 40). Objective grip strength was measured using a calibrated JAMAR hydraulic dynamometer. Radiographic damage was assessed using the modified Total Sharp Score (mTSS) for inflammatory cohorts and the Kellgren-Lawrence (K-L) scale for hand OA. Functional status and psychosocial impact were evaluated through Duruöz Hand Index (DHI), Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (QuickDASH) questionnaire, Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), and the Short Form-36 (SF-36) Health Survey scales. Spearman correlation analyses and adjusted multivariable linear regression models were performed to evaluate the relationship between radiographic damage and functional outcomes. Results Despite marked differences in disease duration, radiographic damage, and treatment profiles, objectively measured grip strength and patient-reported hand disability did not differ significantly among the three disease groups (all p > 0.05). In unadjusted analyses, greater radiographic damage was associated with lower grip strength in PsA (r = - 0.405, 95% CI - 0.637 to - 0.107), but not with QuickDASH or DHI; no significant associations between radiographic damage and these functional outcomes were observed in RA or hand OA. After multivariable adjustment, high radiographic damage remained associated with lower grip strength in PsA (β = - 9.02, 95% CI - 17.19 to - 0.85), but was not associated with QuickDASH or DHI. Disease activity was most strongly associated with functional outcomes in RA, whereas radiographic severity was not independently associated with grip strength or patient-reported hand function in hand OA. Grip strength was inversely correlated with hand-specific patient-reported outcomes across all disease groups. Conclusion Although patients with RA, PsA, and hand OA experience comparable levels of hand dysfunction, the factors associated with functional impairment differ according to disease phenotype. Structural damage appears to have a greater influence on objective hand performance in PsA, whereas disease activity predominates in RA and radiographic severity alone does not explain disability in hand OA. These findings highlight the importance of disease-specific interpretation of structural damage and support comprehensive functional assessment in patients with inflammatory and degenerative hand arthritis. Key Points • Patients with RA, psoriatic arthritis, and hand OA exhibited comparable levels of objectively measured grip strength and patient-reported hand disability despite substantial differences in disease duration and radiographic severity. • Multivariable analyses demonstrated disease-specific determinants of functional impairment: radiographic damage was independently associated with reduced grip strength only in psoriatic arthritis, whereas disease activity was the principal factor associated with functional outcomes in RA and radiographic severity alone did not explain disability in hand OA. • Functional impairment in hand OA cannot be explained solely by structural radiographic changes, underscoring the need for comprehensive functional assessment beyond conventional imaging findings.

title: Heterotopic pregnancy at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital: a case report.
authors: Djokoto RMK, Sarpong BA, Agana EA, Nduroh KA, Arthur-Komeh J, Adarkwa O, Vormawor AP, Ofori AA, Owusu VB.
abstract: Background Heterotopic pregnancy, defined as the coexistence of an intrauterine and an extrauterine pregnancy, is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition. While its incidence in assisted reproductive technology pregnancies is well documented, spontaneous heterotopic pregnancy remains exceedingly rare, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. We present the case of a ruptured heterotopic pregnancy in a haemodynamically unstable patient, highlighting the diagnostic and management challenges in a resource-limited setting. Case presentation We present the case of a 34-year-old Ghanaian woman, Gravida 3 Para 1 (alive) + 1 spontaneous abortion, who presented to the Emergency Unit of the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) with a 2-month history of amenorrhoea and a 1-day history of abdominal pain. Her vital signs on arrival indicated haemorrhagic shock (blood pressure 69/39 mmHg, heart rate 101 beats per minute). Bedside ultrasound revealed a live intrauterine gestation at 8 weeks with cardiac activity and a left adnexal mass with free fluid in the pelvis. She was resuscitated following the ATLS protocol and underwent emergency exploratory laparotomy under general anaesthesia. Intraoperatively, approximately 1.28 L of hemoperitoneum was drained, and a ruptured left isthmic ectopic pregnancy was identified and managed with total salpingectomy. The intrauterine pregnancy remained viable postoperatively. Progesterone supplementation (Depot Primolut injections and progesterone pessaries 400 mg twice daily) was commenced as institutional practice and continued until 16 weeks of gestation. Serial beta-hCG monitoring confirmed resolution of the ectopic component, with levels declining from 45,000 mIU/mL postoperatively to 12,500 mIU/mL by postoperative day 10. The intrauterine pregnancy progressed to 38 weeks of gestation, and the patient delivered a live female baby weighing 2.5 kg. Conclusions This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for heterotopic pregnancy in patients with acute abdominal symptoms, even when an intrauterine pregnancy has been confirmed. Rapid resuscitation, emergency surgical intervention with minimal uterine manipulation, and appropriate postoperative support are critical for maternal and intrauterine pregnancy survival, as demonstrated by the successful delivery at 38 weeks in this case.

title: Gender Experiences of Training and Practicing Orthopaedic Surgeons in Australia: A Mixed Methods Study.
authors: Freeman C, Evans R, Larkins S, Morrey C.
abstract: Introduction Orthopaedic surgery remains Australia's least gender-diverse medical specialty. Despite extensive global literature on barriers to gender equity, no prior study has applied an established gender bias instrument to assess gender bias in Australian orthopaedics. Methods A national mixed methods study was conducted comprising a cross-sectional survey and semi-structured interviews. Eligible participants included all practising orthopaedic surgeons and trainees in Australia. The survey utilised an adapted version of the 47-item Gender Bias Scale and was distributed via the Australian Orthopaedic Association and departmental mailing lists. Interviewees were recruited from survey volunteers and were undertaken to provide explanatory depth and contextualisation to the survey findings. Results 163 orthopaedic surgeons and trainees (85 male, 78 female) completed the survey. Female participants were significantly more likely to report barriers across the male culture and unequal standards domains. Twenty of the 47 GBS items showed significant gender differences (p Conclusion This study presents Australian data on key barriers to gender equity in orthopaedics, providing an evidence base for future policy. Achieving progress will require more than increasing representation. It will take thoughtful policy and continuous effort to address structural and attitudinal barriers.

title: From fluoroscopy to artificial intelligence: three decades of percutaneous pelvic ring fixation-a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis (1996-2026).
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Vicenti G, Ferorelli D, Loiodice M, Sirago G, Solarino G, Dell'Erba A.
abstract: Introduction Percutaneous pelvic-ring fixation requires implant placement within narrow osseous corridors. Navigation, robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) have successively been proposed to improve accuracy and reduce radiation exposure. This study mapped three decades of research on these technologies, characterising publication trends and the field's intellectual, conceptual and social structure. Materials and methods The Web of Science Core Collection (primary dataset, with parsed cited references) and Scopus (robustness comparison) were searched on 8 June 2026. Searches combined pelvic-fixation and technology terms and targeted articles, reviews and conference papers; degenerative-spine, deformity, arthroplasty and isolated acetabular records were excluded, while adjacent WoS categories retained by platform indexing were evaluated in sensitivity analysis. Bibliometrix analyses comprised performance indicators, collaboration patterns, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence, thematic mapping and trend analysis on a harmonised keyword field. Results The primary corpus comprised 271 documents from 97 sources, with 1311 authors and 16.3 mean citations per document. Output rose from low single digits before 2010 to 25-29 documents per year in 2022-2023; an exploratory logistic model indicated continued rapid growth. The Journal of Orthopaedic Trauma and Injury dominated the source landscape, while Germany, China, Switzerland and the United States led production. Foundational percutaneous-fixation studies and the subsequent navigation literature structured the intellectual base. Navigation, fluoroscopy and screw insertion formed the conceptual backbone, whereas explicit AI terminology appeared in only 1 of 271 documents at the author-keyword level. Conclusions Percutaneous pelvic-ring fixation research is in sustained growth around a mature navigation backbone, while robotics, augmented reality and AI form a thin but identifiable emerging frontier. The findings support research prioritisation, cross-border collaboration and transparent reporting of new technologies in trauma orthopaedics.

title: Forearm Pronation Mechanics and Prior Upper Extremity Injury History in Professional Baseball Pitchers: A Biomechanical Analysis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Eskew J, Manzi J, Dowling B, Hingorani A, Mack V, Kew M, Brusalis C, Kremchek T, Gulotta LV, Carr JB, Dines JS.
abstract: Background Forearm pronation during baseball pitching has received increasing attention because of its potential relationship with upper extremity loading. Purpose To evaluate the association between forearm pronation mechanics and prior upper extremity injury history in professional baseball pitchers. Methods Biomechanical data from 304 professional baseball pitchers were analyzed. Forearm pronation at foot contact, maximum pronation velocity, and pronation excursion were evaluated. Logistic regression analyses controlling for age, leg length, elbow varus torque, and handedness assessed associations with pitchers self-reported prior injuries across 24 injury subcategories. Univariate comparisons were performed for Superior Labrum Anterior to Posterior (SLAP)-injured versus pitchers with no prior injury and all pitchers without SLAP/labral injury history. Results 263 (86.5%) pitchers demonstrated forearm pronation at foot contact (mean 36° ± 19°), while 41 (13.5%) exhibited forearm supination (mean -12° ± 11°). No statistically significant associations were identified between forearm pronation mechanics and upper extremity injuries overall (n = 107), elbow injuries (n = 65), UCL sprains/tears (n = 39), or the majority of other injury categories. An exploratory analysis of SLAP/labral injury (n = 16) identified a significant inverse association with forearm pronation excursion (OR 0.597 per 10° increase, 95% CI 0.310-0.978, p = 0.039). This association did not remain significant after FDR correction for multiple comparisons (adjusted p=0.976) but remains directionally consistent across multiple covariate specifications. Univariate analysis confirmed that pitchers with prior SLAP injury had significantly reduced pronation excursion (13° vs 22°, p = 0.017), reduced shoulder external rotation at maximum external rotation (162° vs 166°, p = 0.044), and were older (22.7 vs 21.6 years, p = 0.007) compared to uninjured controls. These differences remained significant when compared against all pitchers without SLAP/labral injury history, regardless of other injury history: pronation excursion (13° vs 21°, p=0.016), SER at MER (162° vs 166°, p=0.042), and age (22.7 vs 21.9 years, p=0.033). Conclusion Forearm pronation mechanics were not significantly associated with prior injury history across the majority of injury categories including the elbow, challenging theoretical concerns regarding flexor-pronator overload. In an exploratory analysis, pitchers with prior labral/SLAP injury demonstrated reduced forearm pronation excursion; however, this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons and was based on a limited number of injury events. Because biomechanical assessment occurred after the reported injuries, the temporal relationship between reduced pronation excursion and SLAP/labral injury cannot be determined. This finding should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

title: Extracellular vesicles in soft tissue sarcomas: From tumor biology to clinical translation.
authors: Del Fiore P, Mathlouthi S, Salmaso S, Rosato A, Mocellin S, Krengli M, Pasqualetti F, Garofalo M.
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STS) comprise a rare, highly heterogeneous group of mesenchymal malignancies characterized by diverse molecular drivers, poor prognosis, and a lack of biomarkers for disease monitoring and therapeutic stratification. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as key mediators of intercellular communication and promising tools in precision oncology. By transporting cargoes, including oncogenic signals reflecting the molecular state of their cells of origin, EVs influence tumor progression, immune modulation, angiogenesis and metastatic dissemination. In line with MISEV2023 standards and advances in clinical translation, this review provides a timely, histotype-stratified synthesis of EV biology in STS, integrating EV-based biomarker discovery with engineered delivery platforms and the regulatory challenges of rare-disease translation. We examine EV biology across STS subtypes, including liposarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, and leiomyosarcoma, highlighting how subtype-specific EV-cargo reprograms the tumor microenvironment. Moving from bench to bedside, we discuss the translational potential of EVs as minimally invasive liquid biopsy tools. Rather than replacing existing circulating markers, EVs may provide orthogonal diagnostic and tumor microenvironment remodeling signals that complement ctDNA, supporting a histotype-dependent approach for longitudinal monitoring and minimal residual disease (MRD) detection. Finally, we critically address the technical and regulatory challenges to clinical implementation, including isolation heterogeneity, Good Manufacturing Practice scalability, and quality control. To overcome these hurdles, we propose a translational roadmap encompassing integrated biobanking networks, multicenter clinical validation, and artificial intelligence-driven analytical platforms. Overall, EVs represent a promising but still investigational platform, offering unprecedented opportunities for patient stratification, disease surveillance, and personalized therapeutic strategies in aggressive sarcomas.

title: Exploration of complex shyness and the relationship between fear and approach behaviors in domestic cats (Felis catus).
authors: Hattori M, Saito A, Yamamoto S.
abstract: Shyness in human psychology is recognized as a complex trait distinct from pure fear, often characterized by an approach-avoidance conflict. While shyness and fear are frequently conflated in animal behavior studies, this research investigated shyness in domestic cats (Felis catus), exploring whether they exhibit multifaceted personality structures similar to those of human infants. We conducted three sequential surveys with cat owners: Study 1 included 82 cats of both sexes, Study 2 included 114 male cats to follow up on the sex-specific pattern observed in Study 1, and Study 3 included 114 stray-born male cats to further examine the pattern identified among stray-born cats in Study 2. We used adapted versions of the Colorado Childhood Temperament Inventory (CCTI) and the Infant Behavior Questionnaire-Revised (IBQ-R) to assess shyness, fear, and approach tendencies. The predicted quadratic relationship between shyness and approach scores was not statistically significant, and thus the primary confirmatory hypothesis was not supported. Subsequent exploratory hierarchical cluster analyses suggested four candidate personality phenotypes in stray-born male cats: "Highly Sociable" (low fear/high approach), "Sociable" (low fear/moderate approach), "Fearful" (high fear/low approach), and a "Human infant-like shyness" type (high fear/high approach). These findings suggest that cat shyness is predominantly linked to fear, as supported by the strong positive correlations between shyness and fear. However, the cluster analyses identified a specific subset of cats exhibiting a complex personality involving high-approach tendencies despite high fear, mirroring human infant-like shyness. This study highlights the multifaceted nature of cat temperament and demonstrates that adapting human psychological frameworks can provide significant insights into animal personality, potentially improving welfare in domestic cats.

title: Evaluating the Association of Fecal Diversion with Morbidity in Patients Undergoing CRS/HIPEC with Pelvic Anastomoses: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Neel NC, Acharya K, Van Doosselaere L, Raclin N, Ahdoot A, Frederick D, Lowy AM, Veerapong J, Baumgartner JM, Kelly K, Mehtsun WT.
abstract: Background Cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) is an established treatment for peritoneal surface malignancies, but is associated with substantial morbidity, particularly when pelvic anastomoses are performed. Diverting ostomies are commonly used to mitigate complications related to anastomotic leak; however, ostomy formation carries its own morbidity, and its benefit in this setting remains controversial. Patients and methods PubMed and Embase were queried for studies of patients undergoing CRS/HIPEC with a pelvic anastomosis, documented use of diverting ostomy, and reported anastomotic leak rates. Eligible studies required combined CRS/HIPEC, explicit reporting of diversion status, and perioperative outcomes stratified by ostomy presence. Abstracts were independently screened by two reviewers, followed by full-text review for final inclusion. A binary odds ratio meta-analysis was performed comparing anastomotic leak between diverted and non-diverted patients. Results Of 506 studies identified, 10 met inclusion criteria and were combined with our institutional cohort, comprising 1506 patients. Overall, diversion was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in anastomotic leak (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.32-1.39, p = 0.28). No differences were observed in grade ≥ 3 complications or length of stay. Diversion was associated with increased 60-day readmissions (OR 3.29, 95% CI 1.52-7.11, p Conclusions Diverting ostomies were not associated with a statistically significant reduction in anastomotic leak in patients undergoing CRS/HIPEC with a pelvic anastomosis. These findings suggest consideration of a selective, rather than routine, diversion strategy in appropriately selected patients.

title: Emergency pancreaticoduodenectomy for traumatic pancreaticoduodenal injury with celiac axis stenosis.
authors: Oishi T, Muroya T, Nakamura F, Ueda K, Tamagaki K, Nakamura Y, Onoe A, Sakuramoto K, Satoi S, Nakamori Y.
abstract: Emergency pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) for trauma is technically demanding, and unrecognized celiac axis stenosis (CAS) may compromise hepatic arterial inflow after gastroduodenal artery (GDA) division. A 59-year-old man presented in hemorrhagic shock after blunt abdominal trauma. Computed tomography demonstrated destructive pancreaticoduodenal injury, active bleeding, and proximal CAS with a hooked configuration suggesting median arcuate ligament (MAL) compression. After inferior pancreaticoduodenal arterial embolization, superior mesenteric arteriography showed retrograde filling of the celiac territory. Persistent hemodynamic instability necessitated emergency laparotomy and PD. Temporary GDA clamping markedly weakened common hepatic artery pulsation, confirming collateral-dependent hepatic arterial inflow. MAL release promptly restored pulsation, allowing PD with immediate reconstruction. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 34. In emergency PD for trauma, CAS or retrograde celiac filling should prompt temporary GDA clamping before irreversible division to guide MAL release or another inflow-preserving strategy.

title: Effects and mechanisms of exercise timing on cognitive function in older type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with mild cognitive impairment: A magnetic resonance imaging-based randomized controlled trial protocol.
authors: Lin Y, Ma Z, Zhang J, Zhuang J.
abstract: Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cognitive impairment progressively impairs self-care abilities, thereby triggering a vicious cycle of poor glycemic control and further cognitive decline. Exercise has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to improve both glycemic control and cognitive function; however, an optimal time of day for exercise to mitigate this neurodegenerative trajectory has not been determined. This trial aims to determine the most effective exercise timing to maximize cognitive benefits in older T2DM patients with MCI (T2DM-MCI) and to investigate the underlying neurobiological mechanisms using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, patients 60-75 years of age with T2DM-MCI will be assigned to a morning exercise group (09:00-10:10), an evening exercise group (19:00-20:10), or a health education group. The exercise groups will complete a 12-week, home-based, remotely supervised exercise program comprising aerobic and resistance exercises. The health education group will receive a 12-week health education program. Cognitive function will be evaluated at baseline and post-intervention using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Color-Word Stroop Test, N-back task, Trail making Test, Attention Network Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test. Additionally, brain structure and function based on imaging, blood biomarkers, and physical fitness will also be assessed. Discussion In this study, we aim to identify the optimal time of day for exercise to maximize cognitive benefits in patients with T2DM-MCI and to elucidate underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. We will examine whether glycemic control mediates the relationship between exercise and cognitive function improvement. This research is expected to provide "time-specific" evidence for exercise prescription to maximize the neurocognitive benefits and mitigate dementia risk in this population. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: [http://www.chictr.org.cn], identifier [ChiCTR2300073737].

title: Differential and directional body coupling analysis in Parkinsonian gait.
authors: Zahir A, Yu J, Jun JS, Park K, Kim R, Jeong H.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. Objective and accessible approaches for quantifying inter-limb and cross-directional coupling during gait remain limited in clinical settings. Using a prospectively collected dataset of individuals with PD and healthy controls (HC), we propose a comprehensive analytical framework based on human pose estimation to extract time-series kinematic signals from key body landmarks. Coupling strengths between body segments were quantified to characterize whole-body coordination patterns. Statistical filtering identified discriminative body coupling factors that significantly differentiated PD from HC. The identified factors demonstrated clear and consistent alterations in coordination patterns across groups. Furthermore, multiple machine learning classifiers validated their discriminative capacity, achieving robust classification performance. Correlation analyses between the top 10 pre-specified directional body coupling factors and MDS-UPDRS III scores demonstrated modest but statistically significant associations in the full PD cohort (n = 121), with 8 of 10 factors surviving FDR correction (ρ=0.27-0.31). These associations suggest that directional body coupling metrics capture clinically relevant variation in motor impairment severity beyond binary PD versus HC discrimination and may serve as potential digital biomarkers of PD-related motor dysfunction. Subtype-stratified analyses were conducted only as exploratory supplementary analyses, and larger, more balanced subtype cohorts are required before subtype-specific conclusions can be drawn. Overall, body coupling metrics provide reliable biomechanical markers of PD-related gait impairment and support the clinical potential of this non-invasive and cost-effective pipeline for early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Resisted Anterior Drawer (RAD) Test for Lateral Elbow Instability in Lateral Epicondylitis.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Caekebeke P, van Riet R.
abstract: Background Lateral epicondylitis (LE) is increasingly recognized as a multifactorial condition in which subtle lateral elbow instability may contribute to persistent pain. However, reliable clinical tests to detect such instability are lacking. Purpose To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the resisted anterior drawer (RAD) test for detecting lateral elbow instability in patients with LE. Methods Consecutive adult patients diagnosed with LE underwent standardized clinical examination followed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The RAD test was considered positive when pain during resisted wrist extension, with the elbow in extension, decreased by at least 1 point on a visual analogue scale (VAS) with anteromedial stabilization of the radial head. MRI-defined instability was defined as the presence of lateral collateral ligament (LCL) injury, posterior sagging, or ulnohumeral joint-line opening of grade ≥1. Diagnostic indices were calculated with 95% confidence intervals and likelihood ratios, and the continuous reduction in pain was evaluated with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results A total of 500 elbows were analyzed (mean age: 51 years). MRI evidence of instability was present in 57.4% of elbows. The RAD test demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.8% (95% CI 92.8-97.6%), specificity of 82.2% (95% CI 76.5-86.7%), and overall accuracy of 90.0% (95% CI 87.1-92.3%), with positive and negative likelihood ratios of 5.4 and 0.05. The area under the ROC curve for the reduction in pain was 0.92 (95% CI 0.90-0.95). The magnitude of pain reduction during the RAD maneuver correlated with the severity of MRI-defined instability (Spearman ρ = -0.71). Increasing MRI severity was associated with a higher number of corticosteroid infiltrations, whereas symptom duration showed only a weak association with structural instability. Conclusion In this Level III diagnostic study, the RAD test showed high sensitivity and good specificity for MRI-defined lateral elbow instability in patients with LE, and the magnitude of pain reduction was correlated with MRI-defined severity. These findings suggest that the RAD test may be a useful screening maneuver for instability-related pain in patients with LE. A prospective, blinded cohort study with an independent reference standard is required to confirm its clinical utility. Level of evidence Level III, Diagnostic Study.

title: Development and evaluation of the first fully 3D-printed 5-mm laparoscopic grasper for surgical training.
authors: Lubet A, Renaux-Petel M, Desmaret C, Sibert L, Delbreilh L, Liard A.
abstract: Background Laparoscopic skill acquisition requires extensive training, but the cost of instruments and simulators limits access, particularly in resource-limited settings. Additive manufacturing could provide low-cost, reproducible training instruments, yet fully 3D-printed laparoscopic graspers reproducing standard clinical dimensions have not been reported. We describe the iterative development and bench-trainer evaluation of the Space Child Laparoscopic Grasper (SCLG), the first fully 3D-printed 5-mm laparoscopic grasper. Methods The SCLG was designed in Fusion 360 and printed from a single photopolymer resin by masked stereolithography. More than twenty prototypes were developed through iterative design-test-redesign cycles. Three bench-trainer evaluation phases compared each SCLG version with a conventional grasper on two tasks (elastic band transfer and peg transfer): feasibility (V1, 16 novices), post-redesign (V2, 37 novices), and expert validation (V3, 10 experienced laparoscopic surgeons). Outcomes were task completion time, object drops, mechanical failures, all-inclusive production cost, and a modified GOALS score. Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used. Results V1 had a 25% mechanical failure rate, 50% of novices reached the time limit, and peg-transfer drops exceeded those with the conventional grasper (7.8 (2.7) vs 2.6 (2.9), p = 0.002). After redesign (V2), no mechanical failures occurred, only 2.7% of novices reached the time limit, and object drops no longer differed significantly. In expert validation, no failures occurred and all surgeons reached the maximum GOALS score (ceiling effect), but completion times remained longer than with the conventional grasper (elastic band transfer: 56.4 vs 33.9 s, p = 0.002; peg transfer: 57.4 vs 42.9 s, p = 0.074); the SCLG was therefore not equivalent. The all-inclusive production cost was approximately €10 per instrument, including €1.50 of resin. Conclusions A fully 3D-printed 5-mm laparoscopic grasper is feasible for simulation-based training. Iterative design optimization, without changing the material, markedly improved reliability and performance. Although not equivalent to a conventional grasper, the SCLG's low production cost and reproducibility make it a promising training tool.

title: Destructive spondyloarthropathy mimicking infectious spondylitis in long-term hemodialysis patients: a two-case report with contrasting outcomes.
authors: Kim SG, Jeong YH, Park GJ, Kim KR.
abstract: Destructive spondyloarthropathy (DSA) is a rare complication of long-term hemodialysis that often mimics infectious spondylitis, making diagnosis challenging. We report two patients with chronic kidney disease on long-term hemodialysis who presented with progressive neurological deficits and destructive spinal lesions suggestive of infection. In both cases, percutaneous biopsy of the lumbar destructive lesions showed no definitive evidence of infection, although occult infection could not be completely excluded. A 56-year-old woman underwent cervical reconstruction and achieved significant neurological recovery with solid fusion at 24 months. In contrast, a 62-year-old man underwent lumbar reconstruction but developed severe postoperative wound complications and died following a fatal cardiac event. These cases highlight the importance of considering DSA in the differential diagnosis of destructive spinal lesions in hemodialysis patients. Histological confirmation is essential before definitive treatment, and surgical outcomes depend not only on technical success but also on the patient's systemic condition and comorbidities.

title: Descriptive Case Volume Should Not Be Used as a Credentialing Standard.
authors: Whelan J.

title: Defining and predicting outcomes of a work-injuries rehabilitation program through multivariate baseline phenotypes and longitudinal modeling.
authors: Bayattork M, Carter T, Walton DM.
abstract: Objective To characterize short-term pain and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) recovery trajectories in injured workers undergoing standardized musculoskeletal rehabilitation. We also examined whether multidimensional baseline phenotypes derived from brief self-report measures predicted these trajectories and subsequent recovery. Methods Adults with work-related musculoskeletal injuries were enrolled at entry into a community-based rehabilitation program (N = 146), of whom 134 contributed to pain and 138 to HRQoL trajectory analyses. Participants were classified into one of 4 latent profiles at intake from a prior analysis: Localized/Resilient (57.0%), Mood-Dominant (21.8%), Neurosensory-Dominant (12.7%), and Complex/Central (8.5%). Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) and HRQoL (EQ-5D-5L index) were measured at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks; self-rated global recovery, self-reported return-to-work status, and administrative discharge/ongoing-care codes were collected at 8 weeks. Growth mixture modeling defined NPRS and EQ-5D-5L trajectories. Odds ratios (ORs) quantified associations between baseline classes and "No Recovery/No Improvement" trajectories, as well as point outcomes. Results Three pain trajectories (Rapid Recovery 34.1%, Incomplete Recovery 42.2%, No Recovery 23.7%) and two QoL trajectories (Good QoL 86.2%, No Improvement 13.8%) were identified. Compared with the Localized/Resilient baseline class, odds of NPRS No Recovery were higher in the Mood-Dominant (OR 3.97, 95%CI 1.32-11.92), Neurosensory‑Dominant (OR 10.99, 3.20-37.38), and Complex, Central (OR 22.67, 4.76-107.90) classes, with similarly graded increases for EQ‑5D‑5L No Recovery (ORs 9.00, 7.50, and 150.00, respectively), although estimates for the small Complex/Central subgroup were imprecise. The Complex /Central class also had higher odds of self-reported "not fully returned to work" (OR 4.18, 1.05-16.64) and being coded as "requires ongoing care" (OR 5.74, 1.93-17.11) relative to Localized/Resilient, whereas self-rated global recovery showed no significant between-class differences. Conclusions Brief, fully self-reported, multivariate phenotypes obtained at program entry stratify acutely injured workers into likely rehabilitation outcomes in the short term. These findings support the potential value of integrating mechanism-informed phenotyping with trajectory modeling to inform stratified, risk-guided musculoskeletal rehabilitation.

title: Deep-learning side-channel analysis of embedded ML-KEM: Single-trace message recovery, cross-device generalization, and frequency-band leakage characterization.
authors: Kuo CW, Hung YI, Lin KL.
abstract: Quantum computing undermines traditional public-key cryptosystems like RSA and ECC, prompting NIST to standardize Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) as a core Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) scheme in August 2024. Despite its theoretical security, ML-KEM's practical vulnerability in embedded systems remains underexplored. This study evaluates ML-KEM on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller under deep learning(DL)-based side-channel attacks (DL-SCA), revealing that a single power trace enables 32-byte message recovery with 99.98% accuracy, while cross-device testing across three chips achieves over 99% accuracy, highlighting critical DL-driven threats. To better understand the spectral characteristics exploited by deep-learning-based side-channel attacks, we conduct a controlled frequency-band sensitivity study using Butterworth and Chebyshev low-pass filters applied to recorded traces. Across different cutoff frequencies and filter orders, the validation accuracy decreases substantially under aggressive attenuation, indicating that a significant fraction of exploitable leakage resides in higher-frequency components. Rather than claiming that offline digital filtering constrains a realistic adversary, we interpret these results as evidence for where leakage-sensitive information is concentrated, thereby providing guidance for implementable countermeasures such as masking, shuffling, desynchronization, and acquisition-path power/EM conditioning in embedded PQC systems. This cost-efficient solution requires no algorithm/hardware modifications, emphasizing the urgency of implementation-level protections for secure PQC deployment in resource-constrained systems.

title: Common acetabular fracture patterns in patients with femoroacetabular impingement.
authors: Garlapaty AR, Townsley S, Touhey DC, Walz JW, Duren D, Cook JL, Crist BD.
abstract: Introduction The incidence of acetabular fractures is rising, affecting both younger and elderly patient populations. Developmental abnormalities such as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and hip dysplasia alter hip biomechanics, potentially predisposing younger patients to fracture. FAI, resulting from a cam and/or pincer deformity, is common, affecting 25% of asymptomatic males and 5% of asymptomatic females, and has been linked to hip pain and early osteoarthritis. However, the relationship between FAI morphology and acetabular fracture pattern remains unclear. Methods Patients, 18-55 years old, treated between 2005 and 2023 for acetabular fracture, hip dislocation, or femoral head fracture were reviewed for FAI morphology using the Judet and Letournel classification systems. Statistical comparisons were conducted using Fisher's exact tests and unpaired t-tests, with significance set at p Results A total of 294 patients (72%) exhibited plain radiographic FAI morphology, while 115 (28%) served as controls. The most common fracture pattern in both groups was posterior wall (PW) fractures (23.1% FAI, 31.3% control). Male FAI patients were significantly more likely to experience transverse fractures (p = 0.032, OR=4.6) and posterior column plus PW fractures (p = 0.035, OR=2.5) than controls. Among FAI patients, posterior column fractures were significantly more likely to occur in females (p = 0.011, OR=19). A total of 31 (27.0%) control patients and 63 (21.4%) FAI patients experienced complications. Conclusions In our data set, FAI patients accounted for 72% of patients undergoing acetabular fracture ORIF. FAI patients most commonly sustained posterior wall fractures, but male FAI patients had a significantly higher rate of transverse and posterior column plus PW. FAI patients experienced a complication rate of 21.4% compared to 27.0% in non-FAI patients.

title: Climate change-driven compound dust storm and heatwave extremes in Central Asia under future CMIP6 scenarios.
authors: Broomandi P, Bagheri M, Middleton N, Mozhdehi Fard A, Fathian A, Ledari DG, Yapiyev V, Radelyuk I, Leuchner M, Kim JR.
abstract: Central Asia (CA) faces rising temperatures and shifting atmospheric conditions, increasing the urgency to address extreme events like heatwaves and dust storms. This study examines the co-evolution and regional co-variability of heatwaves and atmospheric dust loading, represented by dust extinction aerosol optical thickness (AOT). Using a multi-model ensemble of CMIP6 General Circulation Models (GCMs) and high-resolution reanalysis datasets, we analyzed heatwave indices alongside AOT across six clusters from 1992 to 2100. Results show a substantial rise in heatwave activity, with increases in heatwave frequency and intensity projected across much of CA, particularly under future emission scenarios. AOT trends vary regionally, with both increasing and decreasing trends across clusters, periods, and emission scenarios. Spatial and temporal correlations, evaluated with Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (BH-FDR) correction for multiple location-level tests, show regionally heterogeneous dust-heatwave co-variability, with both positive and negative associations across clusters and scenarios. The strongest FDR-supported relationships occur in selected cluster-index combinations, indicating localized and scenario-dependent co-variability rather than a uniform compound dust-heatwave signal across CA. These findings highlight the need for targeted adaptation strategies for CA, which faces intensifying heatwaves and spatially variable dust-related atmospheric conditions. This study supports early warning systems, risk assessments, and mitigation and resilience measures to safeguard vulnerable communities and ecosystems and strengthen resilience to these hazards in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030.

title: Central sensitization partially mediates the relationship between obesity and functional impairment across fibromyalgia and related rheumatic disorders.
authors: Osuna-Diaz MM, Sebastian KR, Nuguri SM, de Lamo Castellvi S, Yu L, Giusti MM, Mikulik Z, Rodriguez-Saona L, Hackshaw KV.
abstract: Background Obesity is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to chronic pain and disability, yet its relationship with central sensitization and symptom burden across rheumatic diseases remains incompletely characterized. While elevated body mass index (BMI) has been associated with worse outcomes in fibromyalgia (FM), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), few studies have evaluated these relationships simultaneously using multidimensional symptom measures and central sensitization assessments. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of prospectively collected baseline data from Ohio State University (recruitment 2018-2025) and the University of Texas at Austin (recruitment beginning September 2020). Participants had fibromyalgia (FM), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or were healthy controls. When both the Revised Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQR) and Symptom Impact Questionnaire (SIQR) were completed, FIQR was retained under the study harmonization rule. Models adjusted for age, sex, race, diagnosis, and study site. Results The baseline cohort comprised 1240 participants (FM 843, RA 194, SLE 127, healthy controls 76). The adjusted continuous-BMI FIQR/SIQR model included 918 observations and estimated a 4.13-point increase in symptom impact per standard-deviation higher BMI (95% CI 2.83-5.43; p Conclusions Higher BMI was associated with greater symptom impact and worse functional outcomes across rheumatic diagnostic groups. CSI statistically accounted for part of the BMI-symptom-impact association, but causal mediation cannot be established from cross-sectional data. Key Points • Increasing BMI was independently associated with greater disability, pain burden, and reduced physical functioning across fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus. • Central sensitization partially mediated the relationship between obesity and functional impairment. • The strongest obesity-related associations involved physical function, pain severity, and fibromyalgia-related disability, supporting a transdiagnostic pattern across inflammatory and non-inflammatory rheumatic disorders • Obesity may represent a modifiable upstream contributor to central sensitization and disability.

title: CT attenuation changes across freeze-thaw preservation states in donated bodies: a preliminary multi-organ anatomical analysis.
authors: Lodolo E, Vara G, Lodi S, Forni L, Tulipano Di Franco F, Gelmi CAE, Leto S, Boschetti E, Manzoli L, Ratti S.
abstract: Purpose To establish the thermal preservation state as a critical pre-analytical variable in quantitative post-mortem CT of donated bodies, with the aim of enabling reliable multi-donor comparisons, improving the performance of automated segmentation tools, and providing a translational experimental model applicable to CT-guided thermal interventions. Material and methods Eight body donors underwent whole-body CT in up to three preservation states: fresh, frozen (- 20 °C), and thawed. CT datasets were automatically segmented using TotalSegmentator in 3D Slicer. Mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values were extracted for major organs and tissue groups. The primary analysis was within-donor: Friedman tests with Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc comparisons in donors with complete data (n = 7), complemented by linear mixed-effects models using all available scans. Results Freezing produced a consistent reduction in CT attenuation across all soft tissues and muscle, with near-complete recovery after thawing. In the primary repeated-measures analysis, preservation state had a significant effect after FDR correction in six of the nine tissue groups (liver, spleen, brain, aorta, pancreas and muscle; q = 0.023-0.042), but not in kidney, heart or bone. Brain and pancreas showed the strongest effects (Kendall's W = 0.80 and 0.76). In the liver, the median within-donor change was - 59.7 HU at freezing and + 60.3 HU at thawing. Mixed-effects models confirmed a significant reduction at freezing in liver, spleen, brain, kidney, pancreas and muscle (β = -35.1 to -52.7 HU) and no residual difference after thawing in any tissue group. Bone attenuation remained stable across all preservation states. Conclusion Freeze-thaw preservation systematically alters CT attenuation in soft tissues while minimally affecting bone. Preservation state should therefore be considered a critical pre-analytical variable in quantitative post-mortem CT, particularly for studies relying on automated segmentation, radiomics, and translational applications involving thermal tissue imaging.

title: CORR Insights®: Is the Parkinson Disease Diagnosis-to-Surgery Interval Associated With 5-year Vascular and Periprosthetic Outcomes After TKA? A Nationwide Large-database Study.
authors: Meermans G.

title: Bladder involvement in Sjögren's disease: a single-centre cohort study of clinical phenotype and therapeutic response.
authors: Xu C, Yao L, Wang H, Huang Y, Xu Z, Li Y.

title: Biomarker trajectories and risk of relapse in giant cell arteritis: a multicenter study.
authors: Pichon S, Leurs A, Mortain L, Behal H, Dalhi N, Jouvray M, Koether V, Ledoult E, Chepy A, Hachulla E, Sobanski V, Launay D, Lambert M.
abstract: Objective The relative value of plasma fibrinogen (PF) compared with C-reactive protein (CRP) for longitudinal monitoring in giant cell arteritis (GCA) is uncertain. We assessed their performance as biomarkers of disease activity and predictors of relapse. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of 465 patients diagnosed with GCA between 2000 and 2023 fulfilling GiACTA inclusion criteria. Baseline demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were collected. In a subset of 135 patients diagnosed from 2017 to 2022, CRP and PF were collected until relapse or up to 2 years. Associations between biomarker dynamics and relapse were analyzed using joint modeling. Results Among 465 patients, 34.2% experienced ≥ 1 relapse within 5 years. At diagnosis, headache, jaw claudication and aortic FDG uptake on PET-CT were associated with higher relapse risk. PF normalization at 1 month was associated with a lower relapse risk over 2 years (HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.28; p Conclusion In our GCA cohort, relapse risk was associated with cranial manifestations and aortic uptake on PET-CT at diagnosis. PF normalization at 1 month was identified as an early marker of a lower relapse risk, although this biomarker requires external validation. CRP and PF trajectories identified distinct phenotypes associated with different relapse risks, supporting further evaluation of longitudinal biomarker-guided follow-up.

title: Beyond Return to Sport: Is the Early Postretirement Period a Missed Opportunity for Rehabilitation and Lifelong Physical Activity?
authors: Williamson CJ.

title: Association between habitual MSG consumption and compulsive eating behaviors in university students: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Al Jabry LK, Shawwa A, Sarhan Y, Issa R, Abweh O, Qashqeesh H, Alagha H.
abstract: Background Monosodium glutamate (MSG), a widely used flavor enhancer, increases food palatability and may influence eating behavior. Although considered safe from a toxicological perspective, its potential association with compulsive eating patterns remains unclear. University students are particularly vulnerable to irregular dietary habits and high consumption of ultra-processed foods. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 555 Palestinian university students aged 18-30 years. MSG intake was assessed using a composite dietary exposure scale and categorized into tertiles (low, moderate, high). Food addiction was measured using the Yale Food Addiction Scale (YFAS), binge-eating severity using the Binge Eating Scale (BES), and perceived stress using the Perceived Stress Scale-4 (PSS-4). Logistic regression examined associations between MSG intake and food addiction, while linear regression assessed relationships with binge-eating severity and YFAS symptom counts, adjusting for age, gender, BMI, perceived stress, and academic year. Results Food addiction was present in 24.7% of participants and increased across MSG tertiles (15.7% low vs. 33.0% high; p Conclusions Higher MSG intake was associated with increased food addiction symptoms and binge-eating severity among university students, suggesting frequent consumption of flavor-enhanced foods is a correlate of reward-driven eating behaviors, warranting further investigation.

title: Association Between Early Joint Awareness and Falls After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
authors: Wada O, Nagai K, Igeta M, Mori A, Mizuno K.
abstract: Background The Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12) is a patient-reported outcome measure of joint awareness after total hip arthroplasty (THA). Falls after THA remain clinically important. However, longitudinal evidence regarding the associations among early FJS-12, subsequent falls, and later recovery of joint unawareness remains limited. Methods This retrospective cohort study used a prospectively maintained institutional database from a single Japanese institution. Consecutive patients who underwent primary THA between January 2021 and December 2023 were included. FJS-12 was assessed at 3 and 12 months postoperatively, and falls occurring between 3 and 12 months postoperatively were identified at the 12-month visit based on patients' self-report over this 9-month interval. Modified Poisson regression was used to examine the association between FJS at 3 months and subsequent falls. Multiple linear regression was used to examine the association between fall occurrence and FJS at 12 months, adjusting for FJS at 3 months. Results Overall, 623 patients were analyzed (mean age 70.8 years; 85.2% female). Ninety-nine patients (15.9%) experienced at least 1 fall between 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Lower FJS at 3 months was associated with a higher risk of subsequent falls. Fall occurrence was associated with lower FJS at 12 months, independent of FJS at 3 months and other covariates. Conclusions Early postoperative joint awareness was associated with subsequent falls after THA, and falls were associated with lower FJS at 12 months. The FJS-12 may provide additional patient-reported information when assessing postoperative fall risk.

title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
authors: Dinesh A, Poursalehian M, Billow D, Peirish RW, Cereijo C, Padubidri A, Patterson B, Vallier HA.
abstract: Background Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery. Methods A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed. Results Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025. Conclusions ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

title: Anti-phosphatidylserine/prothrombin antibodies in antiphospholipid syndrome: Clinical associations and methodological heterogeneity-a scoping review.
authors: Parikh H, Gobbo G, Colesanti M, Dass J, Esteve-Valverde E, Alijotas-Reig J, Simioni P, Hoxha A.
abstract: Objective To map the clinical and laboratory evidence for anti-phosphatidylserine/prothrombin (aPS/PT) antibodies in antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), identify the settings in which testing may add value beyond conventional antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL), and define the methodological barriers to wider clinical implementation. Methods We conducted a prospectively registered scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for human studies published from January 2000 onward that evaluated aPS/PT antibodies in APS or seronegative APS (SN-APS). Clinical associations, laboratory correlations, assay characteristics, cut-off definitions, titre reporting, and persistence were synthesized descriptively. Results Fifty-eight studies were included. Associations with thrombosis were evaluated in 36 studies, of which 32 reported a positive relationship. Pregnancy morbidity was assessed in 36 studies, with 21 reporting a positive association, although outcome definitions were highly variable. The most consistent laboratory finding was the association between aPS/PT and lupus anticoagulant (LA): 31 of 35 studies reported a positive relationship. Twenty-two studies included patients with SN-APS, but only six specifically examined aPS/PT in this population. Commercial assays were used in 42 studies, predominantly ELISA, yet cut-off selection, titre reporting, and confirmation of persistence varied substantially. Only 11 studies assessed persistence at least 12 weeks apart. Conclusions aPS/PT antibodies show a reproducible clinical and laboratory signal across the APS spectrum, but their immediate value is most likely as a selective adjunct in diagnostically challenging settings rather than as a universal fourth criterion antibody. Prospective multicentre studies using harmonized assays must establish whether aPS/PT provides independent diagnostic or prognostic information beyond LA and conventional aPL profiles.

title: Academic entitlement and student well-being: The mediating role of the impostor phenomenon.
authors: Alsuwaylim AM, Alsharif BA, Abdellatif MS, Rahmath M, Ibrahim AR, Nemtallah MA.
abstract: Despite growing evidence linking academic entitlement to diminished student outcomes, the psychological mechanisms through which entitled academic expectations erode student well-being remain insufficiently understood. The present study examines the mediating role of the impostor phenomenon in the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being among university students. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed with a sample of 864 undergraduate students recruited from Al-Azhar University and Kafr El-Sheikh University in Egypt. Participants completed the Academic Entitlement Scale (AES-28), the Short Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS-10), and the BBC Well-Being Scale (BBC-WBS). Mediation analysis was conducted using the PROCESS macro with bootstrapping based on 5,000 resamples. Results revealed that academic entitlement significantly and positively predicted the impostor phenomenon, which in turn significantly and negatively predicted student well-being. The impostor phenomenon partially mediated the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being, accounting for approximately 23% of the total effect. These findings suggest that entitlement-driven expectations are associated with lower overall well-being (composite score), both directly and indirectly by fostering fraudulence-related self-doubt. Mediation was not tested separately for psychological, physical, and relational well-being. Universities, particularly in comparable Egyptian and collectivist contexts, may consider addressing both entitled academic attitudes and impostor-related cognitions through counseling interventions and pedagogical strategies.

title: A three process approach for insomnia-like awakenings.
authors: Rowland Adams J, Angelova M.
abstract: Mathematical modelling of sleep is a growing field, with an increasing number of applications to sleep disorders. However, despite its high prevalence and under-diagnosis worldwide, insomnia has not been among these disorders. We chart the development of sleep models and investigate the hypothesis that they can be simply modified to model insomnia, ultimately introducing a new model focusing on nocturnal awakenings as a starting point of insomnia-like behaviour, based on a three process approach. We find that several of these models can make promising steps towards producing nighttime awakenings characteristic of many types of insomnia with minor modifications, but that none can fully reproduce every key criterion with only minor adaptations. In particular, we find that the stability of the sleeping state is an important factor in more complex contemporary neuronal population models' abilities to incorporate awakenings, with both permanently stable and permanently non-stable sleep proving to be obstacles. Instead, we base our new model on the simpler foundational two process model, incorporating an original, quantitative wakefulness drive. We further analyse the sensitivity of its new parameters and the statistical properties of the nighttime awakening phenomena it produces. This new drive includes both physiology-based arousal impulses and environmental and psychological disturbances, and provides the foundation of a new approach to future quantitative modelling of insomnia phenotypes.

title: Total Knee Arthroplasty as the Initial and Definitive Treatment for the Multiligament Injured Knee.
authors: Williams WA, Mason EM, Daniel AV, Holliday CL, Courington RM, Langford JR, Kupizewski SJ, Stuart MJ, Levy BA, Haidukewych GJ.
abstract: Background Multiligament knee injuries (MLKIs) are complex injury patterns that pose challenges for patients and surgeons alike. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical and functional perioperative outcomes of a cohort of patients with evidence of pre-existing knee osteoarthritic changes that underwent total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as the initial and definitive treatment for MLKI. Methods Patients from 2 tertiary care centers that underwent TKA as primary treatment for their MLKI within 1 year from their initial time of injury were retrospectively identified for study inclusion. Range of motion, and Knee Society Scores were evaluated for all patients. Perioperative complications as well as TKA component types and degrees of implant constraint were also analyzed. Results Twelve patients met study inclusion criteria. Mean follow-up time was 40 months (range 24 to 86 mos). Mean time from MLKI to TKA was 5 months (range 3 days to 11 months). Mean age was 61 years (range 51 to 78). Mean postoperative knee range of motion was 1-106 degrees at last follow-up. Knee Society Scores improved by an average of 129 points at last follow-up. Two patients required rotating hinge TKA components with all others requiring lesser degrees of implant constraint. There were no instances of postoperative knee instability and no patients required revision TKA surgery at last follow-up. Conclusions TKA is a viable primary treatment option for MLKI in older patients with pre-existing multicompartmental knee osteoarthritis. In this patient population, TKA may allow for improved function and adequate stability of the multiligament injured knee. Study design Retrospective case series. Level of evidence IV.

title: Tibiofemoral and patellofemoral kinematics after kinematic versus mechanical alignment in varus TKA-a dynamic knee rig study.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Simon JM, Siedow TM, Thorwächter C, Petri TE, Bauer L, Holzapfel BM, Müller PE, Niethammer TR.
abstract: Introduction Kinematic alignment (KA) in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) of the varus knee shows promising clinical outcomes by preserving individual joint anatomy. However, it remains unknown whether this results in knee joint kinematics that more closely resemble the native baseline condition than mechanical alignment (MA). Therefore, this study evaluated the direct influence of KA versus MA on tibiofemoral and patellofemoral kinematics and contact biomechanics in the varus knee during a standardized dynamic muscle-loaded squat. Materials and methods Seven fresh-frozen human cadaveric knee specimens with constitutional varus (-1.4° to -8.3°) were tested in a dynamic knee rig (30° to 130° flexion) under muscle-controlled loading. Kinematics, retropatellar contact area, peak pressure, and quadriceps force were continuously recorded across three successive states within the same specimen: native, KA TKA, and MA TKA using a medial-pivot implant design. Statistical analysis was performed using one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping, including non-parametric SnPM1D ANOVA and pairwise SnPM{F} tests for kinematics, and paired-samples SPM{t} tests for contact mechanics and quadriceps force. Results Between alignment techniques (KA vs. MA), no statistically significant differences emerged regarding kinematics and patellofemoral biomechanics following Holm-Bonferroni correction (all p adj > 0.05). Descriptively, KA displayed a trend toward unphysiological anterior femoral translation in deep flexion (100°-120°, p = 0.028; p adj = 0.084) and persistent patellar medialization (delta of up to 5 mm) compared to MA, though these did not retain statistical significance post-adjustment. Both TKA techniques significantly reduced patellar contact area (p adj Conclusions KA was not shown to restore native knee kinematics or patellofemoral mechanics more closely than MA. Descriptive kinematic variations suggest that KA does not automatically optimize functional joint mechanics when using standard implant geometries.

title: The growing burden of infectious arthritis in Germany: a nationwide analysis of epidemiology, mortality, and contemporary inpatient care.
authors: Anees H, Muelke M, Merkel PM, Heiss C, El Khassawna T.
abstract: Purpose Infectious arthritis is a destructive joint infection associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. We characterised long-term changes in its inpatient epidemiology and outcomes in Germany and complemented these trends with contemporary nationwide inpatient data. Methods Nationwide hospital discharge data for pyogenic arthritis (ICD-10-GM M00) were obtained from the German Federal Health Monitoring database for 2000-2023. Hospitalisations, age-standardised rates, demographic patterns, pathogen-specific diagnostic codes, in-hospital mortality, and length of stay were analysed. Nationwide Diagnosis-Related Group data from 2019 to 2024 characterised contemporary inpatient and procedural patterns. Temporal trends were assessed by log-linear regression. Results Annual hospitalisations increased from 6,088 in 2000 to 21,051 in 2023 (annual percentage change [APC] 5.28%, 95% CI 4.54-6.03; P Conclusion Infectious arthritis represents a growing inpatient burden in Germany, with increases persisting after age standardisation and accompanied by rising crude in-hospital mortality. The findings support continued surveillance and studies integrating administrative, clinical, and microbiological data.

title: The Ghana Surgical Dialogue: A Whole-of-Society Innovation for Advancing Safe Surgery, Obstetric, Trauma, and Anesthesia Care in Ghana.
authors: Dzirasa ID, Hesse A, Mills JN, Akrofi RA, Hirpe KA, Arthaud L, Titiati P, Agyei-Tuffour E, Selormey R, Ayala R.
abstract: Ghana continues to face major gaps in access to safe surgery, obstetric, trauma, and anesthesia (SOTA) care, especially at district level, where workforce shortages, infrastructure deficits, weak referral systems, and limited data constrain service delivery. To support implementation of the Ghana National Surgical, Obstetric and Anesthesia Plan (NSOAP) 2025-2029, the Ministry of Health convened the inaugural Ghana Surgical Dialogue in Koforidua in August 2025. The Dialogue brought together government, professional associations, clinicians, nurses, biomedical engineers, laboratory professionals, health managers, financiers, civil society, and international partners to identify practical solutions for strengthening SOTA care.
