Key innovations included alignment of SOTA priorities with national budgeting, exploration of public-private partnership models such as build-operate-transfer schemes, investment in district-level mentorship and telemedicine, improved surgical safety and audit culture, and development of biomedical equipment management systems. Participants also emphasized workforce retention, career progression for anesthetists and perioperative nurses, ring-fenced funding, interoperable data systems, and stronger referral networks. The Dialogue demonstrated that sustainable progress in surgical care requires a whole-of-society approach that combines policy, financing, workforce development, technology, and accountability. This report highlights implementation lessons from Ghana that may be useful to other countries seeking to translate surgical plans into action.

title: The Effect of EVOLVE Radial Head Arthroplasty Stem Tilt on Clinical Outcomes.
journal: Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery
authors: Tat J, Kheiran A, Grewal R, Athwal GS, Faber KJ, Drosdowech DS, King GJW.
abstract: Introduction Radial head arthroplasty (RHA) mal-alignment can occur when there is excessive tilt of the radial head stem relative to the radial canal. The etiology, clinical significance and management for increased RHA tilt is poorly understood. Our primary objective was to compare clinical outcomes in patients with excessive radiographic RHA tilt to controls. A secondary objective was to determine the relationship between radiographic stem alignment measurements and clinical outcomes. Methods We performed a retrospective chart review of patients who underwent a smooth stem RHA (EVOLVE, Wright Medical) between 1999 - 2021 for acute radial head fractures requiring isolated RHA. Patient demographics, clinical outcomes scores (PREE, QuickDASH, MEPI), range of motion, complications, reoperations, and radiographic measurements were compared between patients with excessive RHA tilt and controls. Radial head alignment was assessed using several parameters including radial neck-shaft angle, lateral overhang distance RHA implant, proximal radioulnar joint angle, radial neck length, radial neck width, radial neck cut angle, radial tuberosity width, and radiocapitellar line. Excessive RHA tilt was defined as patients with a high-neck shaft angle (greater than 1 Standard Deviation above the mean), while controls had a neck-shaft angle less than 1 Standard Deviation. Regression modelling was used to determine whether the radiographic alignment parameters correlate with of outcomes (PREE, QuickDASH, MEPI), complications and reoperations. A subgroup analysis compared radiographic tilt at 6 weeks and 1 year postoperatively. Results Sixty-one patients were included in the study, 10 patients with mal-alignment of the RHA and 51 patients in the control group. There was no significant difference in patient characteristics between groups (age, gender, handedness, smoking, time to surgery, follow-up time) (p>0.01). The tilt group demonstrated greater neck-shaft angles, RHA lateral overhang, PRUJ angles, and implant lucency, with shorter radial neck lengths and lower radial neck cut angles (all p 2 =0.14, F 1,54 =9.7, p=0.003) and MEPI scores (R 2 =0.10, F 1,53 =7.3, p=0.009). Excessive tilt was more commonly observed at late rather than early follow-up. Conclusion A cohort of patients with excessive RHA tilt cohort had worse overall clinical outcomes scores when compared to the control group, however they did not demonstrate higher rates of complications or revision surgery. In this patient cohort, excessive implant tilt developed late after surgery rather than in early follow-up.

title: Technology Assisted Intraoperative Anatomic Visualization: Surgeon Perspectives and Unmet Needs.
authors: Sakref Y, Adams ME, Chen P, Cosby Z, Davis-Lopez K, Morris AM, Li Z, Holsinger FC, Jopling JK, Knowlton LM.
abstract: Background Iatrogenic injury to critical anatomic structures remains a leading source of surgical morbidity, most commonly due to visual misperception rather than technical error. Despite a rapidly expanding ecosystem of intraoperative visualization adjuncts, the surgeon's perspective on current limitations and unmet needs has not been evaluated. The objective of this study was to characterize practicing surgeons' experiences with intraoperative anatomical visualization, the strategies and adjuncts they currently employ, the perceived limitations of available technologies, and the features they would prioritize in future solutions. Methods Qualitative study using semi-structured one-on-one interviews conducted between September 2025 and March 2026 at a single large academic medical center in the United States. Purposive sampling was used to recruit attending surgeons and fellows representing a range of surgical specialties and levels of experience. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using a deductive and inductive thematic approach with team-based coding. Data analysis was conducted from October 2025 to April 2026. Outcomes were themes reflecting surgeons' perspectives on intraoperative visualization, current adjunct use, barriers to adoption of new technologies, and features of an ideal solution. Results Nineteen attending surgeons and fellows were interviewed (10 [53%] males; 12 [63%] attendings; median duration of independent practice, 14.7 years [IQR, 12.2-19.0]). Five themes emerged: (1) identification of critical structures as a safety imperative tied to injury avoidance and functional preservation; (2) structural, patient-level, and case-level factors as barriers to visualization; (3) reliance on direct visualization supplemented by intraoperative adjuncts and preoperative planning, with adjuncts perceived as imprecise, workflow-disruptive, or limited in depth and specificity; (4) openness to new technology contingent on trade-offs across safety, intraoperative time, cost, operational feasibility, and training implications; and (5) convergence on two paradigms for an ideal solution: real-time, structure-specific identification within the operative field and dynamic superimposition of preoperative imaging onto the operative field. Conclusions Findings from this qualitative study suggest that surgeons evaluate new visualization technologies based on more than clinical effectiveness alone. Grounding the development and evaluation of these technologies in surgeons' experiential knowledge, and engaging explicitly with operational feasibility, cost, training, and equity of access, will improve the likelihood that emerging tools translate into improved intraoperative safety.

title: Synovial plica syndromes: a comprehensive overview from embryology to pathology.
authors: Cerezal A, Cogolludo G, Canga A, Encinas-Ullán CA, Pérez-Carro L, Cruz A, Cerezal L.
abstract: Synovial plicae are folds of synovial tissue in the knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder, representing embryonic remnants of synovial septa. They are usually asymptomatic, but trauma, repetitive microtrauma, or prior surgery can render them thickened and fibrotic, producing pain and mechanical symptoms collectively termed plica syndrome. It is easily overlooked or misdiagnosed because the symptoms are nonspecific and other intra-articular disorders often coexist. This review addresses the embryology, histology, anatomy, clinical presentation, imaging, and treatment of synovial plicae across these joints, with emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. MRI is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating suspected plica syndrome, characterizing the fold and associated abnormalities, and excluding alternative causes of joint pain. Pathologic plicae appear thickened and irregular, with increased signal intensity and frequently associated focal synovitis or adjacent chondral damage. Plica thickness alone has limited diagnostic value, as measurements overlap between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Establishing a diagnosis of symptomatic plica syndrome requires correlation of the imaging findings with the clinical presentation. When joint effusion is absent, magnetic resonance (MR) or computed tomography (CT) arthrography improves delineation of the synovial folds and associated lesions. Plica syndrome occurs most often in young, physically active patients, and management is initially conservative. When symptoms are refractory, arthroscopic resection relieves symptoms, particularly when the plica is the only abnormality and the cartilage is preserved. Most outcome data derive from the knee and the elbow.

title: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome following posterior instrumented correction and fusion of scoliosis managed with structured nutritional escalation.
authors: Rajakaruna DR, Varma N, Alsayyad A, Tambe A.

title: Successful Resection of Transverse Colon Cancer Invading a Reconstructed Jejunum After Pancreaticoduodenectomy: A Case Report.
authors: Oyamada K, Hiyoshi M, Nishida K, Okuno T, Kawasaki H, Kyoden Y.
abstract: The treatment of locally advanced colon cancer is surgically challenging, particularly in patients with prior pancreaticoduodenectomy. Careful assessment after neoadjuvant chemotherapy may enable curative resection while preserving pancreaticobiliary reconstruction. As the postoperative prognosis for pancreaticoduodenectomy improves, similar cases can be expected to increase.

title: State-aware adaptive multimodal fusion for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting using sky cloud images.
authors: Zhao H, Song A, Jin Y, Yu H.
abstract: As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is essential for improving energy utilization and supporting power system operation. However, irradiance variations are jointly influenced by historical trends and rapid cloud changes, making traditional single-modal methods insufficient for capturing complex dynamics under varying weather conditions. This paper proposes a multimodal solar irradiance forecasting framework based on the collaborative representation of sky cloud images and numerical sequences. The framework introduces a heterogeneous modal state encoding mechanism and a state-aware adaptive selective attention fusion mechanism to enhance interactions between visual weather information and historical physical patterns. Specifically, the numerical modality captures irradiance trends and temporal correlations through dependency modeling, while the image modality extracts cloud structures and evolution features through spatiotemporal representation. The proposed fusion mechanism dynamically adjusts modality contributions according to forecasting conditions, enabling effective integration of complementary information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms benchmark models in forecasting accuracy and robustness, validating the effectiveness of combining visual cloud information with numerical evolution patterns for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting.

title: Skin color representation in orthopedic literature.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Goyal RK, Adio AA, Nadiminti H, Black EM, Khan AZ, Horneff JG, Hill BW, Abboud JA.
abstract: Introduction Underrepresentation of skin color in educational materials can undermine diagnostic accuracy and contribute to disparities in orthopedic care for minority populations. While underrepresentation of darker skin types has already been identified in orthopedic literature, this study assessed whether underrepresentation is apparent in open access journals, is uniform across all orthopedic subspecialties, differs between figure types, and has shifted over time as awareness of skin of color disparities has grown. Materials and methods 40,674 figures were accessed from 14 open-access orthopedic journals and assigned a subspecialty and a country of origin based on author affiliation. Automatic filters narrowed the dataset to 4,809 figures. Each figure was processed by a GPT-4o artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline to obtain skin presence (yes/no), figure type (clinical, intraoperative, illustration), Fitzpatrick skin type (I-VI), and a confidence score (1-5). Agreement was high with human review for skin presence and figure type and moderate with a board-certified dermatologist for skin tone, with disagreement biased toward darker ratings. 2,025 skin-containing figures were analyzed. Results Among 2,025 figures, most depicted light skin (65.6%, Fitzpatrick I-II), 29.6% medium (III-IV), and only 4.8% dark (V-VI). This demonstrated severe overrepresentation of light skin (p Conclusions Within open-access orthopedic literature, dark skin is consistently underrepresented and falls short of US and diverse-population benchmarks, regardless of figure type or subspecialty. This systemic pattern narrows the implicit norm of who an orthopedic patient appears to be and warrants editorial attention given documented disparities in orthopedic care.

title: Sex and educational inequalities across functional ability trajectories in Chile: A sequence analysis of a 17-year national panel.
authors: Cabib I, Villalobos Dintrans P, Browne Salas J.
abstract: Context Research on disability and functional ability has increasingly moved from cross-sectional descriptions toward longitudinal analyses of intra-individual change. This shift has shown that functional ability follows heterogeneous pathways, encompassing stability, progressive deterioration, fluctuating limitations, partial recovery, and death. However, evidence remains concentrated in high-income countries, and fewer studies have examined long-term functional ability trajectories in Latin American contexts marked by rapid population aging and high socioeconomic inequality. In addition, comparisons across sex and educational groups require trajectory typologies that are constructed in a way that makes group comparisons methodologically comparable. Methods We used six observation points from the Chilean Social Protection Survey, a nationally representative longitudinal survey, covering the period 2004-2020. The analytic sample included 2,681 individuals aged 46-65 at baseline, contributing 16,086 person-wave observations. Functional ability was measured through self-reported limitations in activities of daily living and classified into five states: no limitation, low limitation, middle limitation, high limitation, and deceased. We reconstructed individual functional ability sequences over 17 years and applied optimal matching followed by hierarchical clustering. To ensure comparability across sex and educational groups, trajectory typologies were estimated within each baseline age group using the full age-group-specific sample. We then examined how membership in these pooled trajectory types varied by sex and educational attainment, referencing the composition of each trajectory type to the overall composition of its baseline age group. Findings Across the four baseline age groups, detailed trajectories were grouped into three broader types: mostly non-declining, progressive-declining, and equivocal-declining. Mostly non-declining trajectories were prevalent in all age groups, although their internal composition changed with baseline age, moving from stable good functional ability in younger age groups toward preserved functional ability before death in older age groups. Progressive-declining trajectories were especially visible among respondents aged 56-60 at baseline and remained substantial among those aged 61-65. Equivocal-declining trajectories were more frequently composed of women, most markedly among respondents aged 61-65 at baseline, and of respondents with primary education or less in the three younger age groups. Sex differences in trajectory membership were statistically significant in all age groups, while educational differences were statistically significant in the first three age groups. Conclusions Long-term functional ability trajectories in Chile are heterogeneous and socially patterned. By deriving pooled trajectory typologies within each baseline age group before comparing sex and educational groups, and by referencing group composition to the marginal composition of each age group, this study provides comparable evidence on how functional aging unfolds across socially stratified groups in an understudied Latin American context.

title: Serum Calprotectin Demonstrates Moderate Diagnostic Performance for Detecting Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
authors: Schelling MH, Schwarze J, Gosheger G, Schneider KN, Bockholt S, Theil C.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a serious complication after total hip and knee arthroplasty, with limited accuracy of conventional biomarkers. This study assessed serum calprotectin (CP) alongside established markers in revision arthroplasty. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 399 patients (232 total knee arthroplasty, 167 total hip arthroplasty). Based on Musculoskeletal Infection Society 2018 criteria, 132 patients were diagnosed with PJI and 267 were classified as non-PJI. All patients underwent serum CP, C-reactive protein (CRP), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) testing; microbiological analyses were performed when indicated. Results Serum CP was significantly higher in PJI than aseptic revisions (median 11,700 ng/mL [interquartile range 8080-18,675] vs 5,440 ng/mL [interquartile range 3600-8300], P Conclusions Serum calprotectin demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance and may may complement conventional serum markers in selected cases in which conventional serum markers are inconclusive.

title: Robotic-assisted versus laparoscopic hysterectomy in Stage I endometrial cancer: a real-world causal mediation analysis of operating time and length of hospital stay.
authors: Jain V, Bhaumik J, Joshi R, Kulkarni Y, Modi KB, Bhati P, Dabas S, Rawal S, Basu K, Ranade RR, Nayyar N, Kapoor P, Roy A, Mishra S, P SS, P V, Pandey P, Dahiya A, Bhaskar R, Sharma I.
abstract: This study estimated the impact of robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) versus laparoscopy (LPS) on operating time (OT), length of hospital stay (LOHS), and examined mediation through perioperative factors. A secondary analysis of individual patient data from a retrospective multicenter study was conducted. Women with histologically confirmed stage I endometrial cancer (EC) undergoing hysterectomy between January 2010 and December 2023 were included. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), baseline covariates achieved standardized mean differences below 0.10. The IPTW-weighted effect estimate of LPS relative to RAS, interpreted as an adjusted association under the assumption of no unmeasured confounding was, 31.4 min for OT (95% CI: 17.8, 46.2) and 0.93 days for LOHS (95% CI: 0.59, 1.34). Blood loss accounted for 11.3 min (36%) of the OT difference and 0.46 days (49%) of the LOHS difference, while other mediators contributed minimally. Direct effects not explained by the measured mediators accounted for 18.6 min (59%) of the OT difference and 0.43 days (46%) of the LOHS difference. At an annual volume of 100 cases, the IPTW-weighted difference between RAS and LPS corresponded to an estimated difference of approximately 52.4 operating-room hours and 93 inpatient bed-days. RAS was associated with shorter OT and LOHS than LPS after adjustment for measured baseline differences. Reduced intraoperative blood loss explained a substantial proportion of these differences, although a considerable residual effect remained unexplained by measured perioperative mediators. Annual resource utilization difference should be interpreted as an illustrative planning estimate rather than a guaranteed operational saving.

title: Resource allocation under uncertainty and equity constraints in Parkinson's disease care: An econometrically grounded machine learning framework.
authors: Momahhed SS, Haghighathoseini A.
abstract: Objective To apply an integrated causal-inference and welfare-optimization framework to Iranian Parkinson's disease (PD) inpatient insurance claims, estimating how resource-allocation decisions relate to recovery, discharge risk, cost and financial burden; testing whether these relationships vary across patient subgroups; and assessing whether budget-neutral reallocation could improve efficiency and equity simultaneously. Setting Six provinces of Iran, using de-identified administrative inpatient claims obtained from the Iran Health Insurance Organization for admissions with a primary or secondary diagnosis of PD during the 2023-2025 observation period. Design Retrospective claims-based cohort study. Transaction-level records (n = 21,121) were aggregated into 1,813 hospitalization episodes and analyzed through a six-stage pipeline: gradient-boosted predictive models; double machine learning and augmented inverse-probability weighting for average treatment effects, restricted to an admission-time-only, pre-treatment severity adjustment; causal forests for subgroup heterogeneity; concentration-index decomposition for socioeconomic inequality; constrained integer-linear-programming optimization for reallocation scenarios; and bootstrap, E-value and design-effect sensitivity analyses. Results Predictive models showed acceptable-to-strong discrimination (recovery, AUC-ROC 0.709; unsuccessful-discharge proxy, AUC-ROC 0.870) and explained 81.3% of variance in total cost. Prolonged length of stay, treated as an exploratory, within-episode exposure rather than a causal one because it is realized during the hospitalization itself, was associated with a 6.4-percentage-point lower discharge proxy and 200% higher cost (E-value limit 1.93-4.04). Higher insurance-coverage generosity, the study's pre-treatment, policy-assignable exposure, was associated with an approximately 40% reduction in cost (E-value limit 2.19) and no significant change in the discharge proxy; effects were consistent across age, severity, hospital sector, rurality and socioeconomic rank, with an attenuated estimate in a small private-hospital subgroup. Recovery was concentrated among higher-socioeconomic episodes, while cost, out-of-pocket burden and length of stay were concentrated among lower-socioeconomic episodes; age and hospital ownership, not disease severity (which contributed only -0.8% to +6.2% of the observed gradients), were the leading correlates. A coverage-based, budget-neutral reallocation scenario reached 35.8% of the cohort within the observed budget. Ninety-eight percent of significant associations remained robust to plausible within-patient clustering, the principal limitation arising from the absence of a patient identifier in these claims data. Conclusion Insurance-coverage generosity showed the strongest evidence of a causal, cost-reducing effect, while socioeconomic inequity in PD hospitalization outcomes was driven primarily by administrative rather than clinical-severity factors. The reallocation scenarios illustrate model-based, budget-neutral efficiency-equity gains and should be read as decision-support for phased piloting, not as empirically demonstrated policy effects. Patient-level claims linkage and validated clinical severity measures are needed to extend this framework toward genuine longitudinal outcomes.

title: Relational learning cues, music receptivity, and performance self-efficacy among piano masterclass participants: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA study.
authors: Zhao Y, Zhu X, Su Y.
abstract: Background Performance self-efficacy is important for musical learning, yet research on its correlates in masterclass settings has mainly emphasized instruction and individual practice. Drawing on social cognitive theory and relationship-interaction-based brand equity, this study examined whether five relational cues in piano masterclasses-brand personality, reciprocity, courtesy, relationship status, and relationship energy-were associated with participants' performance self-efficacy and with affective and attentional music receptivity. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 382 adult and adolescent participants with piano-masterclass experience in mainland China. PLS-SEM tested the hypothesized structural paths. Model evaluation included HTMT, full-collinearity VIFs, SRMR, and ten specific indirect associations estimated with 5,000 two-tailed bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap samples. fsQCA results were examined under stricter frequency, consistency, PRI, and calibration specifications. Results Reciprocity, courtesy, relationship status, and relationship energy were positively associated with performance self-efficacy, whereas brand personality had no significant direct association. Affective receptivity was positively associated with reciprocity, courtesy, status, and energy; attentional receptivity was positively associated with personality, reciprocity, and status. Both receptivity dimensions were positively associated with self-efficacy. Seven of ten specific indirect associations had BCa intervals excluding zero. The baseline fsQCA solution contained seven configurations; stricter robustness specifications yielded fewer configurations, although recurring combinations of relational cues and music receptivity remained. Conclusion Performance self-efficacy in piano masterclasses was associated not only with instructional content but also with relational and experiential cues. Affective and attentional music receptivity represented distinct intervening statistical pathways. Because the survey was cross-sectional, retrospective, and based on convenience recruitment, the results do not establish causality or temporal mediation and should be generalized cautiously beyond this predominantly adult, highly educated, music-trained sample.

title: ROBECS one: feasibility study of a structured robotic curriculum and a proficiency-based framework.
authors: Appel M, Sacher C, Cron L, Dirnberger A, Müller BP, Klasen JM.
abstract: Robotic surgery is increasingly integrated into surgical practice, yet structured, benchmark-driven simulation training remains limited for general surgery trainees. Proficiency-based progression (PBP) offers a practical, specialty-tested approach for structuring robotic surgical training around demonstrated performance rather than case numbers, but standardized PBP curricula for general surgery robotic training remain underdeveloped. This study aimed to test the feasibility of a structured, simulation-based robotic training and, building on this, to develop a preliminary proficiency-based approach whose benchmarks can be formally evaluated in future studies. We conducted a prospective, single-center pilot feasibility study of a structured robotic simulation curriculum over two weeks, combining virtual reality simulation and dry-lab training on the da Vinci Xi system (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA, USA). Advanced and novice robotic surgeons completed stepwise training sessions targeting core robotic skills and procedural tasks. Feasibility was defined by successful implementation within the timeframe, completion of sessions, and participant acceptance, assessed informally; the curriculum was subsequently structured into skill modules with proposed proficiency benchmarks. The curriculum was successfully implemented within the planned two-week timeframe, with six advanced and fifteen novice robotic surgeons participating. The curriculum was structured into six sequential modules, representing key technical and non-technical skills in robotic surgical practice, each with proposed proficiency benchmarks. This pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of a structured robotic simulation curriculum in general surgery. The proposed benchmark-driven structure may inform the development of standardized robotic simulation curricula for general surgery training programs, pending further validation against clinical performance.

title: Psychosocial Outcomes Among Women with Early-stage Breast Cancer Undergoing Mastectomy: A Systematic Review.
authors: Raymond-King L, Morton CR, Moses JV, Kaur A, Godfrey EL, Hamid SA, Lynch O, Brackett AL, Greenup RA, Berger ER.
abstract: Introduction Women undergoing mastectomy for early-stage breast cancer experience physical, emotional, and psychosocial sequalae after surgery. This impact on women's identity, body image, and self-esteem is often studied in isolation, limiting the ability to capture the multidimensional nature of post-mastectomy recovery. Our systematic review aimed to characterize the range of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) used to assess postoperative psychosocial experiences. Methods Three databases were queried for relevant articles from January 1, 1997 to October 25, 2024 using keywords and controlled vocabulary for mastectomy, patient reported outcome measures, and psychology. Results Twenty studies met inclusion criteria. Most were single-institution, cross-sectional studies. More than half of the studies (60%) reported a mean or median participant age between 50-60 years. Most studies that reported participant race (72%) included > 80% White women. Thirty-eight different PROMs were used across 15 studies. Most instruments were used in only one study. Three studies developed their own measures. Seven psychosocial domains were identified: quality of life, sexual health/sexual function, body image, mental health, pain/physical health, psychosocial health, and satisfaction. Compared with mastectomy, breast conservation surgery was associated with better body image (67%) and physical health (38%) as well as improved psychosocial outcomes and satisfaction; reconstruction improved but did not eliminate these differences. Conclusions Mastectomy is associated with poor psychosocial outcomes across multiple domains, yet this is often disregarded as a critical component of postoperative recovery. These findings highlight the critical need to better prepare women for mastectomy and identify tailored support strategies to improve patient-reported outcomes. Protocol registration The study protocol was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (Registration number: CRD42024XXXXXX).

title: Pretreatment calprotectin level as a potential predictor of therapeutic response to tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis patients.
authors: Sun YS, Chen PK, Hung HC, Chen DY.
abstract: Background To promote a treat-to-target goal, there are unmet needs to identify the predictors of therapeutic response. Given a pathogenic role of calprotectin in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), we aimed to assess the predictability of pretreatment calprotectin levels for therapeutic response to tofacitinib, a Janus kinase inhibitor, in RA patients. Methods We enrolled 51 patients receiving 24-week tofacitinib therapy and 25 healthy controls (HCs). RA activity was assessed using the 28-joint disease activity score-erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR), and therapeutic response was evaluated using target attainment dichotomy. Plasma calprotectin levels were measured using the BÜHLMANN-sCAL® turbo turbidimetric assay. Results Twenty-eight (54.9%) patients were classified as the responders with combining remission and low-disease activity, and 23 (45.1%) as the non-responders with post-treatment DAS28-ESR > 3.2. Patients exhibited significantly higher calprotectin levels compared to HCs (median, 0.88 μg/mL vs. 0.24 μg/mL; p Conclusion Pretreatment calprotectin level serves as a potential predictor of tofacitinib response, with higher levels indicating a lower likelihood of favorable response.

title: Presacral Myelolipoma Mimicking Liposarcoma Complicated by Massive Intraoperative Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
authors: Hanaoka D, Shimada S, Miyaoka Y, Hanaoka K, Saito T, Iwaguchi Y, Ichihara S, Yokoyama R.
abstract: Introduction Myelolipoma is a benign tumor composed of mature adipose tissue and hematopoietic elements. Extra-adrenal lesions can occur in the presacral region and may mimic liposarcoma. Resection of a large presacral tumor can also cause life-threatening hemorrhage. We report a presacral myelolipoma that was difficult to diagnose preoperatively and was complicated by massive intraoperative hemorrhage. Case presentation A 71-year-old woman had an incidentally detected 75 × 75 × 125-mm presacral mass with mixed fatty and solid components on contrast-enhanced CT. MRI showed restricted diffusion, and fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT showed mild uptake (maximum standardized uptake value, 3.93). No growth occurred over approximately 3 months. Because liposarcoma could not be excluded, the patient chose open resection without biopsy for diagnosis and treatment. During cranial dissection along the anterior sacrum, massive bleeding occurred from the right internal iliac venous system, and systolic blood pressure decreased to 50-60 mmHg. Manual compression was insufficient, and massive transfusion was initiated. Intraoperatively, a vein communicating with the right internal iliac vein was found to enter the tumor, and the main trunk of the right internal iliac vein was ligated near its junction with the right common iliac vein. Persistent bleeding required ligation of a tumor-entering branch of the right internal iliac artery; the arterial main trunk was preserved. Hemostasis was prioritized, and the tumor was removed in 2 pieces; the capsule was disrupted without macroscopic tumor spillage. Diffuse presacral venous plexus bleeding was controlled with electrocautery and oxidized cellulose. Operative time was 3 h 21 min, and blood loss was 4850 mL; 10 units of leukocyte-reduced red blood cells and 6 units of fresh frozen plasma were transfused. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of myelolipoma. No vascular complications occurred, and contrast-enhanced CT at approximately 1 year showed no residual or recurrent tumor. Conclusions Presacral myelolipoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of fat-containing presacral tumors. In large tumors, the relationship with the internal iliac vessels and presacral venous plexus should be carefully assessed, and adequate blood products, early vascular control, and source-specific hemostatic techniques should be prepared before resection.

title: Prediction of late blight severity in a large panel of potato genotypes using low-altitude aerial images and machine learning methods.
authors: Loayza H, Ninanya J, Palacios S, Silva L, Pujaico Rivera F, Rinza J, Gastelo M, Aponte M, Kreuze JF, Lindqvist-Kreuze H, Heider B, Kante M, Ramírez DA.
abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is a staple crop crucial to global food security, yet its production is severely threatened by late blight (LB), caused by Phytophthora infestans, one of the most destructive plant diseases worldwide. Breeding programs for LB resistance have traditionally relied on labor-intensive and subjective visual assessments, which limit scalability and consistency, particularly in early-generation trials. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing combined with machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative for objective, high-throughput disease phenotyping. This study evaluated the potential of this technology to estimate LB severity at the genotype level across two large potato trials in Peru comprising 2,745 breeding clones and 492 genebank accessions. We compared vegetation index-based approaches with a ML framework that integrates K-means clustering and Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR). While NDVI correlated strongly with visually assessed LB severity, particularly at advanced stages, the multispectral KRR approach outperformed linear NDVI models by capturing nonlinear relationships between spectral response and disease progression. Best linear unbiased estimates (BLUEs) of LB severity from both models were strongly and consistently related to the area under the disease progress curve (AUDPC), particularly in later UAV acquisitions. Selection coincidence with AUDPC-based rankings was substantially higher at intermediate to advanced stages of disease progression, indicating that a single UAV inspection at those stages captures enough phenotypic variation to distinguish genotypes. UAV-based multispectral phenotyping integrated with ML, therefore offers a practical, scalable alternative to the time-consuming visual assessments traditionally used in potato breeding programs.

title: Practice leadership development in intellectual disability services: A qualitative study of practice leaders' experiences.
authors: Doody O, O'Halloran M, Carey E, Kilduff M, Ryan R.
abstract: Background Leadership in intellectual disability services is recognised as having a key role in achieving positive outcomes for people with intellectual disabilities, service quality and workforce wellbeing. However, limited research has explored how leadership capability is developed and enacted by practice leaders within everyday service contexts. Methods This study reports the qualitative findings from a national mixed‑methods evaluation of a bespoke Clinical Leadership Programme for practice leaders in intellectual disability services in Ireland. Following ethical approval, individual semi‑structured interviews were conducted with fourteen participants who completed the programme. Data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Results Participants described leadership development as a transformative process involving shifts in professional identity, confidence and legitimacy rather than the acquisition of discrete leadership skills. Reflection emerged as an important mechanism underpinning leadership development, supporting participants to move from reactive and task‑focused approaches towards more intentional, relational and ethically grounded leadership practice. Participants described the programme as reducing professional isolation and facilitating peer learning relationships that promoted psychological safety and supported learning within a community of practice. Participants also described changes in leadership enactment characterised by greater staff engagement, relational conflict management and the extension of person-centred values to staff teams. Re-engagement with education was viewed as an important outcome, reframing learning as an ongoing component of leadership development and professional growth. However, participants identified systemic challenges, including administrative burden, role overload and compliance-driven organisational cultures, as constraining the enactment of leadership in practice. Conclusion Leadership development in intellectual disability services was described as an identity-based, relational and contextually constrained process. Reflective, practice-based and context-specific leadership programmes may support leadership capacity development; however, participants emphasised that the enactment of leadership in practice also requires supportive organisational structures and cultures.

title: Patients With Critical Humeral Bone Loss Have Similar Patient-Reported Outcomes to Patients Without Critical Humeral Bone Loss After Arthroscopic Shoulder Stabilization at a Mean Follow-Up of 7 Years.
authors: Gilbert R, Lin RT, Dadoo S, Liu A, Cong T, Popchak A, Lesniak BP, Rodosky M, Hughes JD, Lin A.
abstract: Purpose To compare long-term patient-reported outcomes (PROs) between patients with and without critical humeral bone loss (CHBL) and to compare long-term PROs among patients with CHBL who underwent arthroscopic Bankart repair (ABR) alone versus those who received a remplissage augmentation (ABR + R). Methods A retrospective review included patients aged 13 to 50 years who underwent ABR or ABR + R for anterior shoulder instability from 2007 to 2023. Exclusion criteria included 20% glenoid bone loss, off-track Hill-Sachs lesion, concomitant pathology, or revision surgery. CHBL was defined as humeral head defect extension below the 90° equator. Western Ontario Shoulder Index, pain Visual Analog Scale, and Subjective Shoulder Value were collected at the final follow-up. PROs and recurrence rates were compared between cohorts and within the CHBL subgroup. Results Three hundred eighty-four patients were included (mean age 23 ± 9 years (range: 13-49), 78% men), of which 99 (26%) were successfully contacted for PROs: 129 (34%) with CHBL and 255 (66%) without CHBL. The CHBL cohort was older (25 vs 22 years, P P P = .08), but, within the CHBL cohort, recurrence was significantly lower after ABR + R than ABR alone (9% vs 32%, P P > .05). In a multivariable linear regression, only recurrent instability was an independent predictor of inferior PROs; the presence of CHBL was not an independent predictor. Among CHBL patients, PROs were similar between ABR and ABR + R. Conclusions Patients with CHBL had similar long-term PROs to those without CHBL after ABR or ABR + R at a minimum follow-up of 1 year. Furthermore, the addition of remplissage was found to be associated with a reduced rate of recurrent anterior shoulder instability in patients with CHBL. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Pacing strategies and variability during time- vs distance-based trials for estimating maximal aerobic speed in academy soccer players.
authors: Smith K, Shushan T, Wright MD, Chesterton P, Hamilton A, Taylor JM.
abstract: Time- and distance-based trials are widely used to estimate Maximal Aerobic Speed (MAS) in soccer, yet pacing strategies during these tests are under-explored. This study examined pacing profiles during a 6-minute distance trial (6minDT) and 1800-m time trial (1800mTT) in twenty-seven highly trained male academy players (17.1 ± 0.6 years; MAS: 15.71 ± 0.89 km·h -1 ). Tests were performed in counterbalanced order, with instantaneous speed sampled at 10 Hz using GPS. Rolling mean speed was rescaled to 10% completion intervals, and a spline model separated pacing into three phases (0-30%, 30-80%, 80-100%). Parabolic pacing strategies were identified: U-shaped in the 1800mTT and reverse J-shaped in the 6minDT. Linear mixed-effects modelling revealed a higher starting speed during the 6minDT than the 1800mTT (18.4 vs 17.9 km·h -1 ). Both tests showed an early-phase (0-30%) speed reduction (~1 km·h -1 per 10% interval), followed by a stable middle phase (30-80%), with near-zero speed changes and overlapping confidence intervals. A greater end-phase speed increase occurred in the 1800mTT than 6minDT (1.05 vs 0.26 km·h -1 ). Between-athlete variability reduced in the middle phase, with total variance predominantly attributed to within-athlete variability (95.4%). Both trials elicited parabolic pacing, though distinct within-athlete differences emerged across phases.

title: Outside-In Medial Collateral Ligament Release Shows Superior Evidence for Safe Medial Joint Space Widening and Functional Recovery in Knee Arthroscopy: A Systematic Review.
authors: Rezaee H, Ayati Firoozabadi M, Salkhori O, Sahebi M, Mortazavi SMJ.
abstract: Purpose To compare various medial collateral ligament (MCL) release techniques used during knee arthroscopy by evaluating their anatomical targets, biomechanical effects, medial joint space widening, clinical and functional outcomes, and associated complications. Methods A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2000 and June 2025. Eligible studies focused on MCL release in adult knee arthroscopy patients and reported clinical and functional outcomes. Data on medial joint space opening, knee instability, functional scores, and complications were extracted. Results Thirteen studies were included, with the outside-in technique, especially the percutaneous pie-crusting method, being the most extensively studied. The outside-in technique consistently achieved the greatest joint space widening, with increases ranging from 2.5 to 12 mm. The inside-out technique showed moderate joint space expansion (3-7 mm). Functional outcomes improved significantly across all techniques. The outside-in technique reported a Lysholm score increase from 48.2 to 80, a visual analog scale score decrease from 5.6 to 1.8, and an International Knee Documentation Committee score rise from 51.4 to 82.2. The inside-out technique showed a moderate improvement in Lysholm score from 59.3 to 85.7, with no significant differences in instability or long-term complications. Subperiosteal release also enhanced Lysholm scores from 50 to 92.5, with minor increases in joint laxity that resolved over time. All techniques showed low complication rates, with transient needle tract pain and mild ecchymosis being the most common side effects. Conclusions MCL release techniques, especially the outside-in percutaneous pie-crusting method, improve medial joint space visualization and medial joint space during knee arthroscopy, aiding meniscal repair, partial meniscectomy, meniscal root repair, and other procedures. These techniques are generally safe but cause temporary ligamentous laxity similar to a grade I MCL sprain, so they are not entirely "benign." Surgeons must weigh inducing controlled trauma against potential drawbacks of a tighter joint because the risk-benefit balance varies case by case. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

title: Open-Source and Commercial 3-Dimensional Computed Tomography Methods Show Limited Agreement for Classifying Acetabular Morphology in Patients Undergoing Hip Arthroscopy.
authors: Ellingwood AA, Grewal RS, Gass HM, Chen A, Woo D, Beasley BVL, Bomar JD, Parvaresh KC, Upasani VV, Schmitz MR.
abstract: Purpose To compare acetabular morphology classifications derived from a validated open-source (freely available) method with those derived from commercially available software in patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome. Methods We analyzed preoperative 3-dimensional computed tomography imaging in patients with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome using open-source and commercial software. The open-source method calculated acetabular coverage across 5 regions and generated z -scores relative to an internal normative database. Hips with z -scores ≥2 or ≤-2 were classified as abnormal. The commercial method categorized hips as normal, undercovered, or overcovered based on published thresholds (lateral center-edge angle, Tönnis angle, coverage percentage, and crossover sign) and focal depth mapping. The primary outcome was categorical agreement between methods. Results Seventy-six hips (55 women, 21 men; mean age 35.5 ± 12.3 years) were included. The open-source method classified 58/76 hips as normal, 10/76 as dysplastic, and 8/76 as overcovered. The commercial method classified 14/76 hips as normal, 29/76 as undercovered, and 33/76 as overcovered. A total of 23/76 hips were classified the same in both systems and called agreed. Disagreements (53/76 hips) fell into 3 categories: (1) essentially similar despite different labels because of borderline z -scores or small focal areas (n = 24), (2) disagreements driven by Tönnis angle alone (n = 8), and (3) true disagreements (n = 21). Notably, 5 hips (6.6%) showed opposite classifications (e.g., dysplastic vs overcovered). Subanalysis of z -scores showed that 69.8% of disagreements reflected borderline morphology ( z -scores of ±1-2). Conclusions Although both open-source and commercial methods provide 3-dimensional classification of acetabular morphology, categorical agreement was limited. Most disagreements reflected borderline morphology or small focal areas of uncertain clinical relevance. A minority showed true classification opposites. Clinical relevance Awareness of the methodological differences between open-source and commercial 3-dimensional computed tomography platforms may help surgeons appropriately interpret acetabular morphology classifications during preoperative planning for patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome.

title: Open and endoscopic decompression for cubital tunnel syndrome: long-term clinical outcomes, prognostic factors, and comparison of anterior transposition techniques.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Ertem H, Şireci C, Al F, Alyousef A, Çiçek İB, Ertem K.
abstract: Background/objective The optimal surgical treatment for cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS) remains controversial, and comparative evidence regarding endoscopic-assisted anterior transposition is lacking. This study compared the clinical and functional outcomes of open and endoscopic decompression, evaluated open versus endoscopic-assisted anterior transposition, and identified patient-related prognostic factors associated with postoperative outcomes. Methods Fifty-six patients who underwent surgery for CuTS between 2010 and 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Nineteen patients underwent open in situ decompression and 37 underwent endoscopic decompression. Outcomes were assessed using Quick DASH, VAS, Wilson-Krout grading system, patient satisfaction, and job change. An additional comparative analysis was performed in patients requiring anterior transposition because of intraoperative ulnar nerve instability (open, n = 16; endoscopic-assisted, n = 11). Smoking, body mass index (BMI), occupation, and preoperative McGowan grade were evaluated as prognostic factors. Results Median follow-up was 138 months (range, 56-180) in the open group and 76 months (range, 27-156) in the endoscopic group. No statistically significant differences were detected between open and endoscopic decompression in postoperative Quick DASH, VAS, Wilson-Krout grades, patient satisfaction, job change, or complication rates. Among patients undergoing anterior transposition, median follow-up was 148 months (range, 60-180) after open transposition and 105 months (range, 50-156) after endoscopic-assisted transposition. No statistically significant differences were detected in postoperative Quick DASH, VAS or Wilson-Krout grades between patients who underwent open anterior transposition and those who underwent endoscopic-assisted anterior transposition. Increasing preoperative McGowan grade was associated with worse postoperative Quick DASH, VAS, and Wilson-Krout outcomes. Smoking and higher BMI were associated with less favorable Wilson-Krout outcomes, whereas occupation had no significant effect on postoperative recovery. Conclusions No statistically significant differences were detected in long-term clinical and functional outcomes between open and endoscopic decompression for CuTS. Similarly, no statistically significant differences were detected between open and endoscopic-assisted anterior transposition. Greater preoperative disease severity was associated with less favorable postoperative outcomes. Given the retrospective design and limited sample size, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or non-inferiority between the surgical techniques.

title: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in chronic and relapsing musculoskeletal pain: pearls for clinical practice.
authors: Di Martino A, Scaglione F, Graziosi A, Tranquilli Leali P.
abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the principal pharmacological option for inflammatory musculoskeletal pain and are frequently treated as an interchangeable class from which any agent may be selected. This narrative review examines the pharmacological basis of that assumption and organises the evidence around three questions: which molecule, at what dose, and in which formulation. Four observations follow from the available data. COX selectivity is an incomplete predictor of clinical risk, since a non-selective agent may carry a cardiovascular profile comparable to that of the coxibs while a coxib may reduce events across the whole gastrointestinal tract; risk is therefore better assigned to individual molecules at defined doses than to selectivity classes. Comparative efficacy is dose-dependent rather than uniformly equivalent, so equivalence between agents applies only at comparable analgesic doses, and apparent non-response is frequently sub-therapeutic dosing. Organ-specific risk differs in kind as well as in degree across the cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic and haemostatic axes, and proton pump inhibitors protect the upper gastrointestinal tract only. Modified-release formulations alter onset and peak-to-trough fluctuation, but no evidence indicates that they attenuate class-level organ toxicity. Contraindications lying outside the cardiorenal and gastrointestinal axes are stated, together with the clinically relevant drug interactions and the regulatory restrictions applying to individual agents.

title: Multiparametric quantitative MRI in knee osteoarthritis: evidence and requirements for interpretation and reporting.
authors: Jia Y, Liu L, Zhao B, Zhang X, Sun R, Guo X.
abstract: Quantitative MRI can characterize cartilage and other joint tissues beyond visible structural damage, but its contribution to individual management of knee osteoarthritis remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the evidence needed to interpret quantitative measurements, combine parameters, and report their uncertainty. An initial PubMed search in June 2026 was supplemented on 14 September 2026 by an updated PubMed search and broader Embase and Web of Science searches. Targeted full-text assessment addressed incremental value, outcome timing, validation, and measurement error. Selected development studies found better discrimination with integrated diffusion and relaxation measurements than with individual parameters, whereas other combined imaging models did not improve on simpler comparators. Longitudinal associations were outcome-specific, and independent external validation was limited. Treatment studies showed inconsistent agreement between imaging changes and symptomatic benefit. We propose a five-step interpretation framework that establishes the clinical question, verifies technical adequacy, assesses morphology and comparable reference data, evaluates measurement uncertainty, and separates observations from clinical inferences. Two hypothetical scenarios illustrate its application. Quantitative MRI currently provides its strongest support as a controlled research measurement. Demonstrated reproducibility, an appropriate comparator, and evidence of added decision value are required before a quantitative finding can justify patient-level diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-response claims.

title: Methodological considerations in estimating active muscle stiffness index.
authors: Larivière O, Dauvergne M, Etheve F, Testa J, Besombes C, Dalleau G, Caderby T, Peyrot N, Mariani A.
abstract: Accurate quantification of muscle stiffness using shear wave elastography is essential for evaluating neuromuscular function. The active muscle stiffness index, derived from the relationship between shear modulus and force, can be estimated using either continuous ramp or discrete step approaches, which are often considered equivalent. This study aimed to directly compare these two approaches. Thirty healthy women performed isometric knee extensions up to 50% of maximal voluntary contraction under both ramp and step contractions, while shear wave elastography measurements were obtained from the vastus lateralis. The active muscle stiffness index was calculated for each protocol. Agreement between methods was evaluated using paired t-tests, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results revealed a significant difference between protocols (p < 0.001). Although a very strong correlation was observed (r ≈ 0.88), concordance was lower (CCC ≈ 0.81). Bland-Altman analysis indicated a systematic bias of -0.20 kPa/Nm (∼20%) without proportional bias. These findings demonstrate that ramp and step approaches yield systematically different estimates and should not be considered interchangeable.

title: Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw After Dental Extractions During High-Dose Denosumab Therapy in a Patient With Paget's Disease: A Case Report.
authors: Zamani T, Mosannen Mozaffari P, Anvari K, Anbiaee N, Famili K, Mirzaei A, Fallah Toosi F, Shafiee A.
abstract: Patients with Paget's disease who receive high-dose denosumab may develop medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, particularly after dental extractions. Pre-treatment dental assessment, careful risk communication, accurate staging, and coordinated conservative and surgical management are essential. Platelet-rich fibrin may be used only as an adjunct, not as an established standard treatment.

title: Mechanism of activation-dependent shift in the human soleus fascicle force-length relationship studied using a 3D finite element model.
authors: Knaus KR.
abstract: We investigated the force-length relationship of human soleus at varying activation levels to examine effects of complex architecture and aponeuroses on fascicle lengths at which peak active muscle forces occur. Using a three-dimensional (3D) finite element (FE) model, previously validated with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), we simulated soleus muscle excursion while prescribing different activations ranging from passive to fully active. FE simulations demonstrated peaks in average active force-length relationships of fascicles at relative lengths of 1.06, 1.07, 1.08, and 1.09 at 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25% activation, respectively. A rightward shift with decreasing activation in optimal fascicle length where peak active forces occurred emerged from complex 3D architecture, despite a similar shift being absent in the force-length relationship of the underlying muscle material model. This emergent behavior demonstrates that muscle and aponeurosis architectural complexity present in the model contributes to activation-dependent shifts in optimal muscle length, rather than purely subcellular mechanisms not represented in the model's muscle material behavior. Soleus simulations also revealed significant inter-fascicle heterogeneity in lengths and pennation angles which increased with activation, demonstrating that the common one-dimensional conceptual model of a muscle-tendon unit (MTU) oversimplifies the mechanics of complex multipennate muscles when 'subtracting out' effects of tendon compliance to characterize active force-length. The study highlights the importance of considering 3D architectural complexity when scaling muscle mechanics across species from animal to humans, particularly the soleus, as the simplified structure in small mammals may not capture effects of intramuscular aponeuroses on active muscle mechanics.

title: Maximal horizontal deceleration and change-of-direction performance in female rugby union players across age categories and playing positions.
authors: Fink B, Ordóñez-Vega J, Ryan C, van den Tillaar R, Jiménez-Lozano M, Rodriguez-Rosell D, Gálvez-González J.
abstract: This study determined the intra-session reliability of the maximal horizontal deceleration test, compared deceleration and change-of-direction (COD) performance across age categories (U14, U16, U18 and Senior) and playing positions (backs and forwards), and explored associations while controlling for age, body mass and position. One-hundred-and-eight female rugby union players (U14: n = 28; 13.11 ± 0.96 years; U16: n = 24; 15.13 ± 0.74 years; U18: n = 26; 16.69 ± 0.79 years; Senior: n = 30; 23.93 ± 5.48 years) completed two trials each of a 20-m sprint, maximal horizontal deceleration test and 505 COD test in a single session. Moderate to excellent reliability was found (ICC = 0.66-1.00; CV = 0.25-8.10%). U18 and Senior players showed higher maximum velocity (V max ), better average deceleration (DEC ave ) and faster COD times than U14 and U16 players. Compared with forwards, backs showed higher V max , better DEC ave , and faster COD acceleration and total times; they were also faster in COD deceleration in U16, U18 and Senior. DEC ave was associated with COD acceleration, deceleration and total times; V max with COD acceleration, reacceleration and total times; and horizontal braking power with all COD metrics. These findings support assessing maximal horizontal deceleration, as deceleration metrics provide complementary information to sprint velocity when characterising phase-specific COD performance.

title: MRI-based assessment of greater tuberosity exposure in massive rotator cuff tears: a systematic review of current evidence and methodological gaps.
authors: Herrmann J, Limmer J, Neubauer D, Lehmeyer T, Oberfeld J, Rudert M, List K, Hochberger F.
abstract: Background Massive rotator cuff tears (MRCTs) lack a standardized and reproducible imaging-based definition. A recent Delphi consensus introduced greater tuberosity exposure (GTE) as a defining criterion for MRCTs, proposing that MRCTs be classified by either involvement of at least two rotator cuff tendons or ≥ 67% GTE on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Purpose To evaluate the role of GTE in the MRI-based definition and structural characterization of MRCTs and to describe the extent and methodological maturity of the evidence available for GTE and established MRI-derived parameters. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from database inception to February 17, 2026, and updated on October 9 and 11, 2026 with supplementary citation searching, in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies were included if they investigated MRCTs using MRI-based or MRI-transferable imaging and reported structural definitions, measurement methods, or associations with irreparability, structural healing, or clinical outcomes. Prognostic studies were assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. Findings were synthesized narratively; no meta-analysis was performed due to substantial heterogeneity in study designs, imaging protocols, and outcome definitions. The synthesis described the extent and methodological maturity of the available evidence and did not compare diagnostic or prognostic performance between parameters. Results A total of 34 studies were included. No study evaluated GTE as a quantitative MRI-derived parameter. Only two studies addressed footprint coverage on imaging, one qualitatively and one by a semi-quantitative five-zone score of residual tendon attachment; neither measured GTE as a defined exposure parameter or applied predefined thresholds. In contrast, MRCTs were consistently characterized using indirect structural parameters, primarily tendon involvement and tear size. Established MRI-derived variables-including tear size, tendon retraction, fatty infiltration, muscle atrophy, and superior humeral migration-were assessed using established measurement frameworks based on defined anatomical landmarks, notwithstanding methodological heterogeneity in imaging protocols and thresholds across studies. These parameters were frequently evaluated in relation to irreparability, structural healing, and functional outcomes, whereas no study evaluated a direct quantitative MRI-based measure of GTE in relation to a clinical or structural endpoint. Conclusion No standardized and outcome-validated MRI-based method for quantifying GTE was identified within the scope of this review. Despite its conceptual appeal as a direct representation of footprint deficiency, GTE has not yet undergone standardized measurement development or outcome-based validation. The evidence base for established MRI-derived parameters is more extensive and methodologically mature, with operationalized measurement methods and reported outcome associations; this does not imply clinical inferiority of GTE. Future research should focus on developing reproducible MRI-based measurement techniques for GTE and evaluating its diagnostic and prognostic relevance in dedicated validation studies. Study design Systematic review; Level of evidence, 3. Individual included studies ranged from Level II to Level V.

title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.
authors: Yoon YC, Song HK.
abstract: Background Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is used for life-threatening hemorrhage, but evidence has largely focused on acute outcomes. Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized. Methods This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up. Forty-nine REBOA-treated patients were matched 1:1 to 49 non-REBOA patients by major Young-Burgess category, Injury Severity Score, and age. The primary outcome was functional status among hospital survivors, categorized as good/fair/poor. Deep surgical site infection (SSI) after definitive pelvic fixation was the key secondary outcome, and nonunion was exploratory. Main models used a propensity-score linear predictor based on age, Injury Severity Score, initial systolic blood pressure, and lactate. Results Seventy-five patients survived hospitalization (30 REBOA; 45 non-REBOA); median follow-up was 19 months. Good/fair/poor outcomes were 16.7%/46.7%/36.7% in REBOA survivors and 51.1%/37.8%/11.1% in non-REBOA survivors. REBOA exposure was associated with worse functional status after adjustment (common odds ratio [cOR], 3.14; 95% CI, 1.11-8.92; P = 0.032). Among 68 definitive-fixation survivors, deep SSI occurred in 44.0% versus 9.3% (adjusted OR, 7.01; 95% CI, 1.88-31.07; P = 0.003); all observed events occurred within 60 days. Nonunion occurred in 26.7% versus 6.7% (adjusted OR, 9.09; 95% CI, 2.00-53.71; P = 0.004). Sensitivity analyses for deep SSI were directionally consistent. Conclusions Among hospital survivors, REBOA exposure was associated with poorer long-term functional recovery and a higher burden of deep SSI. Nonunion was more frequent but remained exploratory. These findings characterize a high-risk orthopaedic survivor phenotype but do not establish a direct causal effect of REBOA.

title: Knowledge gap in vertebrate genetic diversity in a northern remanent of neotropical rainforest.
authors: Martínez Cano DJ, Reynoso VH, Vázquez-Cruz ML, Alvarado-Robledo EJ, Ángeles-López YI, Zarza E.
abstract: Los Tuxtlas Biosphere Reserve is one of the last remaining areas of primary tropical rainforest in Mexico. This fragile ecosystem heavily reduced by human perturbations is part of the Mesoamerican hotspot. The reserve harbors many endemic species. Thus, identifying, cataloging, and studying the biodiversity of this ecosystem has been of utmost importance. A promising approach for fast species identification to assess biodiversity is the use of DNA barcoding techniques. However, these techniques are limited by reliable DNA databases. Using novel Perl scripts, we generated a barcoding database to assess mitochondrial sequence availability in public databases for 903 vertebrate species that inhabit the reserve. Of these, 39 species had no sequences, 189 had complete mitochondrial genomes sequenced and the rest were partially sequenced. We studied over 80,000 sequences spanning 16 mitochondrial genomic markers and found 5 well-studied markers (COI-5P, CYTB, ND2, 16S rRNA and 12S rRNA) with more than 50% species coverage. The COI-5P region and CYTB were the best studied and most recommended markers for barcoding studies, and 7 additional markers have been preferred for one or more specific taxonomic groups. The remaining markers were almost exclusively sequenced as part of whole mitochondrial genomes. The best-known taxonomic group was mammals while the least known was reptiles. We also evaluated the sequencing frequency distribution for endemic, threatened and trade-restricted species driving interests in ecological research. In general, most species within each group were less sequenced when compared to the mean of all species, skewed by a few highly sequenced species of ecological interest. The most sequenced species are trade-restricted species, especially threatened species. This is driven by ecology-based research in the area. Finally, our results highlight a lack of barcoding research in local and endemic species of the Mesoamerican hotspot focusing on specific species but ignoring the wider range of biodiversity.

title: Kinematic characteristics associated with right-side cross-step blocking performance in elite youth male volleyball players: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Wei Z, Chen H, Liang Y, Wang Z.
abstract: Background Effective blocking is an important contributor to match outcomes in volleyball. However, the phase-specific kinematic characteristics associated with approach velocity (AV) and jump height (JH) during cross-step blocking have not been comprehensively examined. This study aimed to identify the kinematic variables associated with AV and JH during right-side cross-step blocking in elite youth male volleyball players. Methods This cross-sectional study included 22 elite youth male volleyball players performing right-side cross-step blocking under standardized conditions, with each participant's highest-rated eligible trial selected for kinematic analysis based on assessments by two volleyball experts. Kinematic data were recorded using two high-speed video cameras and processed with Fastmove Motion-3D software. Correlation analyses were conducted to identify kinematic variables associated with AV and JH, with p values adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Variables that remained significant after FDR correction were subsequently examined using univariable linear regression, followed by parsimonious multivariable linear regression where appropriate. Results For AV, five kinematic variables remained significantly associated with AV after FDR correction: third-step right hip linear velocity (R-LVH-TS, r = 0.80, FDR q r = 0.71, FDR q = 0.003), second-step left hip linear velocity (L-LVH-SS, r = 0.62, FDR q = 0.015), second-step foot displacement (SFD, r = 0.61, FDR q = 0.015), and third-step right knee linear velocity (R-LVK-TS, ρ = 0.67, FDR q = 0.007). In univariable linear regression models, these variables explained 63.5%, 50.7%, 38.8%, 37.8%, and 24.7% of the variance in AV, respectively. The parsimonious multivariable regression model including third-step right hip linear velocity and second-step left knee angular velocity explained 67.7% of the variance in AV. In this model, only third-step right hip linear velocity remained independently associated with AV. For JH, take-off-phase center-of-mass (CoM) linear velocity was the only variable that remained significantly associated with JH after FDR correction (LVCoM-TO, ρ = 0.65, FDR q = 0.025), explaining 57.9% of the variance in JH in the univariable regression model. Conclusions The findings suggest that AV during right-side cross-step blocking is related to phase-specific lower-limb kinematic coordination during second- and third-step phases, especially right hip linear velocity during the third step. JH is associated with greater CoM linear velocity during take-off. In practice, third-step right hip linear velocity and take-off-phase CoM linear velocity may serve as biomechanical reference points for evaluating approach and jump performance, respectively.

title: Influence of iron metabolism on all-cause death in patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Mo M, Xu Y, Gao T, Nong Z, Liang M, Pan L.
abstract: Objective To investigate the relationship between iron metabolism and all-cause mortality in patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). Methods The clinical data of SA-AKI patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University were analyzed retrospectively. All patients were followed up for 90 days, after which they were divided into survival and death groups Cox regression analysis was used to explore the risk factors for all-cause death in patients with SA-AKI. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and Kaplan-Meier curves were used to analyze the relationship between different iron metabolism indexes and prognosis in patients with SA-AKI. Results A total of 3,049 SA-AKI patients were included, with a male-to-female ratio of 1.22:1 and an average age of 64.32 ± 16.46 years. Of these patients, 40.0% underwent renal replacement therapy (RRT), 21.4% received invasive mechanical ventilation, 14.5% received transfusions, and 44.8% were treated with vasoactive drugs. The 90-day all-cause mortality was 20.5%. The area under the curve (AUC) for the combined indexes of iron metabolism (serum iron, serum ferritin (SF) , and transferrin (TRF)) for predicting all-cause mortality in SA-AKI patients was 0.757. Kaplan-Meier survival curves revealed that the 90-day cumulative survival rate of the increased serum iron, increased SF and decreased TRF groups were significantly lower than that of the normal group. Multivariate Cox regression analysis revealed that the increased serum iron concentration, and SF concentration; decreased TRF concentration were independent risk factors for 90-day all-cause death in SA-AKI patients. Conclusion Elevated serum iron and SF concentrations and decreased TRF concentration are important factors affecting the mortality of patients with SA-AKI. Abnormal iron metabolism indexes in patients with SA-AKI may be associated with a high risk of all-cause death.

title: Influence of dominant sequence artifacts on generative AI for virtual contrast-enhancement in breast MRI.
authors: Brock L, Markale A, Nguyen TT, Metz M, George A, Heidarikahkesh S, Schreiter H, Pfann Hossbach J, Kapsner LA, Ohlmeyer S, Wenkel E, Uder M, Laun FB, Knoll F, Bickelhaupt S.
abstract: Background Virtual contrast-enhanced (vCE) breast MRI is a deep learning approach for generating contrast-like images from non-contrast acquisitions. As diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) has emerged as a major contributor to enhancement synthesis, understanding the influence of DWI-related image artifacts is important for the robustness and potential clinical implementation of AI-based contrast-free imaging approaches. We evaluated the robustness of a pix2pix-based vCE synthesis model to artifact-contaminated DWI during training and inference. Materials and methods This IRB-approved, retrospective study included 1,974 multiparametric breast MRI examinations (mean age: 49 years) acquired with two clinical routine 3T MRI scanners (2017-2022). High b-value (b = 1500 s/mm 2 ) DWI images were automatically classified for high-intensity (HI) and low-intensity (LI) artifacts using a pretrained neural network. A pix2pix 2D-GAN was trained either after excluding artifact-affected slices (vCE-clean) or using all available slices (vCE-all). Performance was evaluated using image similarity metrics, lesion-based analysis, reader assessment, and correlation of artifact scores with reconstruction errors. Results Excluding artifact-affected slices during training resulted in a small but statistically significant increase in whole-image structural similarity index (SSIM) with small effect size (vCE-all 0.843 ± 0.034; vCE-clean 0.849 ± 0.031, p av = 0.20). However, lesion-based metrics and qualitative ratings of lesion enhancement and image quality were comparable between models. During Inference, strong LI DWI artifacts were associated with higher lesion-based errors. Conclusion Controlling for artifacts on diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) during vCE training only minorly influenced technical metrics but not perceived image quality/lesion enhancement. In contrast, severe signal-loss artifacts during inference impaired local performance, highlighting the importance of image quality control during potential deployment.

title: Impact of sarcopenic obesity phenotype on long-term survival in geriatric trauma: A nationwide cohort study using weight-adjusted waist index.
authors: Kim HG, Ju UC, Kim JY, Jung E.
abstract: Background As the global population ages, identifying effective prognostic markers for elderly trauma patients has become crucial. While Body Mass Index (BMI) is commonly used, its utility is limited by the "obesity paradox," failing to differentiate between muscle and fat. This study aimed to evaluate the Weight-Adjusted Waist Index (WWI), a surrogate marker for sarcopenic obesity, as a predictor of 20-year mortality following heavy trauma in the elderly. Methods We analyzed a nationwide cohort of 18,366 elderly patients (age≧65) from the National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (NHIS-NSC) who experienced heavy trauma (hospitalization, surgery, or ICU admission) between 2002 and 2022. Patients were categorized into WWI tertiles. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for 20-year mortality, adjusting for demographics, lifestyle factors, comorbidities, and laboratory findings. Results During the 20-year follow-up, the highest WWI tertile (T3) was associated with significantly higher mortality compared to the lowest tertile (T1). In the fully adjusted model, the HR for 20-year mortality in the T3 group was 1.72 (95% CI 1.55-1.91). Notably, the risk was more pronounced in obese patients (BMI≧25 kg/m2, HR 2.15) and those with low physical activity. Furthermore, high WWI was associated with a higher prevalence of hip and femur fractures (26.0% vs. 15.0%) and prolonged ICU stays. Conclusions WWI is a superior and independent predictor of long-term mortality compared to BMI in elderly trauma patients. By effectively identifying the high-risk sarcopenic obesity phenotype, WWI provides a practical and powerful tool for risk stratification in geriatric trauma management.

title: How Does Hematopoietic Stem Cell Gene Therapy Affect Hip Dysplasia in Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I Hurler Syndrome? Radiological Outcomes at a Minimum 4-year Follow-up.
authors: De Pellegrin M, Cossutta M, Consiglieri G, Contisciani F, Filisetti C, Tucci F, Morosini C, Mellone R, Romeni S, Aiuti A, Bernardo ME.
abstract: Background Mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS IH), or Hurler syndrome, is a lysosomal disorder caused by glycosaminoglycan accumulation due to an α-L-iduronidase deficiency. It is characterized by progressive skeletal impairment and impaired cognitive development. Hip dysplasia is a major skeletal manifestation for which conventional treatments (allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation with or without enzyme replacement therapy) does not prevent progression. Questions/purposes Among patients with MPS IH, does hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy (HSC-GT) result in (1) longitudinal improvement in bony measurements of hip dysplasia, specifically the acetabular index (the angle between the Hilgenreiner line and the line drawn from the Y-cartilage to the lateral edge of the acetabular roof) and migration percentage (the proportion of the femoral head lateral to a Perkins line drawn from the lateral edge of the acetabular roof); (2) improvement in the cartilaginous acetabular index and migration percentage, accounting for the cartilaginous components of the acetabular roof and femoral head; and (3) an increase in the proportion of patients with an acetabular index and cartilaginous acetabular index within published norms? Methods Between 2018 and 2019, 8 patients (6 males, 2 females) with MPS IH received OTL-203, an HSC-GT, in a Phase I/II clinical trial.
