All patients met the trial eligibility criteria, including absence of a suitable allogeneic donor and a Developmental Quotient or Intelligence Quotient score ≥ 70. Median (range) age at treatment was 23.5 months (14 to 34). All patients had dysplastic hip morphology at baseline, with abnormal acetabular index values and reduced femoral head coverage. This secondary analysis used prospectively collected orthopaedic and skeletal data from the same trial cohort, including hip radiographs and MRIs obtained during multidisciplinary follow-up. All patients completed the 5-year follow-up and entered the approved long-term follow-up program (up to 15 years after HSC-GT); no patients were lost to follow-up. One patient with pretreatment bilateral hip dislocation underwent hip surgery and was excluded from the subsequent longitudinal analysis, with radiological data retained up to surgery. One additional patient had missing radiographic assessments because behavioral difficulties precluded imaging; all other patients had 4-year assessments available. Hip dysplasia was assessed at baseline and 1, 2, 3, and 4 years after HSC-GT using acetabular index and migration percentage on radiographs and MRIs, as well as cartilaginous acetabular index and cartilaginous migration percentage on MRI. Radiological measurements were compared with published age- and sex-specific normative values. Mean ± SD age at last follow-up was 5.8 ± 0.5 years. Results Radiographic acetabular index and migration percentage decreased longitudinally (acetabular index: fixed effect estimate = -2.7° per year [95% CI -3.5° to -1.9°]; p Conclusion These findings suggest that hip dysplasia may stabilize or improve after OTL-203 treatment, supporting continued radiological surveillance in young children after HSC-GT. Longer-term prospective multicenter studies are needed to assess durability and clinical relevance and to compare outcomes with bone marrow transplantation. Level of evidence Level IV, therapeutic study.

title: High-Strength Tape for Cable Structure Reconstruction During Arthroscopic Repair of L-Shaped Rotator Cuff Tears.
authors: Liu S, Ren Y, Jia Y, Ye N, Dou Z, Jia J, Na Y.
abstract: With the innovation and progressive maturation of arthroscopic techniques, the advantages of minimally invasive surgery and accelerated rehabilitation have made arthroscopy a preferred option for patients with rotator cuff injuries. However, for complex rotator cuff tears, such as "L-shaped" tendon tears, the risk of postoperative retear remains considerable. The cable structure, serving as a "suspension bridge" within the rotator cuff, is a critical load-bearing component of the shoulder joint. This structure is frequently compromised in "L-shaped" rotator cuff tears. In this report, we describe an arthroscopic technique using high-strength tape to restore the cable structure and treat "L-shaped" rotator cuff tears. The key steps include using high-strength tape to reduce the retracted tendon stump and restore the cable structure, thereby re-establishing mechanical integrity, reducing tension on the repaired tendon, and minimizing the cutting effect of sutures on the tendon. Finally, the sutures from the medial-row anchor are employed to perform a "Margin Convergence" repair of the longitudinal tear component.

title: Gait kinematics and toe-clearance in younger and healthy older adults: A comparison accounting for walking speed.
authors: Sato H, Kamide N, Sakamoto M, Ando M, Shiba Y.
abstract: Age-related reductions in walking speed often confound the interpretation of gait alterations in older adults. This study compared lower-limb kinematics and trip-related parameters between younger and healthy older adults after controlling for body size and sex and adjusting for walking speed. Data from 325 older adults (mean age 72 (SD 4) years) and 100 younger adults (mean age 22 (SD 2) years) were analyzed using quantitative gait analysis. Propensity score matching (1:1 ratio) was performed to pair participants by sex, height, and weight, yielding 76 matched pairs. Kinematic parameters (sagittal plane motion of the pelvis, hip, knee, and ankle) and trip-related parameters (minimum toe clearance [minTC] and probability of tripping [POT]) were compared using ANCOVA with walking speed as a covariate. Regardless of walking speed, older adults exhibited significantly greater peak anterior pelvic tilt and hip flexion than younger adults. During maximum-effort walking, older adults demonstrated significantly higher minTC and lower POT than younger adults. Regression analysis showed that peak knee flexion was more strongly associated with walking speed in older adults, whereas cadence was more strongly associated with walking speed in younger adults. These findings suggest differences between younger and older adults in the gait parameters associated with walking speed. They also indicate that healthy older adults do not necessarily exhibit less favorable toe-clearance-related biomechanical indicators during fast walking than younger adults.

title: GATA2 Deficiency Presenting With a WHIM-Like Phenotype and Subsequent Development of Monosomy 7-Associated Myelodysplastic Syndrome in an Adolescent Female: A Case Report.
authors: Eghbali A, Poortavakol M, Mirmohammadi HS.
abstract: We report an 18-year-old female with GATA2 deficiency presenting with a WHIM-like phenotype, including pancytopenia, monocytopenia, CD19 + B-cell depletion, sensorineural hearing loss, and cutaneous warts. Subsequent cytogenetic evaluation revealed monosomy 7 and 7q22 deletion, with bone marrow progression to MDS. She was treated with azacitidine and referred for allogeneic HSCT.

title: Factors associated with tocilizumab primary failure in the treatment of giant cell arteritis.
authors: de Boysson H, Adoukonou NE, Dumont A, Orvain T, Boutemy J, Delacotte C, Gallou S, Hankard A, Maigné G, Silva NM, Philip R, Trenec M, Rocamora A, Deshayes S, Aouba A.
abstract: Objectives Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is the most common systemic vasculitis in adults over 50. Tocilizumab (TCZ), the first biologic approved in GCA, enables glucocorticoid-sparing remission, but reliable predictors of treatment outcome at initiation are lacking. We aimed to identify baseline and follow-up predictors of TCZ failure in GCA. Methods In this retrospective single-centre cohort study, consecutive GCA patients receiving their first TCZ course at Caen University Hospital (2014-2024) were included, excluding early withdrawal ( Results Of 91 patients, TCZ was successful in 43 (47%) and failed in 48 (53%). Baseline multivariable analysis identified three predictors of failure: CRP > 63.5 mg/L (OR 3.40; 95% CI 1.26-9.77; P Conclusions Baseline CRP, LVV and prior relapses can be combined into a simple predictive score to stratify the probability of TCZ response in GCA. Complete metabolic extinction on FDG-PET/CT during treatment further identifies patients at risk of failure.

title: Examining individual and school-level predictors of positive attitudes towards condom use among adolescents in Tanzania: An exploratory analysis using hierarchical linear modeling.
authors: Bryk S, Shichijo A, Kaaya S, Lema I, Minja A, Cannon AC, Mtei R, Somba M, van Praag E, Egger JR, Baumgartner JN.
abstract: Introduction Adolescents shoulder a disproportionate burden of poor sexual and reproductive health (SRH) outcomes in many lower-income countries, including Tanzania. Availability, access, and use of contraception, including condoms, reduces unintended pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections. Research indicates that early attitudes can influence future behavior, yet little is known about young adolescents' attitudes toward condom use. This study examines whether and how knowledge, beliefs, and sociodemographic factors influence attitudes toward condom use among adolescents in Tanzania. Methods Data are from a school-cluster randomized controlled trial with Standard 7 adolescents in two Tanzanian districts. Using an analytic sample of 1,057 adolescents from 20 primary schools, descriptive analysis and hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) were conducted to parse out individual- and school-level influences that shape attitudes towards condom use. Results Individual and aggregate characteristics of the school environment were associated with attitudes toward condom use. At the individual level, more positive attitudes were associated with being male, having access to condoms, and having knowledge about condom use and pregnancy prevention. At the school-level, more positive attitudes were associated with a larger male population in classes, greater breadth of pregnancy knowledge among students, and having relationships with trusted adults. Conclusions Findings suggest that adolescents largely turn to peers and adults for information and guidance regarding condoms. In turn, the views and beliefs of others can influence attitudes towards condom use. Schools might be an effective unit of change for interventions to facilitate more group-based education about the prevention of negative SRH outcomes.

title: Emergency Resection for Perforated Small Bowel Metastasis from Primary Lung Cancer During Systemic Therapy: A Case Report.
authors: Miyaoka Y, Shimada S, Iwaguchi Y, Ganchiku Y, Saito T, Yokoyama R, Hanaoka D, Taketomi A.
abstract: Introduction Small bowel metastases from lung cancer may remain clinically occult until serious complications, including obstruction, bleeding, and perforation, occur. We report a case of perforated jejunal metastasis with a synchronous ileal metastasis at high risk of obstruction, identified during emergency surgery while several previously documented extraintestinal lesions had decreased in size. Case presentation A 75-year-old woman with metastatic non-small cell lung carcinoma favoring adenocarcinoma had a programmed death-ligand 1 tumor proportion score of 95% and no targetable alteration on the companion-diagnostic panel. Pembrolizumab monotherapy (200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks) was administered for 4 cycles; no antiangiogenic agent had been administered concurrently or previously. Eleven days after the 4th dose, she developed acute abdominal pain. CT showed focal small bowel wall thickening, adjacent extraluminal air, diffuse bowel edema, and ascites. Emergency surgery revealed a perforated jejunal tumor approximately 20 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz. Systematic examination of the entire small bowel identified a 2nd, nearly circumferential ileal tumor approximately 15 cm proximal to the terminal ileum with marked luminal narrowing; both lesions were resected. Histopathological examination showed metastatic poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of pulmonary origin. Neither tumor necrosis nor a histological treatment effect was identified, and the non-neoplastic mucosa showed no findings suggestive of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related enteritis. The patient was discharged on POD 19. Pembrolizumab was not resumed. PET-CT on POD 30 demonstrated widespread disease progression, and the patient transitioned to best supportive care. She died on POD 61 without recurrent gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, or bleeding. Conclusions Clinically occult small bowel metastases may present with perforation or impending obstruction during systemic therapy even while previously documented lesions at other sites decrease in size. Because the intestinal lesions were not identifiable before treatment, true discordant progression could not be established. Histopathological findings supported direct tumor-related perforation rather than treatment-induced tumor necrosis or immune-mediated enteritis. Emergency source control and systematic examination of the entire small bowel may identify additional lesions that alter operative management.

title: Effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Guo Z, Guo W, Gu Y, Ning L, Zhao Y.
abstract: Background Overweight and obesity are common among middle-aged and older adults, and obesity is a chronic, multifactorial disease that, particularly when accompanied by central adiposity or metabolic abnormalities, is associated with increased cardiometabolic, cancer-related, musculoskeletal, and functional risks. Leptin and ghrelin are key hormones involved in energy balance regulation and may be dysregulated in obesity, but evidence regarding the effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity remains inconsistent. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in this population. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from database inception to 5 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials that enrolled middle-aged or older adults with overweight or obesity and reported leptin or ghrelin levels before and after an exercise intervention. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were synthesized using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 15. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 ; a fixed-effect model was used when I 2 I 2 ≥ 50%. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication-bias assessments were conducted. Results Twenty-one randomized controlled trials were included. Exercise interventions were associated with significantly lower leptin levels than control conditions based on 18 comparisons (SMD = -0.32, 95% CI [-0.47 to -0.18], P I 2 = 22%). Exercise interventions were also associated with significantly higher ghrelin levels based on nine comparisons (SMD = 0.45, 95% CI [0.11-0.79], P = 0.01), although heterogeneity was substantial ( I 2 = 74%). Subgroup analyses suggested that exercise-related characteristics may partly contribute to variability in leptin and ghrelin responses, but these findings were exploratory. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses supported the stability of the main estimates. For leptin, Egger's test suggested possible funnel-plot asymmetry, but trim-and-fill analysis did not impute any missing comparison and the pooled estimate remained unchanged. Conclusion Exercise interventions were associated with reduced leptin levels and increased ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity. The leptin finding appeared relatively consistent, whereas the ghrelin finding should be interpreted cautiously because of fewer comparisons and substantial heterogeneity. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and should not be used to define an optimal exercise prescription. Further randomized controlled trials with more standardized exercise protocols, clearer dietary control, and consistent hormone measurement are needed to clarify the clinical relevance of these changes.

title: Duration and barriers of physical education teaching in primary schools in 6 French departments.
authors: Hermand E, Durali S, Rolan H, Munoz L, Pezé T, Smee V.
abstract: Purpose Regular physical activity plays an important role in preventing sedentary lifestyles and reducing the risk of chronic diseases. In French primary schools, Physical Education (PE) represents the main compulsory opportunity for structured physical activity during school hours. This study aimed to assess self-reported weekly PE duration among primary school teachers in six French departments and to identify teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration, as well as the main obstacles to PE delivery reported by teachers. Methods Between March 2021 and June 2024, as the survey implementation in the different areas took place, an anonymous online questionnaire was sent to primary school teachers in six French departments about the time spent teaching PE and their professional habits in this subject. Results A total of 1,967 responses (overall response rate 3.9%) were collected and analysed: mean weekly PE duration reached 2 h 23 min ± 1 h 04 min in preschool and 2 h 28 min ± 51 min in elementary school, both below the mandatory programme durations. Higher PE duration was associated with longer seniority, fewer pupils in class, longer peri-activity around PE (transportation, locker room), multigrade class, suburban schools, the implementation of APQ (Activité Physique Quotidienne, a novel compulsory subject focused on daily physical activity), a higher feeling of competence and fewer obstacles declared. Conclusions In this sample of primary school teachers from six French departments, self-reported PE duration was below the durations recommended by nationals programmes, consistent with previous French studies. Because of its cross-sectional nature, self-report survey conducted in a limited number of departments, no causal relationships can be inferred and the findings should not be generalized to France as a whole. Nonetheless, this study identifies several teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration that may warrant further investigation, including through longitudinal or intervention research. Given the essential role of physical activity in the health of children and future adults, addressing barriers to PE delivery in schools remains a public health priority.

title: Distal Clavicle Plate Combined With EndoButton Device for the Treatment of Neer Type IIB Distal Clavicle Fractures.
authors: Zhu T, Huang C, Fan H, Hu X, Fu Y, Dong H, Zhang Y.
abstract: The present article describes a surgical technique for the management of Neer type IIB distal clavicle fractures using a distal clavicle plate combined with an EndoButton device. The procedure consists of stepwise arthroscopic evaluation and exposure, fracture reduction, conoid ligament reconstruction, and plate fixation. This combined approach allows for concurrent management of intra-articular lesions, provides stable fixation, reduces the risk of iatrogenic clavicle fractures, and facilitates early postoperative rehabilitation. Nevertheless, it has certain limitations: the approach is not minimally invasive, its indications are relatively narrow, and it requires advanced arthroscopic expertise. All in all, this surgical approach is applicable to both acute and chronic Neer type IIB distal clavicle fractures.

title: Correction.
Contemporary management of severe generalized tetanus: an evidence-based review.
authors: Pothumarthy VSK, Tirlangi PK, Nagesh SK, Bhat R, Varma M, Gupta N.
abstract: Background Severe generalized tetanus remains associated with substantial mortality despite being vaccine preventable. Management is complicated by limited high-quality evidence, conflicting trial results, and the need to balance effective control of spasms and autonomic dysfunction against the risks of prolonged mechanical ventilation. Methods We describe the management of a 57-year-old man with Ablett grade III generalized tetanus and use this case as a clinical framework for an expert narrative review. The review synthesizes randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, prospective studies, and relevant observational literature addressing neuromodulatory therapy, airway management, autonomic dysfunction, intrathecal antitoxin, and supportive critical care. Results The patient was managed using a multimodal strategy comprising continuous midazolam infusion, magnesium sulphate, oral baclofen, dexmedetomidine, intramuscular and intrathecal human tetanus immunoglobulin, and meticulous low-stimulation supportive care. Therapy was titrated using serial bedside assessment of neuromuscular burden. He recovered without endotracheal intubation, neuromuscular blockade, or tracheostomy and was discharged on day 21. We argue that discordant findings in tetanus trials are substantially attributable to heterogeneity in disease severity, clinical practice, airway management thresholds, and resource availability, rather than to true therapeutic inconsistency. Available evidence supports a physiology-directed multimodal approach using agents with complementary mechanisms to suppress spasms and autonomic dysfunction while preserving spontaneous ventilation whenever safely feasible. Conclusions Management of severe tetanus should focus on achieving physiological targets rather than escalating individual drugs. A structured, individualized, multimodal neuromodulatory strategy delivered within an experienced, low-stimulation critical care environment may allow selected patients to be managed without mechanical ventilation; safety cannot be established from a single case and requires prospective evaluation. Greater emphasis should also be placed on preventive adult immunization, as vaccination remains the intervention most likely to reduce the burden of severe tetanus.

title: Clinical outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation stratified by paraspinal muscle degeneration: A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Wang L, Shi B, Zhang W, Ma X, Cao B, Xiao H, Zhang H.
abstract: Objective To evaluate pain and functional outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH) stratified by preoperative paraspinal muscle degeneration, and to examine whether degeneration grade was associated with 2-year outcomes. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 129 patients with single-level LDH who underwent surgery between December 2021 and December 2023 and had complete preoperative, 1-month, 6-month, and 2-year follow-up data. Two blinded spine surgeons independently graded bilateral multifidus fatty infiltration from 0 to 4 on axial T2-weighted MRI at the mid-disc level; linearly weighted kappa was 0.967(95% CI, 0.937 to 0.989). Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using covariate-adjusted patient-level random-intercept mixed-effects models with degeneration grade treated as a categorical factor, followed by adjusted 2-year regression and post hoc sensitivity analyses. Results Of 136 screened patients, 129 were included after excluding 2 with incomplete records and 5 lost to follow-up. The cohort included 64 men and 65 women, with a mean age of 57.36 ± 11.63 years; grades 0-4 included 13, 25, 33, 32 and 26 patients, respectively. All grades improved substantially. In covariate-adjusted mixed models treating grade as a factor, the grade effect was significant for back pain VAS (P Conclusions Fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery was associated with substantial pain relief and functional improvement across all multifidus degeneration grades. More severe degeneration showed modest prognostic associations with residual back pain and disability, but the estimated effects were smaller than published minimal clinically important differences. These findings should inform cautious counseling and hypothesis generation rather than be used as a standalone surgical decision rule.

title: Clinical findings associated with diagnosing lumbar foraminal stenosis: systematic review.
authors: Ekedahl H, Av Kák Gustafsson ME, Larsson C.
abstract: Purpose To determine the diagnostic value of history taking and clinical examination tests for diagnosing lumbar radicular pain due to foraminal stenosis (FS) as established using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Method An electronic search of PubMed, CINAHL, Embase and MEDLINE was conducted. Studies with diagnostic accuracy of FS using dichotomous index tests (patient history measures and clinical examination tests) were included. The risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS 2) tool. Diagnostic value of index test was analyzed using proportions of positive findings (sensitivity). Specificity was not obtained. The results of all patients with FS were compared with all patients of a different specific diagnosis, disc herniation (DH) or central spinal stenosis (CSS), by comparing the proportion of positive findings for each index test. Results A total of 2,491records were identified. After title and abstract screening, 1,951 records were excluded, and 84 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility. Finally, 15 studies were included. No study investigating accuracy of tests for patients with recess stenosis was found. In the included studies, 737 subjects had FS, and 10 different index tests were found (2 patient history measures and 8 clinical examination tests). Of the 15 included studies, overall risk of bias was judged as low in two studies, while remaining studies had some concerns primarily due to unclear risk in the index test and flow and timing domains. Applicability concerns were generally low across studies. The index tests with highest average proportion of positive findings in detecting FS were Leg pain at rest (74%; 4 studies, n = 190) and Lumbar extensions test (66%; 11 studies, n = 537); and the test with the lowest proportion of positive findings was Straight leg raise (SLR; 33%; 10 studies, n = 471). Conclusion This review concluded that SLR has the lowest ability to detect lumbar foraminal stenosis, whereas positive Lumbar extension test and Leg pain at rest have the highest ability to detect the diagnosis. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given methodological uncertainties and limited diagnostic accuracy evidence.

title: Care Hotel With Virtual Monitoring as an Alternative Recovery Pathway for Outpatient Total Joint Arthroplasty: Safety and Patient Experience.
authors: Kumar J, Fawcett MA, Ma RT, Sherman CE, Spencer Gardner LS, Ledford CK, Chadha RM, Springer BD.
abstract: Background As total hip (THA) and knee arthroplasty (TKA) transition toward outpatient care, medical centers need to create models to support same-day discharge (SDD) for all patients, particularly those traveling long distances. A care hotel (CH) with virtual monitoring represents a novel postoperative recovery pathway, and our study evaluates patient safety and experience of this alternative model. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 5324 primary THA and TKA patients from a single tertiary referral center between July 2021 and April 2025. Of these, 590 cases (11%) utilized the CH pathway and were compared to traditional inpatient (IP), and SDD cohorts. Outcomes included demographic characteristics, 30-day emergency department (ED) utilization, hospital readmission rates, and patient-reported experience metrics. Results The 30-day ED return rate for CH patients was significantly lower than IP group (3.9 vs 6.8%, P = .006). The CH ED return rate was also lower than SDD; however, not statistically significant (3.9 vs 5.5%, P = .15). Among those returning to the ED, hospital readmission rates were 47.8% for CH, 39.3% for IP and 31.8% for SDD ( P > .22). Patient satisfaction among responders was high, with 94% of CH patients reporting they would be likely or very likely to recommend the alternative recovery pathway. Conclusions The CH provides a safe, well-received recovery pathway for THA and TKA patients with low ED utilization, acceptable readmission rates, and high patient satisfaction among responders. The CH model may represent a scalable strategy to expand access for outpatient THA and TKA while preserving hospital resources.

title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
authors: Fawaz S, Ghaouche J, Bouthors C, Lazure T, Meyrignac O, Cluzel G, Devilder M, Morice P, Court C, Creze M.
abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18 F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

title: Blood-based mass spectrometry in plasma cell disorders: From residual secretory activity to multimodal residual disease assessment.
authors: Han X, Liu T, Zhang Y.
abstract: Bone marrow measurable residual disease (BM-MRD) is a powerful prognostic marker in multiple myeloma but is invasive, spatially limited, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Blood-based mass spectrometry (MS), using serum or plasma according to the assay and study, sensitively detects residual monoclonal immunoglobulin, free light chain (FLC), and clonotypic peptide signals. Recent myeloma studies have used measurable residual activity (MRA) for MS-detectable residual secretory activity; however, MRA remains an emerging, non-standardised concept and is not equivalent to IMWG-defined marrow MRD. This critical review examines the analytical basis, biological interpretation, and clinical evidence for blood-based MS in multiple myeloma, AL amyloidosis, and related plasma cell disorders. Across platforms, blood-based MS detects low-level monoclonal signals beyond conventional electrophoretic methods, although assays are not analytically interchangeable. Blood-marrow discordance may reflect differences in assay target, protein clearance, marrow sampling, and disease distribution. Prospective evidence, including GMMG-HD7, supports serum MS-defined MRA as a prognostic biomarker; combined serum MS and BM-MRD further refined risk, with double-positive patients showing the poorest progression-free survival, but treatment was not modified according to serum MS status. In AL amyloidosis, FLC-MS may refine conventional complete response by detecting persistent amyloidogenic light chains associated with organ response and survival. Blood-based MS should therefore be viewed as a complementary measure of residual secretory activity. Current evidence supports prognostic validity and longitudinal monitoring, but treatment-guiding clinical utility remains unproven.

title: Biological Augmentation of Arthroscopic Partial-Thickness Bursal-Sided Rotator Cuff Repair Using Minced Autologous Glenohumeral Ligament Tissue Particles.
authors: Liu H, Wang X, Mao H, Shen W.
abstract: Rotator cuff tears are associated with high retear rates and limited healing capacity after repair. We describe an arthroscopic biological augmentation technique using minced autologous glenohumeral ligament tissue during double-row partial-thickness bursal-sided rotator cuff repair. Ligament tissue is harvested, processed into particulate grafts, and implanted within a suture-bridge construct to create a stable, biologically active interpositional layer at the repair site. This technique provides a simple and fully autologous method to enhance the local healing environment during rotator cuff repair.

title: Association of tranexamic acid with early death or massive transfusion after severe pelvic ring fractures: A nationwide registry-based cohort study.
authors: Matsumoto S, Aoki M, Shimizu M.
abstract: Introduction Evidence for tranexamic acid during emergency treatment of severe pelvic ring fractures is limited. We examined its association with early death or massive transfusion. Methods We studied adults in the Japan Trauma Data Bank from 2019 to 2023 with blunt pelvic ring fractures of Abbreviated Injury Scale severity 3 or higher. Exposure was any in-hospital tranexamic acid. The primary outcome was death within 24 h after arrival or transfusion of at least 20 Japanese red blood cell units within 24 h after injury. We used multiple imputation, propensity-score overlap weighting, and hospital-clustered standard errors. Results Among 5288 patients, 1985 (37.5%) received tranexamic acid. The weighted primary-outcome risks were 13.0% with tranexamic acid and 18.1% without it (risk ratio 0.72, 95% confidence interval 0.60-0.87). The association was driven by 24-hour mortality (risk ratio 0.62, 95% confidence interval 0.48-0.80); massive transfusion alone (risk ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.73-1.21) and mean red blood cell use did not differ. Any red blood cell transfusion was more frequent with tranexamic acid (risk ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.30). The primary-outcome risk ratio was 0.76 (0.62-0.93) after excluding deaths within 2 h and 0.81 (0.65-1.00) when both components were assessed within 24 h after injury. Conclusion The mortality association was not accompanied by lower transfusion requirements and weakened when outcome time origins were aligned. Because treatment timing was unavailable, these findings do not establish an independent survival benefit and provide no corroborating transfusion evidence of a pelvic-specific hemostatic benefit.

title: Association between dynamic balance and change‑of‑direction performance in athletes: A systematic review and three‑level meta‑analysis.
authors: Wang R, He Z, Bao D, Zhou L.
abstract: Dynamic balance is considered relevant to change-of-direction (COD) performance in athletes, but evidence remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified this association and examined whether it varied by balance test direction, movement plane, COD angle, and sex. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 31 December 2025. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for analytical cross-sectional studies. Thirteen observational studies involving 722 athletes were included. A small but significant negative correlation was observed between dynamic balance and COD completion time (r = -0.217, p = 0.006). Heterogeneity was substantial and mainly attributable to between-study differences (I 2 = 65.9%). Balance test direction significantly moderated the association (p < 0.001). Significant small negative correlations were observed for frontal-plane (r = -0.277, p = 0.002) and 45° diagonal-plane balance (r = -0.192, p = 0.023), but not sagittal-plane balance. Tests limited to anterior, posteromedial, and posterolateral directions showed a medium correlation (r = -0.329, p < 0.001). COD angle and sex were not significant moderators. These findings suggest that dynamic balance should be assessed alongside direct COD testing and other relevant capacities.

title: Arthroscopic Marrow-Stimulating Procedure for Full-Thickness Knee Cartilage Lesions.
authors: M J, C R J, Subramaniam P S R, Thomas AK, M C A.
abstract: Articular cartilage defects remain challenging to treat because cartilage is avascular, sparsely cellular and has limited intrinsic healing potential. If left untreated, these lesions may progress to degenerative osteoarthritis, resulting in persistent pain and functional limitation. Marrow stimulation techniques such as drilling and microfracture are commonly used to promote repair by accessing subchondral bone marrow elements. Although these procedures are simple and widely practiced, their clinical benefits are often limited to the short- to mid-term, and they may disrupt the subchondral bone plate, potentially compromising future cartilage restoration options. Nanofracture represents an evolution of traditional microfracture, using smaller-diameter (1 mm) and deeper (9 mm) perforations to enhance marrow access while minimizing trabecular bone compaction. This article describes an arthroscopic nanofracture technique using a curved guide and depth-controlled wire, allowing precise, evenly spaced perforations and improved access to challenging regions such as the posterior femoral condyles and tibial plateau without added surgical morbidity. By preserving subchondral architecture and ensuring consistent marrow stimulation, nanofracture may improve the biological quality of repair tissue.

title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction With Preservation of the Tibial Insertion of the Hamstring Tendons and Double-Pulley Technique.
authors: Liu Z, Yang Y, Hu L, Su S, Huang P.
abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is one of the most common knee disorders, occurring mostly in sports-related injuries. After injury, knee stability is compromised, leading to further damage to surrounding structures, such as meniscal tears, cartilage wear, and other lesions. Therefore, timely and effective repair of the injured ACL is critical. At present, a variety of surgical techniques are available for ACL reconstruction, with substantial differences in graft selection and fixation methods, and no universal consensus has been reached in the academic community. Hamstring tendons are among the most commonly used autografts. Preservation of the tibial insertion of the hamstring tendons has been proven to provide distinct biological and mechanical advantages. This technical note introduces an ACL reconstruction technique using a double-pulley system, which allows effective intraoperative adjustment of tension in each bundle of the reconstructed ACL to achieve highly uniform tension across all bundles. Furthermore, the native tibial insertions of the hamstring tendons (gracilis and semitendinosus) are preserved, maximizing blood supply to the reconstructed ligament. This approach facilitates the ligamentization of the graft and shortens the tendon-bone healing period.

title: A simple independent high-strength suture augmentation significantly improves tendon biomechanical properties in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
authors: Dung TC, Elsheikh R, Kha TD, An NT, Makram AM, Chanh PT, Nam NH, Huy NT.
abstract: Purpose The all-inside anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) technique heavily depends on continuous graft stability, making graft preparation critical. Graft augmentation techniques have been proposed to enhance stability in ACLR. This biomechanical study investigated whether an independent high-strength suture augmentation, applied parallel to the tendon graft, improves construct properties. Methods Thirty-eight specimens were allocated to three groups: Suture (n = 10; No. 2 non-absorbable braided polyethylene), Graft (n = 13; bovine tendon), and Graft+Suture (n = 15; combined construct). All specimens underwent uniaxial tensile testing, including a preconditioning phase from 0 to 350 N followed by a load-to-failure test at 50 mm/min to determine elongation (mm), ultimate failure load (UFL, in N), and construct stiffness (N/mm). Statistical analysis was performed using one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc analysis. Results The Graft+Suture group exhibited significantly lower elongation (2.72 ± 0.51 mm) compared with both the Graft group (4.44 ± 1.59 mm; MD -1.71 mm, 95% CI -2.86 to -0.56; p = 0.002) and the Suture group (7.77 ± 1.37 mm; MD -5.05 mm, 95% CI -6.29 to -3.81; p Conclusion In this in vitro bovine model, independent high-strength suture augmentation significantly improved tendon graft biomechanical properties, producing higher UFL and stiffness, while reducing elongation. These findings suggest a potential strategy for graft reinforcement, though a more cautious interpretation is warranted pending in vivo and clinical validation. Level of evidence Not applicable.

title: A feasible and cost-effective method to induce distal radius fractures in full-length forearm human cadaveric specimens.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Krüger J, Terndrup M, Thomsen MG, von Keudell A, Andersen JA, Maleitzke T.
abstract: Introduction Reported rates of loss of reduction in nonoperatively treated distal radius fractures (DRF) range from 17 to 71%. Thus, realistic biomechanical models are warranted to test novel immobilization devices that prevent loss of reduction in nonoperative fracture management. Currently available human cadaveric specimen models have several limitations: (i) disrupted soft tissue integrity, (ii) difficulty in replicating complex fracture patterns, and (iii) high technical demands and costs. Therefore, the aim of this study was to establish a feasible and accessible method for inducing DRFs, that accurately reflects in-vivo biomechanical fracture conditions in tissue-intact cadaveric specimens, suitable for testing of novel immobilization devices. Materials and methods Fifteen upper extremity cadaveric specimens were included. Specimens were prepared as full‑length forearm models. Using a repurposed strength training tower as a vertical drop tower, fractures were induced by proximally administering 120-135 J impacts. CT scans were performed pre- and post-fracture induction. All fractures were classified according to the AO/OTA classification. Results DRFs were successfully induced in all 15 specimens. A single 120 J impact produced a DRF in 11 out of 15 cases (73%). A second impact was administered in 4 out of 15 specimens (27%). Eleven of the 15 induced DRFs (73%) were classified as AO/OTA type C fractures, most commonly 2R3C3.2. Concomitant distal ulnar fractures were present in 6 cases, concomitant carpal fractures in 9 specimens. The overall cost of the setup amounted to 947 €. Conclusions This study presents a feasible, cost-effective method to induce DRFs in tissue-intact, full-length human cadaveric forearm specimens. The setup consistently produces DRFs, predominantly AO/OTA type C, which can, with certain limitations, be utilized for biomechanical testing of immobilization devices, while also being uited for surgical and anatomical education.

title: A Case of Recurrent Gastric Cancer in Which Rheumatoid Arthritis and Sjögren's Syndrome Became Evident With Nivolumab.
authors: Takemoto H, Nishibeppu K, Kubota T, Inoue H, Takabatake K, Konishi H, Fujiwara H, Shiozaki A.
abstract: A 59-year-old man with recurrent gastric cancer began nivolumab as third-line therapy and subsequently experienced joint pain and dry eyes. Symptoms worsened despite NSAIDs. He was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome, associated with nivolumab, and was successfully treated with immunosuppressive and anti-rheumatic medications.

title: A Baltic Sea microbiome-derived Type III polyketide synthase produces host-protective alkylresorcinols in E. coli.
authors: López-Gutiérrez S, Espinosa-Barrera LA, Soto-Hernández A, Zuleta-Prada H, Bustos-Brito C, Cardona-Félix CS, Utrilla J, Velazquez-Cruz B, Cárdenas-Conejo Y, Araujo-León JA, Aguilar-Hernández V, Osuna-Castro JA, Esquivel B, Serrano-Posada H, Centeno-Leija S.
abstract: Marine microorganisms are a prolific source of novel polyketide synthases (PKSs) that generate structurally diverse and functional polyketides. Here, we identify a novel type III PKS, ArsMB, from Pontimonas sp. via metagenomic mining of a Baltic Sea microbiome. Heterologous expression of arsMB synthetic gene in an Escherichia coli host that lacks a native type III PKS, combined with a two-step strategy to boost acyl-CoA precursor availability in a glucose-mineral medium, enabled the in vivo synthesis of two cell-associated alkylresorcinols, identified by GC-MS as 5-pentadecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars1) and 5-tridecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars2). The product profile is consistent with a tetraketide alkylresorcinol biosynthetic pathway utilizing C16 and C14 acyl starter units, drawn from the host acyl-CoA pool. In agreement, AlphaFold2-based structural modeling predicts a Cys139/His275/Asn308 catalytic triad and a long hydrophobic substrate tunnel compatible with long-chain acyl starter units. E. coli producing the amphipathic cell-associated alkylresorcinols ars1/ars2 exhibited increased resistance to muralytic digestion by endolysins and to hydrogen peroxide. These findings expand the known repertoire of marine-derived type III PKSs and highlight the biotechnological potential of ArsMB-derived alkylresorcinols.

title: Visually detectable pointer deviation of the nextar surgical navigation system with c-arm, o-arm and ct imaging: a bench-top study using a two-dimensional phantom.
authors: Zaccaria R, Suero E, Lampert C, Simon D, Neudeck R, Hauck S, Weigert A, Reidler P, Böcker W, Wegener B.
abstract: Background The accuracy of surgical navigation systems is critical for their safe and effective clinical use. This bench-top study evaluated whether a positional deviation of the pointer tip from a 1-mm target could be detected on the display of the NextAR surgical navigation system (Medacta International SA, Switzerland) when image-to-patient registration was based on C-arm, O-arm or CT imaging, and whether such a detectable deviation depended on the distance between the fiducial reference marker and the target. The endpoint was a visual observation of the pointer on the display and not an independently measured target registration error (TRE). Methods A flat two-dimensional phantom (millimetre graph paper on a wooden board) carried two parallel rows of 20 steel nails with 1-mm heads. Adjacent nails were 10 mm apart and the rows 120 mm apart. The fiducial was fixed midway between the rows at the start of the grid and defined the origin. The phantom was imaged with a Ziehm Vision RFD 3D C-arm, a Medtronic O-arm MVS O2 and a Siemens SOMATOM Drive CT. Ten image acquisitions, each followed by a new image-to-patient registration, were performed per modality. For each nail within the imaged volume, the tip of a navigated pointer was placed on the nail head and the operator visually inspected the NextAR three-dimensional display for a deviation. NextAR provides no numerical deviation value. No artificial registration error was introduced, and the pointer tip was not independently measured. The primary endpoint, visually detectable pointer deviation (hereafter detectable deviation), was a visible offset of the pointer tip from the centre of the nail head on the display. The threshold of about 1 mm is an approximate limit given by the size of the nail head and the millimetre grid and was neither calibrated nor independently measured. Results are descriptive, with exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence intervals. Results No detectable deviation was observed in any acquisition (0/10 per modality; exact 95% CI 0-30.9%; overall 0/30, 95% CI 0-11.6%). The maximum fiducial-to-target distances evaluated were 143 mm with C-arm, 152 mm with O-arm and 199 mm with CT imaging. The intervals refer to acquisitions under fixed bench-top conditions. Conclusions Under the controlled conditions of this two-dimensional bench-top experiment, no deviation was visible on the NextAR display with any of the three imaging modalities. Because the endpoint was a visual assessment limited to about 1 mm and was not independently measured against an external reference, the study does not establish submillimetre accuracy, equivalence between modalities, absence of distance-related effects, or clinical reliability. Verification in anatomically appropriate cadaveric and clinical settings is required. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Two Additional Variants Expand the Genotypic Spectrum of Dominant Calpain-3 Deficiencies.
authors: Krag T, Dunø M, Witting N, Vissing J.
abstract: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type D4 is caused by a single pathogenic variant of the CAPN3 gene coding for calpain-3 and is clinically milder than the more common recessive form, type R1. It is likely underdiagnosed, and expanding the phenotype-genotype relationship is needed to establish a clinical guideline for this disorder.

title: Tranexamic Acid Administration is Associated With Lower Transfusion Rates and Wound Complications Following Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
authors: Kumaran P, Wier J, Telang SS, Liu SH, Becerra J, Lieberman JR, Heckmann ND.
abstract: Background Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used in total joint arthroplasty, but data on its efficacy in periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) of the knee are scarce. We assessed TXA efficacy in revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for PJI. Methods A national database was queried for patients ≥18 years undergoing stage-one revision TKA for PJI from 2016 to 2023. Patients with and without TXA exposure were propensity matched. Multivariable logistic regression assessed primary outcomes (postoperative transfusion, bleeding complications, and wound complications) and secondary outcomes (thromboembolic complications). Results Overall, 13,247 TXA patients were matched 1:1 to 13,247 non-TXA patients on comorbidities, Charlson Comorbidity Index, demographics, hospital characteristics, and preoperative transfusion rates, all with standardized mean differences P P P = .563). Odds of aggregate venous thromboembolism (aOR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.82-1.13, P = .874), deep vein thrombosis (aOR: 1.00, 95% CI: 1.00-1.01, P = .309), and pulmonary embolism (aOR: 1.06, 95% CI: 0.83-1.34, P = .639) were similar. Conclusions TXA was associated with lower rates of transfusion and aggregate wound complications, without increased venous thromboembolism risk, during revision TKA for PJI.

title: The impact of observing dynamic vs. isometric fatiguing contractions on subsequent strength performance.
authors: Sardroodian M, Rahmani H, Aboozari N, Behm DG.
abstract: Action observation (AO) and empathy engage neural networks involved in motor execution, suggesting that watching others perform actions might influence one's own motor behavior. It remains unclear whether observing fatigue-inducing contractions, affects subsequent performance. Sixteen recreationally active participants completed maximal voluntary isometric contractions and dynamic tasks under both observation and no-observation conditions in a randomized, cross-over design. Key outcomes including quadriceps and hamstrings electromyography (EMG), maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC) force, repetition count, heart rate, and ratings of perceived exertion (RPE). Repeated measures ANOVAs revealed significant and near significant main effects of time for quadriceps EMG F(5,75) = 14.9, ( p p = 0.07), and MVIC (F(1.42, 19.68) = 14.04, p < .001. As expected, fatigue-related decreases in force and EMG activity were observed over time, indicating typical fatigue progression. However, no differences emerged between the observation and control conditions for any variables, suggesting that watching a confederate perform fatiguing actions does not alter motor performance, neuromuscular activation, or subjective effort. These findings highlight that visual exposure to fatigue in others is insufficient to modulate subsequent motor or perceptual responses. This underscores the importance of incorporating emotional salience, social relevance, and task engagement, when aiming to apply them effectively in sports and rehabilitation settings.

title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on bone metabolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials of predominantly first-generation agents.
authors: Safargar M, Ahmadi N, Prabahar K, Zandi R, Kord-Varkaneh H.
abstract: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) improve cardiometabolic outcomes, but their isolated effects on human bone remodeling remain uncertain because prior syntheses pooled heterogeneous study designs and active antidiabetic comparators. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the effects of GLP-1RAs versus placebo on densitometric, biochemical, and inflammatory markers of bone metabolism in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Methods Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and PubMed/MEDLINE were searched from inception through May 12, 2026 for randomized placebo-controlled trials of GLP-1RAs or dual incretin agonists administered for 12 to 52 weeks. Eleven trials provided compatible data for random-effects meta-analysis and one additional trial was synthesized narratively, comprising 11 trials of first-generation agents (exenatide, dulaglutide, liraglutide) and one trial of second-generation semaglutide (1.0 mg/week), with zero eligible placebo-controlled trials identified for semaglutide 2.4 mg/week or tirzepatide. Weighted mean differences (WMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) bone mineral density (BMD), bone turnover markers, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and evidence certainty was rated using GRADE. Results Compared with placebo, GLP-1RA treatment reduced lumbar spine BMD (WMD: -0.02 g/cm 2 , 95% CI: -0.03 to -0.00, I 2 = 0.0%; 3 trials, N = 222; Moderate certainty) and increased the bone resorption marker C-terminal telopeptide (CTX) (WMD: 0.05 μg/L, 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.08, I 2 = 72.5%; 6 trials, N = 439; Low certainty), while reducing serum hs-CRP (WMD: -0.49 mg/L, 95% CI: -0.97 to -0.00, I 2 = 0.0%; 4 trials [5 arms], N = 340; Low certainty). No significant differences were observed for femoral neck BMD (WMD: 0.01 g/cm 2 , 95% CI: -0.02 to 0.04, I 2 = 68.9%; 5 trials [6 arms], N = 323; Very Low certainty), total hip BMD (WMD: 0.00 g/cm 2 , 95% CI: -0.02 to 0.03, I 2 = 70.8%; 5 trials [6 arms], N = 382; Low certainty), or procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide (P1NP) (WMD: -1.24 μg/L, 95% CI: -3.61 to 1.13, I 2 = 0.0%; 5 trials, N = 399; Moderate certainty), and leave-one-out exclusion of the single semaglutide trial did not alter the direction or significance of any pooled estimate. Conclusions Treatment with predominantly first-generation GLP-1RAs over 12 to 52 weeks increases osteoclastic bone resorption and induces a small, borderline reduction in lumbar spine BMD while preserving hip BMD and lowering systemic inflammation. Because existing placebo-controlled RCTs largely reflect earlier-generation agents with moderate weight loss, these findings cannot be extrapolated to higher-potency anti-obesity therapies such as semaglutide 2.4 mg/week or tirzepatide, which require dedicated long-term skeletal safety trials.

title: Staged sternal distraction for early thoracic expansion in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Jarrin Lopez A, Zhao A, Darawsheh R, Kephart D, Sebastian VA, Idowu O, Babbitt C, Kim S.
abstract: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS) is a rare inherited multisystem disorder with variable skeletal involvement; severe neonatal thoracic dystrophy is uncommon but can cause thoracic insufficiency and mimic Jeune syndrome. We report staged sternal distraction in a 5-month-old infant with a severely constricted thorax, pulmonary hypoplasia, refractory pulmonary hypertension, tracheostomy-dependent respiratory failure and an iatrogenic posterior tracheal wall injury. Subsequent trio long-read genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in SBDS , c.183_184delinsCT (p.Lys62Ter), inherited paternally, and c.258+2T>C, inherited maternally, establishing a molecular diagnosis of SDS. At presentation, the chest circumference measured 36cm, compared with an age-expected value of 41cm. The patient underwent staged median sternotomy distraction followed by stabilisation with custom fibular allograft struts. At approximately 3 months, chest circumference had increased to 41cm, peak inspiratory pressures had decreased from 40-50cm H 2 O to the mid-20cm H 2 O range, pulmonary hypertension was no longer evident on echocardiography, and the tracheal injury had healed. At 6 months, he remained on home mechanical ventilation, with peak inspiratory pressures in the upper 20cm H 2 O range. To our knowledge, operative thoracic expansion specifically for SDS-associated thoracic insufficiency has not previously been described. In carefully selected infants with severe thoracic insufficiency who are not yet candidates for conventional thoracic reconstruction, staged sternal distraction may serve as an interim strategy to achieve meaningful thoracic expansion.

title: Species composition in the Balanophora laxiflora species complex (Balanophoraceae): molecular and morphological evidence.
authors: Zavialov AE, Samigullin TH, Lyskov DF, Fomichev CI, Logacheva MD, Nuraliev MS.
abstract: The Balanophora laxiflora species complex is one of the most taxonomically difficult lineages within the holoparasitic genus Balanophora . Over the last century, a number of contrasting opinions have been expressed regarding the identities and relationships of the species currently considered as members of this complex. Although the complex is widely distributed across tropical and subtropical Asia, previous studies have focused on its Japanese and Chinese representatives, whereas populations from Southeast Asia have received little attention. Here, we fill this gap through an integrative study with employment of a set of original specimens from several provinces of Vietnam. We present the results of a comprehensive morphological assessment that includes examination of living plants in situ and analysis of alcohol-fixed specimens using light and electron microscopy. We also provide an expanded molecular phylogenetic reconstruction of the species complex and establish the phylogenetic placement of our Vietnamese specimens. We report extensive contradictions between the characteristics of the studied specimens and the presumed morphological boundaries of the currently recognized species. In particular, the dimensions of the claviform bodies of the female inflorescence and their cuticle morphology frequently showed variants attributed to different species within a single specimen. Even when these features were excluded from consideration, 10 of the 16 studied specimens could not be assigned to any species, because each of these specimens demonstrated a mixture of character states considered diagnostic for different species, most of such plants being morphologically intermediate between B. laxiflora and B. yakushimensis . The phylogenetic results do not contradict the idea of distinctness of B. appressa , B. japonica and B. nipponica . At the same time, B. laxiflora , B. parajaponica and B. yakushimensis were inferred as non-monophyletic, and their monophyly cannot be achieved even if the morphologically intermediate specimens are conventionally assigned to species according to their phylogenetic placement. The morphological and phylogenetic evidence therefore unequivocally indicates the need for re-shaping the interspecific boundaries, with one of the possible decisions being merging of B. laxiflora , B. parajaponica and B. yakushimensis into a single species. Further analysis has shown, however, that even after such a modification, the species in the B. laxiflora complex would only weakly be differentiated from each other morphologically. Thus, recognition of the entire lineage as a single species might appear the most appropriate taxonomic solution. We highlight the importance of comprehensive sampling in studies of intricate lineages similar to the B. laxiflora species complex, especially broad geographical coverage and careful assessment of structural diversity within each analyzed population and specimen.

title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship.
authors: Naumova OY, Dobrynin PV, Litwin G, Rychkov SY, Milham MP, Grigorenko EL.
abstract: Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6-16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

title: Robotic surgery for papillary thyroid carcinoma with lateral cervical lymph node metastasis: a hybrid design, observational, propensity score matching cohort study.
authors: Sun H, Zhan L, Qin X, Wang Y, Gao H, Liu Z, Zhao Q, Liao Z, Qiu W, Cai W, Yan J.
abstract: Background Evidence regarding robotic thyroidectomy with modified radical neck dissection (MRND) for papillary thyroid carcinoma with lateral cervical lymph node metastases remains limited, particularly from prospectively large-sample cohorts. Methods This hybrid cohort design study included 150 prospectively enrolled patients who underwent bilateral axillo-breast approach (BABA) robotic thyroidectomy with MRND between 2018 and 2023, and 509 retrospectively identified patients who underwent open MRND by the same surgical team during the same period. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed at a ratio of 1:2 to balance prespecified tumor-related characteristics, resulting in 150 robotic and 300 matched open cases. Patient demographics, surgical profiles, oncological outcomes, and cosmetic virtues were compared. Results After PSM, the groups were well balanced in the prespecified tumor-related characteristics. Robotic MRND was associated with a longer operation time (200.00 [185.00, 220.00] vs 160.00 [140.00, 190.00], p Conclusions In carefully selected patients with low-risk papillary thyroid cancer and lateral lymph node metastases, robotic MRND via BABA demonstrated comparable safety and oncological completeness to the open approach, while offering superior cosmetic outcomes. Research registration unique identification number (uin) ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07229859.

title: Return to play and performance in Division I collegiate pitchers following ulnar collateral ligament surgery: a retrospective case series.
authors: King BW, Westbrooks B, Bailey EP, Sharp C, Aspang JSU, Hammond K, Danilkowicz RM.
abstract: Background The purpose of this study was to evaluate return to play, postoperative performance, and career advancement in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I baseball players following ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) surgery. Methods NCAA Division I pitchers undergoing UCL surgery between 2015 and 2024 were identified using the Tommy John List. Outcomes included return to play, level of return to play, advancement to professional baseball, and pre- and postoperative earned run average (ERA), walks and hits per innings pitched (WHIP), strikeout-to-walk ratio, and innings pitched per season. Comparisons were made between performance outcomes from all preoperative seasons versus all postoperative seasons for pitchers who returned to Division I. Results A total of 264 pitchers were included, with 239 (90.5%) returning to play following UCL surgery. Return-to-performance analysis included 156 pitchers who returned to play at the Division I level. The only significant difference in pre- and postoperative performance for the full cohort was an increase in innings pitched per season (median difference, 6.25; P=0.002). Subgroup analysis of Power 5 pitchers demonstrated significantly higher postoperative ERA (median difference, 0.42; P=0.01) and WHIP (median difference, 0.05; P=0.03), along with a significant increase in innings pitched per season (median difference, 7.94; P=0.01). Conclusions Division I pitchers returned to play at high rates following UCL surgery. Among those who returned to Division I, no significant differences were observed in postoperative ERA, WHIP, or strikeout-to-walk ratio for the full cohort. However, Power 5 conference pitchers displayed small but statistically significant increases in postoperative ERA and WHIP. Level of evidence: IV.

title: Retraining-free multi-task MR image restoration using a pretrained diffusion model with Bayesian optimization.
authors: Fujita N, Terada Y.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) often requires long scan times, and efforts to shorten scans can lead to image degradation, such as undersampling artifacts, increased noise, and reduced spatial resolution. A restoration framework that can address multiple types of degradation without task-specific retraining would therefore be valuable. In this study, we evaluated whether a pretrained score-based diffusion model combined with Bayesian optimization, termed task guidance design with Bayesian optimization (TGD-BO), could provide retraining-free, multi-task MR image restoration for compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction, super-resolution (SR), and denoising (DN). TGD-BO incorporates data-consistency guidance and gradient guidance into the reverse diffusion process and parameterizes their time-varying strengths using compact low-dimensional B-spline-based guidance schedules. For each task, the schedule was optimized by Bayesian optimization using four paired degraded/reference slices from a single adaptation case, and the resulting task-specific schedule was then applied unchanged to an independent test set. In single-task experiments, TGD-BO improved upon the fixed-guidance diffusion baseline in denoising, compressed-sensing reconstruction, and super-resolution, although the improvement in super-resolution was modest. Compared with task-specific supervised baselines, TGD-BO did not uniformly achieve higher peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) or structural similarity (SSIM); in super-resolution, it showed lower PSNR and SSIM but better perceptual similarity as assessed by learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). In joint-task experiments, schedules optimized directly for DN + CS and DN + SR yielded numerically better image-quality metrics than applying the corresponding single-task schedules. Sensitivity analyses showed that the selected schedule and test performance were unchanged when 1, 4, or 8 slices from the same adaptation case were used, whereas changing the adaptation case substantially affected test performance. These results suggest the feasibility of adapting a single pretrained diffusion prior across multiple MR image restoration tasks through guidance calibration without task-specific weight retraining, while indicating that robustness to adaptation-case selection and computational cost require further investigation.

title: Retraction: Insights into the progressive impact of high-fat-diet induced insulin resistance on skeletal muscle and myocardium: A comprehensive study on C57BL6 mice.
authors: PLOS One Editors.

title: Restoration of continuity following damage control surgery for penetrating colon injury - A South African experience.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Kosna S, Kong V, Ko J, He R, Lee H, Cheung C, Wain H, Bekker W, Bruce J, Laing G, Clarke D.
abstract: Introduction The management of colonic injury following damage control surgery (DCS) remains controversial, particularly regarding whether delayed repair (delayed primary repair or anastomosis) or delayed diversion is the safer approach at the repeat laparotomy. This study evaluates the outcomes of these two strategies in penetrating colon injury patients requiring damage control surgery. Methods A retrospective review was conducted of patients sustaining penetrating colon injuries admitted to a South African tertiary trauma centre over 12 years (2012-2024) using an electronic trauma registry. Patients who underwent DCS and survived to planned second-look laparotomy were analysed. At relook, definitive management was categorised as either restoration of bowel continuity (primary suture repair or resection with anastomosis) or delayed diversion (end colostomy with or without mucus fistula). Data on demographics, admission physiology and Injury Severity Score were analysed, with leak rate, mortality and gastrointestinal complications as primary outcomes. Results A total of 653 patients sustained penetrating colonic injury and 132 (20%) required DCS. After exclusions, 96 patients were analysed (42 in the delayed repair group and 54 in the delayed diversion group). The delayed repair group had a 24% leak rate. In the delayed diversion group, 9% of patients experienced colon-related complications. Colon-related morbidity associated with delayed repair was significantly higher than with delayed diversion. Conclusions Restoration of bowel continuity for penetrating colon injuries at repeat laparotomy following DCS is associated with a high rate of anastomotic leak or suture-line failure. Extreme caution is advised when considering delayed repair in this setting.

title: Repeated sprint training in hypoxia as a post-surgical rehabilitation strategy: A case study in an elite badminton player.
authors: Tee CCL, Chong MC, Yeap MW, Yeo WK.
abstract: Badminton is a racquet sport that imposes high demands on both aerobic and anaerobic capacity and involves repetitive, high-intensity movements, increasing the risk of non-contact injuries to joints and muscle-tendon units. Returning to sport-specific conditioning after injury, particularly post-surgery, presents challenges for deconditioned athletes seeking to restore aerobic capacity while minimising mechanical stress imposed on the injured parts. This case study evaluated the feasibility of integrating short-term repeated sprint training in hypoxia (RSH) as a supplementary modality within a late-stage post-lower back surgery rehabilitation program to support aerobic reconditioning before return to sport-specific conditioning. An elite men's singles badminton athlete completed 4-week RSH (FiO 2 ~ 16.5%), alongside his regular rehabilitation schedule. The intervention consisted of 20 × 4-s all-out cycling sprints interspersed with 30-56-s recovery, performed once weekly. Post-intervention lactate profiling suggested a rightward shift in the blood lactate curve, with estimated increases of 33% and 10% in power output at the aerobic and anaerobic thresholds, respectively, indicative of aerobic reconditioning. However, the present findings should be interpreted cautiously due to observed stage-to-stage blood lactate variability, single-case design, and concurrent rehabilitation. Overall, the present study supports the feasibility of incorporating hypoxic RSH in late-stage rehabilitation to facilitate return to sport-specific conditioning.

title: Recurrent enhancer-promoter interactions across samples.
authors: Weston M, Gunjala S, Hu H, Li X.
abstract: Enhancer-promoter interactions (EPIs) are fundamental to gene regulation, and clarifying their recurrence across diverse biological contexts is key to understanding chromatin architecture. Here, we systematically evaluate EPI recurrence using 95 HiChIP and 266 Hi-C datasets spanning multiple cell types, cell lines, and experimental conditions. We find that each of the majority of EPIs identified in any given sample is also observed in other samples, largely independent of assay type, cellular context, or enhancer annotation strategy. EPIs unique to an individual sample tend to occur in regions with fewer neighboring EPIs or in a sample with greater sequencing depth, indicating that many such "unique" EPIs likely reflect low sequencing depth rather than true biological specificity. Collectively, our results suggest that most human EPIs may have already been cataloged, and that gene regulation primarily relies on the selective reuse of a shared pool of EPIs across contexts. Thus, while EPIs are context-specific in pairwise sample comparisons, they are broadly recurrent when considered across a large compendium of samples. These findings underscore the pervasive and reusable nature of EPIs and have important implications for the interpretation of chromatin conformation data.

title: Quantitative characterization of spatial frequency-dependent effects of conjugate gradient reconstruction in relation to k-space fill ratio in non-contrast-enhanced ultra-short echo time brain magnetic resonance angiography.
authors: Harada S, Takatsu Y, Murayama K, Kumazawa Y, Sano Y, Ikedo M.
abstract: Ultrashort echo time magnetic resonance angiography (UTE-MRA) with radial sampling is increasingly used for non-contrast cerebrovascular imaging due to its low flow dependence and robustness to susceptibility effects. Reducing the k-space fill ratio to shorten acquisition time may alter the spatial-frequency characteristics of reconstructed images. Conjugate gradient (CG)-based iterative reconstruction compensates for incomplete k-space sampling; however, its frequency-dependent effects remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the spatial-frequency characteristics of CG reconstruction in radial UTE-MRA using the normalized integrated power spectrum (NIPS). Phantom and clinical head UTE-MRA were performed at k-space fill ratios of 2.2%-35.2%, with and without CG reconstruction. NIPS findings were evaluated in relation to signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and acquisition time. The effect of CG reconstruction was more pronounced in the low-frequency range at lower fill ratios, with significant higher NIPS values at 2.2% and 4.4% without CG reconstruction. Furthermore, no significant differences were observed among any combination within the low-frequency band when CG reconstruction was applied at fill ratios of 4.4% or higher (0.051 < P < 0.998). High-frequency NIPS values increased with the k-space fill ratio, indicating greater dependence on physical sampling density. SNR increased with the k-space fill ratio and was not significantly affected by CG reconstruction. In clinical analysis, no statistically significant differences were observed between CG reconstruction at 4.4% and conventional gridding at 8.8% in low- or high-frequency NIPS values within the M1 or M3 segments. Among evaluated conditions, 4.4% with CG reconstruction was selected as a practical acquisition condition.

title: Quadrant classification and development path of gymnastics-related research topics in Chinese high-quality journals: Based on SCI, PKU Core and CSSCI source journals.
authors: Yu J, Sun W, Qu L, Wang M, Zhang J, Zhang C.
abstract: Against the macro backdrop of the strategy for developing a strong sporting nation and digital-intelligent transformation, sports organizations have accumulated massive high-value unstructured knowledge assets such as academic literature and reports. Yet their latent strategic value has not been effectively exploited. Converting static knowledge assets into dynamic strategic intelligence represents the central challenge in sports knowledge management.Taking 169 high quality journal papers on gymnastics published from 2016 to 2025 in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI, domestic edition) as research objects, this study identifies seven Topics using the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model: Topic 1: Technical analysis of bar transitions and choreography in gymnastics competitions; Topic 2: Evolution of the global team structure in men's artistic gymnastics; Topic 3: Biomechanical analysis of landing techniques among gymnasts; Topic 4: Research on curriculum design and instructional practice in school gymnastics education; Topic 5: Research on balance capability in 'gymnasts' apparatus performances; Topic 6: Movement technique analysis of elite gymnasts; Topic 7: Talent cultivation for reserve forces in competitive gymnastics. Quantitative Topic evaluation shows that Topic 4 is a high-concentration and high-coverage Topic; Topic 5 and 6 are high-concentration and low-coverage Topics; Topic 1 is a low-concentration and low-coverage Topic; and Topic 2, 3, and 7 are low-concentration and high-coverage Topics. This study conducts a Topic-based four-quadrant classification diagnosis and proposes differentiated development paths. Accordingly, it identifies future research directions for Topics in each quadrant, including theoretical deepening, application expansion, basic cultivation, and knowledge integration.

title: Prognostic value of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in glioma: A meta-analysis.
authors: Guo L, Cao X, Yang L, Zhu X, Liu L, Liu H.
abstract: Objective To systematically evaluate the predictive value of systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) for the prognosis of glioma patients. Methods PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases were searched to collect literature on the relationship between SIRI and glioma prognosis from database inception to July 2026. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). STATA 15.0 and Review Manager 5.4 software were used, and random-effects models were employed with pooled hazard ratios (HR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the prognostic value of SIRI. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed. Results Eight retrospective cohort studies involving 1778 glioma patients were included, forming 12 comparison groups for OS analysis and 4 comparison groups for PFS analysis. Meta-analysis results showed that a higher SIRI was significantly associated with poorer OS (pooled HR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.34-2.38, P Conclusion This meta-analysis suggests that elevated SIRI is associated with poorer OS and PFS in glioma patients, although this association was not consistently observed across all subgroups, particularly in European populations. These findings highlight the need for further validation with standardized cut-off values in diverse populations.

title: Primary Care Physicians' Perspectives on Clinical Integration and Performance Metrics in a Medically Underserved Area.
journal: The Journal of Ambulatory Care Management
authors: Kumar K, Jones J, Harvey J, Jurdi Z.
abstract: Objective This study explored primary care physicians' perspectives on Clinical Integration (CI) program performance, quality metrics, and incentive structures within a Physician Hospital Organization (PHO) serving a medically underserved urban community. The objective was to complement existing CI performance data by identifying contextual factors that influence physician performance and participation in value-based care programs. Methods A qualitative study using a general inductive approach was conducted within a single PHO on Chicago's South Side. All 10 independent primary care physicians participating in the PHO's CI program completed semistructured interviews.
