Interview questions focused on social determinants of health, staffing, incentive structures, quality measurement, barriers to performance, and support needs. Interviews were transcribed and independently coded by two researchers. Through iterative coding and thematic analysis, preliminary codes were consolidated into higher-order themes. Results Six major themes emerged. Physicians reported that low health literacy, socioeconomic hardship, and patient nonadherence reduced their ability to achieve quality targets and earn incentives. Staffing shortages and turnover hindered quality improvement activities and population health management. Participants viewed incentive structures as insufficient, poorly understood, and misaligned with the effort required to improve performance. Physicians also believed that CI performance metrics often failed to reflect the quality of care delivered to high-needs populations. Additional barriers included limited specialty care access, transportation challenges, patient mistrust of the health care system, and other social determinants affecting care engagement. Respondents identified increased administrative support, dedicated CI-focused staff, and improved specialty access as important facilitators of success. Conclusions Standardized CI metrics and incentive structures may inadequately account for the realities of delivering primary care in underserved communities. PHOs, payers, and health system leaders should consider transparent incentive models, context-adjusted performance measures, enhanced staffing support, and investments in patient engagement and specialty care access to promote equitable performance assessment and strengthen value-based care programs.

title: Postoperative Quality of Life (BREAST-Q) in Patients With Breast Cancer After Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy With/Without Reconstruction.
authors: Watanabe H, Sugihara R, Saku S, Katagiri Y, Nakamura A, Matsushima S, Oku H, Hiwaki H, Furukawa M, Fujita F, Ogo E, Toh U.
abstract: Background Recent advances in multi-modality treatments (including systemic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and radiotherapy) have led to a paradigm shift in the surgical management of breast cancer toward less aggressive approaches. This evolution has established breast-conserving (or breast-reconstructive) surgery as the new standard of care, placing a greater emphasis on aesthetic outcomes. Nipple-sparing mastectomy (NSM) has emerged as an oncologically safe option that is increasingly paired with immediate or delayed breast reconstruction. The NSM approach is also used prophylactically for high-risk individuals with BRCA gene mutations. Compared with traditional total mastectomy, an NSM with breast reconstruction preserves the nipple-areolar complex (NAC), offering significant psychosocial and aesthetic advantages that improve patients' cosmetic appearance and body image. However, some breast cancer patients hesitate to undergo the second stage of breast reconstruction after completing the initial NSM. Patients and methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the BREAST-Q questionnaire to assess the postoperative satisfaction and quality of life (QOL) among patients with breast cancer who underwent an NSM with or without subsequent breast reconstruction. Results We analyzed the cases of 73 patients who underwent breast cancer surgery between December 2016 and December 2022 at a single institution. The cohort was divided into two groups: the breast reconstruction (BR) group (n = 45), that is, the patients who underwent tissue expander or silicone breast implant reconstruction after an NSM, and the non-breast reconstruction (NBR) group (n = 28), comprising patients who underwent an NSM with no intent to pursue subsequent reconstruction. We evaluated and compared the post-NSM overall BREAST-Q scores between the BR and NBR groups. Conclusions The results revealed no significant difference in overall postoperative satisfaction or QOL between the BR and NBR groups. However, the BR group demonstrated significantly higher scores in the specific domains of psychosocial and sexual well-being, a trend that was particularly pronounced among the patients with small-to-intermediate breast volumes.

title: Perceived quality teaching and student retention intention: The serial mediation of knowledge, skills, competencies, and student loyalty.
authors: Iqbal S, Taib CAB, Allumi NA, Abu Al-Rejal H, Alvi GF, Kafi MA, Abbas M.
abstract: Student retention intention remains a concern for higher education systems worldwide and is relevant to institutional sustainability and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). Drawing on Human Capital Theory (HCT) and Expectancy-Value Theory (EVT), this study examines the direct and indirect associations between perceived quality teaching and student retention intention through students' self-reported knowledge, skills, competencies and student loyalty. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 395 final-year students across Pakistani universities using a multistage sampling approach, with institutions selected through stratified random sampling and participants recruited via convenience sampling. The proposed relationships were examined using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that perceived quality teaching is positively associated with student retention intention, both directly and indirectly through students' knowledge, skills, and competencies and student loyalty. Significant indirect associations were identified through each mediator separately and through the proposed serial mediation pathway. These findings highlight the relevance of considering students' perceived capability development and institutional attachment together when examining retention intention. HCT provides a rationale for the relationship between perceived teaching quality and students' knowledge, skills, competencies, while EVT offers an interpretive perspective; however, expectancy of success and subjective task value were not directly measured. The cross-sectional design also precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causality. Practically, the findings suggest that faculty development, student-centered pedagogies, digitally supported teaching, and curriculum alignment with labor market needs merit consideration in institutional quality assurance. The findings provide context-specific evidence from Pakistani higher education (HE) and are relevant to SDG 4 through their focus on perceived teaching quality and students' intentions to continue their studies. They do not establish effects on actual retention or broader educational outcomes.

title: Pediatric emergency medicine in Lebanon: Physician-perceived comfort levels, challenges, and educational needs.
authors: Moughnieh N, Abou-Abbas L, Beattie T, Smith L.
abstract: Background Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) is a rapidly evolving subspecialty that improves the quality and safety of care for children. Despite global advancements, PEM remains underdeveloped in many low- and middle-income countries, including Lebanon. Despite a large pediatric population there is no formal paediatric emergency medicine system in place, and care largely delivered by physicians practicing without standardized or specialized training. This lack of dedicated PEM training and organized emergency care pathways may compromise the timely recognition and management of pediatric emergencies, potentially affecting patient outcomes. Objectives The present study aimed to assess physicians perceived comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, identify training gaps, and explore systemic and institutional challenges affecting pediatric emergency care in Lebanon. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among physicians involved in pediatric emergency care across Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed self-reported comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, perceived challenges, and priorities for training and PEM workforce development. Results Responses from 59 physicians were analysed. Most were male 38 (64.4%), with a median clinical experience of 7 years. General pediatricians represented 28 (47.5%), emergency physicians 17 (28.8%), PEM specialists 8 (13.6%), and pediatric intensivists 6 (10.2%). Physicians reported high perceived comfort in pediatric fluid management 52(88.1%), chest X-ray interpretation 46 (77.9%), and general pediatric emergencies 42 (71.2%), but lower comfort in procedural sedation, suturing 35 (59.6%), fracture stabilization 35 (59.4%), and Extended Focused Assessment Sonography in Trauma (EFAST) 22 (41.8%). General pediatricians reported greater comfort with general pediatric emergencies, while emergency-focused physicians had higher comfort with trauma-related skills and procedural interventions. Major challenges included gaps in practical and theoretical training, limited hospital infrastructure, shortages of devices and human resources, and the need for continuing medical education. Nearly all participants 57 (96.6%) supported the establishing a dedicated PEM fellowship, highlighting training priorities in trauma, medical emergencies, life support, procedural skills, and pediatric imaging. Conclusion Pediatric emergency care in Lebanon is constrained by gaps in skills, training, and systemic resources. There is an urgent need to establish standardized PEM training pathways, enhance curricula, and strengthen system-level preparedness. Implementing these measures will support a competent PEM workforce and improve the quality and safety of emergency care for children nationwide.

title: Patient-derived organoid model for predicting chemotherapy response in patients with ampulla of Vater cancer: a prospective observational study.
journal: Annals of Surgical Treatment and Research
authors: Lee HJ, Park SH, Seo HI, Kim DU, Han SY, Lee JH, Park YM, Noh BG.
abstract: Purpose Ampulla of Vater cancer (AoVca) is a rare periampullary malignancy with a high recurrence rate after surgical resection and no established standard adjuvant chemotherapy. This study aimed to predict chemotherapy responses using patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) from surgically resected tissues to identify an appropriate adjuvant chemotherapy regimen for AoVca patients. Methods PDTOs were cultured from surgically resected AoVca tissues of 14 patients. Morphological and phenotypic consistency between PDTOs and primary tumors was verified using H&E and immunohistochemical staining for cytokeratin 7 and caudal-type homeobox 2. Drug sensitivity for 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), cisplatin, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, gemcitabine, and paclitaxel was assessed by comparing the IC 50 values. Results PDTOs were successfully cultured from 11 of the 14 patients, with a phenotypic concordance rate of 82% (9 of 11). Ten PDTOs were successfully expanded for drug screening. These PDTOs showed universal resistance to cisplatin (n = 10), followed by irinotecan (n = 9) and paclitaxel (n = 8). Conversely, gemcitabine demonstrated the highest sensitivity, with resistance observed in only 1 PDTO, followed by 5-FU, which showed resistance in 4 cases. Conclusion Gemcitabine was identified as the most responsive chemotherapeutic agent for AoVca based on PDTO drug screening. For combination therapy, oxaliplatin may be more appropriate than cisplatin. However, further clinical studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Parental knowledge, antibiotic-seeking behavior, and inappropriate antibiotic use in children with respiratory tract infections: a narrative review of behavioral drivers and implications for antimicrobial resistance.
authors: Mamand HH, Hama SA, Murad HW, Ahmed AO.
abstract: Background Inappropriate antibiotic use is one of the main modifiable drivers of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Children with respiratory tract infections receive a large share of avoidable prescriptions, and the reasons lie as much in behavior, communication, and access as in clinical need. Objective To synthesize evidence on the clinical, prescriber-related, parental, communication-related, access-related, and socioeconomic drivers of inappropriate antibiotic use in children with respiratory tract infections, and to appraise the evidence for interventions that target these drivers. Methods We conducted a narrative review guided by the SANRA criteria. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by Google Scholar, were searched for English-language peer-reviewed studies published between January 2014 and December 2025. Thirty studies formed the core thematic synthesis. A supplementary search identified trials and reviews used to appraise stewardship interventions. Results In countries like Italy and Finland, there was a significant decrease in pediatric prescriptions for uncomplicated respiratory infections, despite not being any increase in the occurrence of serious complications. Similarly, studies on acute otitis media indicated low benefits but abundant side effects. Although the parents were often misinformed about this process, knowledge alone was not sufficient to guarantee proper practice. Numerous studies revealed that physicians estimated the parents' needs incorrectly, and numerous children ended up receiving antibiotics that were not even asked for by their parents. One of the reasons for this issue was that patients were purchasing non-prescription medications, using leftover antibiotics, and limiting their access to affordable medical care. Research showed that communication, auditing, and clinical decision support training helped in reducing antibiotic prescriptions, while national training programs were not able to provide similar successes. Conclusions The inappropriate utilization of antibiotics among children is a result of influences from different levels: household, consultations, pharmacy and health system levels. These factors should be treated as associations instead of identified causes due to the fact that the majority of the evidence provided is cross-sectional. There is some evidence suggesting that a combination of clinician-targeted strategies with dispensing and access for medications is more promising than just education alone.

title: PLA/PLC "Smart Patch" functionality assessment for fetal duraplasty in prenatal myelomeningocele repair using a fetoscopic surgical simulator.
authors: Miyabe MM, Duru S, Oria M, Hawes N, Torlak N, Varela MF, Lin CY, Peiro JL.
abstract: Background Fetoscopy has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to open hysterotomy for prenatal repair of myelomeningocele (MMC), which often requires a dural substitute. Our team developed a novel PLA/PCL patch optimized for fetoscopic surgery. This study compared the performance of the PLA/PCL patch with a human umbilical cord (HUC) graft. Methods Twenty-seven medical professionals with varied experience performed four MMC repair tasks in a fetoscopic simulator: patch introduction, manipulation, placement, and suture. In a randomized crossover design, each participant performed the tasks twice, once with each graft. Task times were recorded. After each attempt, participants completed task-specific difficulty questionnaires and the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX); after both attempts, they completed a comparative questionnaire assessing overall preference and perceived performance. Results Participants included nine experts, nine intermediates, and nine novices. Introduction was significantly faster with PLA/PCL across all experience levels and overall (16 ± 7 s vs 35 ± 17 s, p Conclusion The PLA/PCL patch is a promising dural substitute for prenatal MMC repair. Its shape-memory design enabled faster introduction and manipulation and reduced perceived workload compared with HUC, while maintaining comparable total procedural times. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of this novel graft.

title: Outcomes of paediatric preauricular sinus excision - comparison of sinusectomy vs supra-auricular approaches.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Garrard A, Stobiecka R, Krishnan M, De S.
abstract: Introduction Preauricular sinuses are common congenital anomalies that can lead to recurrent infections. Various surgical techniques, including simple sinusectomy and the more extensive supra-auricular approach, are used to excise these tracts. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of sinusectomy vs supra-auricular excision in a paediatric population. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary paediatric referral centre. Cases from the period 2009-2025 were identified and clinical records were reviewed. Data were compiled and analysed between the sinusectomy and supra-auricular approaches. Statistical tests were used to identify significance. Multivariable Firth penalised logistic regression was used to assess recurrence according to surgical approach and operative adjuncts. Results A total of 63 patients (71 ears; mean age 6.9 years) were included: 37 (52.1%) underwent sinusectomy and 34 (47.9%) supra-auricular excision. Postoperative complications occurred in 12 of 37 (32.4%) sinusectomy cases vs 4 of 34 (11.8%) supra-auricular cases (odds ratio [OR] 3.6, p p Conclusions In this paediatric series, supra-auricular excision was associated with lower recurrence and complication rates than sinusectomy. Analysis suggests that cartilage excision may independently contribute to lower recurrence and this association with surgical approach persists after adjustment for operative adjuncts. We recommend the supra-auricular approach as the preferred technique for recurrent or symptomatic preauricular sinuses in children.

title: Open-Wedge High Tibial Osteotomy With Complete Tibial Tubercle Osteotomy to Preserve Patellar Height.
authors: Miyasaka T, Kayama T, Kubota D, Arakawa S, Saito M.
abstract: Distalization of the tibial tubercle is a concern during open-wedge high tibial osteotomy, particularly when a large correction is required, considering the potential for patella baja and patellofemoral problems. This Technical Note describes the use of open-wedge high tibial osteotomy combined with complete tibial tubercle osteotomy to maintain the position of the tibial tubercle during correction. Performing tibial tubercle osteotomy first allows placement of a thin retractor beneath the fragment during the transverse osteotomy, helping to protect the fragment and reduce the risk of an incomplete osteotomy. Temporary fixation of the tibial tubercle to the proximal tibial fragment before wedge opening is a key step in maintaining the original position of the tubercle and preventing distalization during correction. This technique is a practical option for selected patients requiring substantial varus correction when preservation of patellar height is desired.

title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and mesh assistance in immediate DTI subpectoral breast reconstruction: PROs and surgical complications.
authors: Gao P, Jiang H, Kong X, Li M, Wang J, Ji Z, Cui J.
abstract: Background Immediate direct-to-implant (DTI) breast reconstruction after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) remains a clinically relevant issue, particularly when mesh-assisted subpectoral reconstruction is considered. Although existing evidence supports the general safety of immediate reconstruction after NACT, the patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and surgical safety of mesh-assisted DTI reconstruction in this setting remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative BREAST-Q outcomes and surgical complications after immediate DTI subpectoral reconstruction in relation to NACT and mesh assistance. Methods We conducted a two-center retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent immediate DTI subpectoral breast reconstruction at Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, Capital Medical University and Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences between May 2017 and May 2022. The primary analysis compared patients with and without neoadjuvant chemotherapy among those undergoing mesh-assisted reconstruction. An exploratory analysis among patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy compared mesh-assisted and no-mesh reconstruction. PROs were assessed using postoperative BREAST-Q version 2.0. Surgical complications during follow-up were collected from medical records. Results In the mesh-assisted cohort, 22 patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and 144 did not. Age, BMI, implant size, operative time, pretreatment tumor size, clinical T stage, and clinical nodal status did not differ significantly between groups, whereas histologic type, and molecular subtype differed significantly. Patients receiving NACT more frequently underwent axillary resection (72.7% vs 31.3%; P Conclusions Among appropriately selected patients undergoing immediate DTI subpectoral breast reconstruction, no statistically significant differences in postoperative PROs or surgical complications were detected according to NACT status. However, the limited sample size and statistical precision preclude conclusions of equivalence or non-inferiority, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective, adequately powered studies are needed to confirm these observations.

title: Museum visitors' acceptance of digital services in China and Russia: Extending UTAUT2 with individual-level cultural values.
authors: Chen J, Li X, Zhu C, Biryukova M.
abstract: Museum digital services have become an important means of supporting visitors' access to information, understanding of exhibition content, and broader museum experiences. However, the mechanisms underlying visitors' acceptance of these services may vary across visitor groups. Drawing on a context-adapted Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology model (UTAUT2), this study incorporates three individual-level cultural values-collectivism orientation, uncertainty avoidance, and long-term orientation-to examine acceptance intention toward museum digital services in China and Russia. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with survey data from China (n = 316) and Russia (n = 307). Measurement invariance of composites (MICOM) and PLS multigroup analysis (PLS-MGA) were conducted to assess between-sample differences. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and hedonic motivation all had significant positive effects on acceptance intention in both samples. The PLS-MGA results showed no significant between-sample differences in the effects of performance expectancy or social influence. Hedonic motivation had a significantly stronger effect in the Chinese sample, whereas effort expectancy and facilitating conditions had stronger effects in the Russian sample. The latter two differences should nevertheless be interpreted cautiously because compositional invariance was not established for these constructs. Collectivism strengthened the effect of social influence, uncertainty avoidance strengthened the effects of effort expectancy and facilitating conditions, and long-term orientation strengthened the effects of performance expectancy and hedonic motivation. None of the five moderating effects differed significantly between the two samples. These findings show that acceptance intention toward museum digital services is jointly shaped by functional benefits, ease of use, social cues, available support, experiential value, and visitors' individual cultural value orientations. The study provides evidence of both shared acceptance mechanisms and sample-specific path differences and offers a basis for visitor segmentation and the refinement of museum digital services.

title: Musculoskeletal Disorder Risk in Motorcycle Operators: Development and Validation of a Targeted Screening Scale.
journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
authors: Zguira MS, Ayed A, Houas MA, Dergaa I, Moula S, Ceylan HI, Bragazzi NL, Stefanica V, Kasmi S, Rebai H, Douzi W.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a musculoskeletal disorder screening scale for motorcycle operators. Methods In a cross-sectional study, 140 Tunisian operators rated pain in nine body regions on a four-point scale. Results Two factors separated upper-body from lower-body regions and explained 67.5 percent of the variance. Cronbach alpha reached 0.910 and 0.881. The two-factor model outperformed the one-factor model (chi-square difference 67.92, p Conclusions The scale shows a coherent two-factor structure and high internal consistency, with model fit short of the approximation-error threshold.

title: Moral Dissonance Is Greater When Clinicians Act Contrary to Evidence, Experience, and Values Than When They Disappoint the Patient.
authors: Azib N, Spier JD, Ring D, Razi A, and the Science of Variation Group, and the Science of Variation Group and Members of the Science of Variation Group include:.
abstract: Background Most musculoskeletal visits, tests, and treatments are optional. Specialists may experience moral dissonance when patient requests are difficult to reconcile with evidence, experience, and professional values. This dissonance may arise when clinicians feel torn between acquiescing to a request they view as unsupported and declining the request while worrying about disappointing the patient. Understanding the specific factors associated with greater moral dissonance, either in the form of acquiescence or disappointment, may inform efforts to improve both patient and clinician experiences when guiding patients toward effective health strategies. Questions/purposes (1) Is the severity of moral dissonance experienced by musculoskeletal specialists greater when acquiescing to patient requests that are contrary to evidence, experience, and values compared with disappointing the patient by declining a request? (2) What scenario factors are associated with the severity of moral dissonance? Methods We invited members of the Science of Variation Group (SOVG), an international collaborative of musculoskeletal surgeons who participate in monthly survey-based experiments addressing variation in care, to complete an online survey- and scenario-based experiment between April 12 and May 4, 2025. The SOVG is open to all musculoskeletal surgeons, but its active participants are mostly White academic surgeons (54%) in the US and Europe (26%), which is not representative of the average musculoskeletal surgeon. Our experiments are therefore designed to measure associations rather than to estimate rates or prevalence. The analysis depends on variation in how surgeons judge and respond to the same clinical scenarios and should be reproducible in any sample of surgeons with sufficient variation in opinions. Of approximately 200 SOVG members who typically participate in at least one survey annually, 68% (135) of surgeons completed at least one scenario. Participants reviewed 11 clinical scenarios with randomized elements, including patient age, patient gender, and combinations of clinical presentation and patient request. Participants were then randomly assigned to rate moral dissonance as either pressure to act contrary to evidence, experience, and values ("Imagine you give the patient what they want. To what degree do you feel like you are acting contrary to your values and best evidence?") or as a feeling of disappointing the patient ("To what degree do you feel like you're letting the patient down if you can't offer a diagnosis and treatment?"). Both items were rated on a scale from 0 ("I don't feel it at all") to 100 ("I feel it strongly"). Multilevel mixed-effects linear regression models were used to identify factors associated with levels of distress, accounting for surgeon-level nesting. Regression coefficients represent the estimated difference in moral dissonance on the 0-to-100 rating scale associated with each factor compared with the reference category. Positive coefficients indicate higher moral dissonance and negative coefficients indicate lower moral dissonance. For categorical variables, the coefficient represents the average difference in moral dissonance between that category and the reference category, adjusted for the other variables in the model. Results Levels of moral dissonance were higher when rated as acting contrary to evidence, experience, and values (median [IQR] 70 [40 to 90]) than when rated as disappointing the patient (40 [20 to 70]); the group medians differed by 30 points on the 0-to-100 scale. In the multilevel mixed-effects regression model, disappointing the patient was associated with a 21-point lower moral dissonance score than acting contrary to evidence, experience, and values (regression coefficient -21 [95% confidence interval (CI) -27 to -15]). Relative to requests for electrodiagnostic testing for pain with typing, moral dissonance ratings were higher for requests for carpal tunnel release despite normal electrodiagnostic testing results (regression coefficient 6.7 [95% CI 0.9 to 13]) and surgical excision of a wrist ganglion for symptoms consistent with a wrist ganglion (regression coefficient 7.1 [95% CI 1.3 to 13]). These coefficients indicate approximately 7-point higher moral dissonance ratings on the 0-to-100 scale compared with the reference scenario. Moral dissonance ratings were lower than in the reference scenario for requests for proximal median nerve release for nonspecific forearm pain (regression coefficient -14 [95% CI -20 to -8.2]) and surgery for distal biceps tendinopathy (regression coefficient -14 [95% CI -20 to -7.9]), indicating approximately 14-point lower ratings than the reference scenario. Conclusion The finding that moral dissonance was greater when rated as acquiescing to care that conflicts with evidence, experience, and values than when rated as disappointment suggests that the source of distress may be the surgeon's sense of responsibility for potentially reinforcing unhelpful beliefs, exposing patients to low-value care, or contributing to overuse. The variation by clinical presentation and patient request suggests that distress may be greatest when requested care is discretionary but still clinically plausible, making it harder to decline. Clinical relevance These findings suggest that surgeons may reduce moral dissonance by strategizing and practicing specific communication steps when patients request discretionary but plausible care, such as curiosity about the concern and goal driving the request, validation of that concern, and introducing options that might better achieve the patient's goals while introducing less potential harm and false hope.

title: Moisture and material shape microbial communities in the built environment through disturbance-productivity relationships.
authors: Nannini K, Krutkin DD, Kelley ST, Ortiz-Velez A, Brown JD, Ogden S, Terrazas F, Barber NA.
abstract: Background The built environment houses diverse microbial communities whose diversity and composition differ among building materials and environmental conditions. Ecological theory makes predictions about how productivity and diversity shape communities, and experiments in the built environment provide an opportunity to test these predictions. We manipulated moisture (constant or repeated wet-dry cycling) on three common building materials to test hypotheses that environmental disturbance interacts with the potential productivity of building materials to influence alpha and beta diversity. Methods Coupons of different building materials, medium density fiberboard, gypsum wallboard and oriented strand board, were sterilized before passive inoculation, then kept wet or periodically air-dried before rewetting. Microbial communities were sampled using swabs every 14 days for 7-week period. Productivity was measured using bacterial cell counts, fungal hyphal length, and fungal spore density, and microbial diversity was determined via community amplicon sequencing using universal bacterial (16S) and fungal (ITS) primers. Results The most productive material (oriented strand board) supported the highest bacterial alpha and beta diversity, and these diversity levels were reduced by repeated drying disturbances. Diversity patterns for fungi were more variable, with the highest alpha diversity on low-moderate productivity material (gypsum wallboard). Fungal beta diversity was reduced by disturbance on high productivity material but increased on the other materials. These patterns were driven largely by members of Bacillaceae, Sphingomonadaceae, and Aspergillaceae that reached high abundances in some treatments. Conclusions Disturbance regime interacted with building material, so disturbance effects depended on material type. There were also differences between bacteria and fungi, which may be due to the scale-dependence of productivity-diversity relationships, but this pattern was not uniform. Network analysis found evidence of multi-species complexes of bacteria and fungi known to form biofilms, as well as evidence of competitive exclusion on specific materials and conditions. Together, these results indicate that disturbances can interact with building materials, and that these disturbances may be strongly mediated by biotic interactions.

title: Minimally Invasive Zadek Osteotomy vs Open Achilles Debridement for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy in Athletes: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
authors: Genuth G, Stavrou P, Brown C, Iselin LD.
abstract: Background Insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT) is a common cause of posterior heel pain in athletic populations and may require surgical intervention following failed conservative management. Minimally invasive Zadek osteotomy (MIS Zadek) has emerged as an alternative to traditional open Achilles tendon debridement with Haglund resection, with potential advantages in recovery and complication profile. Methods A retrospective comparative cohort study was performed including 50 athletic patients with IAT (25 MIS Zadek, 25 open surgery) treated between 2022 and 2024 at a single high-volume centre. All patients participated in regular sports activity and failed at least 6 months of nonoperative treatment. The primary outcome was time to return to sport. Secondary outcomes included return-to-sport rate, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) physical function (PF), PROMIS pain interference (PI), and postoperative complications. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to adjust for potential confounders. Results Return to sport was achieved in 100% of MIS patients (25/25) and 92% of open patients (23/25; P = .49). Time to return to sport was shorter following MIS Zadek (4.3 ± 1.2 vs 6.1 ± 1.5 months; mean difference -1.8 months, 95% CI -2.6 to -1.0; P P P = .02; Cohen d = 0.69), with a similar pattern for PROMIS PI (47.2 ± 5.5 vs 51.1 ± 6.0; mean difference -3.9, 95% CI -7.1 to -0.7; P = .02; Cohen d = 0.67). By 18 months, PROMIS PF improved further in both groups with comparable outcomes (59.4 ± 4.9 vs 57.8 ± 5.2; mean difference +1.6, 95% CI -1.4 to 4.6; P = .29), and PROMIS PI similarly converged (44.8 ± 4.9 vs 46.3 ± 5.1; mean difference -1.5, 95% CI -4.4 to 1.4; P = .30). Complication rates were lower in the MIS group (2/25, 8%) compared with the open group (6/25, 24%; P = .25), although this difference did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion MIS Zadek osteotomy was associated with faster return to sport and improved early recovery compared with open surgery; with the numbers available, no significant difference in long-term functional outcomes could be detected. Complications were numerically less frequent following MIS Zadek osteotomy, although this difference did not reach statistical significanceLevel of Evidence:Level III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

title: Measurement-derived residual-risk verification through four-way k-space partitioning in self-supervised accelerated brain MRI.
authors: Osei RS, Osei F, Ampadu SO.
abstract: Self-supervised accelerated MRI reconstruction reduces dependence on fully sampled training targets, but it does not inherently provide a separate basis for verifying whether reconstructed image content remains locally consistent with acquired measurements. We developed a measurement-derived verification framework that partitions acquired k-space into four roles: reconstruction input, self-supervised reconstruction-loss evaluation, residual-risk learning, and reserved verification. Residuals from the reserved measurements were transformed into spatial residual-risk targets using density-compensated adjoint projection, probe-based gain normalization, anatomical support weighting, percentile scaling, and logarithmic compression. Using fastMRI brain multicoil data, we evaluated 201 training, 40 calibration, and 40 AXT2 test volumes, comprising 636 test slices and 999,792 sampled pixels. The primary Full-CNN achieved AUPRC 0.8348, mean absolute error 0.0834, Spearman correlation 0.9389, and AUROC 0.9818. The secondary A4-CNN achieved AUPRC 0.8452 with similar scale and rank agreement. MRI-volume intervals achieved at least 90% sampled-location coverage in 39 of 40 test volumes for both predictors. AUPRC declined and MAE increased with fewer reserved measurements and under AXFLAIR sequence shift. Residual-risk maps showed moderate correspondence with fully sampled reference error and differed from the tested predictive-variance measures. The framework provides a measurement-derived verification layer for assessing local residual inconsistency in self-supervised accelerated MRI without requiring fully sampled development targets.

title: Management of recurrent medial ankle pain after total ankle replacement arthroplasty: the role of medial malleolar anterolateral corner resection in resolving bone-to-implant impingement.
authors: Jung SO, Suh JS, Choi JY.

title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Lv H, Gao Y, Yu A.
abstract: Background Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. Method We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Results Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study. Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. Conclusion In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

title: Long-term outcomes of laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass: a retrospective cohort study.
journal: Annals of Surgical Treatment and Research
authors: Jung J, Chang WB, Park Y, Park HS, Lee T.
abstract: Purpose Laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass (LABF) is a minimally invasive option for extensive aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD), but data on its long-term durability are limited. We aimed to evaluate the 10-year outcomes of LABF for patients with TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) II C and D lesions. Methods We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of 20 patients who underwent LABF for TASC II C or D AIOD at a single tertiary center between January 2004 and December 2012. Primary endpoints were primary and secondary patency rates, survival, and postoperative complications. Results The median patient age was 65 years, and 18 (90.0%) were male. TASC II D lesions were present in 18 patients (90.0%). There was one perioperative death (5.0%). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed primary patency rates of 94.7%, 88.8%, 82.0%, and 82.0% at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years, respectively. The 10-year secondary patency rate was 88.0%. Reintervention was required in 2 patients (10.0%) during follow-up. Conclusion LABF provides excellent long-term patency rates comparable to open repair for complex AIOD. With careful patient selection, LABF represents a safe, feasible, and durable minimally invasive alternative, particularly for patients unsuitable for endovascular therapy.

title: Lambrinudi-Type Arthrodesis and Plantar Fasciectomy in the Treatment of Rigid Cavovarus Deformity.
authors: Ruiz R, Susdorf R, Hintermann B.
abstract: Background While using a standard triple arthrodesis in treating rigid cavovarus deformity, the talus often remains extended, leading to anterior ankle impingement and overload. The primary goal of this study was to test our hypotheses that the talus would adopt a more normal flexion position with a Lambrinudi-type triple arthrodesis and that the foot morphology would become more normal by combining it with a plantar fasciectomy. Additionally, the aim was to evaluate whether outcomes differ between neurogenic and non-neurogenic feet. Method Seventeen patients (17 feet; neurogenic [N], 11 feet; non-neurogenic [NN], 6 feet) who underwent a Lambrinudi-type arthrodesis combined with a plantar fasciectomy at our institution from 2016 to 2023, with at least 2 years of follow-up, were included. We prospectively collected radiographic and clinical data to evaluate changes in foot and ankle morphology. Results With the numbers available, no significant difference could be detected between the N and NN groups in clinical outcomes. The VAS scale decreased by 6.5 ± 0.3 points after surgery ( P g = 6.6 [4.9-8.4]), and the EFAS score increased by 31.5 ± 0.9 points ( P g = -8.7 [-10.9 to -6.5]). All radiographic measurements improved significantly ( P P = .024, Hedges g = -0.8 [-1.5 to -0.1]). The foot length increased from 122 ± 16 mm preoperatively to 134 ± 12 mm postoperatively (plus 10.1%, P g = -0.9 [-1.5 to -0.2]). Conclusion A Lambrinudi-type arthrodesis combined with a complete plantar fasciectomy was an effective method for correcting a rigid cavovarus deformity in both N and NN feet. It was intended to unload the anterior tibiotalar joint by flexing the talus and changing the flexion forces, and it increased foot length by 10.1%. It also was associated with significant clinical improvements across all measured outcome domains. Level of evidence Level IV, prospective case series.

title: LC-MS/MS targeted analysis of amino acids in CSF of pediatric tuberculous meningitis.
authors: Plaatjie ON, van Furth AMT, Solomons R, van der Kuip M, Mason S.
abstract: Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) is the most severe manifestation of tuberculosis (TB) and is associated with high mortality and long-term neurological morbidity. Diagnosis is challenging due to a nonspecific clinical presentation overlapping with other forms of meningitis. Delayed diagnosis and subsequent delays in treatment initiation remain major contributors to poor outcomes, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic approaches. Untargeted cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metabolomics studies have revealed perturbed amino acid (AA) metabolism in TBM. Here, we applied liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for targeted profiling of AAs in CSF from a pediatric patient cohort (≤ 13 years old) in the Western Cape Province, South Africa. This study included children with TBM, viral meningitis (VM), and non-meningitis controls (NMC). CSF AA concentrations were markedly elevated in TBM, with most measured AAs significantly increased compared with both VM and NMC; however, serine did not show any significant difference. Lysine, glycine, alanine, proline, tyrosine, and methionine showed the strongest discriminatory potential. Despite elevated CSF protein levels in TBM, AA concentrations did not correlate with total protein. Instead, glycine correlated with leucocyte and lymphocyte counts, suggesting a link between AAs and inflammatory responses. No AAs significantly differentiated VM from NMC. These findings demonstrate substantial AA perturbations in pediatric TBM and highlight the potential of AA profiling to inform future diagnostic biomarker development.

title: Integration of weight-bearing computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging for advanced musculoskeletal statistical shape modeling of the foot and ankle.
journal: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
authors: Requist MR, Moreno E, Reddy C, Peterson AC, Mills MK, Lenz AL.
abstract: Purpose Statistical shape models (SSMs) from three-dimensional (3D) medical imaging describe morphology variation in normal and pathologic anatomy. Within the foot and ankle, weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) is used to characterize skeletal deformity but poorly visualizes soft tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides improved evaluation of soft tissue structures but less accurate bone visualization. This methodologic analysis describes and tests reliability of a novel process to generate SSMs from coregistered MRI and WBCT structures. This method is illustrated via two example models: a combined musculoskeletal model and a distal tibia growth plate model. Methods Bilateral WBCTs and T1-weighted DIXON MRIs of the lower legs were collected from 14 individuals aged 8 to 18 with no prior lower limb surgery in a control group and hereditary neuropathy group. Bones were segmented from WBCT and manually aligned in MRI space. Alignment reliability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Six muscles were segmented semi-automatically and the distal tibia growth plate was manually segmented from MRI. Following cropping, size normalization, and alignment multi-domain SSMs were generated. SSMs were evaluated qualitatively through comparison with expected anatomy and quantitively by calculation of compactness, generalization, and specificity. Results The alignment method demonstrated excellent reliability with an intrarater ICC of 1 and interrater ICC of 0.999. The musculoskeletal model demonstrated expected atrophy in neuromuscular disease and the preliminary growth plate model showed variation in metaphyseal thickness. Both models demonstrated compactness, specificity, and generalization comparable to published SSMs, requiring 11 and 12 modes to account for 95% of population variance. Conclusion This method allows for application of shape modeling to novel questions in musculoskeletal morphology through simultaneous modeling of bone and soft tissue anatomy. Limitations include manual registration and MRI resolution. This analysis presented examples of muscle and growth plate models, but has broader applications in musculoskeletal analysis.

title: Increased risk of infection and reoperation following total knee arthroplasty in patients under 40.
authors: Daley A, Yarden J, Diaz-Coto S, Moschetti W.
abstract: Background Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is increasingly performed in younger patient populations. This study aimed to compare perioperative outcomes between patients under 40 and those over 65, stratified by surgical indication. Methods This retrospective study used the Epic Cosmos dataset to identify primary TKA patients under 40 years old (n = 3,177) or over 65 (n = 698,662). Patients were stratified by surgical indication (primary osteoarthritis, post-traumatic osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, and multiple indications) using ICD-10 codes. Outcomes included superficial wound dehiscence, infection, readmission, and ipsilateral reoperation, assessed at 90 days and 1 year postoperatively. Differences between age groups were assessed using adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) derived from multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for sex, body mass index, comorbidity burden, insurance status and smoking status with significance set at p Results Surgical indications differed significantly between cohorts (standardized proportions difference 0.939, p 65 compared to 64.6% in patients Conclusion Patients under 40 undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty are at increased risk for prosthetic joint infection, superficial wound problems and ipsilateral reoperation at 90 days and 1 year when compared to those over the age of 65, independent of smoking status and comorbidity burden. Those with multiple indications for surgery are also at increased risk for infection and same-side reoperation at both time points.

title: Identification of Endoplasmic reticulum Homeostasis-associated diagnostic biomarkers for Sarcopenia through integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation.
authors: Shi L, Yan H, Lu J, Yu W, Li Y, Zhang Z.
abstract: Sarcopenia is an age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function, yet reliable biomarkers for early diagnosis remain limited. Emerging evidence suggests that disruption of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis contributes to skeletal muscle aging, however, the diagnostic relevance of ER stress- and reticulophagy-related alterations in sarcopenia remains poorly understood. In this study, three skeletal muscle transcriptomic datasets (GSE25941, GSE28422, and GSE38718) were integrated following batch-effect correction to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between sarcopenic and control samples. DEGs were intersected with ER stress and reticulophagy related gene sets to obtain sarcopenia-associated candidate genes. Subsequently, three machine-learning algorithms, including least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), were applied to identify key hub genes. Functional enrichment analyses, transcription factor (TF)-miRNA regulatory network construction, protein-chemical interaction analyses, external validation, nomogram development, and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) verification were performed. A total of 236 DEGs were identified, comprising 34 upregulated and 202 downregulated genes. Intersection analysis with 1,772 ER stress and reticulophagy related genes yielded 10 candidate genes, from which five hub genes ( ACTC1 , NPY , CDKN2B , GADD45G , and GRIA1 ) were consistently identified by machine-learning analyses. Functional enrichment analysis indicated significant involvement in extracellular matrix organization, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, mitochondrial translation, and respiratory electron transport pathways. Regulatory network analyses further revealed potential interactions with multiple transcription factors, miRNAs, and chemical compounds. In the independent validation cohort (GSE1428), ACTC1 showed strong individual discriminative performance, NPY and GADD45G showed moderate performance, whereas GRIA1 showed limited discrimination and CDKN2B showed near-chance individual performance, whereas the combined gene signature exhibited improved discriminative ability. A predictive nomogram was established. Moreover, qRT-PCR analysis of human skeletal muscle biopsy specimens confirmed significantly increased expression of ACTC1 , NPY , CDKN2B , and GRIA1 , together with decreased expression of GADD45G in sarcopenic muscle tissues compared with controls (all p < 0.05). Collectively, our findings identified a five-gene signature associated with ER stress and reticulophagy related molecular networks in sarcopenia. Although these genes are not established core regulators of ER stress or reticulophagy, they exhibited promising diagnostic value and may reflect ER homeostasis-related molecular alterations during skeletal muscle aging, providing novel biomarkers and potential insights into the molecular basis of sarcopenia.

title: How Much Do Horizontally Referenced and Interteardrop-referenced Acetabular Coverage Indices Differ During Standing in Adults With Hip Pain?
authors: Cousins R, Wagner M, Rao M, Pun SY, Smit K, Beaulé P, Grammatopoulos G.
abstract: Background Acetabular coverage is conventionally assessed using the lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) and acetabular index. However, on standing radiographs, these measurements may be referenced either to the pelvis or to the weightbearing horizontal. Whether selection of these reference lines leads to clinically relevant differences in acetabular coverage interpretation is uncertain. Questions/purposes (1) How do horizontally referenced and interteardrop-referenced LCEA and acetabular index measurements compare in patients with nonarthritic hip pain? (2) How are the magnitude and direction of pelvic obliquity associated with differences between horizontally referenced and interteardrop-referenced acetabular coverage measurements? (3) What are the magnitude and direction of pelvic obliquity in young adults undergoing assessment for unilateral nonarthritic hip pain? (4) How are hip-length discrepancy measures based on the lesser trochanter and hip center of rotation associated with the magnitude and direction of pelvic obliquity? Methods In this retrospective comparative study, 598 patients evaluated at a tertiary-referral young-adult hip clinic between June 2021 and June 2025 were identified; 10% (60 of 598) were excluded for bilateral hip involvement or prior procedures, 5% (28 of 598) for insufficient radiographs, and 3% (17 of 598) for age 50 years or older, leaving 493 patients age 16 to 49 years with unilateral nonarthritic hip conditions and standing AP pelvic radiographs to be included. The mean ± SD age was 35 ± 8 years; 39% (191 of 493) were male. Diagnoses included dysplasia; cam-type, mixed, and pincer-type femoroacetabular impingement; isolated labral tears; and other nonarthritic hip conditions. In each hip, LCEA and acetabular index were measured using horizontal and interteardrop-referenced measurements, and classification disagreement was assessed using LCEA ( 40°) and acetabular index ( 10°) categories. Associations between pelvic obliquity magnitude and measurement-difference magnitude were assessed using linear regression, with directional relationships assessed graphically. Pelvic obliquity was measured as the angle between the interteardrop and horizontal reference lines, with direction defined relative to the clinically evaluated side. Hip-length discrepancy measures based on the lesser trochanter and hip center of rotation were compared across pelvic obliquity magnitude and direction groups. After interrater standardization, each patient was randomly allocated to one of two observers, who performed all measurements for that patient; a third observer reviewed a random sample. Interobserver intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.69 to 0.87. Results Mean ± SD absolute differences between horizontally referenced and interteardrop-referenced measurements were 2° ± 1° for both LCEA and acetabular index. Classification disagreement occurred in 14% (69 of 493) using LCEA-based categories and 10% (51 of 493) using acetabular index-based categories, most notably when interteardrop-referenced LCEA indicated borderline dysplasia and horizontally referenced LCEA indicated normal coverage (29% [28 of 95]). Each 1° increase in pelvic obliquity magnitude was associated with an approximately 1° greater measurement difference for LCEA (β = 0.89 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 0.93]; R2 = 0.86; p Conclusion These findings indicate that horizontally referenced and interteardrop-referenced measurements can yield discordant acetabular coverage estimates and radiographic classifications for the same patient. As standing radiographs become more widely incorporated into hip evaluation, comparison of horizontally referenced and interteardrop-referenced LCEA and acetabular index measurements may provide additional information by revealing pelvic-obliquity-associated differences in measured coverage while standing. In patients with appreciable pelvic obliquity, these differences may warrant consideration when interpreting acetabular morphology and discussing the relative indications for treatment or procedural options because they may lead clinicians to disagree about whether the same hip meets thresholds used in treatment planning. Future work should correlate measurements based on horizontal referencing and interteardrop referencing in patients with appreciable pelvic obliquity with clinical and surgical outcomes to (1) determine whether acetabular indices measured using the interteardrop line or floor-based horizontal reference confer superior clinical value and (2) define procedure-specific thresholds for relevant diagnostic subgroups. Level of evidence Level III, diagnostic study.

title: Global research landscape, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of robot-assisted surgical management of pelvic urinary tract fistulas: a bibliometric and knowledge-mapping analysis.
authors: Wu G, Li D, Liu H, Fan C, Du G, Tian J.
abstract: Robot-assisted surgery has been applied to a range of pelvic urinary tract fistulas, but the literature is dispersed across urology, gynecology, colorectal surgery, and reconstructive practice. We examined how this literature developed, how its contributing communities interact, and whether its clinical themes converge. English-language articles and reviews indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded within the Web of Science Core Collection from inception to 1 August 2026 were screened for clinical or technical relevance. The final corpus contained 104 publications, comprising 85 articles and 19 reviews, published between 2005 and 2026. Publication and disciplinary trends, geographic collaboration, historical foundations, reference-based networks, Author Keyword themes, thematic evolution, and journal citation pathways were analyzed. Output remained low and uneven, although higher annual counts became more frequent after 2021. Urology remained the principal disciplinary setting, with broader participation from gynecology, reproductive health, and surgery. Authors from 31 countries or regions contributed; the United States led in both publication output and citations, while international collaboration remained concentrated within a limited network. Historical and thematic analyses identified vesicovaginal fistula repair as the main intellectual and conceptual backbone; colovesical, ureteral, rectourinary, and congenital applications formed smaller, partly separate streams. The literature has acquired a recognizable cross-specialty structure, but its principal clinical strands have not yet converged into a comparable evidence base. Future studies should prioritize multicenter designs and consistent reporting of anatomy, prior treatment, reconstruction, and clinically relevant outcomes.

title: Giant inguinoscrotal hernia repair with anterior component separation: a case report.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Chung C, Michaelides A, Navaratne L, Sahid SM, Wood S, El-Masry N.
abstract: Introduction Giant inguinoscrotal hernias (GIH), defined as hernias extending below the midpoint of the inner thigh, are rare in developed countries. Loss of domain, the risk of abdominal compartment syndrome, and the absence of standardised guidelines make surgical management particularly complex. We present a case of GIH managed with single-stage repair and complex abdominal wall reconstruction, alongside a literature review of surgical strategies. Case history A 55-year-old bed-bound man presented with a progressively enlarging left scrotal swelling over 5 years. Computed tomography demonstrated a giant left inguinoscrotal hernia measuring 53cm craniocaudally with 72% loss of domain, containing the majority of the small and large bowel. He underwent elective single-stage repair via midline laparotomy comprising reduction of hernia contents, omentectomy, left orchidectomy, partial scrotal excision, bilateral anterior component separation and abdominal wall reconstruction using Strattice biologic mesh underlay with Prolene mesh onlay reinforcement. The patient recovered without significant complications with no evidence of recurrence at 15 months. Findings A structured literature review identified 15 published cases of GIH repair with abdominal wall reconstruction. Surgical approaches were categorised into four groups: debulking or resection of abdominal contents, techniques to increase abdominal cavity volume, combination strategies and use of adjuncts such as botulinum toxin. Conclusions There remains no consensus on the optimal surgical management of GIH. This case supports anterior component separation as an effective single-stage strategy for GIH with significant loss of domain. In the absence of a standardised technique, a multidisciplinary approach is essential for optimising outcomes.

title: Giant hepatic cyst causing cardiac and critical inferior vena cava compression: an unusual presentation.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Mohamed E, Clarke C, Ginawi A, Gordon G, Cameron I.
abstract: Liver cysts are often detected as an incidental finding and require treatment in symptomatic cases due mainly to their exerted pressure effect. We present a case of a 77-year-old female patient who was diagnosed three years before with a giant hepatic cyst occupying the right hemi-liver and was subsequently referred to our hepatobiliary services following presenting with progressive dyspnoea, exertional fatigue in addition to bilateral lower limb oedema. Computed tomography imaging revealed an increase in cyst size with cardiac and significant inferior vena cava compression in addition to displacement of the right kidney. This case report highlights the importance of continued surveillance versus consideration of prophylactic drainage in carefully selected patients given the risks of future development of life-threatening complications.

title: Generating standing posture finite element models of the spine with radiation-free imaging.
authors: Incatasciato F, Lafranca PPG, Lee TT, Wu C, Zheng YP, van der Velden TA, Schlösser TPC, van Rietbergen B, Ito K, Kok J.
abstract: Finite element (FE) modelling is a powerful tool for investigating spinal biomechanics. Subject-specific finite element models of the spine are commonly built from supine data obtained from CT images, with harmful radiation and without soft-tissue structures. However, a more accurate evaluation of vertebrae and intervertebral disc loading requires the analysis of the subject in upright posture. In this study we propose a radiation-free alternative to create subject-specific standing FE models by combining supine MRI with ultrasound-based 3D spinal curvature assessment in standing posture. Subject-specific supine FE models of T3-L5 were created from synthetic CT (AI-generated from MRI) of 8 children. Dedicated spinal ultrasound was used to detect the positions of the vertebral laminae, which were used as input to convert the FE model from supine to standing. RMSE was found within 1 mm for the fitted vertebral levels. Validation against conventional radiographic measurements showed no statistical difference in sagittal alignment between the two imaging modalities in the lumbar and mid-to-lower thoracic parameters. In addition, the distance between the vertebral centroids measured from radiographs and from the upright FE model in sagittal and coronal plane was found to be less than 6 mm for the fitted levels. In conclusion, we demonstrate the feasibility of using completely radiation-free imaging as an alternative to CT and bi-planar X-ray to build subject-specific, upright, detailed FE models.

title: From Hunterian to Hunterian: the posterior malleolar fracture.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Bates S, Mason LW.
abstract: Background The posterior malleolar fracture (PMF) is now understood through three-dimensional imaging and mechanism-based classification, yet this understanding is not new. We argue that its central mechanism (rotation of an axially loaded talus within the ankle mortise) was inferred by Bonnin three-quarters of a century ago, obscured by an era of radiographic, size-based description, and later confirmed and made visible by computed tomography (CT). This continuity is frequently overlooked in the wider literature. Methods We present a narrative review of the primary historical literature alongside contemporary CT-based and cadaveric studies. Results Bonnin's cadaveric experiments showed that a rotating, axially loaded talus behaves as a wedge within the mortise, splitting the posterior tibial margin (the injury we now term a rotational pilon fracture) and he held that damage to the plafond, not the size of the fragment, determined the prognosis. Attention later shifted to the proportion of articular surface involved - a quantity poorly measured on radiographs and divorced from mechanism. CT has since reintroduced the mechanism in living patients: the Mason-Molloy classification describes three pathomechanical types that confirm and refine Bonnin's observations, and management has moved from size thresholds to classification-guided fixation. Conclusions Bonnin and Mason, two Hunterian Professors separated by more than half a century, performed essentially the same investigation with the tools available to them and reached the same conclusion. Recognising that the modern classification visualises a mechanism Bonnin had already inferred (rotation of a loaded talus) restores a continuity the wider literature has largely missed.

title: Erlotinib in a once-daily high-dose oral regimen could mitigate Chikungunya virus titer in mice.
authors: Orji CN, Loeanurit N, Sroithongmoon A, Wacharachaisurapol N, Jumroen Y, Eiamart W, Wittayalertpanya S, Chaijamorn W, Sriboonruang T, Vamananda J, Khotavivattana T, Boonyasuppayakorn S.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a re-emerging arbovirus that causes debilitating inflammatory arthritis, for which no approved antiviral therapy currently exists. This study investigated the potential of repurposing erlotinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, as an anti-CHIKV agent. Erlotinib demonstrated promising in vitro antiviral activity, with EC50 values in the low micromolar range and a favorable selectivity index. However, in vivo evaluation in C57BL/6 mice revealed pharmacokinetic limitations, characterized by rapid absorption and clearance, resulting in insufficient drug exposure under standard dosing regimens. Escalation to an intensive four-times-daily (QID) regimen successfully maintained plasma concentrations above the in vitro therapeutic threshold but led to significant body weight loss and failed to reduce viral titers or viral RNA levels in infected tissues. However, a once-daily (OD) regimen improved tolerability and significantly reduced footpad and serum viral titers relative to vehicle-treated controls. Notably, despite the lack of virological control in the QID regimen, erlotinib treatment reduced leukocyte infiltration and tissue inflammation in both treatment regimens, indicating a host-directed immunomodulatory effect. Overall, these findings highlight the critical role of dosing frequency in determining erlotinib's in vivo antiviral efficacy against CHIKV and suggest that once-daily (OD) administration may represent a more viable dosing strategy for further evaluation of erlotinib as a host-directed antiviral against CHIKV. Future strategies should also explore combination approaches with direct-acting antivirals to achieve more viral suppression and mitigation of disease pathology, as well as Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR)-guided scaffold optimization to improve in vivo pharmacokinetic profiles.

title: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate attenuates PAR-2-mediated inflammatory signaling and preserves markers of mitochondrial integrity in osteoarthritic chondrocytes.
authors: Patnaik R, Banerjee Y.
abstract: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), the principal catechin of green tea, exhibits broad anti-inflammatory properties; however, its effect on protease-activated receptor-2 (PAR-2)-mediated signaling in osteoarthritis (OA) has not been investigated. Here, we report that EGCG (5-10 µM) dose-dependently suppresses PAR-2 expression at both mRNA and protein levels in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated human chondrocytes derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. This upstream inhibition attenuated ERK1/2 phosphorylation (pERK/total ERK ratio reduced below basal levels at 10 µM) and produced concordant suppression of three functionally linked effector arms: (i) pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, MCP-1), with near-maximal inhibition at 10 µM and a saturation plateau at 20 µM; (ii) the SOX4-ADAMTS-5 catabolic axis (81.9% and 66.2% protein reduction, respectively); and (iii) RANK/RANKL surface expression. EGCG also restored mitochondrial membrane potential and biomass to near-homeostatic levels. Crucially, small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated PAR-2 silencing reduced LPS-induced TNF-α by ~38% and substantially blunted EGCG's incremental efficacy, supporting PAR-2 as a predominant, though not exclusive, mediator of EGCG's anti-inflammatory action. The effective concentrations employed are physiologically attainable through dietary green tea consumption, as documented by a comprehensive survey of EGCG content across 36 commercial varieties. These findings support PAR-2 as a candidate upstream target of EGCG in OA chondrocytes and suggest a mechanistic model involving PAR-2 → ERK1/2 → TNF-α/SOX4/ADAMTS-5, through which a dietary polyphenol exerts coordinated anti-inflammatory and anti-catabolic effects, while preserving structural and thermodynamic markers of mitochondrial integrity.

title: Enhanced decellularization and human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell repopulation of porcine aorta using SDF-1 and PDGF-BB for potential use as a vascular conduit: an in vitro study.
journal: Annals of Surgical Treatment and Research
authors: Kim HJ, Seo JH, Jeon MJ, Choi GH, Jung TW, Lee T, Park HS.
abstract: Purpose Decellularized vascular grafts have emerged as promising alternatives to synthetic grafts, particularly for small-diameter vessels. However, effective decellularization requires a balance between sufficient removal of cellular components and preservation of extracellular matrix (ECM) integrity, while functional performance depends on successful recellularization. Achieving both remains challenging and requires protocol optimization. Methods Porcine aortic tissue was harvested and decellularized using a sequential protocol consisting of Triton X-100 followed by sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) combined with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). The efficiency of decellularization and ECM preservation was assessed using biochemical and histological analyses. Recellularization was evaluated in vitro using human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBM-MSCs). The effects of stromal cell-derived factor-1 (SDF-1) and platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB) on hBM-MSC attachment and proliferation were examined, as well as their potential to differentiate into endothelial and smooth muscle lineages. Results The modified DMSO-based protocol achieved greater than 99% reduction in DNA content while preserving sulfated glycosaminoglycans and collagen architecture. Supplementation with SDF-1 and PDGF-BB significantly enhanced hBM-MSC proliferation and improved cell attachment on the decellularized scaffold compared with controls. Additionally, hBM-MSCs demonstrated the potential to differentiate into both endothelial and smooth muscle lineages under appropriate induction conditions. Conclusion A sequential Triton X-100 and SDS/DMSO protocol enabled rapid and efficient decellularization of porcine aorta while preserving ECM integrity. The combined application of SDF-1 and PDGF-BB enhanced hBM-MSC attachment to the decellularized scaffold. In addition, hBM-MSCs expressed endothelial and smooth muscle lineage markers under vascular endothelial growth factor and transforming growth factor-β1 induction conditions, respectively.

title: Enablers and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination implementation among key stakeholders in Ethiopia: A qualitative study.
authors: Assefa KT, Worku AG, Muche AA, Geremew BM, Woldetsadik MA, Alemu K.
abstract: Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective and lifesaving intervention against cervical cancer. However, achieving high, equitable, and sustainable uptake remains a significant challenge in low-resource settings, including Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the enablers and barriers to HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia. Methods An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed in purposively selected settings representing diverse socio-ecological contexts (Afar, Amhara, Addis Ababa, and Dire Dawa). Six focus group discussions were conducted with adolescent girls (n = 14), parents of eligible adolescent girls (n = 14), and community representatives (n = 14). In addition, nineteen key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with healthcare providers, Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) coordinators, and technical advisors from governmental and non-governmental organizations. Data were analysed using a combined deductive-inductive content analysis guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0). Results Multiple interacting factors influenced HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia, categorised as enablers and barriers across community, health system, and policy levels. Enablers included the Perceived Vaccine Attributes and Delivery Adaptability, Supportive Policy and Multisectoral Strategic Partnerships, Socio-cultural and Belief-based Drivers, and Health System Readiness and Workforce Motivation. However, several barriers limited implementation, including Suspicions About Targeting 9-14-year-old Girls and Consent-related Administrative Obstacles, Pervasive Misinformation and Cognitive Resistance, Health System Resource Constraints and Coordination Gaps, Donor Dependency Risks and Financial Sustainability Concerns, and Structural Access Constraints and Equity Gaps. Conclusions While policy shifts, external strategic partnerships, and frontline worker dedication have accelerated vaccine reach, the long-term sustainability of Ethiopia's HPV vaccination program remains constrained by multi-level barriers. Progress toward the global 2030 cervical cancer elimination targets requires trust-building risk-communication strategies to counter fertility myths, simplified consent procedures, targeted domestic resource mobilization, and context-specific delivery models tailored to underserved pastoralist and urban sub-populations.

title: Embedded incus into the external auditory canal following temporal bone fracture.
authors: Obeidat M, Sbeitan O, Obeidat GB, Mugdadi TH, Al-Mashagbah MMA.

title: Effects of speed, load, and surface on tibial bending moment and stress.
authors: Wenzel TA, Francis EB, Brown TN.
abstract: This study assessed locomotor speed, body-borne load, and surface on tibial stress and bending. Fourteen recreational runners had tibial bending moments quantified during a jog (3.0 m/s) and run (4.5 m/s) over a flat and uneven surface with and without 15 kg body-borne load. Peak and mean values of AP, ML and resultant tibial stress and bending moments were quantified and submitted to 3-way repeated-measures ANOVA, while stress and bending waveforms were submitted to statistical parametric mapping 3-way ANOVA. During the run, mean and peak AP and resultant tibial bending moments and stress increased (all: p ≤ 0.009), while all stress and bending waveforms were larger from 0 to 11% and 70 to 100% of stance (all: p ≤ 0.031). With the 15 kg load, mean and peak AP and resultant tibial bending moments and stresses increased (all: p ≤ 0.008) and greater waveform from 13 to 36% and 95 to 100% of stance was exhibited for all bending moment and stresses (all: p ≤ 0.043). On the uneven surface, participants decreased mean and peak AP and resultant tibial bending moments and stresses (all: p ≤ 0.010) and used smaller tibial stress and bending waveforms between 0 to 13%, 18 to 20%, and 69 to 86% of stance for all moments and stresses (all: p ≤ 0.033). Faster run speed and heavier load may elevate risk of tibial stress fracture, while traversing an irregular, uneven surface led to significant reduction in tibial stress and may not similarly elevate injury risk.

title: Effects of footwear bending stiffness on direction-specific functional base of support in healthy older adults.
authors: Kramer PS, Takahashi KZ, Franz JR, Fino PC.
abstract: Less than 30 % of the anatomical footprint is typically available for balance control, and this available area, known as the functional base of support (fBoS), can decrease with age. In older adults, smaller fBoS values are associated with a higher risk of falls. Because the strength of intrinsic foot muscles can influence the fBoS, we hypothesized that increasing footwear bending stiffness may similarly increase the fBoS. Twenty-one healthy older adults (70 ± 6 years, 10F/11 M) provided informed consent. Participants "leaned as far as you can with both feet together in one of four directions (forward, backward, right, left) without stepping". Heels, toes, and feet could lift freely to allow full ankle motion.
