Footwear stiffness was manipulated using standardized shoes (S00), S00 with a 1.6 mm carbon-fiber insole (S16), and S00 with a 3.2 mm carbon-fiber insole (S32). The directional fBoS was defined using the minimum distance between the maximum excursion of the center of pressure and direction-specific foot boundary landmarks. There were no differences in fBoS between S00 and S16 (all p-values > 0.05) or between S00 and S32 (all p-values > 0.145). Contrary to our hypotheses, no detectable immediate group-level effect of footwear bending stiffness was observed, suggesting that increasing footwear bending stiffness alone does not fully explain a mechanism underlying decreased fBoS with aging.

title: Effect of a training camp in the heat on nutritional intake of well-trained endurance athletes.
authors: Tiollier E, Fabre M, Louis J, Le Meur Y, Schmit C, Robach P, Marquet LA, Hausswirth C.
abstract: We investigated the effect of a training camp in the heat on energy and macronutrient intake and hunger. Twenty-two athletes completed two training periods (8 days each) of similar load. One group (HEAT, n = 14) trained successively in a temperate environment (10 ± 3°C, RH: 58 ± 11 %) and then in a hot environment (30 ± 5°C, RH: 74 ± 15%), while the other group (CON, n = 8) trained in the same temperate environment. Daily energy intake (EI), carbohydrate (CHO) and protein (PRO) intake were higher (p < 0.001) in HEAT (+23.9 ± 20.3%, +36.1 ± 24.3%, +27.5 ± 21.2%, respectively) during the heat camp compared with the temperate condition. More specifically, EI, CHO and PRO intake were greater at breakfast in HEAT (+90.1 ± 65.5%, +107.2 ± 74.3%, +69.8 ± 54.1 %, respectively). PRO intake also increased at dinner (p < 0.001) in HEAT. Mean EI and macronutrient intake during the training sessions were significantly increased (p < 0.01) in HEAT. Hunger was greater before breakfast in HEAT (p < 0.01) during the heat camp. In CON, none of the measures differed between the two training periods. These results suggest that athletes spontaneously increase their energy intake when training in the heat, with breakfast serving as the primary meal for this nutritional adjustment.

title: Digital rectal examination as a standalone trigger for urgent prostate cancer investigation.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Varuni S R, Gado M, Pinnamaraju P, Hajuthman W, Dsouza R, Jadeja D, Smith G, Young B, Dewan T, Sheikh W, Kathiresan Y, Verma S, Eyong R, Diya M, Tharakan T, Pai A.
abstract: Introduction The contemporary value of digital rectal examination (DRE) as a standalone trigger for urgent prostate cancer investigation remains a subject of intense debate. Increasing scepticism regarding its diagnostic sensitivity, coupled with patient reluctance, has led to declining uptake of DRE in primary care. This study evaluates the outcomes of patients referred solely based on an abnormal DRE to determine its role in identifying clinically significant disease that might otherwise be overlooked by prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 2,700 patients referred via the rapid prostate cancer pathway over a 33-month period. A specific cohort of 288 patients referred primarily because of an abnormal DRE finding - with PSA levels within the age-specific reference range - was identified. Results The mean patient age was 69 years and median PSA was 2.7ng/mL. Following secondary care assessment, 56.6% (163 of 288) of patients underwent biparametric magnetic resonance imaging. Of these, 35.5% had suspicious findings (Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System score ≥3). Ultimately, 14.2% (41 of 288) of patients underwent transperineal biopsy. Clinically significant prostate cancer was diagnosed in 16 patients (cancer detection rate: 5.6%); all 16 underwent radical treatment. Conclusions DRE should not be superseded by PSA testing alone. Rather, it should be offered as part of a comprehensive primary care assessment, with its use determined through shared decision making that balances clinical benefit against patient acceptability. An abnormal DRE, regardless of the PSA level, necessitates urgent referral to a rapid access urology pathway.

title: Diffusion tensor imaging and structural MRI reveal early microstructural injury and progressive atrophy of the olfactory bulb in type 1 diabetic rats.
authors: Gao L, Huang M, Chen J, Wang X.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) can detect early olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) rats and to investigate their relationship with structural and histopathological changes. Methods Control and STZ-induced T1DM rats underwent DTI, high-resolution structural MRI and histological examination at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), axial diffusivity (Da), and radial diffusivity (Dr) were measured in the olfactory nerve layer/glomerular layer/external plexiform layer (ONL/GL/EPL), granule cell layer (GCL), and subependymal zone (SEZ). Results Compared to the controls, T1DM rats showed decreased FA and increased MD, Da, and Dr in the ONL/GL/EPL at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. In the GCL, FA was decreased, whereas Dr was increased. No significant diffusion abnormalities were detected in the SEZ. Ultrastructural examination revealed axolemmal disruption, demyelination, reduced axoplasmic content, and axonal vacuolization in the ONL. Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) demonstrated olfactory bulb atrophy as early as 2 weeks, initially involving the GCL and SEZ, with more extensive and regionally heterogeneous atrophy at 12 weeks. Nissl staining confirmed structural atrophy, and increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity supported apoptosis-related tissue injury. STZ-induced T1DM causes early, layer-specific olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities and progressive structural atrophy. Conclusion The differing spatial and temporal distributions of diffusion abnormalities and atrophy suggest that DTI and volumetric MRI capture partially distinct aspects of diabetes-associated olfactory bulb injury. DTI may provide a sensitive, noninvasive approach for detecting early microstructural abnormalities before widespread structural loss develops.

title: Different osteoarthritis progression rates within early-stage knee osteoarthritis: a retrospective cohort study using machine learning cluster analysis from the osteoarthritis initiative database.
authors: Song JW, Kim SE, Ro DH.
abstract: Background Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous disease with varying progression rates among patients within the same severity grade. This study aimed to identify clinically interpretable radiographic phenotypes among knees with baseline Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grade 2 osteoarthritis and to compare their 4-year radiographic progression patterns using baseline radiographic features, lifetime exercise patterns, and demographic characteristics. Methods Data of patients with baseline KL grade 2 from the Osteoarthritis Initiative database were retrieved. Unsupervised clustering was performed using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) for dimensionality reduction, followed by hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN) to identify distinct subgroups. The proportion of knees progressing to KL grade ≥ 3 within 4 years was compared between subgroups, followed by a survival analysis until knee replacement or progression to KL grade 4. Results A total of 1997 knees with a mean follow-up of 103.3 months (maximum, 108 months) were included. A total of seven subgroups were identified and classified into accelerated osteoarthritis progression (AOP) group and slow osteoarthritis progression (SOP) group according to whether their 4-year KL grade progression proportions were above or below the training-set average. In a supportive long-term survival analysis, the AOP group also showed significantly earlier progression to knee replacement or KL grade 4 than the SOP group (training set, P Conclusions Within baseline KL grade 2 knees, clinically interpretable radiographic phenotypes, including lateral JSN, medial JSN with subchondral sclerosis, osteophyte-dominant changes without JSN, and chondrocalcinosis-dominant patterns, were associated with different 4-year KL grade progression rates. These findings support viewing KL grade 2 knee OA as a heterogeneous radiographic stage that may be further stratified into phenotype-based subgroups with different short-term radiographic prognoses.

title: Clinical and economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to peripheral artery disease in Italy: A nationwide analysis.
authors: Scortichini M, Gargiulo M, Manzi M, Uccioli L, Sciattella P.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16-25% at 180 days and 23-34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.

title: Bi-Mamba-Load: A bidirectional structured state space model with sequence relationship adaptive perception for electricity load forecasting.
authors: Zhu J, Xi L, Liao C, Zhong B, Zhong J, Zhang L.
abstract: The accurate prediction of electricity load is a critical component for smart-grid management, energy allocation, and grid stability. Traditional statistical methods and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) often struggle with nonlinear relationships or long-range temporal dependencies, whereas Transformer architectures incur quadratic complexity in the sequence length. The Structured State Space Model Mamba provides linear sequence modeling but uses a unidirectional scan and a fixed treatment of multivariate dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose Bi-Mamba-Load, which combines a bidirectional Mamba encoder, a custom forget gate, and a Sequence Relationship Adaptive Perception (SRAP) module. Both encoder branches operate exclusively on the observed historical window, so no observations from the forecasting horizon are used as inputs. SRAP computes Spearman correlation statistics from the training split and performs dataset-level selection between channel-independent and channel-mixing tokenization; the selected route remains fixed for all samples in that dataset. Experiments across eight benchmark datasets indicate competitive or superior forecasting accuracy against the evaluated baselines while retaining linear scaling with the input length, subject to the constant-factor overhead of bidirectional scanning.

title: Arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting for Hepple stage V osteochondral lesions of the talus: a retrospective case series.
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Zhang ZH, Xue C, Su CF, Gao SH, Oliva F, Maffulli N, Migliorini F, Feng SM.
abstract: Background Evidence regarding arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting for Hepple stage V osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLTs) remains limited. This study assessed short-term clinical outcomes, postoperative imaging findings, and perioperative characteristics of this technique. Methods This retrospective case series included 23 patients undergoing arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting between March 2020 and July 2024. Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) demonstrated subchondral cystic changes in all lesions, which were classified as Hepple stage V OLTs. The primary outcome was the European Foot and Ankle Society (EFAS) score at final follow-up. Secondary outcomes included the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score during walking, the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, Karlsson Ankle Functional Score (KAFS), 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) pain domain score, Tegner score and ankle range of motion (ROM). Postoperative radiographs and available CT scans were reviewed to assess graft position and subchondral healing; MRI findings were also evaluated when available. Operative time, concomitant lateral ligament repair, and complications were documented. Paired comparisons were performed using the paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, as appropriate after assessment of normality. Results Mean follow-up was 21.0 ± 8.7 months (median, 18.0 months; Q1-Q3, 13.0-24.0), and mean lesion area was 1.94 ± 0.38 cm 2 . Median operative time was 75.0 min (Q1-Q3, 67.5-86.0), and five patients underwent concomitant lateral ligament repair. The median EFAS score improved from 9.0 (Q1-Q3, 8.0-10.0) preoperatively to 19.0 (Q1-Q3, 18.0-20.0) at final follow-up (P Conclusions Arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting was associated with improvements in pain, function, and activity in patients with Hepple stage V OLTs at short-term follow-up. Postoperative CT demonstrated graft incorporation in all patients who underwent CT assessment. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of this technique for appropriately selected cystic lesions, although larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are warranted.

title: Arthroscopic Scapholunate Osseous Ligament Anchor-Based Round-Block Repair for Scapholunate Instability.
authors: de Villeneuve Bargemon JB, Goorens CK, Merlini L, Audiffret L.
abstract: Scapholunate instability remains difficult to treat, particularly in lesions involving detachment of the dorsal intercarpal ligament from the scaphoid. We describe the Scapholunate Osseous Ligament Anchor-based Round-block technique, an arthroscopic anchor-based repair designed to reinsert and retension the dorsal capsuloligamentous complex. The procedure allows dynamic assessment of reduction and may be combined with additional palmar stabilization when needed. This modular technique may represent a useful arthroscopic option for selected patterns of scapholunate instability.

title: Arthroscopic Biologic Meniscal Root Repair With Iliotibial Band Autograft Augmentation.
authors: Piontek T, Rubczak S, Bulinski P, Naczk J, Głowacki J, Bąbik B, Banach A.
abstract: This paper presents a description of a surgical technique-a modified Henning-Piontek procedure-used for meniscal root salvage. The method is intended for difficult, chronic injuries with loss of continuity of the meniscal root. Such cases would most often result in total or subtotal meniscectomy, which, as is well known, significantly accelerates the degenerative changes in the knee. This technique aligns with the "save the meniscus" approach practiced and promoted by the authors. It involves the use of an iliotibial band graft to create a bridge between the damaged meniscus and the anatomical attachment site of the meniscal root. This enables anatomical repair of the meniscal root, facilitates healing, and preserves the natural structure of the joint.

title: All-Inside Posterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Achilles Allograft and Suture Tape Augmentation.
authors: Md Yusoff BAH, Zhafri A, Ramlan MKR, Nik Kamaruzman NKA, Omar A, Mohamad N, Azwan Aziz M.
abstract: Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) reconstruction is challenged by graft elongation and delayed biological integration, often necessitating slow rehabilitation and carrying a risk of arthrofibrosis. This technical report describes an all-inside technique augmented with the modified internal bracing to address these limitations. The technique involves integrating a FiberTape within a quadrupled Achilles tendon allograft, creating a load-sharing composite. An all-inside, retrograde socket method was used for anatomic PCL reconstruction in the knee, with suspensory fixation on both femur and tibia. The graft-tape construct was simultaneously tensioned. The technique provides immediate biomechanical stability by mitigating graft micromotion, elongation, and tunnel abrasion. By closely replicating native PCL stiffness, this construct facilitates an accelerated, protective rehabilitation protocol focused on early motion and quadriceps activation, thereby aiming to reduce failure rates and postoperative stiffness. This method represents a synergistic evolution in PCL reconstruction, combining synthetic reinforcement with biological healing.

title: Agri-PIDNet-S: Lightweight semantic segmentation for field-structure and obstacle perception in seedling-stage cotton fields.
authors: Xin Y, Li Y, Wei W, Cao X, Mao B, Chen Y.
abstract: Reliable joint perception of crop rows, furrows, and obstacles is essential for autonomous inter-row operations in seedling-stage cotton fields. However, small and sparsely distributed plants, perspective-convergent rows, irregular furrow boundaries, and low obstacle pixel coverage jointly challenge fine-detail preservation, long-range structural modeling, and boundary discrimination under real-time constraints. This study formulated cotton-field perception as a four-class semantic segmentation task and constructed a dataset of 709 pixel-wise annotated images comprising background, crop rows, furrows, and obstacles. We developed Agri-PIDNet-S, a field-specific lightweight network based on PIDNet-S. A coordinate-aware multi-kernel inverted residual module (CA-MKIR) preserves shallow details and small-obstacle contours, a squeeze-and-excitation-enhanced deep-to-token module (SaE-D2T) models long-range row and furrow structures, and a boundary-guided window-attention refinement Bag (BWR-Bag) improves semantic-boundary fusion. The network was trained with a composite loss incorporating auxiliary boundary supervision. On the cotton-field test set, Agri-PIDNet-S achieved 92.37% mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 96.02% mean Dice coefficient (mDice) in the model-comparison experiment, while repeated training with three seeds yielded an mIoU of 92.35 ± 0.03%. Relative to PIDNet-S under the same comparison protocol, mIoU increased by 3.53 percentage points, while obstacle IoU improved from 79.60% to 88.67%. The model contained 8.048 million parameters, required 19.161 GFLOPs, and achieved 155.67 frames per second. Zero-shot external evaluation on tomato, watermelon, and maize fields yielded a structural mIoU of 86.29% for the background, crop-row, and furrow classes. Under the evaluated conditions, the task-oriented modifications achieved higher segmentation point estimates than PIDNet-S while maintaining computational efficiency; the external results provide preliminary evidence of cross-crop structural transfer.

title: Access to pharmacological management for osteoporosis by older people with hip fractures in long-term care: A nationwide cross-sectional study.
authors: Inacio MC, Cuthbert AR, Fernando RL, Caughey G, Eshetie T, Crotty M.
abstract: Objectives To examine whether individuals who had a hip fracture while accessing long-term care (LTC) in a facility or at home, or while waiting for LTC, received recommended pharmacological management for osteoporosis before and in the year after fracture. Design A population-based cross-sectional study using the National Historical Cohort of the Registry of Senior Australians. Setting and participants Older people hospitalised with a hip fracture while accessing or waiting for facility or home-based LTC in Australia between 01/01/2012 and 31/12/2018. Methods Utilisation of pharmacological management for osteoporosis (i.e., bisphosphonates, denosumab, teriparatide, strontium) before and one year after hip fracture was examined using linked pharmaceutical, hospital, and aged care data. Logistic regression models examined the associations between individual and LTC setting characteristics and accessing pharmacological management in the year after fracture. Results Of the 52,233 (71.3% female, 87.7 median age) hip fractures that occurred during the study period, 58.3% (n = 30,441) were in individuals receiving facility-based LTC, 14.6% (n = 7603) were receiving home-based LTC, and 27.2% (n = 14,189) were waiting for LTC. Forty three percent (N = 22,622 of 52,233) had received pharmacological management for osteoporosis at any time prior to hip fracture and 21% received it in the previous year. One-year post fracture, 39% of the 30,768 individuals who were still alive had received pharmacological management for osteoporosis. Older age, male gender, having dementia, receiving facility-based LTC, and not receiving pharmacological management prior to fracture were associated with lower receipt of pharmacological management after fracture. Conclusions and recommendations These results highlight that the use of pharmacological management for osteoporosis for older people experiencing a hip fracture while in or waiting for LTC remains low, despite clinical guideline recommendations. Brief summary Of the 52,233 older Australians who had a hip fracture while receiving or waiting for long-term care between 2012 and 2018, 43% had received pharmacological management for osteoporosis at any time prior to fracture. In the year after fracture, 39% of the 30,768 individuals who were still alive received pharmacological management for osteoporosis. These national estimates highlight that access to pharmacolocical management for osteoporosis in long-term care recipients following hip fracture remains low, despite clinical guideline recommendations.

title: ASO Visual Abstract: Impact of Systematic Discontinuation of Mitomycin C HIPEC for Colorectal Peritoneal Metastases on Oncologic Outcomes-A Propensity Score Matched Analysis.
authors: Tanweer MD, Waheed MT, Paz IB, Lwin T, Mohammed H, Melstrom L, Fong Y, Brar G, Castillo D, Kasi PM, Fakih M, Raoof M.

title: A temperature-adaptive logit-standardized knowledge distillation for lightweight network intrusion detection.
authors: Dong X, Yang K, Liu J, Chen W.
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet has made network attacks increasingly frequent, stealthy, and diverse, posing stringent requirements on the accuracy and latency of network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). Although deep-learning-based NIDS can achieve strong detection performance, their large parameter size and high computational cost hinder deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this limitation, we propose a temperature-adaptive logit-standardized knowledge distillation framework for lightweight network intrusion detection. A high-capacity teacher network first learns discriminative representations from network traffic, and a compact student network is then trained to mimic the teacher under a tailored distillation scheme. During distillation, we apply per-sample Z-score standardization to the logits of both teacher and student models to mitigate scale mismatch and emphasize relative inter-class relationships. Moreover, we adapt the distillation temperature according to sample difficulty and training progress, enabling suitably smoothed soft targets across samples and stages, and jointly optimize the student with hard-label supervision. Experiments on benchmark datasets including NSL-KDD and CIC-IDS2017 demonstrate that the proposed method substantially reduces model complexity while maintaining stable and competitive detection performance. Additional repeated-run, ablation, and lightweight baseline analyses further indicate that the proposed framework achieves a favorable accuracy-complexity trade-off.

title: A quantitative assessment of Chinese county high school policies using the PMC index model.
authors: Wu Q, Li G.
abstract: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China's counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial to evaluate current policy texts, identify their shortcomings, and provide empirical evidence for future policy development. This study collected 55 policy texts from provincial and municipal governments, utilizing the Policy Modeling Consistency index model to evaluate 14 representative policies. The results indicate that all the assessed policies fall within the"pass","good",or"with distinction" score category, with no substandard policies identified and none achieving a "perfect" score.A detailed analysis identifies critical policy shortcomings, including the prioritization of short-to-medium-term strategies over long-term planning, fragmented enrollment systems, insufficient campus culture development, as well as limited career guidance, mental health support,and policy guidance for home-school-community joint education. Local governments adopt a conservative stance on educational policy evaluation and systemic institutional reforms.To address these issues, this study recommends that local governments integrate the enrollment systems of public and private high schools within their jurisdictions, strengthen the prohibition of on cross-regional enrollment, increase investment in students' career guidance and mental health education, and launch more programs to encourage parents and communities to participate in school education. Moreover, the central government should urge local authorities to accelerate reforms in the high school education system.

title: "Pauli"-tical science: early single-center experience with the technique of the minimally invasive retromuscular parastomal hernia repair.
authors: Hallis B, Rendell VR, Armstrong RA, Juza RM.
abstract: Background Parastomal hernias cause significant morbidity and are frequent after stoma creation, with reported incidences reaching up to 50%. With current repair methods, recurrence and mesh-related complications remain high. The Pauli Parastomal Hernia Repair (PPHR), developed as a modification of the Sugarbaker approach, utilizes a posterior component separation technique to lateralize the bowel within the retromuscular space to offset the bowel and minimize mesh-related complications. Small series on outcomes show promise, but data are overall lacking for minimally invasive (MIS) modifications of this approach. We report our series of robotic approaches to PPHR. Methods This study is a retrospective case series of patients undergoing elective robotic PPHR (rPPHR) from 2022 to 2024 at a single-institution tertiary referral center by two fellowship-trained abdominal wall surgeons. Patient and hernia characteristics, operative details, and post-operative outcomes were abstracted from the electronic health records. Hernia recurrence (defined as CT evidence or physical exam findings) and 30-day morbidity, including stoma and mesh-related complications, were reported and analyzed. Results During this time period, 26 patients underwent elective robotic PPHR. Twenty patients (77%) had a concomitant midline component, and 13 (50%) had a previous hernia repair with 6 (46%) having previous mesh placement. The average parastomal hernia size was 24 ± 17 cm 2 . Stoma types varied with 11 (42%) end colostomies, 10 (38%) end ileostomies, and 5 (19%) ileal conduits. There were no intra-operative complications. The 30-day morbidity was 23%, which included one surgical site infection (SSI), one seroma, one ileus, and one mechanical obstruction at the stoma. With a median follow-up of 15.4 months, there was a 1-year recurrence rate of 4% and 2-year recurrence rate of 8%. One repair required reoperation for postoperative pouching difficulty without a recurrence present. Conclusion The rPPHR technique for parastomal hernia repair is a technically challenging procedure with promising early outcomes and deserves continued study of longer-term outcomes.

title: Wisdom in surgery in the era of artificial intelligence.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Mahawar K.

title: Wearable Sensor-Based Prediction of Knee Joint Moments in Competitive Rugby Players During Multidirectional Movements.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Gao Z, Trama R, McNish D, Esposito M, Ruschkowski J, Stefanyshyn DJ, Wannop JW.
abstract: This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning framework using plantar-pressure sensors to estimate knee moments during rugby-specific movements. A total of 31 North American competitive rugby players were recruited to perform four common rugby movements on an infilled artificial turf surface in a motion capture laboratory. Synchronized data acquisition was performed for plantar pressure, motion capture, and ground reaction forces. Knee moments were calculated via inverse dynamics. Genetic Algorithm-Deep Forest Regression (GA-DFR) was used to select plantar-pressure sensors and predict resultant moments within participant-level nested cross-validation. Four alternative models predicted the resultant using the same layouts and participant splits. Complementary deep forest regression (DFR) models predicted the three moment components using these layouts. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpreted held-out predictions. Layouts contained 7-18 sensors. Pooled resultant R 2 was 0.795, with root mean square error of 0.0512 N·m/N. DFR performed better than linear regression and the convolutional neural network, with no significant differences from the deep neural network or long short-term memory network. Pooled R 2 was 0.806, 0.662, and 0.675 for flexion-extension, adduction-abduction, and internal-external rotation moments, respectively. Resultant temporal SHAP contributions exceeded their stance-wide mean during 9%-55% of stance, peaking at 24%. Reduced plantar-pressure inputs supported estimation of resultant and direction-specific knee-moment waveforms in unseen rugby players.

title: Using double-bundle Achilles tendon-bone allograft for reconstruction of compound loss of lateral malleolus and lateral ankle ligaments: A rare case report.
authors: Chiu H, Chen JH.
abstract: Rationale Composite defects of the lateral ankle, involving bone loss, ligament disruption, and soft tissue compromise, cause profound mechanical instability and are difficult to reconstruct with techniques that address bone or ligaments alone. Patient concerns We report a 26-year-old woman who presented with progressive right ankle pain, recurrent giving-way, and peroneal tendon subluxation 7 years after a high-energy crush injury that required flap coverage. Diagnoses Lateral malleolar loss with a distal fibular bony defect measuring approximately 5 × 3 × 2 cm and chronic varus instability; complete anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) and calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) rupture; and peroneal tendon dislocation were confirmed by stress radiographs and magnetic resonance imaging. Interventions Single-stage reconstruction with a cryopreserved Achilles tendon-bone allograft. The calcaneal bone block was contoured and fixed to the fibular stump with a 4.5-mm cannulated screw to reconstitute the lateral malleolus. The tendon was split into 2 bundles (7 mm × 30 mm for the ATFL and 7 mm × 40 mm for the CFL) for anatomic ATFL and CFL reconstruction and secured with interference screws at the talar and calcaneal footprints. The peroneal tendons were reduced after bony restoration. Postoperative rehabilitation used an Aircast® brace with non-weight-bearing ambulation for the first 3 weeks, partial weight-bearing from week 3, full weight-bearing by week 6, and brace discontinuation at week 12. Outcomes At the final follow-up of 16 months, the patient ambulated pain-free with a stable ankle. Radiographs demonstrated successful incorporation of the bone allograft, and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed intact ATFL/CFL grafts with maintained peroneal tendon reduction. Functional scores were Karlsson-Peterson 87 and American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society ankle-hindfoot 90. Lessons A double-bundle Achilles tendon-bone allograft enables simultaneous reconstruction of lateral malleolar bone and lateral ligaments, avoiding donor-site morbidity and achieving durable stability in complex, previously reconstructed ankles. This approach should be considered when both osseous and ligamentous deficits coexist.

title: Trends in screening tools for sarcopenia: A bibliometric analysis.
authors: Guan L, Duan F, Qin C, Wu W, Yang G, Yu R, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Wei F, Feng J, Ma K, Zang Z, Li C, Liu Y, Wang R, Wang L, Liu Y.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia, characterized by the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength, and function, poses a significant health challenge in aging populations. Early identification through effective screening tools is critical to mitigate risks such as falls, fractures, and frailty. This study aimed to analyze global research trends in sarcopenia screening tools using bibliometric methods to identify key contributors and emerging hotspots, thereby guiding future research directions. Methods Data were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) for the period from January 2013 to March 2025. A total of 180 articles were analyzed using bibliometric tools such as the R package bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. The analysis focused on publication trends, citation impact, co-authorship networks, and keyword co-occurrence to map research trends and identify influential studies and screening tools. Results The analysis revealed a steady increase in research output since 2013, with an annual growth rate of 38.16%. China emerged as the leading contributor, accounting for 30% of publications, followed by Japan and Brazil. Among the screening tools investigated, the Strength, Assistance in walking, Rise from a chair, Climb stairs, and Falls (SARC-F) questionnaire was the most studied tool, followed by SARC-F combined with calf circumference (SARC-CalF) and calf circumference measurements. Citation analysis highlighted pivotal studies on SARC-F validation, while emerging hotspots included tools like the Mini Sarcopenia Risk Assessment (MSRA) and Ishii test, reflecting a shift toward more practical and accessible screening methods. Conclusion This bibliometric analysis maps global advancements in sarcopenia screening tools, highlighting China's prolific research output (30% of publications) and the development of culturally adapted instruments in Japan (Ishii test, Yubi-wakka method). The SARC-F questionnaire dominates research focus, spurring innovations including SARC-CalF and calf circumference metrics. The findings advocate standardized validation frameworks and integration of evidence-based screening into geriatric care policies, emphasizing tool accessibility and clinical utility to combat sarcopenia in aging populations.

title: Total hip arthroplasty improves global sagittal and coronal spinal imbalance and spinopelvic mobility : a prospective cohort study.
authors: Leung TKC, Chan PK, Cheung A, Luk MH, Lau LCM, Cheung WK, Chiu KY, Fu H.
abstract: Aims The impact of total hip arthroplasty (THA) on global spinal alignment is under-reported. This study prospectively evaluates the effect of THA on coronal and sagittal global spinal balance and spinopelvic kinematics using dynamic whole-body EOS radiographs. Methods We prospectively studied 163 patients (62 male, 101 female; mean age 68.4 years (SD 9.1)) undergoing primary unilateral THA for end-stage osteoarthritis. Full-body EOS images were acquired preoperatively and at a six-month follow-up in standing, relaxed-seated, and deep-seated postures. The primary outcome was change in sagittal vertical axis (SVA). Secondary outcomes included changes in pelvic tilt (PT), sacral slope (SS), proximal femoral angle (PFA), and coronal parameters (C7-central sacral vertical line (C7-CSVL), limb length discrepancy (LLD), and pelvic obliquity (PO)). Preoperative SVA > 50 mm defined sagittal imbalance; C7-CSVL > 20 mm defined coronal imbalance. Statistical analysis employed paired non-parametric tests and multivariate regression. Results In the 58 patients with preoperative sagittal imbalance (SVA > 50 mm), mean SVA improved significantly from 77.9 mm (SD 24.4) to 59.9 mm (SD 36.1; p Conclusion THA improves global sagittal and coronal spinal imbalance, restoring spinopelvic mobility by increasing hip flexion and reducing compensatory pelvic tilt. These dynamic postoperative changes challenge the static assumptions underpinning current hip-spine classifications. Preoperative and postoperative analysis of global dynamic spinopelvic balance and mobility are crucial for managing hip-spine syndrome.

title: Time- and posture-specific management of severe supine hypertension and neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in diabetic autonomic neuropathy: A case report.
authors: Šinigoj Porčnik P, Kabaklić A.
abstract: Rationale Coexistence of neurogenic orthostatic hypotension with supine or nocturnal hypertension creates a therapeutic challenge because treatment of either component may aggravate the other. This case illustrates a clinical management framework based on characterization of the full hemodynamic phenotype, repeated reassessment, and treatment adaptation according to posture and time of day, integrating postural blood pressure (BP) responses, 24-hour BP monitoring, symptoms, functional status, comorbidities, and safety findings. Patient concerns A 63-year-old man with hypertension and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes presented with orthostatic dizziness and presyncope. Antihypertensive therapy was intensified for elevated seated BP. After intensification, upright tolerance worsened, with recurrent syncope, a rib fracture, and loss of functional independence. Symptoms remained disabling despite antihypertensive withdrawal and nonpharmacological measures. Diagnoses Supine-to-seated-to-standing assessment showed a BP fall from 197/99 mm Hg supine to 122/81 mm Hg seated and 79/56 mm Hg standing, with presyncope and heart rate increasing from 72 to 86 beats/min. Supine measurements and 24-hour BP monitoring documented severe supine and nocturnal hypertension, reverse dipping, and mean asleep BP 203/107 mm Hg. Autonomic testing demonstrated combined cardiovagal and adrenergic dysfunction, supporting neurogenic orthostatic hypotension due to diabetic autonomic neuropathy. Interventions Management was tailored to upright and recumbent periods. A removable transdermal nitroglycerin patch was used overnight. Nonpharmacological measures included repeated encouragement to increase fluid intake, but daily intake generally remained below 2 L. Clinical assessment suggested relative volume depletion. Low-dose morning fludrocortisone was introduced cautiously despite severe supine/nocturnal hypertension. After upright tolerance improved, morning lercanidipine was added. Subsequent 24-hour BP monitoring showed a more balanced profile. Outcomes Orthostatic symptoms and upright tolerance improved. No further syncope or falls occurred, and functional independence improved. Later 24-hour BP monitoring showed reduced nocturnal predominance, with mean awake/asleep BP 164/86 and 165/89 mm Hg, respectively. Mild peripheral edema was managed with intermittent torasemide. Lessons This case illustrates how integrating postural BP responses with 24-hour BP patterns can identify competing hemodynamic phenotypes that may require different management during upright and recumbent periods. Repeated reassessment and individualized treatment adaptation according to the documented BP pattern and clinical context may help balance competing risks of upright hypoperfusion and supine/nocturnal hypertension.

title: The robotic arm-assisted versus conventional total knee arthroplasty (RACER-Knee) trial : the question of value and where we go next.
authors: Clement ND, Metcalfe A, Davis ET, Haddad FS.

title: The relationship between sirtuin1 gene polymorphism and coronary heart disease: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Xing XY, Gong J, Song XY, Meng J, Chen JY, Lou DF.
abstract: Background This study systematically assesses the relationship between sirtuin (SIRT)1 gene polymorphisms rs4746720T > C, rs3818292G > A, rs7895833 A > G, and rs7069102C > G with the risk of coronary heart disease (CHD). Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched for literature examining the connection between SIRT1 gene polymorphism and CHD. The search time limit was from the establishment of the database to June 15, 2024. Stata 15.0 software was used for data analysis. Results A total of 9 articles were included (1839 cases in the case group and 1937 cases in the control group). Meta-analysis showed that the rs4746720 dominant model (TC + TT > CC) [odds ratio = 1.321, 95% confidence interval (1.032-1.692), P = .027] was nominally associated with an increased risk of CHD, although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted q = 0.176), whereas the rs7069102 dominant model (CC + CG > GG) [odds ratio = 0.278, 95% confidence interval (0.126-0.612), P = .001] was associated with a decreased risk of CHD and remained significant after correction (adjusted q = 0.013). However, the rs7069102C > G, rs7069102CC > GG, rs7069102 CG > GG, rs7069102CC > CG + GG, rs4746720T > C, rs4746720TC > TT, rs7895833 and rs3818292 gene polymorphisms were not associated with the risk of CHD. Conclusion The rs7069102 CC + CG genotype of SIRT1 may be associated with a reduced risk of CHD, whereas the association between the rs4746720 TC + TT genotype and CHD risk was only nominally significant and did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. However, limited by the quantity and quality of the included studies, the above conclusions need to be verified by more high-quality studies.

title: The effect of personal mastery on depression and anxiety in patients with psoriasis: The mediating role of social support and acceptance of illness.
authors: Yang YC, Li SJ, Zhang XG, Guo SB, Xue LL, Wei F, Ma XX, Bai YZ.
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic skin disease with heterogeneous manifestations and patients frequently experience comorbid depression and anxiety. The purpose of this study is to investigate the influencing factors of comorbid depression and anxiety in patients with psoriasis and analyze the interrelationships between these factors. The study employed a cross-sectional design with a sample size of 235. We used the general information questionnaire compiled by authors and 4 standardized psychometric scales: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Social Support Rate Scale, Acceptance of Illness Scale, and Personal Mastery Scale. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that personal mastery, social support, and acceptance of illness were the influencing factors of depression and anxiety in patients with psoriasis. In addition, these 3 factors are positively correlated with each other (P < .01). Mediation analysis indicated that personal mastery had a direct effect of -0.028 (95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.037 to -0.019) on depression and anxiety. The indirect effect mediated by social support and acceptance of illness were -0.009 (95% CI: -0.017 to -0.002) and -0.017 (95% CI: -0.025 to -0.010), respectively. The chain mediation effect involving both social support and acceptance of illness was -0.012 (95% CI: -0.018 to -0.007). Personal mastery, social support, and acceptance of illness can influence depression and anxiety in patients with psoriasis in direct or indirect ways, with social support and acceptance of illness acting as mediators between personal mastery and the levels of depression and anxiety.

title: The Effects of Force-Velocity Profile-Based Load Prescription on Muscle Power and Functional Performance in Velocity-Deficient Older Adults.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Deboutte J, Delecluse C, Thomis M, Van Roie E.
abstract: Muscle power is essential for functional capacity in older adults and can be improved through power-focused resistance training (PRT). PRT adaptations are load- and velocity-specific, yet optimal load prescription remains unclear. As force and velocity capacities vary between individuals, this 12-week intervention compared two force-velocity (F-V) profile-guided loading strategies: training at loads matched versus not matched to the F-V deficit. F-V profiles of 80 adults ≥ 65 years were assessed on a pneumatic leg press, with maximal force (F 0 ) and velocity (V 0 ) expressed as z-scores relative to a younger reference group (n = 60, 20-35 years). A difference ≥ 1 between z-scores was considered indicative of a deficit, with the direction determining a force- or velocity-deficit profile. As force deficits were rare (n = 4), the intervention only included participants with a velocity deficit (n = 59), of whom 57 initiated the intervention. Participants were randomly assigned to train at loads matched to their deficit (individualized; IND) or at loads deliberately not matched to their deficit (non-individualized; NON-IND). Maximal power, F-V profile parameters and functional performance were assessed at baseline, 6 and 12 weeks. From baseline to 12 weeks, F 0 increased more in NON-IND than IND (p = 0.040), while V 0 increased more in IND than NON-IND (p = 0.009). Changes in power and functional performance did not differ between groups (all p ≥ 0.065). In velocity-deficient older adults, differences in F-V-guided load prescription led to distinct F-V adaptations but did not lead to differences in power or functional performance. Trial Registration: The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06449716).

title: The CALLY index, a novel composite biomarker, is inversely associated with preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm): A nationally representative cross-sectional study.
authors: Ye Y, Zhao Y, Jin L, Zhang J, Jia Q, Bai W, Wang Y.
abstract: Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) is an intermediate pulmonary phenotype with heightened cardiometabolic risk. Effective tools for its identification are lacking. However, its relationship with systemic inflammatory-nutritional balance is underexplored. The CALLY index integrates C-reactive protein, albumin, and lymphocyte count. This composite biomarker reflects inflammatory-nutritional homeostasis. This study aimed to investigate the association between the ln(CALLY) index and PRISm in a nationally representative U.S. adult population. We analyzed data from 7296 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2007-2010. PRISm was defined as FEV1/FVC ≥ 0.7 with FEV1 < 80% predicted. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed the association between ln(CALLY) (as quartiles and per-standard-deviation increases) and PRISm, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic factors. Restricted cubic splines examined the dose-response relationship. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of findings. Among participants, 920 (12.6%) had PRISm. Compared to those with normal pulmonary function, PRISm individuals had significantly lower ln(CALLY) values (1.21 vs 1.77, P < .001). In fully adjusted models, higher ln(CALLY) quartiles had progressively lower PRISm odds: Q2 (OR = 0.71, 95% CI:0.57-0.88), Q3 (OR = 0.63, 0.47-0.84), and Q4 (OR = 0.48, 0.35-0.66) vs Q1 (P-trend < 0.001). Each standard deviation increase in ln(CALLY) reduced PRISm risk by 24% (OR = 0.76, 0.68-0.85). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a monotonic inverse linear dose-response relationship (P-overall < .001, P-nonlinear = .707). Subgroup analyses found stronger protective associations in women (P-interaction = .021) and significant heterogeneity across racial/ethnic groups (P-interaction = .036). Sensitivity analyses treating BMI continuously and using multiple imputation supported these findings. Higher ln(CALLY) is independently associated with lower PRISm prevalence in U.S. adults. Systemic inflammatory-nutritional status may be a modifiable risk factor for PRISm, supporting potential targeted prevention strategies. The CALLY index, derived from routine blood tests, could serve as a readily accessible tool for risk stratification of PRISm.

title: The Biomechanical Signature of Elite Distance Running: A Matched Pairs Analysis Across Multiple Speeds.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Mayo-Nieto C, Cartón-Llorente A, Rafales-Perucha A, Cardiel-Sánchez S, Jaén-Carrillo D, Roche-Seruendo LE.
abstract: This study compared the biomechanical profiles of elite and recreational distance runners across five measurement domains using wearable inertial sensors across treadmill speeds of 10-15 km/h. A total of 104 runners (52 elite; 52 recreational) were assessed using RunScribe sensors during an incremental treadmill protocol. Twenty-three variables spanning spatiotemporal parameters, stiffness and force, impact loading, foot kinematics and vertical dynamics were recorded at each speed. Elite runners were matched 1:1 with recreational runners by sex, age, height, and body mass. For each variable, a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) was fitted to within-pair differences with pair-level random intercepts and speed slopes, and speed and within-pair body mass and age imbalances as fixed effects. FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) was applied to the 23 group-effect and 23 interaction tests independently. Twelve of 23 variables (52.2%) showed a significant group effect, and six (26.1%) a significant group×speed interaction after FDR correction. Elite runners showed shorter contact time (d z = -0.73 to -0.53), higher flight ratio (d z = +0.52 to +0.66) and a more anterior footstrike pattern at initial contact (d z = +0.58 to +0.67). RunScribe-estimated vertical GRF rate and leg stiffness were also higher than in recreational runners (d z = +0.48 to +0.75, and + 0.51 to +0.62, respectively). Step frequency and step length showed no overall group difference. Significant group×speed interactions revealed that, for most affected variables, values changed more steeply with speed in recreational runners. These findings describe a distinct mechanical profile in elite runners across the six evaluated submaximal speeds.

title: The Association Between Oxidative Balance Score and All-Cause Mortality in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
authors: Jia J, Xiao G, Miao J, Zheng Y, Ding J, Zheng Z.
abstract: Background This study aimed to explore the associations of the oxidative balance score (OBS) and all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and to analyze the mediating role of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). Methods Data were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations of total OBS, dietary OBS, and lifestyle OBS with all-cause and CVD mortality. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to explore dose-response relationships, while subgroup analysis was conducted to verify the robustness of the results. Mediation analysis examined NLR-mediated association between OBS and all-cause mortality. Results 887 RA patients were analyzed, with 79 deaths during follow-up. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in total OBS, dietary OBS, and lifestyle OBS was associated with a 6%, 7%, and 25% lower risk of all-cause mortality, respectively. Total OBS was negatively associated with CVD mortality when analyzed as a continuous variable, but not when categorized into tertiles. RCS analysis confirmed linear dose-response relationships between total OBS, dietary OBS, lifestyle OBS, and all-cause mortality. NLR mediated a small proportion of the associations of total OBS (5.47%) and dietary OBS (4.89%) with all-cause mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the negative association between total OBS and all-cause mortality across several subgroups. Conclusion Higher total OBS, dietary OBS, and lifestyle OBS were significantly associated with reduced all-cause mortality in RA patients, with a linear dose-response relationship.

title: Temporal Effects on Intraoperative Bacterial Contamination of Surgical Gloves in Noninfection Orthopaedic Trauma Cases.
authors: Amirhekmat A, Shimabukuro J, Bittencourt C, Beyer RS, Learned JR, Scolaro JA, Lim PK.
abstract: Objectives Surgical site infections (SSIs) are among the most serious complications in orthopaedic trauma surgery, contributing to patient morbidity, mortality, and substantial financial costs. With direct inoculation from intraoperative bacterial contamination being a large contributor to these infections, the temporal dynamics of intraoperative bacterial colonization on surgical gloves in orthopaedic trauma cases was investigated. Methods Surgical glove bacterial cultures were taken by firmly pressing the operating room staff member's gloved fingertips onto a sheep's blood agar plate. Cases, without known preexisting infection, were chosen from a single level 1 trauma center at random between 2023 and 2025. Samples were obtained at 2 intraoperative time points: (1) immediately after draping and (2) after implant placement but before final irrigation. These samples were compared with negative controls of freshly donned, but unused sterile gloves. Glove imprints were then incubated for 2 weeks, and bacterial isolates were identified using MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Results Of 276 total gloves sampled, 70 (25.4% 70/138) demonstrated bacterial growth, compared with 0 controls (0%, 0/138 P Conclusions Intraoperative surgical gloves demonstrated high rates of bacterial contamination, particularly with longer procedure times. Routine glove changes after draping, after final implant placement, and after >75 minutes of operating time may be a simple, low-cost strategy to reduce potential SSI risk. Level of evidence Prognostic Level IV. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Technical Tricks to Improve Iliosacral Screw Safety Using Three-dimensional Computed Tomography Imaging.
authors: Zuelzer DA, Routt MLC.
abstract: Summary This technical note describes a method used to facilitate iliosacral screw fixation with three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography (CT) imaging. Preoperative pelvis CT scans were used to generate 3D reconstructions, which were then manipulated into inlet and outlet orientations. The inlet position for S1 was achieved when the anterior cortex of the S1 body became superimposed on itself; the outlet position was when the S1 nerve root tunnel was viewed en face. On the fluoroscopic inlet view of S1, multiple cortical densities were often visible and could be difficult to distinguish as S1 versus other sacral segments. 3D CT helped distinguish the position and shape of the anterior cortical limit of S1 by referencing preoperative 3D CT inlet images that were reproduced intraoperatively on fluoroscopy using the appearance of the anterior pelvic ring and the relative obliquity of the obturator foramen. This technique was especially valuable in the setting of common posterior pelvic anatomic variations-including asymmetry, degenerative osteophytes, severe sacral slope, and dramatic cortical recesses of the upper sacral segment. These variations were often difficult to anticipate with conventional plain film or standard CT imaging alone, underscoring the potential clinical utility of this technique.

title: Synchronous hepatocellular carcinoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma in a patient with chronic hepatitis B: A case report and literature review.
authors: Zhang S.
abstract: Rationale Synchronous double primary cancers involving hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) are exceptionally rare. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is an established cause of HCC, whereas Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is the major etiological factor for NPC. We report a patient with synchronous HCC and NPC and review the relevant literature. Patient concerns A 63-year-old Chinese man with chronic HBV presented with a liver mass detected on routine screening. He reported nasal obstruction. Diagnoses Contrast-enhanced imaging showed a 46 × 59 mm hepatic lesion with portal vein tumor thrombus and a 41 × 29 mm nasopharyngeal mass with bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Biopsies confirmed moderately differentiated HCC and EBV-associated non-keratinizing NPC. Final diagnoses were HCC Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer Stage C (CNLC IIIa, Child-Pugh A) and NPC T3N2M0 Stage III (AJCC 8th edition). Interventions He received hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC, mFOLFOX) combined with tislelizumab and donafenib; radiotherapy for NPC was deferred after shared decision-making. Entecavir was continued. Outcomes At 19-month follow-up, both tumors remained controlled; the NPC met radiographic complete response criteria. Lessons Synchronous HCC and EBV-associated NPC were controlled during treatment with a tislelizumab-containing multimodality regimen, and the NPC achieved a radiographic complete response. The contribution of each treatment component cannot be determined from a single case, and definitive radiotherapy remains the standard of care for locoregionally advanced NPC. Multidisciplinary management and close monitoring are essential.

title: Surgical management and short-term clinical and radiological outcomes in patients with cervical spondylodiscitis: A single-center retrospective study.
authors: Noh J, Lee S, Oh Y, Eun J.
abstract: Cervical spondylodiscitis (CSD) is a rare but increasingly prevalent spinal infection that may cause rapid neurological deterioration because of its nonspecific clinical presentation. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term clinical and radiological outcomes of surgically treated CSD and to explore whether the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-surgery interval was associated with postoperative neurological recovery. This retrospective single-center cohort study included 25 consecutive patients who underwent surgical management for CSD between January 2016 and December 2025. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the visual analogue scale and modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score. Radiological outcomes were evaluated by measuring the local cervical kyphosis angle. Patients were stratified according to the MRI-to-surgery interval (≤24 vs >24 hours). Surgical treatment significantly improved pain, neurological function, inflammatory markers, and cervical sagittal alignment. Mean visual analogue scale scores decreased from 6.0 to 3.4 (P 24 hours after MRI acquisition (P = .518); however, the timing analysis was limited by the small subgroup sizes and baseline differences in neurological status. Surgical management of CSD was associated with significant short-term clinical and radiological improvement. Although postoperative outcomes did not differ significantly according to the MRI-to-surgery interval, these findings should not be interpreted as supporting delayed surgery once surgical indications are established.

title: Surgical Complications in Patients With Morbid Obesity Undergoing Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Alotaibi AM.
abstract: Aim Few studies have compared surgical outcomes across different grades of obesity. We assessed the effect of severe obesity (SO) on operative time, intraoperative blood loss >100 mL and length of hospital stay (LOS) after laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC). Methods This retrospective cohort study included 1126 patients aged 14 years or older who underwent LC at Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital between January 2019 and December 2021. Patients were grouped according to the presence or absence of SO, defined as a body mass index (BMI) ≥40 kg/m 2 or ≥35 kg/m 2 in patients with obesity-related comorbidities. Demographic, clinical, operative, and postoperative data were compared between groups. Categorical variables were analyzed using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, while continuous variables were analyzed using either the independent Student's t -test or Mann-Whitney U test according to data distribution. Additional multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify whether SO was independently associated with operative time, intraoperative blood loss >100 mL, and LOS. Results Severe obesity was identified in 16.1% (181/1126) of patients. Patients with SO had significantly longer symptom duration and operative times than those without SO (4.00 (2.00-24.00) vs. 4.00 (2.00-12.00), p = 0.007; and 53.5 (39.75-75.5) vs. 48.0 (36.0-65.0) min, p = 0.004, respectively). The SO- group had significantly higher rates of endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) and biliary stenting, whereas the difference in obstructive jaundice was not statistically significant. Intraoperative blood loss >100 mL occurred more frequently in the SO+ group (3.3% vs. 0.5%, p = 0.004). LOS was also significantly longer among SO+ (2.0 (2.0-3.0) vs. 2.0 (2.0-3.0), p = 0.003). In multivariable linear regression analysis, SO remained independently associated with longer operative time (B = 7.48 minutes, 95% CI 2.54-12.42, p = 0.003). Multivariable logistic regression analysis also demonstrated that SO was independently associated with increased odds of intraoperative blood loss >100 mL (odds ratio [OR] = 30.79, 95% CI 5.07-187.03, p p = 0.149). Conclusions Patients with SO undergoing LC experienced longer operative times and higher rates of intraoperative blood loss >100 mL; however, severe obesity was not independently associated with prolonged hospital stay. Multivariable analyses demonstrated that SO remained independently associated with operative time and bleeding risk after adjustment for clinically relevant covariates. These findings suggest that SO is associated with longer operative time and an increased likelihood of intraoperative bleeding during LC, although its association with postoperative outcomes appears limited. Larger prospective studies are needed to further clarify the independent effects of SO on surgical outcomes.

title: Suprascapular nerve block with versus without ultrasound-guided T2 erector spinae plane block for chronic shoulder pain: A retrospective comparative study.
authors: Yu S, Nam S, Lee K, Kim JI, Kim J.
abstract: Suprascapular nerve block (SSNB) is widely used for chronic shoulder pain but may provide suboptimal analgesia because of incomplete coverage of the shoulder's sensory innervation. High thoracic (T2) erector spinae plane block (ESPB) provides broad craniocaudal spread and may complement SSNB. This study evaluated whether SSNB with T2 ESPB was associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with SSNB without T2 ESPB in patients with chronic, conservative-refractory shoulder pain. This retrospective comparative study included 84 adult patients with chronic shoulder pain lasting at least 3 months despite conservative treatment at a tertiary academic hospital. Patients underwent ultrasound-guided SSNB without T2 ESPB (n = 57) or SSNB with T2 ESPB (n = 27). The primary outcome was the proportion of responders, defined as achieving a ≥30% reduction in numeric rating scale (NRS) pain score at 4 weeks. Secondary outcomes included NRS pain score at 4 weeks, patient global impression of change (PGIC), and procedure-related adverse events. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to adjust for potential confounders. At 4 weeks, the responder rate was higher in the SSNB with T2 ESPB group than in the SSNB without T2 ESPB group (59.3% vs 17.5%, P < .001). The combined group also had a lower mean NRS pain score (3.9 ± 2.8 vs 5.2 ± 2.6, P = .049) and higher PGIC scores (median [IQR], 4 [4-5] vs 4 [3-4]; P = .010). In multivariable analysis, SSNB with T2 ESPB remained associated with a positive response (OR 5.931, 95% confidence interval: 2.01-17.50, P = .001). No procedure-related adverse events were identified. SSNB with T2 ESPB was associated with better short-term clinical outcomes than SSNB alone in patients with chronic shoulder pain. Prospective randomized, dose-matched studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify the specific contribution of T2 ESPB.

title: Supervised physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises provide limited additional benefit at 24 months in braced adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis: a randomized trial.
authors: Zhang X, Liang M, Huang Y, Lin B, Lin Y, Yang Y, Wang X, Huang X, Liao B.
abstract: Aims Physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE) are used as an adjunct to bracing in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), although evidence for their long-term benefit remains limited. This randomized trial assessed whether supervised PSSE provide clinically important radiological and patient-reported benefits compared with self-directed exercise in patients with AIS undergoing brace treatment. Methods Patients with AIS (major Cobb angle 25° to 45°; Risser grade 0 to 2) were recruited from a tertiary scoliosis centre between December 2018 and December 2022. Patients were randomized to supervised Schroth-based PSSE, consisting of physiotherapist-led sessions plus daily home exercises, or to self-directed general exercise. The co-primary outcomes were change in major Cobb angle and change in health-related quality of life measured using the Chinese Brace Questionnaire-34. A 5° between-group difference in Cobb angle was prespecified as the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). To provide a clinically anchored interpretation, 24-month radiological outcomes were classified as improved (> 5° decrease), stable (-5° to +5°), or worsened (> 5° increase), and compared using adjusted ordinal logistic regression in intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) analyses. Results Supervised PSSE resulted in a greater reduction in major Cobb angle than self-directed exercise at 24 months (adjusted between-group difference -3.23° (95% CI -3.51 to -2.96); p Conclusion Supervised PSSE provided a statistically significant but clinically modest radiological benefit over self-directed exercise. This did not translate into a higher likelihood of clinically meaningful radiological improvement. No sustained clinically meaningful quality-of-life benefit was shown.

title: Sufficient dietary iron intake is associated with lower all-cause mortality in elderly individuals with autoimmune thyroiditis but not in those without: A population-based study.
authors: Hu T.
abstract: This study evaluates the relationship between dietary iron intake and all-cause mortality in elderly individuals with autoimmune thyroiditis (AT). Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2007-2012) included 2578 participants aged ≥60 years, of whom 464 had AT. Dietary iron intake was assessed by two 24-hour recalls and categorized into tertiles. Mortality data came from the National Death Index. Associations were examined using Cox regression and restricted cubic splines, adjusting for demographics, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Higher dietary iron intake was inversely associated with mortality in elderly AT patients. Each 1-log2 increase in iron intake reduced mortality risk by 24% (hazard ratio = 0.762; 95% confidence interval = 0.633-0.918; P = .004). Adjusted hazard ratios for the second and third tertiles were 0.671 and 0.522, respectively. No significant association was found in participants without AT (P = .057). A nonlinear threshold effect was observed (P = .002), with a cutoff of 13.2 mg/day - above which no additional mortality benefit was seen. Sufficient dietary iron intake lowers all‑cause mortality risk in elderly AT patients, following a nonlinear pattern with a threshold around 13.2 mg/day. This association was not significant in individuals without AT.

title: Successful management of arrow‑rebound‑induced transcervical penetrating trauma with major vascular and pharyngolaryngeal injuries: A case report.
authors: Fei Y, Chen Z, Chai S, He Y, Zhou B.
abstract: Rationale Penetrating neck injury involving major vessels is highly lethal. Long-trajectory transcervical penetration caused by rebounding arrows is exceptionally rare in civilians, posing significant diagnostic and management challenges. Patient concerns A man in his early 50s presented to the emergency department approximately 2 hours after an arrow, rebounding from a nearby training target, penetrated his neck (entering above the left mandible, exiting on the right). He was conscious with minimal external bleeding but copious oropharyngeal secretions. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed the arrow traversing the hyoid bone and oropharynx, abutting the right common carotid artery (CCA) and compressing the right internal jugular vein (IJV). Diagnoses Open neck injury; combined right CCA and IJV injury; hemorrhagic shock; pharyngolaryngeal trauma without aerodigestive perforation; and pulmonary infection with consolidation. Interventions Initial stabilization included arrow shaft shortening by firefighters. Emergency exploration under general anesthesia involved tracheotomy, cervical exploration, primary repair of the right IJV and CCA, and foreign body removal. Postoperative management in the intensive care unit included damage-control resuscitation (transfusion of 7.0 U packed red blood cells, 1100 mL plasma, and 10.5 U cryoprecipitate), antimicrobial therapy (cefuroxime, guided by cultures showing Staphylococcus epidermidis), early individualized anticoagulation (enoxaparin transitioned to rivaroxaban), and systematic correction of coagulopathy and electrolyte disturbances. Outcomes The patient was discharged on postoperative day 12 with healed wounds. Follow-up at 1, 3, 6.5 months, 1, 2, and nearly 3 years showed intact neurological function. Imaging confirmed stable right IJV occlusion. Anticoagulation was discontinued at 1 month without subsequent bleeding or thromboembolism. Although long-term imaging was limited to a 6.5-month non-contrast computed tomography, the patient remained asymptomatic without signs of venous hypertension or neurological deficits throughout the follow-up period. Lessons High-quality preoperative computed tomography angiography with 3D reconstruction is critical for defining the relationship between the foreign body and vital structures. In selected patients, early individualized anticoagulation after excluding active bleeding may mitigate venous thrombosis. Systematic intensive care unit management of coagulopathy, electrolytes, and pulmonary complications is pivotal for survival.

title: Sports-medical integration research (2020-2024): A bibliometric and visual comparative analysis of Chinese and International hotspots and trends.
authors: Wu T, Yang L, Yang Y, Duan X, Li J, Wang X, Guo Y, Sun L, Jiang J, Wang S.
abstract: Objective Sports-medical integration (SMI) is a critical strategy for implementing the Healthy China Initiative and promoting public health globally. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of Chinese and international SMI research from 2020 to 2024, identifying hotspots and trends to provide evidence-based references for researchers and policymakers. Methods A bibliometric analysis was performed using CiteSpace 7.0.R0 on literature retrieved from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure and the Web of Science Core Collection. Chinese SMI literature was identified using direct policy terminology (""), while international literature was captured using clinically oriented constructs (exercise prescription, integrated care, Exercise is Medicine). After screening, 979 Chinese articles were retained, and a complete dataset of 2791 international publications was used for analysis. Co-occurrence analysis, clustering, burst detection, collaboration network mapping, and co-citation analysis were employed. Results International SMI publications increased from 447 in 2020 to 642 in 2022, stabilizing at 564 in 2024. The top 3 institutions were the University of Sydney (80 publications), Harvard University (71), and the University of Toronto (64). Keyword analysis revealed "physical activity" (frequency 1547, centrality 0.21) as the dominant international research theme. Clustering analysis identified 16 major research clusters (Q = 0.8211, S = 0.8742). Author co-citation analysis identified foundational scholars such as Michie S and Braun V. Chinese keyword analysis revealed dominant themes of "Integration of sports and medicine" (frequency 561), "Healthy China" (176), and "Combination of physical exercise and medical treatment" (99). Chinese institutional collaboration networks exhibited significantly lower density than international networks (0.0066 vs 0.0523; bootstrapped 95% CI for the difference 0.038-0.053, effect size r = = 0.82). Conclusion International SMI research is characterized by strong institutional networks, well-established foundational scholarship, and a robust clinical evidence base. Chinese research, while growing rapidly, remains predominantly policy-driven and institutionally fragmented. These divergent patterns appear to reflect distinct disciplinary structures, funding mechanisms, and healthcare system configurations. The findings highlight opportunities for cross-cultural collaboration in exercise prescription, digital health integration, and implementation science, with specific implications for policy interventions such as joint funding mechanisms and the establishment of clinical exercise physiology as a recognized discipline in China.

title: Single Antibiotic Use With Ceftriaxone for Prophylaxis of All Open Fractures.
authors: Koulopoulos MW, Buseck A, Lynch CP, Lutz K, Brand O, Sommers E, Pompo I, Laychur A, Vaughn J, Mann K, Sullivan MP.
abstract: Objectives To compare outcomes for open fractures treated with a prophylactic antibiotic protocol using ceftriaxone (CTX) for all open fractures, referred to as group "CTX," versus a previous protocol using cefazolin for Gustilo I/II fractures and cefazolin plus gentamicin or CTX monotherapy for Gustilo type III fractures only, referred to as group "Classic." Methods . Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria This study included adult patients undergoing surgery for an open fracture from December 2016 to December 2022 with a minimum follow-up of 3 months. Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome of deep infection and secondary outcomes of superficial infection rates, nonunion rate, and time to antibiotic administration were compared between overall groups and subgroups based on Gustilo type. Results A total of 521 patients were included. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups, with no differences in age (CTX 41.1 ± 19.7 vs. classic 39.5 ± 19.3), sex (68.5% vs. 72.0% male), or comorbidities ( P > 0.05). There were no differences in deep infection (7.8% vs. 12.7%, P = 0.095), superficial infection (7.0% vs. 4.7%, P = 0.427), or nonunion (10.3% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.500) between CTX and Classic groups for all Gustilo types. Similarly for only type I/II fractures, rates of deep infection (3.5% vs. 8.9%, P = 0.145), superficial infection (2.9% vs. 3.6%, P = 0.683), and nonunion (3.6% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.340) did not differ. Noninferiority of CTX for deep infection was demonstrated for all Gustilo types (intergroup difference -0.048, P = 0.027) and type I/II fractures (-0.054, P = 0.035). The CTX protocol was associated with shorter time to antibiotic administration (63.9 ± 116.9 vs. 114.1 ± 199.0 minutes, P = 0.002). Conclusions The use of CTX for prophylaxis of all open fractures, regardless of Gustilo type, was associated with noninferior outcomes in deep infection as well as shorter time to antibiotic administration, compared with a regimen where type I/II fractures received cefazolin. No significant differences in rates of superficial infection or nonunion were noted after transition to CTX protocol. The study was notably underpowered to detect a difference in the primary outcome of deep infection. Prophylaxis of all open fractures with CTX may be a safe and effective method of standardizing and expediting care for orthopaedic trauma patients. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Role of metabolites in mediating the effect of lipidomes on osteoporosis: A Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Gao W, Lv H, Zhou Y, Chu Q, Wang Y, Hu Z, Wang J, Jiang T.
abstract: We investigated the causal relationships between the plasma lipidomes, osteoporosis (OP), and potential metabolite mediators using Mendelian randomization (MR). Using summary-level data from a genome-wide association study, bidirectional MR analyses to explore the causal relationships between the plasma lipidomes and OP, and two-step MR to discover potential mediating metabolites. Sensitivity analyses were performed to validate the robustness of the results further. After primary analysis and a series of sensitivity analyses, 7 inflammation-related proteins were identified that have a causal relationship with OP. Ceramide (d40:1) levels (odds ratio [OR] = 0.923; 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.854-0.999; P = .046 < .05), phosphatidylcholine (16:0_18:2) levels (OR = 0.932; 95% CI: 0.883-0.985; P = .012 < .05), phosphatidylc holine (16:1_18:2) levels (OR = 0.939; 95% CI: 0.882-0.999; P = .047 < .05), triacylglycerol (48:3) levels (OR = 0.920; 95% CI: 0.854-0.971; P = .027 < .05), and triacylglycerol (51:4) levels (OR = 0.914; 95% CI: 0.840-0.995; P = .038 < .05) were negatively associated with OP, whereas phosphatidylcholine (O-17:0_15:0) levels (OR = 1.121; 95% CI: 1.019-1.233; P = .019 < .05), and triacylglycerol (48:0) levels (OR = 1.130; 95% CI: 1.042-1.226; P = .003 < .05) were positively associated with OP. Subsequently, we conducted a two-step MR to discover potential mediating metabolites.
