This study found that 14 plasma metabolites may play a mediating role in the relationship between plasma lipidomes and OP, such as 5alpha-androstan-3alpha,17beta-diol monosulfate (1) levels, N6-methyllysine levels, 5-oxoproline levels, 2-hydroxyhippurate levels, glycosyl ceramide (d18:1/20:0, d16:1/22:0) levels, spermidine to 5-methylthioadenosine ratio, serine levels, phosphate to serine ratio, proline to trans-4-hydroxyproline ratio, 1-palmitoyl-GPC (16:0) levels, 7-methylxanthine levels, arachidonoylcholine levels, and spermidine to choline ratio. In conclusion, our study identified a causal relationship between plasma lipidomes and OP, with a proportion of the effect mediated by plasma metabolites.

title: Risk factors and morbidity characteristics of surgical site infection following ankle fracture ORIF: A comprehensive analysis.
authors: Zhao C, Fan X, Pang C.
abstract: This study aimed to describe the incidence and microbiological characteristics of surgical site infection (SSI) after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of ankle fractures and identify clinical factors associated with SSI. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 248 patients who underwent ankle fracture ORIF between January and December 2023. SSI occurring within 30 postoperative days was identified from available inpatient and postoperative medical records. Demographic, injury-related, laboratory, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with and without SSI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with SSI. SSI occurred in 32 of 248 patients (12.9%), including 25 superficial and 7 deep infections. Cultured organisms included Escherichia coli (n = 10), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 7), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 6), Enterobacter cloacae (n = 5), and Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 4). In multivariable analysis, open fracture, wound class II-III, and neutrophil percentage > 75% were associated with SSI. Age and body mass index (BMI) also showed positive associations, although the precise unit-specific effect sizes could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived statistical analysis; these comparatively large per-unit estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of SSI events and potential residual confounding. SSI occurred in 12.9% of this single-center ankle fracture cohort. Older age and higher BMI showed associations with SSI, together with open fracture, less-clean operative wounds, and neutrophilia. The magnitude of the age- and BMI-related effects should be interpreted cautiously because their original regression scaling could not be independently reconstructed.

title: Risk Factors for Failure of Internal Fixation in Postmenopausal Patients With Osteoporotic Intertrochanteric Fractures.
authors: Yu Y, Zhao S, Li H, Jiang Z, Liang Y, Wang S.
abstract: Aim To identify independent risk factors for internal fixation failure after intramedullary nail fixation in postmenopausal patients with osteoporotic intertrochanteric fractures, and to develop and internally validate a predictive model for risk assessment. Methods The clinical data of 360 postmenopausal patients with osteoporotic intertrochanteric fractures admitted to The Second Affiliated Hospital of Liaoning University of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2021 to May 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. The patients were divided into the failure group ( n = 65) and the success group ( n = 295) according to whether internal fixation failure occurred within 6 months after the operation. General data, bone metabolism indices, imaging parameters, and surgery-related factors were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to screen the independent risk factors of internal fixation failure. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to evaluate the model's discriminative ability, while the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and bootstrap resampling calibration curve were used to evaluate calibration. Decision curve analysis was used to assess the clinical utility of the model. Results The failure rate of internal fixation was 18.06% (65/360). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that the quality of fracture reduction was poor (odds ratio (OR) = 3.07, 95% CI: 1.60-5.87, p p = 0.02) was identified as an independent risk factor for internal fixation failure, whereas bone mineral density (BMD) T-score (OR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.06-0.47, p p p p = 0.28), and the calibration curve closely aligned with the ideal line. Decision curve analysis showed that the model had significant net clinical benefit within a wide threshold probability range. Conclusions Poor quality of fracture reduction, the position of the intramedullary nail deviated from the center of the medullary cavity, lower bone mineral density, lower femoral cortical thickness index, and smaller lateral wall thickness are independent risk factors for the failure of internal fixation after intramedullary nail fixation in postmenopausal women with osteoporotic intertrochanteric fractures. The predictive model based on these factors demonstrates good discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Clinicians should pay close attention to the identified risk factors, thoroughly evaluate preoperative bone quality, achieve anatomical reduction, and ensure optimal positioning of the main nail during operation to reduce the risk of internal fixation failure and improve patient outcomes.

title: Risk Factors for Bone Cement Leakage and Re-fracture Following PKP in Patients With Thoracolumbar Spine Fractures.
authors: Li X, Fu M, Liu X, E Z, Wang C.
abstract: Aim Thoracolumbar spine fractures are commonly treated with percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP), but bone cement leakage and re-fracture remain major concerns. Identifying their risk factors is essential for improving prognosis but remains insufficiently characterized. This study was designed to explore the risk factors for bone cement leakage and re-fracture following PKP in patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 115 patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures who underwent PKP at Heilongjiang Provincial Hospital between April 2022 and February 2025 (leakage group: 18 patients with bone cement leakage; non-leakage group: 97 patients without leakage). Risk factors for bone cement leakage were analyzed. Patients were divided into re-fracture (29 cases with re-fractures) and non-re-fracture (86 cases without re-fractures) groups to identify risk factors for postoperative re-fracture. Results Logistic multivariate regression analysis identified age and vertebral wall destruction as independent risk factors for postoperative bone cement leakage ( p p Conclusions Age and vertebral wall destruction are independent predictors of cement leakage, and together with compression severity, also predict re-fracture. These findings support routine preoperative assessment of vertebral wall integrity using high-resolution computed tomography (CT), particularly in elderly patients, as vertebral wall destruction was independently associated with bone cement leakage.

title: Risk Factors and Development of a Prediction Model for Unplanned Reoperation Within 30 Days After Skin Flap Repair in Patients With Basal Cell Carcinoma.
authors: Lai M, Zhang X, Jiang Y.
abstract: Background Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common malignant skin tumor worldwide. Unplanned reoperation may occur after local flap repair, increasing patient suffering and medical burden. At present, evidence regarding the risk factors for and prediction models of unplanned reoperation after flap repair for BCC remains insufficient. The aim of this study was to explore the influencing factors associated with unplanned reoperation after flap repair for BCC and to construct a prediction model, thereby providing a basis for clinical risk assessment and individualized treatment. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 455 patients with BCC who underwent local flap repair at Jiangnan University Medical Center from January 2020 to December 2025 were enrolled. The patients were divided into a reoperation group (45 cases, 9.9%) and a non-reoperation group (410 cases, 90.1%) according to whether unplanned reoperation occurred within 30 days after surgery. Demographic characteristics, tumor-related characteristics, and surgery-related characteristics were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify independent influencing factors, and a prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical utility of the model. Model performance was internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resampling iterations. Results Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that preoperative fasting glucose, infiltration depth, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII; per 10-unit increase), and flap aspect ratio were independent influencing factors for unplanned reoperation. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.852 (95% CI: 0.792-0.912), with a sensitivity of 0.80 and a specificity of 0.79 at the optimal cut-off value. The calibration curve (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p = 0.17) and decision curve analysis showed that the model had a good fit and provided a net clinical benefit. Internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resampling iterations yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.841. Conclusions Preoperative fasting glucose, infiltration depth, SII, and flap aspect ratio are independent risk factors for unplanned reoperation after BCC flap repair. The prediction model based on these variables demonstrated good discrimination and calibration in this single-center cohort, with potential clinical utility. Further external validation is needed before its application in clinical decision-making. However, as this study focused solely on reoperations occurring within the 30-day postoperative period, late reoperations due to positive margins or residual tumors beyond this period were not captured. Studies with extended follow-up are warranted to comprehensively assess the full spectrum of reoperation risk.

title: Risk Assessment for Reoperation After Surgery for Lumbar Degenerative Disease Based on Preoperative Clinical Characteristics and Imaging Parameters: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Jiang J, Xu L, Zhou L, Xiong J, Tao Z.
abstract: Aim To explore the relevant clinical and radiological risk factors for reoperation in patients with lumbar degenerative diseases, and to inform preoperative risk stratification. Methods This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. A total of 653 patients with lumbar degenerative diseases who underwent initial surgical treatment at Nanchang Hongdu Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine Affiliated to Jiangxi University of Chinese Medicine between June 2018 and June 2022 were included. All patients completed a 36-month follow-up. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, perioperative parameters, and preoperative imaging parameters were collected, including the degree of intervertebral disc degeneration (Pfirrmann classification), the degree of paraspinal muscle fat infiltration (Goutallier classification), facet joint effusion distribution, and facet joint angles. Patients were divided into a reoperation group (n = 41) and a non-reoperation group (n = 612) based on whether they underwent reoperation for complications related to the index surgical segment during the follow-up period. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent factors associated with postoperative reoperation, and their discriminative ability was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results The reoperation rate within 36 months postoperatively was 6.28% (41/653). Final multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that age (Odds Ratio [OR] = 1.11, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 1.06~1.15, p p p = 0.004) were independent risk factors for reoperation. Compared with patients with bilateral effusion or synovial cysts, patients with unilateral effusion had a significantly lower risk of reoperation (OR = 0.03, 95% CI 0.00~0.23, p Conclusions Age, preoperative pain level, intervertebral disc degeneration grade, and facet joint effusion status (bilateral effusion or synovial cyst vs. unilateral effusion) may be closely related to the risk of reoperation after lumbar degenerative disease surgery. Patients with these characteristics should be thoroughly evaluated preoperatively to inform the development of individualized treatment strategies.

title: Resection and Individualized Chest Wall Reconstruction for Sternal Osteochondroma Complicated by Superficial Postoperative Wound Infection: A Case Report.
authors: Wei X, Wang C, Li B, Jiang P, Men Y.
abstract: Aim Sternal resection for sternal tumors may result in complex, full-thickness anterior chest wall defects. Chest wall reconstruction in this setting remains surgically challenging, with postoperative wound infection and prosthesis exposure representing common and troublesome complications. This case report aimed to describe a multidisciplinary reconstructive strategy and the long-term clinical outcome of a patient with a complex sternal defect. Case presentation A 48-year-old female patient with locally aggressive benign sternal osteochondroma underwent extended en bloc sternal tumor resection, resulting in a 10 × 12 cm chest wall defect. She underwent combined reconstruction using titanium mesh fixation, an omental flap, and bilateral pectoralis major muscle advancement flaps. Superficial wound infection with methicillin-resistant staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) occurred on postoperative day 14 without deep prosthesis infection. Results The patient was treated with thorough debridement, standardized vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) therapy, and targeted antibacterial treatment with linezolid. The wound infection was completely controlled, microbiological sampling from the prosthesis interface remained negative, and secondary flap repair achieved complete wound healing. During more than four years of clinical follow-up, no prosthesis removal, tumor recurrence, or severe complications were reported, and thoracic wall function remained intact. Conclusions Multidisciplinary collaboration between thoracic surgery, plastic surgery, and oncology teams may be beneficial for complex sternal tumor resection and reconstruction. In this case, the integrated strategy combining rigid titanium mesh skeletal support, dual-flap soft-tissue reconstruction, and VAC wound care was associated with successful wound healing and prosthesis preservation despite postoperative superficial wound infection, suggesting its potential feasibility in selected patients.

title: Reproducibility of Two Novel Bone Defect Classification Systems.
authors: Campbell ST, Campbell ST, Agel J, Levack AE, Bernstein M, Wallace SJ, Meinberg E, Quinnan S, Hernandez-Irizarry R, Saiz AM, Crist BD, Marmor M, Shymon SJ, Lee P, Githens MF, Marecek GS, Orthopaedic Trauma Association.
abstract: Objectives To determine the reproducibility of 2 novel bone defect classification systems, the Tetsworth classification system and the universal long bone defect (ULBD) classification system. Methods Two independent reproducibility studies were undertaken. A series of cases with bone defects was collected and sent to a panel of orthopaedic surgeons who were members of the OTA or Limb Lengthening and Reconstruction Society who routinely manage bone defects. The surgeons were provided with a measurement calibration scale for defect length assessment. Analysis of reproducibility was performed using a Fleiss multirater kappa model, where a Fleiss kappa of 0 indicated agreement no better than random chance, and 1 indicated perfect agreement. Surgeons also rated their confidence in their rating from 1 to 3, with 3 as "very confident." Results For the Tetsworth classification, the Fleiss kappa was 0.264 for the overall classification system (fair agreement) (95% CI, 0.224-0.305). The kappa for the D1, D2, D3 part of the code related to defect completeness (incomplete, subcritical, or critical) was 0.557 (moderate agreement) (95% CI, 0.446-0.648). The kappa for the A, B, C part of the code related to defect shape was 0.402 (moderate agreement) (95% CI, 0.323-0.480). The mean confidence for all cases was 2.46 (range, 1.86-3). For the ULBD classification, the Fleiss kappa for the entire classification was 0.133 (slight agreement) (95% CI, 0.123-0.144). The kappa for the location and segment was 0.568 (moderate agreement) (95% CI, 0.526-0.610). The kappa for the morphology component was 0.124 (slight agreement) (95% CI, 0.114-0.135). The mean confidence for all cases was 2.0 (range, 1.0-3.0). Conclusions The bone defect classification system proposed by Tetsworth et al was reproducible by surgeons familiar with bone defects. The system can be considered for future research use. The ULBD classification system had low overall reproducibility. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Relationship between corneal cutting ratio and early postoperative Q values and higher-order aberrations after small incision lenticule extraction in myopic patients.
authors: Wang Z, Dong W, Zhang Q, Chen G.
abstract: This study investigates the association between the corneal cutting ratio and early postoperative corneal Q values and higher-order aberrations (HOAs) after small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) in myopic patients. A total of 149 patients (288 eyes) with refractive errors who underwent SMILE in our hospital from January 2017 to December 2021 were included. Both eyes were included when they met the eligibility criteria; therefore, the eye was used as the unit of analysis. According to the cutting ratio (corneal cutting depth/preoperative corneal thickness), eyes were divided into the ≤0.16 group (n = 96) and >0.16 group (n = 192). Preoperative and 1-month postoperative uncorrected visual acuity (UCVA), best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), corneal HOAs, and corneal Q values were compared. Pearson correlation analysis was used to assess the associations between cutting ratio and corneal optical parameters. There were no significant differences in baseline refractive parameters or preoperative BCVA, total HOAs, and corneal Q values between the 2 groups (all P > .05), and no significant differences in postoperative UCVA or BCVA (P > .05). The >0.16 group had significantly higher total HOAs and corneal Q values at 1 month than the ≤0.16 group (P < .05). The cutting ratio was positively correlated with total HOAs and corneal Q values (R = 0.462 and 0.432, respectively; both P < .001). At 1 month after SMILE, a higher cutting ratio was associated with higher corneal Q values and HOAs. Because bilateral eyes from some patients were included and follow-up was limited to 1 month, these findings should be interpreted as early postoperative associations rather than evidence of a long-term visual-quality outcome.

title: Quantitative evaluation of muscle relaxation efficacy of moving cupping therapy for chronic low back pain by shear wave elastography: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Kim Y, Park YC, Seo BK, Kim J, Lee T, Jeon SR, Kim Y, Hong Y, Kim E, Yang GY, Baek YH.
abstract: Background Moving cupping is used to reduce pain and muscle tension in chronic low back pain (CLBP), but its effect on paraspinal muscle stiffness has not been compared with that of a sham procedure. We evaluated it using shear wave elastography (SWE). Methods In this single-center, sham-controlled randomized trial, 68 adults with CLBP were assigned 1:1 by computer-generated simple randomization to moving cupping or sham cupping (four sessions over 2 weeks; 18-20 kPa vs 0 kPa). The 66 participants who received the allocated intervention had a mean age of 37.8 ± 9.0 years, and 71.2% were female. Assessors and the analyst were blinded. The primary endpoint was the change in multifidus shear modulus from baseline to the end of treatment; secondary outcomes included shear modulus at 1-week follow-up, pain intensity, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), EQ-5D-5L, and Patient Global Assessment. Intention-to-treat analyses used linear mixed-effects models; a per-protocol mixed 2-way analysis of variance served as a sensitivity analysis. Results A significant group × time interaction was observed for shear modulus (P Conclusions Two weeks of moving cupping reduced multifidus stiffness more than sham cupping, and the difference persisted 1 week after treatment. Pain decreased more with moving cupping, although the between-group difference was small, and there were no significant effects on disability or quality of life. Moving cupping may reduce paraspinal muscle stiffness but is not an established treatment for the broader symptom burden of CLBP.

title: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma with METex14 mutation and high PD-L1: A case report.
authors: Qin J, Xiong Z.
abstract: Rationale Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is a rare and aggressive subtype of lung cancer, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Cases of PSC harboring both MET exon 14 skipping (METex14) mutation and high PD-L1 expression are rarely documented, and reports detailing multimodal treatment involving surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy in such patients are even scarcer. Patient concerns A 54-year-old man presented with a persistent cough for over half a month. He was previously healthy. Physical examination revealed diminished breath sounds in the right upper lung. Diagnoses Initial bronchoscopic biopsy suggested inflammation, and computed tomography (CT)-guided lung biopsy showed atypical giant cells but was inconclusive. Following multidisciplinary team discussion, the patient underwent surgical resection. Postoperative pathology confirmed pleomorphic carcinoma (sarcomatoid carcinoma). Subsequent genetic testing identified a METex14 mutation with high PD-L1 expression (Tumor Proportion Score ≥ 50%). The final diagnosis was stage IIIB (T4N2M0) right PSC, MET-positive, PD-L1-positive. Interventions The initial treatment plan included 1 cycle of toripalimab (an anti-PD-1 antibody) combined with docetaxel and lobaplatin chemotherapy. This was subsequently adjusted to boretinib (a MET inhibitor) targeted therapy combined with docetaxel and lobaplatin chemotherapy. Outcomes The patient achieved and maintained a partial response (PR) for over 6 months of follow-up. Symptoms including cough resolved, and his general condition remained good with satisfactory appetite and sleep. Lessons This case underscores the diagnostic difficulty of PSC, which is prone to misdiagnosis and exhibits rapid growth. Surgery may not be appropriate for unresectable stage IIIB PSC. Gene sequencing and PD-L1 testing are crucial as they expand therapeutic options for PSC patients. The optimal first-line therapy (targeted vs immunotherapy) for PSC with concurrent MET mutation and high PD-L1 expression remains undefined, warranting further exploration of combination strategies.

title: Prognostic value of anti-gp210 antibodies in primary biliary cholangitis: A Systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Zhang Y, Jin Y, Wang M, Pan K, Xu A.
abstract: Background Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by portal inflammation and immune-mediated nonsuppurative destructive cholangitis. Recent studies have shown that anti-gp210 antibodies are associated with the prognosis of PBC. Here, we conducted a pooled analysis of the relationship between anti-gp210 antibodies and the prognosis of PBC patients to identify high-risk patients early and provide individualized interventions. Methods PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases were searched until January 2025. A meta-analysis was undertaken using a fixed-effects model and 95% confidence interval (CI) when no statistically significant heterogeneity existed; otherwise, a random-effects statistical model was used. Results A total of 12 records were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. The results of our meta-analysis showed that anti-gp210 positive PBC patients had a higher incidence of liver failure (relative risk (RR), 6.11; 95% CI, 3.16-11.81) and mortality (RR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.55-2.37) and a lower ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) response rate (RR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73-0.89) compared with anti-gp210 negative patients. Moreover, the presence of anti-gp210 antibodies was independently associated with a poor prognosis in patients with PBC (hazard ratios (HR), 4.53; 95% CI, 2.83-7.26). In addition, anti-gp210 positive PBC patients had higher serum gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT) (mean difference (MD), 53.03; 95% CI, 3.70-102.36), immunoglobulin M (IgM) (MD, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.80-1.78), and immunoglobulin G (IgG) (MD, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.07-2.06) levels and lower albumin (MD, -1.74; 95% CI, -2.80 to - 0.69) levels. Conclusion In conclusion, PBC patients with positive anti-gp210 have a worse prognosis than those with negative anti-gp210. Incorporating anti-gp210 testing into clinical practice could enhance risk stratification and guide personalized management, ultimately improving outcomes for this vulnerable population.

title: Prognostic impact of positive peritoneal washing cytology in surgically treated cervical cancer.
authors: Zhang Q, Li X, Wang Q, Lin Z, Wang T.
abstract: Positive peritoneal washing cytology is an uncommon but potentially clinically relevant finding in cervical cancer. This retrospective cohort study evaluated its association with recurrence, survival, and metastasis-related biomarkers in patients undergoing open surgery for cervical cancer between 2018 and 2023. A total of 120 patients were classified as peritoneal washing cytology-positive (n = 32) or cytology-negative (n = 88). Baseline clinicopathological characteristics were broadly comparable between groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated poorer survival among patients with positive cytology. The estimated 5-year overall survival was 43.7% (95% CI, 26.8-59.4%) in the cytology-positive group and 67.9% (95% CI, 55.2-77.8%) in the cytology-negative group, whereas the corresponding 5-year progression-free survival estimates were 36.5% (95% CI, 20.5-52.6%) and 62.4% (95% CI, 49.8-72.8%), respectively. Recurrence was more frequent among cytology-positive patients, particularly distant-organ recurrence. Serum VEGF and tissue MMP-9 levels were higher in the cytology-positive group. In multivariable analysis, positive peritoneal washing cytology remained associated with poorer overall survival after adjustment for selected clinicopathological variables. A combined VEGF/MMP-9 model showed exploratory discrimination for lymph-node metastasis, although the model requires internal and external validation. These findings suggest that positive peritoneal washing cytology may identify a subgroup with adverse outcomes after surgery, but prospective and externally validated studies are required before clinical application.

title: Primary splenic angiosarcoma initially diagnosed as littoral cell angioma: A case report of a diagnostic pitfall.
authors: Yu Y, Zhang H, Zhang G, Xu L.
abstract: Rationale Primary splenic angiosarcoma (PSAn) is a rare and aggressive vascular malignancy that poses diagnostic challenges because of its overlapping morphological and immunohistochemical features with benign splenic vascular tumors. Patient concerns A 71-year-old woman presented with left upper abdominal pain, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and a splenic lesion. Splenectomy and excision of a separate 1-cm hepatic nodule were performed, with initial pathological diagnoses of splenic littoral cell angioma and hepatic cavernous hemangioma. Persistent postoperative fever, progressive cytopenias, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction, and newly developed diffuse multifocal hepatic lesions subsequently occurred. Diagnoses Pathological reevaluation of the splenic specimen using an expanded immunohistochemical panel resulted in a revised diagnosis of PSAn. The subsequently developed diffuse hepatic lesions were considered highly suspicious for hepatic metastases based on the radiological and clinical findings, although histological confirmation was unavailable. Interventions The patient underwent splenectomy and excision of the initial hepatic nodule. Multidisciplinary reassessment and pathological reevaluation were performed following clinical deterioration. The patient declined liver biopsy and further oncological treatment. Outcomes Despite supportive management, the patient's condition progressively deteriorated. She was discharged after 2 weeks and died 2 months later. Lessons PSAn should be considered in the differential diagnosis of splenic vascular tumors, particularly when morphological and immunohistochemical findings overlap. Unexpected postoperative deterioration should prompt timely multidisciplinary reassessment and pathological review.

title: Prevalence and associated factors of sarcopenia among community-dwelling older adults in Vietnam: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Doan TD, Truong AT, Nguyen DTT, Pham TN, Le HT.
abstract: Sarcopenia is a geriatric syndrome characterized by age-related declines in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. Despite its clinical relevance, it is frequently under-recognized because it is often considered a normal consequence of aging, even though it is associated with adverse outcomes such as functional impairment, falls, hospitalization, and mortality. Therefore, early identification and targeted nutritional and physical interventions are essential. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and its associated factors among community-dwelling older adults in a developing-country setting. A cross-sectional study was conducted in January 2024 among 660 community-dwelling older adults in Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Sarcopenia was defined according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2019 criteria, incorporating handgrip strength, 6-m walking speed, and skeletal muscle mass assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis. Participants underwent standardized anthropometric measurements, physical performance assessments, and nutritional evaluations using body mass index and Mini Nutritional Assessment. Sociodemographic, clinical, frailty, and lifestyle data were collected. Associations with sarcopenia were examined using prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sarcopenia was identified in 42.4% (280/660; 95% CI: 38.6%-46.3%) of the participants. In the fully adjusted model, sarcopenia was independently associated with frailty (adjusted PR [aPR] = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.07-2.76), multimorbidity (aPR = 1.23; 95% CI: 1.04-1.45), and underweight status (aPR = 1.46; 95% CI: 1.27-1.68). A lower prevalence of sarcopenia was observed among participants who were overweight or obese (aPR = 0.45; 95% CI: 0.36-0.54), physically active (aPR = 0.81; 95% CI: 0.69-0.95), or reported no low family economic status (aPR = 0.82; 95% CI: 0.70-0.97). Sarcopenia was highly prevalent among community-dwelling older adults and independently associated with frailty, multimorbidity, and nutritional status, underscoring the need for early community-based screening and integrated nutritional and physical interventions.

title: Preoperative High-Sensitivity Troponin and Risk of In-Hospital Mortality and Cardiac Events After Hip Fracture Surgery.
authors: Touré A, Okafor K, Medilien B, Mather R, Parry J, Hernandez-Irizarry RC, Bradley CA, Ahn J, Schenker ML.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether preoperative high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) elevation predicted in-hospital cardiac events and mortality after hip fracture surgery, and whether surgical delay modified this relationship. Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single Level 1 trauma center in the United States. Patient selection criteria Adult patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2024, and had a preoperative hs-cTn measurement as part of routine perioperative assessment were included. Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital cardiac event or mortality. Secondary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and in-hospital cardiac events analyzed separately. Outcomes were compared across preoperative troponin categories defined as normal ( 100 ng/L), and across surgical delay categories defined as 48 hours. Results A total of 510 patients were included. The mean age was 76.3 ± 14.1 years, and 291 patients (57.1%) were female. Preoperative troponin was normal in 424 patients (83.1%), elevated in 58 patients (11.4%), and significantly elevated in 28 patients (5.5%). Thirty-five patients (6.9%) experienced the composite outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 19 of 424 patients (4.5%) with normal troponin, 6 of 58 patients (10.3%) with elevated troponin, and 10 of 28 patients (35.7%) with significantly elevated troponin ( P Conclusions Preoperative hs-cTn elevation was independently associated with in-hospital cardiac events and mortality after hip fracture surgery. Troponin levels greater than 100 ng/L identified patients at highest risk, independent of surgical delay. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary hip arthroplasty : should the choice of femoral component design and fixation method vary according to the sex and age of the patient?
authors: Børsheim S, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, Gjertsen JE, Furnes O, Dybvik E, Lie SA, Dale H.
abstract: Aims Periprosthetic femoral fracture is a severe complication following hip arthroplasty, influenced by the design of the femoral component and the method of fixation. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of sex and age on the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture. Methods We analyzed 204,041 primary hip arthroplasties from the Norwegian Arthroplasty Register and the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register (1 January 2005 to 31 December 2025). Femoral components were categorized as cemented composite beam (CB), cemented polished taper-slip (PTS), uncemented collarless (UCC-), and uncemented collared (UCC+). Cox regression analysis was used to compare the risk (adjusted hazard rate ratio (aHRR)) of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture stratified by sex and age. Results In males, PTS and UCC- had a nine-times higher risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture than CB. For UCC+, the risk was four times higher than CB. The risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in males aged > 65 years for UCC-; for UCC+ the risk was increased in males aged > 75 years, whereas PTS had higher risk for periprosthetic femoral fracture at all ages, compared with CB. In females, the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in those aged > 70 years for PTS and UCC+ compared with CB, whereas for UCC- the risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture was higher in those aged > 60 years, compared with CB. Conclusion Our findings suggest that CB should be the preferred choice of femoral component, at least for males aged > 75 years and females aged > 70 years. UCC+ components were the best uncemented option, while the use of PTS components was associated with a high risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture among males of all ages.

title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
authors: Zaed I, Ricciardi L, Mezzapesa FP, Di Cosmo L, Ganau M, Iaccarino C, Chibbaro S, Todeschi J, Mallereau CH, Cardia A, Milani D.
abstract: Aim Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. Methods We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition. Results Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p p p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups. Conclusions In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.

title: Pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block with lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) block versus fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) for hip surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Wang MY, Du MQ, Xu YN, Wang Y, Yao SL, Wu X.
abstract: Background Effective analgesia that preserves motor function is essential for early mobilization after hip surgery. Although fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) is recommended for total hip arthroplasty, the comparative efficacy of combined pericapsular nerve group and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve blocks (PENG + LFCN) remains uncertain. Methods Databases including Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Central, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched up to December 8, 2024. Statistical analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan) (computer program, version 5.4, The Cochrane Collaboration, 2020). Results Seven randomized controlled trials involving 572 participants were included. Compared with FICB, PENG + LFCN significantly reduced static pain at 12 hours (mean difference [MD] = -0.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.28 to -0.11; P Conclusion PENG + LFCN may provide superior early analgesia and better preserve lower-limb motor function than FICB after hip surgery. However, the evidence is limited by few trials, small sample sizes, and substantial heterogeneity. Larger, adequately powered trials are warranted.

title: Patient-Reported Outcomes after Distal Radius Fractures Differ Across Geographic and Cultural Populations: A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Bilodeau RE, Bhadouriya RS, Klinger CE, van der List JP, Oquendo YA, Haeberle HS, Victory L, Katzir A, Barth KA, Dvorzhinskiy A, Ricci WM.
abstract: Objectives To assess patient reported outcome (PRO) heterogeneity across different cultural and geographical regions through a systematic review and meta-analysis of PROs after volar plate fixation of distal radius fractures. Methods Data sources PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were queried for randomized controlled trials from 2010 to 2023 reporting Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH), QuickDASH, Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation (PRWE), or Visual Analog Scale (VAS) PROs. Study selection Randomized controlled trials with treatment arms consisting of open reduction and internal fixation using a volar locking plate for adult distal radius fracture (OTA/AO 23) and reported DASH, QuickDASH, PRWE, or VAS PROs were included. Studies not published in English or that provided insufficient extraction data were excluded. Data extraction Studies were characterized by country of origin, continent of origin, and cultural region of origin. Extracted data included PRO outcomes, patient demographics, and follow-up ranges. Data synthesis Random-effects meta-analysis was performed with restricted maximum likelihood method, and subgroup analyses were performed to determine differences in pooled PROs across geographical and cultural regions. Results A total of 52 treatment arms met inclusion criteria for DASH analysis, 33 for PRWE, and 23 for VAS. Significant mean DASH score heterogeneity existed across all studies ( P Conclusions PROs after distal radius volar plate fixation demonstrated meaningful variation across cultural and geographic contexts. Outcomes from one cultural region may not be globally generalizable. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level II. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
authors: Downie S, Kennedy M, Farhan-Alanie OM, Kennedy IW, McKean G, Kelly MP, Young PS.
abstract: Aims Cemented arthroplasty has previously been recommended for treating metastatic bone disease (MBD) around the hip. However, cementing has disadvantages, including restricted femoral component length, loosening due to disease progression, and bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). A long uncemented implant spanning the whole femur could negate these disadvantages; however, there is a paucity of data regarding their use. Our aim was to assess the outcomes of a long uncemented femoral component in MBD. Methods A total of 205 patients with MBD underwent femoral reconstruction using the Restoration Modular Revision Hip System Plasma stem between January 2008 and December 2025. They were identified from the prospectively collected database of a tertiary MBD service. Any patient with symptomatic bone metastases involving the acetabulum or femur, with completed or impending pathological fracture, were included. The primary endpoint was reintervention for femoral implant failure, with exclusion of reintervention for deep infection and/or instability. Results Indications for surgery included pathological fracture (46 of 205; 22%) or lesions at risk of fracture (78%; n = 159). The mean follow-up was 45 months (12 to 131). A total of 140 patients (68%) died during the study period (mean 20 months (0.1 to 128) postoperatively). The mean distance from the centre of the femoral head to the most distal femoral metastasis was 126 mm (5 to 369). Using death as a competing risk, two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and probability of death was 0.507 (95% CI 0.436 to 0.577). At five years, probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and the risk of death was 0.703 (95% CI 0.629 to 0.776). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205) with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure (all periprosthetic femoral fractures). Conclusion This implant demonstrates promising short- to mid-term survivorship, with no patient requiring femoral revision for loosening and a comparatively low complication rate. A long uncemented femoral component may be an appropriate option in selected patients presenting with symptomatic bone metastases around the hip.

title: Osteoporosis treatment gaps and risk of recurrent hip fracture following initial fragility fracture: Insights from over one million cases.
authors: Laurore C, Lezak BA, Xie J, Avila A, Hong C, Yassin S, Ganta A, Egol KA, Konda SR.
abstract: Introduction Patients who sustain a hip fracture are at high risk of a second hip fracture, yet most do not receive osteoporosis pharmacotherapy. We evaluated the association between bone-health medication initiation after a first hip fracture and the risk of a second hip fracture. Methods This retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos, a de-identified multi-institutional electronic health record database. Adults who underwent surgery for a first femoral neck, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric hip fracture were classified as having no bone-health medication, as baseline users (medication documented at admission), or as initiators within six months of the index fracture. Second hip fracture was assessed over fixed 1-, 2- and 5-year horizons. We estimated absolute risks, cumulative incidence accounting for death as a competing risk, and multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models. Results Overall, 1,051,020 patients were eligible for the 5-year analysis: 705,059 (67.1%) had no medication, 83,452 (7.9%) were baseline users and 262,509 (25.0%) initiated medication within six months. Five-year cumulative incidence of second hip fracture was 17.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] 17.1-17.3) with no medication, 14.1% (95% CI 13.8-14.4) among baseline users and 8.9% (95% CI 8.8-9.1) among initiators. In adjusted models, the hazard of second hip fracture was lower among baseline users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71, 95% CI 0.69-0.73) and initiators (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.37-0.39) than among patients with no medication. Conclusions Initiation of bone-health medication within six months of a first hip fracture was associated with a lower risk of a second hip fracture. Baseline users had intermediate risk, which may reflect confounding by indication, agent selection or adherence. These findings support early, coordinated post-fracture osteoporosis treatment; the observational design precludes causal inference.

title: Orthopaedics at crossroads: are we ready for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in research?
authors: Vaishya R, Vaish A, Hernigou P, Scarlat MM.

title: Nursing-Related Risk Characteristics and Identification of High-Risk Patients With In-Hospital Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower-Limb Fracture Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
authors: Ding M, Zhong H, Huang L.
abstract: Aim Lower-limb fractures already contribute ≥5 Caprini points for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk, limiting the ability of the conventional >5 cutoff to discriminate individual risk within this population. We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring. Methods We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024. Of 783 patients screened, 71 were excluded, leaving 712 in the source cohort (61 DVT cases and 651 ultrasound-negative, matchable controls). Cases and controls were matched 1:3 without replacement by age (±5 years), sex, and fracture site, yielding 61 matched sets (244 patients). After matching, non-matching variables were singly imputed using a random forest algorithm for the primary analysis. To assess uncertainty associated with this approach, a separate sensitivity analysis generated 20 completed datasets from the pre-imputation matched records using a stochastic chained-equation multiple-imputation procedure. Regression estimates across the 20 datasets were combined using Rubin's rules. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression stratified by matched set and reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Incremental within-set concordance was corrected using 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples. The primary analysis, complete-case analyses and multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis were conducted separately. Results Matching variables were well balanced after matching, with standardized mean differences (SMD) of 0.02 for age and 0 for sex and fracture site, although several non-matching characteristics remained imbalanced. Three factors were positively associated with in-hospital DVT: admission Caprini ≥9 (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.28-4.61), severe POD1 activity dependence (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.38-10.94), and preoperative immobilization ≥72 h (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.14-5.67). Compared with patients without any core risk features, the OR increased to 2.81 (95% CI 1.46-5.38) among those with one feature and to 6.28 (95% CI 1.57-25.03) among those with two features. Adding severe POD1 activity dependence to Caprini ≥9 was associated with a modest increase in corrected within-set concordance from 0.589 to 0.633, corresponding to a difference of 0.044 (bootstrap SE 0.022, 95% CI 0.003-0.088). Sensitivity analyses generally preserved the direction of the main associations, although the Caprini estimate was attenuated after additional adjustment for trauma-related variables and D-dimer. Conclusions Admission Caprini ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h, and severe POD1 activity dependence were each associated with in-hospital lower-extremity DVT. POD1 activity assessment was associated with a modest improvement in within-set risk ranking beyond Caprini stratification. This finding should not be interpreted as evidence of established clinical utility or improved patient outcomes; however, it may help guide nursing attention toward prophylaxis delivery, activity support, and symptom surveillance. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its clinical relevance.

title: Nucleotide metabolism and cervical cancer: A comprehensive study of molecular subtypes and therapeutic targets.
authors: Li F, Bao C, Liu Y, Liu B, Zhai F.
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is among the most prevalent malignancies in women worldwide. Tumor progression involves profound metabolic reprogramming, in which nucleotide metabolism sustains deoxyribonucleic acid/ribonucleic acid synthesis and proliferation; however, its role in CC remains unclear. Transcriptomic and clinical data of CC patients were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Nonnegative matrix factorization classified patients into molecular subtypes based on nucleotide metabolism-related genes and compared their survival, immune infiltration, somatic mutations, and drug sensitivity. Mfuzz soft clustering identified subtype-associated expression patterns. Gene set variation analysis scoring, differential expression analysis, and Gene Ontology/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment of differentially expressed genes were then performed. Prognostic models were constructed using multiple machine learning algorithms, and the model with the highest concordance index (C-index) was selected. Patients were stratified into high- and low-risk groups and assessed using multivariate Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analyses. Immune checkpoint inhibitor response was predicted using the tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion algorithm, and molecular docking was performed between core genes and candidate compounds. Nonnegative matrix factorization revealed 5 subtypes with distinct outcomes: cluster 2 showed the worst prognosis, whereas clusters 3 and 4 had favorable survival. TTN, KMT2C, HUWE1, and PIK3CA were frequently mutated across subtypes. B cells, regulatory T cells, CD8+ T cells, and M2 macrophages were enriched in clusters 3 and 4. VX-680, CIL70, and BRD-K01737880 exhibited significantly lower IC50 values in the poor-prognosis group. Seven key genes (SERPINE1, CAV1, SOD2, SLC16A1, XDH, CYP27B1, and NAGS) were identified by Mfuzz clustering. Forty-two differentially expressed genes between the high- and low-score groups were predominantly enriched in xenobiotic response, nutrient sensing, small-molecule catabolism, inflammatory response, tumor necrosis factor signaling, apoptosis, and hypoxia. The generalized boosted regression model achieved the highest C-index, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year area under the curves of 0.62, 0.67, and 0.61, indicating modest discrimination. Tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion analysis indicated reduced immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness in the high-risk group. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding between core genes and candidate compounds, providing hypotheses for experimental validation. This study delineates the associations of nucleotide metabolism-related genes with molecular classification and prognosis in CC and identifies potential biomarkers, candidate therapeutic agents, and a prognostic model providing complementary assessment value.

title: Novel and long-term research: where are we?
authors: Haddad FS.

title: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder presenting as rapidly progressive dementia: A case report.
authors: Hua D, Xiang S, Sun L, Hong L, Yang W, Wang H.
abstract: Rationale Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a rare autoimmune astrocytopathy primarily affecting the optic nerves and spinal cord. Diencephalic involvement is commonly detected on neuroimaging but often remains clinically silent. Rapidly progressive dementia (RPD) as the initial and primary manifestation of NMOSD is exceedingly rare. Patient concerns A 64-year-old woman presented with a 10-day history of progressive cognitive slowing and memory decline. On admission, she was disoriented, apathetic, and unable to recognize her family members, with a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 3/30. Laboratory investigations revealed severe hyponatremia (serum sodium 112.60 mmol/L). Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed abnormal signal intensities involving the bilateral basal ganglia, hypothalamus, and mammillary bodies. Diagnoses Autoimmune encephalitis, infectious encephalitis, Wernicke encephalopathy, and prion disease were initially considered and systematically excluded. Serum and cerebrospinal fluid testing revealed positive aquaporin-4 (AQP-4) antibodies with titers of 1:32 and 1:16, respectively. Based on the 2015 International Panel for NMO Diagnosis criteria, a final diagnosis of AQP-4 antibody-positive NMOSD was established. Interventions The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy (1000 mg/d for 3 days, followed by a stepwise tapering regimen) and gradual correction of electrolyte disturbances. Outcomes After 4 weeks of treatment, the patient showed marked cognitive improvement, with the MMSE score increasing from 3 to 18. At the 6-month follow-up, her clinical symptoms had almost completely resolved, the MMSE score had improved to 27/30, electrolyte levels had normalized, and follow-up magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a significant reduction in lesion size with mild enlargement of the third ventricle. Lessons This case demonstrates that AQP-4 antibody-positive NMOSD can present as a reversible RPD, potentially mediated by AQP-4 antibody-associated inflammatory injury of the diencephalon. It underscores that in patients with unexplained RPD - particularly when neuroimaging reveals lesions in AQP-4-enriched regions such as the hypothalamus, mammillary bodies, or periventricular areas surrounding the third ventricle, or when otherwise unexplained hyponatremia is present - NMOSD should be included in the differential diagnosis. Timely AQP-4 antibody testing should be pursued to facilitate early immunotherapy and optimize clinical outcomes.

title: Nail-Plate Constructs Permit Early Weight Bearing and Improved Outcomes Compared With Single Device Constructs in the Treatment of Distal Femur Fractures at One-Year Follow-Up: A Retrospective Analysis.
authors: Patel UJ, Holloway MR, Guedikian CR, Soin SP, Joseph NM, Ketz JP.
abstract: Objectives To investigate clinical, radiographic, and patient reported outcomes in patients undergoing surgical fixation for distal femur fractures with single device construct (lateral locked plate or intramedullary nail) or nail-plate combination. Methods . Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single, academic, tertiary Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria The inclusion criteria were patients with DFFs (OTA/AO 33) treated operatively with lateral locked plate, IM nail, or nail-plate combination between January 2011 and December 2023 with a minimum follow up of 1 year. Outcome measures and comparisons Radiographic fracture healing, complication rates, weight-bearing status, length of stay, gait impairment, and patient-reported outcomes using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System were investigated. Multivariable regression models were used to identify predictors of union, reoperation, discharge disposition, and postoperative complications. Results A total of 191 patients were included, with 153 (131 lateral locked plate, 22 intramedullary nail) treated with a single device construct (mean age 72 years [range 22-95], 16% male) and 38 treated with nail-plate combination constructs (mean age 70 years [range 19-94], 16% male). At one-year postoperatively, nail-plate combination versus single device constructs were associated with significantly lower rates of nonunion (0% vs. 12%, P = 0.03), reoperation (10% vs. 26%, P = 0.05), and gait impairment (26% vs. 58%, P Conclusions Fixation with nail-plate combination constructs, compared with single device constructs, in DFFs seemed to support immediate weight bearing and was associated with improved short-term and midterm outcomes, including reduced rates of nonunion, reoperation, and functional impairment at 1 year. These advantages may be especially relevant for geriatric patients and those with complex or periprosthetic fracture patterns, or with preoperative risk factors for nonunion and functional decline. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Motion style acupuncture treatment for traumatic temporomandibular disorder: A case report.
authors: Kwon MJ, Jang C, Lee Y, Kim D.
abstract: Rationale Traumatic temporomandibular joint disorder (TMD) tends to persist longer than nontraumatic TMD, and conventional treatments show limited effectiveness in such cases. Motion style acupuncture treatment (MSAT), which induces active or passive movement after insertion of acupuncture needles at the affected sites, may help alleviate pain and improve mandibular movement. However, its application to traumatic TMD unresponsive to prior treatments has rarely been reported, and no case has objectively demonstrated its effects using radiologic findings. Patient concerns A patient presented with persistent right temporomandibular joint pain and clicking following a motor vehicle collision, which were unresponsive to previous treatment. Diagnoses The patient was diagnosed with traumatic TMD secondary to the motor vehicle collision, with clinically suspected disc displacement with reduction and concomitant local myalgia. Interventions The patient underwent 6 sessions of MSAT. Outcomes Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), maximal mouth opening, and lateral radiography were performed before and after treatment. Pain during mandibular movement decreased from NRS 8 to 1, and resting pain decreased from NRS 7 to 1. Clicking resolved after the 5th session. Maximal mouth opening increased from 25 mm at baseline to 60 mm after the final session. Lateral radiography demonstrated a change in the distance between the articular eminence and the condylar head from 3.43 to 4.81 mm. The patient also reported reduced subjective discomfort. Lessons The patient demonstrated improvements in both subjective and objective outcomes, suggesting that MSAT may have potential as a treatment option for traumatic TMD. However, as this is a single case report and long-term follow-up was not available to assess the durability of treatment effects or symptom recurrence, further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its efficacy and safety.

title: Minimally invasive surgery improves surgical and analgesic outcomes in overweight or obese patients with borderline ovarian tumors: A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Lee SM, Kim S.
abstract: This study aimed to compare surgical outcomes between minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and open surgery in overweight or obese patients with borderline ovarian tumor (BOT) and identify risk factors for additional analgesic use despite patient-controlled analgesia .We selected patients with a body mass index of 25 or more who underwent surgery for BOT at Korea University Anam Hospital from 2006 to 2023. Patients who underwent laparoscopic or robotic surgery were categorized into the MIS group, while those who underwent open surgery were categorized into the open surgery group. For statistical analysis, the Student t test, chi-square test, Fisher exact test, and logistic regression analysis were performed using SPSS. Of 128 patients, 90 were in the MIS group, and 38 were in the open group. Compared with the open surgery group, the MIS group had a shorter surgical time (P < .001), lower estimated blood loss (P < .001), a shorter hospital stay (P < .001), and a lower rate of additional analgesic use despite patient-controlled analgesia (P = .002). There was no significant difference in disease-free survival between the 2 groups. No deaths occurred during follow-up. MIS compared to open surgery was identified as a factor associated with significantly lower use of additional analgesics (adjusted odds ratio, 0.13; 95% confidence interval, 0.037-0.470; P = .002). In overweight or obese patients with BOT, MIS was associated with better surgical outcomes and a reduced need for additional analgesics during hospitalization compared with open surgery. These findings suggest that MIS may be a feasible surgical option for these patients.

title: Minimally invasive removal of intradural extramedullary tumor using unilateral biportal endoscopic technique: A technical case report.
authors: Que Z, Lin S, Chen D, Xiao K, Chen C, Shu J, Lin GX, Hu B, Rui G.
abstract: Rationale Intradural extramedullary (IDEM) tumors are mostly benign spinal lesions but may lead to progressive neurological symptoms due to spinal cord or nerve root compression. The unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) technique, widely used in spinal decompression and fusion, has rarely been applied to intradural pathologies. This case report presents a case of IDEM tumor resection using the UBE technique. Patient concerns A 50-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of low back pain and 1 month of left leg numbness. Diagnoses Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an IDEM tumor at the T9-T10 level, suggestive of a schwannoma. Interventions The patient underwent tumor resection using a UBE technique. The dura was closed using a continuous 4-0 barbed suture under endoscopic visualization. Outcomes The procedure lasted 7.8 hours, with an estimated blood loss of 200 mL. The postoperative hospital stay was 6 days, and no cerebrospinal fluid leakage occurred. Histopathological examination confirmed a benign schwannoma. The patient's symptoms resolved completely without neurological deficits. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging at 6 months showed no evidence of recurrence. Lessons This case report presents the use of the UBE technique for IDEM tumor resection in a selected patient, with satisfactory surgical outcomes.

title: Metabolic abnormalities and colorectal cancer: An integrated secondary analysis triangulating Mendelian randomization with global burden and temporal trends.
authors: Gao Z, Peng K.
abstract: Metabolic abnormalities are plausible and modifiable contributors to colorectal cancer (CRC), but genetic evidence and population-level burden data are often reported separately. This integrated secondary analysis triangulated Mendelian randomization (MR), Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates, metabolic risk attribution, estimated annual percentage change analyses, geographic and Socio-demographic Index (SDI) comparisons, and observed age-standardized mortality trends to characterize the relationship between metabolic abnormalities and CRC from 1990 to 2021. Genetically predicted body mass index (BMI), diabetes, and familial combined hyperlipidemia (FCHL) were positively associated with CRC risk in inverse-variance weighted MR analyses, with the strongest association observed for BMI. The diabetes (odds ratio = 1.002, 95% confidence interval = 1.001-1.003) and FCHL (odds ratio = 1.0010, 95% confidence interval = 1.0003-1.0017) estimates were statistically significant but extremely close to the null, indicating minimal individual-level effect sizes on the genetic-liability scale and no basis for inferring clinically meaningful risk differences. Globally, CRC incident cases increased substantially from 916,584 in 1990 to 2,194,143 in 2021, while the age-standardized death rate declined from 15.56 to 12.40 per 100,000 population. China showed a particularly steep increase in incident cases and age-standardized incidence rate. Across SDI strata, CRC incidence rose in all strata except high-SDI settings, whereas diabetes incidence increased in every region and stratum. Low-middle SDI settings showed the clearest ecological co-burden, with rising CRC and diabetes burden occurring together. Age-specific analyses showed that CRC burden attributable to high BMI and high fasting plasma glucose increased sharply with age, with the highest attributable death and disability-adjusted life-year rates in the oldest age groups. Observed global CRC age-standardized death rates declined from 1990 to 2021 for both sexes combined, males, and females. These findings support metabolic health as an important and actionable component of CRC prevention, particularly in settings where CRC and diabetes burdens are rising in parallel. The population-level findings should be interpreted as ecological co-burden rather than proof of interaction, and the MR estimates reflect lifelong genetic liability rather than clinical relative risks. In particular, the diabetes and FCHL estimates should not be interpreted as clinically meaningful individual-level effects.

title: Marginal excision of dedifferentiated liposarcoma of the limbs without radiation may be safe in select patients.
authors: Barriga J, Magnan MC, Arafah MA, Griffin AM, Tsoi KM, Wunder JS, Ferguson PC.
abstract: Aims Dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS) is a heterogeneous tumour consisting of low-grade atypical lipomatous tumour (ALT) and high-grade sarcomatous components. This study evaluates local recurrence and metastasis rates after resection of a limb DDLPS, focusing on the impact of tumour grade at surgical margins and the role of adjuvant radiation therapy. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted of 137 patients with a pathologically confirmed limb DDLPS who underwent surgical resection between July 1995 and September 2024. Outcomes assessed included local recurrence-free survival, metastasis-free survival, and overall survival. Statistical analyses used chi-squared tests for categorical variables, independent-samples t -tests for continuous variables, and Kaplan-Meier survival estimates. Results Of the 137 patients (mean age 67 years (28 to 96); mean tumour size 16 cm (2.4 to 39)), 54.7% (n = 75) had negative surgical margins, and 45.3% (n = 62) had positive margins. Of those with positive margins, 48.3% involved only the ALT component. Notably, patients with positive margins confined to the ALT component who did not receive radiation therapy 40% (n = 12) exhibited no local recurrences or metastases. Those patients with negative margins who were treated without radiation therapy (n = 21; 28%) had low rates of recurrence (n = 1; 4.7%) and metastasis (n = 5; 23%). Conclusion Patients with DDLPS can expect high rates of local control and overall survival. In select cases of limb DDLPS in which positive surgical margins are limited to the ALT component, marginal excision without adjuvant radiation therapy may be oncologically safe, offering comparable oncological outcomes to those with negative margins. This approach can enhance functional preservation by avoiding unnecessary exposure to radiation.

title: Magnetic resonance neurography-supported L3-L4 radiculitis presenting as refractory peripatellar neuropathic pain in a patient with diabetes: A case report.
authors: Huang X, Yang D, Wang J, Zheng B.
abstract: Rationale Peripatellar pain is usually attributed to local knee disorders. However, proximal neural lesions can also cause pain around the knee. Third and fourth lumbar (L3-L4) radiculitis presenting mainly as peripatellar neuropathic pain is uncommon and may be missed when typical radicular symptoms are absent. Patient concerns A 75-year-old man with a more than 20-year history of type 2 diabetes presented with severe left peripatellar pain for 10 days. The pain was burning and stabbing and was accompanied by numbness and marked touch-evoked allodynia. The visual analog scale score was 8-9/10, and the Douleur Neuropathique 4 score was 9/10. He had no low back pain, typical radicular pain, motor weakness, or reflex abnormalities. Diagnoses Knee magnetic resonance imaging showed degenerative changes that did not explain the neuropathic pain phenotype. Lumbar magnetic resonance imaging showed no definite compression of the L3 or L4 nerve roots. Electrodiagnostic testing did not provide level-specific localization. Magnetic resonance neurography showed asymmetric hyperintensity involving the left L3 and L4 proximal neural structures, supporting the diagnosis of L3-L4 radiculitis. Interventions Neuropathic pain medications and knee-targeted procedures provided inadequate or only transient relief. The patient was subsequently treated with pregabalin, duloxetine, short-term opioid analgesia, and optimization of glycemic control. Outcomes The pain and allodynia gradually improved within 2 weeks, and analgesic medications were discontinued. At 3 months, the visual analog scale score was 0-3/10 and the Douleur Neuropathique 4 score was 1/10. Touch-evoked allodynia had resolved. Lessons L3-L4 radiculitis may present as refractory peripatellar neuropathic pain without low back pain or typical radicular symptoms. When severe neuropathic pain around the knee cannot be explained by local pathology, a proximal neural lesion should be considered. Magnetic resonance neurography may help identify radiculitis that is not evident on conventional lumbar imaging.

title: Lymphedema as a Significant Risk Factor for Primary Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Failure: A Systematic Review.
authors: Zandi R, Mehrvar A, Keyhaninejad N, Shaterzadeh-Bojd S, Talebi S, Foroughi E, Gouhari F, Abdashti AA, Ehsani A.
abstract: Background Total hip and knee arthroplasty are highly effective for improving quality of life, alleviating pain, and enhancing physical function. However, failure of these joint replacements inflicts considerable burdens on patients and the healthcare system. The impact of lymphedema, as an uncommon comorbidity, in patients undergoing total hip and knee arthroplasties remains unknown. This study aimed to assess the most recent publications and evaluate the results and post-operative complications of total joint arthroplasty in patients with preoperative lymphedema. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases was conducted up to 25th October 2024 to identify relevant studies. Inclusion of studies was established through the application of a predetermined protocol by three independent reviewers. Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal checklists were used for risk of bias assessment. Results Seven articles met the inclusion criteria. Five studies evaluated the outcomes of lymphedema in total knee arthroplasty, one in total hip arthroplasty, and one in total hip and knee arthroplasty. Lymphedema is a significant risk factor for postoperative complications in total hip and knee arthroplasty. The findings highlight the significance of patient optimization and enable improved lymphedema patient counseling. Conclusion Although lymphedema can be measured as a significant risk factor for complications in total hip and knee arthroplasty, further studies are required to investigate and confirm this relationship.

title: Low-Rate Carbohydrate Ingestion Mitigates the Loss of Power Output at the Moderate-To-Heavy Intensity Transition During Prolonged Cycling.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Iten E, Kilding AE, Plews DJ, Maunder E.
abstract: We investigated whether a low carbohydrate ingestion rate during prolonged cycling improves durability and maintains blood glucose concentration. Thirteen trained cyclists and triathletes (V̇O 2 peak: 57.1 ± 7.6 mL·kg -1 ·min -1 ) completed a randomized, single-blind, crossover study including assessment of the intensity domain transitions in three conditions: without prior cycling (FRESH), following prolonged cycling with 15 g·h -1 carbohydrate ingestion (CHO), and following prolonged cycling with placebo ingestion (PLA). Prolonged trials consisted of 150 min of cycling at 90% of the power output associated with the estimated first ventilatory threshold (VT 1 ). The moderate-to-heavy (power output at VT1) and heavy-to-severe (critical power) intensity transitions were assessed via a submaximal incremental test and a three-minute all-out test, respectively. Power output at VT 1 was significantly lower in PLA (176 ± 47 W) than FRESH (193 ± 56 W; p = 0.003) and CHO (189 ± 55 W; p = 0.047), with no difference between CHO and FRESH. Exploratory comparisons at individual timepoints showed blood glucose concentration was higher in CHO than PLA at 30 and 90 min, and prior to the incremental test (5.5 ± 0.5 vs. 4.7 ± 0.3 mmol·L -1 ; p = 0.0008). Critical power was higher in FRESH than PLA (312 ± 72 vs. 298 ± 67 W; p = 0.049), with no differences between CHO and PLA. These findings indicate that carbohydrate ingestion at 15 g·h -1 during prolonged cycling attenuates the decline in power output at VT 1 , and may be associated with improved maintenance of blood glucose concentrations.

title: Lattice radiotherapy followed by chemoimmunotherapy for sustained disease control in bulky centrally located left hilar lung squamous cell carcinoma: A case report.
authors: Ye J, Cao L, Chen X, Wang Q, Yang X, Chen J, Zhou G, You C, Xu T, Gui Y.
abstract: Rationale Bulky centrally located, locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer often abuts critical thoracic structures, making both upfront surgery and conventional radiotherapy dose escalation challenging. Lattice radiotherapy (LRT) may achieve tumor debulking while limiting radiation exposure to surrounding organs at risk. Patient concerns A 70-year-old man presented with a recurrent cough, sputum production, and hemoptysis for 6 months. Diagnoses Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography revealed a 6.6 cm × 6.0 cm irregular left hilar mass with mediastinal invasion, encasement of the adjacent trachea and vessels, and an indistinct interface with the esophagus. Bronchoscopic biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. The programmed death-ligand 1 tumor proportion score was 18%. The final diagnosis was left hilar lung squamous cell carcinoma, cT4N1M0, stage IIIA. Interventions After multidisciplinary team discussion, the patient underwent LRT followed by sequential paclitaxel, carboplatin, and tislelizumab, and then maintenance tislelizumab monotherapy. Outcomes After 3 treatment cycles, the maximum lesion diameter decreased from 6.6 cm to 4.4 cm, meeting the criteria for partial response according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1. Cough and hemoptysis resolved, and the squamous cell carcinoma antigen level decreased from 11.5 to 3.9 ng/mL. At the last follow-up, 12 months after treatment initiation, the lesion remained stable without definite disease progression, and no grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events were observed. Lessons For selected patients with bulky, centrally located, locally advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma who are potentially resectable but at high surgical risk, LRT followed by chemoimmunotherapy may be a feasible individualized strategy. The role of conversion surgery should be determined by dynamic multidisciplinary risk-benefit assessment.

title: Knowledge structure and emerging trends in research on osteoporotic fractures and cardiovascular diseases: A bibliometric analysis from 2005 to 2025.
authors: Zhao Y, Wu Z, Yan S, Yang K, Chen L.
abstract: Background Osteoporotic fractures (OPFs) and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are major age-related conditions that frequently coexist and may be linked through shared biological mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, mineral metabolism disorders, vascular calcification, and frailty. Although research on OPFs and CVDs has expanded rapidly, the intellectual structure, collaborative patterns, and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary field remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map the global research landscape and identify emerging hotspots in OPF-CVD research from 2005 to 2025. Methods English-language articles and reviews published during 2005 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on April 2, 2026. Analyses used VOSviewer 1.6.20 (Centre for Science and Technology Studies [CWTS], Leiden University), CiteSpace 6.4.R1 (Chaomei Chen, Drexel University), bibliometrix 5.3.0 in R 4.5.3 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing), and Microsoft Excel. We examined publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, co-cited references, keyword patterns, and citation bursts. Results A total of 1236 publications were included. Annual output increased from 24 publications in 2005 to 103 in 2025, corresponding to a compound annual growth rate of 7.56%. The United States had the highest publication count, raw citation count, and TLS. Harvard University was the most productive institution, and Katie L Stone was the most productive author. Reference co-citation analysis identified 8 major thematic clusters: calcium, bisphosphonates, heart failure, frailty, renal osteodystrophy, antihypertensive drugs, osteopenia, and phosphorus. Keyword analyses suggested a descriptive shift from epidemiological associations toward bone-vascular mechanisms, risk stratification, fragility-fracture management, diagnosis, and prevention. Conclusions OPF-CVD research has developed into a multidisciplinary field with increasing clinical relevance. The bibliometric patterns are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causal relationships. Future research should evaluate integrated bone-cardiovascular risk assessment, pharmacological safety, and multidisciplinary care using prospective and clinically validated designs.
