title: Joint associations of estimated glucose disposal rate and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with metabolic syndrome in Korean adults: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Ruan L, Ou S.
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS), an important metabolic risk phenotype within the broader cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework, is characterized by insulin resistance and chronic low-grade inflammation; however, evidence regarding the joint relationship of these 2 biological dimensions with MetS remains limited. We analyzed cross-sectional data from 20,781 Korean adults aged ≥ 19 years who were enrolled in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) 2015-2018. MetS was classified using the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III framework with waist circumference thresholds adapted for the Korean/Asian populations. Weighted logistic regression was performed to examine the relationships between estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and MetS. Potential dose-response patterns were further explored using restricted cubic splines. Joint analyses, interaction analysis, and prespecified subgroup analyses were also performed. MetS was present in 29.4% of participants after weighting. In the fully adjusted model, higher eGDR was associated with lower odds of MetS per unit (OR 0.48, 95% CI: 0.47-0.49), whereas log-transformed hs-CRP showed a positive association with MetS, with higher levels corresponding to greater odds (OR 1.71, 95% CI: 1.64-1.79; both P < .001). Dose-response analyses revealed a decreasing pattern for eGDR and an increasing pattern for hs-CRP in relation to MetS. In joint analyses, progressively higher odds of MetS were observed across exposure categories, with the low-eGDR/high-hs-CRP profile corresponding to the greatest odds of MetS. No significant multiplicative interaction was detected (P for interaction = .064). The association of the joint high-risk profile with MetS was generally consistent across subgroups and appeared stronger among younger participants and those without diabetes. Lower eGDR and higher hs-CRP levels were independently associated with MetS in Korean adults, and the low-eGDR/high-hs-CRP profile was associated with the highest odds of MetS. Their joint assessment may provide complementary information for characterizing adverse metabolic profiles within the broader CKM framework, although prospective studies are needed to determine its predictive value.

title: InSafeLock endopin versus conventional distal locking screws for femoral shaft fractures: A comparative laboratory biomechanical study.
authors: Özcan S, Yurten H, Çelen ZE.
abstract: The InSafeLock femoral nail is a recently developed implant that uses endopin instead of screws in its distal locking mechanism. This study aimed to compare the biomechanical features of the distal locking mechanisms of InSafeLock and conventional nails. Twenty-four artificial femoral bones were used for mechanical tests. InSafeLock nails with endopin (Group 1) and conventional nails with distal locking screws (Group 2) were inserted into the artificial bones. The biomechanical features were evaluated using axial compression and rotational performance tests. There was no statistically significant difference between Group 1 and Group 2 in the axial compression displacement tests (P = .683). No visual damage was observed on the artificial bones or intramedullary nails after axial compression fatigue tests in either group. During axial compression failure testing performed after fatigue testing, the mean failure load of Group 1 was significantly lower than that of Group 2 (1132.5 ± 15.5 N vs 11,965.5 ± 9.5 N, respectively; P = .002). Rotational performance tests showed that the torsional yield strength of the groups was not statistically different (P = .333). While the InSafeLock endopin offers ease in distal locking, it exhibits a significantly lower failure load under high axial compression forces than conventional screws.

title: IgD-λ POEMS syndrome presenting with edema, pulmonary hypertension, and renal impairment: A case report.
authors: Feng J, Zhao J, Song C, Cui H, Lin Q.
abstract: Rationale Polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal plasma-cell disorder, and skin changes (POEMS) syndrome is a rare multisystem syndrome associated with clonal plasma-cell disorders. The IgD-λ subtype is uncommon, and a low-level monoclonal protein may escape detection by routine electrophoresis and immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE), delaying diagnosis. Patient concerns A 38-year-old woman was admitted in April 2025 with intermittent bilateral lower-extremity edema for >3 years, elevated serum creatinine for 8 months, and acute worsening over 4 days. She subsequently developed pulmonary hypertension, polyserous effusions, splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, anemia, thrombocytosis, and renal impairment, and had been diagnosed elsewhere with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension. Diagnoses Right-heart catheterization confirmed precapillary pulmonary hypertension. Routine serum and urine protein studies, including IFE, were negative. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, nerve-conduction studies showed peripheral neuropathy; serum vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was elevated; and bone marrow studies demonstrated a clonal plasma-cell population with cytoplasmic λ light-chain restriction. Extended serum IFE, including anti-IgD and anti-IgE antisera, detected a trace, nonquantifiable monoclonal IgD component, establishing IgD-λ POEMS syndrome. Renal biopsy showed POEMS-associated glomerular microangiopathy-like lesions with acute tubular injury. Interventions The patient received dexamethasone acetate plus lenalidomide and underwent autologous stem-cell transplantation on December 2, 2025. Outcomes By March 2026, peripheral edema had resolved, pulmonary hypertension was mild on echocardiography, serum creatinine had decreased to 60 μmol/L, and VEGF had normalized. Lessons POEMS syndrome should be considered in patients with unexplained multisystem disease, particularly edema or polyserous effusions accompanied by pulmonary hypertension and renal impairment. Negative routine M-protein testing should not exclude the diagnosis; VEGF testing, bone marrow evaluation, and extended IFE may reveal an occult plasma-cell clone.

title: Hip-related tenotomy and progression to severe displacement of the hip in nonambulant children with cerebral palsy : a nationwide cohort study.
authors: Bakhtiyar M, Iljazi A, Wong C, Petersen MM, Balslev-Clausen A.
abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to investigate whether a hip-related tenotomy is associated with a lower risk of severe hip outcomes in nonambulant children with cerebral palsy and established displacement of the hip. Methods This nationwide register-based cohort study included children classified as Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level IV or V who were enrolled in the Danish Cerebral Palsy Follow-Up Program (CPOP) between 1 January 2008 and 31 December 2023. Hips with a baseline migration percentage (MP) of between 30% and 49% were included and followed until the first occurrence of a severe hip outcome, defined as a MP of ≥ 50% or osteotomy of the hip. Death was treated as a competing event. The cumulative incidence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator. Associations were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regression with cluster-robust standard errors. Results A total of 259 children, contributing 406 hips, were included, of which 110 underwent a tenotomy. At ten years, the cumulative incidence of a severe hip outcome was 34.7% (95% CI 28.8 to 40.7) without tenotomy, and 20.4% (95% CI 12.4 to 28.5) with tenotomy. In adjusted competing-risk regression, tenotomy was associated with a significantly lower risk of a severe hip outcome (sub-distribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.53 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.84); p = 0.006). GMFCS-specific Fine-Gray analyses showed a significant association in GMFCS level IV (sHR 0.35 (95% CI 0.16 to 0.78); p = 0.010), whereas the association did not reach significance in GMFCS level V (sHR 0.68 (95% CI 0.40 to 1.19); p = 0.180). Spasticity, as classified according to the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) 1 and ≥ 3, was independently associated with a significantly increased risk of a severe hip outcome. Conclusion A hip-related tenotomy was associated with a significantly lower incidence of the subsequent development of a severe hip outcome among nonambulant children with established displacement of the hip, particularly in GMFCS level IV. In GMFCS level V, progression remained substantial irrespective of the soft-tissue release, emphasizing the importance of careful patient selection and continued surveillance.

title: Health-related quality of life following periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip arthroplasty : a propensity score-matched cohort study with trajectory analysis.
authors: Ablett AD, Powell-Bowns MFR, Super JT, Neo C, Yapp LZ, Clement ND, Scott CEH.
abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to quantify the impact of a postoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture following a primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) compared with normal values in the general population, and to assess the agreement between recalled pre-fracture and prospectively collected PROMs. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study involved 140 operatively managed patients with a periprosthetic femoral fracture which was sustained around a primary THA, between 2007 and 2025, with a minimum follow-up of one year. The EQ-5D-3L, EQ-VAS, and Oxford Hip Score (OHS) were collected at a median of 2.9 years (IQR 1.9 to 5.5) after the fracture. Complete case propensity score matching (1:5) balanced patients who had a periprosthetic fracture with Health Survey for England general population controls (n = 700) by sex, age, and deprivation. An agreement cohort with data from a linked arthroplasty database enabled comparison between prospectively collected PROMs one year after THA and recalled pre-fracture PROMs, as well as the analysis of PROMs at four timepoints (before THA, one year after THA, pre-fracture recall, and after the periprosthetic femoral fracture). Results The mean EQ-5D-3L scores after periprosthetic femoral fracture were significantly lower than those in the matched general population (mean difference -0.209 (95% CI -0.264 to -0.154); p Conclusion A periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary THA was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in PROMs in about two-thirds of patients, with one-in-ten reporting health states worse than death, at a median follow-up of about three years. These findings have important implications when counselling patients and for targeted strategies designed to prevent a periprosthetic femoral fracture.

title: Global research trends in confocal laser endomicroscopy for brain tumor surgery, 2010-2026: A bibliometric review.
authors: Dinc S, Emrahoglu ME.
abstract: Background Confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) enables real-time microscopic assessment of tissue during brain tumor surgery and has been investigated as an adjunct to intraoperative diagnosis and fluorescence-guided resection. Previous reviews have largely focused on the technical characteristics and clinical applications of CLE. This study aimed to provide a quantitative overview of the development of the field, its collaborative structure, intellectual foundations, and major research themes. Methods The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on May 30, 2026. After title and abstract screening, 114 publications from 2010 to 2026 were included. Bibliographic data were analyzed using VOSviewer version 1.6.20. Co-authorship, citation, co-citation, author-keyword co-occurrence, and bibliographic coupling analyses were performed. Publications with zero citations were additionally examined according to publication year, document type, and research topic. Results The 114 publications received 1801 citations and had a dataset H-index of 25. Publication output increased after 2018 and reached its highest annual level in 2024. The United States, Germany, and Italy were the leading contributing countries, while Mark C. Preul, Jennifer M. Eschbacher, and Evgenii Belykh were among the leading contributors. The main thematic core included CLE, brain tumors, fluorescein sodium, glioma, and fluorescence-guided surgery, with recent work extending toward telepathology and artificial intelligence-assisted image interpretation. Thirty-two publications (28.1%) were uncited; 16 (50.0%) were meeting abstracts, and 19 (59.4%) were published between 2024 and 2026. Conclusion CLE research in brain tumor surgery has expanded since 2010, with published studies increasingly addressing potential clinical applications, telepathology, and computer-assisted image interpretation rather than demonstrating established adoption in routine clinical practice. Uncited publications included both publication types with lower citation visibility and recent studies with limited time to accumulate citations. These bibliometric patterns should not be interpreted as evidence of the clinical effectiveness of CLE. Further multicenter studies using standardized imaging and interpretation protocols and clinically relevant outcomes are needed to clarify the role of CLE in routine neurosurgical practice.

title: Global growth, persistent hierarchies: A bibliometric and network analysis of international collaboration in anesthesiology (1996-2024).
authors: Kinoshita M, Tanaka K.
abstract: Background Although international collaboration in anesthesiology has increased in recent decades, the evolution of global co-authorship networks and their influence on scholarly impact across the field remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to analyze temporal trends in international, national, and single-institution publications and their citation impact; characterize the evolving structure of the international collaboration network; and identify key contributors through network metrics. Methods We conducted a bibliometric analysis of 1,95,955 articles published between 1996 and 2024 in the Scopus "Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine" category. Temporal trends were assessed across 3 distinct periods: 1996 to 2005, 2006 to 2015, and 2016 to 2024. Publications were categorized by collaboration type (international, national, or single institution) and analyzed for citation impact. Countries and collaborative ties are represented as nodes and links, respectively. Structural evolution was assessed using global metrics, and node-level centrality metrics and Gini coefficients were used to identify influential countries and assess collaboration disparities. Results The share of international collaborative articles has more than doubled from 8.0% (1996-2005) to 17.1% (2016-2024). These articles consistently garnered approximately 2.5 times more citations per publication than those from single institutions. The collaboration network expanded substantially; participating countries increased from 117 (1996-2005) to 190 (2016-2024), and collaborative links surged from 585 (1996-2005) to 5245 (2016-2024). The network became denser and more clustered, with decreasing heterogeneity and stable centralization. Persistently high Gini coefficients for degree and betweenness centrality (range, 0.79-0.93) indicated a concentration of collaborative influence among dominant hub countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Canada, and Australia. Low Gini coefficients for closeness centrality (0.23-0.24) suggested equitable network access among most countries. Conclusions International collaboration in anesthesiology increased substantially between 1996 and 2024, with collaborative articles consistently receiving more citations per publication than single-institution publications. The global collaboration network expanded and became more interconnected, while a small group of countries, primarily in North America and Europe, remained central. These findings illustrate the evolution and growing importance of international collaboration in anesthesiology over the past 3 decades.

title: Functional Outcomes After Bipolar Hip Hemiarthroplasty by Using the Direct Anterior Approach Versus Posterior and Direct Lateral Approaches: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Tham SYY, Ng JPH, Zhang X, Tan TL.
abstract: Objectives To compare functional recovery and length of hospital stay in patients undergoing bipolar hip hemiarthroplasty (BHH) for displaced femoral neck fractures using the direct anterior approach (DAA) versus the posterior approach (PA) and direct lateral approach (DLA). Methods Design Retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained hip fracture registry. Setting Single tertiary care institution in Singapore. Patient selection criteria Patients aged 60 years and older who underwent BHH for displaced femoral neck fractures (OTA/AO 31-B) between 2020 and 2023 were identified from the institutional hip fracture registry. Outcome measures and comparisons Functional outcomes were assessed using the Modified Barthel Index (MBI; higher scores indicate better independence) and Parker Mobility Score (higher scores indicate better mobility) at discharge, 6 and 12 months. Mobility status, length of stay, postoperative complications, reoperation, and 1-year mortality were evaluated. Outcomes were compared between DAA and PA after propensity score matching, with an exploratory comparison with the DLA. Results A total of 504 patients were identified; 400 PA, 79 DAA, and 25 DLA. After matching, 67 DAA cases and 134 PA cases were analyzed. Age and sex distribution were similar between DAA and PA groups (80.7 ± 6.3 vs. 81.1 ± 6.5 years, P = 0.655; female: 79.1% vs. 75.4%, P = 0.556). The DAA group demonstrated a smaller decline in MBI from premorbid baseline to discharge as compared with the PA group [DAA: -49.85 ± 17.88 vs. PA: -55.47 ± 18.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.11-11.13, P = 0.045]. No significant differences were observed between the DAA and PA groups in changes from premorbid to 12-month MBI (DAA: -23.97 ± 27.46 vs. PA: -18.52 ± 26.38, 95% CI: -13.67 to 2.78, P = 0.193) or from premorbid to 12-month Parker Mobility Score (DAA: -2.72 ± 2.90 vs. PA: -2.18 ± 2.46, 95% CI: -1.37 to 0.29, P = 0.198). Length of stay (DAA: 9.88 ± 5.08 vs. PA: 10.20 ± 5.20 days; P = 0.684) and 1-year mortality (DAA: 3.0% vs. PA: 8.2%; P = 0.156) were comparable between DAA and PA groups. Conclusions DAA for BHH was associated with better early functional recovery at hospital discharge than PA. However, this advantage did not persist at 12 months, with no significant differences in functional outcomes, length of hospital stay, or 1-year mortality between DAA and PA groups. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Fasting glucose-to-HDL cholesterol ratio and risk of MASLD in nonobese Chinese adults: A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Luo J, Zhuang Z, Xiong Y, Zhou H, Yi F, Gong D, Nie L, Wu X.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized in nonobese individuals; however, reliable markers for early risk identification remain limited. The fasting glucose-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (FHR) ratio, which reflects integrated glucolipid metabolism, has emerged as a potential indicator. This study aimed to evaluate the association between FHR and the incidence of MASLD in nonobese adults. This retrospective cohort study included 16,173 nonobese Chinese adults (body mass index < 25 kg/m2) from the Wenzhou Health Examination Cohort. Participants without MASLD at baseline were categorized into quartiles according to their FHR levels. Incident MASLD was diagnosed using abdominal ultrasonography during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) after adjusting for demographic, clinical, and metabolic factors. Dose-response relationships were assessed using restricted cubic spline models, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to evaluate predictive performance. During follow-up, 2322 participants developed MASLD. Higher FHR levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of MASLD. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in FHR was associated with a 22% higher risk of MASLD (HR, 1.22; 95% CI: 1.17-1.27, P < .001). Compared to the lowest quartile, the highest quartile showed a significantly elevated risk (HR: 2.10, 95% CI: 1.78-2.48; P for trend < 0.001). A positive dose-response relationship was also observed. ROC analysis showed that FHR had a moderate predictive ability (AUC, 0.701; 95% CI, 0.690 to 0.713), with an optimal cutoff value of 3.87. Elevated FHR was independently associated with an increased risk of MASLD in nonobese Chinese adults. Thus, FHR may serve as a simple and cost-effective biomarker for early risk stratification in this population.

title: Factors associated with postanesthesia care unit length of stay in adult patients undergoing elective surgery: A prospective observational cohort study.
authors: Uluer MS, Sargın M.
abstract: Postanesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay (LOS) is a key determinant of perioperative patient flow and resource utilization, yet the factors that prolong it remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify perioperative factors associated with PACU LOS in adult patients undergoing elective surgery. This prospective observational cohort study was conducted in a tertiary care hospital over a 6-month period. A total of 409 adult patients who underwent elective surgery under general anesthesia, spinal anesthesia, or peripheral nerve block were included. Demographic characteristics, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, anesthetic technique and agents, surgical category and grade, anesthesia duration, PACU vital signs, body temperature, pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting, shivering and rescue analgesia were recorded. PACU LOS was defined as the time from PACU admission until a modified Aldrete score of 9 or higher was achieved. Univariate associations were assessed with nonparametric tests, and independent predictors were identified using a gamma generalized linear model with a log link. The median PACU LOS was 45 minutes (interquartile range, 45-50). In univariate analyses, PACU LOS was associated with anesthesia duration (ρ = 0.158, P = .001), surgical grade (P = .002), anesthetic technique (P = .021; shorter stay after peripheral nerve block), pain score at PACU admission (ρ = 0.110, P = .026), rescue analgesia (P = .027), and postoperative shivering (P < .001), but not with demographic characteristics, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, anesthetic agents, surgical category, body temperature, or postoperative nausea and vomiting. In the multivariable model, major surgery (vs minor surgery; ratio of means 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-1.23), anesthesia duration (1.06 per hour, 95% CI 1.04-1.08), and postoperative shivering (1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.12) were independently associated with longer PACU LOS, whereas the associations of peripheral nerve block and admission pain score did not persist after adjustment. Surgical grade, anesthesia duration, and postoperative shivering were independent predictors of PACU LOS, whereas patient characteristics and the choice of anesthetic agent were not. Although their absolute effects were modest, prevention of postoperative shivering may represent a practical, modifiable target for improving PACU efficiency.

title: Factors Associated With Postoperative High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T Elevation After Thoracic Surgery: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Wang Z, Zheng W, Huang W, Hu Q, Pan L, Liao Z.
abstract: Aim To examine perioperative factors associated with postoperative high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) elevation after thoracic surgery. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study screened 588 consecutive records of patients who underwent thoracic surgery between June 2020 and June 2023, counting only the first eligible operation for each patient. After the exclusion of 128 records, all 460 eligible patients were included in the analysis. The outcome was defined as any hs-cTnT value ≥0.014 µg/L (14 ng/L) on postoperative day 1, 3, or 5. Eleven variables were entered simultaneously into a binary logistic regression model, with surgical method represented by indicator variables. Age was entered in years, and its odds ratio (OR) was expressed per 10-year increase; other continuous variables were analysed in their original units. Results Postoperative hs-cTnT elevation occurred in 155 of 460 patients (33.7%). In the multivariable model, age (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.23-2.63), procedure type (wedge resection: OR 4.47, 95% CI 1.57-12.71; segmentectomy/lobectomy: OR 5.52, 95% CI 2.04-14.96; oesophageal surgery: OR 27.96, 95% CI 5.50-142.27; each compared with other thoracic procedures), operation duration (OR 1.53 per hour, 95% CI 1.21-1.93), preoperative creatinine (OR 1.021 per µmol/L, 95% CI 1.007-1.035), preoperative potassium (OR 3.59 per mmol/L, 95% CI 1.84-7.02), and pre-existing atrial fibrillation (OR 5.56, 95% CI 1.84-16.83) were associated with the outcome. Postoperative day-1 haemoglobin showed an inverse association that did not reach statistical significance (OR 0.972 per g/L, 95% CI 0.942-1.002; p = 0.069), and the inverse association with ejection fraction was also not significant (OR 0.905 per %, 95% CI 0.772-1.060; p = 0.216). Conclusions Older age, procedure type, longer operation duration, higher preoperative creatinine, higher preoperative potassium, and pre-existing atrial fibrillation were associated with postoperative hs-cTnT elevation after multivariable adjustment. These associations do not establish causality or constitute a validated prediction model; rather, they generate hypotheses for the prospective evaluation of postoperative monitoring strategies.

title: Facial burns as functional trauma: Integrating expression, identity and long-term recovery: A narrative review.
authors: Kornhaber R, Beylin D, Cleary M, Goverman J, Haik J.
abstract: Advances in acute burn care have improved survival, shifting focus toward long-term functional recovery. Facial burns present a distinct clinical challenge due to the concentration of ocular, oral, respiratory, and expressive functions within a highly visible anatomical region. This narrative review synthesises functional and psychosocial literature to examine facial burns as trauma that disrupts dynamic facial movement, communication, and participation, and to evaluate limitations in current outcome frameworks. The face supports ocular protection, articulation, alimentation, airway patency, and non-verbal signalling. Contracture patterns, including microstomia, ectropion, nasal distortion, and midfacial contracture, may impair both mechanical function and expressive range. Recovery is typically longitudinal and iterative, addressing evolving distortion rather than restoring pre-injury dynamics. Even subtle restrictions of facial movement may alter speech clarity, eye contact, and self-recognition, with consequences extending beyond visible scarring. Existing outcome measures, including body image scales, burn-specific health instruments, and isolated physical metrics, do not adequately capture the interaction between structural repair, expressive mobility, and communicative participation. Recognition of facial burns as functional trauma supports the need for facial-specific composite outcome models and coordinated multidisciplinary care to optimise long-term recovery.

title: Evaluation of preoperative and perioperative characteristics in patients admitted to a postoperative intensive care unit: A prospective observational study.
authors: Kalkan S, Aydın A.
abstract: Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission is commonly considered for patients perceived to be at increased risk of postoperative complications. This study aimed to describe the preoperative and perioperative characteristics of patients admitted to a postoperative ICU and to explore associations between routinely available clinical parameters, inflammatory biomarkers, and short-term outcomes. This prospective observational study included 126 adult patients admitted postoperatively to a tertiary reanimation ICU. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, ASA physical status, anesthesia type, laboratory parameters, postoperative organ support requirements, ICU length of stay, and mortality were recorded. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) were evaluated. Continuous and categorical variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and chi-square or Fisher exact test, as appropriate. The mean age was 67.3 ± 16.1 years, and 114 (90.5%) patients were classified as ASA III. Abdominal surgery was the most common surgical category (56, 44.4%). Mean NLR and CAR values were 6.17 ± 8.36 and 1.17 ± 2.52, respectively. Two patients died (1.6%; exact 95% CI, 0.2-5.6%). Mortality was not significantly associated with NLR (P = .310), CAR (P = .845), admission SpO2 (P = .084), or hemoglobin level (P = .907). ICU length of stay showed an exploratory association with mortality (P = .004); given that only 2 deaths occurred, this observation cannot establish a prognostic relationship. In this selected postoperative ICU cohort, preoperative and perioperative characteristics did not clearly distinguish patients according to short-term outcomes. Because there was no non-ICU comparator cohort and mortality events were very limited, the findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger multicenter studies are needed to evaluate whether these parameters can support postoperative ICU admission decisions.

title: Estimated glucose disposal rate is inversely associated with frailty and cardiovascular mortality: Evidence from NHANES 2001 to 2018.
authors: Wei S, Yu S, Xue D.
abstract: With global population aging, the prevalence of frailty is steadily increasing. Insulin resistance plays a key role in the development of frailty and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. The estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) has been recognized as a reliable surrogate marker of insulin resistance. To date, no studies have investigated the association between eGDR, frailty, and CVD mortality in the U.S. population. We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001 to 2018 cycles and employed weighted logistic regression and weighted Cox proportional hazards models to evaluate the associations between eGDR and frailty, as well as CVD mortality among frail and non-frail individuals. Restricted cubic spline analysis was used to explore potential nonlinear relationships, and subgroup analyses were conducted to test the robustness of the findings. The results indicated a significant inverse association between eGDR and frailty prevalence; each 1 standard deviation increase in eGDR was associated with a 22.3% decrease in frailty risk (odds ratio = 0.777 [0.760, 0.795]). Higher eGDR levels were also significantly associated with lower CVD mortality risk. Among frail individuals, each standard deviation increase in eGDR was associated with a 4.3% lower risk of CVD mortality (hazard ratio = 0.957 [0.916, 0.988]); among non-frail individuals, the corresponding reduction was 7% (hazard ratio = 0.930 [0.885, 0.977]). The inverse association showed a stronger gradient across eGDR levels among non-frail individuals, whereas this pattern was not observed among frail individuals. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a nonlinear association between eGDR and both frailty and CVD mortality among frail individuals, whereas a linear relationship was observed among non-frail individuals. Subgroup analysis indicated that age modified the associations between eGDR, frailty, and CVD mortality in frail individuals. Smoking status influenced the relationship between eGDR and frailty, while race modified the association between eGDR and CVD mortality among non-frail individuals. eGDR was significantly and inversely associated with frailty and CVD mortality in both frail and non-frail populations. Higher eGDR levels were associated with a lower prevalence of frailty and lower cardiovascular mortality risk, suggesting that eGDR may serve as a potential marker for metabolic and cardiovascular risk stratification.

title: Establishment of normal reference values for ultrasound measurements of fetal cerebellar vermis during mid-trimester: A prospective cross-sectional study.
authors: Zhou M, Lin Z, Zhou C.
abstract: This study aimed to develop preliminary gestational age (GA)-specific reference ranges for ultrasonographic measurements of the fetal cerebellar vermis during mid-trimester at a single center. A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at our hospital from March 2024 to December 2025. A total of 104 singleton pregnancies between 14 and 27 weeks of gestation were enrolled. The midsagittal plane of the posterior fossa was obtained using 2-dimensional transabdominal ultrasound. The anteroposterior diameter, craniocaudal diameter, vermian area, and brainstem-vermis (BV) angle were measured. Polynomial regression analysis and the generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape- lambda-mu-sigma method were applied to model the relationship between each parameter and GA and to construct percentile curves. The anteroposterior diameter, craniocaudal diameter, and vermian area demonstrated significant positive correlations with GA (all P < .001), with growth patterns best fitted by quadratic regression models (R2 = 0.961, 0.954, and 0.978, respectively). The BV angle remained stable throughout mid-trimester, with a mean of 1.67° ± 0.88°. Gestational age-specific percentile reference ranges (5th, 50th, and 95th) were established for all dimensional parameters. Intra-observer and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients exceeded 0.90 for all measurements except the BV angle. This single-center study provides preliminary reference data for fetal cerebellar vermis measurements during mid-trimester, offering a practical quantitative reference for prenatal screening of the posterior fossa. As no affected fetuses were studied and diagnostic performance was not assessed, the study establishes reference ranges rather than demonstrating clinical effectiveness. Fetal sex did not influence any parameter. External and multicenter validation with larger cohorts is warranted.

title: Endurance Training Improves Insulin Sensitivity, Metabolic Flexibility, and Mitochondrial Function in Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Hansen M, Møller S, Blom I, Lange KK, Ziegler AK, Farlov JE, Borch J, Hesselager SA, Hansen JK, Liebmann A, Dal MH, Åkerström T, Helge JW, Hellsten Y, Dela F.
abstract: To determine how endurance training influences insulin sensitivity, metabolic flexibility, and mitochondrial function in individuals with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D). Insulin sensitivity (2-step hyperinsulinaemic-isoglycaemic clamp), metabolic flexibility, and mitochondrial respiratory capacity and H 2 O 2 emission were assessed in participants with T2D (n = 15) and controls (n = 14) before and after 12 weeks of supervised endurance training. Sensitivity analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models including all available participants. At baseline, glucose clearance was lower in individuals with T2D compared with controls. Training increased glucose clearance (mL/min/kg FFM) in both groups, with larger model-derived improvements in T2D (Step 1: +1.43 [0.88-1.97]; Step 2: +3.18 [2.12-4.23]) than in controls (Step 1: +0.76 [0.21-1.31]; Step 2: +1.49 [0.53-2.45]). The group × time interaction was significant at the higher insulin step. Metabolic flexibility to fat-but not glucose-was reduced in T2D and improved modestly with training. Mitochondrial respiratory capacity did not differ between groups; however, training decreased mitochondria-specific respiration and H 2 O 2 emission normalized to CS activity and respiration. Endurance training enhances insulin sensitivity and fat oxidation in individuals with T2D and induces favorable mitochondrial adaptations, despite the absence of intrinsic mitochondrial dysfunction.

title: Emergency MDCT in Internal Hernias: Short Reports Highlighting the Importance of Timely Surgical Intervention.
authors: Scalzone L, Mugnaini C, Cozzi D, Danti G, Grazzini G, Ferrarelli A, Miele V.

title: Efficacy comparison of 9 chemotherapy regimens in nonmetastatic Ewing's sarcoma treatment: A network meta-analysis.
authors: Zhou X, Yu Y, Guo J, Zhang X, Deng J, Deng Z, Xu J.
abstract: Background Optimal chemotherapy for nonmetastatic Ewing's sarcoma (ES) remains undefined, with no global consensus established among the available multidrug regimens. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Chinese databases (VIP [Chinese Scientific Journal Database], WanFang, China National Knowledge Infrastructure) up to May 2024 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing chemotherapy regimens for nonmetastatic ES. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane tools (for RCTs) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (for cohort studies). Efficacy was ranked via surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values for event-free survival and overall survival. Results Twelve studies (3834 patients) evaluating 9 regimens were included. The top 3 regimens for event-free survival were as follows: VDC (vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide) + IE (ifosfamide/etoposide)(In)(intensified regimen) and VTC (vincristine, topotecan, cyclophosphamide) (SUCRA = 92.1%); VDC+IE(In) (SUCRA = 85.4%); VDC+IE(St)(standard regimen) (SUCRA = 79.2%). For overall survival, the ranking was similar. VDC alone ranked lowest in both outcomes. Conclusion The VDC+IE(In)+VTC combination may exhibit superior efficacy among the 9 chemotherapy regimens for nonmetastatic ES, necessitating further validation through RCTs with larger sample sizes.

title: Efficacy and Prognostic Analysis of Neuro-Navigation Robot-Assisted Puncture Drainage for Thalamic Hemorrhage: A Comparison With Neuro-Endoscopy and External Ventricular Drainage.
authors: Luo K, Sun L, Tong F, Guo X, Xia X, Hong Y, Han Y.
abstract: Aim This study aims to compare the clinical efficacy of three surgical techniques-robot-assisted neuro-navigation, external ventricular drainage (EVD), and neuro-endoscopy-in evacuating intracranial hematomas in patients with thalamic hemorrhage. Methods This retrospective study included 110 patients, divided into three groups based on the surgical method: robot group ( n = 30), EVD group ( n = 37), and neuro-endoscopy group ( n = 43). Baseline characteristics, perioperative parameters, neurological function, inflammatory response, complications, and functional outcomes were compared and analyzed among the three patient groups. Results Compared with the EVD and neuro-endoscopy groups, the robot group had shorter operative times ( p p p p p p Conclusions Robot-assisted neuro-navigation-guided puncture drainage was associated with improved neurological recovery and short-term outcomes in patients with thalamic hemorrhage.

title: Effects of a Multicomponent App-Based Exercise Program on Motor Skill Development in Children With Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Secondary Outcome Analysis of a Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Zhu F, Dong Z, Kuang D, Zhu X, Bi X, Li Z, Yang L, Wang Y, Chen J, Xu B, Lin S, Zhou H, Ren Y.
abstract: Motor skill deficits are common in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), while traditional face-to-face exercise interventions are often limited by cost and accessibility. This secondary outcome analysis of a three-arm randomized controlled trial examined the effects of a multicomponent app-based exercise program on motor skill outcomes in children with ADHD. A total of 145 children aged 6-10 years were assigned to an app-based exercise group (Experimental Group 1, EG1; n = 53), a traditional offline exercise group (Experimental Group 2, EG2; n = 45), or a minimal-intervention control group (CG, n = 47). Both intervention groups received a 12-week program (3 sessions/week, 45-60 min/session) involving integrated physical and cognitive exercises, delivered either through a custom-developed WeChat applet ("LeDongYing") or through coach-led in-person sessions. Motor skills were assessed using the Test of Gross Motor Development, Third Edition (TGMD-3) for locomotor and ball skills, and the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (MABC-2) for manual dexterity, aiming and catching, and balance. Intervention effects were examined using linear mixed-effects models. Both EG1 and EG2 showed significant improvements across all motor skill domains (all p < 0.01), whereas the CG showed no significant changes. Pairwise comparisons showed that both intervention groups were superior to the CG on all motor skill outcomes (all p < 0.05), with no statistically significant differences between EG1 and EG2. These findings support the short-term efficacy of a multicomponent app-based exercise intervention for motor-test performance in children with ADHD compared with minimal intervention, suggesting potential as an alternative delivery when access to face-to-face exercise services is limited.

title: Effects of Multicomponent Training on Body Composition and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Skoradal MB, Kristiansen J, Póvoas S, Johannesen HL, Ellingsgaard H, Olsen HW, Mohr M, Sjúrðarson T.
abstract: We investigated whether 14 weeks of multicomponent training delivered as small-sided soccer improves body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and metabolic outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes. Adults aged 40-70 years (n = 111) were randomized to exercise (n = 66; three 60-min sessions per week) or usual care (n = 45). Constrained linear mixed models estimated between-group differences in change. No between-group difference was detected in the primary outcome, lean body mass (0.04 kg, 95% CI -0.97 to 1.05), or in fat mass, body fat percentage, or HbA1c. Compared with usual care, exercise produced greater increases in relative VO 2peak (between-group difference: 2.80 mL·kg -1 ·min -1 , 95% CI 1.69 to 3.92), absolute VO 2peak (237 mL/min, 95% CI 143 to 331), and Yo-Yo Intermittent Endurance Level 1 test performance (122 m, 95% CI 12 to 232). Exploratory analyses showed lower C-peptide (-10.3%, 95% CI -19.0 to -0.6) and HOMA2-IR (-10.8%, 95% CI -20.1 to -0.6), and higher HOMA2-%S (+12.2%, 95% CI 0.6 to 25.1), in the exercise group relative to usual care. Exploratory three-way interaction tests provided no clear evidence that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use modified the effects on lean body mass, fat mass, or absolute VO 2peak . Small-sided soccer improved cardiorespiratory fitness, whereas a benefit for lean body mass was not demonstrated. The metabolic findings require confirmation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06478173.

title: Effects and Moderators of High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) on Physiological Adaptations Among Team-Sport Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Zeng X, Yin M, Xu K, Tao M, Wang J, Zhong Y, Girard O, Nassis GP, Buchheit M, Li Y.
abstract: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is widely used in team sports, but the influence of participant and programme characteristics on physiological adaptations remains unclear. Five databases (Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CNKI) were searched initially on 25 April 2025 and updated on 21 December 2025. Mixed-effects models were used to estimate Hedges' g and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Forty-six studies involving 1204 athletes were included. Compared with regular sport-specific training alone, HIIT produced positive effects on maximal oxygen uptake (VO 2 max; g = 0.76, 95% CI [0.61, 0.92]), maximal aerobic power (g = 0.43, 95% CI [0.04, 0.82]), ventilatory threshold (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.53, 0.88]), Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test performance (g = 1.02, 95% CI [0.76, 1.28]), and 30-s Wingate peak (g = 0.91, 95% CI [0.67, 1.16]) and mean power (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.39, 1.01]). Effects on body composition were generally unclear. Mutually adjusted multivariable meta-regression identified no convincing evidence of differences in VO 2 max or Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test performance effects by sex or training level. Longer training duration was associated with greater VO 2 max effects. In exploratory analyses, model predictions indicated increases in VO 2 max of 2.56 mL·kg -1 ·min -1 (95% CI [1.54, 3.58]) after approximately 5 weeks and 5.11 mL·kg -1 ·min -1 (95% CI [3.32, 6.91]) after approximately 10 weeks. Shorter between-repetition recovery was associated with greater VO 2 max effects, although other programme variables were estimated imprecisely. Overall, adding HIIT to regular sport-specific training improves aerobic and anaerobic performance in trained team-sport athletes, whereas effects on body composition are limited. Associations involving programme characteristics should be interpreted cautiously because they were derived from study-level meta-regression. Trial Registration: PROSPERO Registration CRD42024609379.

title: Effectiveness of Exercise Snacks in Mitigating Adolescent Problematic Smartphone Use: A Four-Wave Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Li L, Peng B, Liu J, Tang D, Ma R.
abstract: Prolonged sedentary behavior and physical inactivity are important concerns in secondary-school settings. This 6-month, four-wave cluster randomized controlled trial evaluated whether integrating high-intensity exercise snacks into the school schedule could reduce adolescent problematic smartphone use. A total of 386 adolescents from 12 classes were randomized at the class level to an intervention group, which performed four daily 2-minute bouts of vigorous physical activity during scheduled school breaks, or a wait-list control group that maintained standard routines. Primary outcomes were smartphone addiction severity and device-derived daily screen time. Secondary outcomes included psychological measures and device-derived physical activity. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and months two, four, and six. The intervention group showed lower mean SAS-SV scores and daily screen time at month four than at baseline, alongside increases in daily steps and improvements in several psychological measures. The unadjusted between-group differences in change from baseline to month four were -6.356 SAS-SV points and -46.829 min/day of screen time. The pooled model-adjusted between-group differences in change from baseline to month four were -6.55 SAS-SV points (95% CI, -7.38 to -5.71) and -52.22 min/day of screen time (95% CI, -67.21 to -37.23). During the 2-month unguided follow-up, some improvements attenuated. These findings suggest that school-based exercise snacks may help reduce problematic smartphone use. The psychological mechanisms and clinical importance of the observed changes require further investigation.

title: Effect of Metatarsophalangeal Joint Position on Maximal Voluntary Isometric Ankle Plantar-Flexion Torque.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Shiotani H, Takahashi K, Taniai K, Tsuru H, Kawakami Y.
abstract: The joint position at which maximal torque is produced indicates the optimal position for agonist muscles to function. It is well-documented that the maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC) torque of ankle plantar-flexion varies with knee and ankle joint positions. However, metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint position may also affect MVIC torque, reflecting force-length relationships of the toe flexor muscles. This study examined the effect of MTP joint position on MVIC torque of ankle plantar-flexion. Sixteen young males performed MVICs of ankle plantar-flexion with the MTP joint at 0°, 15°, 30°, and 45° of dorsiflexion. Ankle plantar-flexion torque, plantar pressure distribution, and surface electromyography (sEMG) were recorded. MVIC torque was significantly greater at 15° than at 0°, 30°, and 45° (+11.0%-21.4%). Similarly, forces applied under the toes were significantly greater at 15° than at the other conditions (+13.4%-37.5%), whereas forces applied under the proximal foot and sEMG amplitudes of the major ankle plantar-flexors remained comparable across MTP joint positions. At 45° MTP joint dorsiflexion, toe forces were 17.5% lower than at 30°, COP shifted 3-5 mm proximally, and sEMG amplitudes were 26.8% lower in abductor hallucis than at 30°, and 28.9% and 26.3% lower in flexor digitorum brevis than at 15° and 30°, respectively. These results demonstrate that MVIC torque of ankle plantar-flexion varies with MTP joint position in an inverted U-shaped manner and is maximized at 15° of MTP joint dorsiflexion, reflecting changes in toe flexor forces, proximodistal COP displacement, and sEMG amplitudes of the intrinsic foot muscles.

title: ECAP-Guided Closed-Loop Spinal Cord Stimulation for Axial Thoracic Pain: A Case Report.
authors: Soin A, Kassis S, Witte RJ, Sloop B, Brittain C.
abstract: Thoracic spine pain is among the least commonly reported pain syndromes. Conventional therapeutic strategies are frequently ineffective and may be associated with adverse events. Closed-loop spinal cord stimulation (SCS) assisted with evoked compound action potentials (ECAPs) has emerged as a promising, safe and effective alternative. In this case report, we describe the successful use of ECAP-controlled closed-loop SCS in a patient with refractory thoracic spine pain. A female patient in her 40s presented with several axial thoracic pain refractory to all conservative and interventional therapies. Upon admission, the numeric rating scale (NRS) for pain score was 8/10. Functional limitations included restricted sleep duration (3 h) and limited standing and walking tolerance (20 min). The patient underwent a one-week trial of ECAP-controlled closed-loop SCS, during which 24 million smart adjustments were automatically performed to maintain consistent neural activation. The dose accuracy was ±5 μV, with a target ECAP of 19.4 μV, and the measure was 16.4 μV, and the patient used the device 100% of the time. Following treatment, the patient reported improvement in pain and functional outcomes, with NRS scores decreasing to 2/10, and substantial improvements in sleep (6 h), standing, and walking duration. This case suggests that ECAP-assisted closed-loop SCS may provide meaningful pain relief and functional improvements in patients with refractory spine pain.

title: Durability of Physiological Determinants of Distance-Running Performance in Warm and Temperate Environments.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Hunter B, Fujii N, Maunder E, Muniz-Pumares D.
abstract: Runners increasingly train and compete in warm conditions, yet it is unclear whether heat stress accelerates the deterioration of the physiological determinants of distance-running performance during prolonged running. Ten trained runners (7 M; 3 F; 38 ± 11 years; peak oxygen uptake (V̇O 2 peak): 56.0 ± 5.7 mL·kg -1 ·min -1 ) visited the laboratory on four occasions. In randomized order, participants completed incremental tests to determine the first ventilatory threshold (VT 1 ), V̇O 2 peak, and end-test speed in temperate (TEMP; 19°C) and warm (WARM; 30°C; both 40% relative humidity) conditions in a "fresh" state (PRE). Tests were repeated (POST) after 90 min of running in the same condition at 5% Δ between the speed at VT 1 (sVT 1 ) and end-test speed. Running economy was measured at 15-min intervals throughout. In the rested state, sVT 1 was ~7% (~0.8 km·h -1 ) lower in WARM than TEMP, and declined after prolonged running in both conditions (TEMP: -8.6%; WARM: -11.1%), with no condition × time interaction. V̇O 2 peak was reduced after prolonged running (TEMP: -4.8%; WARM: -4.0%), with no condition × time interaction. In contrast, running economy deteriorated to a greater extent in WARM (+5.4% vs. +1.7% from 15 to 90 min), and end-test speed declined more in WARM than TEMP (-12.1% vs. -6.8%). We found no evidence that heat altered the durability of sVT 1 and V̇O 2 peak when intensity was prescribed relative to condition-specific capacity. However, sVT 1 was already lower in WARM before prolonged running, so that after prolonged running it was, on average, 17.1% below the rested value in TEMP.

title: Dissecting the Metabolic Costs of Uphill and Downhill Walking.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Jessup LN, Kelly LA, Cresswell AG, Lichtwark GA.
abstract: Work- and collision-based models of locomotion relate the body's mechanical work requirements to metabolic energy expenditure at a system level, but do not capture the underlying force and work demands of muscle that drive energy use. Energy is liberated as heat to activate muscle and maintain force production ("force-related costs") and as heat and work to shorten or lengthen active muscle ("work-related costs"). We collected experimental inverse dynamics, electromyography, and ultrasound data from the main power-producing lower-limb muscles during walking at slopes spanning ±15%. These data were used to evaluate a musculoskeletal modeling approach that simulates muscle states, inputs them to a phenomenological energy cost model to estimate metabolic power, and partitions force- and work-related costs. Simulated metabolic power was compared with indirect calorimetry. Summing simulated metabolic power across only the eight muscles evaluated experimentally correlated more strongly with experimental metabolic power than summing across all modeled muscles (adjusted R 2 = 0.95 vs. 0.86), so analyses focused on this subset. Both approaches differed from experimental metabolic power in absolute terms, so results are interpreted as relative changes across slopes. Simulated force-related costs increased at steeper inclines and declines and were moderately correlated with mean joint moments (adjusted R 2 = 0.67), with unexplained variance likely reflecting muscle operating lengths. Simulated work-related costs increased as slope became more positive and were strongly correlated with net joint work (adjusted R 2 = 0.95). Knee joint mechanics seem particularly indicative of these costs. Incorporating a force-related cost term may offer a more explanatory link to muscle mechanical demands than work- and collision-based models alone.

title: Discordance between levator hiatus morphology and function in pelvic floor dysfunction.
authors: Xue Y, Mu L, Nan S.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize static anatomical and dynamic functional parameters of the levator hiatus in women with bladder prolapse and to examine their diagnostic performance. Primiparous women with a diagnosis of bladder prolapse were recruited as the prolapse group (n = 62), while healthy nulliparous women were included as the control group (n = 60). Nulliparous controls were selected to provide a reference group without childbirth-related pelvic floor remodeling; however, because parity differed systematically between groups, parity-related effects cannot be separated from prolapse-related effects in this case-control design. The levator hiatus area was measured both at rest and during maximal Valsalva maneuver, and the difference between these 2 measurements was calculated. Hierarchical regression analysis was performed to evaluate the independent and joint contributions of group status and body mass index (BMI) to these parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess diagnostic performance within the study cohort. The levator hiatus resting area, Valsalva area, and area change were all significantly greater in the prolapse group than in the control group (P < .001). Static anatomical parameters, including the resting and Valsalva areas, were associated with group status (P < .001), whereas the dynamic functional parameter, namely the area change, was associated with both group status (standardized β = 0.829, P < .001) and BMI (standardized β = 0.139, P = .003). ROC analysis showed very high apparent diagnostic performance for area change in this cohort (AUC = 1.000), compared with the static anatomical parameters (AUC = 0.999 and 0.920, respectively). These findings indicate different statistical association patterns for levator hiatus morphology and dynamic area change. Dynamic functional assessment may provide complementary information beyond static anatomical measures; however, its diagnostic performance requires confirmation in parity-matched and independent validation cohorts.

title: Device-Measured 24-h Movement Behaviors and Arterial Intima-Media Thickness in Young Adults.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
authors: Suorsa K, Laitinen T, Heiskanen J, Leskinen T, Meng Y, Pasanen J, Rovio S, Koskinen JS, Mykkänen J, Heinonen OJ, Viikari J, Rönnemaa T, Niinikoski H, Raitakari O, Stenholm S, Pahkala K.
abstract: Physical activity, including light physical activity (LPA) and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), sedentary behavior (SED), and sleep, often referred to as "24-h movement behaviors", are modifiable behaviors that may be associated with arterial intima-media thickness (IMT). However, their combined associations with arterial IMT, especially aortic IMT, where cardiometabolic risk burden may be reflected at an earlier age, have not been studied before. This study examined how 24-h movement behaviors associate with aortic and carotid IMT among young adults. Participants (n = 327) were healthy young adults (mean age 26.1 years, SD 0.2) from the Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project (STRIP). 24-h movement behaviors were measured using a wrist-worn accelerometer for 1 week. Aortic and carotid IMT were measured with ultrasonography. Associations between 24-h movement behaviors and aortic and carotid IMT were analyzed using compositional data analysis and compositional isotemporal substitution analysis, adjusting for sex, education, smoking, and distribution of dietary fats. Descriptive model-based estimations indicated lower aortic IMT values for compositions with a higher proportion of LPA. However, theoretical time reallocations between LPA and other behaviors did not indicate significant differences in aortic IMT (e.g., 30 min from sleep to LPA, -0.005 mm [95% CI -0.020-0.010 mm], from SED to LPA, -0.006 mm [95% CI -0.018-0.006], and from MVPA to LPA, -0.008 mm [95% CI -0.038-0.021]). No associations were found for carotid IMT either. No apparent associations were observed between 24-h movement behaviors and arterial IMT among young adults.

title: Development and Validation of a LASSO-Based Prediction Model for Postoperative Bleeding Following Pediatric Tonsillectomy and Adenoidectomy.
authors: Yang Y, Li L, Cheng Q.
abstract: Aim Despite technological advancements, children undergoing adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation remain at risk for postoperative bleeding. This study aimed to construct a precise machine learning-based model to predict the risk of postoperative bleeding in this population. Methods A retrospective cohort study involving 306 pediatric patients who underwent the procedure between January 2023 and January 2025 was conducted. Clinical data, including demographic characteristics, preoperative laboratory findings, and surgical details, were collected and cleaned. The dataset was randomly divided into a training set (n = 244) and a validation set (n = 62) at an 8:2 ratio. A predictive model was developed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) cross-validation algorithm, and its performance was assessed in the validation cohort. Results Among 306 children, 24 (7.8%) experienced postoperative bleeding. Univariate comparisons identified significant differences in 11 variables: age, height, weight, body mass index (BMI), disease duration, postoperative infection, dietary compliance, postoperative pain, lymphocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR) (all p Conclusions Postoperative infection, dietary adherence, postoperative pain, and age are significant predictors of bleeding following pediatric adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation. The LASSO-based model provides a reliable tool for identifying high-risk patients and optimizing perioperative management.

title: Delayed pancytopenia following ingestion of wild mushrooms consistent with Hypholoma fasciculare: A case report.
authors: Byeon H, An J.
abstract: Rationale Hypholoma fasciculare (sulfur tuft) is a toxic mushroom commonly associated with gastrointestinal symptoms. However, hematologic toxicity related to Hypholoma species has rarely been reported. In particular, delayed-onset pancytopenia following mushroom ingestion remains poorly understood. Patient concerns A 57-year-old man presented to the emergency department after ingesting self-collected wild mushrooms. Approximately 10 days after ingestion, he developed fever and generalized weakness. Diagnoses Laboratory evaluation revealed delayed-onset pancytopenia. Extensive infectious, autoimmune, and hematological investigations, including viral serology and bone marrow examinations, excluded primary hematological malignancies, aplastic anemia, and infectious causes. Based on the clinical course and the exclusion of alternative etiologies, toxin-mediated bone marrow suppression following mushroom ingestion was considered the most plausible diagnosis. Interventions The patient was conservatively managed with close monitoring and supportive care. No specific antidotal or immunosuppressive agents were administered. Outcomes Hematological parameters gradually recovered without targeted interventions. Follow-up laboratory tests demonstrated complete resolution of the pancytopenia, and the patient remained clinically stable without recurrence during outpatient follow-up. Lessons This case highlights delayed pancytopenia as a potential manifestation of toxic mushroom ingestion, even in the absence of severe initial symptoms. Recognition of this pattern may facilitate a timely diagnosis and appropriate monitoring.

title: Current epidemiological profile and characteristics of traumatic and nontraumatic spinal cord injury in Jinan, China: A two-center retrospective observational study.
authors: Song L, Wang K, Zhao M, Chen X, Chang H, Fu Y, Ruoxian S.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a highly disabling neurological condition associated with long-term functional impairment and substantial healthcare needs. In Jinan, hospital-based evidence directly comparing traumatic SCI (TSCI) and nontraumatic SCI (NTSCI) within the same regional tertiary-care system remains limited. This study aimed to describe and compare their epidemiological and clinical profiles to inform targeted prevention and hospital-based care planning. We conducted a 2-center, hospital-based retrospective observational study of patients with SCI admitted between 2015 and 2024. Categorical variables were summarized as n (%) and compared between TSCI and NTSCI using Pearson chi-square tests or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, as appropriate. Because length of stay was markedly right-skewed, it was summarized as median (interquartile range [IQR]) and compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. All comparisons were two-sided and unadjusted. A total of 1334 patients with SCI were included (1134 TSCI and 200 NTSCI). TSCI showed a greater male predominance than NTSCI (78.66% vs 56.50%, P < .001), and age-group distributions also differed (P < .001). Falls (46.03%) and traffic accidents (40.65%) were the leading TSCI mechanisms; electric bicycle-related crashes accounted for the largest share of traffic-related TSCI (191/461, 41.43%). The leading NTSCI etiologies were neoplasm (33.00%), demyelinating disease (20.00%), infectious disease (17.00%), vascular disease (15.50%), and degenerative disease (14.50%). American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale distributions differed between groups (P < .001). Median length of stay was 12 days (IQR = 8-21) for TSCI and 46 days (IQR = 33.75-61) for NTSCI (P < .001). A primary in-hospital complication was recorded in 78.31% of TSCI and 80.00% of NTSCI patients (P = .591); however, the distribution of primary complication categories differed overall (P = .040). Urinary tract infection was more frequent in TSCI (24.78% vs 16.00%, P = .007), whereas pulmonary infection was more frequent in NTSCI (12.26% vs 18.00%, P = .027). Within these 2 tertiary hospitals in Jinan, TSCI and NTSCI showed different demographic, neurological, treatment, hospitalization, and primary complication patterns. TSCI was characterized by prominent fall- and traffic-related injury mechanisms, whereas NTSCI showed heterogeneous etiologies and substantially longer hospitalization. These hospital-based findings support targeted prevention priorities and differentiated clinical care pathways but should not be interpreted as population-level incidence estimates or as independent effects of traumatic versus nontraumatic etiology.

title: Corticosteroid-sensitive idiopathic hypertrophic spinal pachymeningitis: A case report.
authors: Zhang R, Xi M, Zhang Z, Duan L.
abstract: Rationale Idiopathic hypertrophic spinal pachymeningitis (IHSP) is a rare inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology, characterized by focal or diffuse thickening of the spinal dura. This report describes a patient with progressive lower-limb weakness and paresthesia. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed longitudinally extensive dural lesions exhibiting uniformly low-signal intensity on T1-, T2-, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) sequences. Corticosteroid therapy resulted in marked clinical and radiological improvement. The case underscores the diagnostic value of multimodal MRI, particularly DWI and ADC, when biopsy is not feasible. Patient concerns A 19-year-old female presented with progressive weakness and sensory abnormalities in the lower limbs. Diagnoses Based on cerebrospinal fluid analysis and thoracic spinal MRI findings, and in the absence of dural biopsy (which was declined by the patient), a diagnosis of IHSP was made. Interventions The patient was treated with corticosteroids, which led to significant clinical and imaging improvement. Outcomes Symptoms recurred during corticosteroid dose reduction but improved after dose escalation. The patient remained asymptomatic, with no recurrence of limb weakness or numbness, during the subsequent 3-year follow-up. Lessons Multimodal MRI, especially DWI and ADC sequences, can serve as a valuable diagnostic tool in cases of suspected IHSP when pathological biopsy is not possible.

title: Corrigendum.
authors: Mancino F, Haddad FS.

title: Construction of a nomogram for predicting pathological upgrading after LEEP in patients with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 based on colposcopic morphological features: A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Chen L, Xie Y, Liu D, Liu X.
abstract: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grade 1/2 diagnosed by colposcopy-directed biopsy may underestimate the final lesion grade found on excision. In patients who proceed to Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP), postoperative pathology may show histopathological upgrading relative to the preoperative biopsy. Although HPV testing and ThinPrep Cytology Test (TCT) are standard screening tools, their differential value in this LEEP-selected CIN1/2 population remains unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with pathological upgrading after LEEP and to construct an internally validated nomogram based on colposcopic morphological features. We retrospectively analyzed 122 patients who underwent LEEP for clinical indications between 2020 and 2025 with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2. Pathological upgrading was defined as biopsy CIN1 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN2, or biopsy CIN2 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN3 (invasive carcinoma included). These 2 transitions were prespecified and are clinically distinct; event counts were, therefore, also reported by baseline biopsy grade. Multivariable logistic regression was used to develop a nomogram. Discrimination and calibration were assessed with ROC analysis and bootstrap internal validation; clinical utility was explored with decision curve analysis (DCA). Pathological upgrading occurred in 46/122 (37.7%) patients in this LEEP-selected cohort, including 4/15 (26.7%) with baseline CIN1 and 42/107 (39.3%) with baseline CIN2. In the multivariable model, Reid Colposcopic Index (OR = 1.41, P = .013) and number of involved quadrants (OR = 1.93, P = .018) were significantly associated with upgrading, whereas menopausal status (OR = 2.83, P = .059) and biopsy count (OR = 0.70, P = .068) did not reach conventional significance but were retained as candidate predictors. HPV genotype category and TCT were not significantly associated with upgrading. The nomogram showed apparent AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.719-0.883) on internal evaluation; calibration and DCA supported exploratory clinical utility within this surgical cohort. In women with biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 who already had indications for LEEP, colposcopic morphological features (Reid score and lesion extent) were more informative than HPV/TCT for predicting histopathological upgrading after excision. The nomogram may assist risk stratification within this selected surgical population. An ROC-derived probability threshold of 43% is presented only as an exploratory cut-point requiring external validation and should not yet be used as a standalone rule to choose observation vs LEEP in unselected CIN1/2 patients.

title: Consensus guidelines in the management of paediatric flexible flatfoot : a Delphi study of the British Society of Children's Orthopaedic Surgery.
authors: Morrow EM, Bennet S, Morrison SC, Bridgens A, Mavrotas J, Brousil J, Knight D, Kokkinakis M, BSCOS Flatfoot Consensus Group, Barry M, Bartley H, Carlile G, Chomicki M, Dwyer J, Easton V, Gibbons P, Giles S, Peek A, Phillips K, Robinson E.
abstract: Aims The assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children is inconsistent, reflecting a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. This study aimed to develop a British Society for Children's Orthopaedic Surgery (BSCOS)-led consensus guideline for the multidisciplinary assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children. Methods A modified Delphi consensus opinion study was conducted among the membership of the BSCOS. A multidisciplinary steering committee developed an initial set of statements based on clinical expertise, current evidence, and recognized variation in practice. A total of 33 statements addressing assessment, conservative, and surgical management were scored over two Delphi rounds using a nine-point Likert scale. Participant responses were anonymized. Consensus was defined prospectively as ≥ 75%. Statements that did not meet the consensus threshold were revised and rescored, or discussed and voted on by the steering committee. Results A total of 169 clinicians participated in Round One and 167 in Round Two. Most respondents were consultant orthopaedic surgeons (80%; n = 136), with further representation from registrars/fellows (5%; n = 9), and allied health professionals (AHPs) and advanced nurse practitioners (14%; n = 24). Overall, 24 of 33 statements met the consensus threshold. A further two statements were included following steering committee voting, resulting in 26 final statements. Areas of uncertainty were highlighted in the statements that did not reach consensus, particularly regarding the selection of specific surgical procedures. Conclusion This national consensus guideline provides a framework for clinicians managing children's flexible flatfoot, establishing a benchmark for future evaluation.

title: Congenital and Perinatal Compartment Syndrome: The Things We Have Learned.
authors: Wagner T, Kruit AS, Hovius S, Ulrich D.

title: Computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation of tibial fractures.
authors: Zhao Z, Cai C, Ji G, Xu W.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame (TSF) for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation (UEF) of tibial fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 18 patients with tibial misalignment after UEF between February 2019 and February 2024. Using the TSF technique, X-ray parameters (deformity, frame, and mounting) were entered into software to generate a six-axis correction prescription. Reduction time, number of X-ray exposures, total external fixation duration, clinical fracture healing time, complications, and functional recovery were recorded. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare preoperative and final visual analogue scale (VAS) scores because the paired differences were not normally distributed; data are presented as mean (range) or median (interquartile range [IQR]). All 18 patients were followed up for a mean of 14.9 months (range: 12-18 months). Satisfactory reduction was achieved in all cases after TSF adjustment. Mean reduction time was 19.0 minutes (range, 15-24 minutes), and patients received a mean of 1.4 X-ray exposures (range, 1-3). Clinical fracture healing occurred after a mean of 24.0 weeks (range, 21-29 weeks), and total external fixation lasted a mean of 25.2 weeks (range, 22-30 weeks). Johner-Wruhs ratings at final follow-up were excellent in 15 patients and good in 3 (100% excellent/good). Median VAS scores improved from 7 (IQR, 6-8) before surgery to 1 (IQR, 0-2) at final follow-up (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z = -3.77, P < .001). Superficial pin tract infections developed in 3 patients (16.7%; 3/18) and were controlled with oral antibiotics and dressing changes. No patient had deep infection, pin loosening, nonunion, or bone exposure. In this small, single-arm retrospective cohort, all 18 patients achieved satisfactory reduction with computer-assisted TSF, and adjustment times were short. No patient underwent secondary open reduction or fixation. These preliminary findings suggest that TSF may serve as a feasible minimally invasive option for correcting early malalignment following UEF of tibial fractures; however, multicenter controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these results.

title: Comparison of Telerehabilitation and Face-to-Face McKenzie Therapy Following Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Discectomy: A Multicentre Retrospective Matched Cohort Study.
authors: Zhao C, Zhao N, Lyu Y, Li Z, Chen J, Sun J, Huang L, Lu S, Wu M.
abstract: Aim To compare short-term pain, disability, and functional outcomes between telerehabilitation and face-to-face McKenzie therapy following unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) discectomy for lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Methods This multicentre retrospective matched cohort study included adults undergoing UBE discectomy for LDH at Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital and Xiyuan Hospital of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences between October 2023 and December 2024. Patients received either in-home telerehabilitation (Tele) or in-clinic physiotherapy (Clinic) according to the standard practice of the treating centre rather than by random allocation. Propensity score matching (PSM, 1:1) was used to reduce confounding. Both groups completed a 12-week McKenzie programme. Primary outcomes were Modified Von Korff (MvK) pain and disability scales and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, modified lumbar Schober (MLS), and the 6-minute walk test (6MWT). Results After matching, 122 patients were included (Tele: n = 61; Clinic: n = 61). Matching reduced between-group imbalance for every covariate, with all absolute standardised mean differences (SMDs) below 0.25, although modest residual imbalances remained for some covariates. For the primary outcomes, scores decreased significantly from baseline to 12 weeks in both groups (all time effects, p p = 0.979; MvK disability, p = 0.794; ODI, p = 0.910). The between-group difference on the MvK pain scale at 12 weeks was substantially smaller than the established minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 10 points. All secondary outcomes also improved significantly in both groups (all time effects, p p > 0.05). Overall adverse event rates were comparable between groups. Conclusions Telerehabilitation and face-to-face McKenzie therapy were associated with comparable short-term improvements after UBE discectomy. These findings suggest that telerehabilitation may be a feasible alternative to in-clinic rehabilitation, although prospective randomised trials are needed for confirmation.

title: Comparative Analysis of Nail Plate Combination Over Alternative Fixation Constructs in Low-Energy Distal Femur Fractures: Recovery of Ambulatory Status and Outcomes.
authors: Pereira DE, Rust B, Barton D, Eggebrecht Z, Wilson JL, Obey MR, McAndrew CM, Berkes MB.
abstract: Objectives To compare ambulatory status, union, mortality, and operative complications in patients with distal femur fracture treated with the nail plate combination (NPC) and alternative fixation constructs. Methods . Design Retrospective Cohort Study. Setting Single Level 1, tertiary referral Academic center. Patient selection criteria This study included adults with a low-energy distal femur fracture (OTA/AO33A/C and Su 1-3) that received ORIF within 2018-2024. Exclusions were pathologic fractures, antegrade intramedullary devices, and baseline nonambulators (from ambulatory status evaluation only). Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome was ambulatory status at postoperative intervals using Koval-Walking-Score. Secondary outcomes included radiographic union, mortality, and reoperation. Results A total of 404 patients with a low-energy distal femur fracture were included, with 342 included for mobility analysis. Fixation constructs included 189 NPC (mean age 75.0 ± 10.2, 83.1% female), 118 lateral locking plate (LLP) (mean age 73.4 ± 10.2; 76.3% female), 79 retrograde intramedullary nail (rIMN) (mean age 73.7 ± 11.1, 74.7% female), and 18 dual plate combination (mean age 74.6 ± 10.9, 83.3% female) (age P = 0.567, sex P = 0.701). NPC was more frequently selected for Su 2 (56.2%) and Su 3 (65.9%) ( P = 0.001).
