NPC demonstrated lower average ambulatory impairment score over LLP: 3 weeks (-0.8; P = 0.002), 6 weeks (-1.1; P Conclusions In this study, NPC was associated with superior ambulatory recovery rates to preinjury status over single-implant constructs and improved mortality rates over rIMN. Thus, NPC represented a reliable construct for early ambulation and recovery in these injuries. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Comment on "Efficacy and Safety of Tofacitinib Versus Placebo in Patients With Early-Grade Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial".

title: Clinicopathologic significance of PD-L1 expression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
authors: Onyszczuk M, Szweda-Gandor N, Rynkiewicz M, Drozdzowska B.
abstract: Programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a protein that, when interacting with its receptor programmed cell death protein 1, functions as a negative regulator of the antitumor T-cell-mediated immune response. The prognostic significance of PD-L1 expression in renal cell carcinoma has been examined in previous studies; however, the results remain controversial. The clinicopathologic associations of PD-L1 expression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma were evaluated in 242 cases. PD-L1 immunoreactivity (using anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody, clone ZR3) was assessed separately in tumor cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells (TIICs). PD-L1 positivity in cancer cells was defined as the presence of a membranous immunostaining pattern of any intensity in ≥ 1% of the corresponding cells, while PD-L1 positivity in TIICs was defined as membranous or cytoplasmic staining observed in ≥ 1% of the immune cells at any intensity. Associations with prespecified clinicopathologic variables were analyzed with appropriate categorical or continuous-data tests and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. PD-L1 positivity was detected in tumor cells in 26.4% of specimens and in TIICs in 48.3% of specimens. After false-discovery-rate correction, tumor cells PD-L1 status was associated with tumor-size category, pathologic T stage, WHO/International Society of Urological Pathology grade, tumor necrosis, and sarcomatoid and rhabdoid transformation, while TIICs PD-L1 status was associated only with WHO/International Society of Urological Pathology grade. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in OS according to tumor cells PD-L1 expression (log-rank P = .2925) or TIICs PD-L1 expression (log-rank P = .9748). Compartment-specific PD-L1 expression showed exploratory associations with selected clinicopathologic characteristics; however, neither tumor cells nor TIICs PD-L1 expression was associated with OS. These findings do not establish an independent prognostic role for PD-L1 expression and warrant external validation.

title: Clinically suspected acute myocarditis with ST-segment elevation, multiorgan dysfunction, and reversible conduction disturbance in an older patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis: A case report.
authors: Pang M, Zhao L, Zhang Z, Cao L, Wang H, Cui J, Wu H, Shi S.
abstract: Rationale ST-segment elevation and marked myocardial injury require urgent exclusion of coronary occlusion. Maintenance hemodialysis adds metabolic, volume, biomarker, and bleeding-related uncertainty. Patient concerns A 70-year-old woman receiving thrice-weekly hemodialysis developed chest tightness, dyspnea, and upper abdominal pain during dialysis. She returned with recurrent symptoms, severe metabolic acidosis, lactate 21 mmol/L, ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3, and troponin I that increased from 13,019.45 to >25,000 ng/L. Diagnoses Coronary angiography showed unobstructed epicardial arteries with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction grade 3 flow. Clinically suspected acute myocarditis remained the leading working diagnosis, but cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and endomyocardial biopsy were not performed and other causes of myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries could not be definitively excluded. The course was complicated by pulmonary congestion, metabolic and volume instability, hepatic injury, suspected pancreatic involvement, gastrointestinal bleeding, and symptomatic sinus arrest. Interventions Antithrombotic therapy was reassessed after angiography and withheld when bleeding developed. Early continuous venovenous hemofiltration was performed without circuit anticoagulation, with heparin reintroduced later when clinically appropriate. Continuous renal replacement therapy was used for volume, electrolyte, and acid-base support. A temporary transvenous pacemaker was implanted for telemetry-confirmed sinus arrest with a maximum pause of 8.78 seconds. Outcomes The maximum R-R interval decreased to 1.97 seconds, permitting pacemaker removal. At approximately 3 months, syncope had not recurred, but persistent atrial fibrillation, New York Heart Association class III symptoms, and an left ventricular ejection fraction of 47% indicated incomplete cardiac recovery. Lessons In a hemodialysis patient with a ST-elevation myocardial infarction-like presentation and non-obstructive coronary arteries, subsequent management should combine a structured myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries differential with explicit diagnostic uncertainty and repeated reassessment of bleeding, metabolic, volume, infectious, and rhythm-related risks.

title: Clinical outcomes of transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum in patients aged 50 years or older with hip dysplasia : a propensity score-matched comparative study.
authors: Fujii M, Mochizuki H, Tanaka S, Kawano S, Ueno M, Oba Y, Morimoto T.
abstract: Aims To clarify whether transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum (TOA) in patients aged ≥ 50 years with hip dysplasia provides clinical, radiological, and patient-reported outcomes comparable with those in younger patients. Methods Among 615 patients undergoing TOA between November 1998 and July 2019, 131 patients aged ≥ 50 years were propensity score-matched 1:1 to 131 patients aged Results In patients aged ≥ 50 years, the median mHHS improved from 62 (IQR 54 to 75) to 92 (IQR 84 to 96) (p Conclusion TOA achieved long-term joint survival comparable with that in younger patients, supporting TOA as a joint-preserving option in this age group. However, the sport/recreation score was lower and complications more frequent than in patients aged < 45 years. Preoperative Tönnis grade 2 predicted failure, indicating that joint degeneration, rather than age alone, should guide patient selection.

title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: An aggregated analysis of published case reports and case series.
authors: Zhang H, Chen C, Zhu Z, Meng W, Fu X, Jiang J, Chen W.
abstract: Background To explore the clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (DRONJ). Methods Published case studies about DRONJ were retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, and WANFANG, and relevant information was extracted for analysis. The search covered the period from the inception of each database to November 1, 2024. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify prognostic factors for DRONJ. Results A total of 31 articles were included in this study. Of the 110 patients with DRONJ, 57 (51.8%) healed completely. Logistic regression analysis showed that diabetes (odds ratio [OR] 4.29, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.18-15.63, P = .027) and corticosteroid use (OR 3.44, 95%CI 1.03-11.50, P = .045) were significantly associated with a poor treatment outcome, while surgical treatment (OR 0.19, 95%CI 0.07-0.54, P = .002) was significantly associated with a lower risk of poor prognosis. Conclusion Diabetes, corticosteroid use, and surgical intervention might be associated with the prognosis of DRONJ. Given that the study was based on published case studies, the generalizability of the results should be interpreted with caution due to a high risk of publication and selection bias.

title: Circulating inflammatory proteins mediate the causal relationship between blood alliin and cancer: A two-step, multivariable Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Chen Y, Xiao S, Feng P, Gao G, Wang H, Duan Y, Chen Z, Zhuo Y.
abstract: An association has been found between alliin and reduced risks of various cancers; however, evidence for these causal relationships remain limited. This study utilized Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to assess the potential causal relationships between circulating alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers. We selected instrumental variables from the latest and largest European genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets. First, we comprehensively assessed the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers through two-sample MR analysis. Subsequently, we repeated the validation of instrumental variables using cancer GWAS statistics from different studies and merged the results by meta-analysis. Two-step MR analysis was used to investigate whether 91 inflammatory proteins mediate the effect of alliin on the risk of cancer. Finally, multivariable MR analysis was conducted to determine the direct effects of alliin on the risk of cancer, with adjustment for potential mediators. Inverse variance weighted results were considered the primary observation outcome, and additional sensitivity analyses were conducted. Increased blood alliin levels were significantly causally associated with decreased risks of prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer, lymphoma, and colorectal cancer, with the corresponding meta-analyses also showing significant associations. In the two-step MR analysis, chemokine ligand 23 (CCL23) and oncostatin M (OSM) as well as interleukin-12B (IL12B) were the key mediators of the inverse causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of prostate cancer as well as the risks of ovarian and colorectal cancers, respectively. STAM-binding protein was a key mediator of the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of lymphoma. The results of this study support that increased blood alliin levels can reduce the risks of multiple cancers, with circulating inflammatory proteins potentially mediating this association.

title: Central nervous system hemorrhage related to protein kinase inhibitors: A real-world pharmacovigilance case-control study and genetic correlation study.
authors: Zhang L, Zhao Z, Shu Y, Zhang J.
abstract: Despite the widespread clinical use of protein kinase inhibitors in oncology, evidence regarding their potential to induce central nervous system (CNS) hemorrhage remains limited. This study aims to investigate the occurrence and risk signals of CNS hemorrhagic events associated with different PKI subclasses, identify the most affected patient populations, and examine variations in risk profiles across demographic subgroups. We conducted disproportionality analyses using data from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System to detect CNS hemorrhage signals linked to 14 PKI classes. Subgroup analyses stratified by age, sex, and body weight were performed to explore differential risk patterns. Furthermore, Mendelian Randomization and genetic correlation analyses were utilized to evaluate potential causal relationships between PKI therapeutic indications and CNS hemorrhages. We analyzed 9215 CNS hemorrhage reports linked to 14 PKI classes. We identified 6 CNS hemorrhage related signal of disproportionate reporting significantly associated with PKI use. Both BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors and BTK inhibitors showed consistent positive signals across all 6 signal of disproportionate reportings, with BTK inhibitors presenting analysis the highest risks (e.g., cerebral hemorrhage reporting odds ratio = 3.30 [3.00-3.62], subdural hematoma reporting odds ratio = 5.90 [5.28-6.60]). Mendelian Randomization revealed no causal genetic relationship between PKI indications and CNS hemorrhage, suggesting the hemorrhagic risks are likely attributable to the drugs themselves rather than underlying diseases. Significant disproportionality signals of PKI-related CNS hemorrhage were identified, while causal links between indications and adverse events were excluded. These findings enhance understanding of PKI-associated bleeding risks and support early detection, targeted monitoring, and informed clinical decision-making.

title: Causal relationships of physical activity and leisure sedentary behaviors with scoliosis: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Yang F, Qiu X, Liu H, Wen J.
abstract: Scoliosis is the most common spinal deformity in children and adolescents, and modifiable lifestyle factors such as sedentary behavior and physical activity (PA) have been suggested to influence its risk, although evidence remains conflicting. This study aimed to investigate the relationships between leisure sedentary behaviors, PA, and the risk of scoliosis by using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Genetic variation in television watching time, mobile phone use time, moderate-to-high intensity physical activity (MVPA), and vigorous physical activity (VPA) were used as IVs. The outcome data were derived from the Finn-Gen Scoliosis dataset. The causal relationships were estimated with inverse variance weighted (IVW), MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Sensitivity analysis was conducted using Cochran Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy Residual Sum and Outlier (MR-PRESSO), leave-one-out analysis, and funnel plot to estimate the robustness of our findings. The IVW results indicated the following: watching TV time (odds ration [OR] = 0.623, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.21-1.78, P = .38); time spent on mobile phones (OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.16-1.96, P = .37); MVPA (OR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.09-3.15, P = .49); VPA (OR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.21-1.78, P = .61). The primary IVW MR analysis results were consistent with those of the multiple sensitivity MR Analysis. Genetic susceptibility to leisure sedentary behavior and PA are not associated with the risk of scoliosis. The observed associations may be the result of shared genetic effects or environmental confounding factors.

title: Causal relationship between educational attainment and complications of Type 2 diabetes: Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Han W, Wan Q.
abstract: Educational attainment (EA) is a critical metric for evaluating individual socioeconomic status, as it significantly impacts mortality rates and the occurrence of various diseases. This study aims to investigate the causal relationship between education and complications associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus, while also examining potential mediating pathways. To assess the causal relationship between EA and specific complications of type 2 diabetes, this study employs univariable Mendelian randomization (UVMR). Throughout this analysis, single nucleotide polymorphisms are utilized as genetic tools, thereby minimizing confounding and bias arising from reverse causation. With each 4.2-year increase in EA, patients with type 2 diabetes exhibit a reduced risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with neurological complications (DNC) (0.33; 0.20, 0.54), type 2 diabetes with ophthalmic complications (DOC) (0.57; 0.41, 0.80), type 2 diabetes with peripheral circulatory complications (DPCC) (0.60; 0.39, 0.93), and type 2 diabetes with renal complications (DRC) (0.47; 0.32, 0.69). Among the 27 candidate mediators, body mass index, waist circumference, and watching television showed relatively large mediation proportion point estimates for some outcomes. The findings of this study suggest that EA exerts a causally protective effect on DNC, DOC, DPCC, and DRC. The candidate mediating pathways warrant further investigation because their independent contributions have not been established.

title: Calcium, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and postpartum hemorrhage: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Zhang P, Wang F, Kan Z, Liu X, Zhuang J.
abstract: We aimed to evaluate the causal effect of calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] on the risk of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) using a 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Instrumental variables for calcium and 25(OH)D were selected from corresponding large-scale genome-wide association studies. Summary-level data on PPH were obtained from the latest R10 release of the FinnGen consortium. Inverse-variance weighting (IVW) was performed as the main MR analysis, and MR-Egger and weighted median were performed to strengthen the final MR estimates. Sensitivity analyses were applied to detect possible heterogeneity or pleiotropy. One hundred and four single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for calcium and 117 SNPs for 25(OH)D were selected as candidate instrumental variables. In this study, the MR estimates for calcium and 25(OH)D remained consistent before and after removing confounder-related SNPs. The IVW method suggested a potential inverse association between genetically predicted calcium and PPH (odds ratio [OR] = 0.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.80, 0.99, P = .036); however, this finding was not supported by the pleiotropy‑robust MR‑Egger (OR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.72-1.11, P = .303) or weighted median (OR = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.74-1.10, P = .302) methods. No heterogeneity or pleiotropy was observed in Cochran's Q test (P = .825), MR-Egger intercept test (P = .976), or the MR-Pleiotropy Residual Sum and Outlier (MR-PRESSO) Global Test (P = .842) in the determination of the role of calcium levels in PPH. However, no significant genetic evidence was found to support a causal relationship between 25(OH)D and PPH (IVW: OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.85-1.12, P = .735; MR-Egger: OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.82-1.25, P = .912; Weighted median: OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.85-1.36, P = .525). In summary, our primary analysis suggested a potential inverse association between serum calcium and PPH, but this was not supported by sensitivity analyses robust to pleiotropy, warranting cautious interpretation. For 25(OH)D, our analysis did not provide sufficient evidence to support or refute a causal role in PPH, largely due to limited statistical power.

title: Bone marrow sarcoidosis in Takayasu arteritis: Case report and literature review.
authors: Fakih O, Hachem S, Chamas R, Abi Dargham S, Aitisha Tabesh O, Fayad F.
abstract: Rationale Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a systemic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly involving the aorta and its primary branches. Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous disorder characterized histologically by non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas, most commonly affecting the lungs. Although the coexistence of TA and sarcoidosis has been documented, bone marrow involvement by sarcoidosis in a patient with concomitant TA has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported. Patient concerns A 46-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of TA presented with elevated systemic inflammatory markers and diffuse hypermetabolic activity on positron emission tomography (PET). Clinical, radiological, and pathological evaluations were performed. Diagnoses Bone marrow biopsy revealed multiple non-necrotizing granulomas, supporting bone marrow involvement by sarcoidosis. This overlap of granulomatous conditions was identified in the context of persistent systemic inflammation. Interventions Mycofenolate Mofetil was replaced by Infliximab therapy. Outcomes The patient exhibited significant clinical improvement and marked improvement in inflammatory markers with infliximab therapy. Lessons This case highlights the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in patients with autoimmune or inflammatory diseases who develop new systemic manifestations. Recognizing rare organ involvement in overlapping granulomatous conditions is critical for accurate diagnosis and management.

title: Biomechanical analysis of cervical misalignment and extrication time during heavy vehicle traffic collisions: A randomized, simulation-based experimental study with professional rescuers.
authors: Pons Claramonte M, Pardo Ríos M, Nicolás Carrillo A, López López CA, Nieto Navarro A, Nieto Caballero S.
abstract: Background Traffic collisions remain one of the leading global causes of morbidity and mortality. In vehicle extrication, rescue time and spinal motion restriction play a decisive role in patient prognosis. Current evidence prioritizes minimizing rescue time; however, most studies have focused on passenger vehicles, with limited evidence available regarding rescue operations in heavy vehicles. The aim of this study was to analyze cervical spine biomechanics and extrication times during the rescue of victims involved in heavy-vehicle traffic accidents. Methods A comparative, simulation-based experimental study was conducted to evaluate 3 extrication techniques in a truck cab: standard manual rescue, rapid extrication device, and extrication and immobilization device. Thirty-six professional firefighters participated, organized into randomized teams. Cervical spine motion was recorded using inertial sensors placed on the cervical spine. Execution time was measured, and statistical analyses included repeated-measures analysis of variance, linear regression models, and the Cochran Q test. Results Significant differences were observed among techniques in both cervical spine motion and extrication time. Standard manual rescue demonstrated the lowest overall cervical motion and the shortest execution time. Extrication device provided acceptable immobilization at the expense of longer execution time, whereas rapid extrication device produced greater cervical motion without temporal advantages. Conclusion In the rescue of victims from heavy vehicles, standard manual rescue offers the best balance between biomechanical safety and operational speed, supporting the optimization of rescue protocols based on objective efficiency and time-dependence criteria.

title: Barriers to recruitment in paediatric orthopaedic surgical trials : a qualitative study embedded in the Big BOSS trial.
authors: Kirton JA, Achten J, Young B, Perry DC, Cherry MG.
abstract: Aims Recruitment to randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remains a widely recognized challenge, particularly in surgical and paediatric contexts. The British Orthopaedic Surgery Surveillance (Big BOSS) trial aimed to compare surgical approaches for treating severe stable slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE), a relatively rare but serious adolescent hip condition. Despite national estimates suggesting feasibility, recruitment fell significantly short of targets, and Big BOSS was discontinued. This embedded qualitative study explored the perspectives of consultant surgeons to understand the barriers that contributed to the low recruitment for the trial. Methods Semistructured interviews were carried out with 24 consultant surgeons from 21 NHS sites, including recruiting, non-recruiting, and setup sites. Participants were purposely sampled to ensure variation in experience and involvement in trials. Data were analyzed inductively and thematically, guided by constant comparative methods. Results Five overarching themes were identified: 1) limited availability of eligible patients, with many cases of SCFE either unstable, too mild or managed outside trial centres; 2) challenges in interpreting and standardizing the eligibility criteria; 3) difficulty maintaining clinical equipoise, as surgeons often relied on personal experience and preferred treatment pathways; 4) systemic and logistical barriers, including limited research infrastructure, scheduling complexity, and demands on the resources for trials; and 5) patient-level factors, such as aversion to invasive procedures, logistical constraints, and predetermined expectations of treatment. Together, these themes revealed how clinical, practical, and ethical tensions limited participation in the trial. Conclusion This nested qualitative study highlighted the multifaceted barriers to recruitment in complex surgical RCTs, and showed how embedded qualitative research can help to uncover these challenges and guide the management decisions for trials. The findings emphasize the value of a qualitative investigation to understand the underlying processes and challenges within a trial. This approach facilitates the development of adaptive recruitment strategies, and supports more realistic planning when designing RCTs involving rare conditions or preference-sensitive treatments.

title: Ballistic Forearm Fractures are Associated with Higher Neurovascular Injury, Nonunion, and Complications Compared With Blunt Forearm Injuries.
authors: Barber HF, Pereira DE, Rust BD, Perugini JM, Reaver CN, Guissé NF, Wilson JL, Obey MR, McAndrew CM, Berkes MB.
abstract: Objectives To characterize injury patterns, treatment differences, and clinical outcomes associated with ballistic and blunt forearm fractures. Methods Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Single Level 1 tertiary trauma center, 2018-2023. Patient selection criteria The study included adults (≥18) who underwent operative fixation of diaphyseal radius and/or ulna fractures. Exclusion criteria were ipsilateral intraarticular or unstable elbow injuries, pathologic fractures, or fractures involving preexisting implants. Patients were stratified into 2 groups: ballistic and blunt injuries, which were further subclassified as blunt-closed or blunt-open. Outcome measures and comparisons Primary outcomes included nerve deficit, complication rate, unplanned reoperation, nonunion, and postoperative infection. Results The study included 395 patients with 398 forearm fractures: 81 ballistic fractures in 78 patients [32 years (18-69), 88.9% male], 213 blunt-closed fractures [41 years (18-82), 59.2% male], and 104 blunt-open fractures [46 years (19-92), 71.2% male]. Ballistic fractures had significantly higher rates of nerve deficits (48.2% vs. 6.3%, P Conclusions Ballistic forearm fractures posed unique challenges compared with blunt injuries. They were associated with significantly higher rates of nerve deficit, unplanned reoperations, and overall complications, with higher nonunion observed when compared with blunt-closed injuries. These injuries warrant a high index of suspicion for nerve injury and close long-term follow-up to optimize patient outcomes and address the needs of a disproportionately affected, high-risk population. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Axillary Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor With Aggressive Clinical Course: A Case Report.
authors: Yağmur Y.
abstract: Aim Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) involvement of the axillary region is exceptionally uncommon and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case presentation We report the case of a 41-year-old woman who presented with a left axillary mass initially detected during pregnancy. Imaging revealed a large axillary lesion closely associated with neurovascular structures. Histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses supported an MPNST diagnosis. Despite multimodal management, including partial surgical resection, combination chemotherapy with ifosfamide/doxorubicin-based regimens, radiotherapy, repeated surgical interventions, and reconstructive procedures, the disease demonstrated aggressive behavior with multiple local recurrences, nodal and cutaneous metastases, and an eventual mass in the gluteal region. Results MPNSTs account for 3-10% of soft tissue sarcomas and are frequently associated with poor outcomes, particularly in tumors larger than 5 cm, high-grade lesions, and those associated with neurofibromatosis type 1. Diagnosis relies on a combination of histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and advanced imaging modalities. Complete surgical resection with negative margins remains the only potentially curative treatment; however, this is often not feasible due to tumor location and extent. Radiotherapy may improve local control, while chemotherapy has limited efficacy in advanced disease. Conclusions Axillary MPNST is an exceedingly rare entity with an aggressive clinical course and poor prognosis. This case highlights the challenges in management and underscores the need for early diagnosis, aggressive multimodal treatment, and the development of more effective systemic and targeted therapies.

title: Associations of Quadriceps and Prefemoral Fat Pad MRI Parameters With Postoperative Pain and Functional Outcomes After Total Knee Arthroplasty in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis.
authors: Dong Y, Zhang X, Yan L, Li B, Zeng L, Zhao F, Tao J.
abstract: Aim To investigate the relationship between quantitative magnetic resonance imaging parameters of the quadriceps fat pad (QFP) and prefemoral fat pad (PFP) and pain and functional outcomes at 1 month after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in patients with knee osteoarthritis. Methods We retrospectively collected the clinical and imaging data of patients with knee osteoarthritis who underwent primary unilateral TKA at Shihezi People's Hospital between October 2025 and April 2026 and had completed knee magnetic resonance imaging before surgery. The following imaging parameters were extracted: (1) QFP: the craniocaudal diameter, anteroposterior diameter, oblique diameter, T1 value, T2 value, proton density (PD) value, high signal intensity, and mass effect; and (2) PFP: maximum thickness and high signal intensity. Postoperative pain and physical function scores at 1 month after surgery were obtained from the medical record system. Spearman correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were performed to identify imaging markers associated with postoperative clinical outcomes. Results Spearman correlation analysis showed that the T2 value, hyperintensity, and mass effect of the QFP, as well as the hyperintensity and maximum thickness of the PFP, were positively correlated with postoperative pain and physical function scores. Multiple linear regression analysis showed that the T2 value of QFP, mass effect, QFP hyperintensity, and PFP hyperintensity were significantly associated with postoperative pain. The T2 value of QFP, mass effect, and PFP hyperintensity and maximum thickness were significantly associated with postoperative physical function scores. Conclusions This retrospective study showed that quantitative and morphological parameters of the QFP and PFP extracted from preoperative routine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were significantly associated with postoperative pain and functional outcomes in patients with knee osteoarthritis undergoing TKA. These findings suggest that specific imaging features may be associated with poorer outcomes and provide preliminary evidence for clinical consideration. However, prospective studies with larger sample sizes are warranted to validate these exploratory findings.

title: Association of the triglyceride glucose-waist circumference index with hypertension among US adults: A cross-sectional study from NHANES.
authors: Peng J, Liu H, Long S, Wei D, Feng L.
abstract: The triglyceride glucose-weight-adjusted waist index (TyG-WWI), integrating glycolipid metabolism and central obesity, may offer a novel approach to identifying metabolic dysregulation linked to hypertension, yet its association with hypertension among general adults remains inadequately characterized. In this cross-sectional analysis of 2716 adults (aged ≥ 20 years) from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2015 to 2018, hypertension was defined by self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and exploratory mediation analyses were applied, accounting for the complex survey design with fasting subsample weights. Of 2716 participants, 890 (32.8%) had hypertension. After full adjustment, each unit increase in TyG-WWI was associated with a 2% increase in the odds of hypertension (OR = 1.02, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.03, P < .001). A nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed (P for nonlinearity < .05), with risk accelerating at higher TyG-WWI levels; participants in the highest quartile had 72% higher odds than those in the lowest quartile (OR = 1.72, 95% confidence interval: 1.21-2.46; P for trend < .001). Subgroup analyses showed stronger associations in females and in normal-weight individuals. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that body mass index and uric acid may account for 30.49% and 7.95% of the association, respectively; these estimates are descriptive and should not be interpreted as evidence of biological mediation. Higher TyG-WWI was independently associated with a higher prevalence of self-reported hypertension among United States adults across all body mass index categories. These findings support TyG-WWI as a promising composite marker for hypertension risk stratification; the exploratory mediation estimates warrant confirmation in prospective studies.

title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: He M, Chen Y, Zou X, Zou Y, Ding H.
abstract: Aim To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated. Results No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p Conclusions In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

title: Association of Metabolic Syndrome and Its Components With Functional Status in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis.
authors: Kamiab Z, Bazmandegan G, Khezri-Moghadam Z, Abbasifard M.

title: Association between systemic immune-inflammation index and skeletal muscle mass in patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Peng Q, Yang W, Lu Z, Wu X, Zhang X, Chen X.
abstract: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is characterized by excessive liver fat accumulation, which is associated with inflammatory responses and metabolic disruptions that may affect skeletal muscle mass. However, the specific relationship between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and skeletal muscle mass in NAFLD patients remains unclear. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using data from the 2017 to 2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The study comprised 673 adults with confirmed NAFLD who met inclusion criteria and had complete data on SII and skeletal muscle mass. Generalized weighted linear regression models were employed to assess the association, with adjustment for multiple covariates including demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. After controlling for covariates, regression analysis revealed a significant independent negative correlation between SII and muscle mass (β = -0.037, 95% confidence interval [CI] = -0.055 to -0.019, P < .001). Smooth curve analysis indicated an approximately linear relationship, with an inflection point at 536.63 (1000 cells/μL). Subgroup analyses showed more pronounced negative correlations in males (β = -0.045, 95% CI = -0.073 to -0.018, P = .001) and non-Hispanic white individuals (β = -0.129, 95% CI = -0.193 to -0.065, P < .001). Our findings provide evidence of an independent negative association between SII and skeletal muscle mass in NAFLD patients, suggesting that systemic immune inflammation may contribute to muscle loss in this population.

title: Association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty among adults with a history of stroke: A cross-sectional study of NHANES 1999-2018.
authors: Fu T, Wang A, Peng J, Tian X, Chen X.
abstract: Stroke is one of the leading causes of long-term disability worldwide. Walking difficulty is an important functional limitation among adults with a history of stroke. However, the association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty in this population remains insufficiently studied. This study analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2018 to evaluate the association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty among adults with a self-reported history of stroke. Weighted logistic regression models were used to adjust for confounders. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was conducted to explore potential nonlinear relationships. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. Subgroup analyses and interaction effect tests were conducted to examine heterogeneity across different populations. A total of 488 adults with a self-reported history of stroke were included in this study, representing 15,92,140 individuals in the US population. In the fully adjusted model, each 1 µU/mL increase in serum insulin level was associated with 5% higher odds of self-reported walking difficulty (OR = 1.05, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.09, P = .028). Quartile-based analysis showed that higher insulin levels (Q3, Q4) were significantly associated with greater odds of self-reported walking difficulty, with the highest quartile (Q4) showing an OR of 5.10 (95% confidence interval: 1.93-13.48, P = .001). RCS analysis suggested a possible nonlinear association between serum insulin levels and self-reported walking difficulty (P for non-linearity = .032). The associations observed in the sensitivity analyses were in the same direction as those in the primary analysis. Higher serum insulin levels were associated with greater odds of self-reported walking difficulty among adults with a self-reported history of stroke. These findings do not establish causality or a role for insulin in stroke-related motor recovery.

title: Association between proinflammatory diet and infertility among US reproductive-aged women: A cross-sectional study from NHANES 2013-2018.
authors: Du J, Tan Y.
abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and infertility among United States women of childbearing age and assess whether body mass index (BMI) modifies this relationship. A cross-sectional analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2013-2018) included 2236 women aged 18 to 45 years. DII was derived from 24-hour dietary recall, and infertility was self-reported. Weighted logistic regression and interaction analyses were used. Higher DII scores were associated with increased infertility risk. Compared to the lowest DII quartile, the highest quartile had 54% higher odds of infertility (odds ratio = 1.54; 95% confidence interval: 1.02-2.32; P trend = .026). BMI significantly modified the association (P interaction < .0001). The strongest effect was observed in obese women (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2), with predicted infertility probability reaching 30% at high DII levels. Proinflammatory diets are associated with higher infertility risk, particularly among obese women. Reducing dietary inflammation may be a promising strategy for infertility prevention in vulnerable populations.

title: Association between early central venous pressure monitoring and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis: A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Zheng C, Wang L, Zhou S, Liao X, Zhang Z, Jin Z.
abstract: Central venous pressure (CVP) is widely used in the intensive care unit (ICU), but the optimal timing to initiate CVP monitoring remains unclear for patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis. We explored the association between time to initial CVP measurement and 30-day mortality in this high-risk population. This retrospective cohort study included 9246 critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis from the MIMIC-IV database. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis examined the relationship between time to initial CVP measurement and 30-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting followed by weighted logistic regression was used to assess the association between early CVP monitoring (≤6 hours after ICU admission) and 30-day mortality. A nonlinear J-shaped association emerged, with the lowest risk at 2.89 hours post-admission. Early CVP monitoring was associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR = 0.816, 95% CI: 0.688-0.967, P = .019). A landmark sensitivity analysis comparing no monitoring, early (≤6 hours), intermediate (6-86 hours), and late (>86 hours) monitoring showed a time-dependent relationship: intermediate (OR = 1.396, 95% CI: 1.194-1.632, P < .001) and late monitoring (OR = 3.141, 95% CI: 2.263-4.359, P < .001) were associated with progressively higher mortality. In critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis, early CVP monitoring within 6 hours of ICU admission was associated with lower 30-day mortality, while delayed monitoring carried an elevated risk. Early integration of CVP within a multimodal hemodynamic assessment framework may be a prudent approach in this high-risk population.

title: Association between dietary thiamine intake and serum lipid profiles in U.S. adults: NHANES 2021-2023.
authors: Bakhshi H, Safargar M, Kord-Varkaneh H.
abstract: Thiamine (vitamin B1) is an essential water-soluble vitamin involved in carbohydrate metabolism and energy production. Emerging evidence suggests that thiamin may influence lipid metabolism and cardiovascular risk, yet population-based data are limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to investigate the association between dietary thiamin intake and serum lipid profiles, including total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, and triglycerides, among U.S. adults. Data from 4986 fasting adults aged ≥ 18 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2021 to 2023 were analyzed. Dietary thiamin intake was assessed using the first 24-hour dietary recall and classified into four intake categories based on the distribution of thiamin intake. Linear regression models were used to examine the associations between dietary thiamin intake and serum lipid components, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, dietary, and health-related factors. A sensitivity analysis was additionally performed, adjusting for lipid-lowering medication use. In fully adjusted models, higher thiamin intake was associated with lower total cholesterol (β = -7.13, SE = 2.61, P = .007) and LDL-C (β = -6.72, SE = 3.27, P = .04). No significant associations were observed with HDL-C (β = -0.21, SE = 0.80, P = .79) or triglycerides (β = 13.82, SE = 10.37, P = .183). In the sensitivity analysis additionally adjusted for lipid-lowering medication use, the associations with total cholesterol and LDL-C remained significant, while those with HDL-C and triglycerides remained nonsignificant. These findings indicate an inverse association between dietary thiamin intake and selected atherogenic lipid fractions. Among U.S. adults, higher dietary thiamin intake is associated with lower total and LDL cholesterol levels. Higher thiamin intake may be associated with a more favorable lipid profile and may represent a potential dietary factor relevant to cardiovascular risk management. Given the cross-sectional design, causal relationships cannot be inferred, and further prospective and interventional studies are warranted to confirm these findings and elucidate underlying mechanisms.

title: Association between depression and cognitive function in adults aged 50 years and older: A cross-sectional study of NHANES 2011-2014.
authors: Chen X, Cao M, Chen H.
abstract: Cognitive impairment and depression frequently coexist in older adults. This study examined their association among adults aged ≥50 years using nationally representative National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data. This cross-sectional study analyzed NHANES 2011 to 2014 data from adults aged ≥50 years. Depression was defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score ≥10, and cognitive function was assessed using the Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Word Learning, Animal Fluency Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST). Weighted multivariable linear regression models accounting for the NHANES complex sampling design were used to examine the association between depression status and standardized cognitive performance. Cognitive test scores were converted to Z-scores before regression analysis. Among 2729 participants, 671 had depression (weighted prevalence, 24.59%). Participants with depression performed significantly worse across all cognitive assessments (all P < .01). In fully adjusted models, depression was significantly associated with lower standardized cognitive performance across all domains, including delayed word recall (β = -0.089, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.145--0.034, P = .003), total word recall (β = -0.033, 95% CI: -0.055--0.010, P=.006), Animal Fluency Test performance (β = -0.044, 95% CI: -0.066- - 0.021, P < .001), and Digit Symbol Substitution Test performance (β = -0.031, 95% CI: -0.042--0.019, P < .001). Depression status was associated with poorer cognitive performance across multiple domains in adults aged ≥50 years. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between depression and cognitive decline.

title: Association between arthritis and asthma: An observational analysis of NHANES and a Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Chen T, Wang C.
abstract: Observational studies have linked arthritis and asthma, but establishing causality is challenging due to confounding. We analyzed 30,001 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2003-2018) using survey-weighted logistic regression to assess observational associations. To infer causality, we conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis using publicly available genetic data. In the observational analysis, arthritis was significantly associated with a higher risk of asthma (adjusted odds ratio = 1.96, 95% confidence interval = 1.75-2.19), with similar findings for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA). Mendelian randomization analysis provided evidence for a positive causal effect of genetic predisposition to RA on asthma (inverse-variance weighted odds ratio = 1.037, 95% confidence interval = 1.007-1.068), but found no significant causal effect for OA. This study provides dual evidence supporting a significant and potentially causal relationship between RA and asthma. In contrast, the association with OA appears to be noncausal, likely driven by confounding factors.

title: Assessment of sleep patterns in third-trimester pregnant women: A cross-sectional latent profile analysis.
authors: Wang Z, Cheng W, He D, Wei X, Wang X, Li R.
abstract: This study seeks to categorize different sleep patterns in third-trimester pregnant women (≥28 weeks gestation) using latent profile analysis and to determine associated factors. A cross-sectional survey was carried out at a Shanghai hospital, where sleep information was gathered from 343 pregnant women via electronic questionnaires between June and August 2024. A total of 280 questionnaires were included (with a valid response rate of 81.63%). A 4-profile model was suggested as the optimum: good sleep quality (64.9%), high sleep efficiency-daytime dysfunction (19.3%), high sleep duration-low sleep efficiency (6.5%), and sleep disorder (SLD, 9.3%). Logistic regression analysis identified age, employment status, and anxiety as factors associated with poor sleep quality in pregnant women. Specifically, compared with the Good Sleep Quality group, women of older age (odds ratio [OR] = 1.186, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.072-1.313) were more prone to the High Sleep Efficiency-Daytime Dysfunction group classification. Older age (OR = 1.169, 95% CI = 1.028-1.331) and anxiety (OR = 1.075, 95% CI = 1.007-1.147) were associated with higher odds of SLD group membership, whereas employment (OR = 0.249, 95% CI = 0.102-0.604) was associated with lower odds of SLD group membership. Our study identified disparities in sleep quality among pregnant women based on various factors. Specifically, pregnant women with advanced maternal age or symptoms of anxiety were more likely to have poorer sleep quality. Employment was associated with lower odds of membership in the sleep-disorder profile. This indicates a need for tailored clinical care for different individuals.

title: Assay-aware flow-cytometric interpretation of relapsed B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia after sequential CD19- and CD22-directed therapy: A case report.
authors: Zheng F, Dong J, Cao X, Li S, Ma T, Li J, Wang J, Zhang Y, Lu Z.
abstract: Rationale Sequential CD19- and CD22-directed therapies can make relapse immunophenotyping assay-dependent. Surface and cytoplasmic antigen results address distinct clinical questions and should not be interpreted interchangeably. This case uniquely integrates sequential target exposure, discordant surface and cytoplasmic findings, exclusion of mixed-phenotype acute leukemia, and interpretation of a post-inotuzumab ozogamicin (INO) population between the assay limits of detection and quantification. Patient concerns A 73-year-old woman with B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia received a 14-day course of blinatumomab and later developed marrow relapse after a prolonged gap in specialist follow-up. The available records did not permit reconstruction of the complete treatment-selection history. Diagnoses At relapse, the blasts were positive for cytoplasmic CD19 and CD79a, lacked surface CD19, expressed weak surface CD22 and CD13/CD33, and were negative for cytoplasmic MPO, CD14, and CD64. These findings supported relapsed B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia with aberrant myeloid-associated antigen expression rather than mixed-phenotype acute leukemia. Interventions The records documented blinatumomab exposure followed by INO-based salvage on three occasions. The reason for the abbreviated blinatumomab course and body-surface-area-based INO dosing could not be reconstructed from the reviewed records. Outcomes Posttreatment marrow contained 0.5% blasts and a low-level abnormal population of 0.007% (approximately 30 events), which was above the assay limit of detection but below the limit of quantification. Surface CD22 was not detected on this low-event population with the S-HCL-1 assay. At later assessment, no previously identified leukemia-associated abnormal population was detected under the reported assay conditions. Lessons After sequential antigen-directed therapy, lineage assignment and therapeutic-target assessment require repeated, assay-aware interpretation. Cytoplasmic antigen positivity may support lineage assignment but should not be equated with surface therapeutic-target availability. A low-event multiparameter flow cytometry population below the limit of quantification should be described qualitatively. A single posttreatment sample cannot establish lineage switch, antigen loss, treatment causality, or durable disease control.

title: Articular compliance and tolerance to residual incongruity after intra-articular fracture: A hypothesis-driven narrative review.
authors: Dhar SA, Dar TA, Dar RA, Farooq S, Maajid A, Zargar S, Mughal I.
abstract: Background Residual articular incongruity after intra-articular fracture is widely held to cause post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), yet tolerance of a given step-off differs between joints and between regions of the same joint. Reduction targets are nonetheless expressed as uniform millimetre thresholds, and no tissue-level mechanism has been offered for the variation. Hypothesis The compliance of the osteochondral unit - cartilage thickness, cartilage material properties and subchondral bone stiffness together - modulates tolerance of residual incongruity, and incongruity is more informatively expressed relative to local cartilage thickness than in absolute millimetres. Methods Narrative review with a documented search of PubMed/MEDLINE (inception to 14 October 2026) covering cartilage and subchondral properties of opposing surfaces, experimental and computational studies of articular incongruity, and clinical studies relating residual displacement to outcome. Four searches returned 3928 records, 3579 after deduplication; 54 sources informed the synthesis. This is not a systematic review; reporting follows SANRA. Findings Small, localised contact-stress elevations appear tolerable; step-offs remodel less completely as their height increases; and cumulative contact-stress exposure above a threshold predicts PTOA after tibial plafond fracture. Opposing surfaces differ measurably in cartilage thickness, modulus and subchondral bone thickness, but the direction of the difference reverses between joints and between regions of one joint, so curvature is not a usable proxy for compliance. Clinically, the acetabulum and tibial plafond appear least tolerant, the meniscus-covered tibial plateau more tolerant, and distal radius incongruity predicts radiographic arthrosis more strongly than functional loss. Conclusions The evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, a contribution of osteochondral compliance; joint-level factors confound the clinical data. We set out a Compliance Framework defining measurable determinants, propose relative incongruity as a testable metric, and state four falsifiable predictions with the designs that would test them. Current joint-specific reduction standards should guide practice until those predictions are tested.

title: Are electrolyte levels associated with cholelithiasis risk?: A cross-sectional study of NHANES 2017 to 2023.
authors: Li J, Bao Z, Zhang J.
abstract: To investigate the linear and potential nonlinear associations between 6 common serum electrolyte levels (sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, calcium, and phosphorus) and cholelithiasis risk in the US population. A cross-sectional study was conducted using 2017 to 2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data. 8725 eligible participants were included after strict exclusion criteria. Weighted logistic regression was used to assess linear associations, and restricted cubic spline regression was used to explore nonlinear relationships, with analyses adjusted for multiple covariates (age, gender, body mass index, etc). Only serum potassium had a significant inverse linear association with cholelithiasis risk in the fully adjusted weighted logistic model (odds ratio = 0.653, P = .0054). Both serum potassium and total calcium exhibited significant nonlinear associations, with low concentrations associated with increased odds of cholelithiasis (all P < .05). No significant linear or nonlinear associations were found for bicarbonate, chloride, phosphorus, or sodium with cholelithiasis risk across all adjusted models. Serum potassium and calcium homeostasis may be associated with cholelithiasis risk, with low levels of these electrolytes linked to higher disease risk. No such associations were observed for the other 4 electrolytes, and further prospective studies are required to verify causal relationships.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in acute myocardial infarction: A bibliometric analysis from 2016 to 2025.
authors: Wang X, Yang Y, Li W.
abstract: Background Growing interest suggests that the broad application of artificial intelligence (AI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) has advanced diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. AI methods applied to AMI research have recently yielded significant predictive outcomes. However, few studies have systematically analyzed this field using bibliometric approaches. We employ CiteSpace to examine the visual relationships of publications, identify key research trends and hotspots, and stimulate broader participation in AI-AMI studies. Methods Data for this bibliometric analysis were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. A systematic search strategy was developed using Medical Subject Headings to identify publications pertaining to AI in AMI from January 2016 to December 2025. The initial query returned 2089 records, which were subsequently refined through manual screening and algorithmic deduplication, yielding a final corpus of 2088 eligible publications. Bibliometric analyses were performed using CiteSpace (version 6.2.R6) with the following configuration: annual time slices of 1 year, a selection threshold of the top 25 most frequent items per slice (Top N = 25), and network pruning via the Pathfinder algorithm applied to both sliced and merged networks. Multidimensional analyses were conducted across six node types - country/region, institution, author, cited author, cited journal, and keyword - employing co-occurrence mapping, co-citation analysis, cluster detection, and burst term identification. These approaches collectively delineated the intellectual landscape, collaborative architectures, and thematic evolution characterizing the AI-AMI research domain. Results We analyzed publications, citations, and networks. Post-2016, publications surged from 24 (2016) to 517 (2025) with dramatically increasing citations. Global collaboration centered on the China (705 publications), USA (553 publications), and India (195 publications), with Harvard-linked institutions forming the dominant cluster (e.g., Harvard University: 100 publications, centrality = 0.12). Author networks identified key bridges Saba, Luca (13 publications, centrality = 0.05) and Pontone, Gianluca (centrality = 0.06), contrasting with high-output but low-centrality authors like Acharya, U Rajendra (21 publications). High-centrality cited authors (e.g., ACHARYA UR: centrality = 0.09) were pivotal nexuses. Journal analysis showed CIRCULATION (1375 cites) and J AM COLL CARDIOL (1120 cites) as citation leaders. Keywords revealed evolving focus: prevalent terms ("myocardial infarction": 698 freq., "machine learning": 603 freq.) were highly productive, whereas central terms ("prediction": centrality = 0.36, "acute myocardial infarction": centrality = 0.24) bridged domains. Keywords bursts shifted from computational themes pre-2020 (e.g., "neural network," strength = 8.31) to the practical application of AI post-2020 (e.g., "system," strength = 5.43 and "prevalence," strength = 4.61). Conclusion AI-AMI research exhibits globally distributed multilevel collaboration structures anchored by major nations/institutions and critical author bridges. Knowledge dissemination hinges on domain-bridging journals like CIRCULATION. Thematic emphasis has evolved from computational techniques towards clinical applications, interconnected by high-centrality concepts.

title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
authors: Ruan S, Ruan S, Wang J, Hu X, Guo T, Zhou J.
abstract: Aim Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities. Methods A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction. Results The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group ( p p 85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group ( p p Conclusions The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

title: Application of a Risk Assessment-Based Stratified Early Warning Nursing Model to Prevent Postoperative Delirium in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Orthopedic Surgery.
authors: Liu W, Li D.
abstract: Aim To investigate the effectiveness of a risk assessment-based stratified early warning nursing model in preventing postoperative delirium (POD) in geriatric orthopedic patients. Methods A retrospective study was conducted. Elderly patients who underwent elective orthopedic surgery at The First Hospital of Jilin University between January 2024 and December 2025 were enrolled. Based on the nursing model received, patients were divided into two groups: those receiving routine care were assigned to the control group (98 patients), while those receiving the risk assessment-based stratified early warning nursing model were assigned to the intervention group (113 patients). In the intervention group, a delirium risk assessment tool was used for preoperative risk stratification (low, moderate, and high risk), and graded early warning measures and targeted interventions were implemented according to the risk level. The incidence of postoperative delirium, delirium duration, length of hospital stay, and nursing satisfaction were compared between the two groups. Results The incidence of postoperative delirium was significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (9.73% vs. 19.39%, p = 0.045). The intervention group also had a shorter median delirium duration (3.0 d vs. 5.0 d, p = 0.005), a shorter mean length of hospital stay (12.18 ± 2.60 d vs. 16.48 ± 3.13 d, p p = 0.032). Conclusions The risk assessment-based stratified early warning nursing model may reduce the incidence of postoperative delirium in geriatric orthopedic patients, shorten delirium duration and hospital stay, and improve nursing satisfaction, highlighting its potential clinical value.

title: Application of Multidisciplinary Collaborative Teaching Based on Integrative Medicine in Thoracic Tumor Surgery Education.
authors: Zhai Z, Gao Y, Huang L, Zhu Y, Chen H, Li X, Chen P, Min Y, Lan G.
abstract: Aim To evaluate the effectiveness of a multidisciplinary collaborative teaching model based on integrative medicine in thoracic tumor surgery education. Methods This single-center retrospective study included sixty-one clinical interns who underwent training in the Department of Thoracic Disease Diagnosis and Treatment Center at The Third Affiliated Hospital of Jiaxing University (Zhejiang Rongjun Hospital) from March 2022 to March 2025. Based on the implementation period of the teaching model, participants were assigned to a control group (n = 30) or an observation group (n = 31). The control group received traditional teaching, whereas the observation group received multidisciplinary collaborative teaching based on integrative medicine, including multidisciplinary team (MDT) case discussions, scenario-based simulation, and simulated surgical skills training. Both groups underwent 3 months of training. After training, the theoretical knowledge assessment scores, comprehensive clinical competence (Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX) assessment, including dimensions such as medical history taking and case analysis, clinical reasoning and judgment, doctor-patient communication, and Organization/Efficiency), operational skills (operational standardization, teamwork, instrument proficiency, and mastery of basic surgical skills), and teaching satisfaction were compared between the two groups. Results After training, the observation group achieved significantly higher theoretical knowledge scores than the control group ( p p p = 0.402). Regarding operational skills, the observation group performed significantly better in operational standardization, teamwork, and instrument proficiency (all p p = 0.262). Teaching satisfaction scores for teaching methods, teaching content, learning enthusiasm, and overall satisfaction were significantly higher in the observation group (all p p > 0.05). Conclusions Multidisciplinary collaborative teaching based on integrative medicine was associated with improved theoretical knowledge, selected aspects of clinical competence (history taking and case analysis, clinical reasoning and judgment, Organization/Efficiency), certain operational skills (operation standardization, teamwork, and instrument proficiency), and higher teaching satisfaction. However, improvements were not observed across all competency domains. This teaching model may have value in standardized thoracic oncology training, although prospective studies are needed for further validation.

title: Anterior reconstruction using femoral ring allografts for thoracolumbar infectious spondylitis: Clinical and radiologic outcomes of a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sung MJ, Park CG, Seo HY.
abstract: Surgical treatment is required in infectious spondylitis when conservative management fails or vertebral destruction causes instability. Autologous bone graft is considered the gold standard but is limited by donor-site morbidity and availability. Femoral ring allografts are widely used in degenerative conditions, but their role in infectious spondylitis is unclear. This study evaluated the clinical, radiologic, and laboratory outcomes of anterior reconstruction using femoral ring allografts. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology statement, we reviewed 25 patients who underwent anterior corpectomy and reconstruction using femoral ring allografts followed by posterior instrumentation between December 2011 and September 2023. Clinical outcomes (VAS, Oswestry Disability Index, Frankel grade), laboratory parameters (erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein), and radiologic outcomes (Cobb angle, fusion) were compared preoperatively and at final follow-up. Paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with Hodges-Lehmann estimates, distribution-free 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and effect sizes (r). Infection control and complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 29.2 ± 23.9 months (range, 12.0-87.2 months). VAS improved from 7.3 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 1.0 (Hodges-Lehmann estimate -5.50; 95% CI, -6.00 to -5.00; r = 0.87) and Oswestry Disability Index from 37.7 ± 5.9 to 10.7 ± 3.5 (-26.50; 95% CI, -29.50 to -23.50; r = 0.87; both P < .001). Neurological function improved significantly (r = 0.76, P < .001). Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein decreased significantly (both P < .001). Sagittal alignment was corrected with partial loss over time but remained improved at final follow-up (5.55°; 95% CI, 3.40°-8.95°; r = 0.69; P < .001). Fusion was achieved in 92% and infection control in 96%. Complications occurred in 16%. In patients with large anterior column defects not amenable to tricortical iliac autograft, femoral ring allograft reconstruction achieved reliable infection control, a high fusion rate, and satisfactory clinical and radiologic outcomes over a mean follow-up of 29.2 months. Within this period, it appears a reasonable alternative to structural autograft when donor-site morbidity or graft availability is a concern. Longer-term comparative studies are needed to confirm the durability of graft incorporation and to define its role relative to contemporary titanium-based reconstruction.

title: An encephalitis-like syndrome in an adult with methylmalonic acidemia and hyperhomocysteinemia: A case report.
authors: Zhang R, Sheng X.
abstract: Rationale Methylmalonic acidemia with hyperhomocysteinemia may remain unrecognized until adulthood. When fever, altered consciousness, psychiatric symptoms, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) abnormalities, and electroencephalographic slowing dominate the presentation, infectious or autoimmune encephalitis is often considered first. Glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 antibody positivity may further complicate the diagnostic interpretation. Patient concerns A 56-year-old man presented with fever and slowed responses for 15 days, followed by disorganized speech, visual hallucinations, episodes of impaired consciousness, and pyramidal signs. Diagnoses Total homocysteine was > 100 µmol/L, propionylcarnitine (C3) was 22.42 µmol/L, and the C3/acetylcarnitine ratio was 0.83. Urinary organic acid analysis indicated increased methylmalonic acid and methylcitrate. Serum and CSF glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 antibodies were positive (titers, 1:100 and 1:3.2, respectively); however, the remaining autoimmune encephalitis antibody panel was negative, magnetic resonance imaging was nonspecific, and whole-exome sequencing revealed no clearly pathogenic variant. The findings supported methylmalonic acidemia with hyperhomocysteinemia on biochemical grounds and were clinically suggestive of a cobalamin metabolism-related disorder. Interventions He received vitamin B12, vitamins B1 and B6, folic acid, levocarnitine, intravenous immunoglobulin, empirical anti-infective treatment, mechanical ventilation, and intensive supportive care. Outcomes Following concurrent metabolic, immunologic, anti-infective, and intensive supportive treatments, his clinical symptoms improved. Total homocysteine decreased to 16.04 µmol/L, C3 to 19.50 µmol/L, and the C3/acetylcarnitine ratio to 0.40; CSF protein decreased from 1.78 to 0.80 g/L. Because these interventions were delivered simultaneously, the clinical and biochemical changes could not be attributed to any single treatment. At 6-month telephone follow-up, the family reported no recurrent fever, hallucinations, disorganized behavior, or marked disturbance of consciousness. Lessons In adults with an encephalitis-like syndrome, recurrent neurologic symptoms, anemia, pyramidal signs, and marked hyperhomocysteinemia should prompt early metabolic screening. An antibody result should be interpreted alongside the clinical phenotype, biochemical profile, imaging findings, and CSF data, rather than used alone to assign etiology.

title: Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome associated with SLC16A2 c.1384G>A (p.Gly462Arg): A family case report with retrospective molecular diagnosis in a deceased sibling.
authors: Li L, Li J, Li Z, Lv H, Sun J, Wang X, Hao S, Zheng L, Wang S, Li Z, Li S.
abstract: Rationale Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (monocarboxylate transporter 8 deficiency) is an X-linked disorder caused by pathogenic variants in SLC16A2, with severe neurodevelopmental impairment and a characteristic high-triiodothyronine (T3)/low-thyroxine (T4) thyroid profile. SLC16A2 c.1384G> A (p.Gly462Arg; NM_006517.5) was reported previously. We describe a Chinese family with the same variant, including retrospective molecular confirmation in a deceased maternal half brother. Patient concerns The proband was evaluated at 4.3 years for profound developmental delay. He could not sit, stand, or walk independently and had an intelligence quotient of 36, axial hypotonia with peripheral hypertonia, dystonia, muscle atrophy, joint contractures, and bilateral cryptorchidism. Diagnosis Thyroid testing showed elevated free triiodothyronine and total triiodothyronine, decreased free thyroxine and total thyroxine, and mildly elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed delayed myelination, a thin corpus callosum, and widened frontal subarachnoid spaces. Whole-exome sequencing identified hemizygous SLC16A2 c.1384G> A (p.Gly462Arg); Sanger sequencing confirmed the variant in the proband and heterozygosity in his mother. The same hemizygous variant was detected in DNA from the archived neonatal dried blood spot of a maternal half brother who had severe developmental delay and died at 16 months. Thyroid tests, neuroimaging, and cause of death were not recorded for the deceased child. Interventions The proband received physical, occupational, and speech therapy and underwent bilateral orchiopexy. Triiodothyroacetic acid was not available at diagnosis. Outcomes At the last documented follow-up at age 5 years, he remained unable to sit, stand, or walk independently. Clinical notes described improved head control, but no repeat standardized developmental score was available. Epileptiform electroencephalogram discharges persisted, but no clinical seizures were documented. Lessons This family provides additional clinical and segregation evidence for p.Gly462Arg. Testing an archived neonatal blood spot established the diagnosis in the deceased sibling and strengthened genetic counseling. SLC16A2 testing should be considered in boys with unexplained severe neurodevelopmental delay and a high-triiodothyronine/low-thyroxine pattern. Functional studies are still required to define the effect of p.Gly462Arg on monocarboxylate transporter 8 trafficking and thyroid hormone transport.

title: Age-stratified reference intervals for cerebrospinal fluid total protein in adults undergoing lumbar puncture: A 19-year retrospective study.
authors: Tian Y, Li J, Chen K, Hu Y, Han D, Li S, Wang N, Huang Y, Li R, Xiao J, Xie J, Li L.
abstract: Using 19 years of retrospective clinical data, we estimated age-stratified reference intervals for cerebrospinal fluid total protein (CSF-TP) in a selected reference-like subset of Chinese adults undergoing diagnostic lumbar puncture. We also examined factors associated with CSF-TP concentrations. A retrospective analysis was conducted using 29,519 CSF-TP test records from patients who underwent lumbar puncture at Zhongshan City People's Hospital between 2006 and 2025. Of these, 4217 records met the basic age and laboratory criteria; after structured chart review of the clinical history, 253 candidate cases remained. After 2 statistically identified outliers were removed, 251 cases were included. Nonparametric methods were used to estimate CSF-TP reference intervals (P2.5-P97.5) for the overall sample and the 2 age groups, and 90% confidence intervals were estimated using bootstrap resampling. Sex-stratified estimates were considered exploratory. The overall reference interval for CSF-TP in the study population was 18.13 to 73.33 mg/dL. When stratified by age, individuals aged 18 to 48 years had a reference interval of 17.15 to 55.37 mg/dL, while those aged 49 to 85 years had a higher interval of 21.85 to 80.51 mg/dL. A positive correlation was observed between CSF-TP concentration and age (Spearman's ρ = 0.35, P < .001). The median CSF-TP in the 49- to 85-year-old group was 40.9 mg/dL, which was 19.2% higher than the median of 34.3 mg/dL in the 18- to 48-year-old group. In addition, a significant sex difference was found: males had a median CSF-TP of 38.7 mg/dL, which was higher than the median of 34.2 mg/dL observed in females (P < .001). Statistically significant associations were also found between CSF-TP and cerebrospinal fluid white blood cell and red blood cell counts, but their explanatory power was limited (white blood cell: Pearson r = 0.1684, r2 = 0.0284; red blood cell: Pearson r = 0.1293, r2 = 0.0167). In this single-center reference-like subset of adults undergoing diagnostic lumbar puncture, CSF-TP increased with age. The age-related reference intervals estimated in this study require direct-method validation and may assist the interpretation of CSF-TP results in similar clinical populations.
