title: Adverse event signals associated with targeted therapy plus chemotherapy in colorectal cancer: A FAERS-based pharmacovigilance study.
authors: Liu Y, Li Z, Li G, Lin H.
abstract: Real-world safety profiles of targeted therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) remain incompletely characterized, particularly across different chemotherapy backbones. This study characterizes adverse event (AE) reporting patterns for bevacizumab (BVZ), cetuximab (C225), and panitumumab (VEC), used as monotherapy or in combination with folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) or folinic acid, fluorouracil, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI), within CRC-related reports. CRC-related AE reports from 2006 to 2025 for BVZ, C225, and VEC were extracted from the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System. Disproportionality signals were evaluated using 4 algorithms: the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio, Bayesian confidence propagation neural network, and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker. Time-to-onset, regimen-stratified, and exploratory univariable logistic regression analyses were also conducted. The non-case reference population was restricted to the CRC-related reporting subcohort rather than the entire FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database. A total of 38,117 reports were identified, mainly involving BVZ (n = 20,521). Hematologic, hepatobiliary, and gastrointestinal toxicities showed prominent reporting signals across regimens (ROR = 4.15, 2.84, and 2.46, respectively). BVZ was associated with proteinuria and hand-foot syndrome, while C225 and VEC showed prominent cutaneous and marrow-suppression signals. Nine AE terms overlapped across agents, including thrombocytopenia, with fatality proportions of 23%, 13%, and 10% for BVZ, C225, and VEC, respectively. Median onset of nonfatal thrombocytopenia differed by agent: 121 days for BVZ, 6 days for C225, and 40 days for VEC; fatal C225-associated events also occurred early (median 6 days, P = .006). FOLFOX strengthened thrombocytopenia signals, especially with VEC-FOLFOX (ROR = 10.5) and C225-FOLFOX (ROR = 9.3), and peripheral neuropathy was reported across FOLFOX-containing regimens. CRC targeted therapies showed agent- and regimen-specific AE reporting patterns. Thrombocytopenia varied by onset and fatality and was more prominent with FOLFOX-containing regimens. These findings support tailored monitoring, particularly platelet surveillance for C225 and FOLFOX-based combinations, with longer-term vigilance for BVZ. Given the limitations of spontaneous reporting, including potential co-medication, indication-related, and residual confounding, these signals should not be interpreted as establishing causality.

title: Adult-onset Still's disease and sarcopenia-related traits - muscle mass, strength, and function: A bi-directional Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Wang J, Peng P, Wang Y, Zheng X, Wei Y, Sui X, Xu H, Liu H, Zhang S.
abstract: The causal relationship between adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and sarcopenia remains unclear. Therefore, we employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the causal link between these 2 conditions. This study investigated the causal relationships between AOSD (n = 201,947) and sarcopenia-related traits, including low handgrip strength (n = 256,523), left handgrip strength (n = 406,552), right handgrip strength (n = 461,089), appendicular lean mass (ALM, n = 450,243), and walking pace (WP, n = 459,915). In the first stage, AOSD served as the exposure variable, while the sarcopenia-related traits treated as the outcome variables; in the second stage, the roles were reversed. MR analysis employed inverse variance-weighted, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger methods. Cochran's Q statistic was used to assess heterogeneity, while MR-Egger regression and MR-PRESSO were utilized to evaluate pleiotropy. The robustness of the findings, risk of bias, and causal direction were assessed using leave-one-out analysis, funnel plots, and R2 statistics. AOSD may contribute to reduced muscle mass and strength, but not to impaired muscle function. Genetically predicted AOSD is causally associated with reduced ALM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.971, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.951-0.991; P = .005) and increased risk of low hand grip strength in individuals over 60 (OR = 1.046, 95% CI: 1.001-1.091; P = .048). It also reduces left hand grip strength (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.976-0.992; P < .001), with no significant effect on right hand grip strength (OR = 0.995, 95% CI: 0.987-1.003; P = .240). with no effect on WP is also observed (OR = 0.994, 95% CI: 0.988-1.001; P = .080). Genetically predicted sarcopenia-related traits (ALM and bilateral grip strength) had no robust causal effect on AOSD. While inverse variance-weighted suggested nominally significant associations of reduced grip strength (≥60 years) and slower WP with AOSD, these results were inconsistent across MR methods and warrant cautious interpretation. AOSD leading to a decline in muscle mass, strength However, it does not significantly affect muscle function, whereas most sarcopenia-related traits showed no convincing causal effect on AOSD. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Mohammad HR, Rahman A, Muhammad IM, Gill SS, Selim A, Thomas G, Murray DW, Griffin XL.
abstract: Aims To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. Results A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. Conclusion DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

title: A bibliometric analysis of haemocoagulase: Trends, impact, and future directions.
authors: Shen J, Guo X, Dai Q, Shi J.
abstract: Background Haemocoagulase is extensively employed for the prophylaxis and management of surgical hemorrhage owing to its favorable safety profile, rapid onset of action, and sustained therapeutic effect. However, this agent exhibits a unique pharmacological duality: despite its primary hemostatic action, it paradoxically carries a risk of inducing bleeding. Furthermore, a specific subtype of haemocoagulase possesses anticoagulant and thrombolytic properties and is utilized in the treatment of ischemic cerebrovascular diseases and sudden sensorineural hearing loss. Method Publications on haemocoagulase and related thrombin-like enzyme preparations were identified in the Science Citation Index Expanded database of the Web of Science Core Collection. The structured search was limited to English-language articles and reviews published between 1 January, 1971 and 2 November, 2025. The search combined haemocoagulase, batroxobin, reptilase, venombin A, and closely related terminology. Records were screened by title and abstract, and the final dataset was analyzed bibliometrically. CiteSpace was used for reference and keyword clustering, timeline visualization, and citation burst detection; VOSviewer was used for co-authorship and keyword co-occurrence networks. Results The bibliometric dataset comprised 489 publications contributed by 2037 authors at 565 institutions in 40 countries or regions. China, Capital Medical University, researcher B Blombäck, and the journal *Thrombosis Research* as key contributors; early studies focused on thrombin and anticoagulation therapy, while current research emphasizes serine proteases, fibrinogen, and snake venom-related studies. Conclusion This bibliometric analysis systematically characterizes the global research landscape of haemocoagulase based on published literature. Current scholarly works on haemocoagulase mainly focus on hemorrhagic adverse events related to its clinical application, as well as its therapeutic effects on ischemic cerebrovascular disease and sudden sensorineural hearing loss, which represent the dominant research hotspots in this field. Publication, citation, and keyword patterns indicate growing research attention to broader clinical applications and combination-treatment questions. These patterns describe the published literature and do not establish clinical efficacy, comparative benefit, or causal mechanisms.

title: Ultrafast brain MRI at 3 T for suspected acute ischemic stroke: interchangeability of the ultrafast and standard protocols.
authors: Ozaki K, Ishida S, Haseyama S, Sugioka E, Tanahashi Y, Goshima S.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the interchangeability of the super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR)-based ultrafast protocol with the standard protocol for acute ischemic stroke detection at 3 T. Materials and methods In this prospective study, 100 patients (mean age, 66.1 ± 16.2 years; 65 men) with suspected acute ischemic stroke underwent both the standard and ultrafast protocols (diffusion-weighted, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, and T2*-weighted imaging). All images were reconstructed using SR-DLR; the ultrafast protocol employed accelerated acquisition with a reduced scan time. Two radiologists independently assessed both protocols for acute ischemic lesion detection, vascular territory involvement, and clinically relevant secondary findings. Interchangeability was evaluated using the individual equivalence index (IEI), with a prespecified ± 0.05 equivalence margin. Results Acute ischemic stroke was confirmed in 30 patients (30%). The ultrafast protocol reduced the mean total acquisition time by 61.7% (1 min 43 s vs. 4 min 29 s; P Conclusion The ultrafast protocol was interchangeable with the standard protocol for detecting acute ischemic stroke, with reduced scan time and comparable or marginally improved image quality; however, this work-in-progress diffusion-weighted imaging algorithm warrants further validation.

title: Title: Impact of Coexisting Gout on Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Data from the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative (OBRI).
authors: Kwok TS, Movahedi M, Cesta A, Akhavan P, Carter Thorne J, Pope J, Lau A, Mirza R, Hepworth E, Chow A, Aydin SZ, Kuriya B, OBRI Investigators.
abstract: Objective To determine the prevalence and factors associated with coexisting gout in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and evaluate whether concomitant gout is associated with worse RA disease activity. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of RA patients enrolled in the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative, a multicentre real-world cohort across Ontario, Canada. Coexisting gout was defined by patient- or physician-reported diagnosis or xanthine oxidase inhibitor use. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with coexisting gout and the impact of gout on oral glucocorticoid (GC) use. The association between baseline gout and longitudinal RA disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index, CDAI ≤10) was examined using mixed-effects logistic regression at 24-months, adjusting for prespecified confounders. Results Among 3,703 RA patients, 113 (3.1%) had coexisting gout with mean (SD) age of 66.1 (8.7) years and 52.2% were female. Coexisting gout was associated with older age (OR 1.05 per year), obesity (OR 1.67), cardiovascular disease or hypertension (OR 1.95) and diuretic use (OR 1.68), while female sex was inversely associated (OR 0.31). CDAI scores were similar between patients with and without gout at baseline (18.3±12.5 vs 20.2±13.5) and at 12-months (10.9±9.8 vs 11.0±10.4). After adjustment, baseline coexisting gout was neither significantly associated with oral GC use at 12-months (OR 1.73, 95% CI: 0.96-3.13) or the attainment of CDAI low disease activity/remission by 24-months (OR 1.19, 95% CI: 0.72-1.97). Conclusion In this large real-world RA cohort, coexisting gout was uncommon and associated with traditional gout risk factors but did not statistically influence oral GC use or RA treatment target attainment.

title: Three working windows posterior midline approach for posterior column tibial plateau fractures.
authors: Wang X, Zhang S, Yan J, Jiang D, Shi C, Yin Z, Liang B.
abstract: Background Isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression are challenging because conventional posterior approaches limit instrument trajectories and reduction vectors for distinct posterior fragments. Methods Ten patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures accompanied by combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression were treated using a posterior midline skin incision organized into three working windows. The central window served as the foundational posterior corridor, with medial and lateral windows developed as functional extensions to facilitate region-specific reduction and fixation. Relevant clinical data and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed. Results Postoperative radiographs of all 10 patients showed satisfactory joint reduction and alignment. Radiographic fracture union was achieved in all cases at a mean of 13.9 weeks, with a mean follow up of 11.8 months. At final follow up, mean knee flexion was 124.0°, and mean knee extension was -2.1°, and the mean Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score was 90.8 points. One patient developed a superficial wound infection that resolved with antibiotic treatment, and one patient experienced deep vein thrombosis that was successfully treated with anticoagulation therapy. No neurovascular injuries, deep infections, or fixation failures were observed during follow up. Conclusion A posterior midline approach organized into three working windows may provide a feasible option for selected isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression, allowing region-specific posterior fixation through a single posterior skin incision.

title: The osteoporosis-fracture paradox in older Taiwanese men: lower osteoporosis prevalence but comparable fragility fracture burden.
authors: Lee YY, Huang YC, Kao SW, Chen YC, Cheng MT.
abstract: Despite a substantially lower prevalence of osteoporosis than age-matched women, older men experienced a relatively comparable burden of fragility fractures, demonstrating a marked dissociation between osteoporosis prevalence and fracture burden. Purpose Although osteoporosis is less common in men than in women, male fragility fractures carry substantial morbidity and post-fracture mortality. Whether the lower prevalence of osteoporosis translates into a proportionally lower fracture burden remains unclear. We compared the prevalence of osteoporosis and fragility fractures between age-matched Taiwanese men and women. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated 2093 men undergoing clinical dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) between 2021 and 2023, of whom 2031 met eligibility criteria and were compared with 2031 age-matched women selected via 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching. Osteoporosis was defined as a T-score ≤-2.5 at the lumbar spine, femoral neck and/or total hip. Vertebral and hip fractures were identified from radiographs and electronic medical records. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of fracture. Results The prevalence of osteoporosis in men was approximately half that in women (32.4% vs. 51.4%; P Conclusions Older Taiwanese men exhibited a substantially lower prevalence of osteoporosis than age-matched women but experienced a relatively comparable burden of fragility fractures. These findings demonstrate a marked dissociation between osteoporosis prevalence and fragility fracture burden in older men and reinforce the importance of comprehensive fracture risk assessment integrating BMD with clinical risk factors.

title: The osteoporosis diagnosis and treatment gaps in Iranian older adults: Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program.
authors: Hesari E, Fahimfar N, Khalagi K, Yarmohammadi H, Shahrousvand S, Zarepour P, Gharibzadeh S, Mansourzadeh MJ, Sahafiee G, Farhadi A, Larijani B, Ostovar A, Sanjari M.
abstract: This study examined why many older adults in Iran with osteoporosis are not diagnosed or treated. It found very high rates of missed diagnosis and lack of treatment, especially influenced by age, gender, and education. Addressing these gaps is essential to improve awareness, care access, and prevent serious bone-related health problems. Background Despite the availability of diagnostic and therapeutic facilities for osteoporosis, a significant proportion of older adults remain undiagnosed and untreated. This care gap may stem from various barriers and understanding the underlying reasons for these disparities is crucial for developing targeted interventions. This study aimed to investigate the gaps in osteoporosis diagnosis and treatment among older adults in Iran and to identify the key factors contributing to these gaps. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed data from two phases of the Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program. Participants were selected using multistage cluster random sampling. The first phase, conducted between 2015 and 2017, included 2424 residents aged 60 and above. The second phase, from 2018 to 2021, involved 1721 residents aged 50 and above. Bone mineral density (BMD) was measured using the Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry method and T-score ≤ -2.5 in either of the femoral neck, total hip, or spinal sites was defined as osteoporosis. Participants reported whether a doctor had diagnosed them with osteoporosis and if they received treatment. Those diagnosed via bone densitometry but unaware of their condition were considered underdiagnosed. Those diagnosed through BMD tests but not on osteoporosis medication were considered undertreated. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify determinant factors of the underdiagnosis and undertreatment of osteoporosis. Results A total of 4145 elder adults with a mean age of 65.5 (54.40% female) participated in this study. Underdiagnosis and undertreatment in the participants who underwent DXA were estimated at 1050 (73.06% (and 1328 (92.41), respectively. The undertreatment rate was 666 (91.98%), 836(90.96%) and 868 (92.53%) based on the intervention thresholds of FRAX without BMD, MOF-FRAX with BMD and FRAX with TBS for MOF, respectively. A statistically significant association was found between osteoporosis underdiagnosis and variables including male (OR = 0.57, P Conclusion This study highlights significant gaps in the diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis among participants, with significant disparities linked to demographic and socioeconomic factors. Further research is needed to investigate the causes and extensive interventions at the population level should be taken to fill the gap and raise awareness on osteoporosis as a growing public health concern and provide access to the treatment of the disease.

title: The association of ABO Rh blood groups with 30-day mortality following traumatic injury - A retrospective observational study in the East of England.
authors: Li J, Bell R, Basheer B, Boyle A, Barnard E, Bowman J, Barrett L.
abstract: Background ABO and RhD antigens are expressed on the surface of red blood cells; ABO antigens are also expressed on the surface of endothelial and some epithelial cells. Associations between ABO blood groups and disease have been reported in numerous areas of medicine. Recently there have been conflicting reports of an association between blood group O and mortality following trauma, none of which examine a combination of ABO and RhD groups. The aim of our study was to identify associations between all ABO RhD groups and trauma mortality. Methods A retrospective analysis of trauma patients ≥ 16-years-old admitted to the East of England Major Trauma Centre, and who were included in the Trauma, Audit, & Research Network (TARN) database, 2016-2019. The primary outcome was a comparison of 30-day all-cause mortality between all eight ABO RhD groups. Secondary outcomes included injury pattern analysis on outcome. Results 4188 patients were included; median age 59.3 [IQR 39.0-77.9] years old, and 2634 (62.9%) were male. The median injury severity score was 19.0 [10.0-25.0]. 30-day mortality was 9.3%, and there were significant differences in mortality across groups (p = 0.0094). O negative was associated with greater 30-day mortality compared to all other seven ABO RhD groups combined: 15.1% vs 8.8%; relative risk (RR) 1.7 (95%CI 1.3-2.2), p = 0.0002. Conclusions In this UK study we have demonstrated that blood group O negative is associated with a greater risk of 30-day all-cause mortality in undifferentiated trauma patients. Future trauma studies should consider including ABO RhD blood group as a baseline characteristic to ensure this does not confound results.

title: TMJ Dislocation in Dependent Older Adults in PA/LTC: A Recognition-to-Maintenance Framework.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
authors: Choi E.
abstract: Objectives To reframe temporomandibular joint dislocation as a potentially reversible oral-function emergency in post-acute and long-term care (PA/LTC) and propose a recognition-to-maintenance framework for older adults unable to reliably report symptoms. Design Problem-based narrative review and commentary, illustrated by deidentified composite vignettes. Setting and participants Older adults in PA/LTC, rehabilitation, nursing home, and LTC hospital settings, particularly those with communication impairment, neurologic disease, frailty, edentulism, denture use, enteral feeding, or recent airway manipulation. Methods PubMed was searched from inception, with the search updated on September 8, 2026, using 3 complementary strategies (755 records; 466 unique after deduplication). The updated search results were reviewed for relevance against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and clinically informative sources meeting these criteria were incorporated into the narrative synthesis to identify PA/LTC recognition and maintenance gaps. Results Available evidence, consisting mainly of reviews, retrospective series, and case reports, suggests 3 PA/LTC-relevant vulnerabilities: presentation that is silent or absorbed into neurologic or frailty-related explanations, uncertain onset, and failure to verify maintained reduction or detect recurrence. During neurologic workup, dysarthria, drooling, facial asymmetry, feeding decline, and apparent dysphagia may trigger stroke-oriented assessment while mouth closure may not be deliberately assessed, and dislocation may both mimic and be mimicked by dystonic conditions. The proposed "last-known-normal jaw closure" question is intended as a practical bedside prompt, not a validated triage metric. Conclusions and implications In PA/LTC, temporomandibular joint dislocation should be approached as a recognition-to-maintenance problem. Same-day assessment of oral-function change, avoidance of repeated forceful attempts, maintained-reduction verification, and caregiver-facing recurrence surveillance warrant validation.

title: Step-specific temporal patterns in robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy: an exploratory CUSUM analysis.
authors: Takahashi A, Tanaka Y, Yoneoka Y, Deguchi M, Nakamura A, Amano T, Tsuji S.
abstract: Learning curves for robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy (RSC) are commonly evaluated using total operative or console time, although RSC consists of multiple technically distinct steps. We explored step-specific temporal efficiency patterns using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. We retrospectively analyzed the first 29 consecutive RSC procedures performed by a single surgeon with approximately 100 prior robotic procedures and experience in robotic surgical instruction. Seven procedural steps were timed using prespecified video landmarks. CUSUM curves and Spearman correlations with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were used to describe temporal efficiency patterns. The console-time CUSUM peak was used only for a descriptive post hoc early-versus-late illustration and was not treated as an independently validated learning transition. Median operative and console times were 183 and 139 min, respectively. Neither total operative time nor total console time showed a significant monotonic relationship with case sequence, although both mean-centered CUSUM curves reached their maximum positive deviation at case 14. Step-specific temporal patterns varied substantially. Hysterectomy, anterior and posterior mesh suturing, and peritoneal closure showed negative correlations with case sequence, whereas bladder dissection showed the opposite trend and a later CUSUM peak. Early-versus-late comparisons were descriptive and did not independently validate a transition point. RSC demonstrated heterogeneous step-specific temporal efficiency patterns that were not captured by total console time alone. Because the global time trends were flat, the phase cutpoint was data-derived, and technical quality and safety were not assessed, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of proficiency or training effectiveness.

title: Squat training using virtual target trajectories with structured variability matches traditional training in performance accuracy.
authors: Grigoriadis S, Mavromoustakos-Blom P, Stergiou N, Nikodelis T.
abstract: Strength training often prioritizes exact repetition, potentially constraining movement exploration and adaptability. Optimal Movement Variability Hypothesis posits that structured variability builds robust coordination and improves responsiveness to perturbations, yet whether trainees can accurately execute squats under such variability remains unclear. Grounded in motor-learning and complex-systems accounts, we tested whether young adults can track variable targets with and without structure, while squatting. Participants controlled a virtual avatar with deep/shallow squats and lateral leans to follow onscreen targets. Sixty-seven individuals were randomized to three conditions: non-variable (repeated positions; n = 18), structured variability (pink noise positions; n = 24), and non-structured variability (white-noise positions; n = 25). Performance was assessed across five sets of 30 targets. Accuracy was quantified as target-avatar spatial error; temporal organization was indexed with detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA). The structured and non-variable groups exhibited lower spatial error than the non-structured group, particularly in later sets. DFA was highest in the structured group, intermediate in the non-structured group, and lowest in the non-variable group, indicating more persistent temporal organization under structured variability. Findings indicate that structured-variability squats match traditional accuracy while promoting more organized temporal structure, supporting integration into training and the feasibility of gamified resistance protocols to enhance robustness and skill.

title: Spiral Jejunal Reconstruction of Both Pancreatic Stumps in Type II Portal Annular Pancreas during Pancreaticoduodenectomy: A Case Report.
authors: Suzuki H, Ishikawa K, Bamba T, Nakano M, Inagaki Y, Hamada K, Shoji S, Mori M.
abstract: Introduction Portal annular pancreas (PAP) is a rare congenital anomaly in which the uncinate process encircles the portal vein (PV) or superior mesenteric vein (SMV) and fuses with the dorsal aspect of the pancreatic body. We herein report a case of ampullary carcinoma associated with PAP treated by subtotal stomach-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy. Case presentation A 51-year-old woman presented with scleral icterus and watery diarrhea. Following a detailed examination, she was diagnosed with carcinoma of the ampulla of Vater and underwent surgical treatment. During pancreatic resection, 2 pancreatic cut surfaces were identified on the ventral and dorsal sides of the SMV, leading to the intraoperative diagnosis of PAP. A lifted jejunal limb was rotated in a spiral fashion, and pancreaticojejunostomy was performed for each pancreatic stump. The postoperative course was uneventful, with no evidence of postoperative pancreatic fistula, and the patient was discharged in good condition. Conclusions Although PAP is a rare anatomical anomaly, it requires careful attention during surgical procedures and reconstruction; therefore, it should be recognized preoperatively whenever possible. The reconstruction method employed in the present case may be useful as a reconstructive option for PAP because it avoids excessive pancreatic resection. We report this case with a review of the relevant literature.

title: Smaller Ischiofemoral Space Is Associated With Proximal Hamstring Injuries.
authors: Itthipanichpong T, Retzky J, Curran P, Menta SV, Ranawat AS.
abstract: Purpose To develop a reference ischiofemoral space (IFS) value for patients with proximal hamstring injuries (HSI) and to compare it with individuals without proximal hamstring pathology. Methods We retrospectively collected the data from our institution. Patients aged 18 years or older with a proximal HSI were included. Patients with insufficient imaging data, those with prior hip surgery, those with concurrent femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, and those with concurrent ischiofemoral impingement as defined by quadratus femoris edema on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were excluded. A 1:2 matched-cohort analysis was conducted. Two cohorts were (1) patients with proximal HSI and (2) patients with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome as a control cohort (Control). Both pelvic anteroposterior (AP) radiographs and axial MRI were used to assess IFS and were compared between the 2 cohorts. Additionally, the neck-shaft angle was collected and compared. Results There were 60 patients in the HSI cohort and 124 patients in the control cohort. The mean neck-shaft angle, IFS from the AP pelvis, and IFS from the axial MRI for the HSI cohort were 136.35° ± 5.63°, 24.35 ± 8.60 mm, and 26.57 ± 7.96 mm, respectively. For the control cohort, these values were 135.30° ± 4.53°, 29.83 ± 9.84 mm, and 29.28 ± 8.54 mm, respectively. The IFS in the HSI group was significantly lower than that in the control group on both pelvic AP radiograph ( P P = .036). Conclusions Patients with proximal HSI had a smaller IFS compared with those with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Short-term prognostic models for functional improvement in rheumatic diseases: an exploratory prospective study.
authors: Doskaliuk B, Fedorovych K, Yatsyshyn R.
abstract: Objective To identify baseline factors associated with clinically meaningful short-term improvement in patient-reported physical function and to develop exploratory prognostic models for LEFS and DASH response in patients with rheumatic diseases. Methods This prospective observational study included 64 adults with heterogeneous rheumatic and musculoskeletal diagnoses, assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks of individualized routine pharmacological treatment. Clinically meaningful improvement was defined as a ≥ 9-point increase in the Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) and a ≥ 12-point decrease in the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) score. Separate univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed for each outcome. Apparent model performance was assessed using AUROC and Brier scores, while regression-coefficient uncertainty was examined using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results LEFS response occurred in 43/64 patients (67.2%) and DASH response in 35/64 (54.7%). Shorter disease duration, lower GAD-7 score, and lower BMI were independently associated with response in both models. Higher total protein and lower baseline LEFS were additionally associated with LEFS response, while higher hemoglobin was associated with DASH response. The models demonstrated high apparent discrimination in the development cohort, without optimism correction, with AUROCs of 0.928 (95% CI 0.866-0.990) for LEFS and 0.910 (95% CI 0.837-0.984) for DASH. Corresponding apparent Brier scores were 0.100 and 0.111. Conclusion Simple routinely available baseline characteristics showed promising value for short-term prognostic stratification of functional improvement. The models remain exploratory and their predictive performance requires internal and external validation before clinical application.

title: Severe ARDS and secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis complicating a flare of adult-onset Still's disease: a case-based review.
authors: Karigowda L, Wong V, Tran A, Lau W.
abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder in which parenchymal lung disease is an increasingly recognised complication, and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) - that is, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) secondary to an autoinflammatory or autoimmune condition (MAS-HLH) is a well-established one. Both carry disproportionately high morbidity and mortality. Although AOSD-associated lung disease and MAS-HLH are increasingly recognised as co-occurring manifestations of the same hyperinflammatory process, their combination, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) as the most severe form of lung involvement, remain under-reported. We report a 42-year-old woman with a background of AOSD who developed severe ARDS in the context of a five-week interruption of conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) around incision and drainage of a perianal abscess with complicating fistulous disease and a flare during that period. She developed severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure requiring intubation on the day of admission and later prone positioning, subsequently complicated by development of MAS-HLH, evidenced by hyperferritinaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia, fever and bone marrow-confirmed haemophagocytosis. Her disease trajectory was further complicated by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation. Management required sequential multi-target immunomodulation with corticosteroids, anakinra, ruxolitinib, tocilizumab and rituximab. She was mechanically ventilated for 19 days in intensive care and discharged from ICU on day 34 and from hospital following clinical stabilisation on day 73. This case illustrates that AOSD-related pulmonary disease can present as fulminant ARDS rather than the more indolent infiltrative patterns typically described and may be associated with other manifestations of AOSD including MAS-HLH. Because of concomitant infection and viral reactivation, the illness could not be attributed to AOSD alone. The case also describes survival following early multidisciplinary, multi-target immunomodulation delivered alongside antimicrobial cover, although the overlapping use of several agents precludes any conclusion about their individual or combined efficacy.

title: Research culture methods detect more anaerobes compared to conventional clinical workflows in periprosthetic joint infection: a pilot study of 14 cases.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Visperas A, Lu Q, Lehman B, Foo SS, Chen W, Vachharajani V, Stappenbeck T, Piuzzi N.
abstract: Introduction Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most challenging complications of total joint arthroplasty, often complicated by limitations in diagnostic sensitivity. Standard clinical culture methods fail to identify pathogens in 20%-50% of cases, leading to potential under- or overtreatment. This pilot study aimed to compare the microbial detection capabilities of standard clinical culture methods with enhanced research laboratory techniques, and to explore whether additional microbial findings might have the potential to influence antibiotic treatment planning. Materials and methods Thirteen patients undergoing surgery for PJI, as defined by the 2018 International Consensus Meeting (ICM) on Infection criteria, were prospectively enrolled at a single academic medical center between August 2023 and September 2024. Intraoperative synovial fluid, periprosthetic tissue, and implant swabs were collected and processed using both standard clinical workflows and optimized research protocols. Culture results and treatment decisions were reviewed in collaboration with Infectious Disease specialists. Results Both methods identified primary organisms. However, research techniques detected additional organisms not captured by clinical cultures (p = 0.013). Despite these differences, overall detection rates were comparable (57.1% vs. 59.5%; p = 0.963), with the research workflow achieving similar yield with fewer samples. The potential impact of additional isolate identification on antibiotic selection, if deemed clinically significant, did not appear to result in meaningful changes to antibiotic regimens, although this may have been influenced by the empiric use broad-spectrum antibiotics. Conclusions Clinical culture methods may not detect all organisms in PJI, highlighting possible limitations in current diagnostic approaches. Although this pilot study did not directly assess the impact of enhanced microbial detection on antibiotic prescribing and treatment decisions were largely unchanged, these findings suggest that a more comprehensive microbial detection could potentially inform antibiotic selection and warrants further investigation.

title: Quality of life in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: positive associations with younger age, higher education, low disease activity, and corticosteroid and cyclophosphamide treatment-cross-sectional study in northwestern Poland.
authors: Bobrowska-Snarska D, Snarska-Pękała W, Jurkowska Z, Brzosko M, Przepiera-Będzak H.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) - chronic autoimmune disease affecting health-related quality of life (QoL). To estimate the associations between QoL and age, disease activity, education level, and treatment in patients with SLE. We studied 200 SLE patients. Data collected: sex, age, disease duration, socioeconomic status, disease activity, and treatment. QoL was assessed using the Lupus Quality of Life Questionnaire (LupusQoL), 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ). Younger patients reported better QoL (all p 0.05). The use of CS improved physical health (p = 0.01) and physical functioning (p = 0.03) in the LupusQoL and SF-36, respectively. Intravenous cyclophosphamide improved physical health (p = 0.01), oral cyclophosphamide improved intimate relationships (p = 0.003) in the LupusQoL. Secondary and higher education correlated positively with planning (p = 0.007 and p = 0.005, respectively) and intimate relationships (p = 0.0001 and p = 0.0002, respectively) in the LupusQoL and with role limitations due to emotional problems (p = 0.01 and p = 0.007, respectively) in the SF-36. QoL assessment in patients with SLE was positively associated with younger age, higher education, low disease activity, and treatment.

title: Normal Creatine Kinase in Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies: Disease Characteristics and Outcomes.
authors: Keret S, Chandra T, Kaly L, Silva RL, Gkiaouraki E, Pongtarakulpanit N, Gopalarathinam R, Reddy KS, Moghadam-Kia S, Oddis CV, Aggarwal R.
abstract: Objectives Creatine kinase (CK) is an important biomarker for monitoring idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM). Data regarding normal CK in IIM are limited. We aimed to characterize patients with normal CK levels and investigate the association between CK and disease activity and outcomes. Methods Data were collected from the Rituximab in Myositis (RIM) trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of refractory adult IIM. Myositis core set measures (CSMs) were collected every 4 weeks for 44 weeks. Normal/ near-normal was defined as Results Of 143 patients, 53 (37%) had normal CK. These patients were more frequently White (85% vs. 62%, p Conclusion Normal CK levels are common in IIM, especially in DM, and do not exclude active muscle disease. CK functions as a longitudinal biomarker across IIM, with performance varying by disease subset and baseline CK, supporting nuanced clinical interpretation.

title: Lung Transplantation with Planned Delayed Chest Closure in Severe Pectus Excavatum after Multiple Pleurodeses: A Case Report.
authors: Nakano Y, Watanabe T, Notsuda H, Ikushima T, Kumata S, Onodera K, Watanabe Y, Hirama T, Suzuki T, Oishi H, Kochi T, Okada Y.
abstract: Introduction Lung transplantation combined with pectus excavatum repair has been reported in selected patients with severe pectus excavatum to expand the restricted thoracic cavity and facilitate graft accommodation. However, the safe implementation of this surgical strategy may be challenging in patients with extensive pleural adhesions after repeated pleurodeses, because of the increased risk of postoperative bleeding and re-thoracotomy. Case presentation A 15-year-old boy with interstitial lung disease, secondary pulmonary hypertension, severe pectus excavatum, and multiple prior bilateral pleurodeses underwent deceased-donor bilateral lung transplantation using a planned delayed chest closure (DCC) strategy. Preoperative CT showed marked thoracic deformity with a Haller index of 9.1 and a leftward mediastinal shift. Because extensive pleural adhesions were expected to complicate graft implantation and hemostasis and increase the risk of re-thoracotomy for postoperative bleeding, a 2-stage strategy consisting of planned DCC followed by pectus bar placement at definitive chest closure was established at the time of transplant listing in collaboration with an external pectus specialist. Bilateral lung transplantation was performed under venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support, followed by temporary chest closure. At the second-stage operation on POD 2, 2 pectus bars were placed, and additional graft volume reduction was performed, allowing definitive chest closure without hemodynamic compromise. The patient was discharged home on POD 69 without wound complications or implant-related infections. Conclusions This case suggests that lung transplantation may be feasible in carefully selected patients with severe pectus excavatum and extensive pleural adhesions, with appropriate multidisciplinary planning. A preplanned 2-stage strategy incorporating DCC and pectus bar placement at definitive chest closure represents a potential option for such complex cases.

title: Lumbopelvic fixation for high-energy sacral fractures and spinopelvic dissociation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of complications, unplanned revision and implant removal.
authors: Patel HA, Patel S, Suresh RI, Yang E, Lindley AK, Kidd G, Schneider MB, Zareef U, Padovano A, Bivona LJ, Cavanaugh DL, Koh EY, Hashmi SZ, France JC, O'Toole RV, Ludwig SC, Jauregui JJ.
abstract: Introduction Secondary procedures after lumbopelvic fixation (LPF) include planned implant removal, removal for symptoms and revision for complications. Their differing indications, together with limited comparative evidence, complicate counselling and surgical planning. Methods PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420251036375) for comparative and single-arm studies (≥10 LPF patients). High-energy injuries and fragility fractures were considered separately. Random-effects models summarised complications, unplanned revision, implant removal and within-study comparisons of surgical approaches and fixation strategies. Results Twenty-five studies were included (22 high-energy, 3 fragility). Across 19 high-energy LPF cohorts (564 patients), pooled surgical-site infection was 9.3% (95% CI 6.1-14.1), implant loosening or failure was 5.3%, nonunion occurred in 4 of 389 patients (1.0%) and loss of reduction in 2 of 355. Pooled unplanned revision was 11.9% (95% CI 8.7-16.0; prediction interval 5.3-24.3), most often for infection or wound complications. Implant removal was 79.0% in routine-removal series and 17.3% in selective-removal series. Four studies compared minimally invasive and open LPF. Pooling three studies showed less blood loss with minimally invasive LPF (mean difference -271 mL, 95% CI -367 to -175) and shorter operative time (-51 min, -97 to -5); the operative-time association did not persist with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Infection (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.09-1.83) and revision (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.09-1.43) estimates were inconclusive. Four cohorts comparing LPF with posterior pelvic-ring fixation alone reported higher odds of revision after LPF (OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.63-9.60), with substantial potential for confounding by indication. Certainty was very low. Conclusions Nonunion and loss of reduction were infrequent after LPF, while unplanned revision most often involved infection or wound complications. Implant removal varied with institutional policy and warrants separate counselling. Minimally invasive LPF was associated with less blood loss, but comparative evidence remains insufficient to establish lower complication rates, equivalent mechanical outcomes or superiority of either fixation strategy.

title: Learning curve of da vinci robotic lobectomy: a single-surgeon CUSUM analysis of operative time and perioperative outcomes.
authors: Lo CM, Tsai MY, Huang DKR, Lai HH, Chen Y, Li SH.
abstract: To characterize the operative-time learning curve for da Vinci robotic-assisted lobectomy in a single surgeon's initial experience, and to examine, using trend analyses of patient comorbidity and surgical-complexity variables and adjusted regression models, whether any apparent change in operative time was influenced by a shift in case complexity. We retrospectively reviewed 47 consecutive patients who underwent da Vinci robotic-assisted lobectomy performed by a single board-certified thoracic surgeon at Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital between September 30, 2024, and July 6, 2026. Patients who underwent wedge resection, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), segmentectomy, or resection with the da Vinci SP system were excluded. Cases were ordered chronologically, and cumulative sum (CUSUM) of operative time was calculated as the cumulative deviation from the group mean. Because CUSUM based on the mean deviation is a descriptive method without formal decision limits, a 10,000-iteration permutation test was used to construct an empirical 95% decision-limit envelope and to test whether the observed CUSUM path exceeded the range expected under random case ordering; leave-one-out and moving-average sensitivity analyses were also performed. Early and late phases, divided at the CUSUM peak, were compared using the Mann-Whitney test for continuous variables and Fisher's exact test for categorical variables; time to chest tube removal was additionally analyzed with the Kaplan-Meier method and log-rank test. The relationship between case sequence and Charlson Comorbidity Index and surgical-complexity variables (tumor size on pathology, malignant histology, pathologic T category, nodal status, stage, operative lobe, concomitant procedures, lymph node yield, pleural adhesions) was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation and Fisher's exact test; operative time was additionally modeled by linear regression with robust standard errors, adjusted successively for malignancy, tumor size, nodal status, lobe, concomitant procedures, and Charlson index. The CUSUM curve for operative time peaked at case 20 (value 265.0), with a nearly equal local peak at case 10 (260.5); leave-one-out and smoothing analyses showed the identified peak was unstable between cases 10 and 20, and the entire observed CUSUM path remained within the 95% permutation-derived decision-limit envelope (global p = 0.73), indicating that this descriptive breakpoint could not be formally distinguished from random case-to-case variation at this sample size. Operative time did not differ significantly between early (n = 20) and late (n = 27) phases (median 315.0 [IQR 283.8-357.2] vs. 284.0 [268.5-338.0] minutes, p = 0.186) and showed no monotonic trend with case sequence overall (Spearman's ρ = 0.01, p = 0.93). Chest tube duration differed significantly between phases on both Mann-Whitney testing (p = 0.041) and Kaplan-Meier/log-rank analysis (χ²=5.43, p = 0.020), although this and other secondary comparisons were not corrected for multiplicity. Charlson Comorbidity Index increased significantly with case sequence (ρ = 0.34, p = 0.02); the other surgical-complexity variables moved in the same direction without reaching significance (malignant histology 65% vs. 89%, p = 0.07; concomitant procedures 5% vs. 19%, p = 0.22), tumor size did not change (median 2.2 vs. 2.1 cm, p = 0.80), lobe distribution did not differ between phases, and no patient had pleural adhesions. Adjustment for malignancy and these variables did not materially change the association between case sequence and operative time (unadjusted - 0.03 min per case, 95% CI - 1.53 to + 1.46; fully adjusted + 0.12, - 1.48 to + 1.72) or the early-late difference (- 23.1 min unadjusted vs. -16.0 min adjusted; all p ≥ 0.27), although confidence intervals were wide. By the time of the CUSUM-identified breakpoint (lobectomy case 20), the surgeon had already accumulated 39 total robotic console cases when segmentectomy, wedge resection, and da Vinci SP cases are included. In this single-surgeon series, the operative-time CUSUM breakpoint at approximately case 10-20 should be interpreted as an exploratory, descriptive signal rather than a formally validated learning-to-proficiency transition, as it was not statistically distinguishable from random variation and the dichotomized early/late operative-time comparison was not significant. Comorbidity burden increased significantly over the study period and surgical-complexity indicators trended in the same direction, and adjustment for them did not alter the operative-time estimates; there was thus no evidence that the surgeon progressively selected easier cases, but the small sample precludes firm conclusions, and adhesion severity could not be studied because no patient had adhesions, so the findings may not apply to patients with adhesions. The surgeon's cumulative robotic experience at the time of the breakpoint substantially exceeded the lobectomy case count alone once other robotic procedures are considered.

title: Inequality in secondary fracture prevention supports prioritisation of fracture liaison services in coastal health plans in England and Wales.
authors: Pugh L, Clemeno F, Ghumman R, Javaid MK.
abstract: The 2021 UK Chief Medical Officers' annual report highlighted poorer health in coastal communities but did not include osteoporosis or secondary fracture prevention. Using Fracture Liaison Services database (FLS-DB) data, FLSs in coastal areas were shown to have poorer performance and lower parenteral osteoporosis medication recommendation rates, supporting inclusion of FLSs in coastal health improvement plans. A number of studies have highlighted socio-economic deprivation as a predictor of fragility fractures and poorer outcomes after fracture. In parallel, coastal areas are recognised to be areas with poorer health outcomes, in part due to socio-economic deprivation. Purpose To describe secondary fracture prevention in terms of FLS provision and quality in coastal vs. non-coastal healthcare settings using routinely collected audit data. Methods A cross-sectional, ecological analysis using the missed opportunity counts from the national Fracture Liaison Service (FLS-DB) and Hip Fracture (NHFD) Databases of England and Wales audit data with Office for National Statistics classification of coastal towns. Results Results Coastal sites were not significantly more likely to be non-FLS vs FLS providers (38% vs 24%, p = 0.18). However, coastal FLSs had higher missed opportunity patient counts than non-coastal FLSs (p = 0.02), with lower vertebral identification rates (14.2% vs 20.9%, p = 0.02). While treatment rates were similar, coastal FLSs had significantly lower rates of parenteral anti-resorptive therapy recommended (p Conclusion We have demonstrated a coastal deleterious effect on the quality of secondary fracture prevention of FLS providers as measured by missed opportunities for treatment, vertebral fracture identification and recommendation of parenteral anti-resorptive therapies. Coastal health priority plans in the NHS should prioritise effective FLS provision.

title: Global research on cricket injuries (1982-2025): A bibliometric analysis.
authors: Vaishya R, Singh A, Gupta BM, Vaish A, Dhillon MS, Parmar Y, Orchard J.
abstract: Background Cricket is one of the most widely played sports worldwide and carries a significant burden of musculoskeletal injuries, particularly among fast bowlers. Over the past four decades, research in cricket injury epidemiology, biomechanics, workload monitoring, and surveillance has expanded substantially. Objective To conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global cricket injury research, identifying growth trends, influential publications, leading contributors, collaboration networks, and major thematic domains. Methods Publications from 1982 to 2025 were systematically analyzed using bibliometric indicators including annual growth, authorship productivity, institutional and country contributions, citation impact, total link strength (TLS), and co-authorship networks. The top 100 cited papers and the top 10 highly cited papers (HCPs) were examined in detail to identify landmark contributions and research priorities. Results A sharp rise in publications occurred after 2003, with nearly 90% of output produced in the last two decades. Australia, the United Kingdom, and South Africa led in productivity, citation impact, and collaborative link strength. The top 10 HCPs accounted for 10% of papers but 37.25% of total citations, underscoring concentrated scholarly influence. Fast bowlers consistently demonstrated the highest injury incidence, particularly lumbar spine and lower limb injuries. Workload spikes were strongly associated with increased injury risk, establishing load monitoring as a central preventive strategy. Biomechanical factors such as mixed bowling action, trunk rotation, and front-knee mechanics were linked to lumbar stress injuries. Standardized injury definitions and international consensus surveillance frameworks significantly improved research quality and comparability. Conclusion Cricket injury research has evolved into a mature, collaborative, and high-impact domain centered on fast bowling biomechanics, workload regulation, and surveillance standardization. Expanded global participation and integration of advanced analytics are essential for future injury prevention strategies.

title: From fistula to malignancy: rectal mucinous adenocarcinoma arising in a chronic perianal fistula, a rare diagnostic challenge.
authors: AlMuhsin AM, Tahtouh M, Al Rashid F, Alruwaii ZI, Alshangiti A, Bosaid F.
abstract: Perianal fistula is a common surgical complaint that general surgeon frequently face in daily clinical practice. However, an adenocarcinoma arising from a fistula is an uncommon entity that has the propensity to mimic benign conditions leading to a delays in diagnosis and management. We present a case of a 42-year-old patient with long standing history of perianal fistula. Given the prolonged nature of his disease further investigations were warranted. While colonoscopy ruled out luminal disease, pelvic magnetic resonance imaging and deep tissue biopsies confirmed the diagnosis of invasive adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous component. The patient required neoadjuvant treatment followed by extra levator abdominoperineal excision and pelvic floor reconstruction. At 5-year follow up, the patient didn't have local recurrence or distant metastasis.

title: Fracture characteristics in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus: Clinical significance of medial trochlear involvement.
authors: Ishihara N, Saeki M, Fujihara Y, Saeki S, Tanaka H, Ota H, Kumagai H, Yazaki N, Yamamoto M.
abstract: Background Coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus exhibit diverse fracture-extension patterns that are not fully characterized by conventional classification systems. The clinical significance of fracture extension into the medial or lateral column remains incompletely understood. This study investigated fracture-extension patterns beyond the conventional Dubberley classification and evaluated their associations with clinical outcomes and bone-related complications. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included surgically treated coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus with a minimum follow-up of 12 months at four affiliated institutions between 2012 and 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO/OTA and Dubberley systems. Computed tomography (CT) images were reviewed to assess medial trochlear involvement, lateral column involvement without posterior condylar comminution, and isolated trochlear fractures. Clinical outcomes included elbow range of motion (flexion, extension, and arc of motion) and postoperative complications. Univariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with bone-related complications. Results Among 374 surgically treated distal humeral fractures, 35 coronal shear fractures were included in the final analysis. Medial trochlear involvement was identified in 8 fractures (23%) and was most frequently observed in Dubberley type 3 fractures. Patients with medial trochlear involvement had significantly greater loss of elbow extension at final follow-up than those without medial trochlear involvement (-29° vs. -16°, P = 0.042). Bone-related complications were more frequent in fractures with medial trochlear involvement than in those without (50% vs. 7%, P = 0.016). In univariate logistic regression analysis, medial trochlear involvement was significantly associated with bone-related complications (odds ratio, 12.5; 95% confidence interval, 1.69-92.3; P = 0.013). Neither the AO/OTA nor the Dubberley classification was significantly associated with bone-related complications. Conclusions Medial trochlear involvement was significantly associated with greater loss of elbow extension and bone-related complications at final follow-up in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus. Preoperative CT assessment of medial trochlear involvement may provide clinically useful information complementary to conventional fracture classification systems and may aid surgical planning.

title: Femoral Stem Design Influences Early Periprosthetic Fracture Risk Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
authors: Krez AN, Toomey SD, Swanson KC, Herndon CL, Danoff JR.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic femur fracture (PFF) is a significant complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Modern collared, triple-taper metaphyseal-filling stems may reduce fracture risk. This study compared a triple-taper metaphyseal stem with other cementless designs to assess early PFF risk, fracture risk by age and bone quality, and the impact of collar position. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 774 primary cementless THAs, including triple-taper metaphyseal (n = 311), single-wedge (n = 294), double-wedge (n = 116), and gradual taper/metadiaphyseal-filling (n = 53) stems. Triple-taper stems were implanted through a prospective multicenter trial, while comparison stems were from a single health system. Patients were stratified by stem design, age, Dorr classification, and collar position. The primary outcome was 90-day PFF. Results PFF occurred in 53 patients (6.8%), including 15 (1.9%) postoperative fractures requiring reoperation. Patients with PFF were older ( P P = .02). Triple-taper stems demonstrated lower PFF risk than other designs (odds ratio 0.20; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.48; P P P = .02). Conclusions Collared, triple-taper metaphyseal stems were associated with lower early PFF risk across patient ages and bone quality profiles. Seating the collar on the calcar further reduced fracture incidence.

title: Expert-based classification on the technical difficulty of single-port urological robotic procedures.
authors: Bruyère F, Grilo N, Soria F, Oderda M, Anderson C, Crivellaro S, Lucca I, Gontero P.
abstract: Single-port (SP) robotic surgery represents the latest paradigm shift in minimally invasive urology. Despite its progressive adoption worldwide, no structured classification of procedural difficulty exists for SP urological procedures. We aimed to develop an expert-based scoring system to grade the technical difficulty of urological procedures performed with the da Vinci SP platform. A questionnaire-based expert-consensus study was conducted during an international meeting on SP robotic surgery (Turin, Italy, February 2026). Consensus here refers to the descriptive convergence of independent, single-round ratings rather than a formal iterative (e.g., Delphi) consensus process. Eligible experts had independent or assisted SP robotic experience. Using a structured questionnaire, they rated each procedure on three dimensions - technical difficulty, operative risk and sustained attention required - on a 7-point Likert scale. A composite difficulty score was obtained by summing the three median values. Experts also estimated the number of cases required to reach proficiency and rated the role of prior multi-port robotic experience. Nine procedures were classified. Composite scores ranged from 8 (pyeloplasty, "slightly difficult") to 16 (radical cystectomy with intracorporeal diversion, "very difficult"). Estimated proficiency thresholds ranged from 10 to 33 cases. All experts considered prior multi-port robotic experience necessary before SP adoption. Early challenges were dominated by prolonged operative time, limited exposure and reduced ergonomics rather than instrument collision or spatial disorientation. We propose the first structured expert-based difficulty classification for SP robotic urological surgery. The procedural hierarchy mirrors historical laparoscopic and multi-port robotic classifications, supporting the concept that intrinsic complexity transcends the platform. This framework may inform training curricula, case selection during adoption and safe dissemination of SP robotic surgery.

title: Evaluating the transfer effects of skill acquisition principles on performance in academy soccer players.
authors: More-Chevalier B, Romero Clavijo FA, Labbe D, Faubert J, Romeas T.
abstract: Despite growing evidence for the benefits of skill acquisition principles (SAPs), their effects in real-world settings remain understudied. This study examined the transfer effects of SAPs on soccer players' performance. Fifty male youth players (16.54 ± 1.01 years) and eight professional coaches from an elite soccer academy participated in a within-subject design including a control phase followed by an experimental phase where coaches applied seven SAPs. Performance was assessed at four time points (T0-T3) using match statistics and a video-based test of declarative knowledge. SAP implementation and training load were monitored during all training sessions, and changes over time were analyzed with generalized linear models and t-tests. Following successful SAPs implementation ( p p p < .05). SAPs implementation produced clear changes in training dynamics and trends of transfer in declarative knowledge, while on-field transfer remained limited, likely requiring longer consolidation or more sensitive performance assessment measures.

title: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis is associated with reduced lung function independent of structural lung abnormalities.
authors: Harlianto NI, Oudkerk SF, de Jong PA, Pompe E, Foppen W, Verlaan JJ, Vliegenthart R, Groen HJM, Mohamed Hoesein FAA.
abstract: Introduction Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) has been associated with lower lung volumes and function, but it is unknown whether this is due to structural lung disease. This study aimed to investigate DISH and reduced lung function and volume in relation to structural lung disease in individuals with long-term smoking history. Methods Participants were included from the NELSON lung cancer screening trial. Structural lung abnormalities were automatically quantified (emphysema, airway wall thickness, and air trapping), or visually assessed (interstitial lung abnormalities, bronchiectasis, centrolobular emphysema) by two chest radiologists. Multivariate linear regression analyses were performed with adjustment for participant factors and structural lung disease. Results Among 3514 subjects (100% male, mean age 60.4 years), DISH was present in 241 (6.7%). Individuals with DISH had lower prevalence of Respiratory Bronchiolitis Interstitial Lung Disease (5%vs. 10.4%, p = 0.04) and of centrilobular emphysema (3.3%vs. 7.6%, p = 0.009), but greater airway wall thickness (2.6 vs. 2.4 mm, p 1 (95%CI: -7.1% to -1.7%), 150 ml lower FEV 1 (95%CI: -160, -140 ml), 4.0% lower predicted FVC (95%CI: -6.2%, -1.7%), 170 ml lower FVC (95%CI: -280, -70 ml) and 210 ml lower CT measured lung volume (95%CI: -40, -1 ml), compared to subjects without DISH. Conclusion In long-term smokers, DISH was associated with lower lung function and volumes, not explained by structural lung abnormalities on CT. These findings suggest that DISH may be an extrinsic factor contributing to reduced lung function as a result of thoracic cage stiffening.

title: Diagnostic performance and reproducibility of standardized two-plane ultrasound cine clips for supraspinatus tendon pathology.
authors: Khan S, Lee J, Jibri Z, de Oliveira Cyrineu F, Sampaio ML.
abstract: Objective To determine the diagnostic performance and reader reproducibility of standardized two-plane cine clips for supraspinatus tendon pathology, using the complete radiologist-supervised shoulder ultrasound examination as the clinical reference standard. Materials and methods This prospective single-centre study screened 140 consecutive shoulder ultrasound examinations. Standardized longitudinal and transverse supraspinatus cine clips were independently reviewed by two fellowship-trained musculoskeletal radiologists blinded to the clinical report. Reader 1 read all included examinations (24 twice); Reader 2 read 51. Diagnostic performance (exact 95% confidence intervals) was calculated against the same-day clinical ultrasound report, and reliability with Cohen's κ. Reporting radiologists could access the standardized clips. Results Of 140 examinations, 114 were analyzed (mean age 57 years; 56 women). Reader 1 showed high performance for full-thickness tears (sensitivity 87% [95% confidence interval 69-96%], specificity 98% [92-100%]) and complete tears (sensitivity 73% [39-94%], specificity 97% [92-99%]). Calcific tendinopathy yielded sensitivity/specificity of 79%/85%; partial-thickness tears, 57%/87%; and tendinopathy, 92%/28%. Reader 2 sensitivity was 92% [64-100%] for full-thickness and 18% [2-52%] for partial-thickness tears. Intra-observer κ ranged from 0.17 (tendinopathy) to 0.89 (full-thickness tears). Inter-observer κ was 0.95 for full-thickness, 0.56 for complete and 0.21 for partial-thickness tears. Conclusion Standardized two-plane cine clips demonstrate high diagnostic performance and inter-observer reliability for full-thickness supraspinatus tears. For complete tears, inter-observer agreement was moderate and sensitivity was imprecise. Given limited sensitivity for partial-thickness tears and low specificity for tendinopathy, cine clips alone are insufficient for these pathologies and should complement rather than replace complete real-time shoulder ultrasound examinations.

title: Creation of an Annual Summer Faculty Development Series Centered on Faculty- and Author-Led Book Discussions.
authors: Weathers R, Chawla A, Hoel A, Alam H, Nadig SN, Williams-Karnesky RL.
abstract: Objective Continuous faculty development is a critical component of ensuring quality education for surgical trainees. This paper presents a novel approach to faculty development, utilizing faculty- and author-led book discussions to create a highly engaging series. Design We followed the 4-Cs approach to increasing engagement with faculty development. Each annual faculty development series was anchored by discussion of a leadership development book. Setting Single large academic institution with a primary academic medical center and multiple regional sites. Participants About 24 and 31 faculty participated in the first and second summer development series, respectively. Results Our annual summer faculty development series provides an integrated, interactive and intentional career development experience for surgical faculty in various stages of their career, which has led to robust and continuous engagement. Conclusion A faculty- and author-led book discussion series is an effective approach to increasing surgeon engagement with faculty development.

title: Cost saving strategies for management of postmenopausal women with fragility fractures in Taiwan: a simulation projection model from 2025 to 2045.
authors: Huang ST, Lai HY, Wang CY, Hsiao FY, Yang RS.
abstract: This study used a microsimulation model to assess the impact of improved osteoporosis diagnosis, treatment, and adherence in Taiwan. The combined approach prevented 42,605 fractures and saved NT$4.64 billion by 2045. The results emphasize the importance of comprehensive anti-osteoporosis management in evidence-based healthcare policy. Introduction Taiwan's rapidly aging population presents mounting challenges for osteoporosis management, with healthcare resources increasingly constrained under the National Health Insurance system. This study projected the clinical and economic impact of enhanced osteoporosis diagnosis, treatment, and adherence strategies among postmenopausal women in Taiwan from 2025 to 2045. Methods A cross-sectional microsimulation model projected annual osteoporotic fracture incidence and costs among postmenopausal women aged ≥65 years. Fracture risk was estimated using simplified Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX), with inputs from published literature and national health insurance data informing demographic distribution, treatment patterns, and healthcare costs. Three scenarios evaluated: (1) improved medication adherence alone, (2) increased case finding through enhanced screening and treatment rates, and (3) combined case finding and adherence improvements. Results In the reference scenario, the annual number of osteoporotic fractures are projected to increase by 99% from 137,557 in 2025 to 273,820 in 2045, with annual costs rising from NT$20.10 billion to NT$39.32 billion. Enhanced case finding prevented 12,061 fractures and saved NT$1.21 billion in 2025, escalating to 23,983 prevented fractures and NT$2.49 billion saved by 2045. Improved adherence alone prevented 14,853 fractures (NT$1.57 billion saved) in 2025, increasing to 22,525 fractures (NT$2.33 billion saved) by 2045. The combined approach demonstrated superior outcomes, preventing 22,045 fractures (NT$2.32 billion saved) in 2025 and 42,605 fractures (NT$4.64 billion saved) by 2045. Conclusion Comprehensive osteoporosis management strategies incorporating enhanced case finding and improved adherence will substantially reduce clinical and economic burden in Taiwan's aging population over the next two decades, supporting evidence-based healthcare policy development.

title: Closed reduction in distal radius fractures: manual manipulation vs. finger trap traction-a prospective randomized controlled clinical trial.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Benedikt S, Horling L, Bode S, Stock K, Schmidle G, Arora R.
abstract: Background Initial treatment of distal radius fractures (DRF) can be either performed without reduction or with a reduction method as finger-trap traction (FTT) only or by additional manual reduction (MR) under hematoma block. There is no clear evidence on which reduction method is superior, however, MR is more invasive and seems to lead to higher pain levels and more post reduction complications. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical relevance of MR compared to FTT in acute DRFs. Materials and methods Study design was a prospective, single-centre, balanced randomized [1:1], and parallel grouped, controlled trial. Inclusion criteria were patients with a DRF type A2, A3 or C according to the AO classification and a dorsal tilt of ≥ 10°. The patients were randomized either in the FTT or in the MR group. Depending on the patient's functional demand and the fracture configuration, conservative or operative treatment was initiated. Over one year, clinical and radiological data were assessed at six follow-ups. Results A total of 53 patients were included. Regarding radiological results neither FTT nor MR achieved sufficient reduction results (median dorsal tilt was - 16 to -18 after one year) and none of the techniques was superior. The clinical results between the conservatively treated groups were comparable and showed no significant difference. Complications included one CRPS in the conservative MR group, one CRPS after FTT and operation, one secondary carpal tunnel syndrome in the conservative FTT group and one skin lesion after MR. Conclusion Manual reduction under haematoma block showed no benefit. In patients with AO type A2, A3 and type C fractures and a dorsal tilt ≥ 10° only FTT (if required under a haematoma block or comparable analgesia) is recommended regardless of whether surgery is performed or not. Level of evidence Level I randomized controlled trial. Trial registration number ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07697976, registered 06/22/2026, retrospectively registered, www. Clinicaltrials gov .

title: Clinical patterns and major organ involvement in Behçet's syndrome: a latent class analysis of a regional cohort.
authors: Varkal G, Gökdemir GŞ.
abstract: Behçet's syndrome is a heterogeneous disease with diverse patterns of organ involvement. We aimed to identify clinical subgroups using latent class analysis and evaluate clinical characteristics and treatment patterns across the identified subgroups and sex. We retrospectively evaluated 136 patients fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease. Latent class analysis (LCA) based on six clinical indicators was used to identify clinical subgroups. Clinical manifestations, major organ involvement, and current treatments were compared between the identified latent classes and by sex. Major organ involvement occurred in 79 patients (58.1%). Among the standard LCA models, the two-class solution had the lowest BIC. Class 1 (40.4%) was characterized by absence of pathergy positivity and a very low probability of papulopustular lesions (1.3%), but a higher probability of ocular involvement (60.0%). Class 2 (59.6%) showed high probabilities of pathergy positivity (90.7%) and papulopustular lesions (57.7%). Major organ involvement was more frequent in Class 1 than in Class 2 (70.9% vs. 49.4%, p = 0.020). Male patients had significantly higher rates of ocular (52.7% vs. 35.5%, p = 0.044), vascular (28.4% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.003), and major organ involvement (73.0% vs. 40.3%, p < 0.001), as well as current anti-TNF therapy (23.0% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.019), than female patients. Patients with major organ involvement had significantly lower rates of genital ulcer history (51.9% vs. 84.2%, p < 0.001), pathergy positivity (45.6% vs. 70.2%, p = 0.004), and joint involvement (11.4% vs. 28.1%, p = 0.013). The BIC-selected solution identified two main patient groups, but the class structure was highly sensitive to indicator selection. Overall, our findings support exploratory clinical patterns rather than fixed Behçet phenotypes, with major organ involvement being significantly more frequent among men.

authors: Farina N, Bizioli P, Capparelli E, Guidelli GM, Boffini N, Laria A, Rinaldi M, Cullia MC, Renna D, Cariddi A, Fraticelli G, Tomelleri A, Baldissera E, Matucci-Cerinic M, Selmi C, Faggioli P, Filippini M, Dagna L.

title: Bilateral Lateral Tarsal Artery Bypass and Free Flap Reconstruction of an Infected Gangrenous Heel in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: A Case Report of Three-Year Functional Limb Salvage.
authors: Yokoyama N, Kikuchi S, Jinno H, Uramoto T, Takahashi K, Kamada K, Tatsukawa T, Moriyama U, Yoshida Y, Hinooka R, Fujiki T, Azuma N.
abstract: Introduction Distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is technically demanding when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and revascularization alone seldom heals an extensive heel defect. Case presentation A man in his 60s receiving maintenance hemodialysis presented with bilateral CLTI and gangrene of the left heel after failed endovascular therapy, and bilateral major amputations had been considered before referral. Both limbs were classified as Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stage 4. Diffuse calcification of the infrapopliteal and pedal arteries left the lateral tarsal artery (LTA) as the only suitable distal target, and bilateral superficial femoral artery-to-LTA bypasses were performed with in situ great saphenous vein grafts under nerve block anesthesia. Because repeated debridement left the calcaneus exposed, a free latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap anastomosed to the left bypass graft was transferred and covered with a split-thickness skin graft. The wounds healed after minor amputations, and the patient regained independent ambulation. An ulcer subsequently developed on the weight-bearing surface of the transferred flap and never healed despite pressure-relieving insoles and additional inflow angioplasty; nevertheless, the flap remained viable, both grafts remained patent, and ambulatory function was preserved until the patient died of an unrelated cause 3 years after revascularization.
