Conclusions The LTA can serve as a distal bypass target when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and, when combined with free flap reconstruction, it may achieve long-term functional limb salvage despite extensive heel gangrene. The reconstructed weight-bearing heel nevertheless remains prone to ulceration that may not heal, so preventive off-loading and long-term surveillance are essential.

title: Beyond the heart: a large-cohort study of <sup>11</sup>C-PiB PET revealing organ-specific uptake patterns and diagnostic thresholds in systemic AL amyloidosis.
authors: Zhou Z, Zheng D, Lv Y, Dai Z, Wei S, Wang X, Ruan W, Li H, Gai Y, Liu Q, Sun C, Lan X, Qin C.
abstract: Purpose Systemic AL amyloidosis frequently involves multiple organs, yet non‑invasive imaging for early and comprehensive multi‑organ assessment remains limited. The diagnostic role of 11 C-PiB PET beyond the heart-particularly its organ‑specific uptake patterns and clinically applicable thresholds-has not been systematically defined in a large cohort. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 80 participants (60 ± 10 years, 55 males) undergoing Whole-body 11 C-PiB PET/MR or PET/CT from 2018 to Sep 2024. Final diagnoses were as follows: AL group (n = 65), non‑AL group (n = 10), control group (n = 5). PET indices (SUVmax, SUVRmax, ASUVRmax, ASUVRmean) were quantified for 15 organs. Optimal diagnostic cutoffs were derived using ROC analysis or quartiles. Correlations with clinical and morphofunctional markers were assessed. Results Organ-specific uptake patterns differed across tissues, with clear disease-related accumulation observed in the myocardium, spleen, bone marrow, and tongue, whereas interpretation was limited in organs affected by physiological tracer kinetics, such as the kidney. Myocardial PiB uptake correlated significantly with NT‑proBNP, native T1, and ventricular wall thickness; hepatic uptake was paradoxically reduced, with negative correlations with ALP and projected liver area; renal uptake correlated positively with eGFR and negatively with β2‑microglobulin. Organ-specific diagnostic thresholds were established using the optimal-performing semiquantitative parameters: myocardium SUVmax 2.20 (sensitivity 90%, specificity 100%, AUC 0.995); tongue SUVmax 2.05 (86%, 100%, AUC 0.971); bone marrow SUVRmax 2.05 (70%, 100%, AUC 0.880); liver SUVmax 7.95 (88%, 80%, AUC 0.900). Quartile‑based thresholds further defined involvement in the spleen, thyroid, and salivary glands. Conclusions In this study, 11 C-PiB PET revealed distinct organ-specific uptake patterns and diagnostic thresholds for systemic AL amyloidosis across multiple organs were preliminarily established. It provides a non-invasive, biopsy‑sparing assessment of multi-organ involvement while highlighting organ-specific limitations, particularly related to renal uptake interpretation and the need for further validation in selected tissues.

title: An In-depth Bibliometric Study of Complex General Surgical Oncology (CGSO) Fellowship Graduates Within the First 5-year Period of Independent Practice.
authors: Zheng H, Zheng-Pywell R, Sebikali-Potts A, Russell G, Levine EA, Shen P.
abstract: Introduction The objective of the study is to create a bibliometric profile for recent graduates of complex general surgical oncology (CGSO) fellows to understand their very early career trajectory and inform the current training paradigm. Methods Bibliometric profiling of applicants to our CGSO fellowship program from 2017 to 2021 who completed an accredited program were included. Impact factors were adjusted for authorship position and type of publication. Results Among 232 CGSO graduates, 106 (45.7%) were female, 118 (50.9%) practice at a university-based flagship hospital (UBFH), 57 (43.2%) published, on average, more than 2 manuscripts per year after at least 2 years in independent practice. The median years in independent practice were 3 years (range 1-5 years). As they progressed in their training and career, the proportions of graduates who published, their level of involvement, the type, and quality of their publications evolved. Only 24 (10.3%) graduates published in basic science or translational research studies after fellowship. In a linear regression model, institution type (estimated means UBFH 7.1 vs. non-UBFH 2.8, p Conclusion Majority of CGSO graduates do not consistently publish after fellowship. a minority of them engage in basic science or translational research despite great emphasis during fellowship application. A dual-track model to differentiate clinical and research-oriented fellows is needed.

title: A composite inflammation-nutrition-coagulation score and 1-year mortality in geriatric proximal femur fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Bozgeyik B, Kaya O, Önder C, Atmaca E, Çakar A.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of a composite score integrating the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), serum albumin, and D-dimer levels for predicting 1-year mortality in geriatric patients with proximal femur fractures. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study included 300 patients aged ≥ 65 years who were admitted with proximal femur fractures and underwent surgical treatment between November 2023 and March 2026. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected from hospital records. A composite score based on NLR, albumin, and D-dimer was calculated. An exploratory unweighted 0-3 composite score was constructed from cohort-derived ROC thresholds for NLR, albumin, and D-dimer. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox regression, calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were performed to evaluate predictive performance. Results A total of 300 patients were analyzed, of whom 75 (25.0%) died within 1 year. Non-survivors were older and had significantly higher NLR and D-dimer levels and lower albumin levels (all p Conclusions In this retrospective single-center cohort, the composite score integrating NLR, albumin, and D-dimer was associated with 1-year mortality and showed promising apparent discriminatory performance. The score should be considered an exploratory prognostic tool that may complement comprehensive clinical assessment and support future risk-stratification research. Prospective multicenter studies with external validation and evaluation of clinical impact are required before its use in routine practice can be considered.

title: YouTube Videos on Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition Show Low-to-Moderate Quality and Reliability.
authors: Conteduca J, Longo D, Piacquadio F, Casto A, Valentino L, Bernetti A, Rollo G.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the quality and reliability of YouTube videos on arthrogenic muscle inhibition (AMI) using validated assessment instruments and to identify predictors of higher-quality content. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed English-language YouTube videos identified on November 2, 2025, using the search terms "arthrogenic muscle inhibition" and "AMI." Video quality was assessed using the DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Global Quality Score instruments. Assessments were performed independently by 2 experienced knee surgeons. Correlations between quality scores and video characteristics (views, likes, comments, time online, duration, source, and topic) were analyzed using nonparametric tests and multivariate regression with Bonferroni correction. Results A total of 45 videos were analyzed. Mean scores were 44.9 ± 20.5 for DISCERN, 1.47 ± 1.56 for Journal of the American Medical Association, and 2.93 ± 1.53 for Global Quality Score, indicating overall low-to-moderate quality. Video quality was strongly correlated across scoring systems ( ρ > 0.86, P P ρ = -0.37, P = .046). Video topic was the strongest independent predictor of video quality ( P Conclusions YouTube videos on AMI demonstrate low-to-moderate quality and reliability, with substantial variation by topic and content type. Clinical relevance Improving the quality of online AMI-related content may enhance patient education and promote accurate dissemination of rehabilitation information.

title: Variation in urobiome composition over time in asymptomatic individuals with spinal cord injury and disease using intermittent catheterization.
authors: Tractenberg RE, Groah SL, Newcomb E, Khemmani M, Joyce C, Wolfe AJ, Riegner CR.
abstract: Urinary tract infection (UTI) remains the most common infectious complication among individuals with neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (NLUTD) due to spinal cord injury or disease (SCI/D). Despite widespread reliance on microbiological and symptom-based criteria for UTI diagnosis, significant ambiguity persists-especially in distinguishing clinically meaningful change from normal variability in urinary analysis results. This uncertainty contributes to overdiagnosis, inappropriate antibiotic use, and antimicrobial resistance. The present study sought to operationalize "normal variability" of the urinary microbiome (urobiome) among adults with NLUTD due to SCI/D. Using repeated samples collected from asymptomatic individuals over time, we analyzed inter- and intra-individual microbial composition to determine stability and fluctuation under baseline conditions. We observed wide intra- and inter-individual variability, substantial overlap between asymptomatic and pre-symptomatic states, and a consistent predominance of genera conventionally labeled as "uropathogens" including Escherichia/Shigella, Klebsiella, Enterococcus, Staphylococcus, and Streptococcus, even in the absence of symptoms. Bray-Curtis dissimilarities between paired samples ranged from 0 to 1, confirming substantial within-person compositional change over time. These findings suggest that assumptions drawn from cross-sectional studies-linking particular taxa or diversity values to health or disease-are not supported within individuals over time, at least in people with NLUTD due to SCI/D. Empirically characterizing normal within-person variability is a prerequisite both for interpreting urobiome results in this high-risk population and for improving the accuracy and stewardship of UTI diagnosis and treatment.

title: Using archaeometabolomics to characterise tobacco-usage in human cortical bone from 17th to 19th century Dutch communities.
authors: Bonicelli A, Davies-Barrett AM, Serrano Ruber M, Sandhu J, Jones DJL, Inskip SA.
abstract: Detecting tobacco consumption in historical populations is a complex challenge often encountered by archaeologists. Traditional methods typically involve the morphological examination of teeth for pipe-notches and/or staining. However, when teeth are absent, discerning tobacco-usage becomes impossible, highlighting the need for alternative approaches. Recently, metabolomics has gained attention as a promising tool in the analysis of archaeological artefacts and human remains, offering new insights into ancient smoking habits. In this study, we applied a combination of reversed-phase (RP) C18 and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC), both coupled with mass spectrometry, to analyse a Dutch population spanning pre- and post-tobacco archaeological contexts. Our statistical approach focused on the multivariate analysis of each assay, followed by the integration of the two datasets, and Random Forest modelling to test the effect of covariables. The results demonstrated some separation between tobacco consuming and non-consuming groups, as evidenced by distinct metabolomic profiles in the omic blocks. The single block model exhibited a bias towards correctly classifying the tobacco-consumer group, with a balanced estimation error of 0.375 for the C18 assay. Additionally, integrating the two datasets produced a similar classification accuracy potentially driven by the RP classification potential, particularly when distinguishing between pre- and post-tobacco contexts. Overall, our findings confirm the potential of mass spectrometry-based metabolomics as a powerful tool for studying tobacco consumption habits in past populations, although further work is needed to disentangle wider affects from other variables and tightly dated samples are needed. This method could be validated in the future and complement current morphological methods.

title: Two-Dimensional Electromagnetic Navigation-Assisted Percutaneous Transforaminal Endoscopic Discectomy for Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
authors: Wei Z, Cheng H, Gao R, Wang X, Niu K, Tao Z, An H, Huang B, Xiong C, Lian J.
abstract: Objective To compare the clinical performance, safety, radiation exposure, and learning curve of two-dimensional (2D) electromagnetic navigation-assisted percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy (PTED) with those of three-dimensional (3D) electromagnetic navigation-assisted PTED in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Methods This retrospective cohort study included 82 patients with LDH who underwent PTED between January 2022 and June 2024. Patients were classified into the 2D electromagnetic navigation group or the 3D electromagnetic navigation group according to the navigation workflow used during surgery. Perioperative variables, including total operative time, navigation registration time, radiation exposure, and complications, were recorded. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the visual analogue scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and modified MacNab criteria. Learning curves for both the surgeon and the radiologic technologist were evaluated using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. Results Compared with the 3D group, the 2D group demonstrated a significantly shorter total operative time (66.64 ± 9.67 vs. 88.92 ± 15.98 min, p Conclusion 2D electromagnetic navigation-assisted PTED is a safe and clinically effective alternative to 3D electromagnetic navigation-assisted PTED for the treatment of LDH. Relative to the 3D workflow, the 2D approach offers greater procedural efficiency, reduced radiation exposure, and a shorter learning curve. Although longitudinal analysis revealed different recovery patterns over time for low back pain and ODI between the two groups, both techniques achieved substantial postoperative improvement, favorable final clinical outcomes, and comparable safety. These findings suggest that simplified 2D electromagnetic navigation may represent a more practical and scalable option for routine clinical application.

title: Transverse Cervical Vessels: A Viable Option for Microsurgical Reconstructions in Vessel-Depleted Necks.
authors: Torres Gonzalez JC, Rojas Gómez MC, Álvarez Tamayo AA, Baquero RL, Torres Pabón ML, Olaya Osorio JC, Mallarino Restrepo G.
abstract: Transverse cervical vessels are a safe and reliable recipient alternative for microvascular reconstruction in vessel-depleted necks. In three complex head and neck cases, all anastomoses succeeded, with 100% flap survival, no re-exploration, and no airway or swallowing sequelae at a minimum 2-month follow-up.

title: The optimal operation decisions of expert service enterprises based on queuing system.
authors: Zhang J, Cui L, Liu C, Jiang M.
abstract: Expert service enterprises constitute an important part of the service sector and play a significant role in its development. However, such enterprises face two major challenges. On the one hand, they must satisfy heterogeneous customer demand for experts of different ranks; on the other hand, they must manage compensation constraints in the expert labor market. To address these challenges, this study develops a queueing-theoretic framework that captures the joint effects of expert rank and service time. In doing so, it explicitly endogenies expert rank in the model and examines how enterprises optimize expert rank and service time under different demand scenarios. The results yield several key findings. First, the optimal expert rank chosen by the enterprise is independent of the overall demand volume, which is a somewhat unexpected result. This finding suggests that expert recruitment should be aligned with the firm's long-term strategic positioning rather than adjusted merely in response to short-term demand fluctuations. Second, when market demand is strong, the enterprise can adopt a "low-margin, high-volume" strategy by jointly optimizing service time and service price, thereby expanding customer coverage and maximizing service throughput. Third, when demand is relatively low, the enterprise should carefully adjust service price and expert compensation to maintain profitability without compromising service quality. Overall, this study provides practical managerial insights for expert service enterprises seeking to optimize service delivery strategies, balance customer expectations with expert compensation, and avoid market distortions. By endogenizing expert rank and service time and analyzing equilibrium decision behavior, this study also extends the research perspective on expert service operations.

title: The "Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability Technique" (MERI Technique): A Simple Lateral Tenodesis Reconstructing the Condylar Strap, the Distal Kaplan Fibers, and the Femoral Insertion of the Anterolateral Ligament to Control Internal Rotation During Anterior Cruciate Ligament Surgery.
authors: Bouguennec N, Colombet P, Graveleau N.
abstract: The Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique is a simple and minimally invasive lateral tenodesis designed to enhance internal rotation control during anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction by reconstructing the distal Kaplan fibers, the condylar strap, and the femoral insertion of the anterolateral ligament. Using a 1-cm-wide fascia lata strip, the procedure involves fixation with a single anchor at an isometric point proximal to the anterolateral ligament insertion, followed by a continuous locking suture and fascia lata closure on the anchor, which further reinforces rotational stability without excessive constraint. Although possibly biomechanically less restrictive than traditional lateral extra-articular tenodesis, the Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique strikes a balance between stability and flexibility, potentially reducing postoperative stiffness and morbidity. Its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and minimal invasiveness make it a valuable alternative for addressing anterolateral instability in select anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients.

title: Temporal MRI appearance of postoperative healing after proximal hamstring musculotendinous complex repair.
authors: Mechó S, Pérez P, Congo A, Isern-Kebschull J, Alomar X, Pruna R, Valle X, Yanguas X, Moix I, Puigdellívol J, Lempainen L, Aguilar M, Pedret C, Kassarjian A, Rodas G.
abstract: Objective To describe the temporal MRI features of healing during the first 4 months following surgical repair of complete tears of the proximal hamstring musculotendinous complex. Materials and methods Consecutive case series. Professional football players with MRI-confirmed complete tears surgically repaired between May 2017 and December 2025 were retrospectively identified. Postoperative MRI examinations were obtained during routine clinical follow-up using 3-T systems. Two musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated longitudinal and transverse intratendinous clefts, scar maturation, edema-like signal, postoperative subcutaneous soft-tissue signal change, tendinous angulation, blunt muscle outline, and denervation-like signal. Results Twenty-four complete tears in 20 players underwent surgical repair. Fifteen tendons with an uncomplicated postoperative course comprised the primary descriptive cohort, yielding 43 MRI examinations. Longitudinal intratendinous clefts were observed in 11/15 (73.3%) of tendons, transverse intratendinous clefts in 13/15 (86.7%), postoperative subcutaneous soft-tissue signal change and tendinous angulation in 15/15 (100%), blunt muscle outline in 13/15 (86.7%), and denervation-like signal in 10/15 (66.7%). In the within-tendon analysis, longitudinal and transverse intratendinous clefts resolved by the last available MRI in 6/10 (60%) and 7/12 (58.3%) tendons, respectively. All 10 tendons with an initially immature scar progressed to a mature scar. Among six tendons with postoperative exacerbation, four showed extensive, prominent intratendinous clefts with marked PD-FS hyperintensity on the preceding MRI, associated with immature scar, intratendinous cavity, or persistent interstitial edema-like signal. Conclusion Serial MRI demonstrated different temporal patterns of postoperative healing. Residual intratendinous clefts may coexist with a mature scar during tendon remodeling and do not necessarily indicate delayed healing.

title: Staff experiences of person-centred care and quality of life in nursing homes as influenced by leadership and work situation: a qualitative study.
authors: Eldskott H, Lindkvist M, Niklasson J, Backman A.
abstract: Background PCC is widely recognised as an important approach to supporting QoL in nursing homes. However, staff's ability to provide PCC may be influenced by leadership and working conditions. There is still limited knowledge of how staff themselves experience performing PCC to support residents' QoL in everyday nursing home care. The aim of this study was to explore staff experiences of providing PCC to support resident QoL and how their provision of PCC is influenced by leadership and staff working conditions. Methods A qualitative study design was used. Fifteen semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 enrolled nurses and five nursing assistants working in nursing homes in four Swedish municipalities between February and May 2024. Data were analysed using qualitative conventional content analysis. Results An overarching theme, Creating everyday meaning despite challenges, was supported by three categories: Building human relationships in care, Connecting through communication and teamwork, and Overcoming obstacles for person-centred care. Meaningful relationships, attentiveness and tailored support were described as central to providing PCC and supporting residents' QoL. Communication and teamwork enabled staff to understand and respond to residents' individual needs, while leadership contributed by supporting staff and facilitating teamwork. Organisational barriers, including staffing shortages, time pressure, communication difficulties and limited leadership support, constrained staff members' ability to consistently provide PCC and support residents' QoL. Conclusions Staff described a strong intrinsic commitment to providing PCC that supports residents' QoL. However, their ability to do so was shaped by leadership and organisational conditions. Enabling PCC in nursing homes therefore requires not only staff commitment, but also supportive leadership, adequate staffing and work environments that allow time, communication and continuity in care. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Small-bowel lymphangioma with mesenteric cystic extension causing acute obstruction in an adult: a case report.
authors: Gopalapillai G, Al-Harrasi K.
abstract: Small-bowel lymphangioma is rare in adults and only exceptionally presents with acute obstruction. A 45-year-old man with no previous abdominal surgery presented with sudden severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Computed tomography demonstrated a fluid-density pelvic lesion with a single transition point, twisting of adjacent small bowel and mesentery, proximal dilatation, and mesenteric congestion. Emergency laparoscopy identified bowel twisted around a mesenteric cyst and was converted to laparotomy because distension prevented safe reduction. The lesion was inseparable from the mesentery supplying a 20-cm segment, which was resected en bloc. Histology demonstrated D2-40-positive lymphatic channels extending from mucosa to subserosa and communicating with the mesenteric cyst, confirming lymphangioma. Recovery was uncomplicated and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 7. This case highlights lymphatic malformation as a rare pathological lead point for obstruction in a virgin abdomen.

title: Small poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma with concentric periarterial growth causing popliteal arterial stenosis: a case report.
authors: Nagata S, Shouji Y, Sawano M, Negoto S, Hiraoka K, Nakayama M, Tanoue S.
abstract: Soft-tissue sarcomas arising in the popliteal fossa are uncommon but clinically important because of their close relationship to major neurovascular structures. Poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma is an aggressive histologic subtype of synovial sarcoma. We report a case of a small poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma located in the perivascular region of the popliteal fossa that showed concentric periarterial growth with popliteal arterial stenosis. A 68-year-old woman reported a several-month history of heaviness in the right lower extremity. Ultrasonography revealed a 2-cm irregular hypoechoic solid mass circumferentially surrounding the popliteal artery, with no definite internal Doppler flow. The lesion showed intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous intermediate-to-high signal intensity on fat-suppressed T2-weighted images. MRI showed circumferential arterial encasement with stenosis. Non-contrast-enhanced quiescent-interval slice-selective (QISS) MRA helped define the longitudinal extent of popliteal arterial narrowing. Surgical resection required vascular resection and reconstruction bypass of the popliteal artery and vein. Histopathological examination showed nested proliferation of tumor cells with ovoid-to-round nuclei in a hyalinized fibrous stroma. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for SS18-SSX and SSX, supporting the diagnosis of synovial sarcoma. This case illustrates that even a small synovial sarcoma in the popliteal fossa can circumferentially encase the popliteal artery and cause stenosis.

title: Single-stage matrix-assisted bone marrow-derived cell concentrate implantation for osteochondral talar lesions: a 24-month clinical and MRI follow-up.
authors: Caggiari G, Rinaldi M, Santandrea A, Mercurio D, Lugani G, D'Alessandro S, Deng H, Migliorini F, Pisanu F, Doria C, Cortese F, Puddu L.
abstract: Background The optimal surgical management of larger chronic osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT) remains debated. This study describes 24-month clinical and MRI outcomes after a combined single-stage matrix-assisted procedure using debridement, bone-marrow stimulation, autologous bone marrow-derived cell concentrate, a type I collagen scaffold, and fibrin glue. Methods This exploratory retrospective case series screened consecutive patients treated between January 2016 and December 2020. Twenty-six patients were identified; 15 had sufficiently complete clinical and MRI data for the predefined 24-month complete-case analysis. Eligible lesions were classified as Giannini type II-IIA and Outerbridge grade III-IV. The principal clinical endpoint was the 24-month change in the American Orthopaedic Foot Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot score. Secondary outcomes included Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain, 24-month MRI morphology assessed with the MOCART system, and reoperations. Six- and 12-month assessments were part of routine care but were not sufficiently complete for formal longitudinal analysis. Results The mean AOFAS score increased from 57.3 ± 12.0 at baseline to 92.4 ± 7.1 at 24 months, an absolute improvement of 35.1 points. The mean VAS score decreased from 4.7 ± 1.2 to 1.8 ± 0.8, an absolute reduction of 2.9 points. At 24 months, complete defect filling was observed in 12 of 15 patients (80.0%), hypertrophic filling in 2 (13.3%), and incomplete filling in 1 (6.7%). Complete integration with adjacent tissue was observed in 14 patients (93.3%); preserved surface morphology and uniform repair-tissue structure were each observed in 12 (80.0%). Mean MOCART score was 83.7 ± 14.4. Three patients (20.0%) underwent arthroscopic reoperation for symptomatic anterior impingement. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort, the combined single-stage procedure was associated with improved 24-month pain and functional scores and favorable MRI morphology of repair tissue. The uncontrolled design and multimodal procedure do not establish comparative efficacy, superiority, or an independent cell-specific treatment effect. Larger prospective controlled studies are needed.

title: Significant Geographic Variation in the Epidemiology and Management of Pediatric Osteochondritis Dissecans Exists Between the Asia-Pacific and North America.
authors: Wong JRY, Lam YX, Tan SHS, Hui JHP, Wang M.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate regional variations in epidemiology, diagnostic approaches, and surgical interventions for pediatric osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) between Asia-Pacific (APAC) and North America (NA). Methods A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library databases was conducted from database inception until August 2025. Studies on epidemiology and surgical treatment of pediatric OCD were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data was extracted and collated according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis guidelines, and risk of bias was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies. Results Sixty-five studies comprising 2194 patients were analyzed-29 from APAC (803 patients) and 36 from NA (1391 patients). Patients' age (APAC: 9-18 years; NA: 6-19 years) and follow-up duration (APAC: 8-184 months; NA: 2-216 months) were similar. Significant regional differences were observed across multiple domains. Sex distribution was markedly skewed in APAC, where most studies included predominantly male participants (91.9%) without intentional female disaggregation, compared with a more balanced cohort in NA (55.3%). Although the elbow was the most common OCD site overall, knee involvement was significantly higher in NA (36.1%) than APAC (20.7%). Imaging modalities differed-radiographs were the most common imaging tool in both regions, but magnetic resonance imaging was more frequently used in NA (48.9%) compared with APAC (35.8%). Surgical approaches also varied significantly: osteochondral grafting was more common in APAC (41.7%), whereas arthroscopic techniques were favored in NA (73.5%). In situ fixation rates were similar between regions. Standardized reporting and prospective, multicenter registries are essential for enabling patient-level analysis and guiding region-specific, evidence-based care for pediatric OCD. Conclusions There are significant regional variations in epidemiology, imaging modalities, and surgical management for pediatric OCD. The predominantly male bias in the APAC region, greater use of magnetic resonance imaging, and arthroscopic techniques in the NA region reflect underlying biological, cultural, and health care-related differences. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

title: Severe Thrombocytopenia Induced by Re-Exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam: A Case Report in Critically Ill Patient With COVID-19.
authors: Alharthi AF, Alkathiri MA, Alomeir O, Al Harbi S, Aljuhani O, Alhaidal HA, Al Sulaiman K.
abstract: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia is a condition where certain medications can significantly reduce the platelets in the blood. This can increase the risk of bleeding and bruising. We reported a case of a 73-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities who was admitted to the hospital with COVID-19. Upon admission, the patient received multiple antibiotics, including Piperacillin/Tazobactam. In the following days, she developed severe thrombocytopenia upon re-exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam. Other causes of thrombocytopenia were systematically excluded. After discontinuing the Piperacillin/Tazobactam and administering intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), the thrombocytopenia resolved. A Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score was calculated and indicated a probable (i.e., 6 points) adverse drug reaction. This case underscores the importance of considering Piperacillin/Tazobactam as a potential cause of severe thrombocytopenia in critically ill patients, even in the presence of confounding factors such as COVID-19. To our knowledge, this is a rarely reported presentation in a patient with a recent COVID-19 infection. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between COVID-19 and drug-induced thrombocytopenia.

title: Serum uric acid and bone mineral density: Reappraising an overstated association.
authors: Dimnik JM, Lavender B, Topham JJ.
abstract: A recent acceleration in NHANES-based serum uric acid (SUA) and bone mineral density (BMD) publications has encouraged recommendations to relax the treatment target for hyperuricemia, possibly placing patients at higher risk for gout. We reappraised pooled 2005-2018 NHANES data to determine whether SUA supports a clinically meaningful bone-protective role. Survey-weighted analyses of 3687 to 6039 participants assessed the influence of SUA on BMD at 10 anatomical sites, with femoral neck and total lumbar spine BMD as co-primary outcomes, as well as osteoporosis and fragility fracture. Higher SUA was nominally associated with slightly higher total lumbar spine BMD (βˆ=0.0062, 0.0003-0.0122, P=0.042) but not femoral neck BMD (βˆ=0.0035, -0.0006-0.0076, P=0.093). Allometric analyses revealed a similar pattern. Restricted cubic splines depicted a linear association at the lumbar spine and a nonlinear femoral neck association which flattened near the SUA solubility limit of 6.8 mg/dL. Importantly, all clinical end points were null; SUA was not associated with osteoporosis or fragility fracture in the primary continuous models (ORs 0.960 to 1.007; all P≥0.743). Alternative thresholds, quintile trends, and sensitivity analyses showed no consistent association. Higher SUA was not associated with femoral neck BMD or total lumbar spine BMD across 18/21 and 13/21 sensitivity tests, respectively. Notably, when 24-hour dietary intake was considered in sensitivity analyses, none of the outcomes maintained statistical significance. Thus, modest site-specific associations between SUA and BMD did not translate into clinical benefit. These findings do not support a direct bone-protective role for SUA or relaxation of the 6.0 mg/dL hyperuricemia treatment target.

title: Semimembranosus Autograft Harvesting and Reconstruction for Knee Posteromedial Complex Laxity Using a "Romal Reins" Technique.
authors: Kodkani P.
abstract: This technical report presents semimembranosus tendon harvest and its use as an autograft in knee ligament reconstruction. The distal semimembranosus tendon is a robust and long tendon, which makes it a suitable autograft option with its distal insertions kept intact. It has multiple insertions onto the posteromedial corner of the tibia and the posteromedial ligament complex (PMC). Tensioning this tendon insertion results in tightening of the PMC and thus achieves posteromedial stability. Harvesting the tendon with its lateral third left intact with its muscular attachment retains its dynamic action. Using the medial two-thirds of the tendon as an autograft for PMC reconstruction with a "Romal Reins" concept restores joint stability. The graft is notably beneficial in cases of multiligament laxity where there may be a shortage of free autografts for PMC reconstruction. This technique tightens and reconstructs the major PMC stabilizing structures without requiring individual structural reconstructions. It reduces the need for multiple grafts, reconstructions, bone tunnels, and implants for managing PMC laxity. This technique of semimembranosus tendon graft harvest and PMC reconstruction is safe, simple, minimally invasive, and effective with the least risk of complications. It could possibly be a preferred graft and reconstruction technique for PMC reconstruction.

title: Rotational-progress-dependent pelvic, thoracic, and support-foot kinematics during a standardised Rumba spiral turn in highly trained adolescent female Latin dancers.
authors: Guo M, Ismail MHB, Abdul Ghani DZB, Liang Q, Gao Y.
abstract: Rumba turning involves continuous whole-body reorientation, but discrete kinematic summaries do not localise where consistent directional deviations occur across the turn. This exploratory study examined rotational-progress-dependent patterns of pelvic obliquity, thoracic frontal-plane angle, and right support-foot progression angle during the initial 360° Rumba spiral turn in highly trained adolescent female Latin dancers. Fifteen dancers aged 14-16 years completed five valid trials each (75 trials). Three-dimensional kinematics were recorded using a 10-camera Vicon system at 100 Hz. For each trial, accumulated pelvic rotation was used to define rotational progress, and the three outcome waveforms were resampled to 101 points across 0%-100% of the turn. The five trials from each participant were averaged point by point, yielding 15 participant-level representative waveforms per outcome. Two-tailed one-sample statistical parametric mapping (SPM{t}) tests identified intervals in which group mean waveforms differed from their corresponding Plug-in Gait model-defined 0° references, using a Bonferroni-adjusted primary α = 0.0167 across the three outcomes. Pelvic obliquity showed a positive deviation at 11.3%-47.2% and a negative deviation at 56.5%-97.3% of rotational progress. Thoracic frontal-plane angle showed a negative deviation at 13.2%-41.9% and positive deviations at 57.6%-83.0% and 85.7%-92.0%. Right support-foot progression angle showed negative, positive, and negative deviations at 0.0%-4.8%, 10.4%-49.1%, and 56.2%-100.0%, respectively. Sensitivity analyses without the additional across-outcome Bonferroni adjustment preserved the principal directional patterns, with only modest changes in cluster extent and continuity. These findings identify where, across rotational progress, the measured segmental orientations consistently departed from model-defined references during a standardised Rumba spiral turn, without implying normative targets of optimal dance technique.

title: Reverse histologic transformation from small cell lung carcinoma to epidermal growth factor receptor mutant lung adenocarcinoma with shared genomic backbone.
authors: Nayak R, Nee E, Seetharamu N, Rosca OC, Farmer P, Sullivan KM.

title: Research hotspots and dynamic trends in sacral neuromodulation for pelvic floor dysfunction: a comprehensive bibliometric analysis.
authors: Ma T, Song Y, Ma F, Shi J, Li Z, Cui J, An Q, Lu L, Zhao G.
abstract: Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) includes urinary and bowel dysfunction, chronic pelvic pain, and sexual dysfunction and can substantially impair quality of life. Sacral neuromodulation (SNM) is uesd for selected refractory urinary and bowel disorders, while evidence for other PFD domains continues to develop. We aimed to characterize publication patterns, contributors, collaboration networks, co-citation structures, and keyword trends in the literature on SNM for PFD. Publications on SNM for PFD from January 2000 to November 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Bibliometric and visual analyses were conducted using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R software to evaluate temporal trends, geographic and institutional distributions, journal and author productivity, reference co-citation networks, and keyword dynamics. A total of 1986 publications (1520 original articles and 466 reviews) were included. Annual publication output increased overall during the study period, with year-to-year fluctuations. The United States (n = 681), the United Kingdom (n = 276), the Netherlands (n = 135), and China (n = 125) contributed the largest numbers of publications. Neurourology and Urodynamics, Colorectal Disease, and Diseases of the Colon & Rectum were the most productive journals. The strongest reference bursts were observed for Wexner SD (2010; strength 32.91), Matzel KE (2017; strength 30.40), and Lightner DJ (2019; strength 30.19). Keyword analyses were dominated by sacral neuromodulation, sacral nerve stimulation, fecal incontinence, efficacy, and quality of life; keywords with bursts continuing through 2025 included percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, overactive bladder, and urgency urinary incontinence. This bibliometric analysis maps publication growth, major contributors, collaboration patterns, co-citation structures, and keyword themes in the literature on SNM for PFD. Urinary and bowel dysfunction were the most prominent research themes, whereas chronic pelvic pain and sexual dysfunction were less represented in the keyword analyses. By identifying major thematic concentrations, patterns of scientific collaboration, and comparatively underrepresented topics, these findings may support hypothesis generation, prioritization of future studies on SNM across different PFD domains, and stronger international and interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Patellar Tendon Allograft Reconstruction Using Achilles Graft With Traversing Suprapatellar Cerclage Limbs.
authors: Mahatme RJ, Moore SA, Muthusamy N, Grawe BM, Lamplot JD, Bernholt DL.
abstract: Patellar tendon rupture and chronic extensor mechanism deficiency present significant reconstructive challenges, particularly in revision settings or when native tissue quality is poor. We describe a reproducible surgical technique for patellar tendon reconstruction using an Achilles allograft with traversing suprapatellar cerclage limbs. This construct helps facilitate controlled restoration of patellar height, immediate continuity of the extensor mechanism, and load sharing across the reconstruction during early healing.

title: Paraparesis and left upper extremity weakness after total arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk: possible contributions of spinal cord ischaemia and cervical radiculopathy.
authors: Ishihama T, Yokawa K, Shimatani Y, Uesugi K, Ishimoto K, Higuma T, Yoshida K, Obo H, Wakiyama H.
abstract: An 82-year-old man underwent total arch replacement with the frozen elephant trunk technique for an aortic arch aneurysm. Upon awakening 3 hours postoperatively, the patient exhibited flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities and left upper extremity weakness, whereas the right upper extremity was largely preserved. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage and blood pressure augmentation were initiated for suspected spinal cord ischemia. Lower-extremity motor function partially recovered, but left upper-extremity weakness persisted. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated intramedullary T2 hyperintensity at T2/3 and bilateral neural foraminal stenosis from C3/4 to C6/7. Neurological examination revealed predominant weakness in the left C7 myotome with an absent left triceps reflexes, suggesting concomitant C7 radiculopathy. This case demonstrates that neurological deficits after aortic arch surgery may be multifactorial and highlights the value of detailed neurological examination and spinal imaging when upper extremity weakness is disproportionate.

title: Nationwide trends and demographic projections of hospitalisations for vertebral fractures and postmenopausal osteoporosis in Germany: a 24-year registry-based study.
authors: Anees H, Qadourah K, Georgievski G, Heiss C, El Khassawna T.
abstract: Hospitalisations for vertebral fractures increased in Germany over the past two decades. Although hospitalisation rates have recently stabilised or declined, demographic projections indicate that the absolute inpatient hospitalisation burden may remain substantial through 2050. These findings highlight the need for better osteoporosis prevention and long-term healthcare planning. Background Vertebral fractures represent one of the most common manifestations of skeletal fragility and contribute substantially to morbidity, disability, and healthcare utilisation in ageing populations. However, nationwide long-term hospitalisation trends and the impact of demographic ageing on future inpatient burden remain insufficiently characterised. This study investigated inpatient hospitalisation trends for vertebral fractures and postmenopausal osteoporosis in Germany over a 24-year period and estimated the future inpatient burden through 2050. Methods Nationwide inpatient data from the German Federal Health Monitoring (GBE) database were analysed between 2000 and 2023. Hospitalisations were identified using ICD-10-GM codes for thoracic vertebral fractures (S22.0), lumbar vertebral fractures (S32.0), and postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture (M80.0). Absolute hospitalisations, age-standardised hospitalisation rates, sex-specific trends, in-hospital mortality, and length of hospital stay were evaluated. Temporal trends were assessed using joinpoint regression. Future hospitalisations were projected by applying age-specific hospitalisation rates observed during 2021-2023 to the official German population projections (Destatis main scenario G2L2W2). Results Between 2000 and 2023, annual hospitalisations increased from 14,057 to 27,563 for thoracic vertebral fractures, from 27,683 to 45,280 for lumbar vertebral fractures, and from 2,617 to 11,800 for postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture. In contrast, age-standardised hospitalisation rates increased until the mid-to-late 2010s before stabilising or declining across all three diagnoses. Joinpoint regression identified significant trend reversals for thoracic vertebral fractures (2016), lumbar vertebral fractures (2018), and postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture (2015). Overall, lumbar vertebral fractures (AAPC - 0.65%, p = 0.01) and postmenopausal osteoporosis with osteoporotic fracture (AAPC - 1.17%, p Conclusions Although age-standardised hospitalisation rates have stabilised or declined in recent years, demographic projections indicate that the inpatient hospitalisation burden associated with vertebral fractures may remain substantial in Germany. These findings underscore the need for timely osteoporosis diagnosis, systematic secondary fracture prevention, and long-term healthcare planning for an ageing population.

title: Musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America: Workforce characteristics, resource availability, and territorial disparities.
authors: Zamora T, Vidal C, Suarez H, Botello E, Galli Serra M, Casales N, Zeballos J, Zumarraga JP, Cuervo C, Linares F.
abstract: Purpose Musculoskeletal oncology requires highly specialized, multidisciplinary care. Although the subspecialty has evolved worldwide, information on workforce characteristics, resource availability, and practice patterns across Latin America remains limited. Methods A cross-sectional survey using convenience sampling was conducted among orthopaedic surgeons involved in musculoskeletal oncology throughout Latin America. An adapted version of a previously published questionnaire was distributed through the Latin American Society of Musculoskeletal Tumors (SLATME) and professional networks. The survey explored training background, clinical practice characteristics, perceived support from selected specialties and specialized resources, perceived professional challenges, and treatment preferences. We performed descriptive analyses and comparisons by practice-location population size ( Results A total of 147 surgeons from 17 countries participated. Most respondents reported formal orthopaedic oncology training (76%) and academic orteaching involvement (93%). Respondents practicing in locations with ≥ one million inhabitants were significantly more likely to report treating ≥ 30 cases annually of soft tissue sarcoma (47% vs. 14%, p Conclusion Among survey respondents, musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America was characterized by high rates of specialized training and academic or teaching involvement. However, differences in the reported annual numbers of new malignant tumour cases treated and in access to advanced resources were observed according to practice-location population size. Because this study used a convenience sampling strategy, these findings reflect the respondents' practices but should not be generalized to the entire Latin American musculoskeletal oncology community.

title: Multi-objective optimization of light guide column injection molding process using RSM and NSGA‑II with numerical verification.
authors: Xu H.
abstract: Injection molding technology involves fully melting plastic material through screw agitation at a specific temperature, injecting it into the mold cavity under high pressure, and obtaining the molded part after cooling and solidification. Injection molding offers high production efficiency while meeting the molding demands of complex plastic components. However, enhancing the dimensional accuracy of injection-molded parts has become a critical aspect of this process. The injection-molded components of the XG-99Q2 light guide column were selected as the subject of this study. Initially, three runner system designs were created: "Wang" shape, 'Gong' shape, and "Yi" shape configurations. Each design underwent process analysis for its respective injection molding process. Subsequently, six fundamental injection parameters were identified, and an L32 orthogonal experimental design was employed to systematically investigate their effects on two critical objectives: plastic volume shrinkage and warpage deformation. The experimental design incorporated signal-to-noise ratio processing, with weights for total warpage and volume shrinkage derived using the entropy weight method. This approach facilitated qualitative analysis of gray correlation coefficients and correlations among identified factors, revealing significant relationships between injection time, holding pressure, and melt temperature. Prediction models for warpage and shrinkage were developed using the Box-Behnken experimental design from response surface methodology, providing a foundation for comprehensive quantitative analysis. Additionally, the NSGA-II algorithm was applied to multi-objective optimization, yielding a set of Pareto optimal solutions. Finally, the reliability of the method was verified through simulation based validation.

title: Machine learning models with SHAP explanations for predicting neurosurgical intervention and six month functional outcome after traumatic brain injury.
authors: Zhou Z, Cheng H, Liu H, Zhang D, Wang Q, Shao X.
abstract: Background Admission information can help describe surgical treatment and subsequent functional outcomes following traumatic brain injury (TBI). We developed interpretable machine learning models to address these two tasks. Methods This retrospective study included 673 adults evaluated at a single center between December 2018 and December 2023. Outcomes recorded were neurosurgical intervention and six-month Glasgow Outcome Scale status, dichotomized as favorable (scores 4-5) or unfavorable (scores 1-3). Patients were randomly allocated to training and internal validation sets in a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select predictors for the XGBoost and random forest models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, along with classification and prediction error metrics, was employed for model evaluation. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret model predictions. Results There were 75 unfavorable outcomes and 66 surgical interventions. The reported validation accuracy for XGBoost was 87.56% for predicting functional outcomes and 95.02% for surgical interventions. Validation Brier scores were 0.083 and 0.035, respectively. The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), pupillary light reflex, and blood glucose levels contributed significantly to functional outcome predictions, while GCS, fibrinogen, and white blood cell count were key predictors for surgical interventions. Interpretation of threshold-dependent measures is limited by class imbalance and incomplete specification of outcome coding. Conclusion The models combined routinely collected admission variables to characterize the treatment received and functional outcomes in a selected traumatic brain injury (TBI) cohort. These findings require confirmation through analysis replication and independent validation before they can be applied clinically.

title: Lower-Limb-Predominant Axonal Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy With Severe Proximal Weakness and Possible Myopathic Involvement After Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Case Report of Delayed Recognition.
authors: Kuqo A, Kurti F, Llanaj E.
abstract: Bariatric surgery is increasingly performed in adolescents and young adults. Although sleeve gastrectomy preserves intestinal continuity and is often regarded as nutritionally low-risk, it can still precipitate micronutrient deficiency, and obesity itself predisposes to thiamine deficiency, which can cause both Wernicke encephalopathy and a peripheral neuropathy. Peripheral neuromuscular complications after sleeve gastrectomy are less well characterized than those after malabsorptive procedures. An 18-year-old woman with class II obesity (body-mass index 39.2 kg/m 2 ) underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and, about 10 weeks later, developed progressive lower-limb weakness, distal paresthesiae, myalgia, cognitive fatigue, and loss of independent ambulation, with rapid weight loss (30 kg in three months) but no vomiting and no structured supplementation. Early nerve-conduction studies were non-diagnostic, and the presentation was attributed to a functional disorder, for which olanzapine was started; specialist reassessment was delayed until after objective progression. Repeat studies showed a lower-limb-predominant axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with preserved tibial and upper-limb responses and no demyelinating features. The decisive finding was a discrepancy: Medical Research Council grade 1/5 proximal weakness out of proportion to the modest distal axonal loss, pointing to an unlocalized proximal process-lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy or myopathy-for which needle electromyography of proximal and paraspinal muscles was the highest-yield missing test. Vitamin B12, creatine kinase, and albumin were normal; thiamine, the wider micronutrient panel, and cerebrospinal fluid were never obtained. After rehabilitation, without documented micronutrient repletion, strength recovered to grade 3/5, and assisted walking returned. Nutritional deficiency was suspected but neither confirmed nor treated, so the etiology remains unresolved. The transferable lesson is diagnostic: severe neuromuscular injury can evolve within weeks of a restrictive procedure, nondiagnostic early tests do not exclude it, and objective signs should override a functional label.

title: Long-term use of opioids and neuropathic medication after diaphyseal humerus fractures with or without nerve injury: a nationwide register-based cohort study of 4,185 patients.
authors: Nyman E, Andersson S, Perez R, Zimmerman M, Merlo J, Dahlin LB.
abstract: Background and purpose Diaphyseal humerus fractures may lead to prolonged pain medication use. We aimed to study pain medication use after such fractures, focusing on nerve injury. Methods Using Swedish register data (2007-2015), we identified individuals with diaphyseal humerus fractures. High use of opioids and neuropathic pain medication (≥ 60% of days covered/year; 2-month post-fracture washout) was evaluated in 5 groups: the general population (reference) and fractures treated nonoperatively or surgically, with and without nerve injury. Relative risks (RRs; 95% confidence intervals [CIs]; crude and adjusted [aRR] models; adjusted for age, sex, country of birth, income, and cohabitation status; and for previous high use of pain medication during the first year when analyzing the second year) were estimated in Cox proportional hazards regression models. Results We identified 4,185 individuals with diaphyseal humerus fractures (3.7% with nerve injury; 23% surgically treated). In the first year, opioid use was higher among surgically treated fractures with nerve injury (aRR 17.6, CI 11.0-28.3) and without nerve injury (aRR 9.5, CI 8.2-10.9) than in the general population. In the second year, opioid use declined across most groups but remained elevated among nonoperatively treated fractures with nerve injury (aRR 8.3, CI 2.6-26.1). Neuropathic pain medication use increased in the first year, with no elevated use in the second. Adjustment did not change overall patterns. Women, older adults, lower-income individuals, and those living alone showed higher medication risk use. Conclusion Patients with a diaphyseal humerus fracture were associated with a substantial burden of pain medication use, particularly for opioids during the first year post-injury in surgically treated fractures with nerve injury (RR 17.6) and a persistent risk in the second year among nonoperatively treated fractures with nerve injury (RR 8.3). Demographics and socioeconomic factors strongly relate to medication use, highlighting the need for careful early pain management and monitoring for prolonged medication use in exposed groups.

title: Long-term electricity load forecasting model based on multi-period and multi-scale analysis.
authors: Zhang X, Liu Z, Wang C, Qian Z.
abstract: Existing long-term power load forecasting models face significant challenges due to the complexity of non-stationary electricity data, inadequate information representation, and suboptimal prediction accuracy. To address these issues, this study introduces PowerNet, a novel forecasting framework based on a multi-period and multi-scale approach. PowerNet first employs Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to perform multi-period analysis, transforming one-dimensional time series data into two-dimensional (2D) tensors to capture latent periodic patterns. A multi-scale information representation module is then implemented using computer vision-inspired techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and non-local attention mechanisms to extract robust features from these tensors. Finally, a fully connected layer performs feature reconstruction, while residual connections facilitate multi-step load forecasting. PowerNet was evaluated against state-of-the-art models such as Informer, LogTrans, and ETSformer across two public electricity datasets and one weather dataset. At prediction horizons of 96, 192, 336, and 720 time steps, experimental results demonstrate that PowerNet achieves competitive or superior accuracy on the evaluated datasets. Notably, compared with Autoformer, PowerNet reduces the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 18.77% to 37.41% and the Mean Square Error (MSE) by 18.23% to 47.74%, significantly enhancing the reliability of long-term electricity load forecasting.

title: Life-threatening delayed intrathecal baclofen overdose following catheter contrast study.
authors: Elmowafy R, Pinto A, Falzon A, Dalton C.

title: Joint-preserving reconstruction of an acute Type IV reverse Hill-Sachs lesion following posterior shoulder fracture-dislocation: a case report.
authors: Vitali M, Montalbano F, Salini V.
abstract: Posterior shoulder fracture-dislocation is a rare injury frequently associated with delayed diagnosis because of its subtle clinical and radiographic presentation. Management is primarily determined by the size of the reverse Hill-Sachs lesion, with shoulder arthroplasty generally recommended for extensive humeral head defects. We report the case of a 39-year-old man presenting with an acute posterior fracture-dislocation of the proximal humerus associated with a Type IV reverse Hill-Sachs lesion. Despite the severity of the injury, the patient underwent successful joint-preserving reconstruction using open reduction and internal fixation with cannulated screws, structural bone grafting, and a modified McLaughlin procedure. At 3-month follow-up, clinical and radiographic evaluation demonstrated a stable glenohumeral joint, satisfactory shoulder function, and painless range of motion. This case suggests that, in carefully selected young patients with reconstructable fracture fragments, anatomical reconstruction may represent a feasible alternative to primary shoulder arthroplasty while preserving native bone stock and future surgical options.

title: Internal Brace Augmentation for Scapholunate Interosseous Ligament Injuries Is Supported by Limited Evidence and Is Associated With Early Failures: A Systematic Review.
authors: Roh YT, Lee JY, Im JH, Park JW, Park IJ.
abstract: Background Internal brace augmentation, a recently introduced technique using synthetic suture tape, has emerged as an adjunct to scapholunate ligament repair or reconstruction that provides immediate biomechanical stability and may facilitate earlier rehabilitation. Although early case reports have demonstrated rapid pain relief and functional recovery, recent mid- to long-term studies have raised concerns regarding perianchor osteolysis and late structural failure. To date, no systematic review of which we are aware has evaluated the discrepancy between favorable short-term clinical outcomes and emerging long-term concerns (perianchor osteolysis and structural failure). Questions/purposes (1) Does internal brace augmentation improve pain, function, and disability in patients with scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) injury? (2) Does internal brace augmentation achieve durable radiographic correction of carpal alignment? (3) What proportion of patients had perianchor osteolysis and structural failure? Methods We performed a systematic review according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420261355353). PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through April 3, 2026. We included studies reporting clinical or radiographic outcomes of internal brace augmentation for SLIL injury in adults, with at least five patients and a minimum follow-up of 12 months, and excluded cadaver studies, technique descriptions without patient outcomes, review articles, and case reports with fewer than five patients. Methodological quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS). Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, no meta-analysis was performed; results were synthesized narratively. Eleven studies (161 wrists, 160 patients) were included. Of these, two were comparative studies and nine were single-arm series; four studies assessed perianchor osteolysis and seven did not. Follow-up ranged from 12 to 50 months. Results In the two comparative studies, adding the internal brace did not improve pain, function, or disability compared with reconstruction or fixation without it. Across the single-arm series, pain and function consistently improved (preoperative VAS pain of 6 to 8 improved to 0 to 4; grip strength 62% to 98% of the contralateral side). Radiographically, the scapholunate gap decreased from 4 to 6 mm preoperatively to 2 to 3 mm at most recent follow-up, and the scapholunate angle improved from a preoperative range of 65° to 84° to a postoperative range of 52° to 67°. However, the longest follow-up study (mean 50 months, n = 18) reported structural failure (loss of reduction or attritional rupture of the construct) in 44% of patients. Among the studies that assessed osteolysis, the proportion of patients with perianchor osteolysis was 47% at 14 months, 36% at 16 months, and 59% at 50 months, whereas a single all-arthroscopic study reported 0% at 16 months. One comparative study reported osteolysis in 36% of the internal brace cohort versus 0% in the reduction and association of the scaphoid and lunate (RASL) control group, suggesting that this complication may be related to the internal brace construct. Most studies had short and often incomplete follow-up, less rigorous (unblinded, nonindependent) outcome assessment, and probable selection bias. These limitations most likely overestimated the apparent benefit and underestimated the harm of the technique. Conclusion Most of the included studies lacked suitable comparator groups, did not assess key endpoints such as patient-reported outcomes and structural failure (including osteolysis), or did not follow patients long enough to detect all relevant harms; the apparent benefits of internal brace augmentation are therefore likely overstated. In the only study with follow-up beyond 4 years, structural failure of the anchor construct occurred in nearly one-half of patients, and osteolysis was already evident, both of which are concerning. Surgeons should counsel patients about the risks of late structural failure and perianchor osteolysis. Prospective studies with regular radiographic surveillance and a minimum follow-up of 5 years are needed before this technique is routinely adopted. Level of evidence Level IV, therapeutic study.

title: Imaging of developmental, inflammatory, and benign or malignant neoplastic petrous apex lesions in children: what the radiologist needs to know.
authors: Mertiri L, Mertiri D, Moeller KK, Tran HB, Desai NK, Huisman TAGM.
abstract: The petrous portion of the temporal bone is a complex pyramidal-shaped structure of the central skull base, which contains osseous, air cell, vascular, and neural structures in close proximity, making imaging interpretation challenging. A broad spectrum of lesions may involve this region, including inflammatory, neoplastic (benign or malignant), vascular, and osseous lesions. In the pediatric population, ongoing skull base maturation and normal anatomical variability further complicate imaging assessment and may mimic pathology. Cross-sectional imaging plays a central role, with CT providing detailed assessment of osseous structures and MRI offering superior soft tissue characterization. Familiarity with the normal developmental anatomy, common anatomical variants, imaging pitfalls, and characteristic imaging features of pediatric bone lesions is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate patient management. This review provides a structured overview of pediatric petrous apex lesions, emphasizing imaging protocols, normal developmental variants, and key imaging features across inflammatory, neoplastic, vascular, and miscellaneous entities.

title: ITHUIM: An efficient algorithm for mining inter-transaction high utility itemsets.
authors: Vu VV, Pham TT, Vo B.
abstract: Data mining is an active and vital research field that has led to the development of numerous algorithms and solutions. One significant contribution of this field is the discovery of high utility itemsets (HUIs) in transactional databases, which provides managers with valuable insights for maximizing profit. However, existing work on HUI mining has focused exclusively on the relationship among items within individual transactions, while ignoring relationships that occur across consecutive transactions. To address this limitation, we extend high utility itemset mining by considering mega-transaction relationships. We introduce the concept of mega-transaction and provide related definitions, formally defining the problem of mining inter-transaction high utility itemsets (ITHUIs). Furthermore, we develop and prove several mathematical properties that form the theoretical foundation for practical ITHUI mining. Based on these properties, a candidate pruning technique exploiting extended items is proposed to reduce the search space. Finally, we design a novel mining algorithm for efficiently discovering ITHUIs, named ITHUIM (ITHUI Miner).

title: Hospital-level Variation in Medical Debt After Acute Traumatic Injury.
authors: Mullens CL, Becker NV, Oliphant BW, Ayanian JZ, Fendrick AM, Dimick JB, Ryan AM, Hemmila MR, Scott JW.
abstract: Objective To determine whether the treating hospital contributes to patients' medical debt following injury. Summary background data Trauma patients often have little or no choice in where they receive care. However, variation in hospital billing and collection practices, and their association with patient medical debt, remains poorly characterized. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult trauma patients hospitalized from January 2019 to December 2020 at 29 Level I and II trauma centers within a statewide quality collaborative. Trauma registry data were linked to quarterly consumer credit reports from 12 months preinjury through 18 months postinjury. The primary outcome was change in medical debt in collections from baseline to months 9-18 postinjury. Hierarchical mixed-effects models with empirical Bayes shrinkage and reliability adjustment estimated risk-adjusted hospital-level changes, adjusting for demographics, injury severity, and treatment intensity. Hospitals were classified as outliers if 95% confidence intervals for observed-minus-expected differences excluded zero. Results Among 20,613 patients (mean age 63 y; 49% female; 82% non-Hispanic White), mean change in medical debt was $314 (SD $3464). Four hospitals (14%) were high outliers, generating $365-$566 more debt per patient than expected, while 4 (14%) were low outliers, generating $292-$676 less. Low-outlier hospitals cared for younger, lower-income, and higher-risk patients yet produced less debt than predicted. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions Substantial hospital-level variation in postinjury medical debt persists after adjustment for clinical and demographic factors. Billing, financial assistance, and collection practices may represent modifiable targets to reduce financial hardship after trauma.

title: Hollow viscus injury (HVI) score in adult patients sustaining non-motor vehicle collision blunt trauma: A single-center retrospective validation study.
authors: Nguyen PD, Grigorian A, Dieu AL, Nie J, Finney N, Kuza CM, Salamah H, Jebbia M, Kirby KA, Doben AR, Nahmias J.
abstract: Background Delayed diagnosis of hollow viscus injury (HVI) from blunt trauma (BT) carries increased morbidity. An HVI prediction tool (HVI Score), incorporating vital signs, physical examination, and computed tomography (CT) findings has been validated in patients injured by motor vehicle collision (MVC) with an abdominal seatbelt sign. This study investigated the HVI Score performance in patients with non-MVC blunt trauma. Methods This retrospective single-center study conducted between 2020 and 2024 included adult (>18-years-old) patients sustaining non-MVC BT who underwent CT imaging of the abdomen/pelvis prior to any abdominal operation. The primary outcome was operatively confirmed HVI. HVI Score model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve and by calibration (ratio of observed to expected events, calibration-in-the-large, and calibration slope). Results Of 752 non-MVC BT patients admitted, 19 (2.5%) were high-risk (scores >10), 105 (14.0%) moderate-risk (scores 6-9), and 628 (83.5%) low-risk (scores Conclusion The HVI Score, which was originally validated for MVC patients with a seatbelt sign, had excellent performance in predicting HVI among patients with non-MVC BT. Social media summary The Hollow Viscus Injury (HVI) prediction score has excellent performance in predicting HVI among patients with non-MVC blunt abdominal trauma, thus extending its utility to all blunt trauma patients.

title: High-intensity interval versus moderate-intensity continuous freestyle swimming in obese college students: A randomized controlled study protocol examining glycolipid and vascular endothelial responses.
authors: Yang M, Wang J, Su X, Xiang H, Hou Y.
abstract: Background Obesity among college students may be accompanied by early metabolic and endothelial abnormalities before overt cardiometabolic disease develops. Freestyle swimming combines whole-body energy expenditure with low weight-bearing load. This randomized controlled trial will compare high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) freestyle swimming and examine the relationships between changes in glycolipid markers and vascular endothelial markers. Methods A total of 108 obese college students will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to HIIT, MICT, or a usual-activity control group (36 participants per group). The exercise groups will complete supervised 30-min freestyle swimming sessions three times weekly for 6 months. Total cholesterol (TC) at 6 months, adjusted for baseline TC, will be the single primary outcome. Secondary glycolipid, endothelial, anthropometric, adherence, and safety outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at 2, 4, and 6 months. The primary comparison will use analysis of covariance under the intention-to-treat principle. Longitudinal mixed-effects models and multiple imputation sensitivity analyses will characterize outcome trajectories. Multivariable linear regression will examine the relationships between changes in individual glycolipid markers and changes in ET-1 and NO. Discussion This trial will clarify whether HIIT and MICT freestyle swimming differ in their effects on TC and other glycolipid and endothelial outcomes in obese college students and whether improvements in glycolipid markers are accompanied by changes in ET-1 and NO. The findings may inform safe and more precise exercise prescriptions for young adults with obesity. Clinical trial registration The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600121931) on April 7, 2026.

title: Gradient boosting models for gallstone disease classification: A comparative study using demographic and clinical data.
authors: Hasan KS, Puspita SH.
abstract: Gallstone disease is a prevalent gastrointestinal condition with a substantial healthcare burden. While abdominal ultrasonography is the established first-line diagnostic modality, opportunistic risk stratification using routinely collected health parameters remains underexplored. This study evaluated the discriminatory capacity of four gradient boosting machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and HistGBM) for classifying gallstone status using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory features. A retrospective clinical dataset of 319 patients (161 gallstone-positive individuals and 158 healthy controls) from Ankara VM Medical Park Hospital was analyzed. Model performance was assessed using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation, evaluated via AUC-ROC, accuracy, F1-score, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, and decision curve analysis (DCA), with SHAP analyses employed for model interpretability. CatBoost achieved the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.862±0.061, accuracy = 0.794±0.075) and the lowest Brier score (0.149±0.037), demonstrating statistically significant superiority over competing architectures (Friedman test, p < 0.001). Feature ablation revealed that bioimpedance parameters alone provided substantial independent discriminative signal (AUC = 0.797±0.079), approaching that of laboratory markers (AUC = 0.829±0.070), whereas demographic attributes alone were insufficient (AUC = 0.476±0.097). SHAP analyses identified C-reactive protein, Vitamin D, and bone mass as the most influential variables, alongside non-linear risk associations for visceral fat area and body mass index. Decision curve analysis demonstrated positive net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.10-0.80. These findings demonstrate that gradient boosting models, particularly CatBoost, can provide robust, interpretable retrospective classification of gallstone disease, offering proof-of-concept potential for opportunistic risk stratification in metabolic care settings and pre-imaging triage for ambiguous outpatient presentations rather than replacing first-line ultrasonography.

title: Global Variability in Discoid Meniscus Management: A Comparative Study of Pediatric Research in Sports Medicine Asia-Pacific and the Surgical Cohort Outcome Registry Experience Registry.
authors: Hui SJ, Chew KY, Liew JJL, Loke RWK, Ellis H, Lee QW, Hui JHP.
abstract: Purpose To compare diagnostic emphasis and surgical management strategies for discoid meniscus (DM) between Asia-Pacific surgeons participating in the Pediatric Research in Sports Medicine collaborative and North American surgeons within the Surgical Cohort Outcome Registry Experience registry. Methods Between January and July 2024, a cross-sectional survey was conducted among fellowship-trained pediatric and sports orthopaedic surgeons in the Pediatric Research in Sports Medicine Asia-Pacific collaborative. Surgeons with active clinical experience managing DM were invited to participate, and all 54 completed the survey (response rate 100%). These responses were compared with data from 26 North American surgeons participating in the Surgical Cohort Outcome Registry Experience. Variables, including meniscal morphology, tear patterns, instability location, and surgical management strategies, were harmonized between datasets and compared using χ 2 or Fisher's exact tests. Results A total of 54 Asia-Pacific surgeons and 26 North American surgeons were included. Complete discoid morphology was more commonly reported in North America (57.6% vs 49.0%), whereas incomplete morphology predominated in Asia-Pacific (51.4% vs 42.4%). Horizontal or cleavage tears were more frequent in Asia-Pacific (45.6% vs 20.7%, P = .036). Saucerization was the predominant treatment in both regions (94.3% vs 93.7%). Meniscal repair was reported more frequently in Asia-Pacific (71.4% vs 54.6%), particularly for intrasubstance tears (82.5% vs 24.3%) and rim instability (65.8% vs 8.8%). Among patients aged ≥14 years, repair rates remained higher in Asia-Pacific (74.8% vs 44.1%, P = .012). Conclusions Saucerization was the predominant surgical treatment for DM in both Asia-Pacific and North American cohorts. Regional differences were observed in tear characterization, instability localization, and repair thresholds. These findings show variation in clinical practice patterns despite a shared emphasis on meniscal preservation. Clinical relevance Understanding regional variation in DM diagnosis and management may help improve the recognition of tear patterns and instability across populations. Although saucerization remains the cornerstone of treatment globally, differences in tear characterization and repair thresholds highlight the need for standardized classification systems and internationally aligned treatment strategies to optimize meniscal preservation.

title: Global Burden, Temporal Trends, and Risk Factors of Low Back Pain Among People Aged 15-49 Years.
authors: Lei Y, Tang T, Huang C, Zhou Z.
abstract: Background Low back pain (LBP) remains a leading cause of disability worldwide. However, the disease burden among people aged 15-49 years has been insufficiently addressed. Objective The present study aimed to investigate the global burden, temporal trends, and attributable risk factors of low back pain among people aged 15-49 years.
