Methods Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study 2021, we analyzed the incidence, prevalence, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of LBP across 204 countries and territories. Age-standardized rates (ASRs) were calculated, and temporal trends from 1990 to 2021 were examined using joinpoint regression. Results According to GBD 2021 estimates, there are approximately 16,993,809 new cases of LBP that occurred worldwide, with South Asia bearing the highest case load. Although ASRs of incidence (AAPC: -0.16; 95% CI: -0.20, -0.12), ASRs of prevalence (AAPC: -0.17; 95% CI: -0.20, -0.14), and ASRs of DALYs (AAPC: -0.16; 95% CI: -0.18, -0.14) declined between 1990 and 2021, absolute case numbers and DALYs increased. Occupational ergonomic factors (28.4%, 95% CI: 26.3%-30.7%), tobacco smoking (11.4%, 95% CI: 7.6%-15.2%), and high body mass index (BMI) (10.9%, 95% CI: 1.1%-21.0%) were the major attributable risk factors. Women always bear a more severe disease burden than men, with the age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) being 3788.64 vs. 2380.94 per 100,000; the age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR) being 8822.52 vs. 5410.51 per 100,000; and the age-standardized DALY rates (ASDR) being 999.13 vs. 626.28 per 100,000 in women and men, respectively. When it comes to the socio-demographic index (SDI), ASIR and ASPR initially increased with rising SDI, reaching a peak in Australasia, with ASPR over 12,500 per 100,000 and ASIR over 5000 per 100,000, before subsequently decreasing with further SDI increments. Conclusions Despite declining ASRs, the absolute global burden of LBP among individuals aged 15-49 continues to grow, particularly among women and in high-SDI regions. Targeted preventive strategies and control measures are urgently needed.

title: Geography matters: Variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers.
authors: Goldstein AL, Nino E, Biton D, Kruyer VN, Bar-Haim R, Laks S, Soroksky A, Levit B, Awad A, Wiesel O.
abstract: Background Geodemographic factors create divergent clinical patterns between urban and rural settings. Level-II trauma centers are a vital trauma-care infrastructure for both urban and rural communities. This study compares neck trauma patterns, resource utilization, and outcomes at these distinct geodemographic nodes. Methods Retrospective analysis (2014-2024) of neck trauma at an urban center (UC, n = 65) and a rural center (RC, n = 60). Demographics, mechanism, treatments, interventions, and outcomes were analyzed. Results RC patients sustained more blunt, transport-related multisystem trauma with higher ISS. UC patients predominantly presented with localized penetrating injuries. Rural patients had higher ICU admission rates, longer ICU stays, more transfers to level-I centers yet underwent fewer operative interventions, invasive airway procedures, and CT angiogrophy. Conclusions There are significant variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers. An "intervention paradox" exists were rural centers stabilize high-severity blunt trauma for transfer, while urban centers provide definitive care for penetrating wounds. These findings necessitate geodemographically tailored protocols. Understanding geodemographic variations is a critical aspect of optimizing trauma systems. Level of evidence II Retrospective cohort.

title: GFLNet: A lightweight real-time detector with knowledge-guided compression in remote sensing images.
authors: Zhang J, Mustaffa MR, Khalid F, Kahar ZA, Zhang T.
abstract: Remote sensing images usually exhibits densely distributed targets and scale disparities. In such scenarios, it is still challenging to preserve high detection precision while controlling costs and inference latency. To address this issue, we propose GFLNet, a lightweight single-stage detector, which is based on collaborative feature modeling and knowledge-guided compression. Specifically, Ghost-Shuffle dual fusion convolution (GSD-Fuse) is designed to achieve efficient spatial-channel interaction while reducing computational cost; an adaptive receptive-field selection module inspired by LSKNet is introduced into the deeper backbone and neck stages to adaptively adjust contextual responses for small-object and multi-scale detection; finally, LB-Compress combines layer-adaptive magnitude pruning with Bidirectional Cross-task Knowledge Distillation (BCKD) to form a compact network suitable for practical deployment. Evaluated on the DIOR and UCAS-AOD datasets, GFLNet improves mAP@0.5 over the baseline by 3.9% and 3.4%, respectively. Moreover, the model contains only 2.35M parameters, with a calculation of 5.6 GFLOPs, and an inference speed of 261 FPS on the GPU, thereby delivering a favorable accuracy-efficiency synergy.

title: Frequencies of thyroid-related diagnoses and dyslipidemia among Japanese women with menstrual-related disorders aged under 40 years: A nationwide cross-sectional study using health insurance claims data.
authors: Yoshihara T, Ono Y, Arita H, Nakagomi A, Miyashita D, Tanaka K, Sasatsu S, Yoshino O.
abstract: Women with endometriosis and dysmenorrhea are increasingly recognized as having systemic comorbidities beyond pelvic disease, but large-scale data on endocrine and metabolic comorbidities across a broad menstrual-related disorders population remain limited. Using the Japan Medical Data Center Claims Database, we conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study of women aged under 40 years enrolled in 2023. Women with confirmed diagnoses of endometriosis (ICD-10: N80) and/or dysmenorrhea (N94.4 or N94.6) were classified as the menstrual-related disorders group (n = 257,897); those without such diagnoses were the control group (n = 3,183,032). The primary outcomes were the frequencies of thyroid-related diagnoses (hypothyroidism [E03], non-toxic goiter [E04], hyperthyroidism [E05], thyroiditis [E06], and other thyroid disorders [E07]) and dyslipidemia (E78). Stratified analyses were performed according to prescription for low-dose estrogen-progestin preparations (LEP) or dienogest (DNG). All thyroid-related diagnoses were recorded more frequently among women with menstrual-related disorders than among controls. Hypothyroidism was identified in 2.1% of women with menstrual-related disorders versus 0.8% of controls (prevalence ratio [PR] 2.46; 95% CI 2.39-2.54); the corresponding PR was 3.11 (95% CI 2.99-3.24) in the endometriosis subgroup (n = 96,863). Dyslipidemia was recorded in 5.2% of women with menstrual-related disorders versus 1.4% of controls (PR 3.73; 95% CI 3.66-3.80; prevalence difference +3.78 percentage points). The endometriosis subgroup consistently showed the highest frequencies. These associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for age using the Mantel-Haenszel method (adjusted PR 1.45-3.02 across all comparisons), although adjusted estimates were consistently lower than crude estimates. Among women with menstrual-related disorders, hypothyroidism was more frequent in those without LEP/DNG prescriptions (3.4%) than in those with prescriptions (1.5%), whereas dyslipidemia frequencies were similar (5.2% vs. 5.1%). These findings indicate that young Japanese women with menstrual-related disorders have substantially higher frequencies of thyroid-related diagnoses and dyslipidemia than controls, particularly those with endometriosis. Surveillance bias, age confounding, and confounding by indication cannot be excluded because of the cross-sectional claims-based design.

title: Food insecurity and its related indicators in an Iranian population: An application of machine learning methods in data from Golestan Province.
authors: Nassaj-Torshizi F, Zayeri F, Behnampour N, Honarvar MR, Mohammadzadeh M.
abstract: Background Household food insecurity (FI) is a major public health concern associated with socioeconomic vulnerability. Unfortunately, the prevalence of food insecurity in Iran has increased substantially in recent years due to the economic challenges associated with prolonged international sanctions. In this context, this study aimed to estimate the prevalence of household FI in northern Iran and compare the predictive performance of traditional and machine learning algorithms for classifying households according to presence of FI. Methods This cross-sectional study included 4,948 households from Golestan Province in north of Iran. The study sample was selected using the multistage cluster sampling between December 2021 and September 2022. FI was assessed using the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale. The data was analyzed using the logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, decision tree, naïve Bayes, and artificial neural network models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, balanced accuracy, Brier score, calibration plots, and DeLong's test for pairwise AUC comparisons. The bootstrap resampling was applied to assess the stability and uncertainty of predictor importance. In addition, the estimated rankings derived from the logistic regression and random forest models were compared using the Spearman's correlation coefficient. Results The prevalence of household FI was 61.7%, including 32.3% mild, 20.3% moderate, and 9.1% severe FI. The multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that lower income, lower educational attainment, unemployment, lack of insurance coverage, absence of supplementary insurance, lack of car or house ownership, fewer employed household members, larger household size, being under coverage of supportive organizations, having incurable disease, and Turkmen ethnicity remained associated with FI. The pairwise DeLong's test showed modest differences between the fitted models, with no statistically significant difference between the logistic regression and either neural network or SVM radial models after Bonferroni correction. Household income was ranked as the most important predictor in both the logistic regression and random forest models. Conclusions In general, our estimates revealed that household FI was highly prevalent in the sample under study and strongly associated with socioeconomic disadvantage. Logistic regression, neural network, and SVM models demonstrated relatively similar predictive performance, while more complex ML approaches did not show substantial practical improvement over conventional methods in this dataset. Given the serious consequences of household food insecurity, health policymakers should pay more attention to improve socioeconomic conditions of households residing in the studied areas.

title: Explorative team learning as a catalyst for innovation and performance: Evidence from Vietnam's aviation sector.
authors: Ly HTM, Tučková Z, Pham NT, Nguyen TAV, Nguyen HX.
abstract: In today's dynamic service sectors, particularly aviation and tourism, innovation is a vital driver of performance. While leadership is known to foster innovation, the mechanisms by which leadership influences innovation outcomes through team learning remain underexplored. This study examines the impact of innovation leadership on team performance through team explorative learning, employee innovation, and team innovation, and further examines the moderating role of customer relationship management (CRM) practices in these relationships. Drawing on Social Exchange Theory and Social Learning Theory, innovation is conceptualized as a multi-level outcome shaped by leadership and team dynamics. Using Structural Equation Modelling on survey data from 430 employees and leaders in Vietnam's aviation and tourism sector, the findings show that innovation leadership enhances team explorative learning, which in turn promotes employee and team innovation. These innovation outcomes subsequently enhance team performance, confirming their mediating roles in the relationship between team explorative learning and performance. Moreover, customer relationship management (CRM) practices moderate these relationships by strengthening the effect of team innovation on performance and attenuating the direct relationship between team explorative learning and team performance. In contrast, CRM practices had a limited moderating effect on the relationship between employee innovation and team performance. This study advances understanding of the indirect pathways through which leadership drives innovation and highlights CRM practices as a boundary condition. Practical implications for managing innovation in complex service environments are offered.

title: Endoscopic Posterolateral Subtalar Release.
authors: Pan X, Lui TH, Pan Y, Li CCH, Slocum AMY, Su W, Sun Y.
abstract: Subtalar stiffness is a late complication of calcaneal fractures. It can lead to tightness discomfort and difficulty in walking on uneven surface. Open subtalar release is not a good choice because the extensive surgical wound prohibits early vigorous mobilization exercise. Endoscopic subtalar release has the advantage of smaller surgical wounds, so immediate vigorous mobilization is allowed. In case of joint-depression calcaneal fracture, the formation of posterior calcaneal spur is one of the contributing factors of subtalar stiffness. The purpose of this technical note is to describe the details of endoscopic posterolateral subtalar release. In this endoscopic approach, the posterior calcaneal spur is resected together with soft-tissue release of the posterior and lateral sides of the posterior subtalar joint.

title: Electronic health record phenotype choice and real-world outcome estimates: A propensity score-matched comparison of three invasive breast cancer definitions in TriNetX.
authors: Chiang JK, Chiang PC, Koo M.
abstract: Electronic health record-based oncology studies depend on computable case definitions, but different operational definitions may identify different patient populations and change downstream estimates. This retrospective benchmarking cohort study evaluated three definitions of incident invasive breast cancer in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network: at least one malignant breast cancer diagnosis code (Dx1), a repeated diagnosis-code definition within 90 days (Dx2), and a diagnosis code plus breast cancer-directed treatment evidence (DxTx). Female patients aged 20 years or older were identified after a 12-month washout period and exclusion of patients with carcinoma in situ only. Pairwise one-to-one propensity-score matching was performed using 13 baseline covariates. Outcomes were all-cause mortality and time to the first emergency department visits, assessed from day 180 after the index date to 1, 3, and 5 years after the original index date. Appendicitis and femoral neck fracture were included as negative-control outcomes. Dx1, Dx2, and DxTx identified 1,450,233, 678,739, and 578,576 patients, respectively. After matching, more restrictive definitions were consistently associated with higher hazards of mortality and emergency department visits. For mortality, hazard ratios ranged from 1.26 to 1.32 for DxTx versus Dx1, 1.13 to 1.14 for Dx2 versus Dx1, and 1.13 to 1.17 for DxTx versus Dx2 across assessment windows. Emergency department visit estimates showed a similar but attenuating pattern. These associations should be interpreted as differences between phenotype-defined populations arising from selection and ascertainment mechanisms rather than as treatment effects. Negative-control outcomes were generally close to the null; small appendicitis associations observed in comparisons involving Dx1 did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. These findings indicate that plausible electronic health record-based breast cancer definitions are not analytically interchangeable. Phenotype specification should therefore be treated as a core analytic decision and evaluated through transparent reporting and sensitivity analyses.

title: Ecology and epidemiology of multidrug resistance Salmonella in fruit Bats and shared water sources in Bangladesh.
authors: Uddin MH, Dutta P, Islam M, Rahman MK, Islam S, Karim MR, Rahman F, Forwood JK, Chowdhury S, Epstein JH, Samad MA, Islam A.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global threat to both animal and human health, underscoring the importance of AMR surveillance across all sectors of the One Health triad, including wildlife. Fruit bats in Bangladesh frequently inhabit areas in close proximity to human settlements and livestock facilities, creating ecological conditions that facilitate the co-occurrence of AMR bacteria through direct contact or shared contaminated environments. A cross-sectional study was conducted to determine the prevalence of Salmonella spp. isolation and the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant isolates among confirmed positives, characterize resistance patterns across multiple antimicrobial classes, and identify associated risk factors in fruit bat populations and environmental water sources in Bangladesh. We collected 369 fecal samples from the roosts of two bat species, Pteropus medius and Rousettus leschenaultii, along with 22 water samples from water bodies utilized by humans, livestock, and bats. Salmonella spp. isolates were identified using selective agar culture, followed by biochemical testing and confirmation via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Confirmed isolates underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method against 12 antimicrobials. The prevalence of AMR Salmonella spp. was 7.9% (95% CI: 5.3-11.1%) in bat's roost fecal samples and 31.8% (95% CI: 13.9-54.9%) in environmental water samples. Bat-derived isolates showed high resistance to tetracycline (93%), nalidixic acid (86%), sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (80%), and azithromycin (76%). Among the identified AMR isolates, 28 (96.5%) met the criteria for multidrug resistance (MDR), defined as resistance to three or more antimicrobial classes. Water-derived isolates also demonstrated high resistance, particularly to tetracycline (86%), amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (75%), azithromycin (73%), ceftriaxone (72%), and ciprofloxacin (71%). Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that the odds ratio (OR) of detection of MDR Salmonella spp. in fruit bats was 5.1 times higher during the summer season compared to winter. These findings highlight the evidence of MDR Salmonella spp. in fruit bats and shared environmental water sources in Bangladesh. The co-occurrence of resistant isolates across wildlife and environmental samples highlights the need for integrated AMR surveillance encompassing wildlife reservoirs and shared ecological interfaces. Strengthened antimicrobial stewardship, improved wastewater management, and coordinated One Health surveillance strategies are essential to mitigate the risk of zoonotic spillover and reduce further ecological overlap of MDR bacteria at the wildlife-livestock-human interface in Bangladesh and the broader South Asian region.

title: Digital financial literacy and trust in hybrid AI advisory: Explaining perceived private wealth management capability among digitally engaged retail investors in an emerging market.
authors: Tran MT, Paseková M.
abstract: This study investigates how digital financial literacy, perceived transparency of artificial intelligence advisory services, investment and wealth knowledge, and cyber-risk self-protection shape Perceived Private Wealth Management Capability (PWMC) among digitally engaged retail investors in an emerging-market context. PWMC is conceptualized as a self-assessed capability outcome rather than an objective indicator of wealth-management performance, portfolio returns, or private-banking status. Drawing on the financial capability framework, trust in automation theory, and protection motivation theory, the study develops a trust-to-capability model in which trust in hybrid artificial intelligence advisory and digital wealth management behavior serves as a key explanatory mechanism. A non-probability sample of 249 digitally engaged retail investors in Vietnam was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4.1, with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The results show that digital financial literacy is the strongest antecedent of trust in hybrid artificial intelligence advisory (β = 0.517, p < 0.001). At the same time, perceived advisory transparency also exerts a significant positive effect (β = 0.261, p < 0.001). Investment and wealth knowledge emerged as the strongest predictor of digital wealth management behavior (β = 0.348, p < 0.001). Trust, digital wealth management behavior, and investment and wealth knowledge each positively influence perceived private wealth management capability. Digital wealth management behavior partially mediates the effects of trust, investment, and wealth knowledge on perceived capability. Cyber-risk self-protection limited evidence of a boundary condition by strengthening the relationship between trust and digital wealth management behavior. However, the effect size is small and should be interpreted cautiously (β = 0.098, p = 0.038). The model explains 60.2% of the variance in digital wealth management behavior and 44.3% of the variance in perceived private wealth management capability. By moving beyond conventional explanations of robo-advisory adoption and technology acceptance, this study theorizes hybrid AI advisory as a calibrated trust environment in which retail investors' perceived capability depends not only on whether they trust AI-supported advice but also on whether that trust translates into protective, enacted digital wealth management behavior. The findings should be interpreted in the context of digitally engaged retail investors. They should not be generalized to private banking clients, high-net-worth investors, objective portfolio performance, or verified wealth outcomes.

title: Diagnostic performance of the Normandy score for infective endocarditis in native bone and joint infections.
authors: Pallanza M, Fourré N, Zimmermann V, Boillat-Blanco N, Tzimas G, Monney P, Steinmetz S, Ianculescu N, Senn L, Niclauss L, Kirsch M, Guery B, Papadimitriou-Olivgeris M.
abstract: Purpose The Normandy score was developed to estimate the risk of typical cardiac lesions of infective endocarditis (IE) among patients with native bone and joint infections (NBJI). The aim of this study was to externally validate the Normandy score for the prediction typical cardiac lesions and IE in patients with NBJI. Methods Retrospective study. Setting This study included adult patients with NBJI (2014-2025). Typical cardiac lesions included vegetations, abscess, leaflet perforation, prosthetic valve dehiscence, aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, or fistula identified by echocardiography or cardiac CT, and abnormal metabolic activity on [ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT. IE was diagnosed according to the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria. The primary outcome was the negative likelihood ratio (NLR), with a threshold of Results Among 462 NBJI episodes, typical cardiac lesions were identified in 101 (22%) and IE was diagnosed in 151 (33%). The Normandy score classified 415 (90%) episodes as high risk compared to 450 (97%) that actually had echocardiography. Against the typical cardiac lesion reference standard, the NLR was 0.08 (95% CI 0.01-0.56). Against the IE reference standard, the NLR was 0.14 (0.04-0.44). Conclusions In this highly selected population (89% bacteremic, 33% with IE), the Normandy score met the prespecified NLR threshold for typical cardiac lesions, but not for IE overall. Because it classified 90% of episodes as high risk, it would have reduced echocardiography by only 7 percentage points A more discriminatory prediction tool is needed to meaningfully optimize resource utilization in this population.

title: Design of a power independent of number of slices presaturated ultrashort echo time sequence for accelerated short-T<sub>2</sub> imaging.
authors: Reich JA, MacMillan EL, Feldman RE.
abstract: Simultaneous multi-slice (SMS) techniques have reduced magnetic resonance imaging scan times, but they are challenging to integrate into ultrashort echo time (UTE) sequences. We implemented a novel sequence - the power independent of number of slices (PINS) presaturated UTE (PINS-UTE) sequence - that combines SMS and UTE techniques to increase flexibility in field-of-view and resolution, and reduce scan times for short-T 2 imaging. The PINS-UTE sequence begins with a PINS prepulse and spoiler gradients to presaturate the magnetization profile. Next, a non-selective pulse is used to simultaneously excite six slices and enable UTE data acquisition with an echo time of 0.2 ms. Slice profiles were investigated and images of the skull were acquired in vivo at 3 T. The unwanted signal between the slices was minimized with a prepulse flip angle of 125°. The sequence was used to image a field-of-view of 220 × 220 × 168 mm 3 with resolutions of 1.20 × 1.20 × 4.0 and 0.60 × 0.60 × 4.0 mm 3 in scan times of 2 min 45 s and 5 min 30 s, respectively. These scan times are reduced by factors of 1.4 and 2.8, respectively, as compared to those of 3D UTE sequences with the same repetition time, in-plane field-of-view, and in-plane resolutions. The scan times of the PINS-UTE sequence may be further reduced by imaging fewer slices with a slice gap. As compared to half-pulse 2D UTE sequences, the PINS-UTE sequence is expected to reduce scan times by up to a factor of 12. The PINS-UTE sequence may be applied to accelerate the imaging of tendons, ligaments, and bone.

title: Dental Principles for Plastic Surgery.
authors: Perez-Alvarez I, Shenaq D, Matros E, Kronstadt K.
abstract: Learning objectives After studying this article, the participant should be able to: 1. Understand the relevant dental anatomy, chronicity, nomenclature, and diagnostic imaging. 2. Identify dental pathologies, including congenital abnormalities and dentofacial developmental disorders. 3. Review management strategies for dental infections or trauma. 4. Highlight the role of orthodontics in orthognathic and craniofacial reconstructive surgery. Summary Craniofacial surgery requires a thorough understanding of dental pathology and basic orthodontic principles to treat patients presenting with complex congenital disorders, trauma, and maxillomandibular discrepancies. Despite the close relationship between dentistry, orthodontics, and plastic surgery that dates to the late 1800s, there is a dearth of formalized education of basic dental and orthodontic concepts within plastic surgery curricula. This article outlines basic principles of dental anatomy, dental anomalies, and technology managed by orthodontists to optimize the multidisciplinary approach to craniomaxillofacial pathology.

title: Cultural and structural barriers to HPV vaccine acceptance among young women in the United Arab Emirates.
authors: Langhe R, AlKhatib A, Saber A, Saqr D, Al-Janabi R, Ahmed S, Kelly T, Mahmoud I, Jawdat Barqawi H.
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus, and oncogenic genotypes are linked to cervical cancer. Vaccination reduces cervical cancer burden, yet uptake remains suboptimal in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) despite national immunisation initiatives. This exploratory study aimed to identify and characterize potential cultural and structural barriers that may impede vaccine uptake among educated, digitally connected women in the UAE to inform future, more representative research. Methods A cross-sectional, descriptive study surveyed 1455 women aged 18-30 years across all emirates regarding vaccination status, cultural beliefs, and institutional factors influencing vaccine acceptance and uptake. Results The participants were predominantly educated, non-Emirati, digitally connected young women (mean age 22.4 years, 77.7% non-Emirati, 44.8% healthcare-affiliated). While 58.8% respondents viewed vaccination as culturally acceptable, only 26.2% admitted to being vaccinated. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination included concerns about side effects, feeling too young for vaccination, and fear of family judgment (47.5%, 28.4%, 27.8%, respectively). The most reported reason for receiving the vaccine was its inclusion in the immunisation schedule (37.9%), followed by parental consent and encouragement (36.6%), and for self-protection purposes (25.6%). Furthermore, acceptance increased when the vaccine was presented as a cancer prevention strategy (64.6%), offered at more convenient location (63.8%) or made more affordable (61.5%). Conclusion Overall, the primary barriers to vaccination included concerns regarding the fear of public judgment, reflecting a combination of informational gaps, timing-related considerations, and sociocultural influences affecting HPV vaccine uptake. Future research employing representative sampling is needed to determine whether these barriers generalize to broader UAE populations including non-digitally connected, non-healthcare workers, and Emirati women. Once population level barriers are identified through representative research, public health strategies can be designed to address context-appropriate concerns through targeted education on vaccine safety and culturally sensitive engagement with families and young women to improve uptake.

title: Coronal alignment-related mediolateral load distribution and polyethylene wear in a medial-pivot total knee arthroplasty design.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Lesnicar C, Kistler M, Thorwächter C, Tural I, Simon JM, Niethammer TR, Holzapfel BM, Woiczinski M.
abstract: Introduction While mechanical alignment in total knee arthroplasty aims for a neutral hip-knee-ankle angle, kinematic alignment preserves the native joint line, often allowing residual varus or valgus. Clinically, constitutional variations in alignment affect the coronal joint moments and the mediolateral load distribution, but the impact on polyethylene wear remains unclear. Materials and methods Wear of a medial pivot total knee arthroplasty insert (MS 5C ® , implantcast GmbH, Germany) was evaluated in a knee wear simulator replicating the walking cycle. Inserts were tested under three conditions representing overall lower-limb coronal alignment and the associated mediolateral load distribution: neutral (60% medial / 40% lateral), varus (70% / 30%), and valgus (50% / 50%), with three (n = 3) dynamically loaded inserts and one load-soak control per condition. Testing followed ISO 14243-1:2009 over 5 million cycles. Gravimetric wear and wear patterns were assessed. Results A numerical trend was observed among the groups: The varus-related load distribution demonstrated the lowest overall wear (4.83 ± 1.06 mg/million cycles), whereas the valgus group produced the highest wear (9.43 ± 1.47 mg/million cycles); the neutral group was intermediate (6.81 ± 3.07 mg/million cycles). However, these differences did not reach statistical significance. Visual inspection revealed medial-dominant wear in all groups, with increased lateral wear under valgus-related load distribution. Conclusions Overall lower-limb coronal alignment and the associated mediolateral load distribution appear to influence polyethylene wear in total knee arthroplasty. The observed numerical trend suggests that alignment-related changes in mediolateral load distribution may influence polyethylene wear patterns in this medial-pivot TKA design. Further studies are required to determine the clinical relevance of these observations.

title: Comparative trends of musculoskeletal injury in pickleball and tennis: An 11-year analysis of U.S. emergency department visits.
authors: Kiehl D, Ibrado R, Axelrod A, Vincent HK.
abstract: Background Pickleball participation continues to surge, with many recreational tennis players transitioning to the sport due to perceived ease of play and social appeal. The aim of this study was to compare 11-year injury patterns between patients presenting to the Emergency Department (ED) for pickleball and tennis injuries. Hypothesis We hypothesized that (1) pickleball-related ED visits would increase over time while tennis-related visits would remain stable or decrease; (2) injury patterns would differ between sports by anatomical site, diagnosis, and mechanism; and (3) older adults would account for a higher proportion of fall-related injuries requiring hospital admission. Study design Retrospective comparative epidemiologic study LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III METHODS: National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) data between 2014 and 2024 were sorted for pickleball (product code 3235) and tennis (product code 3284). Cases were manually reviewed to confirm sport participation and exclude non-musculoskeletal injuries. Anatomical site, diagnosis, injury mechanism, treatment disposition, and date of ED visit were extracted. Group comparisons used t-tests and chi-square tests, and linear regression evaluated annual trends. Results A total of 4141 cases were included (pickleball n = 1442; National Estimates (NE) 80,553; tennis n = 2699; NE 110,480). Pickleball-related ED visits increased over time, while tennis-related visits remained stable. Pickleball players were older than tennis players (60.1 (SD 16.7) yr vs. 40.9 (SD 23.3) yr; p Conclusions The rapid rise in pickleball-related injuries necessitates proactive efforts in education, conditioning, and injury prevention to safeguard participants, particularly older adults. Clinical relevance As participation in pickleball grows, especially among older adults, targeted conditioning, emphasizing neuromuscular control and safety education may help reduce injury rates.

title: Clinical quality of large language model responses to thyroid surgery questions: an expert comparative evaluation.
authors: Brucchi F, Balduzzi A, Zhang D, Inama M, Impellizzeri H, Vitali A, Sperotto B, Colombo C, Casaril A, Dionigi G.
abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical information, but their reliability in thyroid surgery remains uncertain. Methods Responses from ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and a blinded human expert comparator were evaluated across 18 thyroid surgery-related clinical questions. Five experienced thyroid surgeons independently rated all responses using a 5-point Likert scale reflecting overall clinical quality. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), and differences between LLMs were analyzed with non-parametric repeated-measures tests; each LLM was compared descriptively with the human comparator. Results Inter-rater agreement ranged from fair to moderate-good (ICC 0.36-0.66). All LLMs achieved high clinical quality scores (median 5), with means slightly below the human comparator (4.47-4.66 vs 4.80). No significant differences were detected among LLMs (Friedman test, p = 0.095), although a marked ceiling effect and question-level variability were observed. Conclusions LLMs may support patient-facing thyroid surgery information, but specialist oversight remains essential.

title: Cheek Reconstruction With a Free Internal Mammary Perforator (IMAP) Flap in an African American Patient With Recurrent Dermatofibrosarcoma.
authors: Noel OF, Becerra CI, Bryant G, Clune JE.
abstract: Traditional flaps dominate head and neck reconstruction; however, the free internal mammary artery perforator (IMAP) flap offers excellent pliability, hidden donor-site closure, and favorable cervicofacial color match. We report the use of a free IMAP flap for cheek reconstruction in an African American patient with recurrent dermatofibrosarcoma, achieving excellent contour restoration, hair-bearing skin match, and minimal donor-site morbidity.

title: Capturing experienced invisibility among people with multiple stigmatized identities: The experienced invisibility scale protocol.
authors: Sesko AK, Fisher AN, Biernat M.
abstract: Invisibility is the experience of not being attended to, remembered, differentiated from others, or given credit for contributions. In the current registered report, we aim to validate the Experienced Invisibility Scale (EIS), a measure designed to capture experiences of invisibility, which are most likely to be experienced by people with multiple stigmatized identities. As proof of concept, we first present a pilot study testing the factor structure of the EIS, in which we found that: 1) a bifactor model ("unheard" and "unnoticed") best represents the structure of experienced invisibility, but that calculating a total score is likely to be sufficient for most purposes, 2) the EIS is most likely to be experienced by those with multiple stigmatized identities, and 3) initial tests of convergent, discriminant, and predictive validity were supported. We then propose three studies to further validate the EIS and its links to social identities. Study 1 will distinguish the EIS from related constructs of social exclusion, objectification, rejection sensitivity, positive and negative affect, and other experiences of discrimination, test the temporal stability of the EIS, and examine relationships with well-being. Study 2 will examine whether the EIS predicts additional outcomes including health, low felt impact, perceived powerlessness, and denial of services or power. Study 3 will test hypotheses that Black women (compared to White women and Black and White men) will report experiencing more invisibility, and will show stronger relationships between invisibility and negative outcomes. We hope this work will aid scholars in better understanding invisibility as a form of discrimination.

title: Can Deltoid Hounsfield Unit/Supraspinatus Hounsfield Unit Predict Postoperative Rotator Cuff Retear?
authors: Wang X, Liu G, Wang X, Ma Y, Zhou H, Shen G.
abstract: Objectives Retear is a common complication after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR), yet available predictors are limited and combined models perform better than single factors. This study investigated whether the preoperative deltoid-to-supraspinatus Hounsfield unit (HU) ratio predicts retear and integrated it with established risk factors to develop an optimal predictive model. Methods This retrospective study included 243 patients with full-thickness rotator cuff tears who underwent arthroscopic repair from July 2021 to January 2025. Preoperative CT and MRI were obtained for all patients; postoperative MRI at 3-6 months evaluated tendon healing using the Sugaya classification (grades I-III: intact healing, n = 208; grades IV-V: retear, n = 35). Statistical analyses used SPSS. After normality testing, continuous variables were compared using t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Variables with group differences were screened by elastic net regression, then entered into binary logistic regression. ROC analysis determined optimal cutoffs, and 1000 bootstrap samples provided an optimism-corrected C-statistic for internal validation. Results Multivariate analysis identified supraspinatus fatty infiltration (FI) (p 1.02 and FI ≥ Goutallier Stage 2 provided the best predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.868, sensitivity of 77.1%, specificity of 81.2%, and accuracy of 89.3%. Conclusions The D/S HU was significantly associated with postoperative rotator cuff retear, and a ratio greater than 1.02 was identified as an effective threshold for predicting retear. Moreover, the combination of a D/S HU > 1.02 and FI ≥ Goutallier Stage 2 yielded the strongest predictive performance. This preoperative risk assessment model may help surgeons optimize treatment planning and better anticipate postoperative outcomes.

title: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellular fractions reflect individual histopathological features in interstitial pneumonia.
authors: Miyoshi S, Sakamoto S, Homma S, Nakamura Y, Usui Y, Shimizu H, Sekiya M, Urabe N, Isshiki T, Azuma Y, Tochigi N, Kishi K.
abstract: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cellular analysis is an adjunctive diagnostic tool in interstitial pneumonia (IP), yet its relationship with individual histopathological features remains unclear. We retrospectively compared BALF cellular fractions with 24 histopathological features in 67 IP patients who underwent BALF and surgical lung biopsy at a single center (2005-2020). False discovery rate correction was applied (q < 0.05), followed by multivariable logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis. BALF lymphocyte proportion was negatively associated with fibroblastic foci (13.0% vs 29.0%, q = 0.002) and positively with bronchiolitis (q = 0.029), intraluminal organization (q = 0.002), and epithelioid cell granulomas (q = 0.012). On multivariable analysis, fibroblastic foci were independently associated with a lower likelihood of BALF lymphocytosis (odds ratio 0.23, p = 0.018), and this association persisted after exclusion of patients with a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) or probable UIP pattern and of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Intraluminal lymphocyte proliferation was also associated with BALF lymphocytosis, although this estimate was based on few patients. Patients with fibroblastic foci had poorer survival (p = 0.003), whereas survival did not differ when patients were stratified by BALF lymphocyte proportion. ROC analysis identified a BALF lymphocyte cutoff of 18.5% for the presence of fibroblastic foci (AUC 0.76), and adding BALF lymphocyte proportion to the high-resolution computed tomography pattern improved discrimination of fibroblastic foci (AUC 0.847 versus 0.686). Neutrophil and eosinophil proportions showed no significant associations after correction. BALF lymphocyte proportion is associated with several histopathological features in IP, most strongly with fibroblastic foci, and may provide complementary information where surgical lung biopsy is not feasible.

title: Atraumatic Subcapital Femoral Neck Fracture as the Initial Presentation of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: A Case-Based Systematic Review.
authors: Plangsiri K, Boonyanuwat W, Kongmalai P.
abstract: Objective Atraumatic subcapital femoral neck fracture associated with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is rare and may be difficult to recognize before surgery, while the available evidence regarding its diagnosis and management remains limited. We therefore aimed to describe an atypical presentation of ONFH as an atraumatic subcapital femoral neck fracture and to synthesize the available evidence on its diagnostic features, treatment patterns, and outcomes through a systematic review. Methods A CARE-compliant case report was combined with a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review registered in PROSPERO. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from inception to February 28, 2026, for reports of atraumatic subcapital or transcervical femoral neck fractures associated with ONFH. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists. Findings were synthesized descriptively because of substantial clinical heterogeneity and the absence of comparative studies. Results Eighteen studies involving 50 patients (58 fractured hips) were included. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was reported in 38 of 50 patients (76%). Reported primary-treatment failures occurred in 3 of 8 internally fixed hips and 1 of 41 hips treated with arthroplasty; however, these uncontrolled descriptive findings do not permit comparative or causal inference. Conclusions ONFH should be considered in atraumatic femoral neck fractures with atypical radiographic features. The available evidence is insufficient to determine the comparative effectiveness of arthroplasty and internal fixation, and treatment decisions should therefore remain individualized.

title: Association of TLR2 T597C, TLR4 A896G, and TLR9 G1174A gene polymorphisms with risk of pulmonary tuberculosis in the Ethiopian population: A case-control study.
authors: Melake A, Mihrete K, Malkamu B.
abstract: Background Toll-like receptor genes have been extensively researched for their role in the susceptibility to pulmonary tuberculosis across different populations. The relationship between variations in toll-like receptor genes and additional risk factors for pulmonary tuberculosis is not well understood, because of the complex interplay between genetic predispositions and environmental influences. This study aimed to elucidate the association of TLR2 T597C, TLR4 A896G, and TLR9 G1174A gene polymorphisms with the risk of developing pulmonary tuberculosis. Methods A total of 306 samples - 153 patients with pulmonary tuberculosis and 153 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were selected using a consecutive sampling technique. Clinical and biochemical variables were measured to assess the associated risk factors. Deoxyribonucleic acid was isolated from blood samples, and the TLR2, TLR4, and TLR9 genotypes were identified using polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism and analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis. Results Our analysis showed that the TLR2-CC genotype (OR = 3.82; 95% CI = 1.79-8.16; P Conclusion The TLR2 T597C gene of the CC genotype and the C allele, the TLR4 A896G genes of the GG genotype and the G allele, and the TLR9 G1174A genes of the AA genotype and the A allele are associated with increased risk of pulmonary tuberculosis among the Ethiopian patients under study.

title: Arthroscopic "Triple-Beam" Biologic Augmentation of Massive Rotator Cuff Tears Using the Combined Long Head of Biceps Transposition and Autologous Palmaris Longus Tendon Bridging.
authors: Zhang C, Liu Z, Chen M, Wang Y, Zheng G, Ma L.
abstract: The management of massive rotator cuff tears remains a substantial clinical challenge. Standard superior capsular reconstruction often fails to adequately restore the dynamic load-transfer mechanics of the shoulder. Furthermore, direct repair of chronic, retracted tears is frequently associated with excessive tension, resulting in high rates of suture cut-through and structural failure. To overcome these limitations, we describe an arthroscopic biological reconstruction technique termed the "Triple-Beam" procedure. This approach combines transposition of the long head of the biceps tendon with augmentation using an autologous palmaris longus tendon bridge. The construct employs the transposed long head of the biceps tendon together with the anterior and posterior limbs of the palmaris longus graft to form a robust 3-beam structure secured to the greater tuberosity. This design is intended to provide both static superior restraints to prevent superior humeral migration and dynamic load distribution, thereby reducing tension at the repair interface. As a cost-effective, autologous strategy, this technique aims to improve biological healing and biomechanical stability in the management of massive rotator cuff tears.

title: Aneurysmal Bone Cyst of the Radial Diaphysis Managed by En Bloc Resection and Fibular Strut Autograft Reconstruction in a Young Adult Female: A Rare Case Report.
authors: Khan AH, Hussain E, Arif L, Akhtar SO, Raza AA, Samadi A, Ahmed N.
abstract: Aneurysmal bone cyst (ABC) of the radial diaphysis is rare and may mimic telangiectatic osteosarcoma on imaging. We report a young woman with progressively enlarging, painful forearm swelling due to ABC, treated by en bloc resection and fibular strut autograft reconstruction, achieving pain-free union, good function and no recurrence at short-term follow-up.

title: Analysis of causative factors and preventive strategies for traumatic orthopedic medical malpractice in Shanghai: a high-responsibility perspective.
authors: Chen C, Gao H, Wang S, Yuan L, Xu W, Yan H, Ye X, Qi H, Li Y, Ma Y, Wu H, Xu P.
abstract: Background Medical malpractice is recognized as the most severe category of adverse medical events, characterized by illegality, negligent conduct, and resultant harm. Cases classified as high-responsibility-level malpractice impose substantial impacts on healthcare institutions and medical personnel. This study aims to identify negligence-related determinants contributing to such cases and to explore targeted preventive strategies designed to reduce the occurrence of high-responsibility-level medical malpractice. Methods A total of 125 cases of traumatic orthopedic medical malpractice were retrieved from the Office of Medical Malpractice Handling under the Shanghai Municipal Health Commission. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 26.0. Descriptive data were presented as counts, frequencies, and percentages. Intergroup differences in negligence-related factors between high- and low-responsibility-level categories were evaluated using chi-square tests. Additionally, binary stepwise logistic regression analysis was performed to determine independent associations between specific negligence factors and high responsibility levels. Results Traumatic orthopedic medical malpractice cases in Shanghai demonstrated several distinct characteristics, including a relatively low mortality rate (4.00%), a notably high disability rate (74.4%), a greater occurrence in secondary hospitals (60.00%), and increased involvement of attending physicians and associate chief physicians (76.80%). High-responsibility-level cases constituted 45.60% of all included cases. Chi-square analysis indicated that inappropriate surgical procedures and violations of clinical practice standards were significantly more prevalent in the high-responsibility-level group compared with the low-responsibility-level group ( P Conclusions Several preventive measures are recommended, including strengthening perioperative management, ensuring strict compliance with clinical diagnostic, therapeutic, and nursing protocols, standardizing imaging examinations and comprehensive physical assessments to reduce missed and misdiagnoses, enhancing physician-patient communication, standardizing medical record documentation, and reinforcing early postoperative rehabilitation strategies.

title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore.
authors: Blythe R, Graves N, Iyer NG, Peres MA.
abstract: Introduction The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. Methods We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type. We applied sex- and cancer-specific Cox regressions to the Singapore Cancer Registry for annual predicted survival from 1992 to 2022. These were combined with census and employment data to estimate HPV-associated income losses in Singapore. Attributable fractions and vaccine effectiveness data for HPV 16/18 from the literature were used to estimate the effectiveness of bivalent HPV vaccination. Structural sensitivity analysis examined the role of 80% population coverage conferring herd immunity. Results The registry contained 17,294 individuals with an HPV-associated cancer diagnosis. Lost income was greatest for cervical cancer due to its high prevalence, however the losses per diagnosis were highest for oropharyngeal cancer. Bivalent HPV vaccination led to income benefits of $SGD1,397 [$895 to $1,838] in girls and -$62 [-$76 to -$48] in boys. A gender-neutral HPV vaccination of 80% of 15-year-old Singaporeans, conferring herd immunity, would have lifetime income protective benefits of $24.4m [$14.2m, $33.7m] per cohort, a five-fold return on investment. Conclusions In addition to avoiding healthcare costs and lost quality of life, parents should consider vaccination as a means of avoiding potential income losses. A national policy of gender-neutral HPV vaccination could deliver substantial income protection due to both individual vaccine protection and herd immunity.

title: Advances in classification-based treatment of Kümmell disease.
authors: Zi'an Z, Feipeng W, Kudereti B, Dapeng L.
abstract: Background Kümmell disease is a special type of delayed vertebral collapse after osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture, characterized by vertebral ischemic osteonecrosis, intravertebral cleft, fracture nonunion, and pseudoarthrosis-like instability. Its treatment should shift from simple pain relief to classification-guided stability reconstruction. Methods This narrative review was conducted with a structured literature search focusing on the pathological mechanism, imaging classification, vertebral augmentation, bone cement distribution, anchoring techniques, fixation strategies, and complication management of Kümmell disease. Main findings Classification-based treatment is important because patients differ in vertebral collapse, intravertebral cleft morphology, posterior wall integrity, dynamic instability, spinal canal compromise, and neurological status. Stable or early-stage cases may be treated with conservative management, percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP), or percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP). Unstable cases with obvious intravertebral clefts, cement aggregation, or high risk of cement loosening and migration may require bone cement distribution optimization, anchoring techniques, bone-filling mesh containers, or intravertebral support devices. Advanced or complex cases with severe posterior wall defect, severe spinal canal compromise, neurological deficit, rigid kyphotic deformity, or poor reducibility may require posterior fixation, decompression, or deformity correction. The treatment boundary for stage III patients with posterior wall disruption but without neurological symptoms remains controversial and requires individualized decision-making. Conclusions Kümmell disease treatment should shift toward classification-guided decision-making, vertebral stability reconstruction, and whole-process osteoporosis management. Emerging techniques may provide additional options for selected patients, but current evidence remains limited and further multicenter prospective studies are needed.

title: Accuracy of Computer-Assisted Navigation in Total Ankle Arthroplasty Surgery Using Computed Tomography: A Short Report.
authors: Rakauskas TR, Henderson AP, Meli G, Herbel C, El Masry S, Boux De Casson F, Hamad C, Haupt E.
abstract: Background Computer-assisted navigation (CAN) offers dynamic intraoperative guidance in total ankle arthroplasty (TAA). Although laboratory data suggest superior precision, in vivo evidence is lacking. This study used weightbearing computed tomography (WBCT) to evaluate CAN accuracy of postoperative TAA implant position relative to the plan. We hypothesized that absolute discrepancies would be Methods Thirteen consecutive patients (November 2024-November 2025) underwent TAA using CAN. Preoperative computed tomography-based 3D models were used for templating. Postoperative WBCT scans were used to measure final implant seating, and computerized measurements were used to identify implant placement discrepancy. We analyzed absolute discrepancies between planned vs final postoperative positions. Results Tibial absolute discrepancies were within desired limits for varus/valgus (1.65° ± 1.43°), slope (1.87° ± 1.34°), and cut height (0.68 ± 0.62 mm) but not for axial rotation (3.97 ± 2.64). For the talus, varus/valgus (2.93° ± 1.86°) and cut height (0.66 ± 0.71 mm) absolute discrepancies were within desired limits. The increased talar slope deviation (3.90 ± 2.89) in the final position may be due to non-navigated implant impaction. Conclusion Although discrepancies persisted in tibial rotational alignment and talar positioning, the low variability across measurements suggests that CAN may support accurate implant positioning. These short-term positioning accuracy findings support the utility of CAN as a potential tool for enhancing implant positioning reproducibility in TAA. Level of evidence Level IV, case series.

title: ASO Visual Abstract: Primary Breast Angiosarcoma: Clinicopathologic Features and Oncologic Outcomes.
authors: Vavolizza RD, Subramaniam A, Yi M, Wingate E, Perez AN, Keung E, Roland CL, Torres K, Scally CP, Lyu H, Yoder A, Mitra D, Farooqi AS, Bishop AJ, Guadagnolo BA, Lazar A, Ravi V, Hunt KK, Lillemoe HA.

title: A self-supervised reconstruction framework for segment-level detection of task-induced deviations in multi-channel EEG.
authors: Saavedra LA, Quintero-Rincón A, Batatia H.
abstract: Understanding brain activations during mental arithmetic tasks provides valuable insights into cognitive processing. However, analyses of the same electroencephalogram (EEG) dataset have produced inconsistent findings about the cortical regions involved, raising methodological questions about global signal treatment. Detecting task-related activations without pre-labelled datasets further remains challenging when supervised approaches are not applicable. This study presents a self-supervised framework for segment-based anomaly detection using deep learning to identify EEG signal outliers during mental arithmetic. Using a hierarchical variational auto-encoder, the study reconstructed multichannel EEG data segmented into 1-second intervals and trained exclusively on resting-state recordings. The study assessed reconstruction quality using multiple error metrics, including dynamic time warping, short-time Fourier transform loss, and signal-to-noise ratio, applied individually to channel segments. Outlier segments were detected based on the elevated reconstruction error relative to the resting baseline, using an unsupervised detection method. By analysing deviations at the segment level rather than treating the signal globally, the proposed framework captured transient cortical dynamics that may otherwise be obscured. The results demonstrated that these outlier segments exhibited distinct temporal and spectral characteristics, particularly within the delta, theta, and beta bands, and were most frequently located in peripheral electrodes such as Fp2, O1, O2, P3, and T6. Additionally, co-occurrence analysis uncovered functional patterns of simultaneous anomalies across specific electrode pairs and triplets, suggesting temporally dynamic and spatially distributed cognitive processes during arithmetic reasoning. Overall, the proposed framework provided a fine-grained temporal and spatial characterisation of EEG deviations during mental arithmetic and offers a methodological perspective that helped explain discrepancies in previously reported electrode-level findings.

title: A randomised feasibility trial of VR-enhanced cue exposure therapy versus neutral VR exposure for cocaine use disorder, with wearable monitoring and JITA-EMA: Feasibility randomised controlled trial protocol.
authors: Brobbin E, Cella M, Copello A, Coulton S, Darvell H, Di Pietro J, Drummond C, Duffy J, Folarin A, Glautier S, Holborn T, Kiyak C, Molai J, Phillips T, Sankesara H, Stahl D, Stewart C, Valmaggia L, Williams C, Deluca P.
abstract: Background Cocaine use disorder (CUD) is associated with high rates of relapse, with craving and cue reactivity playing important roles in ongoing use. Cue Exposure Therapy (CET) aims to reduce conditioned responses to drug-related cues through extinction learning, but traditional approaches may be limited by poor ecological validity. Virtual reality-enhanced Cue Exposure Therapy (VR-CET) offers a potentially more immersive and realistic method of delivering cue exposure. Concurrently, advances in wearable physiological monitoring and just-in-time adaptive ecological momentary assessment (JITA-EMA) enable the real-time assessment of craving in everyday life. Objective To assess the feasibility of recruitment, consent, randomisation, blinding, intervention delivery and retention over 8 weeks post-randomisation. Method This is a two-arm, parallel-group, randomised feasibility trial conducted in UK community drug treatment services. Sixty adults receiving treatment will be randomised (1:1) to either VR-CET or an active VR-Relaxation control condition. Both arms will receive six VR sessions over four weeks, alongside continuous physiological monitoring using a wearable device and smartphone-based JITA-EMA for eight weeks. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment, retention, intervention adherence, wearable wear time, EMA completion, acceptability, and safety. Clinical outcomes will include cocaine use measured by Timeline Follow-Back, cue reactivity assessed through subjective and physiological measures, and participant-confirmed craving episodes captured via wearable-triggered JITA-EMA. Qualitative interviews with participants and service providers will explore intervention acceptability and implementation facilitators, barriers and suggestions. Results Planned start date is July 2026, and enrolment is due to end in April 2027. Data analysis is estimated to be completed by the end of spring 2027. Conclusions To our knowledge, this is the first feasibility RCT of VR-CET for CUD within UK drug treatment services. Results from this trial will help assess the feasibility of integrating VR-CET, continuous physiological monitoring, and real-time craving JITA within CUD treatment. This can be used to inform the design of a future definitive trial and contribute to the development of personalised, technology-enabled approaches to relapse prevention and substance treatment. Trial registration: ISRCTN21409750, https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN21409750.

title: A hybrid car-following behavior prediction framework for snowy weather based on stacking ensemble learning.
authors: Luo Z, Geng F, Zhang Z.
abstract: To improve the accuracy and robustness of vehicle car-following behavior prediction on snowy highways, this paper proposes a hybrid prediction framework based on Stacking ensemble learning. The framework integrates a theoretically driven improved Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) with two state-of-the-art data-driven models-the Prediction-enhanced Intelligent Driver Model (P-IDM) and a Transformer-LSTM hybrid network-within a Stacking ensemble architecture. First, an Icy Condition Enhanced IDM (ICES-IDM) model is developed by introducing a road adhesion coefficient mapping function and a speed perception error coefficient to parameterize the classical IDM for snowy environments. Second, a P-IDM model is constructed by incorporating a self-attention-based preceding vehicle speed prediction module into the classical IDM framework to enhance responsiveness to sudden maneuvers of the leading vehicle. Third, a Transformer-LSTM dual-stream network (TL-Net) is designed to jointly predict car-following acceleration by parallel extraction of temporal attention features and recurrent neural network features. Within the Stacking framework, ICES-IDM and P-IDM serve as physics-driven base learners, TL-Net serves as a data-driven base learner, and XGBoost is adopted as the meta-learner to construct a hybrid acceleration prediction model. The model is trained and validated using naturalistic driving data collected in Norway-comprising a dataset of 311,908 observations that link vehicle measurements with weather, road surface, and lighting conditions, along with a five-month road record dataset from Narvik. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) in acceleration prediction under snowy conditions that is approximately 28.1% lower than that of the standalone ICES-IDM model, 9.2% lower than that of the TL-Net model, and 4.2% lower than that of the conventional Stacking-IDM-LSTM framework. The model exhibits excellent generalization capability across varying snow intensity levels, providing theoretical support for vehicle car-following safety warning systems in snowy environments.

title: A Subscapularis Split Technique for Dynamic Anterior Stabilization and Bankart Repair.
authors: Pelaez-Damy P, Mangino-Rivas C, Orihuela-Fuchs VA.
abstract: Splitting of the subscapularis in a dynamic anterior stabilization procedure can be a challenging and not easily reproducible technique that has many variations. We describe a technique using an arthroscopic cannula to perform the split and maintain a uniform width, as well as an easy long head of the biceps shuttling. This technique is easy to reproduce and is time-saving, especially if a Bankart repair is concomitantly done.

title: A Place to Belong: A Comprehensive Review of Adolescent and Young Adult Surgical Oncology Care.
authors: Srivatsa SB, Boomer L, Englum BR, Rodeberg DA, Mansfield SA, Shaffiey S, Abrams AN, Perez G, Aldrink JH, Cameron DB, APSA Cancer Committee.
abstract: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) oncology has emerged as a distinct field in response to persistent disparities in outcomes among patients aged 15-39 years, who often experience fragmented care across pediatric and adult systems. For surgeons, these challenges are especially relevant because biopsy, resection, metastatic disease management, fertility-preservation procedures, and survivorship planning frequently hinge on the surgical pathway through which patients enter cancer care. This review summarizes the epidemiology, systems-level barriers, biologic considerations, and supportive care priorities that define comprehensive AYA surgical oncology care. AYA malignancies encompass both pediatric-type tumors and adult-onset carcinomas, creating ambiguity in referral patterns, trial access, and treatment setting. Current evidence supports care at specialized or hybrid AYA-focused centers that integrate pediatric and adult expertise, multidisciplinary coordination, psychosocial support, fertility counseling, and survivorship services. However, major gaps remain, including low clinical trial enrollment, inconsistent access to age-appropriate supportive care, financial toxicity, and inadequate coordination of fertility preservation and long-term follow-up. Emerging data also suggest meaningful age-associated differences in tumor biology across reinforcing the need for developmentally and biologically informed treatment planning. Given the rarity and heterogeneity of AYA malignancies, age-informed care pathways built on structured collaboration between pediatric and adult surgeons offer a realistic and scalable model to align surgical decision-making with the developmental and oncologic needs of this population.

title: Wide-awake local anaesthesia without routine tourniquet for cubital tunnel surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Jha G, Malasani S, Elliott W, Kulkarni K, Kheiran A.
abstract: Purpose Cubital tunnel surgery is performed under general or regional anaesthesia. Wide-awake local anaesthesia no tourniquet (WALANT) may reduce anaesthetic dependency, postoperative pain and resource use while permitting active assessment of ulnar nerve stability. We evaluated clinical outcomes, anaesthetic feasibility and reported complications. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidance (PROSPERO CRD420261407435), MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from inception to June 2026, with CENTRAL additionally searched in September 2026. Comparative and uncontrolled studies of decompression, medial epicondylectomy or anterior transposition under awake local infiltration without routine tourniquet inflation were included. Meta-analysis was undertaken where sufficiently comparable data were available. Results Twelve studies comprising 535 participants were included: 328 participants entered an eligible awake-local or intended-WALANT intervention arm and 207 received comparator anaesthesia. The 328 intervention-arm participants accounted for 330 procedures because two participants underwent bilateral surgery. Three non-randomised comparative studies involving 111 participants did not demonstrate clear evidence of a difference in patient-reported disability between awake local and comparator anaesthesia (standardised mean difference 0.13, 95% confidence interval -0.24 to 0.51; I 2 = 0%). Revision or reoperation events were sparse and were not quantitatively pooled because follow-up duration, operative procedure and treatment pathways differed materially between studies. Individual studies reported lower early postoperative pain and shorter perioperative pathways. Supplemental infiltration was sometimes required, and seven of 40 patients in one intended-WALANT cohort ultimately received general anaesthesia, although the timing of pathway alteration was unclear. Reported adverse events were uncommon but inconsistently ascertained. Conclusions Awake local anaesthesia without routine tourniquet inflation appears feasible for selected patients. Available non-randomised comparative evidence has not demonstrated a clear difference in medium-term patient-reported function between awake-local and comparator anaesthetic pathways. Some studies reported lower early postoperative pain and shorter perioperative pathways, but these findings remain susceptible to confounding. Current evidence does not establish superior neurological recovery, lower revision risk or definitive safety.

title: Using a Y-Shaped Artificial Ligament for Posterolateral Corner Reconstruction in Multiligament Knee Injuries: A Surgical Technique.
authors: Zhou H, Xue Z, Wang D, Xu S, Zhang J.
abstract: In multiligament knee injuries, reconstruction of the posterolateral corner is essential for restoring varus and rotational stability of the knee. Autografts and allografts are the current mainstays for posterolateral corner reconstruction; however, their use is associated with inherent limitations, including graft availability, insufficient size, and donor site morbidity. This technical note describes a surgical technique for posterolateral corner reconstruction using a Y-shaped artificial ligament. This approach achieves anatomic reconstruction of the lateral collateral ligament and a functional, nonanatomic reconstruction of the popliteus tendon through a single femoral tunnel. The technique aims to provide reliable knee stability in a relatively minimally invasive manner while circumventing the limitations associated with traditional grafts.

title: Understanding Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP): A single centre case-control study protocol.
authors: Lian SL, Storås TH, Gløersen EM, Løvland G, Hopp E, Mossige I, Hovd M, Uggerud HT, Kardel KR, Bye HA, Buset AL, Valdmanis K, Knapskog AB, Øksengård AR, Fladby T, Nilsen KB, Mardal KA, Ringstad G, Eide PK, Toft M, Nordengen K.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) are proteinopathies characterized by pathological accumulation of amyloid beta, phosphorylated-tau, and alpha-synuclein. Impaired clearance of these proteins is thought to contribute to disease pathogenesis, whereas preserved or enhanced clearance may be compensatory. Beyond intracellular degradation within neurons and glial cells, an extracellular clearance pathway, the glymphatic system, facilitates cerebrospinal fluid flow into perivascular spaces, exchange with interstitial fluid, and subsequent clearance from the brain. Glymphatic transport may therefore be critical for removal of excess proteins and metabolic waste, and its dysfunction could promote protein aggregation and neurodegeneration. The Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP) study is an observational case-control imaging and biomarker study comparing glymphatic clearance in patients with AD, PD, and DLB versus healthy controls. We aim to recruit 70 participants: PD (n = 20), DLB (n = 10), AD (n = 20), and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n = 20). The AD group will be stratified by pathology, with half amyloid-positive/tau-negative (A + T-) and half amyloid- and tau-positive (A + T+). The PD group will be stratified by disease duration. Participants will undergo baseline MRI followed by intrathecal injection of gadobutrol (0.25 mmol) and serial MRI at 5, 24, 48, and 72 hours. Influx and efflux of tracer will be modeled from T1 signal changes. Blood will be sampled repeatedly from 1 to 72 hours; cerebrospinal fluid will be collected at baseline. Individual glymphatic clearance will be estimated using population pharmacokinetic methods, where gadobutrol serves as a tracer. Sleep will be monitored with triaxial accelerometry and sleep diaries. The primary outcome is group differences in glymphatic clearance metrics between each disease group and controls; secondary analyses will explore associations with cognition, disease severity and duration, sleep quality, and cerebrospinal fluid protein levels.

title: Transmalleolar vs Portal-Based Minimally Invasive Tibiotalar Joint Preparation: A Cadaveric Study.
authors: Patel AN, Durudogan E, Arave M, Harish M, Achay J, Huh J, Kadakia A.
abstract: Background Successful ankle arthrodesis depends on thorough preparation of the tibiotalar joint. Open, arthroscopic, and minimally invasive (MIS) techniques exist. MIS burr preparation under fluoroscopy enables smaller incisions and preserves the osteogenic bone slurry. Traditional anteromedial and anterolateral portal-based MIS approaches may leave posterior "blind spots" and limit deformity correction. A transmalleolar MIS technique has been proposed to improve joint access while facilitating apposition and deformity correction. The purpose of this study was to compare the proportion of tibiotalar joint prepared and safety profiles between the transmalleolar and portal-based MIS techniques. Methods Fourteen fresh frozen cadaveric lower extremities (7 matched pairs) were randomized to transmalleolar or portal-based MIS tibiotalar joint preparation (n = 7 each). A single fellowship-trained surgeon performed all procedures using standardized burr instrumentation and fluoroscopy. Specimens were disarticulated, photographed with calibration markers, and analyzed using ImageJ to quantify percent preparation of the tibial plafond, talar dome, and combined surfaces. Two independent reviewers (1 masked) performed measurements. Distances to the posterior tibial tendon, posterior tibial artery, and tibial nerve were measured; t tests, Fisher exact test, and ICC were used ( P Results Transmalleolar MIS achieved greater tibial plafond preparation (94.7% vs 76.8%, P = .009) than the portal technique. Talar dome (67.5% vs 73.5%, P = .534) and combined preparation (83.6% vs 75.5%, P = .248) were similar. Posterior talar zones remained incompletely prepared in most specimens (5/7 vs 6/7). Reliability was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficients >0.90). No neurovascular injuries occurred. Fewer transmalleolar specimens were at risk (28.6% vs 57.1%, P = .592), although not statistically significant. Conclusion Compared with traditional portal-based MIS tibiotalar joint preparation, the transmalleolar MIS technique provided a statistically increased area of tibial plafond preparation without increasing the neurovascular risk. Overall preparation and talar debridement were similar, with comparable safety profiles. Level of evidence Level V, cadaveric / basic science study.

title: The role of speaker accuracy and mutual exclusivity in children's novel word learning.
authors: Banerjee S, Gangopadhyay I.
abstract: Children draw on multiple sources of information during word learning, including speaker testimony and lexical expectations. Yet, little is known about how these cues jointly influence children's ability to learn new words. The present study examined the combined effect of speaker accuracy and mutual exclusivity (ME) on short-term retention of label-object associations in 4- to 7-year-old monolingual English speaking children. Children were presented novel and familiar object pairs, and were taught novel labels by either an accurate speaker (one who previously labeled familiar objects correctly) or an inaccurate speaker (one who previously labeled familiar objects incorrectly). Novel labels were introduced under two conditions: Align-with-ME (speakers labeled the novel object with novel names) and Conflict-with-ME (speakers labeled the familiar object with novel names, conflicting with ME). Results showed that children retained novel labels for novel objects from both accurate and inaccurate speakers when speaker testimony aligned with ME expectations. This suggests that children are open to learning novel words from speakers regardless of their prior accuracy and may also draw on other available cues, such as label-object co-occurrences, during learning. However, when speaker testimony violated ME expectations, children performed poorly, possibly due to difficulty disambiguating between speaker testimony and their existing lexical knowledge. Together, these findings suggest that children's short-term retention of label-object associations is supported when available cues align, irrespective of speaker accuracy status. These associations, however, become less robust when ME and speaker cues provide conflicting information.

title: The influence of step width on muscle contributions to frontal-plane balance control during walking.
authors: Emerson HE, Neptune RR.
abstract: Older adults and those with neuromuscular deficits often have difficulty maintaining dynamic balance and walk with wider steps. Wider steps increase the mediolateral moment arm between the body center of mass and foot center of pressure and have been associated with a higher time rate of change of frontal-plane angular momentum (Ḣ). Previous simulation work has identified the primary muscle contributors to Ḣ, but it remains unclear how those contributions change with altered step widths. The purpose of this study was to analyze how step width influences muscle contributions to Ḣ using musculoskeletal modeling and simulation. A cohort of healthy young adults walked on an instrumented treadmill at four step widths: Narrow, Self-Selected, Wide and Extra Wide. Motion capture, ground reaction force and EMG data were used to generate simulations, and muscle contributions to Ḣ were quantified and compared across step widths. The overall muscle contributions to net Ḣ changed little with increasing step widths. However, muscle contributions to the vertical GRF component of Ḣ increased with step width due to the increased mediolateral moment arm. This effect was opposed primarily by the contribution of the hip abductors to the medial GRF component, and by a decrease in contributions of the gastrocnemius and soleus to the lateral GRF component. These results support the premise that the hip abductors and ankle plantarflexors are critical for frontal-plane balance control and should be a central consideration in developing rehabilitation strategies for those who walk with wider steps.

title: The Boston All-in-One Medial Patellofemoral Complex Reconstruction: A Combined Medial Patellofemoral Ligament and Medial Quadriceps Tendon Femoral Ligament Dynamic Tensioning Technique Using Allograft.
authors: Al-Hourani K, Li X.
