abstract: Recent anatomical understanding of the medial restraints of the patella has evolved over the last decade with a current focus on the medial quadriceps tendon femoral ligament, a distinct anatomical structure to the medial patellofemoral ligament. These combine to form the medial patellofemoral complex. This technical note describes a technique to reconstruct the whole medial patellofemoral complex, replicating anatomical knowledge and allowing for dynamic graft tensioning using an allograft.

title: The 10–6 Method for Tibial Preparation in Kinematically Aligned Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Technical Description and Preliminary Clinical Evaluation
The 10-6 Method for Tibial Preparation in Kinematically Aligned Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Technical Description and Preliminary Clinical Evaluation.
authors: Anderson PM, Nedopil A, Giehl M, Jakuscheit A, Rudert M, Oberfeld J.
abstract: Background Kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty (KA TKA) aims to restore the proximal tibia's prearthritic varus-valgus (V-V) alignment. However, a standardized thickness to correct for proximal tibia cartilage wear has not been established. This study reports the cartilage thickness of the tibial plateau. Secondary objectives include determining the incidence of V-V recuts when a 4-mm correction for cartilage wear is applied and analyzing the V-V alignment between the preoperative tibial joint line and the postoperative tibial component. Methods Using a caliper-based optical method, maximum articular cartilage thickness was measured on 28 resections of the tibial plateaus from 28 patients undergoing unrestricted KA TKA. One surgeon corrected for cartilage wear on the tibial plateau by decreasing the resection thickness by 4 mm using a 10-mm- and 6-mm-stylus (10-6 method). Rates of necessary recuts were documented. Results The mean maximum cartilage thickness was 3.8 mm (95% confidence interval 3.4-4.2 mm), with no significant differences by sex or body mass index. The frequency of V-V recuts was 7 %. The difference in V-V orientation of the tibial component from preoperative was 1.2° (95% confidence interval, 1.7°-0.3°). Conclusions Because the mean maximum cartilage thickness of the tibial plateau is close to 4 mm, a 4-mm correction by using the 10-6-method results in a low recut rate when performing KA TKA. Surgeons using two styli with a 4-mm difference in resection depth (10-6 method) should expect to accurately restore the prearthritic V-V orientation of the proximal tibial while minimizing the need for recuts.

title: Tension-Reducing Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair Using High-Strength Suture Tape in a Suspension Bridge Configuration.
authors: Liu S, Wen H, Dou Z, Ren Y, Feng X, Na Y.
abstract: The maturation of arthroscopic techniques has provided patients with rotator cuff tears a minimally invasive treatment option with favorable outcomes; however, the rate of retear remains high. High-strength suture tape is widely used in procedures such as knee ligament reconstruction and ankle ligament repair, where it enhances the tensile strength during joint motion, thereby reducing the risk of ligament rerupture. In this report, we describe an arthroscopic surgical technique for rotator cuff repair using high-strength suture tape for tension relief. The key steps include passing the high-strength suture tape in a "U-shaped" configuration through the tendon stump, reducing the tendon by securing it with a lateral-row anchor, and then, under nearly "zero tension," using the suture tails from the medial-row anchors to approximate the remaining tendon stump. This technique, by employing high-strength suture tape to reduce the tendon and share the tension load, significantly minimizes the cutting effect of the medial-row anchors on the tendon, thereby lowering the risk of tendon retear and promoting tissue healing.

title: Synovial fluid biomarker changes after acute anterior cruciate ligament injury: comparison with primary osteoarthritis as a biological comparator.
authors: Lan J, Zhao W, Gao X, Lin Y, Huang Z.
abstract: Backgrounds Post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) typically develops 10-20 years after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, but reliable early biomarkers are lacking. We examined synovial fluid biomarker changes in patients with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) and in patients with primary OA. The primary OA group served as a biological comparator representing established degenerative OA, not as a healthy or matched control. Methods Our study included patients from January 1, 2021 to September 30, 2023: 51 with primary OA biological comparator and 53 with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group). Levels of Interleukin (IL)-1β, sulfated glycosaminoglycans (sGAG), aggrecan neoepitope fragment (ARGS-aggrecan), and cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) were measured in synovial fluid and compared between the two groups at baseline and one year later. Patients underwent unilateral knee MRI and bilateral weight-bearing radiography at follow-up. Results The findings demonstrated that synovial fluid from acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) and primary OA biological comparator contained inflammatory mediators, collagen markers, and aging-related indicators such as CRP. Following one year of surgical follow-up, PCT, GAG, CTxI, osteocalcin, β-aspartate, and COMP all showed significant decreases. Biomarker comparisons between groups revealed that the primary OA biological comparator had significantly lower levels of CRP, GAG, ARGS, BMP2, FGF-10, and ADAM-TS5 than the ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group, while CTX-II showed no discernible difference. The Spearman rank correlation was used to examine synovial fluid biomarker concentrations relative to injury duration. Significant time-dependence was observed for: IL-1b (p = 0.025, Rs=-0.112), GAG (p = 0.011, Rs=-0.265), ARGS aggrecan (p = 0.032, Rs=-0.021), C1,2 C (p = 0.002, Rs=0.665), CTxI (p = 0.025, Rs=0.251), C2C (p = 0.011, Rs=0.055), CPII (p = 0.015, Rs=0.336), Osteocalcin (p = 0.029, Rs=0.114), β-aspartate (p = 0.001, Rs=-0.77), D-Asx (p = 0.0215, Rs=-0.425), MMP-3 (p = 0.0201, Rs=0.356), and WOMAC (p = 0.001, Rs=0.264). Univariate regression analysis demonstrated significant associations of IL-1β and osteocalcin with ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group membership. Multivariate logistic regression revealed significant associations with increased levels of β-aspartate, WOMAC, GAG, IL-1β, and osteocalcin. LASSO regression analysis was employed as an exploratory feature selection method to identify the biomarker panel that best distinguished between the ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group and primary OA biological comparators within this cohort. Among the 20 variables included in the analysis, five demonstrated non-zero coefficients in the LASSO model: WOMAC, GAG, β-aspartate, IL-1β, and osteocalcin. These findings suggest that inflammatory markers, matrix turnover products, and functional status are prominent features differentiating the acute post-injury state from chronic degenerative OA in this dataset. However, given the exploratory nature of this analysis and the lack of external validation, these results should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in independent cohorts. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that patients with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) exhibit distinct synovial fluid molecular signatures compared with a primary OA biological comparator. These signatures encompass acute inflammatory responses and early matrix remodeling. However, this study cannot explain why only approximately 18.8% of ACL-injured patients later develop PTOA. Future longitudinal studies including ACL-injured non-progressors and age-, sex-, and activity-matched controls are required.

title: Surgical Intervention for Small Osteochondral Lesions (<1 cm): Proceedings of the International Consensus Meeting on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
authors: Tham A, Rubin J, Butler JJ, Kennedy JG, Hannon CP, Bayer S, Murawski CD, Canata GL, Clanton TO, Haverkamp D, Woo Lee J, O'Malley M, Yinghui H, Stone JW, International Society for Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
abstract: BackgroundEvidence guiding best practices in ankle cartilage repair remains limited and of poor quality. To address this, an international expert group convened to establish consensus opinions on key topics, focusing here on the treatment of small osteochondral lesions, defined as less than 1 cm.MethodsExperts from 25 countries participated in a structured Delphi-based consensus process. Blinded surveys, structured questionnaires, and in-person discussions were used to develop and refine statements, supported by literature review and graded evidence (A1-E). Consensus strength was defined as consensus (51%-74%), strong consensus (75%-99%), or unanimous (100%).ResultsFourteen of 15 proposed statements achieved consensus, including 13 with ≥86% agreement. Bone marrow stimulation (BMS) was recommended for full-thickness osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLTs) that failed conservative therapy, ideally 2 in area, with poorer outcomes expected in larger lesions. Experts emphasized thorough debridement to stable margins, careful subchondral perforation, and the potential value of biologic augmentation such as platelet-rich plasma or concentrated bone marrow aspirate. Repeat BMS was considered a limited option with inferior outcomes compared with primary procedures or salvage techniques.ConclusionsThis international consensus provides standardized guidance for the indications, technique, and biologic augmentation of BMS in the management of OLT. The recommendations redefine lesion size thresholds and clarify the restricted role of revision BMS, offering a global reference framework for clinical practice and future research.

title: Stock-level volatility forecasting using machine learning: A comparative study of GARCH, Random Forest, LSTM, and GRU on US Equities.
authors: Pragadeeshwaran RV, Tarun Narayanan R, Bhavadharini RM.
abstract: Forecasting stock price volatility at the individual stock level is a major challenge in managing financial risks; it has widespread implications for portfolio strategies, pricing derivatives, and assessing regulatory capital adequacy. Although there have been a number of studies using market indices (e.g., VIX and associated methods) to study forecasting stock market volatility, relatively few studies have applied and evaluated a number of different types of machine learning methods to individual stock data in terms of actual (realised) volatility forecasting. This study fills that gap by presenting a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between stock price volatility and various machine learning techniques on a sample of ten well-known US stocks (across three sectors: technology, finance, and energy) based on data from January 2018 to December 2024 (1,759 trading days). We apply five modelling approaches: a classical GARCH(1,1) econometric model, a classical GJR-GARCH(1,1,1) econometric model, a Random Forest regressor, a two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and a two-layer Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network. For each of the four modelling techniques, we use a rolling 5-day annualised actual (realised) volatility forecast as our final outcomes. Evaluation of the prediction results of each of these models was measured using RMSE, MAE, QLIKE loss, parametric Value-at-Risk (VaR) measures, Expected Shortfall (ES), and the Kupiec backtest. We also performed an analysis of the prevailing market regime through K-Means clustering, created an ablation study using variables as features in the models to assess the importance of those variables, and developed a computational efficiency benchmark for each model. In terms of predicted errors, Random Forest was proven to yield very low predicted error (mean RMSE = 0.0892) in comparison to deep learning methods, plus Random Forest was able to be trained approximately 7 times faster than deep learning methods. GRU was ranked second and outperformed LSTM on most of the metrics used in this evaluation. GARCH models remain a viable option for estimating risk measures and calibrating VaR, especially during period of stability in the financial markets.

title: State-dependent crossover between subchondral bone density distribution and cartilage thickness in healthy and osteoarthritic knees: a CT-osteoabsorptiometry and 3D-MRI study.
authors: Moriyama S, Tanaka S, Iwasaki K, Dobashi S, Ukishiro K, Ebata T, Sato D, Matsuoka M, Onodera T, Ohkoshi Y, Kondo E, Iwasaki N.
abstract: Objective Subchondral bone density distribution, quantified by CT-osteoabsorptiometry as the medial ratio, reflects mediolateral load. We examined whether it tracks cartilage thickness, whether it outperforms alignment, and whether this differs between healthy and osteoarthritic (OA) knees. Design This retrospective study analyzed 83 OA and 16 non-OA knees. The medial ratio was measured by CT-osteoabsorptiometry, the hip-knee-ankle (HKA) angle radiographically, and cartilage thickness on 3.0-T MRI, as the mediolateral difference and in nine subregions. Results The medial ratio explained the thickness difference no better than HKA (R 2 = 0.21 and 0.24) with no independent association. The relationship reversed with joint state: in non-OA knees a more medial bone-density distribution accompanied thicker medial cartilage (ρ = +0.68), in OA knees thinner cartilage (ρ = -0.17; Fisher z P = .001). The reversal held against varus knees alone (P = .004) and was absent for alignment (P = .090). Regionally, the medial ratio correlated with thickness in only two subregions, mid-central and mid-external (ρ = -0.40 and - 0.38, Bonferroni-corrected P Conclusions The bone density-cartilage association was positive in healthy knees and negative in OA knees, a reversal not seen for alignment. Within varus knees the medial ratio was related to cartilage thickness in two subregions of the medial plateau, where alignment and compartment-level measures were not. It may therefore be a useful indicator of the state of the joint and of the regional distribution of cartilage loss within it.

title: Soil texture and depth differentially regulate total and available nutrient stoichiometry in Yilong Lake basin agroecosystem, China.
authors: Lai Y, Zhao L, Zhang C, Du Z, Wang Y, Pu T, Liu C, Duan C.
abstract: The stoichiometric ratios of soil available nutrients serve as a pivotal indicator for assessing the sustainability of farmland and nutrient cycling efficiency within fragile ecosystems. Soil texture and depth are significant factors influencing nutrient availability, however, their regulatory mechanisms within highland lakeshore agricultural systems remain poorly understood. This study, conducted in the Yilong Lake watershed of the low-latitude plateau in southwest China, collected 216 soil samples. It innovatively determined both total organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus (SOC, TN, TP) and available carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus (DOC, AN, AP) simultaneously. Path analysis was employed to examine the direct and indirect associations between soil texture (Clay, Loam, Clay Loam, Sand) and depth (0-20 cm, 20-40 cm, 40-60 cm) on nutrient ratio measurements. Findings indicate: (1) Distinct nutrient limitation and leaching risk patterns emerged across soil textures: Loam exhibited strongest carbon and nitrogen sequestration capacity; Although Clay Loam exhibits reduced phosphorus availability due to iron and aluminium oxide immobilisation, it demonstrates pronounced nitrogen limitation rather than phosphorus limitation; Sand though rich in available phosphorus, had the lowest C:N, suggesting heightened carbon and nitrogen leaching risks. (2) Soil depth significantly altered nutrient ratios: topsoil (0-20 cm) showed marked nutrient enrichment, while subsoil (40-60 cm) exhibited elevated TN:TP, suggesting that nitrification may have intensified with increasing depth. (3) Path analysis revealed that texture directly regulates nutrient measurement ratios (DOC:AN) and indirectly governs C:N:P balance by influencing SOC, AP, and AN content; depth directly or indirectly affects measurement relationships through pathways such as TP. This study elucidates the key regulatory roles of soil texture and depth in nutrient ratios, particularly available nutrient balance, providing direct scientific evidence for implementing differentiated, precision nutrient management based on soil physical properties in Yilong Lake basin agroecosystems and other ecologically fragile areas.

title: Short pectus bars with ventral hinge-point stabilization: clinical outcomes in 160 patients.
authors: Weinhandl AC, Schmid W, Rebhandl W.
abstract: Background 'Minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum' (MIRPE) was introduced by Donald Nuss in 1998. Numerous modifications have since been proposed to minimize dislocation of the implanted bar(s). Progress was made by utilizing shorter bars, but the underlying biomechanics have remained somewhat unclear. At our center, we routinely use multiple short bars in modular/flexible (as opposed to closed/rigid) constructs with medial unilateral stabilizers, intended to provide freedom both laterally and between bars. Methods Having used MIRPE since 2001, we settled for the current approach in 2019. In most cases, we use two or three short bars in parallel, crossed, or "XI" configurations, the latter adding a third bar cranial to the cross. Each bar is inserted through the same retrosternal tunnel and fitted unilaterally with one ventral stabilizer near the thoracic entry point, coinciding with the hinge point of bar rotation. Given no bridging, or additional suturing for fixation, each of the bars in this retrospective series was mechanically independent. Results From 07/2019 to 02/2026, this approach was used in 160 consecutive patients. Median age was 16 (IQR: 14-20) years at the time of surgery. Revision due to clinically relevant bar migration was needed in 3 patients (1.88%). Two of these belonged to the minority of 41 adults (≥20 years by WHO criteria), one being a 15-year-old with challenging requirements. Stratified by age groups, the aforementioned rate would translate into 4.88% for adults and 0.84% for children/adolescents. No cases (0%) of bar 'flipping' have been observed (exact upper 95% confidence limit: 2.28%). Conclusions While fully acknowledging patient-based analysis as the standard, no bar flipping has been seen in 356 mechanically independent, short pectus bars with ventral hinge-point stabilization. Three bars had to be revised due to clinically relevant migration. Comparative studies are needed to determine any advantages that this biomechanical concept may hold over other stabilization strategies.

title: Serial ultrasound assessment of flexor carpi ulnaris and biceps brachii cross-sectional area in critically ill patients: A prospective cohort study.
authors: Aoki K, Kasai F, Komaba K, Saito J, Yoshikawa A, Tashiro N, Inoue H, Uchibori K, Fukazawa M.
abstract: Background Serial ultrasound measurements may help characterize muscle wasting in critically ill patients. The flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU) is a superficial forearm muscle that may provide an additional assessment site. We described longitudinal FCU and biceps brachii (BB) cross-sectional area (CSA) changes and explored between-muscle differences and clinical associations. Methods This prospective two-center observational study enrolled 23 intensive care unit (ICU) patients; 20 were included in the analysis (median age, 57 years; range, 33-82). CSA was measured on days 0, 5, 7, and 14 after ICU admission. Analyses used Friedman tests, exact conditional Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction, and exploratory Spearman correlations. Post hoc between-muscle comparisons assessed participant-level percentage changes. Results Mean FCU CSA decreased from 1.36 to 1.08 cm² and mean BB CSA from 6.08 to 5.09 cm² over 14 days, corresponding to reductions of 20.9% and 16.4% in the unrounded group means. The median paired difference in percentage change (FCU minus BB) was -11.9 percentage points on day 7 (unadjusted p = 0.0023), meeting the Bonferroni threshold of 0.05/3. Differences on days 5 and 14 did not meet this threshold (p = 0.1429 and p = 0.2024). Baseline CSA values were correlated (ρ = 0.845, p Conclusions Serial ultrasound documented decreases in FCU and BB CSA in this small cohort, with an exploratory direct comparison identifying a greater proportional FCU decrease on day 7. These findings support further evaluation of FCU ultrasound as an additional muscle-monitoring measure. Its value for earlier detection of muscle wasting or diagnosis of ICU-acquired weakness requires direct validation.

title: SalientNet: mechanistic and reliable saliency maps for medical image classification via unsupervised learning.
journal: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
authors: Sekar S, Akash Guna RT, González Ballester MA, Sikha OK.
abstract: Purpose Interpreting neural network decisions is crucial in healthcare, where both global and local validations are essential for building trust. While saliency maps offer intuitive visualizations of model attention, their limitations-including low sensitivity to input perturbations, lack of causal grounding, and limited mechanistic insight-reduce their reliability in critical medical scenarios. This study aims to develop a more trustworthy and mechanistically interpretable framework for explaining convolutional neural network (CNN) decisions in medical image classification. Methods We propose SalientNet, a data- and architecture-agnostic unsupervised neural network framework for interpreting CNNs. SalientNet consists of two jointly trained components: a CNN examiner, which uses a novel variable channel convolution (VCC) module to extract architecture-independent information from a CNN's intermediate feature maps, and an attribution map generator, built from two coupled U-Nets, which combines this information with the input image to produce a saliency map. Training requires no ground-truth saliency annotations; instead, an Interpretation Loss enforces that the attribution map retains just enough information for a frozen classifier to reproduce its original prediction within a controlled tolerance (dissimilarity temperature), preventing both trivial and overly aggressive masks. We evaluated SalientNet on three medical imaging datasets spanning different modalities and body regions-BreakHis (histopathology), Brain MRI ND5, and FracAtlas (musculoskeletal X-rays)-using ResNet-18, MobileNetV3-Small, and EfficientNet-B0 as the interpreted classifiers. Results Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that SalientNet outperforms popular saliency-based benchmarks, including Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, and LIME, achieving substantially higher faithfulness (Win %) and lower prediction Drop (%) across nearly all dataset-architecture combinations, while keeping spurious confidence increases (Inc %) comparably low. On FracAtlas, SalientNet's explanations also showed strong spatial correlation with fracture regions annotated by medical practitioners, with a mean ground-truth active fraction of up to 0.96 for ResNet-18. A mechanistic analysis further shows that nearly all CNN layers contribute meaningfully to SalientNet's explanations, supporting its interpretive fidelity. Conclusion Our unsupervised framework provides improved interpretability for CNNs in healthcare applications, offering a more reliable and mechanistically grounded alternative to traditional saliency methods for local validation and building trust in AI-assisted medical diagnosis. Our implementation is publicly available https://github.com/S-iddhaarth/Unsupervised-Training-of-an-Interpretable-Neural-Network-to-Explain-Convolutional-Neural-Networks here.

title: Robot-assisted minimally invasive versus conventional open transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion for lumbar degenerative disease: a prospective randomized controlled trial.
authors: Wang P, Shen Z, Ni L, Xu G, Yuan H, Mao Y, Xiao J, Xu W.
abstract: Robotic guidance may improve pedicle screw placement during minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (MIS-TLIF), but its clinical value remains uncertain. In this prospective, single-center, assessor-blinded trial, 128 patients were randomly assigned in a prespecified 1:3 ratio to robot-assisted MIS-TLIF (n = 32) or conventional fluoroscopy-guided open TLIF (n = 96) using an independent statistician's computer-generated sequence. The primary outcome was the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) at 2 weeks. Technical, perioperative, and radiographic outcomes were assessed through 18 months; later assessments were exploratory.At 2 weeks, ODI favored robotic assistance (28.25 ± 6.64 vs 31.52 ± 6.55; mean difference, -3.27; 95% confidence interval, -5.98 to -0.56; P = 0.019), but was below the 10-point sample-size target and nonsignificant at 3 months. Robotic assistance favored grade A screw placement (98.9% vs 94.5%; P = 0.037) and reduced intraoperative adjustment (2.8% vs 7.3%; P = 0.030); facet joint violation and reoperation did not differ significantly. Operative time was longer, whereas blood loss, ambulation, drain removal, and hospital stay favored robotic assistance. Fusion rates and adjacent-segment disc height were similar. Multifidus cross-sectional area was greater with robotic assistance at 12 and 18 months in patients with evaluable imaging. Robot-assisted MIS-TLIF was associated with earlier recovery, higher screw accuracy, and greater postoperative multifidus cross-sectional area, but longer operative time without demonstrated mid-term clinical or fusion benefits. Larger multicenter trials are warranted. Trial Registration:Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400082553.

title: Rip current detection in nearshore areas through UAV video analysis using optical flow and almost local-isometric embedding techniques on the sphere.
authors: Yang K, Leatherman SB, Sun A.
abstract: Rip currents cause most surf-beach lifeguard rescues and most beach drowning incidents, yet automated detection relies on costly instrumentation that scales poorly across the many beaches that lack lifeguards. We propose an end-to-end pipeline producing pixel-level rip-current likelihood maps directly from raw unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video without manual ground-control points - to our knowledge the first to do so from uncalibrated drone video, prior automated approaches operating at video-clip granularity or requiring surveyed camera installations. The pipeline composes (i) dense optical-flow estimation with five classical algorithm variants; (ii) a sphere-aware projection mapping pixel coordinates to local-isometric ground coordinates, with a tilt-aware Jacobian correction of per-pixel velocity; (iii) a CNN six-class scene parser (sky/sea/land/foam/structure/void), trained on frames verified by dense pixel-matching to contain no extraction from either evaluation video; (iv) a per-pixel temporal accumulator flagging pixels whose flow direction agrees with the locally-estimated offshore direction within ±90∘ - the physical boundary of seaward-directed flow, shown robust in an 18-scene sensitivity sweep; and (v) post-processing by Gaussian smoothing (σ=25 px) and a normalized cross-algorithm ensemble. We evaluate on two UAV-captured rip-current videos at Palm Beach and Haulover Park, Florida, annotated by consensus among three coastal-science domain experts. At the physically-neutral T=90∘ default the framework attains precision-recall AUC 0.636 at Palm Beach and 0.660 at Haulover; per-scene selection - of the angular tolerance, ensemble membership, mixing weight, sphere tilt, and which modules are engaged - against the same expert annotation used for evaluation raises these to 0.7066 and 0.7040, reported as an optimistic upper bound rather than an expected-performance estimate. We release the source code, the trained sea-mask refiner, a YOLOv8m-seg deep-learning baseline, and the evaluation scripts. Evaluation is limited to these two expert-annotated scenes, and the method requires visible surface tracers (foam, dye, or sediment fronts) advected by the current.

title: Return to Sport After Foot and Ankle Surgery Is Inconsistently Defined and Assessed: A Systematic Review.
authors: Oikonomou K, Savsani K, Wyatt P, Cyrus J, Ernst B, Anastasio AT, O'Neill CN, Goodloe JB, Amendola A.
abstract: Purpose To conduct a systematic review of return-to-sport (RTS) definitions in the orthopaedic literature, addressing common operative athletic foot and ankle pathologies including ankle instability, Achilles tendon ruptures or tendinopathy, and fifth metatarsal fractures. Methods A systematic review was performed in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Cochrane, Embase, Medline, and CINAHL databases were searched for studies published through March 2024. Inclusion criteria were studies in which subjects were involved in some level of sports and received surgery for 1 of 3 common sports-related injuries: ankle instability, Achilles tendinopathy, and fifth metatarsal fracture. The primary outcome was each study's definition of RTS. Results There were 145 articles that met all inclusion criteria. Of these, 73 articles investigated ankle instability, 56 investigated Achilles tendinopathy, and 16 investigated fifth metatarsal fracture. Seventy-nine articles (54.5%) had an unclear definition of RTS with 66 articles (45.5%) reporting a precise definition. Sixty-four articles (44.1%) provided an isolated binary metric reporting whether a patient returned to sport or failed to provide a method for determining the timepoint for RTS. Thirty-eight (26.2%) of the articles used an objective start criterion (e.g., resumption of competition), followed by custom (n = 27, 18.6%) and standardized patient-reported questionnaire use (n = 21, 14.5%). Conclusions Most articles included in this systematic review did not provide an explicit definition of RTS or a clearly defined assessment methodology. When specified, RTS was assessed using objective events, custom questionnaires, or standardized patient-reported outcome measures, highlighting substantial heterogeneity in both RTS definitions and assessment approaches across foot and ankle literature. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level I to IV studies.

title: Research on the impact of transceiver isolation of GB-SAR on imaging quality.
authors: Hou S, Yang X, Deng K.
abstract: Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GB-SAR) systems frequently suffer from insufficient transceiver isolation due to their compact architecture. This insufficiency leads to transmitted signal leakage into the receiving channel, generating third-order intermodulation distortion (IM3). Consequently, the imaging signal to noise ratio (SNR) is degraded and artifacts in the range direction are introduced. Utilizing an independently developed Ku-band GB-SAR system termed S-SAR M, this study explores the influence mechanism of transceiver isolation on imaging quality through dynamic adjustment of antenna spatial parameters. It identifies a system-specific critical isolation threshold and an optimal design range, thereby offering a theoretical basis and practical guidelines for hardware optimization of GB-SAR systems. The isolation model is quantitatively calibrated against the measured horn radiation pattern and antenna geometry with a root-mean-square error of 1.8 dB, and the critical threshold is derived analytically from receiver nonlinearity parameters through the third-order input intercept point (IIP3). The results indicate that antenna angle is the dominant factor for isolation improvement, with an average enhancement of 56.3 percent achieved as the angle increases from 0 to 60 degrees. Antenna separation exhibits a synergistic effect on isolation at larger angles. A critical isolation threshold of 74 dB is established to suppress range artifacts induced by IM3 in the S-SAR M system; below this threshold, artifacts consistently occur. Moreover, a tri-segmented nonlinear relationship between isolation and SNR is observed, with an optimal balance region located between 74 dB and 80 dB where the peak SNR is maintained. One-way analysis of variance delivers a result with p less than 0.001 and confirms the significance of these trends. A quantitative artifact-to-background energy ratio further corroborates the visual artifact classification. These findings offer important insights for enhancing the performance of GB-SAR systems. It should be noted that the reported numerical thresholds are specific to the S-SAR M hardware configuration; a normalized isolation-margin framework is therefore provided to transfer the methodology, with platform-specific calibration, to GB-SAR systems using other frequency bands or receiver architectures.

title: Repeated-sprint performance in combined heat and hypoxia: Current evidence.
authors: Yamaguchi K, Goto K.
abstract: While the efficacy of repeated-sprint training in hypoxia (RSH) for enhancing performance is widely recognized, repeated-sprint training in combined heat and hypoxia (RSH+H) has recently attracted attention as a potential extension of conventional RSH. The present review summarizes acute performance and physiological responses to repeated-sprint exercise in combined heat and hypoxia (H+H). Unlike endurance performance, repeated-sprint performance appears to be preserved during H+H exposure in the absence of hyperthermia. Notably, the H+H condition may also modify physiological responses associated with RSH, including muscle oxygenation and anaerobic energy production. However, findings remain inconsistent across studies, and it is currently unclear whether these acute responses translate into greater training adaptations or performance gains than those achieved with RSH alone. The available evidence is further limited by the small number of studies, the predominance of acute experimental designs, and the lack of diverse participants. Overall, RSH+H should be regarded as an emerging strategy that warrants further investigation, particularly with respect to long-term training adaptations and optimal combinations of heat and hypoxia.

title: Preoperative coronal tibiofemoral subluxation does not affect 2-year outcomes after mobile-bearing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for anteromedial osteoarthritis.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Kinoshita T, Bunyoz KI, Mortensen KRL, Bredgaard Jensen C, Price A, Gromov K, Troelsen A.
abstract: Introduction Coronal tibiofemoral subluxation (CTFS) is frequently observed in patients with medial knee osteoarthritis; however, its clinical relevance and the acceptable degree of CTFS when considering unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) remain unclear. This study aimed to determine whether preoperative CTFS influences short-term postoperative clinical outcomes in patients with anteromedial osteoarthritis (AMOA) undergoing medial UKA. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, 457 consecutive knees with AMOA who underwent mobile-bearing UKA performed at a single center between August 2016 and May 2023 were analyzed. CTFS, defined as medial translation of the femur relative to the tibia, was measured on preoperative weight-bearing anteroposterior radiographs and expressed as the percentage of tibial plateau width. Patients were categorized into mild (0-5%), moderate (≥ 5% to Results At 2 years, mean OKS improvements were 16.6 ± 8.9, 14.8 ± 8.3, and 16.0 ± 9.3 in the mild, moderate, and severe CTFS groups, respectively. Adjusted mean differences between groups were small, with confidence intervals including zero. The severe CTFS group demonstrated greater joint line convergence angle than the mild and moderate groups (both p Conclusions Preoperative CTFS was not associated with worse outcomes in mobile-bearing UKA for AMOA with correctable deformity. Within the setting of correctable deformity and appropriate patient selection, preoperative CTFS was not associated with inferior 2-year outcomes. Longer-term survivorship and radiographic progression analyses are warranted.

title: Predictors of improvement in distance presenting visual acuity after refraction and reading rehabilitation at ≤ 1.5 M print size in older adults with low vision.
authors: Cabal DM, Ferreira MM, Antunes-Foschini R.
abstract: Background This study aimed to identify factors associated with improvement in distance presenting visual acuity (dpVA) after refraction and with successful reading rehabilitation among patients aged 50 years or older with low vision. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study using medical records from a low-vision rehabilitation center in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo, Brazil, between 2009 and 2019. Improvement after refraction was defined as a gain of at least two 0.2 logMAR after manifest refraction for distance correction. Successful reading rehabilitation using spectacles and/or magnifiers was defined as the ability to read texts of 1.5 M or smaller. Candidate predictors included age, sex, dpVA, distance best-corrected visual acuity, anatomical region responsible for low vision, educational level, spherical equivalent, and cylinder power. Logistic regression was performed, with statistical significance set at p Results Overall, 558 patients were included, with a mean age of 67 years. Retinal involvement was the most frequent anatomical finding. Improvement in dpVA after refraction occurred in 20.3% of patients, and dpVA and spherical equivalent were significant predictors of this outcome. Among 346 literate patients, 252 (72.8%) were able to read 1.5 M texts after rehabilitation. Successful reading rehabilitation was associated with better distance best-corrected visual acuity, retinal involvement, higher educational level, and female sex, whereas older age and worse distance best-corrected visual acuity were associated with lower odds of success. Conclusions Clinical, refractive, and demographic factors were associated with dpVA improvement after refraction and successful reading rehabilitation in older adults with low vision.

title: Pre-Implantation Kidney Biopsy: Assessing Safety in Transplant Outcomes.
authors: Pimenta AC, Fernandes BP, Esteves A, Fragoso P, Leal R, Guedes Marques M, Santos L, Romãozinho C, Figueiredo A, Alves R, Sá H, Rodrigues L.
abstract: Background Pre-implantation kidney biopsy is commonly used to guide deceased donor organ allocation, despite ongoing controversy regarding its predictive value and potential impact on recipient outcomes. Evidence addressing the safety of this procedure from the recipient's perspective remains limited. Methods We performed a cross-sectional retrospective study including adult recipients of single deceased-donor renal transplant at Coimbra Local Health Unit between January 2020 and December 2022. Recipients were stratified according to whether the graft underwent pre-implantation biopsy (allocation or zero-time) or not. Early postoperative outcomes included transfusion requirements, hemoglobin variation at 48 hours, primary nonfunction, and cold ischemia time. Results Among 257 recipients, 114 (44.4%) received a biopsied graft. Cold ischemia time was slightly longer in biopsied grafts, but not significantly (17.9 vs 16.6 hours; p = .08). Pre-implantation biopsy was not associated with increased transfusion requirements (χ² = 0.475, p = 0.491). In non-transfused recipients, hemoglobin variation at 48 hours was comparable between biopsied and non-biopsied grafts (-21.2% vs -21.1%; p = .990). Rates of primary nonfunction (p = .518) did not differ significantly between groups. Two early postoperative deaths occurred in recipients of biopsied grafts, neither related to the biopsy procedure. Conclusions In our cohort, pre-implantation renal graft biopsy was not associated with worse early postoperative outcomes. These findings support the safety of selectively performed procurement biopsies in kidney transplantation practice.

title: Postoperative residual patellar bone thickness and patellar height in patients with quadriceps tendon rupture after total knee arthroplasty: A retrospective case-control study.
authors: Pellicanò D, Presti ML, Neri MP, Di Prima AM, Rubino S, Zaffagnini S.
abstract: Purpose Quadriceps tendon rupture following total knee arthroplasty is a rare but serious complication. This study aimed to compare postoperative residual patellar bone thickness and patellar height between patients who developed quadriceps tendon rupture after primary total knee arthroplasty and matched controls. Methods A retrospective case-control study included 17 patients who developed quadriceps tendon rupture within 6 months after primary total knee arthroplasty and 100 controls without extensor mechanism complications. Controls were selected using group-level frequency matching for age, sex and body mass index. All patients underwent patellar resurfacing. Patellar height was assessed preoperatively and postoperatively using the Insall-Salvati index, while postoperative residual patellar bone thickness was measured on immediate postoperative lateral radiographs. Group comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum and Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between residual patellar bone thickness and tendon rupture, with adjustment for age, sex and body mass index. Results No significant differences were observed between groups in age, sex, body mass index or diabetes mellitus. Median postoperative residual patellar bone thickness was numerically lower in patients with tendon rupture than in controls (11.3 vs. 11.8 mm), but the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Residual patellar bone thickness was also not significantly associated with tendon rupture after adjustment for age, sex and body mass index (adjusted odds ratio 0.77, 95% confidence interval 0.55-1.08; p = 0.127). No significant differences were observed in preoperative or postoperative Insall-Salvati index or changes in patellar height. Conclusions No significant association was identified between postoperative residual patellar bone thickness, patellar height parameters and quadriceps tendon rupture in this cohort. Given the limited number of rupture cases, smaller or moderate associations cannot be excluded. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Policy-Evidence Misalignment in Commercial Payer Coverage Criteria for Knee Osteochondral Allograft Transplantation.
authors: Amin JS, Sachdev D, Acheampong KK, Richter C, Lemme N, Cole BJ, Yanke AB.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate how major United States commercial insurers justify medical-necessity criteria for knee osteochondral allograft (OCA) transplantation, characterize the level of evidence (LOE) cited within their policies, and assess whether coverage criteria are supported by the cited literature. Methods Four major national commercial insurers with publicly available knee OCA policies were identified, and the most recent policy versions were retrieved. Medical-necessity criteria were extracted, and all cited references applicable to knee OCA were screened, assigned an LOE and publication date, and coded for whether they supported each policy criterion. Coverage stance by lesion site was summarized. Publicly available revision histories were reviewed to compare administrative revision and evidence-refresh cadence. A deidentified institutional dataset of current procedural terminology 27415 authorization requests was reviewed to contextualize findings in real-world coverage outcomes. Results Across the 4 insurers, 40 applicable references were cited: Level V n = 7 (17.5%), Level IV n = 30 (75.0%), and Level III n = 3 (7.5%); Level I and II were 0. One insurer provided no OCA-specific coverage criteria and instead deferred determinations to proprietary criteria not publicly available. Among the remaining 3 insurers, coverage was most permissive for unipolar femoral condyle lesions. Patellar lesions were explicitly excluded by 1 insurer, whereas bipolar and tibial plateau lesions were each excluded by 2 insurers. Among payers with assessable revision histories, administrative revisions occurred more frequently than documented evidence-refresh events. In an institutional dataset of 34 current procedural terminology 27415 requests, 7 (20.6%) were initially denied; all cases with documented outcomes were ultimately approved after escalation. Conclusions Commercial payer knee OCA policies are largely based on older, low-level evidence, and cited literature seldom supports key medical-necessity criteria. Clinical relevance Identifying discrepancies between insurance coverage and clinical evidence may help clinicians advocate more effectively during preauthorization and appeal processes, reduce delays in care, and inform payers' efforts to align coverage criteria with modern outcome data.

title: Peri-Operative Infection Control Measures for Implantation of Sacral Nerve Stimulators (SNS): A Scoping Review.
authors: Wynn J, Hennes D, McLeod K.
abstract: Aims Sacral nerve stimulators (SNS) are used to treat refractory urinary symptoms, bowel symptoms, and pelvic pain. There is a risk of surgical site and implant infection; however, manufacturers have not released guidelines regarding infection prevention during their implantation. There are limited data on the pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative considerations for infection prevention. We present a scoping review detailing the current strategies for infection prevention during implantation of SNS and propose a protocol for perioperative infection control strategies based on current available literature. Methods A scoping review was conducted using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta Analysis (PRISMA). A search strategy using search terms "sacral nerve stimulation," "infection," "infection control," and "infection prevention" was used. A search was conducted on medical databases, and a grey literature search was performed. Results Forty-three articles were included for data extraction, published between 2003 and 2022. A total of 10,401 outcomes were reported. Pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative considerations and outcomes were extracted. Significant peri-operative considerations included the use of pre-operative chlorhexidine wash and the use of shallow pocket depths. There was limited data to support other infection control considerations and variability in practices within the SNS implanting community. Conclusions Despite implant infection being a highly morbid and detrimental outcome for the patient, there is no clear consensus on what infection control measures should be routinely performed to reduce the risk of infection during the implantation process. The peri-operative considerations currently covered in the literature have little reported evidence to support the implementation of certain infection prevention considerations, and it seems their use is primarily driven by surgeon preference.

title: Pelvic Obliquity Impacts Acetabular Coverage Measurements, and the Elevated Hip Is More Frequently Symptomatic in Hip Preservation Patients.
authors: Johnson BT, Lewis DC, Metz AK, Matter AL, Peters CL, Anderson LA, Aoki SK.
abstract: Purpose To quantify the impact of femoral head height discrepancies on pelvic-based versus ground-based measurements for lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) and Tönnis angle and to determine whether these discrepancies affected the clinical presentation of patients who presented to a hip preservation clinic. Methods Consecutive patients who underwent a primary hip arthroscopy between May 2021 and August 2021 and consecutive patients who underwent a primary periacetabular osteotomy between January 2020 and December 2023 with available preoperative standing anteroposterior radiographs were included. Patients were excluded if they (1) had undergone a previous surgery in either hip prior to the primary operation or (2) were less than 18 years of age at the time of surgery. The LCEA to the sourcil edge, LCEA to the bone edge, and Tönnis angle were calculated, referencing off (1) the pelvis and (2) the horizontal to the ground. Differences between measurements were calculated in degrees, and differences in femoral head heights to approximate pelvic obliquity were calculated in millimeters. Comparisons were made via regression analysis. Results Fifty hip arthroscopy patients and 75 periacetabular osteotomy patients were included. Regression analysis showed that LCEA to the sourcil edge was impacted by the difference in femoral head height when comparing the pelvic-based measurement with the ground-based measurement ( B = 0.298; R 2 = 0.775; 95% confidence interval = 0.274-0.322; P Conclusions Differences in femoral head height on standing anteroposterior radiographs impact ground- versus pelvic-based radiographic measurements of acetabular coverage by approximately 0.3° per millimeter of femoral head height difference and may result in functional undercoverage of the elevated hip. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective case series.

title: Organ Donation-Reaching the Next Generation: To and Through High School.
authors: Herrmann CS, Ters ME.
abstract: Introduction Current transplant rates meet only 10% of the global demand, and the quintessential reason is the lack of donors. The same holds for blood donations, with the number of younger donors increasingly declining. Objective This project tested the hypothesis that awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels of blood, organ, and bone marrow (BM) donation are low among high school students but can be raised through education. Methods A pre-/post-comparative cohort study was conducted using a 59-item electronic questionnaire administered to students in grades 9, 10, and 11 in a single high school between November 2025 and January 2026 before and after a 10-minute presentation in high school classrooms. Results A total of 112 students participated (59% females, age 14-17). Awareness level (5-point scale from 1 (very aware) to 5 (not aware)) was moderate-high for organ and blood donation and moderate for BM (median (IQR) 2 (1-3), 2 (1-2) and 3 (2-4), respectively). Notable increases in knowledge pertained to the number of patients on the transplant list (from 55% pre to 83% post, P Conclusions Dedicated peer-to-peer initiatives can raise awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels for blood, organ, and BM donation among high schoolers.

title: Operative Treatment of Quadrimalleolar and Quadrimalleolar-Equivalent Ankle Fractures: Radiographic and Clinical Outcomes Following Component-Based Operative Fixation.
authors: Nam JH, Kim HS, Yeo ED, Lee SH, Jung KJ, Hong CH, Won SH, Kim WJ.
abstract: Background Quadrimalleolar (QM) and quadrimalleolar-equivalent (QME) fractures expand the trimalleolar concept by adding an anterior osseous syndesmotic component (Chaput or Wagstaffe fragment). Outcomes after operative fixation remain incompletely defined. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 36 consecutive patients (18 QM, 18 QME) who underwent open reduction and internal fixation between April 2019 and December 2024, with a minimum 12-month follow-up. All patients underwent a component-based operative treatment strategy comprising preoperative computed tomographic (CT) characterization of each malleolar and syndesmotic component, morphology-based management of anterior fragments, and intraoperative arthroscopic assessment of residual instability. Syndesmotic reduction was assessed on bilateral CT 1 cm proximal to the plafond using direct anterior and posterior differences, fibular translation, and fibular rotation, referenced to the contralateral ankle. Clinical outcomes included Olerud-Molander Ankle Score (OMAS) and visual analog scale (VAS). Results Baseline demographics did not differ significantly between groups. QME injuries were predominantly SER (supination-external rotation) type IV/Weber B (94.4%), whereas QM showed an even distribution between SER and PER (pronation-external rotation) and between Weber B and C ( P = .01). No significant side-to-side differences were observed in any of the 4 parameters in either group at 1 year (all P > .05); given the limited sample size, these nonsignificant findings may be subject to a type II error. Intra- and interobserver reliabilities were excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.901-0.988). Mean OMAS improved to 86.1 ± 6.8 (QM) and 85.3 ± 5.7 (QME); VAS decreased to 1.0 ± 0.7 in both (within-group P P = .82). All fractures united; 3 minor wound complications resolved with local care. Conclusion A component-based operative treatment strategy was safe and associated with maintained anatomic distal tibiofibular alignment and favorable short-term outcomes in both QM and QME. The absence of a control group precludes conclusions on clinical necessity or superiority, and combined evaluation of these biomechanically distinct patterns should be interpreted with caution. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective comparative case series.

title: Numerical study on biomechanical analysis of human lumbar spine in daily activities.
authors: Qin B, Zhou L, Zhang X, Liu Y, Qian Z, Zhu Q.
abstract: The aim of this study was to establish and apply a framework that combines musculoskeletal modeling with motion capture data to investigate the biomechanics of the human lumbar musculoskeletal system during daily activities. By combining musculoskeletal modeling with motion capture data and performing inverse dynamics analysis, we quantified the compressive and shear forces on the lumbar intervertebral disc (IVD), total muscle force, muscle activation, and ligament forces during six daily activities (slow walking, walking, fast walking, sweeping the floor, washing windows, and standing on one foot). Our results showed that the mechanical loading on the lumbar IVD, muscles and ligaments increased with the increase of walking speed, and the mechanical loading on most lumbar tissues during sweeping the floor and washing windows was greater than that during walking. The mechanical loading within each tissue (including the lumbar IVD, muscles and ligaments) showed consistent distribution characteristics across different activities. Our study showed that sweeping the floor, washing windows, and increased walking speed resulted in higher mechanical loading on the lumbar IVDs, muscles, and ligaments. Our findings are important for understanding the biomechanics of the lumbar spine during daily activities.

title: Novel bicolumnar fixation with primary cup implantation for pelvic discontinuity in revision hip arthroplasty: a comparative clinical study.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Abul MS, Ağır M, Yılmaz H, Hekim Ö, Sevim ÖF, Tuncay İ.
abstract: Background Pelvic discontinuity is a rare but challenging condition in revision hip arthroplasty. Traditional cage-based reconstruction techniques often rely solely on mechanical fixation and may be associated with implant migration, loosening, and mechanical failure. Alternative strategies aimed at restoring pelvic continuity and achieving biological fixation may improve construct stability and clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective study included 19 patients with intraoperatively confirmed pelvic discontinuity who underwent revision total hip arthroplasty between 2014 and 2024. Patients were divided into three groups according to the reconstruction technique used: Group 1 (n = 8) underwent anti-protrusio cage reconstruction alone, Group 2 (n = 6) received additional anterior quadrilateral surface plating prior to cage implantation, and Group 3 (n = 5) underwent restoration of pelvic continuity through anterior and posterior column fixation followed by implantation of a porous-coated primary acetabular cup. Clinical and radiological outcomes were assessed with a minimum follow-up of 2 years, including complications, loosening, reoperation, and reoperation-free survival. Results Nineteen patients (mean age 71.2 years) with intraoperatively confirmed pelvic discontinuity were included. Aseptic loosening rates differed significantly among the three groups (P = 0.039), occurring in 50% of patients in Group 1 and in none of the patients in Groups 2 or 3. Reoperation rates were higher in Group 1 (75%) than in Group 2 (16.7%) and Group 3 (20%), although this difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.074). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a trend toward lower reoperation-free survival in Group 1; however, differences among the groups were not statistically significant (log-rank P = 0.237). Conclusion Reconstruction strategies involving restoration of pelvic continuity through column stabilization may provide improved mechanical stability and lower complication rates compared with conventional cage-only techniques in the management of pelvic discontinuity. In selected patients, bicolumnar fixation followed by implantation of a porous-coated primary acetabular cup may offer the additional advantage of biological fixation. Larger prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

title: Neurosurgery in Costa Rica: historical evolution and contemporary state.
authors: Acuña-Quirós M, Yeh-Hsieh TY, Freiman TM, Geßler F, Hernández-Durán S.
abstract: Background The development of neurosurgery in Central America has been shaped by the gradual expansion of public healthcare systems, academic medical training, and international collaboration. Costa Rica represents a distinctive case within Latin America due to its universal healthcare model and centralized hospital network. This study aims to describe the origins, institutional development, and contemporary status of neurosurgery in Costa Rica within the broader context of Latin American neurosurgical history. Methods This is a historical and descriptive narrative review, not a systematic review; no protocol was registered. Sources included institutional reports and archives from the Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social and the University of Costa Rica, national and international public-health statistics, English- and Spanish-language peer-reviewed literature, and biographical and historiographic material. Results The emergence of neurosurgery in Costa Rica occurred during the mid-twentieth century alongside the expansion of the national public healthcare system. Early neurosurgical procedures were initially performed by general surgeons until the return of internationally trained physicians established dedicated neurosurgical services. During the 1960s and 1970s, neurosurgical departments were established in the country's principal tertiary hospitals. Today, approximately 54 neurosurgeons provide care to a population of over five million inhabitants through a centralized national referral network. Modern practice incorporates advanced technologies such as neuronavigation and intraoperative neuromonitoring. Nevertheless, challenges persist, including workforce limitations, growing demand for neurosurgical care, and the absence of domestic subspecialty training programs and academic output. Conclusion The history of neurosurgery in Costa Rica illustrates how specialized surgical disciplines can emerge within a small but highly organized healthcare system through academic development and international collaboration. Continued investment in training, infrastructure, and global partnerships will be essential to address current challenges and support the future growth of neurosurgery in the country.

title: Medial-lateral posterior tibial slope asymmetry is associated with the presence of medial meniscus posterior root tear.
authors: Harada K, Mori Y, Abe T, Aki T, Kamimura M, Ogasawara M, Ito K, Aizawa T.
abstract: Background Posterior tibial slope (PTS) has been identified as an important anatomical risk factor for medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT). However, prior studies have primarily focused on the medial slope. The primary aim of this study was to measure medial and lateral PTS on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and to determine whether medial-lateral slope asymmetry is associated with MMPRT. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included patients aged 50-75 years who underwent knee MRI for knee pain at two institutions. Patients with osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4) were excluded. MMPRT was diagnosed on MRI. The medial PTS (MPTS), lateral PTS (LPTS), medial proximal tibial angle (MPTA), and lateral distal femoral angle (LDFA) were measured, and ΔPTS was defined as MPTS - LPTS. Groups were compared before and after 1:1 propensity score (PS) matching for age, sex, and body mass index. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were conducted to evaluate the association and discriminative ability of ΔPTS. Results A total of 120 knees were included, of which 26 (21.7%) demonstrated MMPRT. MPTS did not differ significantly between groups, whereas the MMPRT group showed a significantly smaller LPTS (p Conclusions Knees with MMPRT exhibited a smaller LPTS and greater ΔPTS compared with knees without MMPRT, which remained significant after PS matching. ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminative performance, and a ΔPTS of 4.0° or greater may serve as an exploratory threshold. PTS asymmetry may represent a morphological factor associated with MMPRT. Level of evidence iii

title: Long-term market value after meniscal injury in professional football players largely follows expected career trajectories: A matched cohort study.
authors: D'Ambrosi R, Conteduca J, Mei A, Sorrentino M, Cordani C, Fink C, Baumert P.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate long-term changes in market value following meniscal injury in professional football players compared with matched players without meniscal injury and identify characteristics associated with postinjury market value. Methods This retrospective cohort study analysed 80 meniscal injury episodes (74 players) recorded in Transfermarkt between 2006 and 2024. Market value was assessed during the preinjury season, injury year and annually for five subsequent years. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal changes and associations with age, playing position and competitive level. Injury episodes identifiable in an openly available Transfermarkt-derived database were matched (1:2) to controls without recorded meniscal injury by position, competitive level, calendar year, age and preinjury market value. Covariate balance was assessed using standardised mean differences (SMDs), and trajectories were compared between groups. Results Mean age at injury was 25.05 ± 4.36 years, and mean absence was 103.87 ± 93.48 days. Market value increased at one (+25.61%; p = 0.023) and 2 years (+26.82%; p = 0.019) compared with preinjury values, before declining by 31.56% at 5 years ( p = 0.001). Older age and lower competitive level were independently associated with lower market value. Among 64 matched injury episodes and 128 controls (all SMDs p = 0.30). Sensitivity analyses showed no significant additional decline among injured players. Conclusion Meniscal injuries were not associated with an immediate reduction in market value among professional football players. The long-term decline in market value did not differ significantly from that of matched players without meniscal injury and appeared largely to reflect the expected age-related evolution of player value; however, given the width of the confidence intervals and the absence of clinical detail, a moderate injury-related effect cannot be excluded. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Limb preservation and optimization: A whole-patient approach to comprehensive care after catastrophic extremity injuries.
authors: Cook JL, Rucinski K, Nuelle JAV, Royse LA, London DA, Lalonde SP, Schweser KM, Crist BD.
abstract: Introduction The objective of this study was to describe the Limb Preservation and Optimization Center's (LPOC) components and mechanisms in treating catastrophic extremity injuries and report the initial patient demographics, indications, and outcomes using data from an established registry. Methods A retrospective observational study was performed including all patients entered in the LPOC registry since January 1, 2014. Patient demographics, injury types and treatments, and outcomes, including functional outcomes. Descriptive statistics were calculated to determine proportions, means, standard deviations, and ranges. Results 992 patients were included with a mean final follow-up of 20.5 months (SD:22.1, range 0-114); 178 (17.9%) underwent an amputation. Of those who reported RTW, 164 patients (71.6%) reporting RTW at full capacity. Lower extremity injuries were most common (74.9%). Demographic, health insurance, living setting, and presentation variables were similar among LPOC patients. Fractures and soft tissue injuries predominated across all injury categories with fracture fixation and wound coverage treatments most common. Upper extremity joint injuries and all types of combined injuries were associated with the highest reoperation rates. Treatment failure rates ranged from 11% to 100% with fracture and bone-related injuries being associated with the most favorable outcomes across categories. Discussion Fractures and soft tissue injuries were the primary types of problems affecting all patients utilizing the LPOC. Fracture fixation and wound coverage treatments were the most performed procedures. Return to the operating room to address the limb preservation and optimization goal was extremely common across categories such that patients may expect at least 4 reoperations. Patients return to some type of work 75-88%. Treatment failure rates varied from 11% to 100%, with fracture and bone-related injuries being associated with the most favorable outcomes across categories. Overall, the results are encouraging and will help shape care in these patients.

title: Letter to Editor: Combined Goldilocks and Lateral Intercostal Artery Perforator (LICAP) flap for Breast Reconstruction.
authors: Schwartz JD.

title: Is Gen AI an editor or a revision tool? A case study of EFL students in AI-assisted revision.
authors: Zhang H, Ai S, Zhang L, Lin Y.
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) tools become increasingly integrated into language education, understanding how learners respond to AI-generated feedback during writing revision has become an important research concern. Existing studies have primarily examined the effects of AI on writing performance, with less attention to learners' reported decision-making and reflection during revision. This qualitative study investigated learner-AI interaction, reported revision practices and learner perceptions among 18 first-year non-English-major students enrolled in a university EFL writing course. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews following a Gen AI-assisted revision task and analysed using thematic analysis. The findings identified three interaction patterns with Gen AI: passive AI reliance, adaptive AI engagement, metacognitive AI engagement. Participants differed in how they evaluated and used AI-generated feedback, including passive acceptance, selective uptake, and critical evaluation. Some reported increased confidence, motivation, and awareness of linguistic form, whereas others expressed concerns about overreliance, authorship, and loss of personal voice. These self-reported experiences provide insight into how EFL learners perceive and manage GenAI-assisted revision, highlighting the need for pedagogical approaches that foster critical AI literacy and reflective learner autonomy.

title: Integrative genomic SEM analysis of shared genetic architecture and candidate genes for insulin resistance-related metabolic traits.
authors: Li S, Liang Y, Zhu G, Wu L, Li H, Li Y, Chen Q.
abstract: Insulin resistance is a complex metabolic state involving impaired insulin sensitivity, compensatory insulin secretion, abnormal lipid metabolism, and altered fat distribution. However, the shared genetic architecture underlying these correlated phenotypes remains incompletely defined. In this study, we applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics of fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct an insulin resistance-related latent genetic factor. SNP-level association analysis was then performed for the latent factor, followed by risk locus annotation, fine-mapping, transcriptome-wide association analysis, gene-level prioritization, enrichment analysis, and exploratory structural biology assessment of selected missense substitutions. The single-factor model showed acceptable but not optimal approximate fit and captured a biologically consistent genetic pattern, with positive loadings for fasting insulin, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio and a negative loading for insulin sensitivity index. The latent factor showed detectable SNP heritability and revealed 3,067 genome-wide significant candidate SNPs, with Q_SNP retained as a complementary SNP-level heterogeneity diagnostic.. Functional annotation identified 100 genomic risk loci and 1,530 FDR-significant genes in MAGMA. Fine-mapping prioritized multiple candidate regions, including loci near PPARG, RSPO3, SLC38A11, SLC39A8, BCL2, GDF5, and SPATA5. TWAS and FOCUS further highlighted candidate genes involved in adipocyte biology, glucose-lipid metabolism, insulin secretion, and expression regulation, including PPARG, MLXIPL, TCF7L2, FAM13A, CCDC92, and SLC22A3. Enrichment analyses suggested that genetic signals associated with the insulin resistance-related latent factor were mainly linked to fat distribution, cardiometabolic traits, adipose tissue, mesenchymal cell lineages, and active regulatory genomic regions. In a separate exploratory analysis, AlphaFold3 modeling, ThermoMPNN prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested structural perturbations for three ultra-rare missense substitutions in nominated candidate proteins: BCL2-W188G, GDF5-C400Y, and RSPO3-C129Y. These substitutions were selected using functional-impact annotations and modeling feasibility, were not GWAS lead or fine-mapped causal variants, and do not establish the mechanisms underlying the GWAS associations. These findings provide an integrated genetic and structural framework for understanding shared mechanisms underlying insulin resistance-related metabolic abnormalities, while emphasizing the need for further experimental validation.

title: Injectable autologous chondrocyte transplantation yields sustained clinical mid-term improvement in acetabular cartilage defects in femoroacetabular impingement: A comparative analysis from the German Cartilage Registry (KnorpelRegister DGOU).
authors: Riedl M, Landgraeber S, Thier S, Zinser W, Zimmerer A, Banke IJ, Steens W, Alt V, Fickert S.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate mid-term outcomes of injectable matrix-associated autologous chondrocyte transplantation (MACT) for acetabular cartilage defects in femoroacetabular impingement (FAI), comparing two different ACT products (NOVOCART® Inject vs. Chondrosphere®) using data from the German Cartilage Registry. Methods This retrospective analysis included 91 FAI patients (mean age 31.5 years) with isolated International Cartilage Repair Society (ICRS) Grade 3 or 4 acetabular cartilage defects treated arthroscopically with either NOVOCART® Inject ( n = 48) or Chondrosphere® ( n = 43), with a mean follow-up of 41.8 ± 18.5 months. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the International Hip Outcome Tool (iHOT33) and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain at 6, 12, 24, 36 and 60 months. Clinically important outcome values (minimum clinically important difference, Patient Acceptable Symptom State, substantial clinical benefit) were calculated at 36 months. Subgroup analysis compared defect severity (ICRS Grade 3 vs. 4) and product-specific outcomes. Results Significant improvement in hip function (iHOT33) was observed across all follow-up time points in both groups ( p p Conclusion Arthroscopic MACT was associated with clinical improvement in pain and function up to 5 years in FAI patients with acetabular cartilage defects, with no statistically significant differences detected between hydrogel-based and spheroid-based products; follow-up data at later time points were more limited for NOVOCART® Inject. Although statistically significant pain improvement over time was observed only in the Chondrosphere® group, no significant differences in pain outcomes between the two products were detected. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Influence of water content and organic matter on the mechanical strength characteristics of municipal sewage sludge.
authors: Yang R, Ma J, Zhang Z, Yin J.
abstract: Municipal sewage sludge typically has high moisture and organic matter contents, which exert a significant influence on mechanical strength, dewatering and resource recovery. Organic soil specimens with varying water contents were prepared by mixing raw sewage sludge (RSS) with dry soil powder (DSP), humus, and quartz sand tailings (QST). Unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests were conducted to investigate the effect of water content on the UCS. Results show that the UCS decreases with normalized water content (w₀/wL) following a power-law relationship, and a quantitative formula is established. Specimens with different organic contents were fabricated by blending DSP into RSS. Unconsolidated undrained triaxial tests were performed to assess strength evolution with organic content. For organic high-liquid-limit silt, the angle of internal friction changes slightly with organic content (wu), maintaining a low value of 1-3°. Cohesion decreases gradually when wu 21%. An organic content of 17-21% serves as a possible transition interval for sludge structure and strength degradation. Mechanism analysis reveals that the contribution of organic matter to soil strength is predominantly governed by cementation, with negligible influence on the internal friction angle. The reduction in cohesion is primarily attributed to the decrease in dry unit weight, degradation of mineral skeleton, a predominance of the soft organic matrix, and increased plastic deformation.

title: Indocyanine green near-infrared fluorescence in robotic ureteral and ureteroenteric reconstruction: from ureteral localization to perfusion-guided decision-making.
authors: Zhang C, Yang ZN, Qiao Y, Wu H, Zhang WQ, Gao BS.
abstract: In robot-assisted ureteral and uretero-intestinal reconstruction surgery, indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence technology has seen increasing use to supplement traditional visual assessment. This narrative review explores the evolution of this technology from an anatomical navigation tool to a potential tool for perfusion-guided intraoperative decision-making. A structured literature search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science databases, focusing on robot-assisted reconstruction applications, comparative outcome studies, and quantitative fluorescence methods. Intraluminal ICG enhances luminal contrast, aiding in the identification of the ureter and the localisation of strictures, particularly in reoperative or fibrotic areas. In contrast, intravenous ICG enables real-time assessment of relative tissue perfusion and may influence the selection of ureteral resection margins and anastomotic sites. The results of comparative studies evaluating the efficacy of preventing ureterointestinal anastomotic strictures have been inconsistent and remain limited by factors such as observational study designs, inconsistent fluorescence protocols, varying follow-up periods, and temporal confounding factors. Consequently, current evidence more strongly supports intraoperative utility and decision-making than consistent long-term outcome improvement. Quantitative time-intensity analysis, automated segmentation, and AI-based video analysis may reduce the subjectivity of fluorescent image interpretation; however, there are currently no validated thresholds for in situ ureteral reconstruction. Future research should standardise image acquisition, prospectively document fluorescence-guided changes in surgical strategy, and validate quantitative perfusion indices against clinically meaningful reconstruction failure. Currently, ICG should be used to complement established reconstruction principles, rather than to replace the surgeon's judgement.

title: Improved model predictive current control strategy for overvoltage suppression in long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electrical submersible pump systems.
authors: Gong X, Qi X, Feng M, Zhu L, Wang N.
abstract: Long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electric submersible pump (ESP) systems suffer from significant voltage reflection issues caused by distributed parameter effects, leading to transient overvoltages at the motor terminals that can reach several times the DC bus voltage. This severely threatens system stability and motor insulation integrity, and traditional control methods prove inadequate for effective suppression. To address this challenge, the paper proposes an improved model predictive current control (MPCC) strategy for induction motor ESP systems, which integrates overvoltage suppression and equivalent switching frequency reduction for long-cable PWM-driven applications. The reflection overvoltage mechanism is thoroughly analyzed through mathematical modeling of the motor and long-cable transmission line, and the applicability of predictive current control in such systems is investigated. The core improvement lies in a circular boundary constrained MPCC combined with a dynamic transition voltage vector selection mechanism, which enables dual-mode optimization based on current error boundary conditions: the normal cost function is applied within the circular boundary to jointly optimize voltage tracking, switching frequency, and dv/dt; while the backup cost function is activated outside the boundary to prioritize current error minimization. This effectively optimizes the voltage switching strategy, reducing both switching frequency and dv/dt, thereby preventing overvoltage excitation caused by abrupt voltage vector steps in PWM-driven systems. Simulation models under different cable configurations (1 km with RLC filter and 110 m without RLC filter) and an experimental platform based on a neutral-point-clamped three-level inverter (NPC-TLI) topology are established, with the 110 m no-filter configuration serving as a direct cross-validation baseline. Comparative simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the duration of motor terminal overvoltage while maintaining excellent system dynamic performance. Moreover, the improved MPCC effectively suppresses overvoltage and reduces equivalent switching frequency without requiring hardware filter redesign, while the RLC filter remains necessary for full insulation safety compliance under more demanding long-cable conditions, substantially mitigating the risk of motor insulation breakdown.

title: Higher preoperative Advanced Activities Score of the 2011 Knee Society Score is associated with greater patient satisfaction after ground kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty.
