authors: Hayashi T, Matsumoto T, Ikuta K, Tsubosaka M, Kamenaga T, Kuroda Y, Nakano N, Ishida K, Hayashi S, Kuroda R.
abstract: Purpose Ground kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty, which uses the ground mechanical axis as a reference, has shown favourable clinical outcomes. Nevertheless, preoperative factors associated with post-operative satisfaction remain unclear. This study aimed to identify preoperative predictors of patient satisfaction after ground kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty using patient-reported outcome measures. Methods A total of 117 consecutive patients with varus knee osteoarthritis who underwent primary ground kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were classified into excellent satisfaction (≥32 points) and suboptimal satisfaction ( Results Preoperative Advanced Activities Score was significantly associated with post-operative satisfaction ( B = 0.057). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal cut-off value of 12 (sensitivity = 0.744; specificity = 0.677). Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that higher preoperative Advanced Activities Score was independently associated with excellent post-operative satisfaction (odds ratio = 1.320; p Conclusions Higher preoperative activity level was associated with greater post-operative satisfaction after ground kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Giant Cervicothoracic Ganglioneuroma Misdiagnosed as Neurofibroma on Core Needle Biopsy: Transcervical Resection and Postoperative Neurological Sequelae: A Case Report.
authors: Daas O, Al Kiswani S, Al-Qaisi MZ, Daas A, Al Shakkah A, Salahat S, Nofal A.
abstract: Ganglioneuroma (GN) may be misdiagnosed as neurofibroma when core needle biopsy samples only contain Schwannian stroma without mature ganglion cells. Even giant cervicothoracic GNs may be resectable through a transcervical approach alone. Recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy and Horner syndrome are foreseeable, anatomically predictable risks requiring dedicated preoperative counseling.

title: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma: a case report and literature review.
authors: He Y, Xue W, Feng J, Chen G, Ma D, Niu J.
abstract: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma (GCOC) is an exceedingly rare malignant odontogenic epithelial tumor, distinguished by the presence of ghost cells. GCOC exhibits nonspecific clinical and radiologic features, such as variable pain, swelling, and osteolytic destruction without distinct periosteal reaction, and can be locally destructive and invasive, with the potential for distant metastases. Currently, no effective systemic therapy is recommended for patients. We present a case of a 56-year-old male patient diagnosed with GCOC involving the maxilla, along with a review of the previous literature. The patient underwent en bloc resection of the tumor. However, the tumor recurred 3 months later, and the patient opted for conservative management. Unfortunately, the patient passed away 2 weeks after the recurrence. Based on the case presentation and literature review, we conclude that GCOC represents an aggressive malignancy with a high potential for local recurrence and metastatic disease. This necessitates preoperative accurate imaging diagnosis to guide radical resection, and highlights the need for effective adjuvant therapies, which are currently unavailable, to prevent rapid disease progression and mortality.

title: Fibular aplasia, tibial campomelia and oligodactyly syndrome with associated congenital heart defects.
authors: K R A, Venkatesh BM.

title: Feedforward neuromuscular control and dynamic postural stability in people with chronic ankle instability during single-leg landing.
authors: Li TY, Wang Z, Cascoe R, Aki-Sawyerr J, Zhang P, Yang Y, Fong DTP.
abstract: Individuals with chronic ankle instability(CAI) show deficits in neuromuscular control and postural stability. While feedback mechanisms are well-studied, feedforward mechanisms during dynamic tasks remains underexplored. This study compared feedforward neuromuscular control and dynamic postural stability among CAI, coper and healthy groups. Fifteen CAI(23.5 ± 2.9 years, 11 M/4F), fifteen coper(24.1 ± 3.4 years, 12 M/3F) and fifteen healthy participants(25.5 ± 3.5 years, 11 M/4F) performed single-leg drop landings from 30 cm. Total centre of pressure movement during 1-second and 3-second(TOTEX 1s &TOTEX 3s ), mediolateral sway distance(D ML ), peak vertical GRF(peak vGRF) and root-mean-square of mediolateral GRF in the first 0.4 s(RMS_ML_0.4) were recorded via force plate. Surface electromyography recorded muscle activity 200 ms before landing among tibialis anterior(TA), peroneus longus(PL) and gastrocnemius lateralis(GL). Pre-activation timing was calculated using the Teager-Kaiser energy operator(TKEO). Statistical analysis involved one-way ANOVA(α = 0.05) and Tukey post-hoc testing. Compared to healthy participants, CAI individuals displayed earlier TA(270 ± 73 ms vs. 85 ± 53 ms, p ML (55.6 ± 15.7 mm vs. 39.5 ± 9.0 mm, p ML (42.7 ± 7.0 mm vs. 55.6 ± 15.7 mm, p = 0.008) compared to CAI individuals. CAI exhibited postural control deficits and ineffective feedforward control, shown by lower PL activity despite early pre-activation. Rate of force production training is advised. Increased GL activation may serve as a compensatory response in copers after initial ankle sprain.

title: Feasibility of Longitudinal Home Monitoring of Nocturnal Transcutaneous CO<sub>2</sub> and Relationship to Standard Respiratory Measures in Patients With ALS: A Pilot Cohort Study.
authors: Geronimo A, Cao Q, Elman L, Simmons Z, Ackrivo J.
abstract: Introduction/aims Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) results in respiratory muscle weakness causing hypoventilation, retention of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), and chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure. In this pilot study, we performed a 12-month assessment of daytime and home nocturnal CO 2 to track respiratory progression, determine relationships with surrogate respiratory measures, and assess the impact of non-invasive ventilatory support. Methods Adults with forced vital capacity (FVC) less than 90% predicted secondary to ALS were recruited from two sites in the northeast US. Participants were followed up at standard visits every 3 months for up to five visits. Spirometry, functional scores, and patient-reported outcomes of dyspnea were recorded. Each visit included a 15-min, seated measurement of transcutaneous CO 2 (PtcCO 2 ) while in clinic, followed by 3 nights of home overnight PtcCO 2 monitoring. Linear mixed-effects models were employed to describe the changes that occurred longitudinally and resulting from the initiation of non-invasive ventilation (NIV). Results Sixteen subjects were enrolled, with nine completing the full study. Strength and FVC declined over time, while daytime PtcCO 2 remained stable. Five individuals demonstrated nocturnal hypercapnia that preceded FVC 2 . Discussion Home nocturnal PtcCO 2 assessment in ALS may identify respiratory insufficiency prior to FVC. Transcutaneous CO 2 may play a role in the respiratory management of patients as a biomarker for hypoventilation risk and NIV titration. However, equipment availability and data quality limitations would benefit from professional assistance rather than independent in-home use.

title: Factors associated with choosing diagnostic radiology as a future specialty among Palestinian medical students: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
authors: AbuAttallah IA, Qrareya JA, Adawi RS, Khamaysa J, Aljamal MT.
abstract: Background Understanding factors influencing specialty choice is essential for workforce planning and curriculum development. Recruitment into diagnostic radiology remains challenging in several regions, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Palestinian medical students' consideration of diagnostic radiology as a future specialty, with particular emphasis on educational exposure, perceptions of artificial intelligence (AI), and cognitive influences. Methods A multi-institutional cross-sectional study was conducted to evaluate factors influencing the choice of diagnostic radiology as a future specialty among Palestinian medical students between 2 November 2025 and 5 February 2026. Data were collected using a previously validated questionnaire adapted from Almuhanna et al. Descriptive statistics were performed, followed by bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of considering radiology as a future specialty. Adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported. Results A total of 427 students participated (56.7% female; mean age 21.75 ± 2.1 years). Among 300 valid responses regarding radiology intention, 102 students (34.0%) reported considering radiology as a future specialty. In multivariable analysis, lack of exposure to radiology research (OR = 0.14, 95% CI 0.06-0.34, p Conclusions Palestinian medical students' interest in radiology is strongly associated with modifiable educational exposures, cognitive engagement in diagnostic reasoning, and perceptions of evolving technological practice. These findings support the potential value of structured undergraduate radiology exposure, research opportunities, and mentorship initiatives to improve awareness and interest in radiology.

title: Experiences of self-management behaviors during adaptation to permanent enterostomy among older patients: A qualitative study.
authors: Duan Z, Wu F.
abstract: Object This study aimed to explore the experiences and perceived changes in self-management behaviors among older patients with a permanent stoma during adaptation, providing insights for the development of targeted supportive interventions. Methods Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 13 older colorectal cancer patients with a permanent stoma. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. The data were analyzed and thematically refined using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Results Three overarching themes and several sub-themes were identified. Theme one, decision-making dilemmas and uncertainty, included insufficient and poorly tailored decision support resources and challenges in processing complex self-management information. Theme two, reconstructing daily life and identity after stoma formation, encompassed disruptions in body image and daily routines, emotional struggles between rejection and acceptance, and the development of a new normal in living with a stoma. Theme three, developing resilience through accumulated experience and self-management practice, involved learning through repeated self-adjustment, drawing on previous life experiences as coping resources, and redefining life priorities after illness. Conclusion The findings suggest that older patients living with a permanent stoma experience self-management as an ongoing process involving decisional challenges, psychological adjustment, and the gradual reconstruction of resilience. Healthcare professionals should provide continuous decision support, psychological care, and family-inclusive interventions while adopting a strength-based approach that recognizes patients' existing abilities and lived experiences. Supporting patients in reflecting on their adaptation experiences and accumulated coping strategies may enhance self-efficacy and facilitate sustained self-management.

title: Evaluation of digital binocular therapies for amblyopia after refractive adaptation in treatment-naive children aged 3-13 years: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
authors: Narayanan AT, Robinson DG, Woodhouse JM.
abstract: Background Patching has been the mainstay of unilateral amblyopia treatment, but adherence is challenging. Digital binocular therapies have emerged as a novel approach; however, evidence in treatment-naive children remains limited, as existing studies have predominantly included previously treated children. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of digital binocular therapies versus patching for improving visual acuity in treatment-naive children aged 3-13 years with unilateral amblyopia following refractive adaptation. Design A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261278100). Comprehensive literature searches were conducted from January 2000 to December 2025. Two independent reviewers screened and selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. The primary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity. Data were pooled using a random-effects model. The GRADE approach was used to rate the certainty of evidence. Results Five RCTs (n = 225) were included in the primary analysis. Digital binocular therapies showed no statistically significant difference in visual acuity compared with patching using a random-effects model (MD 0.00 logMAR, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.10; I2 = 50.2%). Sensitivity analysis including two additional RCTs judged to be at high risk of bias, one of which compared digital binocular therapy plus spectacles with spectacles alone (7 RCTs; n = 292), yielded similar results (MD 0.04 logMAR, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.10; I2 = 75.2%). The certainty of evidence for visual acuity was moderate, downgraded for inconsistency. Conclusion Digital binocular therapies may serve as adjunctive treatment options when adherence to patching is challenging. However, current evidence does not demonstrate superiority over patching in treatment-naive children with unilateral amblyopia. The evidence remains limited by the small number of RCTs and modest sample sizes. Registration This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) under registration number CRD420261278100 on 4 January 2026.

title: Embedding muscle attachment sites in statistical shape models can estimate hip muscle attachment sites in patients with hip dysplasia.
authors: Kim N, Wissman MM, Harris MD, Besier T.
abstract: Manual selection of muscle attachment points on musculoskeletal models is time-consuming and susceptible to human error. Statistical shape modelling can accurately predict bone morphology and has the potential to predict regional muscle attachment sites. This study evaluated the variability of manually selected muscle attachment points across a cohort of 20 hip dysplasia patients. Attachment points were compared against the regional attachment sites embedded in a shape model (using a SOMSO anatomical model). Variability of manually selected points was calculated using Euclidean distances between points. Muscle segmentations from each individual were projected onto the surface bone of a shape model and compared to the SOMSO-embedded muscle regions using a Dice Score. Manually selected muscle attachment points varied 4 to 5 mm across all muscles on both the femur and pelvis. Muscles that showed high overlap of regional attachment areas across individuals demonstrated strong agreement with the SOMSO-embedded regions of the shape model. These findings suggest that embedding muscle attachment footprints within a statistical shape model can predict muscle attachment sites within the variability observed from manually selected points. Therefore, this approach can provide a rapid and robust approach to identify patient-specific muscle attachments sites.

title: Effects of exogenous ketones on post-exercise recovery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Bomans S, Jimenez Garcia B, Leemans L, Mohib O, El M'Rabet I, De Waele E, Janssens P, Beckwée D.
abstract: Exogenous ketone supplementation has gained attention as a potential strategy to enhance post-exercise recovery. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis evaluated its effects on recovery outcomes in adults. PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched for randomized controlled and cross-over trials investigating exogenous ketone supplementation. Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which seven were included in the meta-analysis. Meta-analyses showed no significant effects on muscle soreness (SMD = 0.39, 95% CI [-0.29 to 1.07], p = 0.26, I 2 = 0%) or muscle glycogen resynthesis (SMD = 18.21, 95% CI [-19.15 to 55.56], p = 0.34, I 2 = 30%). A small effect on post-exercise lactate concentrations (mmol/L) favored the control condition (MD = 0.34, 95% CI [0.02-0.66], p = 0.04, I 2 = 0%), although its clinical relevance appears limited. No consistent improvements were observed across physical recovery outcomes. Evidence for cognitive recovery was mixed, with isolated improvements in reaction time, while most outcomes remained unaffected. Creatine kinase concentrations were not significantly affected. Overall, current evidence suggests limited benefits of exogenous ketones for post-exercise recovery and is largely restricted to physically active male adults, limiting generalizability. Further well-powered studies in more diverse populations and recovery contexts are needed.

title: Effect of heart rate on hemodynamics in patient-specific intracranial aneurysms: An in vitro study.
authors: El-Khader BAT, Shirdade N, Korte J, Behme D, Berg P, Church EW, Brindise MC.
abstract: The rupture of an intracranial aneurysm (IA) has been linked to local hemodynamic environments, but it remains unclear how transient physiological states such as elevated heart rate modulate those environments, and whether different aneurysm geometries respond similarly. Here, we used volumetric particle tracking velocimetry (PTV) to measure 3D velocity fields in two patient-specific IA phantoms, a right middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysm and a left vertebral artery (LVA) aneurysm, under three heart rates representative of rest (60 bpm), active movement (100 bpm), and exercise (137 bpm). From these measurements, we quantified coherent structures, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), wall shear stress (WSS), and oscillatory shear index (OSI). Increasing heart rate did not simply increase peak inflow; it altered the temporal organization of the flow. In the MCA aneurysm, higher heart rates produced a stronger, more anchored intra-saccular vortex and elevated coherent-structure strength and TKE that persisted into mid- and end-diastole, along with broader spatial coverage of elevated WSS that remained high beyond peak systole. The LVA aneurysm exhibited a more muted response, with minimal changes in streamline topology and WSS across heart rates. These results show that heart rate can drive prolonged high-shear, high-energy loading within the cardiac cycle, but that this amplification is morphology-dependent and non-monotonic rather than universal.

title: Eating behaviour and glycaemic control: A cross-sectional study in adolescents with diabetes.
authors: Şimşekoğlu N, Arslanoğlu İ, Portakal B, Aktaş S.
abstract: Background Achieving early glycemic control in adolescents with diabetes is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between eating attitudes and glycemic control, as well as the factors associated with eating attitudes and glycemic control, in adolescents with diabetes. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study included 143 adolescents with diabetes, aged 10-19 years, who attended a research hospital between February and April 2024. The data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, Eating Attitudes Test (EAT) and an information form questioning the values of some metabolic variables. Results The mean age of the participants was 14 ± 2.3 years and 49.7% had diabetes between 1-5 years. The mean total score of the EAT scale was 16.62 ± 8.30. The mean score of the "Dieting" subscale of the EAT scale was 10.39 ± 5.58, the mean score of the "Bulimia food preoccupation" subscale was 2.33 ± 3.03 and the mean score of the "Oral Control" subscale was 3.79 ± 3.08. There was no significant difference between the mean EAT total score and glycemic control. Conclusions The mean EAT-26 total score was below the commonly used cutoff score, and no significant association was found between EAT-26 scores and HbA1c. Differences in EAT-26 total and subscale scores were observed according to selected demographic and clinical characteristics, including BMI, treatment modality, and treatment adherence. These findings describe self-reported eating attitudes in the study sample and support the inclusion of eating-related assessment within the holistic care of adolescents with Type 1 DM.

title: Digital and technology‑enabled approaches for post‑stroke fatigue: A scoping review protocol.
authors: Huang X, Xu J, Wang L, Huang S, Zhu X.
abstract: Background Post‑stroke fatigue (PSF) affects approximately 50% of stroke survivors and is one of the most common and disabling post‑stroke sequelae. Digital and technology‑enabled approaches have attracted increasing attention in the field of stroke rehabilitation, including mobile health applications (mHealth), wearable devices, virtual reality (VR), remote rehabilitation, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuromodulation technologies. However, no comprehensive scoping review has systematically mapped the full spectrum of evidence on digital and technology‑enabled approaches for PSF. Methods This scoping review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews, be guided by the Population, Concept, Context (PCC) framework, and be reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta‑Analysis Protocols (PRISMA‑P) and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta‑Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA‑ScR). Eight electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PsycINFO) and five gray literature sources (OpenGrey, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, ClinicalTrials.gov, the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and Google Scholar) will be searched. Two reviewers will use NoteExpress to remove duplicates and manage references, and will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full texts. After pilot testing, data will be extracted independently by the two reviewers. Synthesis will involve descriptive numerical summaries and inductive qualitative content analysis. Inter‑rater agreement will be assessed during a calibration phase. The expected output is an evidence map organized by approach category and purpose (assessment, monitoring, prevention, and treatment), which will identify knowledge gaps and guide future research. Registration This protocol has been registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). Registration DOI (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/4WMEK).

title: Development and validation of a model using thoracic vertebrae data from low-dose CT scans for detecting AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis.
authors: Zhang Y, Rong C, Zhang Y, Wang Z, Xiao H, Chen J, Liang Y, Yang X, Xie W.
abstract: Despite evidence supporting opportunistic lumbar osteoporosis screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT), a clinically deployable screening strategy is lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate a model using thoracic bone mineral density (BMD) from LDCT for opportunistic screening. This multi-center, cross-sectional study included 18,298 adults who underwent LDCT with coverage from T1 to L2 at 134 Chinese health check-up centers. Outcome was defined as "artificial intelligence quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) defined lumbar osteoporosis" based on a mean L1-L2 BMD 3 by phantom-less AI-QCT system. Five machine learning models were trained on T1-T12 BMD (n = 11,065) and evaluated internally (n = 4743) and externally (n = 2490). Performance metrics included accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, Brier score, F1 score and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis was present in 1730 (9.5%) participants. Higher thoracic BMD was inversely associated with the AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis. T12 exhibited the strongest association: each 1 mg/cm 3 increment reduced odds by 21.9% (OR: 0.781, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.769, 0.793, P < 0.001). Logistic regression was selected as the final model. In external validation, it achieved an AUC of 0.993 (95% CI: 0.991, 0.996), AUPRC of 0.922 (95% CI: 0.887, 0.951), F1 score (0.813), sensitivity (0.975), and specificity (0.963). AI-QCT-derived thoracic BMD showed potential for identifying AI-QCT-defined lumbar osteoporosis. Integrating phantomless AI-QCT into lung cancer screening may enable large-scale opportunistic screening, but prospective validation against independent standards is required.

title: Deep Intramuscular Vascular Malformations in Pediatric Klippel-Trenaunay Syndrome Mimicking Maffucci Syndrome: A Case Report.
authors: Shah SS, Sajid B, Tabassum M, Ali M, Janoowala T, Farooq T, Ahsan M, Baig MMA, Baig MD, Amin MHJ.
abstract: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare congenital vascular overgrowth disorder characterized by capillary and venous or lymphatic malformations with limb hypertrophy. Deep intramuscular involvement in children is uncommon and may resemble other vascular-overgrowth syndromes. We report a 12-year-old boy with right lower-limb swelling since birth, recurrent cellulitis, chronic ulceration and purulent discharge, progressive limb enlargement, and four previous soft-tissue excisions. Examination showed bilateral nodular ulcerated lesions and vascular skin changes. Laboratory testing demonstrated persistent microcytic anemia and raised inflammatory markers. Doppler ultrasonography identified soft-tissue hypertrophy, macrodactyly, calcified cavernous vascular lesions, superficial venous dilatation, incompetent perforators, and venous reflux, while deep veins remained patent. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging showed extensive intramuscular malformations involving the gastrocnemius and tibialis muscles without marrow or joint involvement. The calcified lesions initially raised concern for Maffucci syndrome; however, the absence of enchondromas and histopathologic confirmation of benign cavernous vascular malformations supported KTS. Progressive symptomatic masses were treated with surgical debulking, drainage, wound care, and culture-directed antibiotics. Recovery was uneventful, with continued conservative surveillance. This case shows how combined clinical assessment, Doppler ultrasonography, magnetic resonance imaging, and histopathology can distinguish atypical pediatric KTS from skeletal dysplasias and guide treatment when genetic testing and multidisciplinary vascular services are limited.

title: Correction to "MERItest™-A multidimensional model for functional evaluation at 6 months after ACL reconstruction".
abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1002/jeo2.70836.].

title: Comparison of bone augmentation techniques in the mandibular posterior region: A randomized clinical trial protocol.
authors: Lanata-Flores A, Armijos Briones M, Benítez Sellán P, Ayala Aguirre PE.
abstract: This randomized, statistician-blinded, parallel-group clinical trial will compare the effectiveness of three bone-augmentation techniques applied to the posterior mandible using the cortical shell approach. Eighty-seven participants will be randomly allocated into three groups (autogenous, xenogeneic, or allogeneic cortical shells), each combined with a 1:1 mixture of autogenous bone chips and biomaterial. Participants may contribute one or two eligible posterior mandibular sites; however, the unit of analysis for the primary outcome will be the participant, using a participant-level summary (mean value when two sites are treated). The study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT06661447). Recruitment has not yet begun. The single primary endpoint is horizontal bone gain (mm) at 6 months, evaluated by cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Additional CBCT assessments at 3 and 12 months will be analyzed as secondary longitudinal outcomes. Volumetric and morphometric analyses will be performed through a standardized digital workflow integrating intraoral scanning, CBCT segmentation, and surface registration. Secondary outcomes will include bone density, surgical duration, and postoperative inflammation. Based on a previous CBCT-based randomized clinical trial with a related horizontal ridge-augmentation methodology, assuming a pooled standard deviation of approximately 1.12 mm and a clinically relevant between-group difference of 1.0 mm, 26 evaluable participants per group are required to achieve approximately 81.5% power for each prespecified primary comparison using a conservative two-sided α of 0.025 for sample-size planning. To allow for an anticipated 10% attrition rate, 29 participants will be recruited per group, resulting in a total planned sample of 87 participants. The primary analysis will use an ANCOVA model adjusted for baseline ridge width. This study aims to generate controlled, quantitative evidence on the volumetric and clinical performance of different cortical graft materials for posterior mandibular reconstruction. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06661447. The registry record will be updated before recruitment begins.

title: Clinical decision-making for decompression-level selection in multilevel degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Long Y, Li L, Zhong Y, Li C, Yang S, Wang G, Sun H, Si J, Li J, Zhang Y.
abstract: Purpose To characterise changes in decompression-level selection during sequential preoperative assessment in patients with multilevel degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis (DLSS) and to describe postoperative outcomes and subsequent events involving initially untreated candidate levels. Methods This retrospective single-centre cohort included 168 patients with two to four MRI-defined candidate levels who underwent endoscopic decompression. Planned decompression levels were reconstructed before walking load testing (WLT), after WLT, after selective nerve root block (SNRB) when performed, and at the final preoperative assessment. Postoperative clinical outcomes and subsequent events involving initially untreated candidate levels were recorded during 24 months of follow-up. Results Planned level sets changed after WLT in 72/168 patients (42.9%), and final plans differed from initial imaging-informed plans in 87/168 patients (51.8%). Among 55 patients undergoing SNRB, post-WLT plans were modified in 22 (40.0%). All final planned levels were decompressed. At 24 months, 143 patients (85.1%) completed follow-up, with a model-estimated 38.44-point improvement in the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI); 123/143 (86.0%) achieved the ODI threshold for patient acceptable symptom state (PASS). Among 231 initially untreated candidate levels, five underwent delayed decompression, with a 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimate of 2.6% (95% CI 1.1-6.0). Conclusion Sequential incorporation of imaging, functional assessment, and selective diagnostic procedures was associated with changes in planned decompression levels in patients with multilevel DLSS. This study describes surgical decision-making and the subsequent clinical course of initially untreated candidate levels after selective decompression planning.

title: Changes in ware-decoration associations in ceramic assemblages from Wacheqsa, Chavín de Huántar, Peru.
authors: Mesía-Montenegro C.
abstract: Ceramic differentiation can involve altered associations among continuing attributes without wholesale categorical replacement. At Wacheqsa, Chavín de Huántar, Peru, this study compares ware composition, decorative techniques, and their associations in 1,308 decorated or surface-treated sherd observations from five archaeological contexts. Early Platforms and Water Flood constitute the earlier Urabarroid aggregate; Stone Rooms, Midden, and Late Platforms constitute the later Janabarroid aggregate. These labels describe ceramic affinities within pre-existing context sets, whose stratigraphic networks are only partly connected and whose formation histories differ. On identical common support of nine wares and six techniques (n = 334/822), ware-margin Hellinger distance is 0.430 (95% fixed-count interval 0.392-0.481), technique-margin distance is 0.588 (0.551-0.634), and joint distance is 0.734 (0.714-0.793). A homogeneous-association model rejects a common ware-technique association after aggregate-specific margins are fitted (G2 = 118.59; pboot = 0.0001); the result persists without Midden (G2 = 90.16; pboot = 0.0001). Early Platforms differs from each later context, and stamping/impression is prominent in all three later samples, although those contexts retain distinct joint profiles. Nine of eleven ware categories occur in both aggregates, with pronounced differences in the association of polished wares with incision and stamping/impression. The contrast is consistent with differing decorated repertoires across activity and depositional settings, including contexts associated with collective consumption. Local superpositions and the published chronology support a temporal interpretation, but the contribution of elapsed time cannot be separated from differences in activity and deposition.

title: Case Report: Limb-threatening desmoid-type fibromatosis of the foot requiring transtibial amputation.
authors: Debordes PA, Hamoudi C, Mota B, Fortunato M, Sbampato V, Tsoupras A, Weingertner N, Brinkert D, Ceroni D.
abstract: Desmoid-type fibromatosis (DTF) is a rare myofibroblastic/fibroblastic neoplasm characterized by infiltrative growth and a tendency towards local recurrence. In its extra-abdominal form, DTF arises in the extremities, head, neck and trunk, and the chest wall, but Desmoid fibromatosis in the foot is exceptionally rare. We present the case of a 41-year-old man who presented with recurrence of a right foot tumor initially diagnosed as a benign spindle cell lesion. The diagnosis was revised to desmoid-type fibromatosis based on a CTNNB1 p.T41A mutation. Despite systemic therapies, the tumor progressed locally, requiring transtibial amputation. Foot involvement in DTF is uncommon and challenging due to anatomical constraints. Even though this condition is not considered to be malignant, the natural history of DTF may be totally unpredictable warranting radical surgical management. This case emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management, as delayed care may result in limb-threatening progression requiring salvage amputation.

title: Care-Need Level Worsening After Hip Fracture Surgery in Kyoto, Japan: Population-Based Cohort Study.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
authors: Sasaki K, Takahashi Y, Nishikawa Y, Toyama M, Kohno A, Sakai M, Ueshima H, Shimamoto T, Tateyama Y, Kato G, Iwami T, Nakayama T.
abstract: Objectives To describe 3-year transitions of care-need level after hip fracture surgery and identify factors associated with subsequent nonfatal worsening among day-180 survivors. Design Retrospective cohort study using linked administrative medical and long-term care insurance claims. Setting and participants Adults aged ≥75 years in Kyoto City, Japan, who underwent hip fracture surgery between 2013 and 2018. The day-180 landmark cohort included 6556 patients who survived to day 180 and were not certified as care-need level 5 before surgery or at the landmark. Methods Follow-up started at day 180. The primary estimand was subsequent nonfatal care-need level worsening among patients alive and still at risk at the landmark; death after the landmark was treated as a competing event. We estimated cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray models with covariate-by-log-time interactions. Supplementary analyses examined a death-inclusive composite end point and alternative landmarks. Results The cumulative incidence of worsening was 10.6% at 12 months, 28.3% at 24 months, and 37.4% at 36 months after surgery. Longer initial claims-based rehabilitation continuity during the postoperative 6 months was associated with a lower incidence of subsequent nonfatal worsening (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio per month, 0.961; 95% CI, 0.941-0.982). The supplementary composite end point analysis showed no clear association between rehabilitation continuity and worsening or death (hazard ratio, 0.988; 95% CI, 0.972-1.006). Associations of higher Hospital Frailty Risk Score and preoperative care-need levels with worsening varied over time. Conclusions and implications Among day-180 survivors after hip fracture surgery, preoperative frailty and care-need levels showed time-varying associations with subsequent nonfatal worsening. Longer initial claims-based rehabilitation continuity was associated with lower incidence of nonfatal worsening but should be interpreted as a claims-based association, not evidence of a causal effect or mortality-inclusive benefit. These findings support ongoing risk assessment and periodic reassessment of care needs beyond the early postoperative period.

title: Cable-routing geometry as a design variable for multiplanar hip assistance in a single-actuator soft exosuit.
authors: Kwon J, Park S, Driscoll HG, Lee G.
abstract: Cable-driven soft exosuits for gait assistance are predominantly sagittal-plane devices, yet pathological gait involves coordinated deviations across all three anatomical planes. This study experimentally evaluated whether cable-routing geometry alone, within a single-actuator hip exosuit, can produce measurable multiplanar hip effects during walking. Ten healthy, exosuit-experienced male adults walked on a treadmill under five conditions: one matched unpowered control and four powered configurations that paired single-plane and multi-plane cable routing with hip-flexion and hip-extension assistance. Three-dimensional hip kinematics were compared across conditions, and exosuit-generated hip torques were estimated from subject-specific musculoskeletal models. Multi-plane routing produced phase-dependent kinematic changes concentrated in the transverse plane. Relative to unassisted walking, multi-plane flexion assistance increased hip internal rotation (3.6°, p = 0.0002), multi-plane extension assistance increased hip external rotation (1.8°, p = 0.0095), and single-plane flexion assistance produced a smaller but significant increase in external rotation (1.1°, p = 0.0463). Frontal-plane differences were not significant for any comparison with unassisted walking, so the hypothesized larger frontal-plane deviations under multi-plane routing were not supported. Multi-plane routing also produced greater sagittal-plane hip excursion than single-plane routing. Overall gait-trajectory similarity between single-plane and multi-plane routing was comparable in most comparisons and differed significantly only in the hip frontal plane during extension assistance. The estimated torques indicated that multi-plane routing introduced larger frontal- and transverse-plane components while the sagittal-plane component remained dominant. These findings show that cable-routing geometry alone can shape phase-localized hip kinematics, reaching significance in the transverse plane, without adding actuators. The effect magnitudes were small and near the measurement uncertainty of the capture system. The all-male, exosuit-experienced sample limits generalizability, so relevance to clinical populations remains to be tested. Cable-routing geometry is therefore proposed as a candidate rather than an established design variable for multi-dimensional assistance in soft exosuits.

title: Biomechanical link between knee osteoarthritis and lumbar spine loading: An experimental and simulation-based analysis.
authors: Jamshidian A, Rouyin A, Nazemi H, Arjmand N, Farahmand F.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and low back pain (LBP) frequently co-occur, yet their biomechanical link remains unclear. This exploratory study investigated whether KOA gait is associated with altered trunk muscle forces and lumbar loading. Motion-capture and ground-reaction-force data were collected from eight individuals with mild-to-moderate medial KOA and ten healthy controls. Participant-scaled OpenSim models were used to estimate trunk muscle forces and lumbar joint reaction forces (JRFs). Between-group comparisons used Mann-Whitney U tests with false-discovery-rate correction. Walking speed did not differ between groups, whereas stride length was shorter in KOA (q = 0.033). Proximal kinematic differences were limited: no pelvic variable remained significant after correction, and only mean thoracic lateral bending differed (q = 0.032), with a small absolute magnitude. Mean knee angle differed between groups (q = 0.014), with additional differences in peak knee and ankle kinematics (q ≤ 0.006). Model-predicted mean and peak multifidus, longissimus, and iliocostalis forces were greater in KOA, whereas internal oblique forces were lower (all q < 0.05). Mean and peak lumbar compression were greater in KOA at all six levels from T12-L1 to L5-S1 (all raw p < 0.001; q < 0.05), and anterior-posterior JRFs were greater at selected levels. These higher muscle forces and JRFs, despite limited group-level proximal kinematic differences, may reflect attenuation or cancellation of heterogeneous individual gait adaptations during averaging, even though these adaptations may still influence internal mechanical demands.

title: BCFL-DAI-PUB: Blockchain-integrated federated learning with dynamic adaptive incentives for privacy-utility balanced credit risk modelling.
authors: Ramachandra P, Vaithiyanathan S.
abstract: Accurate prediction of loan defaulters through collaborative analysis of financial data across multiple institutions is critical for maintaining financial stability and strengthening credit risk management. Although Federated Learning (FL) enables organizations to train models without exchanging raw data, its reliance on a centralized server introduces serious trust concerns, including vulnerability to gradient inversion and membership inference attacks. Blockchain-based Federated Learning (BCFL) addresses these challenges by cryptographically protecting and aggregating model updates through a smart contract, thereby providing a tamper-resistant learning process. In spite of these security enhancements, current BCFL frameworks do not ensure sustained client participation in real-world settings. Moreover, while traditional incentive mechanisms promote truthful participation and discourage free-riding and malicious behavior, they mainly reward model utility and neglect privacy contribution. To mitigate this limitation, we propose BCFL-DAI-PUB, a blockchain-federated learning framework integrating an innovative Dynamic Adaptive Incentive (DAI) mechanism to achieve a Privacy-Utility Balance (PUB). The proposed DAI dynamically applies three complementary incentive components, such as SCAFFOLD-based correction, adaptive differential privacy (DP-Boost), and monetary rewards, to jointly optimize learning utility and privacy protection. This work promotes honest participation, discourages dishonest behavior, and enables rapid recovery from malicious attacks, thereby improving global convergence and overall model effectiveness. The proposed BCFL-DAI-PUB achieves a final AUC of 0.91, improving upon the HE-based BCFL-PS-HER baseline (0.86) by 1.06×. By replacing homomorphic encryption with adaptive differential privacy and combining it with a dynamic incentive mechanism, the proposed framework improves both efficiency and resilience over the baseline, which relies on static reputation-based coordination. Compared with the baseline BCFL-PS-HER model, BCFL-DAI-PUB recovers from malicious disruption 1.82× faster and achieves approximately 1.22× higher MIA resistance, while the baseline incurs approximately 1.09× higher communication overhead and 1.14× higher storage overhead. These results show that BCFL-DAI-PUB improves predictive performance, strengthens privacy protection, reduces system cost, and provides more robust operation in blockchain-enabled federated credit-risk modelling.

title: Assessing the repeatability and accuracy of quantitative double-echo steady-state (qDESS) as a wT<sub>2</sub>-mapping technique in test objects and the lower limb of healthy volunteers.
authors: Rossetto G, Higgins DM, Hollingsworth KG.
abstract: Purpose A multiple-echo spin-echo (MESE) acquisition is conventional for T 2 -mapping of skeletal muscle. Its time-intensive nature can make it impractically long for muscular dystrophies (MDs) such as facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). Here we assess the feasibility of using 3D quantitative double-echo steady-state (qDESS) to quantify muscle-water T 2 (wT 2 ) by evaluating the repeatability and accuracy of the estimated wT 2 values. Methods First, the precision of qDESS as a wT 2 -mapping technique was determined by comparing against MESE and stimulated echo acquisition mode (STEAM) wT 2 values from a phantom of eight MnCl 2 -doped water phantoms with concentrations ranging from 0.1-0.45 mM in 0.05 mM increments. Then, test-retest qDESS muscle-water wT 2 maps of six lower limb muscles from eight healthy volunteers underwent a Bland-Altman analysis to assess repeatability. qDESS- and MESE-derived wT 2 values were assessed against STEAM wT 2 values at matched locations along the gastrocnemius medialis of a further five healthy volunteers to assess and compare accuracy. Results qDESS showed good repeatability and strong agreement with STEAM in test objects and the lower limb. Conclusion 3D qDESS produces repeatable and accurate wT 2 maps of the lower limb with substantially shorter acquisition times than the MESE sequence, making it a viable tool for clinical trials of MDs.

title: Arthroplasty centers logistically separated from general orthopedic departments were associated with a more successful implementation of a standardized day-case setup : A Danish cohort study of 6718 procedures from a fast-track multi-center collaboration.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Jensen CB, Danielsen O, Varnum C, Jakobsen T, Andersen MR, Bieder MJ, Overgaard S, Jørgensen CC, Kehlet H, Gromov K.
abstract: Background Day-case hip and knee arthroplasty can reduce bed occupancy and improve cost-effectiveness, which is crucial for addressing the increasing demand among hip and knee osteoarthritis patients. This study investigated how different arthroplasty center setups were associated with the implementation and day-of-surgery (DOS) discharge rates of a standardized day-case setup. Materials and methods We included unilateral primary hip and knee arthroplasty patients from seven fast-track arthroplasty centers, all implementing a standardized day-case setup in September 2022 with identical eligibility and discharge criteria. Centers were categorized as: Satellite Arthroplasty Centers (SACs): Only primary arthroplasties, separate logistics. Elective Arthroplasty Centers (EACs): Complex primaries, revisions, separate logistics. Arthroplasty Unit Orthopedic Departments (AUOs): Primary and revision procedures, integrated into a general orthopedic department. We compared DOS discharge rates from September 2022 to September 2023 with a baseline period (July 2019-December 2019) using crude percentages. We compared the DOS discharge rate for day-case-eligible patients in study period between the center types using mixed effects models. Results We included 6718 patients (1357 SAC, 4309 EAC, 1052 AUO) during the study period and 3974 in the baseline period. DOS discharge rates increased post-implementation across all centers (SAC: 3.9% to 30%, EAC: 5.5% to 23%, AUO: 7.4% to 14%). Compared with AUOs (36%), successful DOS discharge among eligible patients was more likely in SACs (54%; adjusted OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-7.1; adjusted risk difference 25 percentage points, 95% CI 5.9-44) and EACs (60%; adjusted OR 3.8, 95% CI 1.7-8.5; adjusted risk difference 31 percentage points, 95% CI 13.8-48). Conclusions Arthroplasty centers with logistics separate from the general orthopedic department, SACs and EACs, were associated with higher rates of successful DOS discharge among eligible patients during implementation of a standardized day-case pathway, despite integrated arthroplasty units, AUOs, having higher day-case surgery use before implementation.

title: Aesthetic Reconstruction of the Interlabial Sulcus: from Anatomical Rediscovery to Surgical Approach.
authors: Chang G, Jia D, Ge L, Kang Y, Zhang X, Wang D, Chen J, Xia Z, Long X, Zhu L.
abstract: Background To explore the anatomy of the interlabial sulcus and introduce a simple surgical technique for its reconstruction, and evaluate its efficacy and safety. Methods Anatomical (macroscopic and microscopic) analysis was performed on 18 hemi-perineum specimens. A total of 723 patients undergoing labiaplasty between January 2016 and December 2024 was retrospectively reviewed. Among 315 patients who had composite labia minora and lateral clitoral hood reduction, 274 were identified with an absent interlabial sulcus and were the focus of this study. Of these, 109 patients (198 sides) underwent the four-step sulcal reconstruction (Group 1), while 165 patients (299 sides) received conventional surgery without reconstruction (Group 2). Operative duration and complications were recorded. Satisfaction questionnaires via the Female Genital Self-Image Scale (FGSIS) were completed during follow-up either in the outpatient clinic or online. Results Macroscopic examination reveals a clear demarcation between the labia majora and labia minora. Microscopic analysis showed that collagen and smooth muscle fibers at the interlabial sulcus exhibited a disordered, interwoven pattern. The sulcal reconstruction prolonged operative time by approximately 20 minutes (p Conclusions Anatomical study indicates a distinct tissue boundary at the interlabial sulcus, accompanied by a localized alteration in fiber architecture. The four-step reconstruction technique proved safe and effective, with satisfactory outcomes. Given its advantages of simple steps and natural aesthetic outcomes, this approach holds promising potential for application in vulvar aesthetic surgery.Level of Evidence: IV.

title: Adequately increased postoperative medial proximal tibial angle can prevent medial joint space narrowing after open-wedge high tibial osteotomy: a 3-year cohort study.
authors: Chiba D, Maeda S, Sasaki E, Tsushima T, Kimura Y, Tsuda E, Ishibashi Y.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to investigate the longitudinal relationship between postoperative medial proximal tibial angle (pMPTA) and joint space narrowing or osteophyte formation during a 3-year follow-up period after medial open-wedge high tibial osteotomy (MOWHTO). Methods This retrospective cohort study included 133 knees of 101 patients (58 female patients; 77 female knees) who underwent MOWHTO [mean age: 57.5 ± 7.9 years; body mass index: 26.3 ± 4.0 kg/m 2 ; 32 patients (19 female patients) underwent bilateral surgeries]. On the basis of plain radiograph until 1 month postoperatively (Post Op), pMPTA and change in MPTA (ΔMPTA) (i.e., [pMPTA] - [preoperative MPTA]) were measured. Additionally, the medial and lateral femorotibial joint space widths (MJSW/LJSW) and osteophyte area (MOPA/LOPA) were measured at Post Op, and the JSW and OPA were remeasured at 3-year follow-up (3Y). Amount of changes in JSW and OPA were measured using the following formula: Δ = [JSW 3Y or OPA 3Y ] - [JSW Post Op or OPA Post Op ]. If ΔMJSW was ≤ -0.3 mm, we defined medial knee osteoarthritis as progressed (p-mOA). Results Forty-seven (35.3%) patients were diagnosed with p-mOA. Both pMPTA and ΔMPTA positively correlated with ΔMJSW. Receiver operating characteristic curves of pMPTA detected p-mOA, and the cut-off of pMPTA was 90°. Generalized estimation equations revealed that those with Conclusions Only in those with nonradiographic OA, correcting pMPTA with Level of evidence III.

title: A method for brain tumor detection and localization by means of deep learning and reliable prediction explainability.
authors: Di Giammarco M, Santone A, Cesarelli M, Martinelli F, Mercaldo F.
abstract: Brain tumors, which are abnormal growths in the brain or central spinal canal, represent a serious global health threat. In 2023, they were responsible for 94,390 cases and 18,990 deaths in the US. Early detection with Magnetic Resonance Imaging is critical for effective treatment and higher survival rates. In this paper, we propose a method for the classification and localization of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging. Our method is based on the application of convolutional neural networks and for this task, we introduce and design a new network called the CBP_Net. The experimental analysis includes the Standard_CNN, a network designed by the authors, and other state-of-the-art networks, i.e., MobileNet, DenseNet, InceptionV3, ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0. This study emphasizes both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The results demonstrate that the networks achieve optimal quantitative metrics: from 0.993 to 1.0 in accuracy. Qualitatively, we focus on visual explanations using Class Activation Mapping algorithms, specifically Grad-CAM and Score-CAM, to generate heatmaps highlighting relevant regions in the images. The Structural Similarity Index Measure is then employed to quantitatively measure the similarity between the heatmaps generated by the two CAM algorithms. This approach improves the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-driven brain tumor detection, helping clinicians diagnose.

title: A cascaded U-nets model based on hybrid attention for video anomaly detection.
authors: Li S, Jiang N, Qin J, Gong J, Pang Y, Wang F.
abstract: The aim of video anomaly detection is to identify events that deviate significantly from normal behavior. The majority of the current methods for identifying anomalous behaviors rely primarily on frame reconstruction and frame prediction. However, due to the powerful representation and generation of deep neural networks, it is not sufficient to assume that anomaly events in the reconstruction methods have larger reconstruction errors. Likewise, prediction methods are not robust to noise, which can impact the effectiveness of anomaly detection. In this paper, we propose an anomaly detection method based on cascaded attention U-Nets, combining the advantages and balancing the disadvantages of the reconstruction methods and the prediction methods. Specifically, by integrating the spatial attention module and transformer-based channel attention module into the cascaded U-Nets, the weights of the spatial regions and the channel regions that represent background features can be decreased. Furthermore, to fully utilize the temporal information, a temporal shift module is incorporated into the prediction network to improve future frame prediction. Extensive experiments were conducted on several public benchmark datasets, such as the UCSD Ped dataset, the CUHK Avenue dataset, the ShanghaiTech dataset and the UCF-crime dataset. The results indicate that the proposed method can effectively enlarge the gaps between the normal events and the anomaly events, and achieve AUC 95.6% on the UCSD Ped2 dataset, 84.1% on the UCSD Ped1 dataset, 87.6% on the CUHK Avenue dataset, 75.1% on the ShanghaiTech dataset, 73.5% on the UCF-crime dataset, which outperform other previous state-of-the-art methods.

title: A Simple Knot Technique to Simultaneously Prevent Medial-Row Suture Loosening and Lateral-Row Anchor Failure in Double-Row Rotator Cuff Repair.
authors: Wang W, Gao M, Wang Y, Li S.
abstract: We describe a simple knot-tying technique to augment fixation during double-row rotator cuff repair. After standard lateral-row anchor placement and suture tensioning, the remaining suture limbs are secured with a surgeon's knot positioned flush against the bone-anchor interface. This knot serves as a mechanical stopper: when the retracted cuff exerts medial traction on the medial-row sutures, the knot blocks suture slippage at the lateral bone surface, generating a counterforce that neutralizes pullout forces and maintains footprint compression. No additional implants are required. This technique is particularly valuable in osteoporotic bone or massive cuff tears, where lateral-row anchor fixation is prone to early failure.

title: A Comprehensive Review of the Physical Examination of the Elbow in the Throwing Athlete.
authors: Eskew JR, Soth BT, Alawa J, McGrath TM, Wanich T, Cirino CM, Carr JB.
abstract: Elbow pain is a significant source of morbidity in overhead throwing athletes, arising from a spectrum of pathologies including ulnar collateral ligament injury, valgus extension overload, medial epicondylitis, ulnar neuritis, radiocapitellar pathology, and more. Accurate diagnosis requires a systematic physical examination combined with advanced imaging. This technical note describes a comprehensive examination protocol for the throwing athlete's elbow.

title: When do book-tax differences matter for earnings persistence? The role of sales decline.
authors: Tuan DA, Dung NNK.
abstract: This study examines the association between book-tax differences (BTDs), sales decline, and earnings persistence among non-financial listed firms in Vietnam. Adopting a conditional perspective, the study treats BTDs as observable signals of accounting-tax divergence, reporting environments, and transitory earnings components, while sales decline is conceptualized as an adverse operating state that may weaken the association between current and future earnings. Using a balanced panel of 325 firms from 2013 to 2023, comprising 3,575 firm-year observations, earnings persistence is measured through the association between current and one-year-ahead pre-tax book income. Earnings are further decomposed into operating cash flows and accruals to examine component-level persistence. The empirical analysis uses OLS regressions with industry and year fixed effects and firm-clustered standard errors. Additional analyses control for earnings management and tax avoidance and test the robustness of the findings using a continuous measure of sales decline, a sample excluding the COVID-19 period, and an alternative annual-decile classification of large BTDs. The results show that pre-tax book income is persistent, but its persistence is significantly lower during periods of sales decline. The evidence for BTDs is asymmetric: large positive BTDs are more consistently associated with lower earnings persistence, whereas the evidence for large negative BTDs varies across model specifications and earnings components. The three-way interactions among sales decline, BTD classifications, and current earnings are not statistically significant in the main analyses, indicating that the evidence does not support a broad BTD-specific amplification mechanism. Overall, the findings suggest that earnings persistence is shaped by earnings components, accounting-tax reporting signals, and operating conditions. The study highlights the importance of interpreting BTDs jointly with sales trends and earnings components in the Vietnamese institutional setting.

title: What Is the 40-year Survivorship of Periacetabular Osteotomy Free From Conversion to THA?
authors: Hirt J, Roshardt J, Siebenrock KA, Ganz R, Steppacher SD, Tannast M.
abstract: Background Periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is a widely accepted technique for the surgical treatment of symptomatic acetabular dysplasia with reproducibly favorable short- and midterm outcomes. Long-term follow-up studies are essential because PAO is performed in young patients with the aim of preserving the native hip for many decades. However, follow-up of 30 years remains scarce, and no study has reported 40-year outcomes after PAO. Questions/purposes (1) What is the cumulative 40-year survivorship free from conversion to THA? (2) How did hip function change and osteoarthritis progress during follow-up of the surviving hips? (3) Which preoperative factors were associated with conversion to THA? (4) What clinically relevant thresholds can be identified for preoperative factors associated with conversion to THA? Methods This was a retrospective case series of a consecutive, single-surgeon cohort followed longitudinally and previously reported at 10, 20, and 30 years. Between 1984 and 1987, a total of 75 hips (63 patients) were treated with PAO for acetabular dysplasia at the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery of the Inselspital Bern by the originator of the procedure. Of those, 57% (43 of 75) of hips had reached the endpoint (conversion to THA or arthrodesis) before our previous report on this group (published at a minimum of 27 years). Over the entire follow-up, 5 hips (4 patients) in which the patient died with the hip preserved were treated as competing events. Since the previous report, a further 8 hips were converted and 8 hips (6 patients) were lost to follow-up, leaving 11 hips (7 patients) with complete clinical and radiographic follow-up here, all at a minimum of 36 years. During the study period (1984 to 1987), the only indication for PAO was hip dysplasia with closed triradiate cartilage. The study group here consisted of 83% (52 of 63) women, the median (range) patient age at surgery was 26 years (12 to 55), and the median (range) BMI was 22 kg/m2 (16 to 28). A total of 27 hips had previous surgery to attempt sufficient coverage. Clinical and radiographic follow-up was performed at 10-year intervals, at 10, 20, 30, and 40 years after PAO. Survivorship free from conversion to THA was estimated using a competing-risks analysis with death without conversion treated as a competing event. Twelve patients underwent bilateral PAO and contributed two hips each. Because two hips from the same patient are not independent observations, all confidence intervals (CIs) and p values were calculated using a robust variance estimator with the patient as the clustering unit. Clinical scores, hip ROM, and osteoarthritis grade were described at each follow-up. Preoperative factors associated with conversion to THA were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression with a robust variance estimator clustered on patient. Thresholds for predictive factors were identified using maximally selected rank statistics. This approach tests every observed value of a factor as a potential dividing line and selects the value producing the greatest difference in survivorship between the two resulting groups. Results At 40 years, the survivorship free from conversion to THA was 27% (95% CI 12% to 39%). Merle d'Aubigné-Postel and Harris hip scores improved during the first decade after surgery and remained above the preoperative level at each follow-up visit. Two preoperative factors were independently associated with a higher risk of conversion to THA: a higher Tönnis osteoarthritis grade (HR 2.3 per 1-grade increase [95% CI 1.4 to 3.9]; p Conclusion PAO provides durable joint preservation in acetabular dysplasia and can delay THA for decades, with 27% of hips remaining free from conversion at 40 years. Preoperative osteoarthritis and a positive anterior impingement test result were associated with conversion to THA. Older age was also associated with conversion, with a threshold of 28 years, although age was related to the degree of joint degeneration at presentation. Patient selection should therefore be based primarily on the preoperative condition of the joint, with younger age at surgery as an additional consideration. Level of evidence Level III, therapeutic study.

title: Weightbearing CT in the Evaluation of Athletic Foot and Ankle Injuries.
authors: Brué J, Micicoi L, de Cesar Netto C.
abstract: Purpose of review Subtle foot and ankle injuries in athletes, including syndesmotic sprains, ligamentous Lisfranc injuries, osteochondral lesions of the talus, and proximal fifth metatarsal stress fractures, may be underestimated or misclassified on conventional imaging. This review summarizes the current role of weightbearing CT (WBCT) in their evaluation, focusing on quantitative parameters, recent technical advances, and their potential influence on clinical decision-making. Recent findings Recent evidence has shifted WBCT from qualitative assessment toward reproducible three-dimensional quantification. Volumetric assessment and distance mapping improve characterization of syndesmotic instability, while external-rotation stress can reveal abnormalities not evident during neutral standing. In the midfoot, triplanar realignment and side-to-side comparison improve the reliability of Lisfranc measurements and support detection of subtle instability. Distance mapping permits reproducible quantification of osteochondral lesion surface area, depth, and volume and may improve consistency in surgical planning. WBCT has also characterized sport-specific alignment patterns and a morphologic and bone-density phenotype associated with proximal fifth metatarsal stress fractures. Semiautomated segmentation and deep-learning methods may further reduce observer dependence and analysis time. WBCT provides three-dimensional measurements under physiologic load that complement clinical examination and conventional imaging in selected athletic foot and ankle conditions. Its greatest current value lies in characterizing subtle instability, malalignment, and osseous morphology when these findings may alter treatment planning. However, most available evidence is retrospective and derived from symptomatic or injured cohorts. Prospective studies are needed to validate diagnostic thresholds, determine whether WBCT-derived parameters predict injury or outcomes, and define their role in routine athletic screening and return-to-sport decision-making.

title: Unsafe firearm storage among family caregivers of older persons living with dementia.
authors: Liang J, Testa A.
abstract: Purpose Firearm access in dementia caregiving households poses safety risks. This study examines household firearm ownership and storage practices among dementia caregivers, identifying factors associated with unsafe firearm storage. Methods We analyzed pooled data from 2017, 2021, 2022, and 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS). Weighted logistic regression assessed associations between caregiver characteristics and firearm storage behaviors (unloaded vs. loaded, locked vs. unlocked). Results Dementia caregivers were more likely to live in firearm-owning households than non-caregivers (40.57% vs. 35.12%). Among caregivers in firearm-owning households, 35.8% reported loaded storage, and 50.8% of those also reported unlocked storage. Older caregivers are more likely to report unlocked firearm storage (50-64 years: OR=3.74, 95%CI: 1.75-8.01; 65 + years: OR=5.39, 95%CI: 2.02-14.40; reference: 5 years: OR=0.36, 95%CI: 0.16-0.78) and assisting with household tasks (OR=0.27, 95%CI: 0.11-0.63) were associated with safer storage, though this protective effect was only observed among younger caregivers. Conclusion Household firearm storage patterns among dementia caregivers varied by caregiver age, sex, and caregiving context, highlighting the need for tailored firearm-safety counseling and caregiver-focused public health strategies.

title: Union rate and time to union following platelet-rich plasma therapy in fracture nonunion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Regmi A, Saini R, Baral S, Jain VK, Kulshrestha S, Iyengar KP.
abstract: Background Fracture nonunion remains a challenging clinical problem associated with prolonged disability and repeated surgical interventions. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been proposed as a biological adjunct to enhance bone healing; however, clinical evidence remains inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of PRP in the management of fracture nonunion. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO Registration: CRD420261366849). PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies evaluating PRP in fracture nonunion and reporting union rate or time to union were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to compare PRP with control interventions. Risk ratios (RR) were calculated for union rates and standardized mean differences (SMD) for time to union. Additional single-arm analyses were performed to estimate pooled outcomes in PRP-treated cohorts. Results Twenty-one studies comprising 877 patients were included. Two comparative studies (n = 119) demonstrated a higher likelihood of union with PRP (RR 1.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.36, p Conclusion PRP was associated with higher union rates in the limited comparative evidence, although no statistically significant difference in time to union was demonstrated. Heterogeneity in PRP protocols, methodological limitations, and the small comparative evidence base limit the certainty of these findings. PRP may have a potential role as a biological adjunct in fracture nonunion management, but further well-designed randomized controlled trials are required before definitive clinical recommendations can be made.

title: Third-Line Overactive Bladder Treatments: Cost-Benefit Analysis in an Australian Public Hospital.
authors: Klein Nulend R, Rosario M, Wood D, Kim L, Wang A.
abstract: Introduction and objectives To review the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of third-line overactive bladder (OAB) managements, including percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS), intravesical botulinum toxin A (Botox) and sacral neuromodulation (SNM) in the urology department of a tertiary public hospital. Materials and methods A prospective review was performed to determine the therapeutic outcomes of PTNS, Botox and SNM from 2019 to 2023. Costings data were obtained from the government healthcare portal to determine the overall cost and cost effectiveness of each treatment. Results Twenty-Eight patients underwent basic SNM lead insertion trial during the study period, with a response rate of 84%. Twelve patients proceeded to full implant insertion. The cost of SNM insertion is AU$23736. Comparatively, intravesical Botox has a unit cost of AU$2105 per treatment, with 67% efficacy in our patient cohort. PTNS was performed on 27 patients, with observed efficacy of 42%, at a cost of AU$200 per session. Comparing SNM and Botox, it would take 11.3 Botox treatments to generate equivalent cost to SNM. The Medtronic InterStim II Neurostimulator has a median battery life of approximately 6.2 years; if Botox was given 9-monthly during this time it would require 8.3 treatments, with a cost saving of over AU$6000. Each treatment is cost-effective when compared to the economic burden associated with OAB, with Botox being most cost-effective. Conclusion OAB significantly impacts quality of life and has significant financial and economic burdens. Third-line OAB treatments including PTNS, Botox and SNM differ significantly in their cost, efficacy and durability of effect. The availability of SNM in public hospitals has long been limited due to perceived cost ineffectiveness. Our series suggests a high efficacy associated with SNM in a public hospital setting, and cost-effectiveness when compared to the economic burden associated with OAB. Botox remains the most cost-effective option at our institution.

title: The effect of size, sex and running discipline on the shape of rectus abdominis muscle: A 3D geometric morphometric approach.
authors: Gómez-Recio M, Beyer B, García-Vargas E, Sládek V, Bastir M.
abstract: The morphology of the rectus abdominis muscle is closely related to its biomechanical functions in trunk stabilization and breathing across different activities. However, the three-dimensional morphological characteristics of this muscle remain poorly documented in vivo. Therefore, the present observational cross-sectional study aims to evaluate how size, sex and running discipline influence the 3D shape of this muscle, hypothesising that there are allometric effects, sexual dimorphism effects and that the explosive demands of sprinting require a more specialised morphology than endurance running. This work models the in vivo shape of this muscle at rest in a sample of athletes specialised in endurance running or sprinting. The rectus abdominis muscles were measured directly from CT scan slices, and 3D geometrical models of the muscle were created from the triangulation of 3D coordinates. The shape of the muscle was studied through 3D geometric morphometric analyses. The study revealed the significant effect of sex and running discipline in the 3D shape of the rectus abdominis. The results highlight distinct morphological features in males and females and in sprinters and endurance runners. Males show a more triangularly shaped rectus abdominis (wider in its superior part) compared to females, who show a more rectangular muscle. Similarly, sprinters show thicker and more rectangular muscles, compared to endurance runners. These findings suggest that the functional anatomy of the rectus abdominis muscle could differ depending on sex and running discipline, pointing to potential differences in biomechanics and respiratory performance. This novel approach opens the door to further exploration of in vivo muscle morphology and its implications in physiology applied not only to sports science, but also in clinical settings.

title: The diminishing returns of distance: Computational analysis of approach-avoidance behavior under threat of predation.
authors: Howlett JR, Simmons AN, Harlé KM, Stout DM.
abstract: Foraging under threat of predation is a paradigmatic scenario involving the interplay between approach and avoidance motivation across species. Previous foraging paradigms in humans have revealed aspects of approach-avoidance behavior and its neural underpinnings, but have generally involved simple choices such as a binary decision to stay or flee. Here, we present results from 40 adult participants who completed the Weighing Opportunity and Loss in Foraging (WOLF) task, a novel two-dimensional foraging context with threat of predation in which participants choose from five possible actions at each turn. We fit computational models in which choices depend on the subjective utility of each option, which itself depends on approach motivation (resource richness) and avoidance motivation (predator distance). Model comparison revealed that an inverse power law model, in which the marginal subjective utility of additional distance from the wolf diminished with wolf distance, outperformed a linear model. Model parameters explained more than 75% of the variance in task performance, mediated by the average resource richness of choices (for the approach-related parameter) and the number of deaths on the task (for the avoidance-related parameters). An exploratory analysis found that self-reported anxious arousal was associated with a more linear relationship between wolf distance and avoidance motivation. The results demonstrate that a behaviorally rich foraging paradigm in which participants select from multiple options at each turn can enable explicit modeling of subjective utilities in the interplay between approach and avoidance motivation. Future work can examine neural underpinnings of complex approach-avoidance behavior and their alteration in mental health disorders.

title: The complementary-competitive interplay of consumer information search and experience sharing: Implications for targeted advertising and firm performance.
authors: Dan W, Jiang Z.
abstract: The proliferation of targeted media platforms enables firms to deliver tailored advertising to specific consumer segments, yet the heterogeneous influences of pre-purchase information search and post-purchase sharing on targeted advertising performance remain underexplored in extant research. This paper constructs a two-period symmetric duopoly game model with fully rational firms and consumers to analyze theoretical associations between two distinct consumer information behaviors and firms' equilibrium advertising and profit outcomes. We set homogeneous products, symmetric competitors, and two types of consumers (loyal buyers and comparison shoppers) to explore the strategic interplay of corporate advertising, pricing and consumer information activities. This model adopts a differentiated search cost framework: digital information access incurs zero monetary expenses, yet endogenous cognitive information overload creates non-negligible mental frictions. Search intensity s is the consumer's generic choice variable; s* denotes the endogenous equilibrium search intensity solved from consumer utility maximization (not an exogenous primitive parameter), which lies within interior range (0,1) rather than corner solution s=1. Experience‑sharing intensity e is treated as an exogenous symmetric parameter for analytical tractability. Model-derived predictions are summarized as follows: (1) Consumer information search acts as a complementary force for targeted ads by lowering information frictions, lifting conversion rates and raising equilibrium profitability within valid parameter ranges; (2)Experience sharing generates dual competitive effects: moderate peer reviews expand market awareness, while excessive price-related sharing intensifies cross-brand price rivalry and suppress firm returns; (3) The joint interaction of search and sharing shapes equilibrium advertising intensity: optimal ad spending falls as primitive cognitive‑friction parameters shift to raise endogenous equilibrium search intensity s*, and firms need context-dependent strategies to cope with consumer sharing. Theoretically, this work unifies pre-purchase search and post-purchase sharing into a single dynamic duopoly framework to fill research gaps that separate the two consumer behaviors. Practically, the model provides neutral theoretical insights; tentative suggestions for advertising‑message content represent directions for future empirical testing rather than formal model outputs. All theoretical conclusions derived in this paper hold only within the feasible interior-equilibrium parameter domain defined in Text S2.9. Numerical simulation figures serve purely as numerically illustrated examples; formal mathematical proofs are provided in the appendices. All conclusions are mathematical predictions derived under preset model assumptions, rather than empirically validated causal relationships.

title: Temporary percutaneous trans-tibiofibular K-wire stabilization of selected unstable ankle fractures.
authors: Overgaard AF, Bloch T, Dreyer CH.

title: TRPM7 modulates endothelial cell functions and VEGFA-associated signaling in diabetic foot.
authors: Cheng Y, Jia L, Sheng L, Han X, Zhao Y.
abstract: Background Endothelial dysfunction is a central contributor to the development of diabetic foot complications. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying impaired vascular endothelial cell (VEC) function in diabetic foot remain incompletely understood.
