Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 7 (TRPM7) is implicated in cardiovascular pathology, yet its role in diabetic foot-related endothelial impairment is unclear. Methods Primary VECs were isolated from foot vascular tissues obtained from control participants and patients with DFUs and identified by CD31 and factor VIII immunofluorescence. Proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and in vitro tube formation were quantitatively assessed. TRPM7 was overexpressed in control-derived VECs and knocked down using shRNA in DFU-derived VECs. TRPM7 expression and VEGFA-AKT-ERK-related proteins were evaluated using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) concentrations in conditioned culture supernatants were measured by ELISA. Results Compared with control-derived VECs, DFU-derived VECs exhibited reduced proliferation, migration, and tube formation, together with increased apoptosis and elevated conditioned-supernatant AGE and iNOS protein concentrations. TRPM7 expression was higher in DFU-derived VECs. TRPM7 overexpression in control-derived VECs induced a dysfunctional cellular phenotype, whereas TRPM7 knockdown in DFU-derived VECs partially restored proliferation, migration, and tube formation and reduced apoptosis. TRPM7 manipulation was also accompanied by changes in VEGFA expression and AKT and ERK phosphorylation, indicating an association between TRPM7 status and dysregulated VEGFA-AKT-ERK-related signaling. Conclusion In primary human VEC cultures, increased TRPM7 expression was associated with impaired endothelial proliferation, migration, and tube formation and with altered VEGFA-related AKT/ERK signaling. This supporting TRPM7 as a candidate regulator of endothelial dysfunction under diabetic-foot-related conditions.

title: TFCdetector: Multivariable time series anomaly detection with time-frequency constraints.
authors: Fan J, Zhao J, Ma J, Cai Y.
abstract: The multivariate time series collected from numerous sensors exhibit complex interwoven relationships, arising from both the coupling among different components and the temporal dependencies of fluctuations within each component. Disentangling these relationships remains a persistent challenge for the time series community. Existing reconstruction-based methods attempt to unravel the intertwined relationships through sequence decomposition and multi-scale modeling. However, the decomposed components remain mixtures of complex latent factors. Moreover, most methods overlook anomalies present in the training set, which inadvertently causes the model to develop a certain affinity toward anomalous patterns. To address these limitations, we propose TFCdetector. Motivated by the intrinsic properties of anomalies, TFCdetector leverages time-frequency domain analysis to explicitly suppress the model's representation learning of anomalies across diverse granularities and components. To further constrain the model's learning of anomalies, we propose an energy-correlation constraint loss that operates on both segment-level energy and sequence-level correlation. Notably, the adaptively updated memory storage block enhances the expression of normal patterns by leveraging the affinity between normal patterns in the input sequence and the memory storage block. Furthermore, the meticulously designed twin frequency attention enables the model to dynamically select local or global frequency information beneficial for the task. Extensive experiments on 1 synthetic dataset and 7 real-world datasets show that TFCdetector achieves competitive results in multivariate time series detection tasks.The implementation code is available at https://github.com/FanJY3/TFCdetector.

title: Surgical Resection of a Rapidly Enlarging Endotracheal Schwannoma under Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Support: A Case Report.
authors: Yasuda R, Kubouchi Y, Yasuda S, Ishii H, Futagoishi S, Yamasaki M, Nozaka Y, Fujiwara W, Matsui S, Kidokoro Y, Tanaka Y.
abstract: Introduction Primary tracheal schwannoma is an extremely rare benign tumor, and despite its typical slow growth, it can cause life-threatening airway obstruction as it enlarges. We report a case of an endotracheal schwannoma that exhibited rapid enlargement during the preoperative waiting period. The tumor was safely resected with veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-V ECMO) support because of the risk of complete airway obstruction. Case presentation A 73-year-old woman presented with hemoptysis. CT revealed a broad-based endotracheal tumor measuring 11 × 9 × 14 mm that was located 30 mm proximal to the carina. Bronchoscopic biopsy suggested benign schwannoma. The patient returned with worsening dyspnea and increased cough 2 weeks later. Follow-up CT showed rapid enlargement of the tumor to 17 × 12 × 21 mm, leaving a residual airway diameter of 4.2 mm. Given the risk of ventilation failure during the induction of general anesthesia, V-V ECMO was established while the patient was awake under local anesthesia. After adequate extracorporeal gas exchange was confirmed, general anesthesia was induced, followed by orotracheal intubation. Through a median sternotomy, the cervical and upper mediastinal trachea was exposed. The tumor-bearing tracheal segment was circumferentially resected, and primary end-to-end anastomosis was performed. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient remained recurrence-free at 12 months after surgery. Conclusions Although benign tracheal schwannomas are generally slow-growing, rapid enlargement can occur and potentially cause life-threatening airway obstruction. In patients with severe tracheal obstruction, planned establishment of V-V ECMO before induction of general anesthesia may provide an additional margin of safety during airway management and tracheal reconstruction.

title: Segmental phase angle as predictor of activities of daily living and muscle health in patients with osteoporotic fracture A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Ito Y, Yoshimura Y, Nagano F, Matsumoto A.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to determine whether the segmental phase angle is associated with clinical outcomes such as activities of daily living (ADL), muscle strength, and skeletal muscle mass in patients with osteoporotic fractures. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with osteoporotic fractures admitted to convalescent rehabilitation wards. The primary outcome was a Functional Independence Measure motor (FIM-motor) score at discharge, and secondary outcomes were handgrip strength and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) at discharge. Multivariate analysis was used to adjust for confounders and to examine the association between segmental phase angle and outcome. Results A total of 115 subjects (97 women, age 81.0 ± 10.0 years) were included in the study. The median baseline phase angle was 3.6°. Multiple regression analysis adjusted for confounders showed that arm phase angle was independently positively associated with handgrip strength (β=0.250, P Conclusions The leg phase angle was associated with ADL, muscle strength, and skeletal muscle mass in patients with osteoporotic fractures at discharge. Segmental phase angle may be a useful indicator for considering intervention methods in patients with osteoporotic fractures.

title: Segmental Arthroscopic Hip Labral Reconstruction Using a Peroneus Longus Allograft.
authors: Kody MT, Banffy MB.
abstract: Arthroscopic hip labral reconstruction has become an important tool for treating irreparable labral pathology, particularly in the revision setting. Restoration of the acetabular labrum is critical for hip stability, load distribution, and maintenance of the joint suction seal. Segmental labral reconstruction allows focal defects to be addressed while preserving healthy native labral tissue. This technical note describes a reproducible technique for segmental labral reconstruction using a peroneus longus allograft. The use of a peroneus longus allograft provides consistent graft sizing and avoids donor-site morbidity. This technique emphasizes a stepwise approach, including appropriate patient selection, portal placement, graft preparation, controlled graft delivery, and secure fixation to restore labral function and stability. Segmental reconstruction is particularly useful for focal irreparable defects and may help restore joint mechanics and the suction seal while avoiding unnecessary circumferential reconstruction.

title: ScaffoldForge: Bioinspired generative design of 3D-printed bone scaffolds via conditional diffusion for large segmental bone defect reconstruction.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhang H, Yang H.
abstract: We present ScaffoldForge, a 3D conditional diffusion framework for the generative design of bone scaffolds. ScaffoldForge maps a set of standardized trabecular descriptors (bone volume fraction BV/TV, trabecular thickness Tb.Th, trabecular spacing Tb.Sp, trabecular number Tb.N, connectivity density Conn.D, structure model index SMI, degree of anisotropy DA, and permeability k) to a 3D scaffold architecture in a single forward pass. A multi-objective conditioning mechanism couples these descriptors through adaptive instance normalization, and a physics-constrained loss adds empirical penalties for stiffness, manufacturing feasibility, and perfusion, evaluated on the denoiser's reconstruction of the clean scaffold so that the penalties carry gradient. To address the scarcity of paired geometry-property data, we describe a procedural pipeline whose generated scaffolds reproduce the morphometric distributions of real micro-CT references. In an in silico evaluation on three benchmark datasets, ScaffoldForge attains an estimated 56.6 MPa compressive strength (8.2% over topology optimization; paired t-test, p = 0.043, n = 5 seeds) and reduces design-time cost from 8,400-12 seconds per design, a 700× speedup. Generated structures are diverse rather than memorized, and morphometric accuracy holds across all seven shape descriptors. Three analyses probe the reliability of these results given the small training corpus. Equivalence testing replaces the earlier argument from non-significant difference tests: the procedural and real descriptor distributions are equivalent at a medium margin of 0.5 standard deviations for all seven descriptors, but the 50 available real reference volumes cannot establish equivalence at a strict 0.3-standard-deviation margin for five of them. A classifier two-sample test shows that generated scaffolds retain a measurable but shrinking signature of the procedural generator. Enlarging the corpus from 250 to 2,050 scaffolds leaves in-distribution accuracy nearly unchanged while reducing the cross-dataset descriptor error on unseen anatomy from 0.079 to 0.058, which localizes the cost of the small corpus in generalization rather than in fit. We further illustrate a CT-to-scaffold pipeline for personalized generation. All results are computational; physical, biological, manufacturing, and regulatory validation remain future work.

title: Rural and Urban Hospitals Demonstrate Different Patterns of Declining Inpatient Arthroplasty Volume, 2013-2023.
authors: Byrne AR, Pachipala K, Cecere RA, Follett LY, Sarpong NO.
abstract: Background Total joint arthroplasty has shifted rapidly from inpatient to outpatient settings. We evaluated whether inpatient Medicare arthroplasty volume changed differently across rural and urban hospitals from 2013 to 2023. Methods Medicare Inpatient Hospitals-by Provider and Service files were analyzed. Hospitals with reportable Medicare Severity Diagnosis-Related Group 469/470 volume were classified as urban (Rural-Urban Commuting Area 1-3) or rural (Rural-Urban Commuting Area 4-10). A two-way fixed-effects model with hospital and year fixed effects assessed rural-urban differences in volume change using 2013 as reference. Persistence of reportable inpatient volume was evaluated among hospitals observed in 2013. Results The cohort included 25,002 hospital-year observations across 2911 hospitals. The mean volume declined from 203 to 59 cases at urban hospitals and from 84 to 37 at rural hospitals between 2013 and 2023. Rural hospitals had greater relative declines before 2020, but the association reversed thereafter; rural × year difference-in-differences estimates were +63.4 cases in 2020, +104.2 in 2021, +118.3 in 2022, and +121.0 in 2023 (all P P Conclusions Inpatient arthroplasty declined substantially in both settings. Urban hospitals remaining observable experienced larger post-2020 volume declines, whereas rural hospitals were more likely to disappear from the reportable inpatient dataset. These patterns suggest different geographic manifestations of the national transition away from inpatient arthroplasty.

title: Robotic navigation strategies for PFNA fixation: impact on one-time guide pin success rate and anteversion angle accuracy - a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Huang YY, Tang GX, Chen YF, Li HL, Huang B, Chen WM, He LX.
abstract: This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of three navigation strategies (full robotic navigation, robotic navigation for the main nail only with freehand anteversion, and conventional freehand technique) in PFNA fixation for intertrochanteric fractures, analyzed factors affecting anteversion angle accuracy, and quantified the learning curve of robot-assisted surgery. A retrospective review was conducted on 121 intertrochanteric fracture cases managed with PFNA. We categorized patients into three groups by navigation strategy: G1 (double navigation, n = 41), G2 (single navigation, n = 40), and G3 (non-navigation, n = 40). Perioperative parameters (fluoroscopy time span, total fluoroscopy times, number of attempts, visible intraoperative blood loss, etc.) were compared among groups. The main metric assessed was the attempt frequency for anteversion determination (reflecting one-time success rate). Within G1, Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression explored the associations between anteversion error and medullary canal diameter, as well as fluoroscopy times for main nail insertion. Curve estimation was used to evaluate learning curves for fluoroscopy time span and main nail insertion time. Baseline characteristics were similar across the three groups, with no significant differences (P > 0.05). The number of attempts to determine anteversion in G1 (1.22 ± 0.48) was significantly lower than in G2 (4.30 ± 2.49) and G3 (3.98 ± 1.93) (both P < 0.001). Regarding overall surgical efficiency, fluoroscopy time span in G1 (65.95 ± 8.71 min) was 12.0 min shorter (15.4% reduction, P < 0.05) than in G3 (77.93 ± 29.98 min), total fluoroscopy times (40.63 ± 7.89) were 16.3 fewer (28.6% reduction, P < 0.001); visible intraoperative blood loss (99.8 ± 91.2 mL) was 119.5 mL less (54.5% reduction, P < 0.001), and blood transfusion volume (0.73 ± 1.45 units) was significantly lower than in G3 (2.14 ± 1.72 units, P = 0.002). Compared with G2, G1 also showed significantly reduced fluoroscopy time span, total fluoroscopy times, and visible intraoperative blood loss (all P < 0.05). Main nail insertion time in G2 (43.78 ± 6.94 min) was significantly longer than in G3 (34.65 ± 17.59 min, P = 0.002), whereas G1 (37.80 ± 6.43 min) was not significantly different from G3. Within G1, anteversion error showed a strong negative correlation with medullary canal diameter (r = - 0.807, P < 0.001). Multiple regression identified medullary canal diameter as the only independent predictor of anteversion error (β = - 0.781, P < 0.001). Learning curve analysis demonstrated a marked reduction in fluoroscopy time span with robotic case order (R² = 0.644, P < 0.001), with the quadratic model providing the best fit. Full robotic navigation (double navigation) significantly improves anteversion-angle positioning efficiency (fewer attempts), reduces fluoroscopy time span and exposure frequency (suggesting lower radiation exposure), and decreases visible intraoperative blood loss. However, anteversion accuracy still depends on patient anatomy, particularly medullary canal diameter, necessitating consideration during preoperative planning. Moreover, the learning curve showed rapid early improvement, followed by a gradual plateau.

title: Reply to "High hazard ratios of fracture in gout".
authors: Doo JH, Yu J, Ghang B, Park SM.

title: Repetitive stress injury and burnout among radiology PACS Users: A Cross-Sectional departmental study.
authors: Schranz AL, Patino P, Ammar A, Peddle S, Fleming N, Harisinghani M, Thornhill R, Dos Santos MP.
abstract: Objective Poor workstation ergonomics increase the risk of work-related musculoskeletal symptoms and may contribute to adverse health outcomes among radiologists. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and types of work-related musculoskeletal symptoms among radiologists within our department, identify ergonomic deficiencies, and explore associations between symptom burden and physician burnout. Methods Data were collected through an anonymous REB-approved survey distributed to faculty, residents, and fellows in our radiology department. We collected demographic data and answers to the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire and the Abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory. Multivariate linear regression was performed with total musculoskeletal symptom burden as the dependent variable, while predictors included demographic and burnout variables. Results The departmental response rate was 61 %. Seventy-four percent of respondents reported at least one work-related musculoskeletal symptom, with neck and upper back pain being the most common. Of those affected, 85 % believed their workstation worsened their condition. Additionally, 79 % noted a component of their hospital workstation had been broken in the past year, and 87 % had never received formal ergonomic training. While 52 % responded that their musculoskeletal symptoms contributed to burnout, on multivariate analysis, work-related musculoskeletal symptom burden was significantly associated with higher emotional exhaustion (p = 0.02), with each unit increase in emotional exhaustion score associated with a 4.1-point increase in symptom burden. Conclusion Work-related musculoskeletal symptoms are highly prevalent among radiology PACS users, highlighting a critical occupational health issue. The association between musculoskeletal symptom and emotional exhaustion underscores the need for further research examining whether ergonomic interventions and training may help improve physician well-being and mitigate physician burnout.

title: Remnant preservation and stump suturing in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction reduce tibial tunnel widening without compromising tunnel placement: A computed tomography-based randomised controlled trial.
authors: El-Desouky M, Elkalyoby AS, Rashwan AS, Gaballah AI, Abdelrazek BH.
abstract: Purpose Tunnel widening remains a concern following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction because it may adversely affect graft incorporation and complicate revision surgery. Remnant preservation has been proposed as a strategy to reduce tunnel widening, but its effect on postoperative tunnel remodelling remains uncertain. This study aimed to determine whether remnant preservation with tibial stump suturing reduces tunnel widening without compromising tunnel placement accuracy. Methods In this prospective randomised controlled trial, 179 patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction were randomised to remnant-preserving reconstruction with tibial stump suturing ( n = 88) or conventional stump resection ( n = 91). Standardised three-dimensional computed tomography was performed at 2 weeks and 1 year postoperatively. Tibial and femoral tunnel widening were calculated as the percentage change in tunnel diameter between scans, and tunnel placement accuracy was assessed using the computed tomography-based quadrant method. The incidence of clinically significant tunnel widening (>20%) was also compared. Results Baseline tunnel diameters were comparable between groups. At 1-year follow-up, remnant-preserving ACL reconstruction resulted in significantly less tibial tunnel widening than stump resection (14.58 ± 4.49% vs. 19.74 ± 4.36%, p 20%) (11.4% vs. 25.3%; relative risk, 0.45; p = 0.016). Femoral tunnel widening was similar between groups (18.23 ± 2.92% vs. 18.35 ± 2.59%, p = 0.766). No clinically relevant differences in tunnel placement were observed between groups. Conclusion Remnant-preserving ACL reconstruction with tibial stump suturing selectively reduces tibial tunnel widening at 12 months without compromising anatomic tunnel placement accuracy. These findings support the use of remnant preservation when preservation of tibial tunnel integrity is a surgical consideration. Level of evidence Level I. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07236593; registration date: November 15, 2025 (retrospectively registered).

title: Radial head arthroplasty restores axial construct stiffness in a Monteggia-like injury model: a biomechanical study.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Weber MM, Hockmann JP, Rosenkranz TA, Leschinger T, Müller LP, Rausch V.
abstract: Introduction Monteggia-like lesions are rare but complex elbow injuries involving fractures of both the proximal ulna and the radial head. While the influence of ulnar alignment and soft tissue integrity on radial head stability has been extensively studied, the effect of radial head integrity on the stability of ulnar fixation remains poorly understood. Given the high rates of nonunion and revision surgery after proximal ulna fractures, improved understanding of forearm biomechanics in these combined injuries is highly clinically relevant as it influences the surgical strategy in primary care of these injuries. Accordingly, this study aimed to evaluate the biomechanical impact of radial head resection and radial head arthroplasty on forearm stiffness in a simulated Monteggia-like injury model. We hypothesized that radial head resection would reduce construct stiffness compared with both the native state and radial head arthroplasty, and that arthroplasty would partially restore stiffness toward native levels MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eight fresh-frozen human cadaveric elbow specimens were biomechanically tested under axial loading. After baseline testing in the native state, a standardized segmental comminution model was created and stabilized using locking plate osteosynthesis. Sequential testing was then performed after radial head resection and after implantation of a modular radial head prosthesis. Specimens were loaded cyclically up to 450 N for 1,000 cycles with the elbow positioned at 30° of flexion. Construct stiffness was calculated and compared between testing conditions. Results Mean construct stiffness in the native state was 49.3 ± 4.29 N/mm and decreased significantly after creation and fixation of the ulnar defect (36.05 ± 6.71 N/mm). Radial head resection resulted in a further significant reduction in stiffness (25.83 ± 6.65 N/mm). Following radial head arthroplasty, stiffness increased to 33.8 ± 7.89 N/mm, representing a significant improvement compared with the resection state (p ≤ 0.0026). No significant difference was observed between stiffness after prosthesis implantation and the condition with intact radial head and stabilized ulna. Conclusion Radial head integrity significantly contributes to forearm stiffness in Monteggia-like lesions. Radial head arthroplasty partially restores biomechanical stability after resection and may alter load distribution in a manner that could be relevant for fixation durability. These findings support the need to address the radial column to optimize stability in complex elbow injuries. Level of evidence Biomechanical study.

title: Quantifying laparoscopic camera workspace and kinematics during robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.
authors: Pereira SG, Morais P, Queirós S, Rocha F, Rodrigues N, Quintelas A, Lima E, Vilaça JL.
abstract: Robotic surgery has grown significantly in recent years because, in addition to high precision, the most technologically advanced systems provide surgeons with a high-quality three-dimensional (3D) view. Although studies on autonomous camera control are beginning to emerge, there are still limited data on laparoscopic camera motion, including its kinematics and workspace requirements during surgery. Therefore, this study aims to quantify the 3D workspace and motion metrics, including speed and absolute tangential acceleration, of the laparoscopic camera during robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). This single-centre observational study included ten RARP procedures performed by two surgeons using the da Vinci Xi system (Intuitive Surgical, CA, USA). Camera motion was recorded using a Polaris Vega optical tracking system (NDI, ON, Canada). A reference marker fixed to the robotic platform defined the local coordinate system, and a second marker was attached to the top of the camera. At the end of each surgery, a postoperative calibration was performed to determine the camera-tip position relative to the camera marker. Workspace and motion metrics were computed from valid samples across each recording and within individual surgical phases. Cleaning intervals and periods of marker occlusion or tracking interference were excluded from the analysis. Median valid tracking duration was 36.6 (32.1-63.3) min, with a median valid-sample coverage of 58.2 (38.6-67.9)%. The median complete-procedure workspace bounding-box volume was 356.56 (259.49-791.42) cm³, whereas the median convex-hull volume was 104.35 (81.06-219.51) cm³. The largest phase-specific workspace was observed during vesicourethral anastomosis, whereas the smallest was observed during endopelvic fascia incision. Motion metrics were comparatively consistent across surgical phases. This study quantified the laparoscopic camera workspace and characterized its motion during real RARP procedures, providing preliminary quantitative data to support the development of future autonomous robotic camera-control systems for RARP.

title: Preoperative Frailty as a Predictor of Quality of Life Outcomes Following Cytoreductive Surgery.
authors: Bai Z, Barker L, Shahab R, Koh C, Solomon M, Alexander K, Karunaratne S, Ansari N, Pereira LSM, Lage APD, Steffens D.
abstract: Background Frailty has emerged as a critical determinant of postoperative risk in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS + HIPEC). However, its impact on postoperative quality of life (QoL) remains underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative frailty and postoperative QoL in patients undergoing CRS + HIPEC. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent CRS + HIPEC at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital between May 2017 and June 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), with patients classified as frail (CFS ≥ 4) or non-frail (CFS Results Of the 364 included patients, 49 (13.5%) were classified as frail. Frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes, particularly in mobility, self-care, usual activities, and physical component summary (PCS) scores (all p ≤ 0.003) at baseline. These impairments persisted at three and 6 months postoperatively. Pain and discomfort also emerged as significant issues for frail patients at both three- and 6-months following surgery (p = 0.018 and p = 0.005, respectively). Older frail patients (≥ 65 years) experienced significantly greater impairments in self-care and usual activities at 6 months postoperatively, along with lower mental health summary (MCS) scores at 12 months compared to the non-frail group. Conclusions Preoperative frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes following CRS + HIPEC, highlighting the importance of routine frailty screening and prehabilitation strategies to optimize outcomes in vulnerable patients.

title: Patients Undergoing Proximal Hamstring Repair Have High Rates of Return to Work and Favorable Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
authors: Bindra A, Gillinov SM, Girardi KG, Lord KT, Kodra JD, Lee MS, Atadja L, Norman MB, Moran J, Surucu S, Jimenez AE.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate return-to-work (RTW) rates and functional outcomes after surgical repair of proximal hamstring tendon avulsion injuries. Methods This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews. PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Scopus were searched in April 2025 for studies reporting RTW outcomes after surgical repair of proximal hamstring avulsions. Eligible studies involved human subjects undergoing open or endoscopic repair and reporting RTW rates or patient counts. No minimum follow-up duration was required. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, with discrepancies resolved by a third. Study quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies criteria. Results Six studies (229 patients) met inclusion criteria. Four studies reported an overall RTW rate ranging from 89% to 100%, whereas 2 studies stratified outcomes by Workers' Compensation (WC) status, showing lower RTW rates among WC patients (70.0%-86.3%) compared with non-WC patients (92.5%-94.1%). Return-to-sport rates, when reported, ranged from 58% to 100%. Study-level RTW and return-to-sport outcomes were summarized descriptively without pooled estimates because of heterogeneity in study design, surgical approach, injury chronicity, WC status, and outcome definitions. Complication rates were low overall, with retear or reoperation occurring in 0% to 5.8% of cases. Clinically relevant patient improvement thresholds were only reported in 1 study. Conclusions In this study, most patients undergoing surgical repair for proximal hamstring avulsion injuries return to work with favorable functional outcomes and low complication rates. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

title: Patient experiences with a prescription-based digital health application (DiGA) for knee disorders: a qualitative study in german orthopaedic care.
authors: Burgert S, Raab N, Kornfeld T, Knitza J, Boy K, Schwarz J, May S, Heinze M, Mühlensiepen F.
abstract: Background Musculoskeletal disorders are among the leading causes of chronic pain, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life worldwide. Prescription-based digital health applications (DiGAs) have the potential to improve outpatient care, enhance treatment adherence, and address structural challenges such as shortages in physiotherapy services. However, real-world evidence on the use of DiGAs from the patient perspective in orthopaedic settings within the German healthcare context remains limited. This study aimed to explore acceptance, perceived potential, and challenges associated with DiGA use among patients with knee joint disorders. Methods An exploratory qualitative study was conducted at an academic outpatient clinic for orthopaedics and trauma surgery in Germany. Ten adult patients (aged 18-65 years) with anterior cruciate ligament rupture or meniscal injury and a prescribed DiGA ("Orthopy") were recruited. Semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted at the time of prescription (n = 10) and approximately two to three weeks later (n = 6; one follow-up interview took place after twelve weeks). All four participants who withdrew completed a dropout questionnaire. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis according to Kuckartz. Main categories were derived deductively from the research question; subcategories were developed inductively from the data. Baseline and follow-up interviews of the six completing participants were compared within and across cases. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected to contextualise findings. Trustworthiness was supported by iterative coding, an intra-coder consistency check, and team discussion of the coding frame. Coding was performed by a single researcher. Results Participants were generally open to using the DiGA and valued its flexibility, location independence, and its role in bridging gaps in physiotherapy. The DiGA was primarily perceived as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for conventional therapy. Perceived key strengths included structured exercise guidance, educational content, and easy integration into daily routines, particularly in prehabilitation. Challenges included limited personalisation, insufficient adaptation of feedback, and limited motivational benefit when the app was used without accompanying professional guidance. Additional barriers comprised administrative delays in activation, usability issues among less digitally literate users, and insufficient physician guidance. Data privacy concerns played a minor role. Interviewed participants did not report serious safety concerns during the short observation period. Conclusions Participants perceived the DiGA as a suitable complement to physiotherapy in orthopaedic care, particularly for prehabilitation and continuity of care. Better personalisation, usability, and integration into existing care structures could further enhance its perceived value. Long-term adherence, clinical effectiveness, safety, and sustainable implementation remain to be established. Future research should address these questions and patient-centred design. Trial registration The study was registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00036514) on 10 April 2025, after data collection had begun in January 2025 (retrospective registration).

title: Parathyroid Surgery After Kidney Transplantation: Operative Extent, Biochemical Outcomes, and Early Morbidity in a Contemporary Single-Center Series.
authors: Virga A, Kovács DÁ, Markóth C, Barna S, Andrási M, Tóth D, Győry FB.
abstract: Background Persistent hyperparathyroidism after kidney transplantation, especially with hypercalcemia, is associated with adverse allograft outcomes. We described operative extent, early morbidity, and follow-up calcium-PTH patterns. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 10 patients with a history of kidney transplantation who underwent parathyroid surgery during 2017-2025, including 1 receiving dialysis. Outcomes were summarized descriptively without inferential comparison. Results Eight patients underwent limited parathyroidectomy (7 single-gland and 1 two-gland), and 2 underwent total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation. One limited procedure was a reoperation. A decrease in intraoperative PTH of at least 50% occurred at 10 or 30 minutes in 4 of 9 evaluable patients and at 30 minutes in 3 of 9. At approximately 1-year follow-up, 3 of 8 limited-resection patients had concurrent hypercalcemia and elevated PTH, 4 had isolated PTH elevation, and 1 had calcium and PTH within the reference intervals. Neither total-procedure patient had hypercalcemia or PTH elevation; 1 had calcium below the lower reference limit and the other had PTH below the lower reference limit. Early hypocalcemia occurred after both total procedures and no limited procedure; hypocalcemia was prolonged in 1 patient. No recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, confirmed cervical hematoma, reoperation for bleeding, surgical-site infection, or 30-day mortality occurred. Conclusions In this small heterogeneous series, early hypocalcemia occurred only after total procedures, with a prolonged course in 1 patient. Follow-up calcium-PTH patterns varied across patients and renal-function states. These observations do not establish the superiority of either operative strategy.

title: Pancreatic Acinar Cell Carcinoma in a Patient with Familial Adenomatous Polyposis Who Achieved Long-Term Survival after Repeated Resection of Liver Metastases: A Case Report.
authors: Takahashi A, Ogura T, Yamada N, Kumano K, Fujinuma I, Kanda H, Takahashi A.
abstract: Introduction Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma (PACC) is a rare exocrine pancreatic neoplasm that differs from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in its histogenetic origin and oncological behavior. Although recurrence is common after curative-intent resection, the optimal management of recurrent PACC remains undefined. Furthermore, although a certain number of pancreatic tumors have been reported in association with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), the relationship with PACC in particular remains poorly understood. The present case may help address this issue. Case presentation At age 22, the patient underwent distal pancreatectomy for a pancreatic tumor, which was diagnosed as PACC. A local recurrence occurred in the fourth postoperative year and achieved complete response with chemotherapy. From the tenth postoperative year onward, the patient developed repeated liver metastases, for which a total of 5 hepatectomies were performed; the patient has remained recurrence-free for 72 months since the last surgery. During the clinical course, a pathogenic adenomatous polyposis coli ( APC ) variant was identified, leading to a definitive diagnosis of FAP. Conclusions We experienced a case in which an aggressive surgical approach-repeated hepatectomy for multiple recurrent liver metastases from PACC-achieved long-term recurrence-free survival. This supports active surgical resection as a viable strategy for PACC liver metastases. Furthermore, this rare case of PACC arising in a patient with FAP also raises the hypothesis that the APC/β-catenin pathway may be biologically involved in PACC tumorigenesis; however, a single case cannot establish an epidemiological association between FAP and PACC incidence, and further investigation is warranted.

title: Obesity and perioperative outcomes of robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Gong J, Zhang M, Chen Y, Yang M, Jia X.
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer in obese versus non-obese patients, as classified in the source studies. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for comparative studies of robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer. Obesity was defined as BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² according to each study. The included data were not uniformly restricted to BMI < 40 kg/m²; consequently, the analysis does not represent class I-II obesity alone. Eight retrospective studies involving 1,879 patients were included. No statistically significant differences were detected in operative time (MD, - 9.02 min; 95% CI, - 21.25 to 3.20; p = 0.15), estimated blood loss (MD, 35.69 mL; 95% CI, - 40.54 to 111.93; p = 0.36), or length of stay (MD, - 0.25 days; 95% CI, - 0.61 to 0.10; p = 0.16). Pooled complication estimates were also nonsignificant. These findings do not establish equivalent safety. In the included retrospective studies, obesity as classified by the original reports was not associated with statistically significant differences in the assessed perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted surgery. The estimates are imprecise and potentially confounded; they do not establish equivalence or demonstrate superiority over other surgical approaches.

title: No significant differences between large language model prompting strategies and human experts in summarisation of 'the formal EU-US meniscus rehabilitation consensus: An ESSKA-AOSSM-AASPT Initiative'.
authors: Lindskog J, Öttl F, Yu Y, Paterno MV, Giordano A, Rambaud A, Prill R, Królikowska A, Samuelsson K, Hamrin Senorski E.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the interpretive and applicative performance of three conditions applied to the formal EU-US, ESSKA-AOSSM-AASPT consensus on meniscus rehabilitation: (1) single-pass prompting, (2) sequential chain-of-thought prompting and (3) human expert-written output. Methods This exploratory comparative study evaluated three conditions applied to two parts of the formal EU-US ESSKA-AOSSM-AASPT meniscus rehabilitation consensus: (1) single-pass prompting, (2) sequential chain-of-thought prompting using ChatGPT (GPT-5.1), Claude (Sonnet 4.5), and Gemini (3.0), and (3) human expert-written output from three collaborating human experts. For each part, three tasks were assessed: generation of summaries, application of summaries to three predefined clinical scenarios, and resistance to three predefined misinterpretation queries. Three blinded senior sports physiotherapists evaluated summary quality using five QUEST categories and rated the clinical application and misinterpretation resistance responses. Median ratings were compared using Friedman and post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Gwet's AC2 coefficient with quadratic weights was used to assess inter-rater agreement for each QUEST category and for the clinical application and misinterpretation resistance items. Results Across consensus parts, no statistically significant differences were identified between large language model prompting strategies and human expert outputs for QUEST categories, clinical application, and misinterpretation resistance queries. Sequential chain-of-thought prompting received higher numerical reviewer ratings than single-pass prompting for ChatGPT and Gemini, particularly for quality of information and trust and confidence, although differences were not statistically significant. Inter-rater agreement ranged from substantial to almost perfect (Gwet's AC2 = 0.79-0.99). Conclusion No statistically significant differences in reviewer ratings were observed between ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and human expert output, with generally high ratings for summaries and responses to clinical scenarios. Large language models may therefore represent a potential adjunct for summarisation and interpretation of sports medicine consensus recommendations to inform rehabilitation decision-making. Level of evidence Level V.

title: No significant change in urinary sodium excretion within 48h after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery: the weight LUSER study.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Henry J, Oo S, Lai C, Thakkar R, Bolckmans R, le Roux CW, Welbourn R.
abstract: Introduction Metabolic and bariatric surgery is effective in achieving remission of hypertension and metabolic disease. It is unclear whether metabolic changes within the first 48h after surgery can potentially explain underlying mechanisms of hypertension control. We aimed to assess changes in urinary sodium excretion early after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) as a potential weight-loss-independent mechanism of hypertension remission. Methods All patients undergoing primary RYGB provided a 24-h urine collection, blood pressure (BP) measurement, and blood sampling both preoperatively and 48h postoperatively. The dietary sodium content was similar at both time points. Results Twenty patients were included, of whom 16 met the minimum output urine volume criteria for 24-h urine samples. Mean patient age was 55.2 ± 7.7 years and median body mass index was 48kg/m 2 with 13 patients (65%) diagnosed with hypertension and 7 (35%) with obstructive sleep apnoea. Twenty-four-hour urine sodium excretion was similar immediately prior to surgery and 48h postoperatively (72.1 ± 44.0 vs 74.5 ± 65.2mmol/24h, p = 0.45). There was no significant difference in systolic or diastolic BP immediately prior to surgery compared with 48h postoperatively (143.3 ± 15.1 vs 135.9 ± 16.3mmHg, p = 0.09 and 79.8 ± 9.2 vs 79.9 ± 5.8mmHg, p = 0.47). Both findings were confirmed on further sensitivity analysis. Conclusion No significant change in urinary sodium excretion or BP was detected in the first 48h post RYGB in normotensive patients or those with well-controlled hypertension.

title: Modified Suture-Gripping Technique for Arthroscopic Meniscal Suturing.
authors: Sasaki R, Muroya N, Nishimura T, Hayashi T, Kaneda K, Nagashima M, Kobayashi S, Morioka H.
abstract: Meniscal preservation is essential for the maintenance of knee function. The suture-gripping technique, using a suture shuttle, enables accurate needle insertion from inside the joint and flexible withdrawal of the suture from outside the capsule, thereby facilitating meniscal repair of the anterior segment. Using a continuous suturing technique with this method is possible, and we described a modified approach. We recently recognized that ARTHRO-PIERCE, a device originally designed for hip arthroscopy, can be used to perform the same suture-gripping technique principles for meniscal repair. The ARTHRO-PIERCE has a sharper tip-when compared with a suture shuttle holding a suture at its tip-that improves penetration, a more rigid shaft that improves reach and trajectory toward the anterior horn and anterior body, and robust suture grasping without relying on a loop mechanism than a conventional suture shuttle. Here, we describe the step-by-step surgical technique. This technique expands the versatility of the suture-gripping technique for anterior meniscal suturing with improved device handling and secure suture control.

title: Modern Himalayan marmot faeces analyses: Implications for palaeodietary, palaeoecological, and palaeoclimate analysis.
authors: Basumatary SK, Singh H, Mehta M, Tripathi S, Thakkar MG, McDonald HG, van Asperen EN, Kumar V.
abstract: Pollen and nutrient analyses of the faeces of the Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) were made to understand its preferred dietary plants and ecology. Pollen preserved in the faeces accurately reflected its diet as a mixed feeder including Artemisia, Caryophyllaceae, Asteroideae, and Ephedra, characteristic plants of the Alpine steppe vegetation under a cold and arid climate in the higher Himalaya. Pollen ratio values between Artemisia/Chenopodiaceae, Artemisia/Cyperaceae, and Artemisia/Ephedra are identified from the Pensilla Pass and Rimkhim regions, as useful tools that characterize the Alpine steppe vegetation and climate in the higher Himalaya. Principal Component Analysis of the pollen taxa indicated only a slight difference in the relative abundance between the two localities sampled, Pensila Pass and Rimkhim areas. Coprophilous fungal spores, Sporormiella and Saccobolus, were abundant and considered useful for understanding the interrelationship between vegetation and the marmot's preferred habitat. Fifteen nutritional elements were recorded, and the high concentration of carbon, nitrogen, calcium, silicon, and, phosphorous is considered significant with a direct dietary relationship with the preferred plants consumed. This study provides a modern analogue and a baseline for coprolite and palaeoecological analyses in marmot inhabited regions and to observe the species future response to vegetation and climate change resulting shifts in altitude in the higher Himalaya.

title: Microbiome plasticity during the early life-stage of the angelshark (Squatina squatina) in Las Teresitas (Canary Islands).
authors: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L.
abstract: Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. In this study, we aimed to characterize shifts in the microbiome of the Critically Endangered angelshark (Squatina squatina) during the early stages of development and to assess how environmental factors contribute to the shaping of a specific microbiota. Samples from thirty-nine juvenile angelsharks were collected from Las Teresitas nursery area in the Canary Islands over one year. Skin, oral and cloacal microbiomes were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The sizes of individuals ranged between 24 and 42 cm in length. The shark microbiome was clearly distinct from the surrounding environment, indicating a unique composition from early life stages. Dominant bacteria present in the shark microbiomes included Vibrionaceae (up to 96%), Pseudoalteromonas (up to 63%), Rhodobacteraceae (up to 57%) and Alteromonadaceae (up to 20%). Seawater had a greater influence than sediment on the external skin microbiome, especially in younger individuals. This was not expected due to the burial behaviour of the species. Notably, the abundance of Pseudoalteromonadaceae (assessed by qPCR) was positively correlated with shark growth but was independent of the skin mucus. This suggests a protective role of this phylotype in younger individuals and may help in the adaptation to habitat conditions. This is the first comprehensive microbiome study in angelsharks, highlighting the importance of environmental preservation for microbial integrity and juvenile fitness.

title: Methods for Computed Tomography-Based Glenoid Bone Loss Measurement Show High Interobserver Consistency but Variable Accuracy.
authors: Nair AV, Rajan A, Veerendra K, M P, Yoo YS, Kumar BA, Rashid S, Dalapathi A, Jetty T, Sadda SR, Khan PS.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the reliability of computed tomography (CT)-based glenoid bone loss calculation methods in shoulder instability by assessing interobserver agreement using 3-dimensional virtual bone models and to identify the technique that provides the most optimal balance for clinical application. Methods Between January 2023 and June 2023, normal shoulder CT scans without evidence of instability or prior surgery were retrieved from institutional archives. Virtual anteroinferior glenoid bone defects of predefined sizes (10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, and 40%) were created on a standardized en face glenoid view using CT console-based segmentation tools, establishing a controlled reference standard. Four senior musculoskeletal radiologists independently measured glenoid bone loss on both 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional reconstructions using 4 established techniques (Sugaya, PICO, Hamamoto, and Parada). Interobserver reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and agreement with the predefined defect size was evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis. Results The PICO method showed the highest interobserver reliability (ICC = 0.995) but showed systematic overestimation with the largest mean bias (+6.93 mm) and wide limits of agreement, reflecting proportional bias. The Sugaya method showed both high reproducibility (ICC = 0.854) and minimal bias (-1.06 mm), making it the most balanced technique. The Hamamoto method showed good reliability (ICC = 0.952) but a tendency to overestimate (+4.04 mm). The Parada method showed poor reproducibility (ICC = 0.223) despite moderate accuracy (-2.85 mm). Conclusions The Sugaya method showed the most favorable combination of accuracy and interobserver reliability for CT-based glenoid bone loss measurement in a controlled virtual model. The PICO method, despite excellent interobserver consistency, showed systematic overestimation. The Hamamoto method showed acceptable reliability with moderate overestimation, whereas the Parada method showed poor reproducibility. Clinical relevance Reliable glenoid bone loss estimation is vital for surgical planning in shoulder instability. According to our study, the Sugaya method offers the most accurate and reproducible measurements, helping surgeons make better-informed decisions and avoid inappropriate procedures.

title: Mechanisms of body rotation in the discus throw: contributions of ground reaction forces and the free moment to the angular momentum of the body-discus system in male throwers.
authors: Seki K, Kikuchi S.
abstract: The angular momentum about the vertical axis is closely associated with release speed in the discus throw; however, kinetic studies remain almost nonexistent due to the methodological difficulties of measurement. The present study aimed to investigate the mechanisms underlying angular momentum generation about the vertical axis from the perspective of the ground reaction forces. Twelve elite or highly trained male right-handed discus throwers performed discus throw on force platforms while their motions were captured. The largest contributions to angular momentum were the moments of ground reaction forces (MGRF) of both feet during the first double support phase (DSP1). Furthermore, the MGRF of the right foot during DSP1 and the left foot during the first single support phase (SSP1) were correlated positively with the maximum angular momentum. The leftward shift of the system's center of mass during DSP1 effectively increased the moment arm, thereby enhancing the contribution of the MGRF to the angular momentum. During SSP1, although the contribution of the left foot MGRF was relatively smaller than that during DSP1, its correlation with the maximum angular momentum suggests that precise control of the right leg swing is crucial for minimizing the loss of angular momentum.

title: Limited-Incision Kager's Fascia Flap Coverage Versus Open Repair for Acute Achilles Tendon Rupture: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
authors: Liu C, Wang Z, Fang X, Zhang W, Zhu L, Jiang H, Tan W, Zhou M, Li Z, Yang X, Li P, Chen X, Luo S, Xie Z, Wang X.
abstract: Purpose There is ongoing debate within the medical community regarding the optimal surgical technique for repairing Achilles tendon ruptures. Therefore, this study aimed to compare a novel limited-incision Kager's fascia flap coverage technique with conventional open repair for acute Achilles tendon rupture. Methods Ninety patients surgically treated for acute closed Achilles tendon rupture between January 2017 and December 2021 were retrospectively followed, including 41 with limited-incision Kager's fascia flap coverage technique and 49 with traditional open surgical suture. Functional outcomes were evaluated at 12 months postoperatively using the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score and the Achilles Tendon Total Rupture Score (ATRS). Color Doppler ultrasound examination of Achilles tendon blood supply was performed at 3 months postoperatively to assess hemodynamic parameters. To evaluate the influence of age on outcomes, patients were divided into ≥ 50 years and Results The limited-incision Kager's fascia flap coverage group demonstrated superior outcomes compared with the traditional open surgery group. At 12-month follow-up, the fascia flap group had significantly higher AOFAS scores (91.43 ± 2.74 vs. 84.80 ± 2.85) and ATRS scores (94.56 ± 2.45 vs. 86.26 ± 3.15) than the control group (both p Conclusion The limited-incision Kager's fascia flap coverage technique for treating acute closed Achilles tendon ruptures shows certain efficacy, improving limb function, reducing surgery-related injuries, and potentially promoting Achilles tendon healing by enhancing local blood supply at the rupture site, thereby improving clinical outcomes and outperforming traditional open surgery. Simultaneously, the technology demonstrates good efficacy across different age groups.

title: Letter to the Editor regarding "The fracture orthopedic risk of non-home discharge (FORD) score: A novel bedside predictive tool for non-home discharge in orthopedic trauma patients".
authors: Zhang R, Lu S.

title: Lateral Extra-articular Tenodesis With All-Suture Knotless Anchor.
authors: Lucina L, Tierney S, Patel RM.
abstract: Although many patients have had satisfactory outcomes from arthroscopic anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, persistent rotational instability and graft failure still occur. Therefore, the anterolateral ligament complex has been a newer focus of research. The addition of the lateral extra-articular tenodesis to augment anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction has been found to increase stabilization and reduce rerupture rates. We describe our surgical technique for performing a modified Lemaire lateral extra-articular tenodesis with an all-suture knotless anchor.

title: Late invasive breast cancer after mastectomy for incidentally detected male DCIS: recurrence or new primary?
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Elayyan R, In't Hout B, Caldon L, Ranawaka N, Oweis R.
abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) in men is rare, and its long-term behaviour is not well defined. We report a case of late invasive breast cancer more than two decades after a mastectomy for incidentally detected high-grade DCIS in a 45-year-old man. This case highlights that, although mastectomy for pure DCIS offers excellent local control, invasive occurrence of new primary or local recurrence can still occur. Ongoing awareness and follow-up may therefore be warranted even in male patients treated definitively for DCIS.

title: Laparoscopic resection "recto"pexy with natural orifice specimen extraction for recurrent full-thickness rectal prolapse following Altemeier's procedure.
authors: Tan TJK, Fu CWP.
abstract: Full-thickness external rectal prolapse recurrence after an Altemeier's procedure presents a complex surgical challenge. Redo perineal surgery risks further sphincter damage, while abdominal approaches like ventral mesh rectopexy carry mesh-related risks in extraperitonealised colons. Resection rectopexy is a viable alternative but requires careful navigation of the altered pelvic anatomy. We present a technical note and surgical video demonstrating laparoscopic resection rectopexy combined with transanal Natural Orifice Specimen Extraction (NOSE) and a single-stapled anastomosis for a recurrent prolapse 2 months post-Altemeier's. Essential technical considerations include meticulous close colonic dissection to preserve the inferior mesenteric artery and transanal extraction facilitated by a lax sphincter complex. The procedure was successfully completed with minimal blood loss (40 ml). The patient experienced an uneventful recovery, tolerating a normal diet by postoperative day 2, and was discharged on day 4. At the 6-month follow-up, there was no prolapse recurrence and faecal continence was maintained; mild stool frequency was effectively managed with low-dose anti-diarrhoeal medication. Laparoscopic resection rectopexy integrating transanal NOSE and a single-stapled anastomosis is a feasible, safe, and fully minimally invasive option. For selected, medically fit patients, it addresses the anatomical defects of recurrent prolapse following perineal procedures while minimising morbidity and anastomotic leak risks.

title: Intramedullary nailing versus locking plate fixation for proximal humerus fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authors: Dhillon J, Porter K, Ngoue M, Kirby K, Mierisch C, Hansen L, Krumrey J.
abstract: Proximal humerus fractures (PHFs) are common in the elderly and may require surgical fixation, yet controversy persists regarding the optimal technique-open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) versus intramedullary nailing. This study synthesizes high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evidence to determine the relative efficacy, safety, and functional outcomes. A systematic review was performed by searching PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Embase through February 2026. Eligible RCTs compared intramedullary nailing and plate fixation for PHFs, evaluating range of motion (ROM), strength, complications, reoperation rates, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs). Six RCTs comprising 404 PHFs were included (204 nails, 200 plates). Mean patient age was 69.3 years (nail) and 68.5 years (plate), with average follow-up of 30.6 months. There were no significant differences between intramedullary nailing and locking plate fixation in DASH score (MD, -0.66; 95% CI, -11.94 to 10.62; P=.91), VAS pain (MD, -0.40; 95% CI, -0.93 to 0.13; P=.14), Constant score (MD, 1.33; 95% CI, -2.72 to 5.37; P=.52), or ASES score (MD, 0.74; 95% CI, -5.25 to 6.74; P=.81). Complication rates (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.21-2.25; P=.53) and reoperation rates (RR, 1.5; 95% CI, 0.49-4.59; P=.48) were also not significantly different between fixation methods. In a post hoc fracture-type analysis, nail fixation was associated with higher Constant scores in 3- and 4-part fractures (MD, 6.87; 95% CI, 3.02-10.73; P=.0005), whereas no significant difference was observed in 2-part fractures (MD, -2.43; 95% CI, -5.32 to 0.46; P=.10). Intramedullary nailing and locking plate fixation provide no statistically significant difference in functional and clinical outcomes for PHFs. Complication and reoperation rates varied across studies, with no significant pooled differences between fixation methods. Further high-quality randomized studies are needed to clarify whether specific patient or fracture subgroups may benefit from one fixation strategy over the other.

title: Hemiarthroplasty with a long femoral stem and proximal cement augmentation for a myeloma-related pathological femoral neck fracture: a case report.
authors: Shang Z, Wu C, Liu J.
abstract: Background Pathological femoral neck fractures are a frequent skeletal complication of multiple myeloma due to extensive osteolytic bone destruction. However, extensive proximal femoral invasion with massive cavitary destruction leading to femoral neck fracture is clinically uncommon, and optimal surgical management remains challenging because of poor bone quality and high mechanical failure risk. Case presentation We report a patient with a known history of multiple myeloma who sustained a low-energy fall resulting in a pathological fracture of the right femoral neck. Imaging demonstrated diffuse osteolytic involvement of the pelvis and proximal femur with severe osteoporosis and degenerative hip changes. Given the patient's poor general condition and multiple comorbidities, a multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion involving orthopaedics, hematology, cardiology, endocrinology, and neurology was conducted to formulate an individualized perioperative strategy. Bipolar hemiarthroplasty was performed using a long femoral stem with distal press-fit fixation, combined with debridement of tumor-infiltrated tissue, proximal cement augmentation of osteolytic bone defects, and supplemental plate and cerclage cable fixation. This reconstructive strategy was selected as an alternative to proximal femoral replacement to achieve immediate mechanical stability and facilitate early mobilization. Intraoperative autologous blood salvage and reinfusion were used as part of the perioperative blood-management strategy, with no immediate procedure-related complications observed. Results The patient was followed for 15 months after surgery. At the latest follow-up, she remained ambulatory with satisfactory hip function and a Harris Hip Score of 84 points. Follow-up radiographs demonstrated stable reconstruction without prosthetic loosening, dislocation, periprosthetic fracture, or other major implant-related complications. Conclusion Hemiarthroplasty with a long femoral stem, proximal cement augmentation, and supplemental fixation may represent a viable option for selected patients with multiple myeloma-related pathological femoral neck fractures and extensive osteolytic destruction. Careful assessment of bone loss and individualized multidisciplinary planning are important for balancing mechanical stability and perioperative risk.

title: Healthcare providers' perceptions on barriers to the provision of psychosocial cancer care at Ocean Road Cancer Institute in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
authors: Athumani K, Dharsee N, Iseselo MK, Kiangi RH, Mkoka DA.
abstract: Background Patients with cancer experience substantial psychosocial challenges throughout the cancer journey. Psychosocial cancer care is crucial for addressing patients' psychological, emotional, social, spiritual needs, and for promoting well-being and quality of life. Despite its importance, psychosocial cancer care services remain insufficiently provided within routine cancer care services in many settings. Aim of the study To explore healthcare providers' perceptions of barriers to providing psychosocial cancer care services within routine care at a tertiary cancer hospital in Tanzania. Materials and methods This study adopted an explorative qualitative design. This study was conducted at Ocean Road Cancer Institute in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Purposeful sampling was used to recruit 18 healthcare providers until information saturation was reached. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a semi-structured interview guide. All interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using a thematic analysis approach to identify key patterns and themes. Results Three themes emerged that describe health care providers' perceptions of barriers to the provision of psychosocial cancer care. These barriers include inadequately trained healthcare providers, an unsupportive organizational structure and environment for psychosocial care services, and challenges in establishing a trusting therapeutic relationship between patients and providers. Conclusion Despite its recognized importance in promoting quality of life, the provision of psychosocial cancer care remains insufficiently provided in cancer settings. Findings from this study indicate that psychosocial care provision is limited by inadequate and incompetent staff, a lack of coordination, and an unsupportive organizational structure, and that building effective patient-provider therapeutic relationships was reported to hinder the provision of psychosocial care. To address these barriers, training, the establishment of coordinating units, and the development of protocols to guide the multidisciplinary team are essential. Integrating psychosocial care competencies into healthcare professionals' training curriculum is also essential to bridge the gap.

title: Hand fracture as a sentinel event for frailty in older adults.
authors: Bollard SM, Kneafsey SL, Duggan J, Skeens JB, Geary E, McDonnell J, Lang E, Kennedy S, Carr E, O'Grady K, Dolan RT.
abstract: Hand fractures may represent a sentinel event for vulnerability beyond skeletal frailty alone. We compared longitudinal frailty outcomes in 48 adults ≥ 65 years old presenting with hand fracture with n = 96 age-, sex- and frailty-matched community-based controls. Incident frailty occurred in 17.8% of the fracture cohort compared to 7.8% of controls, over a median follow-up of 3.2 years. This higher observed incidence suggests that hand fracture may identify older adults vulnerable to subsequent frailty, and frailty assessment may complement fracture risk assessment in this cohort.

title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome in Late Pregnancy Following Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
authors: Pereira-Lindley R, Gariba M, Lal D.
abstract: The diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) relies on evolving clinical features, supported by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), laboratory investigations, and electrodiagnostic studies. Early investigations may be nondiagnostic and should not delay treatment when progressive neurological deterioration raises clinical suspicion of GBS. Timely treatment is crucial in optimizing maternal and fetal outcomes.

title: Gender equity in the global rheumatology workforce: results of the Coalition for Health and Gender Equity (CHANGE) survey.
authors: Gupta L, Sarkar M, Ovseiko P, Gossec L, Talreja T, Day J, Traboco L, Russell AM, Haq SA, Hill CL, Dey D, Hassan N, Babini AM, Gonzalez AMA, Gutiérrez CET, Duftner C, Alpizar-Rodríguez D, Badsha H, Nikiphorou E, Harifi G, Hmamouchi I, Von Feldt J, Farani JB, Kalla AA, Rahulan LM, Andreoli L, Souza MP, Palominos PE, Nakashima R, Tanaka Y, Bautista-Molano W, Agarwal V, Ziade N, Wright G, Coates LC, CHANGE Study Group.
abstract: Background/purpose Gender equity remains an elusive goal across many specialist medical fields. The Coalition for Health and Gender Equity (CHANGE) conducted a comprehensive global survey assessing gender equity within the international rheumatology workforce. Methods A cross-sectional online survey of rheumatologists and allied health professionals was conducted between January 2023 and May 2024. The 38-item survey covered demographics, gender discrimination, sexual harassment, work-family interface, and career advancement. It was translated into eight languages and disseminated through professional organisations, mailing lists and social media channels in 105 countries. Analyses included descriptive statistics and comparative tests, with gender differences evaluated after adjustment for years of work experience. Subgroup analyses included country Human Development Index (HDI), professional roles, and caregiving responsibilities, with statistical significance set at p Results Among 1,945 respondents (66.4% female), pronounced gender-based disparities were observed. Male professionals demonstrated higher rates of full-time employment, leadership positions, and clinical experience. Female rheumatology professionals more frequently encountered career barriers, including tasks below their expertise, hostility from colleagues, lacking leadership training opportunities, lower remuneration, and difficulties securing research funding. Women reported greater domestic responsibilities (47.5% vs 36.2%, p Conclusion This global survey provides compelling evidence of gender disparities in rheumatology, necessitating coordinated, evidence-based interventions to address structural barriers and promote inclusive cultures.

title: Gastrostomy as an Adjunctive Gastropexy in Recurrent Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia with Repeated Gastric Herniation: A Case Report.
authors: Ishii M, Azuma S, Kumata Y, Meya Y, Motoki K, Matsumoto H, Sugeno S, Suda S, Aoyama A, Okamoto T, Nagaya K, Miyagi H.
abstract: Introduction Although the survival of patients with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) has improved with advances in perinatal management, postoperative recurrence remains a significant complication. Risk factors for recurrence include large diaphragmatic defects, patch repair, liver herniation, and minimally invasive surgery. Recurrent CDH is associated with a high rate of subsequent recurrence, and the optimal surgical strategy has not been established. We report an infant with recurrent CDH and repeated gastric herniation who was treated with additional diaphragmatic reconstruction combined with gastrostomy fixation. Case presentation A male infant with prenatally diagnosed left-sided CDH underwent primary repair on day 4 of life. A grade C defect with medial diaphragmatic deficiency was repaired using a cone-shaped GORE-TEX patch. At 4 months of age, follow-up imaging demonstrated recurrence with herniation of the stomach and colon into the left thoracic cavity. At reoperation, the lateral fixation of the patch remained intact, while its medial, anterior, and posterior portions had detached, and the patch had become displaced laterally. The defect was reconstructed using an additional patch. One week later, he developed a second recurrence accompanied by progressive intrathoracic gastric herniation with mesenteroaxial gastric volvulus, resulting in poor weight gain. At 5 months of age, a fourth operation revealed a similar pattern of patch detachment, with herniation of the stomach and colon. Additional patch reconstruction and gastrostomy fixation were performed. Postoperatively, the patient's oral intake and weight gain improved markedly, without gastrostomy-related complications. The gastrostomy button was removed at 1 year of age. At 18 months of age (13 months after the final operation and 6 months after gastrostomy removal), the patient demonstrated normal growth and development without recurrence. Conclusions In this patient, the absence of reliable medial anchoring tissue, limitations of patch fixation, and repeated gastric migration may all have contributed to recurrent diaphragmatic reconstruction failures. Although the independent effect of gastrostomy fixation cannot be determined because it was performed concurrently with additional patch reconstruction, it may have helped limit gastric mobility as an adjunct to diaphragmatic re-reconstruction. This combined approach may be considered in selected patients with recurrent CDH, medial diaphragmatic deficiency, and repeated gastric herniation.

title: From Inbox to OR: Generative AI and the Modern Academic Surgeon.
authors: Unadkat K, Noland SS.
abstract: Objective Academic surgeons are increasingly expected to balance clinical care with teaching, mentorship, scholarship, documentation, and a growing number of administrative responsibilities. While these demands are central to academic medicine, they also create administrative and cognitive burdens that compete for time, attention, and patient connection. Design This viewpoint examines emerging applications in surgical education, research, documentation, administrative workflow, and communication. Setting Academic surgery. Participants Academic surgeons. Results Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have rapidly entered academic surgery, yet discussions often focus on replacement rather than practical integration. The greatest near-term value of AI may lie not in replacing surgical expertise, but in supporting the cognitive and workflow demands surrounding modern academic practice. It also highlights important considerations including hallucinations, bias, privacy, and the need for human oversight. Conclusions Thoughtful implementation of generative AI may help reduce administrative burden and allow surgeons to redirect attention toward the human aspects of surgery, including teaching, mentorship, scholarship, and patient care.

title: Epidemiological characteristics and comparison of clinical outcomes between conservative and surgical treatment for rib fractures in South China: A 10‑year retrospective cohort study of 4085 cases with propensity score‑matching analysis.
authors: Zhang T, Cai Q, Liang B, Song X.
abstract: Purpose To systematically describe the epidemiological characteristics of rib fractures in South China and compare the clinical characteristics, hospital stay, and total costs between patients receiving conservative versus surgical treatment, thereby providing evidence‑based support for clinical decision‑making and public health prevention. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on 4085 hospitalized patients with rib fractures admitted to the Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Southern Medical University between January 2014 and December 2023. Data on gender, age, injury mechanism, fracture type, complications, blood group, and occupational distribution were collected. A subgroup analysis comparing conservative (n = 586) versus surgical treatment (n = 137) was conducted among 723 patients admitted between January 2021 and December 2023. Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics between the two groups, and differences in hospital stay, total costs, and injury mechanisms were compared. Results (1) Epidemiological characteristics: Of the 4085 patients, 68.13% (2783/4085) were male, and the 41-60 year age group accounted for the highest proportion (50.35%). Autumn and winter were the peak seasons for injury (54.71%). Traffic accidents were the leading cause of injury (51.18%), followed by falls (21.82%) and height‑related falls (19.13%). Multiple fractures predominated (75.52%). The most common complication was pulmonary contusion (45.14%), followed by traumatic pneumothorax/hemothorax/hemopneumothorax/pleural effusion (40.02%). Among occupations, freelancers were the largest group (34.37%), followed by farmers (23.18%). Blood group O was the most prevalent (42.15%), while blood group B was the least common (5.55%, P Conclusion Based on a large sample of 4085 cases, this study is the first to systematically delineate the full epidemiological profile of rib fractures in South China, with a sample size more than ten times larger than the previous largest regional report. The results indicate that middle‑aged males, freelancers, and farmers are high‑risk populations, with traffic accidents and multiple fractures being predominant, and a unique autumn peak seasonal pattern in South China is reported for the first time. Treatment strategies should be tailored according to injury mechanism and fracture severity. The novel association between blood group O and increased rib fracture risk, reported here for the first time, provides a new perspective for precision prevention; the potential mechanism may involve impaired hemostatic response due to lower baseline levels of von Willebrand factor and factor VIII in individuals with blood group O.

title: Environmental drivers of taste characteristics in wild edible plants: Effects of topographic gradients and human harvesting evaluated using dwarf bamboo culms.
authors: Katayama N, Ryuda N, Ryuda M, Takagi K.
abstract: Wild edible plants grow in natural environments with little direct human management; consequently, their productivity and quality frequently exhibit pronounced spatiotemporal variability, making stable supply difficult. This variability represents a major constraint on the exploitation of wild edible plants as local food resources, and overcoming it requires an ecological understanding of the factors affecting variation in both productivity and quality. Here, we examined the effects of human harvesting and environmental factors on the taste characteristics of young culms of Sasa kurilensis. No statistically significant differences were detected between harvested and control plots in any major taste index, including umami, bitter aftertaste, astringency, umami richness, and sweetness (measured as Brix values). In contrast, taste characteristics showed substantial variation among study plots, suggesting a strong association with local environmental conditions. Elevation and slope angle were significantly correlated with bitter aftertaste, umami, and sweetness; plots at higher elevations and on steeper slopes tended to produce plants with a less bitter aftertaste, and higher sweetness and umami. Principal component analysis integrating multiple taste indices revealed that the major axis of taste variation was significantly associated with elevation, and that harvesting treatment had no detectable effect. These results suggest that the taste characteristics of young culms in the study area are governed primarily by topographic gradients rather than by human harvesting. Although wild edible plants are important food resources in boreal and temperate forests worldwide, many are poorly managed. By quantitatively establishing relationships between taste characteristics and environmental factors in young culms, this study provides a scientific basis for determining the optimal timing, location, and selection criteria for wild edible plant harvesting, thereby contributing to the development of sustainable use strategies.

title: Endplate-to-endplate cement contact and 24-month outcomes after unilateral percutaneous vertebroplasty for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
authors: Zhang K, Xia L, Wang Z.
abstract: Background Bone cement distribution may influence load transfer and late structural failure after vertebral augmentation.
