However, the association between endplate contact and clinical outcomes remains difficult to estimate due to confounding factors. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 620 patients who underwent unilateral percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) at a single institution. Cement distribution was classified as contact with neither endplate (group I), the superior endplate only (group II), the inferior endplate only (group III), or both endplates (group IV). The primary outcome was time to postoperative vertebral refracture within 24 months. Secondary outcomes included longitudinal visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), vertebral recompression, radiographic restoration, cement leakage, and perioperative measures. Confounding was addressed using stabilized multinomial inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Repeated outcomes were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE), and time to refracture was analyzed using Cox regression. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and 10-fold cross-validation were performed. Results Among 620 patients, 150 refractures (24.2%) occurred. Event rates were 30.9%, 26.6%, 25.7%, and 15.2% in groups I-IV, respectively (log-rank P = 0.0069). After weighting, the maximum standardized mean difference (SMD) decreased from 0.231 to 0.053. At 24 months, group IV had lower adjusted VAS scores (mean difference, -0.72; 95% confidence interval ( CI ), -0.93 to -0.51) and ODI scores (mean difference, -6.75; 95% CI , -8.35 to -5.15) than group I. In the Cox model, group IV was associated with a lower refracture hazard (hazard ratio ( HR ), 0.40; 95% CI , 0.25-0.64). Independent risk markers included older age, female sex, lower bone mineral density (BMD) T-score, prior fragility fracture, two-level treatment, intravertebral cleft, intradiscal leakage, absence of anti-osteoporosis treatment, chronic glucocorticoid exposure, and deviation from a midrange cement volume. The association for group IV was stronger during months 0-12 than during months 13-24. Conclusions Cement contact with both endplates was associated with better long-term pain and functional outcomes and greater refracture-free survival after extensive adjustment. However, the adjusted 24-month differences in VAS and ODI did not exceed commonly accepted minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds, so the clinical magnitude remains uncertain. These findings provide useful prognostic information for surgical planning, although prospective validation is warranted.

title: Effect of intraoral glossopharyngeal nerve block on hemodynamic response to mouth retractor placement in transoral robotic surgery: a randomized clinical trial.
authors: Bhasin A, Ganesh V, Singh A, Naik NB, Soni SL, Kaloria N, Patro SK, Panda NK.
abstract: Placement of rigid oral retractors during transoral robotic surgery (TORS) elicits a sympathetic hemodynamic response that may be harmful in high-risk patients. The glossopharyngeal nerve provides sensory innervation to the oropharyngeal structures stimulated during retractor placement, yet no previous trial has evaluated glossopharyngeal nerve block (GPN block) for attenuating this response. In this prospective, single-center, randomized clinical trial, 42 patients (ASA I-II, aged 18-65 years) undergoing TORS were allocated 1:1 to the block group, which received bilateral intraoral GPN block with 2 mL of 2% lignocaine per side or the Control group, which received no block. The outcome assessor was blinded; no sham procedure was performed, and the anaesthesiologist performing the block was not blinded. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with a > 20% increase in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from the pre-retractor baseline within 10 minutes of Feyh-Kastenbauer retractor insertion. Bayesian logistic regression with a Normal (0, 5) prior on the group coefficient was used; the pre-specified decision criterion was a posterior probability of directional benefit P (ARD 20% occurred in 8 of 21 patients (38.1%) in the control group versus 3 of 21 (14.3%) in the block group. The posterior mean absolute risk difference was - 23.9% (95% credible interval [CrI]: - 49.4% to 2.2%), with P (ARD < 0) = 0.964, exceeding the pre-specified threshold. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the direction of effect under neutral, sceptical, and optimistic priors (P(ARD < 0) range: 0.934-0.967), although the posterior probability under the sceptical prior did not exceed the prespecified 0.95 threshold; evidence was equivocal under the pessimistic prior (P(ARD < 0) = 0.57). Maximum MAP and heart rate were lower in the block group (P (difference < 0) = 0.998 and 0.995, respectively). Bispectral index values were comparable between groups throughout the procedure. The GPN block is associated with a high posterior probability of attenuating the hemodynamic response to mouth retractor placement in TORS. The credible intervals were wide, reflecting uncertainty about effect magnitude. A larger confirmatory trial assessing clinical endpoints is warranted.

title: Direct anterior versus conventional approaches for hemiarthroplasty in femoral neck fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional outcomes.
journal: Journal of Clinical Orthopaedics and Trauma
authors: Sarkar MH, Maheshwari S, Vardhan S, Singh L, Das SL, Goyal T.
abstract: Background Femoral neck fracture (FNF) in older adults is associated with morbidity and functional decline. The optimal surgical approach for hemiarthroplasty (HA) remains uncertain. The direct anterior approach (DAA), a muscle-sparing technique, may improve early recovery compared with conventional approaches. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared DAA with conventional approaches following HA for FNF. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched through December 2025 according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Comparative studies of DAA versus conventional approaches were included. The primary outcome was Harris Hip Score (HHS); secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, operative time, blood loss, transfusion, and hospital stay. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251270460). Results Forty-two studies involving 7582 patients were included. Three studies contributed to early HHS analysis, showing no significant difference between approaches (MD, 1.38; 95% CI, -4.85 to 7.60; I 2 = 77.2%). Similarly, three studies at mid-term follow-up showed no significant difference (MD, 1.04; 95% CI, -3.67 to 5.76; I 2 = 67.8%). Only 1 study provided quantitatively evaluable long-term HHS data (MD, 0.70; 95% CI, -2.41 to 3.81). DAA was associated with lower postoperative pain (SMD, -0.38; 95% CI, -0.72 to -0.05; P = 0.02), lower blood loss (MD, -61.0 mL; 95% CI, -103.2 to -18.9 mL; P Conclusions DAA was associated with modest perioperative benefits following HA for FNF. However, HHS analyses did not demonstrate statistically significant functional differences at early or mid-term follow-up, and long-term evidence was limited. Sustained functional superiority of DAA remains uncertain. Level of evidence Level III (systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised and observational comparative studies).

title: Cross bridges, tendons and titin: evolving roles in muscle mechanics.
authors: Nishikawa K, Lindstedt SL.
abstract: All fields of science evolve over time as interpretation of the evidence changes with the discovery of new facts, and muscle physiology is no exception. Ideas once thought preposterous may eventually become accepted dogma, as was the case for the sliding filament theory itself. The currently accepted sliding-filament - swinging cross-bridge paradigm views muscles as motors with static isometric force-length and isotonic force-velocity properties that necessarily limit their ability to store and recover viscoelastic energy. These limitations understandably led to the plausible explanation that tendons must be responsible for energy storage and recovery. However, recent advances in technology have enabled investigation of muscle properties in moving humans and other animals, providing significant new data on dynamic muscle function. Bridging the gap between laboratory studies of ex vivo muscle preparations and in vivo muscle mechanics has resulted in a paradigm shift toward the idea that muscles are tunable viscoelastic actuators that can harvest substantial energy from interactions with the environment. Here, we provide a somewhat chronological account of the contentious history of the field of muscle physiology and the evolution of ideas about muscle function, focusing particularly on muscle viscoelastic properties and energy storage. We argue that accumulating data position titin as a length- and activation-dependent viscoelastic element whose properties can be inferred from, and indeed are critical for, in vivo muscle function. We also provide ideas for future directions to stimulate progress in understanding titin's role in dynamic muscle function.

title: Comparable clinical outcomes but different postoperative Dynamic Alignment of the Knee (DyAK) patterns between cruciate-retaining and posterior-stabilized inserts in functionally aligned robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
authors: Koutserimpas C, Veizi E, Lustig S, Dretakis K.
abstract: Purpose The influence of polyethylene insert design during robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) performed according to functional alignment (FA) principles remains poorly understood. This study compared cruciate-retaining (CR) and posterior-stabilized (PS) inserts with respect to implant positioning, clinical outcomes, implant survivorship and postoperative dynamic knee behaviour using the Dynamic Alignment of the Knee (DyAK) classification. Methods A retrospective comparative study was performed on 284 primary functionally aligned robotic-assisted TKAs. The cohort comprised 148 CR and 136 PS fixed-bearing cemented implants with a minimum follow-up of 3 years (median 44.5 months). Clinical outcomes included Knee Society Score (KSS) and Forgotten Joint Score (FJS). Intraoperative robotic implant positioning, bone resections, polyethylene thickness, DyAK classification, complications and Kaplan-Meier implant survivorship were compared between groups. Results The CR group demonstrated greater preoperative varus alignment (median robotic hip-knee-ankle angle [rHKA] 5° vs. 3°, p = 0.01). Compared with PS implants, CR inserts were implanted with greater tibial varus (2° vs. 1°, p p p = 0.009). Polyethylene inserts >9 mm were required more frequently in the PS group (39.0% vs. 15.5%, p p = 0.56), KSS function ( p = 0.62) and FJS ( p = 0.06) were comparable between groups. No statistically significant difference in survivorship was detected for aseptic loosening (0.68% vs. 0.74%, p = 0.95) and all-cause revision (2.03% vs. 1.47%, p = 0.72). The DyAK classification changed significantly more frequently in the PS group than in the CR group (69.9% vs. 52.7%, p = 0.003), despite similar postoperative clinical outcomes. Conclusion CR and PS polyethylene inserts showed no significant differences in final clinical scores or implant survivorship at a minimum follow-up of 3 years but demonstrated different patterns of postoperative dynamic alignment, suggesting that the DyAK classification may provide complementary information beyond conventional outcome measures. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Colours of the mind: A qualitative study exploring the relationship between neurodivergence and creativity.
authors: Erin B, Shaw SCK, Quadt L, Eccles JA.
abstract: The neurodiversity movement advocates for a societal framework that recognises neurodivergence as a difference, rather than a disorder. Despite the advocacy efforts, neurodivergent people still face issues with their physical and mental health at higher rates than the general population. Some scholars argue that these disproportionate rates originate from stress resulting from discrimination and societal stigma faced by neurodivergent people. This study aims to challenge these societal views through exploring one of the reported strengths of being neurodivergent: creativity. This study aims to explore why neurodivergent populations may be creative. To research this complex relationship between being neurodivergence and creativity a qualitative study was conducted. Ten neurodivergent adults who had studied or were currently studying a creative degree were interviewed on Zoom, exploring their beliefs about this relationship. An inductive thematic analysis was then carried out. The analysis gave rise to three themes: (1) The Construct of Creativity, (2) Resilience, & (3) Empowerment. These themes provided hypotheses for understanding the connection between neurodivergence and creativity. The results provided two hypotheses. The 'innate trait hypothesis' posits that traits thought to be intrinsic to neurodivergence may be beneficial in fostering creativity. The innate traits that arose were divergent thinking, monotropism and communication differences. The 'social isolation hypothesis' posits that the discrimination that neurodivergent people face leads to profound isolation and in some cases mental health challenges. Neurodivergent people may then use creativity as a method for regulating their emotions, providing solace from distress. Moreover, the isolation they experience provides an opportunity for introspection, which fuels creativity. Our results highlight that some neurodivergent traits, when placed within a creative context, can become strengths. This highlights the possibility that the pathologisation of neurodivergent traits is not just damaging but also invalid, with the reality being much more nuanced.

title: Collared cemented femoral stems are associated with lower periprosthetic femoral fracture rates: A systematic review and subgroup meta-analysis.
authors: Laboudie P, Blancatto M.
abstract: Purpose Periprosthetic femoral fracture (PFF) is a severe complication after hip arthroplasty. Cemented femoral stems have been used to reduce this risk, while collars have been associated with lower fracture rates in cementless stems. However, the role of a collar in cemented femoral stems remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared postoperative PFF rates between collared and collarless cemented femoral stems. Methods Nine comparative cohorts directly comparing collared and collarless cemented stems were included in the odds ratio (OR) meta-analysis. Eligible single-arm cohorts were additionally included in pooled incidence analyses. Random-effects models were used throughout. Predefined subgroup analyses were performed according to surgical indication and stem surface finish, including a polished-stem subgroup comparing polished collared with polished collarless designs. Results Collared stems were associated with a lower postoperative PFF rate (OR, 0.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.17-0.49; p I 2 = 71%). Pooled PFF incidence was 0.51% for collared stems and 2.27% for collarless stems. This association was observed in elective arthroplasty cohorts (OR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.15-0.63) and femoral neck fracture cohorts (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.20-0.38). In the polished-stem subgroup, analysis showed a lower odds of PFF with polished collared stems (OR, 0.17; 95% CI, 0.01-2.86; p = 0.22). Pooled incidence was 0.65% for polished collared stems and 2.34% for polished collarless stems. Conclusions Collared stems were associated with lower PFF rates. This association was observed in both elective arthroplasty and femoral neck fracture cohorts. Polished collared designs also showed lower PFF rates than polished collarless designs. Substantial heterogeneity and confounding by other stem characteristics limit interpretation. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Clinical pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationships between drug exposure and the QT/QTc interval: Protocol for a systematic review and quantitative synthesis.
authors: Molana H, Esmaily H, Mohammadnezhad G.
abstract: Drug-induced QT/QTc prolongation is a central component of cardiac safety assessment. Concentration-QT/QTc modelling uses measured or model-predicted systemic drug exposure to estimate the magnitude and uncertainty of effects on ventricular repolarisation and can support regulatory decision-making in early clinical development. However, the evidence is dispersed across dedicated thorough QT studies, early-phase studies, population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic analyses, and secondary pooled analyses, with substantial variation in exposure metrics, electrocardiographic acquisition, heart-rate correction, model structure, assessment of active metabolites and delayed effects, and reporting of uncertainty. This protocol describes a systematic review of quantitative human concentration-QT/QTc evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar will be searched from inception without date or language restrictions. Original human studies will be eligible when drug or metabolite concentrations are measured or estimated from a pharmacokinetic model informed by study data and are quantitatively related to QT or QTc outcomes. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data, and assess methodological limitations. The primary estimands will be the concentration-QT/QTc drug-effect parameter and the predicted placebo-adjusted change from baseline in QTc at a clinically relevant exposure. Random-effects meta-analysis will be undertaken only within the same active moiety when analyte, endpoint, correction method, model estimand, and exposure scenario are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis without meta-analysis will be performed. Risk of bias will be assessed using design-appropriate tools where applicable, supplemented by a prespecified concentration-QT/QTc methodological framework. Certainty will be evaluated for coherent drug-specific bodies of evidence. This review will provide a transparent map of clinical concentration-QT/QTc methods and estimates and identify priorities for future cardiac safety studies. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261469142.

title: Climate-sensitive patterns of premature cardiovascular mortality in a subtropical city.
authors: Carnasciali NMA, Souza FT, Barcellos DDS.
abstract: This study aimed to investigate climate-sensitive temporal patterns associated with premature mortality due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in a large subtropical city in southern Brazil. Daily premature mortality records (ages 30-69) from 2010 to 2019 were analyzed together with meteorological data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation, as well as temporally aggregated climatic indicators. An exploratory analytical framework combining multivariate analysis, clustering, and classification rule mining was applied to identify temporal patterns and combinations of climatic conditions associated with mortality outcomes. The approach was designed to support pattern discovery and hypothesis generation rather than causal inference.Linear associations between individual climatic variables and mortality were weak. However, exploratory analyses revealed distinct climate-sensitive temporal patterns. Premature IHD mortality was more frequently associated with colder temperatures, elevated long-term humidity, and specific combinations of atmospheric pressure and temperature. In contrast, AMI mortality showed associations with intermediate maximum temperatures, lower atmospheric pressure, and moderate levels of solar radiation. The classification models demonstrated moderate performance across outcomes, with the highest accuracy observed for AMI, indicating that complex temporal patterns may not be captured by linear analyses alone. The findings demonstrate that climate-sensitive temporal patterns in premature cardiovascular mortality can be identified using exploratory, data-driven approaches. Although causal relationships were not assessed, the results highlight the value of integrating climatic indicators and temporal aggregation into exploratory environmental health research and hypothesis generation. This framework is transparent, reproducible, and applicable to other urban settings, particularly in low- and middle-income countries facing increasing climate variability.

title: Case Report: A modified Karapandzic flap with bilateral V-Y advancement for reconstruction of a large full-thickness lower lip defect after squamous cell carcinoma excision.
authors: Seok SI, Lim SY, Koh IC.
abstract: Purpose Reconstruction of full-thickness lower lip defects involving more than two-thirds of the vermilion remains surgically challenging. The conventional Karapandzic flap is a labial artery-based musculomucocutaneous flap requiring continuous incisions extending from the labiolabial crease through the labiomandibular fold to the mental crease, often resulting in extensive scarring. Moreover, this technique requires meticulous identification and preservation of the labial artery and perioral nerves, leading to greater technical demands and prolonged operative time, particularly for less experienced surgeons. Herein, we introduce a modified Karapandzic flap technique using bilateral V-Y advancement flaps for lower lip reconstruction following squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) excision. Methods A 74-year-old man presented with SCC of the lower lip. The lesion measured 4.3 × 1.8 cm, and a wedge-shaped wide excision with a 5-mm surgical margin was performed. The resulting full-thickness defect measured 5.3 × 2.3 cm, involving more than two-thirds of the lower lip. Instead of extending incisions across the entire lower lip, bilateral V-Y advancement flaps were designed on both lateral aspects and elevated with partial release of the depressor anguli oris muscle to allow medial mobilization. Results Complete flap survival and satisfactory wound healing were observed without major complications. At approximately four months, oral competence was maintained according to the patient, without liquid leakage, drooling, or food spillage, and without restrictions on food types. During maximal voluntary mouth opening, the intercommissural distance was 2.5 cm, the vertical oral aperture was 4 cm, and the distance between externally marked reference points corresponding to the palpated upper and lower incisal positions was 6 cm. Two-point discrimination was 5 mm at the central and bilateral lower lip sites. Postoperative microstomia resulted in reduced oral aperture, for which secondary commissuroplasty had been anticipated as part of a staged reconstructive plan. Conclusion Bilateral V-Y advancement based on the modified Karapandzic concept may provide a reconstructive option for selected extensive full-thickness lower lip defects without formal neurovascular dissection. Although flap survival and oral competence were maintained in this case, postoperative microstomia and the anticipated need for secondary commissuroplasty should be considered during surgical planning.

title: CT-based adaptation of the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in advanced ovarian cancer: Agreement and inter-reader reproducibility.
authors: Versienti E, Arcieri M, De Martino M, Francioso F, Sallustio G, Como G, Nyangang O, Zanagnolo MF, Filippin S, Restaino S, Driul L, Zuiani C, Girometti R, Vizzielli G, Cereser L.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate agreement of proposed CT-based variants with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in suspected advanced ovarian cancer and assess inter-reader agreement of CT-derived components. Methods This retrospective single-center study included consecutive adults evaluated between January 2021 and November 2025 for suspected advanced ovarian cancer who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT and staging laparoscopy. Proposed CT-based modifications were operationalized as six score variants combining CT-derived peritoneal tumor burden, CT-estimated ascites, cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), and either Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG-PS) or CT-derived body composition parameters. Agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation coefficient, and weighted Cohen's kappa. Results The final cohort included 80 patients. All CT-based variants showed agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. For the variant combining CT-derived PCI, CT-estimated ascites, ECOG-PS, and CA-125, the consistency ICC was 0.76, Spearman's ρ was 0.806, and weighted Cohen's kappa was 0.76. This variant showed 70.0% agreement across the three risk categories and 83.8% agreement for high-risk versus non-high-risk classification, classifying 20 of 22 laparoscopic high-risk patients as high risk. The PCI-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) variant maintained substantial agreement: ICC, 0.73; Spearman correlation coefficient, 0.742; weighted Cohen's kappa, 0.74. Inter-reader agreement was high for CT-derived PCI, with an ICC of 0.91. Conclusion Proposed CT-based variants showed agreement with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. The PCI-based ECOG-PS variant showed the highest agreement metrics, suggesting that structured CT assessment may help approximate laparoscopic risk categories before invasive evaluation.

title: Bridging Simulation and Practice: Designing, Implementing, and Evaluating a Curriculum for Educating Medical Students as Robotic Surgery Bedside Assistants.
authors: Gomes C, Murillo A, Lee YLS, Brian R, Falcone JL, Chern H, Alseidi A, O'Sullivan P.
abstract: Background Medical students often face limited involvement in robotic surgery, leading to unfulfilling learning experiences. Establishing a defined role for students in the operating room (OR) can enhance their engagement and deepen their understanding of robotic surgery. We describe the design and implementation of a curriculum designed to train medical students as robotic surgery bedside assistants and explore the perspectives of key stakeholders involved in the program. Methods We designed a curriculum based on Kern's 6-step approach for curricular development. It included a series of online modules and a simulated hands-on session, followed by case assignments over their 4-week rotation. The curriculum centered on training students in an asset of core bedside skills that had been identified in a previous study. Students initially received supervision in the OR and progressed toward increasing autonomy. Fourth-year medical students could participate during their surgical subinternships. Major stakeholders, including students, residents, faculty, and OR staff participated in semistructured interviews to share their experiences; transcripts were subsequently analyzed using qualitative methods. Results Fourteen students participated and were interviewed. Students valued their defined roles, experiential learning, and interprofessional collaboration, noting increased engagement and confidence. Stakeholders (n = 13) reported that the curriculum enhanced medical student readiness for surgical training by fostering technical skill development, professional integration, and increased autonomy. Residents and faculty observed that students functioned at or near intern level by the end of the rotation and appreciated how student involvement at the bedside supported resident console time. OR staff and faculty acknowledged early implementation challenges, including staff unfamiliarity, but noted that improved communication and onboarding processes helped address these barriers. Conclusions The robotic bedside assist curriculum was perceived to support safe, structured, and inclusive learning while promoting student development within the surgical team, giving students a legitimate role in robotic surgery.

title: Breastfeeding and maternal bone health 10 years postpartum: findings from the ROLO longitudinal cohort study.
authors: Kennedy S, Dunlop K, Callanan S, Crowley RK, McAuliffe FM.
abstract: Brief rationale: To investigate associations between breastfeeding behaviours and maternal bone health at 10-year follow-up. Main result Breastfeeding durations were not associated with DXA measurements. Significance of the paper: These findings add to the evidence that breastfeeding is not associated with adverse long-term maternal bone health. Purpose To investigate associations between breastfeeding behaviours and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements of maternal bone health at 10-year follow-up. Associations with bone turnover markers (BTMs) were examined as exploratory secondary outcomes. Methods This was an analysis of 196 women from the ROLO (Randomised cOntrol trial of a LOw glycaemic index diet in pregnancy to prevent macrosomia) longitudinal cohort study at 10-year follow-up. Data on demographics, lifestyle and breastfeeding were collected by questionnaire. DXA measurements were available for 171 participants and BTM measurements for 60. Exclusive breastfeeding duration, any breastfeeding duration and three mutually exclusive cumulative breastfeeding groups (never breastfed, breastfed for Results The mean (SD) age of participants was 42.8 (3.87) years and 97.9% were premenopausal. Ever breastfeeding rates were 70.9% (n = 139/196) and 40.3% (n = 79/196) had a cumulative breastfeeding duration of ≥12 months. Breastfeeding durations were not associated with DXA measurements at 10-year follow-up. An unadjusted difference in β-CTX-I was observed between the ≥12-month and never-breastfed groups (p = 0.038) however, given the small group size an adjusted analysis was underpowered. Conclusion These findings reassure women that breastfeeding does not have a lasting negative impact on skeletal health. The exploratory BTM finding should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Benefits of surgical task trainers to complement training pathways for junctional haemorrhage control.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Tien L, Chong D, Mittapalli D, Pallister I, Faulconer R.
abstract: Introduction Junctional haemorrhage remains a recognised cause of preventable trauma mortality. Although uncommon in the United Kingdom, such injuries demand prompt haemorrhage control, open vascular exposure and temporary shunting. Opportunities to develop these skills during routine vascular training are limited. This study evaluated whether high-fidelity pulsatile bleeding simulation improved trainees' self-reported confidence in managing groin junctional haemorrhage. Methods A prospective pilot educational evaluation was undertaken during a South West Deanery vascular training day. Nine vascular surgery trainees (ST3-ST7) completed a simulation using the Trauma Simulation® Femoral Injury Groin Task Trainer, identifying the bleeding source, obtaining proximal and distal femoral control, and inserting a temporary shunt under pulsatile haemorrhage. Confidence across four procedural domains was rated on a 5-point Likert scale immediately before and after the exercise, and scores compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank testing. No objective performance assessment was undertaken. Results All nine trainees completed both questionnaires. Median confidence improved in all four domains, although whole-cohort changes were not statistically significant. Among junior trainees (ST3-ST6, n = 6), improvements in haemorrhage management, proximal and distal vascular control, and shunt insertion were significant (all p Conclusions High-fidelity pulsatile bleeding simulation is feasible, was valued by trainees and may help address an experiential gap in UK vascular training. However, confidence is not competence, and objective performance measures are needed before wider curricular adoption.

title: Automated laboratory detection of hypercalcemia: Diagnostic yield, clinical pathway and outcomes in a real-world cohort.
authors: Roig-Marín N, López-Garrigós M, Flores E, Seguí-Ripoll JM.
abstract: Background Automated laboratory detection of hypercalcemia may facilitate the recognition of previously unrecognized primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), but its value in routine clinical practice remains poorly defined, particularly with regard to subsequent etiological evaluation, healthcare resource utilization, and biochemical follow-up. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated an automated laboratory case-finding strategy for hypercalcemia across a healthcare area serving more than 230,000 inhabitants. Consecutive laboratory alerts generated between 2012 and 2020 were reviewed. After duplicate alerts were removed, 685 unique patients constituted the laboratory-detected cohort, of whom 258 underwent sufficient etiological evaluation and constituted the fully evaluated cohort. Clinical, biochemical, imaging, therapeutic, and longitudinal follow-up data were collected. Results Among the 258 fully evaluated patients, definite PHPT was diagnosed in 229 (88.8%). Eight additional patients were retrospectively considered to have probable mild PHPT with concomitant vitamin D deficiency, while other etiologies included tertiary hyperparathyroidism associated with chronic kidney disease, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, medication-related hypercalcemia, familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, sarcoidosis, and vitamin D intoxication. Patients underwent a median of seven specialist consultations. Among patients with an available date of definitive etiological diagnosis, the median interval from the initial laboratory alert to diagnosis was 432 days (IQR 94.5-1219.5). During follow-up, 219/258 patients (84.9%) had at least one documented normocalcemic measurement after biochemical confirmation of persistent hypercalcemia, and 150/258 (58.1%) fulfilled the definition of sustained normocalcemia. In Kaplan-Meier analysis, the median time to first documented normocalcemia was 595 days (95% CI 505-780). Conclusions Automated laboratory case-finding can identify patients with previously unrecognized persistent hypercalcemia and provide an entry point for subsequent etiological evaluation. PHPT was the predominant diagnosis within the fully evaluated cohort, although post-detection selection must be considered when interpreting this proportion. The prolonged diagnostic pathway and substantial healthcare use observed after the initial laboratory alert highlight the need to link automated detection strategies to structured clinical follow-up.

title: Associations between parental support and physical activity in children and adolescents with visual impairments: a mediating analysis of exercise self-efficacy.
authors: Dou L, Chen H, Lu E.
abstract: Purpose Physical activity (PA) is imperative for the physical and mental health of children and adolescents with visual impairments (VI). However, functional impairment often leads to reduced PA, resulting in declines in health and quality of life. Although parental support (PS) has been identified as a key social determinant of PA in typically developing youth, its specific mechanisms, particularly the mediating role of exercise self-efficacy (ESE), remain unclear in children and adolescents with VI. This study aimed to examine the associations between PS and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), as well as the mediating role of ESE, in this population. Methods Using a cross-sectional design, 306 children and adolescents with VI aged 7-18 (mean age 13.80 ± 2.94 years) from specialized schools in East China were recruited through convenience sampling from September to December 2024. Accelerometers were used to objectively measure PA levels, and MVPA was extracted for analysis. PS for PA and ESE were assessed using validated scales. The associations between PS and MVPA were analyzed. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and the bias-corrected (BC) percentile bootstrap method were employed to analyze the direct and indirect effects of PS on MVPA, with ESE tested as a mediator. Results PS and ESE were both positively correlated with MVPA ( r = 0.306 and 0.385, respectively; both P P = 0.000), comprising a direct effect (β = 0.293, 95% CI [0.140-0.438], P = 0.000) and an indirect effect mediated by ESE (β = 0.085, 95% CI [0.039-0.146], P = 0.000). ESE also exerted a significant direct effect on MVPA (β = 0.35, 95% CI [0.229-0.450], P Conclusion This study highlights that both PS and ESE are associated with MVPA in children and adolescents with VI, with ESE acting partially mediating this relationship.

title: Association between cemented and uncemented cups and risk of revision in patients aged 65 years or older following primary total hip arthroplasty: a study of 310,515 patients from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association.
authors: Latifi R, Kornvig S, Mohaddes M, Ali M, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, Eskelinen A, Mäkelä K, Varnum C, Overgaard S.
abstract: Background and purpose Cemented stem fixation in total hip arthroplasty (THA) reduces early femoral fracture risk in elderly patients, but the optimal method of cup fixation remains controversial. We aimed to compare cup revision risk between cemented and uncemented acetabular cups in patients aged 65 years or older undergoing primary THA. Methods This registry-based cohort study used data from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association (NARA). We included patients aged 65 years or older who underwent primary THA for primary osteoarthritis or sequelae of childhood hip disorders between 1995 and 2018. The primary outcome was all-cause cup revision, with prespecified analyses stratified by age and sex. Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, femoral head size, time period, and nation was used. Follow-up was divided into 3 periods: 0-1, 1-6, and 6-26 years. Results Among 310,515 patients, cemented cups were associated with a lower risk of all-cause cup revision during the first year (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.47, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.41-0.53) and a higher risk at 6-26 years (aHR 1.91, CI 1.72-2.13). In patients aged 80 years or older, the sex-specific adjusted hazard ratios after the first year were close to 1, with wide confidence intervals. Conclusion Cemented cups were associated with a lower risk of cup revision during the first year across all age groups and a higher risk at 6-26 years in the overall cohort. Among patients aged 80 years or older, we found no evidence of an association between fixation method and cup revision after the first year.

title: Arthroscopic Suture-Only Intra-articular Soft-Tissue Long-Head Biceps Tenodesis to the Rotator Cuff.
authors: Prasetia R, Pravitha CA, Andri F.
abstract: Pathology of the long head of the biceps tendon (LHBT) is a prevalent source of shoulder pain and is often concomitant with rotator cuff diseases. Various treatment modalities exist for addressing this condition, including surgical approaches, anatomical sites for tenodesis fixation, and types of fixation devices employed. We describe an arthroscopic suture-only intra-articular soft-tissue long-head biceps tenodesis to the rotator cuff technique for managing LHBT pathology using a loop-and-tack configuration with suture shuttling to secure the LHBT to the anterior supraspinatus without anchors. This technique maintains the physiological length-tension relation, mitigates implant-related complications, and offers a cost-effective solution for treating LHBT pathology.

title: All-Inside Stabilization of Discoid Lateral Meniscus Popliteal Hiatus-Related Instability Using Anterior Cord Release With Meniscus Retention.
authors: Toyooka S, Miyazaki H, Osaki Y, Arai N, Kawano H, Nakagawa T.
abstract: Discoid lateral meniscus is a common cause of lateral knee pain, snapping, catching, and intermittent locking. Although saucerization combined with repair has been widely used, postoperative remodeling, reduced meniscal volume, extrusion, and degenerative changes on magnetic resonance imaging have raised concerns regarding meniscal resection. A meniscus-retention concept using anterior cord release with robust suturing has been described, particularly for large displaced longitudinal tears with frank mechanical locking. In daily practice, however, many symptomatic cases present with popliteal hiatus-related posterior peripheral disruption and popliteomeniscal fascicle insufficiency, resulting in peripheral rim instability and anterior translation of the discoid meniscus during knee motion. Here, we describe a simple and physiologic, meniscus-retaining technique that combines anterior cord release to reduce anterior horn tension and facilitate peripheral reduction and targeted all-inside vertical mattress fixation around the popliteus tendon. A pragmatic avoidance criterion is emphasized for extensive, notch-locked displaced tears that likely require more robust fixation, in which inside-out repair is preferred. This technique aims to control dynamic instability while preserving native meniscal tissue and minimizing intra-articular environmental change.

title: After-hours on-site radiologist availability and emergency CT reporting: a roster-based cohort with staffing-boundary analysis.
authors: Konieczka P, Kłosiewicz T, Al-Hosam K.
abstract: Purpose To compare after-hours emergency CT report turnaround during periods with versus without roster-recorded on-site CT radiologist availability. Materials and methods This retrospective roster-based cohort included emergency-department CT examinations from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. The common-support cohort comprised non-holiday weekdays from 15:00 to 06:59 and all weekends and public holidays. Components within 15 min were grouped into packages. The exposure was on-site CT radiologist availability recorded in the final as-worked duty roster; actual reporting route was secondary. The primary outcome was scan-to-complete-report turnaround time (TAT). Models used duty-date-clustered standard errors and adjusted for patient, temporal, workload, and examination characteristics. Results The cohort contained 13,533 CT packages; 13,270 had usable TAT and 12,333 index encounters were clinically linked. Median TAT was 81 min without and 58 min with an on-site radiologist. Absence of an on-site radiologist was associated with 33.9% longer adjusted TAT (95% CI 25.4-43.0). The association was 28.4% for routine non-contrast head CT and 45.5% for abdominopelvic CT (interaction + 15.1%; p = 0.001). A ± 120-minute staffing-boundary analysis estimated 45.7% longer TAT (16.3-82.5), with positive estimates across ± 60- to ± 180-minute bandwidths and no detected covariate discontinuities. Actual-route TAT was 47.7% longer amid 34.5% route discordance. Conclusion During comparable after-hours periods, roster-recorded absence of an on-site CT radiologist was associated with longer complete-report TAT, particularly for abdominopelvic CT. Downstream stay differences were exploratory and may reflect broader hospital processes.

title: Advanced Analytics Show Domain-Specific Performance Changes After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in National Football League Players.
authors: Hayes E, Kerhoulas Z, Matache B, Pickell M.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate return to play, performance, and assess performance changes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using advanced statistics in National Football League players. Methods National Football League players who underwent anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) between 2017 and 2024 were identified using publicly available databases and injury reports. Demographic and outcome data for 1 year preinjury to 2 years postinjury were obtained. Return to play was defined as being listed as active for a regular season game after injury. Return to performance was defined as returning to greater than 90% of preinjury performance. Our primary performance outcome was Sports Information Solutions points above replacement (PAR). Binary logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with return to play and return to performance. Preinjury and postinjury performance data at the first and second postinjury year were compared with paired t -tests. Results We included 237 players in return-to-play and 173 players in return-to-performance analyses. Of players, 75.5% returned to play; players with more preinjury games played, more index games played, starters, and players with greater preinjury PAR were more likely to return to play ( P = .03, P P P P = .004, P P = .002, P = .004), driven at both time points by significantly decreased rushing ( P = .02, P = .001) and pass coverage ( P = .003, P = .03) PAR. Conclusions After anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, National Football League players with more preinjury games played and higher preinjury performance are more likely to return to play; younger players with lower preinjury performance are more likely to return to performance; and there is a significant decrease in overall performance 1 and 2 years after injury, driven by decreased rushing and pass coverage performance. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective case series.

title: Access to Trauma Care for Patients With Proximal Femur Fractures in Resource-Limited Settings: A Prospective Cohort Study in Rural Tanzania.
authors: Eleveld AJ, Mtui GS, Hendriks TCC, Bellet FD, Botman M, Bloemers FW, van Embden D.
abstract: Background The standard of care for proximal femur fractures is internal fixation or arthroplasty within 48 hours after injury. In resource-limited settings, access to surgical services is limited. The aim of this study was to assess access to care for patients with proximal femur fractures in Tanzania by applying the Three Delays framework. Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted in a rural regional referral hospital in Tanzania. All patients with a proximal femur fractures admitted between August 2019 and August 2020 were included. Data were collected on patient demographics, pre- and in-hospital care, timelines and affordability. According to the Three Delays framework, delays and reasons for delays in seeking (first delay), reaching (second delay) and receiving care (third delay) were explored using a structured survey. Results Forty-seven patients were included. Twenty-four patients (51%) delayed in seeking care at a health care facility within 24 hours after injury with a median delay of 13 days (IQR 4-26 days). Ten patients (21%) were delayed in reaching a healthcare facility within 24 hours. Thirteen patients (28%) experienced a delay in receiving initial surgical care. None of the patients were treated according to the international standard. Thirty-eight patients experienced catastrophic expenditure as a result of their hospital admission. Conclusion The majority of patients with a proximal femur fracture experienced a considerable delay in access to care and none of the patients were treated according to international standards. This should be improved by identifying ways to increase the availability of affordable surgical treatment options.

title: A simplified approach to the theoretical basis of the Z-plasty.
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
authors: Humzah MD, Gilbert PM.

title: A foot-level motion remapping framework for inclined stair walking in virtual reality.
authors: Kim JH.
abstract: This paper proposes a foot-level motion remapping framework that enables users to experience inclined stair walking in virtual reality (VR) while physically walking on flat ground. Existing stair-walking and motion remapping approaches often focus on discrete step-height changes, root-level avatar correction, or hardware-assisted interaction, and therefore have limited ability to represent the continuous geometric variation and asymmetric foot-contact behavior that occur on inclined stair-like surfaces. To address this limitation, the proposed method models the foot using separate toe and heel components and decomposes the gait cycle into Lift, Contact, and Release states. For each gait state, toe and heel contributions are adaptively weighted according to the virtual inclination angle using an anchor-based continuous weighting scheme. The resulting foot motion is temporally stabilized and hierarchically propagated to the waist and head to reduce excessive visual oscillation. The framework was implemented in a real-time Unity-based VR system and evaluated under flat, intermediate, and steep inclination conditions. The evaluation additionally includes a non-anchor inclination condition, sequence-level trajectory-fidelity measures, and comparison with a prior stair-remapping method. The results show that the proposed method reduces frame-wise height jitter, improves motion stability, and maintains real-time performance compared with baseline remapping variants. These findings support foot-level state-based remapping as a practical approach for generating trajectory-stable inclined locomotion in VR without requiring a physical stair apparatus.

title: A Decade in Periprosthetic Joint Infection Care: Growing Referrals and High Resource Demands at a High-Volume Center.
authors: Rainey JP, Blackburn BE, Noyd RC, Hammond J, Certain LK, Archibeck MJ, Anderson LA, Peters CL, Gililland JM, Pelt CE.
abstract: Background The management of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) requires a multidisciplinary approach that is not feasible in all healthcare settings. This study characterized the evolving burden of PJI referrals at an academic referral center over the past decade. Methods A retrospective review was conducted of all referred patients who underwent treatment for hip or knee PJI at a single referral center between 2014 and 2024. Demographic data, initial operative time, hospital length of stay (LOS), and number and duration of subsequent surgeries were recorded. Results In total, 523 referred patients were treated for PJI. The mean initial LOS was 7.0 days (standard deviation [SD] 5.7) and the mean operative time was 169.5 min (SD 75.9). Overall, 36% underwent irrigation and debridement with modular component exchange, single stage revision, or a spacer alone. Of the 335 who had at least 1 subsequent surgery, under half (N = 146, 43.5%), received stage two alone. On average, patients underwent 1.8 subsequent surgeries (SD 1.4), ranging from 1 to 14. The cumulative mean operative time for these subsequent surgeries was 306.4 min (SD 253.3). The number of PJIs nearly doubled from 2014-2017 (N = 112) to 2021-2024 (N = 221). There were no significant changes in LOS, number of subsequent surgeries, or cumulative operative time for reoperations during these intervals. Conclusions The volume of referred PJIs has increased substantially over the past decade at our referral center, underscoring the growing demand for PJI care and profound resource burden necessary to care for these patients.

title: Vascular Anatomic Variations in Living Donor Kidney Transplantation: A Single Centre Experience.
authors: Rózsa B, Pőcze B, Kovács J, Remport Á, Wágner L, Cseprekál O, Marton A, Maléth A, Németh K, Somogyi D, Deák-Pál Á, Barabás I, Benkő T, Szijártó A, Piros L.
abstract: The implication of individual renal vascular anatomical variations remains an important consideration in terms of donor safety and successful graft outcomes in living kidney transplantation, and therefore requires careful preoperative assessment and accurate, personalized surgical planning. This study aimed to characterize these variations, describe their surgical management, and explore their associations with donor postoperative complications and recipient graft outcomes. We retrospectively reviewed 466 hand-assisted laparoscopic donor nephrectomies performed at Semmelweis University between March 2008 and December 2023. Vascular anatomical variations, surgical management, donor postoperative complications, and recipient outcomes were assessed. Vascular anatomical variations were identified in 149 cases (32%), while 317 donors (68%) had standard vascular anatomy. Two renal arteries were present in 86 grafts (18.5%); no grafts with 3 or more renal arteries were transplanted. Venous variations occurred in approximately 17% of cases. Postoperative complications occurred in 8 of 149 donors (5.4%) with variant anatomy and 22 of 317 donors (6.9%) with standard anatomy, without a statistically significant difference (Fisher's exact test, P = .686). Two recipients of kidneys with 2 renal arteries lost their grafts due to vascular complications in the perioperative period, whereas no perioperative graft losses occurred among recipients of single-artery kidneys. In our single-center experience, donor postoperative complication rates did not differ significantly between standard and variant vascular anatomy. Hand-assisted laparoscopic donor nephrectomy was feasible in selected donors with vascular variations. Three-dimensional vascular reconstruction may aid surgical planning, although its impact on outcomes requires further evaluation.

title: Uselessness of measuring anti-CD74 antibodies and Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor in axial spondyloarthritis patients in the DESIR cohort.
authors: Degboé Y, Masson M, Pers YM, Dupeyron A, Saraux A, Barnetche T, Clavel C, Tuaillon E, Zabraniecki L, Jamard B, Ruyssen-Witrand A, Constantin A.

title: Unraveling the shared genetic architecture of metabolic bone diseases via genomic structural equation modeling and multi-omics integration.
authors: Yi K, Wang F, Hu F, Tang W, Liu Y, Gao B, Zhang S, Jiang L, Ding J, Lei D, Yu J, Yu S, Wu B.
abstract: Background The shared genetic etiology underlying the comorbidity of skeletal degeneration and metabolic dysregulation remains poorly understood. This study aims to decipher the pleiotropic genetic architecture of multivariate metabolic bone diseases (mvMBDs) through an integrative summary-statistics framework. Methods We applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling (Genomic SEM) to integrate genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for six complex traits: osteoporosis (OP), chronic kidney disease (CKD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and C-reactive protein (CRP). Subsequent analyses incorporated robust fine-mapping (SuSiE/FINEMAP), transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), and partitioned heritability assessments to identify putative functional loci and regulatory mechanisms. Results Genomic SEM revealed significant genetic covariance among the six traits, successfully deriving a latent mvMBD construct. We identified 197 genomic risk loci, including 193 lead SNPs that did not achieve genome-wide significance in the six constituent univariate GWAS, predominantly localized in non-coding cis-regulatory elements (e.g., super-enhancers and intronic regions). Fine-mapping and TWAS prioritized critical pleiotropic genes (e.g., MACF1, CETP, SPP1, and HNF1A). Gene-set enrichment analyses identified enrichment for terms related to bone biology, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. Conclusion Our findings robustly demonstrate that mvMBDs are not isolated clinical entities but rather interconnected systemic syndromes underpinned by glycolipid metabolic dysregulation and shared pleiotropic regulatory networks. This study establishes a novel theoretical paradigm for the genetic basis of metabolic bone diseases, offering promising functional targets for future precision medicine interventions.

title: Understanding the processes involved in sepsis recognition across clinical contexts to guide individualised management: A phenomenographic study.
authors: Nemeckova M, Conner T, Steven A.
abstract: Background Sepsis is a highly heterogeneous condition, yet it is commonly recognised by application of standardised criteria, irrespective of clinical context. Understanding the complexity of sepsis recognition in the heterogeneous populations of patients with sepsis is critical to better target our resources to the needs of patients. Our aim was to examine nurses' clinical experiences to understand the processes involved in sepsis recognition across clinical contexts. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 26 nurses with various levels of experience in caring for patients with sepsis from multiple hospital settings. The interviews were phenomenographically analysed using the Arkelind method. The Cynefin framework was used to inform the organisation of findings according to contextual complexity. Findings We identified four categories of description that represent different ways of experiencing sepsis recognition: recognise sepsis by following protocol-based care, recognise sepsis by following disease-specific care, recognise sepsis according to emergent care, and recognise sepsis according to emergency care. The categories emerged from various clinical contexts, ranging from the simple to the highly complex. This variability directed clinical management by helping nurses decide whether guidelines apply to the individual patient and how they should be integrated into clinical decision-making. Conclusions Despite its apparent simplicity, sepsis recognition is complex and context-dependent. Rather than relying on an identical strategy for all patients, effective clinical decisions require personalisation based on the characteristics of the clinical contexts. Our findings show that considering the availability of data, predictability and cause-and-effect relationships can inform the selection of an appropriate approach to sepsis recognition. This approach demands adaptability; however, unless we adopt an approach that is appropriate to the level of clinical complexity, significant improvements in sepsis recognition may not be seen. Prospective research is required to validate our findings.

title: Transfemoral bone-anchored limbs alter joint-load-line offset during walking.
authors: Gaffney BMM, Milius DW, Melton DH, Christiansen CL, Stoneback JW.
abstract: Individuals with transfemoral amputation are at a heightened risk of musculoskeletal overuse injuries and reduced stability, largely due to altered joint biomechanics. The position of the ground reaction force (GRF) relative to hip and knee joints directly influences both joint biomechanics and dynamic stability and is influenced both by both movement patterns and prosthetic alignment. However, it is unknown if it is influenced by prosthetic suspension type. Our objective was to determine how the position of the GRF relative to hip and knee joint centers during walking differs between individuals with transfemoral amputation using either a socket prosthesis or bone-anchored limb (BAL). Motion capture data was collected from a convenience sample of 17 participants with unilateral transfemoral amputation during overground walking at two timepoints: before and 12-months following BAL implantation. The distances between the GRF line of action and the hip and knee joints in the sagittal and frontal planes were calculated and compared across timepoints (α = 0.05). The distance between the GRF and hip joint center was less medial (p < 0.001) on the amputated limb and more lateral (p < 0.001) on the intact limb during stance period when using a BAL compared to a socket prosthesis. Closer positioning of the GRF relative to the hip joint may reduce frontal plane compensatory strategies required for hip stabilization, potentially reflecting a biomechanical stable gait pattern when using a BAL.

title: TikTok Videos on the Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Have Low Educational Quality and Reliability.
authors: Conteduca J, Brindisino F, Casto A, Valentino L, Scrimitore A, Bernetti A, Rollo G.
abstract: Purpose To assess the quality, reliability, and engagement of TikTok videos addressing the material about medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL). Methods Between November 2 and 24, 2024, a comprehensive search of the TikTok platform was performed using both keyword-based search ("MPFL," "medial patellofemoral ligament") and hashtag-based search (#MPFL) to maximize content capture. Videos were included if they addressed the MPFL with respect to anatomy, injury mechanism, clinical evaluation, surgical management, or rehabilitation. Each video was independently assessed using the DISCERN instrument, Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark criteria, Global Quality Scale, and Patient Education and Decision Support Score. Video characteristics, including duration, number of views, likes, shares, and shares, were recorded, and correlations between engagement metrics and quality scores were analyzed. Results Of 100 videos analyzed, 9% were posted by medical doctors, 3% by physiotherapists, and 88% by private users. Most videos focused on personal experience, representing 74% of the information type and 80% of the content type. The mean scores of DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association , Global Quality Scale, and Patient Education and Decision Support Score were 16.25 ± 4.07, 0.1 ± 0.4, 1.1 ± 0.5, and 0.6 ± 1.88, respectively. Videos uploaded by medical professionals achieved significantly higher quality scores across all metrics ( P P = .173). Engagement metrics (views, likes, shares) showed moderate positive correlations with DISCERN ( r = 0.31) and Patient Education and Decision Support Score ( r = 0.39), whereas video duration showed no correlation with any quality index. Conclusions TikTok videos related to the MPFL show low educational quality and limited reliability, with the most content produced by nonmedical users. Videos uploaded by health care professionals achieved significantly higher quality scores across all evaluated assessment tools. Clinical relevance Patients with MPFL pathology frequently seek medical information on social media platforms. Awareness of the limited educational quality and reliability of MPFL-related content on TikTok may help clinicians better counsel patients regarding online health information.

title: The effect of dual task-oriented circuit training on neuroplasticity and walking adaptability in subacute stroke patients: A pilot and feasibility study.
authors: Arisanti F, Ropii B, Ghaida S, Tristiana Dewi T, Poernomo BCS, Sribudiani Y, Amalia L, Engkasan JP, Biben V.
abstract: Background Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with a substantial proportion of survivors experiencing persistent limitations in functional mobility. Although many individuals regain the ability to walk in structured clinical environments, only a minority achieve independent community ambulation due to cognitive-motor interference (CMI). The subacute phase is characterized by heightened neuroplastic potential and responsiveness to rehabilitation. Dual Task-Oriented Circuit Training (DTOCT) integrates task-oriented circuit training with concurrent cognitive challenges and may provide a functionally relevant approach to addressing cognitive-motor interference. However, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects in subacute stroke remain unclear. Methods This three-arm, participant-blinded, randomized pilot and feasibility trial will recruit 36 individuals with subacute stroke and allocate them equally to DTOCT, Task-Oriented Circuit Training (TOCT), or Dual Task Training (DTT). Participants will receive three supervised sessions per week for 4 weeks (12 sessions). Primary outcomes will assess feasibility and safety, including adherence, retention, adverse events, heart rate, blood pressure, and perceived exertion. Secondary exploratory outcomes will include walking endurance assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test, gait speed using the 10-Meter Walk Test, walking adaptability using the Standardized Walking Obstacle Course, and serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor as an exploratory peripheral biomarker associated with neuroplasticity. Discussion This pilot study is designed to determine the feasibility and safety of DTOCT and to generate preliminary effect estimates for clinical and neurobiological outcomes. The findings will inform primary outcome selection, intervention refinement, and sample-size estimation for a subsequent adequately powered randomized controlled trial rather than establish definitive efficacy or superiority. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07494357 (registered prospectively). Protocol ID: IKFR-202603.01).

title: The Chimeric Osteomyocutaneous Anterolateral Thigh Flap: A Novel Method for Lower Extremity Long Bone Reconstruction.
authors: LoGiudice J, Mather T, Hsieh M, Law B, Neilson J, Wooldridge A, Schmeling G.

title: Surgical treatment of thoracic vertebral chondrosarcoma with total en bloc spondylectomy: a case report.
authors: Sakti YM, Lanodiyu ZA, Prasetyo TE, Nurfadhilah MI, Sari DAP, Ridha M, Santiko W, Darutama AA, Anggunio V, Pratama IA, Aji AS, Calisto KE, Adamina ZN, Rukmoyo T.
abstract: Spinal chondrosarcoma is a rare malignant cartilage-forming tumor that is largely resistant to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, making complete surgical resection the cornerstone of treatment. We report a 60-year-old man with recurrent thoracic chondrosarcoma involving the T4-T6 vertebrae following previous intralesional decompression, spinal stabilization, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Revision surgery was performed through a posterior approach with implant removal, wide tumor excision, total en bloc spondylectomy (TES), spinal reconstruction using an expandable cage, posterior instrumentation, and spinal fusion. Histopathological examination confirmed recurrent grade II conventional chondrosarcoma. The patient remained neurologically stable after surgery without major perioperative complications. The present case indicates the limitations of intralesional surgery and adjuvant therapy in conventional chondrosarcoma and supports TES as the treatment for complete tumor excision and optimal local control, despite its technical difficulty.

title: Sternal "Medusa's head" sign.
authors: Ogul H.

title: Sleep quality, perceived stress, and dry eye disease among university students in Ghana: A cross-sectional study of individual and joint associations.
authors: Ayobi B, Attram GO, Okyere BV, Osrah BA, Assan JK, Abokyi S.
abstract: Purpose Dry Eye Disease (DED) is highly prevalent among university students and may be influenced by modifiable factors such as psychological stress and sleep disturbance. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the associations of sleep disturbance and perceived stress with DED, while the secondary objective was to evaluate their potential interaction. Methods This analytical cross-sectional study included a random sample of university students aged 18-34 years. Perceived stress was assessed using the Perceived Stress Scale, and sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. DED was diagnosed according to TFOS DEWS II criteria using the Ocular Surface Disease Index, tear break-up time, corneal staining, and Schirmer testing. Robust Poisson regression models were used to estimate relative risks (RRs) for DED associated with sleep disturbance and stress. Interaction effects were assessed on both additive and multiplicative scales. Results The prevalence of DED was 77.9%. Sleep disturbance was present in 75.9% of participants, while 21.3% reported high perceived stress. In univariate analyses, both sleep disturbance and stress were significantly associated with DED prevalence (sleep disturbance: χ²(1, 403) = 14.57, p Conclusion Sleep disturbance and perceived stress were independently associated with an increased risk of DED in this student population. However, there was no evidence that stress modified the association between sleep disturbance and DED.

title: Sleep disorders in patients with systemic sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Bayala YLT, Ayouba Tinni I, Sougué C, Kaboré F, Zabsonré-Tiendrebeogo WJS, Ouédraogo DD.
abstract: Background Systemic sclerosis is a rare autoimmune disease associated with substantial morbidity and reduced quality of life. Sleep disturbance has been reported with variable frequency in patients with systemic sclerosis, though its prevalence remains incompletely characterised. Objective This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of sleep disorders in patients with systemic sclerosis. Methods Six databases were searched up to 15th February 2026 without language restriction. Studies reporting sleep outcomes in adults with systemic sclerosis were eligible. Prevalence estimates were pooled using a logit transformation with a random-effects model and Hartung-Knapp correction. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Publication bias was evaluated with Egger's test and the trim-and-fill method. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251152354). Results Twenty-three studies totalling 1487 patients were included across all analyses. Eleven studies (820 patients) contributed to the primary meta-analysis of poor sleep quality assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. The pooled prevalence of poor sleep quality was 76.49% (95% CI 66.62 to 84.13%), with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I 2 =70.1%) and a 95% prediction interval of 49.66 to 91.47%, indicating that the true prevalence may range from approximately half to nearly all patients across different SSc populations. Five studies (346 patients) contributed to the obstructive sleep apnea meta-analysis, yielding a pooled prevalence of 40.30% (95% CI 25.56 to 57.04%, I 2 =71.8%) with a 95% prediction interval of 13.95 to 73.75%. Five additional studies were included in a qualitative synthesis only, and three randomised controlled trials addressed sleep interventions. Egger's test identified possible funnel plot asymmetry. After trim-and-fill adjustment, four studies were imputed and the corrected estimate was 69.62% (95% CI 57.33 to 79.63%), somewhat lower than the primary estimate, suggesting that the primary estimate may be modestly influenced by publication bias. The certainty of evidence was rated as low according to GRADE. Conclusion Available evidence suggests that sleep disorders may affect approximately three quarters of patients with systemic sclerosis when assessed by the PSQI, and obstructive sleep apnea may affect more than one third when evaluated by objective tools. These estimates carry low GRADE certainty and wide prediction intervals, and should not be interpreted as definitive prevalence figures. Larger prospective studies and well-powered randomised trials are needed to establish more precise estimates and to evaluate targeted sleep interventions in this population.

title: Simultaneous Oblique Lateral Interbody Fusion (OLIF) and posterior transpedicular screw fixation in treatment of lumbar pyogenic spondylodiscitis.
authors: Omran K, Abdel-Fattah AS, Hassan MY.
abstract: Background Anterior retroperitoneal spine surgery is advocated for the management of lumbar pyogenic spondylodiscitis (LPS) to target the anterior spondylodiscal pathology. The OLIF corridor provides access to the anterior infective lumbar lesion directly through the pre-psoas space with minimal complications and morbidity, successful debridement, and fusion rate, while respecting surgeon preference, accounting for equipment availability, and the learning curve. Purpose The aim of this study was to analyze the clinical, radiological, and functional outcomes after combined OLIF and posterior transpedicular screw fixation in the treatment of LPS. Study design This was a retrospective single-center clinical study. Methods Twenty-seven patients with complicated LPS were treated surgically by combined OLIF and posterior percutaneous transpedicular screw fixation from 2018 to 2021. Preoperatively and postoperatively, all patients were examined clinically for back or leg pain by applying the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), sensory or motor deficit, Arabic-validated Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and modified Prolo scores; radiologically (plain X-ray, multidetector computerized tomography (MDCT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)). Perioperative data and complications were recorded. All patients were regularly followed for 26 months regarding clinical outcomes, functional status, and radiological measures. Results Significant postoperative improvement in VAS for back and leg pain, ODI, and modified Prolo scores was reported, with statistically significant differences between preoperative, during, and at the final follow-up. The mean fusion time was 10.52 ± 1.24 months. Twenty-five patients (92.6%) showed definitive fusion (grade 5) according to Lee and Suh's criteria. Conclusion This combined surgery is an effective method for treating LPS with adequate canal decompression, radiological correction, and functional recovery.

title: Risk factors of high osteoporosis risk in subjects over 40 years in Mongolia.
authors: Jaalkhorol M, Ikeda Y, Narangerel E, Dashtseren A, Khulgar T, Munkhsonguuli U, Iimaa T, Sampil T, Enkhbayar N, Bruyere O.
abstract: In Mongolia, osteoporosis screening is difficult because advanced scans are scarce. In 356 adults aged 40 years or older, stronger handgrip strength was associated with a lower OSTA-defined osteoporosis risk category in both men and women, whereas lifestyle factors were not. Adding handgrip testing could improve low-cost screening strategies. Background Osteoporosis is a growing public health concern in Mongolia, where access to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is limited. The Osteoporosis Self-Assessment Test (OSTA) provides a simple, low-cost alternative for identifying individuals at risk. This study aimed to examine factors associated with OSTA-defined osteoporosis risk categories among adults aged 40 years and older in Mongolia. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 356 adults (200 men, 156 women) recruited from two urban health units. Sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, medical history, and handgrip strength were assessed through structured interviews and standardized measurements. OSTA scores were categorized into low, moderate, and high risk based on established sex-specific thresholds. Group differences in categorical variables were evaluated using chi-square tests. Logistic regression models were performed separately for men and women to identify factors independently associated with the combined moderate/high OSTA risk category. Results Age, sex, educational level, comorbidities, and BMI were significantly associated with OSTA categories. Higher dominant handgrip strength was associated with lower odds of the combined moderate/high OSTA risk category in both men (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.06-0.58) and women (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.02-0.51). In contrast, lifestyle factors such as smoking, alcohol consumption, diet, and sedentary time were not independently associated with OSTA scores. Conclusion Several demographic and clinical factors were associated with OSTA risk categories in this low-resource setting. The strong association with handgrip strength suggests potential added value in integrating functional assessments into screening strategies. These findings support the development of scalable, low-cost approaches for osteoporosis risk stratification in Mongolia.

title: Revolutionary discoveries and the disruption index: Probing the relationship.
authors: Bornmann L, Haunschild R, Paludan SR, Wray KB.
abstract: A few years ago, the Disruption Index (DI) was proposed as a tool for identifying disruptive research. However, it remains unclear whether the index actually measures what it claims to measure. Our proposed survey plans to examine the extent to which the papers identified by the DI as especially disruptive are the same as the papers that scientists working in a field identify as especially disruptive. We, thus, aim to test an assumption about what the DI measures, specifically, that papers with high DI values are papers reporting revolutionary discoveries. We will focus on the field of immunology. Our survey data will be drawn from researchers who have published many papers in immunology.

title: Revisiting menopausal hormone therapy for bone health: evidence, controversies, and clinical positioning in India in 2026.
authors: Vaghasia N, Nagendra L, Kapoor N, Maldar A, Baro A, Bhandarkar A, Joshi A, Ghosh A, Monteiro AS, Joseph A, Mishra I, Agarwal K, Cherian KE, Tandon N, Kaur P, John R, Shetty S, Das S, Bhadada S, Kalra S, Bhattacharya S, Patra S, Sidana S, Mondal S, Paul TV, Sriram U, Mithal A.
abstract: Menopause is characterized by the rapid decline of estrogen exposure, resulting in accelerated bone loss superimposed on the gradual age-related decline in bone mass. This process is particularly relevant in India, where women experience menopause earlier than Western populations, thereby increasing lifetime fracture risk. Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) has been evaluated extensively over the years for skeletal health, with consistent evidence demonstrating preservation of bone mineral density and reduction in vertebral and hip fractures, especially when initiated early after menopause. Although multiple concerns arose following the Women's Health Initiative in terms of cardiovascular safety and breast cancer risk, leading to a decline in MHT use, subsequent analyses have supported a more favorable benefit-risk profile in appropriately selected younger postmenopausal women. Current evidence suggests that individualized MHT can also improve skeletal outcomes while benefiting menopausal symptoms and overall quality of life. This review revisits the evolving role of MHT in bone health in the Indian context.

title: Revision surgery for osteochondral lesions of the talus: Are there predictive factors for successful surgery?
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
authors: Biehl C, El Khassawna T, Fritzsche C, Walter N, Biehl L, Heiss C, Rupp M.
abstract: Purpose Osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT) are common injuries of the ankle associated with persistent pain and functional impairment. Revision procedures are frequent. Currently, objective criteria to guide revision decision-making remain limited. This retrospective study is designed to identify factors associated with patient-reported outcome after surgery pathways and to enhance selection of patients who may benefit from revision surgery in OLT. Methods Between 2015 and 2018, 64 patients underwent surgical treatment for OLT (97 procedures in total). A symptomatic subgroup of 21 patients required additional procedures (33 revision operations). Outcomes at a mean follow-up of 3 years were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, and the Foot and Ankle Outcome Score (FAOS). Primary outcome was a patient-level PROM-based classification (Success/ Partial relief/No relief) at follow-up. Analyses were performed per patient; procedure counts were reported descriptively. Results Of 64 patients, 43 (67%) achieved a successful outcome after a single procedure, whereas 21 (33%) required multiple procedures. In the multiple-surgery group, 9/21 (43%) were classified as Success at follow-up. PROM categories in follow up correlated significantly with AOFAS, VAS, and FAOS. A longer interval (> 24 months) between procedures might be associated with a higher likelihood of a habituation effect at follow-up. Conclusion PROM-based classification provides a patient-centered assessment of outcome after revision pathways for OLT.
