The FAOS score subdomains proved particularly valuable in identifying specific issues that could justify a revision. The waiting time between surgeries appears relevant and should be considered when planning revision surgery. Our data suggests that a longer interval between surgeries (exceeding 24 months) might be associated with habituation effects and adaptation processes, leading to a reduction in periarticular swelling and the continuation of physiotherapy. Despite moderate success rates, the treatment of OLT remains challenging, and preoperative factors such as age and activity level should be considered when evaluating the chances of success.

title: Research on the design and mechanical properties of extended constant resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolts.
authors: Cheng S, Tang Z, Zhang S, Yu M.
abstract: To address the premature fracture of anchor bolts caused by the mismatched yielding distance between anchor bolts and hydraulic supports in the advanced support section of rock burst-prone roadways, an elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt was designed-with its yielding distance specifically coordinated to match that of hydraulic supports. ABAQUS numerical simulation was utilized to investigate the mechanical characteristics of this novel anchor bolt under static loading, as well as under varying impact energies and impact velocities. A comparative analysis was further performed against the mechanical performance of conventional anchor bolts. The results reveal the following: Under static loading, the elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt exhibits a fracture load of 160.6 kN, a fracture displacement of 523.2 mm, an elongation rate of 20.93%, and an energy absorption capacity of 69.7 kJ. Under impact velocities within 9 m/s, the impact velocity has little effect on the fracture load, elongation, and energy absorption of constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolts, while the impact resistance time exhibits a nonlinear decreasing trend with increasing impact velocity. Under both static and dynamic loading conditions, the extended constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolt exhibits superior impact resistance and can effectively address the problem of premature bolt fracture caused by the mismatch between the bolt yielding distance and that of the hydraulic support in the three-level energy-absorbing support system. The findings provide a new perspective for bolt design.

title: Reply to: "The FAST Protocol: A Novel Approach for Staged Autologous Breast Reconstruction".
authors: Nelissen SH, Maarse W, Krijgh DD.

title: Removal of a large maxillary sinus mucocele via Le Fort I osteotomy during orthognathic surgery: a case report.
authors: Boylu D, Boylu ÖF.
abstract: Maxillary sinus mucoceles are uncommon expansile lesions resulting from impaired sinus drainage and mucus accumulation. We report a 19-year-old male with a large left maxillary sinus mucocele identified during planning for bimaxillary orthognathic surgery. Preoperative cone-beam computed tomography showed complete sinus occupation with extension into the nasal cavity and toward the nasopharynx. During the independently planned Le Fort I osteotomy, maxillary down-fracture provided direct access, allowing intact removal of the well-encapsulated lesion. Histopathological examination confirmed a mucocele. At 2-month follow-up, the patient had no nasal symptoms, and postoperative imaging demonstrated marked sinus re-aeration without radiographic evidence of residual or recurrent disease. When independently indicated, Le Fort I osteotomy may provide effective access for simultaneous management of selected extensive maxillary sinus mucoceles.

title: Reduced cognitive empathy and differences in EEG activity in low-achieving adolescents.
authors: Hernández-González S, Gómez-Climent MÁ, Clemente-Soriano A, Alba Robles JL, Caurín-Alonso C, Solbes J.
abstract: Students with low academic achievement tend to display more maladaptive behaviours in interactions with peers and teachers. Empathy plays a key mediating role in these interactions and is also linked to academic performance. In particular, facial emotion recognition is one component of socioemotional processing that may contribute to empathic responding. To explore the relationship between empathy, emotion recognition, and academic achievement, a comparative study was conducted with 40 students aged 14-17, divided into two groups: one with low academic achievement enrolled in a school support programme, and a control group with adequate academic performance. A multimethod approach was applied, including the Basic Empathy Scale, a facial expression recognition test, and electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings. Results showed significantly lower cognitive empathy in the low-achieving group in the primary between-group analysis. The overall between-group difference in facial emotion recognition accuracy was not statistically significant. EEG analyses identified exploratory between-group differences in source-level oscillatory activity estimates during facial-expression processing. These electrophysiological findings provide complementary information about task-related activity patterns but should not be interpreted as specific neural markers of empathy or as confirmation of a behavioural facial emotion recognition deficit. Overall, the multimethod approach offers complementary perspectives on socioemotional functioning in low-achieving adolescents, although the exploratory EEG findings require cautious interpretation and replication in larger, independent samples.

title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia.
authors: Takaiso H, Nomura K, Watanabe T, Nitta Y, Heak A, Im S, Okubo Y, Miyachi T.
abstract: Background Emergency care capacity remains critically limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in rural areas where specialists and infrastructure are scarce. In Cambodia, stroke and ischemic heart disease are leading causes of mortality, and trauma burdens are increasing alongside rapid infrastructure development. Evidence on emergency equipment availability and frontline provider skills at the facility level in rural provinces remains limited. Methods A facility-based cross-sectional assessment was conducted across all seven public referral hospitals in Battambang Province, Cambodia, in January 2023. Emergency equipment availability was evaluated through structured interviews and direct visual confirmation against the World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care. Clinical skill examinations were administered to physicians (two scenario-based cases: acute stroke with airway compromise; traumatic injury with tension pneumothorax and intra-abdominal bleeding) and nurses (a Basic Life Support [BLS] scenario assessed in pairs). Hospitals were stratified by Complementary Package of Activities (CPA) level: CPA1 (basic care only), CPA2 (including surgery and intensive care), and CPA3 (highest provincial level). Results At Complementary Package of Activities (CPA)1 (basic care only) hospitals, intubation equipment and 12-lead electrocardiogram were each available in only 25% of facilities. None had a crash cart, blood transfusion capacity, basic metabolic panel, or coagulation testing. In the stroke scenario, airway patency was confirmed by 28.6% of physicians at CPA1 hospitals, compared with 70.0% at CPA2 hospitals (including surgery and intensive care), 57.1% at the CPA3 hospital (highest provincial level), and 75.0% at the Provincial Health Department. In the trauma scenario, no physician at CPA1 hospitals correctly performed spinal immobilization with the spine kept straight or thoracentesis at the correct anatomical location. Among 38 nurse pairs, 97.4% initiated chest compressions promptly, but only 21.1% demonstrated correct compression technique, and 13.2% provided effective bag-valve-mask ventilation. Deficiencies in equipment and clinical skills were most pronounced at CPA1 hospitals. Conclusions Emergency care capacity in Battambang Province was substantially limited, with the greatest deficiencies at CPA1 hospitals. Recurrent low-cost training and targeted strengthening of basic emergency care should be prioritized at lower-level facilities.

title: Prehospital damage-control amputation and packed red blood cell transfusion for severe bilateral lower-limb crush injury in a remote setting: a case report.
authors: Li J, Ma M, Liu Q, Tian W, Li J, Zhang C.
abstract: Prehospital damage-control amputation in civilian emergency systems is rare, especially combined with prehospital packed red blood cell transfusion. We report a 30-year-old man with bilateral lower-limb crush injury after entrapment in an industrial roller machine in a remote area. Despite initially preserved blood pressure, he developed marked hemodynamic deterioration and arrived at the hospital with a blood pressure of 74/49 mmHg. Both limbs were non-salvageable. Prehospital bilateral amputation with vascular ligation was performed on scene, followed by transfusion of one local unit of packed red blood cells (~200 ml). He survived after stump revision, intensive care, and rehabilitation. This case describes the sequential use of prehospital hemorrhage control and packed red blood cell transfusion during the same prehospital episode in a patient with a life-threatening entrapment injury and delayed transport.

title: Predicting Return to Play After Achilles Tendon Injury in National Football League Players Using Machine Learning.
authors: Chen Z, Wang NM, Lei Z, Thomas GM, Pedowitz D, Parekh SG.
abstract: BackgroundNational Football League (NFL) players frequently experience Achilles tendon (AT) injuries. However, there is mixed evidence regarding factors influencing return to play (RTP) after AT injury. The objective of this study is to develop machine learning models to predict NFL players' likelihood of RTP within 1 year of an AT tear. Hypothesis Machine learning models can predict 1-year RTP status in NFL players following AT tear. Study design Retrospective Cohort.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted to identify NFL players who sustained unilateral AT injuries from 2004 to 2024. Player demographics and performance data were recorded. Return to play was defined as generating playing statistics. Five machine learning models were developed: logistic regression, random forest classifier, XGBoost, Gaussian naive Bayes, and K-nearest neighbors. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 were used to assess model performance.ResultsOne hundred seventy-six NFL players were identified with an AT injury. One hundred eight players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 63 players did not (class 0). In the full cohort, injury etiology was the most influential feature associated with 1-year RTP, followed by pre-injury performance. Among the 99 players with a confirmed AT tear, 48 players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 51 players did not (class 0). Within the confirmed-tear cohort, draft round and games started were the leading predictors of 1-year RTP, which was best predicted by random forest with a mean accuracy of 0.69, precision of 0.68, recall of 0.70, and an F1-score of 0.69 for class 0.ConclusionMachine learning models that combine clinical and performance metrics of NFL athletes demonstrated potential for predicting 1-year RTP after AT injury and identifying factors associated with RTP. Clinical relevance Machine learning could be integrated into clinical decision-making and prognosis to refine rehabilitation approaches in NFL players. Level of evidence Level 3.

title: Oxidative stress-driven cellular heterogeneity in Knee Osteoarthritis: scRNA-seq pinpoints SPP1 and CYBA for diagnostic development.
authors: Liu Y, Chi Y, Yin J, Yao J.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Oxidative stress plays a critical role in KOA pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with machine learning to uncover potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for KOA. ScRNA-seq data from KOA cartilage tissues were obtained from the GEO database to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify disease-associated chondrocyte subsets. CellChat was used to analyze intercellular communication, and Monocle2 was applied to reconstruct cell differentiation trajectories. Oxidative stress activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell, while high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was performed to identify oxidative stress-related gene modules. Candidate genes were screened using Venn analysis and further refined by LASSO regression, SVM-RFE, and XGBoost combined with SHAP analysis. Diagnostic performance was assessed, and biological relevance was explored through immune infiltration and pathway analyses. Experimental validation was conducted using qRT-PCR and western blot assays in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. InfC and ProFC were detected specifically in OA cartilage and exhibited high oxidative stress activity. InfC was enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways, whereas ProFC was associated with cell cycle regulation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Integrated hdWGCNA and machine-learning analyses consistently identified CYBA and SPP1 as candidate genes. The two-gene model achieved bootstrap-corrected AUCs of 0.937 and 0.825 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. qRT-PCR and western blot analyses further showed increased CYBA and SPP1 expression in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. Conclusion InfC and ProFC may represent OA-associated chondrocyte states characterized by enhanced oxidative stress, while CYBA and SPP1 may serve as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Given the small cohort sizes and preliminary in vitro validation, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts and functional studies.

title: OsteoNet-X: A deep residual learning framework for automated osteoporosis detection from knee X-ray images.
authors: Sangula SK, Ibrahim SPS.
abstract: Osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mineral density and increased susceptibility to fractures, making early diagnosis essential for effective clinical intervention and long-term patient management. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated significant potential for automated bone disease assessment using medical imaging modalities. In this study, a unified deep learning framework, termed OsteoNet-X, is proposed for automated osteoporosis detection and multi-class bone health classification using knee X-ray images. Unlike conventional image classification approaches, OsteoNet-X integrates YOLO-based Region of Interest (ROI) localization, DenseNet-based feature extraction, Feature-Aware Learning (FAL) optimization, and Grad-CAM-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance both classification performance and model interpretability. The ROI extraction stage automatically identifies anatomically relevant knee joint regions, reducing background interference and enabling more discriminative feature learning. Subsequently, DenseNet facilitates efficient feature propagation and hierarchical representation learning for distinguishing normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis conditions. The incorporation of XAI further provides visual explanations of model decisions by highlighting clinically relevant regions within the knee joint. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that OsteoNet-X achieves a classification accuracy of 97.08%, a macro F1-score of 96.61%, and a weighted F1-score of 97.11%.

title: Orthotopic heart transplantation associated with hemiarch reconstruction for advanced heart failure and chronic aortic dissection: a case report.
authors: Sánchez OE, Pérez-Ariza V, Cruz Buitrago RH, Parra JF, Rios W, Nuñez F.
abstract: Concomitant orthotopic heart transplantation and aortic arch replacement are extremely rare, particularly in chronic Stanford type A dissection. A 43-year-old man with end-stage heart failure and chronic aortic dissection underwent combined orthotopic heart transplantation and hemiarch replacement. Because of concomitant liver donation, the donor inferior vena cava required pericardial patch reconstruction. Despite early right ventricular dysfunction requiring veno-arterial ECMO, the patient recovered completely and was discharged with preserved graft function. This case demonstrates the feasibility of a single-stage combined approach with excellent postoperative outcomes in carefully selected patients.

title: On the variability of generative artificial intelligence methods in conceptual modeling: an experimental evaluation on combining causal maps.
authors: Flandre NY, Daumas C, Giabbanelli PJ.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly support time-consuming conceptual modeling tasks such as building or combining models from text. In this context, causal maps are labeled, directed graphs that represent causal relationships (edges) between selected factors (nodes) in a problem domain. Modelers control the output through the LLM's prompt and decoding parameters such as temperature, and recent studies either use a default temperature or minimize it by expecting that it supports replicability. However, evidence about this expectation remains limited, as does our understanding of how different LLMs and decoding or prompting strategies shape results. We assess the extent to which findings are an artifact of the LLM or its variability rather than a reflection of the modeler's controls. We focus on the common conceptual modeling task of combining models, exemplified through three algorithms that reflect a variety of prompting techniques. We use five LLMs (DeepSeek, Gemini, GPT, Qwen, Ministral) and different versions to account for the potential impact of the architectures. Using the Design of Experiments approach of factorial analyses (supplemented by paired tests and confidence interval checks), our results show that outcomes differ significantly across LLMs and versions. Depending on the algorithm, randomness from the LLM can be the dominating factor, responsible for up to 96% of the variation in results. This happens even if we directly control the decoding, as evidenced by our comparison of greedy, beam-search, and contrastive decoding. We find that prompt effects are systematic but metric-dependent, while decoding affects performance but there is no universally best strategy. Since our findings suggest that replicability of conceptual modeling studies using LLMs may be limited, future studies may report the distribution of performance measures alongside exact model, decoding, replication, and baseline-normalization settings.

title: Numerical study on infill fracturing of mature wells under free-drainage boundary conditions.
authors: Jiang X, Cong Z, Hubuqin H, Peng G, Li Y.
abstract: Infill fracturing of mature wells involves re-fracturing within previously stimulated clusters, targeting unstimulated regions of the parent well's fracture network. This strategy sustainably enhances hydrocarbon recovery from depleted reservoirs without the environmental footprint of new drilling. Establishing a numerical simulation model for this process is essential for optimization. In this study, a numerical model for mature well infill fracturing was developed based on the extended finite element method and a free-drainage boundary module. The results indicate that prior production from mature wells primarily affects the fracture length and curvature in the infill wells. As infill fracturing-induced fractures propagate toward the far-field region, they are significantly influenced by the heterogeneous pore pressure distribution in the reservoir. This leads to a pronounced increase in fracture curvature. Compared with conventional fracturing, the curvature of fractures under infill fracturing is approximately 30% higher within the same simulation time, while the fracture length is notably shorter. With the increase in production time, fractures in infill wells tend to exhibit greater tortuosity. This enhanced complexity allows for more effective contact between the fractures and the reservoir, thereby improving the production potential of the infill wells to some extent.

title: Not the Last Word: Are Orthopaedic Surgeons Working Class?
authors: Bernstein J.

title: Neurological deterioration after posterior decompression of an unrecognised calcified thoracic disc: recovery following endoscopic discectomy.
authors: Mobbs RJ, Lui EHY, Reidy J.
abstract: Calcified thoracic disc herniation is uncommon but carries substantial operative risk. A 67-year-old man with 12 months of progressive myelopathy from a T7-T8 disc herniation underwent posterior laminectomy and instrumented fusion without preoperative computed tomography (CT). He developed near-complete paraplegia, with lower-limb power of Medical Research Council grade 0-1/5. Subsequent CT demonstrated a densely calcified ventral disc. Following transfer, full-endoscopic transforaminal discectomy was performed to address the ventral compression without spinal cord retraction. By three months after the revision procedure, power improved to grade 4-4+/5 and he regained ambulation using a walking frame. Thoracic disc herniations being considered for surgery should be characterised with CT as well as magnetic resonance imaging. Calcified lesions warrant subspecialty review and an approach that directly addresses the ventral pathology. In selected patients, endoscopic discectomy may achieve effective decompression with limited access morbidity.

title: MyotonPRO-derived hamstring mechanical properties across testing positions and their associations with maximal strength.
authors: Herszfang S, Avitan N, Kalron A.
abstract: The MyotonPRO is increasingly used to quantify skeletal muscle mechanical properties; however, hamstring measurements may vary across testing positions, and the relationships between these measurements and maximal strength remain unclear. This study investigated differences in MyotonPRO-derived mechanical properties of the biceps femoris and semitendinosus across four testing positions and examined their exploratory associations with maximal isometric hamstring strength. Thirty healthy adults (18 males, 12 females; age 27.4 ± 4.9 years) underwent MyotonPRO assessment in the prone position, prone with the knee flexed to 90°, bilateral standing, and single-leg standing. Oscillation frequency, dynamic stiffness, logarithmic decrement, relaxation time, and creep were measured in both muscles. Maximal isometric hamstring strength was assessed using the End Range Hamstring Strength Test with handheld dynamometry. MyotonPRO-derived mechanical properties differed significantly across testing positions, with large position effects (partial η 2 = 0.355-0.822). Stiffness and oscillation frequency generally increased toward weight-bearing positions, whereas relaxation time and creep decreased; logarithmic decrement showed a less consistent pattern. Exploratory correlation analyses showed moderate-to-strong associations between maximal hamstring strength and stiffness, frequency, and relaxation time, as well as creep (|r| = 0.38-0.67), whereas logarithmic decrement showed weaker and more variable associations. In an exploratory hierarchical regression, adding logarithmic decrement to the selected stiffness measure increased R 2 from 0.440 to 0.500, but the incremental change was not statistically significant (ΔR 2 = 0.060, p = 0.082). These findings indicate that MyotonPRO-derived hamstring mechanical properties differ across testing positions and should therefore be interpreted within standardized testing conditions.

title: Mutation-resolved ABL1 inhibitor resistance prediction under mutation-disjoint and temporal cross-study validation.
authors: Deif MA, Hafez MA, Khishe M, Solyman A, Elhaty IAM.
abstract: Computational prediction of ABL1 tyrosine-kinase inhibitor (TKI) resistance is difficult because available mutation-drug datasets are small, imbalanced, and heterogeneous. This study evaluates structure-aware resistance prediction under mutation-disjoint internal validation and temporal cross-study outcome validation. The development benchmark comprised 144 ABL1 mutation-TKI records (19 resistant and 125 susceptible) labelled by a ten-fold affinity-loss criterion. A fixed panel of 11 documented structural and energetic predictors was used to minimize data-adaptive feature selection within the validation framework. A calibrated ensemble combining Elastic-Net logistic regression, radial-basis-function support-vector machines, random forests, and XGBoost was evaluated using mutation-disjoint five-fold grouped out-of-fold prediction repeated ten times. Temporal validation used a later prime-editing resistance map, yielding 84 exact mutation-TKI matches across imatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, and ponatinib; 61 had binary Sensitive/Resistant outcomes and 23 were retained as Intermediate. The 11-feature stack achieved grouped internal AUROC 0.645 (95% CI 0.429-0.830) and PR-AUC 0.230, with mean ± SD AUROC 0.583 ± 0.101 across repeated grouped splits. On the 61 binary later-study outcomes, AUROC was 0.605 (95% CI 0.431-0.874) and PR-AUC 0.835, modestly above the resistance-prevalence baseline of 0.770. External calibration was poor (Brier score 0.583; calibration slope 0.441). Elastic-Net showed somewhat higher temporal discrimination (AUROC 0.643; PR-AUC 0.877). These results indicate limited transportability across mutation identities and experimental platforms and support use of the framework for hypothesis-generating resistance screening rather than clinically calibrated treatment selection.

title: Minimally Invasive Surgery for Adult Scoliosis: Recent Updates and Advancements.
authors: Khan F, Hoofnagle MD, Mummaneni PV, Chan AK, Chou D.
abstract: Purpose of review Circumferential minimally invasive surgery (cMIS) for adult scoliosis has evolved over the past five years. Here, we review how advances in patient selection, operative technique, and technology have transformed the capabilities of cMIS for deformity. Recent findings Early cMIS was constrained by a "corrective ceiling" that limited its use to flexible deformities. Patient selection has since grown more nuanced, incorporating surgical complexity, patient-specific factors, and the deformity itself rather than radiographic thresholds alone. Technique has changed in parallel, as correction is now distributed across multiple interbody levels with segmental release, performed through both anterior and lateral techniques. Workflow and technology have adapted as well: single-position prone transpsoas and lateral prepsoas approaches may reduce intraoperative repositioning, staging extends treatment to patients with greater deformity or frailty, and robotics and patient-specific implants improve the precision of planning and execution. These advances have been accompanied by data demonstrating improved patient-reported outcomes and spinopelvic alignment at lower morbidity in appropriately selected patients. With the safety and efficacy of cMIS established, the field continues to push its boundaries toward more challenging pathology, as illustrated by contemporary cases of severe multiplanar deformity and complex revision. The boundaries of cMIS have expanded considerably beyond the flexible, moderate deformities for which these techniques were initially developed. Careful patient selection remains essential, as not all deformities are amenable to minimally invasive correction. Nevertheless, advances in surgical technique, operative workflow, and patient-specific planning have enabled increasingly severe and complex deformities to be addressed while preserving the fundamental advantages of minimally invasive surgery.

title: Mesenchymal progenitor cell Zeb1 regulates bone homeostasis and PTH-dependent anabolic responses.
authors: Liu B, Yang J, Chen Z, Liu Y, Niu S, Higashi Y, Takagi T, Tang Y, Weiss SJ, Chen G, Zhu L.
abstract: The regulation of postnatal bone homeostasis by specific transcriptional programs in skeletal mesenchymal progenitor cells remains incompletely understood. While epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcription factors are critical drivers of cellular plasticity, their physiological roles in bone-forming lineages are largely unknown. Here, we identify the EMT transcription factor Zeb1 as a central regulator of osteogenic differentiation in vitro and in vivo. Conditional knockout of Zeb1 in bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) using Prrx1-Cre impairs bone formation, giving rise to a significant osteopenic phenotype. At the cellular level, Zeb1-deficient BMSCs display impaired osteogenic differentiation and self-renewal. Transcriptional profiling further defined a role for Zeb1 in regulating the expression of the parathyroid hormone type 1 receptor (PTH1R), a key mediator of skeletal anabolism. Consequently, Zeb1 loss attenuated PTH1R levels and blunted downstream PTH signaling, rendering mice refractory to the bone-anabolic effects of intermittent PTH treatment. Taken together, these studies identify Zeb1 as a key transcriptional regulator governing osteoblastogenesis, bridging skeletal mesenchymal progenitor cell fate regulation with PTH-mediated anabolic control of bone mass.

title: Local Microenvironment in Adenoid Hypertrophy and Its Clinical Relevance.
authors: Ma JY, Chen AN, Yao Y, Wang H.
abstract: Adenoid hypertrophy (AH) is among the most common otolaryngologic disorders in childhood, and its development cannot be adequately explained by a single inflammatory process. Increasing evidence suggests that the adenoid functions not only as an important component of upper airway mucosal immunity but also as a critical site for persistent microbial colonization and local immune remodeling. This review examines AH from structural, immunologic, and microecological perspectives, offering an integrated analytical framework to better understand coordinated imbalance within the adenoidal microenvironment. Furthermore, we investigate the relationships between distinct microenvironmental patterns and clinical phenotypes and discuss both current therapeutic strategies and emerging precision intervention approaches. Collectively, existing evidence indicates that AH is a multifaceted disorder closely associated with microenvironmental reprogramming, and its clinical heterogeneity appears to be attributed to diverse underlying biological processes.

title: Letter: Radiocarpal stability in chronic radiocarpal dislocation: Osteotomy is only one part of reconstruction.
authors: de Villeneuve Bargemon JB, Audiffret L.

title: Length of stay and nhi-reimbursed expenditures after robotic-assisted surgery in taiwan: a nationwide population-based study.
authors: Chen PD, Chung CH, Lu CY, Su TW, Wu YM.
abstract: Population-level evidence comparing robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with laparoscopic surgery (LS)/video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open surgery (OS) across multiple procedures from a payer perspective remains limited. This study aimed to compare postoperative length of stay (LOS) and insurer-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures among RAS, LS/VATS, and OS across representative procedures following the expansion of RAS reimbursement in Taiwan. This retrospective nationwide population-based cohort study was conducted using claims data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. We identified adults (age ≥ 18 y) who underwent 1 of 12 representative procedures spanning thoracic, hepatobiliary-pancreatic, colorectal, urologic, and gynecologic specialties between September 1 and December 31, 2024. Surgical approaches were classified as robotic-assisted surgery (RAS), laparoscopic or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (LS/VATS), or open surgery (OS) using the corresponding procedure and robotic-assistance codes in the NHI claims database. The outcomes were postoperative LOS and total NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials during the index hospitalization. Procedure-specific stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to each pairwise comparison. This study included 17 549 patients. Of these patients, 2900, 9763, and 4886 underwent RAS, LS/VATS, and OS, respectively. RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS than LS/VATS for lung resection, colectomy, partial nephrectomy, and nephroureterectomy and with lower reimbursed expenditures for lung resection, partial pancreatectomy, nephroureterectomy, and radical prostatectomy. Compared with OS, RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, with the largest difference noted for colectomy (8.38 vs. 14.80 d). Moreover, RAS was associated with lower reimbursed expenditures than OS for lung resection, minor hepatectomy, partial pancreatectomy, colectomy, and malignant hysterectomy. During the early period following the September 2024 expansion of NHI reimbursement for RAS in Taiwan, RAS was associated with shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, whereas differences in NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials varied by procedure and comparator. Given the observational study design, residual confounding, and limited propensity-score overlap in several comparisons, particularly RAS versus OS, these findings should be interpreted as procedure-specific associations rather than evidence of clinical or economic superiority.

title: Introducing the rodent open science skeletal archive.
authors: Maye P, Kelleher B, Shostak W, Mark A, Sinder B, Che X, Choi JY, Huang CH, Salisbury J, Shin DG, Andersen TL, Rowe DW.
abstract: Musculoskeletal diseases affect more than half of the adult population, yet the mechanisms underlying skeletal pathology remain incompletely understood. Rodent animal models have been central to advancing this knowledge, generating decades of skeletal phenotyping data through well-established quantitative methods. Despite this, no dedicated repository exists to archive and share this data, leaving the vast majority of rodent skeletal phenotyping results accessible only through individual publications and unavailable for broader integration and reuse. Here we introduce the Rodent Open Science Skeletal Archive (ROSSA; rossa.uchc.edu), an NIH-funded, open-access web-based repository designed to store and share rodent skeletal phenotyping data. We describe the architecture of ROSSA and report on three core deliverables completed in this first phase of development: a data submission system, a core facility registry, and the underlying database infrastructure. The data submission system supports a wide range of experimental paradigms, including genetically modified animal models, pharmacological interventions, and gonadectomy procedures, and accepts quantitative phenotyping data generated by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), microcomputed tomography (μCT), bone histomorphometry, mechanical strength testing, and serum, plasma, and urine biomarker assays. Submitted data are preserved in original form to ensure authenticity and parsed into a relational database to support flexible search functionality and programmatic access. The core facility registry catalogs institutional resources available to the skeletal research community. Together, these components establish ROSSA as a foundational resource for the skeletal biology community and lay the groundwork for future cross-study data integration and meta-analysis.

title: Intra-articular osteoid osteoma of the talar neck initially managed as early avascular necrosis: a case report.
authors: Evoniuk C, Hartman G, Freeland E.
abstract: Intra-articular osteoid osteoma is an uncommon benign osteoblastic tumor that frequently presents with atypical clinical and radiographic findings, often delaying diagnosis. Lesions involving the talus are challenging because marrow edema and synovitis may obscure the characteristic nidus on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), mimicking other pathologic processes. We present the case of a young male with a greater than 2-year history of atraumatic ankle pain and diffuse talar marrow edema on MRI, initially interpreted as osteonecrosis. He underwent ankle arthroscopy and talar core decompression, with minimal improvement. Repeat MRI demonstrated an evolving dorsolateral talar neck lesion, raising concern for osteoid osteoma and prompting excision. Histopathology demonstrated osteoid osteoma. At 6-month follow-up, he reported full pain resolution and unrestricted activity. This case highlights that intra-articular osteoid osteoma of the talus should be considered in young patients with persistent atraumatic ankle pain and diffuse marrow edema when the clinical course becomes discordant with avascular necrosis.

title: Influences on veterinary professionals to perform wildlife medicine in the United Kingdom: A qualitative multifocal study.
authors: Lang R, Mullineaux E, Thomas L.
abstract: Introduction In the United Kingdom (UK) thousands of wild animals enter veterinary clinics and wildlife centres requiring medical support and rehabilitation care due to natural and anthropogenic diseases and injuries. The objectives of this empirical research were to survey veterinary professionals, wildlife centre personnel and academic educators to explore the influences of culture, working relationships, education and professional obligations on wildlife treatment experienced by the veterinary community. Methods A mixed-method of a semi-quantitative survey and qualitative interviews was conducted. Purposive, convenience sampling was used for an online survey which was completed by 409 veterinary participants and 20 veterinary professionals, seven wildlife centre personnel and six academic educators were interviewed. The survey data was analysed descriptively and the interview data was analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Themes associated with promoting wildlife treatment composed of Competency, Motivation and Collaborations. Themes associated with inhibiting wildlife treatment consisted of Uncertainty, Lack of Resources and Conflicts. The Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS) had an influential role on both promoter and inhibitor themes. Conclusion A proactive wildlife medicine culture in the UK would benefit from the recognition and promotion of the values and benefits of working with wildlife. Starting with the inclusion of wildlife medicine to veterinary curricular. Support and communication within and between veterinary practices and wildlife centres to utilitise resources and information, develop networks and mitigate challenges to promote competency, motivation and collaboration. With support from the RCVS to refine educational and professional standards and enforce the regulation of the veterinary community in their provision of wildlife medicine.

title: Inflammatory and nutritional indices as predictors of poor prognosis in pyogenic liver abscesses: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sun B, Liu Z, Liu S, Yu T, Liu L.
abstract: Objective This retrospective study of 458 pyogenic liver abscesses (PLA) patients explored the link between inflammation/nutrition-based indices and poor prognosis in PLA, aiming to enhance the prediction of poor prognosis such as mortality, septic shock, or intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Methods Patient data, including demographics, comorbidities, clinical presentations, laboratory results, and treatment outcomes, were extracted from medical records. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to identify independent predictors and evaluate their discriminative power. A simplified joint prediction model was developed based on rigorous variable selection criteria, and its performance was assessed using internal validation. Results Patients with poor prognosis ( n = 33) exhibited lower lymphocyte counts, hemoglobin, platelets, and albumin, alongside elevated inflammation markers. Multivariable analysis identified the neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR) (odds ratio (OR) 6.87 per standard deviation (SD), 95% confidence interval (CI) [2.13-22.17], p = 0.001), prognostic nutritional index (PNI) (OR 0.99 per SD, 95% CI [0.894-0.997], p = 0.038), and controlling nutritional status (CONUT) score (OR 1.37 per SD, 95% CI [1.164-1.602], p p p p p Conclusion This investigation reveals that easily obtainable inflammatory and nutritional indices (NAR, PNI, CONUT and PLT) serve as reliable predictors of poor prognosis in PLA. A combined model integrating PLT and CONUT demonstrates promising discriminative performance, enabling early risk stratification.

title: Impact of Adjuvant Abemaciclib on Immediate Breast Reconstruction.
authors: Boydstun AG, Elmorsi R, Schaverien MV, Mericli AF, Clemens MW, Dickey RM, Parham CS, Piotrowski MJ, Barcenas CH, Olenczak JB.

title: Imaging [18F]FDG PET/CT pilot study of nicotinic acetylcholinergic receptor α2 knock-out mice and α2 hypersensitive mice compared to control mice: Male-female differences and nicotine effects.
authors: Liang C, Tucker TE, Coronel ADL, Nguyen EHN, Nguyen JL, Intskirveli I, Lazar R, Metherate R, Mukherjee J.
abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholinergic receptors (nAChRs), comprising of α and β subunits are present in the brain and whole body. The less abundant α2-subunit is a fast-acting receptor subtype and plays an important role in cognition and learning. To understand cellular functional consequences, this study evaluated glucose metabolism using [18F]FDG PET/CT in α2 knockout (α2KO) and α2 hypersensitive (α2HS) mice. Control (CN; 4M, 3F), α2 knockout (α2KO; 4M, 4F) and α2 hypersensitive (α2HS; 4M,4F), 12-16 month old mice were used. Mice were fasted and injected with [18F]FDG (3-5 MBq) while awake. After 40 minutes they underwent whole body PET/CT. On a separate day, nicotine challenge [18F]FDG studies were done. Reconstructed images were analyzed to obtain standard uptake values (SUV) of [18F]FDG in brain and interscapular brown adipose tissue (IBAT). Statistical analysis was performed comparing the three groups of mice. The α2HS male mice exhibited the largest brain increase in [18F]FDG compared to α2KO male mice. The rank order of brain [18F]FDG uptake in the three groups: α2HS♂ > CN♂ > α2KO♂ > CN♀= = α2KO♀ ≥ α2HS♀. Nicotine treatment reduced brain [18F]FDG uptake in all mice. Females had lower [18F]FDG uptake compared to males and were less sensitive to α2 nAChR. In the case of IBAT, α2KO mice had significantly higher baseline [18F]FDG uptake compared to the other two groups: α2KO♂ > α2KO♀ > α2HS♀ > α2HS♂ > CN♀ > CN♂. Nicotine decreased IBAT in α2KO mice rather than increase as observed in CN and α2HS mice.This preliminary study shows that α2 nAChRs play a significant role in brain activation as exhibited by the increase in [18F]FDG in α2HS mice. In the absence of regulatory control by the α2 nAChR, the α2KO mice IBAT exhibited higher [18F]FDG uptake compared to controls and α2HS mice. Female mice were less affected by nicotine compared to the male mice.

title: Iguratimod combined with tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis patients with inadequate response to conventional synthetic or biological DMARDs: a retrospective study.
authors: Wang W, Chang J.
abstract: Introduction Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a common, chronic immunologically mediated inflammatory disease causing joint inflammation and damage. While disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) are effective, some patients respond inadequately. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of combining iguratimod, an anti-rheumatic agent originally developed in Japan, with tofacitinib, an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, in RA patients with inadequate response to conventional synthetic or biologic DMARDs. Methods A retrospective study analyzed the medical records of adult RA patients with moderate-to-high disease activity (DAS28 > 3.2) despite prior treatment with conventional DMARDs, biologics, or monotherapy with either iguratimod or tofacitinib for at least 3 months. Patients received combination therapy with standard doses (iguratimod 25 mg bid, tofacitinib 5 mg bid) for 24 weeks. Primary outcomes were the change in DAS28-ESR score and ACR20/50/70 response rates at 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included serial measurements of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 24. Proportions were summarized with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and repeated measures of ESR and CRP were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model with estimated marginal mean changes from baseline and a linear trend test. Results 28 patients were included, and all 28 completed the 24-week follow-up and constituted the full analysis set, without withdrawal or loss to follow-up. After 24 weeks of combination therapy, DAS28-ESR decreased from 5.30 ± 0.50 to 3.07 ± 0.83 (mean change - 2.23, 95% CI - 2.48 to - 1.97; P Conclusion In this retrospective study of refractory RA patients, combination therapy with iguratimod and tofacitinib for 24 weeks demonstrated significant improvements in disease activity (DAS28-ESR, ACR response rates) and inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) with limited adverse events observed. Given the small sample size and single-arm design, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The results suggest this oral combination therapy warrants further evaluation in larger, prospective, randomized controlled trials.

title: Identifying knowledge gaps in a biodiversity database and their spatial determinants.
authors: Guery A, Alard D.
abstract: Open-access biodiversity databases are valuable resources in the structuring and accessibility of species occurrence data. By compiling different data sources, they reveal the uneven spatial distribution of knowledge, with certain areas and taxonomic groups being better represented. Understanding the determinants of spatial and taxonomic knowledge gaps helps in informing the use of open-access data. Here, we identified determinants of knowledge gaps within a French regional biodiversity database, in the largest administrative region in France. Knowledge gaps were assessed using two metrics, completeness and ignorance scores, for 8 taxonomic groups covering five vertebrate and three insect groups. The data were analyzed for the entire region, but also at the level of the three former sub-regions, to identify the potential drivers that may account for knowledge gaps' determinants locally. Our findings show that insects were characterized by higher knowledge gaps than vertebrates. Overall, knowledge gaps are influenced by variables related to sites' accessibility rather than ecological appeal across both metrics. All groups shared similar determinants of gaps, except for the impact of agricultural pressure which is found to be more significant for insects than vertebrates. Ultimately, our study emphasizes the impact of biodiversity governance, through local funding and regional political decisions, on knowledge distribution in open-access databases. We recommend limiting these biases by redirecting biodiversity funding towards under-sampled taxonomic groups and under-prospected areas. When not possible, users of data extracted from these databases should correct for spatial-sampling biases (SSP) using maps of knowledge gaps in order to get a more accurate understanding of species occurrence.

title: How i do it: a survey of practice patterns in robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.
authors: Khanmammadova N, Wang J, Nguyen TT, Nguyen DT, Abubakr M, Vanta J, Myklak K, Jiang D, Ali SN, Basilius J, Shahait M, Lee DI.
abstract: Despite the global availability and utilization of robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), it remains a technically complex operation, with wide variation in training paradigms, surgical technique, and perioperative management. This study examines international RARP practices and aims to identify trends and gaps in clinical practice. A multiple-choice questionnaire consisting of 32 questions was distributed between January and July 2023. A total of 102 responses were received. Responses with ≥ 5 questions with missing data (n = 8) were excluded. Among 94 participants, 91.5% were male, 69.1% practiced outside the United States (US), and 72.3% were fellowship-trained. Most surgeons (79.8%) reported performing ≥ 3 RARPs monthly. About 75% of surgeons reported performing ≥ 90% of their radical prostatectomies (RP) robotically. Seven (7.45%) respondents who reported performing RPs only via laparoscopic or open approach were excluded from subsequent analyses. Regarding the surgical technique, transperitoneal anterior approach was the most preferred (62.1%). For nerve-sparing, the combined antegrade-retrograde approach (43.7%) and the antegrade-only approaches (36.8%) were most common. Approximately half of respondents (51.7%) preferred cut-and-suture ligation for dorsal venous complex control. For pelvic lymph node dissection, standard (44.8%) or limited (29.9%) templates were preferred over the extended (24.1%) template. The most common method for vascular control was clips for vascular pedicle ligation (79.3%). Of the continence-preserving techniques, most respondents agreed on the importance of maximal urethral length preservation (93.1%), bladder neck preservation (80.5%), and posterior reconstruction (64.4%). Postoperatively, most surgeons endorsed early mobilization (92%), early oral nutrition (85.1%), and non-opioid oral analgesia (57.5%). All US-based surgeons reported discharging ≥ 70% of patients on postoperative day 1, whereas discharge patterns varied among non-US surgeons. There are significant global variations in the practice of RARP. These findings point to the potential utility of consensus-driven, evidence-based guidelines to optimize RARP practices worldwide.

title: Health-Related Performance Decrements Resulted in Substantial Financial Loss for Team USA Athletes at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.
authors: Oeding JF, Anderson T, Triplett AN, Donaldson A, Finnoff JT, Vincent HK, Post EG.
abstract: Purpose To estimate the financial impact of injury and illness among Team USA athletes who participated in the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a feasible illness prevention program. Methods All Team USA athlete-events at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games were analyzed. Precompetition betting markets were used to derive the expected performance. Counterfactual finish distributions were generated using a Markov ranking model. Injury- and illness-associated performance decrements were estimated relative to expected medal placement outcomes and translated into expected financial losses across 3 domains: Operation Gold performance incentives, athlete stipends, and estimated commercial value. Losses were summarized at the athlete-event, athlete, and Team USA levels. A cohort Markov cost-effectiveness model evaluated a potential illness prevention program using probabilistic sensitivity analysis. Results Across 808 Team USA athlete-events, 186 injuries and 108 illnesses were recorded. Total injury- and illness-attributable financial losses were estimated at $1,014,210 under conservative commercial value assumptions ( B = $10,000), including $462,409 attributable to injuries and $551,802 attributable to illnesses. Median athlete-event-level financial loss was $3000 (75th percentile: $5094; 90th percentile: $7758), whereas median athlete-level loss was $4710 (90th percentile: $15,617; maximum: $62,915), indicating substantial right skewness and concentration of losses. Illness events were associated with higher mean financial losses per event than injuries ($5109 vs $2486). An illness prevention program costing $200 per athlete and reducing illness risk by 40% was cost-saving, averting $220,721 in expected losses at a total cost of $117,000, yielding net savings of $103,721, and remaining cost-saving in 95.2% of probabilistic simulations. Conclusions Injury and illness at the Olympic Games are associated with substantial and highly concentrated financial losses, with illnesses accounting for a disproportionate share of the total impact on Team USA athletes. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective cohort study with counterfactual performance modeling.

title: Getting REAL balance: a simple and reproducible method for imageless robotic TKA.
authors: Rossi SMP, Sangaletti R, Muci C, Capitani P, Benazzo F, Andriollo L.
abstract: Background In imageless robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA), intraoperative assessment of ligament balance may be influenced by asymmetric cartilage wear, potentially misrepresenting true soft-tissue behavior. Functional alignment (FA) aims to restore constitutional alignment while respecting the native ligament envelope. Using the unworn compartment as the primary reference for intraoperative balancing may reduce the effect of asymmetric wear and improve mediolateral symmetry. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on 180 knees (176 patients) undergoing femur-first imageless RA-TKA with a functional alignment strategy at a single-volume center. All procedures were performed using the ROSA Knee System with a medial congruent implant. Intraoperative balancing prioritized the unworn or less affected compartment, targeting a 19-mm implant space with near-symmetric medial-lateral laxity in extension and flexion. Medial and lateral laxities were recorded robotically before implantation and after final component placement and classified using the Robotic Evaluation of Articular Laxity (REAL). Results Preoperatively, lateral laxity exceeded medial laxity in both extension and flexion. Following implantation, mediolateral symmetry was restored with a significant reduction in medial-lateral laxity differences (p Conclusions In femur-first imageless RA-TKA performed according to functional alignment principles, unworn-compartment-based balancing enables reliable restoration of mediolateral ligament symmetry with balanced REAL phenotypes and a limited need for soft-tissue releases, representing a refinement of robotic ligament assessment in knees with asymmetric osteoarthritis during contemporary robotic surgery.

title: Geometry and cooling effects on an induction self-heating insert for rapid mold temperature control: Experimental, Multiphysics, and artificial neural network-based analysis.
authors: Do TT, Uyen TMT, Son Minh P.
abstract: Control of mold-cavity surface temperature strongly affects filling, premature frozen-layer formation, and cycle time in thin-wall injection molding. This study evaluates an induction self-heating insert with a thin heating zone directly coupled to a cooling layer using experiments, a sequentially coupled electromagnetic-thermal model, and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The design space contains 25 Taguchi L25 geometries defined by T, W, and L; X and Y coordinates are added so that the ANN predicts the surface temperature field. Three cooling states are considered: No Water (NW), Stagnant Water (SW), and Flowing Water (FW). Experimental ANN targets are the mean of five repeated tests. The simulation reproduced the location of the hot zone; among four cases with reported quantitative differences, three differed by no more than about 10 °C and one showed a peak difference of about 20 °C. To prevent data leakage, all 846 points from each geometry were kept together during geometry-wise validation. The resulting R² values were 0.746, 0.653, and 0.493 for NW, SW, and FW, with Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) values of 17.03, 12.97, and 12.62 °C, respectively. The effects of T, W, and L depended on the cooling state and were not consistently monotonic. A proof-of-concept molding test showed complete filling of a Chip 2 part using Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE); the mean spacing was 28.6 µm for a nominal 30 µm, and the mean height was 106.6 µm for a nominal 100 µm. These results show that combining insert geometry, cooling-water state, and a surrogate model can support local thermal design, delay frozen-layer formation, and improve filling in injection molding.

title: Gamified spatial‑participatory model for urban social cohesion in a post‑conflict city: Bridging accessibility, inclusion, and intergroup trust through co‑design in Kabul.
authors: Formolly A, Saraei MH, Siahi E.
abstract: Post‑conflict cities exhibit profound socio‑spatial fractures, institutional weakness, and eroded public trust. Conventional planning repeatedly fails to address ethnic segregation, accessibility disparities, and social fragmentation. The aim of this study is to propose and empirically validate an integrated model, the Gamified Spatial-Participatory Model (GSPM), that combines spatial justice theory, participatory co-design, and conflict-sensitive gamification to foster social cohesion. Using Kabul, Afghanistan, as a paradigmatic case, a sequential mixed‑methods design was employed. Quantitative spatial diagnostics mapped severe accessibility deficits, while qualitative inquiry identified deep trust deficits and cultural barriers; these jointly informed gamified co‑design workshops as the intervention. Pilot results provide strong preliminary evidence of GSPM efficacy: 90% of participants reported substantially increased engagement; gamification correlated strongly with intergroup trust (r = 0.76, p < 0.01); perceived accessibility improved by 38% in intervention areas. Critically, 70% of women and 55% of ethnic minorities reported meaningfully stronger belonging. The study demonstrates that this approach shifts planning epistemology from technocratic to deeply human, operationalising spatial justice in fragile settings, and offers transferable principles for fostering inclusion in divided urban contexts.

title: From accounting systems to business performance: A serial mediation model with IPMA evidence from Vietnamese SMEs.
authors: Tran VT, Le NNT, Ngo NNT, Nguyen TN, Pham KV.
abstract: This study examines how organisational and technological antecedents shape management accounting information quality and adoption level among Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and how these characteristics influence decision quality and business performance, with business environment uncertainty as a moderator. Using a cross-sectional survey of 503 Vietnamese SME managers, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and importance-performance map analysis to test a five-antecedent serial mediation model grounded in contingency theory and information processing theory. All ten hypotheses were supported. Information technology capability was the strongest driver of accounting information quality (β = 0.508), and market competition intensity was the strongest driver of adoption level (β = 0.385). Decision quality was the strongest direct driver of business performance (β = 0.558), and business environment uncertainty positively moderated this relationship (β = 0.238). All five serial indirect paths to business performance were statistically significant. The importance-performance analysis identified information technology capability as the highest-priority investment area, combining high importance with low realised performance (52.01 out of 100). To our knowledge, this study offers one of the first comprehensive tests of a serial mediation model linking these antecedents to business performance through accounting characteristics and decision quality in Vietnamese SMEs, one of the first importance-performance prioritisation maps for managers in this context, and extends contingency theory by identifying business environment uncertainty as a pure moderator rather than a direct antecedent. Findings suggest Vietnamese SME managers should prioritise digital accounting infrastructure investment ahead of expanding accounting tool adoption, and that government support for digital accounting tools may be warranted. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, partly addressed through theoretically grounded antecedent ordering, predictive validity testing, and multi-method bias assessment; the single-country scope reflects Vietnam's structural representativeness of wider ASEAN transition economies.

title: Externally validated MRI radiomics machine learning models for differentiating between myxoid liposarcoma and myxoma.
authors: Chen YH, Bazanjani S, Wang Z, Bauer F, Sharp A, Hung YP, Ossiani T, Saraee M, Smith G, Viator M, Gonzalez M, Chen A, Kerimo E, Palmer W, Pianykh O, Lozano-Calderón SA.
abstract: Objective To develop and externally validate a radiomics-based machine learning model for differentiating myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) from myxoma on MRI and compare its diagnostic performance with that of experienced musculoskeletal radiologists. Methods In this retrospective study, T1-weighted and fluid-sensitive MRI sequences from 109 patients with histologically confirmed MLS or myxoma were used to train support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB) classifiers. Models were evaluated in an independent external cohort of 32 patients from a second institution using different scanner hardware and protocols. Diagnostic performance was compared with that of two fellowship-trained senior musculoskeletal radiologists. Secondary analysis assessed MLS grading. Results The T1-weighted SVM achieved the strongest external binary performance (accuracy, 0.84; AUC, 0.91), outperforming RF and XGB (p = 0.005 and p 0.05), although the study was not powered to establish equivalence. Fluid-sensitive SVM performance was limited (accuracy, 0.56; AUC, 0.60), indicating sequence-dependent generalizability. Models and radiologists demonstrated limited MLS grading accuracy, reflecting tumor heterogeneity. Conclusion Externally validated radiomics-based machine learning supported noninvasive differentiation of MLS from myxoma primarily on T1-weighted MRI. T1-weighted SVM performance was not significantly different from that of experienced radiologists, although equivalence was not established, whereas fluid-sensitive performance was substantially weaker. T1-weighted quantitative imaging biomarkers may complement soft tissue tumor characterization, but extrapolation to fluid-sensitive sequences requires caution.

title: Evaluating treatment efficacy for Iliotibial Band Syndrome: A comparison of combined foam rolling and stretching with strengthening exercises versus strengthening alone in athletes.
authors: Naderi A, Azizi S.
abstract: Background Iliotibial Band Syndrome (ITBS) lacks effective conservative treatment protocols, often relying on expert opinion without addressing individual factors. This study compared the effectiveness of integrating foam rolling and stretching exercises with strengthening routines versus strengthening exercises alone in athletes with ITBS. Twenty athletes with confirmed ITBS (11 males, 9 females; mean age: 33.6 ± 9.5 years) were randomized into two groups: the Integrated Training Group (ITG, n = 10) and the Strengthening-Focused Group (SFG, n = 10). Both underwent 24 sessions over eight weeks intervention, lasting 25-30 minutes per session. Outcomes included a primary measure of pain intensity (Visual Analog Scale) and secondary measures of lower extremity function (LEFS), hip abductor strength, iliotibial band flexibility, and quality of life (SF-36), were measured pre- and post-intervention. The ITG showed significantly greater improvements in pain reduction (79.7% vs. 81.0% reduction, p = 0.02), lower extremity function (25.7% vs. 21% improvement, p = 0.02), iliotibial band flexibility (59.4% vs. 1.7% improvement, p = 0.001), and overall QoL (19.9% vs. 12.6% improvement, p = 0.006) compared to the SFG. However, no significant differences were noted in hip abductor strength or physical and psychological QoL components (p > 0.05). Based on the sample examined, integrating foam rolling and stretching with strengthening exercises versus strengthening exercises alone resulted in greater improvements in pain, lower extremity physical function, iliotibial band flexibility, and overall QoL. However, additional studies with larger sample sizes and in other populations are needed before definitive conclusions can be reached.

title: Esophageal pendulum: a rare case report of a giant solitary fibrous tumor of the esophagus.
authors: Khan MA, Anees A, Ahmed M, Jameel H.
abstract: Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is a rare mesenchymal neoplasm, accounting for <2% of soft-tissue tumors. Initially described in the pleura, it can arise at various extra pleural sites. Identification of the NAB2-STAT6 fusion gene has improved diagnostic accuracy. Complete surgical excision remains the treatment of choice. A 21-year-old female presented with progressive dysphagia and refractory anemia for six months. Imaging revealed a well-circumscribed intraluminal esophageal mass extending from the cervical to mid-thoracic esophagus and prolapsing into the stomach. The tumor was excised via an open left cervical approach with transgastric extraction. Histology showed spindle cells with CD34 and SMA positivity and nuclear STAT6 positivity, confirming SFT. Recovery was uneventful with no recurrence on follow-up, highlighting the importance of complete excision and immunohistochemical evaluation.

title: Environmental modulation of methyl farnesoate release in two clones of Daphnia pulex differing in the sensitivity to exogenous stimuli.
authors: Bellin N, Riboni N, Buschini A, Bianchi F, Careri M, Conciatori C, Facchini C, Filonzi L, Nicolosi S, Rossi V.
abstract: Daphnia is a widely recognised model organism in ecotoxicological studies, exhibiting environmental sex determination. Environmental cues such as temperature, photoperiod and crowding are known to trigger transitions from parthenogenetic to sexual reproduction. Experimental studies based on exogenous exposure suggest that methyl farnesoate (MF), a juvenile hormone-like compound, is associated with male production and predator-induced defensive traits in Daphnia; however, direct evidence of endogenous MF production and environmental dynamics remains limited. In this study, we investigated the release of endogenous MF into the rearing water of Daphnia pulex. Two D. pulex clonal lineages differing in propensity for male, ephippia and neckteeth production were selected. Experimental conditions simulating crowding and different habitat suitability, including variations in population density, food availability, photoperiod and temperature, were investigated. MF was quantified at ultra-trace levels using solid-phase microextraction coupled to gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In the first generation, MF concentrations decreased from approximately 18.5-20.0 ng/L in controls to 11.0-14.5 ng/L under crowding conditions and 6.7-7.2 ng/L under crowding combined with MK-801. In the second generation, concentrations were approximately 10.5 ng/L in control offspring and 12.0-12.3 ng/L after recovery from crowding. Exposure to crowding over two generations resulted in clone-specific concentrations, whereas MF remained below the limit of quantification of 0.08 ng/L, when parental females had been exposed to MK-801. In the density and seasonal experiments, MF released in the medium was higher release per female under early-spring conditions and in clone S. These variations occurred under conditions promoting male production, ephippia formation and antipredator responses. While not demonstrating a causal endocrine role of MF, our findings provide quantitative and environmentally relevant evidence that D. pulex releases MF into the aquatic environment and this release is modulated by both environmental conditions and genetic background.

title: Enhancing Cancer Care Through Ambulatory Care Model Redesign: Impacts on Disease-Based Care and Scheduling Teams in US Specialty Hospitals.
journal: The Journal of Ambulatory Care Management
authors: Price DD, Altomare AE.
abstract: Objective The Ambulatory Care Model Redesign (ACMR) initiative sought to improve patient-centered, team-based oncology care in a leading US cancer specialty hospital by strengthening care coordination, optimizing care team roles, improving scheduling reliability, and increasing operational efficiency across ambulatory clinics. The initiative sought to address increasing care complexity, workforce strain, and patient throughput challenges by redesigning care delivery through interprofessional collaboration and agile implementation strategies. Methods ACMR was implemented as a quality improvement initiative using Plan-Do-Check-Act methodology, agile project management, and a tri-level governance structure involving executive leaders, operational leaders, and frontline care teams. Key interventions included pooled rooming; top-of-license role optimization for medical assistants, registered nurses, and advanced practice providers; embedded disease-team scheduling; standardized point-of-service scheduling workflows; expanded electronic health record (EHR) checkout functionality; and real-time performance dashboards. Outcomes were monitored using key performance indicators, including order entry, same-day scheduling, EHR in-basket turnaround, checkout completion, and patient experience. Findings ACMR produced measurable improvements in clinic operations, care coordination, and patient experience. Orders placed before checkout increased by 15.4 percentage points (pp), same-day checkout completion rose by 30.0 pp, and appointment scheduling before patient departure improved by nearly 20.0 pp. EHR in-basket optimization reduced scheduling-related messages per provider by 44.0%, with 80.0% addressed within 48 hours. Patient satisfaction improved by 15.3 pp for ease of scheduling and by 11.3 pp for perceived care coordination. Embedding schedulers within disease-specific teams also improved interprofessional collaboration and role clarity. Despite these gains, barriers including physician hesitancy, staffing variability, and dashboard fatigue highlighted the need for sustained leadership engagement, cultural alignment, and adaptive change management. Conclusion Structured ambulatory oncology redesign supported by interprofessional governance, role optimization, EHR-enabled workflows, and real-time data can improve access, coordination, and patient experience. Sustaining gains requires continued leadership engagement, staffing alignment, and iterative performance monitoring.

title: En bloc multivisceral resection for a giant retroperitoneal dedifferentiated liposarcoma: technical considerations.
authors: Al-Hassani S, Akingboye A, Merlini I, Di Saverio S.
abstract: Retroperitoneal sarcomas are rare, aggressive malignancies that often present late owing to the retroperitoneum's anatomical expansibility. Dedifferentiated liposarcoma is the most common high-grade subtype. We describe the technical management of a 65-year-old man with a giant retroperitoneal dedifferentiated liposarcoma involving multiple adjacent organs, treated by radical en bloc multivisceral resection including the kidney, adrenal gland, spleen, and distal pancreas. Postoperative recovery was complicated by a Grade B pancreatic leak and a left pleural effusion, managed with percutaneous and thoracic drainage, respectively. Histology confirmed a dedifferentiated liposarcoma resected with clear (R0) margins. At 18 months, no radiological recurrence had been observed, although this follow-up interval remains short relative to the recurrence interval reported for high-grade dedifferentiated liposarcoma. This case illustrates the technical conduct of multivisceral resection for a giant retroperitoneal sarcoma and the perioperative surveillance required to manage expected complications such as pancreatic leak.

title: Efficacy evaluation of the cervical posterior "keyhole technique" in the treatment of cervical radiculopathy: A retrospective case series.
authors: Tang R, Yin J, Zhang Z, Chen Z, Li Y, Zhou Z.
abstract: Study design Retrospective clinical study. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression for cervical radiculopathy and to investigate the correlation between decompression parameters and clinical outcomes. Summary of background data Cervical radiculopathy traditionally requires anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) or open posterior decompression. Although ACDF is the gold standard, it is associated with adjacent segment degeneration and implant-related complications. Minimally invasive posterior keyhole techniques aim to reduce surgical trauma; however, the optimal extent of decompression required for symptomatic relief remains unclear. Methods Forty patients with single-level cervical radiculopathy treated via unilateral endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression (strictly limited to targeted foraminotomy and partial medial facetectomy) (2021-2024) were reviewed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Neck Disability Index (NDI) preoperatively, at discharge, and at 6 months postoperatively. Decompression parameters were quantified via postoperative CT. Statistical analysis included paired t-tests and Pearson correlation. Results All 40 procedures were successful. Specifically, 25 patients underwent isolated foraminotomy, and 15 received foraminotomy combined with discectomy, without any progression to interlaminar decompression or laminectomy. The mean operative time was 70.4 ± 24.7 minutes, and the mean blood loss was 11.7 ± 10.9 ml. Significant improvements in clinical scores were observed at all postoperative time points (P Conclusions This study demonstrates that endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression is a safe and feasible technique that provides favorable short-term clinical outcomes with minimal surgical trauma. The findings strongly suggest that clinical efficacy depends on targeted neural decompression (determined by intraoperative nerve root mobility) rather than the maximal removal of disc tissue or extensive laminoforaminotomy.

title: Does receiving red yeast rice prescriptions (LipoCol Forte®) increase the risk of end-stage renal disease or not? A retrospective cohort study.
authors: Chang CC, Lam F, Yeh CC, Lin JG, Chen TL, Liao CC.
abstract: Background The potential relationship between the consumption of red yeast rice (RYR) and the development of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains poorly understood. We aimed to evaluate the risk of ESRD in patients who used RYR. Methods Utilizing insurance claim records from 2010 to 2014, we performed a retrospective cohort analysis comparing 67,876 individuals using RYR against a control group of 90,836 lovastatin users (non-RYR group), with follow-up extending through 2019. The incidence of ESRD was analyzed using adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) within Cox proportional hazard models. Results During follow-up, the ESRD incidence was 0.9 per 1,000 person-years in RYR users, compared to 3.7 per 1,000 person-years in lovastatin users (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.32-0.40). A dose-dependent reduction in ESRD risk was observed with increasing RYR prescriptions. Sensitivity analysis, excluding ESRD cases within the initial six months, confirmed a persistent association between RYR use and reduced ESRD risk (adjusted HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.81). Conclusion RYR intake may be linked to a decreased likelihood of progressing to ESRD. Despite these promising results, factors such as medication adherence necessitate cautious interpretation. Further randomized controlled trials are required to validate these findings and clarify RYR's role in slowing kidney disease progression.

title: Does greater orthoplastic integration reduce deep infection after open tibial fracture? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Choi B, Ghaie S, Shah A, Boriani F.
abstract: Objective Combined orthoplastic management of open tibial fractures is widely recommended, but existing evidence has not quantified whether the degree of care-pathway integration, beyond a binary orthoplastic-versus-orthopaedic distinction, is associated with a graded difference in outcome. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified deep infection and secondary outcome rates across four care-pathway models of increasing team continuity. Methods MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and grey literature were searched in collaboration with a specialist medical librarian. Studies were classified into four care-pathway groups: Group 1, single-setting simultaneous fixation and soft tissue coverage; Group 2, staged care with continuous orthoplastic team involvement; Group 3, discontinuous or delayed plastic surgical involvement; Group 4, purely orthopaedic management. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled deep infection, limb salvage, reoperation, and non-union rates per group. Comparative meta-analyses used genuine within-study comparator arms. Confounding was assessed via meta-regression and subgroup analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE. Results Fifty-eight studies (81 classified arms) were included. Pooled deep infection rates rose progressively with decreasing care-pathway integration: 8% (95% CI 5-12%) in Group 1, 16% (9-24%) in Group 2, 28% (11-49%) in Group 3, and 37% (25-50%) in Group 4. A similar gradient was observed for non-union (4-26% across groups). Limb salvage was near-universal (94-99%) and did not discriminate between pathways. Leave-one-out and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness for Groups 1, 2, and 4; Group 3's estimate was substantially influenced by a single Critical-risk-of-bias study, with deep infection rates attenuating from 28% to 23% on exclusion. No significant publication bias was detected. Certainty of evidence, per GRADE, was Very Low for majority of the pooled estimates, reflecting serious risk of bias and inconsistency, and Low where heterogeneity was minimal. Conclusion Progressive care-pathway integration is associated with a consistent, graded reduction in deep infection and non-union risk following open tibial fracture, independent of injury mechanism. These findings support continued investment in combined orthoplastic care, including partial integration models where single-setting surgery is not achievable.

title: Disaster-induced migration and local labor markets: Heterogeneous effects by skill level and industry structure.
authors: Hu Y, Mao Y, Luo Q, Cutler H.
abstract: Natural disasters can trigger large-scale population displacement, resulting in labor market shocks in destination areas. Nonetheless, important aspects of migration-driven shocks remain unclear, particularly how relative inflow intensity, the spatially concentrated inflow of low-skilled migrants, and industry structure moderate these impacts.
