Using Hurricane Katrina as a natural experiment and a Difference in Difference framework, this study reveals that displacement shock reduces wages in the low-skill localized sector, but this negative impact is heavily characterized by non-linear congestion effects, intensifying sharply from $-0.15 to $-0.27 drop in wage rates when the inflow concentration crosses certain threshold. Decomposing the demand-side channels shows that while the influx stimulates local business creation, this countervailing buffer is economically modest and insufficient to offset the supply-driven wage depression. Furthermore, sectoral mobility and joint wage-setting analyses confirm that low-skill localized and traded industries remain highly segmented in the short run. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for both supply and demand channels, non-linear thresholds, and sectoral frictions to improve regional labor market policies after demographic shocks.

title: Density patterns and age structure of the queen conch (Aliger gigas) in a coral reef lagoon in the Mexican Caribbean.
authors: Benítez-Castillo IA, Castro-Pérez JM, Medina Quej A, Cohuo-Duran S, Acosta-González G.
abstract: The queen conch ( Aliger gigas ) is one of the most important fishery resources in the Caribbean; however, its populations have declined markedly as a result of overexploitation. This study evaluated the population density and size structure of the species within the Banco Chinchorro Biosphere Reserve, Mexico, during 2015, 2016, and 2018, encompassing the final phase of a 5-year total fishing closure and the period immediately following its termination. A total of 35 sampling stations were distributed across six zones of the reef lagoon. At each station, five circular surveys with an 8 m radius were conducted during each sampling campaign. The highest densities were observed in the Central and Southern Leeward zones, whereas the lowest occurred in the Southern Windward zone. Population density increased during the fishing closure and reached its maximum in 2016, suggesting a partial recovery associated with reduced fishing pressure. Despite this increase, the population was dominated by juveniles and subadults, while sexually mature individuals represented only a small proportion of the stock. Spatial variation in size distribution revealed distinct areas functioning as recruitment, growth, and potentially reproductive habitats within the reserve. Conversely, the scarcity of large individuals suggests the long-term effects of selective harvesting on the adult component of the population. Comparison between siphonal length and lip thickness indicated that only 6.2% of individuals simultaneously met the legal minimum harvest size and a morphological criterion associated with sexual maturity, whereas 10.03% attained the minimum legal size without having reached reproductive maturity. These findings indicate that siphonal length alone may not adequately protect the reproductive stock of A. gigas . Accordingly, size-based management regulations should be complemented by biological indicators of maturity, such as lip thickness, to enhance conservation measures and promote the sustainable management of queen conch populations in Banco Chinchorro. Collectively, these findings provide a robust scientific baseline for future conservation and management actions aimed at safeguarding reproductive stocks and ensuring the long-term sustainability of A. gigas fisheries.

title: Cross-platform comparison of diabetic foot ulcer transcriptomes identifies partially concordant disease-associated signals.
authors: Huang S, Li Y.
abstract: The extent to which diabetic foot ulcer transcriptomic findings agree across cohorts remains uncertain. We compared an RNA sequencing cohort of 13 ulcer and eight diabetic foot skin samples with a microarray cohort of six ulcer and three diabetic foot skin samples. Single-cell data from 26 participants were analyzed after aggregating gene counts within each patient and cell type. A further cohort of 10 ulcer and 11 healthy foot-skin samples provided a descriptive directional comparison. Healing-status comparisons were exploratory. The primary analysis selected 4,704 differentially expressed gene identifiers; 2,943 were represented among the 17,502 gene symbols shared with the microarray cohort. Of these, 1,254 had concordant directions and nominal microarray P < 0.05, including 1,028 with microarray false discovery rate < 0.05. Direction agreement was 70.2%, and overall effect-rank correlation was modest (Spearman ρ = 0.29). Five Hallmark gene sets met the cross-cohort enrichment criteria. More specific functional analysis of the stricter supported set highlighted cornified-envelope formation, keratinization and inflammatory-cell migration. In the additional cohort, 611 of 823 represented genes from this set agreed in direction, although its comparator differed. Twelve keratinocyte genes met the cell-type differential-expression threshold; this finding does not establish cell-type exclusivity. Healing-status results were sensitive to covariate adjustment. These data support partial concordance in ulcer-associated epithelial, inflammatory and metabolic expression patterns. Limited cohort coverage, comparator differences and unresolved confounding preclude a universal disease signature, healing predictor or causal interpretation.

title: Correction: Single double-loaded anchor repair of isolated Lafosse III subscapularis tears in patients not involved in physically demanding activities provides satisfactory functional and radiologic outcomes at minimum 5-year follow-up.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery
authors: Aral F, Oklaz EB, Ahmadov A, Asiret E, Delice C, Oklaz EBG, Akdulum I, Kanatli U.

title: Construction and validation of a unified 3D convolutional neural network framework for automated identification of cervical spinal cord injury based on CT imaging.
authors: Ou D, Mo Y, Huang Y, Ye Y, Lin S, Pan L, Lin R, Huang S, Pan S.
abstract: Objective To construct and validate a standardized three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D CNN) framework based on cervical spine CT imaging for automated identification of cervical spinal cord injury (CSCI), and to evaluate its stability across multicenter data and potential clinical applicability. Methods Cervical spine CT images were retrospectively collected from two independent clinical centers, including cases with and without cervical spinal cord injury. All images were converted to NIfTI format through a unified preprocessing pipeline, and three-dimensional spinal cord regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated using ITK-SNAP to assess interobserver consistency. A standardized 3D CNN architecture was constructed, and the dataset was divided into training, internal validation, and external validation sets using a stratified random strategy. Model training was performed using the PyTorch framework. Classification performance across different datasets was systematically evaluated, and ROC curves, precision-recall (PR) curves, prediction probability distributions, and threshold sensitivity analyses were used to explore the model's clinical application characteristics. Results The model demonstrated stable discriminative performance across the training, internal validation, and external validation sets, with AUC-ROC values of 0.943, 0.953, and 0.948, respectively, and AUC-PR values of 0.936, 0.939, and 0.943, respectively. Performance metrics showed minimal variation among datasets, with no evident overfitting or performance degradation. Prediction probability distributions indicated good separation between injured and non-injured samples. Threshold sensitivity analysis showed that the model could achieve performance trade-offs under different threshold settings, suggesting a degree of flexibility for clinical decision-making. Conclusion Based on standardized data processing and network design, the 3D CNN effectively extracted latent spatial information associated with cervical spinal cord injury from CT images. The proposed framework demonstrated good stability and reproducibility across multicenter data and may serve as a preliminary research framework for CT-based CSCI risk evaluation, particularly in scenarios where MRI is unavailable or limited. Prospective validation is required before clinical deployment. It also provides a methodological reference for the standardized construction of deep learning models in medical imaging research.

title: Conserved mobile genetic contexts associated with bla NDM-1 and bla NDM-5in Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from two hospitals in Thailand.
authors: Kitti T, Kaewphu K, Khuekankaew A, Boonlao C, Khongfak S, Sitthisak S.
abstract: Background Acinetobacter baumannii has emerged as a major nosocomial pathogen due to its remarkable ability to develop resistance to multiple classes of antimicrobial agents. The emergence and dissemination of the bla NDM gene among multidrug-resistant A. baumannii (MDRAB) are closely associated with mobile genetic elements (MGEs), which facilitate horizontal gene transfer and accelerate the spread of carbapenem resistance. This study investigated the distribution of bla NDM -positive A. baumannii isolates, characterized their antimicrobial resistance phenotypes and genetic determinants, and elucidated the genetic context surrounding bla NDM alleles using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Methods A total of 286 clinical A. baumannii isolates collected from a tertiary hospital in Thailand were screened for metallo- β -lactamases encoding genes( bla NDM ), OXA carbapenemase-encoding genes, IS Aba1 , and IS Aba125 using polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The bla NDM variants were characterized by gene sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility profiles were determined. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on eight representative bla NDM -positive isolates, comprising four isolates from the present study and four isolates obtained from another hospital in Thailand. Results Among the 286 A. baumannii isolates, 55 (19.23%) carried bla NDM . All bla NDM -positive A. baumannii isolates were identified as carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB), and 90.91% were classified as MDRAB strains. The prevalence of bla OXA-23 and bla OXA-58 was 85.45% and 16.36%, respectively. The insertion sequences IS Aba1 and IS Aba125 were detected in 89.09% and 81.82% of the isolates, respectively. Sequence analysis revealed that 49 (89.09%) bla NDM -positive A. baumannii harbored bla NDM-1 , whereas six (10.91%) showed sequence identity with bla NDM-5 . WGS analysis of eight bla NDM -positive A. baumannii demonstrated variability in K-locus and OC-locus types. MLST analysis revealed that the four bla NDM-1 -positive isolates belonged to three distinct sequence types (ST16, ST23, and ST213), while predominance of bla NDM-5 -positive isolates were ST2. Comparative genomic analysis of the genetic environments surrounding the bla NDM genes revealed highly conserved genetic organization, with strong synteny among isolates belonging to the same bla NDM type. Conclusion These findings demonstrate the emergence and persistence of multiple resistance determinants among A. baumannii isolates in Thailand, thereby underscoring the urgent need to strengthen antimicrobial stewardship program and infection prevention control strategies.

title: Competence narrowing in AI-assisted oral English instruction: A quasi-experimental study of the spiral synergy framework.
authors: Zhang J.
abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI tools into spoken English instruction has produced measurable fluency and accuracy gains, but whether these are evenly distributed across the dimensions of communicative competence remains underexplored. This quasi-experimental study compares the Spiral Synergy Framework (SSF), a three-layer pedagogical sequence (AI Consolidation, Bridging Tasks, Interpersonal Activation), against conventional AI-integrated instruction in two intact Business English classes at a Chinese higher vocational college (experimental n = 36, control n = 34), using oral recordings at three time points scored on five competence dimensions, 15 weeks of classroom observation, and an intra-rater reliability check. The two classes differed significantly at baseline on the oral composite score and three of five dimensions (control higher), though not on CET-4 proficiency or questionnaire items. Because treatment is confounded with class membership and both classes received AI-assisted practice, findings are reported as associations rather than demonstrated causal effects. Linear mixed-effects models testing Group × Time interactions across five outcomes (four dimensions and the composite), corrected for multiple comparisons, identified one outcome - real-time responsiveness - on which the classes diverged: the experimental class maintained responsiveness across the semester while the control class declined despite its baseline advantage (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = .029), a result that held under a cluster-robust sensitivity check. No corrected between-group difference was found for improvisation, coherence, naturalness, or the composite score; improvisation declined descriptively in both classes over the semester. Classroom observation data (experimental class only) document a recurring, non-monotonic cycle of AI-dependency reduction and rebound across 15 weeks. Intra-rater test-retest reliability of the oral-competence ratings was moderate to good (ICC = .67-.91), though this reflects a single rater familiar with participants rather than independent inter-rater agreement. Implications for multidimensional assessment, task sequencing, and cautious interpretation of AI-integrated curriculum research are discussed.

title: Comparison of internal fixation outcomes in young femoral neck fractures: three cannulated compression screws versus the femoral neck system.
authors: Xiao B, Lu M, Chen X, Qiu D, He Y, Li X.
abstract: Background Femoral neck fractures in young patients typically result from traumatic injury, present significant treatment challenges, and are associated with a high risk of complications. The cannulated compression screw (CCS) is a common fixation device, whereas the femoral neck system (FNS) is a newer fixation device. Objective To compare the clinical efficacy of the FNS and CCS in the treatment of femoral neck fractures in young patients. Methods Between September 2021 and September 2023, 82 patients with femoral neck fracture aged 18-60 years were admitted to our hospital. According to the different fixation methods, the patients were divided into the FNS (38 cases) and CCS (44 cases) groups. The perioperative indicators, complications and follow-up function scores were compared between the two groups, and the follow-up time was ≥ 12 months. Results The FNS group had shorter operation time (53.71 ± 11.20 vs. 64.61 ± 11.27 min, p p p p p = 0.026) and a lower incidence of lateral thigh irritation (7.89% vs. 29.55%, p = 0.014), along with less severe femoral neck shortening (4.68 ± 2.04 vs. 7.14 ± 2.27 mm, p p p p p Conclusion Compared to CCS, FNS has better intraoperative efficiency, a lower internal fixation failure rate, and less severe femoral neck shortening in the treatment of femoral neck fractures in young adults. However, given the retrospective design, relatively small sample size, limited follow-up time, and differential follow-up duration between the groups, these conclusions should be interpreted with caution.

title: Comparison of IOL power calculation formulas in short eyes using ESCRS calculator and eyetemis: Influence of anterior segment biometry.
authors: Kim CY, Oh JY, Choi HJ, Kim MK, Yoon CH.
abstract: This study compared the refractive prediction accuracy of seven contemporary intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation formulas in eyes with short axial length and assessed the influence of anterior chamber depth (ACD) and lens thickness (LT) on prediction error (PE). A total of 124 eyes with an axial length ≤22.0 mm that underwent uncomplicated phacoemulsification with implantation of a Tecnis ZCB00 IOL were included. Predicted postoperative refractions were obtained using the ESCRS calculator for Barrett Universal II, Cooke K6, EVO 2.0, Hill-RBF 3.0, Hoffer QST, Kane, and Pearl-DGS. Formula performance was evaluated using robust trimmed-mean analyses of trueness, precision, and accuracy implemented in the Eyetemis platform, along with conventional PE metrics and the proportions of eyes within predefined error thresholds. The mean axial length was 21.67 ± 0.31 mm, and the mean implanted IOL power was 25.2 ± 1.6 D. Kane showed a lower trimmed-mean absolute PE than Hoffer QST (0.376 vs. 0.445 D; p = 0.014). No significant inter-formula differences were observed at clinically relevant error thresholds. ACD and LT showed weak, formula-specific associations with PE; however, these findings were exploratory and not clinically actionable. Overall, contemporary formulas provided broadly comparable refractive accuracy in short eyes, although small formula-specific differences were observed.

title: Comparative genomics of seven Tenacibaculum maritimum isolates from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in Canada and Norway reveals conserved features.
authors: Lagadec E, Gulla S, Småge SB, Pino-Martinez E, Solheim K, Handeland SO, Nylund A.
abstract: Tenacibaculum maritimum is a major bacterial pathogen of marine fish responsible for ulcerative disease outbreaks and high mortality in numerous fish species and represents an important challenge in aquaculture worldwide. In this study, we characterized seven newly sequenced T. maritimum isolates recovered from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in British Columbia (Canada) and Norway, including the first complete genome of T. maritimum isolated from Atlantic salmon in Norway. Comparative genomic analysis revealed the presence of a complete Type IX secretion system (T9SS) and the canonical gliding-associated machinery. We also identified a largely conserved repertoire of candidate T9SS substrates and several major host-interaction proteins. Phylogenetic analysis placed the isolates in several well-supported clades comprising strains from different geographic origins and host species. Characterization of the O-antigen gene clusters identified three different types (1-0, 2-1, and 4-0), whose distribution was not congruent with the phylogenetic relationships among isolates. Colony development of the four Norwegian isolates on agar was strongly influenced by incubation temperature, with rapid growth at 20-24°C, slower growth at 12-16°C, and only limited growth at 8°C. This study expands the available genomic resources for T. maritimum and highlights the importance of integrating genomic and environmental surveillance to improve tenacibaculosis management in aquaculture systems.

title: Causality-enhanced and symmetry-preserving PINNs for damped elastodynamic PDEs.
authors: Israr M, Ahmad S, Zaman FD, Ali I.
abstract: This study develops a causality-enhanced and symmetry-preserving Physics-Informed Neural Network (S-PINN) framework for nonlinear damped elastodynamic partial differential equations. The governing nonlinear elastic wave equation with viscous damping is reduced through Lie symmetry analysis into four invariant ordinary differential equation forms, including scaling, translation, damped, and generalized damped symmetries. The proposed framework combines symmetry-aware solution reconstruction, composite residual and symmetry losses, and causality-based temporal weighting to improve the training stability and physical consistency of PINNs. Numerical experiments are performed using a fully connected neural network with four hidden layers, 128 neurons per layer, the tanh activation function, and the L-BFGS optimizer. The S-PINN solutions are compared with conventional PINNs and exact analytical references for all four symmetry-reduced cases. The results show that the proposed S-PINN framework provides faster convergence, lower loss, and improved solution accuracy. In Case IV, S-PINNs achieve a 35% faster convergence rate during the first 500 epochs and reduce the final loss from 3.8 for PINNs to 2.4. The S-PINN loss stabilizes after approximately 1000 epochs, whereas the PINN loss continues to oscillate with fluctuations up to 15%. The gradient norm remains within 0.5-1.5 for S-PINNs, compared with 0.2-2.5 for PINNs. At α=0.4, the S-PINN solution attains 98% agreement with the exact solution, and its maximum absolute error remains below 0.05, compared with 0.18 for the standard PINN. Contour comparisons further show less than 5% distortion for S-PINNs, while PINNs exhibit distortions up to 18%. These findings demonstrate that embedding Lie symmetries and causal temporal learning into PINNs constrains the solution space to physically admissible manifolds and improves the reliability of neural solvers for nonlinear wave propagation in computational mechanics.

title: CD47 blockade augments anti-GD2 driven phagocytosis in vitro but fails to improve in vivo efficacy in immunocompetent, chemoresistant neuroblastoma preclinical models.
authors: Himsworth C, Jackson T, Bowers C, Munnings-Tomes S, Nair G, Muller H, Tucker E, Erbe-Gurel AK, Sondel PM, Chesler L, Mazjner R, Anderson J.
abstract: CD47 delivers a dominant "Don't Eat Me" signal that inhibits macrophage‑mediated clearance of tumour cells. Using immunocompetent, chemoresistant neuroblastoma (NB) models, we tested a Fc‑silent CD47 blocker (ALX301) with anti‑GD2 antibody alone and in combination with a clinically aligned temozolomide/irinotecan chemoimmunotherapy backbone. Tumours expressed GD2 and CD47, and bound ALX301. In macrophage coculture assays, anti-GD2 antibody induced dose-dependent phagocytosis, whereas ALX301 or an anti-CD47 antibody alone did not. CD47 blockade in combination with a suboptimal concentration of anti-GD2 antibody showed an additive effect on phagocytosis in vitro. In vivo, however, ALX301 failed to improve tumour control or survival when added to anti‑GD2 or to chemoimmunotherapy in the dosing regimens and two independent models tested. Toxicity was acceptable, showing only mild, expected red‑cell changes without overt organ injury. This form of CD47 inhibition is therefore mechanistically active in vitro but insufficient to enhance anti‑GD2 antibody-based therapy in immunocompetent mice bearing a chemoresistant NB, highlighting the potential need for myeloid‑reprogramming partners.

title: Bispecific immune cell engagers for solid tumors: Molecular engineering and therapeutic perspectives.
authors: Kumari P, Shrivastava A, Raul SS, Priyanjali BN, Dey A, Bordoloi D.
abstract: Bispecific immune cell engagers are among the most promising modalities in cancer immunotherapy, having made a significant impact on the treatment of hematological malignancy. However, their translation to solid tumors has remained challenging, leaving a critical gap for most cancer patients. A central obstacle is the lack of a mechanistic framework that integrates the complex biology of solid tumors with clinical outcomes, preventing a coherent interpretation of trial failures and impeding the development of more effective strategies. This review addresses that gap. We have reviewed clinical data from diverse engager formats recruiting T cells, NK cells, γδ T cells and monocytes across both successful and discontinued programs, showing how target selection, antigen accessibility, effector choice and molecular engineering collectively determine efficacy, half-life, tolerability and durability of response. We thereby construct a clinically grounded framework for designing next-generation engagers.

title: Beyond mid-thigh: Ultrasound assessment of hamstring muscle architecture at multiple muscle lengths in relation to strength.
authors: Karaca Yilmaz G, Dagli AC, Gozubuyuk OB, Akalan NE, Devran S, Oren Celik MM, Bayraktar B.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the relationship between ultrasound-based muscle architecture parameters and isometric knee flexor muscle strength in healthy individuals, and to evaluate whether distal (25%) and proximal (75%) measurement sites differ in their ability to reflect muscle strength compare to the commonly used mid-thigh (50%) region. Methods Isometric muscle strength was measured in 20 healthy (22.15 ± 2.41 y; 8 females, 12 males) participants using a hand-held dynamometer. Ultrasound parameters (cross-sectional area, muscle thickness, pennation angle) of the biceps femoris-long head, semitendinosus, and semimembranosus were measured at 25%, 50%, and 75% of thigh length. Associations between strength and ultrasound-based parameters were examined using multiple linear regression analysis. Results Moderate-to-high correlations (r = 0.615-0.815) were observed between muscle strength and cross-sectional area for all muscles at 50%. The regression model explained 89% of the variance in muscle strength (p Conclusions The cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus at 50% of muscle length showed the strongest ultrasound-based predictor of isometric muscle strength. However, measurement at the distal site demonstrated robust associations, suggesting this region may serve as a practical alternative. In contrast, proximal measurements were limited and showed non-significant associations with strength. These findings can help expand the clinical and research applications of ultrasound imaging for assessing hamstring strength. Given the exploratory nature of this study, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Between-hospital variation in prices for robot-assisted surgery: a multilevel analysis of Korea's 2026 non-covered price disclosure data.
authors: Kim W, Kim KS.
abstract: Robot-assisted surgery is not reimbursed by Korea's National Health Insurance, and hospitals set their own prices. In April 2026, procedure-specific codes for robot-assisted surgery were introduced into the national non-covered price disclosure system, enabling procedure-level comparisons of hospital-posted prices. We analyzed posted prices retrieved in October 2026 from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service: 733 hospital-procedure observations from 115 hospitals across 10 procedure-specific codes, using two-level linear mixed models of log-transformed posted minimum prices. For breast surgery, which has no specific code, we classified 318 hospital-defined items from 40 hospitals. Median posted minimum prices ranged from 7.00 to 10.00 million Korean won; within procedures, the 90th-percentile price was 1.7-2.6 times the 10th-percentile price. After adjustment for procedure type and measured hospital characteristics, the between-hospital share of residual log-price variance (intraclass correlation coefficient) was 0.54 (95% CI 0.38-0.62; 0.48 after excluding one outlying hospital). University-owned hospitals posted 15.2% lower minimum prices than private hospitals; public ownership, hospital type, bed count, and location were not significantly associated with minimum price. Each additional code with a reported price was associated with a 4.2% higher posted maximum price. Among breast surgery items, 20.1% did not specify the procedure, and 22.5% of hospitals posted prices by grade alone. Because these are posted prices, they do not show what patients paid or which price tier applied. Standardized procedure codes and transparent tier definitions could improve comparability.

title: Axial spondyloarthropathy with peripheral joint involvement mimicking gout on ultrasound: A case of double contour sign pitfall.
authors: Lee YE, Park EH.
abstract: Axial spondyloarthropathy (axSpA) may present with peripheral joint involvement, which makes the diagnosis more challenging when axial symptoms are unrecognized. In this report, a 66-year-old man presented with chronic left knee pain and swelling as the initially recognized musculoskeletal manifestation of axSpA. A double contour sign (DCS)-like appearance near the fibular head and a DCS at the first metatarsophalangeal joint initially suggested gout. Subsequent evaluations, including dual-energy CT, sacroiliac joint CT and MRI, and HLA-B27 testing, led to a diagnosis of axSpA with peripheral joint involvement. This case highlights diagnostic pitfalls in musculoskeletal ultrasound, particularly the gout-specific DCS. It also emphasizes the importance of correlating imaging findings with clinical symptoms and pain distribution.

title: Automated loop invariant inference through learning-guided program structure analysis.
authors: Hadad AS, Zheng J, Ahmed AA, Saeed F, Alkhatib M, Mohammed SH.
abstract: Automated loop invariant inference remains a fundamental challenge in formal verification due to the inherently unbounded search space of candidate invariants. Existing approaches either incur substantial computational overhead during invariant synthesis or rely on manually predefined templates, limiting both scalability and automation. Although recent learning-based methods have shown promise, they often fail to fully exploit the rich structural and semantic information embedded within program representations. This paper presents a learning-guided framework for fully automated loop invariant inference based on a systematic analysis of program structure and semantics. The framework performs a joint analysis of syntactic constructs, control-flow structure, and data-dependence relationships to determine invariant structure before instantiation. These complementary representations are embedded and integrated within a learning-based model that identifies structurally and semantically features and infers expressive invariant templates directly from program structure. The inferred templates are instantiated using execution-derived values, yielding constraint systems that are solved and formally validated using a Satisfiability Modulo Theories solver. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves competitive invariant inference performance on challenging benchmarks. By integrating multi-representation program analysis, the framework effectively supports a wide range of loop structures and advances the state of the art in scalable, expressive, and fully automated loop invariant inference.

title: Associations between countermovement jump impulse and running kinetics following ACL reconstruction.
authors: Ghani S, Lucron EM, Chan LY, Paton B.
abstract: Persistent deficits in lower-limb loading are commonly observed following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and may influence running biomechanics. Countermovement jump (CMJ) impulse can provide a phase-specific measure of force-time characteristics to reflect limb loading capacity; however, its relationship with running kinetics remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify phase-specific CMJ impulse following ACLR and examine associations with vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) metrics during treadmill running at the return-to-running phase. Forty-two participants performed three unilateral and bilateral CMJs on dual force plates and ran at 8 km/hr on an instrumented treadmill. Concentric, eccentric braking, and landing impulses were calculated. Running variables included weight acceptance rate, weight acceptance peak force, and maximum applied force. Inter-limb differences were assessed using Wilcoxon/paired t-tests. Impulse-vGRF relationships were analysed using Pearson/Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression. The ACLR limb exhibited significant deficits across all unilateral and bilateral CMJ phases, except for unilateral landing impulse. Deficits were greatest for unilateral concentric impulse (Δ1.3Ns·kg -0.67 , d = 1.49, p 2 = 0.25, p 2 = 0.38, p 2 = 0.37, p < 0.001). No meaningful relationships were observed for eccentric impulses or weight acceptance rate metrics. These findings indicate that jump impulse testing may provide clinically relevant indicators of running kinetics.

title: Association of the serum sialic acid-to-albumin ratio with prostate cancer and bone metastasis: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
authors: Ji Y, Guo C, Zhao Y, Yi L, Liu R, Qiu L, Gu G, Li D.
abstract: Background Prostate cancer (PCa) is a growing global health concern, with bone metastasis significantly worsening outcomes. Current diagnostics such as prostate-specific antigen (PSA) lack specificity, therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the clinical utility of the serum sialic acid-to-albumin ratio (SAAR) in assisting the identification of PCa and assessing bone metastasis status. Materials and methods This study retrospectively collected the clinical data form patients diagnosed with PCa and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) at Qilu Hospital of Shandong University from August 2014 to February 2022. SAAR levels were compared between the two groups, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to assess its discriminative capability. The bone metastasis cohort included 254 patients with PCa whose bone metastasis status was clearly determined, randomly split into training and testing sets. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression (LASSO) was used for variable selection in the training set, followed by multivariable logistic regression to develop a model for assisting in the identification of bone metastasis. Model performance was evaluated using the ROC curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). To evaluate the incremental value of SAAR, model area under curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test, alongside the calculation of net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results SAAR levels were higher in PCa patients compared to BPH patients, although the ability to differentiate PCa from BPH was limited. Among patients whose bone metastasis status was clearly determined, SAAR levels were significantly higher in those with bone metastasis. Multivariable logistic regression suggested that SAAR may be independently associated with bone metastasis. Further comparisons across multiple models showed that incorporating SAAR into the baseline model of PSA and Gleason score modestly improved discrimination and risk reclassification. The clinical model incorporating SAAR, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), PSA, and pathological grade demonstrated favorable performance. Conclusion SAAR is associated with PCa and the presence of bone metastasis. Its ability to differentiate PCa from BPH is limited, but it may provide adjunctive information for identifying bone metastasis. The proposed model show s acceptable internal performance and requires external validation before clinical use.

title: Arthroscopic Technique for Anterior Calcaneal Process Avulsion Fractures and Bifurcate Ligament Injuries Using Suture Tape Augmentation.
authors: Díaz-Fernández R.
abstract: Avulsion fractures of the anterior process of the calcaneus are frequently associated with injury to the bifurcate ligament and may result in persistent lateral midfoot pain and instability. Although open fixation or fragment excision has traditionally been used, these approaches may fail to restore ligamentous function and joint stability. Arthroscopic techniques for combined management of bony and ligamentous pathology at the calcaneocuboid joint remain poorly described. We describe an arthroscopic technique for the management of anterior calcaneal process avulsion fractures associated with bifurcate ligament injury. The procedure combines endoscopic excision of symptomatic intra-articular fragments with internal brace augmentation of both limbs of the bifurcate ligament using suture tape fixation, preserving residual native fibers and restoring ligamentous stability. This arthroscopic technique allows minimally invasive management of combined osseous and ligamentous pathology of the calcaneocuboid joint, providing stable ligament augmentation while avoiding the morbidity of open surgery and rigid across-joint fixation. Arthroscopic bifurcate ligament internal brace augmentation may represent a valuable option for selected patients with symptomatic anterior calcaneal process avulsion fractures and associated midfoot instability.

title: Arthroscopic Repair of Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Tear: Transtibial Fixation With 2 Lasso-Loop Sutures and 1 Samsung Medical Center Sliding Knot for Tensioning Secured by a Tibial Button.
authors: Arican N, Guven S, Karaman Y, Atalay M, Bingol I.
abstract: Medial meniscus posterior root tears disrupt the circumferential load-transmission function of the meniscus and negatively affect knee biomechanics. This technical note describes a reliable and reproducible arthroscopic repair technique using 2 lasso-loop sutures and 1 Samsung Medical Center sliding knot through a single transtibial tunnel, secured with a tibial cortical button, emphasizing controlled anatomic reduction and balanced tensioning at the meniscus-suture interface. This method provides strong tissue capture and secure tibial fixation while allowing controlled footprint restoration and minimizing suture loosening or cut-through, thereby enabling anatomic reduction of the meniscal root.

title: Are Cannabis and Cannabinoids a Valid Treatment Option in Patients with Rheumatic Diseases? A narrative review.
authors: Perrot S.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate current evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of cannabis and cannabinoids in patients with rheumatic diseases. Methods A narrative review was conducted based on a search for studies published between 2000 and 2026 evaluating cannabinoid therapies in rheumatic diseases. Results We identified 17 preclinical studies on the mechanisms of action of cannabis and 43 clinical studies published between 2000 and 2026, including randomized trials, observational studies and systematic reviews. We identified two articles on rheumatoid arthritis, 10 on osteoarthritis (2 reviews and 8 clinical studies), 28 on fibromyalgia (9 reviews, 7 randomized control trials, 12 clinical studies), one on psoriatic arthritis, and one on systemic sclerosis. The evidence of an effect of cannabinoids was strongest for fibromyalgia and limited for rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. Most studies reported improvements in pain and sleep quality. Globally, cannabinoids were well tolerated. Conclusion Some studies suggest short-term symptomatic benefits of cannabinoid-based therapies, particularly in fibromyalgia, but the findings are inconsistent and limited by small samples, heterogeneous formulations, and risk of bias. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use or recommendations in rheumatic diseases.

title: Alpha1-Antitrypsin Mitigates Radiation-Induced Capsular Contracture and Fibrosis In-Vivo.
authors: Farber I, Anav Y, Halpern D, Sheffer L, Goldstein O, Retchkiman M, Krieger Y, Ogen-Shtern N, Cohen S, El-Saied S, Lewis EC, Silberstein E.
abstract: Introduction Capsular contracture remains a significant complication after alloplastic breast reconstruction, particularly following post-mastectomy radiotherapy. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of human alpha-1 antitrypsin (hAAT) in reducing radiation-associated capsular fibrosis. Methods Textured silicone-discs were implanted subcutaneously in female C57BL/6 mice on day 0, followed immediately by localized 15 Gy irradiation of the implantation site. Mice were assigned to non-irradiated controls, irradiated albumin-treated controls, or irradiated hAAT-treated groups. Albumin control or hAAT was administered locally on days 0, 3, and 6. Capsule formation was assessed by MRI on day 21. Explants were collected on days 14 and 21 for histology, and day-21 tissues were further analyzed by gene expression profiling of inflammatory and fibrotic mediators. Human dermal fibroblasts were used to assess hAAT effects on radiation-associated TGFβ expression in vitro. Result Irradiated controls developed significant capsule thickening, disorganized collagen deposition, and inflammatory infiltration compared with non-irradiated controls. In contrast, hAAT-treated irradiated mice demonstrated capsule thickness comparable to non-irradiated controls, with improved extracellular matrix organization and reduced inflammation. hAAT treatment reduced interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ), and collagen type I expression, increased the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist/interleukin-1 beta (IL-1Ra/IL-1β) ratio, and upregulated Sloan-Kettering Institute proto-oncogene (SKI) expression, resulting in predominance of SKI over TGFβ compared with irradiated controls. In a separate in-vitro human dermal fibroblast model, hAAT attenuated radiation-induced TGFβ upregulation. Conclusion Local hAAT treatment may reduce early radiation-associated peri-silicone inflammation and fibrotic capsule formation, supporting its further investigation as a prophylactic strategy in implant-based reconstruction.

title: Adaptive cranial simulation programme: matching procedural challenge and simulation capability to learner need.
authors: Roche AF, Kavanagh DO, Crimmins D, Houlihan LM, Zilani G, Healy V, Horan J, Condron CM.
abstract: Introduction Procedural simulation must provide meaningful learning for trainees with differing levels of operative experience. We developed a mixed-level cranial simulation programme designed to align procedural challenge, available simulation resources and faculty support with individual learner needs. Curriculum design and delivery A half-day cranial simulation programme was delivered twice annually, combining parallel foundational and advanced circuits, with procedural content informed by a previously published needs assessment. Activities were allocated according to operative experience, observed progression and anticipated clinical responsibilities rather than training grade alone. Readiness-based stretch tasks provided selected trainees with supervised exposure to more advanced procedural challenges. Implementation considerations Simulation modality, instrumentation and supporting technology were matched to procedural complexity and learning objectives. Authentic operative equipment and advanced simulation technologies were incorporated where appropriate, with industry partnerships supporting access to specialist resources. The parallel circuit structure enabled foundational and advanced activities to be delivered concurrently while concentrating specialist faculty, equipment and higher-capability simulation resources where they were most relevant to learner needs. Lessons learned and next steps This report describes curriculum design and implementation rather than effectiveness. Future development will extend selected stations from isolated technical skills towards scaffolded rehearsal of complete procedural workflows and integrate structured formative assessment throughout practice. A stable foundational curriculum with adaptable advanced content may provide a practical framework for supporting learners with differing levels of experience with a shared simulation programme.

title: A scoping review evaluating artificial intelligence applications across various injury prevention domains.
authors: Othman Y, Kasabwala D, Jayagopi K, Lemoine J, Park D, Hamza D, Elkbuli A.
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly utilized for injury prevention across diverse clinical and community settings including machine learning (ML). This scoping review aimed to synthesize the current literature on the applications and predictive performance of AI across multiple injury prevention domains. Methods This scoping review searched five major databases, including PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, and the Cochrane Library, to identify studies evaluating AI applications for injury prevention published through May 2026. Eligible studies included original U.S.-based, English-language research across self-harm and suicide, abuse and violence, fall prevention, and sports injury prediction. Studies were excluded if they lacked measurable prevention outcomes or sufficient methodological detail, or focused on injury treatment rather than prevention, to ensure relevant and interpretable evidence for synthesis. Results Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. ML models generally outperformed or matched traditional screening methods for self-harm and suicide prediction (AUC 0.81-0.82), while multimodal approaches achieved the highest predictive accuracy (AUC 0.90). In abuse and violence prevention, AI predicted intimate partner violence with an AUC of 0.88 and identified cases before formal disclosure. AI also improved fall risk assessment by accurately categorizing patient risk levels, predicting future falls, and mitigating fall injuries through wearable airbag technology. ML models predicted future sports-related injuries (AUC 0.76-0.84), while identifying modifiable risk factors including workload, strength deficits, prior injury burden, and concussion history. Conclusion ML-based prediction showed promise for risk stratification in self-harm, suicide, intimate partner violence, and recurrent victimization. Additionally, AI predicted fall risk and identified athletes at risk for future sports-related injuries while detecting modifiable risk factors, including workload, prior injury burden, and strength deficits. Although these findings suggest that AI and ML may have potential applications in supporting earlier risk identification, informing targeted prevention strategies, and facilitating more personalized approaches to injury prevention, the limited available evidence warrants careful interpretation.

title: A multi-attention mechanism-improved ResNet18 approach for lithology identification and classification.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhang F, Li J, Huang L, Li R.
abstract: Lithology identification is vital for improving geological exploration accuracy, optimizing petroleum exploration schemes, and ensuring construction engineering safety. Traditional identification methods suffer from low efficiency, high cost, and heavy dependence on domain expertise. This study proposes a lithology identification approach based on the ResNet18 backbone, in which five lightweight attention mechanisms, namely CBAM, channel-only attention, ECA, SE, and spatial-only attention, are systematically compared, and the best-performing CBAM module is embedded to strengthen feature extraction and discrimination capacity. The Open-Source Computer Vision (OpenCV) library is adopted for dataset preprocessing, where raw images are converted to grayscale to suppress interference from irrelevant information. Comparative experiments demonstrate that CBAM outperforms the other evaluated attention modules and is therefore incorporated into the final network architecture. A hyperparameter sensitivity analysis of the CBAM-based model demonstrates that the model performance varies with different combinations of learning rate and batch size. When trained with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a batch size of 16, the model achieves a lithology identification accuracy of 86.36%, substantially improving overall recognition performance. By integrating CBAM into ResNet18, the proposed method enables accurate recognition to support multi-field engineering applications, reduce risks, and promote intelligent precision.

title: "Tired but wired" - First-time parents lived experiences of sleep loss, tiredness and wellbeing during the first six months postpartum.
authors: Hughes Spence S, Leech A, Goss H, O'Connor S, Smyth S, O'Hagan AD.
abstract: Objectives Sleep loss is a common experience amongst first-time parents and can result in postpartum fatigue. There is a lack of research on first-time parents' lived experiences of sleep and sleep loss, and its associated effects on mental health, parental relationships, and overall wellbeing as new parents. We examined first-time parents' perceptions, experiences and attitudes to sleep loss, tiredness and wellbeing during the first six months postpartum in Ireland. Methods One-to-one semi-structured interviews were conducted with fourteen first-time parents (female n = 10, male n = 4) from October to December 2025. The interviews took place online. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings Four themes were identified: 1) the gendered experience of sleep as a new parent, 2) (in)ability to sleep, 3) postpartum wellbeing struggles and 4) resilience and adapting. These themes highlighted how first-time parents navigate their sleep in their new role as a mother or father, their difficulty getting adequate sleep, complex wellbeing struggles as a result of sleep loss, and the discovery of new ways to function when dealing with sleep loss in the postpartum period. Conclusions These findings highlight the need for healthcare professionals to recognise postpartum sleep loss as both a physiological and psychological experience, and to incorporate holistic, routine discussions of sleep into postnatal care.
